sanskrit: adṛṣṭa pūrvam hṛṣitaḥ asmi dṛṣṭvā bhayena ca pravyathitam manaḥ me tat eva me darśaya deva rūpam prasīda deva īśa jagat nivāsa
reference: After seeing this universal form, which I have never seen before, I am gladdened, but at the same time my mind is disturbed with fear. Therefore please bestow Your grace upon me and reveal again Your form as the Personality of Godhead, O Lord of lords, O abode of the universe.
baseline: Having seen that God is in the past and having suffered with fear the mind should be shown to me. The form of God should be worshipped. God should live in the world.
morphology: Having seen that I am ill-fated and ill-treated in the past and having gone through fear I express the same to you as the form of God.

sanskrit: kirīṭinam gadinam cakra hastam icchāmi tvām draṣṭum aham tathā eva tena eva rūpeṇa catuḥ bhujena sahasra bāho bhava viśva mūrte
reference: O universal form, O thousand-armed Lord, I wish to see You in Your four-armed form, with helmeted head and with club, wheel, conch and lotus flower in Your hands. I long to see You in that form.
baseline: I wish to see you with the crown the neck the chakra the hand the four arms in the same manner. You are the thousand arms in your image.
morphology: I wish to see you with the crown the neck the chakra the hand and in the same way with the four arms a thousand arms. You are the image of the universe.

sanskrit: śrī bhagavān uvāca mayā prasannena tava arjuna idam rūpam param darśitam ātma yogāt tejaḥ mayam viśvam anantam ādyam yat me tvat anyena na dṛṣṭa pūrvam
reference: The Supreme Personality of Godhead said: My dear Arjuna, happily have I shown you, by My internal potency, this supreme universal form within the material world. No one before you has ever seen this primal form, unlimited and full of glaring effulgence.
baseline: The Lord Śrī said that with the pleasure of you Arjuna this form has been shown to me. By the yogic practice of the self I am the manifestation of the universe and infinite. I have not seen you before.
morphology: The Lord Śrī said With pleasure I have shown you Arjuna in this form. By the yoga of the self you have shown me the manifestation of the universe and infiniteness.

sanskrit: na veda yajña adhyayanaiḥ na dānaiḥ na ca kriyābhiḥ na tapobhiḥ ugraiḥ evam rūpaḥ śakyaḥ aham nṛ loke draṣṭum tvat anyena kuru pravīra
reference: O best of the Kuru warriors, no one before you has ever seen this universal form of Mine, for neither by studying the Vedas, nor by performing sacrifices, nor by charity, nor by pious activities, nor by severe penances can I be seen in this form in the material world.
baseline: One who does not worship the Vedas studies charity deeds penance strife and other forms would be able to see the form of a man. You should do it with another man.
morphology: One who does not worship the Vedas studies charity deeds penance zealotry and other forms would be able to see the form of a man.

sanskrit: mā te vyathā mā ca vimūḍha bhāvaḥ dṛṣṭvā rūpam ghoram īdṛk mama idam vyapeta bhīḥ prīta manāḥ punaḥ tvam tat eva me rūpam idam prapaśya
reference: You have been perturbed and bewildered by seeing this horrible feature of Mine. Now let it be finished. My devotee, be free again from all disturbances. With a peaceful mind you can now see the form you desire.
baseline: Do not disturb them and seeing the foolishness the form is terrible. Then again you will see that my mind is beautiful. You will see this form.
morphology: Do not disturb them and seeing the foolishness the form is terrible. Then again you will find that the mind is dear to me. Then you will get that form again.

sanskrit: sañjayaḥ uvāca iti arjunam vāsudevaḥ tathā uktvā svakam rūpam darśayām āsa bhūyaḥ āśvāsayām āsa ca bhītam enam bhūtvā punaḥ saumya vapuḥ mahā ātmā
reference: Sañjaya said to Dhṛtarāṣṭra: The Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, having spoken thus to Arjuna, displayed His real four-armed form and at last showed His two-armed form, thus encouraging the fearful Arjuna.
baseline: Having said this that Arjuna should show the form of ones self. Having said that O Vāsudeva one should be fearful. Having become softer one becomes great.
morphology: Having said this to Arjuna Vāsudeva one should show one's own form. One would get comfort and fear. Having become sober again one would become a great soul.

sanskrit: arjunaḥ uvāca dṛṣṭvā idam mānuṣam rūpam tava saumyam janārdana idānīm asmi saṁvṛttaḥ sa cetāḥ prakṛtim gataḥ
reference: When Arjuna thus saw Kṛṣṇa in His original form, he said: O Janārdana, seeing this humanlike form, so very beautiful, I am now composed in mind, and I am restored to my original nature.
baseline: When Arjuna sees this form of man he becomes gentle and now he becomes a circle. He goes to nature.
morphology: When Arjuna sees this form of man he becomes gentle and now he has become the circle of God. He thinks that he has gone to nature.

sanskrit: śrī bhagavān uvāca su durdarśam idam rūpam dṛṣṭavān asi yat mama devāḥ api asya rūpasya nityam darśana kāṅkṣiṇaḥ
reference: The Supreme Personality of Godhead said: My dear Arjuna, this form of Mine you are now seeing is very difficult to behold. Even the demigods are ever seeking the opportunity to see this form, which is so dear.
baseline: The Lord Śrī has said that he has seen this form of darkness. He would like to see this form always.
morphology: The Lord Śrī has said that he has seen this form of darkness. He would like to see the form of my god always.

sanskrit: na aham vedaiḥ na tapasā na dānena na ca ijyayā śakyaḥ evam vidhaḥ draṣṭum dṛṣṭavān asi mām yathā
reference: The form you are seeing with your transcendental eyes cannot be understood simply by studying the Vedas, nor by undergoing serious penances, nor by charity, nor by worship. It is not by these means that one can see Me as I am.
baseline: Neither the Vedas nor the penance nor the charity nor the gift made by me. He saw me in such a way as he could see.
morphology: I have not seen the Vedas nor the penance nor the charity nor the manner in which I could see such a thing.

sanskrit: bhaktyā tu ananyayā śakyaḥ aham evam vidhaḥ arjuna jñātum draṣṭum ca tattvena praveṣṭum ca param tapa
reference: My dear Arjuna, only by undivided devotional service can I be understood as I am, standing before you, and can thus be seen directly. Only in this way can you enter into the mysteries of My understanding.
baseline: One can know the manner of Arjuna by devotion and by the unique means. One has to see and enter the principle of the supreme penance.
morphology: One should know the manner of Arjuna and see him in such a way as to enter him with the principle of devotion. One should do penance.

sanskrit: mat karma kṛt mat paramaḥ mat bhaktaḥ saṅga varjitaḥ nirvairaḥ sarva bhūteṣu yaḥ saḥ mām eti pāṇḍava
reference: My dear Arjuna, he who engages in My pure devotional service, free from the contaminations of fruitive activities and mental speculation, he who works for Me, who makes Me the supreme goal of his life, and who is friendly to every living being – he certainly comes to Me.
baseline: One who has done his deed to me is the supreme one. One who worships me and does not associate with others is free from all evil spirits. He is my Pandava.
morphology: He who has done his duty to me and who is the supreme devotee of me who is forbidden to associate with me is the king of all demons.

sanskrit: arjunaḥ uvāca evam satata yuktāḥ ye bhaktāḥ tvām paryupāsate ye ca api akṣaram avyaktam teṣām ke yoga vit tamāḥ
reference: Arjuna inquired: Which are considered to be more perfect, those who are always properly engaged in Your devotional service or those who worship the impersonal Brahman, the unmanifested?
baseline: Arjuna thus said that those devotees who are constantly connected with you those who worship you and those who do not understand the scriptures those are known as the yogis.
morphology: Arjuna thus said that those devotees who are constantly connected with you those who worship you and those who do not understand the letter those are those who are able to do such yoga.

sanskrit: śrī bhagavān uvāca mayi āveśya manaḥ ye mām nitya yuktāḥ upāsate śraddhayā parayā upetāḥ te me yukta tamāḥ matāḥ
reference: The Supreme Personality of Godhead said: Those who fix their minds on My personal form and are always engaged in worshiping Me with great and transcendental faith are considered by Me to be most perfect.
baseline: The Lord Śrī said that those who worship me with everlasting devotion and worship me should be worshipped with faith. Those who believe in me should worship others.
morphology: The Lord Śrī said to me that those who worship me with their heart always and are worthy of me those who are worthy to be worshipped with their faith those people who are worth me they are entitled to me.

sanskrit: ye tu akṣaram anirdeśyam avyaktam paryupāsate sarvatra gam acintyam ca kūṭa stham acalam dhruvam sanniyamya indriya grāmam sarvatra sama buddhayaḥ te prāpnuvanti mām eva sarva bhūta hite ratāḥ
reference: But those who fully worship the unmanifested, that which lies beyond the perception of the senses, the all-pervading, inconceivable, unchanging, fixed and immovable – the impersonal conception of the Absolute Truth – by controlling the various senses and being equally disposed to everyone, such persons, engaged in the welfare of all, at last achieve Me.
baseline: Those who find the letter undefined unexplained hidden everywhere and who find a place in the circle unbroken immovable fixed fixed in the ground the village of senses everywhere and have equal understanding get me.
morphology: Those who find the letters undefined unexplained hidden and pervading everywhere and who find a place in the sky with a fixed pole and the sensory village everywhere with equal intelligence get all the ghosts.

sanskrit: kleśaḥ adhika taraḥ teṣām avyakta āsakta cetasām avyaktā hi gatiḥ duḥkham deha vadbhiḥ avāpyate
reference: For those whose minds are attached to the unmanifested, impersonal feature of the Supreme, advancement is very troublesome. To make progress in that discipline is always difficult for those who are embodied.
baseline: The misery is more than that. They are bound to be bound by the undefined consciousness. The undefiled movement and misery of the body are made to be revealed by them.
morphology: The misery is more than that. Their undefined attachment and consciousness their undefiled movement and sorrow are expressed by the body.

sanskrit: ye tu sarvāṇi karmāṇi mayi sannyasya mat parāḥ ananyena eva yogena mām dhyāyantaḥ upāsate teṣām aham samuddhartā mṛtyu saṁsāra sāgarāt bhavāmi na cirāt pārtha mayi āveśita cetasām
reference: But those who worship Me, giving up all their activities unto Me and being devoted to Me without deviation, engaged in devotional service and always meditating upon Me, having fixed their minds upon Me, O son of Pṛthā – for them I am the swift deliverer from the ocean of birth and death.
baseline: Those who meditate on me and worship me with the same yogic practice as me the other side of me and those who worship me in the same way as me. I will not get rid of you from the sea of death.
morphology: Those who meditate on me and worship me with the same yoga as my mother and others with all their deeds. Those who worship me after having meditated on me will never get rid of me and will never die.

sanskrit: mayi eva manaḥ ādhatsva mayi buddhim niveśaya nivasiṣyasi mayi eva ataḥ ūrdhvam na saṁśayaḥ
reference: Just fix your mind upon Me, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and engage all your intelligence in Me. Thus you will live in Me always, without a doubt.
baseline: The mind should be placed in me and the mind in me and you should live in me. Therefore you cannot rise above me.
morphology: O Lord of my heart you have placed your mind in me invest your intellect in me and you will live in me.

sanskrit: atha cittam samādhātum na śaknoṣi mayi sthiram abhyāsa yogena tataḥ mām icchā āptum dhanam jaya
reference: My dear Arjuna, O winner of wealth, if you cannot fix your mind upon Me without deviation, then follow the regulative principles of bhakti-yoga. In this way develop a desire to attain Me.
baseline: Then the mind cannot be satisfied with me. Then with the practice of yogic practice you want me to get wealth and victory.
morphology: Then the mind would not be able to be satisfied with me. Then with the practice of yogic practice you would wish me wealth and victory.

sanskrit: abhyāse api asamarthaḥ asi mat karma paramaḥ bhava mat artham api karmāṇi kurvan siddhim avāpsyasi
reference: If you cannot practice the regulations of bhakti-yoga, then just try to work for Me, because by working for Me you will come to the perfect stage.
baseline: One who is not able to practice even if he has done his duty is the supreme one. You will get the meaning of his duty by doing his duty.
morphology: One who is not able to practice even if he has done his duty is the supreme one. You also have the meaning of his duty and you get the accomplishment.

sanskrit: atha etat api aśaktaḥ asi kartum mat yogam āśritaḥ sarva karma phala tyāgam tataḥ kuru yata ātma vān
reference: If, however, you are unable to work in this consciousness of Me, then try to act giving up all results of your work and try to be self-situated.
baseline: In order to do this also one who is weak should do yoga on me. One should do all the actions and sacrifice the fruits of the actions.
morphology: In order to do so one who is also weak should do yoga on my own and then give up all the deeds and fruits.

sanskrit: śreyaḥ hi jñānam abhyāsāt jñānāt dhyānam viśiṣyate dhyānāt karma phala tyāgaḥ tyāgāt śāntiḥ anantaram
reference: If you cannot take to this practice, then engage yourself in the cultivation of knowledge. Better than knowledge, however, is meditation, and better than meditation is renunciation of the fruits of action, for by such renunciation one can attain peace of mind.
baseline: One who practices knowledge will get the benefits. One who meditates on the results of his actions and sacrifices will get peace.
morphology: One who practices knowledge would be blessed with knowledge. One who meditates with knowledge would get the fruits of action and sacrifice. One would get peace by renunciation.

sanskrit: adveṣṭā sarva bhūtānām maitraḥ karuṇaḥ eva ca nirmamaḥ nirahaṅkāraḥ sama duḥkha sukhaḥ kṣamī santuṣṭaḥ satatam yogī yata ātmā dṛḍha niścayaḥ mayi arpita manaḥ buddhiḥ yaḥ mat bhaktaḥ saḥ me priyaḥ
reference: One who is not envious but is a kind friend to all living entities, who does not think himself a proprietor and is free from false ego, who is equal in both happiness and distress, who is tolerant, always satisfied, self-controlled, and engaged in devotional service with determination, his mind and intelligence fixed on Me – such a devotee of Mine is very dear to Me.
baseline: One who is a devotee of me who is devoted to me and who is friendly to all the demons and compassionate and unyielding one who is free from sorrow happiness forgiveness contentment self determination mind and intellect etc. is always a yogin.
morphology: One who is willing to be friends with all the devils and has compassion and is ready to be selfless is content with the same sorrows and pleasures and is satisfied with the eternal yogin. One who has faith in the spirit and the mind given to him by me and is devoted to me is dear to me.

sanskrit: yasmāt na udvijate lokaḥ lokāt na udvijate ca yaḥ harṣa amarṣa bhaya udvegaiḥ muktaḥ yaḥ saḥ ca me priyaḥ
reference: He by whom no one is put into difficulty and who is not disturbed by anyone, who is equipoised in happiness and distress, fear and anxiety, is very dear to Me.
baseline: One who does not get irritated by this and does not feel irritated from this world and who is free from fear and anxiety is dear to me.
morphology: One who does not get excited by this and does not feel excited by that and one who is free from fear and anxiety is dear to me.

sanskrit: anapekṣaḥ śuciḥ dakṣaḥ udāsīnaḥ gata vyathaḥ sarva ārambha parityāgī yaḥ mat bhaktaḥ saḥ me priyaḥ
reference: My devotee who is not dependent on the ordinary course of activities, who is pure, expert, without cares, free from all pains, and not striving for some result, is very dear to Me.
baseline: One who is pure without any fear and who has gone into indifference and has left all the beginnings of suffering would be dear to me.
morphology: One who is pure without any fear and who has gone into indifference would leave all the beginnings of suffering. He who is devoted to me would be dear to me.

sanskrit: yaḥ na hṛṣyati na dveṣṭi na śocati na kāṅkṣati śubha aśubha parityāgī bhakti mān yaḥ saḥ me priyaḥ
reference: One who neither rejoices nor grieves, who neither laments nor desires, and who renounces both auspicious and inauspicious things – such a devotee is very dear to Me.
baseline: He who does not lose or suffer or suffer from evil or want to give up good or bad or renounce good or evil is dear to me.
morphology: One who does not lose or hate or suffer or desire good or bad or renounces or gives up his devotion is dear to me.

sanskrit: samaḥ śatrau ca mitre ca tathā māna apamānayoḥ śīta uṣṇa sukha duḥkheṣu samaḥ saṅga vivarjitaḥ tulya nindā stutiḥ maunī santuṣṭaḥ yena kenacit aniketaḥ sthira matiḥ bhakti mān me priyaḥ naraḥ
reference: One who is equal to friends and enemies, who is equipoised in honor and dishonor, heat and cold, happiness and distress, fame and infamy, who is always free from contaminating association, always silent and satisfied with anything, who doesn’t care for any residence, who is fixed in knowledge and who is engaged in devotional service – such a person is very dear to Me.
baseline: One who is equal to the enemy and friend and in honour and dishonour in cold warm happy in sorrow in company in opposition in the same manner in praise in silence in peace in steadfast belief in devotion in love in friendship in afflictions in misery in common with others in equal harmony in association in discontentment is satisfied.
morphology: One who is equal to the enemy and friend and in honour and dishonour in cold warm happy in sorrows in company in the same manner in opposition in praise in silence in peace in steadfast belief in devotion in love in man in friendship in misery in union in association in common with others is satisfied.

sanskrit: ye tu dharma amṛtam idam yathā uktam paryupāsate śraddadhānāḥ mat paramāḥ bhaktāḥ te atīva me priyāḥ
reference: Those who follow this imperishable path of devotional service and who completely engage themselves with faith, making Me the supreme goal, are very, very dear to Me.
baseline: Those who worship me with devotion and devotion are dear to me.
morphology: Those who worship me with devotion and devotion as mentioned above are dear to me.

sanskrit: arjunaḥ uvāca prakṛtim puruṣam ca eva kṣetram kṣetra jñam eva ca etat veditum icchāmi jñānam jñeyam ca keśava śrī bhagavān uvāca idam śarīram kaunteya kṣetram iti abhidhīyate etat yaḥ vetti tam prāhuḥ kṣetra jñaḥ iti tat vidaḥ
reference: Arjuna said: O my dear Kṛṣṇa, I wish to know about prakṛti [nature], puruṣa [the enjoyer], and the field and the knower of the field, and of knowledge and the object of knowledge. The Supreme Personality of Godhead said: This body, O son of Kuntī, is called the field, and one who knows this body is called the knower of the field.
baseline: O Arjuna one who knows the nature the man the region the area the knowledge the Lord said that he wants to worship this temple. One who knows that temple and the body should be worshipped by Lord Śrī Kaṇṭheya. One should know that the temple is worshipped in the form of a temple.
morphology: O Arjuna one who knows the nature the man the region the area the knowledge the mind the body and the mind should be worshipped by Lord Śrī.

sanskrit: kṣetra jñam ca api mām viddhi sarva kṣetreṣu bhārata kṣetra kṣetra jñayoḥ jñānam yat tat jñānam matam mama
reference: O scion of Bharata, you should understand that I am also the knower in all bodies, and to understand this body and its knower is called knowledge. That is My opinion.
baseline: Having known the territory and having known me in all the territories one should know the territory of India. That knowledge is my belief.
morphology: The knowledge of the territory is known to me and the knowledge of all the territories of India and the territories is known by me. That knowledge is my belief.

sanskrit: tat kṣetram yat ca yādṛk ca yat vikāri yataḥ ca yat saḥ ca yaḥ yat prabhāvaḥ ca tat samāsena me śṛṇu
reference: Now please hear My brief description of this field of activity and how it is constituted, what its changes are, whence it is produced, who that knower of the field of activities is, and what his influences are.
baseline: The area that is distorted by the fact that it is a defect and the effect that it has is known to me by the word samāṣa.
morphology: That area which is distorted by the fact that it is a defective area and that which is affected by it is known to me by the word samasa.

sanskrit: ṛṣibhiḥ bahudhā gītam chandobhiḥ vividhaiḥ pṛthak brahma sūtra padaiḥ ca eva hetu madbhiḥ viniścitaiḥ
reference: That knowledge of the field of activities and of the knower of activities is described by various sages in various Vedic writings. It is especially presented in Vedānta-sūtra with all reasoning as to cause and effect.
baseline: The sages should recite many songs and separate the Brahman Sutras from the various others. These are for the same reason.
morphology: The sages should recite many songs and separate the Brahman Sutras from the various others. The reason for this is determined by these.

sanskrit: mahā bhūtāni ahaṅkāraḥ buddhiḥ avyaktam eva ca indriyāṇi daśa ekam ca pañca ca indriya go carāḥ icchā dveṣaḥ sukham duḥkham saṅghātaḥ cetanā dhṛtiḥ etat kṣetram samāsena sa vikāram udāhṛtam
reference: The five great elements, false ego, intelligence, the unmanifested, the ten senses and the mind, the five sense objects, desire, hatred, happiness, distress, the aggregate, the life symptoms, and convictions – all these are considered, in summary, to be the field of activities and its interactions.
baseline: The great ghosts the ego the intellect the hidden senses the ten and the five senses of the cow the desire hatred happiness sorrow conflict consciousness strife this area is described as a disorder.
morphology: The great ghosts the ego the intellect the hidden senses the ten and the five senses. The desire hatred happiness sorrow conflict consciousness strife and disorder are described in the following lines.

sanskrit: amānitvam adambhitvam ahiṁsā kṣāntiḥ ārjavam ācārya upāsanam śaucam sthairyam ātma vinigrahaḥ indriya artheṣu vairāgyam anahaṅkāraḥ eva ca janma mṛtyu jarā vyādhi duḥkha doṣa anudarśanam asaktiḥ anabhiṣvaṅgaḥ putra dāra gṛha ādiṣu nityam ca sama cittatvam iṣṭa aniṣṭa upapattiṣu mayi ca ananya yogena bhaktiḥ avyabhicāriṇī vivikta deśa sevitvam aratiḥ jana saṁsadi adhyātma jñāna nityatvam tattva jñāna artha darśanam etat jñānam iti proktam ajñānam yat ataḥ anyathā
reference: Humility; pridelessness; nonviolence; tolerance; simplicity; approaching a bona fide spiritual master; cleanliness; steadiness; self-control; renunciation of the objects of sense gratification; absence of false ego; the perception of the evil of birth, death, old age and disease; detachment; freedom from entanglement with children, wife, home and the rest; even-mindedness amid pleasant and unpleasant events; constant and unalloyed devotion to Me; aspiring to live in a solitary place; detachment from the general mass of people; accepting the importance of self-realization; and philosophical search for the Absolute Truth – all these I declare to be knowledge, and besides this whatever there may be is ignorance.

One who does not want to do the same thing would become a devout woman a dev
morphology: One who has not been able to attain the goal of selfhood would become unmanageable. One who does not want to be unarmed one who is not able to do it one that does not have the ability to do so one with a sense of self self vanity self and ego one without selfs control one in the sense of sense one is born suffering from death one suffering from disease one having no sense of mind one would get the same happiness and happiness as one who has never had a bad life. One would become a devout woman one living in

sanskrit: jñeyam yat tat pravakṣyāmi yat jñātvā amṛtam aśnute anādi mat param brahma na sat tat na asat ucyate
reference: I shall now explain the knowable, knowing which you will taste the eternal. Brahman, the spirit, beginningless and subordinate to Me, lies beyond the cause and effect of this material world.
baseline: It is said that one who knows that the manifestation of the divine nature is going to happen would not be able to attain the elixir. One who does not know that there is no Brahman beyond him would not get it.
morphology: It is said that one should know that the manifestation of the immortality of the universe is not possible. One should know the manifestations of the Brahman beyond the past.

sanskrit: sarvataḥ pāṇi pādam tat sarvataḥ akṣi śiraḥ mukham sarvataḥ śruti mat loke sarvam āvṛtya tiṣṭhati
reference: Everywhere are His hands and legs, His eyes, heads and faces, and He has ears everywhere. In this way the Supersoul exists, pervading everything.
baseline: The feet are everywhere the head is everywhere and the face is everywhere.
morphology: The feet are everywhere the head is everywhere and the face is everywhere.

sanskrit: sarva indriya guṇa ābhāsam sarva indriya vivarjitam asaktam sarva bhṛt ca eva nirguṇam guṇa bhoktṛ ca
reference: The Supersoul is the original source of all senses, yet He is without senses. He is unattached, although He is the maintainer of all living beings. He transcends the modes of nature, and at the same time He is the master of all the modes of material nature.
baseline: All the sensory qualities are manifest in the mind. All the sense organs are unattached and all the senses are not able to be absorbed. All that is undefiled is the quality of the consumer.
morphology: All sensory qualities are manifest in the mind. All senses are different in nature. All the senses and all the objects are imperishable. All that is imperishible is the quality of the mind and the enjoyment of food.

sanskrit: bahiḥ antaḥ ca bhūtānām acaram caram eva ca sūkṣmatvāt tat avijñeyam dūra stham ca antike ca tat
reference: The Supreme Truth exists outside and inside of all living beings, the moving and the nonmoving. Because He is subtle, He is beyond the power of the material senses to see or to know. Although far, far away, He is also near to all.
baseline: The outer and inner parts of the body are the same as the outer parts of a body and are the subtle parts. They are not known to be far away and are not visible to others.
morphology: The outer and inner parts of the body are the same as the outer parts of a body and are the subtle parts. They are not known to be far away and they are the end.

sanskrit: avibhaktam ca bhūteṣu vibhaktam iva ca sthitam bhūta bhartṛ ca tat jñeyam grasiṣṇu prabhaviṣṇu ca
reference: Although the Supersoul appears to be divided among all beings, He is never divided. He is situated as one. Although He is the maintainer of every living entity, it is to be understood that He devours and develops all.
baseline: One who is undivided and divided among the demons and who is situated on the ground of a ghost and who knows that should be worshipped by Lord Vishnu.
morphology: One who is unbroken and divided among the demons and who is possessed by a ghost should know that.

sanskrit: jyotiṣām api tat jyotiḥ tamasaḥ param ucyate jñānam jñeyam jñāna gamyam hṛdi sarvasya viṣṭhitam
reference: He is the source of light in all luminous objects. He is beyond the darkness of matter and is unmanifested. He is knowledge, He is the object of knowledge, and He is the goal of knowledge. He is situated in everyone’s heart.
baseline: The astrologer should also say that the light is above all knowledge. The knowledge is known to be known. The heart is the secret of all.
morphology: The same light is said to be the astrology. One should know the knowledge. One who knows the knowledge should know it. The heart should be established for all.

sanskrit: iti kṣetram tathā jñānam jñeyam ca uktam samāsataḥ mat bhaktaḥ etat vijñāya mat bhāvāya upapadyate
reference: Thus the field of activities [the body], knowledge and the knowable have been summarily described by Me. Only My devotees can understand this thoroughly and thus attain to My nature.
baseline: The devotee should know this area and know the knowledge. He should know it from the same point of view.
morphology: The devotee should know this area and the knowledge. He should know that. He would get this knowledge from him.

sanskrit: prakṛtim puruṣam ca eva viddhi anādī ubhau api vikārān ca guṇān ca eva viddhi prakṛti sambhavān
reference: Material nature and the living entities should be understood to be beginningless. Their transformations and the modes of matter are products of material nature.
baseline: The nature and the man are the same as those who know both the vikas and the virtues.
morphology: The nature the man both the senses are known to be the same. The nature is known to have the same qualities and disorders.

sanskrit: kārya kāraṇa kartṛtve hetuḥ prakṛtiḥ ucyate puruṣaḥ sukha duḥkhānām bhoktṛtve hetuḥ ucyate
reference: Nature is said to be the cause of all material causes and effects, whereas the living entity is the cause of the various sufferings and enjoyments in this world.
baseline: The cause of the action is called Prakṛti. The cause is said to be happiness sorrow enjoyment consumption and consumption.
morphology: The cause of action is called Prakṛti. The cause is called happiness misery consumption consumption etc.

sanskrit: puruṣaḥ prakṛti sthaḥ hi bhuṅkte prakṛti jān guṇān kāraṇam guṇa saṅgaḥ asya sat asat yoni janmasu
reference: The living entity in material nature thus follows the ways of life, enjoying the three modes of nature. This is due to his association with that material nature. Thus he meets with good and evil among various species.
baseline: One who is born in the womb of a man should know the qualities of the nature. One who knows the nature would get the qualities due to the association of qualities.
morphology: One who is born with the qualities of a man should know the nature. One who acquires the qualities due to nature should know that the qualities are associated with it.

sanskrit: upadraṣṭā anumantā ca bhartā bhoktā mahā īśvaraḥ parama ātmā iti ca api uktaḥ dehe asmin puruṣaḥ paraḥ
reference: Yet in this body there is another, a transcendental enjoyer, who is the Lord, the supreme proprietor, who exists as the overseer and permitter, and who is known as the Supersoul.
baseline: One who is persecuted by the enemy and the enemy of the enemy would be called a great devotee of God and the supreme soul. One would be said to be a man in this body.
morphology: The husband who is persecuted by the enemy and the enemy is said to be a great devotee of God and the supreme soul.

sanskrit: yaḥ evam vetti puruṣam prakṛtim ca guṇaiḥ saha sarvathā vartamānaḥ api na saḥ bhūyaḥ abhijāyate
reference: One who understands this philosophy concerning material nature, the living entity and the interaction of the modes of nature is sure to attain liberation. He will not take birth here again, regardless of his present position.
baseline: One who does so and acquires the qualities of purusha Prakṛti and Prakrti in all things is not known to the earth.
morphology: One who does so and acquires the qualities of purusha Prakṛti and others in all things is not known to the earth.

sanskrit: dhyānena ātmani paśyanti kecit ātmānam ātmanā anye sāṅkhyena yogena karma yogena ca apare
reference: Some perceive the Supersoul within themselves through meditation, others through the cultivation of knowledge, and still others through working without fruitive desires.
baseline: One sees the self by meditating one sees the soul by the number of others and one sees it by doing yoga and others by the practice of yoga.
morphology: One sees the self by meditating one sees the soul by the other and one sees it by doing yoga and others by the others.

sanskrit: anye tu evam ajānantaḥ śrutvā anyebhyaḥ upāsate te api ca atitaranti eva mṛtyum śruti parāyaṇāḥ
reference: Again there are those who, although not conversant in spiritual knowledge, begin to worship the Supreme Person upon hearing about Him from others. Because of their tendency to hear from authorities, they also transcend the path of birth and death.
baseline: If others do not know how to do so they worship others. They are more prone to death.
morphology: If others do not know the same they worship others. They worship others and they are more prone to death.

sanskrit: yāvat sañjāyate kiñcit sattvam sthāvara jaṅgamam kṣetra kṣetra jña saṁyogāt tat viddhi bharata ṛṣabha
reference: O chief of the Bhāratas, know that whatever you see in existence, both the moving and the nonmoving, is only a combination of the field of activities and the knower of the field.
baseline: As long as one acquires some of the qualities and attains the ground one should know the ground. He should learn to do so. That is known as Bharata Rishabha.
morphology: As long as one acquires some of the qualities and attains the ground one should know the ground and the area. He should learn the practice of yoga.

sanskrit: samam sarveṣu bhūteṣu tiṣṭhan tam parama īśvaram vinaśyatsu avinaśyantam yaḥ paśyati saḥ paśyati
reference: One who sees the Supersoul accompanying the individual soul in all bodies, and who understands that neither the soul nor the Supersoul within the destructible body is ever destroyed, actually sees.
baseline: He who sees the same thing as all the devils and destroys that supreme god is seen to be unbroken.
morphology: He who sees the Supreme Being standing on all the devils and destroys them till they are destroyed will see him.

sanskrit: samam paśyan hi sarvatra samavasthitam īśvaram na hinasti ātmanā ātmānam tataḥ yāti parām gatim
reference: One who sees the Supersoul equally present everywhere, in every living being, does not degrade himself by his mind. Thus he approaches the transcendental destination.
baseline: One who observes the equilibrium everywhere is not equal to God. One who does not perceive the existence of the self would then move beyond it.
morphology: One who observes the equilibrium everywhere is not equal to God. One who does not perceive the self with the spirit should move beyond that.

sanskrit: prakṛtyā eva ca karmāṇi kriyamāṇāni sarvaśaḥ yaḥ paśyati tathā ātmānam akartāram saḥ paśyati
reference: One who can see that all activities are performed by the body, which is created of material nature, and sees that the self does nothing, actually sees.
baseline: One who sees the actions done by the same nature as all others would see the spirit.
morphology: One who sees the actions done by the same nature as all others would see the spirit. One who does not know the nature of the soul would see it.

sanskrit: yadā bhūta pṛthak bhāvam eka stham anupaśyati tataḥ eva ca vistāram brahma sampadyate tadā
reference: When a sensible man ceases to see different identities due to different material bodies and he sees how beings are expanded everywhere, he attains to the Brahman conception.
baseline: When one finds that the spirit is separate from one another and one place is not there then only the expansion of Brahman becomes possible.
morphology: When one finds that the spirit is separate from one another and one place is not there then only the expansion of the universe becomes possible.

sanskrit: anāditvāt nirguṇatvāt parama ātmā ayam avyayaḥ śarīra sthaḥ api kaunteya na karoti na lipyate
reference: Those with the vision of eternity can see that the imperishable soul is transcendental, eternal, and beyond the modes of nature. Despite contact with the material body, O Arjuna, the soul neither does anything nor is entangled.
baseline: Since the supreme self is undefiled by the absence of the undesirables it does not make any mention of the existence of the body and is not recorded.
morphology: The supreme self is not known even if it does not belong to the body and is not recorded as having been destroyed by the incantation.

sanskrit: yathā sarva gatam saukṣmyāt ākāśam na upalipyate sarvatra avasthitaḥ dehe tathā ātmā na upalipyate
reference: The sky, due to its subtle nature, does not mix with anything, although it is all-pervading. Similarly, the soul situated in Brahman vision does not mix with the body, though situated in that body.
baseline: Just as the sky is not available to all without having gone through it the body is everywhere and the soul is not found.
morphology: Just as the sky is not available to all the passersby. It is not found to be everywhere in the body. The soul is not obtained to others.

sanskrit: yathā prakāśayati ekaḥ kṛtsnam lokam imam raviḥ kṣetram kṣetrī tathā kṛtsnam prakāśayati bhārata
reference: O son of Bharata, as the sun alone illuminates all this universe, so does the living entity, one within the body, illuminate the entire body by consciousness.
baseline: As one illuminates a created world one divinities a field one illiquid world and one that illuminated a region is called India.
morphology: As one illuminates the world of the creation one divinities the realm of the universe and the kingdom of the world.

sanskrit: kṣetra kṣetra jñayoḥ evam antaram jñāna cakṣuṣā bhūta prakṛti mokṣam ca ye viduḥ yānti te param
reference: Those who see with eyes of knowledge the difference between the body and the knower of the body, and can also understand the process of liberation from bondage in material nature, attain to the supreme goal.
baseline: Those who know the difference between the fields and the fields the eyes the ghosts nature and salvation. those who know these things go to the Lord.
morphology: Those who know the difference between the fields and the fields the eyes the ghosts nature salvation and the disciples go to the Supreme Lord.

sanskrit: śrī bhagavān uvāca param bhūyaḥ pravakṣyāmi jñānānām jñānam uttamam yat jñātvā munayaḥ sarve parām siddhim itaḥ gatāḥ
reference: The Supreme Personality of Godhead said: Again I shall declare to you this supreme wisdom, the best of all knowledge, knowing which all the sages have attained the supreme perfection.
baseline: The lord Śrī said that the knowledge of the gods should be passed on to the higher beings. Knowing that it is better for them to know the knowledge the sages should go to the highest perfection.
morphology: The lord Śrī said that the knowledge of the gods should be better for the higher beings. Knowing that all the sages are superior to the higher gods they should go to the highest point.

sanskrit: idam jñānam upāśritya mama sādharmyam āgatāḥ sarge api na upajāyante pralaye na vyathanti ca
reference: By becoming fixed in this knowledge, one can attain to the transcendental nature like My own. Thus established, one is not born at the time of creation or disturbed at the time of dissolution.
baseline: Having attained this knowledge and having attained the attainment of my righteousness one would not get the fruits even in heaven and would not suffer in the calamity.
morphology: Having attained this knowledge those who come to me as equals would not be born in heaven and would not suffer in the calamity.

sanskrit: mama yoniḥ mahat brahma tasmin garbham dadhāmi aham sambhavaḥ sarva bhūtānām tataḥ bhavati bhārata
reference: The total material substance, called Brahman, is the source of birth, and it is that Brahman that I impregnate, making possible the births of all living beings, O son of Bharata.
baseline: The great Brahman in my womb is my yoni. I put the womb in that womb. Then all the devils become India.
morphology: The great Brahman in my womb is my yoni. I put the womb in that womb. Then all the devils are born in India.

sanskrit: sarva yoniṣu kaunteya mūrtayaḥ sambhavanti yāḥ tāsām brahma mahat yoniḥ aham bīja pradaḥ pitā
reference: It should be understood that all species of life, O son of Kuntī, are made possible by birth in this material nature, and that I am the seed-giving father.
baseline: Having covered all the parts of the uterus the image should be made possible. These are the brahmins. The great vagina the seed should be given by the father.
morphology: Having covered all the parts of the āvagina the figures are made possible. The brahmins and the great āviras are given to them by me.

sanskrit: sattvam rajaḥ tamaḥ iti guṇāḥ prakṛti sambhavāḥ nibadhnanti mahā bāho dehe dehinam avyayam
reference: Material nature consists of three modes – goodness, passion and ignorance. When the eternal living entity comes in contact with nature, O mighty-armed Arjuna, he becomes conditioned by these modes.
baseline: The virtues of sattva rajā tāma and prakṛti are said to be the great arms and the body.
morphology: The virtues of sattva rajā tāmā and prakṛti are said to be the great arms and the body.

sanskrit: tatra sattvam nirmalatvāt prakāśakam anāmayam sukha saṅgena badhnāti jñāna saṅgena ca anagha
reference: O sinless one, the mode of goodness, being purer than the others, is illuminating, and it frees one from all sinful reactions. Those situated in that mode become conditioned by a sense of happiness and knowledge.
baseline: The manifestation of the manifestation therein is pure. It is destroyed with pleasure and with knowledge.
morphology: The manifestation of the spirit is there with pureness the manifestation is known with pleasure the oblation with knowledge and the destruction with knowledge.

sanskrit: rajaḥ rāga ātmakam viddhi tṛṣṇā saṅga samudbhavam tat nibadhnāti kaunteya karma saṅgena dehinam
reference: The mode of passion is born of unlimited desires and longings, O son of Kuntī, and because of this the embodied living entity is bound to material fruitive actions.
baseline: The king should explain the raga the self the association of the body with the desire the union of the world and the union with the body.
morphology: One who knows the raga the self the body and the union of the body with the karma of the king should be bound together by the preceptor Trīṣṇa.

sanskrit: tamaḥ tu ajñāna jam viddhi mohanam sarva dehinām pramāda ālasya nidrābhiḥ tat nibadhnāti bhārata
reference: O son of Bharata, know that the mode of darkness, born of ignorance, is the delusion of all embodied living entities. The results of this mode are madness, indolence and sleep, which bind the conditioned soul.
baseline: India will fix the illusion of the body with the sleep of the illiterate and ignorant jama viddhi mohana all the dead.
morphology: One who does not know the meaning of the word jāma viddhi mohāna all the sins of the body laziness sleep and sleep are the means to end it.

sanskrit: sattvam sukhe sañjayati rajaḥ karmaṇi bhārata jñānam āvṛtya tu tamaḥ pramāde sañjayati uta
reference: O son of Bharata, the mode of goodness conditions one to happiness; passion conditions one to fruitive action; and ignorance, covering one’s knowledge, binds one to madness.
baseline: Having covered the knowledge of India one gets happiness and wealth.
morphology: Having covered the knowledge of the king one acquires happiness wealth deeds knowledge knowledge of India and then one attains glory.

sanskrit: rajaḥ tamaḥ ca abhibhūya sattvam bhavati bhārata rajaḥ sattvam tamaḥ ca eva tamaḥ sattvam rajaḥ tathā
reference: Sometimes the mode of goodness becomes prominent, defeating the modes of passion and ignorance, O son of Bharata. Sometimes the mode of passion defeats goodness and ignorance, and at other times ignorance defeats goodness and passion. In this way there is always competition for supremacy.
baseline: The king the king and the king of the kingdom of India become the king. The king of India becomes the king and his king becomes the lord of the kings.
morphology: The king the king and the king of the kingdom of India become the king. The king of India becomes the king and his kingdom becomes the kingdom.

sanskrit: yadā sattve pravṛddhe tu pralayam yāti deha bhṛt tadā uttama vidām lokān amalān pratipadyate
reference: When one dies in the mode of goodness, he attains to the pure higher planets of the great sages.
baseline: When the body is destroyed by the destruction when it has already grown in the seventh month the good deeds of the people are said to be good deeds.
morphology: When the body has been destroyed by the evil one the good deeds of the people are said to be done.

sanskrit: rajasi pralayam gatvā karma saṅgiṣu jāyate tathā pralīnaḥ tamasi mūḍha yoniṣu jāyate
reference: When one dies in the mode of passion, he takes birth among those engaged in fruitive activities; and when one dies in the mode of ignorance, he takes birth in the animal kingdom.
baseline: One who has gone to the abyss of the king and has done the work in the company of his companions becomes a fool. One who is not obedient becomes an idiot.
morphology: One who has gone to the kings house and has done the work in the company of the king and who has done it in the muṣḍha vagina.

sanskrit: karmaṇaḥ su kṛtasya āhuḥ sāttvikam nirmalam phalam rajasaḥ tu phalam duḥkham ajñānam tamasaḥ phalam
reference: The result of pious action is pure and is said to be in the mode of goodness. But action done in the mode of passion results in misery, and action performed in the mode of ignorance results in foolishness.
baseline: One who has done good deeds should be virtuous pure fruitful noble sorrowful ignorant evil evil and evil.
morphology: One who has done good deeds should be pure pure fruitful rich suffering ignorance ignorance and ignorance.

sanskrit: sattvāt sañjāyate jñānam rajasaḥ lobhaḥ eva ca pramāda mohau tamasaḥ bhavataḥ ajñānam eva ca
reference: From the mode of goodness, real knowledge develops; from the mode of passion, greed develops; and from the mode of ignorance develop foolishness, madness and illusion.
baseline: The knowledge obtained from the truth is called rajasa greed illusion temptation ignorance and ignorance.
morphology: One gets knowledge by virtue of knowledge greed pretence illusion ignorance ignorance etc.

sanskrit: ūrdhvam gacchanti sattva sthāḥ madhye tiṣṭhanti rājasāḥ jaghanya guṇa vṛtti sthāḥ adhaḥ gacchanti tāmasāḥ
reference: Those situated in the mode of goodness gradually go upward to the higher planets; those in the mode of passion live on the earthly planets; and those in the abominable mode of ignorance go down to the hellish worlds.
baseline: The king goes to the top and the virtuous places remain in the middle. The evil qualities of kings go to the lower places.
morphology: The king goes up and the virtuous places remain in the middle. The evil qualities of kings go down.

sanskrit: na anyam guṇebhyaḥ kartāram yadā draṣṭā anupaśyati guṇebhyaḥ ca param vetti mat bhāvam saḥ adhigacchati
reference: When one properly sees that in all activities no other performer is at work than these modes of nature and he knows the Supreme Lord, who is transcendental to all these modes, he attains My spiritual nature.
baseline: When the seer does not know the merits of another person he acquires his sense of self after having acquired the meriters.
morphology: When the seer does not know the merits of another person he acquires his sense of self after having judged those qualities above.

sanskrit: guṇān etān atītya trīn dehī deha samudbhavān janma mṛtyu jarā duḥkhaiḥ vimuktaḥ amṛtam aśnute
reference: When the embodied being is able to transcend these three modes associated with the material body, he can become free from birth, death, old age and their distresses and can enjoy nectar even in this life.
baseline: Having transcended these qualities one becomes immortal by having three bodies bodies and the birth death and sorrows.
morphology: Having transcended these qualities one becomes immortal by having three bodies the body and the world. One becomes free from the sorrows of birth and death.

sanskrit: arjunaḥ uvāca kaiḥ liṅgaiḥ trīn guṇān etān atītaḥ bhavati prabho kim ācāraḥ katham ca etān trīn guṇān ativartate
reference: Arjuna inquired: O my dear Lord, by which symptoms is one known who is transcendental to these three modes? What is his behavior? And how does he transcend the modes of nature?
baseline: O Arjuna the lord of the three gāṇas should know what the three qualities are. What is the conduct of the lord and how these three qualities can be derived from him.
morphology: O Arjuna who has said that the three qualities of the Lord are superior to those of the other linga what is the practice of the lord and how these three qualities are superior.

sanskrit: śrī bhagavān uvāca prakāśam ca pravṛttim ca moham eva ca pāṇḍava na dveṣṭi sampravṛttāni na nivṛttāni kāṅkṣati udāsīna vat āsīnaḥ guṇaiḥ yaḥ na vicālyate guṇāḥ vartante iti evam yaḥ avatiṣṭhati na iṅgate sama duḥkha sukhaḥ sva sthaḥ sama loṣṭa aśma kāñcanaḥ tulya priya apriyaḥ dhīraḥ tulya nindā ātma saṁstutiḥ māna apamānayoḥ tulyaḥ tulyaḥ mitra ari pakṣayoḥ sarva ārambha parityāgī guṇa atītaḥ saḥ ucyate
reference: The Supreme Personality of Godhead said: O son of Pāṇḍu, he who does not hate illumination, attachment and delusion when they are present or long for them when they disappear; who is unwavering and undisturbed through all these reactions of the material qualities, remaining neutral and transcendental, knowing that the modes alone are active; who is situated in the self and regards alike happiness and distress; who looks upon a lump of earth, a stone and a piece of gold with an equal eye; who is equal toward the desirable and the undesirable; who is steady, situated equally well in praise and blame, honor and dishonor; who treats alike both friend and enemy; and who has renounced all material activities – such a person is said to have transcended the modes of nature.
baseline: One who does not want to be distracted by the qualities of the lord the manifestation of the Lord the inclination the enchantment the circumcision the two directions the pāṇḍavas the indifferent ones the sitting ones those who do not care for the virtues the ones who are not moved by the attributes the others who are suffering from the same things the one who loses their position the other one who is not satisfied the same suffering the person who has lost his place the beloved one the man who is in love the enemy
morphology: One who does not think that the qualities of the Pandava are indifferent sitting and not being distracted by the virtues of the lord Śrī the manifestation of the Lord the inclination the attachment the dispassionately dispiritedness the desire to leave all the beginnings and the qualities that are left behind in the past. One who has not experienced the same sorrow happiness loss of his own place the same kind of love dislike courage self-sacrifice honour honour and humiliation would be equal to those of friends and allies.

sanskrit: mām ca yaḥ avyabhicāreṇa bhakti yogena sevate saḥ guṇān samatītya etān brahma bhūyāya kalpate
reference: One who engages in full devotional service, unfailing in all circumstances, at once transcends the modes of material nature and thus comes to the level of Brahman.
baseline: One who consumes me with devotion and yoga after having worshipped me without any pretence would equal these qualities and make him a brahman.
morphology: One who serves me with devotion and yoga by offering unspeakable offerings to me would equate these qualities with Brahman.

sanskrit: brahmaṇaḥ hi pratiṣṭhā aham amṛtasya avyayasya ca śāśvatasya ca dharmasya sukhasya aikāntikasya ca
reference: And I am the basis of the impersonal Brahman, which is immortal, imperishable and eternal and is the constitutional position of ultimate happiness.
baseline: I am the manifestation of Brahman the immortality the impermanence the eternity the righteousness the happiness and the solitude.
morphology: The glory of Brahman the immortal abode of immortality the eternal abode and the seat of righteousness happiness and harmony.

sanskrit: śrī bhagavān uvāca ūrdhva mūlam adhaḥ śākham aśvattham prāhuḥ avyayam chandāṁsi yasya parṇāni yaḥ tam veda saḥ veda vit
reference: The Supreme Personality of Godhead said: It is said that there is an imperishable banyan tree that has its roots upward and its branches down and whose leaves are the Vedic hymns. One who knows this tree is the knower of the Vedas.
baseline: The Lord Śrī should say that the root above and the branch below should be made ascending and the branches ascending. The leaves of which are left are made to fall down. The Veda should be said to be the Veda.
morphology: The Lord Śrī should say that the root above and the branch below should be made ascending and the leaves of the Āśvātva tree should be removed from the ground.

sanskrit: adhaḥ ca ūrdhvam prasṛtāḥ tasya śākhāḥ guṇa pravṛddhāḥ viṣaya pravālāḥ adhaḥ ca mūlāni anusantatāni karma anubandhīni manuṣya loke
reference: The branches of this tree extend downward and upward, nourished by the three modes of material nature. The twigs are the objects of the senses. This tree also has roots going down, and these are bound to the fruitive actions of human society.
baseline: The branches are spread above and below and the qualities are increased. The subject matter is spread below and following the roots. The people are bound by the deeds.
morphology: The branches are spread above and below. They are of good quality. The subjects are of high order. The roots are found below and above. The people are bound by the rules of conduct.

sanskrit: na rūpam asya iha tathā upalabhyate na antaḥ na ca ādiḥ na ca sampratiṣṭhā aśvattham enam su virūḍha mūlam asaṅga śastreṇa dṛḍhena chittvā tataḥ padam tat parimārgitavyam yasmin gatāḥ na nivartanti bhūyaḥ tam eva ca ādyam puruṣam prapadye yataḥ pravṛttiḥ prasṛtā purāṇi
reference: The real form of this tree cannot be perceived in this world. No one can understand where it ends, where it begins, or where its foundation is. But with determination one must cut down this strongly rooted tree with the weapon of detachment. Thereafter, one must seek that place from which, having gone, one never returns, and there surrender to that Supreme Personality of Godhead from whom everything began and from whom everything has extended since time immemorial.
baseline: The form of the same is neither found in the body nor in the beginning nor the present form. Having pierced it with a strong weapon with the root of the opposite limb the legs should be straightened out and the feet should be made to pass through those places where the legs do not move and the man should reach the first place as the inclinations spread to the cities.
morphology: The form of the same is neither found in the inner part nor in the outer part of the body. Having pierced it with a strong weapon with the root of the opposite part the legs should be straightened out and the feet should be made to pass through those places where the legs do not move and the man should reach the upper part of his body.

sanskrit: niḥ māna mohāḥ jita saṅga doṣāḥ adhyātma nityāḥ vinivṛtta kāmāḥ dvandvaiḥ vimuktāḥ sukha duḥkha saṁjñaiḥ gacchanti amūḍhāḥ padam avyayam tat
reference: Those who are free from false prestige, illusion and false association, who understand the eternal, who are done with material lust, who are freed from the dualities of happiness and distress, and who, unbewildered, know how to surrender unto the Supreme Person attain to that eternal kingdom.
baseline: Those who are free from strife pleasure sorrow and misfortune. Those who do not respect others those who are in a position to gain victory and those who do wrong those living in a state of selfishness those going beyond the limits of their knowledge go beyond the meaning of the word.
morphology: Those who are free from strife pleasure sorrow and misfortune those who are not willing to accept the victory of the enemy those living in the country and those who do not want to live with the enemy and those going to the enemy go to the king.

sanskrit: na tat bhāsayate sūryaḥ na śaśāṅkaḥ na pāvakaḥ yat gatvā na nivartante tat dhāma paramam mama
reference: That supreme abode of Mine is not illumined by the sun or moon, nor by fire or electricity. Those who reach it never return to this material world.
baseline: Neither the sun nor the sāshankha nor the pāvakas that do not go and return to the abode of the Supreme Being.
morphology: Neither the sun nor the samskara nor the pauka go and that which does not return is the supreme abode.

sanskrit: mama eva aṁśaḥ jīva loke jīva bhūtaḥ sanātanaḥ manaḥ ṣaṣṭhāni indriyāṇi prakṛti sthāni karṣati
reference: The living entities in this conditioned world are My eternal fragmental parts. Due to conditioned life, they are struggling very hard with the six senses, which include the mind.
baseline: One who does not have the means of living living earth eternal mind six senses nature and other places would be drawn away by me.
morphology: One who does not have the means of living one who is living and one who has the spirit and the mind and the six senses of nature.

sanskrit: śarīram yat avāpnoti yat ca api utkrāmati īśvaraḥ gṛhītvā etāni saṁyāti vāyuḥ gandhān iva āśayāt
reference: The living entity in the material world carries his different conceptions of life from one body to another, as the air carries aromas. Thus he takes one kind of body and again quits it to take another.
baseline: The body which is found in the ground and which has been destroyed by the Lord is taken away and the air is made to be like a mound.
morphology: The body that is found in the ground and that which is not found in it is taken away by the Lord and the air is made to reach it by the same means as the gandha.

sanskrit: utkrāmantam sthitam vā api bhuñjānam vā guṇa anvitam vimūḍhāḥ na anupaśyanti paśyanti jñāna cakṣuṣaḥ
reference: The foolish cannot understand how a living entity can quit his body, nor can they understand what sort of body he enjoys under the spell of the modes of nature. But one whose eyes are trained in knowledge can see all this.
baseline: The foolish do not see the merits of the object even if it is situated in the direction of the eye. The wise eye does not see it.
morphology: The foolish do not see the merits of the object even if it is situated in the opposite direction. They see the knowledge of the eye.

sanskrit: yatantaḥ yoginaḥ ca enam paśyanti ātmani avasthitam yatantaḥ api akṛta ātmānaḥ na enam paśyanti acetasaḥ
reference: The endeavoring transcendentalists who are situated in self-realization can see all this clearly. But those whose minds are not developed and who are not situated in self-realization cannot see what is taking place, though they may try.
baseline: The yogis see the existence of the self even if they do not perceive it.
morphology: The yogis see the existence of the self even when they are not aware of it.

sanskrit: yat āditya gatam tejaḥ jagat bhāsayate akhilam yat candramasi yat ca agnau tat tejaḥ viddhi māmakam
reference: The splendor of the sun, which dissipates the darkness of this whole world, comes from Me. And the splendor of the moon and the splendor of fire are also from Me.
baseline: The light that has gone into the world and that which is in the fire and the moon is all that is floating in the world. That light is known to me.
morphology: The light that has gone into the world and that which is floating in the earth and the light that is seen in the fire and the moon.

sanskrit: gām āviśya ca bhūtāni dhārayāmi aham ojasā puṣṇāmi ca auṣadhīḥ sarvāḥ somaḥ bhūtvā rasa ātmakaḥ
reference: I enter into each planet, and by My energy they stay in orbit. I become the moon and thereby supply the juice of life to all vegetables.
baseline: Having seen the gaṇa the vaṇī and the bhūtas one should worship with vigour and all the herbs. One becomes sāma and one becomes rasa and self.
morphology: Having seen the gaṇas one should hold the spirits one who consumes all the herbs and medicines with vigour and one who becomes sāma rasa and atmana.

sanskrit: aham vaiśvānaraḥ bhūtvā prāṇinām deham āśritaḥ prāṇa apāna samāyuktaḥ pacāmi annam catuḥ vidham
reference: I am the fire of digestion in the bodies of all living entities, and I join with the air of life, outgoing and incoming, to digest the four kinds of foodstuff.
baseline: Having become a universal being one who is dependent on the body of the living beings one should eat food in four different ways.
morphology: Having become the master of the universe I eat food in four different ways.

sanskrit: sarvasya ca aham hṛdi sanniviṣṭaḥ mattaḥ smṛtiḥ jñānam apohanam ca vedaiḥ ca sarvaiḥ aham eva vedyaḥ vedānta kṛt veda vit eva ca aham
reference: I am seated in everyone’s heart, and from Me come remembrance, knowledge and forgetfulness. By all the Vedas, I am to be known. Indeed, I am the compiler of Vedānta, and I am the knower of the Vedas.
baseline: I am the heart of all and the mind is present in the heart. I am also the knowledge the knowledge and the subjugation of the Vedas and the Vedic scriptures.
morphology: I am the heart of everything and the mind the memory the knowledge and the knowledge of the Vedas and all the things mentioned in the Veda.

sanskrit: dvau imau puruṣau loke kṣaraḥ ca akṣaraḥ eva ca kṣaraḥ sarvāṇi bhūtāni kūṭa sthaḥ akṣaraḥ ucyate
reference: There are two classes of beings, the fallible and the infallible. In the material world every living entity is fallible, and in the spiritual world every living entity is called infallible.
baseline: A letter that contains all the ghosts is said to be a letter with two letters āma purus lokā kāra alkra and alkrā.
morphology: The letters are said to be the same as the letters the two men the people and the characters all the ghosts and the letters are placed in the circle.

sanskrit: uttamaḥ puruṣaḥ tu anyaḥ parama ātmā iti udāhṛtaḥ yaḥ loka trayam āviśya bibharti avyayaḥ īśvaraḥ
reference: Besides these two, there is the greatest living personality, the Supreme Soul, the imperishable Lord Himself, who has entered the three worlds and is maintaining them.
baseline: One who is said to be a good man and another to be the supreme soul is saidto be a man who is manifest in three forms and who confers on him the unmanifest God.
morphology: The best man is another supreme soul. The man who has three manifestations is said to be the supreme god.

sanskrit: yasmāt kṣaram atītaḥ aham akṣarāt api ca uttamaḥ ataḥ asmi loke vede ca prathitaḥ puruṣa uttamaḥ
reference: Because I am transcendental, beyond both the fallible and the infallible, and because I am the greatest, I am celebrated both in the world and in the Vedas as that Supreme Person.
baseline: Since I am better than the letters the person who has been introduced into the Vedas would be better.
morphology: Since I am better than the letters the man is better in the Vedas and the people.

sanskrit: yaḥ mām evam asammūḍhaḥ jānāti puruṣa uttamam saḥ sarva vit bhajati mām sarva bhāvena bhārata
reference: Whoever knows Me as the Supreme Personality of Godhead, without doubting, is the knower of everything. He therefore engages himself in full devotional service to Me, O son of Bharata.
baseline: One who knows me as such and does not know me well as a man is good. He worships me with all his heart.
morphology: One who knows me as such and knows me well as a man is good. He worships me with all devotion.

sanskrit: iti guhya tamam śāstram idam uktam mayā anagha etat buddhvā buddhi mān syāt kṛta kṛtyaḥ ca bhārata
reference: This is the most confidential part of the Vedic scriptures, O sinless one, and it is disclosed now by Me. Whoever understands this will become wise, and his endeavors will know perfection.
baseline: Having said this the scripture should be said to be false. I should say this to the intellect. If I have done it with the intellect it should be done in India.
morphology: Having said this I should say that the scriptures should be made to be known to the intellect.

sanskrit: śrī bhagavān uvāca abhayam sattva saṁśuddhiḥ jñāna yoga vyavasthitiḥ dānam damaḥ ca yajñaḥ ca svādhyāyaḥ tapaḥ ārjavam ahiṁsā satyam akrodhaḥ tyāgaḥ śāntiḥ apaiśunam dayā bhūteṣu aloluptvam mārdavam hrīḥ acāpalam tejaḥ kṣamā dhṛtiḥ śaucam adrohaḥ na ati mānitā bhavanti sampadam daivīm abhijātasya bhārata
reference: The Supreme Personality of Godhead said: Fearlessness; purification of one’s existence; cultivation of spiritual knowledge; charity; self-control; performance of sacrifice; study of the Vedas; austerity; simplicity; nonviolence; truthfulness; freedom from anger; renunciation; tranquillity; aversion to faultfinding; compassion for all living entities; freedom from covetousness; gentleness; modesty; steady determination; vigor; forgiveness; fortitude; cleanliness; and freedom from envy and from the passion for honor – these transcendental qualities, O son of Bharata, belong to godly men endowed with divine nature.
baseline: O Srivaṇa the Supreme Lord the supreme being the pure one the knowledge the yogic arrangement the gift the strength the sacrifice the practice of self-sacrifice the attainment of penance the realization of truth the renunciation of unfulfilled desires peace the absence of evil spirits the death of evil beings the forgiveness of evil deeds the cleansing of the enemy the invulnerability of wealth the power of the divine the superior and the kingdom of India are not overrated.
morphology: O lord one who invents srī bhāgavāṇa sattva sākhuṣa purification knowledge yogic arrangement charity patience sacrifice self-sacrifice penance ahimsa truth renunciation peace unbrokenness mercy oblation oblivion death oblations to demons the abyssal of the gods forgiveness of the illusion of the spirit forgiving of the evil one defilement treachery treason wealth

sanskrit: dambhaḥ darpaḥ abhimānaḥ ca krodhaḥ pāruṣyam eva ca ajñānam ca abhijātasya pārtha sampadam āsurīm
reference: Pride, arrogance, conceit, anger, harshness and ignorance – these qualities belong to those of demoniac nature, O son of Pṛthā.
baseline: The arrogance pride anger ignorance and ignorance are the prerogative of the noble.
morphology: The arrogance pride anger ignorance ignorance etc. are the virtues of the noble and the wealth of the demons.

sanskrit: daivī sampat vimokṣāya nibandhāya āsurī matā mā śucaḥ sampadam daivīm abhijātaḥ asi pāṇḍava
reference: The transcendental qualities are conducive to liberation, whereas the demoniac qualities make for bondage. Do not worry, O son of Pāṇḍu, for you are born with the divine qualities.
baseline: The Pandavas are the nobles who possess the wealth of the gods without having to be worshipped by a demon to redeem them.
morphology: The Pandava lord should not be considered as a demigod for the purpose of redeeming the divine property. He should be known as the lord of the divine wealth.

sanskrit: dvau bhūta sargau loke asmin daivaḥ āsuraḥ eva ca daivaḥ vistaraśaḥ proktaḥ āsuram pārtha me śṛṇu
reference: O son of Pṛthā, in this world there are two kinds of created beings. One is called divine and the other demoniac. I have already explained to you at length the divine qualities. Now hear from Me of the demoniac.
baseline: One who has two ghosts one who is the lord of the universe and the other who is a demigod and a demi-god is known to be a great demon.
morphology: One who has two ghosts one who is a god and one who has a demigod is known to be a god.

sanskrit: pravṛttim ca nivṛttim ca janāḥ na viduḥ āsurāḥ na śaucam na api ca ācāraḥ na satyam teṣu vidyate
reference: Those who are demoniac do not know what is to be done and what is not to be done. Neither cleanliness nor proper behavior nor truth is found in them.
baseline: Neither the attitude nor the retirement of the people nor the demons nor defilement nor conduct are true in them.
morphology: There is neither inclination nor retirement among the people nor demons nor defilement nor conduct and truth among them.

sanskrit: asatyam apratiṣṭham te jagat āhuḥ anīśvaram aparaspara sambhūtam kim anyat kāma haitukam
reference: They say that this world is unreal, with no foundation, no God in control. They say it is produced of sex desire and has no cause other than lust.
baseline: If the falsehood is not established whether the unbelieving god of the world exists in each other or not whether it is a matter of desire or not.
morphology: If they are false they are not true. They are the world unbelieving gods and other things.

sanskrit: etām dṛṣṭim avaṣṭabhya naṣṭa ātmānaḥ alpa buddhayaḥ prabhavanti ugra karmāṇaḥ kṣayāya jagataḥ ahitāḥ
reference: Following such conclusions, the demoniac, who are lost to themselves and who have no intelligence, engage in unbeneficial, horrible works meant to destroy the world.
baseline: Having lost sight of these things the soul would get a little wisdom. The fiery deeds would get destroyed and the world would be destroyed.
morphology: Having lost sight of these things the spirit is destroyed and given little intelligence. The fiery deeds are destroyed and the world is destroyed.

sanskrit: kāmam āśritya duṣpūram dambha māna mada anvitāḥ mohāt gṛhītvā asat grāhān pravartante aśuci vratāḥ
reference: Taking shelter of insatiable lust and absorbed in the conceit of pride and false prestige, the demoniac, thus illusioned, are always sworn to unclean work, attracted by the impermanent.
baseline: Having relied on lust one should hold on to the illusion. One should hold onto the illusory vow and take away the illusions.
morphology: Having relied on lust one should hold on to the illusion. One should hold onto the illusory vow. One who takes away the illusions and takes them away would go on to do evil deeds.

sanskrit: cintām aparimeyām ca pralaya antām upāśritāḥ kāma upabhoga paramāḥ etāvat iti niścitāḥ āśā pāśa śataiḥ baddhāḥ kāma krodha parāyaṇāḥ īhante kāma bhoga artham anyāyena artha sañcayān
reference: They believe that to gratify the senses is the prime necessity of human civilization. Thus until the end of life their anxiety is immeasurable. Bound by a network of hundreds of thousands of desires and absorbed in lust and anger, they secure money by illegal means for sense gratification.
baseline: Having thought of the unspeakable and the immaterial abiding in the abyss of the end one should seek pleasure and enjoyment. One would be bound by the promise of the past and bound by anger and hatred. One should seek enjoyment and gain wealth by doing wrong.
morphology: The sense of desire desire want want and want are bound together in the form of desire and desire. One who is determined to enjoy these things would be bound by the forces of hope anger anger and fear.

sanskrit: idam adya mayā labdham imam prāpsye manaḥ ratham idam asti idam api me bhaviṣyati punaḥ dhanam asau mayā hataḥ śatruḥ haniṣye ca aparān api īśvaraḥ aham aham bhogī siddhaḥ aham bala vān sukhī āḍhyaḥ abhijana vān asmi kaḥ anyaḥ asti sadṛśaḥ mayā yakṣye dāsyāmi modiṣye iti ajñāna vimohitāḥ
reference: The demoniac person thinks: “So much wealth do I have today, and I will gain more according to my schemes. So much is mine now, and it will increase in the future, more and more. He is my enemy, and I have killed him, and my other enemies will also be killed. I am the lord of everything. I am the enjoyer. I am perfect, powerful and happy. I am the richest man, surrounded by aristocratic relatives. There is none so powerful and happy as I am. I shall perform sacrifices, I shall give some charity, and thus I shall rejoice.” In this way, such persons are deluded by ignorance.
baseline: This is the chariot of the mind that I got today and this is the one that I get. Again if I kill the enemy and harm others God will kill me. I am satisfied I am strong happy good obedient who else is there. I will give it to the enemy.
morphology: This is the chariot of the mind that I have got today and this is the one that I will get again. Again if I kill the enemy and harm others then God should be pleased with me. I should become strong happy obedient proud and present to others. Just as if I give to the goddess.

sanskrit: aneka citta vibhrāntāḥ moha jāla samāvṛtāḥ prasaktāḥ kāma bhogeṣu patanti narake aśucau
reference: Thus perplexed by various anxieties and bound by a network of illusions, they become too strongly attached to sense enjoyment and fall down into hell.
baseline: Many of them who are deluded by the illusion of the mind and who are entangled in a web of temptations fall into the abode of lusts and enjoyments.
morphology: Many of them who are deluded by the illusion of the mind and entangled in the web of envy fall into the illusions of lust and uncleanness.

sanskrit: ātma sambhāvitāḥ stabdhāḥ dhana māna mada anvitāḥ yajante nāma yajñaiḥ te dambhena avidhi pūrvakam
reference: Self-complacent and always impudent, deluded by wealth and false prestige, they sometimes proudly perform sacrifices in name only, without following any rules or regulations.
baseline: Those who are self-sufficient and have been given the boon of wealth and wine should be worshipped with the sacrifice of the names. They should not be arrogant.
morphology: They should be worshipped with the praise of the self the glory of wealth the honour of wine the renunciation of names the sacrifice of names and the pretence of the past.

sanskrit: ahaṅkāram balam darpam kāmam krodham ca saṁśritāḥ mām ātma para deheṣu pradviṣantaḥ abhyasūyakāḥ
reference: Bewildered by false ego, strength, pride, lust and anger, the demons become envious of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is situated in their own bodies and in the bodies of others, and blaspheme against the real religion.
baseline: The ego strength glory lust anger etc. should be worshipped in the spirit and other parts of the body.
morphology: The ego strength glory lust anger etc. should be worshipped. Those who teach me should spread the spirit beyond the body.

sanskrit: tān aham dviṣataḥ krūrān saṁsāreṣu nara adhamān kṣipāmi ajasram aśubhān āsurīṣu eva yoniṣu
reference: Those who are envious and mischievous, who are the lowest among men, I perpetually cast into the ocean of material existence, into various demoniac species of life.
baseline: I shall make them two hundred and four times as evil as the evil ones. I shall cast out the evil men and the bad ones in the wombs of the demons.
morphology: I shall make them two hundred times as many as the savages men and the poor as possible. Many evil things are cast into the wombs of the demons.

sanskrit: āsurīm yonim āpannāḥ mūḍhāḥ janmani janmani mām aprāpya eva kaunteya tataḥ yānti adhamām gatim
reference: Attaining repeated birth amongst the species of demoniac life, O son of Kuntī, such persons can never approach Me. Gradually they sink down to the most abominable type of existence.
baseline: The demons the vaginas the fools the borns and those born without me are said to be evil.
morphology: The demons the vagabonds the foolish people the people who give birth to me without knowing it should be called poor.

sanskrit: tri vidham narakasya idam dvāram nāśanam ātmanaḥ kāmaḥ krodhaḥ tathā lobhaḥ tasmāt etat trayam tyajet
reference: There are three gates leading to this hell – lust, anger and greed. Every sane man should give these up, for they lead to the degradation of the soul.
baseline: This gate of hell is destroyed in three ways. The desire of the self is anger and greed. One gets rid of these three things.
morphology: This gate of hell is destroyed in three ways. The desire of the self is anger and greed. This is the third way.

sanskrit: etaiḥ vimuktaḥ kaunteya tamaḥ dvāraiḥ tribhiḥ naraḥ ācarati ātmanaḥ śreyaḥ tataḥ yāti parām gatim
reference: The man who has escaped these three gates of hell, O son of Kuntī, performs acts conducive to self-realization and thus gradually attains the supreme destination.
baseline: Having liberated himself from these things the man who performs the ritual of tāma with the three gates should then proceed to the other side.
morphology: Having liberated himself from these things the man who performs the ritual with the three gates should then proceed to the other direction.

sanskrit: yaḥ śāstra vidhim utsṛjya vartate kāma kārataḥ na saḥ siddhim avāpnoti na sukham na parām gatim
reference: He who discards scriptural injunctions and acts according to his own whims attains neither perfection, nor happiness, nor the supreme destination.
baseline: One who expels the scriptures and practices the law and does not get perfection or happiness or other progress.
morphology: One who expands the scriptures and practices the law and does not get perfection happiness and other things will not be achieved.

sanskrit: arjunaḥ uvāca ye śāstra vidhim utsṛjya yajante śraddhayā anvitāḥ teṣām niṣṭhā tu kā kṛṣṇa sattvam āho rajaḥ tamaḥ
reference: Arjuna inquired: O Kṛṣṇa, what is the situation of those who do not follow the principles of scripture but worship according to their own imagination? Are they in goodness, in passion or in ignorance?
baseline: Arjuna said that the devotion of those who have been worshipped with faith after having revealed the scriptures and the rules should be called kṛṣṇa sattva or rajā.
morphology: Arjuna said that those who have been given the scriptures and the method of worship and are bound by faith should be trusted.

sanskrit: śrī bhagavān uvāca tri vidhā bhavati śraddhā dehinām sā sva bhāva jā sāttvikī rājasī ca eva tāmasī ca iti tām śṛṇu
reference: The Supreme Personality of Godhead said: According to the modes of nature acquired by the embodied soul, one’s faith can be of three kinds – in goodness, in passion or in ignorance. Now hear about this.
baseline: One should know that ŚrīBhāgavāṇa is the three modes of devotion. He should know the nature of the body and his own feelings. He is known as Satvika Rajyāṣa Tamasī.
morphology: One should know that the lord Śrī is of three kinds. One should have faith in the body and one should know his own nature. One who is king sātvīka tāmasī etc...

sanskrit: sattva anurūpā sarvasya śraddhā bhavati bhārata śraddhā mayaḥ ayam puruṣaḥ yaḥ yat śraddhaḥ saḥ eva saḥ
reference: O son of Bharata, according to one’s existence under the various modes of nature, one evolves a particular kind of faith. The living being is said to be of a particular faith according to the modes he has acquired.
baseline: The belief of all is similar to that of the sātva. The man who has faith in me is called Bharata.
morphology: The belief of all is similar to the belief of the sattva. The man who has faith in me is known as Bharata.

sanskrit: yajante sāttvikāḥ devān yakṣa rakṣāṁsi rājasāḥ pretān bhūta gaṇān ca anye yajante tāmasāḥ janāḥ
reference: Men in the mode of goodness worship the demigods; those in the mode of passion worship the demons; and those in the mode of ignorance worship ghosts and spirits.
baseline: The king should protect the gods gods spirits ghosts ganas and other beings.
morphology: The king should protect the gods and goddesses from evil spirits and other spirits and demons.

sanskrit: aśāstra vihitam ghoram tapyante ye tapaḥ janāḥ dambha ahaṅkāra saṁyuktāḥ kāma rāga bala anvitāḥ karṣayantaḥ śarīra stham bhūta grāmam acetasaḥ mām ca eva antaḥ śarīra stham tān viddhi āsura niścayān
