reference: Those who undergo severe austerities and penances not recommended in the scriptures, performing them out of pride and egoism, who are impelled by lust and attachment, who are foolish and who torture the material elements of the body as well as the Supersoul dwelling within, are to be known as demons.
baseline: Those who perform the penance prescribed by the priest who are arrogant arrogant and possess the power of anger pull the body and the village of the ghost and the body into the unconscious. Those who do not know the nature of the body are determined by the god.
morphology: Those who practice the aṣāstra prescribed by the priest those who are arrogant arrogant and possess the power of anger and desire and pull away the body the village the ghost the subconscious the body and me in the body are determined by the god.

sanskrit: āhāraḥ tu api sarvasya tri vidhaḥ bhavati priyaḥ yajñaḥ tapaḥ tathā dānam teṣām bhedam imam śṛṇu
reference: Even the food each person prefers is of three kinds, according to the three modes of material nature. The same is true of sacrifices, austerities and charity. Now hear of the distinctions between them.
baseline: The three types of food are the beloved sacrifices the penance the charity and the difference between them.
morphology: The three types of food are the beloved sacrifices the penance the gift and the difference between them.

sanskrit: āyuḥ sattva bala ārogya sukha prīti vivardhanāḥ rasyāḥ snigdhāḥ sthirāḥ hṛdyāḥ āhārāḥ sāttvika priyāḥ
reference: Foods dear to those in the mode of goodness increase the duration of life, purify one’s existence and give strength, health, happiness and satisfaction. Such foods are juicy, fatty, wholesome, and pleasing to the heart.
baseline: One who is endowed with the virtues of life health happiness love prosperity longevity good habits good health good fortune good cheerfulness good spirits good heart good food and good health.
morphology: One who is endowed with life strength health happiness love prosperity prosperity etc. and who is steadfast in the heart food sattvic and affectionate is blessed with good health.

sanskrit: kaṭu amla lavaṇa ati uṣṇa tīkṣṇa rūkṣa vidāhinaḥ āhārāḥ rājasasya iṣṭāḥ duḥkha śoka āmaya pradāḥ
reference: Foods that are too bitter, too sour, salty, hot, pungent, dry and burning are dear to those in the mode of passion. Such foods cause distress, misery and disease.
baseline: The king should be served with bitter salt acid salt very hot sharp bitter bitter and bitter food.
morphology: The king should be given bitter salt acid salt very hot sharp bitter bitter and bitter food.

sanskrit: yāta yāmam gata rasam pūti paryuṣitam ca yat ucchiṣṭam api ca amedhyam bhojanam tāmasa priyam
reference: Food prepared more than three hours before being eaten, food that is tasteless, decomposed and putrid, and food consisting of remnants and untouchable things is dear to those in the mode of darkness.
baseline: One who consumes the juice after having gone to the place of his journey and having eaten the food after having been removed from the place is fond of staying.
morphology: One who consumes the juice after having gone to the place of his journey and has not eaten the food should be removed from the place. One who does not eat food should stay here.

sanskrit: aphala ākāṅkṣibhiḥ yajñaḥ vidhi diṣṭaḥ yaḥ ijyate yaṣṭavyam eva iti manaḥ samādhāya saḥ sāttvikaḥ
reference: Of sacrifices, the sacrifice performed according to the directions of scripture, as a matter of duty, by those who desire no reward, is of the nature of goodness.
baseline: One who performs the ritual of sacrifice with unfathomable desires and who observes that the sacrifice is to be performed should bury his mind. He is virtuous.
morphology: One who performs the ritual of sacrifice with unfathomable desires and who observes that the mind is to be destroyed should be buried.

sanskrit: abhisandhāya tu phalam dambha artham api ca eva yat ijyate bharata śreṣṭha tam yajñam viddhi rājasam
reference: But the sacrifice performed for some material benefit, or for the sake of pride, O chief of the Bhāratas, you should know to be in the mode of passion.
baseline: The meaning of the pretence is that the fruit is arrogant and the sacrifice made by the king is said to be superior to that of Bharata.
morphology: The meaning of the word bhārāta means arrogance and that which is said to be superior to bharāta should be worshipped and worshipped.

sanskrit: vidhi hīnam asṛṣṭa annam mantra hīnam adakṣiṇam śraddhā virahitam yajñam tāmasam paricakṣate
reference: Any sacrifice performed without regard for the directions of scripture, without distribution of prasādam [spiritual food], without chanting of Vedic hymns and remunerations to the priests, and without faith is considered to be in the mode of ignorance.
baseline: One who does not follow the rules would be known as poor. He would not eat food. He should not chant a mantra. One who is devoid of devotion would not perform a sacrifice.
morphology: One who does not know the meaning of the sacrifice would be known to him as poor. Poor food poor mantra poor conduct devoid of faith and without devotion.

sanskrit: deva dvija guru prājña pūjanam śaucam ārjavam brahmacaryam ahiṁsā ca śārīram tapaḥ ucyate
reference: Austerity of the body consists in worship of the Supreme Lord, the brāhmaṇas, the spiritual master, and superiors like the father and mother, and in cleanliness, simplicity, celibacy and nonviolence.
baseline: The worship of the god the twījā guru the learned man the practice of defecation celibacy nonviolence and penance of the body is called penance.
morphology: The worship of the god the dvījī guru the learned man the practice of defecation celibacy brahmacarya nonviolence penance of the body etc. is said to be the highest form of worship.

sanskrit: anudvega karam vākyam satyam priya hitam ca yat svādhyāya abhyasanam ca eva vāk mayam tapaḥ ucyate
reference: Austerity of speech consists in speaking words that are truthful, pleasing, beneficial, and not agitating to others, and also in regularly reciting Vedic literature.
baseline: A penance is said to be a statement that is true well liked good and self taught.
morphology: The word anudvāga kārām is true the word beloved is good and the same is said for the practice and practice of self.

sanskrit: manaḥ prasādaḥ saumyatvam maunam ātma vinigrahaḥ bhāva saṁśuddhiḥ iti etat tapaḥ mānasam ucyate
reference: And satisfaction, simplicity, gravity, self-control and purification of one’s existence are the austerities of the mind.
baseline: This penance is called manasa. It is said to be benign quiet selfless free from grace purifying and purifying.
morphology: This penance is called manasa. It is said to be benign quiet selfless meritorious and pure.

sanskrit: śraddhayā parayā taptam tapaḥ tat tri vidham naraiḥ aphala ākāṅkṣibhiḥ yuktaiḥ sāttvikam paricakṣate
reference: This threefold austerity, performed with transcendental faith by men not expecting material benefits but engaged only for the sake of the Supreme, is called austerity in goodness.
baseline: One who has warmed the ground with devotion and then warmed it in three different ways with unyielding desires would get acquainted with the virtues.
morphology: One who has warmed the ground with devotion and has three kinds of desires is known to be sattvic.

sanskrit: sat kāra māna pūjā artham tapaḥ dambhena ca eva yat kriyate tat iha proktam rājasam calam adhruvam
reference: Penance performed out of pride and for the sake of gaining respect, honor and worship is said to be in the mode of passion. It is neither stable nor permanent.
baseline: The meaning of the worship of the king is to do with austerity and arrogance. It is said to be the kings conduct and unbroken.
morphology: The meaning of the worship of the king is to do with austerity and arrogance. It is said to be the conduct of kings.

sanskrit: yat tu prati upakāra artham phalam uddiśya vā punaḥ dīyate ca parikliṣṭam tat dānam rājasam smṛtam
reference: But charity performed with the expectation of some return, or with a desire for fruitive results, or in a grudging mood is said to be charity in the mode of passion.
baseline: The king should remember the gift which would be difficult for him if it was given to him or to him again.
morphology: The king should remember the gift which would be given to you in return for the benefit or the fruits.

sanskrit: adeśa kāle yat dānam apātrebhyaḥ ca dīyate asat kṛtam avajñātam tat tāmasam udāhṛtam
reference: And charity performed at an impure place, at an improper time, to unworthy persons, or without proper attention and respect is said to be in the mode of ignorance.
baseline: The gift given to the unbelievers at the prescribed time is said to be a violation of the law.
morphology: The gift given to the unbelievers at the time of the decree is said to have been done in the absence of the order.

sanskrit: oṁ tat sat iti nirdeśaḥ brahmaṇaḥ tri vidhaḥ smṛtaḥ brāhmaṇāḥ tena vedāḥ ca yajñāḥ ca vihitāḥ purā
reference: From the beginning of creation, the three words oṁ tat sat were used to indicate the Supreme Absolute Truth. These three symbolic representations were used by brāhmaṇas while chanting the hymns of the Vedas and during sacrifices for the satisfaction of the Supreme.
baseline: The Brahmanas are said to have memorized three kinds of things. The Brahmins are thus instructed to perform the Vedas and the sacrifices.
morphology: The Brahmanas are said to have memorized the three forms of oblation. The Brahmans are thus instructed to perform the Vedas and sacrifices.

sanskrit: tasmāt oṁ iti udāhṛtya yajña dāna tapaḥ kriyāḥ pravartante vidhāna uktāḥ satatam brahma vādinām
reference: Therefore, transcendentalists undertaking performances of sacrifice, charity and penance in accordance with scriptural regulations begin always with oṁ, to attain the Supreme.
baseline: The practice of offering sacrifices giving sacrifices doing penance doing deeds etc. is said to be continuous for the Brahmanical cause.
morphology: The practice of offering sacrifices giving sacrifices doing penance etc. is said to be continuous.

sanskrit: tat iti anabhisandhāya phalam yajña tapaḥ kriyāḥ dāna kriyāḥ ca vividhāḥ kriyante mokṣa kāṅkṣibhiḥ
reference: Without desiring fruitive results, one should perform various kinds of sacrifice, penance and charity with the word tat. The purpose of such transcendental activities is to get free from material entanglement.
baseline: That is the undefined fruit. Sacrifices penance charity charity etc. are done in different ways by those desirous of liberation.
morphology: That is the undeniable result. Sacrifices penance charity charity etc. are done in different ways by the devotees seeking salvation.

sanskrit: sat bhāve sādhu bhāve ca sat iti etat prayujyate praśaste karmaṇi tathā sat śabdaḥ pārtha yujyate yajñe tapasi dāne ca sthitiḥ sat iti ca ucyate karma ca eva tat arthīyam sat iti eva abhidhīyate
reference: The Absolute Truth is the objective of devotional sacrifice, and it is indicated by the word sat. The performer of such sacrifice is also called sat, as are all works of sacrifice, penance and charity which, true to the absolute nature, are performed to please the Supreme Person, O son of Pṛthā.
baseline: It is said to be true true good good and true. The words pārtha and pātha are used in the sacrifice penance charity and standing are true. It is also known to be the true meaning of action.
morphology: It is said to be true true good good and true. It is used to describe actions done by the devotee. The word pārtha is used in the sacrifice penance charity and standing. It says that action is the meaning of action.

sanskrit: aśraddhayā hutam dattam tapaḥ taptam kṛtam ca yat asat iti ucyate pārtha na ca tat pretya na u iha
reference: Anything done as sacrifice, charity or penance without faith in the Supreme, O son of Pṛthā, is impermanent. It is called asat and is useless both in this life and the next.
baseline: One who has given a sacrifice without having done so would be called a penance. One who does not do so would not get it.
morphology: One who has given a penance after having not obeyed the order should say that it was done without doing so. One should not say that he would not accept it.

sanskrit: arjunaḥ uvāca sannyāsasya mahā bāho tattvam icchāmi veditum tyāgasya ca hṛṣīkeśa pṛthak keśi niṣūdana
reference: Arjuna said: O mighty-armed one, I wish to understand the purpose of renunciation [tyāga] and of the renounced order of life [sannyāsa], O killer of the Keśī demon, master of the senses.
baseline: Arjuna said that he would like to have the great baho principle of asceticism on the altar and sacrifice on the head of the elephant and separate the hair from the head.
morphology: Arjuna said that he would like to have the great bāhū principle of renunciation and sacrifice on the altar.

sanskrit: śrī bhagavān uvāca kāmyānām karmaṇām nyāsam sannyāsam kavayaḥ viduḥ sarva karma phala tyāgam prāhuḥ tyāgam vicakṣaṇāḥ
reference: The Supreme Personality of Godhead said: The giving up of activities that are based on material desire is what great learned men call the renounced order of life [sannyāsa]. And giving up the results of all activities is what the wise call renunciation [tyāga].
baseline: The Lord Śrī describes the duties of the lord as trust renunciation and renunciation. All actions are performed by the poet. Fruits and sacrifices are offered by the lord. Sacrifices are offered to the disciples.
morphology: O lord of the universe one who trusts in the desires deeds sāyānasya kavīda renounces all deeds fruits sacrifices sacrifices etc. should be worshipped.

sanskrit: tyājyam doṣa vat iti eke karma prāhuḥ manīṣiṇaḥ yajña dāna tapaḥ karma na tyājyam iti ca apare
reference: Some learned men declare that all kinds of fruitive activities should be given up as faulty, yet other sages maintain that acts of sacrifice, charity and penance should never be abandoned.
baseline: One who does the same deed as the waste the wrong thing one who gives sacrifices and does penance should say that the deed is not a waste.
morphology: One who performs the same action would be called waste evil and one who gives sacrifices would be known as austerity. One who does not do the same would not be a waste.

sanskrit: niścayam śṛṇu me tatra tyāge bharata sat tama tyāgaḥ hi puruṣa vyāghra tri vidhaḥ samprakīrtitaḥ
reference: O best of the Bhāratas, now hear My judgment about renunciation. O tiger among men, renunciation is declared in the scriptures to be of three kinds.
baseline: If one knows for sure that he would give up his life there he should give up the three forms of the male tiger.
morphology: If I know for sure that there is a sacrifice in the form of Bharata then the sacrifice should be made in three ways.

sanskrit: yajña dāna tapaḥ karma na tyājyam kāryam eva tat yajñaḥ dānam tapaḥ ca eva pāvanāni manīṣiṇām
reference: Acts of sacrifice, charity and penance are not to be given up; they must be performed. Indeed, sacrifice, charity and penance purify even the great souls.
baseline: Sacrifice giving doing penance doing nothing is wasteful doing that offering giving etc. are sacred for the virtuous.
morphology: The sacrifice offering doing of penance doing nothing is a waste doing only that giving of charity doing penance are sacred and virtuous.

sanskrit: etāni api tu karmāṇi saṅgam tyaktvā phalāni ca kartavyāni iti me pārtha niścitam matam uttamam
reference: All these activities should be performed without attachment or any expectation of result. They should be performed as a matter of duty, O son of Pṛthā. That is My final opinion.
baseline: Having said this it is better to leave the association of actions and give fruits.
morphology: Having said this it is better to leave the association of the deeds and give fruits.

sanskrit: niyatasya tu sannyāsaḥ karmaṇaḥ na upapadyate mohāt tasya parityāgaḥ tāmasaḥ parikīrtitaḥ
reference: Prescribed duties should never be renounced. If one gives up his prescribed duties because of illusion, such renunciation is said to be in the mode of ignorance.
baseline: The renunciation of a sannyasa for the purpose of doing the prescribed duties would not be acceptable. The renouncement of that sannyāsa for the sake of his enmity would be known to Tamasa.
morphology: The renunciation of a sannyasa for the purpose of doing the prescribed duties should not be accepted. The renunciations made by him are known to Tamasa.

sanskrit: duḥkham iti eva yat karma kāya kleśa bhayāt tyajet saḥ kṛtvā rājasam tyāgam na eva tyāga phalam labhet
reference: Anyone who gives up prescribed duties as troublesome or out of fear of bodily discomfort is said to have renounced in the mode of passion. Such action never leads to the elevation of renunciation.
baseline: One who abandons a deed due to fear of suffering would not get the result of renunciation.
morphology: One who abandons a deed which is a misfortune or a fearful one would not get the result of renouncing the throne.

sanskrit: kāryam iti eva yat karma niyatam kriyate arjuna saṅgam tyaktvā phalam ca eva saḥ tyāgaḥ sāttvikaḥ mataḥ
reference: O Arjuna, when one performs his prescribed duty only because it ought to be done, and renounces all material association and all attachment to the fruit, his renunciation is said to be in the mode of goodness.
baseline: The same is the case with the action which is determined by Arjuna. The sacrifice is the result of leaving the company. That is the sattvic belief.
morphology: One who gives up the association of Arjuna and gets the fruits of the same is said to be a renunciation.

sanskrit: na dveṣṭi akuśalam karma kuśale na anuṣajjate tyāgī sattva samāviṣṭaḥ medhāvī chinna saṁśayaḥ
reference: The intelligent renouncer situated in the mode of goodness, neither hateful of inauspicious work nor attached to auspicious work, has no doubts about work.
baseline: One who does not do two things without skill does not perform any work with skill and does not give up the goodness of the self. One who is wise will be destroyed.
morphology: One who does not do evil or illiterate does not perform good deeds and does not give up goodness does good deeds and is not able to do good deeds.

sanskrit: na hi deha bhṛtā śakyam tyaktum karmāṇi aśeṣataḥ yaḥ tu karma phala tyāgī saḥ tyāgī iti abhidhīyate
reference: It is indeed impossible for an embodied being to give up all activities. But he who renounces the fruits of action is called one who has truly renounced.
baseline: One who does not give up his deeds to leave the body undefiled is known as a renunciator.
morphology: He who does not give up his deeds and leaves the body unfulfilled is known as a renunciator.

sanskrit: aniṣṭam iṣṭam miśram ca tri vidham karmaṇaḥ phalam bhavati atyāginām pretya na tu sannyāsinām kvacit
reference: For one who is not renounced, the threefold fruits of action – desirable, undesirable and mixed – accrue after death. But those who are in the renounced order of life have no such result to suffer or enjoy.
baseline: The three kinds of actions are evil desirable and mixed. One would get the result by offering the same to the sages and not by the ascetic.
morphology: The three kinds of actions are good and mixed. One would get the result by doing these things without having to worship the sāṇīs.

sanskrit: pañca etāni mahā bāho kāraṇāni nibodha me sāṅkhye kṛta ante proktāni siddhaye sarva karmaṇām
reference: O mighty-armed Arjuna, according to the Vedānta there are five causes for the accomplishment of all action. Now learn of these from Me.
baseline: The five great causes of death are known to me. Having done these things in numbers one should know all the causes for the accomplishment of the deeds.
morphology: The five great causes of death should be explained in the following lines. At the end of the calculation all the actions should be completed.

sanskrit: adhiṣṭhānam tathā kartā karaṇam ca pṛthak vidham vividhāḥ ca pṛthak ceṣṭāḥ daivam ca eva atra pañcamam
reference: The place of action [the body], the performer, the various senses, the many different kinds of endeavor, and ultimately the Supersoul – these are the five factors of action.
baseline: The fifth element here is the seat of the lord the doer and the other forms of action. Different forms of actions are performed in different ways. The five elements are the gods.
morphology: The fifth element here is the adhyastha and the kārtaka. The different forms of action are different. Different forms of actions are different and the divine is different.

sanskrit: śarīra vāk manobhiḥ yat karma prārabhate naraḥ nyāyyam vā viparītam vā pañca ete tasya hetavaḥ
reference: Whatever right or wrong action a man performs by body, mind or speech is caused by these five factors.
baseline: One who commences his work by speaking of the body the mind the man is justified by the five things.
morphology: One who commences his work by speaking the body the mind the man the five things are just or wrong.

sanskrit: tatra evam sati kartāram ātmānam kevalam tu yaḥ paśyati akṛta buddhitvāt na saḥ paśyati durmatiḥ
reference: Therefore one who thinks himself the only doer, not considering the five factors, is certainly not very intelligent and cannot see things as they are.
baseline: One who does so only when he sees the soul and does not understand it. One who sees it without understanding is evil.
morphology: One who does not see the spirit only when he has done so and does not understand it will see evil.

sanskrit: yasya na ahaṅkṛtaḥ bhāvaḥ buddhiḥ yasya na lipyate hatvā api saḥ imān lokān na hanti na nibadhyate
reference: One who is not motivated by false ego, whose intelligence is not entangled, though he kills men in this world, does not kill. Nor is he bound by his actions.
baseline: One who does not conceive of the ego the intellect the mind and the mind are not able to conceal even if he kills these people.
morphology: One who is not proud of his feelings and whose intellect is not written down even if he kills such people he will not be killed or imprisoned.

sanskrit: jñānam jñeyam parijñātā tri vidhā karma codanā karaṇam karma kartā iti tri vidhaḥ karma saṅgrahaḥ
reference: Knowledge, the object of knowledge, and the knower are the three factors that motivate action; the senses, the work and the doer are the three constituents of action.
baseline: One who acquires knowledge by doing three kinds of deeds is called a doer of deeds.
morphology: One who knows the knowledge and knows the three ways of doing a deed would be called a doer of deed. One who does deed should collect deed in three ways.

sanskrit: jñānam karma ca kartā ca tridhā eva guṇa bhedataḥ procyate guṇa saṅkhyāne yathā vat śṛṇu tāni api
reference: According to the three different modes of material nature, there are three kinds of knowledge, action and performer of action. Now hear of them from Me.
baseline: The three qualities of knowledge action and the doer are different from the other. The qualities are known to be in the numbers.
morphology: The three qualities of knowledge action and the doer are different from the other. These qualities are known to be the same in numbers.

sanskrit: sarva bhūteṣu yena ekam bhāvam avyayam īkṣate avibhaktam vibhakteṣu tat jñānam viddhi sāttvikam
reference: That knowledge by which one undivided spiritual nature is seen in all living entities, though they are divided into innumerable forms, you should understand to be in the mode of goodness.
baseline: One who desires to have the same feeling in all the beings and is undivided and divided is known to be sattvic.
morphology: One who desires to have the same feeling among all the spirits and who wants to be undivided and divided should know the knowledge of sattva.

sanskrit: pṛthaktvena tu yat jñānam nānā bhāvān pṛthak vidhān vetti sarveṣu bhūteṣu tat jñānam viddhi rājasam
reference: That knowledge by which one sees that in every different body there is a different type of living entity you should understand to be in the mode of passion.
baseline: The knowledge which is separated by the separation of the different forms and the different ways of manifestation should be given to all beings.
morphology: The knowledge which is different from the knowledge of the gods should be divided into different parts. That knowledge should be different from that of all beings.

sanskrit: yat tu kṛtsna vat ekasmin kārye saktam ahaitukam atattva artha vat alpam ca tat tāmasam udāhṛtam
reference: And that knowledge by which one is attached to one kind of work as the all in all, without knowledge of the truth, and which is very meager, is said to be in the mode of darkness.
baseline: One who has done so would be able to do such a thing. The meaning of the same is said to be small. That is the example given by Tāmasma.
morphology: One who has done such a thing would be able to do it. The meaning of that thing is a little. That is what is said by Tāmasma.

sanskrit: niyatam saṅga rahitam arāga dveṣataḥ kṛtam aphala prepsunā karma yat tat sāttvikam ucyate
reference: That action which is regulated and which is performed without attachment, without love or hatred, and without desire for fruitive results is said to be in the mode of goodness.
baseline: The act done by the enemy with the intention of having no association is said to be virtuous.
morphology: The act done by the enemy with the intention of having no association is said to be sattvic.

sanskrit: yat tu kāma īpsunā karma sa ahaṅkāreṇa vā punaḥ kriyate bahula āyāsam tat rājasam udāhṛtam
reference: But action performed with great effort by one seeking to gratify his desires, and enacted from a sense of false ego, is called action in the mode of passion.
baseline: One who does the work again with the ego or with the desire to do the work is said to have great fatigue.
morphology: One who does the work again with the desire of the lord or with the ego would suffer great fatigue. That is said to be king.

sanskrit: anubandham kṣayam hiṁsām anapekṣya ca pauruṣam mohāt ārabhyate karma yat tat tāmasam ucyate
reference: That action performed in illusion, in disregard of scriptural injunctions, and without concern for future bondage or for violence or distress caused to others is said to be in the mode of ignorance.
baseline: The contract is said to be a loss and the desire to gain wealth starts from the attachment of the man. That is called tāmasam.
morphology: The contract is said to be a loss and the desire to attain the highest position starts with the attachment of the male person. The action is called tāmasma.

sanskrit: mukta saṅgaḥ anaham vādī dhṛti utsāha samanvitaḥ siddhi asiddhyoḥ nirvikāraḥ kartā sāttvikaḥ ucyate
reference: One who performs his duty without association with the modes of material nature, without false ego, with great determination and enthusiasm, and without wavering in success or failure is said to be a worker in the mode of goodness.
baseline: A virtuous doer is said to be free from association. He who does not get pleasure from it and does not want to get success is called a virtuous person.
morphology: One who is free from attachment one who does not attain perfection and does not get pleasure from the combination of enthusiasm and devotion is called sattvic.

sanskrit: rāgī karma phala prepsuḥ lubdhaḥ hiṁsā ātmakaḥ aśuciḥ harṣa śoka anvitaḥ kartā rājasaḥ parikīrtitaḥ
reference: The worker who is attached to work and the fruits of work, desiring to enjoy those fruits, and who is greedy, always envious, impure, and moved by joy and sorrow, is said to be in the mode of passion.
baseline: The king should be known to be a ragi a man of good deeds a king of evil conduct a person of unclean nature and a king who is known to have done evil deeds.
morphology: The king is known to have done the work of a ragi to get the fruits of his actions to rob him to make him selfish to be unclean to enjoy happiness to suffer sorrow to do the king.

sanskrit: ayuktaḥ prākṛtaḥ stabdhaḥ śaṭhaḥ naiṣkṛtikaḥ alasaḥ viṣādī dīrgha sūtrī ca kartā tāmasaḥ ucyate
reference: The worker who is always engaged in work against the injunctions of the scripture, who is materialistic, obstinate, cheating and expert in insulting others, and who is lazy, always morose and procrastinating is said to be a worker in the mode of ignorance.
baseline: A person who is unyuktā is said to be silent in nature. A man who is lazy in nature and has a long thread is called tāmas.
morphology: A person who is ayuktā is said to be silent in nature. A man who is lazy lazy and has a long thread is called tāmas.

sanskrit: buddheḥ bhedam dhṛteḥ ca eva guṇataḥ tri vidham śṛṇu procyamānam aśeṣeṇa pṛthaktvena dhanam jaya
reference: O winner of wealth, now please listen as I tell you in detail of the different kinds of understanding and determination, according to the three modes of material nature.
baseline: The difference between the intellect and the dhritā is said to be the same as that of the three qualities. One should know the three kinds of the prācāmāna. One who separates the wealth from the infinite one would get victory.
morphology: One should know the difference between the intellect and the qualities of the dhrita in three different ways. One should learn to distinguish between the three forms of knowledge and wealth.

sanskrit: yayā dharmam adharmam ca kāryam ca akāryam eva ca ayathā vat prajānāti buddhiḥ sā pārtha rājasī
reference: O son of Pṛthā, that understanding which cannot distinguish between religion and irreligion, between action that should be done and action that should not be done, is in the mode of passion.
baseline: The king who has knowledge of the subjects should say that he has no righteousness iniquity inefficiency in doing his work and is not doing his duty.
morphology: The king who gives wisdom to the subjects should say that he has not done any work which is not righteous unrighteous and unprofitable.

sanskrit: dhṛtyā yayā dhārayate manaḥ prāṇa indriya kriyāḥ yogena avyabhicāriṇyā dhṛtiḥ sā pārtha sāttvikī
reference: O son of Pṛthā, that determination which is unbreakable, which is sustained with steadfastness by yoga practice, and which thus controls the activities of the mind, life and senses is determination in the mode of goodness.
baseline: One who holds the mind the soul the senses the actions of the mind and the mind with the dhrutya the abhicharīna dhruti with the yogic practice is said to be the ultimate sattvikī.
morphology: One who holds the mind life senses and actions with the dhrutīya is said to have attained the position of the mind with the practice of yogāna.

sanskrit: yayā tu dharma kāma arthān dhṛtyā dhārayate arjuna prasaṅgena phala ākāṅkṣī dhṛtiḥ sā pārtha rājasī
reference: But that determination by which one holds fast to fruitive results in religion, economic development and sense gratification is of the nature of passion, O Arjuna.
baseline: The king who desires to get fruits from the kingdom of Arjuna would be the king of the kingdom.
morphology: The king of the kingdom of Partha is said to be desirous of getting fruits from the context of Arjuna.

sanskrit: yayā svapnam bhayam śokam viṣādam madam eva ca na vimuñcati durmedhā dhṛtiḥ sā pārtha tāmasī
reference: And that determination which cannot go beyond dreaming, fearfulness, lamentation, moroseness and illusion – such unintelligent determination, O son of Pṛthā, is in the mode of darkness.
baseline: One who dreams fears grieves regrets drinks and does not give up the illusion of the mind is the one who has not been able to overcome the evil spirit.
morphology: One who dreams fears grieves regrets drinks and does not give up the illusion of fear would become the enemy.

sanskrit: sukham tu idānīm tri vidham śṛṇu me bharata ṛṣabha abhyāsāt ramate yatra duḥkha antam ca nigacchati
reference: O best of the Bhāratas, now please hear from Me about the three kinds of happiness by which the conditioned soul enjoys, and by which he sometimes comes to the end of all distress.
baseline: The three ways of happiness are known to me. One who enjoys the practice of rīṣabha is known as Bharata where sorrow and sorrow end.
morphology: One should know the three ways of happiness. One gets pleasure from the practice of Bharata rīṣabha where the sorrow and the end of suffering is attained.

sanskrit: yat tat agre viṣam iva pariṇāme amṛta upamam tat sukham sāttvikam proktam ātma buddhi prasāda jam
reference: That which in the beginning may be just like poison but at the end is just like nectar and which awakens one to self-realization is said to be happiness in the mode of goodness.
baseline: That which has been shown to be a poison in the past and the resultant elixir is said to be happiness sattvic selfishness wisdom and wealth.
morphology: That which has been shown to be the elixir in the form of poison is described as happiness and sattvic. It is said to be self-awareness.

sanskrit: viṣaya indriya saṁyogāt yat tat agre amṛta upamam pariṇāme viṣam iva tat sukham rājasam smṛtam
reference: That happiness which is derived from contact of the senses with their objects and which appears like nectar at first but poison at the end is said to be of the nature of passion.
baseline: The subject matter should be described as having been perfected by the senses. The object should be imitated by the nectar. The result should be like poison. It should be remembered as happiness.
morphology: The subject matter should be described as having been achieved by the senses. The object should be imitated by the nectar. The result should be like poison. It should be remembered as happiness.

sanskrit: na tat asti pṛthivyām vā divi deveṣu vā punaḥ sattvam prakṛti jaiḥ muktam yat ebhiḥ syāt tribhiḥ guṇaiḥ
reference: There is no being existing, either here or among the demigods in the higher planetary systems, which is freed from these three modes born of material nature.
baseline: Neither the earth nor the gods nor the goddesses are again the manifestations of the nature. One should be free from these three qualities.
morphology: There is no such thing as the earth the gods the goddesses and again the sattva nature and life are liberated by these three qualities.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa kṣatriya viśām śūdrāṇām ca param tapa karmāṇi pravibhaktāni svabhāva prabhavaiḥ guṇaiḥ
reference: Brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas and śūdras are distinguished by the qualities born of their own natures in accordance with the material modes, O chastiser of the enemy.
baseline: The Brahmanas Kshatriyas and the Shudras should be worshipped with the qualities of the nature and influence.
morphology: The Brahmana Kshatriya Visha Shudras and others should be worshipped with the qualities of the nature and influence of the deeds of penance.

sanskrit: śauryam tejaḥ dhṛtiḥ dākṣyam yuddhe ca api apalāyanam dānam īśvara bhāvaḥ ca kṣātram karma svabhāva jam
reference: Heroism, power, determination, resourcefulness, courage in battle, generosity and leadership are the natural qualities of work for the kṣatriyas.
baseline: One should display valour brilliance strife war sacrifice charity devotion devotion to God and the nature of action.
morphology: One should display valour brilliance devotion devotion in battle charity devotion to God sacrifice deeds nature etc..

sanskrit: kṛṣi go rakṣya vāṇijyam vaiśya karma svabhāva jam paricaryā ātmakam karma śūdrasya api svabhāva jam
reference: Farming, cow protection and business are the natural work for the vaiśyas, and for the śūdras there are labor and service to others.
baseline: The nature of a sudra is also the nature of the vaiṣyaśa.
morphology: The nature of the vaiṣya the nature of action the conduct of service the self the work of the Śudra and the nature also of commerce the protection of cows agriculture agriculture and trade.

sanskrit: sve sve karmaṇi abhirataḥ saṁsiddhim labhate naraḥ sva karma nirataḥ siddhim yathā vindati tat śṛṇu
reference: By following his qualities of work, every man can become perfect. Now please hear from Me how this can be done.
baseline: A man acquires success by doing his own deeds. He knows how to accomplish the same by continuing his deeds.
morphology: A man acquires success by doing his own deeds. He knows the way to accomplish his deeds.

sanskrit: yataḥ pravṛttiḥ bhūtānām yena sarvam idam tatam sva karmaṇā tam abhyarcya siddhim vindati mānavaḥ
reference: By worship of the Lord, who is the source of all beings and who is all-pervading, a man can attain perfection through performing his own work.
baseline: A man who has known the nature of the ghosts and all that he does would prove to be perfect by reciting his deeds.
morphology: A man who has a tendency to devils and who has done all these things would prove to be perfect by telling him his deeds.

sanskrit: śreyān sva dharmaḥ viguṇaḥ para dharmāt su anuṣṭhitāt svabhāva niyatam karma kurvan na āpnoti kilbiṣam
reference: It is better to engage in one’s own occupation, even though one may perform it imperfectly, than to accept another’s occupation and perform it perfectly. Duties prescribed according to one’s nature are never affected by sinful reactions.
baseline: One who does not know the merits of one's own nature and does not do the work assigned to him by the nature of the religion should be held responsible for the evil deeds.
morphology: One who does not know the merits of one's own nature and does not do the deeds assigned to him by his own nature should be held responsible for his own conduct.

sanskrit: saha jam karma kaunteya sa doṣam api na tyajet sarva ārambhāḥ hi doṣeṇa dhūmena agniḥ iva āvṛtāḥ
reference: Every endeavor is covered by some fault, just as fire is covered by smoke. Therefore one should not give up the work born of his nature, O son of Kuntī, even if such work is full of fault.
baseline: He who does not give up even the faults by doing the same with the fire should be covered with smoke and fire with the same faults.
morphology: If one does not give up even the faults that he has committed with others all the steps should be covered with smoke and fire.

sanskrit: asakta buddhiḥ sarvatra jita ātmā vigata spṛhaḥ naiṣkarmya siddhim paramām sannyāsena adhigacchati
reference: One who is self-controlled and unattached and who disregards all material enjoyments can obtain, by practice of renunciation, the highest perfect stage of freedom from reaction.
baseline: One who has not attained the intellect of the self is victorious everywhere. One who does not lose the spirit of the past attains perfection with the supreme asceticism.
morphology: Having conquered everywhere and having lost the spirit one attains perfection by the supreme asceticism.

sanskrit: buddhyā viśuddhayā yuktaḥ dhṛtyā ātmānam niyamya ca śabda ādīn viṣayān tyaktvā rāga dveṣau vyudasya ca vivikta sevī laghu āśī yata vāk kāya mānasaḥ dhyāna yoga paraḥ nityam vairāgyam samupāśritaḥ ahaṅkāram balam darpam kāmam krodham parigraham vimucya nirmamaḥ śāntaḥ brahma bhūyāya kalpate
reference: Being purified by his intelligence and controlling the mind with determination, giving up the objects of sense gratification, being freed from attachment and hatred, one who lives in a secluded place, who eats little, who controls his body, mind and power of speech, who is always in trance and who is detached, free from false ego, false strength, false pride, lust, anger, and acceptance of material things, free from false proprietorship, and peaceful – such a person is certainly elevated to the position of self-realization.
baseline: One who is pure in mind and has the right to control the soul with the righteousness the words the hatred the indifference the discrepancy and the discretization of the mind the mind and the mind should be constantly meditated upon in the yogic way. One who has the strength and the power of self the desire the anger the circumference and the calmness of the body should be prepared for the coming of Brahman.
morphology: One who is pure with the mind and has established the self with the righteousness and has left aside the words and other things and has kept aside the anger hatred hatred etc. and has maintained the mind on the yogic path with constant devotion pride strength desire anger circumambulation calmness calm and selfless will attain the goal of Brahman.

sanskrit: brahma bhūtaḥ prasanna ātmā na śocati na kāṅkṣati samaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu mat bhaktim labhate parām
reference: One who is thus transcendentally situated at once realizes the Supreme Brahman and becomes fully joyful. He never laments or desires to have anything. He is equally disposed toward every living entity. In that state he attains pure devotional service unto Me.
baseline: One who is pleased with the Brahman the spirit does not suffer from sorrow and does not desire the same. One gets devotion in all the spirits.
morphology: One who is pleased with the Brahman the spirit does not feel sad and does not desire the same. One gets devotion in all the spirits.

sanskrit: bhaktyā mām abhijānāti yāvān yaḥ ca asmi tattvataḥ tataḥ mām tattvataḥ jñātvā viśate tat anantaram
reference: One can understand Me as I am, as the Supreme Personality of Godhead, only by devotional service. And when one is in full consciousness of Me by such devotion, he can enter into the kingdom of God.
baseline: One who knows me by the principle of what he is and then knows me in the principle would be known by him.
morphology: One who knows me by the principle of what I am and then knows me in the principle is known to me by devotion.

sanskrit: sarva karmāṇi api sadā kurvāṇaḥ mat vyapāśrayaḥ mat prasādāt avāpnoti śāśvatam padam avyayam
reference: Though engaged in all kinds of activities, My pure devotee, under My protection, reaches the eternal and imperishable abode by My grace.
baseline: All deeds should always be performed by the priest. He would get the best from me. The position would be retained for ever.
morphology: All deeds should always be performed by the priest. He will always be blessed by me. He would never be able to attain this position.

sanskrit: cetasā sarva karmāṇi mayi sannyasya mat paraḥ buddhi yogam upāśritya mat cittaḥ satatam bhava
reference: In all activities just depend upon Me and work always under My protection. In such devotional service, be fully conscious of Me.
baseline: All actions should be done with the conscious mind and the mind should be constantly fixed on me.
morphology: All the deeds done by me with the conscious mind should be done by the mind of the mind. Having meditated on me with wisdom and yoga my mind should remain constant.

sanskrit: mat cittaḥ sarva durgāṇi mat prasādāt tariṣyasi atha cet tvam ahaṅkārāt na śroṣyasi vinaṅkṣyasi
reference: If you become conscious of Me, you will pass over all the obstacles of conditioned life by My grace. If, however, you do not work in such consciousness but act through false ego, not hearing Me, you will be lost.
baseline: All the fortifications of my mind will be taken away from me by the prasadam. If you do not listen to me out of pride you will be destroyed.
morphology: All the fortifications of my mind will be taken away from me by the prasadam. If you do not listen to me out of pride you will be destroyed.

sanskrit: yat ahaṅkāram āśritya na yotsye iti manyase mithyā eṣaḥ vyavasāyaḥ te prakṛtiḥ tvām niyokṣyati
reference: If you do not act according to My direction and do not fight, then you will be falsely directed. By your nature, you will have to be engaged in warfare.
baseline: If you believe that the ego is not dependent on you the nature will take you into the occupation.
morphology: If you believe that the ego is dependent on you and not on you then nature will take you away from you.

sanskrit: svabhāva jena kaunteya nibaddhaḥ svena karmaṇā kartum na icchasi yat mohāt kariṣyasi avaśaḥ api tat
reference: Under illusion you are now declining to act according to My direction. But, compelled by the work born of your own nature, you will act all the same, O son of Kuntī.
baseline: One who does not want to do the deeds by himself by the nature of the self and does not wish to do it by the illusion would also do the same to others.
morphology: One who is bound by the nature of the mind and does not want to do the work of one's own self would do the same thing even if he does it out of the illusion.

sanskrit: īśvaraḥ sarva bhūtānām hṛt deśe arjuna tiṣṭhati bhrāmayan sarva bhūtāni yantra ārūḍhani māyayā
reference: The Supreme Lord is situated in everyone’s heart, O Arjuna, and is directing the wanderings of all living entities, who are seated as on a machine, made of the material energy.
baseline: Lord Arjuna is the heart of all the devils in the country. Having wandered all the demons and the instruments are mounted.
morphology: Lord Arjuna is the heart of all the demons in the country. All the devils and machines are set on the earth.

sanskrit: tam eva śaraṇam gaccha sarva bhāvena bhārata tat prasādāt parām śāntim sthānam prāpsyasi śāśvatam
reference: O scion of Bharata, surrender unto Him utterly. By His grace you will attain transcendental peace and the supreme and eternal abode.
baseline: One who takes refuge in that place would get eternal peace from all the devotees of India.
morphology: One who takes refuge in that place would get eternal peace and prosperity from the offerings made to him by all the devotees.

sanskrit: iti te jñānam ākhyātam guhyāt guhya taram mayā vimṛśya etat aśeṣeṇa yathā icchasi tathā kuru
reference: Thus I have explained to you knowledge still more confidential. Deliberate on this fully, and then do what you wish to do.
baseline: Having said this that knowledge should be called out of the cave. Having found out the quality of that cave I shall make it as far as I want.
morphology: That knowledge should be called that. Having gone out of the cave and having found out the quality of it one should do as much as he desires with the utmost of his ability.

sanskrit: sarva guhya tamam bhūyaḥ śṛṇu me paramam vacaḥ iṣṭaḥ asi me dṛḍham iti tataḥ vakṣyāmi te hitam
reference: Because you are My very dear friend, I am speaking to you My supreme instruction, the most confidential knowledge of all. Hear this from Me, for it is for your benefit.
baseline: Having said this I shall say that I am the supreme voice. I am firm. Then I shall speak that which is good.
morphology: Having said this I shall say that I am the supreme voice. I am firm. Then I shall speak that which is good.

sanskrit: mat manāḥ bhava mat bhaktaḥ mat yājī mām namaskuru mām eva eṣyasi satyam te pratijāne priyaḥ asi me
reference: Always think of Me, become My devotee, worship Me and offer your homage unto Me. Thus you will come to Me without fail. I promise you this because you are My very dear friend.
baseline: O my heart you are my devotee my servant you salute me you bless me and you are truly my beloved.
morphology: O Lord of my heart you are my devotee O Lord you salute me You bless me and you bless me. You are truly dear to me and they are dear to you.

sanskrit: sarva dharmān parityajya mām ekam śaraṇam vraja aham tvām sarva pāpebhyaḥ mokṣayiṣyāmi mā śucaḥ
reference: Abandon all varieties of religion and just surrender unto Me. I shall deliver you from all sinful reactions. Do not fear.
baseline: Having renounced all religions one should seek refuge in me and know that I will make you free from all sins.
morphology: Having renounced all religions one should seek refuge in me and know that I will make you free from all sins.

sanskrit: idam te na atapaskāya na abhaktāya kadācana na ca aśuśrūṣave vācyam na ca mām yaḥ abhyasūyati
reference: This confidential knowledge may never be explained to those who are not austere, or devoted, or engaged in devotional service, nor to one who is envious of Me.
baseline: He who does not teach me nor the world nor me would never do it. He would never be ungodly.
morphology: He who does not know me nor the world nor me never becomes ungodly and unattached.

sanskrit: yaḥ idam paramam guhyam mat bhakteṣu abhidhāsyati bhaktim mayi parām kṛtvā mām eva eṣyati asaṁśayaḥ
reference: For one who explains this supreme secret to the devotees, pure devotional service is guaranteed, and at the end he will come back to Me.
baseline: Whoever finds this supreme cave among his devotees will get the devotion after having worshipped me and will give it to me.
morphology: Whoever finds this supreme cave among his devotees will get the devotion from me and will give it to me.

sanskrit: na ca tasmāt manuṣyeṣu kaścit me priya kṛt tamaḥ bhavitā na ca me tasmāt anyaḥ priya taraḥ bhuvi
reference: There is no servant in this world more dear to Me than he, nor will there ever be one more dear.
baseline: Neither shall I make any of the men dear to me. Neither shall i make any dear to you. Neither will I make another dear to him.
morphology: Neither shall any of the men whom I have loved say that I am yours. Neither shall I make another beloved like that.

sanskrit: adhyeṣyate ca yaḥ imam dharmyam saṁvādam āvayoḥ jñāna yajñena tena aham iṣṭaḥ syām iti me matiḥ
reference: And I declare that he who studies this sacred conversation of ours worships Me by his intelligence.
baseline: One who studies and becomes righteous should say that he would get knowledge by sacrificing it. By doing so he would become good.
morphology: One who studies and becomes righteous should say that he would get knowledge by sacrificing his knowledge. By doing so he would become good.

sanskrit: śraddhā vān anasūyaḥ ca śṛṇuyāt api yaḥ naraḥ saḥ api muktaḥ śubhān lokān prāpnuyāt puṇya karmaṇām
reference: And one who listens with faith and without envy becomes free from sinful reactions and attains to the auspicious planets where the pious dwell.
baseline: One who is free from evil will also get good deeds and good deeds.
morphology: One who is free from evil will also get good deeds.

sanskrit: kaccit etat śrutam pārtha tvayā eka agreṇa cetasā kaccit ajñāna sammohaḥ praṇaṣṭaḥ te dhanam jaya
reference: O son of Pṛthā, O conqueror of wealth, have you heard this with an attentive mind? And are your ignorance and illusions now dispelled?
baseline: O king of the world you have heard this story. You have become conscious by one of the gods. You know that story you are not aware of it. You are worshipped. You conquer wealth.
morphology: O king of the world if you hear this sound from a man who is conscious and does not know the sound of the sound you will be blessed with that wealth.

sanskrit: arjunaḥ uvāca naṣṭaḥ mohaḥ smṛtiḥ labdhā tvat prasādāt mayā acyuta sthitaḥ asmi gata sandehaḥ kariṣye vacanam tava
reference: Arjuna said: My dear Kṛṣṇa, O infallible one, my illusion is now gone. I have regained my memory by Your mercy. I am now firm and free from doubt and am prepared to act according to Your instructions.
baseline: O Arjuna you have lost the attachment the memory and you have got that. By offering you I am standing firm. If you doubt the promise made by me.
morphology: O Arjuna you have lost the attachment you get the memory. You have got that by offering you I am standing firm. If you doubt the promise made by me you will get it.

sanskrit: sañjayaḥ uvāca iti aham vāsudevasya pārthasya ca mahā ātmanaḥ saṁvādam imam aśrauṣam adbhutam roma harṣaṇam
reference: Sañjaya said: Thus have I heard the conversation of two great souls, Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna. And so wonderful is that message that my hair is standing on end.
baseline: I am the great self of Vasudeva Partha and the great spirit. This is said to be the voice of the hearers the wonderful Rūma and Hārśana.
morphology: The great spirit of Vasudeva and Partha should be said to be the supreme one. This is the great voice of the hearers the wonderful voice of Rome and Hārśana.

sanskrit: vyāsa prasādāt śrutavān etat guhyam aham param yogam yoga īśvarāt kṛṣṇāt sākṣāt kathayataḥ svayam
reference: By the mercy of Vyāsa, I have heard these most confidential talks directly from the master of all mysticism, Kṛṣṇa, who was speaking personally to Arjuna.
baseline: Having heard from Vyasa the prasadam one should say this cave the yoga of the Supreme Lord the Yoga of God and Krishna directly.
morphology: Having heard from Vyasa the prāsāda one should say this cave the yoga of the Supreme Lord Śiva and Śrīkṛṣṇa directly.

sanskrit: rājan saṁsmṛtya saṁsmṛtya saṁvādam imam adbhutam keśava arjunayoḥ puṇyam hṛṣyāmi ca muhuḥ muhuḥ
reference: O King, as I repeatedly recall this wondrous and holy dialogue between Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna, I take pleasure, being thrilled at every moment.
baseline: The king should remember that he has accomplished the task. Having accomplished that task he should say that he will achieve the task and that he would have achieved great success. He would have lost the virtues of Arjuna and others.
morphology: The king should remember that he has achieved all things. Having achieved all these things he should say that he would achieve great things. He would also destroy the virtues of Arjuna and others.

sanskrit: tat ca saṁsmṛtya saṁsmṛtya rūpam ati adbhutam hareḥ vismayaḥ me mahān rājan hṛṣyāmi ca punaḥ punaḥ
reference: O King, as I remember the wonderful form of Lord Kṛṣṇa, I am struck with wonder more and more, and I rejoice again and again.
baseline: Having recollected that and having accomplished that one should recall the form as very wonderful. One who is a great king would be astonished and would lose again and again.
morphology: Having remembered that and having accomplished that one should recall the form as very wonderful. One who has become a great king and who is amazed by the form one who has attained great glory and one who becomes great king again and again.

sanskrit: yatra yoga īśvaraḥ kṛṣṇaḥ yatra pārthaḥ dhanuḥ dharaḥ tatra śrīḥ vijayaḥ bhūtiḥ dhruvā nītiḥ matiḥ mama
reference: Wherever there is Kṛṣṇa, the master of all mystics, and wherever there is Arjuna, the supreme archer, there will also certainly be opulence, victory, extraordinary power, and morality. That is my opinion.
baseline: Where there is yoga god lord lord of the earth bow sword king king of victory king and king of earth the principle of righteousness is my belief.
morphology: Where there is yoga God Krishna earth bow and earth there is victory the earth the pole and the principle.

sanskrit: kāścitkanakakāṃcībhirmukharābhiritastataḥ | babhramurdarśayaṃtyo 'sya śroṇīstanvaṃśukāvṛtāḥ ||
reference: Others, with their golden zones tinkling, wandered about here and there, showing to him their hips veiled with thin cloth.
baseline: Then there should be a lotus and a cow and the head should be placed on the ground. Then the pelvis should be covered with the hairs of the calf and the forehead should be removed.
morphology: One should not be afraid of a man who has a lotus. He should be made to look at the head and face with his hands and legs and his pelvis should be covered with a thread.

sanskrit: cūtaśākhāṃ kusumitāṃ pragṛhyānyā lalaṃbire | suvarṇakalaśaprakhyān darśayaṃtyaḥ payodharān ||
reference: Others leaned, holding a mango-bough in full flower, displaying their bosoms like golden jars.
baseline: One who has made a lumbar stone with the branches of a sundial and the hair of a kusum should be made to grow. The golden kalashas should be shown to the devotees.
morphology: One should draw the branches of the sundial and the hair of the kusum in the upper lumbar region and show the golden kalas and the faces of the pigeons.

sanskrit: kācitpadmavanādetya sapadmā padmalocanā | padmavaktrasya pārśve 'sya padmaśrīriva tasthuṣī ||
reference: Another, coming from a lotus-bed, carrying lotuses and with eyes like lotuses, stood like the lotus-goddess Padmā, by the side of that lotus-faced prince.
baseline: Having offered the kacchita pādmavana the lotus should be placed on the side of the pāḍmā scripture. The pādhāmasrī scripture should be kept on the other side.
morphology: Having offered the kacchita pādmavana one should offer the sapādaṇa lotus. The pādhāmasrī scripture should be placed next to the pāḍma.

sanskrit: madhuraṃ gītamanvarthaṃ kācitsābhinayaṃ jagau | taṃ svasthaṃ codayaṃtīva vaṃcito 'sītyavekṣitaiḥ ||
reference: Another sang a sweet song easily understood and with the proper gesticulations, rousing him, self-subdued though he was, by her glances, as saying, ‘O how thou art deluded!’
baseline: One should perform a piece of music with sweetness and sweetness. He should be made healthy by the devotees who have not seen him.
morphology: One should perform a piece of music with sweetness and sweetness. One should do it after having been cured. One would be deprived of it by the devotees.

sanskrit: śubhena vadanenānyā bhrūkārmukavikarṣiṇā | prāvṛtyānucakārāsya ceṣṭitaṃ vīralīlayā ||
reference: Another, having armed herself with her bright face, with its brow-bow drawn to its full, imitated his action, as playing the hero.
baseline: Having spoken with good words one should do the practice of making the forehead look like a bearer of evil eye. One should try to do the same by doing the ritual of brahmin.
morphology: Having spoken with good words one would get the hair of the forehead and face. One would get rid of the hair by walking around and doing the ritual of vairālilīla.

sanskrit: pīnavalgustanī kācidvātāghūrṇitakuṃḍalā | uccairavajahāsainaṃ samāpnotu bhavāniti ||
reference: Another, with beautiful full bosoms, and having her earrings waving in the wind, laughed loudly at him, as if saying, ‘Catch me, sir, if you can!’
baseline: The spire should be made of water with the spire the spade the axe the round finger the bow the neck and the head.
morphology: The spire should be made of water with the spears and the spindle should be round and round. One should be able to see the upper body with the frown.

sanskrit: apayāntaṃ tathaivānyā babaṃdhurmālyadāmabhiḥ | kāścitsākṣepamadhurairjagṛhurvacanāṃkuśaiḥ ||
reference: Some, as he was going away, bound him with strings of garlands, — others punished him with words like an elephant-driver’s hook, gentle yet reproachful.
baseline: One who has not been able to do so would be bound by the hands of the king. One would get some relief by the servants of the lord of the house.
morphology: One who has not been able to do so would be bound by a bondage a bond of property a friend a neighbour a relative a servant a nobleman a king a priest a cow a man a woman and a man.

sanskrit: pratiyogārthinī kācidgṛhītvā cūtavallarīm | idaṃ puṣpaṃ tu kasyeti papraccha madaviklavā ||
reference: Another, wishing to argue with him, seizing a mango-spray, asked, all bewildered with passion, ‘This flower, whose is it?’
baseline: Having chosen a woman for the purpose of competing one should kiss her daughter. The flower should be said to be of ones choice.
morphology: A woman seeking a rival should be given a kiss and the flower should be offered to her. This flower is said to be of ones own choice.

sanskrit: kācitpuruṣavatkṛtvā gatiṃ saṃsthānameva ca | uvācainaṃ jitaḥ strībhirjaya bhoḥ pṛthivīmimām ||
reference: Another, assuming a gait and attitude like those of a man, said to him, ‘Thou who art conquered by women, go and conquer this earth!’
baseline: The movement is the same as that of the body. By doing so the victory is achieved by the woman and the victory by the earth.
morphology: The movement is the same as that of the body. By doing this the victory is achieved by the woman and the victory by the earth.

sanskrit: atha loleksaṇā kācijjighraṃtī nīlamutpalam | kiṃcinmadakalairvākyairnṛpātmajamabhāṣata ||
reference: Then another with rolling eyes, smelling a blue lotus, thus addressed the prince with words slightly indistinct in her excitement,
baseline: Then the loleksana is said to be the blue flower of the tiger the red colour of the elephant the golden flower of a man the white colour of a cow and the spirit of the soul.
morphology: Then the loleksana is said to be the blue flower of the king of the earth. Then it should be called the ātmana.

sanskrit: paśya bhartaścitaṃ cūtaṃ kusumairmadhugaṃdhibhiḥ | hemapaṃjararuddho vā kokilo yatra kūjati ||
reference: ‘See, my lord, this mango covered with its honey-scented flowers, where the kokila sings, as if imprisoned in a golden cage.
baseline: See the bhaṭrāṣti pus is made of kusuma and honey and gandhi. The hemā the garland of a cage or the place where the cow crows are made to bow.
morphology: One should see the bhaṭrātha pus is made of saffron and honey and the kokila is made from a hemp cage.

sanskrit: aśoko dṛśyatāmeṣa kāmiśokavivardhanaḥ | ruvaṃti bhramarā yatra dahyamānā ivāgninā ||
reference: ‘Come and see this aśoka tree, which augments lovers’ sorrows, — where the bees make a noise as if they were scorched by fire.
baseline: The image of Ashoka is seen in the same way as the image of Kāmisoka the manifestation of the universe. One who wanders in the wilderness and burns like a fire.
morphology: The image of Ashoka is visible in the form of a kāmīśoka. The vivardhana of the Kāmisoka is seen in the image of the king of the earth. The incinerator is said to be burning like fire.

sanskrit: cūtayaṣṭyā samāśliṣṭo dṛśyatāṃ tilakadrumaḥ | śuklavāsā iva naraḥ striyā pītāṃgarāgayā ||
reference: ‘Come and see this tilaka tree, embraced by a slender mango-branch, like a man in a white garment by a woman decked with yellow unguents.
baseline: One who has made a man look like a sukla or a woman with the garland of peat should be seen as having made a lotus. The male should be made to look like the son of a sukha.
morphology: A man should be made to look like a woman with a penis and a woman should be drawn like a sukla.

sanskrit: phullaṃ kuruvakaṃ paśya nirmuktālaktakaprabham | yo nakhaprabhayā strīṇāṃ nirbhartsita ivānataḥ ||
reference: ‘Behold this kuruvaka in flower, bright like fresh resin-juice, which bends down as if it felt reproached by the colour of women’s nails.
baseline: One who has depended on women for their livelihood by the preceptor of the nails should see the flower of the bridegroom.
morphology: One who has depended on women for protection by the preceptor of the nails should see the flower of the cow.

sanskrit: bālāśokaśca nicito dṛśyatāmeṣa pallavaiḥ | yo 'smākaṃ hastaśobhābhirlajjamāna iva sthitaḥ ||
reference: ‘Come and see this young aśoka, covered all over with new shoots, which stands as it were ashamed at the beauty of our hands.
baseline: One who is standing on the ground with the hands of our lord is seen as having a child a cow and a pallava.
morphology: One who is standing on the ground with the palms of children and children is seen sitting on the hill.

sanskrit: dīrghikāṃ prāvṛtāṃ paśya tīrajaiḥ siṃduvārakaiḥ | pāṃḍurāṃśukasaṃvītāṃ śayānāṃ pramadāmiva ||
reference: ‘See this lake surrounded by the sinduvāra shrubs growing on its banks, like a fair woman reclining, clad in fine white cloth.
baseline: One should see the arches covered with sand and sand. One would get the sand of Pandura and other parts of the river.
morphology: One should observe the circumambulation of the arches with the sindhvarākas and the sandwiches with the pāndurāksha and the prāmāmī of the shaitas.

sanskrit: dṛśyatāṃ strīṣu māhātmyaṃ cakravāko hyasau jale | pṛṣṭhataḥ preṣyavadbhāryāmanuvṛtyānugacchati ||
reference: ‘See the imperial power of females, — yonder ruddy-goose in the water goes behind his mate following her like a slave.
baseline: One who has seen the greatness in women and the chakravaka in the water would get the pleasure of worshiping the husband as if he had sent him from behind.
morphology: One who has seen the greatness of women and the chakravaka in the waters would be like a woman sent by a man from behind.

sanskrit: mattasya parapuṣṭasya ruvataḥ śrūyatāṃ dhvaniḥ | aparaḥ kokilo 'nutkaḥ pratiśrutyeva kūjati ||
reference: ‘Come and listen to the notes of this intoxicated cuckoo as he sings, while another cuckoo sings as if consenting, wholly without care.
baseline: The sound of a drunken man is heard from the other side of the river. The other one is called kokila and the other one cries as promised.
morphology: The sound of a drunken man crying out for help is heard from the other side. The other one cuckoos and shouts the same promise.

sanskrit: api nāma vihaṃgānāṃ vasaṃtenāhito madaḥ | na tu ciṃtayataścittaṃ janasya prājñamāninaḥ ||
reference: ‘Would that thine was the intoxication of the birds which the spring produces, — and not the thought of a thinking man, ever pondering how wise he is!’
baseline: One should not be afraid of the name of the king. One should never be afraid to drink wine without having the knowledge of the people.
morphology: The names of the people should not be mentioned in the words of the wise men.

sanskrit: ityevaṃ tā yuvatayo manmathoddāmacetasaḥ | kumāraṃ vividhaistaistairupacakramire nayaiḥ ||
reference: Thus these young women, their souls carried away by love, assailed the prince with all kinds of stratagems.
baseline: Thus the young man should be made to think like that. The kumara should be different. These are the forms of the chakramis.
morphology: Thus the young man should be made to feel the heart of the bridegroom and the bride should be different.

sanskrit: evamākṣipyamāṇo 'pi sa tu dhairyāvṛteṃdriyaḥ | martavyamiti sodvego na jaharṣa na sismiye ||
reference: But although thus attacked, he, having his senses guarded by self-control, neither rejoiced nor smiled, thinking anxiously, ‘One must die.’
baseline: One who throws the same thing should be patient. He should not be afraid of death. One who does not want to suffer death should be afraid.
morphology: He should then be thrown away. He should be patient and considerate. One should not be afraid of death.

sanskrit: tāsāṃ tattvena vasthānaṃ dṛṣṭvā sa puruṣottamaḥ | sasaṃvignena dhīreṇa ciṃtayāmāsa cetasā ||
reference: Having seen them in their real condition, that best of men pondered with an undisturbed, and stedfast mind.
baseline: Having seen the place of abode with the same principle as before he becomes purūṣṇu the Supreme Being. He becomes conscious of the mind slowly with the manifestation of the same.
morphology: Having seen the place of worship with the principle of āhā one becomes purūṣottama. One becomes conscious of the mind gradually by the manifestation of the same.

sanskrit: kiṃ vinā nāvagacchaṃti capalaṃ yauvanaṃ striyaḥ | yato rūpeṇa saṃpannaṃ jareyaṃ nāśayiṣyati ||
reference: ‘What is it that these women lack that they perceive not that youth is fickle? for this old age will destroy whatever has beauty.
baseline: A woman should walk on a ship without having to do anything. A woman who is young would destroy the ship if she is rich in form.
morphology: A woman should walk on a ship without having to do anything. A woman who is young will destroy a ship which is rich in form.

sanskrit: nūnametā na paśyaṃti kasyacid rogasaṃplavam | tathā hṛṣṭā bhayaṃ tyaktvā jagati vyādhidharmiṇi ||
reference: ‘Verily they do not see any one’s plunge into disease, and so dismissing fear, they are joyous in a world which is all pain.
baseline: One who does not see the disease of any one would get afflicted by it. One would get rid of fear and go to the world.
morphology: One who does not see a disease or a disease in the world would get rid of the fear of the disease.

sanskrit: anabhijñāśca suvyaktaṃ mṛtyoḥ sarvāpahāriṇaḥ | tathā svasthā nirudvegāḥ krīḍaṃti ca hasaṃti ca ||
reference: ‘Evidently they know nothing of death which carries all away; and so at ease and without distress they can sport and laugh.
baseline: The unbelievers and those who eat all things without knowing the manifest death. Those who do not know the nature of death are free from evil deeds. They play games and fight.
morphology: The unbelievers and those who do not know the manifest death are all eaters of death. Those who are not aware of the state of affairs and do not play games are the sufferers of the disease.

sanskrit: jarāṃ mṛtyuṃ ca vyādhiṃ ca ko hi jānan sacetanaḥ | svasthastiṣṭhan niṣīdedvā supedvā kiṃ punarhaset ||
reference: ‘What rational being, who knows of old age, death and sickness, could stand or sit down at his ease or sleep, far less laugh?
baseline: One should know who causes death and disease. One should be conscious of the health of those who have been cured and who will be cured. What is the benefit of the cure?
morphology: One who knows the cause of death and disease should be aware of it. One who is healthy should be cured and put back to life.

sanskrit: yastu dṛṣṭvā paraṃ jīrṇaṃ vyādhitaṃ mṛtameva ca | svastho bhavati nodvigno yathācetāstathaiva saḥ ||
reference: ‘But he verily is like one bereft of sense, who, beholding another aged or sick or dead, remains self-possessed and not afflicted.
baseline: One who sees the body after having been worn out and has become diseased and is dead becomes healthy as if he had not seen it.
morphology: One who sees the body after having been worn out and is injured and is dead becomes healthy as if he had not seen it.

sanskrit: viyujyamāne 'pi tarau puṣpairapi phalairapi | patati cchidyamāne vā taruranyo na śocate ||
reference: ‘(So) even when a tree is deprived of its flowers and fruits, or if it is cut down and falls, no other tree sorrows.’
baseline: If the water is washed away and flowers are also flushed out it will fall down and will not be affected by the fall.
morphology: If the water is not well drained and the flowers are flushed with water it will fall and the water will not get dirty.

sanskrit: iti dhyānaparaṃ dṛṣṭvā viṣayebhyo gataspṛham | udāyī nītiśāstrajñastamuvāca suhṛttayā ||
reference: Seeing him thus absorbed in contemplation, with his desires estranged from all worldly objects, Udāyin, well skilled in the rules of policy, with kindly feelings addressed him:
baseline: Having seen that the mind is meditative one should go to the house for the sake of things. One who knows the principles should rise up and make a friend of him.
morphology: Having seen this meditation one should go beyond the things. One who knows the principles should rise up and make a friend of him.

sanskrit: ahaṃ nṛpatinā dattaḥ sakhā tubhyaṃ kṣamaḥ kila | yasmāttvayi vivakṣā me tayā praṇayavattayā ||
reference: ‘Since I was appointed by the king as a fitting friend for thee, therefore I have a wish to speak to thee in this friendliness of my heart.
baseline: If I have given to you by the lord of the king forgive me. Forgive me if I have done wrong. That is because of my love.
morphology: If I have given to you by the lord of the king forgive me. For that reason I will forgive you.

sanskrit: ahitāt pratiṣedhaśca hite cānupravartanam | vyasane cāparityāgastrividhaṃ mitralakṣaṇam ||
reference: ‘To hinder from what is disadvantageous, to urge to what is advantageous — and not to forsake in misfortune, — these are the three marks of a friend.
baseline: One should avoid harm and avoid harm. One should treat the enemy with a knife and a sword as if he were a friend.
morphology: One should avoid harm and avoid harm. One should treat others as friends in the form of a slap in the mouth.

sanskrit: so 'haṃ maitrīṃ pratijñāya puruṣārthātparāṅmukham | yadi tvāṃ samupekṣeyaṃ na bhavenmitratā mayi ||
reference: ‘If I, after having promised my friendship, were not to heed when thou turnest away from the great end of man, there would be no friendship in me.
baseline: So let me promise friendship to you and face you in the front. If you are not close to me then you should be friends with me.
morphology: Then shall I promise friendship to you. If you are not close to me you will be friends with me.

sanskrit: tadbravīmi suhṛdbhūtvā taruṇasya vapuṣmataḥ | idaṃ na pratirūpaṃ te strīṣvadākṣiṇyamīdṛśam ||
reference: ‘Therefore I speak as thy friend, — such rudeness as this to women is not befitting for one young in years and graceful in person.
baseline: Having said this one should be pleased with the young man. This is not the likeness of the woman.
morphology: Having said this one should be pleased with the young man. This is not the likeness of the woman.

sanskrit: anṛtenāpi nārīṇāṃ yuktaṃ samanuvartanam | tadvrīḍāparihārārthamātmaratyarthameva ca ||
reference: ‘It is right to woo a woman even by guile, this is useful both for getting rid of shame and for one’s own enjoyment.
baseline: One should not engage in the same conduct as the other women. In the same way one should engage in a game for the sake of the soul.
morphology: One should not engage in the same conduct as a woman. The same practice should be done for the sake of the soul.

sanskrit: saṃnatiscānuvṛttiśca strīṇāṃ hṛdayabaṃdhanam | snehasya hi guṇā yonirmānakāmāśca yoṣitaḥ ||
reference: ‘Reverential behaviour and compliance with her wishes are what binds a woman’s heart; good qualities truly are a cause of love, and women love respect.
baseline: The merits of the marriage are to be made by the husband wife husband husband and wife. The virtues of love are to make the wife.
morphology: The merits of women should be the union of their hearts and the virtues of love. Women should have the qualities of love in the making of the womb.

sanskrit: tadarhasi viśālākṣa hṛdaye 'pi parāṅmukhe | rūpasyāsyānurūpeṇa dākṣiṇyenānuvartitum ||
reference: ‘Wilt thou not then, O large-eyed prince, even if thy heart is unwilling, seek to please them with a courtesy worthy of this beauty of thine?
baseline: The image should be placed on the right side of the heart with the broad eyelids and on the upper face with the form of the āyāsana.
morphology: The image should be placed on the right side of the heart with the broad eyelids and on the upper face with the form of the āyāsana.

sanskrit: dākṣiṇyamauṣadhaṃ strīṇāṃ dākṣiṇyaṃ bhūṣaṇaṃ param | dākṣiṇyarahitaṃ rūpaṃ niṣpuṣpamiva kānanam ||
reference: ‘Courtesy is the balm of women, courtesy is the best ornament; beauty without courtesy is like a grove without flowers.
baseline: A woman should be given the form of a man without the righteousness. The form of the woman should not be like that of a pure man.
morphology: A woman should be given the form of a man without the righteousness. The form of the woman without the left would be like that of an unclean man.

sanskrit: kiṃ vā dākṣiṇyamātreṇa bhāvenāstu parigrahaḥ | viṣayān durlabhāṃllabdhvā na hyavajñātumarhasi ||
reference: ‘But of what use is courtesy by itself? let it be assisted by the heart’s feelings; surely, when worldly objects so hard to attain are in thy grasp, thou wilt not despise them.
baseline: One would not know if he had done anything or had done nothing. He would not get the things which are scarce and would not be known by him.
morphology: One should not know whether one is righteous or wrong. One would not know if one finds the things which are scarce and one does not get grace.

sanskrit: kāmaṃ paramiti jñātvā devo 'pi hi puraṃdaraḥ | gautamasya muneḥ patnīmahalyāṃ cakame purā ||
reference: ‘Knowing that pleasure was the best of objects, even the god Puraṃdara (Indra) wooed in olden time Ahalyā the wife of the saint Gautama.
baseline: Having known the perfection of the kāma one should worship the god. The wife of Gautama should be worshipped in the palace.
morphology: Having known the perfection of kāma one should worship the god. The wife of Gautama should be worshipped in the palace.

sanskrit: agastyaḥ prārthayāmāsa somabhāryāṃ ca rohiṇīm | tasmāt tatsadṛśaṃ lebhe lopāmudrāmiti śrutiḥ ||
reference: ‘So too Agastya wooed Rohiṇī, the wife of Soma; and therefore, as Śruti saith, a like thing befell Lopāmudrā.
baseline: The goddess Agastya prays to the lord Sūmā and to the wife of the goddess Rohini in the same way.
morphology: The goddess Agastya prays to the goddess Rohini in the marriage of Soma. Thus the goddess Śrutī should be worshipped in the same manner in the month of Lopamudram.

sanskrit: autathyasya ca bhāryāyāṃ mamatāyāṃ mahātapāḥ | mārutyāṃ janayāmāsa bharadvājaṃ vṛhaspatiḥ ||
reference: ‘The great ascetic Vṛhaspati begot Bharadvāja on Mamatā the daughter of the Maruts, the wife of Autathya.
baseline: One who is born in the kingdom of Marutis and has a wife with great qualities in the form of love is called Bharadwaja.
morphology: One who is born in the kingdom of Marutis and has a wife with great qualities in love should worship Bharādvāja and Brihaspati.

sanskrit: vṛhaspatermahiṣyāṃ ca juhvatyāṃ juhvatāṃ varaḥ | budhaṃ vibudhadharmāṇaṃ janayāmāsa caṃdramāḥ ||
reference: ‘The Moon, the best of offerers, begat Budha of divine nature on the spouse of Vṛhaspati as she was offering a libation.
baseline: One who is blessed with the boon of jhuvatya and juhuvata in the form of a large spacer the moon is born with the knowledge of the religion of Budha.
morphology: One who is blessed with the great element jhuvatya the boon of juhuvata the sun the moon and the moon are born with the belief of the intellect.

sanskrit: kālīm caiva purā kanyāṃ jalaprabhavasaṃbhavām | jagāma yamunātīre jātarāgaḥ parāśaraḥ ||
reference: ‘So too in old time Parāśara, overpowered by passion on the bank of the Yamunā, lay with the maiden Kālī who was the daughter of the son of the Water (Agni).
baseline: One should worship Kali the goddess of water the daughter of the whole world the jagāma and the raga born on the banks of the river yamuna.
morphology: The goddess Kali should be worshipped in the form of a virgin and the water should be made available to her. The jaga should be placed on the banks of the river Yamuna and the raga should be raised above the river.

sanskrit: mātaṃgyāmakṣamālāyāṃ garhitāyāṃ riraṃsayā | kapiṃjalādaṃ tanayaṃ vasiṣṭho 'janayanmuniḥ ||
reference: ‘The sage Vaśiṣṭha through lust begot a son Kapiñjalāda on Akṣamālā a despised low-caste woman.
baseline: One who is born in the temple of Maṭāṅga Yāmāśmāla Garhita Rīrāṇsa Kapīñjala Tāṇā Vāṣṭhī and others.
morphology: One should worship the mother the mother and the mother of the child in the temple. One should offer water to the cow with the riramsha. One would get water from the water of the cup and one would get the water from Vāṣṭhī.

sanskrit: yayātiścaiva rājarṣirvayasyapi vinirgate | viśvācyāpsarasā sārdhaṃ reme caitrarathe vane ||
reference: ‘And the seer-king Yayāti, even when the vigour of his prime was gone, sported in the Caitraratha forest with the Apsaras Viśvācī.
baseline: The king should also give a gift of water to those who live in the forest in the month of Chaitra along with the gift of faith.
morphology: The king should also visit the forest in the month of Chaitra along with the king sage and other people who live in the forest.

sanskrit: strīsaṃsargaṃ vināśāṃtaṃ pāṃḍurjñātvāpi kauravaḥ | mādrīrūpaguṇākṣiptaḥ siṣeve kāmajaṃ sukham ||
reference: ‘And the Kaurava king Pāṇḍu, though he knew that intercourse with his wife would end in death, yet overcome by the beauty and good qualities of Mādrī yielded to the pleasures of love.
baseline: The Kauravas also know the union of women and the destruction of Pandurga. One who is born as a mother and has been cast into the folds is blessed with happiness and pleasure.
morphology: One who knows that a woman is bound to be destroyed by the union of men and women one who is not known to be a virgin is born as a mother and is blessed with happiness.

sanskrit: karālajanakaścaiva hṛtvā brāhmaṇakanyakām | avāpa bhraṃśam apyeva na tu tyajecca manmatham ||
reference: ‘And so Karālajanaka, when he carried off the Brāhman’s daughter, incurred loss of caste thereby, but he would not give up his love.
baseline: One who lives in a forest should kill a brahmin and another. One who does not give up his property should not commit the crime of theft.
