morphology: One who lives in a forest should kill a brahmin and another. One who does not give up the land should not commit a mistake.

sanskrit: evamādyā mahātmāno viṣayān garhitānapi | ratihetorbubhujire prāgeva guṇasaṃhitān ||
reference: ‘Great heroes such as these pursued even contemptible desires for the sake of pleasure, how much more so when they are praiseworthy of their kind?
baseline: In the same way the subjects of the great soul should be mentioned in the sacred scriptures. The virtues should be introduced in the arches of the gods.
morphology: In the same way the subjects of the great soul should be mentioned in the sacred scriptures.

sanskrit: tvaṃ punarnyāyataḥ prāptān balavān rūpavān yuvā | viṣayānavajānāsi yatra saktamidaṃ jagat ||
reference: ‘And yet thou, a young man, possessed of strength and beauty, despisest enjoyments which rightly belong to thee, and to which the whole world is devoted.’
baseline: You have again made those things which have been obtained by the righteousness strong and young. Knowing the subject you know where the world is.
morphology: You have again made those things which have been obtained by the righteousness strong and young. You know the world where you can get it.

sanskrit: iti śrutvā vacastasya ślakṣṇamāgamasaṃhitam | meghastanitanirghoṣaḥ kumāraḥ pratyabhāṣata ||
reference: Having heard these specious words of his, well-supported by sacred tradition, the prince made reply, in a voice like the thundering of a cloud:
baseline: Having heard this the son of the king said that he should be blessed with a lotus flower. The son of lord Gūmarā said that the goddess should be placed in the clouds.
morphology: Having heard this the son of the king said that he would get a gift from the king. The king of the kingdom of the clouds would return the gift.

sanskrit: upapannamidaṃ vākyaṃ sauhārdavyaṃjakaṃ tvayi | atra ca tvānuneṣyāmi yatra mā duṣṭhu manyase ||
reference: ‘This speech manifesting affection is well-befitting in thee; but I will convince thee as to where thou wrongly judgest me.
baseline: The words mentioned above are for the sake of harmony. Here also I am going to tell you where you are not considered evil.
morphology: The words mentioned above are for the sake of harmony. Here also I am for you. You should not be considered a bad person.

sanskrit: nāvajānāmi viṣayāñjāne lokaṃ tadātmakam | anityaṃ tu jaganmatvā nātra me ramate manaḥ ||
reference: ‘I do not despise worldly objects, I know that all mankind are bound up therein; but remembering that the world is transitory, my mind cannot find pleasure in them.
baseline: The world is similar to that of the world in the sense of knowing the subject matter. Having become aware of it the mind becomes happy in the night.
morphology: The world is similar to that of the world in the sense of knowing the subject. Having become aware of it the mind becomes happy in the night.

sanskrit: jarā vyādhiśca mṛtyuśca yadi na syādidaṃ trayam | mamāpi hi manojñeṣu viṣayeṣu ratirbhavet ||
reference: ‘Old age, disease, and death — if these three things did not exist, I too should find my enjoyment in the objects that please the mind.
baseline: If there is no disease or death in the three parts of the body then it should be considered as a disease.
morphology: If there is no disease or death then it is threefold. I should also be aware of these things.

sanskrit: nityaṃ yadyapi hi strīṇāmetadeva vapurbhavet | sasaṃvitkasya kāmeṣu tathāpi na ratiḥ kṣamā ||
reference: ‘Yet even though this beauty of women were to remain perpetual, still delight in the pleasures of desire would not be worthy of the wise man.
baseline: One should always worship the goddess of women. One would never forgive her for the desires of her husband.
morphology: One should always worship women with the same devotion. One would never forgive the wife for her lusts.

sanskrit: yadā tu jarayā pītaṃ rūpamāsāṃ bhaviṣyati | ātmano 'pyanabhipretaṃ mohāttatra ratirbhavet ||
reference: ‘But since their beauty will be drunk up by old age, to delight therein through infatuation cannot be a thing approved even by thyself.
baseline: When the form of the soul is formed by the burning of the jar it becomes the month. The spirit should be worshipped in the month of Rāti.
morphology: When the form of the soul is formed by the burning of the jar it becomes the month of the month. It should be placed at the place where the spirit desires to be destroyed.

sanskrit: mṛtyuvyādhijarādharmo mṛtyuvyādhijarātmabhiḥ | ramamāṇo 'pyasaṃvignaḥ samāno mṛgapakṣibhiḥ ||
reference: ‘He who himself subject to death, disease, and old age, can sport undisturbed with those whose very nature implies death, disease, and old age, such a man is on a level with birds and beasts.
baseline: One who is suffering from death disease religion death diseases evil spirits pleasure pleasure and affliction should be accompanied by birds of prey.
morphology: One should worship the gods of the earth and the spirits of the dead and the birds of prey.

sanskrit: yadapyāttha mahātmānaste 'pi kāmātmakā iti | saṃvego 'tra na kartavyo yadā teṣāmapi kṣayaḥ ||
reference: ‘And as for what thou sayest as to even those great men having become victims to desire, do not be bewildered by them, for destruction was also their lot.
baseline: If they are of a great spirit then they are called lustful. When they do not grow fast enough they also become weak.
morphology: If they are of a great spirit then they are said to be lustful. When they are not able to do so they also become weak.

sanskrit: māhātmyaṃ na ca tanmanye yatra sāmānyataḥ kṣayaḥ | viṣayeṣu prasaktirvā yuktirvā nātmavattayā ||
reference: ‘Real greatness is not to be found there, where there is universally destruction, or where there is attachment to earthly objects, or a want of self-control.
baseline: One who does not possess the greatness or the power of the spirit would generally lose it. One who is interested in the matter would be able to do so by the means of the master.
morphology: One who does not have the greatness of the mind would generally lose it. One who is interested in the things would be able to do so with the wisdom of the soul.

sanskrit: yadapyātthānṛtenāpi strījane vartyatāmiti | anṛtaṃ nāvagacchāmi dākṣiṇyenāpi kiṃcana ||
reference: ‘And when thou sayest, “Let one deal with women even by guile,” I know nought about guile, even if it be accompanied with courtesy.
baseline: If a woman has not been married she should go to the right side of the ship.
morphology: If a woman has not gone to the right side of the river she should go to the left side.

sanskrit: na cānuvartanaṃ tanme rucitaṃ yatra nārjavam | sarvabhāvena saṃparko yadi nāsti dhigastu tat ||
reference: ‘That compliance too with a woman’s wishes pleases me not, if truthfulness be not there; if there be not a union with one’s whole soul and nature, then “out upon it” say I.
baseline: One who does not like to walk on the path of the moon and does not have contact with all the elements would be a bad person.
morphology: One who does not like to walk on the path of the moon and does not have contact with all the elements would be a bad person.

sanskrit: anṛte śraddadhānasya saktasyādoṣadarśinaḥ | kiṃ hi vaṃcayitavyaṃ syājjātarāgasya cetasaḥ ||
reference: ‘A soul overpowered by passion, believing in falsehood, carried away by attachment and blind to the faults of its objects, — what is there in it worth being deceived?
baseline: One who has not been able to pay attention to the matter would be able to avoid it. One who is not willing to do so would be deprived of the knowledge of the king.
morphology: One who has not been able to pay heed to the orders of the king should be punished with the same punishment.

sanskrit: vaṃcayaṃti ca yadyeva jātarāgāḥ parasparam | nanu naiva kṣamaṃ draṣṭuṃ narāḥ strīṇāṃ nṛṇām striyaḥ ||
reference: ‘And if the victims of passion do deceive one another, — are not men unfit for women to look at and women for men?
baseline: If one does not forgive each other the wives of the men and women of the women should be seen to forgive.
morphology: If a man does not forgive another he would be wronged. The men would be better off than the women and the women would be worse off.

sanskrit: tadevaṃ sati duḥkhārttaṃ jarāmaraṇabhoginam | na māṃ kāmeṣvanāryeṣu pratārayitumarhasi ||
reference: Since then these things are so, thou surely wouldest not lead me astray into ignoble pleasures, — me afflicted by sorrow, and subject to old age and death?
baseline: Having done so one would suffer and suffer death. One would not be deceived by me in the matter of lusts.
morphology: Having done so one would suffer and suffer death. One would not be deceived by me in the matter of desires.

sanskrit: aho 'tidhīraṃ balavacca te manaścaleṣu kāmeṣu ca sāradarśinaḥ | bhaye 'pi tīvre viṣayeṣu sajjase nirīkṣamāṇo maraṇādhvani prajāḥ ||
reference: ‘Ah! thy mind must be very firm and strong, if thou canst find substance in the transitory pleasures of sense; even in the midst of violent alarm thou canst cling to worldly objects, when thou seest all created beings in the road of death.
baseline: O king those who are strong in their hearts and their lusts and fearful in their affairs and are ready for death should be seen by the people.
morphology: O king of the earth those who are strong in heart in lust and in mind are afraid of death. Those who are ready for such a thing are afraid.

sanskrit: ahaṃ punarbhīruratīvaviklavo jarāvipadvyādhibhayaṃ viciṃtayan | labhe na śāṃtiṃ na dhṛtiṃ kuto ratiṃ niśāmayan dīptamivāgninā jagat ||
reference: ‘But I am fearful and exceedingly bewildered, as I ponder the terrors of old age, death, and disease; I can find no peace, no self-command, much less can I find pleasure, while I see the world as it were ablaze with fire.
baseline: I am again fearful fearful and restless. There is no peace in the world. Neither is there any fear in the earth nor is there a fear of fire.
morphology: I am again fearful fearful and restless. There is no peace in the world. The world is like the fire.

sanskrit: asaṃśayaṃ mṛtyuriti prajānato narasya rāgo hṛdi yasya jāyate | ayomayīṃ tasya paraimi cetanāṃ mahābhaye rakṣati yo na roditi ||
reference: ‘If desire arises in the heart of the man, who knows that death is certain, — I think that his soul must be made of iron, who restrains it in this great terror and does not weep.’
baseline: The heart of a man whose anger is caused by the death of an immortal person and who does not weep should be protected from the fear of the enemy.
morphology: One whose heart is angry with a man who dies without having any fear of death one who does not cry should protect his consciousness from the fear of the enemy.

sanskrit: athau kumāraśca viniścayātmikāṃ cakāra kāmāśrayaghātinīṃ kathām | janasya cakṣurgamanīyamaṃḍalo mahīdharaṃ cāstamiyāya bhāskaraḥ ||
reference: Then the prince uttered a discourse full of resolve and abolishing the objects of desire; and the lord of day, whose orb is the worthy centre of human eyes, departed to the Western Mountain.
baseline: Having said this the priest should make a sacrifice for the protection of the eyes of the people. The priest should also make an offering for the worship of the lord.
morphology: Having said this a priest should be made to see the eyes of a man and a priest who is a devotee of a great god.

sanskrit: tato vṛthādhāritabhūṣaṇasrajaḥ kalāguṇaiśca praṇayaiśca niṣphalaiḥ | sva eva bhāve vinigṛhya manmathaṃ puraṃ yayurbhagnamanorathāḥ striyaḥ ||
reference: And the women, having worn their garlands and ornaments in vain, with their graceful arts and endearments all fruitless, concealing their love deep in their hearts, returned to the city with broken hopes.
baseline: Then a woman who has made a vow of oblivion and love for a man of good qualities would become unfruitful. Having said that in her own spirit she should take the sacred thread of the city and the voice of a man who has become a virgin.
morphology: Then a woman who has made a vow of gold and gold based on the wasteful things and having made love with the virtues of art would become unfruitful. Having made her own vow she should take the mantras of the king and the king of the virgins.

sanskrit: tataḥ purodyānagatāṃ janaśriyaṃ nirīkṣya sāyaṃ pratisaṃhṛtāṃ punaḥ | anityatāṃ sarvagatāṃ viciṃtayan viveśa dhiṣṇyaṃ kṣitipālakātmajaḥ ||
reference: Having thus seen the beauty of the troop of women who had gone out to the city-garden, now withdrawn in the evening, — the prince, pondering the transitoriness which envelopes all things, entered his dwelling.
baseline: Then the priest should visit the garden and observe the shelter of the people in the evening. Then again he should be beaten again. Then the disciple should be killed by the enemy.
morphology: Then the priest should visit the garden and observe the shelter of the people in the evening. Then again he should be beaten in the night. Then he should worship the goddess Vivaśa. He should be destroyed.

sanskrit: tato mārabalaṃ jitvā dhairyeṇa ca śamena ca | paramārthaṃ vijijñāsuḥ sa dadhyau dhyānakovidaḥ ||
reference: Then, having conquered the hosts of Māra by his firmness and calmness, he the great master of meditation set himself to meditate, longing to know the supreme end.
baseline: Having thus conquered the battle force with courage he would be able to overcome it with the knowledge of the Supreme Being. He would become meditative.
morphology: Having thus conquered the forces of Marārā he becomes calm with courage and knowledge for the sake of the Supreme Being.

sanskrit: sarveṣu dhyānavidhiṣu prāpya caiśvaryamuttamam | sasmāra prathame yāme pūrvajanmaparaṃparām ||
reference: And having attained the highest mastery in all kinds of meditation, he remembered in the first watch the continuous series of all his former births.
baseline: Having attained all the meditative practices one should first observe the tradition of the previous birth.
morphology: Having attained all the meditative practices one would get the best of wealth. One should first follow the tradition of previous birth.

sanskrit: amutrāhamayaṃ nāma cyutastasmādihāgataḥ | iti janmasahasrāṇi sasmārānubhavanniva ||
reference: ‘In such a place I was so and so by name, and from thence I passed and came hither,’ thus he remembered his thousands of births, experiencing each as it were over again.
baseline: One who gives birth to a thousand children would be blessed with the name Amrutra.
morphology: One who gives birth to a thousand children would get the name of the mother.

sanskrit: smṛtvā janma ca mṛtyuṃ ca tāsu tāsūpapattiṣu | tataḥ sattveṣu kāruṇyaṃ cakāra karuṇātmakaḥ ||
reference: And having remembered each birth and each death in all those various transmigrations, the compassionate one then felt compassion for all living beings.
baseline: One who remembers the birth and death of a person would be blessed with the same. Then he would have mercy on the seven others.
morphology: One who remembers the birth and death of a person would be blessed with the same. Then one would be merciless by doing mercy on those who are seven.

sanskrit: kṛtveha svajanotsargaṃ punaranyatra ca kriyāḥ | atrāṇaḥ khalu loko 'yaṃ paribhramati cakravat ||
reference: Having wilfully rejected the good guides in this life and done all kinds of actions in various lives, this world of living beings rolls on helplessly, like a wheel.
baseline: One who has done this would again go to his own people and perform the same action here and there. One who does this would go around the world like a wheel.
morphology: One who has done this would go to his own people and again to another place. One who does this would be moving around like a wheel.

sanskrit: ityevaṃ smaratastasya babhūva niyatātmanaḥ | kadalīgarbhaniḥsāraḥ saṃsāra iti niścayaḥ ||
reference: As he thus remembered, to him in his strong self-control came the conviction, ‘All existence is insubstantial, like the fruit of a plantain.’
baseline: It is thus remembered as the abode of destiny. It is said to be the world without bananas and garbha.
morphology: It is thus remembered as the end of the world. It is said to be the world without bananas and garbha.

sanskrit: dvitīye tvāgate yāme so 'dvitīyaparākramaḥ | divyaṃ cakṣuḥ paraṃ lebhe sarvacakṣuṣmatāṃ varaḥ ||
reference: When the second watch came, he, possessed of unequalled energy, received a pre-eminent divine sight, like the highest of all sight-gifted beings.
baseline: The second eye should be the second in the order of its occurrence. The divine eye should then be placed on the left side of the head and all other parts of the body as a gift.
morphology: The second one comes to you in the second order. The divine eye should be placed on the left side of the head and all other parts of the body.

sanskrit: tatastena sa divyena pariśuddhena cakṣuṣā | dadarśa nikhilaṃ lokamādarśa iva nirmale ||
reference: Then by that divine perfectly pure sight he beheld the whole world as in a spotless mirror.
baseline: Then the eyes are purified by the divine. The eyes are pure and the eyes of the world are pure.
morphology: Then he should be cleansed of the eyes by the divine. The eyes should be as pure as the eyes of the world.

sanskrit: sattvānāṃ paśyatastasya nikṛṣṭotkṛṣṭakarmaṇām | pracyutiṃ copapattiṃ ca vavṛdhe karuṇātmatā ||
reference: As he saw the various transmigrations and rebirths of the various beings with their several lower or higher merits from their actions, compassion grew up more within him.
baseline: One would see the virtues of those who do evil and good deeds. One would get the gift of a cow and the spirit of compassion would increase.
morphology: One would see the virtues of the god the evil and the good deeds of the lord the good things of the king and the mercies of the kingdom.

sanskrit: ime duṣkṛtakarmāṇaḥ prāṇino yāṃti durgatim | ime 'nye śubhakarmāṇaḥ pratiṣṭhaṃte tripiṣṭape ||
reference: ‘These living beings, under the influence of evil actions, pass into wretched worlds, — these others, under the influence of good actions, go forward in heaven.
baseline: This is the deed of evil. The deception of the living entity is said to be good. This deed should be placed in the three parts of the temple.
morphology: One who has done this evil deed would get evil deeds. He would get good deed on the three sides of the temple.

sanskrit: upapannāḥ pratibhaye narake bhṛśadāruṇe | amī duḥkhairbahuvidhaiḥ pīḍyaṃte kṛpaṇaṃ vata ||
reference: ‘The one, being born in a dreadful hell full of terrors, are miserably tortured, alas! by many kinds of suffering;
baseline: O suba pāṇa one who is blessed with the gift of goodness will go to hell and suffer from many problems. One who is afflicted with misfortune and many other things will get the grace.
morphology: O subāpāṇa one who is blessed with the gift of goodness who is in hell and who is afflicted with many problems and afflictions.

sanskrit: pāyyaṃte kvathitaṃ kecidagnivarṇamayorasam | āropyaṃte ruvaṃto 'nye niṣṭaptastaṃbhamāyasam ||
reference: ‘Some are made to drink molten iron of the colour of fire, others are lifted aloft screaming on a red-hot iron pillar;
baseline: One who has made a fire or a stone of the colour of fire is said to be the one who has broken it. One who is not a pillar should be charged with the same.
morphology: The pyre should be boiled in the same way as the pyre and the fire should be painted with the same colour. The pillar should be placed on the same side as that on the other side.

sanskrit: pacyaṃte piṣṭavatkecidayaskuṃbhīṣvavāṅmukhāḥ | dahyaṃte karuṇaṃ keciddīpteṣvaṃgārarāśiṣu ||
reference: ‘Others are baked like flour, thrown with their heads downwards into iron jars; others are miserably burned in heaps of heated charcoal;
baseline: One should eat five pieces of butter and one piece of water with the mouth facing the face. One should offer some pieces of gold in the form of fire.
morphology: One should eat five pieces of butter and one piece of water with the mouth facing the face of the head. One should offer mercy on the other parts of the body.

sanskrit: kecittīkṣṇairayodaṃṣṭrairbhakṣyaṃte dāruṇaiḥ śvabhiḥ | keciddhṛṣṭairayastuṃḍairvāyasairāyasairiva ||
reference: ‘Some are devoured by fierce dreadful dogs with iron teeth, others by gloating crows with iron beaks and all made as it were of iron;
baseline: A person who has not seen the eye has to face the earth. He would be facing the earth tomorrow. Some would have seen the sky. One would have to face heaven and earth.
morphology: A child should be made to see the eyes of a cow and eat the food of the mother. Some of the children should be taken to the temple of the goddess Sārāya.

sanskrit: keciddāhapariśrāṃtāḥ śītacchāyābhikāṃkṣiṇaḥ | asipatraṃ vanaṃ nīlaṃ baddhā iva viśaṃtyamī ||
reference: ‘Some, wearied of being burned, long for cold shade; these enter like bound captives into a dark blue wood with swords for leaves.
baseline: A small forest should be covered with blue leaves with a small piece of cloth and covered with cold cloth.
morphology: A small forest should be covered with blue leaves and covered with green leaves.

sanskrit: pāṭyaṃte dāruvat kecitkuṭhārairbahubāhavaḥ | duḥkhe 'pi na vipadyaṃte karmabhirdhāritāsavaḥ ||
reference: ‘Others having many arms are split like timber with axes, but even in that agony they do not die, being supported in their vital powers by their previous actions.
baseline: O Bahu the sons of Bahu and others who are in a certain room and are in distress should drink in the garden. They should not suffer in the absence of work.
morphology: One who drinks in a small room should not suffer from misfortune. One who does not suffer in the absence of work should drink in the same room.

sanskrit: sukhaṃ syāditi yatkarma kṛtaṃ duḥkhanivṛttaye | phalaṃ tasyedamavaśairduḥkhamevopabhujyate ||
reference: ‘Whatever deed was done only to hinder pain with the hope that it might bring pleasure, its result is now experienced by these helpless victims as simple pain.
baseline: One who has done a good deed would get the result of the misfortune. One who does so would also get the benefit of the ill-will.
morphology: The result of any act done to bring happiness and sorrow would be the same as that done to a person who has suffered a loss.

sanskrit: sukhārthamaśubhaṃ kṛtvā ya ete bhṛśaduḥkhitāḥ | āsvādaḥ sa kimeteṣāṃ karoti sukhamaṇvapi ||
reference: These who did something evil for the sake of pleasure and are now grievously pained, — does that old taste produce even an atom of pleasure to them now?
baseline: One who has done good deeds for the sake of happiness and those who have been afflicted by it would enjoy them. One who does good deeds would also enjoy it.
morphology: One who has made these things pleasant and pleasant and who has been afflicted by them would enjoy them and make them happy.

sanskrit: hasadbhiryatkṛtaṃ karma kaluṣaṃ kaluṣātmabhiḥ | etatpariṇate kāle krośadbhiranubhūyate ||
reference: ‘The wicked deed which was done by the wicked-hearted in glee, — its consequences are reaped by them in the fulness of time with cries.
baseline: The evil deeds done by the evil spirits are said to be evil. In such a situation one would feel the evil spirit in the past.
morphology: The evil deeds done by the evil spirits are said to be evil. In such a situation one would feel the evil spirit.

sanskrit: yadyeva pāpakarmāṇaḥ paśyeyuḥ karmaṇāṃ phalam | vameyuruṣṇarudhiraṃ marmasvabhihatā iva ||
reference: ‘If only evil doers could see the fruits of their actions, they would vomit hot blood as if they were smitten in a vital part.
baseline: If any of the sins are committed the result of the actions should be considered as the merits of the marriage.
morphology: If one does any sinful deed he will get the fruits of his deed. He will get water from the sun and blood as if he were married.

sanskrit: śārīrebhyo 'pi duḥkhebhyo nārakebhyo manasvinaḥ | anāryaiḥ saha saṃvāso mama kṛcchratamo mataḥ || |
reference: ‘And worse still than all these bodily tortures in hell seems to me the association of an intelligent man with the base.
baseline: One who has made his own soul fit for the body sorrow hell desire and others would be able to live with the non-beings.
morphology: One who has made his mind fit for the misery of the body for the hell and for the death of the enemy and for his association with the strangers is said to be my abode.

sanskrit: ime 'nye karmabhiścitraiścittavispaṃdasaṃbhavaiḥ | tiryagyonau vicitrāyāmupapannāstapasvinaḥ ||
reference: ‘Others also, through various actions arising from the spasmodic violence of their minds, are born miserable in the wombs of various beasts.
baseline: These are the deeds of the gods the gifts and the things which are possible. The gods of the world are strange and evil.
morphology: These are the deeds of the gods the gifts and the things which are possible. The gods of the world are strange. They should be worshipped.

sanskrit: māṃsatvagbāladaṃtārthaṃ vairādapi madādapi | hanyaṃte kṛpaṇā yatra baṃdhūnāṃ paśyatāmapi ||
reference: ‘There the poor wretches are killed even in the sight of their kindred, for the sake of their flesh, their skin, their hair, or their teeth, or through hatred or for mere pleasure.
baseline: One who has not eaten meat or other meat should also offer a gift to the enemy. One who does not eat meat or eat food should also seek the mercy of his kinsmen.
morphology: One who has not been able to bear the loss of a brother or a brother would also get the benefit of the enemy for the sake of the sacrifice.

sanskrit: aśaknuvaṃto 'pyavaśāḥ kṣuttarṣaśramapīḍitāḥ | go 'śvabhūtāśca vāhyaṃte pratodakṣatamūrtayaḥ ||
reference: ‘Even though powerless and helpless, oppressed by hunger, thirst, and fatigue, they are driven along as oxen and horses, their bodies wounded with goads.
baseline: The cow should be offered to the lord as a gift and the cow should not be taken away from him.
morphology: The cow should be kept in a safe place in the form of a cow and should be offered to the poor.

sanskrit: vāhyaṃte gajabhūtāśca balīyāṃso 'pi durbalaiḥ | aṃkuśakliṣṭamūrdhānastāḍitāḥ pādapārṣṇibhiḥ ||
reference: ‘They are driven along, when born as elephants, by weaker creatures than themselves for all their strength, — their heads tormented by the hook and their bodies kicked by foot and heel.
baseline: The outer part of the elephant should be covered with a piece of cloth and the outer part should be made of cloth. The head should be tied with a rope and the feet should be fastened together.
morphology: The outer part of the elephant should be covered with a piece of cloth and the other parts should be kept under the feet.

sanskrit: satsvapyanyeṣu duḥkheṣu duḥkhaṃ yatra viśeṣataḥ | parasparavirodhācca parādhīnatayaiva ca ||
reference: ‘And with all these other miseries there is an especial misery arising from mutual enmity and from subjection to a master.
baseline: One would get misery in the absence of good and bad things and especially in the case of mutual contradictions and subjugation.
morphology: One should be able to bear the miseries of others in the same way. One would get the opposites and subjugation in particular.

sanskrit: khasthāḥ khasthairhi bādhyaṃte jalasthā jalacāribhiḥ | sthalasthāḥ sthalasaṃsthaistu prāpyaṃte cetaretaraiḥ ||
reference: ‘Air-dwellers are oppressed by air-dwellers, the denizens of water by the denizens of water, those that dwell on dry land are made to suffer by the dwellers on dry land in mutual hostility.
baseline: One gets the position of the ground by the servants of the water after having toil hard. The position of land is obtained by the officers of the other departments.
morphology: One gets the position of land by the servants of water after having toil hard. One gets that position by the officers of water and other agencies.

sanskrit: upapannāstathā ceme mātsaryākrāṃtacetasaḥ | pitṛloke nirāloke kṛpaṇaṃ bhuṃjate phalam ||
reference: ‘And others there are who, when born again, with their minds filled with envy, reap the miserable fruit of their actions in a world of the Pitṛs destitute of all light;
baseline: One who subconsciously offers a gift to the mother wife wife and children will get the fruit of the mercies in the world of the father without any fear.
morphology: One who subconsciously practices the abode of the gods the king of the earth and the kingdom of the king should be worshipped in the open sky. One who does good in the world of the father would get the fruit.

sanskrit: sūcīchidropamamukhāḥ parvatopamakukṣayaḥ | kṣuttarṣajanitairduḥkhaiḥ pīḍyaṃte duḥkhabhāginaḥ ||
reference: ‘Having mouths as small as the eye of a needle and bellies as big as a mountain, these miserable wretches are tortured with the pains of hunger and thirst.
baseline: The faces of the mountains are made to be pierced by the threads and the faces are broken by the axe. Those who suffer from the wrath of the king are afflicted by the sorrows.
morphology: Those facing the mountains and mountains should be shaken with the threads and cut open and the others suffering from the wrath of the king should be grieved.

sanskrit: puruṣo yadi jānīta mātsaryasyedṛśaṃ phalam | sarvathā śivivaddadyāccharīrāvayavānapi ||
reference: ‘If a man only knew that such was the consequence of selfishness, he would always give to others even pieces of his own body like Śibi.
baseline: If the man knows the fruit of the mother he will get the fruit. He will have to give the body of both the devotees in all circumstances.
morphology: If the man knows that he is the mother of all beings he will get the same result. He would have the body of both the sons of Śiva.

sanskrit: āśayā samabhikrāṃtā ghāryamāṇāḥ svakarmabhiḥ | labhaṃte na hyamī bhoktuṃ pravṛddhānyaśucīnyapi ||
reference: ‘Rushing up filled with hope but held back by their former deeds, they try in vain to eat anything large, however impure.
baseline: One should not eat food without having the desire to enjoy it. One would not get it by doing his own work. One should never eat food and increase it even if he is unclean.
morphology: One should not be afraid of others by their actions. One would not be able to eat food and grow even if one does not clean it.

sanskrit: ime 'nye narakaṃ prāpya garbhasaṃjñe 'śucihrade | upapannā manuṣyeṣu duḥkhamarchaṃti jaṃtavaḥ ||
reference: ‘Others, having found a hell in an impure lake called the womb, are born amongst men and there suffer anguish.
baseline: Having attained this hell the womb should be placed in the sacred pit. The animals should be offered gifts to men for the remission of sorrow.
morphology: Having attained this hell one should conceive in the holy cave. The animals which are the victims of misery and misery should be worshipped in the upper room.

sanskrit: sa rājavatsaḥ pṛthupīnavakṣāstau havyamaṃtrādhikṛtau vihāya | uttīrya gaṃgāṃ pracalattaraṃgāṃ śrīmadgṛhaṃ rājagṛhaṃ jagāma ||
reference: The prince, he of the broad and lusty chest, having thus dismissed the minister and the priest, crossed the Ganges with its speeding waves and went to Rājagṛha with its beautiful palaces.
baseline: The king is the king the king and the king of the king's house. The king should be the king. He should go up and down to the Ganges and move to the upper court. The lord should visit the palace.
morphology: The king should visit the king's palace. He should leave the earth the earth and the earth together with the powers of the king the river Ganga and the king.

sanskrit: śailaiḥ suguptaṃ ca vibhūṣitaṃ ca dhṛtaṃ ca pūtaṃ ca śivaistapodaiḥ | paṃcācalāṃkaṃ nagaraṃ prapede śāṃtaḥ svayaṃbhūriva nākapṛṣṭham ||
reference: He reached the city distinguished by the five hills, well guarded and adorned with mountains, and supported and hallowed by auspicious sacred places, — like Brahman in a holy calm going to the uppermost heaven.
baseline: The sun should be placed on the top of the hill and the feet should be adorned with the prasadam and the leaves of the goddess Śiva. The five chalks of the city should be kept quiet in the open air and the nose should be covered by the nose.
morphology: The sun should be set on the rocks and adorned with flowers. The feet should be placed on the feet of Lord Śiva. The five chalks should be fixed on the sides of the city and the nose should be kept calm.

sanskrit: gāṃbhīryamojaśca niśāmya tasya vapuśca dīptaṃ puruṣānatītya | visismiye tatra janastadānīṃ sthāṇuvratasyeva vṛṣadhvajasya ||
reference: Having heard of his majesty and strength, and his splendid beauty, surpassing all other men, the people of that region were all astonished as at him who has a bull for his sign and is immovable in his vow.
baseline: Having taken away the glory and glory of the Lord one should bring forth a man who is bright in the sky. One should stand there on the twenty-second day. One of the bulls should be placed on the flag.
morphology: Having drawn the image of the great man the light of his body should be brought to the man. The light should be placed there in the evening and the flag of a bull should be raised at that time.

sanskrit: taṃ prekṣya yo 'nyena yayau sa tasthau yaścātra tasthau pathi so 'nvagacchat | drutaṃ yayau yaṃ sadayaṃ sadhīraṃ yaḥ kaścidāste sma sa cotpapāta ||
reference: On seeing him, he who was going elsewhere stood still, and he who was standing there followed him in the way; he who was walking gently and gravely ran quickly, and he who was sitting at once sprang up.
baseline: One who sends him should go to the place where he is going with others. One who goes quickly one who is righteous and hastens the path would fall down.
morphology: He who sends him away with another person should go to the same place where he went. He who goes quickly and hastens the path would fall into the pit.

sanskrit: kaścittamānarca janaḥ karābhyāṃ satkṛtya kaścicchirasā vavaṃde | snigdhena kaścidvacasābhyanaṃdannaivaṃ jagāmāpratipūjya kaścit ||
reference: Some people reverenced him with their hands, others in worship saluted him with their heads, some addressed him with affectionate words, — not one went on without paying him homage.
baseline: One who has done good by doing good with the penance of a knight one who has made a wish one with a penitentiary and one who worships the jagāma after having done good.
morphology: One who has done good by doing good by the words of the lord one who has made a wish another one who is pleased by the word of the Lord another who has worshipped the Lord of the earth by doing evil by doing a good deed and one who does not have a desire to do evil.

sanskrit: taṃ jihriyuḥ prekṣya vicitraveṣāḥ prakīrṇavācaḥ pathi maunamīyuḥ | dharmasya sākṣādiva saṃnikarṣānna kaścidanyāyamatirbabhūva ||
reference: Those who were wearing gay-coloured dresses were ashamed when they saw him, those who were talking on random subjects fell to silence on the road; no one indulged in an improper thought, as at the presence of Religion herself embodied.
baseline: Having sent him away by the jihri one should wear strange clothes and speak in silence on the way. On the day of the testimony of righteousness one would be judged by the judge.
morphology: Having sent him away by the jihri one should be silent on the way with strange clothes and scattering words. One should not be a judge except by the testimony of righteousness.

sanskrit: anyakriyāṇāmapi rājamārge strīṇāṃ nṛṇāṃ vā bahumānapūrvam | tadeva kalpaṃ naradevasūtraṃ nirīkṣamāṇā na tu tasya dṛṣṭiḥ ||
reference: In the men and the women on the highway, even though they were intent on other business, that conduct alone with the profoundest reverence seemed proper which is enjoined by the rules of royal homage; but his eyes never looked upon them.
baseline: One should not observe the image of a male god by any other action or by the way of the king or by any honorable person. The same is the view of the male god.
morphology: One should not observe the manifestations of gods and men in the same manner as those of women and women on the way to the king.

sanskrit: bhruvau lalāṭaṃ mukhamīkṣaṇaṃ vā vapuḥ karau vā caraṇau gatiṃ vā | yadeva yastasya dadarśa tatra tadeva tasyānubabaṃdha cakṣuḥ ||
reference: His brows, his forehead, his mouth, or his eyes, — his body, his hands, his feet, or his gait, — whatever part of him any one beheld, that at once riveted his eyes.
baseline: The eye should be made to look at the face with the forehead forehead or feet and the movement of the feet. If one has a sight of the eye the eye should remain connected with it.
morphology: The eye should be closed in the face with the forehead facing the face the feet facing the feet or the feet moving. If one has a sight of the eye the eye should remain connected with the eye.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā śubhorṇabhruvamāyatākṣaṃ jvalaccharīraṃ śubhajālahastam | taṃ bhikṣuveśaṃ kṣitipālanārhaṃ saṃcukṣubhe rājagṛhasya lakṣmīḥ ||
reference: Having beheld him with the beautiful circle of hair between his brows and with long eyes, with his radiant body and his hands showing a graceful membrane between the fingers, — so worthy of ruling the earth and yet wearing a mendicant’s dress, — the Goddess of Rājagṛha was herself perturbed.
baseline: Having seen the image of the celestial body with the bright colour of the forehead the body of the fire the hands of the goddess should be kept in a safe place. Having worshipped the beggar the goddess of the king's house should be circumcised.
morphology: Having seen the image of the celestial body with the bright colour of the forehead the body of the fire and the hands of the goddess should be kept in a safe place. Having worshipped the beggar the goddess of the king's house should be worshipped in a quiet place.

sanskrit: śreṇyo 'tha bhartā magadhājirasya vāhyādvimānādvipulaṃ janaugham | dadarśa papraccha ca tasya hetuṃ tatastamasmai puruṣaḥ śaśaṃsa ||
reference: Then Śreṇya, the lord of the court of the Magadhas, beheld from the outside of his palace the immense concourse of people, and asked the reason of it; and thus did a man recount it to him:
baseline: The king of Magadha should pay tribute to the king of the kingdom of the east and the king the king and his wife. The king should pay homage to him.
morphology: The king of Magadha should pay tribute to the king of the kingdom of Gāṇḍhā the king who had built a palace on the outer side of the earth and had built the palace of the king. The king should pay homage to that man.

sanskrit: jñānaṃ paraṃ vā pṛthivīśriyaṃ vā viprairya ukto 'dhigamiṣyatīti | sa eva śākyādhipatestanūjo nirīkṣyate pravrajito janena ||
reference: ‘He who was thus foretold by the Brāhmans, “he will either attain supreme wisdom or the empire of the earth,” — it is he, the son of the king of the Śākyas, who is the ascetic whom the people are gazing at.’
baseline: One who is said to be above knowledge or the kingdom of the earth or the mighty one would come. He would be the master of the power. The king would see that man who has gone away would go away.
morphology: One who is said to be above knowledge or earthly abode and has great fortitude will come. He who is the master of the power will see the man who has departed from him.

sanskrit: tataḥ śrutārtho manasā gatārtho rājā babhāṣe puruṣaṃ tameva | vijñāyatāṃ kva pratigacchatīti tathetyathainaṃ puruṣo 'nvagacchat ||
reference: The king, having heard this and perceived its meaning with his mind, thus at once spoke to that man: ‘Let it be known whither he is going;’ and the man, receiving the command, followed the prince.
baseline: Then the king should explain the meaning of the voice and the man in the speech. He should know who is going back. Then the man should go back.
morphology: Then the king should explain the meaning of the words and the man should be called the king. He should know who is going to return. Then the person should go to the king as far as possible.

sanskrit: alolacakṣuryugamātradarśī nivṛttavāgyaṃtritamaṃdagāmī | cacāra bhikṣāṃ sa tu bhikṣuvaryo nidhāya gātrāṇi calaṃ ca cetaḥ ||
reference: With unrestless eyes, seeing only a yoke’s length before him, with his voice hushed, and his walk slow and measured, he, the noblest of mendicants, went begging alms, keeping his limbs and his wandering thoughts under control.
baseline: The seer who sees the image of a beggar would return to his home and go to the temple. He would give the beggars a begging bag and would make a bequest and move his feet.
morphology: The seer who sees the image of a beggar should return to his home and go to the temple. He should offer alms to the beggars. He would give alms and move his feet.

sanskrit: ādāya bhaikṣaṃ ca yathopapannaṃ yayau gireḥ prasravaṇaṃ viviktam | nyāyena tatrābhyavahṛtya cainanmahīdharaṃ pāṃḍavamāruroha ||
reference: Having received such alms as were offered, he retired to a lonely cascade of the mountain; and having eaten it there in the fitting manner, he ascended the mountain Pāṇḍava.
baseline: Having obtained the income and the food obtained from the mountain the waters of the mountain should be separated from the river. Having gone from there with justice the king of the Pandavas should be made to sit in peace.
morphology: The king of the Pandavas should make a sacrifice of the same amount of money as he earns by the fall of the mountain. Having gone from there with justice he should be made to climb the mountain of Pandava.

sanskrit: tasminvane lodhravanopagūḍhe mayūranādapratipūrṇakuṃje | kāṣāyavāsāḥ sa babhau nṛsūryo yathodayasyopari bālasūryaḥ ||
reference: In that wood, thickly filled with lodhra trees, having its thickets resonant with the notes of the peacocks, he the sun of mankind shone, wearing his red dress, like the morning sun above the eastern mountain.
baseline: In that forest there should be a lotus tree and a peacock tree in the temple full of flowers. The king should be the son of a cow and the king of a boy should be placed on the temple.
morphology: In that forest there should be a lotus tree and a peacock tree in a well full of flowers. He should be the son of the king of the cow and the son or son of a sun.

sanskrit: tatraivamālokya sa rājabhṛtyaḥ śreṇyāya rājñe kathayāṃ cakāra | saṃśrutya rājā sa ca bāhumānyāttatra pratasthe nibhṛtānuyātraḥ ||
reference: That royal attendant, having thus watched him there, related it all to the king Śreṇya; and the king, when he heard it, in his deep veneration, started himself to go thither with a modest retinue.
baseline: Having seen the king the servant of the king should speak to the king for the sake of his rank. Having said this the king would go back and forth on his journey.
morphology: Having seen the king the king's servant said to the king that he should be of good standing. Having agreed with him he went on his journey in a quiet place.

sanskrit: sa pāṃḍavaṃ pāṃḍavatulyavīryaḥ śailottamaṃ śailasamānavarṣmā | maulīdharaḥ siṃhagatirnṛsiṃhaścalatsaṭaḥ siṃha ivāruroha ||
reference: He who was like the Pāṇḍavas in heroism, and like a mountain in stature, ascended Pāṇḍava, that noblest of mountains, — a crown-wearer, of lion-like gait, a lion among men, as a maned lion ascends a mountain.
baseline: He is like a Pandava like a warrior like the best of rocks like that of a rock like an ox a maulidhara a lion a jaguar and a lion.
morphology: He is like a Pandava a warrior a king a ruler a lion a tiger a horse a maulidhara a mountain and a lion.

sanskrit: calasya tasyopari śṛṃgabhūtaṃ śāṃteṃdriyaṃ paśyati bodhisattvam | paryaṃkamāsthāya virocamānaṃ śaśāṃkamudyaṃtamivābhrakūṭāt ||
reference: There he beheld the Bodhisattva, resplendent as he sat on his hams, with subdued senses, as if the mountain were moving, and he himself were a peak thereof, — like the moon rising from the top of a cloud.
baseline: The bodhisattva sees the seat of tranquillity fixed on the chariot and the head above it. He has to face the circumambulation. He will face the enemy from the side of the earth.
morphology: The bodhisattva sees the seat of tranquillity fixed on the chalā and the head above it. He has to face the circumambulation of the sāśaṇaka the muṇṇa and the bhraṇakuta.

sanskrit: taṃ rūpalakṣmyā ca śamena caiva dharmasya nirmāṇamivopadiṣṭam | savismayaḥ praśrayavān nareṃdraḥ svayaṃbhuvaṃ śakra ivopatasthe ||
reference: Him, distinguished by his beauty of form and perfect tranquillity as the very creation of Religion herself, — filled with astonishment and affectionate regard the king of men approached, as Indra the self-existent (Brahman).
baseline: Having worshipped him with the garlands of the form the building of the dharma is said to have been completed. Having blessed him with a miraculous form he would be able to do so.
morphology: He should be worshipped with the garlands of roopalakshmya and shāma. He is said to have built the dharma. He would be blessed with the glory of the self.

sanskrit: taṃ nyāyato nyāyavatāṃ variṣṭhaḥ sametya papraccha ca dhātusāmyam | sa cāpyavocatsadṛśena sāmnā nṛpaṃ manaḥsvāsthyamanāmayaṃ ca ||
reference: He, the chief of the courteous, having courteously drawn nigh to him, inquired as to the equilibrium of his bodily humours; and the other with equal gentleness assured the king of his health of mind and freedom from all ailments.
baseline: He should be judged justly and the superior should be made to sit on the floor with the metal in front of him. He should face the face with the face of the face and the mind should be healthy.
morphology: He should be judged justly by the superior. Having covered his face with metal he should bow down and face the face with the face of the face and the mind.

sanskrit: tataḥ śucau vāraṇakarṇanīle śilātale 'sau niṣasāda rājā | nṛpopaviśyānumataśca tasya bhāvaṃ vijijñāsuridaṃ babhāṣe ||
reference: Then the king sat down on the clean surface of the rock, dark blue like an elephant’s ear; and being seated, with the other’s assent, he thus spoke, desiring to know his state of mind:
baseline: Then the king should be clean and made to sit on a stone of blue colour. The king should speak to the king of the king and his wife.
morphology: Then the king should be clean and made to sit on a stone of blue colour in the sky. The king should speak to the king with the voice of the prophet Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: prītiḥ parā me bhavataḥ kulena kramāgatā caiva parīkṣitā ca | jātā vivakṣā suta yā yato me tasmādidaṃ snehavaco nibodha ||
reference: ‘I have a strong friendship with thy family, come down by inheritance and well proved; since from this a desire to speak to thee, my son, has arisen in me, therefore listen to my words of affection.
baseline: Having said that after having received love from you one should come back to your family and get tested. One would get the benefit of the discrepancy. That is because he has shown affection to me.
morphology: Having said this after having been treated with your kulā in order to be pleased with you one would get the benefit of the discrepancy. That is because he has shown affection to me.

sanskrit: ādityapūrvaṃ vipulaṃ kulaṃ te navaṃ vayo dīptamidaṃ vapuśca | kasmādiyaṃ te matirakrameṇa bhaikṣāka evābhiratā na rājye ||
reference: ‘When I consider thy widespread race, beginning with the sun, thy fresh youth, and thy conspicuous beauty, — whence comes this resolve of thine so out of all harmony with the rest, set wholly on a mendicant’s life, not on a kingdom?
baseline: He should be nine years old and have a large family before the death of Aditya and should be given light. He should not be a coward in the state.
morphology: He should be nine years old and have a great family before the death of Aditya and should be given light. He should not be a coward in the kingdom.

sanskrit: gātraṃ hi te lohitacaṃdanārhaṃ kāṣāyasaṃśleṣamanarhametat | hastaḥ prajāpālanayogya eṣa bhoktuṃ na cārhaḥ paradattamannam ||
reference: ‘Thy limbs are worthy of red sandal-wood perfumes, — they do not deserve the rough contact of red cloth; this hand is fit to protect subjects, it deserves not to hold food given by another.
baseline: It is said to be the size of a stone. It should not be used for the purpose of making a bow. The hand should be made to hold a butterfly. It is better not to eat food and drink it with charu.
morphology: It is said to be the size of a stone. It should not be placed on the ground. The hands should be made to hold a flower. It is better not to place the food on the floor.

sanskrit: tatsaumya rājyaṃ yadi paitṛkaṃ tvaṃ snehātpiturnecchasi vikrameṇa | na ca kṣamaṃ marṣayituṃ matiste bhuktvārdhamasmadviṣayasya śīghram ||
reference: ‘If therefore, gentle youth, through thy love for thy father thou desirest not thy paternal kingdom in thy generosity, — then at any rate thy choice must not be excused, — accepting forthwith one half of my kingdom.
baseline: If you wish to gain the kingdom with the same kind of affection as your father you should do so with the help of Vikram. If you do not want to get forgiveness and kill him then you should pay half of that amount as soon as possible.
morphology: If you wish to gain the kingdom with the same kind of affection as your father you should do so with the help of Vikram. If you do not want to get forgiveness and kill him then you should pay half of the amount of the debt as soon as possible.

sanskrit: evaṃ hi na syātsvajanāvamardaḥ kālakrameṇāpi śamaśrayā śrīḥ | tasmātkuruṣva praṇayaṃ mayi tvaṃ sadbhiḥ sahīyā hi satāṃ samṛddhiḥ ||
reference: ‘If thou actest thus there will be no violence shown to thine own people, and by the mere lapse of time imperial power at last flies for refuge to the tranquil mind; therefore be pleased to do me a kindness, — the prosperity of the good becomes very powerful, when aided by the good.
baseline: In this way one would not get the wealth of his wife even after the passage of time. He would get the love of the wife of the son of the same name. He should get the prosperity of the husband of the daughter of that son.
morphology: In the same way one would not get wealth even after the death of a sage. One would get prosperity by having the love of a man with the same kindness and goodness.

sanskrit: atha tvidānīṃ kulagarvitatvādasmāsu viśraṃbhaguṇo na te 'sti | vyūhānyanekāni vigāhya vāṇairmayā sahāyena parāñjigīṣa ||
reference: ‘But if from thy pride of race thou dost not now feel confidence in me, then plunge with thy arrows into countless armies, and with me as thy ally seek to conquer thy foes.
baseline: Then one who has not been able to do so would become weak. He would not be able to rest on us. Having said so many things with the help of the voice he would go to the king.
morphology: Then one who has not been able to make a sacrifice would not be able to rest on us. One who has made a series of sacrifices would become a king with the help of a vāṇirma.

sanskrit: tadbuddhimatrānyatarāṃ vṛṇīṣva dharmārthakāmān vidhivadbhajasva | vyatyasya rāgādi ha hi trivargaṃ pretyeha vibhraṃśamavāpnuvaṃti ||
reference: ‘Choose thou therefore one of these ends, pursue according to rule religious merit, wealth, and pleasure; for these, love and the rest, in reverse order, are the three objects in life; when men die they pass into dissolution as far as regards this world.
baseline: Having understood these three things one should observe the ritual of charity. One should do the rāgāda of the intercession. One would do the three rāga of worship. He would do all the illusions.
morphology: Then the three things that are good for you should be known by the same wisdom. If you do not know the difference between the three parts of the raga you will get the illusion.

sanskrit: yo hyarthadharmau paripīḍya kāmaḥ syāddharmakāmye paribhūya cārthaḥ | kāmārthayoścoparameṇa dharmastyājyaḥ sa kṛtsno yadi kāṃkṣitārthaḥ ||
reference: ‘That which is pleasure when it has overpowered wealth and merit, is wealth when it has conquered merit and pleasure; so too it is merit, when pleasure and wealth fall into abeyance; but all would have to be alike abandoned, if thy desired end were obtained.
baseline: One who has attained the righteousness of the heart and has attained to the rightful self and has acquired the goodness of his own self should do so. One who acquires the rightfulness of the self and has achieved the desire of the soul should do it.
morphology: One who has attained the goal of righteousness by doing good deeds and having attained the aim of righteously doing good works should do good deeds. One who attains the goal by doing righteous deeds by doing the goal is doing good. If he has achieved that goal then he should do it.

sanskrit: tasmāttrivargasya niṣevaṇena tvaṃ rūpametatsaphalaṃ kuruṣva | dharmārthakāmādhigamaṃ hyanūnaṃ nṛṇāmanūnaṃ puruṣārthamāhuḥ ||
reference: ‘Do thou therefore by pursuing the three objects of life, cause this beauty of thine to bear its fruit; they say that when the attainment of religion, wealth, and pleasure is complete in all its parts, then the end of man is complete.
baseline: Then you will make a good profit by the offering of the same kind of food to the family. You will also get the gift of charity. The gift of the lord is to be given to the poor. The sacrifice of the poor is to give to men.
morphology: Then you will make a reward of this form by the offering of the same kind of offerings. You will get the gift of charity good deeds honor renunciation sacrifice sacrifice etc..

sanskrit: tanniṣphalau nārhasi kartumetau pīnau bhujau cāpavikarṣaṇārhau | māṃdhātṛvajjetumimau hi yogyau lokāni hi trīṇi hi kiṃ punargām ||
reference: ‘Do not thou let these two brawny arms lie useless which are worthy to draw the bow; they are well fitted like Māndhātṛ’s to conquer the three worlds, much more the earth.
baseline: One who does not eat the fruits of that fruit should be thrown into the pit of the ground and should not be beaten with the axe. One should drink the metal of that part of the earth. These are the three people who deserve it. What is the recompense?
morphology: One who does not eat the fruit of that fruit should be thrown into the pit of the pit and the ground should be covered with mud. These three men should be re-insured.

sanskrit: snehena khalvetadahaṃ bravīmi naiśvaryarāgeṇa na vismayena | imaṃ hi dṛṣṭvā tava bhikṣuveśaṃ jātānukaṃpo 'smyapi cāgatāśruḥ ||
reference: ‘I speak this to you out of affection, — not through love of dominion or through astonishment; beholding this mendicant-dress of thine, I am filled with compassion and I shed tears.
baseline: Having seen him one should bow down with affection. One should not be astonished by the appearance of the celestial body. Seeing this one would get the illusion of being a beggar. One would also come back with tears.
morphology: Having seen him one should bow down with affection. One should not be astonished by the presence of the divine god Brahma. Seeing this one one would get the illusion of being a beggar. One would also come to see him with tears.

sanskrit: tadbhuṃkṣva bhikṣāśramakāma kāmānkāle 'si kartā priyadharma dharmam | yāvatsvavaṃśapratirūparūpaṃ na te jarābhyetyabhibhūya bhūyaḥ ||
reference: ‘O thou who desirest the mendicant’s stage of life enjoy pleasures now; in due time, O thou lover of religion, thou shalt practise religion; — ere old age comes on and overcomes this thy beauty, well worthy of thy illustrious race.
baseline: One who does this should seek the labour of alms and make a wish for the same. One should do it till he becomes a member of his own clan.
morphology: One who does that should seek the labour of alms and make a sacrifice for the sake of his desire. Until he becomes the incarnation of his own clan he should be proud of his deeds.

sanskrit: śaknoti jīrṇaḥ khalu dharmamāptuṃ kāmopabhogeṣvagatirjarāyāḥ | ataśca yūnaḥ kathayaṃti kāmānmadhyasya vittaṃ sthavirasya dharmam ||
reference: ‘The old man can obtain merit by religion; old age is helpless for the enjoyment of pleasures; therefore they say that pleasures belong to the young man, wealth to the middle-aged, and religion to the old.
baseline: One who has lost his sense of self would get rid of the righteousness and enjoyment of his lusts. Therefore one would say that the wealth in the midst of the lust is the rightfulness of the one standing on the ground.
morphology: One who has lost his righteousness would get rid of his lusts and enjoyments. Therefore one would say that the wealth in the midst of lust would be the rightfulness of the rest.

sanskrit: dharmasya cārthasya ca jīvaloke pratyarthibhūtāni hi yauvanāni | saṃrakṣyamāṇānyapi durgrahāṇi kāmā yatastena yathā haraṃti ||
reference: ‘Youth in this present world is the enemy of religion and wealth, — since pleasures, however we guard them, are hard to hold, therefore, wherever pleasures are to be found, there they seize them.
baseline: These are the young men who have been placed in the world of life for the sake of righteousness and good deeds. Those who are protected should be taken to the strongholds as if they were the harantis.
morphology: These are the young men who have been placed in the world of life for the sake of righteousness and good deeds. Those who are protected should be taken to the fortifications.

sanskrit: vayāṃsi jīrṇāni vimarśayaṃti dhīrāṇyavasthānaparāyaṇāni | alpena yatnena śamātmakāni bhavaṃtyagatyeva ca lajjayā ca ||
reference: ‘Old age is prone to reflection’, it is grave and intent on remaining quiet; it attains unimpassionedness with but little effort, unavoidably, and for very shame.
baseline: One who has lost his body and has lost it would find it difficult to maintain it. One would find that with a little care one would be able to heal it and one would get it out of shame.
morphology: One who is ill should discuss the things that are going to be destroyed with patience and place. One who has done good things with a little care should speak to you with shame.

sanskrit: ataśca lolaṃ viṣayapradhānaṃ pramattamakṣāṃtamadīrghadarśi | bahucchalaṃ yauvanamabhyatītya nistīrya kāṃtāramivāśvasaṃti ||
reference: ‘Therefore having passed through the deceptive period of youth, fickle, intent on external objects, heedless, impatient, not looking at the distance, — they take breath like men who have escaped safe through a forest.
baseline: Therefore one who is lilac has the superiority of the subject matter has a superior position and has a long vision. Having attained the age of many years one who has attained the height of the lotus ceases to be able to do so.
morphology: Therefore one who has attained the height of a lotus the highest point of the subject and the longest point of view would be able to attain great heights. After having attained the age of many years one would become calm and rest on the earth.

sanskrit: tasmādadhīraṃ capalapramādi navaṃ vayastāvadidaṃ vyapaitu | kāmasya pūrvaṃ hi vayaḥ śaravyaṃ na śakyate rakṣitumiṃdriyebhyaḥ ||
reference: ‘Let therefore this fickle time of youth first pass by, reckless and giddy, — our early years are the mark for pleasure, they cannot be kept from the power of the senses.
baseline: Then the nine steps should be taken to remove it. It should be done before the desire. It is not possible to protect the senses.
morphology: Then the nine steps should be taken in front of the head and the nine feet should be covered with water. It should not be done before the body is made to be able to protect the mind.

sanskrit: athau cikīrṣā tava dharma eva yajasva yajñaṃ kuladharma eṣaḥ | yajñairadhiṣṭhāya hi nākapṛṣṭhaṃ yayau marutvānapi nākapṛṣṭham ||
reference: Or if religion is really thy one aim, then offer sacrifices, — this is thy family’s immemorial custom, — climbing to highest heaven by sacrifices, even Indra, the lord of the winds, went thus to highest heaven.
baseline: O king the sacrifice of the people is your righteousness. The worship of the family is the religion of your family. The service of the priest should be done on the sides of the nose and the death of the deceased should be on the side of the nostrils.
morphology: O king the sacrifice of your family is your righteousness. The sacrifice of the family is the righteous religion. The nose nose mouth and mouth of the deceased are the rightfuls.

sanskrit: suvarṇakeyūravidaṣṭabāhavo maṇipradīpojjvalacitramaulayaḥ | nṛparṣayastāṃ hi gatiṃ gatā makhaiḥ śrameṇa yāmeva mahārṣayo yayuḥ ||
reference: ‘With their arms pressed by golden bracelets, and their variegated diadems resplendent with the light of gems, royal sages have reached the same goal by sacrifices which great sages reached by self-mortification.’
baseline: One who goes to the great king with the labour of the makhas should go to the king with gold kayur vidṣa bāhā garland ghee lamp light bright light and other things.
morphology: One who goes to the great king with the gold kaiyur vidṣa bāhā mālī garland lamp light image maulī nirāpāsara raṣaṭa gait sage maka and labour should go to the noble king.

sanskrit: ityevaṃ magadhapatir[vaco] babhāṣe yaḥ samyagvalabhidiva dhruvaṃ babhāṣe | tacchrutvā na sa vicacāra rājasūnuḥ kailāso giririva naikacitrasānuḥ ||
reference: Thus spoke the monarch of the Magadhas, who spoke well and strongly like Indra; but having heard it, the prince did not falter, (firm) like the mountain Kailāsa, having its many summits variegated (with lines of metals).
baseline: The king of Magadha should say the same thing to the king of the kingdom of Gāgādhā. He who does not speak well and does not talk about the pole should say that he is not a wise king. He should not speak illusory things like kāla girīrī and many pictures.
morphology: The king of Magadha should say the same thing to the king of the kingdom of Gāgādhā. He who has spoken the good scripture should say that the pole is good and the king should not speak the illusion of the king. He should not say a picture of the mountain.

sanskrit: ā janmano janmajarāṃtakasya tasyātmajasyātmajitaḥ sa rājā | ahanyahanyarthagajāśvamitrairvṛddhiṃ yayau siṃdharivāṃbuvegaiḥ ||
reference: From the time of the birth of that son of his, who, the true master of himself, was to end all birth and old age, the king increased day by day in wealth, elephants, horses, and friends as a river increases with its influx of waters.
baseline: The king is the one who gives birth to the son of a jārantaka the king who acquires the life of his son the soul of the son and the king of the sons of a gājāśva the sons sons and daughters of the king.
morphology: The king is the one who gives birth to a son a son and a son to a daughter. He is the king who gives life to the daughter of a son. He should be killed and the sons of the king should be raised up.

sanskrit: dhanasya ratnasya ca tasya tasya kṛtākṛtasyaiva ca kāṃcanasya | tadā hi naikātmanidhīnavāpi manorathasyāpyatibhārabhūtān ||
reference: Of different kinds of wealth and jewels, and of gold, wrought or unwrought, he found treasures of manifold variety, surpassing even the capacity of his desires.
baseline: One should give him a piece of money a jewel and the things made by him. Then he should be subject to the same spirit and the mind should be taken care of.
morphology: One should give him a piece of money a jewel a gift made by him and a gift. Then he should be subject to the same spirit. He should be able to bear the burden of the mind.

sanskrit: ye padmakalpairapi ca dvipeṃdrairna maṃḍalaṃ śakyamihābhinetum | madotkaṭā haimavatā gajāste vināpi yatnādupatasthurenam ||
reference: Elephants from Himavat, raging with rut, whom not even princes of elephants like Padma could teach to go round in circles, came without any effort and waited on him.
baseline: One who has a lotus and two other parts of the body is able to get a māhābhi. One who does not have a cow would get a cow without having two parts.
morphology: One who has a lotus in the middle of the earth and has a circle with two centers should be able to reach the earth. One who does not have a cow would get a cow without having a cow.

sanskrit: nānāṃkacihnairnavahemabhāṃḍairabhūṣitairlaṃbasaṭaistathānyaiḥ | saṃcukṣubhe cāsya puraṃ turaṃgairbalena maitryā ca dhanena cāptaiḥ ||
reference: His city was all astir with the crowds of horses, some adorned with various marks and decked with new golden trappings, others unadorned and with long flowing manes, — suitable alike in strength, gentleness, and costly ornaments.
baseline: One would get the city with the strength of a tower friendship and wealth by having the gold ornaments adorned with the bhaṇḍas of the earth with the various symbols.
morphology: One should be adorned with a lotus with a number of symbols and with a piece of gold and gold. He should be blessed with the city with the strength of a sword and friendship and wealth.

sanskrit: puṣṭāśca tuṣṭāśca tadāsya rājye sādhvyo 'rajaskā guṇavatpayaskāḥ | udagravatsaiḥ sahitā babhūvurbahvyo bahukṣīraduhaśca gāvaḥ ||
reference: And many fertile cows, with tall calves, gathered in his kingdom, well nourished and happy, gentle and without fierceness, and producing excellent milk.
baseline: One who is blessed with a lotus a cow and a cow should be meritorious in that kingdom. One who has been afflicted by the evil spirits should be blessed with many things.
morphology: One who is blessed with good qualities and good fortune in that kingdom should be blessed with the gift of flowers. One who has suffered from the evil spirits many diseases and many diseases should be worshipped by the cow.

sanskrit: madhyasthatāṃ tasya ripurjagāma madhyasvabhāvaḥ prayayau suhṛttvam | viśeṣato dārḍhyamiyāya mitraṃ dvāvasya pakṣāvaparastu nāśam ||
reference: His enemies became indifferent; indifference grew into friendship; his friends became specially united; were there two sides, — one passed into oblivion.
baseline: One who mediates on the two sides of the enemy should be called a friend by using his repurposed nature. One who has a strong friend should be destroyed by the side of the adversary in particular.
morphology: One who mediates on a person should be called a friend in the middle of his nature. A friend who has a strong nature should be destroyed by the side of the two friends.

sanskrit: tathāsya maṃdānilameghaśabdaḥ saudāminīkuṃḍalamaṃḍitāṃgaḥ | vināśmavarṣāśanipātadoṣaiḥ kāle ca deśe pravavarṣa devaḥ ||
reference: Heaven rained in his kingdom in due time and place, with the sound of gentle winds and clouds, and adorned with wreaths of lightning, and without any drawback of showers of stones or thunderbolts.
baseline: Then the word sāudāminikūṇī kundalā the limb of the mantle and the body of the king is mentioned in the slanting of the earth. The god of the rain falling on the earth in the time of destruction and misfortune should be worshipped in the year of annihilation.
morphology: Then the word māḍaṇīla māgha sāudāmanī kundal mandi and other parts of the body should be mentioned. One who brings rain to the country in the time of destruction and misfortune should be worshipped as a god.

sanskrit: ruroha saṃyak phalavadyathārtu tadākṛtenāpi kṛṣiśrameṇa | tā eva caivauṣadhayo rasena sāreṇa caivābhyadhikā babhūvuḥ ||
reference: A fruitful crop sprang up according to season, even without the labour of ploughing; and the old plants grew more vigorous in juice and substance.
baseline: One would get the fruits by doing the same with the help of the same kind of agricultural labour. He would get more than that by doing all the things with the same amount of herbs and juice.
morphology: One who does not get the fruits by doing any agricultural work would get more profit by doing the same with the combination of herbs and juice.

sanskrit: śarīrasaṃdehakare 'pi kāle saṃgrāmasaṃmarda iva pravṛtte | svasthāḥ sukhaṃ caiva nirāmayaṃ ca prajajñire garbhadharāśca nāryaḥ ||
reference: Even at that crisis which threatens danger to the body like the collision of battle, pregnant women brought forth in good health, in safety, and without sickness.
baseline: A woman who doubts the body and does not fight in time would be like a warmaker. She would get well and would be cured by the people and the womb.
morphology: One who doubts the body would then become a warmaker in time. One who is healthy would get well and would get rid of the diseases of the people and the womb would get destroyed by women.

sanskrit: yacca pratibhvo vibhave 'pi śakye na prārthayaṃti sma narāḥ parebhyaḥ | abhyarthitaḥ sūkṣmadhano 'pi cāyaṃ tadā na kaścidvimukho babhūva ||
reference: And whereas men do not willingly ask from others, even where a surety’s property is available, — at that time even one possessed of slender means turned not his face away when solicited.
baseline: If one does not wish to be able to do so one would not wish for others. If one wishes for the same one should not seek the gift. Then no one would get the favour.
morphology: If a man is not able to do so he should not ask for money. If he is willing for money he would not be able to get money.

sanskrit: nāśe vadho baṃdhuṣu nāpyadātā naivāvrato nānṛtiko na hiṃsraḥ | āsīttadā kaścana tasya rājye rājño yayāteriva nāhuṣasya ||
reference: There was no ruin nor murder, — nay, there was not even one ungenerous to his kinsmen, no breaker of obligations, none untruthful nor injurious, — as in the days of Yayāti the son of Nahuṣa.
baseline: One who destroys a bridegroom and does not destroy his kinsman and who does not harm his brother is not a violent person. One who is a king or a wanderer in his kingdom is not an enemy.
morphology: One who destroys a bridegroom does not destroy his relatives is not a violent person. One who does not go to the king or a non-violent person should not enter the kingdom.

sanskrit: udyānadevāyatanāśramāṇāṃ kūpaprapāpuṣkariṇīvanānām | cakruḥ kriyāstatra ca dharmakāmāḥ pratyakṣataḥ svargamivopalabhya ||
reference: Those who sought religious merit performed sacred works and made gardens, temples, and hermitages, wells, cisterns, lakes, and groves, having beheld heaven as it were visible before their eyes.
baseline: One should worship the gods of the garden and the forest. One should do the chakra of the pitchers and the flowers of the forest and the sacred things are found in heaven.
morphology: The gods of the garden and the forest are worshipped in the form of a well a flower a tree a cow a bird a horse a man of good deeds and the gods of righteousness are found in heaven.

sanskrit: muktaśca durbhikṣabhayāmayebhyo hṛṣṭo janaḥ svargamivābhireme | patnīṃ patirvā mahiṣī patiṃ vā parasparaṃ na vyabhiceratuśca ||
reference: The people, delivered from famine, fear, and sickness, dwelt happily as in heaven; and in mutual contentment husband transgressed not against wife, nor wife against husband.
baseline: One who is free from the fear of famine and fear should not commit adultery with his wife wife husband wife or husband.
morphology: One who is free from the fear of famine and fear should not marry a wife or a husband or commit adultery among themselves.

sanskrit: kaścitsiṣeve rataye na kāmaṃ kāmārthamarthaṃ na jugopa kaścit | kaściddhanārthaṃ na cacāra dharmaṃ dharmāya kaścinna cakāra hiṃsām ||
reference: None pursued love for mere sensual pleasure; none hoarded wealth for the sake of desires; none practised religious duties for the sake of gaining wealth; none injured living beings for the sake of religious duty.
baseline: One who does not practice law for the sake of lust one who does nothing for the cause of laziness one for the purpose of earning and one who practices righteousness for the purposes of religion and one for doing violence.
morphology: One who does not worship for the sake of lust one who does nothing for the purpose of earning one not for the cause of righteousness one for the reason of religion one does not do anything for the purposes of violence.

sanskrit: steyādibhiścāpyabhitaśca naṣṭaṃ svasthaṃ svacakraṃ paracakramuktam | kṣemaṃ subhikṣaṃ ca babhūva tasya purāṇyaraṇyāni yathaiva rāṣṭre ||
reference: On every side theft and its kindred vices disappeared; his own dominion was in peace and at rest from foreign interference; prosperity and plenty belonged to him, and the cities in his realm were (healthy) like the forests.
baseline: One who has lost his body and got it from the sins of the sages and others is cured. He has got his own wheel and other wheels. He is blessed with good health and prosperity. He will get his old habits in the same way in the country.
morphology: One who has suffered loss by doing these things would get better. One would get his own wheel and other parts of the body. He would get good health and prosperity. He should get his old habits as well as his wealth.

sanskrit: tadā hi tajjanmani tasya rājño manorivādityasutasya rājye | cacāra harṣaḥ praṇanāśa pāpmā jajvāla dharmaḥ kaluṣaḥ śaśāma ||
reference: When that son was born it was in that monarch’s kingdom as in the reign of Manu the son of the Sun, — gladness went everywhere and evil perished; right blazed abroad and sin was still.
baseline: Then the king of that kingdom would be born in the kingdom of the son of the mind lord of the universe and the king would be destroyed by the destruction of the heart and the destruction by the sinful conduct of the king.
morphology: Then the king of that kingdom would be born as a son of a mani vivedyātis in the kingdom. The king would be destroyed by the destruction of the heart the destruction by the sin the loss of righteousness the evil by the evil one.

sanskrit: evaṃvidhā rājasutasya tasya sarvārthasiddhiśca yato babhūva | tato nṛpastasya sutasya nāma sarvārthasiddho 'yamiti pracakre ||
reference: Since at the birth of this son of the king such a universal accomplishment of all objects took place, the king in consequence caused the prince’s name to be Sarvārthasiddha.
baseline: Thus the kings son would get all the benefits from it. Hence the name of his son would be declared to be all benefits.
morphology: Thus the king has achieved all the benefits of his kingdom. Therefore the name of his son is declared to be the best benefit.

sanskrit: devī tu māyā vibudharṣikalpaṃ dṛṣṭvā viśālaṃ tanayaprabhāvam | jātaṃ praharṣaṃ na śaśāka soḍhuṃ tato 'vināśāya divaṃ jagāma ||
reference: But the queen Māyā, having seen the great glory of her new-born son, like some Ṛṣi of the gods, could not sustain the joy which it brought; and that she might not die she went to heaven.
baseline: Having seen the image of the goddess the illusion of the mind the great power and the influence. One would not get the victory. He would not be able to destroy it.
morphology: Having seen the image of the goddess the illusion of the mind and the power of the universe one would get a great effect. One would not be able to destroy the enemy. One should go to the earth for destruction.

sanskrit: tataḥ kumāraṃ suragarbhakalpaṃ snehena bhāvena ca nirviśeṣam | mātṛṣvasā mātṛsamaprabhāvā saṃvardhayāmātmajavadbabhūva ||
reference: Then the queen’s sister, with an influence like a mother’s, undistinguished from the real mother in her affection or tenderness, brought up as her own son the young prince who was like the offspring of the gods.
baseline: Then the image of the son son daughter son and son are made to be unique by the love and affection of the mother. By the mother the mother and the lord of the body and the mother should be enriched by the manifestation of the spirit.
morphology: Then the image of the son son daughter son and son should be expressed with affection and affection. The mother should be worshipped with the same spirit as the mother.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa bālārka ivodayasthaḥ samīrito vahnirivānilena | krameṇa samyagvavṛdhe kumārastārādhipaḥ pakṣa ivātamaske ||
reference: Then like the young sun on the eastern mountain or the fire when fanned by the wind, the prince gradually grew in all due perfection, like the moon in the fortnight of brightness.
baseline: Then the boy should be placed on the ground in front of the king. Then the king should be seated on the right side of the hill and gradually raise his head in the right direction.
morphology: Then the boy should be placed on the ground in the middle of the hill and then the king should be raised gradually in the right direction. The king should stand on the right side.

sanskrit: tato mahārhāṇi ca candanāni ratnāvalīścauṣadhibhiḥ sagarbhāḥ | mṛgaprayuktānrathakāṃśca haimānācakrire 'smai suhṛdālayebhyaḥ ||
reference: Then they brought him as presents from the houses of his friends costly unguents of sandalwood, and strings of gems exactly like wreaths of plants, and little golden carriages yoked with deer;
baseline: Then there are great things sandals jewels herbs ornaments and other things used for hunting. The king should be made to sit on the wheel of the elephant.
morphology: Then the great things are made of sandalwood gems and herbs. The gods used for hunting are made to be used in the chakras of the king.

sanskrit: vayo 'nurūpāṇi ca bhūṣaṇāni hiraṇmayā hastimṛgāśvakāśca | rathāśca gāvo vasanaprayuktā gaṃtrīśca cāmīkararūpyacitrāḥ ||
reference: Ornaments also suitable to his age, and elephants, deer, and horses made of gold, carriages and oxen decked with rich garments, and carts gay with silver and gold.
baseline: The figures of men women men animals animals and animals are described as having the shape of a lion. The images of horses cows horses horses and horses are described in the scriptures as having four forms.
morphology: The figures of men women men animals horses horses and horses are described as having the same shape as those of men.

sanskrit: evaṃ sa taistairviṣayopacārairvayo 'nurūpairupacaryamāṇaḥ | bālo 'pyabālapratimo babhūva dhṛtyā ca śaucena dhiyā śriyā ca ||
reference: Thus indulged with all sorts of such objects to please the senses as were suitable to his years, child as he was, he behaved not like a child in gravity, purity, wisdom, and dignity.
baseline: He should thus treat those things in the same manner as the children. The child should be worshipped as the image of the child. The boy should be washed with the dhrutya and the goddess Śrīya.
morphology: In this way he would treat those things in the same manner as the children. He would be worshipped as the child the child and the image of the child. He should be washed with the dhruti the shiva and the Śrīya.

sanskrit: vayaśca kaumāramatītya madhyaṃ saṃprāpya bālaḥ sa hi rājasūnuḥ | alpairahobhirbahuvarṣagamyā jagrāha vidyāḥ svakulānurūpāḥ ||
reference: When he had passed the period of childhood and reached that of middle youth, the young prince learned in a few days the various sciences suitable to his race, which generally took many years to master.
baseline: Having attained the age of puberty and having reached the middle the boy should be called the king of the king. He should be known as the son of a king who is less than the king and who has knowledge in the form of his clan.
morphology: Having attained the age of virginity and having attained the middle grade the boy should be called the king of the king. He should be known as the son of a king who is less than the king and who has knowledge of the world.

sanskrit: naiḥśreyasaṃ tasya tu bhavyamarthaṃ śrutvā purastādasitānmahārṣeḥ | kāmeṣu saṃgaṃ janayāṃbabhūva vṛddhirbhavacchākyakulasya rājñaḥ ||
reference: But having heard before from the great seer Asita his destined future which was to embrace transcendental happiness, the anxious care of the king of the present Śākya race turned the prince to sensual pleasures.
baseline: The king of the clan should be pleased to hear that the king should be magnificently pleased by the merits of his actions. The king should also be pleased with the combination of his desires and increase his wealth.
