morphology: The king of the kingdom of the chakra clan should increase his wealth by having heard of these great things.

sanskrit: kulāttato 'smai sthiraśīlasaṃyutātsādhvīṃ vapurhrīvinayopapannām | yaśodharāṃ nāma yaśoviśālāṃ tulyābhidhānaṃ śriyamājuhāva ||
reference: Then he sought for him from a family of unblemished moral excellence a bride possessed of beauty, modesty, and gentle bearing, of wide-spread glory, Yaśodharā by name, having a name well worthy of her, a very goddess of good fortune.
baseline: The name of Yāśodhara should be called Yāsovīśala and the name of the equilibrium should be mentioned as Śrīmā.
morphology: One who has been given the name of Yāśovīśala the son of Yṣodharā is called Śrīmā.

sanskrit: athāparaṃ bhūmipateḥ priyo 'yaṃ sanatkumārapratimaḥ kumāraḥ | sārdhaṃ tayā śākyanareṃdravadhvā śacyā sahasrākṣa ivābhireme ||
reference: Then after that the prince, beloved of the king his father, he who was like Sanatkumāra, rejoiced in the society of that Śākya princess as the thousand-eyed (Indra) rejoiced with his bride Śacī.
baseline: The image of Sanatkumara is said to be the favorite of the lord of the land the son of the king of the earth and the king should be killed by the sākhyaṇa king after having killed him.
morphology: The image of Sanatkumara is said to be the son of the lord of the land and the king of the earth should be worshipped with a thousand cubits.

sanskrit: kiṃcinmanaḥkṣobhakaraṃ pratīpaṃ kathaṃca paśyediti so 'nuciṃtya | vāsaṃ nṛpo hyādiśati sma tasmai harmyodareṣveva na bhūpracāram ||
reference: ‘He might perchance see some inauspicious sight which could disturb his mind,’ — thus reflecting the king had a dwelling prepared for him apart from the busy press in the recesses of the palace.
baseline: One who sees a thing which is not good enough for him to disturb him and who says something to him would not be able to do his duty. He would not let him walk on the earth without being harmed.
morphology: He who sees a thing that is not good for him and does not disturb him or disturb him and who is not living or living in the country would not be able to visit the land.

sanskrit: tataḥ śarattoyadapāṃḍareṣu bhūmau vimāneṣviva raṃjiteṣu | harmyeṣu sarvartusukhāśrayeṣu strīṇāmudārairvijahāra tūryaiḥ ||
reference: Then he spent his time in those royal apartments, furnished with the delights proper for every season, gaily decorated like heavenly chariots upon the earth, and bright like the clouds of autumn, amidst the splendid musical concerts of singing-women.
baseline: Then there should be a lotus flower in the ground and in the air. All the flowers should be placed in the sanctuaries with the help of a woman a woman and a man living in the fields.
morphology: Then there should be a lotus flower in the ground and an airplane in the fields. All the animals should be kept in the sanctuaries with women men and children.

sanskrit: kalairhi cāmīkarabaddhakakṣairnārīkarāgrābhihatairmṛdaṃgaiḥ | varāpsaronṛtyasamaiśca nṛtyaiḥ kailāsavattadbhavanaṃ rarāja ||
reference: With the softly-sounding tambourines beaten by the tips of the women’s hands, and ornamented with golden rims, and with the dances which were like the dances of the heavenly nymphs, that palace shone like Mount Kailāsa.
baseline: The king should make the palace of Kailāśa vatā with the merriment of the heart and arms of the king with the dance of varāpāsaraṇa and other forms of dance.
morphology: The king should make the palace of Kailāśavata abode with the merriment of the heart and limbs and the dance of varāpāsara sāmā and vāṇas.

sanskrit: vāgbhiḥ kalābhirlalitaiśca hārairmadaiḥ sakhelairmadhuraiśca hāsaiḥ | taṃ tatra nāryo ramayāṃbabhūvurbhrūvaṃcitairardhanirīkṣitaiśca ||
reference: There the women delighted him with their soft voices, their beautiful pearl-garlands, their playful intoxication, their sweet laughter, and their stolen glances concealed by their brows.
baseline: He should be adorned with the garlands of garlands garlands and garlands with the fragrance of a flower. He should also be seen standing there with a woman a woman and a man standing on the ground and sitting on a tree.
morphology: He should be adorned with garlands garlands and garlands of flowers and made to look beautiful by the presence of a woman a woman and a man standing on the ground and waiting for him.

sanskrit: tataśca kāmāśrayapaṃḍitābhiḥ strībhirgṛhīto ratikarkaśābhiḥ | vimānapṛṣṭhānna mahīṃ jagāma vimānapṛṣthādiva puṇyakarmā ||
reference: Borne in the arms of these women well-skilled in the ways of love, and reckless in the pursuit of pleasure, he fell from the roof of a pavilion and yet reached not the ground, like a holy sage stepping from a heavenly chariot.
baseline: Then a woman should be blessed with the kāmāsāraśāra and the rātika kāśa. She should be worshipped on the day of the flight without the plane.
morphology: Then a woman should be blessed with the kāmāsāraśāra and the rātika kāśa. She should be worshipped on the day of the flight of the plane and not on the plane of the sky.

sanskrit: nṛpastu tasyaiva vivṛddhihetostadbhāvinārthena ca codyamānaḥ | śame 'bhireme virarāma pāpādbheje damaṃ saṃvibabhāja sādhūn ||
reference: Meanwhile the king for the sake of ensuring his son’s prosperity and stirred in heart by the destiny which had been predicted for him, delighted himself in perfect calm, ceased from all evil, practised all self-restraint, and rewarded the good.
baseline: One should ask the sages for the sake of their welfare and for the benefit of their wellbeing. The sāmma should be worshipped in the form of a serpent and the sādham should be given to the sinners in the absence of sin.
morphology: One should ask the sages for the increase in the number of sins and for the purpose of their welfare. The sāma viraṇa virāma and dāma should be given to the sāmīs for the remission of their sins.

sanskrit: nādhīravat kāmasukhe sasaṃje na saṃraraṃje viṣamaṃ jananyām | dhṛtyeṃdriyāśvāṃścapalān vijigye baṃdhūṃśca paurāṃśca guṇairjigāya ||
reference: He turned to no sensual pleasures like one wanting in self-control; he felt no violent delight in any state of birth; he subdued by firmness the restless horses of the senses; and he surpassed his kindred and citizens by his virtues.
baseline: One should not create evil in the midst of the fire or in the presence of evil spirits like nādhirā lust pleasure happiness misfortune fear desire sense heart mind arms arms etc. and the qualities of the brothers and the citizens should be attained.
morphology: One should not create evil in the midst of the fire or in the presence of evil spirits such as nādhira kāśuṇa sāsandhāna dhārṣṇī śvāṇḍīva bājīga bṛṣṇu pūrśi and others.

sanskrit: nādhyaiṣṭa duḥkhāya parasya vidyāṃ jñānaṃ śivaṃ yattu tadadhyagīṣṭa | svābhyaḥ prajābhyo hi yathā tathaiva sarvaprajābhyaḥ śivamāśaśaṃse ||
reference: He sought not learning to vex another; such knowledge as was beneficent, that only he studied; he wished well to all mankind as much as to his own subjects.
baseline: One should know the wisdom of Lord Śiva in the face of misery and misery. In the same way he should be known to his subjects one should be worshipped by Lord śiva in all subjects.
morphology: One should know the wisdom of the lord Śiva in the midst of the misery and misery. In the same way as it is for one's own people one should give the knowledge of Śivā to all citizens.

sanskrit: taṃ bhāsuraṃ cāṃgirasādhidevaṃ yathāvadānarca tadāyuṣe saḥ | juhāva havyānyakṛśe kṛśānau dadau dvijebhyaḥ kṛśanaṃ ca gāśca ||
reference: He worshipped also duly the brilliant (Agni) that tutelary god of the Aṅgirasas, for his son’s long life; and he offered oblations in a large fire, and gave gold and cows to the Brāhmans.
baseline: He should give the same to the gods of the earth as the bhaśura chāngira sādhī and gāda in that lifetime. He should offer the same amount of wheat wheat maize wheat and wheat for two days.
morphology: He should give him the bhaśura as well as the sādhī of the goddess of good and evil in the same lifetime. He should also give the kṛṣa of the sky and the krṣa and the kaśa of two cows.

sanskrit: sasnau śarīraṃ pavituṃ manaśca tīrthāṃbubhiścaiva guṇāṃbubhiśca | vedopadiṣṭaṃ samamātmajaṃ ca somaṃ papau śāṃtisukhaṃ ca hārdam ||
reference: He bathed to purify his body and mind with the waters of holy places and of holy feelings; and at the same time he drank the soma-juice as enjoined by the Veda, and the heartfelt self-produced happiness of perfect calm.
baseline: One should worship the body mind and other virtues of the people living in the temple. One should observe the Vedas as equanimous as one would get. One would be a sinner one would enjoy peace and happiness.
morphology: One should worship the body mind and other virtues of the people living in the temple. One should observe the Vedas as equanimous as the soul. One who is a sinner one who enjoys peace and happiness.

sanskrit: sāṃtvaṃ babhāṣe na ca nārthavadyajjajalpa tattvaṃ na ca vipriyaṃ yat | sāṃtvaṃ hyatatvaṃ paruṣaṃ ca tattvaṃ hriyāśakannātmana eva vaktum ||
reference: He only spoke what was pleasant and not unprofitable; he discoursed about what was true and not ill-natured, he could not speak even to himself for very shame a false pleasant thing or a harsh truth.
baseline: One should not speak the principle of sātvanta bābhāṣa nātravāda vājjala jalāla viprāya santavata hātā pāruśa and hryāsaka.
morphology: One should not speak in the same manner with the syllable sātva bābhāṣa nātravāda vājjala jalāla and the syllables santa vaṭva hātvā pārusha hryāsaka śātmā.

sanskrit: iṣṭeṣvaniṣṭeṣu ca kāryavatsu na rāgadoṣāśrayatāṃ prapede | śivaṃ siṣeve 'vyavahāralabdhaṃ yajñaṃ hi mene na tathā yathāvat ||
reference: In things which required to be done, whether they were pleasant or disagreeable, he found no reason either for desire or dislike; he pursued the advantageous which could be attained without litigation; he did not so highly value sacrifice.
baseline: One should not resort to evil deeds in the course of his life. One would not accept the sacrifice of the lord Śiva if he does not do the same in the future.
morphology: One should not resort to evil deeds in the course of his life. One would not accept the sacrifice if one does not do the same in the future. One should avoid the practice of siva in the past.

sanskrit: āśāvate cābhigatāya sadyo deyāṃbubhistarṣamacecchidiṣṭa | yuddhādṛte vṛttaparaśvadhena dvidarpamudvṛttamabebhidiṣṭa ||
reference: When a suppliant came to him with a petition, he at once hastened to quench his thirst with the water sprinkled on his gift; and without fighting, by the battle-axe of his demeanour he smote down the arrogant armed with double pride.
baseline: One should not be afraid of the enemy. One should be prepared to face the enemy with a sword and two rounds with a circle and a circle.
morphology: One should not be afraid of the battle. One should be divided into two parts with a circle and a circle in the course of the war.

sanskrit: ekaṃ vininye sa jugopa sapta saptaiva tatyāja rarakṣa paṃca | prāpa trivargaṃ bubudhe trivargaṃ jajñe dvivargaṃ prajahau dvivargam ||
reference: Thus he took away the one, and protected the seven; he abandoned the seven and kept the five; he obtained the set of three and learned the set of three; he understood the two and abandoned the two.
baseline: One who has made a sacrifice should leave seven or five of them and get three orgas of knowledge and know that he has two orgasm of the subjects and five orgasms.
morphology: One who has chosen one of them would get seven of them. The other five would get three of them after having learnt the wisdom. Having learnt the three of these one would get two of them and the other one would be divided into two.

sanskrit: kṛtāgaso 'pi pratipādya vadhyānnājīghanannāpi ruṣā dadarśa | babaṃdha sāṃtvena phalena caitāṃstyāgo 'pi teṣāṃ hyanapāyadṛṣṭaḥ ||
reference: Guilty persons, even though he had sentenced them to death, he did not cause to be killed nor even looked on them with anger; he bound them with gentle words and with the reform produced in their character, — even their release was accompanied by no inflicted injury.
baseline: Having said so one should also see the rusks in the form of a bandage and the fruits of the bondage. They should be given to them as a gift.
morphology: Having said this the king should also say that he would not be able to bear the loss of his life. He should be bound with a bond and the fruits should be given to them.

sanskrit: ārṣāṇyacārītparamavratāni vairāṇyahāsīccirasaṃbhṛtāni | yaśāṃsi cāpadguṇagaṃdhavaṃti rajāṃsyahāsīnmalinīkarāṇi ||
reference: He performed great religious vows prescribed by ancient seers; he threw aside hostile feelings long cherished; he acquired glory redolent with the fragrance of virtue; he relinquished all passions involving defilement.
baseline: The chariots of the king are made up of four different kinds of objects. The chords of the kings are made of two kinds of sandal and the chariot of the gods are made out of a piece of cloth.
morphology: The chariots of the king are made up of four different kinds of weapons. The chords of the enemy the chariot the elephant the king the lion the bearer of the sword the mermaid and the king of the kingdom are made of two kinds of horses.

sanskrit: na cājihīrṣīdbalimapravṛttaṃ na cācikīrṣītparavastvabhidhyām | na cāvivakṣīddviṣatāmadharmaṃ na cādidhakṣīddhṛdayena manyum ||
reference: He desired not to take his tribute of one-sixth without acting as the guardian of his people; he had no wish to covet another’s property; he desired not to mention the wrong-doing of his enemies; nor did he wish to fan wrath in his heart.
baseline: One should not make a vow or make a promise to the king of the kingdom of Bihar. One should never make a false promise to him. One would not accept the promise of the king without having the keys and the righteousness of the twenty-seven gods.
morphology: One should not make a mistake by making a false statement about the conduct of the priest the chief minister the principal officer the governor of the city the king of the kingdom of Bihar and the king. One should never make a false claim about the righteousness of the people. One would not be able to do so with the heart.

sanskrit: tasmiṃstathā bhūmipatau pravṛtte bhṛtyāśca paurāśca tathaiva ceruḥ | śamātmake cetasi viprasanne prayuktayogasya yatheṃdriyāṇi ||
reference: When the monarch himself was thus employed his servants and citizens followed his example, like the senses of one absorbed in contemplation whose mind is abstracted in profound repose.
baseline: The same is the case with the lord of the land the master of the property the servant the priest and the cowherd. In the same way the senses of the spirit are the same as those of the yogic body used in the manifestation.
morphology: The same is the case with the lord of the land the master of the property the servant of the lord the priest and the priest in the same way. The mind of the spirit is the same as that of the body.

sanskrit: kāle tataścārupayodharāyāṃ yaśodharāyāṃ suyaśodharāyām | śauddhodanerāhusapatnavaktro jajñe suto rāhula eva nāmnā ||
reference: In course of time to the fair-bosomed Yaśodharā, — who was truly glorious in accordance with her name, — there was born from the son of Śuddhodana a son named Rāhula, with a face like the enemy of Rāhu.
baseline: In the same time the king should be worshipped in the form of a warrior warrior jasudhara suyāsudhara and the son of a king. The king of the kings son and son should be worshiped in the name of Rahula.
morphology: In the same time the king should be called the king of the warriors the chief minister the governor of the kingdom of Yāśodhara the king who is known to be the son of the king and the ruler of the principality.

sanskrit: atheṣṭaputraḥ paramapratītaḥ kulasya vṛddhiṃ prati bhūmipālaḥ | yathaiva putraprasave nanaṃda tathaiva pautraprasave nanaṃda ||
reference: Then the king who from regard to the welfare of his race had longed for a son and been exceedingly delighted [at his coming], — as he had rejoiced at the birth of his son, so did he now rejoice at the birth of his grandson.
baseline: One who has eight sons is the highest in the family. One who does not give birth to a son should do likewise to a grandson.
morphology: One who has eight sons is the highest in the family. One who gives land to the growth of the clan is called Naṇḍa in the birth of a son and one who gives birth to a grandson.

sanskrit: pautrasya me putragato mamaiva snehaḥ kathaṃ syāditi jātaharṣaḥ | kāle sa taṃ taṃ vidhimālalaṃbe putrapriyaḥ svargamivārurukṣan ||
reference: ‘O how can I feel that love which my son feels for my grandson?’ Thus thinking in his joy he at the due time attended to every enjoined rite like one who fondly loves his son and is about to rise to heaven.
baseline: How can one describe the affection of a grandson when he is born to a son. He should then treat him as if he were a son in the lawful manner. He would be like heaven.
morphology: When a son of a great-grandson comes to me how can I say that he has affection for me. In those days he should treat him as if he were a son and beloved in heaven.

sanskrit: sthitvā pathi prāthamakalpikānāṃ rājarṣabhāṇāṃ yaśasānvitānām | śuklānyamuktvāpi tapāṃsyatapta yajñe ca hiṃsārahitairayaṣṭa ||
reference: Standing in the paths of the pre-eminent kings who flourished in primaeval ages, he practised austerities without laying aside his white garments, and he offered in sacrifice only those things which involved no injury to living creatures.
baseline: Having stood on the path the first choice should be made by the king the king and the king of the kingdom and the success should be achieved by the practice of penance and by the offering of the sacred threads without violence.
morphology: Having stood on the path the first choices should be made by the king the king and the king of the kingdom and the success should be achieved. The meritorious ones should be liberated from the temptations and the sacrifices made by them should be done without violence.

sanskrit: ajājvaliṣṭātha sa puṇyakarmā nṛpaśriyā caiva tapaḥśriyā ca | kulena vṛttena dhiyā ca dīptastejaḥ sahasrāṃśurivotsisṛkṣuḥ ||
reference: He of holy deeds shone forth gloriously, in the splendour of royalty and the splendour of penances, conspicuous by his family and his own conduct and wisdom, and desirous to diffuse brightness like the sun.
baseline: He should be worshipped as a virtuous man as the son of a noble man and as the lord of penance as well as as as the king of the world. He should have a circle with a kulana and light.
morphology: He should be worshipped as a virtuous man with the grace of the unbroken body as the son of the king of the kingdom of Nriṣrāya as a penance as well as as having the power of the circle of the clan.

sanskrit: svāyaṃbhuvaṃ cārcikamarcayitvā jajāpa putrasthitaye sthitaśrīḥ | cakāra karmāṇi ca duṣkarāṇi prajāḥ sisṛkṣuḥ ka ivādikāle ||
reference: Having offered worship, he whose own glory was secure muttered repetitions of Vedic texts to Svayambhū for the safety of his son, and performed various ceremonies hard to be accomplished, like the god Ka in the first aeon wishing to create living beings.
baseline: Having worshipped the priest in the church with his own hands the judge should be seated in the seat of the son. Then the king should perform the deeds of the poor people and the sissarcus.
morphology: Having worshipped the priest in his own house the judge should be seated in the seat of the son. Then the king should perform the deeds of the poor people and those of the sages.

sanskrit: tatjyāja śastraṃ vimamarśa śāstraṃ śamaṃ siṣeve niyamaṃ viṣehe | vaśīva kaṃcidviṣayaṃ na bheje piteva sarvānviṣayān dadarśa ||
reference: He laid aside weapons and pondered the Śāstra, he practised perfect calm and underwent various observances, like a hermit he refused all objects of sense, he viewed all his kingdoms like a father.
baseline: The law should be explained in the following lines. One should not drink the kāṇḍiva water without having to wash it and then the weapon should be washed and the scriptures should be shaved. One would see all the things.
morphology: One who does not eat and drink without having prepared the ingredients for the sacrifice would be able to see all the things.

sanskrit: babhāra rājyaṃ sa hi putrahetoḥ putraṃ kulārthaṃ yaśase kulaṃ tu | svargāya śabdaṃ divamātmahetordharmārthamātmasthitimācakāṃkṣa ||
reference: He endured the kingdom for the sake of his son, his son for his family, his family for fame, fame for heaven, heaven for the soul, — he only desired the soul’s continuance for the sake of duty.
baseline: The kingdom of Bābhāra is the kingdom of the son the son and the clan for the sake of the family the clan and the kingdom for the benefit of the clan. The word for heaven for the cause of the soul and for the purpose of the self is my wish.
morphology: The kingdom of Bābhāra is the kingdom of a son a son and a clan for the sake of the family. The word for heaven the word for the soul for the purpose of the self and the state of the soul is my desire.

sanskrit: evaṃ sa dharmaṃ vividhaṃ cakāra sadbhirnipātaṃ śrutitaśca siddham | dṛṣṭvā kathaṃ putramukhaṃ suto me vanaṃ na yāyāditi nāthamānaḥ ||
reference: Thus did he practise the various observances as followed by the pious and established from revelation, he asking himself, ‘now that he has seen the face of his son, how may my son be stopped from going to the forest?’
baseline: Having thus diversified his righteousness and having heard of the fall of the god he becomes perfect. Having seen how the thread should be placed on the face of the son he should not go to the forest.
morphology: Having thus diversified his righteousness he would have heard of the fall of goodness and would have seen how the face of his son is not the thread of the forest.

sanskrit: rirakṣiṣaṃtaḥ śriyamātmasaṃsthā rakṣaṃti putrān bhuvi bhūmipālāḥ | putraṃ nareṃdraḥ sa tu dharmakāmo rarakṣa dharmādviṣayeṣvamuṃcat ||
reference: The prudent kings of the earth, who wish to guard their prosperity, watch over their sons in the world; but this king, though loving religion, kept his son from religion and set him free towards all objects of pleasure.
baseline: One who protects the sons of the king by protecting the body the spirit the earth the son of lord narendra the protector of righteousness and the protection of the righteous.
morphology: The son of Śrīma should protect the body of the soul and protect the sons of the earth. He should be known as narendra. He would protect the righteousness of the people and protect them.

sanskrit: tasminśca bodhāya kṛtapratijñe rājarṣivaṃśaprabhave mahārṣau | tatropaviṣṭe prajaharṣa lokastatrāsa saddharmaripustu māraḥ ||
reference: When the great sage, sprung from a line of royal sages, sat down there with his soul fully resolved to obtain the highest knowledge, the whole world rejoiced; but Māra, the enemy of the good law, was afraid.
baseline: Then the king should make a vow to the lord of the kingdom of the king the king of the kings and the lord the chief minister of the people. The king should be placed in the palace of the lord.
morphology: Then the king should make a vow to the lord of the kingdom of the king the king of the kings the lord the chief minister the governor of the people and the chief priest.

sanskrit: yaṃ kāmadevaṃ pravadaṃti loke citrāyudhaṃ puṣpaśaraṃ tathaiva | kāmapracārādhipatiṃ tameva mokṣadviṣaṃ māramudāharaṃti ||
reference: He whom they call in the world Kāmadeva, the owner of the various weapons, the flower-arrowed, the lord of the course of desire, — it is he whom they also style Māra the enemy of liberation.
baseline: One who preaches kāmadeva the image of the people the weapon the flower the garland etc. and the preceptor of lust the preacher of love is said to be the one who gives salvation and protection.
morphology: One who preaches kāmadeva the weapon of the image the flower and the garland etc. is the master of the propagation of lust. He is the one who gives salvation and the gift of mārmuda.

sanskrit: tasyātmajā vibhramaharṣadarpāstisro ratiprītitṛṣaśca kanyāḥ | papracchurenaṃ manaso vikāraṃ sa tāṃśca tāścaiva vaco babhāṣe ||
reference: His three sons, Confusion, Gaiety, and Pride, and his three daughters, Lust, Delight, and Thirst, asked of him the reason of his despondency, and he thus made answer unto them:
baseline: The daughter of the king of that kingdom is the illusion of the spirit the fear of the enemy the love of the country the desire for a wife and the desire to marry a woman. The king of the kingdom of the gods is said to be the one who destroys the mind and the people living in that kingdom.
morphology: The king of that soul is illusory the king of the mother the wife of the wife the daughter of the beloved daughter the mother of the child and the wife who has a mind that is distorted by it.

sanskrit: asau munirniścayavarma bibhrat sattvāyudhaṃ buddhiśaraṃ vikṛṣya | jigīṣurāste viṣayānmadīyān tasmādayaṃ me manaso viṣādaḥ ||
reference: ‘This sage, wearing the armour of resolution, and having drawn the arrow of wisdom with the barb of truth, sits yonder intending to conquer my realms, — hence is this despondency of my mind.
baseline: Having thus determined the matter one would be misguided by the power weapon intellect and other things. One would be distressed by that.
morphology: Having determined that he would not be able to fight the enemy he would be distracted by the illusion of the power the weapon the mind and the mind.

sanskrit: yadi hyasau māmabhibhūya yāti lokāya cākhyātyapavargamārgam | śūnyastato 'yaṃ viṣayo mamādya vṛttāccyutasyeva videhabhartuḥ ||
reference: ‘If he succeeds in overcoming me and proclaims to the world the path of final bliss, all this my realm will to-day become empty, as did that of the disembodied lord when he violated the rules of his station.
baseline: If one does not like the way of the class of people one should go to the house of the lord. He should leave the matter to me.
morphology: If one does not like the way of the class of people one should go to the other. One who has not heard of the matter should go away from me.

sanskrit: tadyāvadevaiṣa na labdhacakṣurmadgocare tiṣṭhati yāvadeva | yāsyāmi tāvadvratamasya bhettuṃ setuṃ nadīvega ivābhivṛddhaḥ ||
reference: ‘While, therefore, he stands within my reach and while his spiritual eyesight is not yet attained, I will assail him to break his vow as the swollen might of a river assails a dam.’
baseline: If one does not get the eye of the god he should remain in the temple. He should then go to the other side of the river.
morphology: If one does not get such a thing as a goddess he should be placed in the temple. He should be able to reach the river without the need of the two gods.

sanskrit: tato dhanuḥ puṣpamayaṃ gṛhītvā śarāṃstathā mohakarāṃśca paṃca | so 'śvatthamūlaṃ sasuto 'bhyagacchadasvāsthyakārī manasaḥ prajānām ||
reference: Then having seized his flower-made bow and his five infatuating arrows, he drew near to the root of the Aśvattha tree with his children, he the great disturber of the minds of living beings.
baseline: Then the bow should be taken with the flower of the five gods and the five beasts of the beast the source of the earth and the spirit of the people.
morphology: Then the bow should be taken with the flower of the five gods and the five elves should be given to the king. Then the source of the earth should be made clear to the people.

sanskrit: atha praśāṃtaṃ munimāsanasthaṃ pāraṃ titīrṣuṃ bhavasāgarasya | viṣajya savyaṃ karamāyudhāgre krīḍañśareṇedamuvāca māraḥ ||
reference: Having fixed his left hand on the end of the barb and playing with the arrow, Māra thus addressed the calm seer as he sat on his seat, preparing to cross to the further side of the ocean of existence:
baseline: Then one should sit in the seat of the sage and cross the sea of the sea. Having said so one should make a sacrifice by playing with the arms of the lord.
morphology: Then one should calmly cross the sage's seat across the sea of the three rivers and make a sacrifice by playing with the arms of the king.

sanskrit: uttiṣṭha bhoḥ kṣatriya mṛtyubhīta varasva dharmaṃ tyaja mokṣadharmam | vāṇaiśca [yajñaiśca] vinīya lokān lokān parān prāpnuhi vāsavasya ||
reference: ‘Up, up, O thou Kṣatriya, afraid of death! follow thine own duty and abandon this law of liberation! and having conquered the lower worlds by thy arrows [and sacrifices], proceed to gain the higher worlds of Indra.
baseline: A Kshatriya who is afraid of death and abandons the righteousness of his wife and renounces the religion of salvation should be worshipped as a kṣatriya. He should worship the people and get the people from others.
morphology: A Kshatriya who is afraid of death and abandons the righteousness of his heirs and renounces the religion of salvation should be humbled by the sacrifice of men men and others.

sanskrit: paṃthā hi niryātumayaṃ yaśasyo yo vāhitaḥ pūrvatamairnareṃdraiḥ | jātasya rājarṣikule viśāle bhaikṣākamaślāghyamidaṃ prapattum ||
reference: ‘That is a glorious path to travel, which has been followed by former leaders of men; this mendicant life is ill-suited for one born in the noble family of a royal sage to follow.
baseline: One who has been carried away by the king of the east and beyond should be blessed with the gift of a cow in the form of a pāṇṭha. One who is born in the hill of the king should be worshipped in the temple of the goddess Vīṣa.
morphology: One who carries the path of victory by the three directions of the east should be blessed with a large bhaikṣa. One who is born on the hill of the king should be worshipped in the temple.

sanskrit: athādya nottiṣṭhasi niścitātmā bhava sthiro mā vimucaḥ pratijñām | mayodyato hyeṣa śaraḥ sa eva yaḥ sūryake mīnaripau vimuktaḥ ||
reference: ‘But if thou wilt not rise, strong in thy purpose, — then be firm if thou wilt and quit not thy resolve, — this arrow is uplifted by me, — it is the very one which was shot against Sūryaka, the enemy of the fish.
baseline: One who does not know the meaning of the word should be assured of the spirit. One who is free from the sun and the waters of the sea should not be constrained by the promise of vimuṣa.
morphology: If you do not eat and drink the same thing then you are sure of the spirit. You do not make the promise of vimuṣu. The one who is free from the sun and pisces is the one who gives the promise.

sanskrit: pṛṣṭaḥ sa cānena kathaṃcidaiḍaḥ somasya naptāpyabhavadvicittaḥ | sa cābhavacchāṃtanurasvataṃtraḥ kṣīṇe yuge kiṃ vata durbalo 'nyaḥ ||
reference: ‘So too, I think, when somewhat probed by this weapon, even the son of Iḍā, the grandson of the moon, became mad; and Sāntanu also lost his self-control, — how much more then one of feebler powers now that the age has grown degenerate?
baseline: He would say that he would get rid of the sāma by the choice. He would then say that one would become weak in the age when he would lose his freedom and would not be able to do so.
morphology: He would say that he would get rid of the soma by the choice. He would not be able to do so. He said that he was weak in the age when he was tired and had no freedom.

sanskrit: tatkṣipramuttiṣṭha labhasva saṃjñāṃ vāṇo hyayaṃ tiṣṭhati lelihānaḥ | priyābhidheyeṣu ratipriyeṣu yaṃ cakravākeṣvapi notsṛjāmi ||
reference: ‘Therefore quickly rise up and come to thyself - for this arrow is ready, darting out its tongue, which I do not launch even against the cakravāka birds, tenderly attached as they are and well deserving the name of lovers.’
baseline: One who gets the knowledge of the forest and the forest should remain in the forest. One who does not suffer from diseases and those who do not love the enemy should also be sent to the king.
morphology: One who gets that gift from the king would get the knowledge from the forest. One who does not fall into the illusion of the enemy would get it from those who do not love the enemy.

sanskrit: ityevamukto 'pi yadā nirāstho naivāsanaṃ śākyamunirbibheda | śaraṃ tato 'smai visasarja māraḥ kanyāśca kṛtvā purataḥ sutāṃśca ||
reference: But when, even though thus addressed, the Śākya saint unheeding did not change his posture, then Māra discharged his arrow at him, setting in front of him his daughters and his sons.
baseline: Then when he is liberated from this and has made his abode empty he should be given a bath by the goddess Sākya. Then he should give the wife and daughter to her and then he should go to the east.
morphology: When this has been released the sākya muṇirvītā should be removed from the place of worship and the bride should be given a bath in the morning and the wife should be taken to the east.

sanskrit: tasmiṃstu vāṇe 'pi sa vipramukte cakāra nāsthāṃ na dhṛteścacāla | dṛṣṭvā tathainaṃ viṣasāda māraściṃtāparītaśca śanairjagāda ||
reference: But even when that arrow was shot he gave no heed and swerved not from his firmness; and Māra, beholding him thus, sank down, and slowly thus spoke, full of thought:
baseline: He should not be made to walk in the wilderness. He should neither walk nor walk without having to face it. Seeing it he should kill him with poison and make him drink with it.
morphology: He should not be made to walk on the ground without having done so. Seeing that he would not walk on fire and would not get drunk he should kill him with the poison and make him drink water.

sanskrit: śaileṃdraputrīṃ prati yena viddho devo 'pi śaṃbhuścalito babhūva | na ciṃtayatyeṣa tameva vāṇaṃ kiṃ syādacitto na śaraḥ sa eṣaḥ ||
reference: ‘He does not even notice that arrow by which the god Śambhu was pierced with love for the daughter of the mountain and shaken in his vow; can he be destitute of all feeling? is not this that very arrow?
baseline: One who has made a vow to the daughter of Śailendra the god of the gods and the goddess of the sambhu is not worried about what would happen to her. One who does not want to do so would be the king.
morphology: One who has become a god of knowledge by the worship of the daughter of Śailendra and one who has been given to Śāmbhu does not think what he wants to do. He does not want to do that.

sanskrit: tasmādayaṃ nārhati puṣpavāṇaṃ na harṣaṇaṃ nāpi raterniyogam | arhatyayaṃ bhūtagaṇairaśeṣaiḥ saṃtrāsanātarjanatāḍanāni ||
reference: ‘He is not worthy of my flower-shaft, nor my arrow “gladdener,” nor the sending of my daughter Rati (to tempt him); he deserves the alarms and rebukes and blows from all the gathered hosts of the demons.’
baseline: One would not get a flower a garland a hares or a fire. One would get half of the death by the use of the arrow and the rest of the ghosts by the incantation of orange leaves.
morphology: One would not get the flowers from it. One would get the rejoicing from the sun one would get victory from the king of the demons. One should get victory by the sacrifice of the king from the relics of the ghosts.

sanskrit: sasmāra māraśca tataḥ svasainyaṃ vidhvaṃsanaṃ śākyamuneścikīrṣan | nānāśrayāścānucarāḥ parīyuḥ śaradrumaprāsagadāsihastāḥ ||
reference: Then Māra called to mind his own army, wishing to work the overthrow of the Śākya saint; and his followers swarmed round, wearing different forms and carrying arrows, trees, darts, clubs, and swords in their hands;
baseline: Then he would destroy his own army with the sword and destroy it with the help of the sākya muṇas. He would destroy them with the aid of various weapons and would destroy their enemies.
morphology: Then they destroy their army with the sword and destroy it with the help of the sākya muṇas. They will destroy the enemy with the aid of various weapons and will destroy them.

sanskrit: varāhamīnāśvakharoṣṭravaktrā vyāghrarkṣasiṃhadviradānanāśca | ekekṣaṇā naikamukhāstriśīrṣā laṃbodarāścaiva pṛṣodarāśca ||
reference: Having the faces of boars, fishes, horses, asses, and camels, of tigers, bears, lions, and elephants, — one-eyed, many-faced, three-headed, — with protuberant bellies and speckled bellies;
baseline: The king of the kingdom of Vārāhaminā the prophet the tiger the lion and the lion are worshipped with the gift of the two gods. The king living in Lamborghini and the king of Perus is said to have three heads at one go.
morphology: One should offer a tiger a lion a bull a tiger and a lion and the king of the kingdom of Vārāhamīna the king living in Lamborghini and the lord of Prāsodara with three faces at one go.

sanskrit: ajāsu saktā ghaṭajānavaśca daṃṣṭrāyudhāścaiva nakhāyudhāśca | kabaṃdhahastā bahumūrtayaśca bhagnārdhavaktrāśca mahāmukhāśca ||
reference: Blended with goats, with knees swollen like pots, armed with tusks and with claws, carrying headless trunks in their hands, and assuming many forms, with half-mutilated faces, and with monstrous mouths;
baseline: One who is armed with a sword a sword and a sword should be bound with a piece of cloth. One who has broken a piece and a great mouth should be tied with a thread.
morphology: One who is armed with a sword a sword and a sword should be bound with a knife. One who has a sword is bound with the sword and has a great mouth.

sanskrit: tāmrāruṇā lohitaviṃducitrāḥ khaṭvāṃgahastā haridhūmrakeśāḥ | laṃbasrajo vāraṇalaṃbakarṇāścarmāṃbarāścaiva niraṃbarāśca ||
reference: Copper-red, covered with red spots, bearing clubs in their hands, with yellow or smoke-coloured hair, with wreaths dangling down, with long pendulous ears like elephants, clothed in leather or wearing no clothes at all;
baseline: The body of a man should be made of copper red white white and white. The body should be of white colour. The head should be long and white and the head should not be dark.
morphology: The body of a man should be made of copper red white red and white. The body should be of green colour. The head should be long and straight and the head should not be long.

sanskrit: śvetārdhavaktrā haritārdhakāyāstāmrāśca dhūmrā harayo 'sitāśca | vyāḍottarāsaṃgabhujāstathaiva praghuṣṭaghaṃṭākulamekhalāśca ||
reference: Having half their faces white or half their bodies green, — red and smoke-coloured, yellow and black, — with arms reaching out longer than a serpent, and with girdles jingling with rattling bells.
baseline: The white half of the mouth is equal to the green half of that of the head and the smoldering half to the white half and the golden half is equal in size to that of a head.
morphology: The white half of the mouth should be half of that of the green half. The smog should be equal to that of that which is green. The bell should be opened with the same sound as the bell.

sanskrit: tālapramāṇāśca gṛhītaśūlā daṃṣṭrākarālāśca śiśupramāṇāḥ | urabhravaktrāśca vihaṃgamāśca mārjāravaktrāśca manuṣyakāyāḥ ||
reference: Some were as tall as palm-trees, carrying spears, — others were of the size of children with projecting teeth, others birds with the faces of rams, others with men’s bodies and cats’ faces;
baseline: One who takes a piece of gold a piece made of clay a small piece of cloth a man who is a prophet a person with a wide face and a man with a mouth is called a prāmana.
morphology: One who takes a piece of gold and a piece one who has a bow and a bow and a child is known to be a prophet a man who speaks in the sky and a man with a mouth.

sanskrit: prakīrṇakeśāḥ śikhino 'rdhamuṃḍā rajjvaṃbarā vyākulaveṣṭanāśca | prahṛṣṭavaktrā bhṛkuṭīmukhāśca tejoharāścaiva manoharāśca ||
reference: With dishevelled hair, or with topknots, or half-bald, with rope-garments or with head-dress all in confusion, — with triumphant faces or frowning faces, — wasting the strength or fascinating the mind.
baseline: One who has a wide hair a long hair an arched head a string of ropes a troubled neck a pretentious speaker a dumb face a bright and beautiful person living in the sky is known to be a great man.
morphology: One who has a wide hair a long hair an arched head a rope a nervous neck a sharp mouth a fiery face a bright face and a beautiful person living in the midst of the sky is said to be a great man.

sanskrit: kecidvrajaṃto bhṛśamāvavalguranyo 'nyamāpupluvire tathānye | cikrīḍurākāśagatāśca kecitkecicca cerustarumastakeṣu ||
reference: Some as they went leaped about wildly, others danced upon one another, some sported about in the sky, others went along on the tops of the trees.
baseline: One would get two kinds of flowers one with the leaves another with the flowers another one with bhiṣma vālāgurā and others with the flower. One with the chakrīdura akāśagatā and a few others would get a lot of flowers.
morphology: One should also worship the goddess Bhṛṣma Vālāgurā and others. The goddesses of the sky and other things should be worshipped in the temple.

sanskrit: nanarta kaścidbhramayaṃstriśūlaṃ kaściddha pusphūrja gadāṃ vikarṣan | harṣeṇa kaścidvṛṣavannanarta kaścitprajajvāla tanūruhebhyaḥ ||
reference: One danced, shaking a trident, another made a crash, dragging a club, another bounded for joy like a bull, another blazed out flames from every hair.
baseline: One who has made a journey by walking on the ground and having made a trip by sitting on the trunk of a bull one who has drawn a mace another who has done two rounds of fire by rejoicing has made the fire of a cow.
morphology: Then one of them would go around the earth and make a journey. Then another would go across the mound and defile the mace. Then the other would go down with joy and light a flame.

sanskrit: evaṃvidhā bhūtagaṇāḥ samaṃtāttadbodhimūlaṃ parivārya tasthuḥ | jighṛkṣavaścaiva jighāṃsavaśca bharturniyogaṃ paripālayaṃtaḥ ||
reference: Such were the troops of demons who encircled the root of the Bodhi tree on every side, eager to seize it and to destroy it, awaiting the command of their lord.
baseline: In the same way one should treat the ghosts in the same manner as those living in the forest. One should treat them with the knowledge of the earth. One who lives in the wilderness should take care of his wife and his relatives.
morphology: In the same way the members of the family should be aware of the existence of ghosts. Those who live in the jigha and jighas should take care of their relatives.

sanskrit: taṃ prekṣya mārasya ca pūrvarātre śākyarṣabhasyaiva ca yuddhakālam | na dyauścakāśe pṛthivī cakaṃpe prajajvaluścaiva diśaḥ saśabdāḥ ||
reference: Beholding in the first half of the night that battle of Māra and the bull of the Śākya race, the heavens did not shine and the earth shook and the (ten) regions of space flashed flame and roared.
baseline: Having seen him the king should pay tribute to him in the night before and the king of sākhya śārva in the war. He should not give the sky the earth the chakmpa the people living in the fire and the direction of the battle.
morphology: Having seen him the king should be sent to war in the night before and the king of sākhya śrva should be given the night. The king should not be seen in the sky the earth the fire the people and the people living in the fire.

sanskrit: viṣvagvavau vāyurudīrṇavegastārā na rejurna babhau śaśāṃkaḥ | tamaśca bhūyo vitatāra rātreḥ sarve ca saṃcukṣubhire samudrāḥ ||
reference: A wind of intense violence blew in all directions, the stars did not shine, the moon gave no light, and a deeper darkness of night spread around, and all the oceans were agitated.
baseline: O Vishva the wind the water the steam the sky the earth the sea the sun and the sea are all pervading in the night.
morphology: The sky should be divided into two parts. The sea should not be divided by the wind water wind fire water and water. The earth should be separated by the sea.

sanskrit: mahībhṛto dharmaparāśca nāgā mahāmunervighnamamṛṣyamāṇāḥ | māraṃ prati krodhavivṛttanetrā niḥśaśvasuścaiva jajṛṃbhire ca ||
reference: The mountain deities and the Nāgas who honoured the Law, indignant at the attack on the saint, rolling their eyes in anger against Māra, heaved deep sighs and opened their mouths wide.
baseline: The great gods the virtuous ones the great men the misguided ones those who are living in the midst of the enemy and those who live in the land of the king without any fear of wrath.
morphology: The great gods and the virtuous ones are those who do not behave themselves in a manner which is not acceptable to the king. They are those living in the heart and in the body of the judge who are not angry with the king and who are living in a state of ignorance.

sanskrit: śuddhādhivāsā vibudharṣayastu saddharmasiddhyarthamiva pravṛttāḥ | māre 'nukaṃpāṃ manasā pracakrurvirāgabhāvāttu na roṣamīyuḥ ||
reference: But the god-sages, the Śuddhādhivāsas, being as it were absorbed in the perfect accomplishment of the good Law, felt only a pity for Māra in their minds and through their absolute passionlessness were unruffled by anger.
baseline: One who is pure and does not get angry by the presence of evil spirits should be punished with the sādharma method. One who does not suffer from evil thoughts should not be angry with the mind.
morphology: One should not get angry by the presence of the mind in the midst of a purified state of mind. One should do good deeds in the same manner as one would do. One would not get irritated by the illusion of the heart.

sanskrit: tadbodhimūlaṃ samavekṣya kīrṇaṃ hiṃsātmanā mārabalena tena | dharmātmabhirlokavimokṣakāmairbabhūva hāhākṛtamaṃtarīkṣam ||
reference: When they saw the foot of the Bodhi tree crowded with that host of Māra, intent on doing harm, — the sky was filled with the cry raised by all the virtuous beings who desired the world’s liberation.
baseline: Having seen the image of the earth with the spirit of violence and the force of war one would get rid of the world of righteousness. One would get the manifestation of the mind.
morphology: Having seen the image of the earth with the spirit of violence and the force of war one should be able to see the image. One should be free from the evil spirit and the world.

sanskrit: upaplutaṃ dharmavidastu tasya dṛṣṭvā sthitaṃ mārabalaṃ mahārṣiḥ | na cukṣubhe nāpi yayau vikāraṃ madhye gavāṃ siṃha ivopaviṣṭaḥ ||
reference: But the great sage having beheld that army of Māra thus engaged in an attack on the knower of the Law, remained untroubled and suffered no perturbation, like a lion seated in the midst of oxen.
baseline: Having seen him who knows the righteousness of the people the king of Marābāla is sitting on the ground. He is not sitting in the middle of the fire nor sitting on a lion.
morphology: The great sage who knows the righteousness of the people should be seen standing in front of him. He should not be seen sitting in the middle of the fire or sitting on a lion.

sanskrit: mārastato bhūtacamūmudīrṇāmājñāpayāmāsa bhayāya tasya | svaiḥ svaiḥ prabhāvairatha sāsya senā taddhairyabhedāya matiṃ cakāra ||
reference: Then Māra commanded his excited army of demons to terrify him; and forthwith that host resolved to break down his determination with their various powers.
baseline: The king should be afraid of the ghosts and the demons. Having been influenced by them the army should be divided for the sake of their patience.
morphology: Having feared the ghosts and other evil spirits and having been influenced by them the army agreed to the division of their fortitude.

sanskrit: keciccalannaikavilaṃbijihvāstīkṣṇogradaṃṣṭrā harimaṃḍalākṣāḥ | vidāritāsyāḥ sthiraśaṃkukarṇāḥ saṃtrāsayaṃtaḥ kila nāma tasthuḥ ||
reference: Some with many tongues hanging out and shaking, with sharp-pointed savage teeth and eyes like the disk of the sun, with wide-yawning mouths and upright ears like spikes, — they stood round trying to frighten him.
baseline: One should observe a cave with a stone of a small size. One should have a mound of green leaves with a piece of water and a stone with a fixed conch and orange hair.
morphology: One should observe a cave with a little bit of water and the ground should be covered with green grass. One who is standing on the ground with a steady conch and an orange hair should be called a fort.

sanskrit: tebhyaḥ sthitebhyaḥ sa tathāvidhebhyaḥ rūpeṇa bhāvena ca dāruṇebhyaḥ | na vivyathe nodvivije mahārṣiḥ krīḍan subālebhya ivoddhatebhyaḥ ||
reference: Before these monsters standing there, so dreadful in form and disposition, the great sage remained unalarmed and untroubled, sporting with them as if they had been only rude children.
baseline: He should be present in those places and should be worshipped in the form of a priest and for those who do evil deeds. He should not be seen playing with the mighty men who do not get victory in the battle.
morphology: He should be present in those places and should be worshipped in the form of a priest a nobleman and a noble man. He should not be seen playing in the streets and conquering the mighty men.

sanskrit: kaścittato raudravivṛttadṛṣṭistasmai gadāmudyamayāṃcakāra | tastaṃbha bāhuḥ sagadastato 'sya puraṃdarasyeva purā savajraḥ ||
reference: Then one of them, with his eyes rolling wildly, lifted up a club against him; but his arm with the club was instantly paralysed, as was Indra’s of old with its thunderbolt.
baseline: One who sees a cow in the midst of a storm and a man sitting on the ground with a donkey is called a sow. The pillar should be placed on the right arm and the temple should be completely covered with water.
morphology: One who sees a cow in the middle of a row with a frown should offer the donkey a piece of cloth. The pillar should be placed in the right arm and the whole of the temple should be covered with water.

sanskrit: kecitsamudyamya śilāstarūṃśca viṣehire naiva munau vimoktum | petuḥ savṛkṣāḥ saśilāstathaiva vajrāvabhagnā iva viṃdhyapādāḥ ||
reference: Some, having lifted up stones and trees, found themselves unable to throw them against the sage; down they fell, with their trees and their stones, like the roots of the Vindhya shattered by the thunderbolt.
baseline: The stone should not be placed on the ground after having been covered with a piece of stone. The leaves should be kept in the ground with a tree a stone and a vindhyapada like a diamond.
morphology: The stone should not be placed on the ground with the help of a stone or a stone. The leaves should be made to stand on a tree and the leaves should also be made like a diamond and a fig tree.

sanskrit: kaiścitsamutpatya nabho vimuktāḥ śilāśca vṛkṣāśca paraśvadhāśca | tasthurnabhasyeva na cāvapetuḥ saṃdhyābhrapādā iva naikavarṇāḥ ||
reference: Others, leaping up into the sky, flung rocks, trees, and axes; these remained in the sky and did not fall down, like the many-coloured rays of the evening clouds.
baseline: After having obtained some of these things the stones are liberated. The trees and other parts of the earth are not covered by the fire. They are not as many colours as the sun water and sand.
morphology: After having obtained some of these things the stones are liberated. The trees and other parts of the earth are not covered by the fire. They are not as many colours as the sun moon and the sun.

sanskrit: cikṣepa tasyopari dīptamanyaḥ kaḍaṃgaraṃ parvataśṛṃgamātram | yanmuktamātraṃ gaganasthameva tasyānubhāvācchatadhā babhūva ||
reference: Another hurled upon him a mass of blazing straw as big as a mountain-peak, which, as soon as it was thrown, while it hung poised in the sky, was shattered into a hundred fragments by the sage’s power.
baseline: The image of the mountain is only the top of the hill and the sky is the only thing that is free from it.
morphology: The image of a mountain is only the top of the mountain. The only thing that is liberated from it is the feeling of the sky.

sanskrit: kaścijjvalannarka ivoditaḥ khādaṃgāravarṣaṃ mahadutsasarja | cūrnāni cāmīkarakaṃdarāṇāṃ kalpātyaye meruriva pradīptaḥ ||
reference: One, rising up like the sun in full splendour, rained down from the sky a great shower of live embers, as at the end of an aeon blazing Meru showers down the pulverised scoriae of the golden valleys.
baseline: One who has made a fire or a fire one who has not been burned has made an offering of gold and gold and a gift of a great amount of gold. One who makes the stones of the churṇas and the walls of the temples is illuminated by the mermaid.
morphology: One who has made a fire or a fire one who has given a rain of gold and a great fire and who has cast stones and other objects on the earth is illuminated by the mermaid.

sanskrit: tadbodhimūle pravikīryamāṇamaṃgāravarṣaṃ tu savisphuliṃgam | maitrīvihārādṛṣisattamasya babhūva raktotpalapatravarṣaḥ ||
reference: But that shower of embers full of sparks, when scattered at the foot of the Bodhi tree, became a shower of red lotus-petals through the operation of the great saint’s boundless charity.
baseline: The golden year should be described as the best year for the cultivation of crops. The best year is the year of blood and leaves produced by the practice of maitrivihara.
morphology: The golden year is said to be the best year for the cultivation of fruits. The best year of the harvest is the year of blood and leaves.

sanskrit: śarīracittavyasanātapaistairevaṃvidhaistaiśca nipātyamānaiḥ | naivāsanācchākyamuniścacāla svaṃ niścayaṃ baṃdhumivopaguhya ||
reference: But with all these various scorching assaults on his body and his mind, and all these missiles showered down upon him, the Śākya saint did not in the least degree move from his posture, clasping firmly his resolution as a kinsman.
baseline: Having destroyed the body mind and the body in any manner. Having destroyed them one should make sure that the body and the lower body are not covered by the evil spirit.
morphology: One who destroys the body mind and body in any way would be bound by the rules of the body. One who does not wear clothes and does not walk should be bound to his own relatives.

sanskrit: athāpare nirjagalurmukhebhyaḥ sarpānvijīrṇebhya iva drumebhyaḥ | te maṃtrabaddhā iva tatsamīpe na śaśvasurnotsasṛjurna celuḥ ||
reference: Then others spat out serpents from their mouths as from old decayed trunks of trees; but, as if held fast by a charm, near him they neither breathed nor discharged venom nor moved.
baseline: Then the serpent should be sent to the other side of the earth as if it were a snake. They should not be placed near it as if they were tied with a mantra. The celestial body should be made of gold.
morphology: Then they should be made to look like serpents in front of the world without any fear. They should not be placed near it as if they were bound by a mantra.

sanskrit: bhūtvāpare vāridharā vṛhaṃtaḥ savidyutaḥ sāśanicaṃḍaghoṣāḥ | tasmin drume tatyajuraśmavarṣaṃ tatpuṣpavarṣaṃ ruciraṃ babhūva ||
reference: Others, having become great clouds, emitting lightning and uttering the fierce roar of thunderbolts, poured a shower of stones upon that tree, — but it turned to a pleasant shower of flowers.
baseline: The bhaṭtavāpāra is a large and electrifying river. It is said to be the best year for the sowing of flowers.
morphology: Then there should be a great wave of water and electricity. In that wave the sun should be lit up and the rain of flowers should be poured out in the year of ten years.

sanskrit: cāpe 'tha vāṇo nihito 'pareṇa jajvāla tatraiva na niṣpapāta | anīśvarasyātmani dhūryamāṇo durmarṣaṇasyeva narasya manyuḥ ||
reference: Another set an arrow in his bow, — there it gleamed but it did not issue forth, like the anger which falls slack in the soul of an ill-tempered impotent man.
baseline: The spirit of the unbeliever should not be destroyed by the force of the forest or by the fire. The soul of a man should not suffer evil deeds.
morphology: The spirit of the unbeliever should not be destroyed by the forces of the forest or the fire. The soul of a man should be made to suffer evil.

sanskrit: paṃceṣavo 'nyena tu vipramuktāstasthurnayatyeva munau na petuḥ | saṃsārabhīrorviṣayapravṛttau paṃceṃdriyāṇīva parīkṣakasya ||
reference: But five arrows shot by another stood motionless and fell not, through the saint’s ruling guidance, — like the five senses of him who is well experienced in the course of worldly objects and is afraid of embodied existence.
baseline: One should not get the king of the world without having to do five or more things. One who is fearful of the universe would not get it. The judge should have five senses.
morphology: One should not get rid of the evil spirit by the use of fifty others. One who does not get the fear of the world would get the five senses of the judge.

sanskrit: jighāṃsayānyaḥ prasasāra ruṣṭo gadāṃ gṛhītvābhimukho mahārṣeḥ | so 'prāptakālo vivaśaḥ papāta doṣeṣvivānarthakareṣu lokaḥ ||
reference: Another, full of anger, rushed towards the great saint, having seized a club with a desire to smite him; but he fell powerless without finding an opportunity, like mankind in the presence of faults which cause failure.
baseline: One who takes a mace and holds it with his face and then throws it into the great river should be punished by the king.
morphology: One who takes a donkey and holds it with his mouth and then throws it at the king should be punished by the king.

sanskrit: strī meghakālī tu kapālahastā kartuṃ mahārṣeḥ kila mohacittam | babhrāma tatrāniyataṃ na tasthau calātmano buddhirivāgameṣu ||
reference: But a woman named Meghakālī, bearing a skull in her hand, in order to infatuate the mind of the sage, flitted about unsettled and stayed not in one spot, like the mind of the fickle student over the sacred texts.
baseline: A woman should be made to face the clouds with her forehead and the head with her head and the neck with her hands. The king should not be allowed to move the body and mind in the coming days.
morphology: A woman should be made to face the clouds and the forehead should be shaven with a maharāśa. The king should not be allowed to move in the presence of the mind.

sanskrit: kaścitpradīptaṃ praṇidhāya cakṣurnetrāgnināśīviṣavaddidhakṣuḥ | tatraiva nāsīttamṛṣiṃ dadarśa kāmātmakaḥ śreya ivopadiṣṭam ||
reference: Another, fixing a kindling eye, wished to burn him with the fire of his glance like a poisonous serpent; but he saw the sage and lo! he was not there, like the votary of pleasure when true happiness is pointed out to him.
baseline: One who is not able to see the best of the crops and who is having a desire to see is said to be blessed. One who does not see the fire and poison in the eyes and who has no desire to do so is not good.
morphology: One who has not seen the best of the crops and has not had any illusion would be blessed with the fire poison and poison.

sanskrit: gurvīṃ śilāmudyamayaṃstathānyaḥ śaśrāma moghaṃ vihataprayatnaḥ | niḥśreyasaṃ jñānasamādhigamyaṃ kāyaklamairdharmamivāptukāmaḥ ||
reference: Another, lifting up a heavy rock, wearied himself to no purpose, having his efforts baffled, like one who wishes to obtain by bodily fatigue that condition of supreme happiness which is only to be reached by meditation and knowledge.
baseline: One should worship the cow the stone the mound the serpent the pitchers the cow and the cow. One should be free from evil thoughts and do good deeds.
morphology: One should worship the cow the stone the mound the serpent the goddess of peace the mother of knowledge and the goddess Kaikalma.

sanskrit: tarakṣusiṃhākṛtayastathānye praṇeduruccairmahataḥ praṇādān | sattvāni yaiḥ saṃcukucuḥ samaṃtādvajrāhatā dyauḥ phalatīti matvā ||
reference: Others, wearing the forms of hyenas and lions, uttered loudly fierce howls, which caused all beings round to quail with terror, as thinking that the heavens were smitten with a thunderbolt and were bursting.
baseline: The prāṇas should be made with the spears horns and the prāmanas of the gods. The virtues should be worshipped with the saṃtākuṣuṣa and the two jāhāras. It is believed to be the fruit.
morphology: One should offer the prāṇas of the gods with the arrow and the lion in the forehead and with the māhātamā. One would get the benefits of having two cubes of water with which one would be able to bear the fruits.

sanskrit: mṛgā gajāścārttaravān sṛjaṃto vidudruvuścaiva nililyire ca | rātrau ca tasyāmahanīva digbhyaḥ khagā ruvaṃtaḥ paripeturārttāḥ ||
reference: Deer and elephants uttering cries of pain ran about or lay down, — in that night as if it were day screaming birds flew around disturbed in all directions.
baseline: One who has created the earth who dwells in the blue sky and who has made the earth and the earth. One who does not know the direction of the earth in the night one who is the king of the sky and the god of the world is known to be the king.
morphology: He who creates the earth who creates it and who dwells in the blue sky who makes the earth fall from the directions of the sun and the sky in the night and the king of the earth.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ praṇādaistu tathāvidhaistaiḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣvapi kaṃpiteṣu | munirna tatrāsa na saṃcukoca ravairgarutmāniva vāyasānām ||
reference: But amidst all these various sounds which they made, although all living creatures were shaken, the saint trembled not nor quailed, like Garuḍa at the noise of crows.
baseline: All the spirits should be worshipped by them. The sages should not be made to bow down to the sun or the wind.
morphology: All the spirits should be worshipped by them and all the spirits are shaken by them. The sage should not be made to sit therein nor to be carried away by the wind.

sanskrit: bhayāvahebhyaḥ pariṣadgaṇebhyo yathā yathā naiva munirbibhāya | tathā tathā dharmabhṛtāṃ sapatnaḥ śokācca roṣācca sasāra māraḥ ||
reference: The less the saint feared the frightful hosts of that multitude, the more did Māra, the enemy of the righteous, continue his attacks in grief and anger.
baseline: The king should not be afraid of fearful people and the council members. In the same way the king should be ashamed of his righteousness and his wife and brother in law.
morphology: The king should not be afraid of the fearful people in the council. In the same way the king should be ashamed of his righteousness and his wife and his father in law.

sanskrit: bhūtaṃ tataḥ kiṃcidadṛśyarūpaṃ viśiṣṭarūpaṃ gaganasthameva | dṛṣṭvārṣaye drugdhamavairaruṣṭaṃ māraṃ babhāṣe mahatā svareṇa ||
reference: Then some being of invisible shape, but of pre-eminent glory, standing in the heavens, — beholding Māra thus malevolent against the seer, — addressed him in a loud voice, unruffled by enmity:
baseline: Then there is another manifestation of the ghost in the sky. In the year of the sighting one gets to see milk and other things. The sound of the demon is great in the speech.
morphology: Then there is a manifestation of the ghost. The manifestation is in the sky. In the year of the sighting the milk is made to appear in the air. The sound of the voice is great.

sanskrit: moghaṃ śramaṃ nārhasi māra kartuṃ hiṃsrātmatāmutsṛja gaccha śarma | naiṣa tvayā kaṃpayituṃ hi śakyo mahāgirirmerurivānilena ||
reference: ‘Take not on thyself, O Māra, this vain fatigue, — throw aside thy malevolence and retire to peace; this sage cannot be shaken by thee any more than the mighty mountain Meru by the wind.
baseline: O king of the mighty army you have not been able to make an effort to kill him. You go to the king with a fierce spirit. You are not able to shake him and you are not going to be able to fight him.
morphology: If you do not make an effort to kill the enemy you will be ashamed to go to the king. You could not shake the king and the king of the mighty army.

sanskrit: apyuṣṇabhāvaṃ jvalanaḥ prajahyādāpo dravatvaṃ pṛthivī sthiratvam | anekakalpācitapuṇyakarmā na tveva jahyādvyavasāyameṣaḥ ||
reference: ‘Even fire might lose its hot nature, water its fluidity, earth its steadiness, but never will he abandon his resolution, who has acquired his merit by a long course of actions through unnumbered aeons.
baseline: One who does not practice many imaginative and virtuous practices would be a fire a vessel a people a liquid an earth a stable entity. One who is not doing any other occupation would be an enemy.
morphology: One who does not practice many things and does not engage in any other occupation should be subject to heat fire water liquid earth stability etc.

sanskrit: yo niścayo hyasya parākramaśca tejaśca yadyā ca dayā prajāsu | aprāpya notthāsyati tattvameṣa tamāṃsyahatveva sahasraraśmiḥ ||
reference: ‘Such is that purpose of his, that heroic effort, that glorious strength, that compassion for all beings, — until he attains the highest wisdom, he will never rise from his seat, just as the sun does not rise, without dispelling the darkness.
baseline: If one is sure of his strength and brilliance then he will get mercy from his subjects. He will not get the elements. He would get a thousand rāśmis for his death.
morphology: If one is sure of his strength and glory one will get mercy from his subjects. He will not get the elements. A thousand rāmasis will be killed by him.

sanskrit: kāṣṭhaṃ hi mathnan labhate hutāśaṃ bhūmiṃ khanan viṃdati cāpi toyam | nirbaṃdhinaḥ kiṃca na nāsya sādhyaṃ nyāyena yuktaṃ ca kṛtaṃ ca sarvam ||
reference: ‘One who rubs the two pieces of wood obtains the fire, one who digs the earth finds at last the water, — and to him in his perseverance there is nothing unattainable, — all things to him are reasonable and possible.
baseline: One who digs into the ground would get the wood and eat it. One who does not destroy the prisoners would get justice and all that is done.
morphology: One who digs a piece of land and drinks water from the ground would get the wood. One who does not destroy the prisoners would get justice.

sanskrit: tallokamārttaṃ karuṇāyamāno rogeṣu rāgādiṣu vartamānam | mahābhiṣagnārhati vighnameṣa jñānauṣadhārthaṃ parikhidyamānaḥ ||
reference: ‘Pitying the world lying distressed amidst diseases and passions, he, the great physician, ought not to be hindered, who undergoes all his labours for the sake of the remedy knowledge.
baseline: The image of the heart is present in diseases and diseases and in anger. Great distortions and disturbances are found in the body for the sake of knowledge and healing.
morphology: One who has experienced the illness of the heart and the disease of the body should be blessed with the gift of the word tāloka. One who experiences the great evil would be destroyed by the evil one.

sanskrit: hṛte ca loke bahubhiḥ kumārgaiḥ sanmārgamanvicchati yaḥ śrameṇa | sa daiśikaḥ kṣobhayituṃ na yuktaṃ sudeśikaḥ sārtha iva pranaṣṭe ||
reference: ‘He who toilsomely pursues the one good path, when all the world is carried away in devious tracks, — he the guide should not be disturbed, like a right informant when the caravan has lost its way.
baseline: The one who leads the way with a lot of heart and hands to a noble person with hard work is not worthy of provoking the enemy. He who does not want to provoke the enemy should be sent to the king as far as possible.
morphology: One who has a lot of people in his heart and leads the way with the hands of a nobleman with hard work would not be able to provoke the enemy. One who does not want to disturb the enemy would become a good neighbour.

sanskrit: sattveṣu naṣṭeṣu mahāṃdhakārairjñānapradīpaḥ kriyamāṇa eṣaḥ | āryasya nirvāpayituṃ na sādhu prajvālyamānastamasīva dīpaḥ ||
reference: ‘He who is made a lamp of knowledge when all beings are lost in the great darkness, — it is not for a right-minded soul to try to quench him, — like a lamp kindled in the gloom of night.
baseline: This is the lamp of knowledge which is the great destroyer among the seventy destroyed beings. It is the same lamp which is not lit by the saint to extinguish the evil one.
morphology: This is the lamp of knowledge which is the great destroyer among the seven destroyed gods. It is the same lamp which is not lit by the saint to dispel the evil one.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā ca saṃsāramaye mahaughe magnaṃ jagatpāramaviṃdamānam | yaścedamuttārayituṃ pravṛttaḥ kaścinnayettasya tu pāpamāryaḥ ||
reference: ‘He who, when he beholds the world drowned in the great flood of existence and unable to reach the further shore, strives to bring them safely across, — would any right-minded soul offer him wrong?
baseline: One who looks at the world and sees it in the great open space and the world as a whole and is inclined to do the same would be guilty of the sin.
morphology: One who looks at the world and sees it in the great open world and who is inclined to make a return to the world would be guilty of sin.

sanskrit: kṣamāśipho dhairyavigāḍhamūlaścāritrapuṣpaḥ smṛtibuddhiśākhaḥ | jñānadrumo dharmaphalapradātā notpāṭanaṃ hyarhati vardhamānaḥ ||
reference: ‘The tree of knowledge, whose roots go deep in firmness, and whose fibres are patience, — whose flowers are moral actions and whose branches are memory and thought, — and which gives out the law as its fruit, — surely when it is growing it should not be cut down.
baseline: The flower of remembrance is the flower of forgiveness patience misfortune wisdom knowledge knowledge and the fruit of righteousness.
morphology: The flower of remembrance is the flower of forgiveness the root of fortitude and the root. The flower that gives knowledge and the fruit of righteousness is the fruitful flower of knowledge.

sanskrit: baddhāṃ dṛḍhaiścetasi mohapāśairyasya prajāṃ mokṣayituṃ manīṣā | tasmin jighāṃsā tava nopapannā śrāṃte jagadbaṃdhanamokṣahetoḥ ||
reference: ‘Him whose one desire is to deliver mankind bound in soul by the fast snares of illusion, — thy wish to overthrow him is not worthy, wearied as he is for the sake of unloosing the bonds of the world.
baseline: Having said that one would like to liberate the subjects of the illusion. One would get rid of the bondage if one does not suffer the loss of his life.
morphology: He should be bound and made firm. He would be willing to free the subjects of the illusion. He should not suffer the loss of his life and the world.

sanskrit: bodhāya karmāṇi hi yānyanena kṛtāni teṣāṃ niyato 'dya kālaḥ | sthāne tathāsminnupaviṣṭa eṣa yathaiva pūrve munayastathaiva ||
reference: ‘To-day is the appointed period of all those actions which have been performed by him for the sake of knowledge, — he is now seated on this seat just as all the previous saints have sat.
baseline: The actions done by him should be explained by the priest. The time fixed for them should be fixed. He should be seated in the same place as the king in the east.
morphology: The deeds done by him in order to make him aware of these things should be fixed at the appointed time. He should be seated in the place and the moon should be placed in the east as before.

sanskrit: eṣā hi nābhirvasudhātalasya kṛtsnena yuktā parameṇa dhāmnā | bhūmerato 'nyo 'sti hi na pradeśo veśaṃ samādherviṣayo hitasya ||
reference: ‘This is the navel of the earth’s surface, endued with all the highest glory; there is no other spot of the earth than this, — the home of contemplation, the realm of well-being.
baseline: This is the abode of the Supreme Being which is made up of the abyss of the navel and the ground. It is not a place or a place for the enjoyment of others.
morphology: This is the abode of the Supreme Being which is situated on the ground and is not a place for the enjoyment of others.

sanskrit: tanmā kṛthāḥ śokamupehi śāṃtiṃ mā bhūnmahimnā tava māra mānaḥ | viśraṃbhituṃ na kṣamamadhruvā śrīścale pade kiṃ padamabhyupaiṣi ||
reference: ‘Give not way, then, to grief but put on calm; let not thy greatness, O Māra, be mixed with pride; it is not well to be confident, — fortune is unstable, — why dost thou accept a position on a tottering base?’
baseline: Having said this do not make peace with yourself in the face of sorrow. Do not make your mother proud by resting on the ground. Do you not forgive the priest and the priest in the posture of Śrī.
morphology: O lord of the earth do not make peace by doing the same with you and do not be ashamed of your honour. Do not forgive me for resting on the pole and the feet of the lord.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa saṃśrutya ca tasya tadvaco mahāmuneḥ prekṣya ca niṣprakaṃpatām | jagāma māro vimanā hatodyamaḥ śarairjagaccetasi yairvihanyase ||
reference: Having listened to his words, and having seen the unshaken firmness of the great saint, Māra departed dispirited and broken in purpose with those very arrows by which, O world, thou art smitten in thy heart.
baseline: Then he would make a promise and send him to a great lord. He would destroy the king by killing him and then he would destroy him by attacking him.
morphology: Then he would make a promise and send him to a great lord like him. He would destroy the king by killing him and then he would destroy him by attacking him.

sanskrit: gatapraharṣā viphalīkṛtaśramā praviddhapāṣāṇakaḍaṃgaradrumā | diśaḥ pradudrāva tato 'sya sā camūrhatāśrayeva dviṣatā dviṣaccamūḥ ||
reference: With their triumph at an end, their labour all fruitless, and all their stones, straw, and trees thrown away, that host of his fled in all directions, like some hostile army when its camp has been destroyed by the enemy.
baseline: One who enters the temple after having failed in the previous journey would get a mountain mountain forest and river. The direction of the river would be two hundred and twenty feet.
morphology: After having entered the temple after having failed in the previous journey he would enter the temple of Paṇaṇa. Then the direction would become polluted. Then he would lie in the shelter of the elephant. He would get two hundred and twenty feet.

sanskrit: dravati saparapakṣe nirjite puṣpaketau jayati jitatamaske nīrajaske mahārṣau | yuvatiriva sahāsā dyauścakāśe sacaṃdrā surabhi ca jalagarbhaṃ puṣpavarṣaṃ papāta ||
reference: When the flower-armed god thus fled away vanquished with his hostile forces and the passionless sage remained victorious, having conquered all the power of darkness, the heavens shone out with the moon like a maiden with a smile, and a sweet-smelling shower of flowers fell down wet with dew.
baseline: One who dissolves in the other side of the river and leaves flowers one who conquers the king with the victory of the victory one with the king of the waters the great king with his wife and daughter the sun the sky the water and the sun and the rain of flowers fall from the sky.
morphology: The king of the king should be merciless in the face of the river. He should be victorious in the victory of the goddess Nirājāsaka. The king should also be accompanied by a young woman and the king of Sācāndra Surabhi and the goddess of water and rain flowers.

sanskrit: tathāpi pāpīyasi nirjite gate diśaḥ praseduḥ prababhau niśākaraḥ | divo nipeturbhuvi puṣpavṛṣṭayo rarāja yoṣeva vikalmaṣā niśā |
reference: When the wicked one thus fled vanquished, the different regions of the sky grew clear, the moon shone forth, showers of flowers fell down from the sky upon the earth, and the night gleamed out like a spotless maiden.
baseline: However the sinner would get rid of him. Then the king would go to the direction of the king. The king would get the rain of flowers from the sun and the goddess would get destroyed.
morphology: However the sinner would be destroyed. The king should be destroyed by the rain of flowers and flowers.

sanskrit: śriyaṃ parārdhyāṃ vidadhadvidhātṛjit tamo nirasyannabhibhūtabhānubhṛt | nudannidāghaṃ jitacārucaṃdramāḥ sa vaṃdyate 'rhanniha yasya nopamā ||
reference: That Arhat is here saluted, who has no counterpart, — who, as bestowing the supreme happiness, surpasses (Brahman) the Creator, — who, as driving away darkness, vanquishes the sun, — and, as dispelling all burning heat, surpasses the beautiful moon.
baseline: One who has won the victory of the king of the kingdom of Sāriyam the king who has conquered the king and who has lost his fortune is worshipped as the king.
morphology: One who has won the victory of the king of the kingdom of Sri the king who has conquered the king who has lost his wealth and who has not lost his fortune and who enjoys the glory of the moon is worshipped.

sanskrit: āsīdviśālonnatasānulakṣmyā payodapaṃktyeva parītapārśvam | udagradhiṣṇyaṃ gagaṇe 'vagāḍhaṃ puraṃ maharṣeḥ kapilasya vastu ||
reference: There was a city, the dwelling-place of the great saint Kapila, having its sides surrounded by the beauty of a lofty broad table-land as by a line of clouds, and itself, with its high-soaring palaces, immersed in the sky.
baseline: One who is sitting on the ground should have the upper part of the feet covered with a lotus and the other side with a water column. One who has raised the feet of the sun in the air one who has built a tower one of the great cities and one who belongs to the king of Kapila.
morphology: One who has been given the gift of the sun the great king the king of the king and his wife should be placed on the right side of the sky with the same finery as that of the prophet the god of fire the lord of the air the city of fire and the objects of Kapil.

sanskrit: sitonnateneva nayena hṛtvā kailāsaśailasya yadabhraśobhām | bhramādupetān vahadaṃbuvāhān saṃbhāvanāṃ vā saphalīcakāra ||
reference: By its pure and lofty system of government it, as it were, stole the splendour of the clouds of Mount Kailāsa, and while it bore the clouds which came to it through a mistake, it fulfilled the imagination which had led them thither.
baseline: Having destroyed the stone of Kailāsa with the new stone of Sītonnatā one would get the illusion of the walls of the hill. One would get success by making the illusions of the gods and the possibilities.
morphology: Having destroyed the stone of Kailāsa with the new stone of Sītonnatā one would get the illusion. One would get illusion illusion and illusion or illusion in the future.

sanskrit: ratnaprabhodbhāsini yatra lebhe tamo na dāridryamivāvakāśam | parārdhyapauraiḥ sahavāsatoṣāt kṛtasmitevātirarāja lakṣmīḥ ||
reference: In that city, shining with the splendour of gems, darkness like poverty could find no place; prosperity shone resplendently, as with a smile, from the joy of dwelling with such surpassingly excellent citizens.
baseline: The king lakshmi is the king of the earth. One who does not want to suffer from poverty would be blessed with the gift of jewels and wealth. One would get the gift by having pleasure in the company of other citizens.
morphology: The king lakshmi is the king of these two cities. The king of lakshmīs kingdom is made to be happy by the association with the other gods.

sanskrit: yadvedikātoraṇasiṃhakarṇairatnairdadhānaṃ prativeśama śobhām | jagatyadṛṣṭveva samānamanyatspardhāṃ svagehairmitha eva cakre ||
reference: With its festive arbours, its arched gateways and pinnacles, it was radiant with jewels in every dwelling; and unable to find any other rival in the world, it could only feel emulation with its own houses.
baseline: One who looks at the world as if he is equal to the face of a lion and the head of the lion the head and the neck of the neck and the eyes of the king are the glory of the universe.
morphology: One who looks at the world as if he is facing the sky with a lion a lion and a lion in the sky and the other side with a golden face is said to be equal in the world.

sanskrit: rāmāmukheṃdūn paribhūtapadmān yatrāpayāto 'pyavimanya bhānuḥ | saṃtāpayogādiva vāri veṣṭuṃ paścātsamudrābhimukhaḥ pratasthe ||
reference: There the sun, even although he had retired, was unable to scorn the moon-like faces of its women which put the lotuses to shame, and as if from the access of passion, hurried towards the western ocean to enter the (cooling) water.
