baseline: One should worship the gods facing the sea on the day of the wrath of Lord Rama. One should pray to Lord Bhanu on the same day. Then one should worship him facing the ocean.
morphology: One should worship the gods facing the sea on the day of the wrath of Lord Rama. Then one facing the ocean would be besieged.

sanskrit: śakyārjitānāṃ yaśasāṃ janena dṛṣṭvāṃtabhāvaṃ gamito 'yamindraḥ | iti dhvajaiścārucalatpatākairyanmārṣṭumasyāṃkamivodayacchat ||
reference: ‘Yonder Indra has been utterly annihilated by the people when they saw the glories acquired by the Sakyas,’-uttering this scoff, the city strove by its banners with gay-fluttering streamers to wipe away every mark of his existence.
baseline: One who has seen the glory of those who have achieved it should say that the king of the kingdom of Yāmīrtha has gone away. The king of yāmārtha is said to have raised the flag and the figure of the king.
morphology: The king of the kingdom of Yāmīrtha said that he had seen the success of those acquired by the people. He had seen that the spirit had gone away. He also said that the flag should be worn with the flag and the number of the meritorious men should be raised.

sanskrit: kṛtvāpi rātrau kumudaprahāsamiṃdoḥ karairyadrajatālayasthaiḥ | sauvarṇaharmyeṣu gatārkapādairdivā sarojadyutimālalaṃbe ||
reference: After mocking the water-lilies even at night by the moonbeams which rest on its silver pavilions, — by day it assumed the brightness of the lotuses through the sunbeams falling on its golden palaces.
baseline: The kārtas are made of water and the kūmudas are placed in the night and the hymns are made from water and water. The garlands are made up of golden flowers and the feet of the goddess Saroja are made out of water.
morphology: The kārtas are made of water and the kumudas are placed in the night and the hymns are placed on the ground. The golden garlands are made up of the feet of the goddess Sarārja.

sanskrit: mahībṛtāṃ mūrdhni kṛtābhiṣekaḥ śuddhodano nāma nṛpo 'rkabaṃdhuḥ | adhyāśayo vā sphuṭapudarīkaṃ purādhirājaṃ tadalaṃcakāra ||
reference: A king, by name Śuddhodana, of the kindred of the sun, anointed to stand at the head of earths monarchs, — ruling over the city, adorned it, as a bee-inmate a full-blown lotus.
baseline: O king of the ancient kingdom the priest should be worshipped with the muḍhṇī mūrdhī mā the purest offering is called nrāporkā bāndhu. The king should be blessed with a cleansing cloth or purified leaves.
morphology: O king of the ancient kingdom the priest should be worshipped with the muḍhṇī mūrdhī. One should be called pure and one who is a brother of the king of Nāpokara. One who is pure and has a cleansing mouth should be offered with the prādhīraja.

sanskrit: bhūbhṛtparārdhyo 'pi sapakṣa eva pravṛttadāno 'pi madānupetaḥ | īśo 'pi nityaṃ samaḍṛṣṭipātaḥ saumyasvabhāvo 'pi pṛthupratāpaḥ ||
reference: The very best of kings with his train ever near him, — intent on liberality yet devoid of pride; a sovereign, yet with an ever equal eye thrown on all, — of gentle nature and yet with wide-reaching majesty.
baseline: O Lord of the earth the one who gives to the earth and the earth in the same way as to the other is called a man of good fortune. O Lord He is everlasting and gentle. He is the glory of the world.
morphology: O Lord of the earth the one who gives to the earth and the earth in the same way as to the other is called a man. O Lord He is everlasting and gentle.

sanskrit: bhujena yasyābhihatāḥ pataṃto dviṣaddvipeṃdrāḥ samarāṃgaṇeṣu | udvāṃtamuktāprakaraiḥ śirobhirbhaktyeva puṣpāṃjalibhiḥ praṇemuḥ ||
reference: Falling smitten by his arm in the arena of battle, the lordly elephants of his enemies bowed prostrate with their heads pouring forth quantities of pearls as if they were offering handfuls of flowers in homage.
baseline: One should offer flowers to the head and head with the open arms and open the battlefields in the two directions after having fallen down with the arms.
morphology: One should offer flowers to the head and head with the arms arms hands arms and arms. On the fall one should place the two arms in the battlegrounds. One should worship the head head and body with the offerings of flowers.

sanskrit: atipratāpādavadhūya śatrūnmahoparāgāniva tigmabhānuḥ | udyotayāmāsa janaṃ samaṃtātpradarśayannāśrayaṇīyamārgān ||
reference: Having dispersed his enemies by his preeminent majesty as the sun disperses the gloom of an eclipse, he illuminated his people on every side, showing them the paths which they were to follow.
baseline: Having made the enemy suffer a great loss of fire the king should make the people stand on the paths of refuge without the fear of the enemy.
morphology: O king of the world one who has made an attempt to destroy the enemy by making a great fire and making a fire of his feet should make the path of refuge open to him.

sanskrit: dharmārthakāmā viṣayaṃ mitho 'nyaṃ na veśamācakramurasya nītyā | vispardhamānā iva tūgrasiddheḥ sugocare dīptatarā babhūvuḥ ||
reference: Duty, wealth, and pleasure under his guidance assumed mutually each other’s object, but not the outward dress; yet as if they still vied together they shone all the brighter in the glorious career of their triumphant success.
baseline: One should not think about the matter of charity. One should do not dress in the garb of a priest one should not wear the garland of a knight one who has become illuminant in the well-wishes as if he is going to rise up.
morphology: One should not think about the matter of charity. One should do not dress in the garb of a priest one should not wear a mask and one who is angry should be illuminated in the well-wishes.

sanskrit: udārasaṃkhyaiḥ sacivāirasaṃkhyaiḥ kṛtāgrabhāvaḥ sa udagrabhāvaḥ | śaśī yathā bhairakṛtānyathābhaiḥ śakyeṃdrarājaḥ sutarāṃ rarāja ||
reference: He, the monarch of the Śākyas, of native pre-eminence, but whose actual pre-eminence was brought about by his numberless councillors of exalted wisdom, shone forth all the more gloriously, like the moon amidst the stars shining with a light like its own.
baseline: The king of the kingdom of Sāsī should be able to do the same thing as the king of Bhairā by the generous numbers and the number of servants.
morphology: The king of the kingdom of Sāsī is said to be as good as the king of Bhāra as he is capable of doing with the numbers of his servants.

sanskrit: tasyātiśobhāvisṛtātiśobhā raviprabhevāstatamaḥ prabhāvā | samagradevīnivahāgradevī babhūva māyāpagateva māyā ||
reference: To him there was a queen, named Māyā, as if free from all deceit (māyā) — an effulgence proceeding from his effulgence, like the splendour of the sun when it is free from all the influence of darkness, a chief queen in the united assembly of all queens.
baseline: The image of the lord Śiva is the manifestation of that manifestation. The manifestations of the divine manifestation are as follows. The goddess of the universe as a whole is called the goddess of illusion.
morphology: The image of the goddess Śiva is the manifestation of that manifestation. The manifestations of the divine manifestation are the same as those of the manifestations. The goddess Vihaṇu is the ultimate manifestation and the manifesting goddess of the universe. Mayāya is the incarnation of the great goddess.

sanskrit: prajāsu māteva hitapravṛttā gurau jane bhaktirivānuvṛttā | lakṣmīrivādhīśakule kṛtābhā jagatyabhūduttamadevatā yā ||
reference: Like a mother to her subjects, intent on their welfare, — devoted to all worthy of reverence like devotion itself, — shining on her lord’s family like the goddess of prosperity, — she was the most eminent of goddesses to the whole world.
baseline: One who has worshipped the mother among his subjects the master the devotee the lord of the world the supreme god of the earth and the king of the king should be worshipped.
morphology: One who has worshipped the mother among his subjects and the master should be blessed with the best of gods. One who is worshipped in the temple of lord lakshmī rivadhiṣa should worship the world.

sanskrit: kāmaṃ sadā strīcaritaṃ tamisraṃ tathāpi tāṃ prapya bhṛśaṃ vireje | na hīṃdulekhāmupagamya śubhāṃ naktaṃ tathā saṃtamasatvameti ||
reference: Verily the life of women is always darkness, yet when it encountered her, it shone brilliantly; thus the night does not retain its gloom, when it meets with the radiant crescent of the moon.
baseline: One should always worship a woman with the lust of the mother and then spread it with the brim of water. One would not be able to reach the pen of the Hindu scripture. One should not say good things and one would get eternal happiness.
morphology: One should always worship a woman with the lust the tāmisrām the bhiṣma and the vīraśa. One who does not reach the Hindu scriptures would not be able to enjoy the auspiciousness of the sun and the sāṇtamasattva.

sanskrit: atīṃdriyenātmani duṣkuho 'yaṃ mayā jano yojayituṃ na śakyaḥ | itīva sūkṣmāṃ prakṛtiṃ vihāya dharmeṇa sākṣādvihitā svamūrtiḥ ||
reference: ‘This people, being hard to be roused to wonder in their souls, cannot be influenced by me if I come to them as beyond their senses,’ - so saying, Duty abandoned her own subtile nature and made her form visible.
baseline: One who has not been able to connect with others would not be able to do so. This is the manifestation of one who witnesses by righteousness except by the subtle nature.
morphology: One who has not been able to reconcile with others one who is evil beyond the realm of the senses and who has given testimony by virtue of his own nature except for the subtle nature is a manifestation of the self.

sanskrit: cyuto 'tha kāyāttuṣitāt trilokīmudyotayannuttamabodhisattvaḥ | viveśa tasyāḥ smṛta eva kukṣau naṃdāguhāyāmiva nāgarājaḥ ||
reference: Then falling from the host of beings in the Tuṣita heaven, and illumining the three worlds, the most excellent of Bodhisattvas suddenly entered at a thought into her womb, like the Nāga-king entering the cave of Nandā.
baseline: One who has not been able to understand the three worlds of the world is called a kāyātuṣṭu. The king who has been in the cave of Nandā is known to have the best understanding of the universe. He is known as Vivaśa.
morphology: One who has not been able to understand the three worlds of the world would be better off by having a kyūtu  kāyātuṣṭu. One who remembers the image of the king should have a kuśuṇa cave and a nāgārāja cave.

sanskrit: rakṣāvidhānaṃ prati lokapālā lokaikanāthasya divo 'bhijagmuḥ | sarvatra bhāṃto 'pi hi caṃdrapādā bhajaṃti kailāsagirau viśeṣam ||
reference: The guardians of the world hastened from heaven to mount watch over the world’s one true ruler; thus the moonbeams, though they shine everywhere, are especially bright on Mount Kailāsa.
baseline: The lord of the people the lord of ones own country and the god of the world should be worshipped everywhere. One should worship the moon and the mountain of Kailasa.
morphology: The lord of the people is the protector of the world. He worships the moon and the mountain everywhere. He worshipped the moon.

sanskrit: mayāpi taṃ kukṣigataṃ dadhānā vidyudvilāsaṃ jaladāvalīva | dānābhivarṣaiḥ parito janānāṃ dāridryatāpaṃ śamayāṃcakāra ||
reference: Māyā also, holding him in her womb, like a line of clouds holding a lightning-flash, relieved the people around her from the sufferings of poverty by raining showers of gifts.
baseline: May God bless him with water and electricity. May God heal the poor people with the gift of water and water.
morphology: May God bless him with water and electricity. May God heal the poor people by increasing the quantity of grains.

sanskrit: sātaḥ purajanā devī kadācidatha luṃbinīm | jagāmānumate rājñaḥ saṃbhūtottamadohadā ||
reference: Then one day by the king’s permission the queen, having a great longing in her mind, went with the inmates of the gynaeceum into the garden Lumbinī.
baseline: The king should be blessed with seven cities and the goddess with lumbini. The king would be bestowed with the jagmana.
morphology: The king should worship the goddess lumbini with seven deities. The king would be blessed with the best of the gods.

sanskrit: śākhāmālaṃbamānāyāḥ puṣpabhārāvalaṃbinīm | devyāḥ kukṣiṃ vibhidyāśu bodhisattvo viniryayau ||
reference: As the queen supported herself by a bough which hung laden with a weight of flowers, the Bodhisattva suddenly came forth, cleaving open her womb.
baseline: The bodhisattva should be the one who divides the arms of the goddess from the branches the arms and the flowers of the gods.
morphology: The bodhisattvas should be divided into two parts. The branches should be of the same size and the flowers should be borne by the goddess.

sanskrit: tataḥ prasannaśca babhūva puṣyastasyāśca devyā vratasaṃskṛtāyāḥ | pārśvātsuto lokahitāya jajñe nirvedanaṃ caiva nirāmayaṃ ca ||
reference: At that time the constellation Puṣya was auspicious, and from the side of the queen, who was purified by her vow, her son was born for the welfare of the world, without pain and without illness.
baseline: Then the goddess should be pleased with him and worship him. He should be worshipped by the side of the goddess for the welfare of the people and should be given peace and healing.
morphology: Then the goddess should be pleased with him and worship him. Having worshipped him for the welfare of the people with his side he should be cured by offering him without remorse.

sanskrit: prātaḥ payodādiva tigmabhānuḥ samudbhavanso 'pi ca mātṛkukṣeḥ | sphuranmayūkhairvihatāṃdhakāraiścakāra lokaṃ kanakāvadātam ||
reference: Like the sun bursting from a cloud in the morning, — so he too, when he was born from his mother’s womb, made the world bright like gold, bursting forth with his rays which dispelled the darkness.
baseline: The morning should be the morning morning evening evening and evening in the mother's womb. One should give the world to a man who is not afraid of the enemy.
morphology: The morning morning and evening should be worshipped in the mother's womb. One should offer the world with the fragrance of the sun and the fragrant water and the offerings made by the mother.

sanskrit: surapradhānaiḥ paridhāryamāṇo dehāṃśujālairanuraṃjayaṃstān | saṃdhyābhrajāloparisaṃniviṣṭaṃ navoḍurājaṃ vijigāya lakṣmyā ||
reference: Carried about by the chief suras, and delighting them with the rays that streamed from his body, he surpassed in beauty the new moon as it rests on a mass of evening clouds.
baseline: The body should be surrounded by the head of the sun water and water. The king should be seated on the sandhya bed and the king of the nine rivers should be worshipped by Lakshmi.
morphology: The body should be surrounded by the head of the sun water and water. The king should be seated on the sandhya and the waters of the sea. Having conquered the king of the nine gods lakshmī should be worshipped.

sanskrit: ūroryathaurvasya pṛthośca hastānmāṃdhāturiṃdrapratimasya mūrdhnaḥ | kakṣīvataścaiva bhujāṃsadeśāttathāvidhaṃ tasya babhūva janma ||
reference: As was Aurva’s birth from the thigh, and Pṛthu’s from the hand, and Māndhātṛ’s, who was like Indra himself, from the forehead, and Kakṣīvat’s from the upper end of the arm, — thus too was his birth (miraculous).
baseline: The image of Indra is said to be born with the hands of the king of Oorāyā and the forehead the head of the image of the god and the head. He was born after having been instructed by the gods to live in the cave.
morphology: The image of Indra is said to be born with the hands hands arms arms and head. He was born as a son of a man living in a forest.

sanskrit: krameṇa garbhādabhiniḥsṛtaḥ san babhau gataḥ khādiva yonyajātaḥ | kalpeṣvanekeṣviva bhāvitātmā yaḥ saṃprajānan suṣuve na mūḍhaḥ ||
reference: Having thus in due time issued from the womb, he shone as if he had come down from heaven, he who had not been born in the natural way, — he who was born full of wisdom, not foolish, as if his mind had been purified by countless aeons of contemplation.
baseline: One who gradually falls into the womb and then goes into the uterus and gives birth to food one who has not been able to conceive or conceive of any other soul is not foolish in his sleep.
morphology: One who has gone into the womb after having been aborted by the mother one who is born of a woman who has eaten food and has not had any illusions and one who has not been able to understand the spirit of a man is not foolish.

sanskrit: dīptyā ca dhairyeṇa śriyā rarāja bālo ravirbhūmimivāvatīrṇaḥ | tathātidīpto 'pi nirīkṣyamāṇo jahāra cakṣūṃṣi yathā śaśāṃkaḥ ||
reference: With glory, fortitude, and beauty he shone like the young sun descended upon the earth; when he was gazed at, though of such surpassing brightness, he attracted all eyes like the moon.
baseline: The king is described as having the power of light and courage. The king as Balā the king of the earth as the king as the lord of the sky as well as the eyes as the sāśaṇaka.
morphology: O king of the kingdom of Śrīya the king of Balā the lord of the earth the light of the sky and the eye of the eye are seen by the sāśṇaka.

sanskrit: sa hi svagātraprabhayojjvalaṃtyā dīpaprabhāṃ bhāskaravanmumoṣa | mahārhajāṃbūnadacāruvarṇo vidyotayāmāsa diśaśca sarvāḥ ||
reference: With the radiant splendour of his limbs he extinguished like the sun the splendour of the lamps; with his beautiful hue as of precious gold he illuminated all the quarters of space.
baseline: He is the manifestation of the lamp with the fiery flame of his own body. He is also the incarnation of Bhākārāma. He has four colours four colours and four directions.
morphology: He is the one who gives light and light in his house the great jambu the four colours of the sky and the directions of the four directions.

sanskrit: anākulānyabjasamudgatāni niṣpeṣavaṃtyāyatavikramāṇi | tathaiva dhīrāṇi padāni sapta saptarṣitārāsadṛśo jagāma ||
reference: Unflurried, with the lotus-sign in high relief, far-striding, set down with a stamp, — seven such firm footsteps did he then take, — he who was like the constellation of the seven Ṛṣis.
baseline: Those who go to the temple of Anakulanya Bājāsamudra are called vikrama. Similarly the steps of dhiṣṇī are seven and seven years long.
morphology: The steps leading to anakula bajjā and samudra should be repeated in the same manner as the steps for seven years.

sanskrit: bodhāya jāto 'smi jagaddhitārthamaṃtyā tathotpattiriyaṃ mameti | caturdiśaṃ siṃhagatirvilokya vāṇīṃ ca bhavyārthakarīmuvāca ||
reference: ‘I am born for supreme knowledge, for the welfare of the world, — thus this is my last birth,’ thus did he of lion gait, gazing at the four quarters, utter a voice full of auspicious meaning.
baseline: One who knows the meaning of the world and the source of its production would become a great exponent of the four directions of a lion a man who would speak a great word.
morphology: One who knows the meaning of the world and the origin of the universe would become a great exponent of the four directions of the lion and the great expanse of speech.

sanskrit: khātprasrute caṃdramarīciśubhre dve vāridhāre śiśiroṣṇavīrye | śarīrasaukhyārthamanuttarasya nipetaturmūrdhani tasya saumye ||
reference: Two streams of water bursting from heaven, bright as the moon’s rays, having the power of heat and cold, fell down upon that peerless one’s benign head to give refreshment to his body.
baseline: The sun should be lit with a lotus a crescent a moon a chariot a flower two flowers a sesame and a sun and the body should be washed with water and the mind should be cleansed with water.
morphology: O Lord of the earth one should worship the sun moon water and two other forms of wealth in the form of a lotus water and water. One should treat the body and the mind as well as the mind with the grace of the Lord.

sanskrit: śrīmadvitāne kanakojjvalāṃge vaiḍūryapāde śayane śayānam | yadgauravātkāṃcanapadmahastā yakṣādhipāḥ saṃparivārya tasthuḥ ||
reference: His body lay on a bed with a royal canopy and a frame shining with gold, and supported by feet of lapis lazuli, and in his honour the yakṣa-lords stood round guarding him with golden lotuses in their hands.
baseline: One should lie down on the bed of a cow on the right side of the hill on the left side of a mound. Having said this one should lie on the ground on the foot of a mountain on the other side. Having worshipped the king of the bulls he should stand on that bed.
morphology: One should lie down on the bed of a cow on the right side of the hill on the left side of a mound. Having said this one should be made to sit on the ground on the foot of a mountain. Having worshipped the king of the bulls he should stand on it.

sanskrit: māyātanūjasya divaukasaḥ khe yasya prabhāvātpraṇataiḥ śirobhiḥ | ādhārayan pāṇdaramātapatraṃ bodhāya jepuḥ paramāśiṣaśca ||
reference: The gods in homage to the son of Māyā, with their heads bowed at his majesty, held up a white umbrella in the sky and muttered the highest blessings on his supreme wisdom.
baseline: One who has the power of the divine eye of the illusion should be guided by the heads of the gods. One who supports the mother and the mother should be worshipped by the lord.
morphology: One who has the influence of the goddess mayātānuja the goddess of the sun and the goddess dvaukasa should be worshipped with the heads. One who supports the mother and the mother should be worshiped with the hands and feet.

sanskrit: mahoragā dharmaviśeṣatarṣādbuddheṣvatīteṣu kṛtādhikārāḥ | yamavyajan bhaktiviśiṣṭanetrā maṃdārapuṣpaiḥ samavākiraṃśca ||
reference: The great dragons in their great thirst for the Law, — they who had had the privilege of waiting on the past Buddhas, — gazing with eyes of intent devotion, fanned him and strewed Mandāra flowers over him.
baseline: One who has done great deeds one who has fought a war for three years and has done good deeds is known as Yama Vyājana Bhakti Pratinā Nītara Mandara flowers and other objects.
morphology: One who has done great deeds one who has made great sacrifices and has fought many wars has done good deeds. One who is a devotee a leader a great leader has got equal rights with the flowers of mandara.

sanskrit: tathāgatotpādaguṇena tuṣṭāḥ śuddhādhivāsāśca viśuddhasattvāḥ | devā nanaṃdurvigate 'pi rāge magnasya duḥkhe jagato hitāya ||
reference: Gladdened through the influence of the birth of the Tathāgata, the gods of pure natures and inhabiting pure abodes were filled with joy, though all passion was extinguished, for the sake of the world drowned in sorrow.
baseline: Then one should come and enjoy the virtues and purify oneself with pure nature. One who is not angry with the gods would get happiness in the world.
morphology: Then one who has come and gone with the goodness of the products and has been purified with the virtues of the living beings would become pure. Then the world would be better off in the sorrow of the anger and misery.

sanskrit: yasmin prasūte girirājakīlā vātāhatā nauriva bhūścacāla | sacaṃdanā cotpalapadmagarbhā papāta vṛṣṭirgagaṇādanabhrāt ||
reference: When he was born, the earth, though fastened down by (Himālaya) the monarch of mountains, shook like a ship tossed by the wind; and from a cloudless sky there fell a shower full of lotuses and water-lilies, and perfumed with sandalwood.
baseline: One who gives birth to a mountain a king a woman a cow a bird a land a horse a sheep a calf a buffalo a pigeon a raven or a cow should walk on the earth.
morphology: One who gives birth to a mountain king hill wind river earth water water and water should be washed away with the help of water.

sanskrit: vātā vavuḥ sparśasukhā manojñā divyāni vāsāṃsyavapātayaṃtaḥ | sūryaḥ sa evābhyadhikaṃ cakāśe jajvāla saumyārciranīrito 'gniḥ ||
reference: Pleasant breezes blew soft to the touch, dropping down heavenly garments; the very sun, though still the same, shone with augmented light, and fire gleamed, unstirred, with a gentle lustre.
baseline: O Vāṇu one who touches and experiences the divine abode the sun is more than that. He is the sun the light the sound and the water.
morphology: O Vāṇu one who touches the sky and knows the mind and dispels the illusion of the abode of the divine. The sun is more than that.

sanskrit: prāguttare cāvasathapradeśe kūpaḥ svayaṃ prādurabhūtsitāṃbuḥ | aṃtaḥ purāṇyāgatavismayāni yasmin kriyāstīrtha iva pracakruḥ ||
reference: In the north-eastern part of the dwelling a well of pure water appeared of its own accord, wherein the inhabitants of the gynaeceum, filled with wonder, performed their rites as in a sacred bathing-place.
baseline: A well in the north of the east in the four quarters of the north is said to be a well which has been destroyed by fire. One who does the miracles of the ancient past should do the same in the interior.
morphology: In the north in the north and in the south the well itself is said to have been a great object. One who performs the miracles of the ancient past should spread it as if he had done so.

sanskrit: dharmārthibhirbhūtagaṇaiśca divyaistaddarśanārthaṃ balamāpa pūraḥ | kautūhalenaiva ca pādapaiśca prapūjayāmāsa sagaṃdhapuṣpaiḥ ||
reference: Through the troops of heavenly visitants, who came seeking religious merit, the pool itself received strength to behold Buddha, and by means of its trees bearing flowers and perfumes it eagerly offered him worship.
baseline: One should worship the gods of the world and the gods with the garlands of flowers and spices. One should offer a strong purāpa to the goddess for the worship of the goddess. One would worship the feet and feet with fragrance and flowers.
morphology: One should worship the gods of the world and the gods with the garlands of the gods and the feet and flowers of fragrance and fragrance.

sanskrit: puṣpadumāḥ svaṃ kusumaṃ pukulluḥ sasīraṇodrāmitadiksugaṃdhi | susaṃbhramadnṛgavadhūpagītaṃ bhujaṃgaṃvṛdāpihitāttavātam ||
reference: The flowering trees at once produced their blossoms, while their fragrance was borne aloft in all directions by the wind, accompanied by the songs of bewildered female bees, while the air was inhaled and absorbed by the many snakes (gathering near).
baseline: The flowers flowers kusum pukullu sārīna udrama ḍīksu gandhi the song of cows cows and cows are worshipped in the morning and evening.
morphology: The flowers should be made of kusum pukula sārīna dirāma dikṣa gaṇgandhi the song of cows cows horses horses and horses.

sanskrit: kvacit kvaṇattūryamṛdaṃgagītairvīṇāmukuṃdāmurajādibhiśca | svīṇāṃ calatkuṃḍalabhūṣitānāṃ virājitaṃ cobhayapārścatastat ||
reference: Sometimes there resounded on both sides songs mingled with musical instruments and tabours, and lutes also, drums, tambourines, and the rest, from women adorned with dancing bracelets.
baseline: One would get a lotus flower with a heart a song a bow a mace a sword and a bow. One would gain the victory of the king by having the kundas adorned with the chariot and a spade.
morphology: One would get a lotus flower with a heart a song a bow a sword a mace a pearl a piece of cloth and a piece containing a kundamurjā.

sanskrit: yadrājaśāstraṃ bhṛguraṃgirā vā na cakraturvaṃśakarāvṛṣī tau | tayoḥ sutau tau ca sasarjatustatkālena śukraśca bṛhaspatiśca ||
reference: ‘That royal law which neither Bhṛgu nor Aṅgiras ever made, those two great seers the founders of families, their two sons Śukra and Vṛhaspati left revealed at the end.
baseline: The king of Yādrāja is neither the king of Bhrīgurāngira nor the ruler of Vṛṣṇa. He should be called the chakraturvamshakara and the lord of Vrṣiśa. The king should be worshipped with the celestial instruments of Śukrā and Brihaspati.
morphology: The king of Yadrāja is not the king of Bhrīgurāngira or the son of Vṛṣṇāra the king who is the bearer of the chakraturva vamshākara. He should be called Sāsārjata and Śukrāda and Brihaspati.

sanskrit: sārasvataścāpi jagāda naṣṭaṃ vedaṃ punaryaṃ dadṛśurna pūrvam | vyāsastathainaṃ bahudhā cakāra na yaṃ vaśiṣṭhaḥ kṛtavānaśaktiḥ ||
reference: ‘Yea, the son of Sarasvatī I proclaimed that lost Veda which they had never seen in former ages, — Vyāsa rehearsed that in many forms, which Vaśiṣṭha helpless could not compile;
baseline: The veda should be recited again with the syllable Śvarāśvatā and the jagāda. The vyāstha is not the power which has been made by Vāṣṭha by the expulsion of the vyasa.
morphology: The veda should be repeated with the syllable Śarvātā. The vāṣṭhīta did not do the power which was done by Vāśṭhita by making the vyāsattha more numerous than before.

sanskrit: vālmīkinādaśca sasarja padyaṃ jagraṃtha yanna cyavano mahārṣiḥ | cikitsitaṃ yacca cakāra nātriḥ paścāttadātreya ṛṣirjagāda ||
reference: ‘The voice of Vālmīki uttered its poetry which the great seer Cyavana could not compose; and that medicine which Atri never invented the wise son of Atri proclaimed after him;
baseline: The king should recite a poem of the name Valmiki and the words of Yāna and the great sage Yāṇvā. He should do whatever is done to cure the sage. The sage should repent.
morphology: The king should recite the verses of Valmiki Nāda and Sāsārja Jagrantha Yāna and Yāṇvāna. The great sage should do whatever is done to cure the sage.

sanskrit: yacca dvijatvaṃ kuśiko na lebhe tadgādhanaḥ sūnuravāpa rājan | velāṃ samudre sagaraśca dadhre nekṣvākavo yāṃ prathamaṃ babaṃdhuḥ ||
reference: ‘That Brahmanhood which Kuśika never attained, — his son, O king, found out the means to gain it; (so) Sagara made a bound for the ocean, which even the Ikṣvākus had not fixed before him.
baseline: The king who does not get the double the amount of money and the wealth of the king would be the first one to be married to the king. The king would get the wealth from the sea and the king from the river and the bridegroom from the land.
morphology: The king who does not get the double the amount of money and the wealth of the king should be the first one to be married to a man who is a slave in the sea a slave a king who has not got the money.

sanskrit: ācāryakaṃ yogavidhau dvijānāmaprāptamanyairjanako jagāma | khyātāni karmāṇi ca yāni śauraiḥ śūrādayasteṣvabalā babhūvuḥ ||
reference: ‘Janaka attained a power of instructing the twice-born in the rules of Yoga which none other had ever reached; and the famed feats of the grandson of Śūra (Kriṣṇa) Śūra and his peers were powerless to accomplish.
baseline: The preceptor should be known as the one who has attained the highest degree of knowledge in the practice of yoga. He should also be known to have performed the deeds done by the knight.
morphology: The preceptor should be known to be the master of the two forms of yoga. He should also be known as the king of the world. He is known to have performed deeds which are done by the mighty warriors.

sanskrit: tasmātpramāṇaṃ na vayo na kālaḥ kaścitkvacicchraiṣṭhyamupaiti loke | rājñāmṛṣīṇāṃ ca hitāni tāni kṛtāni putrairakṛtāni pūrvaiḥ ||
reference: ‘Therefore it is not age nor years which are the criterion; different persons win pre-eminence in the world at different places; those mighty exploits worthy of kings and sages, when left undone by the ancestors, have been done by the sons.’
baseline: One who does not wish to do so would not be able to live long. The king and the sons of the king would get the benefits. Those things were done by the sons and daughters of the previous rulers.
morphology: One who does not know the time and place of the king and his sons should not do so. The king should not be afraid of the people. The good things done by the sons and daughters of the kings should be taken care of by the elders.

sanskrit: evaṃ nṛpaḥ pratyayitairdvijaistairāśvāsitaścāpyabhinaṃditaśca | śaṃkāmaniṣṭāṃ vijahau manastaḥ praharṣamevādhikamāruroha ||
reference: The king, being thus consoled and congratulated by those well-trusted Brāhmans, dismissed from his mind all unwelcome suspicion and rose to a still higher degree of joy;
baseline: In this way the king should be assured of the victory of the king. He should be blessed with the confidence of the lord. He would be able to overcome any doubt and would be more powerful than the king of the kingdom.
morphology: In this way the king should believe that the king has been blessed with the gift of the gods. Having received such trust he should be blessed. Having a doubtful mind the king would rise above the danger.

sanskrit: prītaśca tebhyo dvijasattamebhyaḥ satkārapūrvaṃ pradadau dhanāni | bhūyādayaṃ bhūmipatiryathokto yāyājjarāmetya vanāni ceti ||
reference: And well-pleased he gave to those most excellent of the twice-born rich treasures with all due honour, — ‘May he become the ruler of the earth according to your words, and may he retire to the woods when he attains old age.’
baseline: One should give the two elements of the kingdom with the gift of wealth and wealth before being blessed by them. One should go to the king's palace and visit the forest.
morphology: The king should pay tribute to those who have been blessed with the gift of gold gold and silver. He should go to the king's palace and visit the forest.

sanskrit: athau nimittaiśca tapobalācca tajjanma janmāṃtakarasya buddhvā | śākyeśvarasyālayamājagāma saddharmatarṣādasito mahārṣiḥ ||
reference: Then having learned by signs and through the power of his penances this birth of him who was to destroy all birth, the great seer Asita in his thirst for the excellent Law came to the palace of the Śākya king.
baseline: The king should worship the goddess of birth and death for this and other reasons. He should worship her in the temple of the god of strength and prosperity.
morphology: The king should worship the goddess of birth and death for this and other reasons. He should worship her in the temple of the god śākyeśvarā and the goddess sādharma.

sanskrit: taṃ brahmavidbrahmavidāṃ jvalaṃtaṃ brāhmyā śriyā caiva tapaḥśriyā ca | rājño gururgauravasatkriyābhyāṃ praveśayāmāsa nareṃdrasadma ||
reference: Him shining with the glory of sacred knowledge and ascetic observances, the king’s own priest, — himself a special student among the students of sacred knowledge, — introduced into the royal palace with all due reverence and respect.
baseline: He should be worshipped by the brahmins the Brahmanists the fiery Brahman and the celestials the king the guru the priest and the king of the king should be entered into the abode of Narendra.
morphology: He should be worshipped by the Brahman the divine one the fiery one and the brahmin the king the guru the priest the lord of the king and the king of the kingdom. The king should enter the abode of Narendra.

sanskrit: sa pārthivāṃtaḥpurasaṃnikarṣaṃ kumārajanmāgataharṣavegam | viveśa dhīro balasaṃjñayaiva tapaḥprakarṣācca jarāśrayācca ||
reference: He entered into the precincts of the king’s gynaeceum, which was all astir with the joy arisen from the birth of the young prince, — grave from his consciousness of power, his pre-eminence in asceticism, and the weight of old age.
baseline: He should be the earthly end the upper end of the earth the height of the universe the speed of the movement of the body of the son the strength of the mind and the strength. He should perform penance and express himself with the zaaraśra.
morphology: He should be the earthly end the upper end of the universe the son of a son the head of a daughter the heart of a great man the mind of a brave man and the knowledge of strength.

sanskrit: tato nṛpastaṃ munimāsanasthaṃ pādyārghyapūrvaṃ pratipūjya samyak | nimaṃtrayāmāsa yathopacāraṃ purā vasiṣṭhaṃ sa ivāṃtidevaḥ ||
reference: Then the king, having duly honoured the sage, who was seated in his seat, with water for the feet and an arghya offering, invited him (to speak) with all ceremonies of respect, as did Antideva in olden time to Vaśiṣṭha:
baseline: Then the priest should worship him in the seat of the sage before the feet. He should offer the same kind of worship as before to the lord Vāṣṭhiva.
morphology: Then the priest should worship him in the seat of the sage before the feet. He should offer the same kind of treatment as the priest called Vāṣṭhī.

sanskrit: dhanyo 'smyanugrāhyamidaṃ kulaṃ me yanmāṃ didṛkṣurbhagavānupetaḥ | ājñāpyatāṃ kiṃ karavāṇi saumya śiṣyo 'smi viśraṃbhitumarhasīti ||
reference: ‘I am indeed fortunate, this my family is the object of high favour, that thou shouldst have come to visit me; be pleased to command what I should do, O benign one; I am thy disciple, be pleased to show thy confidence in me.’
baseline: O blessed one I shall give to you such a clan as may be acceptable to you. Having ordered what should be done by me the disciple should rest on me.
morphology: O blessed one I shall give such a family as I have received. Having been instructed what to do the disciple who is gentle should rest in peace.

sanskrit: evaṃ nṛpeṇopanimaṃtritaḥ sansarveṇa bhāvena muniryathāvat | savismayotphullaviśāladṛṣṭirgaṃbhīradhīrāṇi vacāṃsyuvāca ||
reference: The sage, being thus invited by the king, filled with intense feeling as was due, uttered his deep and solemn words, having his large eyes opened wide with wonder:
baseline: In this way the sages should be worshipped with the sound of the sun and the spirit. The sage should be surprised by the words of the great sage and the great man who has a great vision.
morphology: In this way the sages should be worshipped with the sound of the sun and the spirit of the goddess. The sage should be amazed with the words of the great sage and the mighty sage with his great vision.

sanskrit: mahātmani tvayyupapannametat priyātithau tyāgini dharmakāme | sattvānvayajñānavayo 'nurūpā snigdhā yadevaṃ mayi te matiḥ syāt ||
reference: ‘This is indeed worthy of thee, great-souled as thou art, fond of guests, liberal and a lover of duty, — that thy mind should be thus kind towards me, in full accordance with thy nature, family, wisdom, and age.
baseline: The great men should be worshipped by you. They should be offered to you in the name of righteousness knowledge and knowledge. If they are worshipped in the form of a snake they should be given to me.
morphology: The great men should be worshipped by you in the form of a devotee. They should be worshiped with the spirit of renunciation. The knowledge of the spirit should be given to me as a snighna.

sanskrit: etacca tadyena nṛparṣayaste dharmeṇa sūkṣmāṇi dhanānyapāsya | nityaṃ tyajaṃto vidhivadbabhūvustapobhirāḍhyā vibhavairdaridrāḥ ||
reference: ‘This is the true way in which those seer kings of old, rejecting through duty all trivial riches, have ever flung them away as was right, — being poor in outward substance but rich in ascetic endurance.
baseline: O king one who has not been able to do so should always renounce the virtues of the poor and the rich. One who is not able to bear the burden of the evil will be punished by the law.
morphology: O king one who has not been able to do so should always renounce the righteousness of the poor and the wealth of the rich. One who does not give up the law should be given the power of the king.

sanskrit: prayojanaṃ yattu mamopayāne tanme śṛṇu prītimupehi ca tvam | divyā mayā divyapathe śrutā vāgbodhāya jātastanayastaveti ||
reference: ‘But hear now the motive for my coming and rejoice thereat; a heavenly voice has been heard by me in the heavenly path, that thy son has been born for the sake of supreme knowledge.
baseline: If it is useful for me to worship you you should know that you are the one who loves me. You should hear me speak in the way of the divine. You have heard me speak to you.
morphology: O Divine One when you hear of the benefits of the worship of God you know that you are a beloved one. If you hear me speak in the way of the Divine you will be blessed.

sanskrit: śrutvā vacastacca manaśca yuktvā jñātvā nimittaiśca tato 'smyupetaḥ | didṛkṣayā śākyakuladhvajasya śakradhvajasyeva samucchritasya ||
reference: ‘Having heard that voice and applied my mind thereto, and having known its truth by signs, I am now come hither, with a longing to see the banner of the Śākya race, as if it were Indra’s banner being set up.’
baseline: Having heard the words and having understood the reason for the same one should be able to understand the meaning of the words of the sākhya kuldhvaja kārakrdhvajga and the sound of the swords.
morphology: Having heard it and having understood it properly and knowing the reason one should follow it. One should see the flag of the sākhya kuldhvaja kārakrdhvaj and the flag covered with it.

sanskrit: ityetadevaṃ vacanaṃ niśamya praharṣasaṃbhrāṃtagatirnareṃdraḥ | ādāya dhātryaṃkagataṃ kumāraṃ saṃdarśayāmāsa tapodhanāya ||
reference: Having heard this address of his, the king, with his steps bewildered with joy, took the prince, who lay on his nurse’s side, and showed him to the holy ascetic.
baseline: Having said these words one should go to the center of the earth and worship the gods. One should visit the lord who comes from the land of the mother and worships him.
morphology: Having said these words the king should go to the center of the earth and visit the lord of the motherland.

sanskrit: cakrāṃkapādaṃ sa tathā mahārṣirjālāvanaddhāṃgulipāṇipādam | sorṇabhruvaṃ vāraṇavastikośaṃ savismayaṃ rājasutaṃ dadarśa ||
reference: Thus the great seer beheld the king’s son with wonder, — his foot marked with a wheel, his fingers and toes webbed, with a circle of hair between his eyebrows, and signs of vigour like an elephant.
baseline: The feet of the chakra are the same as those of the great sage jālava and the limbs of the king. The king should be seen as having a golden forehead and a white forehead.
morphology: The feet of the chakra are similar to those of the king. The king is said to have seen the golden eyebrows the white forehead the golden arms the celestial body and the great king.

sanskrit: dhātryaṃkasaṃviṣṭamavekṣya cainaṃ devyaṃkasaṃviṣṭamivāgnisūnum | babhūva pakṣmāṃtarivāṃcitāśrurniśvasya caivaṃ tridivonmukho 'bhūt ||
reference: Having beheld him seated on his nurse’s side, like the son of Agni (Skanda) seated on Devī’s side, he stood with the tears hanging on the ends of his eyelashes, and sighing he looked up towards heaven.
baseline: Having seen the image of the goddess sitting on the seat of the god one should observe that the fire is seated on the side of the body. One should observe the image facing the three gods with the eyes of the lord standing on the sides.
morphology: Having seen the image of the goddess sitting on the seat of the mother one should observe the image as sitting on a fire. One should see the image with the eyes of the three gods standing on the sides of the earth.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvāsitaṃ tvaśrupariplutākṣaṃ snehāttu putrasya nṛpaścakaṃpe | sagadgadaṃ bāṣpakaṣāyakaṃṭhaḥ papraccha ca prāṃjalirānatāṃgaḥ ||
reference: But seeing Asita with his eyes thus filled with tears, the king was agitated through his love for his son, and with his hands clasped and his body bowed he thus asked him in a broken voice choked with weeping,
baseline: One who has seen the wind and has fondness for the son should be fond of it. One who does not have the desire to see him should be afraid of him. The body should be covered with water and the body should not be swallowed up by the fire.
morphology: One who has seen the wind one who has fondness for you and the sons heart and back one with the arms the body with the mouth the heart with the air the mouth with the ears the head with the hands the forehead with the feet the limbs with the legs with the forearms the neck with the throat with the voice of the vapour the chest with the head and the body of the body.

sanskrit: svalpāṃtaraṃ yasya vapurmuneḥ syādbahvadbhutaṃ yasya ca janma dīptam | yasyottamaṃ bhāvinamāttha cārthaṃ taṃ prekṣya kasmāttava dhīra vāṣpaḥ ||
reference: ‘One whose beauty has little to distinguish it from that of a divine sage, and whose brilliant birth has been so wonderful, and for whom thou hast prophesied a transcendent future, — wherefore, on seeing him, do tears come to thee, O reverend one?
baseline: One who gives birth to a person who is blessed with a great gift after a while and who is born bright should be sent to the best of the future. One who sends that gift should be patiently warmed.
morphology: One who gives birth to a child who is blessed with a great gift after a while and who is born bright and who has the best future should be sent to him.

sanskrit: api sthirāyurbhagavan kumāraḥ kaccinna śokāya mama prasūtaḥ | labdhaḥ kathaṃcit salilāṃjalirme na khalvimaṃ pātumupaiti kālaḥ ||
reference: ‘Is the prince, O holy man, destined to a long life? Surely he cannot be born for my sorrow. I have with difficulty obtained a handful of water, surely it is not death which comes to drink it.
baseline: A son born to me after having attained a stable life is said to be born with little sorrow. He would not be able to pay tribute to him for a long time.
morphology: A son born to me after having attained a stable life is said to be born with little sorrow. He would not be able to pay the tribute to the son of the same name for a long time.

sanskrit: apyakṣayaṃ me yaśaso nidhānaṃ kacciddhruvo me kulahastasāraḥ | api prayāsyāmi sukhaṃ paratra supte 'pi putre 'nimiṣaikacakṣuḥ ||
reference: ‘Tell me, is the hoard of my fame free from destruction? Is this chief prize of my family secure ? Shall I ever depart happily to another life, — I who keep one eye ever awake, even when my son is asleep?
baseline: The son should sleep for a minute with his eyes closed.
morphology: If I lose the eye the eyeballs should be kept for a minute. Then I will try to sleep comfortably in the back.

sanskrit: kaccinna me jātamaphullameva kulaprabālaṃ pariśoṣabhāgi | kṣipraṃ vibho brūhi na me 'sti śāṃtiḥ snehaṃ sute vetsi hi bāṃdhavānām ||
reference: ‘Surely this young shoot of my family is not born barren, destined only to wither! Speak quickly, my lord, I cannot wait; thou well knowest the love of near kindred for a son.’
baseline: One who is born with a little hair and becomes full of hair and has the ability to bear the burden of many children should not be afraid of others. One who does not have peace and love and sleeps should be bound by the same.
morphology: A child born young should be blessed with a lot of fruits a child born old and having a strong body and having no fear. He should not suffer in the absence of peace and love.

sanskrit: ityāgatāvegamaniṣṭabuddhyā buddhvā nareṃdraṃ sa* munirbabhāṣe | mā bhūnmatiste nṛpa kācidanyā niḥsaṃśayaṃ tadyadavocamasmi ||
reference: Knowing the king to be thus agitated through his fear of some impending evil, the sage thus addressed him: ‘Let not thy mind, O monarch, be disturbed, — all that I have said is certainly true.
baseline: Having thus understood the speed of movement with the conscious mind he should say the words of the sage narendra. If he does not worship the earth then he should not worship him.
morphology: Having thus understood the speed of movement with the conscious mind he should say to the sage narendra that if he does not worship the earth then he should not worship him.

sanskrit: nāsyānyathātvaṃ prati vikriyā me svāṃ vaṃcanāṃ tu prati viklavo 'smi | kālo hi me yātumayaṃ ca jāto jātikṣayasyāsulabhasya boddhā ||
reference: ‘I have no feeling of fear as to his being subject to change, but I am distressed for mine own disappointment. It is my time to depart, and this child is now born, — he who knows that mystery hard to attain, the means of destroying birth.
baseline: I sell my property to the enemy. I sell it to those who defraud me. I buy black goods and go to the king. I get the good news of the loss of the nation.
morphology: If I sell a piece of land for a nasa it will be sold to those who have defrauded me. I will go to the black one and will get the knowledge of the loss of the nation and its prosperity.

sanskrit: vihāya rājyaṃ viṣayeṣvanāsthastīvraiḥ prayatnairadhigamya tattvam | jagatyayaṃ mohatamo nihaṃtuṃ jvaliṣyati jñānamayo hi sūryaḥ ||
reference: Having forsaken his kingdom, indifferent to all worldly objects, and having attained the highest truth by strenuous efforts, he will shine forth as a sun of knowledge to destroy the darkness of illusion in the world.
baseline: Having left the kingdom and having been concerned with it one would get the principle by their efforts. The sun would ignite the world and destroy it.
morphology: Having left the kingdom and having been concerned with it one would attain the ultimate goal by their efforts. The sun would ignite the world and destroy it.

sanskrit: duḥkhārṇavādvyādhivikīrṇaphenājjarātaraṃgānmaraṇogravegāt | uttārayiṣyatyayamuhyamānamārttaṃ jagajjñānamahāplavena ||
reference: ‘He will deliver by the boat of knowledge the distressed world, borne helplessly along, from the ocean of misery which throws up sickness as its foam, tossing with the waves of old age, and rushing with the dreadful onflow of death.
baseline: O king of the earth you will get relief from the wrath of sorrow misfortune misery destruction and death. You will get rid of this great flood of knowledge.
morphology: O Lord of the earth you will get relief from the wrath of sorrow misfortune death death and destruction. You will get victory by the great flood of knowledge and knowledge.

sanskrit: prajñāṃbuvegāṃ sthiraśīlavaprāṃ samādhiśītāṃ vratacakravākām | asyottamāṃ dharmanadīṃ pravṛttāṃ tṛṣṇārditaḥ pāsyati jīvalokaḥ ||
reference: ‘The thirsty world of living beings will drink the flowing stream of his Law, bursting forth with the water of wisdom, enclosed by the banks of strong moral rules, delightfully cool with contemplation, and filled with religious vows as with ruddy geese.
baseline: One who is conscious and steadfast in the course of time and observes the vow of the chakra should be buried in the same place. One who practices the river of righteousness would pass through the world of living beings with thirst.
morphology: One who is conscious and steadfast in the course of time and observes the vow of the chakra on the day of samadhi the river of righteousness on the other side of the river will pass through the world of life with thirst.

sanskrit: tābhyāṃ saha ca kathāṃ tāmāśvāsya sa sātavāhanastasyāḥ / tadbhāṣayāvatāraṃ vaktuṃ cakre kathāpīṭham //
reference: And having recovered the sense of that tale with their help, Sātavāhana composed the book named Kathāpīṭha, in order to show how the tale came to be first made known in the Paiśācha language.
baseline: Having heard the words of Satavahana with them he should speak to them in the same manner.
morphology: Having heard the words of Satavahana with them he should speak to them in the same manner.

sanskrit: sā ca citrarasanirbharā kathā vismṛtāmarakathā kutūhalāt / tadvidhāya nagare nirantarāṃ khyātimatra bhuvanatraye gatā //
reference: Now that tale was so full of various interest that men were so taken with it as to forget the tales of the gods, and after producing that effect in the city it attained uninterrupted renown in the three worlds.
baseline: He forgets the story of the king and goes to the city of the three worlds of fame continuously.
morphology: He forgets the story of the king and goes to the city of the three worlds with constant fame.

sanskrit: prathamas taraṅgaḥ / gaurīnavapariṣvaṅge vibhoḥ svedāmbu pātu vaḥ / netrāgnibhītyā kāmena vāruṇastramivāhitam //
reference: [Additional note: The Paiśāchī language] INVOCATION MAY the water of Śiva’s sweat, fresh from the embrace of Gaurī,[1] which the God of Love when afraid of the fire of Śiva’s eye employs as his aqueous weapon, protect you.
baseline: The first wave should be of the form of the garu the fragrance in the background the water of the sun the fire of the eyes and the fire.

morphology: He should be blessed with the gift of sātis and the testimony of the god Śrī. He should get the money and the son and the lord of the earth.

sanskrit: kiṃ śrīdattastvamityukto lubdhakena ca tatra saḥ / sa eva mandabhāgyo 'hamityuvāca viniḥśvasan // tataḥ sa lubdhako 'vādīttarhi vacmi sakhe śṛṇu / dṛṣṭā sā te mayā bhāryā krandantī tvāmitastataḥ // pṛṣṭvā tataśca vṛttāntamāśvāsya ca kṛpākulaḥ / nijāṃ pallīmito 'raṇyāddīnāṃ tāṃ nītavānaham //
reference: Then the hunter asked him: “Are you Śrīdatta?” and he, sighing, replied: “I am that unfortunate man.” Then that hunter said: “Listen, friend, I have somewhat to tell you. I saw that wife of yours wandering hither and thither lamenting your absence, and having asked her her story, and consoled her, moved with compassion I took her out of this wood to my own village.
baseline: He should say whether he has given you a gift and the robber should go there. He should be the one who is lucky in his own way. Then he should tell the robbers that he is not interested in you. Then I should tell him that he has seen that his wife is crying. Having asked him to do so he should take him to his village. Having taken him away from me.

sanskrit: tatra cālokya taruṇān pulindān sabhayena sā / mathurānikaṭaṃ grāmaṃ nītā nāgasthalaṃ mayā // tatra ca sthāpitā gehe sthavirasya dvijanmanaḥ / viśvadattābhidhānasya nyāsīkṛtya sagauravam //
reference: But when I saw the young Pulindas[16] there I was afraid, and I took her to a village named Nāgasthala, near Mathurā.[17] And then I placed her in the house of an old Brāhman named Viśvadatta, commending her with all due respect to his care.
baseline: Having walked there the young men the elves the serpents and the people of the city were taken to the village of Mathura. The place of the serpent was placed there by me. Having made him the heir of the world he should be blessed with the title of the second generation.
morphology: Having walked there the young men the elves the serpents and the people of the village of Mathura were taken to the place of the serpent. I placed there two sons of Vira who had been born in the same place. Having made him the heir of the world he became proud.

sanskrit: tataś cāham ihāyāto buddhvā tvannāma tanmukhāt / tām anveṣṭuṃ tato gaccha śīghraṃ nāgasthalaṃ prati // ityukto lubdhakenāśu sa śrīdattastato yayau / taṃ ca nāgasthalaṃ prāpadaparedyurdinātyaye //

baseline: Having said that one should seek him forthwith from his face and go to the place of the serpent. That is to say, he should be given to the king without having been robbed. He should be taken to that place.

sanskrit: tacchrutvā viśvadattastaṃ śrīdattaṃ nijagāda saḥ / mathurāyāṃ suhṛnme 'sti brāhmaṇo guṇināṃ priyaḥ // upādhyāyaśca mantrī ca śūrasenasya bhūpateḥ / tasya haste tvadīyā sā gṛhiṇī sthāpitā mayā //
reference: Then he entered the house of Viśvadatta and when he saw him said: “Give me my wife, who was placed here by the hunter.” Viśvadatta when he heard that answered him: “I have a friend in Mathurā, a Brāhman, dear to all virtuous men, the spiritual preceptor and minister of the King Śūrasena;
baseline: Having given him the gift of the universe he has given him his own body. He is in Mathura a brahmin and a friend of the virtuous. He has been placed in the hands of the lord of the mighty army the minister the teacher and the lord. I have placed the housekeeper in his hands.

sanskrit: bhayaṃ hi vijano grāmo na tadrakṣākṣamo bhavet / tatprātastatra gaccha tvamadya viśramyatāmiha //
