baseline: One should see a thread named after the daughter one named after that animal the relics of that animal and the new blood of that person. One would see the child in the form of a janu a pippilika a dādāśya a free cow and a kātra in the kingdom of Uruḍa.
morphology: One who has a daughter a daughter and a thread named after that animal the name of that animal and the names of the other animals should be mentioned in the scriptures. One who sees the new blood and the rest of the blood should be called jānu jaṇu tīrā jāna pīpilika dādānśa dandasya kārākara katara free from bondage in the kingdom of Oruḍa.

sanskrit: tāvatā tumulākrandamantaḥ puramajāyata / rājāpi putra putreti cikranda prākṛto yathā //
reference: Thereupon the whole harem was full of confused lamentation, and the king himself shrieked out, ‘My son! my son!’ like a common man.
baseline: Then the king should worship the son of the king as well as the son as if he had worshipped the king.
morphology: Then the king should be blessed with a son son daughter son and son.

sanskrit: kṣaṇāttasminsamāśvaste bāle 'pāstapipīlike / duḥkhaikakāraṇaṃ rājā sa ninindaikaputratām //
reference: The boy was soon comforted, the ant having been removed, and the king blamed the misfortune of his only having one son as the cause of all his grief.
baseline: The king should not condemn the son for one of the reasons for his misery.
morphology: The king should be punished for one cause of misery by the king.

sanskrit: asti kaścidupāyo me yena syurbahavaḥ sutāḥ / iti tatparitāpena papraccha brāhmaṇāṃśca saḥ //
reference: And he asked the Brāhmans in his affliction if there was any expedient by which he might obtain a large number of children.
baseline: He should say that he is the son of one of the brahmins. He should be called the sun the sun and the thread.
morphology: He should say that he is the son of a man who is a cow who is the source of water and the thread. Then he should say with his own words to the Brahmins.

sanskrit: te taṃ pratyabruvanrājannupāyo 'tra tavāstyayam / havaitaṃ tvatsutaṃ vahnau tanmāsaṃ hūyate 'khilam // tadgandhāghrāṇato rājñyaḥ sarvāḥ prāpsyanti te sutān / etac chrutvā sa rājā tat tathā sarvam akārayat //
reference: They answered him: ‘O king, there is one expedient open to you: you must slay this son and offer up all his flesh in the fire.[4] By smelling the smell of that sacrifice all thy wives will obtain sons.’ When he heard that, the king had the whole ceremony performed as they directed;
baseline: The king has made all the objects of the king's power by making him drink water with the fragrance of water. Having made him drink it the king should make him drink the water of water and drink it with the sound of gandha. The queen should get all the elements of the sun. After having made him eat it he should make all things.
morphology: They should be placed in front of the king with the help of the goddess Brāvana. The king should place it here. The goddess should be washed with water with the fragrance of gandha. The queen should get all the perfumes by smelling it. Having removed it the king should make it all.

sanskrit: svapatnīsamasaṃkhyāṃś ca sa putrān prāptavān nṛpaḥ / atas tavāpi homena sādhayāmo vayaṃ sutam // ityuktvā dhanadattaṃ te brāhmaṇāḥ kḷptadakṣiṇam / homaṃ cakrustatastasya vaṇijo jātavānsutaḥ //
reference: So we can obtain a son for you also by a burnt-offering.” When they had said this to Dhanadatta, the Brāhmans, after a sacrificial fee had been promised them, performed a sacrifice: then a son was born to that merchant. That son was called Guhasena, and he gradually grew up to man’s estate.
baseline: He got equal number of sons by his wives. Then he would get the same amount of money from the lord. That is to say, he would give the money to the brahmins. The king would get his wife from the king. He would get a son from the merchant.
morphology: He got equal number of sons from his wife. He should then also get the money from Homa. That is to say, he should give the money to the Brahmins. He would get the goods from the king. The king would get his wife from the merchant.

sanskrit: guhasenābhidhānaśca sa balo vavṛdhe kramāt / pitātha dhanadatto 'sya bhāryāmanviṣyati sma saḥ // tataḥ sa tatpitā tena tanayena samaṃ yayau / dvīpāntaraṃ snuṣāhetorvaṇijyāvyapadeśataḥ //
reference: Then his father Dhanadatta began to look out for a wife for him. Then his father went with that son of his to another country, on the pretence of traffic, but really to get a daughter-in-law;
baseline: He would call the army of the cave and the army in the order of strength and breadth. He would then take the wife of the one who had given him wealth with his father. Then he would go to the island with his son. Then the king would go into the island and sell his goods with his wife.
morphology: He would then take the wife of the one who had given him wealth with his father in order to build a cave and the army in order. Then he would go to the island with his son. He would go back to the king and trade with him.

sanskrit: tatra devasmitāṃ nāma dharmaguptādvaṇigvarāt / svaputraguhasenasya kṛte kanyāmayācata //
reference: there he asked an excellent merchant of the name of Dharmagupta to give him his daughter named Devasmitā for his son Guhasena.
baseline: There the name of the god is mentioned in the scriptures. One would get a virgin for the sake of his son and his wife.
morphology: The name of the deity should be mentioned there in the scriptures. One should take a virgin for the sake of his son and his wife.

sanskrit: dharmaguptastu saṃbandhaṃ na tamaṅgīcakāra saḥ / ālocya tāmraliptīṃ tāṃ durāṃ duhitṛvatsalaḥ //
reference: But Dharmagupta, who was tenderly attached to his daughter, did not approve of that connection, reflecting that the city of Tāmraliptā was very far off.
baseline: He who does not agree with the relationship between the two gods should not discuss the matter. He should discuss it with the copper plate and give it to the enemy.
morphology: He who does not agree with the relationship between the two gods should be called a dharmagupta. He should be made to drink copper and other precious stones.

sanskrit: sā tu devasmitā dṛṣṭvā guhasenaṃ tadaiva tam / tadguṇākṛṣṭacittatvādbandhutyāgaikaniścayā // sakhīmukhena kṛtvā ca saṃketaṃ saha tena sā / priyeṇa pitṛyuktena rātrau dvīpāttato yayau //
reference: But when Devasmitā beheld that Guhasena, her mind was immediately attracted by his virtues, and she was set on abandoning her relations, and so she made an assignation with him by means of a confidante, and went away from that country at night with her beloved and his father.
baseline: Having seen the goddess of gods one should go to the cave with the same quality and with the determination of having a friend and having a companion and having the sign with her. One would go to island with his beloved father in the night.
morphology: Having seen the goddess of gods one should place her in the cave with a vow to bind her with the gift of goodness and good will. Having said this with the face of a friend she should leave the island with her beloved father in the night.

sanskrit: tāmraliptīmatha prāpya tayoḥ kṛtavivāhayoḥ / jāyāpatyormithaḥ premapāśabaddhamabhūnmanaḥ //
reference: When they reached Tāmraliptā they were married, and the minds of the young couple were firmly knit together by the bond of mutual love.
baseline: Having obtained the sum of copper copper and copper the marriage made between them is said to be love bound.
morphology: Having obtained the sum of copper copper and copper the marriage made between them should be said to be of love.

sanskrit: athāstaṃ pitari prāpte prerito 'bhūtsa bandhubhiḥ / kaṭāhadvīpagamane guhaseno yadṛcchayā //
reference: Then Guhasena’s father died, and he himself was urged by his relations to go to the country of Kaṭāha [see notes on the identification of Kaṭāha] for the purpose of trafficking;
baseline: Then the father would receive it from the apostle with his friends. Then he would go to Katah and the island of the cave.
morphology: Then the father would receive it. The apostle would be sent by his friends to visit the island of Katah and the cave army as he wished.

sanskrit: taccāsya gamanaṃ bhāryā tadā nāṅgīcakāra sā / serṣyā devasmitā kāmamanyastrīsaṅgaśaṅkinī //
reference: but his wife Devasmitā was too jealous to approve of that expedition, fearing exceedingly that he would be attracted by some other lady.
baseline: Then the wife should go to that place. Then she should leave the place naked. Then the goddess should be worshipped with the penance of the gods. The woman should be accompanied by the grace of her husband.
morphology: Then the wife should go to that place. Then she should go naked. Then the goddess should be mercilessly worshipped and the woman should be consoled.

sanskrit: tataḥ patnyāmanicchantyāṃ prerayatsu ca bandhuṣu / kartavyaniścalo mūḍho guhaseno babhūva saḥ //
reference: Then, as his wife did not approve of it, and his relations kept inciting him to it, Guhasena, whose mind was firmly set on doing his duty, was bewildered.
baseline: Then he would send his wives and his friends to the cave. He would become a fool and a soldier.
morphology: Then he would send his wives and relatives to the enemy. He would be a foolish and a coward.

sanskrit: aha gatvā nirāhāraścakre devakule vratam / upāyamiha devo me nirdiśatviti cintayan // sāpi devasmitā tadvattena sārdhaṃ vyadhādvratam / tato 'nayoḥ śivaḥ svapne daṃpatyordarśanaṃ dadau //
reference: Then he went and performed a vow in the temple of the god, observing a rigid fast, trusting that the god would show him some way out of his difficulty. And his wife Devasmitā also performed a vow with him. Then Śiva was pleased to appear to that couple in a dream;
baseline: Having gone to the temple of the gods and observing a fast one should observe a fast. One should also observe a vow with the advice given by the gods. One who is a devasmita should follow the same course of action. Then one should see the couple in a dream by the name of Śiva.
morphology: Having gone to the temple of the gods and having fasted one should observe a vow. One should worship the gods in the same way. One would also worship the goddess with the same spirit. Then one would see the couple in a dream.

sanskrit: dve ca raktāmbuje dattvā sa devastāvabhāṣata / haste gṛhṇītamekaikaṃ padmametadubhāvapi //
reference: and giving them two red lotuses, the god said to them: “Take each of you one of these lotuses in your hand.
baseline: Having given two to the goddess in the form of a red arrow he said to her that one lotus should be taken in his hand and the other one should be given to her.
morphology: Having given the two raktambhujas he said that the gods should be worshipped. One lotus should be taken in his hand and the other two should be offered.

sanskrit: dūrasthatve ca yadyekaḥ śīlatyāgaṃ kariṣyati / tadanyasya kare padmaṃ mlānimeṣyati nānyathā // etacchrutvā prabudhyaiva daṃpatī tāvapaśyatām / anyonyasyeva hṛdayaṃ hastasthaṃ raktamambujam //
reference: And if either of you shall be unfaithful during your separation the lotus in the hand of the other shall fade, but not otherwise.”[5] After hearing this the two woke up, and each beheld in the hand of the other a red lotus, and it seemed as if they had got one another’s hearts.
baseline: One who renounces the nobleness in a distant place will get rid of the lotus in the hands of another. Having said this the couple should understand that the heart of one should be held in the hand and the blood should be collected.
morphology: One who renounces the virtues of another would get the lotus in his hand. Having said this the couple should understand that the heart of one should be placed in the hands of another and the blood should be sent to him.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa cakre prasthānaṃ guhaseno dhṛtāmbujaḥ / sā tu devasmitātatra tasthau padmārpitekṣaṇā //
reference: Then Guhasena set out, lotus in hand, but Devasmitā remained in the house with her eyes fixed upon her flower.
baseline: Then he departs from the circle goes to the cave and enters the cave. Then he should go to the temple of the gods. He should see the idol of Padmarpita.
morphology: Then he departs from the circle goes to the cave and worships the goddess dhrutambuja. Then he is placed in the temple of the gods and is worshipped as a lotus.

sanskrit: guhaseno 'pi taṃ prāpa kaṭāhadvīpamāśu saḥ / kartuṃ pravavṛte cātra ratnānāṃ krayavikrayau //
reference: Guhasena for his part quickly reached the country of Kaṭāha, and began to buy and sell jewels there.
baseline: He would then find the cave. He would go about buying and selling gems in the cave and the island of Katah.
morphology: Having found him in a cave he would go to the island of Katah and sell the gems there.

sanskrit: haste ca tasya taddṛṣṭvā sadaivāmlānamambujam / atra kecidvaṇikputrāścatvāro vismayaṃ yayuḥ //
reference: And four young merchants in that country, seeing that that unfading lotus was ever in his hand, were greatly astonished.
baseline: Having seen him always with his hands one should know that there are two sons and three daughters.
morphology: Having seen him always with his hands one should be amazed by the presence of two sons and three daughters here.

sanskrit: te yuktyā taṃ gṛhaṃ nītvā pāyayitvā bhṛśaṃ madhu / papracchuḥ padmavṛttāntaṃ so 'pi kṣībaḥ śaśaṃsa tam //
reference: Accordingly they got him to their house by an artifice, and made him drink a great deal of wine, and then asked him the history of the lotus, and he being intoxicated told them the whole story.
baseline: Having taken him into the house with that ploy after having made him drink honey he should be blessed with a lotus flower.
morphology: Having taken him into the house with that ploy after having made him drink honey he should be blessed with the lotus.

sanskrit: tatastaṃ ciranirvāhyaratnādikrayavikrayam / vicintya guhasenaṃ te catvāro 'pi vaṇiksutāḥ // saṃmantrya kautukātpāpāstadbhāryāśīlaviplavam / cikīrṣavo yayuḥ śīghraṃ tāmraliptīmalakṣitāḥ //
reference: Then those four young merchants, knowing that Guhasena would take a long time to complete his sales and purchases of jewels and other wares, planned together, like rascals as they were, the seduction of his wife out of curiosity, and eager to accomplish it, set out quickly for Tāmraliptā without their departure being noticed.
baseline: Then the four of them who have been sold by the sale of gold gold and other precious stones should be taken care of. Then they would be able to sell their gold and gold. They would get a good deal by chanting the mantra. Then their wives would go to war. They should go to the land of copper copper and copper.
morphology: Then the four men would sell the carcass of a rat after having thought about it and after having discussed it they would go to the market. After having spoken the words of the king they should go to his wife and the revolution. They would soon get a copper plate.

sanskrit: tatropāyaṃ vicinvantaḥ sugatāyatanasthitām / pravrājikāmupājagmurnāmnā yogakaraṇḍikām //
reference: There they cast about for some instrument, and at last had recourse to a female ascetic of the name of Yogakaraṇḍikā, who lived in a sanctuary of Buddha;
baseline: Then one should draw a spade of yogic notes named as āgmūrna which is said to be the propitiatory lotus.
morphology: Then one should think of the place where one has attained prosperity. The king of Pravrājīkā the king of the transcendent world the lord of the universe the card of the yogic spheres named after him.

sanskrit: prītipūrvaṃ ca tām ūcur bhagavaty asmadīpsitam / sādhyate cet tvayā tat te dāsyāmo 'rthān bahūn iti // sāpyuvāca dhruvaṃ yūnāṃ kāpi strī vāñchiteha vaḥ / tadbhūta sādhayāmyeva dhanalipsā ca nāsti me //
reference: and they said to her in an affectionate manner: “Reverend madam, if our object is accomplished by your help we will give you much wealth.” She answered them: “No doubt you young men desire some woman in this city, so tell me all about it, I will procure you the object of your desire; but I have no wish for money.
baseline: If you have done that before the love and desire of the Lord you would have done it. If you do that you will have to do that. You would have accomplished that. If a woman wants to have a pole a man would get it. There is no such thing as wealth and greed.
morphology: If you raise them before the love of the Lord and make them light up with us you will get them as servants. If you want a woman to have a pole and a snake you want it. You will get it. There is no money in that.

sanskrit: asti siddhikarī nāma śiṣyā me buddhiśālinī / atprasādena saṃprāptamasaṃkhyaṃ hi dhanaṃ mayā //
reference: I have a pupil of distinguished ability named Siddhikarī;
baseline: The disciples are known as siddhikari. I am wise. The number obtained by the offering of the same is my wealth.
morphology: The disciples are known as siddhikari. I am wise. The number obtained by offering the same is my wealth.

sanskrit: kathaṃ śiṣyāprasādena bhūri prāptaṃ dhanaṃ tvayā / iti taiḥ sā vaṇikputraiḥ pṛṣṭā pravrājikābravīt // kautukaṃ yadi tatputrāḥ śrūyatāṃ varṇayāmi vaḥ / iha ko'pi vaṇikpūrvamāyayāvuttarāpathāt //
reference: owing to her kindness I have obtained untold wealth.” The young merchants asked: “How have you obtained untold wealth by the assistance of a pupil?” Being asked this question, the female ascetic said: “If you feel any curiosity about the matter, listen, my sons, I will tell you the whole story: Long ago a certain merchant came here from the north;
baseline: He should explain to the disciples how he got wealth by offering gifts. He should ask his sons to go back and tell them the story. If he had seen his sons then he should tell the story of the same. He would have done it in the past.
morphology: He should explain to the disciples how he got wealth by offering gifts. He should ask his sons and explain to them the merriment shown by his sons. If he had done so he would have done it in the past.

sanskrit: tasyehasthasya macchiṣyā sā gatvā śiśriye gṛhe / yuktyā karmakarībhāvaṃ kṛtarūpavivartanā //
reference: while he was dwelling here my pupil went and obtained, with a treacherous object, the position of a serving-maid in his house, having first altered her appearance;
baseline: He should go to the disciple's house with the mermaids in his arms and perform the deed with his disciple.
morphology: He should go to the disciple's house with the help of his master and make his disciple do his duty by changing his form.

sanskrit: viśvāsya vaṇijaṃ taṃ ca tadgṛhātsvarṇasaṃcayam / sarvaṃ muṣitvā pracchannaṃ pratyūṣe sātha niryayau //
reference: and after she had gained the confidence of that merchant she stole all his hoard of gold from his house and went off secretly in the morning twilight.
baseline: Having believed him the merchant should collect gold from that house and after wiping everything away the hidden one should be sent with him to the king.
morphology: Having believed the merchant he should collect gold from that house and wash everything and take it away with him.

sanskrit: nagarīnirgatāṃ dṛṣṭvā śaṅkāśīghragatiṃ ca tām / mṛdaṅgahasto moṣāya ḍombaḥ ko 'pyanvagāddrutam //
reference: And as she went out from the city, moving rapidly through fear, a certain Ḍomba,[6] with his drum in his hand, saw her, and pursued her at full speed with the intention of robbing her.
baseline: Having seen the inner part of the city one should fear it and move quickly. One would get a domba with the mound of mud a limb a cow and a cow.
morphology: Having seen the inner part of the city one should fear the speed of movement. One should hold the bow with the hands of the mridangam the bow of the cow and the sword of the king.

sanskrit: nyagrodhasya talaṃ prāpya sā dṛṣṭvā tamupāgatam / ḍombaṃ siddhikarī dhūrtā sadainyevedamabravīt // bhartrā sahādya kalahaṃ kṛtvāhaṃ nigatā gṛhāt / martuṃ tadbhadra pāśo 'tra tvayā me badhyatāmiti //
reference: When she had reached the foot of a Nyagrodha tree she saw that he had come up with her, and so the cunning Siddhikarī said this to him in a plaintive manner: “I have had a jealous quarrel with my husband, and I have left his house to die, therefore, my good man, make a noose for me to hang myself with.” Then the Ḍomba thought: “Let her hang herself.
baseline: Having found the bottom of the pit of the enemy when he saw it he came to Tāmupā. Having perfected the domb the dhūrtha worshipped him in the eternal form. Having accompanied the husband he said that he would fight with him. Having taken him away from the house he would kill him.
morphology: Having found the bottom of the pit of the enemy when he sees it he comes to Tāmupā. Having accomplished the goal he said that he would fight with his wife he would have to fight with her and take her home. He would have killed her.

sanskrit: pāśena mriyatāmeṣā kimenāṃ hanmyahaṃ striyam / matveti tatra vṛkṣe 'sau ḍombaḥ pāśamasajjayat //
reference: Why should I be guilty of her death, especially as she is a woman?” and so he fastened a noose for her to the tree.
baseline: Having killed a woman by the side of a tree he has set up a dumb ox in the forest.
morphology: Having killed a woman by the side of a tree he has set a dumb ox on the tree.

sanskrit: tataḥ siddhikarī ḍombaṃ sā mugdheva jagāda tam / kriyate kathamudbandhastvayā medarśyatāmiti // tataḥ sa ḍombas taṃ dattvā mṛdaṅgaṃ pādayoradhaḥ / itthaṃ kriyata ityuktvā svakaṇṭhe pāśamarpayat //
reference: Then Siddhikarī, feigning ignorance, said to the Ḍomba: “How is the noose slipped round the neck? Show me, I entreat you.” Then the Ḍomba placed the drum under his feet, and saying, “This is the way we do the trick,” he fastened the noose round his own throat.
baseline: Then the dove should be set on the ground with the dumbbells. Then he should offer the dobbs and the mridangam should be placed on the feet. He should do so by placing a stick on his ears.
morphology: Then the dove should be set on the ground with the mridangam. Then he should be made to lie on the floor with the dumbbells. He should be bound with the threads. Then after giving the dobams he should place the domb on the feet of the doer. Then the bow should be placed on his ears with a stick.

sanskrit: sāpi siddhikarī sadyastaṃ mṛdaṅgamacūrṇayat / pādāghātena ḍombo 'tha so 'pi pāśe vyapadyata // tatkālamāgato 'nveṣṭuṃ vṛkṣamūle dadarśa saḥ / muṣitāśeṣakoṣāṃ tāṃ dūrātsiddhikarīṃ vaṇik //
reference: Siddhikarī for her part smashed the drum to atoms with a kick, and that Ḍomba hung till he was dead.[7] At that moment the merchant arrived in search of her, and beheld from a distance Siddhikarī, who had stolen from him untold treasures, at the foot of the tree.
baseline: The sāpīdhikārī has now filled him with the mud the dumbbells with the blows of the feet and he should immediately return to the tree. He would then show the moustache and the leftovers in the forest.
morphology: He who has already accomplished the task should be immediately covered with a piece of mud. He should be thrown into the side of the tree with the help of a dumbo with the stabbing of his feet. He would immediately return to the tree and show the moustache and other parts of the body to the man who had accomplished it.

sanskrit: sāpi dṛṣṭvā tamāyāntaṃ vṛkṣe tasminnalakṣitam / āruhya tasthau śākhāyāṃ pattraughacchannavigrahā //
reference: She too saw him coming, and climbed up the tree without being noticed, and remained there on a bough, having her body concealed by the dense foliage.
baseline: The tree should be placed on the right side of the tree and the leaves should be kept on the left side.
morphology: The tree should be placed on the right side of the tree and the leaves should be kept on the left side of it.

sanskrit: sa cāgatya vaṇigyāvatsabhṛtyaḥ pāśabandhanam / ḍombameva tamadrākṣīnna tu siddhikarīṃ kvacit //
reference: When the merchant came up with his servants he saw the Ḍomba hanging by his neck, but Siddhikarī was nowhere to be seen.
baseline: He should come and sing the song of the festival. The bandage should be tied with a stick. The domba should be made of copper and the dribbler should be set on the ground.
morphology: He should come and sing a song and perform a ritual and bind a pascha bandha. The domba is the same as the tāmādrākshetra.

sanskrit: mā nāma vṛkṣamārūḍhā sā bhavediti tatkṣaṇam / eko 'sya vaṇijo bhṛtyastarumārohati sma tam //
reference: Immediately one of his servants said, “I wonder whether she has got up this tree,” and proceeded to ascend it himself.
baseline: One who is a merchant should immediately make a garland of trees named Na ̄ ma. He would then make a barber of the same tree and kill him.
morphology: One who is a merchant should immediately make a garland of trees named Na ̄ ma. He would then make a barber of the same tree and kill him.

sanskrit: sadā tvayyeva me prītirihārūḍhastvameva ca / tatsundara tavaivedaṃ dhanamehi bhajasva mām //
reference: Then Siddhikarī said: “I have always loved you, and now you have climbed up where I am, so all this wealth is at your disposal, handsome man;
baseline: May always you always be pleased with me. May you worship me with that beautiful scripture and wealth.

baseline: The body is subject to the virtues of time and action. It is five things. One should not confuse others. One would be possessed by a serpent as before.
morphology: One who is subject to the virtues of time action body five material things and others should be covered by the snake.

sanskrit: ahastāni sa hastānām apadāni catuḥ padām phalgūni tatra mahatām jīvaḥ jīvasya jīvanam
reference: Those who are devoid of hands are prey for those who have hands; those devoid of legs are prey for the four-legged. The weak are the subsistence of the strong, and the general rule holds that one living being is food for another.
baseline: He who gives the hands and hands of a great creature would be blessed with four great qualities.
morphology: He who gives the hands and hands of a person is said to have done four great deeds. He should give the life of a living being.

sanskrit: tat idam bhagavān rājan ekaḥ ātmā ātmanām sva dṛk antaraḥ anantaraḥ bhāti paśya tam māyayā urudhā
reference: Therefore, O King, you should look to the Supreme Lord only, who is one without a second and who manifests Himself by different energies and is both within and without.
baseline: One who is the king of the gods one who has seen the innermost part of the soul and the inner part of it should see it.
morphology: One who is the king of the gods one who has seen the innermost parts of the soul and the inner part of the self would see it.

sanskrit: saḥ ayam adya mahārāja bhagavān bhūta bhāvanaḥ kāla rūpaḥ avatīrṇaḥ asyām abhāvāya sura dviṣām
reference: That Supreme Personality of Godhead, Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, in the guise of all-devouring time [kāla-rūpa] has now descended to the earth to eliminate the envious from the world.
baseline: He is the king lord spirit spirit and the form of time. This is the reason for the absence of these two notes.
morphology: He should be worshipped as the king lord ghost spirit spirit and the form of time.

sanskrit: niṣpāditam deva kṛtyam avaśeṣam pratīkṣate tāvat yūyam avekṣadhvam bhavet yāvat iha īśvaraḥ
reference: The Lord has already performed His duties to help the demigods, and He is awaiting the rest. You Pāṇḍavas may wait as long as the Lord is here on earth.
baseline: The one who has executed the deva should wait for the remnant till the time you observe the deiva.
morphology: You should observe the execution of the deva and wait for the remaining deed till it is done by the lord.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ saha bhrātrā gāndhāryā ca sva bhāryayā dakṣiṇena himavataḥ ṛṣīṇām āśramam gataḥ
reference: O King, your uncle Dhṛtarāṣṭra, his brother Vidura and his wife Gāndhārī have gone to the southern side of the Himālaya Mountains, where there are shelters of the great sages.
baseline: Dhritarashtra and his brother Gandhari accompanied by his wife went to the abode of the sages from the southern side of the Himalayas.
morphology: Having accompanied Dhritarashtra and his brother Gandhari he went to the abode of the sages from the south with his wife Himavata.

sanskrit: srotobhiḥ saptabhiḥ yā vai svardhunī saptadhā vyadhāt saptānām prītaye nānā sapta srotaḥ pracakṣate
reference: The place is called Saptasrota [“divided by seven”] because there the waters of the sacred Ganges were divided into seven branches. This was done for the satisfaction of the seven great ṛṣis.
baseline: The seven sources of gold are known to be different.
morphology: The seven sources of gold are described as having seven sources. The seven different sources of love are described in the scriptures.

sanskrit: snātvā anusavanam tasmin hutvā ca agnīn yathā vidhi ap bhakṣaḥ upaśānta ātmā saḥ āste vigata eṣaṇaḥ
reference: On the banks at Saptasrota, Dhṛtarāṣṭra is now engaged in beginning aṣṭāṅga-yoga by bathing three times daily, in the morning, noon and evening, by performing the Agni-hotra sacrifice with fire and by drinking only water. This helps one control the mind and the senses and frees one completely from thoughts of familial affection.
baseline: After having washed one should follow the path of fire and eat food as per the custom. The spirit should be calm.
morphology: After having washed one should follow the path of fire. One who eats food as prescribed by the law and the spirit is at peace.

sanskrit: jita āsanaḥ jita śvāsaḥ pratyāhṛta ṣaṭ indriyaḥ hari bhāvanayā dhvasta rajaḥ sattva tamaḥ malaḥ
reference: One who has controlled the sitting postures [the yogic āsanas] and the breathing process can turn the senses toward the Absolute Personality of Godhead and thus become immune to the contaminations of the modes of material nature, namely mundane goodness, passion and ignorance.
baseline: Having conquered the seat having conquered the breath having removed the six senses the king is destroyed by the spirit of Hari.
morphology: Having conquered the seat having conquered the breath the six senses are destroyed by the spirit of Hari the king the sātva tāma and the māla.

sanskrit: vijñāna ātmani saṁyojya kṣetra jñe pravilāpya tam brahmaṇi ātmānam ādhāre ghaṭa ambaram iva ambare
reference: Dhṛtarāṣṭra will have to amalgamate his pure identity with intelligence and then merge into the Supreme Being with knowledge of his qualitative oneness, as a living entity, with the Supreme Brahman. Being freed from the blocked sky, he will have to rise to the spiritual sky.
baseline: Having known the realms of knowledge and the attainment of the self one should know that Brahman is the base of the soul.
morphology: Having known the realms of knowledge the self the attainment of the self and having known them one would get Brahman on the basis of that self.

sanskrit: dhvasta māyā guṇa udarkaḥ niruddha karaṇa āśayaḥ nivartita akhila āhāraḥ āste sthāṇuḥ iva acalaḥ tasya antarāyaḥ mā eva abhūḥ sannyasta akhila karmaṇaḥ
reference: He will have to suspend all the actions of the senses, even from the outside, and will have to be impervious to interactions of the senses, which are influenced by the modes of material nature. After renouncing all material duties, he must become immovably established, beyond all sources of hindrances on the path.
baseline: Having destroyed the merits of the illusion one should stop all the actions. One should not obstruct the whole diet as if it were fixed.
morphology: Having destroyed the merits of the illusion one should avoid all the things that are good for him. One who does not obstruct him should not stop all the actions.

sanskrit: saḥ vā adya tanāt rājan parataḥ pañcame ahani kalevaram hāsyati svam tat ca bhasmī bhaviṣyati
reference: O King, he will quit his body, most probably on the fifth day from today. And his body will turn to ashes.
baseline: The king who laughed at him on the fifth day after having departed from him would become the incinerator himself.
morphology: The king who laughed at the priest on the fifth day after having departed from him would be burnt alive by him.

sanskrit: dahyamāne agnibhiḥ dehe patyuḥ patnī saha uṭaje bahiḥ sthitā patim sādhvī tam agnim anu vekṣyati
reference: While outside observing her husband, who will burn in the fire of mystic power along with his thatched cottage, his chaste wife will enter the fire with rapt attention.
baseline: A husband standing outside with his wife on the ground with fire in the form of fire should be worshipped by the sage.
morphology: The husband standing outside with his wife on the altar with the fire burning in the fire should be worshipped by the sage.

sanskrit: viduraḥ tu tat āścaryam niśāmya kuru nandana harṣa śoka yutaḥ tasmāt gantā tīrtha niṣevakaḥ
reference: Vidura, being affected with delight and grief, will then leave that place of sacred pilgrimage.
baseline: O Vidura one who does not want to go to the temple would be surprised by that. O Nandana one with joy sorrow and sorrow. One who does so would be prohibited from visiting it.
morphology: O Vidura when you see that wonder you should do it. O Nandana you get happiness and sorrow. Then you get rid of the pilgrimage.

sanskrit: iti uktvā atha āruhat svargam nāradaḥ saha tumburuḥ yudhiṣṭhiraḥ vacaḥ tasya hṛdi kṛtvā ajahāt śucaḥ
reference: Having spoken thus, the great sage Nārada, along with his vīṇā, ascended into outer space. Yudhiṣṭhira kept his instruction in his heart and so was able to get rid of all lamentations.
baseline: Having said this one should ascend to heaven with Narada. Having said that Yudhishthira should bow down with his heart.
morphology: Having said this one should ascend to heaven with Narada. Having said that Yudhishthira should bow down with his heart and recite the scriptures.

sanskrit: sūtaḥ uvāca samprasthite dvārakāyām jiṣṇau bandhu didṛkṣayā jñātum ca puṇya ślokasya kṛṣṇasya ca viceṣṭitam
reference: Śrī Sūta Gosvāmī said: Arjuna went to Dvārakā to see Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa and other friends and also to learn from the Lord of His next activities.
baseline: One should know the virtuous verses of Lord Śiva and Lord Kṛṣṇa in the doorway of the temple.
morphology: One should know the virtuous scriptures of Lord Śiva and Lord Kṛṣṇa in the doorway of the sanctum sanctorum.

sanskrit: vyatītāḥ katicit māsāḥ tadā na āyāt tataḥ arjunaḥ dadarśa ghora rūpāṇi nimittāni kuru udvahaḥ
reference: A few months passed, and Arjuna did not return. Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira then began to observe some inauspicious omens, which were fearful in themselves.
baseline: Then Arjuna would see the evil forms for a few months.
morphology: Then Arjuna would see the evil forms for a few months.

sanskrit: kālasya ca gatim raudrām viparyasta ṛtu dharmiṇaḥ pāpīyasīm nṛṇām vārtām krodha lobha anṛta ātmanām
reference: He saw that the direction of eternal time had changed, and this was very fearful. There were disruptions in the seasonal regularities. The people in general had become very greedy, angry and deceitful. And he saw that they were adopting foul means of livelihood.
baseline: The course of time and the nature of anger should be reversed. The seasons should be devoted to righteousness sinfulness anger greed hatred anger and hatred.
morphology: The course of time is the opposite of anger. The seasons are righteous the sinners the enemies the spirits the greed the anger and the desire.

sanskrit: jihma prāyam vyavahṛtam śāṭhya miśram ca sauhṛdam pitṛ mātṛ suhṛt bhrātṛ dam patīnām ca kalkanam
reference: All ordinary transactions and dealings became polluted with cheating, even between friends. And in familial affairs, there was always misunderstanding between fathers, mothers and sons, between well-wishers, and between brothers. Even between husband and wife there was always strain and quarrel.
baseline: The tongue should be often treated with a stick and mixed with friendship the father the mother the friend the brother and the husband.
morphology: The jihm should be often used with the help of a stick and mixed with friendship the father mother friend brother and husband.

sanskrit: nimittāni ati ariṣṭāni kāle tu anugate nṛṇām lobha ādi adharma prakṛtim dṛṣṭvā uvāca anujam nṛpaḥ
reference: In course of time it came to pass that people in general became accustomed to greed, anger, pride, etc. Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira, observing all these omens, spoke to his younger brother.
baseline: Having seen the nature of iniquity and the greed of the niras in the past for reasons beyond doubt one should follow them. One should say anunjam nirpa.
morphology: The reasons are very bad. Seeing the greed of the enemies and the nature of iniquity at the beginning one should follow them in time one should say anunjam nripa.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiraḥ uvāca sampreṣitaḥ dvārakāyām jiṣṇuḥ bandhu didṛkṣayā jñātum ca puṇya ślokasya kṛṣṇasya ca viceṣṭitam
reference: Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira said to his younger brother Bhīmasena: I sent Arjuna to Dvārakā to meet his friends and to learn from the Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, of His program of work.
baseline: Yudhisthira said that he would communicate with Jīṣṇu at the doorstep of the dvākāśṇa temple. He would like to know the merits of the shlokas and that of Kṛṣṇa by the eye of the friend.
morphology: Yudhisthira communicated the words of Jīṣṇu at the doorstep of the dvākārṣṇa brother. He sought to know the virtuous scriptures of Krishna by sight.

sanskrit: gatāḥ sapta adhunā māsāḥ bhīmasena tava anujaḥ na āyāti kasya vā hetoḥ na aham veda idam añjasā
reference: Since he departed, seven months have passed, yet he has not returned. I do not know factually how things are going there.
baseline: O Bhimsena for the past seven months now your younger brother does not come. For the sake of any one else I am not going to study the Vedas.
morphology: O Bhimsena for the past seven months your younger brother does not come. For the sake of any one else I am not going to study the Vedas.

sanskrit: api deva ṛṣiṇā ādiṣṭaḥ saḥ kālaḥ ayam upasthitaḥ yadā ātmanaḥ aṅgam ākrīḍam bhagavān utsisṛkṣati
reference: Is He going to quit His earthly pastimes, as Devarṣi Nārada indicated? Has that time already arrived?
baseline: The time when the body part of the self should be worshipped by the lord and the sage should be ordered to do so is the present time.
morphology: The time when the body part of the self should be worshipped by the gods and the sages is said to be present.

sanskrit: yasmāt naḥ sampadaḥ rājyam dārāḥ prāṇāḥ kulam prajāḥ āsan sapatna vijayaḥ lokāḥ ca yat anugrahāt
reference: From Him only, all our kingly opulence, good wives, lives, progeny, control over our subjects, victory over our enemies, and future accommodations in higher planets have become possible. All this is due to His causeless mercy upon us.
baseline: Since there was no wealth kingdom army life clan people victory and people the grace that was given to them would be of seven kinds.
morphology: By the grace of the king the king and the king of the kingdom and the sons of Prana the clan and the people were conquered by the seven gods.

sanskrit: paśya utpātān nara vyāghra divyān bhaumān sa daihikān dāruṇān śaṁsataḥ adūrāt bhayam naḥ buddhi mohanam
reference: Just see, O man with a tiger’s strength, how many miseries due to celestial influences, earthly reactions and bodily pains — all very dangerous in themselves — are foreboding danger in the near future by deluding our intelligence.
baseline: Behold the male tiger the divine the earth the carnal the evil and the illusory are not feared from far away.
morphology: Behold the male tiger the divine one the earth the physical one and the evil one are not afraid from far away.

sanskrit: ūru akṣi bāhavaḥ mahyam sphuranti aṅga punaḥ punaḥ vepathuḥ ca api hṛdaye ārāt dāsyanti vipriyam
reference: The left side of my body — my thighs, arms and eyes — are all quivering again and again. I am having heart palpitations due to fear. All this indicates undesirable happenings.
baseline: The arms arms and limbs of the king are made to swell in me. The body and the heart are given to me by the goddess Aāra.
morphology: The arms arms and arms of the āuṇu are made to swell with me. The limbs and the vetas are given to me again and again.

sanskrit: śivā eṣā udyantam ādityam abhi rauti anala ānanā mām aṅga sārameyaḥ ayam abhirebhati abhīru vat
reference: Just see, O Bhīma, how the she-jackal cries at the rising sun and vomits fire, and how the dog barks at me fearlessly.
baseline: O Śiva this is the beginning and the end of the universe. O Anāṇa one who gives me the organs and the essence of the world.
morphology: O Śiva this is the beginning and the end of the universe. O Anāṇa one who gives me the essence of the body one should worship it.

sanskrit: śastāḥ kurvanti mām savyam dakṣiṇam paśavaḥ apare vāhān ca puruṣa vyāghra lakṣaye rudataḥ mama
reference: O Bhīmasena, tiger amongst men, now useful animals like cows are passing me on my left side, and lower animals like the asses are circumambulating me. My horses appear to weep upon seeing me.
baseline: A man should make a tiger cry at the goal of me. The animals should be sent to the right and the horses to the left. The tiger cries at the target.
morphology: The six men are doing me the right hand the animals the other hand and the horses. The men are crying at the target of the tiger.

sanskrit: mṛtyu dūtaḥ kapotaḥ ayam ulūkaḥ kampayan manaḥ pratyulūkaḥ ca kuhvānaiḥ viśvam vai śūnyam icchataḥ
reference: Just see! This pigeon is like a messenger of death. The shrieks of the owls and their rival crows make my heart tremble. It appears that they want to make a void of the whole universe.
baseline: The angel of death the dove the rat the mole the heart the sponge the khuva the world and the world are empty.
morphology: The angel of death the dove the rat the mole the mind every mole and the universe are empty.

sanskrit: dhūmrāḥ diśaḥ paridhayaḥ kampate bhūḥ saha adribhiḥ nirghātaḥ ca mahān tāta sākam ca stanayitnubhiḥ
reference: Just see how the smoke encircles the sky. It appears that the earth and mountains are throbbing. Just hear the cloudless thunder and see the bolts from the blue.
baseline: The direction of the smoke and the circumference of the earth trembling with the force of the fire should be great. Then the body should be covered with a large amount of water and the breasts should be shaken with it.
morphology: The direction of the smoke and the circumference of the earth trembling with the force of the wind are great. Then they should be covered with a lotus and their breasts should be shaken.

sanskrit: vāyuḥ vāti khara sparśaḥ rajasā visṛjan tamaḥ asṛk varṣanti jaladāḥ bībhatsam iva sarvataḥ
reference: The wind blows violently, blasting dust everywhere and creating darkness. Clouds are raining everywhere with bloody disasters.
baseline: The wind the door the mouth the touch the water the rain and the water are like a beast.
morphology: The wind the door the mouth and the touch of the razor and the water of the river are like a beast.

sanskrit: sūryam hata prabham paśya graha mardam mithaḥ divi sa saṅkulaiḥ bhūta gaṇaiḥ jvalite iva rodasī
reference: The rays of the sun are declining, and the stars appear to be fighting amongst themselves. Confused living entities appear to be ablaze and weeping.
baseline: The sun is killed the lord is seen the planet is dead the goddess is illusory the sun is like burning with the compasses of ghosts.
morphology: The sun should be killed and the lord should be seen. The planets should be destroyed. The goddess should be lit with the garlands and the ghosts.

sanskrit: nadyaḥ nadāḥ ca kṣubhitāḥ sarāṁsi ca manāṁsi ca na jvalati agniḥ ājyena kālaḥ ayam kim vidhāsyati
reference: Rivers, tributaries, ponds, reservoirs and the mind are all perturbed. Butter no longer ignites fire. What is this extraordinary time? What is going to happen?
baseline: The rivers rivers rivulets rivers etc. are not able to be destroyed by the fire. What is the punishment for this.
morphology: The rivers rivers rivulets rivers etc. are not able to be destroyed by the fire. What will happen if the fire does not get burnt.

sanskrit: na pibanti stanam vatsāḥ na duhyanti ca mātaraḥ rudanti aśru mukhāḥ gāvaḥ na hṛṣyanti ṛṣabhāḥ vraje
reference: The calves do not suck the teats of the cows, nor do the cows give milk. They are standing, crying, tears in their eyes, and the bulls take no pleasure in the pasturing grounds.
baseline: The breasts are not to be drunk the mother is to be weeped over the breasts and breasts do not suffer the mouth of a cow does not suffer from tears and the head of the cow is not destroyed.
morphology: The breasts are not drunk the mother is not suffering from the disease and the mother cries and the cow is not killed.

sanskrit: daivatāni rudanti iva svidyanti hi uccalanti ca ime jana padāḥ grāmāḥ pura udyāna ākara āśramāḥ bhraṣṭa śriyaḥ nirānandāḥ kim agham darśayanti naḥ
reference: The Deities seem to be crying in the temple, lamenting and perspiring. They seem about to leave. All the cities, villages, towns, gardens, mines and hermitages are now devoid of beauty and bereft of all happiness. I do not know what sort of calamities are now awaiting us.
baseline: The gods are heard crying and the feet of the people are raised. The villages towns cities gardens inns sanctuaries houses houses etc. are corrupt. The devotees of the gods are not known to be happy.
morphology: The gods are heard crying as if they are standing on the ground. These people are the steps the villages the cities the gardens the houses and the sanctuaries. They are corrupt and do not show the happiness of the devotees.

sanskrit: manye etaiḥ mahā utpātaiḥ nūnam bhagavataḥ padaiḥ ananya puruṣa śrībhiḥ hīnā bhūḥ hata saubhagā
reference: I think that all these earthly disturbances indicate some greater loss to the good fortune of the world. The world was fortunate to have been marked with the footprints of the lotus feet of the Lord. These signs indicate that this will no longer be.
baseline: O lord of the universe the king should be worshipped with these great gifts. The king should not be killed by the king of the king. He should be killed with the help of the god.
morphology: O lord of the universe the king should be worshipped with these great gifts. The king should not be killed by the king of the king.

sanskrit: iti cintayataḥ tasya dṛṣṭā ariṣṭena cetasā rājñaḥ prati āgamat brahman yadu puryāḥ kapi dhvajaḥ
reference: O Brāhmaṇa Śaunaka, while Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira, observing the inauspicious signs on the earth at that time, was thus thinking to himself, Arjuna came back from the city of the Yadus [Dvārakā].
baseline: Having thought about this the king came to him with the conscious thought of the king with the image of Arīṣta. The flag should be a copy of the Purāṇa flag.
morphology: Having thought about this the king should come to Brahman and the king with a conscious heart with the image of Arishta.

sanskrit: tam pādayoḥ nipatitam ayathā pūrvam āturam adhaḥ vadanam ap bindūn sṛjantam nayana abjayoḥ
reference: When he bowed at his feet, the King saw that his dejection was unprecedented. His head was down, and tears glided from his lotus eyes.
baseline: He should be thrown down on his feet. He should bow down on the ground in the east and raise up the dots.
morphology: He should be thrown down on his feet. He should bow down on the ground in the east with his hands and eyes.

sanskrit: vilokya udvigna hṛdayaḥ vicchāyam anujam nṛpaḥ pṛcchati sma suhṛt madhye saṁsmaran nārada īritam
reference: Seeing Arjuna pale due to heartfelt anxieties, the King, remembering the indications of the sage Nārada, questioned him in the midst of friends.
baseline: Having seen the heart getting agitated the king asked the younger brother to do the same in the midst of the merriment. Narada said that he would do it.
morphology: Having seen the heart getting irritated one should ask the younger brother to do the same in the midst of the merriment.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiraḥ uvāca kaccit ānarta puryām naḥ sva janāḥ sukham āsate madhu bhoja daśārha arha sātvata andhaka vṛṣṇayaḥ
reference: Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira said: My dear brother, please tell me whether our friends and relatives, such as Madhu, Bhoja, Daśārha, Ārha, Sātvata, Andhaka and the members of the Yadu family are all passing their days in happiness.
baseline: Yudhishthira said that one should not make his own people happy by saying that a blind man should eat honey and drink water.
morphology: Yudhishthira said that the king should not be afraid of the evil gods. He should not make his people happy and enjoy honey and eat food. The king should be able to do so. The god Vrṣṇu should be blind.

sanskrit: śūraḥ mātāmahaḥ kaccit svasti āste vā atha māriṣaḥ mātulaḥ sa anujaḥ kaccit kuśalī ānaka dundubhiḥ
reference: Is my respectable grandfather Śūrasena in a happy mood? And are my maternal uncle Vasudeva and his younger brothers all doing well?
baseline: The son of a nobleman should be the son of his maternal uncle. The son son daughter uncle uncle and uncle should be of the same age.
morphology: One who is brave and has a mother mother uncle or self or one who has a maternal uncle a younger brother a skillful man or an evil person should be punished.

sanskrit: sapta sva sāraḥ tat patnyaḥ mātulānyaḥ saha ātma jāḥ āsate sasnuṣāḥ kṣemam devakī pramukhāḥ svayam
reference: His seven wives, headed by Devakī, are all sisters. Are they and their sons and daughters-in-law all happy?
baseline: The seven elements of the self should be accompanied by the wives and maternal uncles. The chief deities should be the sons of the gods.
morphology: The seven elements of the self should be accompanied by the wives and maternal uncles. The chief deities should be the sons of the mother and the chief of the gods themselves.

sanskrit: kaccit rājā āhukaḥ jīvati asat putraḥ asya ca anujaḥ hṛdīkaḥ sa sutaḥ akrūraḥ jayanta gada sāraṇāḥ āsate kuśalam kaccit ye ca śatrujit ādayaḥ kaccit āste sukham rāmaḥ bhagavān sātvatām prabhuḥ
reference: Are Ugrasena, whose son was the mischievous Kaṁsa, and his younger brother still living? Are Hṛdīka and his son Kṛtavarmā happy? Are Akrūra, Jayanta, Gada, Sāraṇa and Śatrujit all happy? How is Balarāma, the Personality of Godhead and the protector of devotees?
baseline: A king who is a kaccha is alive. A son who is the younger brother of the king a hridika is born to him. He who is born as a kāccha jayanta gada saraṇa akusala kutcha kuta kucha kuti kruta jitu adyaka is happy rāma lord of seven gods.
morphology: A king who is a kutcha ahoka a living man a son a younger brother a hearty one a sutta akrūr jayanta gada sāraṇas kusalā kutta and a king who has conquered enemies a lord of seven gods is said to be happy.

sanskrit: pradyumnaḥ sarva vṛṣṇīnām sukham āste mahā rathaḥ gambhīra rayaḥ aniruddhaḥ vardhate bhagavān uta
reference: How is Pradyumna, the great general of the Vṛṣṇi family? Is He happy? And is Aniruddha, the plenary expansion of the Personality of Godhead, faring well?
baseline: The lord Pradyumna should be pleased with all the vrishṇis. The great chariot should be of a serious nature. Aniruddha should be magnified.
morphology: The lord Pradyumna should be pleased with all the vrishṇis. The great chariot should be of a serious nature. The king Aniruddha should be blessed.

sanskrit: suṣeṇaḥ cārudeṣṇaḥ ca sāmbaḥ jāmbavatī sutaḥ anye ca kārṣṇi pravarāḥ sa putrāḥ ṛṣabha ādayaḥ
reference: Are all the chieftain sons of Lord Kṛṣṇa, such as Suṣeṇa, Cārudeṣṇa, Sāmba the son of Jāmbavatī, and Ṛṣabha, along with their sons, all doing well?
baseline: The sons of Sūsena Charudeshna Samba Jambavati Sutā others are the sons of Kārśṇī. The sons are named Rishabha.
morphology: The son of Sūsena Charudeshna Samba Jambavati Suta and others are the sons of Kārśṇī.

sanskrit: tathā eva anucarāḥ śaureḥ śrutadeva uddhava ādayaḥ sunanda nanda śīrṣaṇyāḥ ye ca anye sātvata ṛṣabhāḥ api svasti āsate sarve rāma kṛṣṇa bhuja āśrayāḥ api smaranti kuśalam asmākam baddha sauhṛdāḥ
reference: Also, Śrutadeva, Uddhava and others, Nanda, Sunanda and other leaders of liberated souls who are constant companions of the Lord are protected by Lord Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa. Are they all doing well in their respective functions? Do they, who are all eternally bound in friendship with us, remember our welfare?
baseline: In the same way those who follow the lord and listen to him those who rise up from the sun who rise from the top who fall from the head and those who fall down from the seat of the sage who come from the side of the king all those who seek the shelter of Lord Krishna and others also remember us.
morphology: In the same way those who follow the lord and listen to him those who rise up from the sun who rise from the top who fall from the head and those who fall down from the seat of the sage should remember all those who come and worship Lord Rama Krishna and Bhuj.

sanskrit: bhagavān api govindaḥ brahmaṇyaḥ bhakta vatsalaḥ kaccit pure sudharmāyām sukham āste suhṛt vṛtaḥ
reference: Is Lord Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who gives pleasure to the cows, the senses and the brāhmaṇas, who is very affectionate towards His devotees, enjoying the pious assembly at Dvārakā Purī surrounded by friends?
baseline: One who is a devotee of the gods Govinda Brahman Vatsala and others would get happiness in good deeds.
morphology: One who is a devotee of the god Govinda Brahman Vatsalā and others would get happiness and happiness by doing good.

sanskrit: maṅgalāya ca lokānām kṣemāya ca bhavāya ca āste yadu kula ambhodhau ādyaḥ ananta sakhaḥ pumān yat bāhu daṇḍa guptāyām sva puryām yadavaḥ arcitāḥ krīḍanti parama ānandam mahā pauruṣikāḥ iva
reference: The original Personality of Godhead, the enjoyer, and Balarāma, the primeval Lord Ananta, are staying in the ocean of the Yadu dynasty for the welfare, protection and general progress of the entire universe. And the members of the Yadu dynasty, being protected by the arms of the Lord, are enjoying life like the residents of the spiritual sky.
baseline: One who is pleased with the welfare of the people and for the well being of the country one who is blessed by the family one with an eternal happiness and one who plays with the arms of the pūmā in the secret place of the priest and the worshippers who play with the supreme bliss is like the great men.
morphology: One who is blessed with good things and good things for the welfare of the people one who is born with a great family and who has an eternal happiness and who plays with the hands and hands of the pūmās in the secret place and who is worshipped by the priests should enjoy the supreme bliss as if they were great men.

sanskrit: yat pāda śuśrūṣaṇa mukhya karmaṇā satya ādayaḥ dvi aṣṭa sahasra yoṣitaḥ nirjitya saṅkhye tri daśān tat āśiṣaḥ haranti vajra āyudha vallabhā ucitāḥ
reference: Simply by administering comforts at the lotus feet of the Lord, which is the most important of all services, the queens at Dvārakā, headed by Satyabhāmā, induced the Lord to conquer the demigods. Thus the queens enjoy things which are prerogatives of the wives of the controller of thunderbolts.
baseline: The first two thousand women should be set free and the number of ten should be divided into three parts. Those who have served the feet and performed the main deeds should be given the gift of the diamond weapons.
morphology: The chief karmās who serve the feet are true. Eight thousand women are victorious. Those who do not do so are blessed with three tenths of the number. The weapons of the vajra and the vālabhā are given to them.

sanskrit: yat bāhu daṇḍa abhyudaya anujīvinaḥ yadu pravīrāḥ hi akutobhayāḥ muhuḥ adhikramanti aṅghribhiḥ āhṛtām balāt sabhām sudharmām sura sat tama ucitām
reference: The great heroes of the Yadu dynasty, being protected by the arms of Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, always remain fearless in every respect. And therefore their feet trample over the Sudharmā assembly house, which the best demigods deserved but which was taken away from them.
baseline: One who has won the battle with the force of the enemy would be able to overcome the misfortune of the enemies. One who gains the power of the opposition would be better off.
morphology: One who has won the battle with the force of the enemy should be punished with a fine of one hundred rupees. Those who have conquered the enemy would be better off with the same amount of force.

sanskrit: kaccit te anāmayam tāta bhraṣṭa tejāḥ vibhāsi me alabdha mānaḥ avajñātaḥ kim vā tāta ciroṣitaḥ
reference: My brother Arjuna, please tell me whether your health is all right. You appear to have lost your bodily luster. Is this due to others disrespecting and neglecting you because of your long stay at Dvārakā?
baseline: If they are not good enough they should be destroyed. If they do not get good good good things then they should not be destroyed and their honour should be taken care of.
morphology: If they are found to be unclean then they should be divided into corrupt elements. If they do not understand me whether they have been defrauded or not.

sanskrit: kaccit na abhihataḥ abhāvaiḥ śabda ādibhiḥ amaṅgalaiḥ na dattam uktam arthibhyaḥ āśayā yat pratiśrutam
reference: Has someone addressed you with unfriendly words or threatened you? Could you not give charity to one who asked, or could you not keep your promise to someone?
baseline: The words given by the forefathers and the members of the unbelievers are said to be good and not to be evil. It is said to have been promised by the means of hope.
morphology: The words given to the poor in the beginning and the members of the poor should not be said to be true. The words promised to the needy should not have been said to have been given by the poor.

sanskrit: kaccit tvam brāhmaṇam bālam gām vṛddham rogiṇam striyam śaraṇa upasṛtam sattvam na atyākṣīḥ śaraṇa pradaḥ
reference: You are always the protector of the deserving living beings, such as brāhmaṇas, children, cows, women and the diseased. Could you not give them protection when they approached you for shelter?
baseline: A brahmin a boy an old man a sick woman a noble person should take refuge. A tyrant should not seek refuge.
morphology: A brahmin a boy an old man a sick woman a woman should take refuge. A sattva a tyrant and not a cow should be given refuge.

sanskrit: kaccit tvam na agamaḥ agamyām gamyām vā asat kṛtām striyam parājitaḥ vā atha bhavān na uttamaiḥ na asamaiḥ pathi
reference: Have you contacted a woman of impeachable character, or have you not properly treated a deserving woman? Or have you been defeated on the way by someone who is inferior or equal to you?
baseline: A woman who has not come or gone or has not done so or has been defeated will neither be good nor will she be able to pass through the country.
morphology: A woman who has not come or gone or has not done so should be defeated. You are neither good nor good.

sanskrit: api svit parya bhuṅkthāḥ tvam sambhojyān vṛddha bālakān jugupsitam karma kiñcit kṛtavān na yat akṣamam
reference: Have you not taken care of old men and boys who deserve to dine with you? Have you left them and taken your meals alone? Have you committed some unpardonable mistake which is considered to be abominable?
baseline: O king of the world thou hast not done any work which would have been impossible for the old boys who had been seduced by you.
morphology: You have done nothing to please the old boys who have been seduced by the sound of the bhuṇkha.

sanskrit: kaccit preṣṭha tamena atha hṛdayena ātma bandhunā śūnyaḥ asmi rahitaḥ nityam manyase te anyathā na ruk
reference: Or is it that you are feeling empty for all time because you might have lost your most intimate friend, Lord Kṛṣṇa? O my brother Arjuna, I can think of no other reason for your becoming so dejected.
baseline: Having said this one should not repeat the same thing with the heart self kinsman friend friend and friend. He should always be considered as free.
morphology: One who has left the body with the heart and the soul with the relatives would be free from it. He would not be able to do so without it.

sanskrit: sūtaḥ uvāca evam kṛṣṇa sakhaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ bhrātrā rājñā vikalpitaḥ nānā śaṅka āspadam rūpam kṛṣṇa viśleṣa karśitaḥ
reference: Sūta Gosvāmī said: Arjuna, the celebrated friend of Lord Kṛṣṇa, was griefstricken because of his strong feeling of separation from Kṛṣṇa, over and above all Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira’s speculative inquiries.
baseline: Then the king should be called kṛṣṇa the brother the son of krṣṇā the king and the king. He should be made to understand the various aspects of the form.
morphology: Then the king should be called kṛṣṇa the brother the son of krīṣna the king and the king.

sanskrit: śokena śuṣyat vadana hṛt sarojaḥ hata prabhaḥ vibhum tam eva anusmaran na aśaknot pratibhāṣitum
reference: Due to grief, Arjuna’s mouth and lotuslike heart had dried up. Therefore his body lost all luster. Now, remembering the Supreme Lord, he could hardly utter a word in reply.
baseline: The heart of Saroja should be washed away with sorrow and the lord should be killed. He would not be able to destroy them.
morphology: The heart of Saroja should be washed away with sorrow. The Lord should be killed by the enemy. He should not be able to destroy them.

sanskrit: kṛcchreṇa saṁstabhya śucaḥ pāṇinā āmṛjya netrayoḥ parokṣeṇa samunnaddha praṇaya autkaṇṭhya kātaraḥ
reference: With great difficulty he checked the tears of grief that smeared his eyes. He was very distressed because Lord Kṛṣṇa was out of his sight, and he increasingly felt affection for Him.
baseline: Having said this with the penitentiary one should draw the penis with the eye and then raise the head with the prāṇa.
morphology: Having said this with the penitentiary one should draw the penis with the eye and then raise the head with the forehead.

sanskrit: sakhyam maitrīm sauhṛdam ca sārathya ādiṣu saṁsmaran nṛpam agrajam iti āha bāṣpa gadgadayā girā
reference: Remembering Lord Kṛṣṇa and His well wishes, benefactions, intimate familial relations and His chariot driving, Arjuna, overwhelmed and breathing very heavily, began to speak.
baseline: Having established friendship friendship alliance friendship etc. in the beginning one should say Nripa Agrajāma aha vapāda gādaḍa.
morphology: Having established friendship friendship alliance friendship etc. in the beginning one should say  O Nriṣṇu the elder.

sanskrit: arjunaḥ uvāca vañcitaḥ aham mahā rāja hariṇā bandhu rūpiṇā yena me apahṛtam tejaḥ deva vismāpanam mahat
reference: Arjuna said: O King! The Supreme Personality of Godhead, Hari, who treated me exactly like an intimate friend, has left me alone. Thus my astounding power, which astonished even the demigods, is no longer with me.
baseline: Arjuna said that I am a great king. Hari is a friend and Rupina is a great god.
morphology: Arjuna said that he had deceived the great king Hari his friend Rupina who had taken away the glory of the gods.

sanskrit: yasya kṣaṇa viyogena lokaḥ hi apriya darśanaḥ ukthena rahitaḥ hi eṣaḥ mṛtakaḥ procyate yathā
reference: I have just lost Him whose separation for a moment would render all the universes unfavorable and void, like bodies without life.
baseline: A person who dies after having lost his life is said to have lost his sight of the world.
morphology: One who has lost his soul for a while is said to be dead.

sanskrit: yat saṁśrayāt drupada geham upāgatānām rājñām svayaṁvara mukhe smara durmadānām tejaḥ hṛtam khalu mayā abhihataḥ ca matsyaḥ sajjī kṛtena dhanuṣā adhigatā ca kṛṣṇā
reference: Only by His merciful strength was I able to vanquish all the lusty princes assembled at the palace of King Drupada for the selection of the bridegroom. With my bow and arrow I could pierce the fish target and thereby gain the hand of Draupadī.
baseline: The king should be remembered by the mouth of the king who has come to me with the help of the sahyāśa. He should be killed by me. The fish should be prepared and the money should be acquired by Krishna.
morphology: The king should be remembered by the mouth of the king as having been benefited by the recitation of the hymn drupa gā which is said to have destroyed the glory of the evil gift. The fish prepared by me should be destroyed and the money acquired by me from him should be collected.

sanskrit: yat sannidhau aham u khāṇḍavam agnaye adām indram ca sa amara gaṇam tarasā vijitya labdhā sabhā maya kṛtā adbhuta śilpa māyā digbhyaḥ aharan nṛpatayaḥ balim adhvare te
reference: Because He was near me, it was possible for me to conquer with great dexterity the powerful King of heaven, Indradeva, along with his demigod associates and thus enable the fire-god to devastate the Khāṇḍava Forest. And only by His grace was the demon named Maya saved from the blazing Khāṇḍava Forest, and thus we could build our assembly house of wonderful architectural workmanship, where all the princes assembled during the performance of Rājasūya-yajña and paid you tributes.
baseline: Having conquered the immortal group of gods in the presence of which I am the pillar of fire Indra and others are worshipped. Having conquered that great group of people the king of the king should offer sacrifices to the gods.
morphology: One who has conquered the immortal race of Indra by setting him on fire in front of the pit of which he is standing should offer a sacrifice to the king of the king. He should be worshipped by the king after having made a magnificent sculpture of him and having won the battle.

sanskrit: yat tejasā nṛpa śiraḥ aṅghrim ahan makha artham āryaḥ anujaḥ tava gaja ayuta sattva vīryaḥ tena āhṛtāḥ pramatha nātha makhāya bhūpāḥ yat mocitāḥ tat anayan balim adhvare te
reference: Your respectable younger brother, who possesses the strength of ten thousand elephants, killed, by His grace, Jarāsandha, whose feet were worshiped by many kings. These kings had been brought for sacrifice in Jarāsandha’s Mahābhairava-yajña, but they were thus released. Later they paid tribute to Your Majesty.
baseline: The head of the king of the kingdom that is bright that which is unbroken that of the son of arya that is the head of ahāna that means that which has been made of the elephant that has been given to the king that that which was given to him by the king and that which had been liberated from the earth.
morphology: The head of the king of the kingdom that is the fiercest the head of that which is called āhāṇ the body of that king the spirit of the lord of the country the animal of the great king that is called ahṇa that means ahāna ahaṇ ahān ayah aya anja the elephant sātva semen that has been eaten by him that which has been released by the lord nātha mākhā and the earth.

sanskrit: patnyāḥ tava adhimakha kḷpta mahā abhiṣeka ślāghiṣṭha cāru kabaram kitavaiḥ sabhāyām spṛṣṭam vikīrya padayoḥ patita aśru mukhyāḥ yaḥ tat striyaḥ akṛta hata īśa vimukta keśāḥ
reference: It was He only who loosened the hair of all the wives of the miscreants who dared open the cluster of your Queen’s hair, which had been nicely dressed and sanctified for the great Rājasūya sacrificial ceremony. At that time she fell down at the feet of Lord Kṛṣṇa with tears in her eyes.
baseline: The chief of the women who fell down on the steps after having touched the grave four times and the head of the body with the words of the wife and the upper face of the head the great anointing and boasting of the great abode of the four should be done.
morphology: The head of the wife should be covered with the hair of your master. The head should be made to shed tears after touching the grave and the feet of the chief minister. The woman should be removed and killed by the king.

sanskrit: yaḥ naḥ jugopa vane etya duranta kṛcchrāt durvāsasaḥ ari racitāt ayuta agra bhuk yaḥ śāka anna śiṣṭam upayujya yataḥ tri lokīm tṛptām amaṁsta salile vinimagna saṅghaḥ
reference: During our exile, Durvāsā Muni, who eats with his ten thousand disciples, intrigued with our enemies to put us in dangerous trouble. At that time He [Lord Kṛṣṇa], simply by accepting the remnants of food, saved us. By His accepting food thus, the assembly of munis, while bathing in the river, felt sumptuously fed. And all the three worlds were also satisfied.
baseline: One who does not go into the forest of jugaṇa and after having prepared the rice with the help of the arduous fire one who has eaten vegetables grains etc. should be prepared with the advice of the chief minister. One who is not satisfied with the three things would be reduced to the union of the sālilas.
morphology: One who does not go into the wilderness and after having prepared arri with the arrhythmias of the abyss of misfortune and misery would become a member of the group. One who consumes vegetables grains etc. would be satisfied by the three people.

sanskrit: yat tejasā atha bhagavān yudhi śūla pāṇiḥ vismāpitaḥ sa girijaḥ astram adāt nijam me anye api ca aham amunā eva kalevareṇa prāptaḥ mahā indra bhavane mahat āsana ardham
reference: It was by His influence only that in a fight I was able to astonish the personality of god Lord Śiva and his wife, the daughter of Mount Himālaya. Thus he [Lord Śiva] became pleased with me and awarded me his own weapon. Other demigods also delivered their respective weapons to me, and in addition I was able to reach the heavenly planets in this present body and was allowed a half-elevated seat.
baseline: One who has given the weapon to the king of the hill who is a mighty warrior who has spread the waters of the bull and who has got the weapon of the other. One who gets a great seat in the house of Indra by the same art as Amu gets half of the seat.
morphology: The one who has given the weapon to the king of the hill who is a fiery warrior who has spread the waters of the sword and who has got the great seat in the house of Indra half of the seat is obtained by me.

sanskrit: tatra eva me viharataḥ bhuja daṇḍa yugmam gāṇḍīva lakṣaṇam arāti vadhāya devāḥ sa indrāḥ śritāḥ yat anubhāvitam ājamīḍha tena aham adya muṣitaḥ puruṣeṇa bhūmnā
reference: When I stayed for some days as a guest in the heavenly planets, all the heavenly demigods, including King Indradeva, took shelter of my arms, which were marked with the Gāṇḍīva bow, to kill the demon named Nivātakavaca. O King, descendant of Ajamīḍha, at the present moment I am bereft of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, by whose influence I was so powerful.
baseline: There I shall sit down and make a pair of bhujas dandas gandis and the gods of the earth fall into the sea. Having heard that Indra was killed by the gods I should be ashamed of the fact that I am alive today.
morphology: Then the gods of the kingdom of Indra heard that I should be killed by a man who has been killed by the king of the country by a pair of bhujas dandas and rhinoceros.

sanskrit: yat bāndhavaḥ kuru bala abdhim ananta pāram ekaḥ rathena tatare aham atīrya sattvam pratyāhṛtam bahu dhanam ca mayā pareṣām tejāḥ padam maṇi mayam ca hṛtam śirobhyaḥ
reference: The military strength of the Kauravas was like an ocean in which there dwelled many invincible existences, and thus it was insurmountable. But because of His friendship, I, seated on the chariot, was able to cross over it. And only by His grace was I able to regain the cows and also collect by force many helmets of the kings, which were bedecked with jewels that were sources of all brilliance.
baseline: If any of the friends do the same with the strength of the chariot beyond the limit of infinity one of them should take away the power of the other. I have lost many things and the position of gold and gold.
morphology: The friends who do so are bound to the limit of the strength of the enemy. I have taken away the power of the king by a chariot and much wealth. I lost the position and money of the chieftains.

sanskrit: yaḥ bhīṣma karṇa guru śalya camūṣu adabhra rājanya varya ratha maṇḍala maṇḍitāsu agecaraḥ mama vibho ratha yūtha pānām āyuḥ manāṁsi ca dṛśā sahaḥ ojaḥ ārcchat
reference: It was He only who withdrew the duration of life from everyone and who, in the battlefield, withdrew the speculative power and strength of enthusiasm from the great military phalanx made by the Kauravas, headed by Bhīṣma, Karṇa, Droṇa, Śalya, etc. Their arrangement was expert and more than adequate, but He [Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa], while going forward, did all this.
baseline: The one who worships Bhīṣma Karna the master Sālya and the king and then the chariot the chars the circle and the chords of the king should be worshipped together with the vision the spirit the mind and the life of the young man.
morphology: One who worships Bhīṣma Karna Śālya the king of the chariots and the king in the army and who is worshipped by the king as the king and the charyas of the king one who is the preceptor of my vivhava chariot youth drink life and mind should be worshipped along with the vision.

sanskrit: yat doḥṣu mā praṇihitam guru bhīṣma karṇa naptṛ trigarta śalya saindhava bāhlika ādyaiḥ astrāṇi amogha mahimāni nirūpitāni na upaspṛśuḥ nṛhari dāsam iva asurāṇi
reference: Great generals like Bhīṣma, Droṇa, Karṇa, Bhūriśravā, Suśarmā, Śalya, Jayadratha and Bāhlika all directed their invincible weapons against me. But by His [Lord Kṛṣṇa’s] grace they could not even touch a hair on my head. Similarly, Prahlāda Mahārāja, the supreme devotee of Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva, was unaffected by the weapons the demons used against him.
baseline: One who does not engage in the acts of the god Bhīṣma Karna the master the knower the king the three horses the bull the mace the elephant the lion the bearer the cow the archers the great men the noble men and the servants of the king are not described as having the power to destroy the enemies.
morphology: One who does not engage in the acts of the god Bhīṣma Karna the master the king of the three horses the sālikas sāndhavas the sons of Bahlikā the first ones the weapons the great men the subconscious and the servants of the gods the demons the gods and goddesses are not described as having the power.

sanskrit: sautye vṛtaḥ kumatinā ātma daḥ īśvaraḥ me yat pāda padmam abhavāya bhajanti bhavyāḥ mām śrānta vāham arayaḥ rathinaḥ bhuvi ṣṭham na prāharan yat anubhāva nirasta cittāḥ
reference: It was by His mercy only that my enemies neglected to kill me when I descended from my chariot to get water for my thirsty horses. And it was due to my lack of esteem for my Lord that I dared engage Him as my chariot driver, for He is worshiped and offered services by the best men to attain salvation.
baseline: The feet of the god Śivāṇa which are not in the form of lotus should be placed on the right side of the earth. The feet which are in the absence of lotuses should be worshipped by the lord. The chariots of the king and the chariot should not be carried away by the mind.
morphology: The feet of the god Śivāṇu which are falling on the south and the soul falling on it should be worshipped in the absence of the lotus. You should not be afraid of me. The chariots of the king and the earth should be carried away by the mind which has not been able to bear the feelings.

sanskrit: narmāṇi udāra rucira smita śobhitāni he pārtha he arjuna sakhe kuru nandana iti sañjalpitāni nara deva hṛdi spṛśāni smartuḥ luṭhanti hṛdayam mama mādhavasya
reference: O King! His jokings and frank talks were pleasing and beautifully decorated with smiles. His addresses unto me as “O son of Pṛthā, O friend, O son of the Kuru dynasty,” and all such heartiness are now remembered by me, and thus I am overwhelmed.
baseline: O Partha O Arjuna the meritorious one the gentle one who adorns the heart with a generous liking the male one who touches the heart of the gods and the smarter one who plunders my heart and my mothers heart is called Nandana.
morphology: O Partha O Arjuna who is blessed with the gift of goodness good taste good fortune good conduct and good conduct the gods of men gods hearts senses and spirits of the mind and the heart of my mother are plundered by the smarthus.

sanskrit: śayya āsana aṭana vikatthana bhojana ādiṣu aikyāt vayasya ṛtavān iti vipralabdhaḥ sakhyuḥ sakhā iva pitṛvat tanayasya sarvam sehe mahān mahitayā kumateḥ agham me
reference: Generally both of us used to live together and sleep, sit and loiter together. And at the time of advertising oneself for acts of chivalry, sometimes, if there were any irregularity, I used to reproach Him by saying, “My friend, You are very truthful.” Even in those hours when His value was minimized, He, being the Supreme Soul, used to tolerate all those utterings of mine, excusing me exactly as a true friend excuses his true friend, or a father excuses his son.
baseline: Having sold the seat of the bed the seat and the food should be prepared in the beginning and the old man should be given the gift of the wife. He should be like a friend and father to the mother. The king should offer all the gifts of the mother and son.
morphology: Having sold the seat and having bought food together with the old man one should say that he would get the gift of a friend as well as his father.

sanskrit: saḥ aham nṛpa indra rahitaḥ puruṣa uttamena sakhyā priyeṇa suhṛdā hṛdayena śūnyaḥ adhvani urukrama parigraham aṅga rakṣan gopaiḥ asadbhiḥ abalā iva vinirjitaḥ asmi
reference: O Emperor, now I am separated from my friend and dearmost well-wisher, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and therefore my heart appears to be void of everything. In His absence I have been defeated by a number of infidel cowherd men while I was guarding the bodies of all the wives of Kṛṣṇa.
baseline: He is the one who is not the master of Indra the man who is good to me the friend the lover the heart the enemy the enemies the body the members of the body and the body.
morphology: He should be a good man without the presence of Indra a friend with a good heart and a friend who is empty from the heart a member of the lower body and the body of the body should be kept in a circle.

sanskrit: tat vai dhanuḥ te iṣavaḥ saḥ rathaḥ hayāḥ te saḥ aham rathī nṛpatayaḥ yataḥ ānamanti sarvam kṣaṇena tat abhūt asat īśa riktam bhasman hutam kuhaka rāddham iva uptam ūṣyām
reference: I have the very same Gāṇḍīva bow, the same arrows, the same chariot drawn by the same horses, and I use them as the same Arjuna to whom all the kings offered their due respects. But in the absence of Lord Kṛṣṇa, all of them, at a moment’s notice, have become null and void. It is exactly like offering clarified butter on ashes, accumulating money with a magic wand or sowing seeds on barren land.
baseline: The same bow the same chariot the other chariots the king the captain the charioteer and the king of the king. The king would be destroyed by the fire. He would be burnt empty and burnt in the fire as if he were a cow.
morphology: The same bows the bows and the chariots are the same. They should be the same as that of the king. They are the king of the charyas. The king should be ashamed of everything. He should be burnt empty and burnt as if he were a cow.

sanskrit: rājan tvayā anupṛṣṭānām suhṛdām naḥ suhṛt pure vipra śāpa vimūḍhānām nighnatām muṣṭibhiḥ mithaḥ vāruṇīm madirām pītvā mada unmathita cetasām ajānatām iva anyonyam catuḥ pañca avaśeṣitāḥ
reference: O King, since you have asked me about our friends and relatives in the city of Dvārakā, I will inform you that all of them were cursed by the brāhmaṇas, and as a result they all became intoxicated with wine made of putrefied rice and fought among themselves with sticks, not even recognizing one another. Now all but four or five of them are dead and gone.
