baseline: The king should not be able to bear the misfortune of the fools and the curse of the king. Having drunk wine with his fists the king should be able not to know the illusion of the senses. Five others were left as if they were in a state of panic.
morphology: The king should not be able to remove the curse of fools and foolish people by making them drink wine with his fists. Having drunk wine the king should know that four or five others are left in the midst of each other.

sanskrit: prāyeṇa etat bhagavataḥ īśvarasya viceṣṭitam mithaḥ nighnanti bhūtāni bhāvayanti ca yat mithaḥ
reference: Factually this is all due to the supreme will of the Lord, the Personality of Godhead. Sometimes people kill one another, and at other times they protect one another.
baseline: The illusion of God and the evil of God is often said to be false. The illusions of ghosts are believed to be true.
morphology: The illusion of God and the evil spirits of God would be removed by the ancient gods.

sanskrit: jalaukasām jale yadvat mahāntaḥ adanti aṇīyasaḥ durbalān balinaḥ rājan mahāntaḥ balinaḥ mithaḥ evam baliṣṭhaiḥ yadubhiḥ mahadbhiḥ itarān vibhuḥ yadūn yadubhiḥ anyonyam bhū bhārān sañjahāra ha
reference: O King, as in the ocean the bigger and stronger aquatics swallow up the smaller and weaker ones, so also the Supreme Personality of Godhead, to lighten the burden of the earth, has engaged the stronger Yadu to kill the weaker, and the bigger Yadu to kill the smaller.
baseline: The king who sacrifices the weak ones with the water of the jalauksa and gives it to the great ones would be able to bear the burdens of the mighty ones.
morphology: The king who sacrifices the weak among the poor and the great among the people should be given a jalokasa in the water. The king should be able to bear the burden of the mighty men men women men and others.

sanskrit: deśa kāla artha yuktāni hṛt tāpa upaśamāni ca haranti smarataḥ cittam govinda abhihitāni me
reference: Now I am attracted to those instructions imparted to me by the Personality of Godhead [Govinda] because they are impregnated with instructions for relieving the burning heart in all circumstances of time and space.
baseline: The heart and the heat and other elements of the body are called desh kaal meaning and the mind is called Govinda.
morphology: The heart the heart and the heat and the senses are called desh kaal meaning and the mind is called Govinda.

sanskrit: sūtaḥ uvāca evam cintayataḥ jiṣṇoḥ kṛṣṇa pāda saroruham sauhārdena ati gāḍhena śāntā āsīt vimalā matiḥ
reference: Sūta Gosvāmī said: Thus being deeply absorbed in thinking of the instructions of the Lord, which were imparted in the great intimacy of friendship, and in thinking of His lotus feet, Arjuna’s mind became pacified and free from all material contamination.
baseline: One should think in this way as if one were sitting on the feet of Lord Śeśṇu the god of water the goddess Vimla who was very deep and calm with harmony.
morphology: One should think in this way as if one were sitting on the feet of Lord Śeśṇu Śiva Saru and one who was very calm and calm with the harmony of the feet and feet.

sanskrit: vāsudeva aṅghri anudhyāna paribṛṁhita raṁhasā bhaktyā nirmathita aśeṣa kaṣāya dhiṣaṇaḥ arjunaḥ
reference: Arjuna’s constant remembrance of the lotus feet of Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa rapidly increased his devotion, and as a result all the trash in his thoughts subsided.
baseline: O Vāsudeva the king of Angrī without having to meditate on him and without doing any work for the sake of the family having built a temple of devotion one who has made a lotus is called Arjuna.
morphology: O Vasudeva the king of Angrī one who does not want to be a part of the family without having to meditate on it and one who has built a devotional house and has made a lotus tree is called Arjuna.

sanskrit: gītam bhagavatā jñānam yat tat saṅgrāma mūrdhani kāla karma tamaḥ ruddham punaḥ adhyagamat prabhuḥ
reference: Because of the Lord’s pastimes and activities and because of His absence, it appeared that Arjuna forgot the instructions left by the Personality of Godhead. But factually this was not the case, and again he became lord of his senses.
baseline: The lord should know the song the knowledge of the lord the time of the battle the conduct of the war the action of the fool the ceasing of the fight the attainment of the master again.
morphology: The lord should know the song the knowledge of God the time of the battle and the action of the enemy. He should stop the action and go back to his master.

sanskrit: viśokaḥ brahma sampattyā sañchinna dvaita saṁśayaḥ līna prakṛti nairguṇyāt aliṅgatvāt asambhavaḥ
reference: Because of his possessing spiritual assets, the doubts of duality were completely cut off. Thus he was freed from the three modes of material nature and placed in transcendence. There was no longer any chance of his becoming entangled in birth and death, for he was freed from material form.
baseline: The illusion of Brahman is impossible by the absence of the nature and the unalloyed nature.
morphology: The illusion of Brahman with the wealth of the universe is impossible only by the union of the two elements.

sanskrit: niśamya bhagavat mārgam saṁsthām yadu kulasya ca svaḥ pathāya matim cakre nibhṛta ātmā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
reference: Upon hearing of Lord Kṛṣṇa’s returning to His abode, and upon understanding the end of the Yadu dynasty’s earthly manifestation, Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira decided to go back home, back to Godhead.
baseline: O Yudhishthira the soul should be fixed in the circle of the path of the clan and the path should be established as that of the lord.
morphology: O Yudhisthira the self the path of the clan should be completed by making him obey the Lord. Having fixed his mind in the circle the spirit should be made to follow the path.

sanskrit: pṛthā api anuśrutya dhanañjaya uditam nāśam yadūnām bhagavat gatim ca tām eka anta bhaktyā bhagavati adhokṣaje niveśita ātmā upararāma saṁsṛteḥ
reference: Kuntī, after overhearing Arjuna’s telling of the end of the Yadu dynasty and disappearance of Lord Kṛṣṇa, engaged in the devotional service of the transcendental Personality of Godhead with full attention and thus gained release from the course of material existence.
baseline: Having promised the same thing to the Lord one should worship the Lord as ones end and destroy the gods of the yadus by giving them wealth. One who has placed the soul in the lower abode would be able to attain the highest form of wealth.
morphology: Having promised the same amount of money one should worship the Lord as ones inner self and attain the highest form of wealth.

sanskrit: yayā aharat bhuvaḥ bhāram tām tanum vijahau ajaḥ kaṇṭakam kaṇṭakena iva dvayam ca api īśituḥ samam
reference: The supreme unborn, Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, caused the members of the Yadu dynasty to relinquish their bodies, and thus He relieved the burden of the world. This action was like picking out a thorn with a thorn, though both are the same to the controller.
baseline: The two elements are equal in weight. The two are equal. The three elements are the same as the two elements.
morphology: The two elements are equal in weight. The two are equal. The three elements are the thorns and the thistle.

sanskrit: yathā matsya ādi rūpāṇi dhatte jahyāt yathā naṭaḥ bhū bhāraḥ kṣapitaḥ yena jahau tat ca kalevaram
reference: The Supreme Lord relinquished the body which He manifested to diminish the burden of the earth. Just like a magician, He relinquishes one body to accept different ones, like the fish incarnation and others.
baseline: Just as a fish would destroy the original forms of the earth the king should destroy the ground and the weight of the ship.
morphology: Just as a fish would destroy the original forms of the earth the actor should destroy the ground and the weight of the ship.

sanskrit: yadā mukundaḥ bhagavān imām mahīm jahau sva tanvā śravaṇīya sat kathaḥ tadā ahaḥ eva aprati buddha cetasām abhadra hetuh kaliḥ anvavartata
reference: When the Personality of Godhead, Lord Kṛṣṇa, left this earthly planet in His selfsame form, from that very day Kali, who had already partially appeared, became fully manifest to create inauspicious conditions for those who are endowed with a poor fund of knowledge.
baseline: When Mukundā is said to be the lord of the universe to me to you to hear your own voice then you should say that you are the supreme intellect.
morphology: When Mukundā is said to be the lord of the universe. He should hear his own voice. Then the voice of the supreme intellect should be heard.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiraḥ tat parisarpaṇam budhaḥ pure ca rāṣṭre ca gṛhe tathā ātmani vibhāvya lobha anṛta jihma hiṁsana ādi adharma cakram gamanāya paryadhāt
reference: Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira was intelligent enough to understand the influence of the Age of Kali, characterized by increasing avarice, falsehood, cheating and violence throughout the capital, state, home and among individuals. So he wisely prepared himself to leave home, and he dressed accordingly.
baseline: The Lord Yudhishthira should offer the same to the Buddha and the nation in the house. Having conceived the self and having sought it he should go to the circle of unrighteousness as early as possible by making the jhim reach him.
morphology: Having worshipped Yudhishthira the Buddha the whole nation and the home the spirit should be made to go into the circle of iniquity.

sanskrit: sva rāṭ pautram vinayinam ātmanaḥ su samam guṇaiḥ toya nīvyāḥ patim bhūmeḥ abhyaṣiñcat gajāhvaye
reference: Thereafter, in the capital of Hastināpura, he enthroned his grandson, who was trained and equally qualified, as the emperor and master of all land bordered by the seas.
baseline: One should take his own son grandson brother wife son wife and children with equal qualities.
morphology: One should take his own son grandson brother wife son wife and children with equal qualities.

sanskrit: mathurāyām tathā vajram śūrasena patim tataḥ prājāpatyām nirūpya iṣṭim agnīn apibat īśvaraḥ
reference: Then he posted Vajra, the son of Aniruddha [grandson of Lord Kṛṣṇa], at Mathurā as the King of Śūrasena. Afterwards Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira performed a Prājāpatya sacrifice and placed in himself the fire for quitting household life.
baseline: The king should offer a diamond in Mathura and a diamond to the king of the mighty king. Then after having described the king he should offer the same to the firemen.
morphology: The king should offer a diamond in Mathura a diamond a sword a piece of silver a pot and then the king should be offered a lotus and the fire should be given to him.

sanskrit: visṛjya tatra tat sarvam dukūla valaya ādikam nirmamaḥ nirahaṅkāraḥ sañchinna aśeṣa bandhanaḥ
reference: Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira at once relinquished all his garments, belt and ornaments of the royal order and became completely disinterested and unattached to everything.
baseline: Having thrown all that is therein one should make a circle of two parts. One should make it free from evil conduct. One would be bound without any bond.
morphology: Having thrown all that is therein one should make a circle of two parts. One should make it free from evil conduct. One would be bound beyond bounds.

sanskrit: vācam juhāva manasi tat prāṇe itare ca tam mṛtyau apānam sa utsargam tam pañcatve hi ajohavīt
reference: Then he amalgamated all the sense organs into the mind, then the mind into life, life into breathing, his total existence into the embodiment of the five elements, and his body into death. Then, as pure self, he became free from the material conception of life.
baseline: He should remember the words of another person in his life that person should be killed. He should offer him sacrifice on the fifth day.
morphology: He should remember the words of the priest that which is alive and that which has died in others. He should offer the sacrifice to the five gods.

sanskrit: tritve hutvā ca pañcatvam tat ca ekatve ajuhot muniḥ sarvam ātmani ajuhavīt brahmaṇi ātmānam avyaye
reference: Thus annihilating the gross body of five elements into the three qualitative modes of material nature, he merged them in one nescience and then absorbed that nescience in the self, Brahman, which is inexhaustible in all circumstances.
baseline: The sage who has attained the five elements in the form of the three elements and the same is called as ones self. The sages who have attained all the aspects of the self are called brahmins.
morphology: The sage should have the five elements of the three elements in one. The sages should have all the elements in the self. The Brahman should be made invisible in the universe.

sanskrit: cīra vāsāḥ nirāhāraḥ baddha vāk mukta mūrdhajaḥ darśayan ātmanaḥ rūpam jaḍa unmatta piśāca vat anavekṣamāṇaḥ niragāt aśṛṇvan badhiraḥ yathā
reference: After that, Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira dressed himself in torn clothing, gave up eating all solid foods, voluntarily became dumb and let his hair hang loose. All this combined to make him look like an urchin or madman with no occupation. He did not depend on his brothers for anything. And, just like a deaf man, he heard nothing.
baseline: A deaf person who is blind and deaf should be made to see the manifestation of the self by a man who has broken his mouth and is on a hunger strike. A deaf man who is not aware of the nature of the soul should be shown the form of a man possessed by a mad man.
morphology: A deaf person who is blind and has no voice should be made to see the manifestation of the self by a man who is not aware of the nature of the soul.

sanskrit: udīcīm praviveśa āśām gata pūrvām mahā ātmabhiḥ hṛdi brahma param dhyāyan na āvarteta yataḥ gataḥ
reference: He then started towards the north, treading the path accepted by his forefathers and great men, to devote himself completely to the thought of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. And he lived in that way wherever he went.
baseline: Having entered into the abode of Udiṣṇu one should not repeat the meditation on Brahman with the great spirits in the east.
morphology: The heart should be meditated upon by the Brahman with the great spirits in the past. It should not be repeated if it has entered the upper reaches of the sky and has gone to the east.

sanskrit: sarve tam anunirjagmuḥ bhrātaraḥ kṛta niścayāḥ kalinā adharma mitreṇa dṛṣṭvā spṛṣṭāḥ prajāḥ bhuvi
reference: The younger brothers of Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira observed that the Age of Kali had already arrived throughout the world and that the citizens of the kingdom were already affected by irreligious practice. Therefore they decided to follow in the footsteps of their elder brother.
baseline: All those who do not follow him those who are determined to do evil by their brethren those people who are touched by a friend and who see the evil deeds done by them should be punished.
morphology: All the brethren who have committed the crime should follow him. Seeing that the friend has done the wrong thing the people who have been touched should speak to him.

sanskrit: te sādhu kṛta sarva arthāḥ jñātvā ātyantikam ātmanaḥ manasā dhārayām āsuḥ vaikuṇṭha caraṇa ambujam
reference: They all had performed all the principles of religion and as a result rightly decided that the lotus feet of the Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa are the supreme goal of all. Therefore they meditated upon His feet without interruption.
baseline: Having known all the meanings of the sādhu the supreme self should be worshipped with the mind. The asura should be placed at the feet of Vaikuntha.
morphology: Having known all the meanings of the sādhu one should bear the mind of the ultimate self. One should follow the steps of Vaikuntha and Ambu.

sanskrit: tat dhyāna utriktayā bhaktyā viśuddha dhiṣaṇāḥ pare tasmin nārāyaṇa pade ekānta matayaḥ gatim avāpuḥ duravāpām te asadbhiḥ viṣaya ātmabhiḥ vidhūta kalmaṣāḥ sthānam virajena ātmanā eva hi
reference: Thus by pure consciousness due to constant devotional remembrance, they attained the spiritual sky, which is ruled over by the Supreme Nārāyaṇa, Lord Kṛṣṇa. This is attained only by those who meditate upon the one Supreme Lord without deviation. This abode of the Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, known as Goloka Vṛndāvana, cannot be attained by persons who are absorbed in the material conception of life. But the Pāṇḍavas, being completely washed of all material contamination, attained that abode in their very same bodies.
baseline: Having meditated on that and having worshipped it with pure devotion one should follow the path of Narayana in that posture alone. One should do the same with the mind. One who has been separated by the spirit from the illusion of the body should do so.
morphology: Having meditated on it one should worship it with pure devotion. One should follow the path of Narayana alone in that position. He should not be afraid of the matter. He would destroy the place of the abyss of the earth by the illusion of the spirit.

sanskrit: viduraḥ api parityajya prabhāse deham ātmanaḥ kṛṣṇa āveśena tat cittaḥ pitṛbhiḥ sva kṣayam yayau
reference: Vidura, while on pilgrimage, left his body at Prabhāsa. Because he was absorbed in thought of Kṛṣṇa, he was received by the denizens of the Pitṛloka planet, where he returned to his original post.
baseline: Having left the body the self the mind and the mind with the zeal of Kṛṣṇa in the preceptor one would get rid of his own loss by the parents.
morphology: Having left the disciple also one should leave the body in the abode of the lord the spirit the mind and the mind with the zeal of Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit: draupadī ca tadā ājñāya patīnām anapekṣatām vāsudeve bhagavati hi eka anta matiḥ āpa tam
reference: Draupadī also saw that her husbands, without caring for her, were leaving home. She knew well about Lord Vāsudeva, Kṛṣṇa, the Personality of Godhead. Both she and Subhadrā became absorbed in thoughts of Kṛṣṇa and attained the same results as their husbands.
baseline: Then Draupadi should give orders to her husband and her husband to do the same. Lord Vāsudeva should give her one end.
morphology: Then Draupadi should give orders to her husband and her husband. The lord Vasudeva should give her one final opinion.

sanskrit: yaḥ śraddhayā etat bhagavat priyāṇām pāṇḍoḥ sutānām iti samprayāṇam śṛṇoti alam svastyayanam pavitram labdhvā harau bhaktim upaiti siddhim
reference: The subject of the departure of the sons of Pāṇḍu for the ultimate goal of life, back to Godhead, is fully auspicious and is perfectly pure. Therefore anyone who hears this narration with devotional faith certainly gains the devotional service of the Lord, the highest perfection of life.
baseline: One who hears this by the belief of the lord the beloved one the Pandavas the Sūtāṇas and the sāmrāma. Having attained the sanctity of the abode of alam swastyaṇa attains the perfection of devotion.
morphology: One who listens to the sermons of the lord and his beloved Pandu and Sutāna with the belief that he has achieved the perfection of devotion by attaining the sanctity of the abode of alam swastya hara and attains perfection.

sanskrit: sūtaḥ uvāca tataḥ parīkṣit dvija varya śikṣayā mahīm mahā bhāgavataḥ śaśāsa ha yathā hi sūtyām abhijāta kovidāḥ samādiśan vipra mahat guṇaḥ tathā
reference: Sūta Gosvāmī said: O learned brāhmaṇas, Mahārāja Parīkṣit then began to rule over the world as a great devotee of the Lord under the instructions of the best of the twice-born brāhmaṇas. He ruled by those great qualities which were foretold by expert astrologers at the time of his birth.
baseline: The sūtā is said to be the supreme form of knowledge. Then the sūta should be tested twice and the sāsāsha should be worshipped with the teaching of the great bhagavata. The sātā should be given to the noble and noble kovids.
morphology: The sūtā is said to be the supreme quality. The sutā should be tested twice and taught the great Bhagavata. As the sūta the noble and the eloquent are said to have attained great qualities.

sanskrit: saḥ uttarasya tanayām upayeme irāvatīm janamejaya ādīn caturaḥ tasyām utpādayat sutān
reference: King Parīkṣit married the daughter of King Uttara and begot four sons, headed by Mahārāja Janamejaya.
baseline: He should use the sun of the north the sky the earth the people the chaturas the sons of the king and produce it.
morphology: He should use the sun of the north the moon of the earth the sky the earth and the earth.

sanskrit: ājahāra aśva medhān trīn gaṅgāyām bhūri dakṣiṇān śāradvatam gurum kṛtvā devāḥ yatra akṣi gocarāḥ
reference: Mahārāja Parīkṣit, after having selected Kṛpācārya for guidance as his spiritual master, performed three horse sacrifices on the banks of the Ganges. These were executed with sufficient rewards for the attendants. And at these sacrifices, even the common man could see demigods.
baseline: The three horses of the god Ajāharā Medha and the dākhins of the king should be placed in the Ganges and the four gurus should be worshipped.
morphology: The three horses of the god Ajāhara Medha Bhūri Dākṣṇī Sarādvatā and others are worshipped in the Ganges.

sanskrit: nijagrāha ojasā vīraḥ kalim digvijaye kvacit nṛpa liṅga dharam śūdram ghnantam go mithunam padā
reference: Once, when Mahārāja Parīkṣit was on his way to conquer the world, he saw the master of Kali-yuga, who was lower than a śūdra, disguised as a king and hurting the legs of a cow and bull. The King at once caught hold of him to deal sufficient punishment.
baseline: One who has conquered the kings linga dhārā sudra cow mithuna cow and other things should be worshipped as the king.
morphology: One who conquers the king of the kingdom of Kali with the power of his own self one who is mighty who has conquered the king who is a lord of the linga a shudra a cow a mithuna a horse and a horse should be placed in the position of the king.

sanskrit: śaunakaḥ uvāca kasya hetoḥ nijagrāha kalim digvijaye nṛpaḥ nṛ deva cihna dhṛk śūdrakaḥ asau gām yaḥ padā ahanat tat kathyatām mahā bhāga yadi kṛṣṇa kathā āśrayam
reference: Śaunaka Ṛṣi inquired: Why did Mahārāja Parīkṣit simply punish him, since he was the lowest of the śūdras, having dressed as a king and having struck a cow on the leg? Please describe all these incidents if they relate to the topics of Lord Kṛṣṇa.
baseline: One should say that if the great part of the story of Kṛṣṇa is said to be the victory of the king the king of the gods the lord of the goddesses the god of dhruk the sudra the cow and the cow are killed by him.
morphology: The king of Shouṇaka said that if the king of Śaṇa who had conquered the kingdom of his own country for the sake of whom he had conquered should say the great part of the land that was lost by the sudras the king should say that the lord of the gods should be destroyed by him.

sanskrit: athavā asya pada ambhoja makaranda lihām satām kim anyaiḥ asat ālāpaiḥ āyuṣaḥ yat asat vyayaḥ
reference: The devotees of the Lord are accustomed to licking up the honey available from the lotus feet of the Lord. What is the use of topics which simply waste one’s valuable life?
baseline: Or whether the words ambhoja makarandā lihā satam or others should be said to be ayūṣa.
morphology: Or should one worship the nectar of the makarandas or the other. One should speak to the other as well as to the lord of life.

sanskrit: kṣudra āyuṣām nṛṇām aṅga martyānām ṛtam icchatām iha upahūtaḥ bhagavān mṛtyuḥ śāmitra karmaṇi
reference: O Sūta Gosvāmī, there are those amongst men who desire freedom from death and get eternal life. They escape the slaughtering process by calling the controller of death, Yamarāja.
baseline: One should wish for the death of the members of the nārṇas with the small ayūṣa and the meritorious deeds of the lord.
morphology: O Lord of the universe the lesser life the members of the body and the dead should be worshipped.

sanskrit: na kaścit mriyate tāvat yāvat āste iha antakaḥ etat artham hi bhagavān āhūtaḥ parama ṛṣibhiḥ aho nṛ loke pīyeta hari līlā amṛtam vacaḥ
reference: As long as Yamarāja, who causes everyone’s death, is present here, no one shall meet with death. The great sages have invited the controller of death, Yamarāja, who is the representative of the Lord. Living beings who are under his grip should take advantage by hearing the deathless nectar in the form of this narration of the transcendental pastimes of the Lord.
baseline: One should not die till the time one dies. This means that the Lord has called the supreme sages. The people should drink the nectar of Hari lila.
morphology: The meaning of the word antaṇa is called oh Lord. O rāśīs the supreme sages and the people should drink the word Hari lila amruta till one dies.

sanskrit: mandasya manda prajñasya vayaḥ manda āyuṣaḥ ca vai nidrayā hriyate naktam divā ca vyartha karmabhiḥ
reference: Lazy human beings with paltry intelligence and a short duration of life pass the night sleeping and the day performing activities that are for naught.
baseline: One who is in a state of sluggishness dull consciousness dull life and sleep would be destroyed by the evil deed.
morphology: One who is in a state of sluggishness dull consciousness dull life and sleep would get destroyed by the evil deed.

sanskrit: sūtaḥ uvāca yadā parīkṣit kuru jāṅgale avasat kalim praviṣṭam nija cakravartite niśamya vārtām anati priyām tataḥ śarāsanam saṁyuga śauṇḍiḥ ādade
reference: Sūta Gosvāmī said: While Mahārāja Parīkṣit was residing in the capital of the Kuru empire, the symptoms of the Age of Kali began to infiltrate within the jurisdiction of his state. When he learned about this, he did not think the matter very palatable. This did, however, give him a chance to fight. He took up his bow and arrows and prepared himself for military activities.
baseline: When the thread has been tested the king should enter the forest and make his own king enter it and bring the message. Then he should perform the sārāsana and the yuga sāundī.
morphology: When the thread has been tested it should be placed in the forest. It should be removed from the king. It is said to be a good thing. Then the king should perform the ritual of sārāsana and perform the yuga sāundī.

sanskrit: su alaṅkṛtam śyāma turaṅga yojitam ratham mṛga indra dhvajam āśritaḥ purāt vṛtaḥ ratha aśva dvipapatti yuktayā sva senayā digvijayāya nirgataḥ
reference: Mahārāja Parīkṣit sat on a chariot drawn by black horses. His flag was marked with the sign of a lion. Being so decorated and surrounded by charioteers, cavalry, elephants and infantry soldiers, he left the capital to conquer in all directions.
baseline: The chariot adorned with a dark tower with the garland of Indra and the flag of Indra is placed in the rear. The charyotel with the armoury of horses and two legs is drawn out of the city with its own army for victory.
morphology: The chariot adorned with a white turret with the garland of Indra and the flag of Indra should be taken from the city and the chariots should be made of two parts.

sanskrit: bhadrāśvam ketumālam ca bhāratam ca uttarān kurūn kimpuruṣa ādīni varṣāṇi vijitya jagṛhe balim
reference: Mahārāja Parīkṣit then conquered all parts of the earthly planet — Bhadrāśva, Ketumāla, Bhārata, the northern Kuru, Kimpuruṣa, etc. — and exacted tributes from their respective rulers.
baseline: Having conquered the years of Bhadrāśva Kētumala and Bharata the kuruṇas and the kīrūṇas in the north the Kīmpurṣas and others one should offer sacrifice in the temple.
morphology: Having conquered the years of Bhadrāśva Kētumala and Bharāṭa the kuruṇas of the north and the kīmpurṣas of other parts of the world are worshipped.

sanskrit: tatra tatra upaśṛṇvānaḥ sva pūrveṣām mahā ātmanām pragīyamāṇam ca yaśaḥ kṛṣṇa māhātmya sūcakam ātmānam ca paritrātam aśvatthāmnaḥ astra tejasaḥ sneham ca vṛṣṇi pārthānām teṣām bhaktim ca keśave tebhyaḥ parama santuṣṭaḥ prīti ujjṛmbhita locanaḥ mahā dhanāni vāsāṁsi dadau hārān mahā manāḥ
reference: Wherever the King visited, he continuously heard the glories of his great forefathers, who were all devotees of the Lord, and also of the glorious acts of Lord Kṛṣṇa. He also heard how he himself had been protected by the Lord from the powerful heat of the weapon of Aśvatthāmā. People also mentioned the great affection between the descendants of Vṛṣṇi and Pṛthā due to the latter’s great devotion to Lord Keśava. The King, being very pleased with the singers of such glories, opened his eyes in great satisfaction. Out of magnanimity he was pleased to award them very valuable necklaces and clothing.
baseline: There are the sub-shrines there the manifestations of the great spirits of the east the glory of Kṛṣṇa the symbol of greatness the emancipation of the spirit the arms the fire the love the devotion of the bulls the gods the supreme contentment the blissful lotus the great wealth the garlands and the great heart.
morphology: There are the sub-shrines there the manifestation of the great spirits of the east the glory of Kṛṣṇa the symbol of greatness the emancipation of the spirits the arms of Āśvātāma the fire the love of the gods the devotion to them the supreme contentment the great wealth the garlands and the great heart.

sanskrit: sārathya pāraṣada sevana sakhya dautya vīra āsana anugamana stavana praṇāmān snigdheṣu pāṇḍuṣu jagat praṇatim ca viṣṇoḥ bhaktim karoti nṛ patiḥ caraṇa aravinde
reference: Mahārāja Parīkṣit heard that out of His causeless mercy Lord Kṛṣṇa [Viṣṇu], who is universally obeyed, rendered all kinds of service to the malleable sons of Pāṇḍu by accepting posts ranging from chariot driver to president to messenger, friend, night watchman, etc., according to the will of the Pāṇḍavas, obeying them like a servant and offering obeisances like one younger in years. When he heard this, Mahārāja Parīkṣit became overwhelmed with devotion to the lotus feet of the Lord.
baseline: One who worships Lord Viṣṇu with the chariot pārśa and other arms the king who follows the seat of the mighty warrior and offers salutations and prays to the world among the Pandavas in the form of a serpent and worships the world.
morphology: One who worships Lord Viṣṇu with the chariot pārśa and other instruments follows the heroic posture and offers salutations to the Pandavas and the world.

sanskrit: tasya evam vartamānasya pūrveṣām vṛttim anvaham na ati dūre kila āścaryam yat āsīt tat nibodha me
reference: Now you may hear from me of what happened while Mahārāja Parīkṣit was passing his days hearing of the good occupations of his forefathers and being absorbed in thought of them.
baseline: I shall not say that it was so far away from the present and the former.
morphology: I shall explain to you the fact that it was not so far away from him as it was in the past.

sanskrit: dharmaḥ padā ekena caran vicchāyām upalabhya gām pṛcchati sma aśru vadanām vivatsām iva mātaram
reference: The personality of religious principles, Dharma, was wandering about in the form of a bull. And he met the personality of earth in the form of a cow who appeared to grieve like a mother who had lost her child. She had tears in her eyes, and the beauty of her body was lost. Thus Dharma questioned the earth as follows.
baseline: One who has found a cow with the feet and feet of a cow should ask the mother for a gift like a gift of tears.
morphology: One would ask the mother for a cow after having been found in the forest with the feet of dharma one foot and one foot.

sanskrit: dharmaḥ uvāca kaccit bhadre anāmayam ātmanaḥ te vicchāyā asi mlāyatā īṣat mukhena ālakṣaye bhavatīm antarādhim dūre bandhum śocasi kañcana amba
reference: Dharma [in the form of a bull] asked: Madam, are you not hale and hearty? Why are you covered with the shadow of grief? It appears by your face that you have become black. Are you suffering from some internal disease, or are you thinking of some relative who is away in a distant place?
baseline: One who has said that he would like to have a friend at a distance from him by the medium of dharma would have said that one should have a brother at home.
morphology: One who has said that he would like to have a friend away from him by the means of the medium of dharma would have said that one should have an unclean spirit. He would have erased it by the medium.

sanskrit: pādaiḥ nyūnam śocasi mā eka pādam ātmānam vā vṛṣalaiḥ bhokṣyamāṇam āhoḥ sura ādīn hṛta yajña bhāgān prajāḥ uta svit maghavati avarṣati
reference: I have lost my three legs and am now standing on one only. Are you lamenting for my state of existence? Or are you in great anxiety because henceforward the unlawful meat-eaters will exploit you? Or are you in a sorry plight because the demigods are now bereft of their share of sacrificial offerings because no sacrifices are being performed at present? Or are you grieving for living beings because of their sufferings due to famine and drought?
baseline: One should not suffer one foot or the soul less than the feet. One who eats food from the bulls should not be afraid of the sacrifice of the people or the people.
morphology: One should not suffer less than one foot from the feet or the soul from the bulls. One who eats food from the horses should not be afraid of the sacrifice of the people or the people.

sanskrit: arakṣyamāṇāḥ striyaḥ urvi bālān śocasi atho puruṣa ādaiḥ iva ārtān vācam devīm brahma kule kukarmaṇi abrahmaṇye rāja kule kula agryān
reference: Are you feeling compunction for the unhappy women and children who are left forlorn by unscrupulous persons? Or are you unhappy because the goddess of learning is being handled by brāhmaṇas addicted to acts against the principles of religion? Or are you sorry to see that the brāhmaṇas have taken shelter of administrative families that do not respect brahminical culture?
baseline: Women who are illiterate men who suffer childbirth women who suffer in the absence of children men mothers women children women and children gods Brahmā Kūla Kukrāma Abrahmanī king clan elders etc. should be worshipped.
morphology: The women who are the protectors of the king the sons of the poor the children of the oppressed the men of the country the gods of the kingdom of Brahman the mischief of the enemies the king of the princely state the chieftains the elders the goddess of the people the god of the gods and the king.

sanskrit: kim kṣatra bandhūn kalinā upasṛṣṭān rāṣṭrāṇi vā taiḥ avaropitāni itaḥ tataḥ vā aśana pāna vāsaḥ snāna vyavāya unmukha jīva lokam
reference: The so-called administrators are now bewildered by the influence of this Age of Kali, and thus they have put all state affairs into disorder. Are you now lamenting this disorder? Now the general populace does not follow the rules and regulations for eating, sleeping, drinking, mating, etc., and they are inclined to perform such anywhere and everywhere. Are you unhappy because of this?
baseline: Whether the kṣṭrātra or the kālīna or the rāṣatras created by them are brought down by them. Then the living entity should be placed in the abode of water and bathing.
morphology: The kāṣtra-bandhins or the kālīna-like nations or the nations that have been subjugated by them are then reduced. Then the living entity should go to the abode of water and bath.

sanskrit: yadvā amba te bhūri bhara avatāra kṛta avatārasya hareḥ dharitri antarhitasya smaratī visṛṣṭā karmāṇi nirvāṇa vilambitāni
reference: O mother earth, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Hari, incarnated Himself as Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa just to unload your heavy burden. All His activities here are transcendental, and they cement the path of liberation. You are now bereft of His presence. You are probably now thinking of those activities and feeling sorry in their absence.
baseline: Having made the incarnation as aṇbha bhūrī bha bharā hare dhṛti hāre hara dhrītī and the recollection of the incarnations the deeds done in the past have been delayed.
morphology: Having made the incarnation of Bhūrī bhaṇa with the garlands of the incarnations hāre dhrutri hārī and hināhita the remembrance of the manifestations of the unmanifested should be repeated in the morning.

sanskrit: idam mama ācakṣva tava ādhimūlam vasundhare yena vikarśitā asi kālena vā te balinām balīyasā sura arcitam kim hṛtam amba saubhagam
reference: Mother, you are the reservoir of all riches. Please inform me of the root cause of your tribulations by which you have been reduced to such a weak state. I think that the powerful influence of time, which conquers the most powerful, might have forcibly taken away all your fortune, which was adored even by the demigods.
baseline: This is the sound of the bālikas that have been worshipped in the form of a strong bow or the sound that has been deflected by the same time. What is the loss of the head of the mother and the source of your body in Vasundhara?
morphology: O Lord of the universe whether it is my son or the son of Vasundhara or the king of the gods of the kingdom of Vāsundhara who has erased the sound of those sacrifices.

sanskrit: dharaṇī uvāca bhavān hi veda tat sarvam yat mām dharma anupṛcchasi caturbhiḥ vartase yena pādaiḥ loka sukha āvahaiḥ
reference: The earthly deity [in the form of a cow] thus replied to the personality of religious principles [in the form of a bull]: O Dharma, whatever you have inquired from me shall be known to you. I shall try to reply to all those questions. Once you too were maintained by your four legs, and you increased happiness all over the universe by the mercy of the Lord.
baseline: The dhārṇī should say that you are the Vedas. You should offer me all that is righteous. One should walk around with four legs in order to bring happiness to the people.
morphology: One should say that you are the Vedas. You should offer me all that is good for me. One should walk around with four legs in order to bring happiness to the people.

sanskrit: satyam śaucam dayā kṣāntiḥ tyāgaḥ santoṣaḥ ārjavam śamaḥ damaḥ tapaḥ sāmyam titikṣā uparatiḥ śrutam jñānam viraktiḥ aiśvaryam śauryam tejaḥ balam smṛtiḥ svātantryam kauśalam kāntiḥ dhairyam mārdavam eva ca prāgalbhyam praśrayaḥ śīlam sahaḥ ojaḥ balam bhagaḥ gāmbhīryam sthairyam āstikyam kīrtiḥ mānaḥ anahaṅkṛtiḥ ete ca anye ca bhagavan nityāḥ yatra mahā guṇāḥ prārthyāḥ mahattvam icchadbhiḥ na viyanti sma karhicit tena aham guṇa pātreṇa śrī nivāsena sāmpratam śocāmi rahitam lokam pāpmanā kalinā īkṣitam
reference: In Him reside (1) truthfulness, (2) cleanliness, (3) intolerance of another’s unhappiness, (4) the power to control anger, (5) self-satisfaction, (6) straightforwardness, (7) steadiness of mind, (8) control of the sense organs, (9) responsibility, (10) equality, (11) tolerance, (12) equanimity, (13) faithfulness, (14) knowledge, (15) absence of sense enjoyment, (16) leadership, (17) chivalry, (18) influence, (19) the power to make everything possible, (20) the discharge of proper duty, (21) complete independence, (22) dexterity, (23) fullness of all beauty, (24) serenity, (25) kindheartedness, (26) ingenuity, (27) gentility, (28) magnanimity, (29) determination, (30) perfection in all knowledge, (31) proper execution, (32) possession of all objects of enjoyment, (33) joyfulness, (34) immovability, (35) fidelity, (36) fame, (37) worship, (38) pridelessness, (39) being (as the Personality of Godhead), (40) eternity, and many other transcendental qualities which are eternally present and never to be separated from Him. That Personality of Godhead, the reservoir of all goodness and beauty, Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, has now closed His transcendental pastimes on the face of the earth. In His absence the Age of Kali has spread its influence everywhere, so I am sorry to see this condition of existence.
baseline: O Lord of the universe one who does not know the importance of great virtues renunciation satisfaction contentment repentance patience penance equanimity superiority knowledge detachment valour brilliance strength memory strength and strength courage fortitude courage and determination strength along with grace fortuitousness firmness strength in the body steadfastness tenacity pride selfishness honor honour honour etc. one who has not desired the great qualities of the lord and the noble nature of the world should be
morphology: One who has heard the words of Satya Shauṣa Daya Kshanti Sāmya Sūṣṇa Sattva Arjā Samyā Dāma Tapas Tītikṣa and Uparāṣa should have knowledge detachment opulence valour brilliance strength memory strength and strength courage strength. courage fortitude strength, strength strength along with the strength fortitudes strength in the heart strength of the body strength etc. should be able to

sanskrit: ātmānam ca anuśocāmi bhavantam ca amara uttamam devān pitṝn ṛṣīn sādhūn sarvān varṇān tathā āśramān
reference: I am thinking about myself and also, O best amongst the demigods, about you, as well as about all the demigods, sages, denizens of Pitṛloka, devotees of the Lord and all men obedient to the system of varṇa and āśrama in human society.
baseline: One who is the soul the sorrowful ones self the immortal one the best of gods the fathers the sages the saints all the colours and the abode of the saints should be worshipped.
morphology: One who has experienced the soul sorrow immortality good gods fathers sages saints saints and all other forms should seek refuge in you.

sanskrit: brahma ādayaḥ bahu titham yat apāṅga mokṣa kāmāḥ tapaḥ samacaran bhagavat prapannāḥ sā śrīḥ sva vāsam aravinda vanam vihāya yat pāda saubhagam alam bhajate anuraktā tasya aham abja kuliśa aṅkuśa ketu ketaiḥ śrīmat padaiḥ bhagavataḥ samalaṅkṛta aṅgī trīn ati aroce upalabhya tataḥ vibhūtim lokān saḥ mām vyasṛjat utsmayatīm tat ante
reference: Lakṣmījī, the goddess of fortune, whose glance of grace was sought by demigods like Brahmā and for whom they surrendered many a day unto the Personality of Godhead, gave up her own abode in the forest of lotus flowers and engaged herself in the service of the lotus feet of the Lord. I was endowed with specific powers to supersede the fortune of all the three planetary systems by being decorated with the impressions of the flag, thunderbolt, elephant-driving rod and lotus flower, which are signs of the lotus feet of the Lord. But at the end, when I felt I was so fortunate, the Lord left me.
baseline: Having said this the Lord should worship the feet of the celestial god Brahma at the beginning many times the limbs the senses of liberation the desires the penance of the Lord the abode of the great god the king who has left the forest of the Aravinds and worshipped him the feet the grace the glory the wealth the arms the hands arms arms and arms of the king. Having said these three things he has made me aware of him.
morphology: Having said this the king should worship the feet of the goddess Brahma at the beginning the three great elements of the world the goddess of the universe the abode of the gods and the goddess Śrī who has been worshipped by the Lord as well as the goddess Aurobindo and the gods of the forest. Having said that after having worshipped the feet the feet and the sacred things of the almā he should be worshipped.

sanskrit: yaḥ vai mama ati bharam āsura vaṁśa rājñām akṣauhiṇī śatam apānudat ātma tantraḥ tvām duḥstham ūna padam ātmani pauruṣeṇa sampādayan yaduṣu ramyam abibhrat aṅgam
reference: O personality of religion, I was greatly overburdened by the undue military phalanxes arranged by atheistic kings, and I was relieved by the grace of the Personality of Godhead. Similarly you were also in a distressed condition, weakened in your standing strength, and thus He also incarnated by His internal energy in the family of the Yadus to relieve you.
baseline: The king should be given a hundred cubits by the king of the kingdom of Aksha who is overbearing me and a demon. He should be made to perform the position of a woolen garment by the priest of the self. The body should be mercilessly broken.
morphology: The king should be given a hundred cubits by the king who is overbearing me a demon an axe a sword a piece of wool and a part of the body by the man who is ill.

sanskrit: kā vā saheta viraham puruṣa uttamasya prema avaloka rucira smita valgu jalpaiḥ sthairyam sa mānam aharat madhu māninīnām roma utsavaḥ mama yat aṅghri viṭaṅkitāyāḥ
reference: Who, therefore, can tolerate the pangs of separation from that Supreme Personality of Godhead? He could conquer the gravity and passionate wrath of His sweethearts like Satyabhāmā by His sweet smile of love, pleasing glance and hearty appeals. When He traversed my [earth’s] surface, I would be immersed in the dust of His lotus feet and thus would be sumptuously covered with grass which appeared like hairs standing on me out of pleasure.
baseline: One who observes the love of a good man and attains steadfastness with the mercilessly flowing jalpas would get the honour. One who celebrates the festival of honey mani and roma would get my body broken.
morphology: One who observes the love of a good man and attains steadfastness with the merciless and merry flowers would get the honour. One who celebrates the feast of honey and honey would get victory over the enemy.

sanskrit: tayoḥ evam kathayatoḥ pṛthivī dharmayoḥ tadā parīkṣit nāma rāja ṛṣiḥ prāptaḥ prācīm sarasvatīm
reference: While the earth and the personality of religion were thus engaged in conversation, the saintly King Parīkṣit reached the shore of the Sarasvatī River, which flowed towards the east.
baseline: Then the king should say that the sage should be tested for the righteousness of the earth. The sage got the name prācī and Sarasvati.
morphology: Then the king should be called the sage and the goddess Sarāsvati should be described as such.

sanskrit: sūtaḥ uvāca tatra go mithunam rājā hanyamānam anātha vat daṇḍa hastam ca vṛṣalam dadṛśe nṛpa lāñchanam
reference: Sūta Gosvāmī said: After reaching that place, Mahārāja Parīkṣit observed that a lower-caste śūdra, dressed like a king, was beating a cow and a bull with a club, as if they had no owner.
baseline: The king should be killed by a cow a mithuna an orphan an elephant a bull a man with a hand and a bull on his head.
morphology: The king should be killed by a cow a mithuna an orphan an elephant a bull a sword and a bull.

sanskrit: vṛṣam mṛṇāla dhavalam mehantam iva bibhyatam vepamānam padā ekena sīdantam śūdra tāḍitam
reference: The bull was as white as a white lotus flower. He was terrified of the śūdra who was beating him, and he was so afraid that he was standing on one leg, trembling and urinating.
baseline: A bull should be made to look like a mace a mridāla a dhāvala a vapāmana a siddhanta and a shudra should be tied with one foot.
morphology: A bull should be made to look like a mace a mridula a dhāvala a vepamana a siddhanta and a shudra should be tied with one foot.

sanskrit: gām ca dharma dughām dīnām bhṛśam śūdra pada āhatām vivatsām āśru vadanām kṣāmām yavasam icchatīm
reference: Although the cow is beneficial because one can draw religious principles from her, she was now rendered poor and calfless. Her legs were being beaten by a śūdra. There were tears in her eyes, and she was distressed and weak. She was hankering after some grass in the field.
baseline: One would like to have the cow dharma milk clothes clothes and clothes of a sudra who has been suffering from the disease a cow a bull a bearer of ill health a poor man a barbarian a woman who has suffered from ill health.
morphology: One would like to have the cow dharma milk the hair of the dīna the feet of the shudra the body of the injured the arms of the vivaśu the clothes of the ashrūs the food of the poor the fruits of the yavas.

sanskrit: papraccha ratham ārūḍhaḥ kārtasvara paricchadam megha gambhīrayā vācā samāropita kārmukaḥ
reference: Mahārāja Parīkṣit, well equipped with arrows and bow and seated on a gold-embossed chariot, spoke to him [the śūdra] with a deep voice sounding like thunder.
baseline: The chariot should be mounted on the pāprāccha. The garland should be covered with a garland of kārtasvara. The covenant should be solemnly concluded.
morphology: The chariot should be mounted on the pāprāccha. The garland should be covered with kārtasvarā the cloud should be solemnly wrapped with the vow.

sanskrit: kaḥ tvam mat śaraṇe loke balāt haṁsi abalān balī nara devaḥ asi veṣeṇa naṭa vat karmaṇā advi jaḥ
reference: Oh, who are you? You appear to be strong and yet you dare kill, within my protection, those who are helpless! By your dress you pose yourself to be a godly man [king], but by your deeds you are opposing the principles of the twice-born kṣatriyas.
baseline: Who is that man who takes refuge in me and destroys me by force and makes me weak sacrificial male female god who does not act with a dress and others.
morphology: Who is it that you protect the people from the forces of evil and destroy them. The gods of the poor and the poor should be worshipped with the garlands of the gods.

sanskrit: yaḥ tvam kṛṣṇe gate dūram saha gāṇḍīva dhanvanā śocyaḥ asi aśocyān rahasi praharan vadham arhasi
reference: You rogue, do you dare beat an innocent cow because Lord Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna, the carrier of the Gāṇḍīva bow, are out of sight? Since you are beating the innocent in a secluded place, you are considered a culprit and therefore deserve to be killed.
baseline: One who goes to Krsna and lies down with a rhino at a distance and is blessed with wealth should be killed by attacking the disciples of Aśośa.
morphology: If you go to Krishna and lie down with a rhino at a distance and get rich with it you should kill the king by attacking him with a sword.

sanskrit: tvam vā mṛṇāla dhavalaḥ pādaiḥ nyūnaḥ padā caran vṛṣa rūpeṇa kim kaścit devaḥ naḥ parikhedayan
reference: Then he [Mahārāja Parīkṣit] asked the bull: Oh, who are you? Are you a bull as white as a white lotus, or are you a demigod? You have lost three of your legs and are moving on only one. Are you some demigod causing us grief in the form of a bull?
baseline: One who is not a god should be circumcised by the figure of Tūmrāla or Dhāvāla with his feet less than the feet.
morphology: One should not judge a god in the form of a bull. He should not know whether he is a man of good fortune or a man with weak feet.

sanskrit: na jātu kaurava indrāṇām dordaṇḍa parirambhite bhū tale anupatanti asmin vinā te prāṇinām śucaḥ
reference: Now for the first time in a kingdom well protected by the arms of the kings of the Kuru dynasty, I see you grieving with tears in your eyes. Up till now no one on earth has ever shed tears because of royal negligence.
baseline: If the Kauravas do not protect the enemies of Indra they would not be able to reach the ground without knowing the nature of the creatures.
morphology: If the Kauravas do not protect the elves they would be left on the ground without the knowledge of animals.

sanskrit: mā saurabheya atra śucaḥ vyetu te vṛṣalāt bhayam mā rodīḥ amba bhadram te khalānām mayi śāstari
reference: O son of Surabhi, you need lament no longer now. There is no need to fear this low-class śūdra. And, O mother cow, as long as I am living as the ruler and subduer of all envious men, there is no cause for you to cry. Everything will be good for you.
baseline: If they do not fear the bulls they should be punished. They should not be afraid of the bull. They are not afraid of me. The king of the pitchers should punish me.
morphology: Do not fear the bulls do not be afraid of them O son of the sun and teach them to me.

sanskrit: yasya rāṣṭre prajāḥ sarvāḥ trasyante sādhvi asādhubhiḥ tasya mattasya naśyanti kīrtiḥ āyuḥ bhagaḥ gatiḥ eṣaḥ rājñām paraḥ dharmaḥ hi ārtānām ārti nigrahaḥ ataḥ enam vadhiṣyāmi bhūta druham asat tamam
reference: O chaste one, the king’s good name, duration of life and good rebirth vanish when all kinds of living beings are terrified by miscreants in his kingdom. It is certainly the prime duty of the king to subdue first the sufferings of those who suffer. Therefore I must kill this most wretched man because he is violent against other living beings.
baseline: In a nation in which the people are all afflicted by the sādhyas the sadhus and the unrighteous destroy the spirit of the king. The king should be punished with the title of āyū bhāga gāti dharma hī rātā arta and subjugation. That is why he should be killed.
morphology: The nation in which the subjects are all afflicted by the sages and those who are unrighteous will lose their wealth. The king will be killed by the king by the evil spirits. The kingdom will be destroyed by the devils. He will be put to death by the demon.

sanskrit: kaḥ avṛścat tava pādān trīn saurabheya catuḥ pada mā bhūvan tvādṛśāḥ rāṣṭre rājñām kṛṣṇa anuvartinām
reference: He [Mahārāja Parīkṣit] repeatedly addressed and questioned the bull thus: O son of Surabhi, who has cut off your three legs? In the state of the kings who are obedient to the laws of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, there is no one as unhappy as you.
baseline: One should not make four steps with the feet of the sun three times and the king should be followed by Krishna in the kingdom.
morphology: One should say that the king should not walk on four steps with three of your feet and follow the king and Krishna.

sanskrit: ākhyāhi vṛṣa bhadram vaḥ sādhūnām akṛta āgasām ātma vairūpya kartāram pārthānām kīrti dūṣaṇam
reference: O bull, you are offenseless and thoroughly honest; therefore I wish all good to you. Please tell me of the perpetrator of these mutilations, which blacken the reputation of the sons of Pṛthā.
baseline: Having said this a bull a noble man should be taken away from the sages and the king should be made to look like the self.
morphology: Having said this the bull the noble the sage the king of the sages and the king should be made to look like the spirit. The glory of the gods should be destroyed.

sanskrit: jane anāgasi agham yuñjan sarvataḥ asya ca mat bhayam sādhūnām bhadram eva syāt asādhu damane kṛte
reference: Whoever causes offenseless living beings to suffer must fear me anywhere and everywhere in the world. By curbing dishonest miscreants, one automatically benefits the offenseless.
baseline: The fear of the sages should be always expressed in the manner of the people who are unruly and want to fight against the evil.
morphology: The fear of the sages should be the same in the case of those who do not obey the law.

sanskrit: anāgaḥsu iha bhūteṣu yaḥ āgaḥ kṛt niraṅkuśaḥ āhartā asmi bhujam sākṣāt amartyasya api sa aṅgadam
reference: An upstart living being who commits offenses by torturing those who are offenseless shall be directly uprooted by me, even though he be a denizen of heaven with armor and decorations.
baseline: One who has made a fire in the form of an anāga agha and the body of a person who has cast it directly into the body is called ahm.
morphology: One who has made a fire in the form of an anāga that which has been made by the demons and who has cast it with the bare hands should also immortalize the body of the body.

sanskrit: rājñaḥ hi paramaḥ dharmaḥ sva dharma stha anupālanam śāsataḥ anyān yathā śāstram anāpadi utpathān iha
reference: The supreme duty of the ruling king is to give all protection to law-abiding persons and to chastise those who stray from the ordinances of the scriptures in ordinary times, when there is no emergency.
baseline: The king is the supreme dharma. One should follow his own dharma and rule others as if he had not been given the scriptures.
morphology: The king is the supreme righteousness. One should follow his own righteous conduct and rule others as per the scriptures.

sanskrit: dharmaḥ uvāca etat vaḥ pāṇḍaveyānām yuktam ārta abhayam vacaḥ yeṣām guṇa gaṇaiḥ kṛṣṇaḥ dautya ādau bhagavān kṛtaḥ
reference: The personality of religion said: These words just spoken by you befit a person of the Pāṇḍava dynasty. Captivated by the devotional qualities of the Pāṇḍavas, even Lord Kṛṣṇa, the Personality of Godhead, performed duties as a messenger.
baseline: One should say dharma that which is associated with the Pandavas that is the meaning of abhaya the qualities of which Kṛṣṇa made the mission at all times.
morphology: One should say that these are the virtues of the Pandavas. One should understand the qualities with which Lord Kṛṣṇa had made the mission.

sanskrit: na vayam kleśa bījāni yataḥ syuḥ puruṣa ṛṣabha puruṣam tam vijānīmaḥ vākya bheda vimohitāḥ
reference: O greatest among human beings, it is very difficult to ascertain the particular miscreant who has caused our sufferings, because we are bewildered by all the different opinions of theoretical philosophers.
baseline: We do not suffer the seeds because the men should be men men rishabha men and men. They should be afraid of the difference between the words.
morphology: We do not suffer the seeds of misery because the men should be like Rishabha the men the disciples should be afraid of the difference between the words.

sanskrit: kecit vikalpa vasanāḥ āhuḥ ātmānam ātmanaḥ daivam anye apare karma svabhāvam apare prabhum
reference: Some of the philosophers, who deny all sorts of duality, declare that one’s own self is responsible for his personal happiness and distress. Others say that superhuman powers are responsible, while yet others say that activity is responsible, and the gross materialists maintain that nature is the ultimate cause.
baseline: Some of the options are to be found in the abode of the self. The self is to be worshipped by the gods. Others are to do deeds and others are to worship the lord.
morphology: One should choose ones own self self god other nature of action one lord others.

sanskrit: apratarkyāt anirdeśyāt iti keṣu api niścayaḥ atra anurūpam rāja ṛṣe vimṛśa sva manīṣayā
reference: There are also some thinkers who believe that no one can ascertain the cause of distress by argumentation, nor know it by imagination, nor express it by words. O sage amongst kings, judge for yourself by thinking over all this with your own intelligence.
baseline: In some cases it is said to be undefined by the king. The king should be known to the sage as such.
morphology: It is also said that in some cases it is not possible to make a decision without having to argue with the king. It should be done by the wise man.

sanskrit: sūtaḥ uvāca evam dharme pravadati saḥ samrāṭ dvija sattamāḥ samāhitena manasā vikhedaḥ paryacaṣṭa tam
reference: Sūta Gosvāmī said: O best among the brāhmaṇas, the Emperor Parīkṣit, thus hearing the personality of religion speak, was fully satisfied, and without mistake or regret he gave his reply.
baseline: The king should thus say that he would enter into the righteousness of the king. He should be absorbed by the two sattvas and the mind should be divided.
morphology: The king should thus say that he would enter into the dharma. He would then confine himself to the two sattvas of the king. Then he would go to the disciple.

sanskrit: rājā uvāca dharmam bravīṣi dharma jña dharmaḥ asi vṛṣa rūpa dhṛk yat adharma kṛtaḥ sthānam sūcakasya api tat bhavet
reference: The King said: O you, who are in the form of a bull! You know the truth of religion, and you are speaking according to the principle that the destination intended for the perpetrator of irreligious acts is also intended for one who identifies the perpetrator. You are no other than the personality of religion.
baseline: The king should say dharma brahmin dharma and know the dharma. The dharma should be the form of a bull and the place of the denier should be that of the one who has done the iniquity.
morphology: The king should say dharma brahmin dharma and dharma. The dharma should be in the form of a bull and the place of the denier should be the same.

sanskrit: athavā deva māyāyāḥ nūnam gatiḥ agocarā cetasaḥ vacasaḥ ca api bhūtānām iti niścayaḥ
reference: Thus it is concluded that the Lord’s energies are inconceivable. No one can estimate them by mental speculation or by word jugglery.
baseline: Or one who is determined to be a deva a māya a nūna a kati a vaśvāṣa and a bhūtana a person who is not aware of the nature of the universe.
morphology: It is said to be the manifestation of the gods mayas nūna gati agnotracha chetas vaśvatas and bhutas.

sanskrit: tapaḥ śaucam dayā satyam iti pādāḥ kṛte kṛtāḥ adharma aṁśaiḥ trayaḥ bhagnāḥ smaya saṅga madaiḥ tava
reference: In the age of Satya [truthfulness] your four legs were established by the four principles of austerity, cleanliness, mercy and truthfulness. But it appears that three of your legs are broken due to rampant irreligion in the form of pride, lust for women, and intoxication.
baseline: The practice of penance defecation mercy truthfulness and other practices should be done for the sake of the feet. Then the three pieces of the body should be washed with wine.
morphology: O Lord of the three parts of your body that have been destroyed by the evil deeds done by you for the sake of the feet repentance cleansing mercy truth and peace.

sanskrit: idānīm dharma pādaḥ te satyam nirvartayet yataḥ tam jighṛkṣati adharmaḥ ayam anṛtena edhitaḥ kaliḥ
reference: You are now standing on one leg only, which is your truthfulness, and you are somehow or other hobbling along. But quarrel personified [Kali], flourishing by deceit, is also trying to destroy that leg.
baseline: He should now follow the dharma and perform the truthful deeds. He would be punished for doing unrighteousness.
morphology: He should now follow the dharma and perform the truthful rites. He would be punished for doing unrighteousness.

sanskrit: iyam ca bhūmiḥ bhagavatā nyāsita uru bharā satī śrīmadbhiḥ tat pada nyāsaiḥ sarvataḥ kṛta kautukā
reference: The burden of the earth was certainly diminished by the Personality of Godhead and by others as well. When He was present as an incarnation, all good was performed because of His auspicious footprints.
baseline: This land should be given to the lord with the garland of āru and sāti. The same should be done everywhere with the guise of srimad.
morphology: This land is believed to be of the nature of the gods. It is said to be filled with water and made by Srimad with the belief of that position.

sanskrit: śocati aśru kalā sādhvī durbhagā iva ujjhitā satī abrahmaṇyāḥ nṛpa vyājāḥ śūdrāḥ bhokṣyanti mām iti
reference: Now she, the chaste one, being unfortunately forsaken by the Personality of Godhead, laments her future with tears in her eyes, for now she is being ruled and enjoyed by lower-class men who pose as rulers.
baseline: The sātī who is waking up like a poor sage with tears and sorrows would eat me with the vyādaṇas and the sudras.
morphology: O Sāti the goddess of tears and sorrows the sage of misfortune the wife of the god Avrahmanya the king of vyājas and the lord of sūdras eat me.

sanskrit: iti dharmam mahīm ca eva sāntvayitvā mahā rathaḥ niśātam ādade khaḍgam kalaye adharma hetave
reference: Mahārāja Parīkṣit, who could fight one thousand enemies single-handedly, thus pacified the personality of religion and the earth. Then he took up his sharp sword to kill the personality of Kali, who is the cause of all irreligion.
baseline: Having comforted the great chariot with the same dharma greatness one would get the sword of the king.
morphology: Having comforted the great chariot with the same dharma and greatness one should draw a sword at the same time.

sanskrit: tam jighāṁsum abhipretya vihāya nṛpa lāñchanam tat pāda mūlam śirasā samagāt bhaya vihvalaḥ
reference: When the personality of Kali understood that the King was willing to kill him, he at once abandoned the dress of a king and, under pressure of fear, completely surrendered to him, bowing his head.
baseline: Having said that one should not touch the feet and the head with fear.
morphology: Having said that one should not touch the head with the feet. One would be afraid to touch the feet with the head.

sanskrit: patitam pādayoḥ vīraḥ kṛpayā dīna vatsalaḥ śaraṇyaḥ na avadhīt ślokyaḥ āha ca idam hasan iva
reference: Mahārāja Parīkṣit, who was qualified to accept surrender and worthy of being sung in history, did not kill the poor surrendered and fallen Kali, but smiled compassionately, for he was kind to the poor.
baseline: A hero who has fallen down on his feet should be blessed with the grace of the god Vatsala. He should not be taken captive. The words aha haha are similar to haśana.
morphology: One who has fallen on the feet and is a hero should not fall on the path of the god Vatsala. He should not bow down to the gods.

sanskrit: rājā uvāca na te guḍākeśa yaśaḥ dharāṇām baddha añjaleḥ vai bhayam asti kiñcit na vartitavyam bhavatā kathañcana kṣetre madīye tvam adharma bandhuḥ
reference: The King thus said: We have inherited the fame of Arjuna; therefore since you have surrendered yourself with folded hands you need not fear for your life. But you cannot remain in my kingdom, for you are the friend of irreligion.
baseline: The king should say that he is not a friend of the king. He should not be afraid of the fear of the enemy. You should not do anything in any of the fields mentioned by him. You are the friend of iniquity.
morphology: The king should say that he is not afraid of the gods the gods and the gods of the earth. He should not behave in any way in any of the fields mentioned by you. You are a friend of lawlessness.

sanskrit: tvām vartamānam nara deva deheṣu anupravṛttaḥ ayam adharma pūgaḥ lobhaḥ anṛtam cauryam anāryam aṁhaḥ jyeṣṭhā ca māyā kalahaḥ ca dambhaḥ
reference: If the personality of Kali, irreligion, is allowed to act as a man-god or an executive head, certainly irreligious principles like greed, falsehood, robbery, incivility, treachery, misfortune, cheating, quarrel and vanity will abound.
baseline: One who is present in the body of a male god and who is circumventing the body is not good. One who has not been able to do any evil or evil should be called the superior. One with a brahminous ego should not do any crime. One should not be arrogant and fight with others.
morphology: One who is present in the body of a man a god a person who is circumscribed by the body one who is unrighteous who is greedy who has committed theft who does not want to do it who wants to do good and who is arrogant.

sanskrit: na vartitavyam tat adharma bandho dharmeṇa satyena ca vartitavye brahma āvarte yatra yajanti yajñaiḥ yajña īśvaram yajña vitāna vijñāḥ
reference: Therefore, O friend of irreligion, you do not deserve to remain in a place where experts perform sacrifices according to truth and religious principles for the satisfaction of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
baseline: One should not practice that which is bound up with unrighteousness righteousness and truth. One should practice Brahman in the circle where one has to offer sacrifices to God. One who has knowledge of the sacrifice should do so.
morphology: One should not practice that which is bound up with unrighteousness righteousness and truth. One should practice Brahman in the roundabout manner by offering sacrifices and offering sacrifices to God.

sanskrit: yasmin hariḥ bhagavān ijyamānaḥ ijya ātma mūrtiḥ yajatām śam tanoti kāmān amoghān sthira jaṅgamānām antaḥ bahiḥ vāyuḥ iva eṣaḥ ātmā
reference: In all sacrificial ceremonies, although sometimes a demigod is worshiped, the Supreme Lord Personality of Godhead is worshiped because He is the Supersoul of everyone, and exists both inside and outside like the air. Thus it is He only who awards all welfare to the worshiper.
baseline: Having given the image of the self to Hari the lord of the universe one would get the elixir of the soul. One would find the lusts in the body and the immortals standing in the air outside.
morphology: The image of the self should be given to the goddess Hari in which it is worshipped. The spirit should be made to feel the lusts and the elixir of the body. It should be fixed inside and out like the air.

sanskrit: sūtaḥ uvāca parīkṣitā evam ādiṣṭaḥ saḥ kaliḥ jāta vepathuḥ tam udyata asim āha idam daṇḍa pāṇim iva udyatam
reference: Śrī Sūta Gosvāmī said: The personality of Kali, thus being ordered by Mahārāja Parīkṣit, began to tremble in fear. Seeing the King before him like Yamarāja, ready to kill him, Kali spoke to the King as follows.
baseline: He should be tested by the thread. He would be called a kālī. The vapātha should be charged with the same punishment as the pāṇī.
morphology: He who is ordered to be tested with a thread should be made to stand on the path. He should be punished with the same punishment as the water.

sanskrit: kaliḥ uvāca yatra kva vā atha vatsyāmi sārva bhauma tava ājñayā lakṣaye tatra tatra api tvām ātta iṣu śarāsanam
reference: O Your Majesty, though I may live anywhere and everywhere under your order, I shall but see you with bow and arrows wherever I look.
baseline: O Kali one should say that wherever there is a place or a place of worship all the lands should be made as per your command and there also you should be placed in this seat.
morphology: O Kali wherever there is a place or place of worship I shall make all the places of worship as per your commandments. There also you should offer me the seat of worship.

sanskrit: tat me dharma bhṛtām śreṣṭha sthānam nirdeṣṭum arhasi yatra eva niyataḥ vatsye ātiṣṭhan te anuśāsanam
reference: Therefore, O chief amongst the protectors of religion, please fix some place for me where I can live permanently under the protection of your government.
baseline: That is the best place for me to worship. Wherever you wish to worship the priest you should teach them discipline.
morphology: That is why you should give me the righteousness and the superior position. Wherever you are staying in the place assigned to you they should be disciplined.

sanskrit: sūtaḥ uvāca abhyarthitaḥ tadā tasmai sthānāni kalaye dadau dyūtam pānam striyaḥ sūnā yatra adharmaḥ catuḥ vidhaḥ
reference: Sūta Gosvāmī said: Mahārāja Parīkṣit, thus being petitioned by the personality of Kali, gave him permission to reside in places where gambling, drinking, prostitution and animal slaughter were performed.
baseline: When the suit is said to have been made and the request is made to him he should be given the places of worship. The wife should drink water and the four kinds of worship should be done in the same manner.
morphology: The woman should drink water and drink water in four different ways in which there is iniquity.

sanskrit: punaḥ ca yācamānāya jāta rūpam adāt prabhuḥ tataḥ anṛtam madam kāmam rajaḥ vairam ca pañcamam
reference: The personality of Kali asked for something more, and because of his begging, the King gave him permission to live where there is gold because wherever there is gold there is also falsity, intoxication, lust, envy and enmity.
baseline: Then the lord would give the form of the beggar again. Then the king would have to pay a fine. The fifth is love and enmity.
morphology: Then the lord would give the form of the beggar again. Then the king would be pleased with the wine lust enmity and enmities.

sanskrit: amūni pañca sthānāni hi adharma prabhavaḥ kaliḥ auttareyeṇa dattāni nyavasat tat nideśa kṛt
reference: Thus the personality of Kali, by the directions of Mahārāja Parīkṣit, the son of Uttarā, was allowed to live in those five places.
baseline: The five places given by the king to the unbelievers are the five places. These are the places given to the king by the priest. These places are given as directions.
morphology: The five places given by the king of Adharma are five. These are the five places which are given by him.

sanskrit: atha etāni na seveta bubhūṣuḥ puruṣaḥ kvacit viśeṣataḥ dharma śīlaḥ rājā loka patiḥ guruḥ
reference: Therefore, whoever desires progressive well-being, especially kings, religionists, public leaders, brāhmaṇas and sannyāsīs, should never come in contact with the four above-mentioned irreligious principles.
baseline: Thus a man who does not serve these things would be a man of little faith. A king who is good at religion and a master would be the husband of the people.
morphology: The king the husband of the people the master the king and the king of righteousness should be worshipped in particular.

sanskrit: vṛṣasya naṣṭān trīn pādān tapaḥ śaucam dayām iti pratisandadhe āśvāsya mahīm ca samavardhayat
reference: Thereafter the King reestablished the lost legs of the personality of religion [the bull], and by encouraging activities he sufficiently improved the condition of the earth.
baseline: Having destroyed the bull the three legs should be done with penance defecation and mercy. In the same manner as in the opposite order one should be assured of victory and increase the greatness.
morphology: The three legs of a bull destroyed by the attack should be covered with the words of penance defilement mercy and peace.

sanskrit: saḥ eṣaḥ etarhi adhyāste āsanam pārthiva ucitam pitāmahena upanyastam rājñā araṇyam vivikṣatā āste adhunā saḥ rāja ṛṣiḥ kaurava indra śriyā ullasan gajāhvaye mahā bhāgaḥ cakravartī bṛhat śravāḥ
reference: The most fortunate emperor Mahārāja Parīkṣit, who was entrusted with the kingdom of Hastināpura by Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira when he desired to retire to the forest, is now ruling the world with great success due to his being glorified by the deeds of the kings of the Kuru dynasty.
baseline: The king should recite this poem with the forefathers the king sage Kauravas Indra Shriya Gājāva the great part of the king should be heard by the great sage.
morphology: The king should recite this poem with the forefathers and the king should say that the king is now a sage king sage and king king and king of Indra king of the king lord of the elephant king who is a great partaker and a great hearer.

sanskrit: ittham bhūta anubhāvaḥ ayam abhimanyu sutaḥ nṛpaḥ yasya pālayataḥ kṣauṇīm yūyam satrāya dīkṣitāḥ
reference: Mahārāja Parīkṣit, the son of Abhimanyu, is so experienced that by dint of his expert administration and patronage, it has been possible for you to perform a sacrifice such as this.
baseline: Thus the spirit of Abhimanyu should be worshipped by the king. You should be initiated into the house of Satra.
morphology: Thus the spirit feeling of Abhimanyu the son of Nripa the one whom you worship should be initiated into the house of Satra.

sanskrit: sūtaḥ uvāca yaḥ vai drauṇi astra vipluṣṭaḥ na mātuḥ udare mṛtaḥ anugrahāt bhagavataḥ kṛṣṇasya adbhuta karmaṇaḥ
reference: Śrī Sūta Gosvāmī said: Due to the mercy of the Personality of Godhead, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who acts wonderfully, Mahārāja Parīkṣit, though struck by the weapon of the son of Droṇa in his mother’s womb, could not be burned.
baseline: One who does not wear a weapon and does not defile the mothers abdomen and dies by grace would be able to perform the miracles of Lord Kṛṣṇa.
morphology: One who does not break the arms of a cow one who dies in the womb of his mother by the grace of the lord krsna should perform miracles.

sanskrit: brahma kopa utthitāt yaḥ tu takṣakāt prāṇa viplavāt na sammumoha uru bhayāt bhagavati arpita āśayaḥ
reference: Furthermore, Mahārāja Parīkṣit was always consciously surrendered to the Personality of Godhead, and therefore he was neither afraid nor overwhelmed by fear due to a snake-bird which was to bite him because of the fury of a brāhmaṇa boy.
baseline: One who has raised the anger of Brahman from the ground one who does not fight against the life of the enemy one should not be afraid of the spirit.
morphology: One who has raised the anger of Brahman from the ground one who does not revolve the soul from the earth and one who is not afraid of the spirit and the will of God.

sanskrit: utsṛjya sarvataḥ saṅgam vijñāta ajita saṁsthitiḥ vaiyāsakeḥ jahau śiṣyaḥ gaṅgāyām svam kalevaram
reference: Furthermore, after leaving all his associates, the King surrendered himself as a disciple to the son of Vyāsa [Śukadeva Gosvāmī], and thus he was able to understand the actual position of the Personality of Godhead, and at last gave up his material body on the bank of the Ganges.
baseline: The disciple should know the union of all things by worshipping him. He should be able to attain that position. One should worship him in the Ganges.
morphology: The disciple should know the union of all things by making offerings. He should attain the same position. He would then make his disciple walk in the Ganges.

sanskrit: na uttama śloka vārtānām juṣatām tat kathā amṛtam syāt sambhramaḥ anta kāle api smaratām tat pada ambujam
reference: This was so because those who have dedicated their lives to the transcendental topics of the Personality of Godhead, of whom the Vedic hymns sing, and who are constantly engaged in remembering the lotus feet of the Lord, do not run the risk of having misconceptions even at the last moment of their lives.
baseline: If the story is immortal and the words are not good the story should be remembered even at the end.
morphology: If the story is immortal and the words are not good the story should be remembered even in the last hour.

sanskrit: tāvat kaliḥ na prabhavet praviṣṭaḥ api iha sarvataḥ yāvat īśaḥ mahān urvyām ābhimanyavaḥ eka rāṭ
reference: As long as the great, powerful son of Abhimanyu remains the Emperor of the world, there is no chance that the personality of Kali will flourish.
baseline: Even if the kālī does not enter the lord it should be placed in all places as long as the Śiva is the great fertilizer and the others are one rat.
morphology: Then the kālī did not enter the lord even as far as it is concerned. One of the other gods would be a rat.

sanskrit: yasmin ahani yarhi eva bhagavān utsasarja gām tadā eva iha anuvṛttaḥ asau adharma prabhavaḥ kaliḥ
reference: The very day and moment the Personality of Godhead, Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, left this earth, the personality of Kali, who promotes all kinds of irreligious activities, came into this world.
baseline: One who does not do any work in the same way as the Lord would have done in the previous one would become the source of wealth. Then he would be able to do the same.
morphology: One who does not know the nature of the universe and who creates the source of life would become a god. He would then become a king.

sanskrit: na anudveṣṭi kalim samrāṭ sāram ga iva sāra bhuk kuśalāni āśu siddhyanti na itarāṇi kṛtāni yat
reference: Mahārāja Parīkṣit was a realist, like the bees who only accept the essence [of a flower]. He knew perfectly well that in this Age of Kali, auspicious things produce good effects immediately, whereas inauspicious acts must be actually performed [to render effects]. So he was never envious of the personality of Kali.
baseline: One who does not do evil deeds and does not know the essence of the king would be able to do good deeds.
morphology: One who does not do evil deeds and does not know the essence of the king one who is hungry for the benefits of the master and others would not be able to do so.

sanskrit: kim nu bāleṣu śūreṇa kalinā dhīra bhīruṇā apramattaḥ pramatteṣu yaḥ vṛkaḥ nṛṣu vartate
reference: Mahārāja Parīkṣit considered that less intelligent men might find the personality of Kali to be very powerful, but that those who are self-controlled would have nothing to fear. The King was powerful like a tiger and took care for the foolish, careless persons.
baseline: One who is a cowardly coward with a cow and a cowherd should be alert. The one who is in the herd should be careful.
morphology: One who is a cowardly coward with a cow a cowherd with a bull or a cow has to be alert. One who has a tree in his head should be careful.

sanskrit: upavarṇitam etat vaḥ puṇyam pārīkṣitam mayā vāsudeva kathā upetam ākhyānam yat apṛcchata
reference: O sages, as you did ask me, now I have described almost everything regarding the narrations about Lord Kṛṣṇa in connection with the history of the pious Mahārāja Parīkṣit.
baseline: This is described above and the virtues have been tested. I have heard the story of Vasudeva and the narration which has not been revealed.
