morphology: This has been described as good. I have seen the story of Vasudeva. The story of Vāsudeva is described as evil.

sanskrit: yāḥ yāḥ kathāḥ bhagavataḥ kathanīya uru karmaṇaḥ guṇa karma āśrayāḥ pumbhiḥ saṁsevyāḥ tāḥ bubhūṣubhiḥ
reference: Those who are desirous of achieving complete perfection in life must submissively hear all topics that are connected with the transcendental activities and qualities of the Personality of Godhead, who acts wonderfully.
baseline: The stories which the lord narrates should be told to the children of the gods. The virtues and deeds of the children should be worshipped by the devotees.
morphology: Those stories which are told by the Lord the qualities of the deeds done by him the works done by the devotees should be served by the gods.

sanskrit: ṛṣayaḥ ūcuḥ sūta jīva samāḥ saumya śāśvatīḥ viśadam yaśaḥ yaḥ tvam śaṁsasi kṛṣṇasya martyānām amṛtam hi naḥ
reference: The good sages said: O grave Sūta Gosvāmī! May you live many years and have eternal fame, for you are speaking very nicely about the activities of Lord Kṛṣṇa, the Personality of Godhead. This is just like nectar for mortal beings like us.
baseline: The sage the one who is born alive and living in the form of a son the man who is good and everlasting and who is able to heal you is not the immortal nectar of Krishna.
morphology: The sage who is high who lives in peace and who is everlasting who has been able to heal you who becomes the elixir of Krishna's death is not the same.

sanskrit: karmaṇi asmin anāśvāse dhūma dhūmra ātmanām bhavān āpāyayati govinda pāda padma āsavam madhu
reference: We have just begun the performance of this fruitive activity, a sacrificial fire, without certainty of its result due to the many imperfections in our action. Our bodies have become black from the smoke, but we are factually pleased by the nectar of the lotus feet of the Personality of Godhead, Govinda, which you are distributing.
baseline: In this action in the absence of breath you make the souls of the gods and the lotuses and honey by making them smoke.
morphology: In this action in the absence of breath you make the spirits of the gods and the lotus and honey.

sanskrit: tulayāma lavena api na svargam na apunaḥ bhavam bhagavat saṅgi saṅgasya martyānām kim uta āśiṣaḥ
reference: The value of a moment’s association with the devotee of the Lord cannot even be compared to the attainment of heavenly planets or liberation from matter, and what to speak of worldly benedictions in the form of material prosperity, which are for those who are meant for death.
baseline: Even with love one would not get heaven. One would not be blessed by the god. What is the merits of the association and death?
morphology: Even with the love one would not be able to compare heaven and heaven. You would be like the god the companion of the company and the mortal beings. What is the blessing.

sanskrit: kaḥ nāma tṛpyet rasa vit kathāyām mahat tama ekānta parāyaṇasya na antam guṇānām aguṇasya jagmuḥ yoga īśvarāḥ ye bhava pādma mukhyāḥ
reference: The Personality of Godhead, Lord Kṛṣṇa [Govinda], is the exclusive shelter for all great living beings, and His transcendental attributes cannot even be measured by such masters of mystic powers as Lord Śiva and Lord Brahmā. Can anyone who is expert in relishing nectar [rasa] ever be fully satiated by hearing topics about Him?
baseline: One who has not been blessed with the name of the great god should not be singled out by the king. One who does not possess the qualities and the fire one who is the master of the world should be worshipped by the gods of yoga.
morphology: One who has not been blessed with the name the words of the king the greatness of the story the loneliness the absence of the qualities the fire the jagmu yoga the gods the chief among you are the feet.

sanskrit: tat naḥ bhavān vai bhagavat pradhānaḥ mahat tama ekānta parāyaṇasya hareḥ udāram caritam viśuddham śuśrūṣatām naḥ vitanotu vidvan
reference: O Sūta Gosvāmī, you are a learned and pure devotee of the Lord because the Personality of Godhead is your chief object of service. Therefore please describe to us the pastimes of the Lord, which are above all material conception, for we are anxious to receive such messages.
baseline: That is not the same as that of the lord the chief lord great lord lonely lord greedy lord generous lord pure lord minister sage noble lord wise man should not be sold.
morphology: That is not the same as that of the lord the chief one the great one one who is alone the king of the enemy the noble one those who are not good and those who do not care for the pure one should be sent to the learned.

sanskrit: saḥ vai mahā bhāgavataḥ parīkṣit yena apavarga ākhyam adabhra buddhiḥ jñānena vaiyāsaki śabditena bheje khaga indra dhvaja pāda mūlam
reference: O Sūta Gosvāmī, please describe those topics of the Lord by which Mahārāja Parīkṣit, whose intelligence was fixed on liberation, attained the lotus feet of the Lord, who is the shelter of Garuḍa, the king of birds. Those topics were vibrated by the son of Vyāsa [Śrīla Śukadeva].
baseline: He should be judged by the great Bhagavata that is known as a vāgarga. He should know the wisdom of a vaiṣaka. He would be called the flag of Indra.
morphology: He should be judged by the great Bhagavata that is called the category of evil. He should know the wisdom of evil and sound the flag of Indra.

sanskrit: tat naḥ param puṇyam asaṁvṛta artham ākhyānam ati adbhuta yoga niṣṭham ākhyāhi ananta ācarita upapannam pārīkṣitam bhāgavata abhirāmam
reference: Thus please narrate to us the narrations of the Unlimited, for they are purifying and supreme. They were spoken to Mahārāja Parīkṣit, and they are very dear to the pure devotees, being full of bhakti-yoga.
baseline: That is the supreme virtue. that is the meaning of the narration. that of the most wonderful yoga. that which is said to be faithful. that that which has been done without end. that one who has experienced the manifestation of the divine abhiraṇa.
morphology: The meaning of the above virtues is said to be excellent. The description is very wonderful. The narration is said as devotion. The exposition is done without ceasing. The preceptor is known to be the supreme god.

sanskrit: sūtaḥ uvāca aho vayam janma bhṛtaḥ adya ha āsma vṛddha anuvṛttyā api viloma jātāḥ dauṣkulyam ādhim vidhunoti śīghram mahat tamānām abhidhāna yogaḥ
reference: Śrī Sūta Gosvāmī said: O God, although we are born in a mixed caste, we are still promoted in birthright simply by serving and following the great who are advanced in knowledge. Even by conversing with such great souls, one can without delay cleanse oneself of all disqualifications resulting from lower births.
baseline: The sūtā states that one who gives birth to a son one who becomes old and becomes obese even after the continuation of the yogic practice becomes weak and widows become weak. One who does this will soon attain greatness.
morphology: The sutta says that one who has given birth to a child and today becomes obese even after having grown old becomes obnoxious becomes weak and widowed and becomes ill soon.

sanskrit: kutaḥ punaḥ gṛṇataḥ nāma tasya mahat tama ekānta parāyaṇasya yaḥ ananta śaktiḥ bhagavān anantaḥ mahat guṇatvāt yam anantam āhuḥ
reference: And what to speak of those who are under the direction of the great devotees, chanting the holy name of the Unlimited, who has unlimited potency? The Personality of Godhead, unlimited in potency and transcendental by attributes, is called Ananta [Unlimited].
baseline: The greatness of that which has been taken away from him is called the greatness. The great power of the Lord is called to be infinite. That which is infinite is called infinite by the great quality.
morphology: The greatness of that which has been taken away from him is called the greatness. The great power of the Lord is called infinite. That which is endowed with great qualities is called eternal.

sanskrit: etāvatā alam nanu sūcitena guṇaiḥ asāmya anati śāyanasya hitvā itarān prārthayataḥ vibhūtiḥ yasya aṅghri reṇum juṣate anabhīpsoḥ
reference: It is now ascertained that He [the Personality of Godhead] is unlimited and there is none equal to Him. Consequently no one can speak of Him adequately. Great demigods cannot obtain the favor of the goddess of fortune even by prayers, but this very goddess renders service unto the Lord, although He is unwilling to have such service.
baseline: Having thus described the alam one should not be ashamed of the merits of the bed and pray to others. One who has the power to do so would be pleased by the invocation of the king.
morphology: Having thus described the alam one should not be ashamed of the qualities mentioned in it. One who invokes others for the sake of his wellbeing would be blessed with the glory of the king.

sanskrit: atha api yat pāda nakha avasṛṣṭam jagat viriñca upahṛta arhaṇa ambhaḥ sa īśam punāti anyatamaḥ mukundāt kaḥ nāma loke bhagavat pada arthaḥ
reference: Who can be worthy of the name of the Supreme Lord but the Personality of Godhead, Śrī Kṛṣṇa? Brahmājī collected the water emanating from the nails of His feet in order to award it to Lord Śiva as a worshipful welcome. This very water [the Ganges] is purifying the whole universe, including Lord Śiva.
baseline: One who does not know the meaning of the word bhāgavādvā means one who is born without the feet nails hands feet arms arms and hands.
morphology: One who does not know the meaning of the word bhāgavā means one who is born out of the muṇukundas who is the name of the people and who is worshipped by the Lord.

sanskrit: yatra anuraktāḥ sahasā eva dhīrāḥ vyapohya deha ādiṣu saṅgam ūḍham vrajanti tat pārama haṁsyam antyam yasmin ahiṁsā upaśamaḥ sva dharmaḥ
reference: Self-controlled persons who are attached to the Supreme Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa can all of a sudden give up the world of material attachment, including the gross body and subtle mind, and go away to attain the highest perfection of the renounced order of life, by which nonviolence and renunciation are consequential.
baseline: Where the protector suddenly disappears from the body he should go to the other side of the body. That is the end of the fight in which the relief would be achieved by doing the abhinaya is his dharma.
morphology: Where the protector suddenly becomes impenetrable and the body becomes united with others the end of the battle is achieved by the end. The relief obtained by doing so is his own dharma.

sanskrit: aham hi pṛṣṭaḥ aryamaṇaḥ bhavadbhiḥ ācakṣe ātma avagamaḥ atra yāvān nabhaḥ patanti ātma samam patattriṇaḥ tathā samam viṣṇu gatim vipaścitaḥ
reference: O ṛṣis, who are as powerfully pure as the sun, I shall try to describe to you the transcendental pastimes of Viṣṇu as far as my knowledge is concerned. As the birds fly in the sky as far as their capacity allows, so do the learned devotees describe the Lord as far as their realization allows.
baseline: One who has fallen down on the earth should be made to fall on the ground with the help of āyāma pāṭha aryāmana aśvatmā aṣvāṇa viṣṇu vipāṣṭrīna sāmā and vīśnu.
morphology: O Śiva you are the one who brings forth the self in the sky. Those who fall here are equal to the self those who fall down from the ground and those who move away from the path of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: ekadā dhanuḥ udyamya vicaran mṛgayām vane mṛgān anugataḥ śrāntaḥ kṣudhitaḥ tṛṣitaḥ bhṛśam jala āśayam acakṣāṇaḥ praviveśa tam āśramam dadarśa munim āsīnam śāntam mīlita locanam
reference: Once upon a time Mahārāja Parīkṣit, while engaged in hunting in the forest with bow and arrows, became extremely fatigued, hungry and thirsty while following the stags. While searching for a reservoir of water, he entered the hermitage of the well-known Śamīka Ṛṣi and saw the sage sitting silently with closed eyes.
baseline: Once the bow has wandered and wandered in the forest following the deer one who is hungry after having suffered from hunger and having had no water should enter the hermitage. The sage should be seated in the dādarshana seat and calm and calm.
morphology: Once the bow has moved and wandered in the wilderness following the deer one who is hungry hungry has not had enough water and enters the hermitage of the sage sitting in the serenity of his seat and having found the lotus.

sanskrit: pratiruddha indriya prāṇa manaḥ buddhim upāratam sthāna trayāt param prāptam brahma bhūtam avikriyam
reference: The muni’s sense organs, breath, mind and intelligence were all restrained from material activities, and he was situated in a trance apart from the three [wakefulness, dream and unconsciousness], having achieved a transcendental position qualitatively equal with the Supreme Absolute.
baseline: The mind sense mind mind and intellect are opposed to the three elements of Brahman.
morphology: The mind the mind and the senses are opposed to each other. The Brahman that is found above the three places is known as Bhūta.

sanskrit: viprakīrṇa jaṭa ācchannam rauraveṇa ajinena ca viśuṣyat tāluḥ udakam tathā bhūtam ayācata
reference: The sage, in meditation, was covered by the skin of a stag, and long, compressed hair was scattered all over him. The King, whose palate was dry from thirst, asked him for water.
baseline: The jāta should be covered with a thick cloth and the palate should be washed with the rauvaṇa and ajīna. The same is said to be the udaka.
morphology: The pitchers should be made to be covered with a thread of water and the palate should be covered by fire. The palms should be kept open and the ghost should be asked for.

sanskrit: alabdha tṛṇa bhūmi ādiḥ asamprāpta arghya sūnṛtaḥ avajñātam iva ātmānam manyamānaḥ cukopa ha
reference: The King, not received by any formal welcome by means of being offered a seat, place, water and sweet addresses, considered himself neglected, and so thinking he became angry.
baseline: The land of the grass which has not been tilled should be offered to the poor. It should be given as a gift and the soul should be considered as a matter of disobedience.
morphology: The land of the grass which has not been tilled should be given to the poor. The land which has been offered to them after having been made barren should be considered as a matter of disobedience.

sanskrit: abhūta pūrvaḥ sahasā kṣut tṛḍbhyām ardita ātmanaḥ brāhmaṇam prati abhūt brahman matsaraḥ manyuḥ eva ca
reference: O brāhmaṇas, the circumstances having distressed him with extreme hunger and thirst, the King directed toward the sage his anger and envy, which he had never before directed toward a brāhmaṇa.
baseline: The self should be worshipped with the prāmana prāśa and the three prāṣas suddenly. The Brahman should be envied by the Brahmana.
morphology: One who has made an attempt to destroy the Brahman would become envious of him by suddenly making an attempt at the east the east and the south.

sanskrit: saḥ tu brahma ṛṣeḥ aṁse gata asum uragam ruṣā vinirgacchan dhanuḥ koṭyā nidhāya puram āgataḥ
reference: While leaving, the King, being so insulted, picked up a lifeless snake with his bow and angrily placed it on the shoulder of the sage. Then he returned to his palace.
baseline: He should go to the city of Brahma and the sage Avirga. The sage should be worshipped with a bow and bows and come to the town.
morphology: He should go to the city of Brahma and the sage Avirga. The sage should be worshipped with a bow and bows and come to the town.

sanskrit: eṣaḥ kim nibhṛta aśeṣa karaṇaḥ mīlita īkṣaṇaḥ mṛṣā samādhiḥ āho svit kim nu syāt kṣatra bandhubhiḥ
reference: Upon returning, he began to contemplate and argue within himself whether the sage had actually been in meditation, with senses concentrated and eyes closed, or whether he had just been feigning trance just to avoid receiving a lower kṣatriya.
baseline: What is this and what is the ultimate cause of death. What is the illusion of the body of the deceased whether it is a grave or not? What is it? What should be done by the relatives of the kṣatra.
morphology: What is this and what is the limitless amount of money. What is the amount of wealth that is left in the earth. What should happen to the body of the son of the king? What is it? What should be done to him?

sanskrit: tasya putraḥ ati tejasvī viharan bālakaḥ arbhakaiḥ rājñā agham prāpitam tātam śrutvā tatra idam abravīt
reference: The sage had a son who was very powerful, being a brāhmaṇa’s son. While he was playing with inexperienced boys, he heard of his father’s distress, which was occasioned by the King. Then and there the boy spoke as follows.
baseline: His son became very bright and the boy got the king's favour from the children. Having heard of it he said that he should go there.
morphology: His son became very bright and the boy got the king's favour from the children. He heard that the king got it from him.

sanskrit: aho adharmaḥ pālānām pīvnām bali bhujām iva svāmini agham yat dāsānām dvāra pānām śunām iva
reference: [The brāhmaṇa’s son, Śṛṅgi, said:] O just look at the sins of the rulers who, like crows and watchdogs at the door, perpetrate sins against their masters, contrary to the principles governing servants.
baseline: O Adharma the sacrifice of the Palas the servants the brethren and the servants should be offered to the lord as the bhuja.
morphology: O Adharma the sacrifice of the Palas and the Peavas should be offered to the lord as the bhuja. The door of the servants should be made open and the hearth should be heard.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇaiḥ kṣatra bandhuḥ hi gṛha pālaḥ nirūpitaḥ saḥ katham tat gṛhe dvāḥ sthaḥ sa bhāṇḍam bhoktum arhati
reference: The descendants of the kingly orders are definitely designated as watchdogs, and they must keep themselves at the door. On what grounds can dogs enter the house and claim to dine with the master on the same plate?
baseline: A brahmin who is a ksatra and a kinsman should be placed in the same house as a pāla. He should sit in that house twice and eat the food.
morphology: A brahmin who is a relative of a ksatra and a guardian of a house should be told how he can eat the bhaṇḍa by staying in that house for two days.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇe gate bhagavati śāstari utpatha gāminām tat bhinna setūn adya aham śāsmi paśyata me balam
reference: After the departure of Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Personality of Godhead and supreme ruler of everyone, these upstarts have flourished, our protector being gone. Therefore I myself shall take up this matter and punish them. Just witness my power.
baseline: Having gone to Kṛṣṇa the scripture of the gods and having created the villages and having built them separately today I see that I am strong.
morphology: Having gone to Krsna the scriptures of the gods have created the villages. Today I see the strength.

sanskrit: iti uktvā roṣa tāmra akṣaḥ vayasyān ṛṣi bālakaḥ kauśikī āpaḥ upaspṛśya vāk vajram visasarja ha
reference: The son of the ṛṣi, his eyes red-hot with anger, touched the water of the River Kauśika while speaking to his playmates and discharged the following thunderbolt of words.
baseline: Having said this one should say that the sage should be of age copper axe boy cowherd ape and the king should touch the diamond.
morphology: Having said this one should say that the sage of old age should be the axis of copper. One who touches a boy a man of skill a person who has spoken a word should give a diamond.

sanskrit: iti laṅghita maryādam takṣakaḥ saptame ahani daṅkṣyati sma kula aṅgāram coditaḥ me tata druham
reference: The brāhmaṇa’s son cursed the King thus: On the seventh day from today a snake-bird will bite the most wretched one of that dynasty [Mahārāja Parīkṣit] because of his having broken the laws of etiquette by insulting my father.
baseline: The seventh person who has violated this honor would be called a cow. He would get the sumptuous amount of blood. Then he would get it.
morphology: The seventh ego of the king is said to have violated this honor. He should be beaten with the axe and then he should be thrown into the pit.

sanskrit: tataḥ abhyetya āśramam bālaḥ gale sarpa kalevaram pitaram vīkṣya duḥkha ārtaḥ mukta kaṇṭhaḥ ruroda ha
reference: Thereafter, when the boy returned to the hermitage, he saw a snake on his father’s shoulder, and out of his grief he cried very loudly.
baseline: Then after having visited the hermitage the boy saw the serpent kalavara in the throat and the father. He heard the sound of sorrow and the voice of free speech.
morphology: Then after having visited the hermitage the boy saw the serpent kalavara in the throat and the father. He heard the sound of sorrow and the voice of free speech.

sanskrit: saḥ vai āṅgirasaḥ brahman śrutvā suta vilāpanam unmīlya śanakaiḥ netre dṛṣṭvā ca aṁse mṛta uragam
reference: O brāhmaṇas, the ṛṣi, who was born in the family of Aṅgirā Muni, hearing his son crying, gradually opened his eyes and saw the dead snake around his neck.
baseline: He would then hear the voice of Brahman and hear the sound of the cow and see it in the eyes of the bulls.
morphology: He should also hear the voice of Brahman from the angiras who are asleep who wail in the eyes of cows and who see the dead osprey.

sanskrit: visṛjya tam ca papraccha vatsa kasmāt hi rodiṣi kena vā te apakṛtam iti uktaḥ saḥ nyavedayat
reference: He threw the dead snake aside and asked his son why he was crying, whether anyone had done him harm. On hearing this, the son explained to him what had happened.
baseline: Having thrown him away he should ask him why he cried or said that he had done wrong.
morphology: Having thrown him away he should ask him why he cried or said that he had done wrong.

sanskrit: niśamya śaptam atat arham nara indram saḥ brāhmaṇaḥ na ātma jam abhyanandat aho bata aṁhaḥ mahat adya te kṛtam alpīyasi drohe uruḥ damaḥ dhṛtaḥ
reference: The father heard from his son that the King had been cursed, although he should never have been condemned, for he was the best amongst all human beings. The ṛṣi did not congratulate his son, but, on the contrary, began to repent, saying: Alas! What a great sinful act was performed by my son. He has awarded heavy punishment for an insignificant offense.
baseline: The brahmin who did not worship the self should be cursed with the words ārtha man and īndra. He should not be worshipped with the word aha vata abhyāra. Today he has done a little treachery.
morphology: O Brahmana he who does not worships the self should be cursed with the words ārtha man and Indra. He should not worship the self. He would not do great deeds. He did such a thing today. He had done a little treachery.

sanskrit: na vai nṛbhiḥ nara devam para ākhyam sammātum arhasi avipakva buddhe yat tejasā durviṣaheṇa guptāḥ vindanti bhadrāṇi akutaḥ bhayāḥ prajāḥ
reference: O my boy, your intelligence is immature, and therefore you have no knowledge that the king, who is the best amongst human beings, is as good as the Personality of Godhead. He is never to be placed on an equal footing with common men. The citizens of the state live in prosperity, being protected by his unsurpassable prowess.
baseline: One who does not know the nature of the gods and men without knowing them would not be able to understand them. The wise man would tell the wise men and the people without fear that the Guptas would be poisoned by the evil spirits.
morphology: The king should not speak of a male god without the knowledge of the other gods. He would not be able to speak to the wise man. The guptas would speak of the evil poison with the brilliance and evil poison. The noble men would be afraid.

sanskrit: alakṣyamāṇe nara deva nāmni ratha aṅga pāṇau ayam aṅga lokaḥ tadā hi caura pracuraḥ vinaṅkṣyati arakṣyamāṇaḥ avivarūtha vat kṣaṇāt
reference: My dear boy, the Lord, who carries the wheel of a chariot, is represented by the monarchical regime, and when this regime is abolished the whole world becomes filled with thieves, who then at once vanquish the unprotected subjects like scattered lambs.
baseline: The chariot the body the limbs the head and the body of the king should be left unattended. Then the charioteer would lose a great deal of his body and the king would become impotent.
morphology: The chariot should be called Nāradeva in the absence of the king the king of the chariots should be worshipped in the presence of the lord. Then the king would be destroyed by a great number of thieves.

sanskrit: tat adya naḥ pāpam upaiti ananvayam yat naṣṭa nāthasya vasoḥ vilumpakāt parasparam ghnanti śapanti vṛñjate paśūn striyaḥ arthān puru dasyavaḥ janāḥ
reference: Due to the termination of the monarchical regimes and the plundering of the people’s wealth by rogues and thieves, there will be great social disruptions. People will be killed and injured, and animals and women will be stolen. And for all these sins we shall be responsible.
baseline: That would not be a sin today. If the servants of the lord were to be destroyed they would harm each other with the arrow and curse the men women men robbers and men.
morphology: That would not be a sin today. The enemies of the enemy would destroy the enemy. They would harm each other with the arrow. The men would destroy animals women men robbers and people.

sanskrit: tadā ārya dharmaḥ pravilīyate nṛṇām varṇa āśrama ācāra yutaḥ trayī mayaḥ tataḥ artha kāma abhiniveśita ātmanām śunām kapīnām iva varṇa saṅkaraḥ
reference: At that time the people in general will fall systematically from the path of a progressive civilization in respect to the qualitative engagements of the castes and the orders of society and the Vedic injunctions. Thus they will be more attracted to economic development for sense gratification, and as a result there will be an unwanted population on the level of dogs and monkeys.
baseline: Then the ārya dharma is revealed as the three colours of the gods. The three forms of the goddess may be described as the kāmā and the three forms are described as having the same colour as the sūna and kāpīs.
morphology: Then the dharma of the Aryans is revealed. Then the karna of the niras should be divided into three parts. The kāmā should be defined as the kāma of the soul and the kapīna of the sun.

sanskrit: dharma pālaḥ nara patiḥ saḥ tu samrāṭ bṛhat śravāḥ sākṣāt mahā bhāgavataḥ rāja ṛṣiḥ haya medhayāṭ kṣut tṛṭ śrama yutaḥ dīnaḥ na eva asmat śāpam arhati
reference: The Emperor Parīkṣit is a pious king. He is highly celebrated and is a first-class devotee of the Personality of Godhead. He is a saint amongst royalty, and he has performed many horse sacrifices. When such a king is tired and fatigued, being stricken with hunger and thirst, he does not at all deserve to be cursed.
baseline: A man who is the husband of a man who does not practice righteousness a sage who is a great son of a king and a great devotee of a great sage would not be able to bear the curse of a poor man if he does not do good deeds.
morphology: The husband of a man who is a follower of dharma the king of the great sages the sage of the king the great god of the world the wise man the poor man who does not do any work and who does no evil should be cursed.

sanskrit: apāpeṣu sva bhṛtyeṣu bālena apakva buddhinā pāpam kṛtam tat bhagavān sarva ātmā kṣantum arhati
reference: Then the ṛṣi prayed to the all-pervading Personality of Godhead to pardon his immature boy, who had no intelligence and who committed the great sin of cursing a person who was completely free from all sins, who was subordinate and who deserved to be protected.
baseline: One who commits a sin on the part of his servants in the form of an unclean child with an unintelligent mind would be able to forgive all souls.
morphology: One who commits a sin by doing evil in the presence of his servants with a child without understanding would be forgiven by the Lord.

sanskrit: tiraḥ kṛtāḥ vipralabdhāḥ śaptāḥ kṣiptāḥ hatāḥ api na asya tat pratikurvanti tat bhaktāḥ prabhavaḥ api hi
reference: The devotees of the Lord are so forbearing that even though they are defamed, cheated, cursed, disturbed, neglected or even killed, they are never inclined to avenge themselves.
baseline: One who has made the arrow and made it fall from the ground and has made a curse and killed it would not be able to bear the loss of that devotee.
morphology: Those who do not worship the gods and the gods of the world are not harmed by the evil spirits.

sanskrit: iti putra kṛta aghena saḥ anutaptaḥ mahā muniḥ svayam viprakṛtaḥ rājñā na eva agham tat acintayat
reference: The sage thus regretted the sin committed by his own son. He did not take the insult paid by the King very seriously.
baseline: Having said this the great sage repented that his son had done this. The king did not think that he should do this.
morphology: Having made such a son agha he repented and the great sage thought that the king should not be the king.

sanskrit: prāyaśaḥ sādhavaḥ loke paraiḥ dvandveṣu yojitāḥ na vyathanti na hṛṣyanti yataḥ ātmā aguṇa āśrayaḥ
reference: Generally the transcendentalists, even though engaged by others in the dualities of the material world, are not distressed. Nor do they take pleasure [in worldly things], for they are transcendentally engaged.
baseline: Often people who are good and do not agree with others on the issues will not suffer and will not be harmed because the soul is not safe.
morphology: Often people who are good and do not get involved in disputes with others do not suffer. They do not lose their souls and take refuge in fire.

sanskrit: sūtaḥ uvāca mahī patiḥ tu atha tat karma garhyam vicintayan ātma kṛtam su durmanāḥ aho mayā nīcam anārya vat kṛtam nirāgasi brahmaṇi gūḍha tejasi
reference: Śrī Sūta Gosvāmī said: While returning home, the King [Mahārāja Parīkṣit] felt that the act he had committed against the faultless and powerful brāhmaṇa was heinous and uncivilized. Consequently he was distressed.
baseline: O Sūtā the husband of the mother the wife of the wife the mind of the self the actions taken by the husband the evil ones oh my god the unholy ones the illiterate Brahman the secret manifestation of the spirit.
morphology: O Sūta the husband of the mother the wife of the wife the mother of the husband and the wife should do the same thing. The soul should be thought of as evil. O Brahman the secret manifestation of the self the evil one the one who has done evil the other who is evil and has said that he is innocent.

sanskrit: dhruvam tataḥ me kṛta deva helanāt duratyayam vyasanam na ati dīrghāt tat astu kāmam hi agha niṣkṛtāya me yathā na kuryām punaḥ evam addhā
reference: [King Parīkṣit thought:] Due to my neglecting the injunctions of the Supreme Lord I must certainly expect some difficulty to overcome me in the near future. I now desire without reservation that the calamity come now, for in this way I may be freed of the sinful action and not commit such an offense again.
baseline: Then the pole should be removed from the seat of the deity. The attachment should not be too long. The desire should be taken out. The action should be repeated as if it were not done.
morphology: Then the pole should be removed from the seat of the deity. The attachment should not be too long. The desire should be kept at the same distance. Then I should not do it again.

sanskrit: adya eva rājyam balam ṛddha kośam prakopita brahma kula analaḥ me dahatu abhadrasya punaḥ na me abhūt pāpīyasī dhīḥ dvija deva gobhyaḥ
reference: I am uncivilized and sinful due to my neglect of brahminical culture, God consciousness and cow protection. Therefore I wish that my kingdom, strength and riches burn up immediately by the fire of the brāhmaṇa’s wrath so that in the future I may not be guided by such inauspicious attitudes.
baseline: Today the kingdom has become strong and the corpse has been burnt. Then I will burn the unclean one again. I will not be able to bear the sinful cow.
morphology: Today the kingdom should be strengthened and the corpse should be burnt with the brahmā kula analāla. If I do not burn the unclean cow again I will not be able to bear the sinful cow.

sanskrit: saḥ cintayan ittham atha aśṛṇot yathā muneḥ suta uktaḥ nirṛtiḥ takṣaka ākhyaḥ saḥ sādhu mene na cireṇa takṣaka analam prasaktasya virakti kāraṇam
reference: While the King was thus repenting, he received news of his imminent death, which would be due to the bite of a snake-bird, occasioned by the curse spoken by the sage’s son. The King accepted this as good news, for it would be the cause of his indifference toward worldly things.
baseline: He should think about this and then repeat the same thing as said in the foreword. He should say tākṣa. He would not accept the sādhu. The reason for the distortion is that he would not be able to do so.
morphology: He thought of this and said that he would not be able to do so. He would not accept the sādhu and would not do it.

sanskrit: atho vihāya imam amum ca lokam vimarśitau heyatayā purastāt kṛṣṇa aṅghri sevām adhimanyamānaḥ upāviśat prāyam amartya nadyām
reference: Mahārāja Parīkṣit sat down firmly on the banks of the Ganges to concentrate his mind in Kṛṣṇa consciousness, rejecting all other practices of self-realization, because transcendental loving service to Kṛṣṇa is the greatest achievement, superseding all other methods.
baseline: Having left the earth and discussed the world together with these two things one should say that Krishna should serve the unbroken people in front of him. He should sit on the river Amartya for some time.
morphology: Having left this place the people should be discussed. Having said this Lord Krishna should sit on the river of Amartya for the rest of his life.

sanskrit: yā vai lasat śrī tulasī vimiśra kṛṣṇa aṅghri reṇu abhyadhika ambu netrī punāti lokān ubhayatra sa īśān kaḥ tām na seveta mariṣyamāṇaḥ
reference: The river [by which the King sat to fast] carries the most auspicious water, which is mixed with the dust of the lotus feet of the Lord and tulasī leaves. Therefore that water sanctifies the three worlds inside and outside and even sanctifies Lord Śiva and other demigods. Consequently everyone who is destined to die must take shelter of this river.
baseline: Whichever one is lost Śrī tulsi vimṛṣa kṛṣṇa angrī renu abhīdhi ambu nirāṇī the king of the two worlds will be killed without having served him.
morphology: Whichever one is lost Śrī tulsi vimṛṣa kṛṣṇa angrī renu abhīdhi ambu nirāṇī who will serve the people and who will not serve him.

sanskrit: iti vyavacchidya saḥ pāṇḍaveyaḥ prāya upaveśam prati viṣṇu padyām dadhau mukunda aṅghrim ananya bhāvaḥ muni vrataḥ mukta samasta saṅgaḥ
reference: Thus the King, the worthy descendant of the Pāṇḍavas, decided once and for all and sat on the Ganges’ bank to fast until death and give himself up to the lotus feet of Lord Kṛṣṇa, who alone is able to award liberation. So, freeing himself from all kinds of associations and attachments, he accepted the vows of a sage.
baseline: Having said this he should say the words of Viṣṇu to the Pandavas and then fast for the rest of the day. He should offer the vow of Mukunda Angrī the unique vow of the sage and observe the fast for all the company.
morphology: Having explained this he should recite the verse of Viṣṇu to the Pandavas and then fast for the rest of the day. He should offer the vow of Mukunda Angrī Anākāṇī Sage and the whole association should be liberated.

sanskrit: tatra upajagmuḥ bhuvanam punānāḥ mahā anubhāvāḥ munayaḥ sa śiṣyāḥ prāyeṇa tīrtha abhigama apadeśaiḥ svayam hi tīrthāni punanti santaḥ
reference: At that time all the great minds and thinkers, accompanied by their disciples, and sages who could verily sanctify a place of pilgrimage just by their presence, arrived there on the plea of making a pilgrim’s journey.
baseline: There the disciple should be reincarnated in the form of the subjunctive form the earth the great senses the sages the disciples the ancient ones and the devotees. The disciples themselves would be reacquainted with the teachings of the sage.
morphology: One who has made a great experience by worshipping the gods there and the sages the disciples the ancient ones the sage and the saints would return to the holy places with the instructions to enter the sacred places of worship.

sanskrit: atriḥ to nāradaḥ
reference: From different parts of the universe there arrived great sages like Atri, Cyavana, Śaradvān, Ariṣṭanemi, Bhṛgu, Vasiṣṭha, Parāśara, Viśvāmitra, Aṅgirā, Paraśurāma, Utathya, Indrapramada, Idhmavāhu, Medhātithi, Devala, Ārṣṭiṣeṇa, Bhāradvāja, Gautama, Pippalāda, Maitreya, Aurva, Kavaṣa, Kumbhayoni, Dvaipāyana and the great personality Nārada.
baseline: Here is Narada.
morphology: Here is Narada.

sanskrit: anye ca devarṣi brahmarṣi varyāḥ rājarṣi varyāḥ aruṇa ādayaḥ ca nānā ārṣeya pravarān sametān abhyarcya rājā śirasā vavande
reference: There were also many other saintly demigods, kings and special royal orders called aruṇādayas [a special rank of rājarṣis] from different dynasties of sages. When they all assembled together to meet the Emperor [Parīkṣit], he received them properly and bowed his head to the ground.
baseline: The other gods brahmarshi varīsī rajārsī varāsī and arūna adyā are worshipped together with the prophets.
morphology: The other gods brahmarshi vārya rajarshi and aruna the king of the kingdom of Adyāya and the king should be worshipped along with the prophets in the vavandana.

sanskrit: sukha upaviṣṭeṣu atha teṣu bhūyaḥ kṛta praṇāmaḥ sva cikīrṣitam yat vijñāpayām āsa vivikta cetāḥ upasthitaḥ agre abhigṛhīta pāṇiḥ
reference: After all the ṛṣis and others had seated themselves comfortably, the King, humbly standing before them with folded hands, told them of his decision to fast until death.
baseline: Having made offerings to the gods sitting in the well one should know that one who is separated from others and present in front of him should be worshipped.
morphology: Having worshipped the gods sitting in the well one should know that he is attracted to them. One who is present in a place of his own choice should be informed by the disciple. One should take Pāṇī further.

sanskrit: rājā uvāca aho vayam dhanya tamāḥ nṛpāṇām mahat tama anugrahaṇīya śīlāḥ rājñām kulam brāhmaṇa pāda śaucāt dūrāt visṛṣṭam bata garhya karma
reference: The fortunate King said: Indeed, we are the most grateful of all the kings who are trained to get favors from the great souls. Generally you [sages] consider royalty as refuse to be rejected and left in a distant place.
baseline: The king should say oh we are blessed. The great men of the king should bless the king. Having said that the king's clan should be separated from the brahmin feet.
morphology: The king said oh we are blessed. The king's clan should be described as brahminous and spread far away from the feet of the king.

sanskrit: tasya eva me aghasya parā avara īśaḥ vyāsakta cittasya gṛheṣu abhīkṣṇam nirveda mūlaḥ dvija śāpa rūpaḥ yatra prasaktaḥ bhayam āśu dhatte
reference: The Supreme Personality of Godhead, the controller of both the transcendental and mundane worlds, has graciously overtaken me in the form of a brāhmaṇa’s curse. Due to my being too much attached to family life, the Lord, in order to save me, has appeared before me in such a way that only out of fear I will detach myself from the world.
baseline: One who is not aware of the nature of the two forms of curses should be placed in the houses of the mind. One who does not know the origin of the evil forms should be put in the house of the spirit. One whose fear is present in the form of a double curse should be removed immediately.
morphology: One who is above that and above that of agha one who is separated from the other and who is in the houses of the mind and whose root is undefiled and whose form is the double curse and where fear is present is immediately destroyed.

sanskrit: tam mā upayātam pratiyantu viprāḥ gaṅgā ca devī dhṛta cittam īśe dvija upasṛṣṭaḥ kuhakaḥ takṣakaḥ vā daśatu alam gāyata viṣṇu gāthāḥ
reference: O brāhmaṇas, just accept me as a completely surrendered soul, and let mother Ganges, the representative of the Lord, also accept me in that way, for I have already taken the lotus feet of the Lord into my heart. Let the snake-bird — or whatever magical thing the brāhmaṇa created — bite me at once. I only desire that you all continue singing the deeds of Lord Viṣṇu.
baseline: One who does not worship the gods Viṣṇu Ganga Dhrutī Chitta Esha Dwijaka Kuṣakā Takshaka and others should sing the hymn of Viśṇu.
morphology: One who does not worship the goddess Viṣṇu Ganga dhrutī chita Śiva the pitchers the elves the kuṣakas or the eloquent elves should recite the alam.

sanskrit: punaḥ ca bhūyāt bhagavati anante ratiḥ prasaṅgaḥ ca tat āśrayeṣu mahatsu yām yām upayāmi sṛṣṭim maitrī astu sarvatra namaḥ dvijebhyaḥ
reference: Again, offering obeisances unto all you brāhmaṇas, I pray that if I should again take my birth in the material world I will have complete attachment to the unlimited Lord Kṛṣṇa, association with His devotees and friendly relations with all living beings.
baseline: Then again one should worship the gods of the two worlds. One should worship them in the sanctuaries the great places of worship the creation friendship friendship etc..
morphology: Then again one should worship the divine god Ananta the goddess of the earth the king of the world the great goddess of refuge the creation of the universe friendship friendship and friendship.

sanskrit: iti sma rājā adhyavasāya yuktaḥ prācīna mūleṣu kuśeṣu dhīraḥ udaṅ mukhaḥ dakṣiṇa kūle āste samudra patnyāḥ sva suta nyasta bhāraḥ
reference: In perfect self-control, Mahārāja Parīkṣit sat down on a seat of straw, with straw-roots facing the east, placed on the southern bank of the Ganges, and he himself faced the north. Just previously he had given charge of his kingdom over to his son.
baseline: The king is said to be adamant and courageous in the corners of the ancient city. He should face the sea on the right bank. The wife should carry the burden on her bed.
morphology: The king is said to be adamant and courageous in the corners of the ancient city. The king should be on the right bank of the sea and his wife should be carried by him.

sanskrit: evam ca tasmin nara deva deve prāya upaviṣṭe divi deva saṅghāḥ praśasya bhūmau vyakiran prasūnaiḥ mudā muhuḥ dundubhayaḥ ca neduḥ
reference: Thus the King, Mahārāja Parīkṣit, sat to fast until death. All the demigods of the higher planets praised the King’s actions and in pleasure continually scattered flowers over the earth and beat celestial drums.
baseline: In this way the male gods and goddesses would often be seated in the same place. The group of gods would be divided into two parts. The king would be pleased with the land and the king would not be afraid of evil.
morphology: In this way the male gods and goddesses would often be seated in the same place. The group of gods would be divided into two parts. The king would be pleased with the land and the king would not be afraid of evil.

sanskrit: maharṣayaḥ vai samupāgatāḥ ye praśasya sādhu iti anumodamānāḥ ūcuḥ prajā anugraha śīla sārāḥ yat uttama śloka guṇa abhirūpam
reference: All the great sages who were assembled there also praised the decision of Mahārāja Parīkṣit, and they expressed their approval by saying “Very good.” Naturally the sages are inclined to do good to common men, for they have all the qualitative powers of the Supreme Lord. Therefore they were very much pleased to see Mahārāja Parīkṣit, a devotee of the Lord, and they spoke as follows.
baseline: The great sages who come to us are considered to be virtuous. The noble people who accept us as the saints are known to be blessed with good scriptures.
morphology: The great sages who come to us and who are accepted as the saints of the country the noble people the virtuous people those who are blessed with grace and all that is good the qualities of the shlokas are manifest in us.

sanskrit: na vā idam rājarṣi varya citram bhavatsu kṛṣṇam samanuvrateṣu ye adhyāsanam rāja kirīṭa juṣṭam sadyaḥ jahuḥ bhagavat pārśva kāmāḥ
reference: [The sages said:] O chief of all the saintly kings of the Pāṇḍu dynasty who are strictly in the line of Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa! It is not at all astonishing that you give up your throne, which is decorated with the helmets of many kings, to achieve eternal association with the Personality of Godhead.
baseline: The image of the king should not be drawn by the king sage lord kṛṣṇa and those who are sitting on the throne king crown lord and other objects.
morphology: The image of the king should not be drawn by the king the king and the king who are sitting on the throne and the crown.

sanskrit: sarve vayam tāvat iha āsmahe atha kalevaram yāvat asau vihāya lokam param virajaskam viśokam yāsyati ayam bhāgavata pradhānaḥ
reference: We shall all wait here until the foremost devotee of the Lord, Mahārāja Parīkṣit, returns to the supreme planet, which is completely free from all mundane contamination and all kinds of lamentation.
baseline: All of us should be worshipped as far as possible. The chief deity of the universe would be the world without us and the universe without us.
morphology: All of us should be worshipped as long as we are present. The Lord will be the chief devotee of the world.

sanskrit: āśrutya tat ṛṣi gaṇa vacaḥ parīkṣit samam madhu cyut guru ca avyalīkam ābhāṣata enān abhinandya yuktān śuśrūṣamāṇaḥ caritāni viṣṇoḥ
reference: All that was spoken by the great sages was very sweet to hear, full of meaning and appropriately presented as perfectly true. So after hearing them, Mahārāja Parīkṣit, desiring to hear of the activities of Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Personality of Godhead, congratulated the great sages.
baseline: Having recited the scriptures the sage should be examined and given equal amount of honey. The master should praise them and call them unbelievers. The disciples should be worshipped by Lord Viṣṇu.
morphology: Having recited the scriptures the sage should be examined and given equal amount of honey. The master should greet them with the words abhilikā. The disciples should be worshipped by the god Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: samāgatāḥ sarvataḥ eva sarve vedāḥ yathā mūrti dharāḥ tri pṛṣṭhe na iha atha na amutra ca kaścana arthaḥ ṛte para anugraham ātma śīlam
reference: The King said: O great sages, you have all very kindly assembled here, having come from all parts of the universe. You are all as good as supreme knowledge personified, who resides in the planet above the three worlds [Satyaloka]. Consequently you are naturally inclined to do good to others, and but for this you have no interest, either in this life or in the next.
baseline: All the Vedas are the same in all respects. The image is placed on the three sides. It has no meaning. It is not the son of the mother. It gives grace and self-righteousness.
morphology: All the vedas should be worshipped in the same way as the idol the ground and the three sides. It does not have any meaning. It has no meaning except grace and self-righteousness.

sanskrit: tataḥ ca vaḥ pṛcchyam imam vipṛcche viśrabhya viprāḥ iti kṛtyatāyām sarva ātmanā mriyamāṇaiḥ ca kṛtyam śuddham ca tatra āmṛśata abhiyuktāḥ
reference: O trustworthy brāhmaṇas, I now ask you about my immediate duty. Please, after proper deliberation, tell me of the unalloyed duty of everyone in all circumstances, and specifically of those who are just about to die.
baseline: Then one should ask the accused to do the same by resting in the abode of the gods. He should do it with all the spirits and those who are dying and are pure.
morphology: Then he should ask the accused who had committed the act of killing all the souls by doing the same by the rest of the world and the dead.

sanskrit: tatra abhavat bhagavān vyāsa putraḥ yadṛcchayā gām aṭamānaḥ anapekṣaḥ alakṣya liṅgaḥ nija lābha tuṣṭaḥ vṛtaḥ ca bālaiḥ avadhūta veṣaḥ
reference: At that moment there appeared the powerful son of Vyāsadeva, who traveled over the earth disinterested and satisfied with himself. He did not manifest any symptoms of belonging to any social order or status of life. He was surrounded with women and children, and he dressed as if others had neglected him.
baseline: The son of the god Vyāsa was born there. Having not considered the choice of the gāma and the subject the linga would be pleased with his gain and would be disguised as having been possessed by boys.
morphology: The son of the god Vyāsa became there. Having ignored the desire of the cow the lord got his advantage and the linga became pleased with him. He was disguised as a boy.

sanskrit: tam dvi aṣṭa varṣam su kumāra pāda kara ūru bāhu aṁsa kapola gātram cāru āyata akṣa unnasa tulya karṇa subhru ānanam kambu sujāta kaṇṭham
reference: This son of Vyāsadeva was only sixteen years old. His legs, hands, thighs, arms, shoulders, forehead and the other parts of his body were all delicately formed. His eyes were beautifully wide, and his nose and ears were highly raised. He had a very attractive face, and his neck was well formed and beautiful like a conchshell.
baseline: Then the feet of the kumara should be eight years long and the arms should be four cubits long and equal to the height of the axes.
morphology: The feet of the kumara should be two to eight years long. The arms should be four cubits long and the ears should be equal to the height of the axes. The ears should have the shape of four cubit. The neck should be eight cubits wide.

sanskrit: nigūḍha jatrum pṛthu tuṅga vakṣasam āvarta nābhim vali valgu udaram ca dik ambaram vaktra vikīrṇa keśam pralamba bāhum su amara uttama ābham
reference: His collarbone was fleshy, his chest broad and thick, his navel deep and his abdomen beautifully striped. His arms were long, and curly hair was strewn over his beautiful face. He was naked, and the hue of his body reflected that of Lord Kṛṣṇa.
baseline: The outer part of the body should be covered with a deep jatrum. The inner part should cover the chest with a thread the navel with a string the belly with a ring the abdomen with a piece of hair spread out in the direction of the mouth and the outer part with the arms.
morphology: The outer part of the body should be covered with a piece of cloth covering the chest with the thread the navel the neck the abdomen the forehead the arms with the hair spread out by the speaker and the arms.

sanskrit: śyāmam sadā apīvya vayaḥ aṅga lakṣmyā strīṇām manaḥ jñam rucira smitena pratyutthitāḥ te munayaḥ sva āsanebhyaḥ tat lakṣaṇa jñāḥ api gūḍha varcasam
reference: He was blackish and very beautiful due to his youth. Because of the glamor of his body and his attractive smiles, he was pleasing to women. Though he tried to cover his natural glories, the great sages present there were all expert in the art of physiognomy, and so they honored him by rising from their seats.
baseline: Having always worshipped Śyama one should know the heart of the women with the limbs laksmī those sages who are pleased with the beauty of their seats and who have been resurrected with the spirit.
morphology: Having always worshipped the goddess Śyama one should know the heart of the women with the limbs lakshmī and those sages who are pleased with the beauty of their seats and who have been resurrected with the grace.

sanskrit: saḥ viṣṇu rātaḥ atithaye āgatāya tasmai saparyām śirasā ājahāra tataḥ nivṛttāḥ hi abudhāḥ striyaḥ arbhakāḥ mahā āsane sa upaviveśa pūjitaḥ
reference: Mahārāja Parīkṣit, who is also known as Viṣṇurāta [one who is always protected by Viṣṇu], bowed his head to receive the chief guest, Śukadeva Gosvāmī. At that time all the ignorant women and boys ceased following Śrīla Śukadeva. Receiving respect from all, Śukadeva Gosvāmī took his exalted seat.
baseline: He came with the guest Viṣṇu for the night and worshipped him with the head around him. Then he retired. He sat down in the great seat with the naked women and children.
morphology: He came to the guest of Vishnu in the night and worshipped him with the head around him. Then he retired. He sat down in the great seat for the women and children.

sanskrit: saḥ saṁvṛtaḥ tatra mahān mahīyasām brahmarṣi rājarṣi devarṣi saṅghaiḥ vyarocata alam bhagavān yathā induḥ graha ṛkṣa tārā nikaraiḥ parītaḥ
reference: Śukadeva Gosvāmī was then surrounded by saintly sages and demigods just as the moon is surrounded by stars, planets and other heavenly bodies. His presence was gorgeous, and he was respected by all.
baseline: He would be able to do so. There would be great brahmins kings gods sages confederations elites and gods. The gods would be like the gods of the earth and the stars.
morphology: The great Brahma the king the queen the lord of gods and the confederations should be worshipped there.

sanskrit: praśāntam āsīnam akuṇṭha medhasam munim nṛpaḥ bhāgavataḥ abhyupetya praṇamya mūrdhnā avahitaḥ kṛta añjaliḥ natvā girā sūnṛtayā anvapṛcchat
reference: The sage Śrī Śukadeva Gosvāmī sat perfectly pacified, intelligent and ready to answer any question without hesitation. The great devotee, Mahārāja Parīkṣit, approached him, offered his respects by bowing before him, and politely inquired with sweet words and folded hands.
baseline: Having worshipped the Supreme Being with the prasanta the seat the intellect the sage the lord of the universe the god of the earth the king of the world the chiefly one should bow down with the bow and bow with the head. Having kneeled down the goddess should be worshipped with the sun.
morphology: Having worshipped the Supreme Being with the prasanta the seat the mind the sage the lord of the universe and the god of the world the priest bowed down with the bow and bowed his head with the head and the head of the goddess Gīrāna.

sanskrit: parīkṣit uvāca aho adya vayam brahman sat sevyāḥ kṣatra bandhavaḥ kṛpayā atithi rūpeṇa bhavadbhiḥ tīrthakāḥ kṛtāḥ
reference: The fortunate King Parīkṣit said: O brāhmaṇa, by your mercy only, you have sanctified us, making us like unto places of pilgrimage, all by your presence here as my guest. By your mercy, we, who are but unworthy royalty, become eligible to serve the devotee.
baseline: The testor said oh today we are brahmins. The servants of the kṣṭraṇas and their relatives should please make you pilgrims as guests.
morphology: The testor said oh today we are brahmins. The servants of the Kshatriyas and their relatives should please make you pilgrims as guests.

sanskrit: yeṣām saṁsmaraṇāt puṁsām sadyaḥ śuddhyanti vai gṛhāḥ kim punaḥ darśana sparśa pāda śauca āsana ādibhiḥ
reference: Simply by our remembering you, our houses become instantly sanctified. And what to speak of seeing you, touching you, washing your holy feet and offering you a seat in our home?
baseline: The houses of those who have been worshipped with the recitation of the sāmya and purify themselves for the time being should be visited again with the touch feet toilet etc.
morphology: Those houses which are now purified by the recollection of their good deeds should be visited again. Do they touch the feet wash the feet etc.

sanskrit: sānnidhyāt te mahā yogin pātakāni mahānti api sadyaḥ naśyanti vai puṁsām viṣṇoḥ iva sura itarāḥ
reference: Just as the atheist cannot remain in the presence of the Personality of Godhead, so also the invulnerable sins of a man are immediately vanquished in your presence, O saint! O great mystic!
baseline: Those great yogis who are in the presence of the gods and who have been destroyed by the forces of Mahāyogī are said to be as good as those of Viṣṇu.
morphology: The great yogis who are in the presence of the great gods and the great men of the world are destroyed by the presence. They are like the sound of Vishnu.

sanskrit: api me bhagavān prītaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ pāṇḍu suta priyaḥ paitṛ svaseya prīti artham tat gotrasya ātta bāndhavaḥ
reference: Lord Kṛṣṇa, the Personality of Godhead, who is very dear to the sons of King Pāṇḍu, has accepted me as one of those relatives just to please His great cousins and brothers.
baseline: Then one who loves the lord Śeśṇa the Pandu the Sūta the Pāita one who is beloved by himself and who is a friend of that tribe.
morphology: Then one who loves the lord  one who is a Pandu a son a beloved son and one who has affection for others in his own way means one who enjoys the friends of that tribe.

sanskrit: anyathā te avyakta gateḥ darśanam naḥ katham nṛṇām nitarām mriyamāṇānām saṁsiddhasya vanīyasaḥ
reference: Otherwise [without being inspired by Lord Kṛṣṇa] how is it that you have voluntarily appeared here, though you are moving incognito to the common man and are not visible to us who are on the verge of death?
baseline: Otherwise they would have gone into obscurity. One would not have seen the figures of men who had died in the night. One who had been killed would have achieved success.
morphology: If they are not known to be true how can they not be known to the king and the king of the dead.

sanskrit: ataḥ pṛcchāmi saṁsiddhim yoginām paramam gurum puruṣasya iha yat kāryam mriyamāṇasya sarvathā
reference: You are the spiritual master of great saints and devotees. I am therefore begging you to show the way of perfection for all persons, and especially for one who is about to die.
baseline: Therefore one should ask the supreme master for the accomplishment of all things and for the attainment of perfection for the person who dies.
morphology: Therefore one should ask the supreme master to accomplish all the achievements of the yogis and the actions of the man who dies.

sanskrit: yat śrotavyam atho japyam yat kartavyam nṛbhiḥ prabho smartavyam bhajanīyam vā brūhi yad vā viparyayam
reference: Please let me know what a man should hear, chant, remember and worship, and also what he should not do. Please explain all this to me.
baseline: One should listen to what is said and chant it. One should remember the Lord with the forefathers and worship him or vice versa.
morphology: One should listen to the voice of the Lord and chant the hymns. One should remember the Lord with the hands and worship him or the other.

sanskrit: nūnam bhagavataḥ brahman gṛheṣu gṛha medhinām na lakṣyate hi avasthānam api go dohanam kvacit
reference: O powerful brāhmaṇa, it is said that you hardly stay in the houses of men long enough to milk a cow.
baseline: One would not notice the presence of gods brahmins houses maidens and cows.
morphology: One would not notice the presence of gods brahmins houses maidens and cows in the houses.

sanskrit: sūtaḥ uvāca evam ābhāṣitaḥ pṛṣṭaḥ saḥ rājñā ślakṣṇayā girā pratyabhāṣata dharma jñaḥ bhagavān bādarāyaṇiḥ
reference: Śrī Sūta Gosvāmī said: The King thus spoke and questioned the sage, using sweet language. Then the great and powerful personality, the son of Vyāsadeva, who knew the principles of religion, began his reply.
baseline: Having said so the king should be made to speak with a gentle mouth. Having known his righteousness he should speak to the king.
morphology: Having said so the king should be rebuked with a gentle gesture. Having known the righteousness of the king he should speak to the king.

sanskrit: śrī śukaḥ uvāca varīyān eṣaḥ te praśnaḥ kṛtaḥ loka hitam nṛpa ātmavit sammataḥ puṁsām śrotavya ādiṣu yaḥ paraḥ
reference: Śrī Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: My dear King, your question is glorious because it is very beneficial to all kinds of people. The answer to this question is the prime subject matter for hearing, and it is approved by all transcendentalists.
baseline: The lord Śūkā said that he had asked the superior men to do good to the people. He would listen to the preceptors who would do good for the soul.
morphology: The lord Śiva said that he had asked the superior men to do good to the people. He should listen to them in the preceptors who had agreed to do well for him.

sanskrit: śrotavya ādīni rājendra nṛṇām santi sahasraśaḥ apaśyatām ātma tattvam gṛheṣu gṛha medhinām
reference: Those persons who are materially engrossed, being blind to the knowledge of ultimate truth, have many subject matters for hearing in human society, O Emperor.
baseline: Having heard the words of the ancient king Rajendra one should observe the principle of the self in the houses.
morphology: One should hear the words of the ancient king Śrīṇḍā who is the master of a thousand gods. One should observe the principle of the self in the houses and houses.

sanskrit: nidrayā hriyate naktam vyavāyena ca vā vayaḥ divā ca artha īhayā rājan kuṭumba bharaṇena vā
reference: The lifetime of such an envious householder is passed at night either in sleeping or in sex indulgence, and in the daytime either in making money or maintaining family members.
baseline: A king is destroyed by sleep or by the act of marriage or by a divine act. This means that the king should be destroyed by the maintenance of the family.
morphology: The king is destroyed by sleep by the destruction of property and by the occupation of property or by the maintenance of the family.

sanskrit: deha apatya kalatra ādiṣu ātma sainyeṣu asatsu api teṣām pramattaḥ nidhanam paśyan api na paśyati
reference: Persons devoid of ātma-tattva do not inquire into the problems of life, being too attached to the fallible soldiers like the body, children and wife. Although sufficiently experienced, they still do not see their inevitable destruction.
baseline: One would not see the death of the sons of the body and the forces of the self in the beginning even if one had seen their greatness.
morphology: One who has left the body and left behind the body would not see the death of the chief among the forces of the spirit.

sanskrit: tasmāt bhārata sarvātmā bhagavān īśvaraḥ hariḥ śrotavyaḥ kīrtitavyaḥ ca smartavyaḥ ca icchatā abhayam
reference: O descendant of King Bharata, one who desires to be free from all miseries must hear about, glorify and also remember the Personality of Godhead, who is the Supersoul, the controller and the savior from all miseries.
baseline: Therefore one would like to hear the whole of India the Supreme Self the Lord of all beings the gods and to be praised and remembered.
morphology: Therefore one would like to hear the whole of India the Supreme Self the Lord of all beings the lord of all gods and to be praised and remembered.

sanskrit: etāvān sāṅkhya yogābhyām sva dharma pariniṣṭhayā janma lābhaḥ paraḥ puṁsām ante nārāyaṇa smṛtiḥ
reference: The highest perfection of human life, achieved either by complete knowledge of matter and spirit, by practice of mystic powers, or by perfect discharge of occupational duty, is to remember the Personality of Godhead at the end of life.
baseline: After having performed these yogic practices with devotion to one's own religion one would get the benefits of birth. At the end of the day one would be able to attain the benefits.
morphology: After having performed these many yogic practices one would get the benefits of birth by being faithful to one's own religion. At the end of the day one would be able to attain the benefits.

sanskrit: prāyeṇa munayaḥ rājan nivṛttāḥ vidhi ṣedhataḥ nairguṇya sthāḥ ramante sma guṇa anukathane hareḥ
reference: O King Parīkṣit, mainly the topmost transcendentalists, who are above the regulative principles and restrictions, take pleasure in describing the glories of the Lord.
baseline: The king who is a sage by the time of his death ceases to be a ruler. He who is not good enough to do good deeds should return to his native place. He should be blessed with good qualities.
morphology: The king who is a sage in the olden days and has retired from the course of his life should be mercilessly placed in the righteous places.

sanskrit: idam bhāgavatam nāma purāṇam brahma sammitam adhītavān dvāpara ādau pituḥ dvaipāyanāt aham
reference: At the end of the Dvāpara-yuga, I studied this great supplement of Vedic literature named Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, which is equal to all the Vedas, from my father, Śrīla Dvaipāyana Vyāsadeva.
baseline: This bhāgavatam the name of the Purāṇa the Brahmana and the other two are said to be the two aspects of the dual nature of the father.
morphology: This bhāgavatam the name of the Purāṇa the Brahmana and the other two are the two aspects of the universe.

sanskrit: pariniṣṭhitaḥ api nairguṇye uttama śloka līlayā gṛhīta cetāḥ rājarṣe ākhyānam yat adhītavān
reference: O saintly King, I was certainly situated perfectly in transcendence, yet I was still attracted by the delineation of the pastimes of the Lord, who is described by enlightened verses.
baseline: The king who had made the statement by the king should be taken with the leela and the good scripture should be done in the pure form even if he had been obedient.
morphology: The king should be able to narrate the story even if he is pure and has taken a good verse with lila.

sanskrit: tat aham te abhidhāsyāmi mahā pauruṣikaḥ bhavān yasya śraddadhatām āśu syāt mukunde matiḥ satī
reference: That very Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam I shall recite before you because you are the most sincere devotee of Lord Kṛṣṇa. One who gives full attention and respect to hearing Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam achieves unflinching faith in the Supreme Lord, the giver of salvation.
baseline: That is what I shall say to those great men who have been worshipped by you. The one whom you have worshipped should be worshipped in the forehead.
morphology: That is what I shall say to you. You are a great citizen and you should be known by the name of the chief minister. You should be worshipped by me.

sanskrit: etat nirvidyamānānām icchatām akutaḥ bhayam yoginām nṛpa nirṇītam hareḥ nāma anu kīrtanam
reference: O King, constant chanting of the holy name of the Lord after the ways of the great authorities is the doubtless and fearless way of success for all, including those who are free from all material desires, those who are desirous of all material enjoyment, and also those who are self-satisfied by dint of transcendental knowledge.
baseline: This is the wish of those who are not living. The fear of the yogis should be determined by the priest. The name of the lord is mentioned as Hare.
morphology: This is the wish of those who are not living. The fear is determined by the yogis. One should chant the name of the lord hāre.

sanskrit: kim pramattasya bahubhiḥ parokṣaiḥ hāyanaiḥ iha varam muhūrtam viditam ghaṭate śreyase yataḥ
reference: What is the value of a prolonged life which is wasted, inexperienced by years in this world? Better a moment of full consciousness, because that gives one a start in searching after his supreme interest.
baseline: What happens to the prāmata with many indirect things and the muhurta is known to be a boon. It is said to be good.
morphology: What happens to the preceptor with many indirect actions and with the hymns. This boon is known to happen at the time of the muhurta.

sanskrit: khaṭvāṅgaḥ nāma rāja ṛṣiḥ jñātvā iyattām iha āyuṣaḥ muhūrtāt sarvam utsṛjya gatavān abhayam harim
reference: The saintly King Khaṭvāṅga, after being informed that the duration of his life would be only a moment more, at once freed himself from all material activities and took shelter of the supreme safety, the Personality of Godhead.
baseline: Having known the name of the king the sage the king of the khatvāṅga has said that after having removed everything from the muhurta of the month of ayūṣa he should go to the abode of Hari.
morphology: Having known the name of the king the sage khatvāṅga one should know that after having exhorted everything from the muhurta of this life one should go to the abode of Hari.

sanskrit: tava api etarhi kauravya saptāham jīvita avadhiḥ upakalpaya tat sarvam tāvat yat sāmparāyikam
reference: Mahārāja Parīkṣit, now your duration of life is limited to seven more days, so during this time you can perform all those rituals which are needed for the best purpose of your next life.
baseline: You should also observe this week as the living period and all that is common to you.
morphology: You should also prepare a week for the same period of life and all that is common to you.

sanskrit: anta kāle tu puruṣaḥ āgate gata sādhvasaḥ chindyāt asaṅga śastreṇa spṛhām dehe anu ye ca tam
reference: At the last stage of one’s life, one should be bold enough not to be afraid of death. But one must cut off all attachment to the material body and everything pertaining to it and all desires thereof.
baseline: In the last hour the man should go ahead and cut off the sādhvasa with the weapon of the unarmed man and the body of the man who has not been able to do so.
morphology: In the last hour the man should go ahead and cut off the sādhvasa with the weapon of the unarmed part of the body.

sanskrit: gṛhāt pravrajitaḥ dhīraḥ puṇya tīrtha jala āplutaḥ śucau vivikte āsīnaḥ vidhivat kalpita āsane
reference: One should leave home and practice self-control. In a sacred place he should bathe regularly and sit down in a lonely place duly sanctified.
baseline: Having departed from the house one should do the ritual sitting in the seat of the knower in the holy place with water and water.
morphology: Having departed from the house one who is courageous having blessed the holy place with water sitting in a clean place and sitting in the seat should be done as per the custom.

sanskrit: abhyaset manasā śuddham tri vṛt brahma akṣaram param manaḥ yacchet jita śvāsaḥ brahma bījam avismaran
reference: After sitting in the above manner, make the mind remember the three transcendental letters [a-u-m], and by regulating the breathing process, control the mind so as not to forget the transcendental seed.
baseline: The mind should be pure and the three letters of the Brahman scripture should be mentioned above. The breath should be won. The seed of Brahman should be forgotten.
morphology: The mind should be pure and the three letters of Brahman should be mentioned above. The heart should be known as the winning breath. The seed of Brahma should be forgotten.

sanskrit: niyacchet viṣayebhyaḥ akṣān manasā buddhi sārathiḥ manaḥ karmabhiḥ ākṣiptam śubha arthe dhārayet dhiyā
reference: Gradually, as the mind becomes progressively spiritualized, withdraw it from sense activities, and by intelligence the senses will be controlled. The mind too absorbed in material activities can be engaged in the service of the Personality of Godhead and become fixed in full transcendental consciousness.
baseline: The mind should be directed to the objects and the mind should bear the illusion of the mind and the conduct of the heart in a good sense.
morphology: The mind should be directed to the objects and the mind should hold the objects in good sense by the actions of the master.

sanskrit: tatra eka avayavam dhyāyet avyucchinnena cetasā manaḥ nirviṣayam yuktvā tataḥ kiñcana na smaret padam tat paramam viṣṇoḥ manaḥ yatra prasīdati
reference: Thereafter, you should meditate upon the limbs of Viṣṇu, one after another, without being deviated from the conception of the complete body. Thus the mind becomes free from all sense objects. There should be no other thing to be thought upon. Because the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Viṣṇu, is the Ultimate Truth, the mind becomes completely reconciled in Him only.
baseline: One should meditate on one of the parts therein. One should not think about the subject matter of the mind without being conscious and then remember the position of the Supreme Being. The mind of Lord Viṣṇu would be pleased with that position.
morphology: One should meditate on one of the parts therein. One should not think about the subject matter of the mind without having thought about it. Then one should not remember the position where the mind of the Supreme Lord Viṣṇu is pleased.

sanskrit: rajaḥ tamobhyām ākṣiptam vimūḍham manaḥ ātmanaḥ yacchet dhāraṇayā dhīraḥ hanti yā tat kṛtam malam
reference: One’s mind is always agitated by the passionate mode of material nature and bewildered by the ignorant mode of nature. But one can rectify such conceptions by the relation of Viṣṇu and thus become pacified by cleansing the dirty things created by them.
baseline: The king who has made a fool of the mind by the use of the tāmā and by holding on to that which he has made will kill the brave man.
morphology: One who has made a fool of the mind and the soul by holding on to the king the king and the king of the kingdom and the goddess Tamā is killed by the brave man.

sanskrit: yasyām sandhāryamāṇāyām yoginaḥ bhakti lakṣaṇaḥ āśu sampadyate yogaḥ āśrayam bhadram īkṣataḥ
reference: O King, by this system of remembrance and by being fixed in the habit of seeing the all-good personal conception of the Lord, one can very soon attain devotional service to the Lord, under His direct shelter.
baseline: The yogis who possess the same qualities of devotion and wealth are said to be good.
morphology: The qualities of devotion of the yogis in the presence of which they are situated are as follows. The wealth of the people is obtained from the same. The shelter is made from the good.

sanskrit: rājā uvāca yathā sandhāryate brahman dhāraṇā yatra sammatā yādṛśī vā haret āśu puruṣasya manaḥ malam
reference: The fortunate King Parīkṣit, inquiring further, said: O brāhmaṇa, please describe in full detail how and where the mind has to be applied and how the conception can be fixed so that the dirty things in a person’s mind can be removed.
baseline: The king would say that the mind of a man should be destroyed as if he had accepted the concept of Brahman.
morphology: The king should say that the mind of a man should be destroyed as if he had accepted the concept of Brahman.

sanskrit: śrī śukaḥ uvāca jita āsanaḥ jita śvāsaḥ jita saṅgaḥ jita indriyaḥ sthūle bhagavataḥ rūpe manaḥ sandhārayet dhiyā
reference: Śukadeva Gosvāmī answered: One should control the sitting posture, regulate the breathing process by the yogic prāṇāyāma and thus control the mind and senses and with intelligence apply the mind to the gross potencies of the Lord [called the virāṭ-rūpa].
baseline: O Śrī Śuṇa one who has conquered the seat won the breath conquered the association conquered sense organs and has established the mind in the form of the Supreme Lord.
morphology: O Śrī Śuṇa the seat of victory the breath of victory and the association of the senses should be established in the form of God.

sanskrit: viśeṣaḥ tasya dehaḥ ayam sthaviṣṭhaḥ ca sthavīyasām yatra idam vyajyate viśvam bhūtam bhavyam bhavat ca sat
reference: This gigantic manifestation of the phenomenal material world as a whole is the personal body of the Absolute Truth, wherein the universal resultant past, present and future of material time is experienced.
baseline: The body of that particular person should be placed on the ground and the place where it is placed should be described as the universe the world the universe and the universe.
morphology: The body of a person is said to be standing on the ground and the world is saidto be great.

sanskrit: aṇḍa kośe śarīre asmin sapta āvaraṇa saṁyute vairājaḥ puruṣaḥ yaḥ asau bhagavān dhāraṇā āśrayaḥ
reference: The gigantic universal form of the Personality of Godhead, within the body of the universal shell, which is covered by sevenfold material elements, is the subject for the virāṭ conception.
baseline: A man who is the king of a kingdom and who has the belief in the lord should take refuge in the seven mantles of the body in the egg shell.
morphology: The king who is the king of the kingdom and who has taken refuge in the belief of the lord should cover the body with seven layers in the egg shell.

sanskrit: pātālam etasya hi pāda mūlam paṭhanti pārṣṇi prapade rasātalam mahātalam viśva sṛjaḥ atha gulphau talātalam vai puruṣasya jaṅghe
reference: Persons who have realized it have studied that the planets known as Pātāla constitute the bottoms of the feet of the universal Lord, and the heels and the toes are the Rasātala planets. The ankles are the Mahātala planets, and His shanks constitute the Talātala planets.
baseline: The feet of this person are recited at the base of the ground. The sides of the earth are described as having the rasāṭla form. The world is created as the gulphu form of the base.
morphology: The feet of this person are the base of the path. The sides of the river are the mainsides. The great path is the path of the universe. The path of a man is the bridge of the bottom.

sanskrit: dve jānunī sutalam viśva mūrteḥ ūru dvayam vitalam ca atalam ca mahītalam tat jaghanam mahīpate nabhastalam nābhi saraḥ gṛṇanti
reference: The knees of the universal form are the planetary system of the name Sutala, and the two thighs are the Vitala and Atala planetary systems. The hips are Mahītala, and outer space is the depression of His navel.
baseline: The two janunee sutras are taken by the lord of the world the ūrva sūrtas the vītala the atala and the māhyata. The navel is taken from the celestial body by the king.
morphology: The two jāṇuni sutras are the image of the universe the two vītla and the ātalam. The outermost part of the body is the abode of the earth. The upper part of it is the navel.

sanskrit: uraḥ sthalam jyotiḥ anīkam asya grīvā mahaḥ vadanam vai janaḥ asya tapaḥ varāṭīm viduḥ ādi puṁsaḥ satyam tu śīrṣāṇi sahasra śīrṣṇaḥ
reference: The chest of the Original Personality of the gigantic form is the luminary planetary system, His neck is the Mahar planets, His mouth is the Janas planets, and His forehead is the Tapas planetary system. The topmost planetary system, known as Satyaloka, is the head of He who has one thousand heads.
baseline: One should worship the goddess Ura Sthā Jyotī Anikā Maha and Vādaṇa of the neck Vādana Varātī Viḍu Adi Puṣābhiṣa Satya and the heads of thousands of heads.
morphology: One should worship the goddess Ura Sthā Jyotī Anikā Mahā Vādaṇa the neck neck and head. One should perform this penance vāratī vidrāṣa adi pūrāhāya sīrtha srīkṣara siṛti shirāṣṇa.

sanskrit: indra ādayaḥ bāhavaḥ āhuḥ usrāḥ karṇau diśaḥ śrotram amuṣya śabdaḥ nāsatya dasrau paramasya nāse ghrāṇaḥ asya gandhaḥ mukham agniḥ iddhaḥ
reference: His arms are the demigods headed by Indra, the ten directional sides are His ears, and physical sound is His sense of hearing. His nostrils are the two Aśvinī-kumāras, and material fragrance is His sense of smell. His mouth is the blazing fire.
baseline: Having destroyed the sound of Indra Adi Bahu Uṣa Kārna Dhiṣṇu Śvrātā Amuśya in the month of Dāśra the smell of the fragrance of the supreme nostrils and the smell from the mouth and fire is described.
morphology: Having destroyed the sound of Indra Adi Bahu Uṣa Kārna Dīṣṇu Sūrtā Amuśya the smell of the fragrance of the supreme nostrils on the day of Dussehra the mouth of fire fire etc.

sanskrit: dyauḥ akṣiṇī cakṣuḥ abhūt pataṅgaḥ pakṣmāṇi viṣṇoḥ ahanī ubhe ca tat bhrū vijṛmbhaḥ parameṣṭhi dhiṣṇyam āpaḥ asya tālū rasaḥ eva jihvā
reference: The sphere of outer space constitutes His eyepits, and the eyeball is the sun as the power of seeing. His eyelids are both the day and night, and in the movements of His eyebrows, Brahmā and similar supreme personalities reside. His palate is the director of water, Varuṇa, and the juice or essence of everything is His tongue.
baseline: The eyes of the king should be made to look like a kite the wings the arms of Lord Viṣṇu the head the forehead the upper limbs the palate the mouth the tongue and the mouth.
morphology: The eyes of the king should be made to look like a kite the wings the arms of the god Viṣṇu the forehead the head the face the palate the mouth the tongue and the mouth.

sanskrit: chandāṁsi anantasya śiraḥ gṛṇanti daṁṣṭrāḥ yamaḥ sneha kalāḥ dvijāni hāsaḥ jana unmāda karī ca māyā duranta sargaḥ yat apāṅga mokṣaḥ
reference: They say that the Vedic hymns are the cerebral passage of the Lord, and His jaws of teeth are Yama, god of death, who punishes the sinners.
