The art of affection is His set of teeth, and the most alluring illusory material energy is His smile. This great ocean of material creation is but the casting of His glance over us.
baseline: The head of the eternal person is taken by the chāṇḍā abhyāsī. Yāma the art of affection yāmā yaṇā laudā jāna hysteria maya the heaven of misfortune that is the liberation of the unarmed is done by the two.
morphology: The head should be taken as the head of the eternal one. Yama should be worshipped with ten shlokas the art of affection the two laughed at the manic form the illusion of vanity the great heaven that is the liberation of the disabled the world.

sanskrit: vrīḍa uttara oṣṭha adharaḥ eva lobhaḥ dharmaḥ stanaḥ adharma pathaḥ asya pṛṣṭham kaḥ tasya meḍhram vṛṣaṇau ca mitrau kukṣiḥ samudrāḥ girayaḥ asthi saṅghāḥ
reference: Modesty is the upper portion of His lips, hankering is His chin, religion is the breast of the Lord, and irreligion is His back. Brahmājī, who generates all living beings in the material world, is His genitals, and the Mitrā-varuṇas are His two testicles. The ocean is His waist, and the hills and mountains are the stacks of His bones.
baseline: One who has the righteousness the breasts the path of iniquity his sheep his scorpions his friends his arms the sea his body his bones and his body should be placed on the ground.
morphology: One who has the righteousness the breasts the path of iniquity his sheep his scorpions his friends his arms the sea his bones his body his legs his neck his head his back his chest his knees his feet his face his heart his mind his eyes his mouth his stomach his hands his mother his wife his father his brother his sister his friend his brothers his family his son his uncle his aunt his fiance his daughter his husband his

sanskrit: nadyaḥ asya nāḍyaḥ atha tanū ruhāṇi mahī ruhāḥ viśva tanoḥ nṛpa indra ananta vīryaḥ śvasitam mātariśvā gatiḥ vayaḥ karma guṇa pravāhaḥ
reference: O King, the rivers are the veins of the gigantic body, the trees are the hairs of His body, and the omnipotent air is His breath. The passing ages are His movements, and His activities are the reactions of the three modes of material nature.
baseline: The rivers are the rivers of this world. The rivers of the universe are the waters of the soul. The waters of Vīśva Indra Eternal sperms Breathing and the mother of the earth are the qualities of action. They are the streams.
morphology: The rivers rivers streams rivers and rivers of the earth the spirit the mind the world the body the mother the speed the virtues of action the flow the nature of life the eternal sperms the breath of Indra and the mother.

sanskrit: īśasya keśān viduḥ ambu vāhān vāsaḥ tu sandhyām kuru varya bhūmnaḥ avyaktam āhuḥ hṛdayam manaḥ ca saḥ candramāḥ sarva vikāra kośaḥ
reference: O best amongst the Kurus, the clouds which carry water are the hairs on His head, the terminations of days or nights are His dress, and the supreme cause of material creation is His intelligence. His mind is the moon, the reservoir of all changes.
baseline: The hair of the god should be divided into two parts. The sun should be placed at dusk. The earth should be left undefiled. The heart and mind should be made to rest on the moon. All the disorders should be destroyed.
morphology: The hair of the god should be washed with the ointment. The sun should be placed in the evening and the earth should be covered with the blood. The heart and mind should be left undefiled. The moon should be the source of all ills.

sanskrit: vijñāna śaktim mahim āmananti sarva ātmanaḥ antaḥ karaṇam giritram aśva aśvatari uṣṭra gajāḥ nakhāni sarve mṛgāḥ paśavaḥ śroṇi deśe
reference: The principle of matter [mahat-tattva] is the consciousness of the omnipresent Lord, as asserted by the experts, and Rudradeva is His ego. The horse, mule, camel and elephant are His nails, and wild animals and all quadrupeds are situated in the belt zone of the Lord.
baseline: All the spirits horses horsemen oxen camels cows mules ducks animals ears etc. are worshipped with the power of knowledge and greatness.
morphology: All beings who possess the power of knowledge and wisdom and enjoy the greatness of the self the horses horses oxen camels cows mongoose deer animals birds etc. should be worshipped in the country.

sanskrit: vayāṁsi tat vyākaraṇam vicitram manuḥ manīṣā manujaḥ nivāsaḥ gandharva vidyādhara cāraṇa apsaraḥ svara smṛtīḥ asura anīka vīryaḥ
reference: Varieties of birds are indications of His masterful artistic sense. Manu, the father of mankind, is the emblem of His standard intelligence, and humanity is His residence. The celestial species of human beings, like the Gandharvas, Vidyādharas, Cāraṇas and angels, all represent His musical rhythm, and the demoniac soldiers are representations of His wonderful prowess.
baseline: The grammar of the vāyāsī is strange. The man man sage man abode the gāndharva the learned man the cow the apsara the voice the memory the serpent and the semen.
morphology: O Viṣābyāsī the grammar is strange. Manṣṇu the man of mind is the abode of Gandharva Vidyādhara the master of knowledge Apsara the voice of memory Asura the son of Anīkā and Srimārna.

sanskrit: brahma ānanam kṣatra bhujaḥ mahātmā viṭ ūruḥ aṅghri śrita kṛṣṇa varṇaḥ nānā abhidhā abhījya gaṇa upapannaḥ dravya ātmakaḥ karma vitāna yogaḥ
reference: The virāṭ-puruṣa’s face is the brāhmaṇas, His arms are the kṣatriyas, His thighs are the vaiśyas, and the śūdras are under the protection of His feet. All the worshipable demigods are also overtaken by Him, and it is the duty of everyone to perform sacrifices with feasible goods to appease the Lord.
baseline: One should worship Brahman Anāṇa Kṣatra Bhūjā Vita Uru Angri Śrī Krsna Varna various forms of the gods and obtain wealth by worshipping them.
morphology: Having worshipped Brahman Anāṇa Kāstra Bhūjā Vītā Uruva Angrī Kṛṣṇa and other forms of beings one would get wealth by worshipping them.

sanskrit: iyān asau īśvara vigrahasya yaḥ sanniveśaḥ kathitaḥ mayā te sandhāryate asmin vapuṣi sthaviṣṭhe manaḥ sva buddhyā na yataḥ asti kiñcit
reference: I have thus explained to you the gross material gigantic conception of the Personality of Godhead. One who seriously desires liberation concentrates his mind on this form of the Lord, because there is nothing more than this in the material world.
baseline: These are the images of God. The scene mentioned by me is said to be recorded in this poem. The mind is not conscious because it is not aware of it.
morphology: These are the images of God. The scenes mentioned by me are said to be recorded. In this case the mind is not conscious because it is sitting on the ground.

sanskrit: saḥ sarva dhī vṛtti anubhūta sarve ātmā yathā svapna jana īkṣita ekaḥ tam satyam ānanda nidhim bhajeta na anyatra sajjet yataḥ ātma pātaḥ
reference: One should concentrate his mind upon the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who alone distributes Himself in so many manifestations just as ordinary persons create thousands of manifestations in dreams. One must concentrate the mind on Him, the only all-blissful Absolute Truth. Otherwise one will be misled and will cause his own degradation.
baseline: One should not worship that true treasure of bliss and enjoyment in any other place as one would wish for all the souls in his dream. He should not be worshipped elsewhere because the soul is the path.
morphology: He should know all the virtues of the soul. One should worship the true blissful treasure as one desires in the dream. One would not worship it anywhere else because the soul is the path.

sanskrit: śrī śukaḥ uvāca evam purā dhāraṇayā ātma yoniḥ naṣṭām smṛtim pratyavarudhya tuṣṭāt tathā sasarja idam amogha dṛṣṭiḥ yathā apyayāt prāk vyavasāya buddhiḥ
reference: Śrī Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Formerly, prior to the manifestation of the cosmos, Lord Brahmā, by meditating on the virāṭ-rūpa, regained his lost consciousness by appeasing the Lord. Thus he was able to rebuild the creation as it was before.
baseline: The s ́ ri ̄ sukṣa states that the mind should be pleased with the destruction of the consciousness of the self by holding it in its fullness. The mind should also be able to perceive the infinite vision of the body.
morphology: O Śrī Śuṇa one who has taken the whole of the body and destroyed the consciousness of the Śvāṇīva yogini should be pleased with the sight of the Sāsārja as it would be done before.

sanskrit: śābdasya hi brahmaṇaḥ eṣaḥ panthāḥ yat nāmabhiḥ dhyāyati dhīḥ apārthaiḥ paribhraman tatra na vindate arthān māyā maye vāsanayā śayānaḥ
reference: The way of presentation of the Vedic sounds is so bewildering that it directs the intelligence of the people to meaningless things like the heavenly kingdoms. The conditioned souls hover in dreams of such heavenly illusory pleasures, but actually they do not relish any tangible happiness in such places.
baseline: One who meditates on the path of Brahman with the names of the sound should not go around with the misunderstandings. One who sleeps with the fragrance of the senses should not forget the meanings.
morphology: One who meditates on the path of Brahman with the names of the sound should not repeat the meanings of the illusions. One who sleeps with the fragrance of the senses should be able to understand the meaning.

sanskrit: ataḥ kaviḥ nāmasu yāvat arthaḥ syāt apramattaḥ vyavasāya buddhiḥ siddhe anyathā arthe na yateta tatra pariśramam tatra samīkṣamāṇaḥ
reference: For this reason the enlightened person should endeavor only for the minimum necessities of life while in the world of names. He should be intelligently fixed and never endeavor for unwanted things, being competent to perceive practically that all such endeavors are merely hard labor for nothing.
baseline: Therefore the poet should be careful as to the meaning of the names. Otherwise the knowledge of the profession would not be meaningful.
morphology: Therefore the poet should be careful as to the meaning of the names. If he does not understand the business and knowledge then he should not make any effort.

sanskrit: satyām kṣitau kim kaśipoḥ prayāsaiḥ bāhau sva siddhe hi upabarhaṇaiḥ kim sati añjalau kim purudhā anna pātryā dik valkala ādau sati kim dukūlaiḥ
reference: When there are ample earthly flats to lie on, what is the necessity of cots and beds? When one can use his own arms, what is the necessity of a pillow? When one can use the palms of his hands, what is the necessity of varieties of utensils? When there is ample covering, or the skins of trees, what is the necessity of clothing?
baseline: If one has lost the righteousness in the arms after having made an effort one should do the ablution of the arms with the recitation of the hymn añjala or the purudha should be done with the food and utensils.
morphology: If one has lost the righteousness whether one has suffered from the misfortune of the two hands if one has done this by sitting on the right side of the arms whether the man should go back and forth with the food and utensils.

sanskrit: cīrāṇi kim pathi na santi diśanti bhikṣām na eva aṅghripāḥ para bhṛtaḥ saritaḥ api aśuṣyan ruddhāḥ guhāḥ kim ajitaḥ avati na upasannān kasmāt bhajanti kavayaḥ dhana durmada andhān
reference: Are there no torn clothes lying on the common road? Do the trees, which exist for maintaining others, no longer give alms in charity? Do the rivers, being dried up, no longer supply water to the thirsty? Are the caves of the mountains now closed? Or above all, does the Almighty Lord not protect the fully surrendered souls? Why then do the learned sages go to flatter those who are intoxicated by hard-earned wealth?
baseline: One who has not been able to find a way out whether there are holes or no way out one who is not willing to give alms or not should not go to the cave. One who is impure and not able to do so would not be able to get rid of the ill-fated and ill-informed.
morphology: One would find that there are no roads or holes. One would see that the beggars are not being fed and the cows are not getting fed. One who is not clean would find a cave closed and would not be able to get rid of them. One could find that the poet would not get wealth and evil and blindness.

sanskrit: evam sva citte svataḥ eva siddhaḥ ātmā priyaḥ arthaḥ bhagavān anantaḥ tam nirvṛtaḥ niyata arthaḥ bhajeta saṁsāra hetu uparamaḥ ca yatra
reference: Thus being fixed, one must render service unto the Supersoul situated in one’s own heart by His omnipotency. Because He is the Almighty Personality of Godhead, eternal and unlimited, He is the ultimate goal of life, and by worshiping Him one can end the cause of the conditioned state of existence.
baseline: In this way the self is perfected in its own mind. The meaning of the soul is endowed with the eternal God. The prescribed meaning is worshipped in the above places for the sake of the attainment.
morphology: In this way one who is self-sufficient in his own mind one who loves the self the Lord endowed with infinite means and who worships it with the prescribed meaning should be worshipped above and above.

sanskrit: kaḥ tām tu anādṛtya para anucintām ṛte paśūn asatīm nāma kuryāt paśyan janam patitam vaitaraṇyām sva karma jān paritāpān juṣāṇam
reference: Who else but the gross materialists will neglect such transcendental thought and take to the nonpermanent names only, seeing the mass of people fallen in the river of suffering as the consequence of accruing the result of their own work?
baseline: One who disobeys him or her and then neglects the cause of the death of the animals should be called a cow. One who has lost his or her life should be punished.
morphology: One who disobeys him should then call the beasts and animals to be killed without thinking. One who sees the beast falling down and descending down should know his deeds. He should pay tribute to those who suffer.

sanskrit: kecit sva deha antaḥ hṛdaya avakāśe prādeśa mātram puruṣam vasantam catuḥ bhujam kañja ratha aṅga śaṅkha gadā dharam dhāraṇayā smaranti
reference: Others conceive of the Personality of Godhead residing within the body in the region of the heart and measuring only eight inches, with four hands carrying a lotus, a wheel of a chariot, a conchshell and a club respectively.
baseline: Some people recall the presence of the heart within their body and the territory of the man the spring the four arms the chariot limb conch mace and dharma.
morphology: Some people recall the presence of the four arms the chariot limb conch and mace in their body and heart.

sanskrit: prasanna vaktram nalina āyata īkṣaṇam kadamba kiñjalka piśaṅga vāsasam lasat mahā ratna hiraṇmaya aṅgadam sphurat mahā ratna kirīṭa kuṇḍalam
reference: His mouth expresses His happiness. His eyes spread like the petals of a lotus, and His garments, yellowish like the saffron of a kadamba flower, are bedecked with valuable jewels. His ornaments are all made of gold, set with jewels, and He wears a glowing headdress and earrings.
baseline: The eloquent speaker should be drawn with a reed. One should draw a bow a mace a pisces a piece of cloth and the body should be covered with a huge diamond. One would get a ring of diamond. The maha gems would be the crown and the kundal.
morphology: The eloquent speaker should be drawn with a reed. One should draw a piece of water with the kādāmbha kinjala pisāngā vāsām and the body should be made of a large diamond. The part should be placed in the ring of the crown.

sanskrit: unnidra hṛt paṅkaja karṇikā ālaye yoga īśvara āsthāpita pāda pallavam śrī lakṣaṇam kaustubha ratna kandharam amlāna lakṣmyā vana mālayā ācitam
reference: His lotus feet are placed over the whorls of the lotuslike hearts of great mystics. On His chest is the Kaustubha jewel, engraved with a beautiful calf, and there are other jewels on His shoulders. His complete torso is garlanded with fresh flowers.
baseline: The heart of the unnidrā pāṇja kārṇika the seat of the feet placed by the lord in the temple the pāḍa pālava sri lakshana kaustubha gems kandhārā and amla are worshipped by lakshmī with the garland of forest.
morphology: The heart of unnidra the pāṇjā the kārṇika the abode of yogic gods and the feet of pallavas are placed in the temple. The kaśṭubha gems kāṇḍharā lakshmī forest garland with amla and kāśṇā are worshipped.

sanskrit: vibhūṣitam mekhalayā aṅgulīyakaiḥ mahā dhanaiḥ nūpura kaṅkaṇa ādibhiḥ snigdha amala ākuñcita nīla kuntalaiḥ virocamāna ānana hāsa peśalam
reference: He is well decorated with an ornamental wreath about His waist and rings studded with valuable jewels on His fingers. His leglets, His bangles, His oiled hair, curling with a bluish tint, and His beautiful smiling face are all very pleasing.
baseline: Having adorned the area with the fingers of the great goddess Nūpu the brow of the heart and the neck of the head are made to be smooth and the hair is made to look like a piece of cloth and the arms are made of blue spears.
morphology: Having adorned the ground with the fingers of the great goddess Nupur and the bracelets of the king the goddess should be made to look soft and soft with the blue spears.

sanskrit: adīna līlā hasita īkṣaṇa ullasat bhrū bhaṅga saṁsūcita bhūri anugraham īkṣeta cintāmayam enam īśvaram yāvat manaḥ dhāraṇayā avatiṣṭhate
reference: The Lord’s magnanimous pastimes and the glowing glancing of His smiling face are all indications of His extensive benedictions. One must therefore concentrate on this transcendental form of the Lord, as long as the mind can be fixed on Him by meditation.
baseline: Having laughed at Adin Leila one would enjoy the moment of breaking the eyebrows. One would find that the grace of the forehead would be good and one would think of this god as long as the mind holds on to it.
morphology: Having laughed at Adīnī lila one would enjoy the brow breaking and thus would be able to enjoy the grace. One would think of this god as long as the mind is occupied with it.

sanskrit: eka ekaśaḥ aṅgāni dhiyā anubhāvayet pāda ādi yāvat hasitam gadā bhṛtaḥ jitam jitam sthānam apohya dhārayet param param śuddhyati dhīḥ yathā yathā
reference: The process of meditation should begin from the lotus feet of the Lord and progress to His smiling face. The meditation should be concentrated upon the lotus feet, then the calves, then the thighs, and in this way higher and higher. The more the mind becomes fixed upon the different parts of the limbs, one after another, the more the intelligence becomes purified.
baseline: One should feel the limbs one by one. The feet should be covered with a mace covered with hair till the beginning. The victory should be held after having taken away the place. The body should be purified as if it were the body.
morphology: One should feel the limbs one by one. The feet should be covered with a mace covered with hair till the beginning of the war. The victory should be taken away and the place should be retained. Then the body should be cleansed.

sanskrit: yāvat na jāyeta para avare asmin viśva īśvare draṣṭari bhakti yogaḥ tāvat sthavīyaḥ puruṣasya rūpam kriyā avasāne prayataḥ smareta
reference: Unless the gross materialist develops a sense of loving service unto the Supreme Lord, the seer of both the transcendental and material worlds, he should remember or meditate upon the universal form of the Lord at the end of his prescribed duties.
baseline: One should remember the form of a man standing still till one has seen the universe in the presence of God.
morphology: One should remember the form of a man standing at the end of the action till one has seen the universe here and the god. One should observe Bhakti yoga.

sanskrit: sthiram sukham ca āsanam āsthitaḥ yatiḥ yadā jihāsuḥ imam aṅga lokam kāle ca deśe ca manaḥ na sajjayet prāṇān niyacchet manasā jita asuḥ
reference: O King, whenever the yogī desires to leave this planet of human beings, he should not be perplexed about the proper time or place, but should comfortably sit without being disturbed and, regulating the life air, should control the senses by the mind.
baseline: When the seat is fixed and comfortable and the body is in place the body should be placed in a position that is not prepared for the world and the country. The mind should be fixed on the soul.
morphology: When the seat is fixed and comfortable and the body is not prepared for the world and the country the body should be placed in the seat. The mind should be fixed on the soul.

sanskrit: manaḥ sva buddhyā amalayā niyamya kṣetra jñe etām ninayet tam ātmani ātmānam ātmani avarudhya dhīraḥ labdha upaśāntiḥ virameta kṛtyāt
reference: Thereafter, the yogī should merge his mind, by his unalloyed intelligence, into the living entity, and then merge the living entity into the Superself. And by doing this, the fully satisfied living entity becomes situated in the supreme stage of satisfaction, so that he ceases from all other activities.
baseline: The mind should determine the area by the execution of its own mind. Knowing this it should be taken into account. Having restrained the self the self and having attained the attainment of the subhātimāna. It should be done after ceasing.
morphology: The mind should be determined by the execution of its own mind knowing the area and taking it away. Having restrained the self the self and the self from doing so the patient person should attain peace by ceasing to do so.

sanskrit: na yatra kālaḥ animiṣām paraḥ prabhuḥ kutaḥ nu devāḥ jagatām ye īśire na yatra sattvam na rajaḥ tamaḥ ca na vai vikāraḥ na mahān pradhānam
reference: In that transcendental state of labdhopaśānti, there is no supremacy of devastating time, which controls even the celestial demigods who are empowered to rule over mundane creatures. (And what to speak of the demigods themselves?) Nor is there the mode of material goodness, nor passion, nor ignorance, nor even the false ego, nor the material Causal Ocean, nor the material nature.
baseline: The lord of the universe is not known to be the one who gives the world without time and the king or the king. He is neither evil nor great.
morphology: The lord of the universe is not known to be the lord of time and other things. He is neither the king nor the chief ruler nor the king.

sanskrit: param padam vaiṣṇavam āmananti tat yat na iti na iti iti atat utsisṛkṣavaḥ visṛjya daurātmyam ananya sauhṛdāḥ hṛdā upaguhya arha padam pade pade
reference: The transcendentalists desire to avoid everything godless, for they know that supreme situation in which everything is related with the Supreme Lord Viṣṇu. Therefore a pure devotee who is in absolute harmony with the Lord does not create perplexities, but worships the lotus feet of the Lord at every moment, taking them into his heart.
baseline: The vaṣṇava who has attained the highest position would say that there is no position. The vāṣṇiva who has excelled the zeal of the spirit would attain the position of position after having attained the heart of the supreme position and having attained unparalleled harmony would attain that position.
morphology: One who is not pleased with the position of Vaisnava should say that the position should be placed in the upper position. One who does not want to be happy should then go to the heart with the spirit of friendship and happiness. One should place the position in the lower position.

sanskrit: ittham muniḥ tu uparamet vyavasthitaḥ vijñāna dṛk vīrya su randhita āśayaḥ sva pārṣṇinā āpīḍya gudam tataḥ anilam sthāneṣu ṣaṭsu unnamayet jita klamaḥ
reference: By the strength of scientific knowledge, one should be well situated in absolute realization and thus be able to extinguish all material desires. One should then give up the material body by blocking the air hole [through which stool is evacuated] with the heel of one’s foot and by lifting the life air from one place to another in the six primary places.
baseline: The sage should then place the semen of the sage on the top of the pot and give it to him with his own hands. Then the anus should be raised in six places.
morphology: Then the sage should give the semen prepared by the above mentioned sage with his own hands and then the anus should be raised in six places.

sanskrit: nābhyām sthitam hṛdi adhiropya tasmāt udāna gatya urasi tam nayet muniḥ tataḥ anusandhāya dhiyā manasvī sva tālu mūlam śanakaiḥ nayeta
reference: The meditative devotee should slowly push up the life air from the navel to the heart, from there to the chest, and from there to the root of the palate. He should search out the proper places with intelligence.
baseline: The sage should not raise the heart standing on the ground and then raise it. Then the sage would seek it and find out the heart. He would not let his palate be formed by the cow.
morphology: The sage should not raise the heart standing on these two sides and then go to the ground and find out the root of his palate. He should not touch the cow.

sanskrit: tasmāt bhruvoḥ antaram unnayeta niruddha sapta āyatanaḥ anapekṣaḥ sthitvā muhūrta ardham akuṇṭha dṛṣṭiḥ nirbhidya mūrdhan visṛjet param gataḥ
reference: Thereafter the bhakti-yogī should push the life air up between the eyebrows, and then, blocking the seven outlets of the life air, he should maintain his aim for going back home, back to Godhead. If he is completely free from all desires for material enjoyment, he should then reach the cerebral hole and give up his material connections, having gone to the Supreme.
baseline: Then the gap between the two eyebrows should be raised and the circumference should be fixed at seven rectangles and the forehead should be kept half a meter wide.
morphology: Then the gap between the two eyebrows should be raised and the circumference should be fixed at seven rectangles. The muhurta should be half a meter wide and the eyes should be straight and the foolish one should be thrown away.

sanskrit: yadi prayāsyan nṛpa pārameṣṭhyam vaihāyasānām uta yat vihāram aṣṭa ādhipatyam guṇa sannivāye saha eva gacchet manasā indriyaiḥ ca
reference: However, O King, if a yogī maintains a desire for improved material enjoyments, like transference to the topmost planet, Brahmaloka, or the achievement of the eightfold perfections, travel in outer space with the Vaihāyasas, or a situation in one of the millions of planets, then he has to take away with him the materially molded mind and senses.
baseline: If one tries to do so one would get a vihara with eight dominions and the mind and senses with eight qualities.
morphology: If one has tried to attain the height of the mountain one would get the vihara with eight superior qualities and the mind and the senses.

sanskrit: yoga īśvarāṇām gatim āhuḥ antaḥ bahiḥ tri lokyāḥ pavana antaḥ ātmanām na karmabhiḥ tām gatim āpnuvanti vidyā tapaḥ yoga samādhi bhājām
reference: The transcendentalists are concerned with the spiritual body. As such, by the strength of their devotional service, austerities, mystic power and transcendental knowledge, their movements are unrestricted, within and beyond the material worlds. The fruitive workers, or the gross materialists, can never move in such an unrestricted manner.
baseline: One who practices yoga the movement of the gods the three worlds in and out the winds in and the actions of the spirits one who does not follow the movements of the souls would attain the path of yoga penance samadhi bhaja.
morphology: One who practices yoga the movement of the gods the three worlds in and out the winds in and the actions of the spirits one who does not practice the practice of yoga penance yoga samadhi bhaja etc. will attain that movement.

sanskrit: vaiśvānaram yāti vihāyasā gataḥ suṣumṇayā brahma pathena śociṣā vidhūta kalkaḥ atha hareḥ udastāt prayāti cakram nṛpa śaiśumāram
reference: O King, when such a mystic passes over the Milky Way by the illuminating Suṣumṇā to reach the highest planet, Brahmaloka, he goes first to Vaiśvānara, the planet of the deity of fire, wherein he becomes completely cleansed of all contaminations, and thereafter he still goes higher, to the circle of Śiśumāra, to relate with Lord Hari, the Personality of Godhead.
baseline: Having departed from the cosmic realm one who has gone to the path of Brahman with the sun one would find that the illusion of the form of the universe would be repeated by the king.
morphology: Having departed from the cosmic realm one who has gone to the path of Brahman with the sun one would find that the illusion of the form of the universe would be repeated by the king.

sanskrit: tat viśva nābhim tu ativartya viṣṇoḥ aṇīyasā virajena ātmanā ekaḥ namaskṛtam brahma vidām upaiti kalpa āyuṣaḥ yat vibudhāḥ ramante
reference: This Śiśumāra is the pivot for the turning of the complete universe, and it is called the navel of Viṣṇu [Garbhodakaśāyī Viṣṇu]. The yogī alone goes beyond this circle of Śiśumāra and attains the planet [Maharloka] where purified saints like Bhṛgu enjoy a duration of life of 4,300,000,000 solar years. This planet is worshipable even for saints who are transcendentally situated.
baseline: Having overstated the navel of the universe one should worship the Brahman with the spirit of Viṣṇu by the abyss of the anyaśa river. One should worship Brahman without the illusion of the illusions of life.
morphology: Having overstretched the navel of the universe one should worship the Brahman with the spirit of Viṣṇu by the virginity of the anyaśa. One should worship Brahman without the illusion of the illusions of life.

sanskrit: atho anantasya mukha analena dandahyamānam saḥ nirīkṣya viśvam niryāti siddheśvara yuṣṭa dhiṣṇyam yat dvai parārdhyam tat u pārameṣṭhyam
reference: At the time of the final devastation of the complete universe [the end of the duration of Brahmā’s life], a flame of fire emanates from the mouth of Ananta [from the bottom of the universe]. The yogī sees all the planets of the universe burning to ashes, and thus he leaves for Satyaloka by airplanes used by the great purified souls. The duration of life in Satyaloka is calculated to be 15,480,000,000,000 years.
baseline: Having seen that the face of the infinite is being touched with the arrow one would see that the universe is being destroyed. The one who has destroyed the two worlds would be destroyed by the Supreme Lord.
morphology: Having seen that the face of the eternal one is covered with a thread he expands the universe. Having said this to the Supreme Personality of Godhead he would be able to achieve the goal of the two worlds.

sanskrit: na yatra śokaḥ na jarā na mṛtyuḥ na artiḥ na ca udvegaḥ ṛte kutaścit yat cit tataḥ adaḥ kṛpayā an idam vidām duranta duḥkha prabhava anudarśanāt
reference: In that planet of Satyaloka, there is neither bereavement, nor old age nor death. There is no pain of any kind, and therefore there are no anxieties, save that sometimes, due to consciousness, there is a feeling of compassion for those unaware of the process of devotional service, who are subjected to unsurpassable miseries in the material world.
baseline: There is neither sorrow nor death nor strife nor anxiety nor anything else. Then the image should be described as having been created by the Lord. It should be said as far as possible.
morphology: There is neither sorrow nor loss of life nor death nor anxiety nor anger nor anything else.

sanskrit: tataḥ viśeṣam pratipadya nirbhayaḥ tena ātmanā āpaḥ anala mūrtiḥ atvaran jyotiḥ mayaḥ vāyum upetya kāle vāyu ātmanā kham bṛhat ātma liṅgam
reference: After reaching Satyaloka, the devotee is specifically able to be incorporated fearlessly by the subtle body in an identity similar to that of the gross body, and one after another he gradually attains stages of existence from earthly to watery, fiery, glowing and airy, until he reaches the ethereal stage.
baseline: Then one who is fearless by the manifestation of a particular spirit should offer the image of a person who is not afraid of the spirit. One who has left the air for the time being would get the light of the soul. One would get a great body and the penis of the self.
morphology: Then after having described the special thing one should fearlessly worship the image of Aṇāla with the spirit. One who gives light to the air should leave the spirit with the air and the linga with the great spirit in time.

sanskrit: ghrāṇena gandham rasanena vai rasam rūpam ca dṛṣṭyā śvasanam tvacā eva śrotreṇa ca upetya nabhaḥ guṇatvam prāṇena ca ākūtim upaiti yogī
reference: The devotee thus surpasses the subtle objects of different senses like aroma by smelling, the palate by tasting, vision by seeing forms, touch by contacting, the vibrations of the ear by ethereal identification, and the sense organs by material activities.
baseline: Having seen the smell smell taste juice form breath skin hearing the abhinaya and the pranayama are used by the yogis.
morphology: Having seen the fragrance smell taste juice form breath skin hearing and other things with the help of fragrance and pranayama the yogis get the benefits of the akutī.

sanskrit: saḥ bhūta sūkṣma indriya sannikarṣam manaḥ mayam deva mayam vikāryam saṁsādya gatyā saha tena yāti vijñāna tattvam guṇa sannirodham
reference: The devotee, thus surpassing the gross and the subtle forms of coverings, enters the plane of egoism. And in that status he merges the material modes of nature [ignorance and passion] in this point of neutralization and thus reaches egoism in goodness. After this, all egoism is merged in the mahat-tattva, and he comes to the point of pure self-realization.
baseline: The spirit is the subtle sense object and the mind is the deification of the demigods. It is the principle of knowledge and the control of virtues with its movement.
morphology: That spirit is subtle sensory sensual mental divine perverse capable and capable of moving along with it. The principle of knowledge quality and obstruction of the mind.

sanskrit: tena ātmanā ātmānam upaiti śāntam ānandam ānanda mayaḥ avasāne etām gatim bhāgavatīm gataḥ yaḥ saḥ vai punaḥ na iha viṣajjate aṅga
reference: Only the purified soul can attain the perfection of associating with the Personality of Godhead in complete bliss and satisfaction in his constitutional state. Whoever is able to renovate such devotional perfection is never again attracted by this material world, and he never returns.
baseline: Then the soul is made to enjoy the soul with calmness bliss joy pleasure and happiness. In the end one who has gone through this movement and has gone to Bhagavad-gītā would never again be poisoned by this body.
morphology: Then the spirit is used by the soul. The calmness joy pleasure happiness and the loss of the body go to the one who has not again destroyed the body.

sanskrit: ete sṛtī te nṛpa veda gīte tvayā abhipṛṣṭe ca sanātane ca ye vai purā brahmaṇe āha tuṣṭaḥ ārādhitaḥ bhagavān vāsudevaḥ
reference: Your Majesty Mahārāja Parīkṣit, know that all that I have described in reply to your proper inquiry is just according to the version of the Vedas, and it is eternal truth. This was described personally by Lord Kṛṣṇa unto Brahmā, with whom the Lord was satisfied upon being properly worshiped.
baseline: The Lord Vasudeva worshipped in the Vedas the hymns the songs the sermons and the sacred rites of the Lord Brahman.
morphology: The Lord Vasudeva worshipped in the Veda song and the Sanatana that you have worshipped with these three syllables and who is pleased with the Brahman of the whole world.

sanskrit: na hi ataḥ anyaḥ śivaḥ panthāḥ viśataḥ saṁsṛtau iha vāsudeve bhagavati bhakti yogaḥ yataḥ bhavet
reference: For those who are wandering in the material universe, there is no more auspicious means of deliverance than what is aimed at in the direct devotional service of Lord Kṛṣṇa.
baseline: One who does not know the path of another Śiva would become a devotee of the god Vāsudeva. This would be the yoga of devotion.
morphology: One who does not follow the path of another Śiva would thus become a devotee of the god Vāsudeva.

sanskrit: bhagavān brahma kārtsnyena triḥ anvīkṣya manīṣayā tat adhyavasyat kūṭa sthaḥ ratiḥ ātman (ātmani) yataḥ bhavet
reference: The great personality Brahmā, with great attention and concentration of the mind, studied the Vedas three times, and after scrutinizingly examining them, he ascertained that attraction for the Supreme Personality of Godhead Śrī Kṛṣṇa is the highest perfection of religion.
baseline: Having sought the three things of the lord Brahma with the kārtasṇya thread one should know that the thread should be placed in the heart and the soul.
morphology: Having searched for the three gods Brahma and Kārtasṇya one should understand that the kuta should be placed in the heart and the soul.

sanskrit: bhagavān sarva bhūteṣu lakṣitaḥ sva ātmanā hariḥ dṛśyaiḥ buddhi ādibhiḥ draṣṭā lakṣaṇaiḥ anumāpakaiḥ
reference: The Personality of Godhead Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa is in every living being along with the individual soul. And this fact is perceived and hypothesized in our acts of seeing and taking help from the intelligence.
baseline: The Lord is visible to all beings by means of the manifestations of his own self. He is seen by the senses the intellect etc. by the signs and measures.
morphology: The Lord is visible to all beings. He is visible by the self. He sees by the intellect. He perceives by the senses the signs.

sanskrit: tasmāt sarva ātmanā rājan hariḥ sarvatra sarvadā śrotavyaḥ kīrtitavyaḥ ca smartavyaḥ bhagavān nṛṇām
reference: O King, it is therefore essential that every human being hear about, glorify and remember the Supreme Lord, the Personality of Godhead, always and everywhere.
baseline: Therefore the king should always be heard everywhere with all the spirits and should be remembered as the supreme god.
morphology: Then the king should be always heard everywhere with all the spirits. The king should always be heard everywhere and should be glorified.

sanskrit: pibanti ye bhagavataḥ ātmanaḥ satām kathā amṛtam śravaṇa puṭeṣu sambhṛtam punanti te viṣaya vidūṣita āśayam vrajanti tat caraṇa saroruha antikam
reference: Those who drink through aural reception, fully filled with the nectarean message of Lord Kṛṣṇa, the beloved of the devotees, purify the polluted aim of life known as material enjoyment and thus go back to Godhead, to the lotus feet of Him [the Personality of Godhead].
baseline: Those who drink from the Lord the spirit the truth the elixir the sound the words the secret of the soul the matter and the matter are absorbed in the leaves. Those who do so again will get the illusion.
morphology: Those who drink from the Lord the spirit the truth the elixir the words of the soul the sound of the heart the matter and the matter are covered in the leaves. They give the illusion of the matter to the king.

sanskrit: śrī śukaḥ uvāca evam etat nigaditam pṛṣṭavān yat bhavān mama nṛṇām yat mriyamāṇānām manuṣyeṣu manīṣiṇām
reference: Śrī Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Mahārāja Parīkṣit, as you have inquired from me as to the duty of the intelligent man who is on the threshold of death, so I have answered you.
baseline: Śrī Śuṇa thus said that it is appointed. He asked thee to make my sons who are dying among men wise.
morphology: The Lord Śrī Śuṇa thus said that it was appointed. He asked the king to give me the sons of men who were dying.

sanskrit: brahma varcasa kāmaḥ tu yajeta brahmaṇaḥ patim indram indriya kāmaḥ tu prajā kāmaḥ prajāpatīn devīm māyām tu śrī kāmaḥ tejaḥ kāmaḥ vibhāvasum vasu kāmaḥ vasūn rudrān vīrya kāmaḥ atha vīryavān anna adya kāmaḥ tu aditim svarga kāmaḥ aditeḥ sutān viśvān devān rājya kāmaḥ sādhyān saṁsādhakaḥ viśām āyuḥ kāmaḥ aśvinau devau puṣṭi kāmaḥ ilām yajet pratiṣṭhā kāmaḥ puruṣaḥ rodasī loka mātarau rūpa abhikāmaḥ gandharvān strī kāmaḥ apsaraḥ urvaśīm ādhipatya kāmaḥ sarveṣām yajeta parameṣṭhinam yajñam yajet yaśaḥ kāmaḥ kośa kāmaḥ pracetasam vidyā kāmaḥ tu giriśam dāmpatya arthaḥ umām satīm
reference: One who desires to be absorbed in the impersonal brahmajyoti effulgence should worship the master of the Vedas [Lord Brahmā or Bṛhaspati, the learned priest], one who desires powerful sex should worship the heavenly King, Indra, and one who desires good progeny should worship the great progenitors called the Prajāpatis. One who desires good fortune should worship Durgādevī, the superintendent of the material world. One desiring to be very powerful should worship fire, and one who aspires only after money should worship the Vasus. One should worship the Rudra incarnations of Lord Śiva if he wants to be a great hero. One who wants a large stock of grains should worship Aditi. One who desires to attain the heavenly planets should worship the sons of Aditi. One who desires a worldly kingdom should worship Viśvadeva, and one who wants to be popular with the general mass of population should worship the Sādhya demigod. One who desires a long span of life should worship the demigods known as the Aśvinī-kumāras, and a person desiring a strongly built body should worship the earth. One who desires stability in his post should worship the horizon and the earth combined. One who desires to be beautiful should worship the beautiful residents of the Gandharva planet, and one who desires a good wife should worship the Apsarās and the Urvaśī society girls of the heavenly kingdom. One who desires domination over others should worship Lord Brahmā, the head of the universe. One who desires tangible fame should worship the Personality of Godhead, and one who desires a good bank balance should worship the demigod Varuṇa. If one desires to be a greatly learned man he should worship Lord Śiva, and if one desires a good marital relation he should worship the chaste goddess Umā, the wife of Lord Śiva.
baseline: O Brahman Virśa Kāmā Indra sense lust love people subjects gods goddesses mayas Śrī kāma Tejā Kám Vābhava Kâm vaśu vasu kaamā Rudra Rudras Sperma anna Aditi Swargāṇa Kaama Sun Satavas Vishva Ayu Kama Asvīṇu Deva Pusyātha
morphology: O Brahman Virśa Kāmā Indra Indrā Kámā and Kāma the subjects the objects the gods the goddess the abode the universe the fire the vaśva the cosmic the celestial the sensual the virgin the earth the sun the sky the heaven the world the king the kingdom the state the lord the saviour the god of life Śiva the Lord the mother the form of the universe and the form

sanskrit: dharma arthaḥ uttama ślokam tantuḥ tanvan pitṝn yajet rakṣā kāmaḥ puṇya janān ojaḥ kāmaḥ marut gaṇān
reference: One should worship Lord Viṣṇu or His devotee for spiritual advancement in knowledge, and for protection of heredity and advancement of a dynasty one should worship the various demigods.
baseline: The meaning of dharma is good scripture. The thread should be given to the fathers. The kāmā should protect the virtuous people. The kaamā should be worshipped by the noble people.
morphology: The meaning of dharma is good. The threads should be given to the fathers. The kāmā should protect the virtuous people the kāma should be worshipped and the gāna should be killed.

sanskrit: rājya kāmaḥ manūn devān nirṛtim tu abhicaran yajet kāma kāmaḥ yajet somam akāmaḥ puruṣam param
reference: One who desires domination over a kingdom or an empire should worship the Manus. One who desires victory over an enemy should worship the demons, and one who desires sense gratification should worship the moon. But one who desires nothing of material enjoyment should worship the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
baseline: The king should worship men gods and goddesses. The lord should worship kama kāma soma akām and other beings.
morphology: One should worship the king the gods the goddess of the kingdom the king and the king of the king. One should pray to the lord of the earth the lord lord of lust and lord of all beings.

sanskrit: akāmaḥ sarva kāmaḥ vā mokṣa kāmaḥ udāra dhīḥ tīvreṇa bhakti yogena yajeta puruṣam param
reference: A person who has broader intelligence, whether he be full of all material desire, without any material desire, or desiring liberation, must by all means worship the supreme whole, the Personality of Godhead.
baseline: One who has attained all the desires or the desires for salvation with a generous heart with devotion and yoga should be worshipped as the supreme man.
morphology: One should offer all the desires of the person with a generous heart and devotion and yoga.

sanskrit: etāvān eva yajatām iha niḥśreyasa udayaḥ bhagavati acalaḥ bhāvaḥ yat bhāgavata saṅgataḥ
reference: All the different kinds of worshipers of multidemigods can attain the highest perfectional benediction, which is spontaneous attraction unflinchingly fixed upon the Supreme Personality of Godhead, only by the association of the pure devotee of the Lord.
baseline: One who acquires these things would be free from any fear. One would get unbroken feeling of God.
morphology: These are the same things. One should rise free from evil and attain the unbroken feeling of God in the company of the divine.

sanskrit: jñānam yat ā pratinivṛtta guṇa ūrmi cakram ātma prasādaḥ uta yatra guṇeṣu asaṅgaḥ kaivalya sammata pathaḥ tu atha bhakti yogaḥ kaḥ nirvṛtaḥ hari kathāsu ratim na kuryāt
reference: Transcendental knowledge in relation with the Supreme Lord Hari is knowledge resulting in the complete suspension of the waves and whirlpools of the material modes. Such knowledge is self-satisfying due to its being free from material attachment, and being transcendental it is approved by authorities. Who could fail to be attracted?
baseline: The knowledge that the qualities of the ārūmī are represented by the ūrma chakra the prāśāma of the self or the path agreed upon by the kāvālāga of the qualities is thus known as bhakti yogā one who does not get rid of the elements of the story of Hari should not get pleasure.
morphology: The knowledge that the qualities of the ūrma are represented in the form of the circle the prāśāma of the self the path of the unbroken path of qualities and the path agreed upon. Who would not be able to enjoy the virtues of the devotional path and the story of Hari.

sanskrit: śaunakaḥ uvāca iti abhivyāhṛtam rājā niśamya bharata ṛṣabhaḥ kim anyat pṛṣṭavān bhūyaḥ vaiyāsakim ṛṣim kavim
reference: Śaunaka said: The son of Vyāsadeva, Śrīla Śukadeva Gosvāmī, was a highly learned sage and was able to describe things in a poetic manner. What did Mahārāja Parīkṣit again inquire from him after hearing all that he had said?
baseline: Having said this the king said that the cow should be worshipped. Having said that Bharata and Rishabha asked what else was there. Bhūya Vyāsakī Rishi Poet.
morphology: Having said this the king said that the son of a cow should be worshipped. The king asked Bharata and Rishabha what else was there. He asked Bhūya Vyāsaka Rishi Poet.

sanskrit: etat śuśrūṣatām vidvan sūta naḥ arhasi bhāṣitum kathāḥ hari kathā udarkāḥ satām syuḥ sadasi dhruvam
reference: O learned Sūta Gosvāmī! Please continue to explain such topics to us because we are all eager to hear. Besides that, topics which result in the discussion of the Lord Hari should certainly be discussed in the assembly of devotees.
baseline: One who has learnt to perform this service should say the story of Hari the story the stories of Udaaraka the truth the dhruva.
morphology: One who does not know the meaning of the story should speak the story of Hari the story and the stories of Udaṇa. One who is good at this service should say the dhruva.

sanskrit: saḥ vai bhāgavataḥ rājā pāṇḍaveyaḥ mahā rathaḥ bāla krīḍanakaiḥ krīḍan kṛṣṇa krīḍām yaḥ ādade
reference: Mahārāja Parīkṣit, the grandson of the Pāṇḍavas, was from his very childhood a great devotee of the Lord. Even while playing with dolls, he used to worship Lord Kṛṣṇa by imitating the worship of the family Deity.
baseline: The king should play with the great chariot of the Pandavas and the children with the players. One who plays the game of Kṛṣṇa would get victory.
morphology: The king of the Pandavas should play with the great chariot and the children with the players. He should play the game of Krsna.

sanskrit: vaiyāsakiḥ ca bhagavān vāsudeva parāyaṇaḥ urugāya guṇa udārāḥ satām syuḥ hi samāgame
reference: Śukadeva Gosvāmī, the son of Vyāsadeva, was also full in transcendental knowledge and was a great devotee of Lord Kṛṣṇa, son of Vasudeva. So there must have been discussion of Lord Kṛṣṇa, who is glorified by great philosophers and in the company of great devotees.
baseline: O Vaivasaki Lord Vasudeva and others should be worshipped with the merits of goodness.
morphology: O Vaivasaki Lord Vasudeva and others should be worshipped with the merits and virtues.

sanskrit: āyuḥ harati vai puṁsām udyan astam ca yan asau tasya ṛte yat kṣaṇaḥ nītaḥ uttama śloka vārtayā
reference: Both by rising and by setting, the sun decreases the duration of life of everyone, except one who utilizes the time by discussing topics of the all-good Personality of Godhead.
baseline: The best verse should be said to describe the time taken for the worship of the gods in the morning and evening.
morphology: One who destroys the life of a person would get the benefits of the garden. One who takes away that moment would get better by reciting a good hymn.

sanskrit: taravaḥ kim na jīvanti bhastrāḥ kim na śvasanti uta na khādanti na mehanti kim grāme paśavaḥ apare
reference: Do the trees not live? Do the bellows of the blacksmith not breathe? All around us, do the beasts not eat and discharge semen?
baseline: Whether the swarms live or die whether the animals do not breathe or do not eat whether animals live in villages or other places.
morphology: Whether the swarms live or do not breathe or eat or eat animals in the villages or other places.

sanskrit: śva viṭ varāha uṣṭra kharaiḥ saṁstutaḥ puruṣaḥ paśuḥ na yat karṇa patha upetaḥ jātu nāma gadāgrajaḥ
reference: Men who are like dogs, hogs, camels and asses praise those men who never listen to the transcendental pastimes of Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the deliverer from evils.
baseline: A man should not be made to walk on the path of the ear. He should be called a donkey.
morphology: A man should not walk on the path of the ear and the animal should be made to walk on a mound. The mace should be called the donkey.

sanskrit: bile bata urukrama vikramān ye na śṛṇvataḥ karṇa puṭe narasya jihvā asatī dārdurikā iva sūta na ca upagāyati urugāya gāthāḥ
reference: One who has not listened to the messages about the prowess and marvelous acts of the Personality of Godhead and has not sung or chanted loudly the worthy songs about the Lord is to be considered to possess earholes like the holes of snakes and a tongue like the tongue of a frog.
baseline: One who does not hear the sound of the bow bow arrow and the voice of a man should be heard in the form of the ear mouth and tongue. One who is not able to sing the song of the sun like a dardurika should not be heard by the ear.
morphology: One who does not hear the sound of the bow bow arrow bow and disc and who is not listening to the voice of a man on the ear mouth and tongue would not be able to sing a song like the dardurika.

sanskrit: bhāraḥ param paṭṭa kirīṭa juṣṭam api uttama aṅgam na namet mukundam śāvau karau no kurute saparyām hareḥ lasat kāñcana kaṅkaṇau vā
reference: The upper portion of the body, though crowned with a silk turban, is only a heavy burden if not bowed down before the Personality of Godhead who can award mukti [freedom]. And the hands, though decorated with glittering bangles, are like those of a dead man if not engaged in the service of the Personality of Godhead Hari.
baseline: One who does not wear the headgear or the crown the head the neck and the head should not be worn. One who is not wearing a muṇḍa or a cow should not wear a green cloth or a braid.
morphology: One who does not wear the headgear or the crown and the body should not wear a mask. One who is not wearing a muṇḍu a cow a deer a monkey or a monkey should not do it.

sanskrit: barhāyite te nayane narāṇām liṅgāni viṣṇoḥ na nirīkṣataḥ ye pādau nṛṇām tau druma janma bhājau kṣetrāṇi na anuvrajataḥ hareḥ yau
reference: The eyes which do not look at the symbolic representations of the Personality of Godhead Viṣṇu [His forms, name, quality, etc.] are like those printed on the plumes of the peacock, and the legs which do not move to the holy places [where the Lord is remembered] are considered to be like tree trunks.
baseline: The legs of the two sons of Viṣṇu who do not see the linga of the nāraṇas in the way of the banhāīya are not the same as those of the sons of Śiva. The sons of these sons are born in the fields.
morphology: Those who do not see the linga of the female in the form of the legs and the legs of the male in the manner of the bridegroom should be removed from the ground. Those who are not aware of the position of the females should be left alone.

sanskrit: jīvan śavaḥ bhāgavata aṅghri reṇum na jātu martyaḥ abhilabheta yaḥ tu śrī viṣṇu padyāḥ manu jaḥ tulasyāḥ śvasan śavaḥ yaḥ tu na veda gandham
reference: The person who has not at any time received the dust of the feet of the Lord’s pure devotee upon his head is certainly a dead body. And the person who has never experienced the aroma of the tulasī leaves from the lotus feet of the Lord is also a dead body, although breathing.
baseline: One who does not know the body of the living entity the god of the body the king of the gods the lord of the earth the son of the god Viṣṇu the man of the position of the lord Viṣnu the body that does not smell the Veda and the breath of the goddess Tulasa is not worthy of death.
morphology: One who does not know the body of the living entity one who is alive and one who has not been killed by the enemy one whose body is not the fragrance of the Vedas one should know that the body is good for the dead person.

sanskrit: tat aśma sāram hṛdayam bata idam yat gṛhyamāṇaiḥ hari nāma dheyaiḥ na vikriyeta atha yadā vikāraḥ netre jalam gātra ruheṣu harṣaḥ
reference: Certainly that heart is steel-framed which, in spite of one’s chanting the holy name of the Lord with concentration, does not change when ecstasy takes place, tears fill the eyes and the hairs stand on end.
baseline: The sum of that ashma the heart and the heart should be taken and the names of the gods should not be sold. When there is a disorder in the eyes the water should be given to the eyes.
morphology: The sum of that ash is the heart. One should not sell the names of Hari and Dheya with these things. One would get happiness when one has a disorder water in the eyes and a lotus.

sanskrit: atha abhidhehi aṅga manaḥ anukūlam prabhāṣase bhāgavata pradhānaḥ yat āha vaiyāsakiḥ ātma vidyā viśāradaḥ nṛpatim sādhu pṛṣṭaḥ
reference: O Sūta Gosvāmī, your words are pleasing to our minds. Please therefore explain this to us as it was spoken by the great devotee Śukadeva Gosvāmī, who is very expert in transcendental knowledge, and who spoke to Mahārāja Parīkṣit upon being asked.
baseline: The preceptor should thus say that the body should be made to fit the mind and the principal one should say that aha vaśakī is the knowledge of the self. Viṣārāda is the master of the king.
morphology: Then the preceptor should say in this manner that the body is suited to the mind the principal one should say aha vaśāka the knowledge of the self viṣārāḍa nrāpādi sādhu.

sanskrit: sūtaḥ uvāca vaiyāsakeḥ iti vacaḥ tattva niścayam ātmanaḥ upadhārya matim kṛṣṇe auttareyaḥ satīm vyadhāt
reference: Sūta Gosvāmī said: Mahārāja Parīkṣit, the son of Uttarā, after hearing the speeches of Śukadeva Gosvāmī, which were all about the truth of the self, applied his concentration faithfully upon Lord Kṛṣṇa.
baseline: The word vaiṣaka is said to be the preceptor. Having established the principle of the self one should follow the principles of the mind. One who has attained sati should be worshipped by Kṛṣṇa.
morphology: The principle of vaiṣāka is said to be true. Having established the principle of the self one should believe that the kṛṣṇa would be able to attain the goal of sati.

sanskrit: ātma jāyā suta āgāra paśu draviṇa bandhuṣu rājye ca avikale nityam virūḍhām mamatām jahau
reference: Mahārāja Parīkṣit, as a result of his wholehearted attraction for Lord Kṛṣṇa, was able to give up all deep-rooted affection for his personal body, his wife, his children, his palace, his animals like horses and elephants, his treasury house, his friends and relatives, and his undisputed kingdom.
baseline: One should always fight against the enemies of the kingdom and the enemies in the kingdom of the animals and the king.
morphology: The soul should be kept in a stable place. The animals should be constantly facing the enemy in the kingdom of the king and the enemies.

sanskrit: papraccha ca imam eva artham yat mām pṛcchatha sattamāḥ kṛṣṇa anubhāva śravaṇe śraddadhānaḥ mahā manāḥ saṁsthām vijñāya sannyasya karma trai vargikam ca yat vāsudeve bhagavati ātma bhāvam dṛḍham gataḥ
reference: O great sages, the great soul Mahārāja Parīkṣit, constantly rapt in thought of Lord Kṛṣṇa, knowing well of his imminent death, renounced all sorts of fruitive activities, namely acts of religion, economic development and sense gratification, and thus fixed himself firmly in his natural love for Kṛṣṇa and asked all these questions, exactly as you are asking me.
baseline: The same thing is said to be true in the case of the king. Having asked me one should pay attention to the feelings of Kṛṣṇa. Having heard the great mind knowing that the three categories of the actions of the sānaṇīs are accomplished and having said this one would become strong in the sense of self.
morphology: The same thing is said to be true when one has asked me if one has heard the feeling of Kṛṣṇa the great mind the deeds of the sāna the three classes of sāṇas and the spirit of the lord Vāsudeva.

sanskrit: rājā uvāca samīcīnam vacaḥ brahman sarva jñasya tava anagha tamaḥ viśīryate mahyam hareḥ kathayataḥ kathām
reference: Mahārāja Parīkṣit said: O learned brāhmaṇa, you know everything because you are without material contamination. Therefore whatever you have spoken to me appears perfectly right. Your speeches are gradually destroying the darkness of my ignorance, for you are narrating the topics of the Lord.
baseline: The king should say that he is good enough and that he knows all the things about Brahman. He should tell me the story.
morphology: The king should say that he is good enough. He should tell the story to you. The king would say that if he knows everything about Brahman he would be pleased with you.

sanskrit: bhūyaḥ eva vivitsāmi bhagavān ātma māyayā yathā idam sṛjate viśvam durvibhāvyam adhīśvaraiḥ
reference: I beg to know from you how the Personality of Godhead, by His personal energies, creates these phenomenal universes as they are, which are inconceivable even to the great demigods.
baseline: The universe is created by the Lord of the earth the self the illusion of the self and the illusory gods.
morphology: The universe is created by the Lord of the universe as if by the illusion of the self.

sanskrit: yathā gopāyati vibhuḥ yathā saṁyacchate punaḥ yām yām śaktim upāśritya puru śaktiḥ paraḥ pumān ātmānam krīḍayan krīḍan karoti vikaroti ca
reference: Kindly describe how the Supreme Lord, who is all-powerful, engages His different energies and different expansions in maintaining and again winding up the phenomenal world in the sporting spirit of a player.
baseline: The vivah should be worshipped as it is and the power should be restored to it. Having worshipped the power of the puru the pūṇa and the spirit should be played and sold.
morphology: The vivah should be worshipped as it is and the power should be restored. The pūrū should be placed above the power of the soul and play with the spirit and sell the games.

sanskrit: nūnam bhagavataḥ brahman hareḥ adbhuta karmaṇaḥ durvibhāvyam iva ābhāti kavibhiḥ ca api ceṣṭitam
reference: O learned brāhmaṇa, the transcendental activities of the Lord are all wonderful, and they appear inconceivable because even great endeavors by many learned scholars have still proved insufficient for understanding them.
baseline: One who does good and evil deeds should be worshipped by the gods brahmins hares and the poets.
morphology: One should also try to find out the meaning of the word namā bhāgavata brahman hare marvellous deeds evil deeds etc. by the poets.

sanskrit: yathā guṇān tu prakṛteḥ yugapat kramaśaḥ api vā bibharti bhūriśaḥ tu ekaḥ kurvan karmāṇi janmabhiḥ
reference: The Supreme Personality of Godhead is one, whether He alone acts with the modes of material nature, or simultaneously expands in many forms, or expands consecutively to direct the modes of nature.
baseline: The qualities of the nature should be divided into two parts in the same way. One should do the deeds by the birth.
morphology: The qualities of the nature should be divided into two parts in the same way. One should do the deeds by the birth.

sanskrit: vicikitsitam etat me bravītu bhagavān yathā śābde brahmaṇi niṣṇātaḥ parasmin ca bhavān khalu
reference: Kindly clear up all these doubtful inquiries, because you are not only vastly learned in the Vedic literatures and self-realized in transcendence, but are also a great devotee of the Lord and are therefore as good as the Personality of Godhead.
baseline: May the Lord explain this to you as if you are a master of Brahman and you are good at it.
morphology: May the Lord explain this to me as if you are a master of Brahman. You are good at that.

sanskrit: sūtaḥ uvāca iti upāmantritaḥ rājñā guṇa anukathane hareḥ hṛṣīkeśam anusmṛtya prativaktum pracakrame
reference: Sūta Gosvāmī said: When Śukadeva Gosvāmī was thus requested by the King to describe the creative energy of the Personality of Godhead, he then systematically remembered the master of the senses [Śrī Kṛṣṇa], and to reply properly he spoke thus.
baseline: The king should recite the sūtā as mentioned in the subjunctive verse. In the recitation of the hymn hare hrishikesā one should recall the syllable hrisikesā and repeat it in the following manner.
morphology: The king should recite the sutta as the subjunctive word for the merits of the king. In the same manner as in the case of a king who is a haraṇa he should recall the hrishikesa and repeat it.

sanskrit: śrī śukaḥ uvāca namaḥ parasmai puruṣāya bhūyase sad udbhava sthāna nirodha līlayā gṛhīta śakti tritayāya dehinām antaḥ bhavāya anupalakṣya vartmane
reference: Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Let me offer my respectful obeisances unto the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who, for the creation of the material world, accepts the three modes of nature. He is the complete whole residing within the body of everyone, and His ways are inconceivable.
baseline: O Śrī Śuṇa Oṣṇu Ośṇuṣṇo O Sūkā Oṃ Viṣṭuṣa one who invents the sun and the sun should be placed on the other side of the body. One should take the seat of good origin and hold it with the lila. The body should be made to look like the inner body and not like that.
morphology: O Śrī Śuṇa Ośā O Sūkā one who invents the name of the other person the place of good origin should be occupied with the garbha lila and the body should be placed inside the threefold body.

sanskrit: bhūyaḥ namaḥ sat vṛjina chide asatām asambhavāya akhila sattva mūrtaye puṁsām punaḥ pāramahaṁsye āśrame vyavasthitānām anumṛgya dāśuṣe
reference: I again offer my respectful obeisances unto the form of complete existence and transcendence, who is the liberator of the pious devotees from all distresses and the destroyer of the further advances in atheistic temperament of the nondevotee-demons. For the transcendentalists who are situated in the topmost spiritual perfection, He grants their specific destinations.
baseline: Having said the bhūyaṇa namā one who has not been able to attain all the sattvas of the world would be able to do so. One would be allowed to return to the abode of the supreme god after having placed them in the sanctum.
morphology: Having worshipped the goddess Bhūyā one who is not able to attain all the qualities of the body would again be allowed to enter the sanctum sanctorum of the abode of the Supreme Being.

sanskrit: namaḥ namaḥ te astu ṛṣabhāya sātvatām vidūra kāṣṭhāya muhuḥ ku yoginām nirasta sāmya atiśayena rādhasā sva dhāmani brahmaṇi raṁsyate namaḥ
reference: Let me offer my respectful obeisances unto Him who is the associate of the members of the Yadu dynasty and who is always a problem for the nondevotees. He is the supreme enjoyer of both the material and spiritual worlds, yet He enjoys His own abode in the spiritual sky. There is no one equal to Him because His transcendental opulence is immeasurable.
baseline: O rādhāsā one who has destroyed the yogis by doing namā namā and that which is standing on the right hand of rīṣabha the seventh one the farthest one and the muhu the one who is standing in the left hand the same is done by rādha.
morphology: O rādhasa one who has destroyed the yogis by the same means should offer namā namā and tē rīśabha vīdura and muhu sāhvata kū ku yoginā.

sanskrit: yat kīrtanam yat smaraṇam yat īkṣaṇam yat vandanam yat śravaṇam yat arhaṇam lokasya sadyaḥ vidhunoti kalmaṣam tasmai subhadra śravase namaḥ namaḥ
reference: Let me offer my respectful obeisances unto the all-auspicious Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, about whom glorification, remembrances, audience, prayers, hearing and worship can at once cleanse the effects of all sins of the performer.
baseline: One who recites the hymn should recall the words iṣṇā vāṇā and hear the words that are said to be the means of earning the world. One who invents the scriptures should say Śubhadrā Śrāvase Namāh.
morphology: One who recites the kirtana or the recitation of the hymn ikṣṇa or the invocation the hearing the renunciation of the word śvāṇa and the reciting of the penitentiary scripture should be called subhadra Śrāvase namah.

sanskrit: vicakṣaṇāḥ yat caraṇa upasādanāt saṅgam vyudasya ubhayataḥ antaḥ ātmanaḥ vindanti hi brahma gatim gata klamāḥ tasmai subhadra śravase namaḥ namaḥ
reference: Let me offer my respectful obeisances again and again unto the all-auspicious Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa. The highly intellectual, simply by surrendering unto His lotus feet, are relieved of all attachments to present and future existences and without difficulty progress toward spiritual existence.
baseline: The disciples who worship the feet of the Lord and associate with him on both sides of the path are called Brahman. The disciple who moves in the direction of Brahman should be called subhadra śravaṣe namāhā.
morphology: The disciples who worship the feet of a devotee on the two sides of the vyudha are worshipped with the syllable Śubhadra Śrāvaṣe Namah.

sanskrit: tapasvinaḥ dāna parāḥ yaśasvinaḥ manasvinaḥ mantra vidaḥ su maṅgalāḥ kṣemam na vindanti vinā yat arpaṇam tasmai subhadra śravase namaḥ namaḥ
reference: Let me offer my respectful obeisances unto the all-auspicious Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa again and again because the great learned sages, the great performers of charity, the great workers of distinction, the great philosophers and mystics, the great chanters of the Vedic hymns and the great followers of Vedic principles cannot achieve any fruitful result without dedication of such great qualities to the service of the Lord.
baseline: The offerings made by the penitents to the meritorious and successful persons without having to say the mantra of Śuṇgālaṇa do not bring welfare. The offerings that are made without the subhadra should be offered to the sāravaśe.
morphology: The offerings made by the penitents to the meritorious and successful persons without having knowledge of the mantras of the mind the virtuous ones the benevolent ones and those who do not give welfare without having subhadra.

sanskrit: kirāta hūṇa āndhra pulinda pulkaśāḥ ābhīra śumbhāḥ yavanāḥ khasa ādayaḥ ye anye ca pāpāḥ yat apāśraya āśrayāḥ śudhyanti tasmai prabhaviṣṇave namaḥ
reference: Kirāta, Hūṇa, Āndhra, Pulinda, Pulkaśa, Ābhīra, Śumbha, Yavana, members of the Khasa races and even others addicted to sinful acts can be purified by taking shelter of the devotees of the Lord, due to His being the supreme power. I beg to offer my respectful obeisances unto Him.
baseline: O lord Viṣṇu the Lord of the earth the goddess of the sun the cow the elephant the tiger the pigeon the mound the deep cave the young man the king the sinner the poor and the other sins are purified by the abode of the god.
morphology: O Lord Viṣṇu the Lord of the universe the pitchers of the Śuṇas the deep sambhas the kīrātas hūṇas and the Āndras the elixirs the abyssals and the other sins which are committed by the yāṇas.

sanskrit: saḥ eṣaḥ ātmā ātmavatām adhīśvaraḥ trayī mayaḥ dharma mayaḥ tapaḥ mayaḥ gata vyalīkaiḥ aja śaṅkara ādibhiḥ vitarkya liṅgaḥ bhagavān prasīdatām
reference: He is the Supersoul and the Supreme Lord of all self-realized souls. He is the personification of the Vedas, religious scriptures and austerities. He is worshiped by Lord Brahmā and Śiva and all those who are transcendental to all pretensions. Being so revered with awe and veneration, may that Supreme Absolute be pleased with me.
baseline: He should worship the three gods atman the supreme self dharma penance vāliṣa ajā and Śankara.
morphology: He should worship the three gods ātman the supreme self my dharma my penance my pastime my vālyas and my lord.

sanskrit: śriyaḥ patiḥ yajña patiḥ prajā patiḥ dhiyām patiḥ loka patiḥ dharā patiḥ patiḥ gatiḥ ca andhaka vṛṣṇi sātvatām prasīdatām me bhagavān satām patiḥ
reference: May Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who is the worshipable Lord of all devotees, the protector and glory of all the kings like Andhaka and Vṛṣṇi of the Yadu dynasty, the husband of all goddesses of fortune, the director of all sacrifices and therefore the leader of all living entities, the controller of all intelligence, the proprietor of all planets, spiritual and material, and the supreme incarnation on the earth (the supreme all in all), be merciful upon me.
baseline: The husband of a devotee should be worshipped as the husband of the devotee the husband who is the servant of the subjects the wife of the people the spouse of the earth and the husband whose speed is dark and the son of a man should be blessed with seven sons of the god Sat.
morphology: The husband of a srīya the husband of sacrifice the wife of a subjects the spouse of a man the partner of a people the member of a kingdom the owner of a house the master of a ship the driver of a bull the king of a race the lord of seven gods the god of the earth the prophet of the seven gods and the king.

sanskrit: yat aṅghri abhidhyāna samādhi dhautayā dhiyā anupaśyanti hi tattvam ātmanaḥ vadanti ca etat kavayaḥ yathā rucam saḥ me mukundaḥ bhagavān prasīdatām
reference: It is the Personality of Godhead Śrī Kṛṣṇa who gives liberation. By thinking of His lotus feet at every second, following in the footsteps of authorities, the devotee in trance can see the Absolute Truth. The learned mental speculators, however, think of Him according to their whims. May the Lord be pleased with me.
baseline: The poet should say that he would like to worship the goddess Mukunda. He should be pleased with the fact that the body of the enemy is destroyed by the washing of the ashes. He would not be able to do so.
morphology: The poet should describe the principle of the body which is not found in the body of a man who has been buried by the enemy. He should say that the poet would like to do so. He would be pleased by the lord.

sanskrit: pracoditā yena purā sarasvatī vitanvatā ajasya satīm smṛtim hṛdi sva lakṣaṇā prādurabhūt kila āsyataḥ saḥ me ṛṣīṇām ṛṣabhaḥ prasīdatām
reference: May the Lord, who in the beginning of the creation amplified the potent knowledge of Brahmā from within his heart and inspired him with full knowledge of creation and of His own Self, and who appeared to be generated from the mouth of Brahmā, be pleased with me.
baseline: Having been inspired by Śrīṣabha the sage should be pleased with the sages of the kingdom. Having remembered the sati of Ajāja the heart should be blessed with its own qualities. He should be worshipped by the rishis.
morphology: Having been inspired by the sage Sarāsvati the sati of the goddess and the memory of her husband should be remembered. The heart should be blessed with her qualities. Having said this one should be pleased with the sages and Rishabha.

sanskrit: bhūtaiḥ mahadbhiḥ yaḥ imāḥ puraḥ vibhuḥ nirmāya śete yat amūṣu pūruṣaḥ bhuṅkte guṇān ṣoḍaśa ṣoḍaśa ātmakaḥ saḥ alaṅkṛṣīṣṭa bhagavān vacāṁsi me
reference: May the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who enlivens the materially created bodies of the elements by lying down within the universe, and who in His puruṣa incarnation causes the living being to be subjected to the sixteen divisions of material modes which are his generator, be pleased to decorate my statements.
baseline: One who builds these cities with the help of the gods gods and goddesses and who consumes the virtues of a man who is a man of the sixteenth and sixteenth self would be able to worship the lord with his ornaments.
morphology: One who builds these cities with the help of the gods gods and goddesses and who consumes the qualities of a man who has been worshipped by the gods of the sixteenth and sixteenth self should worship the lord with the ornament of the goddess.

sanskrit: namaḥ tasmai bhagavate vāsudevāya vedhase papuḥ jñānam ayam saumyāḥ yat mukha amburuha āsavam
reference: I offer my respectful obeisances unto Śrīla Vyāsadeva, the incarnation of Vāsudeva who compiled the Vedic scriptures. The pure devotees drink up the nectarean transcendental knowledge dropping from the lotuslike mouth of the Lord.
baseline: O Lord Vasudeva O Lord of the worlds the prophet should know that the face of Amburuha should be of the same soundness.
morphology: O Lord of the universe O Lord Vasudeva O lord of the world O Pāpu the knowledge of the face of the goddess Amburuha should be known to you.

sanskrit: etat eva ātma bhūḥ rājan nāradāya vipṛcchate veda garbhaḥ abhyadhāt sākṣāt yat āha hariḥ ātmanaḥ
reference: My dear King, Brahmā, the firstborn, on being questioned by Nārada, exactly apprised him on this subject as it had been directly spoken by the Lord to His own son, who was impregnated with Vedic knowledge from his very birth.
baseline: This is the self the earth the king the narada and the veda and the womb.
morphology: This is the self the earth the king the narada and the veda and the womb.

sanskrit: nāradaḥ uvāca deva deva namaḥ te astu bhūta bhāvana pūrva ja tat vijānīhi yat jñānam ātma tattva nidarśanam
reference: Śrī Nārada Muni asked Brahmājī: O chief amongst the demigods, O firstborn living entity, I beg to offer my respectful obeisances unto you. Please tell me that transcendental knowledge which specifically directs one to the truth of the individual soul and the Supersoul.
baseline: Narāda said that one should worship the gods and goddesses. He should know the spirit before the conception of the spirit. That knowledge is the manifestation of the essence of the self.
morphology: Narāda said that one should worship the gods and goddesses. He should know the spirit before the conception of the spirit. He is the manifestation of knowledge and the principle of the self.

sanskrit: yat rūpam yat adhiṣṭhānam yataḥ sṛṣṭam idam prabho yat saṁstham yat param yat ca tat tattvam vada tattvataḥ
reference: My dear father, please describe factually the symptoms of this manifest world. What is its background? How is it created? How is it conserved? And under whose control is all this being done?
baseline: The form which is established because it has been created should be said by the lord to be the one who is able to do that. The principle should be told.
morphology: The form which is the seat of existence is said to be created by the Lord. He who is able to do this is called the principal.

sanskrit: sarvam hi etat bhavān veda bhūta bhavya bhavat prabhuḥ kara āmalaka vat viśvam vijñāna avasitam tava
reference: My dear father, all this is known to you scientifically because whatever was created in the past, whatever will be created in the future, or whatever is being created at present, as well as everything within the universe, is within your grip, just like a walnut.
baseline: You are the supreme god of the Vedas. You should do the Lord's work. You have the knowledge of the universe.
morphology: You are the supreme god of the Vedas. The Lord of the universe is known as Amalaka. You are known as Veda.

sanskrit: yat vijñānaḥ yat ādhāraḥ yat paraḥ tvam yat ātmakaḥ ekaḥ sṛjasi bhūtāni bhūtaiḥ eva ātma māyayā
reference: My dear father, what is the source of your knowledge? Under whose protection are you standing? And under whom are you working? What is your real position? Do you alone create all entities with material elements by your personal energy?
baseline: The knowledge that is the basis for the creation of the self is said to be the self. The spirit beings are the spirits. The self is illusory.
morphology: The knowledge that is the basis for the creation of the self is said to be the self. One who creates the self the ghosts the demons the self and the illusion.

sanskrit: ātman (ātmani) bhāvayase tāni na parābhāvayan svayam ātma śaktim avaṣṭabhya ūrṇa nābhiḥ iva aklamaḥ
reference: As the spider very easily creates the network of its cobweb and manifests its power of creation without being defeated by others, so also you yourself, by employment of your self-sufficient energy, create without any other’s help.
baseline: One who does not perceive the spirits one who is not able to perceive them and who is unable to understand the power of the self is as wise as those who are not aware of the forces of the body.
morphology: One who does not perceive the spirits one who is not able to perceive them and who is unable to understand the power of the self one should be able to do so by the same means as one who has not been able to understand them.

sanskrit: na aham veda param hi asmin na aparam na samam vibho nāma rūpa guṇaiḥ bhāvyam sat asat kiñcit anyataḥ
reference: Whatever we can understand by the nomenclature, characteristics and features of a particular thing — superior, inferior or equal, eternal or temporary — is not created from any source other than that of Your Lordship, thou so great.
baseline: There is nothing above the Vedas which is not equal to the other. It is not the same as the name of the form. It has some other qualities.
morphology: There is nothing else in this scripture that is not equal to the Veda. It should be described as having the qualities of the form and the name Vibhava.

sanskrit: saḥ bhavān acarat ghoram yat tapaḥ su samāhitaḥ tena khedayase naḥ tvam parā śaṅkām ca yacchasi
reference: Yet we are moved to wonder about the existence of someone more powerful than you when we think of your great austerities in perfect discipline, although your good self is so powerful in the matter of creation.
baseline: He should not be afraid of you. If you do not repent and give you doubt you will get the punishment.
morphology: He should not be afraid of you. If he does not repent of the abomination which he has committed he will not be sorry. He will give you doubt.

sanskrit: etat me pṛcchataḥ sarvam sarva jña sakala īśvara vijānīhi yathā eva idam aham budhye anuśāsitaḥ
reference: My dear father, you know everything, and you are the controller of all. Therefore, may all that I have inquired from you be kindly instructed to me so that I may be able to understand it as your student.
baseline: This is the question that I ask. Knowing everything knowing everything the Lord is victorious. Just as I understand this I am disciplined.
