morphology: I ask this question. Knowing everything knowing everything the Lord is victorious. In the same way as I understand this I am disciplined.

sanskrit: brahmā uvāca samyak kāruṇikasya idam vatsa te vicikitsitam yat aham coditaḥ saumya bhagavat vīrya darśane
reference: Lord Brahmā said: My dear boy Nārada, being merciful to all (including me) you have asked all these questions because I have been inspired to see into the prowess of the Almighty Personality of Godhead.
baseline: He should say to Brahma that he is good and meritorious. He should know that I am a benevolent god and should see the semen.
morphology: He should say that Brahma is good and merciful. He should know that I am a gentle lord and should see the semen.

sanskrit: na anṛtam tava tat ca api yathā mām prabravīṣi bhoḥ avijñāya param mattaḥ etāvat tvam yataḥ hi me
reference: Whatever you have spoken about me is not false because unless and until one is aware of the Personality of Godhead, who is the ultimate truth beyond me, one is sure to be illusioned by observing my powerful activities.
baseline: He would not be able to do so even if he had not done so. He would have done so without knowing me. This is because of you.
morphology: He should not be afraid of you. He should be angry with you because he is not aware of me.

sanskrit: yena sva rociṣā viśvam rocitam rocayāmi aham yathā arkaḥ agniḥ yathā somaḥ yathā ṛkṣa graha tārakāḥ
reference: I create after the Lord’s creation by His personal effulgence [known as the brahmajyoti], just as when the sun manifests its fire, the moon, the firmament, the influential planets and the twinkling stars also manifest their brightness.
baseline: One who invents the universe with his own desire one who invokes the fire the spirit the sun the planets and stars.
morphology: One who invents the universe with his own desire one who invokes the fire the sun the planets stars etc. should be worshipped.

sanskrit: tasmai namaḥ bhagavate vāsudevāya dhīmahi yat māyayā durjayayā mām vadanti jagat gurum
reference: I offer my obeisances and meditate upon Lord Kṛṣṇa [Vāsudeva], the Personality of Godhead, whose invincible potency influences them [the less intelligent class of men] to call me the supreme controller.
baseline: O Lord of the universe the Lord of all beings should be worshipped with the words tāmā namā bhāgavātē vāsudeva maya māyā and the king mājaya.
morphology: O Lord of the universe the Lord of all beings should be worshipped with the hymn namā tāmā namā vāsudeva and the goddess mayāya should be said to me by the invincible lord.

sanskrit: vilajjamānayā yasya sthātum īkṣā pathe amuyā vimohitāḥ vikatthante mama aham iti durdhiyaḥ
reference: The illusory energy of the Lord cannot take precedence, being ashamed of her position, but those who are bewildered by her always talk nonsense, being absorbed in thoughts of “It is I” and “It is mine.”
baseline: One who has sought the place of his abode with the vow of vilajjāmaṇa would be enchanted by the path of Amu.
morphology: One who is ill willed by the illusion of his place in the path of the enemy would be destroyed by the delusion of the illusions.

sanskrit: dravyam karma ca kālaḥ ca sva bhāvaḥ jīvaḥ eva ca vāsudevāt paraḥ brahman na ca anyaḥ arthaḥ asti tattvataḥ
reference: The five elementary ingredients of creation, the interaction thereof set up by eternal time, and the intuition or nature of the individual living beings are all differentiated parts and parcels of the Personality of Godhead, Vāsudeva, and in truth there is no other value in them.
baseline: The matter action time feeling and life are the same as those of Vasudeva. Brahman has no other meaning than that of the principle.
morphology: The matter action and time are the manifestations of ones own being the living entity one who is above vāsudeva the Brahman and has no other meaning.

sanskrit: nārāyaṇa parāḥ vedāḥ devāḥ nārāyaṇa aṅga jāḥ nārāyaṇa parāḥ lokāḥ nārāyaṇa parāḥ makhāḥ
reference: The Vedic literatures are made by and are meant for the Supreme Lord, the demigods are also meant for serving the Lord as parts of His body, the different planets are also meant for the sake of the Lord, and different sacrifices are performed just to please Him.
baseline: The gods of the Vedas are Narāyana the limbs the members of the body the people and...
morphology: The gods of the Vedas are Narāyana the limbs of Śāṇāya the people of the other parts of the universe Śiva Nārāyaṇa and others.

sanskrit: nārāyaṇa paraḥ yogaḥ nārāyaṇa param tapaḥ nārāyaṇa param jñānam nārāyaṇa parā gatiḥ
reference: All different types of meditation or mysticism are means for realizing Nārāyaṇa. All austerities are aimed at achieving Nārāyaṇa. Culture of transcendental knowledge is for getting a glimpse of Nārāyaṇa, and ultimately salvation is entering the kingdom of Nārāyaṇa.
baseline: One who practices yoga above nārāyaṇa one who practices penance above nárāṇa and one who has knowledge above nērāyana and moves beyond.
morphology: One who practices yoga on the nārāyaṇa side one who practices penance on the naṛāṇa. one who has knowledge on the Naṛāna side and one who moves on the other side.

sanskrit: tasya api draṣṭuḥ īśasya kūṭa sthasya akhila ātmanaḥ sṛjyam sṛjāmi sṛṣṭaḥ aham īkṣayā eva abhicoditaḥ
reference: Inspired by Him only, I discover what is already created by Him [Nārāyaṇa] under His vision as the all-pervading Supersoul, and I also am created by Him only.
baseline: One who sees the image of the same one who is in the body of the god and who creates the whole of the self is called to be created by the eye.
morphology: One who sees the image of Śiva and the image that is placed in the temple of Āṣṇu should create the whole of the self. One who is created by the eye is called Āksha.

sanskrit: sattvam rajaḥ tamaḥ iti nirguṇasya guṇāḥ trayaḥ sthiti sarga nirodheṣu gṛhītāḥ māyayā vibhoḥ
reference: The Supreme Lord is pure, spiritual form, transcendental to all material qualities, yet for the sake of the creation of the material world and its maintenance and annihilation, He accepts through His external energy the material modes of nature called goodness, passion and ignorance.
baseline: The virtues of Nirguna such as sattva rajā tāma are held in three positions in the heavenly confinement.
morphology: The three positions of the qualities of Nirguna Sattva Raja and Tama are held in the precincts of heaven.

sanskrit: kārya kāraṇa kartṛtve dravya jñāna kriyā āśrayāḥ badhnanti nityadā muktam māyinam puruṣam guṇāḥ
reference: These three modes of material nature, being further manifested as matter, knowledge and activities, put the eternally transcendental living entity under conditions of cause and effect and make him responsible for such activities.
baseline: One who has done the work for the sake of doing the work and knowing the material things and doing the works for the benefit of the people will always be free from evil deeds.
morphology: One who does the work for the sake of the cause and does the knowledge of things the actions of the protector and the protectors of things are always free and meritorious.

sanskrit: saḥ eṣaḥ bhagavān liṅgaiḥ tribhiḥ etaiḥ adhokṣajaḥ su alakṣita gatiḥ brahman sarveṣām mama ca īśvaraḥ
reference: O Brāhmaṇa Nārada, the Superseer, the transcendent Lord, is beyond the perception of the material senses of the living entities because of the above-mentioned three modes of nature. But He is the controller of everyone, including me.
baseline: He is the lord of all three linga the lower body and the direction of all Brahman and my God.
morphology: He is the lord of all the three linga forms. He is known to be the master of all beings. He has not been able to move beyond the bounds of the universe. He also is my lord.

sanskrit: kālam karma svabhāvam ca māyā īśaḥ māyayā svayā ātman (ātmani) yadṛcchayā prāptam vibubhūṣuḥ upādade
reference: The Lord, who is the controller of all energies, thus creates, by His own potency, eternal time, the fate of all living entities, and their particular nature, for which they were created, and He again merges them independently.
baseline: One who has acquired the self by doing the kālāma karma nārtā mayiā one who has attained the selfs self by doing such a deed would be blessed by the Lord.
morphology: The nature of the kālama should be described as the nature and the illusion of the self. One who acquires the self from the self by the illusions of the mind should be taught to those who are illiterate.

sanskrit: kālāt guṇa vyatikaraḥ pariṇāmaḥ svabhāvataḥ karmaṇaḥ janma mahataḥ puruṣa adhiṣṭhitāt abhūt
reference: After the incarnation of the first puruṣa [Kāraṇārṇavaśāyī Viṣṇu], the mahat-tattva, or the principles of material creation, take place, and then time is manifested, and in course of time the three qualities appear. Nature means the three qualitative appearances. They transform into activities.
baseline: One who deviates from the virtues by time would get the results of the actions by nature. One would get great wealth by taking birth.
morphology: One who deviates from the virtues by time would get the result. One would be born born with the qualities of deeds by nature and would become a great man.

sanskrit: mahataḥ tu vikurvāṇāt rajaḥ sattva upabṛṁhitāt tamaḥ pradhānaḥ tu abhavat dravya jñāna kriyā ātmakaḥ
reference: Material activities are caused by the mahat-tattva’s being agitated. At first there is transformation of the modes of goodness and passion, and later — due to the mode of ignorance — matter, its knowledge, and different activities of material knowledge come into play.
baseline: The king should be made great by the practice of vikrvana and the king should become the chief minister by the use of the sub-brahmins. The master should be the master of the matter.
morphology: One who becomes great by the manifestation of vikrvaṇa the king sattva subbrāhita tāmā became supreme by the knowledge of matter knowledge and action of self.

sanskrit: saḥ ahaṅkāraḥ iti proktaḥ vikurvan samabhūt tridhā vaikārikaḥ taijasaḥ ca tāmasaḥ ca iti yat bhidā dravya śaktiḥ kriyā śaktiḥ jñāna śaktiḥ iti prabho
reference: The self-centered materialistic ego, thus being transformed into three features, becomes known as the modes of goodness, passion and ignorance in three divisions, namely the powers that evolve matter, knowledge of material creations, and the intelligence that guides such materialistic activities. Nārada, you are quite competent to understand this.
baseline: He is said to be egoistic. He should have three senses and three tājāsas. The Lord has said that there is material power action power knowledge power.
morphology: He is said to be egoistic. He should be equal to the three spirits. He is known to be a man of good will. He has been described as having the power of knowledge.

sanskrit: tāmasāt api bhūta ādeḥ vikurvāṇāt abhūt nabhaḥ tasya mātrā guṇaḥ śabdaḥ liṅgam yat draṣṭṛ dṛśyayoḥ
reference: From the darkness of false ego, the first of the five elements, namely the sky, is generated. Its subtle form is the quality of sound, exactly as the seer is in relationship with the seen.
baseline: One who has seen the linga after having seen it would not get its qualities even after having experienced the illusion of the ghost.
morphology: One who has seen the linga should not be afraid of the presence of ghosts. He should be aware of the qualities of the same.

sanskrit: nabhasaḥ atha vikurvāṇāt abhūt sparśa guṇaḥ anilaḥ para anvayāt śabdavān ca prāṇaḥ ojaḥ sahaḥ balam vāyoḥ api vikurvāṇāt kāla karma svabhāvataḥ udapadyata tejaḥ vai rūpavat sparśa śabdavat tejasaḥ tu vikurvāṇāt āsīt ambhaḥ rasa ātmakam rūpavat sparśavat ca ambhaḥ ghoṣavat ca para anvayāt viśeṣaḥ tu vikurvāṇāt ambhasaḥ gandhavān abhūt para anvayāt rasa sparśa śabda rūpa guṇa anvitaḥ
reference: Because the sky is transformed, the air is generated with the quality of touch, and by previous succession the air is also full of sound and the basic principles of duration of life: sense perception, mental power and bodily strength. When the air is transformed in course of time and nature’s course, fire is generated, taking shape with the sense of touch and sound. Since fire is also transformed, there is a manifestation of water, full of juice and taste. As previously, it also has form and touch and is also full of sound. And water, being transformed from all variegatedness on earth, appears odorous and, as previously, becomes qualitatively full of juice, touch, sound and form respectively.
baseline: The qualities of touch obtained from the manifestation of the sky the sound of fire the energy of fire and fire and the force of air are derived from that manifestation. The nature of energy obtained from manifestation the form touch sound brilliance vibration taste taste and sound are obtained by manifestation and the fragrance obtained from propagation is obtained by imitation.
morphology: The qualities of touch obtained from the manifestation of the air the sound of fire fire light energy energy and energy obtained from manifestation the nature of action obtained from propagation from manifestations the form form touch sound brilliance vibration form and form the manifestations of matter and sound etc.

sanskrit: vaikārikāt manaḥ jajñe devāḥ vaikārikāḥ daśa dik vāta arka pracetaḥ aśvi vahni indra upendra mitra kāḥ
reference: From the mode of goodness the mind is generated and becomes manifest, as also the ten demigods controlling the bodily movements. Such demigods are known as the controller of directions, the controller of air, the sun-god, the father of Dakṣa Prajāpati, the Aśvinī-kumāras, the fire-god, the King of heaven, the worshipable deity in heaven, the chief of the Ādityas, and Brahmājī, the Prajāpati. All come into existence.
baseline: Having learned the mind from the spirit the spirit of the gods should be directed ten times. The spirit of Indra and Upendra should be sent to the earth.
morphology: One who knows the mind from the spirit one who has the heart from the ten directions of the spirit and who has sent the spirit to the gods and who is the friend of Indra Upendra and others.

sanskrit: taijasāt tu vikurvāṇāt indriyāṇi daśa abhavan jñāna śaktiḥ kriyā śaktiḥ buddhiḥ prāṇaḥ ca taijasau śrotram tvak ghrāṇa dṛk jihvāḥ vāk doḥ meḍhra aṅghri pāyavaḥ
reference: By further transformation of the mode of passion, the sense organs like the ear, skin, nose, eyes, tongue, mouth, hands, genitals, legs, and the outlet for evacuating, together with intelligence and living energy, are all generated.
baseline: The senses are tenfold in size by the sound of the voice the power of knowledge the energy of action the strength of intellect the sense of hearing the fragrance of smell the sight of the tongue the speech of the sheep the voice of the cow the sound and sound of fire.
morphology: Then the senses become ten by the sound of the voice the power of knowledge action intelligence hearing smell sight tongue speech speech and speech.

sanskrit: yadā ete asaṅgatāḥ bhāvāḥ bhūta indriya manaḥ guṇāḥ yadā āyatana nirmāṇe na śekuḥ brahma vit tama
reference: O Nārada, best of the transcendentalists, the forms of the body cannot take place as long as these created parts, namely the elements, senses, mind and modes of nature, are not assembled.
baseline: When these are incompatible with the manifestations of the senses the sense organs and the mental qualities are not formed in the rectangle the Brahman is not formed.
morphology: When these are incompatible with the manifestations of the senses the sense organs and the mind are not able to form the rectangle the Brahman is not able.

sanskrit: tadā saṁhatya ca anyonyam bhagavat śakti coditāḥ sat asattvam upādāya ca ubhayam sasṛjuḥ hi adaḥ
reference: Thus when all these became assembled by force of the energy of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, this universe certainly came into being by accepting both the primary and secondary causes of creation.
baseline: Then one should kill the other and the power should be sought as if it were the Lord. Both the gods should be worshipped as the creator.
morphology: Then one should kill the other by doing the same thing. Both the gods should be worshipped with the same power as the gods. Both should be given the same gift.

sanskrit: varṣa pūga sahasra ante tat aṇḍam udake śayam kāla karma svabhāva sthaḥ jīvaḥ ajīvam ajīvayat
reference: Thus all the universes remained thousands of aeons within the water [the Causal Ocean], and the Lord of living beings, entering in each of them, caused them to be fully animated.
baseline: The egg should be laid at the end of a thousand years in the sun and should be kept in the bed for a period of time. The organism should be immortal.
morphology: The egg should be laid at the end of a thousand years in the morning and the body should be kept in the sun for a period of time.

sanskrit: saḥ eva puruṣaḥ tasmāt aṇḍam nirbhidya nirgataḥ sahasra ūru aṅghri bāhu akṣaḥ sahasra ānana śīrṣavān
reference: The Lord [Mahā-Viṣṇu], although lying in the Causal Ocean, came out of it, and dividing Himself as Hiraṇyagarbha, He entered into each universe and assumed the virāṭ-rūpa, with thousands of legs, arms, mouths, heads, etc.
baseline: The same man would then lay an egg without fear and leave a thousand cubits. He would then raise the arms and the axes of a thousand heads.
morphology: The same man would then lay an egg without fear and leave a thousand cubits.

sanskrit: yasya iha avayavaiḥ lokān kalpayanti manīṣiṇaḥ kaṭi ādibhiḥ adhaḥ sapta sapta ūrdhvam jaghana ādibhiḥ
reference: Great philosophers imagine that the complete planetary systems in the universe are displays of the different upper and lower limbs of the universal body of the Lord.
baseline: One who has these parts of the body would be able to draw people with the hands and hands. One would get seven high feet below the waist and above the head.
morphology: One who has these parts of the body would be able to imagine the people. The wise man would have seven upper legs below the waist and seven upper limbs below the back.

sanskrit: puruṣasya mukham brahma kṣatram etasya bāhavaḥ ūrvoḥ vaiśyaḥ bhagavataḥ padbhyām śūdraḥ vyajāyata
reference: The brāhmaṇas represent His mouth, the kṣatriyas His arms, the vaiśyas His thighs, and the śūdras are born of His legs.
baseline: The face of the man is called brahmā kṣatra the arms are called varva the vaiṣya the bhagavata the shudra and the pāda.
morphology: The face of the man is said to be Brahma. The arms of this man are called Uvarva. The lord of the vaiṣṇas is described as Śudra.

sanskrit: bhūḥ lokaḥ kalpitaḥ padbhyām bhuvaḥ lokaḥ asya nābhitaḥ hṛdā svarlokaḥ urasā maharlokaḥ mahā ātmanaḥ
reference: The lower planetary systems, up to the limit of the earthly stratum, are said to be situated in His legs. The middle planetary systems, beginning from Bhuvarloka, are situated in His navel. And the still higher planetary systems, occupied by the demigods and highly cultured sages and saints, are situated in the chest of the Supreme Lord.
baseline: The earth the world the earth and the world are created. The heart the heaven the fire and the great soul are enshrined in this world.
morphology: The earth the world the earth and the world are created. The heart the heaven the fire the great spirit are created by the earth.

sanskrit: grīvāyām janalokaḥ asya tapolokaḥ stana dvayāt mūrdhabhiḥ satyalokaḥ tu brahmalokaḥ sanātanaḥ
reference: From the forefront of the chest up to the neck of the universal form of the Lord are situated the planetary systems named Janaloka and Tapoloka, whereas Satyaloka, the topmost planetary system, is situated on the head of the form. The spiritual planets, however, are eternal.
baseline: One who is born in the womb of the world one who is obedient to the rules of this world and who is foolish in the two breasts is the true world. One who becomes Brahman is eternal.
morphology: One who has two heads in the neck one who has a penitentiary and one who is obedient in the breasts is the true world. One who is eternal is Brahman.

sanskrit: tat kaṭyām ca atalam kḷptam ūrubhyām vitalam vibhoḥ jānubhyām sutalam śuddham jaṅghābhyām tu talātalam mahātalam tu gulphābhyām prapadābhyām rasātalam pātālam pāda talataḥ iti loka mayaḥ pumān
reference: My dear son Nārada, know from me that there are seven lower planetary systems out of the total fourteen. The first planetary system, known as Atala, is situated on the waist; the second, Vitala, is situated on the thighs; the third, Sutala, on the knees; the fourth, Talātala, on the shanks; the fifth, Mahātala, on the ankles; the sixth, Rasātala, on the upper portion of the feet; and the seventh, Pātāla, on the soles of the feet. Thus the virāṭ form of the Lord is full of all planetary systems.
baseline: It should be cut with a piece of ground a piece made of wood a sheet of water a jute a sieve a cotton a pure jungla a lotus a large watermelon a gulf a pot of water and a stone made of water.
morphology: It should be cut with a piece of ground a piece made of mud a stone made of water a jade made of sandal and pure jungles a lotus made of clay and a stone of water made of gulpha a pot of water and water.

sanskrit: bhūrlokaḥ kalpitaḥ padbhyām bhuvarlokaḥ asya nābhitaḥ svarlokaḥ kalpitaḥ mūrdhnā iti vā loka kalpanā
reference: Others may divide the whole planetary system into three divisions, namely the lower planetary systems on the legs [up to the earth], the middle planetary systems on the navel, and the upper planetary systems [Svarloka] from the chest to the head of the Supreme Personality.
baseline: The earthly world is conceived of as the earth and the earth is not conceived as this. The worldly world as it is is is conceived as the world of gold and the world as foolishness.
morphology: The world is conceived of as having the earth. The world of earth is conceived as having a sky and the world of gold as having been created by the sun.

sanskrit: brahmā uvāca vācām vahneḥ mukham kṣetram chandasām sapta dhātavaḥ havya kavya amṛta annānām jihvā sarva rasasya ca
reference: Lord Brahmā said: The mouth of the virāṭ-puruṣa [the universal form of the Lord] is the generating center of the voice, and the controlling deity is Fire. His skin and six other layers are the generating centers of the Vedic hymns, and His tongue is the productive center of different foodstuffs and delicacies for offering to the demigods, the forefathers and the general mass of people.

reference: Beginning from me [Brahmā] down to you and Bhava [Śiva], all the great sages who were born before you, the demigods, the demons, the Nāgas, the human beings, the birds, the beasts, as well as the reptiles, etc., and all phenomenal manifestations of the universes, namely the planets, stars, asteroids, luminaries, lightning, thunder, and the inhabitants of the different planetary systems, namely the Gandharvas, Apsarās, Yakṣas, Rakṣas, Bhūtagaṇas, Uragas, Paśus, Pitās, Siddhas, Vidyādharas, Cāraṇas, and all other different varieties of living entities, including the birds, beasts, trees and everything that be, are all covered by the universal form of the Lord at all times, namely past, present and future, although He is transcendental to all of them, eternally existing in a form not exceeding nine inches.

sanskrit: sva dhiṣṇyam pratapan prāṇaḥ bahiḥ ca pratapati asau evam virājam pratapan tapati antaḥ bahiḥ pumān

sanskrit: saḥ amṛtasya abhayasya īśaḥ martyam annam yat atyagāt mahimā eṣaḥ tataḥ brahman puruṣasya duratyayaḥ
reference: The Supreme Personality of Godhead is the controller of immortality and fearlessness, and He is transcendental to death and the fruitive actions of the material world. O Nārada, O brāhmaṇa, it is therefore difficult to measure the glories of the Supreme Person.

morphology: All the spirits should be placed on the feet in the position of the feet. The position should be of the three types of elixir.

reference: O Nārada, because I have caught hold of the lotus feet of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Hari, with great zeal, whatever I say has never proved to have been false. Nor is the progress of my mind ever deterred. Nor are my senses ever degraded by temporary attachment to matter.

morphology: Neither the heart nor the body nor the mind nor the movements of the body should be remembered in the manner in which the heart and the heart should be worshipped.

sanskrit: saḥ aham samāmnāya mayaḥ tapaḥ mayaḥ prajāpatīnām abhivanditaḥ patiḥ āsthāya yogam nipuṇam samāhitaḥ tam na adhyagaccham yataḥ ātma sambhavaḥ
reference: Although I am known as the great Brahmā, perfect in the disciplic succession of Vedic wisdom, and although I have undergone all austerities and am an expert in mystic powers and self-realization, and although I am recognized as such by the great forefathers of the living entities, who offer me respectful obeisances, still I cannot understand Him, the Lord, the very source of my birth.

reference: Therefore it is best for me to surrender unto His feet, which alone can deliver one from the miseries of repeated birth and death. reference: Since neither Lord Śiva nor you nor I could ascertain the limits of spiritual happiness, how can other demigods know it? And because all of us are bewildered by the illusory, external energy of the Supreme Lord, we can see only this manifested cosmos according to our individual ability.

reference: Let us offer our respectful obeisances unto that Supreme Personality of Godhead, whose incarnations and activities are chanted by us for glorification, though He can hardly be fully known as He is.
