morphology: One whose incarnations and deeds are sung to him one who does not know the principles of the beginning should worship him.

sanskrit: saḥ eṣaḥ ādyaḥ puruṣaḥ kalpe kalpe sṛjati ajaḥ ātmā ātmani ātmanā ātmānam saḥ saṁyacchati pāti ca
reference: That supreme original Personality of Godhead, Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, expanding His plenary portion as Mahā-Viṣṇu, the first incarnation, creates this manifested cosmos, but He is unborn. The creation, however, takes place in Him, and the material substance and manifestations are all Himself. He maintains them for some time and absorbs them into Himself again.
baseline: He is the first man who creates in the imagination the spirit the self the soul and the self. He completes the creation of the soul by the spirit.
morphology: He is the first man who creates in the imagination the spirit the self the soul and the self. He makes the self possible by the spirit. He becomes the father.

sanskrit: viśuddham kevalam jñānam pratyak samyak avasthitam satyam pūrṇam anādi antam nirguṇam nityam advayam ṛṣe vidanti munayaḥ praśānta ātma indriya āśayāḥ yadā tat eva asat tarkaiḥ tiraḥ dhīyeta viplutam
reference: The Personality of Godhead is pure, being free from all contaminations of material tinges. He is the Absolute Truth and the embodiment of full and perfect knowledge. He is all-pervading, without beginning or end, and without rival. O Nārada, O great sage, the great thinkers can know Him when completely freed from all material hankerings and when sheltered under undisturbed conditions of the senses. Otherwise, by untenable arguments, all is distorted, and the Lord disappears from our sight.
baseline: One who is pure only knowing fully present full of truth eternal undefiled everlasting and unselfish always acquainted with sages tranquil beings senses desires when that is the same should be worshipped by the sages.
morphology: One who is pure only knowledge one who is well situated full of truth end without beginning one with the qualities of the self and one who has never been unattached to others would always be blessed with the sage calm self sensory desires when those are the same.

sanskrit: ādyaḥ avatāraḥ puruṣaḥ parasya kālaḥ svabhāvaḥ sat asat manaḥ ca dravyam vikāraḥ guṇaḥ indriyāṇi virāṭ svarāṭ sthāsnu cariṣṇu bhūmnaḥ
reference: Kāraṇārṇavaśāyī Viṣṇu is the first incarnation of the Supreme Lord, and He is the master of eternal time, space, cause and effects, mind, the elements, the material ego, the modes of nature, the senses, the universal form of the Lord, Garbhodakaśāyī Viṣṇu, and the sum total of all living beings, both moving and nonmoving.
baseline: The first incarnation of a man is the manifestation of time nature mind matter disorder qualities senses sound sound and position.
morphology: The first incarnation of a man is the manifest time and the nature. The mind is the matter and the qualities are the distortions. The senses are the sound and the earth are the objects.

sanskrit: aham bhavaḥ yajñaḥ ime prajā īśāḥ dakṣa ādayaḥ ye bhavat ādayaḥ ca svarloka pālāḥ khagaloka pālāḥ nṛloka pālāḥ talaloka pālāḥ gandharva vidyādhara cāraṇa īśāḥ ye yakṣa rakṣa uraga nāga nāthāḥ ye vā ṛṣīṇām ṛṣabhāḥ pitṝṇām daitya indra siddha īśvara dānava indrāḥ anye ca ye preta piśāca bhūta kūṣmāṇḍa yādaḥ mṛga pakṣi adhīśāḥ yat kim ca loke bhagavat mahasvat ojaḥ sahasvat balavat kṣamāvat śrī hrī vibhūti ātmavat adbhuta arṇam tattvam param rūpavat asva rūpam
reference: I myself [Brahmā], Lord Śiva, Lord Viṣṇu, great generators of living beings like Dakṣa and Prajāpati, yourselves [Nārada and the Kumāras], heavenly demigods like Indra and Candra, the leaders of the Bhūrloka planets, the leaders of the earthly planets, the leaders of the lower planets, the leaders of the Gandharva planets, the leaders of the Vidyādhara planets, the leaders of the Cāraṇaloka planets, the leaders of the Yakṣas, Rakṣas and Uragas, the great sages, the great demons, the great atheists and the great spacemen, as well as the dead bodies, evil spirits, satans, jinn, kūṣmāṇḍas, great aquatics, great beasts and great birds, etc. — in other words, anything and everything which is exceptionally possessed of power, opulence, mental and perceptual dexterity, strength, forgiveness, beauty, modesty, opulence, and breeding, whether in form or formless — may appear to be the specific truth and the form of the Lord, but actually they are not so. They are only a fragment of the transcendental potency of the Lord.
baseline: I abhu yagya i bhu bhut kuśmanda jaṇḍa jāśmā i bhū gāṣmā and śvāda Śvā abhā pālā kāśma śva ṣvā and gāṇḍharva pala gaṇṭra Ā gān loka pála nr lok ṇ āśvara
morphology: I am the sacrifice of you the people the gods the wise and the meritorious those who are the beginning the celestial the pale the dark and the dark the palmyra the gandharbhava the learned and the cowherd the yaksha the serpent the snake the elephant the king the demon the god of the sages the sage the lord of the fathers the demigods the vulture the ghost the cow the deer the bird the lion the spirit the animal the

sanskrit: prādhānyataḥ yān ṛṣe āmananti līlā avatārān puruṣasya bhūmnaḥ āpīyatām karṇa kaṣāya śoṣān anukramiṣye te imān su peśān
reference: O Nārada, now I shall state, one after another, the transcendental incarnations of the Lord known as līlā-avatāras. Hearing of their activities counteracts all foul matters accumulated in the ear. These pastimes are pleasing to hear and are to be relished. Therefore they are in my heart.
baseline: Those who are worshipped in the preeminence of the sage lila the incarnations of a man should be placed on the ground and the ear should be cut open and the hair should be drawn.
morphology: Those who are worshipped in the preeminence of the sage Lila the incarnations of the lord should be placed on the ground of the male. They should be made to have their ears pierced and their hands covered with blood.

sanskrit: brahmā uvāca yatra udyataḥ kṣiti tala uddharaṇāya bibhrat krauḍīm tanum sakala yajña mayīm anantaḥ antar mahā arṇave upāgatam ādi daityam tam daṁṣṭrayā adrim iva vajra dharaḥ dadāra
reference: Lord Brahmā said: When the unlimitedly powerful Lord assumed the form of a boar as a pastime, just to lift the planet earth, which was drowned in the great ocean of the universe called the Garbhodaka, the first demon [Hiraṇyākṣa] appeared, and the Lord pierced him with His tusk.
baseline: O brahmana one who has gone to the place where he is going to raise the sky and the ground is misguided. One who has offered all sacrifices to the gods of the universe and has come to the great ark from within is called the Adi Daitā. He should be given the king of the earth.
morphology: O Brahma one who has gone to the place where the sky is falling and has gone astray for the purpose of lifting up the ground one should offer all the sacrifices to the goddess Ananta. One who comes to the great ark from within would be blessed with the first demon. He would get a diamond like that of a diamond.

sanskrit: jātaḥ ruceḥ ajanayat suyamān suyajñaḥ ākūti sūnuḥ amarān atha dakṣiṇāyām loka trayasya mahatīm aharat yat ārtim svāyambhuvena manunā hariḥ iti anūktaḥ
reference: The Prajāpati first begot Suyajña in the womb of his wife Ākūti, and then Suyajña begot demigods, headed by Suyama, in the womb of his wife Dakṣiṇā. Suyajña, as the Indradeva, diminished very great miseries in the three planetary systems [upper, lower and intermediate], and because he so diminished the miseries of the universe, he was later called Hari by the great father of mankind, namely Svāyambhuva Manu.
baseline: One who has attained happiness by doing the sacrifice of a suyāman the supreme sacrifice of the immortals and the great sacrifice of three men in the south should be said to be aarti by the lord of the self.
morphology: One who has chosen the best of the three gods should offer a sacrifice to the king of the south. One who does not know whether the king would be good or not should offer the supreme sacrifice of three gods to the lord of the South. One should say that the king should be great.

sanskrit: jajñe ca kardama gṛhe dvija devahūtyām strībhiḥ samam navabhiḥ ātma gatim sva mātre ūce yayā ātma śamalam guṇa saṅga paṅkam asmin vidhūya kapilasya gatim prapede
reference: The Lord then appeared as the Kapila incarnation, being the son of the prajāpati brāhmaṇa Kardama and his wife, Devahūti, along with nine other women [sisters]. He spoke to His mother about self-realization, by which, in that very lifetime, she became fully cleansed of the mud of the material modes and thereby achieved liberation, the path of Kapila.
baseline: The bridegroom should repeat the steps of Kapila in the house with the words jāgāṇā kārdā dvījā devā hūtā and the nine women in the same manner as the husbands feet.
morphology: The bridegroom should repeat the steps of Kapila in the house of the king and the two gods in the houses of the goddesses in the same manner as the women. The nine gods should raise the speed of the self to the height of their own self. The wife should be able to bear the virtues of the husband.

sanskrit: atreḥ apatyam abhikāṅkṣataḥ āha tuṣṭaḥ dattaḥ mayā aham iti yat bhagavān saḥ dattaḥ yat pāda paṅkaja parāga pavitra dehāḥ yoga ṛddhim āpuḥ ubhayīm yadu haihaya ādyāḥ
reference: The great sage Atri prayed for offspring, and the Lord, being satisfied with him, promised to incarnate as Atri’s son, Dattātreya [Datta, the son of Atri]. And by the grace of the lotus feet of the Lord, many Yadus, Haihayas, etc., became so purified that they obtained both material and spiritual blessings.
baseline: The son should be born at home and the child should be given to me with a wish. The god should give me the feet hair pollen holy body yoga wisdom blood and both.
morphology: One who gives a son to a person with the desire of having a son at home and who is satisfied with the wish of having one should say that he has been given by the lord that which is the pāṇga pāṅga prāga purified body yogā riddhi yāpu yaṇu hāhā yūhā and ya.

sanskrit: taptam tapaḥ vividha loka sisṛkṣayā me ādau sanāt sva tapasaḥ saḥ catuḥ sanaḥ abhūt prāk kalpa samplava vinaṣṭam iha ātma tattvam samyak jagāda munayaḥ yat acakṣata ātman
reference: To create different planetary systems I had to undergo austerities and penance, and the Lord, thus being pleased with me, incarnated in four sanas [Sanaka, Sanatkumāra, Sanandana and Sanātana]. In the previous creation the spiritual truth was devastated, but the four sanas explained it so nicely that the truth at once became clearly perceived by the sages.
baseline: The sage who had asked for the principle of the self should first know that after having done his own penance he would get four sons. He would have destroyed the concept of self. He should explain the principles of self to the sages.
morphology: The sage who had asked the sages for the principles of the self should first hear the tapas of the four sāṇas before the four months of his penance were completed.

sanskrit: dharmasya dakṣa duhitari ajaniṣṭa mūrtyām nārāyaṇaḥ naraḥ iti sva tapaḥ prabhāvaḥ dṛṣṭvā ātmanaḥ bhagavataḥ niyama avalopam devyaḥ tu anaṅga pṛtanāḥ ghaṭitum na śekuḥ
reference: To exhibit His personal way of austerity and penance, He appeared in twin forms as Nārāyaṇa and Nara in the womb of Mūrti, the wife of Dharma and the daughter of Dakṣa. Celestial beauties, the companions of Cupid, went to try to break His vows, but they were unsuccessful, for they saw that many beauties like them were emanating from Him, the Personality of Godhead.
baseline: Having seen the effect of his penance on the image of Narayana as male and not of an unknown nature and having experienced the virtuousness of the dharma one would not be able to escape the law of the self the lord the gods and the unorganized elements.
morphology: Having seen the effect of his penance on the image of the god Nārāyaṇa one who is not aware of the righteousness of the gods should not be able to do the same without having to follow the rules of the lord.

sanskrit: kāmam dahanti kṛtinaḥ nanu roṣa dṛṣṭyā roṣam dahantam uta te na dahanti asahyam saḥ ayam yat antaram alam praviśan bibheti kāmaḥ katham nu punaḥ asya manaḥ śrayeta
reference: Great stalwarts like Lord Śiva can, by their wrathful glances, overcome lust and vanquish him, yet they cannot be free from the overwhelming effects of their own wrath. Such wrath can never enter into the heart of Him [the Lord], who is above all this. So how can lust take shelter in His mind?
baseline: One who does not burn the anger in the sight of the anger of those who have done the burning of the desire or those who do not burn it will hear the heart of the enemy again.
morphology: One who does not burn the anger in the sight of the anger of those who have done the burning of lust or those who do not burn it should hear the heart of the person who has entered the inner world and has no desire.

sanskrit: viddhaḥ sapatni udita patribhiḥ anti rājñaḥ bālaḥ api san upagataḥ tapase vanāni tasmai adāt dhruva gatim gṛṇate prasannaḥ divyāḥ stuvanti munayaḥ yat upari adhastāt
reference: Being insulted by sharp words spoken by the co-wife of the king, even in his presence, Prince Dhruva, though only a boy, took to severe penances in the forest. And the Lord, being satisfied by his prayer, awarded him the Dhruva planet, which is worshiped by great sages, both upward and downward.
baseline: The son of the king should also come up with the seven leaves of the goddess Viddha. He should also go to the forest after doing penance. Having taken the pole the goddess should be pleased and praised by the sage who is placed on the top.
morphology: The son of the king should be brought up with seven leaves and the son should be given the forest after having gone to the king. The king should take the pole and the goddess which is above and below and praise the goddess after having given him the forest.

sanskrit: yat venam utpatha gatam dvija vākya vajra niṣpluṣṭa pauruṣa bhagam niraye patantam trātvā arthitaḥ jagati putra padam ca lebhe dugdhā vasūni vasudhā sakalāni yena
reference: Mahārāja Vena went astray from the path of righteousness, and the brāhmaṇas chastised him by the thunderbolt curse. By this King Vena was burnt with his good deeds and opulence and was en route to hell. The Lord, by His causeless mercy, descended as his son, by the name of Pṛthu, delivered the condemned King Vena from hell, and exploited the earth by drawing all kinds of crops as produce.
baseline: The two words that are derived from the vena which has gone beyond the vajra purūṣa bhāga nirā bhagā śvattha jagatī son pāda leva milk vasudha vāsudha and sakalā are said to have been obtained by the fall of the earth.
morphology: The word vena which is born out of the two elements of vaṇa and which has passed away is called jāgatī son post milk vasudha sakalā vāsudha.

sanskrit: nābheḥ asau ṛṣabhaḥ āsa sudevi sūnuḥ yaḥ vai cacāra sama dṛk jaḍa yoga caryām yat pāramahaṁsyam ṛṣayaḥ padam āmananti svasthaḥ praśānta karaṇaḥ parimukta saṅgaḥ
reference: The Lord appeared as the son of Sudevī, the wife of King Nābhi, and was known as Ṛṣabhadeva. He performed materialistic yoga to equibalance the mind. This stage is also accepted as the highest perfectional situation of liberation, wherein one is situated in one’s self and is completely satisfied.
baseline: The sage should observe the practice of jāda yoga in the same manner as that of sundevi son of a goddess who is in the form of the navel rīśabha rāśva sage sages who perform the posture of parāmahā and make the position sound and tranquil.
morphology: The sage should observe the practice of jāda yoga in the same manner as that of sundevi son of a goddess who is in the form of the navel rīśabha rāśva sage sages and sages should perform the posture of pārṣṇa and purified association.

sanskrit: satre mama āsa bhagavān haya śīraṣā atha sākṣāt saḥ yajña puruṣaḥ tapanīya varṇaḥ chandaḥ mayaḥ makha mayaḥ akhila devatā ātmā vācaḥ babhūvuḥ uśatīḥ śvasataḥ asya nastaḥ
reference: The Lord appeared as the Hayagrīva incarnation in a sacrifice performed by me [Brahmā]. He is the personified sacrifices, and the hue of His body is golden. He is the personified Vedas as well, and the Supersoul of all demigods. When He breathed, all the sweet sounds of the Vedic hymns came out of His nostrils.
baseline: In the course of the session the lord should be worshipped in the form of a sīrṣa. Then the sacrificial man should be offered to the lord in the same manner. He should worship the colours of the body the rhythm the mākhma māyā all deities the spirit the breath and the breath.
morphology: In the course of the session the lord should be seated in the seat of the goddess. The man who performs the sacrifice should be placed on the head of the mother. He should be worshipped in the form of a varna. The rhythm should be made of my mind my heart all the gods the spirit the breath should be uttered.

sanskrit: matsyaḥ yuga anta samaye manunā upalabdhaḥ kṣoṇīmayaḥ nikhila jīva nikāya ketaḥ visraṁsitān uru bhaye salile mukhāt me ādāya tatra vijahāra ha veda mārgān
reference: At the end of the millennium, the would-be Vaivasvata Manu, of the name Satyavrata, would see that the Lord in the fish incarnation is the shelter of all kinds of living entities, up to those in the earthly planets. Because of my fear of the vast water at the end of the millennium, the Vedas come out of my [Brahmā’s] mouth, and the Lord enjoys those vast waters and protects the Vedas.
baseline: The fish is found in the end of the age and the body of the living entity is found to be pure. One who has not been able to get rid of the poisonous substance should come from the mouth in fear of the āruva. One should get victory there. One would get the path of the Vedas.
morphology: The fish is the end of the age and the body of the living entity is found to be empty and the ākṣonimya is found in the body. One should come here from the mouth of the Śālī who is afraid of the illusion of the oracles.

sanskrit: kṣīra udadhau amara dānava yūtha pānām unmathnatām amṛta labdhaya ādi devaḥ pṛṣṭhena kacchapa vapuḥ vidadhāra gotram nidrākṣaṇaḥ adri parivarta kaṣāṇa kaṇḍūḥ
reference: The primeval Lord then assumed the tortoise incarnation in order to serve as a resting place [pivot] for the Mandara Mountain, which was acting as a churning rod. The demigods and demons were churning the Ocean of Milk with the Mandara Mountain in order to extract nectar. The mountain moved back and forth, scratching the back of Lord Tortoise, who, while partially sleeping, was experiencing an itching sensation.
baseline: The immortal demons in the form of milk water drink drink and drink and get the nectar. The gods of the past are the kutcha vapu vidadhara gothra sleep and kāṇḍu.
morphology: The immortal demons in the form of milk water drink drink and drink the elixir of the abode of the primordial gods. The kutcha and the vapu of the vidadhara got the support of the tribe of vidāra got the protection of sleep and the kandu of kāśana got the eloquence.

sanskrit: trai piṣṭapa uru bhaya hā saḥ nṛsiṁha rūpam kṛtvā bhramat bhru kuṭi daṁṣṭra karāla vaktram daitya indram āśu gadayā abhipatantam ārāt ūrau nipātya vidadāra nakhaiḥ sphurantam
reference: The Personality of Godhead assumed the incarnation of Nṛsiṁhadeva in order to vanquish the great fears of the demigods. He killed the king of the demons [Hiraṇyakaśipu], who challenged the Lord with a club in his hand, by placing the demon on His thighs and piercing him with His nails, rolling His eyebrows in anger and showing His fearful teeth and mouth.
baseline: Having formed the form of the three pitchers the fearful one would become the enemy the brahmin the cow the king the speaker the demon Indra would be destroyed by the arrow and the king would be killed by the claws of the knives.
morphology: The three stripes the fear of the enemy the illusion of the form of the king the brow the buttocks the mouth the voice of the demon Indra the arrow and the fangs of the disciple Indra are destroyed by the arrows and the claws of the god Viḍḍa.

sanskrit: antaḥ sarasi uru balena pade gṛhītaḥ grāheṇa yūtha patiḥ ambuja hastaḥ ārtaḥ āha idam ādi puruṣa akhila loka nātha tīrtha śravaḥ śravaṇa maṅgala nāma dheya
reference: The leader of the elephants, whose leg was attacked in a river by a crocodile of superior strength, was much aggrieved. Taking a lotus flower in his trunk, he addressed the Lord, saying, “O original enjoyer, Lord of the universe! O deliverer, as famous as a place of pilgrimage! All are purified simply by hearing Your holy name, which is worthy to be chanted.”
baseline: Having taken the position with the strength of the uru in the inner body the young husband should hold the arms of the goddess Ambuja. The artha is called as Adi purūṣa abhīla loka natha tirtha śravaṇa māṅgala.
morphology: Having taken the position with the strength of the uru the young man should hold the seat with the hands of the artha the arms of the lord Ambuja the forehead the head of the king the lord of the world the god of all beings and the god āhā.

sanskrit: śrutvā hariḥ tam araṇa arthinam aprameyaḥ cakra āyudhaḥ pataga rāja bhuja adhirūḍhaḥ cakreṇa nakra vadanam vinipāṭya tasmāt haste pragṛhya bhagavān kṛpayā ujjahāra
reference: The Personality of Godhead, after hearing the elephant’s plea, felt that the elephant needed His immediate help, for he was in great distress. Thus at once the Lord appeared there on the wings of the king of birds, Garuḍa, fully equipped with His weapon, the wheel [cakra]. With the wheel He cut to pieces the mouth of the crocodile to save the elephant, and He delivered the elephant by lifting him by his trunk.
baseline: Having heard of it Hari should offer the arrow and the weapon of the king. The king should be seated on a chakra. Having said this the king should bow down with the chakras. He should take it in his hand and offer it to the lord.
morphology: Having heard of him the king should take a wheel and armour of the king. The king should hold a kite with a wheel. Having kneeled down with the axe and spread it in his hands he should take it with the grace of the lord.

sanskrit: jyāyān guṇaiḥ avarajaḥ api aditeḥ sutānām lokān vicakrame imān yat atha adhiyajñaḥ kṣmām vāmanena jagṛhe tripada chalena yācñām ṛte pathi caran prabhubhiḥ na cālyaḥ
reference: The Lord, although transcendental to all material modes, still surpassed all the qualities of the sons of Aditi, known as the Ādityas. The Lord appeared as the youngest son of Aditi. And because He surpassed all the planets of the universe, He is the Supreme Personality of Godhead. On the pretense of asking for a measurement of three footsteps of land, He took away all the lands of Bali Mahārāja. He asked simply because without begging, no authority can take one’s rightful possession.
baseline: The king should not walk on the path of the king who has won the victory by the merits of the people. He should also give the people of the kingdom in a different order. He would then know that the king should go to the king of the country with the help of a trumpet. The king would not walk in the way of the lord.
morphology: The king should also give the people of Sūtana in a different way with the merits of victory. He should know that the king should not walk on the path of the king by walking on the ground with the trumpet and the sword of the lord.

sanskrit: na arthaḥ baleḥ ayam urukrama pāda śaucam āpaḥ śikhā dhṛtavataḥ vibudha adhipatyam yaḥ vai pratiśrutam ṛte na cikīrṣat anyat ātmānam aṅga manasā haraye abhimene
reference: Bali Mahārāja, who put on his head the water washed from the lotus feet of the Lord, did not think of anything besides his promise, in spite of being forbidden by his spiritual master. The king dedicated his own personal body to fulfill the measurement of the Lord’s third step. For such a personality, even the kingdom of heaven, which he conquered by his strength, was of no value.
baseline: One who does not know the meaning of the word āṇa bālā.... that which is not the part of the soul and which has been promised by the lord should be made aware of the fact that it is not a matter of the mind.
morphology: One who does not understand the meaning of the force the conduct of the feet the purification of the body the holding of the flame the power of the lord the promise of the master the other part of the soul the mind and the mind should be destroyed.

sanskrit: tubhyam ca nārada bhṛśam bhagavān vivṛddha bhāvena sādhu parituṣṭaḥ uvāca yogam jñānam ca bhāgavatam ātma sa tattva dīpam yat vāsudeva śaraṇāḥ viduḥ añjasā eva
reference: O Nārada, you were taught about the science of God and His transcendental loving service by the Personality of Godhead in His incarnation of Haṁsāvatāra. He was very much pleased with you, due to your intense proportion of devotional service. He also explained unto you, lucidly, the full science of devotional service, which is especially understandable by persons who are souls surrendered unto Lord Vāsudeva, the Personality of Godhead.
baseline: One who is a sage and a devotee of the god Vruddha Narada Vriddha Bhābhava Vrudha Pārituṣta said that yoga knowledge bhāgavata the self the principle of the lamp vāsudeva śāraṇa vidu anjāsa is the same.
morphology: One who is blessed with the god Narada and the greatness of the mind and the spirit of the sage is said to have attained yoga knowledge and the divine self. The principle of vāsudeva śarāṇa vidu anjāja is the lamp.

sanskrit: cakram ca dikṣu avihatam daśasu sva tejaḥ manvantareṣu manu vaṁśa dharaḥ bibharti duṣṭeṣu rājasu damam vyadadhāt sva kīrtim satye tri pṛṣṭhe uśatīm prathayan caritraiḥ
reference: As the incarnation of Manu, the Lord became the descendant of the Manu dynasty and ruled over the miscreant kingly order, subduing them by His powerful wheel weapon. Undeterred in all circumstances, His rule was characterized by His glorious fame, which spread over the three lokas, and above them to the planetary system of Satyaloka, the topmost in the universe.
baseline: The chakra should be placed on the right side of the three sides of the chariot. The ten figures should be worshipped with the mantra of Śiva. The king should be seated on the left side of his chariots.
morphology: The chakra should be placed on the right side of the head and the diksha on the left side. In the ten months of the reign of the king manu should be seated on the ground and the king should be made to stand on the wrong side and his glory should be established on the three sides.

sanskrit: dhanvantariḥ ca bhagavān svayam eva kīrtiḥ nāmnā nṛṇām puru rujām rujaḥ āśu hanti yajñe ca bhāgam amṛta āyuḥ ava avarundhe āyuṣya vedam anuśāsti avatīrya loke
reference: The Lord in His incarnation of Dhanvantari very quickly cures the diseases of the ever-diseased living entities simply by His fame personified, and only because of Him do the demigods achieve long lives. Thus the Personality of Godhead becomes ever glorified. He also exacted a share from the sacrifices, and it is he only who inaugurated the medical science or the knowledge of medicine in the universe.
baseline: The lord of wealth and glory should be the same as that of the king. One who kills the kings wife daughter son daughter and son of a noble person in the name of renunciation should be given part of the sacrifice. He should be endowed with immortal life. One should be blessed with the scriptures and the Vedas in the absence of obstacles.
morphology: The lord of wealth wealth and fame should be worshipped in the name of the lord himself. The king of the niras should be killed as soon as possible. The sacrifice should be part of the immortal life. The life of the god should be spent in the absence of obstacles. The veda should be punished.

sanskrit: kṣatram kṣayāya vidhinā upabhṛtam mahātmā brahma dhruk ujjhita patham naraka ārti lipsu uddhanti asau avanikaṇṭakam ugra vīryaḥ triḥ sapta kṛtvaḥ urudhāra paraśvadhena
reference: When the ruling administrators, who are known as the kṣatriyas, turned astray from the path of the Absolute Truth, being desirous to suffer in hell, the Lord, in His incarnation as the sage Paraśurāma, uprooted those unwanted kings, who appeared as the thorns of the earth. Thus He thrice seven times uprooted the kṣatriyas with His keenly sharpened chopper.
baseline: Having destroyed the kṣatra the path of Brahman is made to be lit up by the method of worship. The path of fire should be lit by the god Brahma. The pitchers should be raised by the lips of Avāṇikantaka fiery sperms three cubits seven cubits and the upper body should be worshipped by the goddess Parvāśvadha.
morphology: Having destroyed the kṣatra the path of Brahman is lit up by the method of worship. Having worshipped the path to hell one would get rid of the fiery sperms of Avana Kanta Urdhara Parashvadha and seven other things.

sanskrit: yathā bhavadbhiḥ pṛṣṭo'haṃ vadanārthe mahātmabhiḥ | purāvṛttaṃ mayā proktaṃ śivārcanavidheḥ phalam | śivena dattaṃ sālūpyaṃ na gṛhītaṃ mayā tadā || 77 || yācitaṃ ca mayā śaṃbhorvadanaṃ vānarasya ca | śivena kṛpayā dattaṃ mama kāruṇyaśālinā || 78 ||
reference: As he was told thus, he in his arrogance due to his might, asked me about my face in the same manner as I have been asked about my face by you noble-souled ones. The old story was recounted by me about the benefit of the holy rite of the worship of Śiva. “Sārūpya (having the same form as that of the lord) was granted by Śiva, but it was not accepted by me then. The face of a monkey was requested by me from Śaṃbhu. It was then granted to me kindly by Śiva who is by nature compassionate.
baseline: As you have asked me I have told the great man that I should worship Lord Śiva. I have said that the fruits of the worship should be offered to Lord śiva. Then I would not accept the gift given to me by the lord. If I do not accept it then I would have asked for the gift of Śambhovarvada and the gift from the king of monkeys. By the grace of my kindness the gift would have been given by Lord ṣiva.
morphology: As you have asked me I have told the great men that I should worship Lord Śiva. I have said that the fruit of the worship of Lord śiva should be taken away from me. Then I would not accept the gift given to me by Śabha. What is asked for by me would be given to Śambhovarvada and the monkeys. By the grace of my kindness to me.

sanskrit: nirābhimānino ye ca nirdabhā niṣparigrahāḥ | śaṃbhoḥ priyāste vijñeyā hyanye śivavabahiṣkṛtāḥ || 79 ||
reference: Those who are devoid of false prestige, those who are free from arrogance and those who have no property or possessions, should be known as favourites of Śaṃbhu. Others are excluded by Śiva.”
baseline: Those who are selfless and fearless those who are innocent and defenseless and those who love the Lord of all beings should be killed by the knowledge of Lord Śiva.
morphology: Those who are selfless and selfless those who love the lord of the earth and those who do not want to be harmed by the evil one are worshipped by Lord Śiva.

sanskrit: tathāvadanmayā sārddhaṃ rāvaṇastapaso balāt | mayā ca yācitānyeva daśa vaktrāṇi dhīmatā || 80 ||
reference: 80-86a. Then Rāvaṇa said to me: “On the strength of my penance, I had been sensible enough to request for ten heads.”
baseline: Then the voice of Ravana should be made strong with the words of the same name. And if I ask for ten words it will be slow.
morphology: Then the voice of Ravana should be raised with the same force as that of the demon Avādaṇma. If I ask for ten words it would be slow.

sanskrit: upahāsakaraṃ vākyaṃ paulastyasya tadā surāḥ | mayā tadā hi śapto'sau rāvaṇo lokarāvaṇaḥ || 81 ||
reference: At his derisive statement, Rāvaṇa who made the world scream, was cursed by me then:
baseline: Then the words of Paul which were mocking were sung. Then I cursed him. This is Ravana Loka Ravana.
morphology: Then the words of Paul which are mocking are heard in the voice. Then I cursed him. He is the king of the people.

sanskrit: īdṛśānyeva vaktrāṇi yeṣāṃ vai saṃbhavaṃti hi | taiḥ sameto yadā ko'pi naravaryo mahātapāḥ | māṃ puraskṛtya sahasā haniṣyati na saṃśayaḥ || 82 ||
reference: “When an excellent man of great penance accompanied by those who have faces like this (monkey faces like mine) (comes to your city) keeping me at the head, he will undoubtedly kill you.”
baseline: When such a thing happens to those who speak in the same manner there is no doubt that a man would kill me suddenly after having worshipped me.
morphology: When such a thing happens to those who speak in the same manner there is no doubt that a man will honour me and kill me suddenly.

sanskrit: evaṃ śapto mayā brahmanrāvaṇo lokarāvaṇaḥ | arcitaṃ kevalaṃ liṃgaṃ vinā tena mahātmanā || 83 || pīṭhikārūpasaṃsthena vinā tena surottamāḥ | viṣṇunā hi mahābhāgāstasmātsarvaṃ vidhāsyati || 84 || devadevo mahādevo viṣṇurūpī maheśvaraḥ | sarve yūyaṃ prārthayaṃtu viṣṇuṃ sarvaguhāśayam || 85 ||
reference: Thus, O Brahmā, Rāvaṇa who made the world scream, was cursed by me. Only the Liṅga was worshipped by Ṛāvaṇa without the noble-souled Viṣṇu stationed in the form of the pedestal, O excellent Suras. Hence, O excessively fortunate ones, Maheśvara, Mahādeva, the lord of Devas, in the form of Viṣṇu will carry out everything. May all of you pray to Viṣṇu lying within the cavity of the heart of everyone. Therefore, I shall be at the head of all Devas.
baseline: The Lord Brahman the king of the people the lord of the rivers the goddess worshipped by him without having a penis the great man without having the preceptor the god of the world without having an institution the supreme god of Gods Lord Viṣṇu Lord Mahāśvaru the Lord of gods the form of Vishnu and all the gods should be worshipped in this manner.
morphology: In this way the Lord Brahman should be worshipped without having the penis of the king the king of the people the lord of the gods of the world the great king of India without having established the preceptor the god of the universe and the great god Viṣṇu. The great part of the kingdom should be given to him by him. Gods gods goddesses gods and gods should be worshiped by you all. Lord Viśṇu should have all the caves.

sanskrit: ahaṃ hi sarvadevānāṃ purovartī bhavāmyataḥ | te sarve naṃdino vākyaṃ śrutvā muditamānasāḥ | vaikuṃṭhamāgatā gīrbhirviṣṇuṃ stotuṃ pracakrire || 86 ||
reference: 86b. On hearing the words of Nandī, all of them became joyous in their minds. They came to Vaikuṇṭha and began to eulogize Viṣṇu by means of (good) words.
baseline: I am the preceptor of all gods for you. All those who have heard the words of Nandīṇu should be worshipped. One who has gone to Vaikuntha should worship Lord Viṣṇu.
morphology: I am the preceptor of all gods for you. Having heard all the words of Nandīṇu the mind of the devotees should be worshipped. One who has returned to Vaikuntha one who has worshipped the god Gīrbhirvīṣṇu should be worshiped.

sanskrit: devā ūcuḥ | namo bhagavate tubhyaṃ devadeva jagatpate | tvadādhāramidaṃ sarvaṃ jagadetaccarācaram || 87 ||
reference: Devas said: 87. Obeisance to you, the lord, O lord of Devas, O lord of the universe. This entire universe consisting of mobile and immobile beings has you for its basis and support.
baseline: O Lord O Lord of the worlds you are the source of all beings. You are the world.
morphology: O Lord of the worlds you are the source of everything.

sanskrit: etalliṃgaṃ tvayā viṣṇo dhṛtaṃ vai piṇḍirūpiṇā | mahāviṣṇusvarūpeṇa ghātitau madhukaiṭabhau || 88 ||
reference: 88. This Liṅga has been held by you, O Viṣṇu, in the form of the Piṇḍī (globular pedestal). In the form of Mahāviṣṇu (the demons) Madhu and Kaiṭabha were killed by you.
baseline: The image of Viṣṇu is said to be like that of a pindiputra. He is killed by the form of Vishnu and the image of the great Vishnu.
morphology: You are the body of Viṣṇu in the form of a linga and the body is like that of a pindi. You are killed by the image of Vishnu. You have become the mother of honey.

sanskrit: tathā kamaṭharūpeṇa dhṛto vai maṃdarācalaḥ | varāharūpamāsthāya hiraṇyākṣo hatastvayā || 89 ||
reference: 89. Similarly, in the form of a tortoise, the Mandara mountain was held up and supported by you (at the time of churning of ocean for nectar). Assuming the form of a boar, Hiraṇyākṣa was killed by you.
baseline: Similarly a deer should be killed in the form of a boar in the manner of a kāmatha and the charioteer should be beaten in the same manner.
morphology: In the same way a deer in the form of a boar should be killed in the manner of a kamatha.

sanskrit: hiraṇyakaśipurdaityo hato nṛharirūpiṇā | tvayā caiva balirbaddho daityo vāmanarūpiṇā || 90 ||
reference: 90. Hiraṇyakaśipu, the Daitya, was killed by you by assuming the form of Nṛhari (Man-lion). Bali, the Daitya, was held and bound by you in the form of Vāmana (Dwarf).
baseline: One who is born as Hiranyaka the son of a sage and the god of war should be worshipped as Nrīhāri. One who has attained the form of a demon would be called as Vamana.
morphology: The goddess Hiranyaka Sīpura and the goddess Nrīhārī are worshipped. You are the goddess of sacrifice and the demon of the left.

sanskrit: bhṛgūṇāmanvaye bhūtvā kṛtavīryātmajo hataḥ | itopyasmānmahāviṣṇo tathaiva paripālaya || 91 ||
reference: 91. The son of Kṛtavīrya (Sahasrārjuna) was killed by you after taking birth in the family of Bhṛgus. Hereafter too, O great Viṣṇu, protect us in the same manner.
baseline: One who has done this after having worshipped Bhriguṇa should be killed. He should maintain the spirit in the same way.
morphology: One who has done this after having worshipped Bhriguṇa should be killed. He should maintain the spirit in the same way as the other gods.

sanskrit: rāvamasya bhayādasmāttrātuṃ bhūyorhasi tvaram || 92 ||
reference: 92. It behoves you to protect us instantaneously from the fear of Rāvaṇa.
baseline: The fear of the night should be expressed in the same manner as that of the earth. It should be done with haste.
morphology: The fear of Ravāma should be expressed in the same manner as that of the earth.

sanskrit: evaṃ saṃprārthito devairbhagavānbhūtabhāvanaḥ | uvāca ca surānsarvānvāsudevo jaganmayaḥ || 93 ||
reference: 93. On being entreated thus by Devas, the lord Vāsudeva, the sanctifier (the creator) of all living beings, who is immanent in the universe, said to all those Suras:
baseline: In this way one becomes the manifestation of the manifestations of the gods. One becomes aware of all beings. One gets to know God by all means. One attains life.
morphology: In this way one becomes aware of the manifestations of the gods and the manifestation of the senses. One becomes conscious of the deities who are manifest in the form of the sun and all beings.

sanskrit: he devāḥ śrūyatāṃ vākyaṃ prastāvasadṛśaṃ mahat | śailādiṃ ca puraskṛtya sarve yūyaṃ tvarānvitāḥ | avatārānprakurvantu vānarīṃ tanumāśritāḥ || 94 ||
reference: 94. “O Devas, let this important statement he heard. It is relevant to this occasion. With Śailādi (Nandin) as your head (leader), all of you immediately take incarnations in the form (bodies) of monkeys.
baseline: O gods the words spoken are as great as the words offered. Having worshipped the rock all of you havetened to worship the avatars. Let the monkeys be worshipped by you.
morphology: O gods the words spoken are as great as the words offered. Having praised the rock all of you havetened to worship the avatars of the monkeys.

sanskrit: ahaṃ hi mānuṣo bhūtvā hyajñānena samāvṛtaḥ | saṃbhaviṣyāmyayodhyāyaṃ gṛhe daśarathasya ca | brahmavidyāsahāyosmi bhavatāṃ kāryasiddhaye || 95 ||
reference: 95. I shall become a human being enveloped by Ajñāna (Ignorance). I shall be born in Ayodhyā in the abode of Daśaratha for the attainment of your objectives. I am having Brahmavidyā (the knowledge of Brahman) as my assistant.
baseline: Having become ones own person and having been absorbed with knowledge the battle should be fought in the house of Dasharatha. Having knowledge of Brahman I am ready to accomplish your task.
morphology: Having become a man I am absorbed by the knowledge of the Lord Śiva. The battle of Śāstraṣṭha should happen in the house. Having attained the attainment of your mission with the knowledge and knowledge of Brahman I shall be able to do your work.

sanskrit: janakasya gṛhe sākṣādbrahmavidyā janiṣyati | bhakto hi rāvaṇaḥ sākṣācchivadhyānaparāyaṇaḥ || 96 ||
reference: 96. Brahmavidyā herself will be born in the abode of Janaka.[7] In fact, Rāvaṇa is (my) devotee as he is directly engaged in the meditation on Śiva.
baseline: The knowledge of Brahman will be born in the house of the father. One who is a devotee will find that Ravana is attentive.
morphology: The knowledge of Brahman will be born in the house of the father. The devotee should observe the manifestation of Rāvaṇa. He should become meditative.

sanskrit: tapasā mahatā yukto brahmavidyāṃ yadecchati | tadā susādhyo bhavati puruṣo dharmanirjitaḥ || 97 ||
reference: 97. When a man endowed with great penance desires for Brahmavidyā, he can be easily managed and won over by means of virtue.”
baseline: One who practices penance and acquires great knowledge of Brahman would then be able to attain the attainment of perfection. One would become free from righteousness.
morphology: One who practices penance and acquires great knowledge of Brahman would get happiness. Then one would become free from the evil.

sanskrit: evaṃ saṃbhāṣya bhagavānviṣṇuḥ paramamaṅgalaḥ | vālī cendrāṃśasaṃbhūtaḥ sugrīvoṃ śumataḥ sutaḥ || 98 ||
reference: 98-100. After saying this, lord Viṣṇu, the highly auspicious one (vanished).
baseline: Having thus spoken Lord Viṣṇu is the supreme benediction. One who has the righteousness of the four parts of the body would be blessed with good health.
morphology: Having thus spoken Lord Viṣṇu is the supreme benediction. One who has the righteousness of the mind and the senses of the heart would be blessed with good health.

sanskrit: tathā brahmāṃśasaṃbhūto jāmbavānnṛkṣakuñjaraḥ | śilādatanayo naṃdī śivasyānucaraḥ priyaḥ || 99 || yo vai caikādaśo rudro hanūmānsa mahākapiḥ | avatīrṇaḥ sahāyārthaṃ viṣṇoramitatejasaḥ || 100 ||
reference: Vālī was born of a part of Indra. Sugrīva was the son of the Sun. Jāmbavān, the leading Ṛkṣa (bear), was born of a part of Brahmā. Naṇḍī, the son of Śilāda, who was a favourite follower of Śiva, incarnated as the great monkey Hanūmān for rendering assistance to Viṣṇu of unmeasured splendour.
baseline: Similarly a jamba a tree a kunjara a stone a nāndī a man of the nature of Śiva a person of the liking a cow a dog a horse a monkey a lion a elephant a king a great man a lord of the gods Viṣṇu and others are worshipped.
morphology: In the same way, one who is blessed with Brahman jambavā nāraksha kunjara nandī sthila tāna siva sage and his son is beloved. One who is worshipped by the disciple of the god Rudra hanumana and the great king of the universe is known to be the incarnation of Lord Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: maiṃdādayo'tha kapayaste sarve surasattamāḥ | evaṃ sarve suragaṇā avateruryathā tatham || 101 ||
reference: 101. The monkeys beginning with Mainda were all the excellent Suras. Thus, all Suras incarnated in a befitting manner.
baseline: If all the elements of the sun are cut in the same way then all the objects of the sky should be made to appear in this way.
morphology: If all the figures are cast in the same way then all the images should be cast in this way.

sanskrit: tathaiva viṣṇurutpannaḥ kauśalyānaṃdavarddhanaḥ | viśvasya ramaṇāccaiva rāma ityucyate budhaiḥ || 102 ||
reference: 102. Similarly, Viṣṇu was born as one who increased the delight of Kausalyā. He is called Rāma by learned men, because he pleased and gratified the entire universe.
baseline: In the same way Viṣṇu is said to be the source of wealth. One who gains happiness by the means of skill and makes the world happy is called Rama by the Buddha.
morphology: In the same way Viṣṇu is said to be the source of wealth. One who is blessed with the qualities of the universe is called Rama.

sanskrit: śeṣopi bhaktyā viṣṇośca tapasā'vātaradbhuvi || 103 ||
reference: 103. Due to his devotion to Viṣṇu, Śeṣa descended on the earth by means of the power of his penance.
baseline: The rest of the devotee should worship Lord Viṣṇu and perform penance.
morphology: The rest of the devotee of Viṣṇu should be worshipped with penance.

sanskrit: dordaṇḍāvapi viṣṇośca avatīrṇau pratāpinau | śatrughnabharatākhyau ca vikhyātau bhuvanatraye || 104 ||
reference: 104. The mighty arms of Viṣṇu incarnated as the valorous (Princes) named Śatrughṇa and Bharata well-renowned in the three worlds.
baseline: The king of Dordandava the king of Viṣṇu the chiefly one of the three gods known as Satrughṇa Bharata and others.
morphology: Dordandava and Viṣṇu are the incarnations of the great king Satrughn and Bharata and are known to be the three gods.

sanskrit: mithilādhipateḥ kanyā yā uktā brahmavādibhiḥ | sā brahmavidyāvataratsurāṇāṃ kāryyasiddhaye | sītā jātā lāṃgalasya iyaṃ bhūmivikarṣaṇāt || 105 ||
reference: 105. She who was mentioned as Brahmavidyā by the expounders of the Vedas, incarnated as the daughter of the ruler of Mithilā for the fulfilment of the task of Suras. She was born from a furrow arising from the ploughing of the field with the ploughshare.[8]
baseline: The daughter of Mithila the ruler of the kingdom of Mithilā who is said to be a brahmin by the Brahmanists to be the master of the universe and the king of the sārutas should be accomplished by the creation of Sita. This is the land of the langla.
morphology: The daughter of Mithila the ruler of the kingdom of Mithilā who is said to be a brahmins to be the master of Brahman to know the universe and to be able to do the work of the sārutas to become Sita.

sanskrit: tasmātsīteti vikhyātā vidyā sānvīkṣikī tadā | mithilāyāṃ samutpannā maithitītyabhidhīyate || 106 ||
reference: 106. Hence, she became famous as Sītā. She was the Science of Metaphysics (personified). Since she was born in Mithilā, she is called Maithilī.
baseline: Then the disciple should be taught the scriptures. Then he should be instructed to do the same in Mithila. The disciples should be made to do so.
morphology: Then the knowledge should be explained. Then it should be described as the creation of the sea in Mithila.

sanskrit: janakasya kule jātā viśrutā janakātmajā | khyātā vedavatī pūrvaṃ brahmavidyāghanāśinī || 107 ||
reference: 107. She was born in the family of Janaka. Hence, she is well-known as Janakātmajā (Jānakī). This Brahmavidyā, the destroyer of sins, was formerly known as Vedavatī.
baseline: Having been born in the clan of the father the son of the mother the king of the body the goddess of the Vedas known as Brahma and the goddess who destroyed the knowledge of Brahman.
morphology: Having been born in the clan of Janaka one who rests in the family of Janāka the spirit of the people the Vedic goddess known as Brahma and Vīdvā were destroyed earlier.

sanskrit: sā dattā janakenaiva viṣṇave paramātmane || 108 || tayātha vidyayā sārddhaṃ devadevo jagatpatiḥ | ugre tapasi līno'sau viṣṇuḥ paramaduṣkaram || 109 || rāvaṇaṃ jetukāmo vai rāmo rājīvalocanaḥ | araṇyavāsamakaroddevānāṃ kāryasiddhaye || 110 ||
reference: 108-110. She was given by Janaka himself to Viṣṇu, the Supreme Soul. Along with her, the Vidyā (incarnated), Viṣṇu the greatest among the auspicious ones, the lord of Devas, the lord protector of the universe, became engaged in a severe penance. As he was desirous of defeating Rāvaṇa for the sake of the fulfilment of the task of Devas, the lotus-eyed Rāma stayed in forest (for the same purpose).
baseline: One who has given that person to Viṣṇu the supreme god the lord of the universe the god of gods with his knowledge the king of the world the Lord of the earth Viṣnu the Supreme adversary Ravana Trikuta Rāma Rajeev and others should be worshipped in the forest.
morphology: One who has given that person to Viṣṇu the supreme god the lord of the universe the god of gods with his knowledge the king of the world Viśṇu and the king who had done penance in the past and had conquered the forest and had accomplished the task of the invaders should be worshipped.

sanskrit: śeṣāvatāro'pi mahāṃstapaḥ paramaduṣkaram | tatāpa parayā śaktyā devānāṃ kāryasiddhaye || 111 ||
reference: 111. Though the great incarnation of Śeṣa, (Lakṣmaṇa) performed an exceedingly difficult penance by means of his great Śakti (power), for the sake of the fulfilment of the task of Devas.
baseline: The great pillar is also the last incarnation. It is the supreme evil. Then the work of the gods should be accomplished by the power of others.
morphology: The great incarnation is also the supreme evil. Then the work of the gods should be accomplished by the power of others.

sanskrit: śatrughno bharataścaiva tepatuḥ paramaṃ tapaḥ || 112 || tato'sau tapasā yuktaḥ sārddhaṃ tairdevatāgaṇaiḥ | sagaṇaṃ rāvaṇaṃ rāmaḥ ṣaḍbhirmāsairajīhanat | viṣṇunā ghātitaḥ śastraiḥ śivasārūpyamāptavān || 113 || sagamaḥ sa punaḥ sadyo baṃdhubhiḥ saha suvratāḥ || 114 ||
reference: 112-115. Śatrughna and Bharata too performed very great penance. Rāma who was thus endowed with the power of penance and was assisted and accompanied by those groups of Devas, killed Ṛāvaṇa along with his followers within six months. Killed by Viṣṇu by means of weapons, O sages of holy rites, he attained Sārūpya (having the same form as the god) of Śiva, along with his kinsmen and followers. By the grace of Śiva, he became (realized) the entire Dvaitādvaita (the essence of the philosophy of dualism and non-dualism).[9] Even the sages are deluded in the matter of discrimination between dualism and non-dualism. Men who are engaged in worshipping Śiva derive all those things.
baseline: One who lives with enemies Bharata and others would get the supreme repentance. One who has done penance with the gods would get rid of the enemy one who is killed by Lord Viṣṇu who has killed him and another who is alive by the six brahmins of Lord Śiva would again get acquainted with him and his relatives.
morphology: One who lives with enemies Bharata and others would get the supreme repentance. One who has done penance with the gods of the three gods would get rid of the enemy the son of Ravana the brother of Lord Rama and the king of the six virgins. Having been killed by Lord Viṣṇu he would get back to the form of Lord Śiva.

sanskrit: ye'rcayaṃti śivaṃ nityaṃ liṃgarūpiṇameva ca | striyo vāpyatha vā śūdrāḥ śvapacā hyaṃtyavāsinaḥ | taṃ śivaṃ prāpnuvaṃtyeva sarvaduḥkhopanāśanam || 116 ||
reference: 116. Those who continuously worship Śiva in the form of Liṅga, whether they be women or śūdras or cāṇḍālas or other low-caste people, do attain Śiva, the destroyer of all miseries.
baseline: One who invents Śiva always as the form of the linga one who invokes Śuṇḍra the goddess of the sun or one who worships Śudra one should worship him. One who acquires śiva would get all the sorrows and sorrows.
morphology: One who chooses Śiva always as the form of the linga one who worships the goddess Śudra the goddess of the sun and the inhabitants of Śvāṇtya should pay tribute to him. One who acquires śiva would get all the sorrows and sorrows.

sanskrit: paśavo'pi paraṃ yātāḥ kiṃ punarmānuṣādayaḥ || 117 || ye dvijā brahmacaryeṇa tapaḥ paramamāsthitāḥ | varṣairanekairyajñānāṃ te'pi svargaparā bhavan || 118 ||
reference: 117-118. Even animals have attained the supreme lord. What then to say about human beings? The twice-born castes who have practised great penance observing the vow of celibacy and who have performed Yajñas for many years have attained (merely) Svarga (Heaven).
baseline: Those who go beyond the animals and are again men those who attain the supreme state of austerity by the practice of brahmāra those people who do not know the nature of the rain those also become heavenly.
morphology: Those who go beyond the animals and those who go back to man those who do penance by the practice of brahmāra those are the highest. Those who do not know the nature of the rain those also go to heaven.

sanskrit: jyotiṣṭomo vājapeyo hyatirātrādayo hyamī | yajñāḥ svargaṃ prayacchaṃti sattrīṇāṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ || 119 || tatra svargasukhaṃ bhuktvā puṇyakṣayakaraṃ mahat | puṇyakṣaye'pi yajvāno martyalokaṃ pataṃti vai || 120 || patitānāṃ ca saṃsāre daivādbuddhiḥ prajāyate | guṇatrayamayī viprāstāsutāstviha yoniṣu || 121 ||
reference: 119-123. There are many Yajñas[10] such as Jyotiṣṭoma, Vājapeya, Atirātra and so on. These Yajñas undoubtedly do bestow heavenly pleasures on those who perform them. After enjoying the heavenly pleasures, when their merits become exhausted, those sacrificers come back to the mortal world. Having descended to the world, they are born in the different species with their intellect of the nature of the three Guṇas of Sattva, Rajas and Tamas. Thus, many souls wander about in cycles of birth and death. By chance or as good luck would have it, some of them serve Śiva.
baseline: O astrologer the one who has lost his life who has made a sacrifice has made an attempt to reach heaven. One who has not experienced the blissful bliss of the heaven has experienced great loss of virtues and has lost the virtues of the world has fallen into the abyss of the gods and has attained the three qualities of vanity and vanity.
morphology: One who offers sacrifices and sacrifices to the gods of the heavenly states and the king of the kings kingdom and his wifes family and his sons is said to be a great man. Having enjoyed the glory of heaven one who has lost his virtues who has fallen into the world of death who is a man of three qualities and who has become a king of gods who becomes a king in the world.

sanskrit: śivadhyānaparāṇāṃ ca narāṇāṃ yatacetasām | māyānirasanaṃ sadyo bhaviṣyati na cānyathā || 124 ||
reference: 124. Instantaneous removal of Māyā takes place in the case of men who are engaged in regular meditation on Śiva and who have restrained their minds and not otherwise.
baseline: One who has meditated on Śiva the followers of Śivā and those who do not care for others would not be able to do the abode of the illusion of maya.
morphology: One who has meditated on Śiva the followers of Śivā the sons of Nāra and those who have not done so would not be able to do the abode of the illusion of maya.

sanskrit: māyānirasanātsadyo naśyatyeva guṇatrayam | yadā guṇatrayātīto bhavatīti sa muktibhāk || 125 ||
reference: 125. When Māyā is dispelled, the three Guṇas perish. Then a person transcends the three Guṇas and becomes liberated thereby.
baseline: The three qualities are destroyed by the practice of the illusion of the gods. When the qualities are not attained he becomes liberated.
morphology: The three qualities are destroyed by the practice of the illusion of the gods. When the qualities are not attained it becomes liberating.

sanskrit: tasmālliṅgārcanaṃ bhāvyaṃ sarveṣāmapi dehinām | liṅgarūpī śivo bhūtvā trāyate saṃcarācaram || 126 ||
reference: 126-128. Hence, the worship of Liṅga should be thought of and pursued by all embodied beings. Śiva assumes the form of Liṅga and protects all mobile and immobile beings.
baseline: One who worships the same linga should worship all beings. One who becomes the form of the linga Śiva one who becomes a celestial body and then becomes a charioteer.
morphology: One who worships the linga should worship all beings. One who becomes a linga a form of Shiva becomes a celestial body and becomes a charioteer.

sanskrit: purā bhavadbhiḥ pṛṣṭo'haṃ liṅgarūpī kathaṃ śivaḥ | tatsarvaṃ kathitaṃ viprā yāthātathyena saṃprati || 127 ||
reference: Formerly I have been asked by you about how Śiva assumed the form of Liṅga. Everything has now been truthfully spoken (by me), O Brāhmaṇas.
baseline: The Lord has asked you how I am a form of Śiva in the form of a linga. All these things have been said by Viṣṇu.
morphology: The Lord has asked you to explain to me how he looks like a linga. He has said all these things.

sanskrit: kathaṃ garaṃ bhakṣitavāñchivo lokamaheśvaraḥ | tatsarvaṃ śrūyatāṃ viprā yatāvatkathayāmi vaḥ || 128 ||
reference: How Śiva, the great lord of the worlds, swallowed poison (Halāhala), may be listened to, O Brāhmaṇas, I shall recount it to you as it actually took place. FOOTNOTES AND REFERENCES:
baseline: The Lord of the worlds should explain how one eats the grain. Then he should explain to you all the things. Then I will tell you.
morphology: The Lord has revealed to the world the manner in which the pit is eaten. The Lord will explain to you all the things.

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca | ekadā tu sabhāmadhya āsthito devarāṭ svayam | lokapālaiḥ parivṛto devaiśca ṛṣibhistathā || 1 || apsarogaṇasaṃvīto gaṃdharvaiśca puraskṛtaḥ | upagīyamānavijayaḥ siddhavidyādharairapi || 2 ||
reference: 1-2. On one occasion Indra, the lord of Devas, was seated in the middle of the assembly surrounded by the guardians of the worlds, Devas and Sages. He was encircled by bevies of celestial damsels and was honoured by Gandharvas. Songs in praise of his conquest were being sung by Siddhas and Vidyādharas.
baseline: Once the king of gods standing in the middle of the assembly is said to be a sage one who is surrounded by ombudsmen is blessed with a saṃgāragaṇa and gandharva. One who has attained victory is known as siddhividya.
morphology: Once the king of gods standing in the middle of the assembly is said to be a sage one who is surrounded by ombudsmen and the god is blessed with apsaraogaṇa sāmvita gandharva siddha vijayāda vīdhyāra siṣṇu sambhārā.

sanskrit: tadā śiṣyaiḥ parivṛto devarājaguruḥ sudhīḥ | āgato'sau mahābhāgo bṛhaspati rudāradhīḥ || 3 ||
reference: 3. At that time Bṛhaspati who was the scholarly preceptor of the king of Devas and was of exalted fortune and liberal-minded, came there surrounded by his disciples.
baseline: Then the master of the god should be surrounded by his disciples. Then he should come and worship Brihaspati and Rudra.
morphology: Then the master of the god should be surrounded by his disciples. Then the great figure Brihaspati should come and worship him.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā sahasā devāḥ praṇemuḥ samupasthitāḥ | iṃdropi dadṛśe tatra prāptaṃ vācaspatiṃ tadā || 4 ||
reference: 4. On seeing him Devas who had been sitting there promptly bowed down to him. Indra too had seen Vācaspati’s (Bṛhaspati’s) arrival.
baseline: Having seen him suddenly the gods and goddesses were seated in front of him. Then Indra also got the voice there.
morphology: Seeing him suddenly the gods were seated in front of him. Then Indra also got the speech found there.

sanskrit: novāca kiṃciddurmedhāvaco mānupuraḥsaram | nāhvānaṃ nāsanaṃ tasya na visarjanameva ca || 5 ||
reference: 5. But the vicious-minded lord did not utter a single word in his honour. No word of welcome, no offer of seat, no formal permission to leave was accorded to him.
baseline: One should not make any mistake or make any mischief or destroy the body of man. One would not be able to dissolve it.
morphology: One should not make a mistake by making a mistake not making any mistake and not dissolving it.

sanskrit: śakraṃ pramattaṃ jñātvātha madādrājyasya durmatim | tirodhānamanuprāpto bṛhaspatī ruṣānvitaḥ || 6 ||
reference: 6. Knowing that Śakra had become arrogant and evil-minded due to royal authority, Bṛhaspati became angry and he vanished.
baseline: Having known the importance of Śakra the kingdom of Madāda one would be destroyed. Having attained the goal of vanishing Brihaspati would become a demon.
morphology: Having known the importance of the lord the king of Madāda kingdom would be destroyed. Having attained the goal of vanishing the king Brihaspati would become a demon.

sanskrit: gate devagurau tasminvimanaskā'bhavansurāḥ | yakṣā nāgāḥ sagaṃdharvā ṛṣayo'pi tathā dvijāḥ || 7 ||
reference: 7. When the preceptor of Devas had departed, Suras became dejected. Yakṣas, Serpents, Gandharvas and sages also became depressed in mind, O Brāhmaṇas.
baseline: Then the lord should be placed in the same position as the priest. The serpents should be worshipped as the same as the sages.
morphology: Then the gods gurus spirits gods gods and goddesses should be worshipped in the same way. The serpents serpentines and sages should be worshiped in similar manner.

sanskrit: gāṃdharvasyā vasāne tu labdhasaṃjño hariḥ surān | papraccha tvaritenavai kva gato hi mahātapāḥ || 8 ||
reference: 8. At the end of the music recital, Indra (as it were) regained consciousness. He asked Suras immediately, “Where has (the preceptor) of great penance gone?”
baseline: One who finds the sound of the sun in the abode of Gandharva one who knows the sound should be quickened by the mouth of Hari. One who has gone to the great god should go to it.
morphology: One who has attained knowledge in the abode of Gandharva one who has heard the hymns should go forth with speed.

sanskrit: tadaiva nāradenoktaḥ śakro devādhipastathā | tvayā kṛtā hyavajñā ca gurornastyatra saṃśayaḥ || 9 || guroravajñayā rājyaṃ gataṃ te balasūdana | tasmātkṣamāpanīyo'sau sarvabhāvena hi tvayā || 10 ||
reference: 9-10. At the very same time, Śakra, the lord of Devas, was informed by Nārada: “The preceptor has been insulted by you. There is no doubt about it. O slayer of Bala, your kingdom has gone due to the disrespect (shown by you) to the preceptor. Hence, by all means, you have to plead to him for forgiveness.”
baseline: Then the king of Narada should be said to be the ruler of the gods. You have done this and the knowledge of the master should be doubted here. By the wisdom of the teacher the kingdom should be passed by force. Then you should forgive him for all his sins.
morphology: Then the king of Narada should be said to be the ruler of the gods. You have done this and the knowledge of the master is doubtful. By the wisdom of that master the kingdom has gone by force. You forgive him for all his sins.

sanskrit: etacchrutvā vacastasya nāradasya mahātmanaḥ | āsanātsahasotthāya taiḥ sarvaiḥ parivāritaḥ | āgacchattvarayā śakro gurorgehamataṃdritaḥ || 11 ||
reference: 11. On hearing these words of the noble-souled Nārada, Śakra suddenly got up from his seat. Surrounded by all of them (Devas etc.), he hastened to the abode of his preceptor promptly (without any slackness).
baseline: Having made such a ruse he said to Narada the great man that he should be seated in the seat and that all of them should be entranced by him. By the incarnation of the sun the cow should be worshipped in front of the priest.
morphology: Having made such a stir he said to Narada the great man. He should be seated in the seat and made to sit with all his family. The head of the cow should be placed in the front seat and the head should be made to stand in front of the priest.

sanskrit: pṛṣṭvā tārāṃ praṇamyādau kva gato hi mahātapāḥ | na jānāmītyuvācedaṃ tārā śakraṃ nirīkṣatī || 12 ||
reference: 12. He bowed down to Tārā at the outset and asked her, “Where has (our preceptor) of great penance gone?” Tārā stared at Śakra and said, “I do not know.”
baseline: Having asked the star one should bow down to it. One would not know the star and would not see the star.
morphology: After having asked the star one should bow down to it. One would not see the star without knowing it.

sanskrit: tadā ciṃtānvito bhūtvā śakraḥ svagṛhamāvrajat | etasminnaṃtare svarge hyaniṣṭāndbhutāni ca || 13 || abhavansarvaduḥkhārthe śakrasya ca mahātmanaḥ | pātālasthena balinā jñātaṃ śakrasya ceṣṭitam || 14 ||
reference: 13-15. Thereupon, Śakra became worried and returned to his own house. In the meantime, there appeared mysterious ill-omens in heaven, causing misery to everyone including the noble-minded Śakra himself.
baseline: Then after having thought the king should return to his own house. In the meantime the king would have to pay tribute to those who had been killed in heaven. The king should have done three great things for the sake of the protection of the poor and afflicted. He should have known the sacrifice made by him in the abyss.
morphology: Then after having thought about the matter the king should return to his house. In the meantime the king would have to pay tribute to the king. The king would also pay tribute by offering sacrifices to the goddess of the earth.

sanskrit: yayau daityaiḥ parivṛtaḥ pātālādamarāvatīm | tadā yuddhamatīvāsīddevānāṃ dānavaiḥ saha || 15 ||
reference: All the activities of Śakra were known to Bali who was stationed in the nether worlds. Surrounded by Daityas, he went from Pātāla to Amarāvatī. Thereupon a great fight ensued between Devas and Dānavas.
baseline: Then the king of Paṭāla should be surrounded by the demons. Then he should live with the gods of war and with the god of gods.
morphology: Then the king of Paṭāla and the goddess of the earth would be surrounded by the demons. Then he would live in war with the gods and the gods.

sanskrit: devāḥ parājitā daityai rājyaṃ śakrasya tatkṣaṇāt | saṃprāptaṃ sakalaṃ tasya mūḍhasya ca durātmanaḥ || 16 || nītaṃ sarvaprayatnena pātālaṃ tvaritaṃ gatāḥ | śukraprasādātte sarve tathā vijayino'bhavan || 17 || śakro'pi niḥśriko jāto devaistyaktastato bhṛśam | devī tirodhānagatā babhūva kamalekṣaṇā || 18 ||
reference: 16-18. Devas were defeated by Daityas. Instantaneously the whole of the kingdom of Śakra, the deluded and evil-minded one, was conquered by them and everything (belonging to Śakra) was quickly carried to Pātāla. It was by the grace of Śukra that all of them became victorious. Śakra became bereft of glory and splendour. So he was utterly abandoned by Devas. The goddess (of fortune) with lotus-like eyes vanished.
baseline: The gods are defeated by the gods and the kingdom is established immediately. All that is gained by him and his fools is made to go to the bottom of the earth with the same effort. All those who have been defeated by Gods are made to walk on the path of victory. The gods who have lost their power are destroyed by the forces of evil. The goddess is destroyed by Kamālikasana.
morphology: One who has conquered the kingdom of the gods and the king of the kingdoms of the kingdom is immediately defeated by the gods. One who gains everything from the misfortune of his fools and hastens to the bottom of the earth with all his efforts should go to the king. On the day of the offering of thanks one should become victorious and become free from the fear of the god one who becomes a king without the loss of the goddess becomes a liar.

sanskrit: airāvato mahānāgastathaivoccaiḥśravā hayaḥ | evamādīni ratnāni anekāni bahūnyapi | nītāni sahasā daityairlobhādasādhuvṛttibhiḥ || 19 ||
reference: 19. The great elephant Airāvata, the horse Uccaiḥśravas and many other precious things and jewels were taken away immediately by Daityas of evil behaviour due to greed.
baseline: One who comes from a great country with a great army should hear the sound of many gems and many other things. One who gives gifts should be taken away suddenly with the gift of food and resources.
morphology: One should hear the great coming of the Airavata with the loud voice and many other gems and other things. One should give them suddenly with the words of the goddess lūbhāda and sādhvritti.

sanskrit: puṇyabhāṃji ca tānyeva patitāni ca sāgare | tadā sa vismayāviṣṭo balirāha guruṃ prati || 20 ||
reference: 20. The good ones among them fell into the ocean. Bali who was surprised at this, remarked to his preceptor:
baseline: Then the virtuous man should be thrown into the sea and his body fell into it. Then he would be astonished and would offer sacrifice to the master.
morphology: Then the virtuous man should be thrown into the sea and his body fell down. Then he would be astonished and would sacrifice to the master.

sanskrit: devānnirjitya cāsmābhirānītāni bahūni ca | ratnāni tu samudre'tha patitāni tadadbhutam || 21 ||
reference: 21. “It is mysterious that many jewels brought by us after defeating Devas have fallen into the ocean.”
baseline: Many things are said to have been created by the gods and destroyed by us. The gems that have fallen into the sea are wonderful.
morphology: Many things are said to have been created by the gods and many other things. It is wonderful to see the gems falling into the sea.

sanskrit: balestadvacanaṃ śrutvā uśanā pratyuvāca tam | aśvamedhaśatenaiva surarājyaṃ bhaviṣyati | dīkṣitasya na saṃdehastasmādbhokta sa eva ca || 22 || aśvamedhaṃ vinā kiṃcitsvargaṃ bhoktaṃ na pāryate || 23 ||
reference: 22-23. On hearing the words of Bali, Uśanas (i.e. Śukra) replied to him: “One can attain the heavenly kingdom only through performance of a hundred horse-sacrifices. There is no doubt about it that it will be acquired by one who is initiated in it. Hence, the enjoyer is also he himself. Without performing a horse-sacrifice, heavenly pleasures cannot at all be enjoyed.”
baseline: Having heard the words of Balayya one should return to him and say that the kingdom of Sura would be established only after the death of the horse. One who has been ordained would not doubt that he is the one who consumes it. One would not be able to pass through the heaven without the death or death of a horse.
morphology: Having heard the words of the prophet Uṣṇa he said to him that the kingdom of Sūrā would be established by the death of the horse. He would not doubt that he would be ordained. He who eats it would not be able to pass through the heaven without the sacrifice of a horse.

sanskrit: gurorvacanamājñāya tūṣṇīṃbhūto balistataḥ | babhūva devaiḥ sārddhaṃ ca yathocitamakārayat || 24 ||
reference: 24. Understanding the utterance of his preceptor, Bali became quite silent. What was proper and befitting was carried out through and along with Devas.
baseline: One who has spoken to the teacher and obeyed the orders of the priest should be sacrificed. He should do the same with the gods.
morphology: One who has spoken to the teacher and obeyed the orders of the priest should be sacrificed with the blood of Tūṣṇim. He should do the right thing with the gods.

sanskrit: indropi śocyatāṃ prāpto jagāma parameṣṭhinam | vijñāpayāmāsa tathā sarvaṃ rājyabhayādikam || 25 ||
reference: 25. Indra too, on attaining a miserable plight, went to Parameṣṭhin (Brahmā) and informed him of everything, such as the danger to his kingdom and other things.
baseline: One who has attained the supreme position of the earth is known as Indra. He also knows that everything is a matter of fear for the kingdom.
morphology: One who acquires the knowledge of Indra also becomes supreme. One who gives knowledge of the universe and the fear of the kingdom is known to all.

sanskrit: śakrasya vacanaṃ śrutvā parameṣṭhī uvāca ha || 26 || saṃmilitvā surānsarvāṃstvayā sākaṃ tvarānvitāḥ | ārādhanārthaṃ gacchāmo viṣṇuṃ sarveśvareśvaram || 27 ||
reference: 26-28. On hearing the words of Śakra, Parameṣṭhī said: “We shall gather together all the Suras and go immediately along with you to Viṣṇu, the lord of all lords, in order to propitiate him.”
baseline: Having heard the word of the lord the supreme lord said that after having gathered all the sundials together one should go forth with him and go to worship Viṣṇu the lord of all gods.
morphology: Having heard the word of the lord the supreme lord said ha. Having gathered all the sundas together one should make haste with them. One should go to worship Lord Viṣṇu and all the gods.

sanskrit: tatheti gatvā te sarve śakrādyā lokapālakāḥ | brahmāṇaṃ ca puraskṛtya taṭaṃ kṣīrārṇavasya ca | prāpyopaviśya te sarve hariṃ stotuṃ pracakramuḥ || 28 ||
reference: Saying “So be it” all those guardians of the worlds beginning with Śakra went to the shore of the Milk Ocean with Brahmā at their head. After sitting there all of them began to eulogize Hari. Brahmā said:
baseline: Then they should go and worship all the lokpalakas. Having worshipped Brahman the river and the river of milk they should worship Hari and others.
morphology: Having gone there all of them should worship the lord Brahma and the king of the river Kshetra. Having received the gift of milk and water they should worship Hari.

sanskrit: brahmovāca | devadeva jagānnātha surāsuranamaskṛta | puṇyaślokāvyayānaṃta paramātmannamo'stu te || 29 ||
reference: 29-31. O lord of the universe, O lord of Devas bowed down to by Suras as well as Asuras, obeisance to you, O great Ātman, of auspicious reputation, O infinite one, O immutable one, free from decay.
baseline: O Brahman the supreme god of the universe Lord of the gods Lord Jaganna and Lord Surasura are worshipped. He should be worshipped as the supreme deity by the recitation of the sacred scriptures.
morphology: O Brahman the supreme god of the universe Lord Jaganna Lord Surasura the highest of all gods and the supreme beings are worshipped.

sanskrit: yajño'si yajñarūpo'si yajñāṃgo'si ramāpate | tato'dya kṛpayā viṣṇo devānāṃ varado bhava || 30 ||
reference: You yourself are Yajña. You are of the form of Yajña, O consort of Lakṣmī. Hence, be the bestower of boons unto the Devas.
baseline: One who performs a sacrifice is the form of a sacrifice. One who does so is the part of the sacrifice and one who enjoys it. Then one should worship the gods of Viṣṇu.
morphology: One who offers a sacrifice is the form of a sacrifice. One who gives a sacrifice becomes happy. Then one would be blessed by the gods of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: guroravajñayā cādya bhraṣṭarājyaḥ śatakratuḥ | jātaḥ surarṣibhiḥ sākaṃ tasmādenaṃ samuddhara || 31 ||
reference: By insulting his preceptor, Indra has lost (everything) from his kingdom along with the celestial sages. Hence redeem him.
baseline: The kingdom of the corrupt is said to have been established by the knowledge of the preceptor the sages and the sārrsis.
morphology: The kingdom of a corrupt man should be established by the knowledge of the preceptor. He should be destroyed by the sages.

sanskrit: śrībhagavānuvāca | dukokalajñayā sarvaṃ nasyatīti kimadbhutam | ye pāpino hyadharmiṣṭhāḥ kevalaṃ viṣayātmakāḥ | pitarau niṃditau yaiśca nirdaivātvena saṃśayaḥ || 32 ||
reference: The Lord said: 32. There is no wonder in the fact that everything perishes by insulting the preceptor. Those who are sinners, who are completely engaged in evil activities, who indulge only in sensual pleasures and by whom parents are censured, are undoubtedly godless ones.
baseline: The Lord said What is so wonderful that all things are destroyed by the knowledge of evil deeds. Those sinners those who are not of the heart those people who are only subject to evil deeds those accused by the parents and those who doubt God without any fault.
morphology: The Lord said that it would be wonderful if everything is destroyed by the knowledge of evil. Those sinners those who are devoid of the righteousness of the heart are only subjective. Those who are accused of the evil deeds of the father and those who doubt God are innocent.

sanskrit: anena yatkṛtaṃ brahmansadyastatphalamāgatam | karmaṇā cāsya śakrasya sarveṣāṃ saṃkaṭāgamaḥ || 33 ||
reference: 33. Immediately he has acquired the fruit, O Brahmā, of what he has committed. Difficulty and misfortune have befallen all due to the act of this Śakra.
baseline: The result of this action should be known as brahmana and all the troubles that may arise from it.
morphology: The result of this action should be that the Brahman should be able to bear all the sufferings.

sanskrit: viparīto yadā kālaḥ puruṣasya bhavettadā | bhūtamaitrīṃ prakurvaṃti sarvakāryārthasiddhaye || 34 ||
reference: 34. When a person faces adverse circumstances, they say that, he must be friendly with all living beings in order to achieve all his purposes.
baseline: When the time is contrary to that of a man he should offer three things to the king. He would get all the benefits.
morphology: When the time is contrary to that of a man the three elements are given to him and all the functions are accomplished.

sanskrit: tena vai kāraṇeneṃdra madīyaṃ vacanaṃ kuru | kāryahetostvayā kāryo daityaiḥ saha samāgamaḥ || 35 ||
reference: 35. For that reason, Indra, do as I suggest. For the realization of your purpose, alliance should be formed by you with Daityas.
baseline: O Lord of the universe you should say that the king should do the same thing for the sake of your work. You should do it together with the demons.
morphology: O Lord of the universe you should speak to me in the same way. You should associate with the demons for the sake of your work.

sanskrit: evaṃ bhagavatādiṣṭaḥ śakraḥ paramabuddhimān | amarāvatīṃ yayau hitvā sutalaṃ daivataiḥ saha || 36 ||
reference: 36. On being commanded by the lord, the highly intelligent Śakra left Amarāvatī and went to Sutala along with Devas.
baseline: In this way one who enjoys the gods would become wise. He would get the best of the gods by worshipping the goddess Amāravati. He should get the sandal with the gods.
morphology: In this way one who enjoys the gods would become wise. He would get the victory of Amāravati along with the gods.

sanskrit: indraṃ samāgataṃ śrutvā iṃdraseno ruṣānvitaḥ | babhūva saha sainyena haṃtukāmaḥ puraṃdaram || 37 ||
reference: 37. On seeing that Indra had come, Indrasena became furious. Along with his army, he was desirous of killing Indra.
baseline: Having heard of the presence of Indra the army of Indra was besieged by the army. With this army we would kill the king.
morphology: Having heard of the presence of Indra the army of Indra was besieged by the enemy. With this army they killed the king.

sanskrit: nāradena tadā daityā baliśca balināṃ varaḥ | nivāritastadvadhācca vākyairuccāvacaistathā || 38 ||
reference: 38. Then by means of different types of (consoling) words, Daityas and Bali, the most excellent one among strong persons, were prevented from killing him by Nārada.
baseline: Then the god of the sacrifice should be worshipped by Narada and the boon of the sacrifices should be offered. The words of the two men should be said to be good.
morphology: Then the gods sacrifices and gifts of the sacrifices should be offered with the narada. These two things should be said to be avoided.

sanskrit: ṛṣestasyaiva vacanāttyaktamanyurbalistadā | babhūva saha sainyena āgato hi śatakratuḥ || 39 || indrasenena dṛṣṭo'sau lokapālaiḥ samāvṛtaḥ | uvāca tvarayā yuktaḥ prahasanniva daityarāṭ || 40 ||
reference: 39-40. At the instance of that same sage, Bali controlled (abandoned) his anger. Indra then came in along with his array. He was seen by Indrasena surrounded by the guardians of the worlds. The king of Daityas hastened to tell him laughingly:
baseline: One who has come with an army of sages and hastened to capture the king of the mighty king should say that he should be sent to the king. He should be accompanied by a centurion. morphology: One should say that he was sent to the king with a promise made to him. He came with an army and said that he should be taken into custody by the lokpalas. He was seen by Indra. He said that the king should be sent with haste.

sanskrit: kasmādihāgataḥ śakra sutalaṃ prati kathyatām | tasyaitadvacanaṃ śrutvā smayamāna uvācatam || 41 ||

morphology: You are all the same as us. As we are you you are the illusion.

sanskrit: mama rājyaṃ kṣaṇenaiva nītaṃ daivavaśāttavayā | tathā hyetāni tānyena ratnāni subahūnyapi | gatāni tatkṣaṇādeva yatnānītāni vai tvayā || 43 ||

reference: 51-52. He has come to your presence with words asking for refuge. He is worthy of being protected by you. There is no doubt in this matter.” On being told thus by Nārada, the lord of Daityas himself pondered over everything with great understanding regarding what was right and what was wrong.
