morphology: You have pierced the sides of the earth with a diamond and have made a hundred mountains. How can I get the ground for your work?

baseline: The mountain that is said to be the abode of ksheera is called Rasatala. He went immediately and became the king of Rama. The king got it immediately.
morphology: The mountain that is said to be in the region of Ksheera is called Rasatala. He went immediately and became the king of Rama. The king became a great king after being mentioned.

sanskrit: bhrāmyamāṇastataḥ śailo noditaḥ suradānavaiḥ | bhramamāṇo nirādhāro bodhaśceva guruṃ vinā || 88 ||
reference: 88. When the mountain rotated, it was further pulled and pushed by Suras and Dānavas. Now it rotated without any basis, like the understanding without a preceptor.
baseline: One who wanders without the knowledge of the master should be guided by the sound of a stone and not by the gift of music.
morphology: One who is wandering without the knowledge of the master should not be afraid of the illusion.

sanskrit: paramātmā tadā viṣṇurādhāro maṃdarasya ca | dorbhiścaturbhiḥ saṃgṛhya mamaṃthābdhiṃ sukhāvaham || 89 ||
reference: 89. Viṣṇu, the supreme soul, then became the basic support of the Mandara mountain. With his four hands he gathered it up and churned pleasantly.
baseline: Then the lord Viṣṇu should be worshipped in the temple. Having collected the artefacts from the temple one would get happiness from me.
morphology: Then the supreme god Viṣṇu should be worshipped in the temple. Having collected the mantras from the two sides of the temple one should enjoy the peace of my mind.

sanskrit: tadā surāsurāḥ sarve mamaṃthuḥ kṣīrasāgaram | ekībhūtvā balenaivamatimātraṃ balotkaṭāḥ || 90 ||
reference: 90. Then all Suras and Asuras churned the Ocean of Milk after uniting together. Very powerful themselves, by uniting together, they became all the more powerful.
baseline: Then the sun the sea of milk and all that belong to me should be gathered together and the ball should be made of the same quantity.
morphology: Then the sun the sea of milk and all that is there in my mind should be united and the ball should be thrown at the same height.

sanskrit: pṛṣṭhakaṃṭhorujānvaṃtaḥ kamaṭhasya mahātmanaḥ | tathāsau parvataśreṣṭho vajrasāramayo dṛḍhaḥ | ubhayorgharṣaṇādeva vaḍavāgniḥ samutthitaḥ || 91 ||
reference: 91. The excellent mountain had adamantine strength. It rolled on the back, neck, thighs and the space between the knees of the noble-souled tortoise. Due to the friction of these two, submarine fire was generated.
baseline: One who is standing on a hill and having the greatness of a lotus is said to be the greatest. One who has the highest mountain and the highest diamond is strong. Both the faces of the king are raised by the incursion of the yogarśa.
morphology: One who is standing on a hill and having the greatness of a lotus is said to be the greatest. One who has got the best of mountains and has the strength of a diamond one who has raised the head and the head of a great ship from the collision of the two yogarśa is saidto be the fourth one.

sanskrit: halāhalaṃ ca saṃjātaṃ tadṝṣṭvā nāradena hi | tato devānuvācedaṃ devarṣiramitadyutiḥ || 92 ||
reference: 92. The Halāhala poison too emerged and it was seen by Nārada. Thereafter, the celestial sage of unmeasured splendour spoke these words:
baseline: Having prepared the halāhalā and having prepared it with the narāda one should worship the gods. One should offer the same to the sages.
morphology: Having prepared the halāhalā and having prepared it with the narāda one should worship the gods.

sanskrit: na kāryaṃ mathanaṃ cābdherbhavadbhiradhunā'khilaiḥ | prārthayadhvaṃ śivaṃ devāḥ sarve dakṣasya yājanam | tadvismṛtiṃ ca voyātaṃ vīrabhadreṇa yatkṛtam || 93 ||
reference: 93-94, “The churning of the ocean should not be carried on by you all now. O Devas, all of you pray to Śiva.[2] Have you forgotten the sacrifice of Dakṣa and what Vīrabhadra did there?
baseline: One should pray to Lord Śiva for the salvation of all the dakshas and the remembrance of the death of the king.
morphology: One should pray to Lord Śiva for the salvation of all the dakshas. One should remember that the death of the king is done by the meritorious one.

sanskrit: tasmācchivaḥ smaryatāṃ cāśu devāḥ paraḥ parāṇāmapi vā paraśca | parātparaḥ paramānaṃdarūpo yogidhyeyo niṣprapaṃco hyarūpaḥ || 94 ||
reference: Hence, let Śiva be immediately remembered, O Devas. He is greater than the greatest; he is beyond the greatest. He is the embodiment of supreme bliss. He is worthy of being meditated upon by Yogins; he has no form. (As a matter of fact) however, he is formless and unmanifest (or without diversity).”
baseline: Those who wish to do so should be remembered as those who worship the gods and the gods of the world. The supreme god is the manifestation of bliss and bliss. One who does not want to do any harm is known as a pancha.
morphology: Those who wish to be worshipped should be remembered as the chāśu gods the parāṇas the paramāpārās the manifestations of bliss and bliss.

sanskrit: te mathyamānāstvaritā devāḥ svātmārthasādhakāḥ | abhilāṣaparāḥ sarve na śrṛṇvaṃti yato jaḍāḥ || 95 ||
reference: 95. Devas were eager to achieve their purpose. Therefore, they hurriedly went on churning the ocean. All those who are overwhelmed by desires do not listen (to the advice of others), because they become irrational and stupid.
baseline: Those who worship the gods of their own selves are not able to hear all the desires of the people because they are the roots.
morphology: Those who worship the gods of their own selves and possess the meaning of their self are not all the objects of desire. They do not hear the sound of the roots.

sanskrit: upadeśaiśca bahubhirnopadeśyāḥ kadācana | te rāgadveṣasaṃghātāḥ sarve śivaparāṅmukhāḥ || 96 ||
reference: 96. They should not be given many pieces of advice and instructions. They are subject to Rāga (desire) and Dveṣa (hatred). All of them are averse to Śiva.
baseline: The preceptors should be of many kinds. Sometimes they should be associated with the two ragas. They should be directed to the gods of Śiva.
morphology: The preceptors should be of many kinds. Sometimes they are associated with ragas all those facing the gods of Śiva.

sanskrit: kevalodyamasaṃvītā mamaṃthuḥ kṣīrasāgaram | atinirmathanājjātaṃ kṣīrābdheścahalāhalam || 97 ||
reference: 97. With their sheer continuous exertion, they churned the Ocean of Milk. Due to excessive churning, the poison called Halāhala was generated from the Ocean of Milk.[3]
baseline: The sea of milk should be offered to me with the sum of only one ounce of water. The sea should be made with the highest amount of milk and the sea should not be made of milk.
morphology: The sea of milk should be offered to me with the same amount of water as the kewalodāma. The water should be made of the highest amount of milk and should be filled with water.

sanskrit: trailokyadahane prauḍhaṃ prāptaṃ haṃtuṃ divaukasaḥ | ata ūrdhvaṃ diśaḥ sarvā vyāptaṃ kṛtsnaṃ nabhastalam | grasituṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ kālakūṭaṃ samabhyayāt || 98 ||
reference: 98. It was strong enough to burn down the three worlds. It came up to kill the heaven-dwellers. It went up still further and spread to all quarters. The entire sky was pervaded by it. The Kālakūṭa poison advanced to consume all the living beings.
baseline: One who has attained maturity in the form of a threefold body should be killed by the Divyauksha. The upper part of the body is covered by the śvāstra sthāla. One should have the kalakuta of all the elements to be captured.
morphology: One who has attained maturity in the form of a trilokyadhana should be killed by the Divyauksha. The upper direction should be covered with the entire open space. One should get the kalakuta of all the elements to be captured.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā bṛhaṃtaṃ svakarasthamojasā taṃ sarparājaṃ saha parvatena | tatraiva hitvāpayayustadānīṃ palāyamānā hyasuraiḥ sametāḥ || 99 ||
reference: 99. They observed the huge king of serpents grasped by their own hands. They left him there along with the mountain and then went (immediately) away. They fled along with Asuras.
baseline: Having seen the great mountain one should place it with the king of serpents on the mountain. One should say that he would escape from there and join them.
morphology: Having seen the great mountain one should place it on the mountain with the king of serpents in his possession. One should say that he would escape from there and join them.

sanskrit: tathaiva sarva ṛṣayo bhṛgvādyāḥ śataśāmyati | dakṣasya yajanaṃ tena yathā jātaṃ tathābhavat || 100 ||
reference: 100. So also the sages beginning with Bhṛgu, sages in hundreds (fled in all directions). It was like what happened at the sacrifice of Dakṣa.
baseline: In the same way all the sages should pay tribute to Bhrīgvādi in the hundredth day. The yajna of Daksha should be done as per their wish.
morphology: In the same way all the sages would be able to attain the hundredth position of Bhrigavadi. The victory of Daksha would be achieved by that.

sanskrit: satyalokaṃ gatāḥ sarve bhuguṇā noditā bhṛśam | vedavākyaiśca vividhaiḥ kālakūṭaṃ śataśastataḥ | devā nāstyatra saṃdehaḥ satyaṃ satyaṃ vadāmi vaḥ || 101 ||
reference: 101. Earnestly urged by Bhṛgu, all of them went to Satyaloka: “This poison Kālakūṭa will be quelled by means of various Vedic Sentences. O Devas, there is no doubt in this matter. It is true; I am speaking the truth unto you.”
baseline: All who have gone to the true world should go to the false world. One who has not heard the scriptures or spoken the various things should give a hundred times. One should doubt the gods and say the truth.
morphology: All who have gone to the true world should be made aware of the earth the scriptures the words of the different worlds the kalakutas and others. If there is no doubt in the Lord I will tell the truth.

sanskrit: bhṛguṇoktaṃ vacaḥ śrutvā kālakūṭaviṣārdditāḥ | satyalokaṃ samāsādya brahmāṇaṃ śaraṇaṃ yayuḥ || 102 ||
reference: 102. On hearing these words uttered by Bhṛgu, all of them distressed by the poison Kālakūṭa went to Satyaloka and sought refuge in Brahmā.
baseline: Having heard the words of Bhrīguṇa the kālakutas are said to be poisoned. They should seek refuge in the universe by meeting the true world.
morphology: Having heard the words of Bhriguṇa the kālakutas should be ashamed of themselves. They should seek refuge in the universe by meeting the true world.

sanskrit: tadā jājvalyamānaṃ vai kālakūṭaṃ prabhojjavalam | dṛṣṭvā brahmātha tāndṛṣṭvā hyakarmajñānasurāsurān | teṣāṃ śapitumārebhe nāradena nivāritaḥ || 103 ||
reference: 103. Brahmā saw the blazing Kālakūṭa with sparkling lustre. He found that Suras and Asuras were ignorant of their duties. He was about to curse them, but he was prevented by Nārada.
baseline: Then when the king of the kingdom of Brahma sees the image of Kaalākuta the master of the universe standing on the fire he sees it. Having seen it he has knowledge of the action of the king. He has removed the evil spirits from the earth.
morphology: Then when the king of the kingdom of Brahma saw the fire of the king he saw the flame of the lord of the gods. Having seen it he said that the gods of the world would be destroyed by Narada.

sanskrit: brahmovāca | akāryaṃ kiṃ kṛtaṃ devāḥ kasmātkṣobhoyamudyataḥ | īśvarasya ca jāto'dya nānyathā mama bhāṣitam || 104 ||
reference: Brahmā said: 104. O Devas, what a wrong thing has been committed by you? Why has this explosive thing cropped up? It is Īśvara’s anger. My speech cannot be otherwise.
baseline: O brahm what has been done by the gods by causing disturbances. The birth of the gods is said to be nāṇya.
morphology: O brahm what has been done by the gods to disturb them? The birth of the gods is said to be nāṇya.

sanskrit: tato devaiḥ parivṛto vedopaniṣadaistathā | nānāgamaiḥ parivṛtaḥ kālakūṭabhayādyayau || 105 ||
reference: 105. Thereupon, surrounded by Devas, the Vedas, the Upāniṣads and the different kinds of Āgamas, he proceeded ahead out of fear of the Kālakūṭa.
baseline: Then the Vedas should be enshrined with the gods. Many of them should be covered with the mantras of the kālakutas.
morphology: Then the vedas should be enshrined with the gods. Many of them should be covered with the mantras of kāla kutas and be afraid of them.

sanskrit: tataściṃtānvitā devā idamūcuḥ parasparam | avidyākāmasaṃvītāḥ kuryāmaḥ śaṃkaraṃ ca kam || 106 ||
reference: 106. Then, Devas who were worried said to to one another, “We are enveloped in Avidyā (nescience) and lust. How can we do anything to Śaṅkara?”
baseline: Then the gods should be worshipped together. The kārīmas should be worshiped without any illusion. The gods should worship the goddess Śankara and others.
morphology: Then the gods should be worshipped in the same way. These two should be offered to each other. They should be made to worship the gods of the unruly and the lustful. The gods of Śankara should be worshiped together.

sanskrit: brahmāṇaṃ ca puraskṛtya tadā devāstvarānvitāḥ | vaikuṇṭhamāvrajansarve kālakūṭa bhayārdditāḥ || 107 ||
reference: 107. Then Devas kept Brahmā at their head and hurriedly went to Vaikuṇṭha, because they were afraid of Kālakūṭa.
baseline: Having worshipped Brahman the gods are worshipped in the same manner. The gods are feared by the gods of Vaikuntha Mārājana and Kaalakuta.
morphology: Having worshipped Brahman the gods are worshipped in the same manner. The gods are feared by the gods of Vaikuntha Mārājana and Kaalakuta.

sanskrit: brahmādayaścarṣigaṇāśca tadā pareśaṃ viṣṇuṃ purāṇapuruṣaṃ prabhaviṣṇumīśam | vaikuṇṭhamāśritamadhokṣajamādhavaṃ te sarve surāsuragaṇāḥ śaraṇaṃ prayātāḥ || 108 ||
reference: 108. Brahmā and others as well as the groups of sages sought refuge in the great lord Viṣṇu, the primordial Puruṣa, the mighty lord who had resorted to Vaikuṇṭha, Mādhava, Adhokṣaja. The groups of Suras and Asuras sought refuge in lord Viṣṇu.
baseline: Then the gods Brahma Vīṣṇu Purāṇā Prabhavīśnu Mūsī Vaikuntha Mahā Madhokṣamā Dhaśmā Sura Urga and others seek refuge.
morphology: Then the gods Brahma Vīṣṇu Purāṇā Prabhavīśṇu and others should be worshipped. All those who seek refuge in the sun the gods of the sun and the sky should be worshiped with the mantras of Vaikuntha Madhokṣa and others.

sanskrit: tāvatpravṛddhaṃ sumahatkālakūṭaṃ samabhyayāt | dagdhvādo brahmaṇo lokaṃ vaikuṇṭhaṃ ca dadāha vai || 109 ||
reference: 109. By that time, the great poison Kālakūṭa came there. After burning Brahmā’s world at the outset, it burned Vaikuṇṭha.
baseline: Then one should get the sumahata kālakuta of the superior form and the Brahmana form of the world and Vaikuntha form of fire.
morphology: Then the superior one should be offered a sumahata kaalakuta. The brahmins should be burnt and the world should be destroyed.

sanskrit: kālakūṭāgninā dagdho viṣṇuḥ sarvaguhāśayaḥ | pārṣadaiḥ sahitaḥ sadyastamālasadṛśacchaviḥ || 110 ||
reference: 110. Viṣṇu who dwells in the cavity of the heart of everyone, was burned by the fire of Kālakūṭa also with his attendants. Immediately he acquired the colour of Tamāla.
baseline: One who has burned the fire of Kaalakuta and burnt all the caves one who is present with the gods on the other side and who looks like a garland should be worshipped.
morphology: One who has burned the fire of Kaalakutā one who has destroyed all the caves one with the other gods and one with whom he is seen as a garland is called Vīṣṇu.

sanskrit: vaikuṇṭhaṃ ca sunīlaṃ ca sarvalokaiḥ samāvṛtam | jalakalmaṣasaṃvītāḥ sarve lokāstadābhavan || 111 ||
reference: 111. Vaikuṇṭha also became blue in colour. It was surrounded by all the worlds. Hence, all the worlds became encircled by the poisonous substance from the waters.
baseline: The Vaikuntha and the Sun are the elements of all worlds. All beings who possess water and water are known to be the objects of the universe.
morphology: The Vaikuntha the Sun and all the worlds are included in it. All the people who possess water and water are known to be the same.

sanskrit: aṣṭāvaraṇasaṃvītaṃ brahmāṃḍaṃ brahmaṇā saha | bhasmībhūtaṃ cakārāśu jalakalmaṣamadbhutam || 112 ||
reference: 112. The wonderful poison of the waters reduced to ash the whole of the Cosmic Egg with its eight outer coverings and along with Brahmā.
baseline: The Brahmana with Brahman is the eight parts of the universe. The four elements of water and water are wonderful.
morphology: One who has got eight parts of the universe with Brahman one who has destroyed the earth one with water and other elements is blessed with great wealth.

sanskrit: nobhūmirna jalaṃ cāgnirna vāyurna nabhastadā | nāhaṃkāro na ca mahānmūlāvidyā tathaiva ca | śivasya kopātsaṃjātaṃ tadā bhasmākulaṃ jagat || 113 ||
reference: 113. There was no earth, no water, no fire, no wind, and no ether. There was neither Ahaṃkāra (Cosmic Ego), nor Mahat (the Great Principle). There was no Mūlāvidyā. On account of Śiva’s wrath, the entire universe became reduced to ash. Notes regarding the Churning of the Ocean: This is a favourite topic of Purāṇa-writers as can be seen from its description in Mbh, Ādi. 18, VR 1.45.17-18, BhP VIII.5.U-18, BdP I.ii.25, MtP 249-250 to mention a few. The background of the churning of the ocean is different in our text. It is for the recovery of the gems of Indra which were sunk into the sea that Devas and Asuras agreed to churn the ocean. In Mbh. it was god Nārāyaṇa who advised god Brahmā to churn the ocean for getting Amṛta (Ādi. 17.10-13).
baseline: One who does not drink water from the ground fire air fire and fire and does not enjoy the great virtues of the world is born out of the anger of Lord Śiva.
morphology: One should not drink water from the ground fire air fire and other things. One should never drink the same thing as the great elemental knowledge. One who is born out of the wrath of Śiva would then burn the world.

sanskrit: munaya ūcuḥ | yattvayā kathitaṃ brahmanbrahmāṃḍaṃ sacarācaram | bhasmībhūtaṃ rudrakopātkālakūṭāgninā'tha़khilam || 1 ||
reference: The sages said: 1. O holy Sir, you said that the Cosmic Egg including the mobile and immobile beings was entirely reduced to ash by the fire of Kālakūṭa on account of the wrath of Rudra.
baseline: One who is said to have raised the Brahman Brahma Brahman and others in the form of fire should be burnt with the fire of Rudra and Kālaka.
morphology: O Brahman the Brahman and the Brahma are said to be the most common forms of fire. The fire is said to have been destroyed by the fire of Rudra and Kāṭaka.

sanskrit: brahmāṃḍāṃtarataḥ kiṃ tu rudraṃ manyāmahe vayam | tadā carācaraṃ naṣṭaṃ brahmaviṣṇupurogamam || 2 || bhasmībhūtaṃ rudrakopātkathaṃ sṛṣṭiḥ pravartitā | kuto brahmā ca viṣṇuśca kutaścaṃdrapurogamāḥ || 3 || anye surā surāḥ kutra bhasmībhūtā layaṃ gatāḥ | ata ūrdhvaṃ kimabhavattatsarvaṃ vaktumarhasi || 4 ||
reference: 2-4. But, we consider Rudra to be within the Cosmic Egg. Then the mobile and immobile beings with Brahmā and Viṣṇu as leaders were destroyed and reduced to ash through the wrath of Rudra. How was creation resumed and made to function? Wherefrom did Brahmā, Viṣṇu and other Suras and Asuras with the Moon at their Head (originate again)? Where did they get merged? Where were they reduced to ash? What happened after that? It behoves you to recount everything.
baseline: Then we shall consider the form of Rudra within the universe. Then the image of Brahma Viṣṇu Uśṇu and Uśna should be destroyed. The creation of Rudrākopataka is made of fire Brahma and Viśnu Kuta Indra and others are made of water. Where else are the objects of fire and water. Then what is the nature of fire?
morphology: Then we will understand the nature of Rudra beyond the universe. Then the earth is destroyed by Brahma Viṣṇu and the path of creation has been established by the incineration of Rudrākopātaka. Then Brahma and Viṣnu are incinerated by the fire. The path of Indra and others are set on fire by the sun. Then you will say what is above.

sanskrit: vyāsaprasādātsakalaṃ vettha tvaṃ nāparo hi tat | tasmājjñānamayaṃ śāstraṃ tajjānāsi na cāparaḥ || 5 ||
reference: 5. By the grace of Vyāsa you know everything. No one else knows it. Hence you understand the holy scripture full of knowledge as no one else does.
baseline: You do not know the meaning of the scripture. One who does not know it is a scribe.
morphology: You do not know the meaning of the scriptures. One who does not know them would not be a scribe.

sanskrit: iti pṛṣṭastadā sarvairmunibhirbhāvitātmabhiḥ | sūto vyāsaṃ namaskṛtya vākyaṃ cedamathābravīt || 6 ||
reference: 6. Asked thus by all those sages of sanctified souls, Sūta bowed down to Vyāsa and spoke these words:
baseline: Having said this one should bow down with the thread of the thread and the words should be said with the syllable 6.
morphology: Having said this one should bow down with the thread of the threads and the words should be said with all the senses.

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca | yadā brahmāṃḍamadhyasthā vyāptā devā viṣāgninā | haribrahmādayo hyete lokapālāḥ savāsavāḥ | tadā vijñāpitaḥ śaṃbhurheraṃbena mahātmanā || 7 ||
reference: Lomaśa said: 7. When Devas beginning with Hari and Brahmā, stationed in the middle of the Cosmic Egg, as well as the guardians of the worlds including Indra were enveloped by the fire of poison, Śaṃbhu was informed by the noble-souled Heraṃba (Gaṇeśa): Heraṃba said:
baseline: When the lord is spread in the middle of the universe by fire the gods are spread by poison and the gods of the world are destroyed by fire. The king of the people is known as Sāvasa. Then the king is declared to be sambhurhara.
morphology: When the lord is spread in the middle of the universe by the fire of poison the gods of the world are spread by the goddess Hari Brahma and the rulers of the people are destroyed. Then the great man is declared to be sambhurhendra.

sanskrit: heraṃba uvāca | he rudra he mahādeva he sthāṇo ha jagatpate | mayā vighnaṃ vinodena kṛtaṃ teṣāṃ sudurjayam || 8 || bhayena mati mohāttvāṃ nārccayaṃti ca māmapi | udyogaṃ ye prakurvanti teṣāṃ kleśo'dhiko bhavet || 9 || evamabhyarthitastena pinākī vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ | vighnāṃdhakārasūryeṇa gaṇādhipatinā tadā || 10 ||
reference: 8-9. O Rudra, O Mahādeva, O Sthāṇu, the lord of the universe, an obstacle very difficult to be surmounted has been created for them by me by way of amusement.[1] There are persons who start an enterprise, but either because of their fear or through the delusion of their minds, they do not worship you or me. The distress unto them will be very great.
baseline: O Rudra O Mahadeva O Sthaṇo O Jagatata I have created disturbances by merriment and won them well. By fear the heart of the enemy and the head of the army should be destroyed. Those who give employment should be afflicted by the same. Then the king of the kingdom of the sun should make the sound of the trumpet sound with the sounding of the bell.
morphology: O Rudra O Mahadeva O Sthaṇo O Jagat. I have created disturbances by merriment and won them well. By fear the mind of the enemy and the king of the country also gives me the victory. Those who give employment should be afflicted by the evil forces. Then the king who creates disturbances and disturbances should be punished with the sound of the trumpet.

sanskrit: liṃgarūpo'bravīcchaṃbhurnirākāro nirāmayaḥ | niraṃjano vyomakeśaḥ kaparddī nīlalohitaḥ || 11 ||
reference: 10-11. On being requested thus by the over-lord of Gaṇas, who dispels obstacles like the sun dispelling darkness, the Pināka-bearing Lord with a bull for his emblem, the Lord Nīlalohita with matted hair, the lord devoid of ailments, the lord in the form of Liṅga, the unsullied lord without form or features, the sky-haired lord Śiva, Śaṃbhu spoke thus: Maheśvara said[3]:
baseline: The form of the linga is the same as that of the chakṣambhūra the shape of the anus the form of a phallus and the shape is the one who is clean. The outer part of the body is called kāpardī.
morphology: The form of the linga is the same as that of the chakṣambhūra the shape of the anus the form of water and the shape is the one that is cured. The body of the celestial body is pure and the body is blue.

sanskrit: maheśvara uvāca | heraṃba śrṛṇu me vākyaṃ śraddhayā parayā yutaḥ | ahaṃkārātmakaṃ caiva jagadetaccarācaram || 12 || sthitiṃ karotyahaṃkāraḥ pralayotpattimeva ca | jagadādaugaṇapate tadā vijñaptimātrataḥ || 13 || māyāvirahitaṃ śāṃtaṃ dvaitādvaitaparaṃ sadā | jñaptimātrasvarūpaṃ tatsadānaṃdaikalakṣaṇam || 14 ||
reference: 12-14. O Heraṃba, listen to my words with great faith and attention. This universe consisting of the mobile and immobile beings is of the form of Ahaṃkāra (Cosmic Ego). This Ahaṃkāra creates, sustains and destroys. At the beginning of the universe, O Gaṇapati, Vijñapti (Intelligence, Consciousness) alone (remained). It was devoid of Māyā. īt was quiescent and of the form of Dvaita and Advaita (duality and non-duality). It was in the form of intelligence alone characterized by existence and eternal bliss.
baseline: O Mahesvarā said One who gives the word hārambā one who gives it away with belief and who gives to the world one should do good deeds. One who does not give it to the king who is arrogant and who has created destruction by doing the position of the king and who is always silent without the illusion of illusion and the manifestation of the two forms of knowledge is one of the manifestations of the gift.
morphology: O Mahesvarā said One who gives the word hārumbā one who gives it away with belief and one who does not know the meaning of the word one should do it with confidence. One who does the position of the world and does not get arrogance and does the destruction would get destroyed. One would get the manifestation of peace without the illusion of illusion and one would get a sign of knowledge and the same would be given.

sanskrit: gaṇapatiruvāca | yadi tvaṃ kevalo hyātmā paramānandalakṣaṇaḥ | tasmāttvadaparaṃ kiṃcinnānyadasti paraṃtapa || 15 ||
reference: Gaṇapati said: 15. If you are the sole Ātman, characterized by supreme bliss, O Scorcher of foes, then there is nothing other than you.
baseline: If you are the lord of Ganapātiruva. You are the manifestation of bliss in this matter. Then what else is there to be given to you.
morphology: If you are the lord of Ganapātiruva then you are a manifestation of bliss. Then what else is beyond that.

sanskrit: nānārūpaṃ kathaṃ jātaṃ surāsuravilakṣaṇam | vicitraṃ mohajananaṃ tribhirddevaiśca lakṣitam || 16 ||
reference: 16. Then how did the different forms originate, differentiated as Suras and Asuras? It is of variegated form observed by the three Devas. It is the cause of delusion.
baseline: How does one get the manifestation of the nine forms of the sun the manifestations of the universe the creation of strange forms and the manifesting of illusions are described in three different ways.
morphology: How does one get the manifestation of the nine forms of the sun the manifestations of the universe the creation of strange forms and the manifesting of illusions are described in the three directions.

sanskrit: bhūtagrāmaiścaturbhiśca nānābhedaiḥ samanvitaiḥ | jātaṃ saṃsāracakraṃ ca nityānityavilakṣaṇam || 17 ||
reference: 17. The cycle of worldly existence originated as different from Nitya (eternal) and Anitya (transient). It consists of four types or species of living beings endowed with many distinctive features etc.
baseline: There are many differences between the villages of the ghosts and the gods. The cycle of the world is called eternal.
morphology: The villages of the ghosts and the cities are divided into different parts. The cycle of the world is called eternal.

sanskrit: parasparavirodhena jñānavādena mohitāḥ | karmavādaratāḥ kecitkecitsvaguṇamāśritāḥ || 18 ||
reference: 18. People are deluded by various doctrines and tenets of knowledge antagonistic to one another. Some are devoted to the doctrine of Karman. Some resort to their (intrinsic) qualities.
baseline: They are attracted by the wisdom and the contradiction among themselves. Some of the virtues of their actions are worshipped.
morphology: They are enamoured by the contradictions among themselves with the wisdom with their deeds with some virtues.

sanskrit: jñānaniṣṭhāśca ye kecitparasparavirodhinaḥ | evaṃ saṃśayamāpannaṃ trāhi māṃ vṛṣabhadhvaja || 19 ||
reference: 19. A few are adherents of the path of knowledge but they are opposed to one another. O Bull-bānnered Lord, thus I have been overwhelmed by doubts. Save me (by dispelling the doubt).
baseline: Those who do not have knowledge and are hostile to each other one should fear the cow.
morphology: Those who do not know and those who oppose each other should be afraid of me.

sanskrit: ahaṃ gaṇaśca kutratyāḥ kva cāyaṃ vṛṣabhaḥ prabho | ete cānye ca bahavaḥ kuto jātāśca kutra vai || 20 ||
reference: 20. Where do I and the Gaṇas belong to? Whence is this bull, O'Lord? From where are these and many others born? Where (do they go)?
baseline: Where are these two cows and the bulls from? Many of them are killed and where are they from.
morphology: Where are the cows cows bulls and horses from? Many of these cows and cows are born from.

sanskrit: kṛtāḥ sarve mahābhāgāḥ sāttvikā rājasāśca vai | prahasya bhagavāñchaṃbhurgaṇeśaṃ vaktumudyataḥ || 21 ||
reference: 21. Whence are all these exceedingly fortunate ones made into Sāttvikas, Rājasas etc.? Lord Śaṃbhu laughed and began to speak to Gaṇeśa:
baseline: All the great things done are said to be virtuous and the king to be wise. The king should be able to speak in the form of the divine lamp.
morphology: All the great things done are said to be good and the king to be righteous. One who is the lord of the universe should speak in the form of the four horns.

sanskrit: maheśvara uvāca | kālaśaktyā ca jātāni rajaḥsattvatamāṃsi ca | tairāvṛtaṃ jagatsarvaṃ sadevāsumānuṣam || 22 ||
reference: Maheśvara said: 22. Rajas, Sattva and Tamas are produced by Kālaśakti (Power of Time). The entire universe including Devas, Asuras and human beings is enveloped by them.
baseline: O Mahesvara the king of the kingdom of Kālaśakti and the king who created the earth and the earth is known to have created the universe.
morphology: O Mahesvara the king of the kingdom of the king who is born with the power of time the lord of the world the god of the universe the man of the earth the goddess of heaven and earth.

sanskrit: paridṛśyamānametaccānaśvaraṃ paramārthataḥ | viddhyetatsarvasiddhyaiva kṛtakatvācca naśvaram || 23 ||
reference: 23. This (world) that is being seen is imperishable ultimately, but, understand that as an evolved effect it is perishable. It is evolved by means of all Siddhis.
baseline: One who has seen the manifestations of the universe and the manifestation of the supreme god should be destroyed by the creation of the world.
morphology: One who has seen the manifestations of the universe one who has attained the highest form of life and who has not been able to do so would become a mortal.

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca | yāvadgaṇeśasaṃyukto bhāṣamāṇaḥ sadāśivaḥ | liṃgarūpī viśvarūpaḥ prādurbhūtā sadāśivāt || 24 || śivarūpā jagadyoniḥ kāryakāraṇarūpiṇī | liṃgarūpī sa bhagavānnimagnastatkṣaṇādabhūt || 25 ||
reference: 24-25. While Sadāśiva of Cosmic Form and in the form of the Liṅga was conversing with Gaṇeśa, His Power (Śakti called Śiva), the source of the universe of the nature of cause and effect was born of Sadāśiva. At the same instant, the Lord in the form of the Liṅga became submerged.
baseline: One who has spoken with the linga the form of the universe is said to be sāsādiva. One who is a linga and has the combination of the two linga forms is described as sādavīṣṇu siva jagāda jāga kārākāna linga. He is worshipped in the presence of the lord.
morphology: One who has spoken with the voice of the lord as long as he is alive one who has the form of the linga the universal form of sāsādiva the forms of Śiva jagadī and kārākāna the lingus the lord of the universe and the king of jagadas would become the king.

sanskrit: ekā sthitā parā śaktirbrahmavidyātmalakṣaṇā | gaṇeśo vismayāviṣṭo hyavalokanatatparaḥ || 26 ||
reference: 26. The single supreme Śakti, characterized as the Ātman of Brahmavidyā abided (there). Overwhelmed by wonder, Gaṇeśa became engrossed in looking (at that form).
baseline: One who is standing on the same side and having the strength the knowledge the qualities of the self is called Ganesha. One who enjoys the wonder one who has the power and knowledge of the universe is called Hāvāloka.
morphology: The image of Brahman the power and the knowledge of the self is standing in one place. Lord Ganesha is the manifestation of the mind.

sanskrit: ṛṣaya ūcuḥ | prakṛtyantargataṃ sarvaṃ jagadetaccarācaram | gaṇeśasya pṛthaktvaṃ ca kathaṃ jātaṃ taducyatām || 27 ||
reference: The sages asked: 27. If this entire universe consisting of the mobile and immobile beings is included within Prakṛti, how is it then that Gaṇeśa was able to preserve his separate entity? Let this be explained.
baseline: The sage should rise up. All that is within the nature should be worshipped in the world. How can the separation of Ganesha be achieved.
morphology: The sage should rise up. All that is within the nature should be worshipped in the world. How does the separation of Ganesha happen?

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca | sākṣātprakṛtyāḥ saṃbhūto gaṇeśo bhagavānabhūt | yathārūpaḥ śivaḥ sākṣāttadrūpo hi gaṇeśvaraḥ || 28 ||
reference: Lomaśa replied: 28. Lord Gaṇeśa was directly born of Prakṛti herself.[4] Gaṇeśvara has the same form as that of Śiva himself.
baseline: The form of Lord Ganesha should be described as the manifestation of the manifest form of the god Śiva. The manifestation is described as that which is manifest in the form of lord Ganesha.
morphology: The figure of Ganesha is said to be the manifestation of the manifest nature of the universe. The image of Lord Ganesha is described as that of Lord Shiva.

sanskrit: śivena saha saṃgrāmo hyabhūttasya mahātmanaḥ | ajñānātprakṛto bhūtvā bahukālaṃ nirantaram || 29 ||
reference: 29-30. A battle ensued between Śiva and that noble-souled one who had been Prākṛta (born of Prakṛti) due to ignorance. That battle continued without a break for a long time.
baseline: The great man who fought with Śiva would be destroyed by ignorance for a long period of time.
morphology: The great man who fought with the god Śiva would be destroyed by ignorance for a long period of time.

sanskrit: tasya dṛṣṭvā hyajeyatvaṃ gajārūḍhasya tattadā | triśūlenāhanacchaṃbhuḥ sagajaṃ tamapātayat || 30 ||
reference: On observing that he was invincible as long as he was riding an elephant, Śaṃbhu hit him with his trident and toppled him down along with the elephant.
baseline: Having seen him the king of the Ghajaras should be defeated. He should not be made to wear a helmet with the tridents. The king should be cast into the ground.
morphology: Having seen him one would get victory. One would get the crown of the elephant without having to wear the tridents. He would lose the shield of the lion.

sanskrit: tadā stuto mahādevaḥ paraśaktyā paraṃtapaḥ | paraśaktimuvācedaṃ varaṃ varaya śobhane || 31 ||
reference: 31. Then Mahādeva the scorcher of enemies, was eulogized by the Supreme Power (Prakṛti). The lord then said to the great Śakti, “O splendid lady, choose your boon.”
baseline: Then one should praise the gods with the power of the other. One should give gifts to the lord of the two powers and make them beautiful.
morphology: Then the gods should be praised with the power of the other gods. The gods should also be blessed with the powers of the others.

sanskrit: tadā vṛto mahādevo vareṇa parameṇa hi | yo'yaṃ tvayā hato deva mama putro na saṃśayaḥ || 32 || tvāṃ na jānātyayaṃ mūḍhaḥ prakṛtyaṃśasamudbhavaḥ | tasmātputraṃ jīvayemaṃ mama tṛṣṭyarthameva ca || 33 ||
reference: 32-33. Then an excellent boon was chosen from Mahādeva: “O lord, he who was killed by you was undoubtedly my son. Being born of a part of Prakṛti, he is deluded. Hence he does not know you. In order to gratify me, resuscitate this son of mine.”
baseline: Then there is a great god named Vrta the lord of the universe and the supreme god. The one who is yours is not my son without doubt. He is not known to be a fool a man of nature a person of the same nature. He should be my son and the same is my life.
morphology: Then the god Vrta the lord of the universe and the supreme god of the world should be worshipped. You are the god of my son. You know that you are not a fool you know that your nature is eternal and you are the son of life. You do not know that.

sanskrit: prahasya bhagavānrudro māyāputramajīvayat | siṃdhuravadanenaiva mukhe sa samayojayat || 34 ||
reference: 34. Lord Rudra laughed loudly and revived the son of Māyā. He fixed the head of an elephant to his body.
baseline: The preceptor Rudra is said to have worshipped the goddess Mayāputrā. He has given time for the recitation of sindhura in his mouth.
morphology: The preceptor Rudra the god of the universe living in the form of the goddess mayā puttram has given time for the recitation of the same word in the mouth of the sindhu.

sanskrit: tadā gajānano jātaḥ prasādācchaṃkarasya ca | māyāputropi nirmāyo jñānavānsaṃbabhūva ha || 35 ||
reference: 35. Thus the elephant-faced lord was born by the grace of Śaṅkara. Although he was the son of Māyā, he was free from the clutches of Māyā and became endowed with (spiritual) knowledge.
baseline: Then the king should be pleased with the image of the king. He should also make a son of maya and kill the wise man.
morphology: Then the king should be pleased with the image of the king. He should also kill the wise man who had created the son of maya.

sanskrit: ātmajñānāmṛtenaiva nityatṛpto nirāmayaḥ | samādhisaṃsthito raudraḥ kālakālāṃtako'bhavat || 36 ||
reference: 36. He was perpetually contented with the nectar of the knowledge of Ātman. He was free from ailments. Sitting in deep meditation, he became very fierce and then destroyed Kāla (god of death) of black complexion.
baseline: One who is ever satisfied with the knowledge of the self becomes healthy. One who remains in the grave and has anger for a long time becomes ill.
morphology: One who is ever satisfied with the knowledge of the self becomes healthy. One who remains in the grave and becomes angry for a long time becomes ill.

sanskrit: yogadaṃḍārthamutpāṭya svakīyaṃ daśanaṃ mahat | kare gṛhya gaṇādhyakṣaḥ śabdhabrahmātivarttate | ṛddhisiddhidvayenaiva ekatvena virājitaḥ || 37 ||
reference: 37. He pulled out his own huge tooth for the sake of Yogadaṇḍa[5] (the mystic wand of Yogic practice) and held it in his hand. He was the presiding deity of the Gaṇas. He surpasses the Śabdabrahman (the Vedas or the supreme spiritual knowledge expressed in words). Though accompanied by both Ṛddhi and Siddhi, he shines in his aloneness.
baseline: Having derived the meaning of the yogic punishment the chief of the army is said to be great. Having taken the gunpowder the king is known as Brahma. He is known to be one of the two siddhis.
morphology: Having derived the meaning of yogic punishment the chief of the army is said to be great. Having taken the charge of the guna one should return to Brahman. One who has attained the position of the king of the two siddhis would become supreme.

sanskrit: ye te gaṇāśca vighnāśca ye cānye'bhyadhikā bhuvi | teṣāmapi patirjātaḥ kṛto'sau śaṃbhunā tadā || 38 ||
reference: 38. The groups of Gaṇas and Vighnas (obstacles) and many others superior to these—whatever there was on the earth, he became the lord thereof. He was made so by Śaṃbhu then.
baseline: Those who are born out of fear of the enemy and those who are married to the enemy should be killed by the king. Then the king of the war should do the same for those sons of his wife.
morphology: Those who are born out of their husbands and those who are widowed those who do not want to be married those children should be married to a man named Shambhu.

sanskrit: tasmādvi lokayāmāsa prakṛtiṃ viśvarūpiṇīm | pṛthaksthitvāgrato jānālliṃgaṃ prakṛtimeva ca | dadarśa vimalaṃ liṃgaṃ prakṛtisthaṃ svabhāvataḥ || 39 || ātmānaṃ ca gaṇaiḥ sāddhaṃ tathaiva ca jagattrayam | līnaṃ liṃge samastaṃ taddherambo jñānavānapi || 40 ||
reference: 39. Hence he was able to see Prakṛti which has the Cosmic form. He remained separate and was able to realize the Liṅga as well as the Prakṛti. He saw the pure Liṅga naturally abiding in the Prakṛti. 40. Heraṃba who was equipped with perfect knowledge saw himself along with the Gaṇas as well as the three worlds entirely merged in the Liṅga.
baseline: The nature of the world is thus described as the manifestation of the universe. One who is separated from the world one who is living in the open space and one who has the linga in the form of nature one whose eyes are visible and the soul is formed by the ganas and the world. One with the līna līnga and all that he has is also known as the jāgatrā.
morphology: The nature of the world is thus described as the worldly form. The open space of the universe is different and the nature is the same. The linga of the body is different from the linga that is in nature. The soul is divided into the ganas and the world. The leaning linga is also known as the līna the whole linga and the knowledgeable linga.

sanskrit: mumoha ca punaḥ saṃjñāṃ pratilabhya prayatnataḥ | nanāma śirasā tābhyāmīśābhyāṃ sa gaṇeśvaraḥ || 41 ||
reference: 41. Though he was endowed with perfect knowledge, he lost his consciousness. He regained it with very great effort. The lord of the Gaṇas bowed down his head to those two supreme powers.
baseline: Then again one should repeat the preceptor and try to repeat it. One should say namā head forehead and the other two things. That is Lord Ganesha.
morphology: Then again one should try to repeat the preceptor the lord of the gods Ganesha by the repetition of the hymn mūmoho namā śīrṣa tāmīśa and others.

sanskrit: tadā dadarśa tatraiva lokasaṃhārakārakam | brahmāṇaṃ caiva rudraṃ ca viṣṇuṃ caiva sadāśivam || 42 ||
reference: 42. Then he saw there itself Brahmā, Rudra, Viṣṇu and Sadāśiva in the form of the annihilator of the worlds.
baseline: Then there is the spectator who destroys the world. Brahman Rudra Viṣṇu Satāsiva.
morphology: Then there is a spectator who destroys the world. Brahman Rudra Viṣṇu Satāsiva.

sanskrit: dadarśa pretatulyāni liṃgaśaktyātmakāni ca | brahmāṇḍagolakānyeva koṭiśaḥ paramāṇuvat || 43 || līyaṃte ca vilīyaṃte maheśe liṃgarūpiṇi | prakṛtyaṃtargataṃ liṃgaṃ liṃgasyāṃtargatā ca sā || 44 ||
reference: 43-45. He saw some beings resembling ghosts. They were the Liṅgaśaktis. He saw crores of spherical Cosmic Eggs like so many atoms. They were getting merged and dissolved in Maheśa who was in the form of a Liṅga.
baseline: One who has seen the manifestations of the spirits and the powers of the linga the universe the spheres and the atoms of the universe would be multiplied by a million. One who is born into the universe and who is the form of the ālinga would be merged with the Āṣeṣha. One would become the liga within the nature and the līga within the lingas.
morphology: One who has seen the manifestations of the spirits and the powers of the linga the universe the spheres and the billions of atoms of the universe and the forms of the lingas in the form of the māhṣeśa and the inner linga and the internal linga are the objects of the nature.

sanskrit: śaktyā liṃgaṃ ca saṃchannaṃ tadā sarvamadṛśyata | liṃgena śaktiḥ saṃchannā parasparamavartata || 45 ||
reference: The Liṅga was inside the Prakṛti and the Prakṛti was within the Liṅga. The whole of the Liṅga was seen covered by Śakti. The Śakti was covered by the Liṅga. Thus the two encompassed each other.{GL_NOTE::}
baseline: Then the linga should be cleansed with force. Then all the forces should be purified with force and the power should be transferred to each other.
morphology: Then the linga should be cleansed with force. Then all the forces should be purified with force with force and force should be transferred to each other.

sanskrit: śivābhyāṃ saṃśritaṃ lokaṃ jagadetaccarācaram | gaṇeśo vāpi tajjñānaṃ na pare'pi tathāvidan || 46 ||
reference: 46. The whole world consisting of the mobile and immobile beings stayed supported by both Śivas (i.e. Śiva ānd Śakti). Only Gaṇeśa and none else, though great, had that knowledge.
baseline: The world that has been built by the two gods Śiva the king of the world Ganesha Vapi and others are not known.
morphology: The world that has been built by the two gods Śiva is the world. Lord Ganesha and his disciples have not known it.

sanskrit: tadovāca mahātejā gaṇādhyakṣo gaṇaiḥ saha | saśaktikaṃ stūyamānaḥ śaktyā ca parayā tadā || 47 ||
reference: 47. The presiding deity of the Gaṇas (Lord Gaṇeśa), of great splendour, accompanied by the Gaṇas eulogized with great strength, the lord accompanied by Śakti.
baseline: Then the chief of the army should be accompanied by the mighty men. Then the mighty man should be praised and the mighty one should be exalted.
morphology: Then the chief priest should be accompanied by a large number of men. Then the mighty man should be praised with strength and power.

sanskrit: gaṇeśa uvāca | namāmi devaṃ śaktyānvitaṃ jñānarūpaṃ prasannaṃ jñānātparaṃ paramaṃjyotirūpam | rūpātparaṃ paramaṃ tattvarūpaṃ tattvātparaṃ paramaṃ maṃgalaṃ ca ānaṃdākhyaṃ niṣkalaṃ nirviṣādam || 48 ||
reference: Gaṇeśa prayed: 48. I bow down to the god accompanied by His Śakti (Power)—the Lord who is the embodiment of knowledge, who is kindly disposed (but) beyond the ken of knowledge and of the form of supreme Light, who transcends forms, is the Supreme Reality incarnate, who is beyond the principles (categories of Sāṅkhyas), supremely auspicious, who is called Bliss undivided and uncontaminated by sorrow.
baseline: O Ganesha one who worships the gods with the power of knowledge happiness knowledge supreme enjoyment the form of the elements the supreme element the ultimate good the blissful and the purest of all things is known to be the manifestation of the manifestations.
morphology: O Ganesha one who worships the gods with the power knowledge happiness knowledge and the supreme enjoyment the highest element the supreme element matter happiness and bliss the purest and undisturbed.

sanskrit: dhūmātparamayovahnirdhūmavatpratibhāsate | prakṛtyaṃtargastvaṃ hi lakṣyase jñānisaṃbhavaḥ | prakṛtyaṃtargatastvaṃ hi māyāvyaktiritīyase || 49 ||
reference: 49-50. The fire in (a ball of) iron is beyond smoke (smokeless), but it appears as though filled with smoke. You who are the source of knowledge, appear to be within Prakṛti. You who are present within the Prakṛti by Māyā, are spoken of as manifested.
baseline: One who has not been able to attain the goal of the goal is known to be the nature of the object. One who does not want to get lost is known as the manifestation of the illusion.
morphology: One who is not afraid of the smoke and the heat of the earth should be aware of it. One should be conscious of the nature as it is within one's own self. One would become wise as if he were within ones own body as if it were within the nature.

sanskrit: evaṃvidhastvaṃ bhagavansvamāyayā sṛjasyatholuṃpasi pāsi viśvam | asmādgarātsarvamidaṃ pranaṣṭaṃ sabrahmavipreṃdrayutaṃ carācaram || 50 ||
reference: You whose nature is such, O lord, create, annihilate and protect the universe by your Māyā. On account of this poison, the entire universe consisting of the mobile and immobile beings and accompanied by Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Indra, has been destroyed.
baseline: In the same way the universe should be destroyed by the creation of the universe by the Lord Himself. All that is lost from our city is destroyed by all.
morphology: In the same way the universe should be destroyed by the creation of the universe with the help of the gods gods and goddesses. All these things should be removed from our city.

sanskrit: yathā purāsīrbhagavānmaheśastrailokyanātho'si carācarātmā | kuruṣya śīghraṃ sahajīvakośaṃ carācaraṃ tatsakalaṃ pradagdham || 51 ||
reference: 51. You are lord Maheśa. You are the lord of the three worlds. You are the immanent soul of the mobile and immobile beings. The mobile and immobile beings along with the vestures of individual souls, have been completely burnt down. Please revive them quickly and make it (the world) as it was before.
baseline: Just as one who is the master of the universe one who possesses weapons is the supreme soul. One who is quick to destroy the corpse of the living organism should also destroy the body.
morphology: Just as one who is the master of the universe one who has armed the world and who has destroyed the soul of the enemy would soon destroy the corpse of his fellowman and spread the same blood.

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca | evaṃ stuto gaṇeśena bhagavānbhūtabhāvanaḥ | yadutthitaṃ kālakūṭaṃ lokasaṃhārakārakam || 52 || liṃgarūpeṇa tadgrastaṃ vimalaṃ cākarottadā | sadevāsuramartyāśca sarvāṇi trijaganti ca | tatkṣaṇādrakṣitānyeva kṛpayā parayā yutaḥ || 53 ||
reference: 52-54. On being eulogized thus by Gaṇeśa, the Lord (Siva), the sanctifier of all living beings, assumed the form of a Liṅga and consumed the Kālakūṭa that arose there and caused the destruction of all the worlds. He made everything free from impurities. Since the lord was endowed with great compassion and considerateness, all Devas, Asuras and human beings and all the three worlds were instantaneously saved.
baseline: One who has raised the kālakuta as a linga and who destroys the world should be worshipped with the words hāmāśuṇa kālaṣṇu gāṇeśa bhūbhuta bhābhava bhava kalakaṭa vimāla chakrāda vīlāma sādevāsura mārtī and all the three worlds.
morphology: One who has raised the kālakuta as a linga and who destroys the world should be worshipped with the hymn lāśmī. One who raises the kalakuta in the form of the linga one who is possessed by it and who has destroyed it should be given the vimalā as a chakra. One should protect the three worlds from the evil spirits of the gods the gods and the mortal beings.

sanskrit: brahmā viṣṇuḥ sureṃdraśca lokapālāḥ saharṣayaḥ | yakṣā vidyādharāḥ siddhā gaṃdharvāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ | utthitāścaiva te sarve nidrāparigatā iva || 54 ||
reference: Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Surendra, the Guardians of the Quarters along with the sages, Yakṣas, Vidyādharas, Siddhas, Gandharvas and groups of celestial damsels—all of them got up as though from sleep.
baseline: Brahma Viṣṇu Surendra Lokāpala Sahasrīya Yaksha Vidyadhara Siddha Gandharva Vāsārasas and others who live on the ground are all sleeping.
morphology: Brahma Viṣṇu Surendra Lokāpala Sāhārṣya Yaksha Vidyādhara Siddha Gandharva Vāsārasas and others are all sleeping.

sanskrit: vismayena samāviṣṭā babhūvurjātasādhvasāḥ | sarve devāsurāścaiva ūcurāścaryavattataḥ || 55 ||
reference: 55. They were struck with wonder. They were agitated and frightened. All Devas and Asuras said in dismay:
baseline: All the gods and goddesses living in the world are astonished.
morphology: All the gods and goddesses who dwell in the earth and the earth are covered with wonder.

sanskrit: kva kālakūṭaṃ sumahadyena vidrāvitā vayam | mṛtaprāyāḥ kṛtāḥ sadyaḥ salokapālakā hyamī || 56 || ityabruvaṃstadā daityāstūṣṇīṃbhūtāstadā sthitāḥ | śakrādayo lokapālā viṣṇuṃ sarveśvareśvaram | brahmāṇaṃ ca puraskṛtya idamūcuḥ samedhitā || 57 ||
reference: 56-62. “Where is that immense Kālakūṭa by which we had been compelled to flee and made almost dead along with the Guardians of the Quarters?” So said they, but Daityas remained silent. The Guardians of the Quarters beginning with Śakra, who were able to regain strength and happiness with god Brahmā as their leader, said this after honouring Viṣṇu, the lord of all lords:
baseline: Having worshipped the god Viṣṇu the lord of all gods the king of the universe and the goddess of all beings should be worshipped in the same manner.
morphology: Having worshipped the goddess Kaalakuta with the fragrance of the sun one who has been killed by the enemy should worship the goddess Sālokāpakā. One who has worshipped a demon in the past would be blessed with the gift of the lord Viṣṇu the lord of the universe and the king of the world would be worshipped by the king.

sanskrit: kenedaṃ kāritaṃ viṣṇo na vidāmo'lpamedhasaḥ | tadā prahasya bhagavānbrahmaṇā saha taiḥ suraiḥ || 58 || samādhimagamansarve'pyekāgramanasastadā | tattvajñānena nirhṛtya kāmakrodādikāndvijāḥ || 59 || tadātmani sthitaṃ liṃgamapaśyanvi budhādayaḥ | viṣṇuṃ puraskṛtya tadā tuṣṭuvuḥ paramārthataḥ || 60 ||
reference: “By whom has this been caused? We do not know as we are deficient in intelligence.” Then Viṣṇu laughed at Brahmā and all those (Suras). All of them then began to meditate with great concentration of their minds. O Brāhmaṇas, that dispelled base emotions such as lust and anger as well as other feelings by means of the knowledge of Reality. Then Devas and others saw the Liṅga present in their own Ātman (Soul). Keeping Viṣṇu at their head, they eulogized the Lord for the attainment of the ultimate truth:
baseline: Then the disciples of Viṣṇu should be worshipped in the form of a serpent. Then they should be accompanied by Brahman the supreme god of the universe. They should be buried with the sound of the sun the sound and sound of a celestial body the spirit of the gods the mind of the king the gods of the world the goddess of the earth the lord of the worlds the king of gods and the king. Having known the principles they should worship the goddess. Having worshipped Viśṇu the Lord of all beings should be pleased.
morphology: Then the gods of the universe should be worshipped together with Brahman and the other gods in the form of the king. Having made a sacrifice they should be destroyed. Having destroyed the king of the kingdom by the knowledge of the principles the king should be removed from the kingdom of the gods. Having worshipped Lord Viṣṇu and the goddess of the world the lord should be pleased with the supreme god.

sanskrit: ātmanā paramātmānaṃ yoginaḥ paryupāsate || 61 || liṃgameva paraṃ jñānaṃ liṃgameva paraṃ tapaḥ | liṃgameva paro dharmo liṃgameva parā gatiḥ | tasmālliṃgātparataraṃ yacca kiṃcinna vidyate || 62 ||
reference: “Yogins worship the Supreme Soul through their own souls. The Liṅga alone is the greatest knowledge. The Liṅga alone is the greatest penance. The Liṅga alone is the greatest Dharma. The Liṅga alone is the greatest goal. Hence, there is nothing at all which (can be called) greater than the Liṅga.”
baseline: The yogis are endowed with the supreme spirit by the self. One who knows the linga one who has knowledge ones linga and one who practices penance one should practice linga or dharma and one should move beyond linga. What else is there beyond the lingas?
morphology: One who practices the supreme self with the self the yogis the linga the knowledge the lingam the penance and the dharma one who practices dharma and the liga the movement is above that of a linga. One who does so is above all else.

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvaṃto hi tadā surāsurāḥ salokapālā ṛṣibhiśca sākam | viṣṇuṃ puraskṛtya tamālavarṇaṃ śaṃbhuṃ śaraṇyaṃ śaraṇaṃ prapannāḥ || 63 ||
reference: 63. After saying thus, Suras and Asuras along with the Guardians of the Quarters and sages kept Viṣṇu whose complexion is dark like the Indian cinnamon, at their head. They then sought refuge in Śaṃbhu who is worthy of being resorted to:
baseline: In this way the sun should be worshipped by the sun the sun and the sages. Having worshipped Lord Viṣṇu one should offer him the colour of tāla shambhu sārāṇya and the shelter.
morphology: In this way one should worship the sun sage serpent sages serpents and sages. One should worship Lord Viṣṇu in the form of a lotus and give him the colour of a tāmala.

sanskrit: trāhitrāhi mahādeva kṛpālo parameśvara | purā trātā yathā sarve tathātvaṃ trātumarhasi || 64 ||
reference: 64. “Save us, save us, O Mahādeva, O merciful lord, O Supreme God. It behoves you to save us as we had been saved before (by you).
baseline: One who is blessed with the gift of the three gods the lord of grace the god of all things and the lord is blessed by the Lord.
morphology: One who is blessed with the trāhitrāhi māhadeva gracious pārśvāṇu the whole of the tratrātā should be worshipped in the same way as one who is worshipped.

sanskrit: taddevadeva bhavataścaraṇāraviṃdaṃ sevānubaṃdhamahimānamanaṃtarūpam | tvadāśritaṃ yatparamānukaṃpayā namo'stu te devavara prasīda || 65 ||
reference: 65. O Lord of Devas, your lotus-like feet possess greatness befitting our repeated service. They have infinite forms. We have resorted to them. (Save us) with the greatest mercy. Obeisance to you, O excellent one among Devas. Be pleased.”
baseline: Then you should worship the gods gods and goddesses. You should worship them in the form of a bond of service and honor. You have worshipped them with the fragrance of a man. They should worship God.
morphology: O Lord of gods you are the manifestation of the bondage of the mind that is bound by the service. You are worshipped with the fragrance of man. You worship the gods.

sanskrit: liṃgasvarūpamadhyastho bhagavānbhūtabhāvanaḥ | sarvaiḥ suragaṇaiḥ sākaṃ babhāṣedaṃ ramāpatiḥ || 66 ||
reference: 66. Lord Ramāpati (Viṣṇu), the sanctifier of the living beings, stood in the middle of the form of Liṅga along with ail the groups of Suras and spoke thus:
baseline: One who has the form of the linga in the middle and the feeling of the lord one who has all the senses should speak with the voice of Rama.
morphology: One who has the form of the linga in the middle and has the feeling of God one who has all the senses should speak with the voice of the lord.

sanskrit: tvaṃ liṃgarūpī bhagavāñjagatāmabhayapradaḥ | viṣṇunā saṃstuto devo liṃgarūpī maheśvaraḥ || 67 || mṛtāstrātā garātsarve tasmānmṛtyuṃjaya prabho | rakṣarakṣa mahākāla tripurāṃta namostu te || 68 ||
reference: 67-69. “You are the Lord in the form of the Liṅga. You bestow protection from fear on all the worlds. All those who died on account of the poison, have been saved. Hence, O Lord, the conqueror of Mṛtyu (Death), save us, save us. O Mahākāla, the destroyer of Tripura, obeisance to you.”
baseline: You are the form of the linga the god of the gods the one who gives fear to us the deity worshipped by Lord Viṣṇu the liga the lord of the goddesses the goddess of the earth the king of the dead and the king the master of the pitchers the great king of rakshas and the great god of war in Tripura.
morphology: You are the form of the Linga the god of the universe the one who gives fear to us the lord of the world the goddess of the earth the Lord of the worlds the king of the gods Viṣṇu the deity of the linga Mahesvara the master of the dead armour and the king the great king of fire the supreme king of rakshara and the great god of war in Tripura.

sanskrit: viṣṇunā saṃstuto devo liṃgarūpī maheśvaraḥ | prādurbabhūva sāṃbo'tha bodhayanniva tānsurān || 69 ||
reference: On being eulogized by Viṣṇu, Lord Maheśvara in the form of the Liṅga appeared before them along with Aṃbā (goddess Pārvatī). He appeared to awaken (i.e. enlighten) those Suras:
baseline: Lord Viṣṇu the lord of the linga and Lord Mahesvara are known to be the manifest manifestations of the earth.
morphology: Lord Viṣṇu the lord of the gods in the form of the linga and Lord Mahesvara should be worshipped.

sanskrit: he viṣṇo he surāḥ sarva ṛṣayaḥ śrūyatāmidam | manyate'pi hi saṃsāre anitye nityatākulam || 70 || avilokayatā'tmātmanā vibudhādayaḥ | kiṃ yajñaiḥ kiṃ tapobhiśca kimudyogena karmaṇām || 71 || ekatvena pṛthaktvena kiṃcinnaiva prayojanam | yasmādbhavadbhirmilitaiḥ kṛtaṃ yatkarma duṣkaram || 72 ||
reference: 70-74. “O Viṣṇu, ye all Suras and Sages, let this be heard. Ordinary people think that the worldly existence is eternal, while it is only transitory. Thereby, they are agitated. O Devas and others, of what avail are the Yajñas, austerities and activities connected with holy rites, if one does not perceive the (Supreme) Ātman by means of (his individual Ātman)? There is no benefit therefrom, whether they are performed collectively or separately. All of you joined together and carried out a very difficult task, namely the churning of the ocean. T??? you did for the sake of getting nectar. But why was it performed after rejecting Mṛtyuñjaya and always disrespecting me? Hence all of you undoubtedly fell into the mouth of Death.
baseline: O Viṣṇu all sages should listen to the notes of the sages. It is believed to be eternal in the world. It should be explained by the spirit of the unbelievers. What are the sacrifices made by the devotees what are the penances made by them what is the work done by them by them. What is the benefit of doing these things by being separated from one another. What has been done by those who have been created by them is described as evil.
morphology: O Viṣṇu all the sages should hear the notes of the sun. It is believed to be eternal in the world. It should be explained by the spirit of the self. What should be done with sacrifices what should be performed with the penance of the heart what would be done by the self what is done with the mind and what should happen with the effort. What is the purpose of the deeds done by those who have been separated from one another.

sanskrit: tasmātsarve mṛtyumukhaṃ patitā vai na saṃśayaḥ | asmābhirnirmito devo gaṇeśaḥ kāryasiddhaye || 74 ||
reference: Lord Gaṇeśa has been created by us for the purpose of achieving success in an undertaking.
baseline: There is no doubt that the god Ganesha who created us would get the work done.
morphology: There is no doubt that the god Ganesha who created us would get the work done.

sanskrit: na namaṃti gaṇeśaṃ ca durgāṃ caiva tathāvidhām | kleśabhājo bhaviṣyati nātra kāryā vicāraṇā || 75 ||
reference: 75. Those who do not bow down to Gaṇeśa as well as Durgā of similar nature will be victims of distress. There is no doubt about this.
baseline: One should not worship Ganesha and the fort in such a way as to disturb him. The worship of the goddess would be done in the night.
morphology: One should not worship Ganesha and the fort in such a way. The worship of tribulation would be done in the night.

sanskrit: yūyaṃ sarve tvadharmiṣṭhāḥ stabdhāḥ paṃḍitamāninaḥ | kāryākāryamavijñāya kevalaṃ mānamohitāḥ || 76 ||
reference: 76. All of you are sinful and stubborn. You profess to be learned without knowing what is right and what is wrong. You are deluded by mere false prestige.
baseline: All of you who are devoted to you the learned men are known to be meritorious. You are known only for the knowledge of the work and for the enjoyment of honour.
morphology: All of you who are devoted to you who have been worshipped by the learned men who are only fond of honour for the sake of knowledge of the work.

sanskrit: prarocanaparāḥ sarve kṣudrāśceṃdrādayo vṛthā | nātmānaṃ ca prapaṃcena vetsi tvaṃ hi śacīpate || 78 ||
reference: 77-78. All of you, groups of Devas beginning with Indra, are devoted to the Vedas. All those beginning with Indra are mediocres, pleasure-seekers, praise-mongers and useless ones. O consort of Śacī (i.e. Indra), you do not understand yourself on account of delusion.
baseline: All the pretentiousness of the mind and the heart should be wasted. The spirit should not be deceived by the evil spirit.
morphology: All the preceptors and others should be given to you in vain. You should not be deceived by the evil spirit and evil spirits.

sanskrit: kṛtaḥ prayatno hi mahānamṛtārthaṃ tvayā śaṭha | aśvamedhaśatenaiva yadrājyaṃ prāptavānasi | api tacca parādhīna tanna jānāsi durmate || 79 ||
reference: 79. A great effort has been made by you for getting nectar, O rogue. You attained a kingdom by performing a hundred horse-sacrifices. Even that is under the control of your enemies now. O vicious one, you do not know that.
baseline: If you have made a great effort for the sake of that great man the king would get the same amount of wealth as the king. But if you do not subjugate him the man would die.
morphology: If you have made a great effort for the sake of that great man you will get the kingdom by the death of the horse and if you do not subjugate him he will die.

sanskrit: yairvadavākyaistvaṃ mūḍha saṃstuto'si tapasvibhiḥ | te mūḍhāsto ṣayaṃti tvāṃ tattadrāgaparāyaṇāḥ || 80 ||
reference: 80. O deluded one, you have been eulogized by ascetics through the Vedic statements (hymns). Those ascetics are fools. They propitiate you, because they are prompted by different passions.
baseline: One who is foolish should say the same thing as one who is a penitent. Those who are fools should say that. You are the king of the world.
morphology: He should be made to speak as if he were foolish. He should do asceticism. Those who are foolish should say that you are the king of the world.

sanskrit: viṣṇo tvaṃ ca pakṣapātānna jānāsi hitāhitam | kecidadhatāstvayā viṣṇo rakṣitāścaiva kecana || 81 ||
reference: 81. O Viṣṇu, on account of your partiality you do not know what is good and what is otherwise. Some persons are killed by you, O Viṣṇu, and some have been protected.
baseline: One should know that there are some people who protect Viṣṇu.
morphology: One should know that you are not a partaker of Viṣṇu. Some people who protect Viśṇu should be protected by this.

sanskrit: icchāyuktastvamatraiva sadā bālakaceṣṭitaḥ | ye'nye ca lokapāḥ sarve teṣāṃ vārtā kutastviha || 82 ||
reference: 82. You are desirous of certain things in this matter. You are always childish in your activities. Why talk of all the other Guardians of the Quarters?
baseline: The children always strive here with the will of the Lord. Who are these people and all those who are more than that?
morphology: The children always try to be here with you with the desire. All those people who are more than this are told by you.

sanskrit: anyathā hi kṛte hyarthe anyathātvaṃ bhaviṣyati | kāryasiddhirbhavedyena bhavadbhirvismṛtaṃ ca tat || 83 ||
reference: 83. If a matter is pursued in a way other than what is proper, the result is bound to be in a way other than (what is expected). You all forgot that thing whereby your efforts are crowned with success.
baseline: If not for this the other things will happen in the heart. You will be forgotten by the performance of the task.
morphology: If not for this there will be another thing in the heart. You will be surprised by the achievement of the task.

sanskrit: yenādya rakṣitāḥ sarve kālakūṭamahābhayāt | yena nīlīkṛto viṣṇuryena sarve parājitāḥ || 84 || lokā bhasmīkṛtā yena tasmādyenāpi rakṣitāḥ | tasyārccanāvidhiḥ kāryo gaṇeśasya mahātmanaḥ || 85 ||
reference: 84-85. It is he by whom all (of you) have been saved from the great fear of Kālakūṭa today. It is he by whom you have been saved from a poison by which Viṣṇu is turned blue (dark-complexioned), by which all of you were defeated and by which all the worlds have been reduced to ash. Hence, the worship of that noble-souled Gaṇeśa should be performed by you.
baseline: All those who were saved by the fire of the god Kaalakuta by the fear of the gods Viṣṇu and Nīlikruta were defeated by the people. Those who were destroyed by him would be saved by Ganesha.
morphology: All those who are saved by the fire of Kaalakuta are defeated by the fear of Viṣṇu. The people who are destroyed by him are saved. The king of Ganesha is said to have performed the ritual of the fire.

sanskrit: karmāraṃbhe tu vighneśaṃ ye nārcaṃti gaṇādhipam | kāryasiddhirna teṣāṃ vai bhavettu bhavatāṃ yathā || 86 ||
reference: 86. If at the beginning of any holy rite, people do not worship Gaṇādhipa (Gaṇeśa), they will never realize their objectives as in your own case.”
baseline: One who has not been able to perform the task should be as good as those who have done the task in the beginning.
morphology: One who has not been able to do the work should do the same as those who have done the work.

sanskrit: etanmaheśasya vaco niśamya surāsurāḥ kiṃnaracāraṇāśca | pūjāvidhānaṃ paramārthato'pi papracchurenaṃ ca tadā girīśam || 87 ||
reference: 87. On hearing these words of Maheśa, Suras, Asuras, Kinnaras and Cāraṇas asked Girīśa about the method of worship in the proper manner. FOOTNOTES AND REFERENCES:
baseline: Having said this one should worship the sun the sun and the moon. One should then worship the god Gīrīṣa and spread the word of goodness.
morphology: Having said this one should worship the sun the sun and other elements of the universe. One should then worship the god Gīrīṣa and spread the word of the supreme god.

sanskrit: maheśvara uvāca | pratipakṣe caturthyāṃ tu pūjanīyo gaṇādhipaḥ | snātvā śuklatilaiḥ śuddhaiḥ śuklapakṣe sadā nṛbhiḥ || 1 ||
reference: Maheśvara said: 1. In every fortnight Gaṇeśa should be worshipped on the fourth day. (But) in the bright half of the month a devotee, after taking bath, should worship always with white sesamum seeds.[1]
baseline: The chief priest should be worshipped on the fourth day of the month of Mahesvara. One should always bathe with the leaves of the sukula tree and clean with the sūkla leaves on the four sides.
morphology: The chief priest should be worshipped on the fourth day of the month of Mahesvara. After bathing with the leaves of sūkala and purifying them with sūkhla leaves one should always walk on the side of the sun.

sanskrit: kṛtvā cāvasyakaṃ sarvaṃ gaṇeśasyārcanakriyām | prayatnenaiva kurvīta gaṃdhamālyākṣatādibhiḥ || 2 ||
reference: 2. After finishing all necessary daily routine religious duties, the devotee should perform the worship of Gaṇeśa with great care, by means of scents, garlands, akṣatas (raw unbroken rice grains) etc.
baseline: Having done this one should worship Ganesha in all the ways. One should try to do this with the perfume of the perfumes.
morphology: Having done this one should worship Lord Ganesha in all the ways. One should try to do this with the perfume of the perfumes.

sanskrit: dhyānamādau prakartavyaṃ gaṇeśasya yathāvidhi | āgamā bahavo jātā gaṇeśasya yathā mama || 3 ||
reference: 3. At the outset, meditation on Gaṇeśa should be performed in. accordance with scriptural injunctions.
baseline: One should meditate on Ganesha in the same way as before. The next lot of Ganesha should be done as before by me.
morphology: One should meditate on Ganesha in the same way as before. One should go to Ganesha in many ways as before and as before me.

sanskrit: bahudhopāsakā yasmāttamaḥ sattvarajonvitāḥ | gaṇabhedena tānyeva nāmāni bahudhā'bhavat || 4 ||
reference: 4. As the worshippers are of various types having Tāmasa, Sāttvika and Rājasa traits, the names also (of Gaṇeśa) became many in number according to their class (characterized by a particular Guṇa).
baseline: Many worshippers are known to be virtuous. The names of those worshippers have been enumerated in the list.
morphology: The names of those worshippers are many. These are the names given to those who have attained great power. These names have become many.

sanskrit: paṃcavaktro gaṇādhyakṣo daśabāhustrilocanaḥ | kāṃtasphaṭikasaṃkāśo nīlakaṃṭho gajānanaḥ || 5 ||
reference: 5. They are as follows: Pañcavaktra (Five-faced), Gaṇādhyakṣa (Chief of the Gaṇas—Śiva’s attendants), Daśabāhu (Ten-armed), Trilocana (Three-eyed), Kāntasphaṭika-saṅkāśa (Resembling a shining crystal), Nīlakaṇṭha (Blue-throated), Gajānana (Elephant-faced).
baseline: One who is the chief of a group of five or so gods should be ten times the size of an astrallo. One who has got a lotus crystal aksāṇa a saṃkasa a nilgaṇa and gājana should be five.
morphology: One who is the chief of a group of five or so gods should have ten arms. One who has got a kanta akṣaṇa a kantaka aksha a nilgaṇa and gājāna should have five arms.

sanskrit: mukhāni tasya paṃcaiva kathayāmi yatātatham || 6 ||
reference: 6. I shall describe his five faces correctly.
baseline: The five faces of that person are said to be the same.
morphology: I shall tell the faces of five of them.

sanskrit: madhyamaṃ tu mukhaṃ gauraṃ caturdantaṃ trilocanam | śuṃḍādaṃḍamanojñaṃ ca puṣkare modakānvitam || 7 ||
reference: 7. The middle face is fair in colour with four teeth and three eyes. It is beautiful with a long trunk. In the trunk he keeps a modaka (a round piece of sweetmeat).
baseline: The middle part of the face is said to be fourfold and the third part to be threefold. The head and trunk are said to have been placed in the pond.
morphology: The middle face is said to be fourfold and the threefold face to be threefold. The head and trunk are said to have been placed in a well.

sanskrit: tathānyatpītavarṇaṃ ca nīlaṃ ca śubhalakṣaṇam | piṃgalaṃ ca tathā śubhraṃ gaṇeśasya śubhānanam || 8 ||
reference: 8. The other faces of Gaṇeśa are yellow, auspicious blue, tawny and grey. The faces are splendid and characterized by good features.
baseline: The colour blue is the auspicious colour for the worship of Ganesha. The colour pingalam is auspicious and the auspicious name of Ganesha is auspicious.
morphology: The colour blue is the auspicious colour for the worship of Ganesha. The colour pingalum is auspicious for the worshipping of Lord Ganesha.

sanskrit: tathā daśabhujeṣveva hyāyudhāni bravīmi vaḥ | pāśaṃ pasśupadme ca aṃkuśaṃ daṃtameva ca || 9 ||
reference: 9-10. I shall tell you the weapons in the ten hands (of Gaṇeśa). They are: noose, axe, lotus, goad, tusk, rosary, ploughshare, pestle, varada (mudrā—gesture) (the hand indicating bestowal of boons) and a vessel containing modakas. One should meditate that he is holding the vessel in his hand.
baseline: Similarly the arms should be made of ten cubits and the arms of brahmins should be of five cubits each. The wings should be placed on the left side of the head and the tips on the right side of it.
morphology: In the same way the arms should be ten cubits long and the brahmins should be three cubits wide and the wings should be five cubits.

sanskrit: laṃbodara virūpākṣaṃ nivītaṃ mekhalānvitam | yogāsane copaviṣṭaṃ caṃdralekhāṃ kaśekharam || 11 ||
reference: 11-14. The meditation is of three types. In Sāttvika meditation contemplate thus: (He is) Laṃbodara (Pot-bellied). Virūpākṣa (of uneven eyes = three-eyed), Nivīta (sacred thread worn like a garland). He is having a girdle. He is seated in the Yogic posture; the crescent-moon adorns his head.
baseline: The circumambulation is done with the lumbuḍara virupuksha and the chowk should be placed in the yogic posture with the crescent stone.
morphology: A lotus should be placed in the middle of the circle and the chandralakṣa should be kept in the yoga posture.

sanskrit: caturbhujaṃ trinayanamekadaṃtaṃ mahodaram | pāśāṃkuśadharaṃ devaṃ daṃtamodakapātrakam || 13 ||
reference: Rājasa meditation is as in the case of men. The deity has pure golden complexion. (He is) elephant-faced and super-natural. He has four hands, three eyes, one tusk and huge belly.
baseline: The four cubits are the three parts of the mākhādaṇa. The māhādāra is the pāśaṇa and kuṣḍhara. The deva is the ivory and the potar.
morphology: The four elements are the three main ones. One is the great one. The other is the elephant the elephant and the god. The ivory and the potter.

sanskrit: nīlaṃ ca tāmasaṃ dhyānamevaṃ trividhamucyate | tataḥ pūjā prakartavyā bhavadbhiḥ śīghrameva ca || 14 ||
reference: Thus there are three types of Dhyāna. Thereafter, the worship should be begun quickly by you all.
baseline: The three forms of meditation should be blue tāmas and tāmā. Then the worship should be done by you soon.
morphology: The three forms of meditation should be blue tāmas and tāmā. Then you should offer worship as soon as possible.

sanskrit: ekaviṃśatidūrvābhirdvābhyāṃ nāmnā pṛthakpṛthak | sarvanāmabhirekaiva dīyate gaṇanāyake || 15 ||
reference: 15. Twenty-one Dūrvā grass-blades are (to be) taken. Two blades of grass are offered after uttering one name. (Thus ten names are uttered and twenty blades of grass are offered.) In the end, all the names are uttered and one blade of grass is offered to the lord of Gaṇas.
baseline: One hundred and twenty-one names should be assigned to each of them. The other name should be given to each one of them and the other to the one who has to be counted.
morphology: One hundred and twenty-one names should be assigned to each of them. The other name should be given to the leader.

sanskrit: tathaiva nāmabhirdeyā ekaviṃśatimodakāḥ | daśanāmānyahaṃ vakṣye pūjanārthaṃ pṛthakpṛthak || 16 ||
reference: 16. Similarly twenty-one modakas should be offered. I shall mention the ten names intended for worshipping separately.
baseline: In the same way there are twenty-one gods named after the god. I am considered to be ten. A separate earth for worship should be formed.
morphology: In the same way there are twenty-one gods named after the god. One should consider the ten names for worship in the form of a tree and separate earth for worship.

sanskrit: gaṇādhipa namastestu umāputrāghanāśana | vināyakeśaputroti sarvasiddhipradāyaka || 17 || ekadaṃtebhavaktreti tathā mūṣakavāhana | kumāragurave tubhyaṃ pūjanīyaḥ prayatnataḥ || 18 ||
reference: 17-18. The names are: 1. Gaṇādhipa (Lord of Gaṇas), 2. Umāputra (Son of Umā), 3. Aghanāśana (Destroyer of sins), 4. Vināyāka, 5. Īśaputra (Son of Lord Śiva), 6. Sarvasiddhipratdāyaka (Bestower of all Siddhis), 7. Ekadanta (One-tusked), 8. Ibhavaktra (Elephant-faced), 9. Mūṣakavāhana (Mouse-vehicled) and 10. Kumāraguru (The elder brother of Kumāra). At the end of every word namaste'stu (Obeisance to you) should be added. In the case of the last, the words Kumāragurave tubhyaṃ namo’stu, ‘Obeisance to you, O Kumāraguru’ should be uttered. Thus Gaṇeśa should be worshipped with care.
baseline: The chief priest of the Ganā is worshipped as the son of ūma son of Gāhāna the destroyer of all sins the one who gives victory to the sons of Viṇāṇeśa one who is the bearer of the gods the rat the caravan the lord of the lotus and the priest. One who worships you should be worshipped with effort.
morphology: The chief priest of the Ganā is worshipped as the son of ūma son of Gāhāna the destroyer of all siddhās the one who is born of Viṇeśa and the one that is born out of the spirit of the rats and the vehicle of rats. One who worships you in the lord of the lotuses should be worshipped.

sanskrit: evamuktvā surānsadyaḥ pariṣvajya ca sādaram | viṣṇuṃ guhāśayaṃ sadyo brahmāṇaṃ ca sadāśivaḥ || 19 || tirodhāna gataḥ sadyaḥ śaṃbhuḥ paramaśobhanaḥ | praṇamya śaṃbhuṃ te sarve gaṇādhyakṣārccane ratāḥ || 20 ||
reference: 19-20. After speaking thus to Suras, Sadāśiva, Śaṃbhu, the highly splendid lord, eagerly embraced Viṣṇu who abides in the cavity of heart, as well as Brahmā, and (he) immediately vanished. All of them bowed down to Śaṃbhu and then became engaged in worshipping Gaṇādhyakṣa (Gaṇeśa).
baseline: Having liberated him one should worship Viṣṇu the cave the sun the sky and the universe. Having worshipped him Śāmbhu the supreme son of Brahma who had gone to the abode of the gods and having worshipped Śabha all of them should worship him.
morphology: Having liberated the same one should worship Viṣṇu the cave the sun the sky and the universe. Having worshipped him one who has gone to the abode of the god Śambhu the supreme god of the universe should bow down to him. Having saluted him all of them should worship him.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃpūjya vidhivadgaṇādhyakṣārccane ratāḥ | upacārairanekaiśca dūrvābhiśca pṛthakpṛthak || 21 ||
reference: 21. After worshipping him in accordance with the injunctions, they became engaged in honouring him with various Upacāras (ways of service) and the Dūrvā grass blades separately.
