baseline: Then after having completed the procedure the chief priests should be sent to the temple. The treatment should be given to the poor and the poor.
morphology: Then after having completed the ritual prayers and the chief priests should be made to hear the call. One who has not been treated should be separated from the other.

sanskrit: saṃtuṣṭo hi gaṇādhyakṣo devānāṃ varado'bhavat | pradakṣiṇaṃ namaskṛtya taiḥ sarvairabhitoṣitaḥ || 22 ||
reference: 22. Gaṇeśa who was contented and delighted (by their worship) bestowed boons on Devas. They circumambulated him, bowed down to him and propitiated him.
baseline: Having satisfied ones head the chief of the army the lord of the gods is blessed. Having worshipped the circumambulation he is pleased with all.
morphology: Having satisfied the chief of the army he was blessed by the gods. Having worshipped the circumambulation he became pleased with all.

sanskrit: tamoguṇānvitāḥ sarve hyasurā nābhyapūjayan | upahāsaparāste vai devānpratyasurottamāḥ || 23 ||
reference: 23. Asuras who possessed only Tamas Guṇa did not worship Gaṇeśa.[2] The excellent Asuras were engaged in ridiculing Devas.
baseline: All those worshipping the gods should be worshipped with the garland of the navel. The same is said to be the case with the gods.
morphology: All those who worshiped the gods should be worshipped with the navel of the goddess Tāmoguṇa.

sanskrit: pūjayitvā śāṃkariṃ te punaḥ kṣīrārṇavaṃ yayuḥ | brahmā viṣṇuśca ṛṣayo devadaityāḥ surottamāḥ || 24 || maṃthānaṃ maṃdaraṃ kṛtvā rajjuṃ kṛtvātha vāsukim | mamaṃthuśca tadā devā viṣṇuṃ kṛtvātha sannidhau || 25 ||
reference: 24-25. Devas finished worshipping the son of Śaṅkara and went to the Milk Ocean once again. Brahmā, Viṣṇu, the excellent Suras, Devas, Daityas and sages made Mandara the churning rod and Vāsuki the churning rope. Keeping Viṣṇu near them, Devas began the churning.
baseline: Having worshipped the goddess Śankari they again go to the abode of Ksheera Viṣṇu the sages goddesses gods and goddesses. Having made the mantras and the rope made of water they are worshipped in the presence of the god Viśṇu.
morphology: Having worshipped the goddess Shankari they again go to Ksheera Karnava Brahma Viṣṇu Sage Deva and the goddess of the sun. Having made the mantras and the rope made of water they should be worshipped in the presence of the god Viśṇu.

sanskrit: mathyamāne tadābdhau ca nirgataścaṃdra agrataḥ | pīyūṣapūrṇaḥ sarveṣāṃ devānāṃ kāryasiddhaye || 26 ||
reference: 26. When the ocean was being churned, it was the Moon that came out at the outset,[3] for the purpose of realizing the objectives of all Devas. He was full of nectar.
baseline: One who is full of piṣuṣa should then go forth and perform the duties of all the gods.
morphology: One who is full of piṣuṣa should then proceed to the other side of the temple and perform the duties of all the gods.

sanskrit: śaunaka uvāca | arṇave kiṃ purā caṃdro nikṣiptaḥ kena suvrata | gajādikāni ratnāni kathitāni tvayā purā || 27 || etatsarvaṃ samāsena ādau kathaya me prabho | jñātvā sarve vayaṃ sūta paścādāvarṇayāmahe || 28 ||
reference: Śaunaka said: 27-29. O sage of holy rites, was the Moon formerly placed in the ocean? By whom was he placed? It was told by you formerly that the excellent gems like the elephant etc. (had been cast into the ocean). O lord, tell me all these things briefly in the beginning. After understanding these, all of us shall later describe them.
baseline: O Lord knowing all that is behind the sun we shall explain to you why the full moon has been thrown into the sky. The gems of the earth have been said to be full by you. Saying this in the same way with the words of the lord. Knowing all these things we are going to describe the back.
morphology: Having said this to the lord knowing all these things we shall explain the story behind the story.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tadvacanaṃ śrutvā sūto vākyamupādade || 29 ||
reference: On hearing their words, Sūta began his narrative:
baseline: Having heard the words of those who have spoken the same thing one should say the following words.
morphology: Having heard of them one should say the following words.

sanskrit: caṃdra āpomayo viprā atriputro guṇānvitaḥ | utpanno hyanasūyāyāṃ brahmaṇoṃ'śātsamudbhavaḥ | rudrasyāṃśāddhi durvāsā viṣṇoraṃśāttu dattakaḥ || 30 ||
reference: 30. Candra (the Moon) is watery by nature, O Brāhmaṇas. He was born as the son of Atri. He was endowed with all good qualities. He was born of Anasūya from a part of Brahmā. Durvāsas was born from a part of Rudra and Dattaka (i.e. Datta) was born from a part of Viṣṇu.
baseline: The son of the god Brahman is born in the month of Hāyānṣuya. He is blessed with a son named Chandra Apomya. The son named Brahmana is given to him in the year of Rudra. The king named Durvasa is given the title of Vishnu.
morphology: The son of the king is born to the son of a man named Chandra Apomya and is endowed with virtues. The son born to Brahman who is born in Hanasuya who has eight sons and who has been adopted by the king of the kingdom of Rudra who was born in Durbasa and who was adopted by Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: kṣīrābdhiṃ mathyamānaṃ tu dṛṣṭvā caṃdro mudānvitaḥ | kṣīrābdhirapi caṃdraṃ ca dṛṣṭvā so'pyutsuko'bhavat || 31 ||
reference: 31. On seeing the Milk Ocean being churned, Candra became delighted. On seeing the Moon, the Milk Ocean too became extremely attached to him.
baseline: Having seen the moon covered with milk one would get rid of it. Having seen that covered with water one gets rid of the moon. One would get the illusion.
morphology: Having seen that the moon is made of milk and the other parts of the body are made of water. Seeing that the other part of milk is also made of the moon one becomes a follower.

sanskrit: praviṣṭaścobhayaprītyā śrṛṇvatāṃ bho dvijottamāḥ | caṃdro hyamṛta pūrṇobhūdagrato devasannidhau || 32 ||
reference: 32. Since both of them liked each other, Candra entered the Ocean. Let this be heard, O excellent Brāhmaṇas. In front of and in the presence of Devas, Candra became filled with nectar.
baseline: Having entered and having enjoyed the earth one should worship the moon and the earth in two parts. The moon should be made full of the earth and be worshipped by the gods.
morphology: Having entered and having enjoyed the waters the moon should be placed in two parts. The sun should be made full of water and the earth should be given to the gods.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā ca kāṃtiṃ tvarito'tha caṃdro nīrājito devagaṇaistadānīm | vāditragoṣaistumulairanekairmṛdaṃgaśaṃkhaiḥ paṭahairanekaiḥ || 33 ||
reference: 33. On seeing the splendour of Candra, the Nīrājana rite (waving light around the face) was immediately performed by the groups of Devas with respect to Candra, along with the loud and tumultuous sounds of musical instruments, drums of many types and conchs.
baseline: Having seen the moon the king of the gods should be quickened. The goddess should be given a cow with a mule a cow a horse with a heart and a calf and a horse.
morphology: Having seen the moon the king of the gods should be quickened. The king should offer the goddess with the garlands of cows and horses and with the horns of the heart and arms and the king should be made to walk on the earth.

sanskrit: namaścakruśca te sarve sasurāsuradānavāḥ | tadā gargaṃ pṛcchamānā balaṃ caṃdrasya tattvataḥ || 34 ||
reference: 34. They all then bowed down to him along with Suras, Asuras and Dānavas. Then they asked Garga about the genuine inherent power of Candra.[4]
baseline: All those worshipping and worshipping are the gifts of the father mother and son. Then the gargha should be asked for strength from the principle of the moon.
morphology: All those worshipping and worshipping are the gifts of the father-in-law son-in law son of the king. Then the gargha should be worshipped as the strength of the moon.

sanskrit: gargeṇoktāstadā sarveṣāṃ balamadya vai | keṃdrasthānagatāḥ sarve bhavatāmuttamā grahāḥ || 35 || caṃdraṃ muruḥ samāyāto budhaścaiva samāgataḥ | ādityaśca tathā śukraḥ śaniraṃgārako mahān || 36 || tasmāccaṃdrabalaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ bhavatāṃ kāryasiddhaye | gomaṃtasaṃjñakonāma muhūrto'yaṃ jayapradaḥ || 37 ||
reference: 35-37. Thereupon, Garga told them, “All the Planets are powerful today. All the excellent Planets are in their central positions. (Therefore they are beneficial) to you. Guru (Jupiter) has come in conjunction with Candra (the Moon). Budha (Mercury) has also come in his contact. So also the Sun, Śukra (Venus), Śani (Saturn) and the great Planet Aṅgāraka (Mars). Hence the power and influence of Candra is very excellent for the realization of your objectives. This Muhūrta (auspicious time) named Gomanta[5] is the bestower of victory.”
baseline: Having said this all the powers should be given to you. Having come to the centre you should worship all the planets. Having worshipped the moon muru samayata Budha the inhabitants of the world should be worshipped. Having said so having worshipped Śaṇī Ranga great and having given Śāṇī and Ranga and having said Śeśṇi the best of the forces should be done. Having knowledge of the cow the muhurta the name of the king should be declared as the victory.
morphology: The king of Garagena said that all the powers should be given to him. All the planets should be placed in the centre. The moon should be worshipped in the form of the sun the moon the sun and the inhabitants of Budhha. The king should be blessed with good fortune the lord of the sky the king of the great king the god of the gods the great god of victory and the king who is known to be the best.

sanskrit: evamāśvāsitā devā gargeṇaiva mahātmanā | mamaṃthurabdhiṃ tvaritā garjamānā mahābalāḥ || 38 ||
reference: 38. At this encouraging assurance of the noble-souled Garga, the mighty Devas began to churn the ocean vigorously and roared (lustily in their eagerness).
baseline: The gods who believe in me the garghaṇas the mahātmās the great ones who hear me and make me growl the mighty ones who roar are quick to rise.
morphology: The gods who believe in me the garghaṇas the mahātmās the great ones who hear me sounding the thunderbolt the mighty ones who make me rise fast.

sanskrit: dviguṇaṃ balamāpannā mahātmāno dṛḍhavratāḥ | maheśaṃ smaramāṇāste gaṇeśaṃ ca punaḥ punaḥ || 39 ||
reference: 39. Remembering Maheśa and Gaṇeśa again and again, those noble-souled (Devas) of firm holy rites attained double strength.
baseline: The great spirits are made strong by having twice the strength. One who remembers the greatness of the Lord is called Ganesha.
morphology: The great spirits are strengthened by having twice the strength. One who remembers the greatness of the Lord is known as Ganesha.

sanskrit: nirmathyamānādudadhergarjamānācca sarvaśaḥ | nirgatā surabhiḥ sākṣāddevānāṃ kāryasiddhaye || 40 ||
reference: 40. During churning, Surabhi (divine cow) came out directly for the sake of the accomplishment of the tasks of Devas, from the ocean that was roaring with a rumbling sound on all sides.
baseline: One who has made a sacrifice for the sake of the cause of the gods should be able to do all things. One who gives a sacrifice should be successful in the performance of the duties of the deities by the voice of the manifestation.
morphology: One who has built a temple who has made a sacrifice and who has created a temple and who is worshipped by the gods in the form of a voice should be able to accomplish the task of the gods.

sanskrit: tuṣṭā kapilavarṇāṃ sā ūdhobhāreṇa bhūyasā | taraṃgopari gacchaṃtī śanakaiḥ śanakaistataḥ || 41 ||
reference: 41. Tawny in colour and with quite heavy udders, the cow, in a contented mood, came very slowly floating over the waves.
baseline: He should wear the colour of Kapila with the garland of a bull and go on the wave with the cow.
morphology: He goes on the wave with the bulls and the bull is made to look like him.

sanskrit: kāmadhenuṃ samāyāṃtīṃ dṛṣṭvā sarve surāsurāḥ | puṣpavarṣeṇa mahatā vavarṣuramitaprabhām || 42 ||
reference: 42. On seeing Kāmadhenu (Wish-yielding Cow) coming up, all Suras and Asuras showered flowers on that (cow) of unmeasured splendour.
baseline: Having seen the beauty of the sun all the suns are beautiful. The rain of flowers is great and the rain of rain is great.
morphology: Having seen the beauty and beauty of Kaṇḍhādheṇa all the suns are great. One who is blessed with the rain of flowers the great rain and the mighty lord of the earth.

sanskrit: tadā tūryāṇyanekāni nedurvādyānyanekaśaḥ | ānītā jalamadhyācca saṃvṛtā gośatairapi || 43 ||
reference: 43. Various kinds of trumpets and musical instruments were played and drums were beaten. She was brought from the middle of the. waters (though) surrounded by hundreds of cows.
baseline: Then there should be a lot of offerings made to the people of the region. The water should be brought in the middle of the river and the cows should be offered.
morphology: Then there should be a lot of offerings made to the people of the region. Then they should be brought to the middle of the water. They should also be offered to the cows.

sanskrit: tāsu nīlāśca kṛṣṇaśca kapilāśca kapiṃjalāḥ | babhravaḥ śyāmakā raktā jaṃbūvarṇāśca piṃgalāḥ | ābhiryuktā tadā gobhiḥ surabhiḥ pratyadṛśyata || 44 ||
reference: 44. Among them there were cows of various colours such as blue, black, tawny, partridge-coloured, smoke-coloured, dark-coloured, red ones, wooḍ-apple-coloured and reddish-brown ones. Surabhi was seen accompanied by these cows.
baseline: Then blue black white red yellow pink purple pink and pink are the colours of the kapis. Then the cow and its horns are made to appear in the sky.
morphology: Then the blue black black and white kapilas are made to look like a mirror. The brats are black red jumbo pink and pingal. Then the cow is made to sound like a trumpet.

sanskrit: asurāsurasaṃvītāṃ kāmadhenuṃ yayācire | ṛṣayo harṣasaṃyuktā devāndaityāṃśca tatkṣaṇāt || 45 ||
reference: 45. Sages who were delighted instantly entreated Devas and Asuras (to give to them) Kāmadhenu which was closely surrounded by them (Devas and Asuras).
baseline: One should immediately worship the gods of the sages asuras samsvatis kāmādhanas yāyaciris rīṣis hāsākṣaṇa and others.
morphology: One who has the desire to have the peace of the demons and the gods should immediately go to Yāyācira. The sage should be pleased with the combination of the two gods.

sanskrit: sarvebhyaścaiva viprebhyo nānāgotrebhya eva ca | surabhīsahitā gāvo dātavyā nātra saṃśayaḥ || 46 ||
reference: 46. “These cows aloṇg with Surabhi should be given to all Brāhmaṇas belonging to various Gotras. There is no doubt about it.”
baseline: All the inhabitants of the country should be given a cow with the horns. There is no doubt about it.
morphology: All the inhabitants of the country should be given cows with the horns. There is no doubt about it.

sanskrit: tairyācitāste'tra surāsurāśca daduśca tā gāḥ śivatoṣaṇāya | taiḥ svīkṛtāstā ṛṣibhiḥ sumaṃgalairmahātmabhiḥ puṇyatamaiḥ surabhyaḥ || 47 ||
reference: 47. On being requested by them, Suras and Asuras gave those cows to them in order to gratify Śiva. Those Surabhis (cows) were accepted by the noble-minded sages of great auspiciousness and excessive merit.
baseline: When it is prepared the cow should be offered to Lord Śiva and the elephant should be given to the sages the sage the meritorious and the virtuous.
morphology: When the sun is ready the cow should be offered to Lord Śiva and the elephant should be given to him. These should be accepted by the sages the saints the spirits and the virtuous.

sanskrit: puṇyāhaṃ munibhiḥ sarvaiḥ kāritāste tadā surāḥ | devānāṃ kāryasiddhyarthamasurāṇāṃ kṣayāya ca || 48 ||
reference: 48. Then Puṇyāhavācana[6] (the formal religious declaration ‘This is an auspicious day’) was performed for Suras by all those sages in order to enable Devas to achieve their objects and to cause the destruction of Asuras.
baseline: The virtuous deeds are done by the sages and all. Then the deeds of the gods should be accomplished. The deeds should be done for the destruction of the sage.
morphology: The virtuous man should be worshipped by all sages. Then the duties of the gods should be fulfilled by the meritorious men and their deeds should be destroyed.

sanskrit: punaḥ sarve susaṃrabdhā mamaṃthuḥ kṣīrasāgaram | mathyamānāttadā tasmādudadheśca tathā'bhavat || 49 || kalpavṛkṣaḥ pārijātaścūtaḥ saṃtānakastathā | tāndrumānekataḥ kṛtvā gandharvanagaropamān | mamaṃthurugraṃ tvaritāḥ punaḥ kṣīrārṇavaṃ budhā || 50 ||
reference: 49-50. All of them once again exerted themselves very well and churned the Milk Ocean. From the ocean that was being churned rose up Kalpavṛkṣa, Pārijāta, Cūta and Santānaka. They set apart those trees on one side, like the city of Gandharvas. Immediately those wise (Suras and Asuras) resumed the churning of the Milk Ocean powerfully in all earnestness.
baseline: Then the sea of milk should be made ready for me. Then the same thing happened to me. The kalpa tree should be removed and the children should be taken out of the forest. Having removed the trees from the river they should be sent back to Gandharva and the city. Then again the ksheera should be brought back to me by me.
morphology: Then the sea of milk should be made ready for me. Then the same thing happened in the middle of the sea. The kalpa tree should be removed and the children should be brought back from the land of Parijata. Then they should be sent back to Gandharva and the city of Gandhara. Then again the ksheera should be taken away from me.

sanskrit: nirmathyamānādudadherabhavatsūryavarcasam | ratnānāmuttamaṃ ratnaṃ kaustubhākhyaṃ mahāprabham || 51 ||
reference: 51. From the ocean that was being churned emerged a highly refulgent, extremely bright, most excellent gem having the brilliance of the Sun. It was called Kaustubha.
baseline: One who has built a temple of the same name would be blessed with the best of jewels. One who does so would be the king of the great kingdom of Kaustubhaka.
morphology: One who has built a temple of the same name would be blessed with the best of jewels. One who gets the highest of gems would be called Kaustubhakha and Mahaprabhā.

sanskrit: svakīyena prakāśena bhāsayaṃtaṃ jagattrayam | ciṃtāmaṇiṃ puraskṛtya kaustubhaṃ dadṛśurhi te || 52 || sarve surā dadustaṃ vai kaustubhaṃ viṣṇave tadā | ciṃtāmaṇi tataḥ kṛtvā madhye caiva surāsurāḥ | mamaṃthuḥ punarevābdhiṃ garjaṃtaste balotkaṭāḥ || 53 || mathyamānāttatastasmāduccaiḥśravāḥ samadbhutam | babhūva aśvo ratnānāṃ punaścairāvato gajaḥ || 54 ||
reference: 52-53. With its brilliance, it illuminated the three worlds. Keeping the Cintāmaṇi (a miraculous stone) in front, they saw the Kaustubha brightening the worlds. All those Suras gave the Kaustubha to Viṣṇu. Suras and Asuras of enhanced strength lustily roared again and began to churn the ocean keeping Cintāmaṇi in the middle.
baseline: Having worshipped the goddess Kaustubha after having worshipped her with her own light the goddess of the world the cow the elephant and the elephant in the form of the jewels are worshipped. The goddess Viṣṇu is worshipped with all the hymns. Having done so the sun goddess Viśṇu the king of the cow and the goddess Višṇu are worshipping with the voice of the sun. The elephant is worshipping her with the sound of the roar and sound of gold.
morphology: Having worshipped him with the light of his own self he should worship the world and give him Kaustubha. He should worship him with all the suras. Then he would worship Viṣṇu with the same suras then he would have worshipped Sura then again with the roar of my mind and then with the sound of the ballot. The sound of these gems would be heard with the voice of the great elephant.

sanskrit: tathaiva gajaratnaṃ ca catuḥṣaṣṭyā samanvitam | gajānāṃ pāṃḍurāṇāṃ ca caturddantaṃ madānvitam || 55 || tānsarvānmadhyataḥ kṛtvā punaścaiva mamaṃthire | nirmathyamānādudadhernirgatāni bahūnyatha || 56 || madirā vijayā bhṛṃgī tathā laśunagṛṃjanāḥ | atīva unmādakaro dhattūraḥ puṣkarastathā || 57 ||
reference: 54-58. From the ocean that was being churned rose up Uccaiḥśravas, the wonderful gem of a horse, and then Airāvata, the gem of an elephant, along with sixty-four other white elephants each with four tusks and in the rut. They set apart all these in the middle and churned once again. Many precious things then arose from the ocean that was being churned, viz. the wine Vijayā, Bhṛṅgī, garlic, turnip, the poisonous and highly intoxicating Dhattūra (Datura Alba) which causes too much of madness, and Puṣkara. All these were placed on the shore of the ocean without any hurry. Again those great Asuras churned the ocean along with the excellent Suras.
baseline: In the same way the gājaratnas are composed of four sixty gās elephants pānduras and four mādaṇī. Having placed them in the middle of each of them they again reside in my temple. Many of them are made of wine vijaya bhringi lasagna and gharanjana. The most hysterical dhātura is called Pūśkara.
morphology: In the same way the gārājratnas are composed of four and sixty elements. The four parts of the elephant and the Panduras are placed in the middle of each of them and the rest of the people living in the temple are placed on the ground. The objects of the temple should be placed on a lotus. The idols of the king should be made of wine victory bhringi lustre garland and many other things. The most hysterical gods should be worshipped in the form of a puskar.

sanskrit: vadaṃti sarve kenasiddhāṃtayuktāṃ yāṃ yogamāyāṃ jñānaśaktyānvitā ye || 61 ||
reference: 59-61. As the ocean was being churned once again, that divine Lakṣmī,[7] the sole protector of the worlds, rose up from it. Those who are the knowers of Brahman call her Ānvīkṣikī (Metaphysics). Others praise her as Mūlavidyā. Some competent persons call her Brahmavidyā. Some call her Siddhi (Success), Ṛddhi (Prosperity), Ājñā (Command) and Āśā (Hope). Some Yogins call her Vaiṣṇavī. Some exponents of Māyā always engaged in Yogic practice call her Māyā. All people call her Kenasiddhāntayuktā (the one associated with Brahman—the Principle spoken of in the Kenopaniṣad). Those who are equipped with the power of knowledge call her Yogamāyā.
baseline: It is said that all those who have attained the attainment of knowledge in the practice of yoga should be endowed with the principles of kāṇa.
morphology: It is said that all those who have knowledge and power in the practice of yoga should be equipped with some principles.

sanskrit: nānāratnapradīpaiśca nīrājitamukhāṃbujām | cāruprasannavadanāṃ hāranūpūraśobhitām || 65 || mūrddhani dhriyamāṇena cchatreṇāpi virājitām | cāmarairvījyamānāṃ tāṃ gaṃgākallolalohitaiḥ || 66 || pāṃḍuraṃ gajamārūḍhāṃ stūyamānāṃ maharṣibhiḥ | suradrumapuṣpamālāṃ bibhratīṃ mallikāyutām || 67 ||
reference: 62-69. They saw Mahālakṣmī coming slowly. She was very fair, youthful and tender with the filaments of the lotus for her ornaments. She was sweetly smiling with beautiful teeth. A lady of slender shade, she had the fresh youthfulness as an adornment. Her garments and ornaments were variegated with the refulgence of many gems. Her lips were red like the Biṃba (Momordica monadelpha) fruits; the nose was very beautiful and the neck and the eyes were very splendid. She was very slender with fine waistline and splendid buttocks. The hips were large. Her lotus-like face was brilliantly illuminated by means of a number of gems that served the purpose of the lights in a Nīrājana rite for her face. Her face was fascinating and delightful. She was remarkably splendid with her necklaces and anklets. An umbrella was gorgeously held above her head. She was being fanned with chowries gently shaken by the waves of Gaṅgā. She was riding a white elephant and was being eulogized by great sages. With the ends of her hands, she held a garland of the flowers of heavenly trees along with jasmine flowers.
baseline: One should also wear a garland of four pearls a garlands of flowers a muṣa and a mukha which are made of blue colour. One should wear the garlands made of pearls and garlands and wear them with the chariots of the goddess Ganga and the garland made of gold. One who has washed them with ghee and stones would get the garb of Pandura elephant garlanded with flowers garlands with gold and ghee. One would get rid of malika.
morphology: One should also wear a garland of four pearls a garlands of flowers a muṣa and a mukha that is made of blue colour a necklace made of gold and gold and a garb of gold. One should wear the garlands made of pearls and a piece of cloth made of chariot a lotus a cow a horse a elephant a bull a sage a flower and a pearl made of sandal and water. One who has washed them should be worshipped by the great sages.

sanskrit: karāgre dhriyamāṇāṃ tāṃ dṛṣṭvā devāḥ samutsukāḥ | ālokanaparā yāvattāvattāndadṛśe hyasau || 68 || devāṃśca dānavāṃścaiva siddhacāraṇapannagān | yathā mātā svaputrāṃśca mahālakṣmīstathā satī || 69 ||
reference: On seeing her Devas were eager to look at her at close quarters. But she, Mahālakṣmī, the chaste lady, looked at Devas, Dānavas, Siddhas, Cāraṇas and Serpents in the same manner as a mother looks (affectionately) at her children.
baseline: Having seen that the goddess is wearing a garland one should worship the gods as well as the goddesses. One should observe that the gods should be worshipped as far as possible. The goddess should be worshiped as the mother and her son are worshipped by the gods living in the sanctum sanctorum. As the mother becomes the goddess of the world.
morphology: Having seen the carcass of the king one would be pleased with the gods. One would get to see the goddess as far as possible. The gods living in the kingdom of the gods and the demons would be satisfied with the virtuous conduct of the people. Just as the mother and her son would be blessed by the goddess Mahalakshmi.

sanskrit: ālokitāstathā devāstayā lakṣmyā śriyānvitāḥ | sañjātāstatkṣaṇādeva rājya lakṣaṇalakṣitāḥ | daityāste niḥśrikā jātā ye śriyā'navalokitāḥ || 70 ||
reference: 70. Devas were glanced at by that Lakṣmī. So they became prosperous instantaneously and were characterized by those indications of attainment of the kingdom. Daityas who were not glanced at by Lakṣmī became devoid of splendour (royal glory).
baseline: The gods who are worshipped by the goddess lakshmī are illuminated by it. The kingdom is immediately visible by the manifestation of the divine manifestation. The demigods who are oblivious to the manifestations of śrīya are known as Śrīyas.
morphology: The gods who have been illuminated by him are worshipped by Lakshmī. The kingdom is immediately identified with the demigods. The demons who have become oblivious to him are known as Śrīyas.

sanskrit: nirīkṣyamāṇā ca tadā mukundaṃ tamālanīlaṃ sukapolanāsam | vibhrājamānaṃ vapuṣā pareṇa śrīvatsalakṣmaṃ sadayāvalokam || 71 ||
reference: 71-72. She glanced (lovingly) at Mukunda who was blue in complexion like Tamāla (Xanthochymus pictorius), whose cheeks and nose were very handsome, who shone brilliantly with his superior person and was characterized by Śrīvatsa and looked (at everyone mercifully).
baseline: Then one should observe and observe the mukundam tamala nilgai sukapola nasa vāpuṣa pārāṇa srīvatsalāśma sādaivāya lokā.
morphology: Then one should observe the mukundam tamala nilgai sukapola nasa vapuśa pārāṇa srivatasala svatasalāma sādaivyavloka.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā tadaiva sahasā vanamālayānvitā lakṣmīrgajādavatatāra suvismayaṃtī | kaṃṭhe sasarja puruṣasya parasya viṣṇormālāṃ śriyā viracitāṃ bhramarairupetām || 72 ||
reference: On seeing him, Lakṣmī suddenly got down from her elephant with the garland of forest flowers (still in her hands). With a broad smile, she put round the neck of the Supreme Being Viṣṇu, the garland that was wreathed by Śrī herself and wherein bees swarmed together.
baseline: Then suddenly the goddess lakshmī who is in the forest and the goddess of the earth and the king of the king is surprised to see the manifestation of a man lying on the ground. The king should make a journey by making a manifestation in the temple of Viṣṇu.
morphology: Then suddenly the goddess lakshmī who is in the forest garland and who is present at the time of the fall of the king would be surprised to see the manifestation of the god Viṣṇu. The king would make a journey by making a manifestation.

sanskrit: vāmāṃgamāśritya tadā mahātmanaḥ sopāviśattatra samīkṣya tā ubhau | surāḥ sadaityā mudamāpuradbhutāṃ siddhāpsaraḥ kiṃnaracāraṇāśca || 73 ||
reference: 73. She then sat there leaning on the left side of the great Ātman. On seeing them both, Suras and Daityas experienced a wonderful joy. So also Siddhas, Apsarās (celestial damsels), Kinnaras and Cāraṇas.
baseline: Then the great man should bow down on the left side of the body and look at the feet. Both the lines should be repeated with the words śādaṭīta mudāmpura bhuṭvaṇa siddha pāsara kāṇara and kāraṇa.
morphology: The great man should then bow down on the left side of the body and look at the two sides of the feet. He should say the words sūrātī mudāmapura bhuṭva siddha pāsara kinna kārāna kīrāṇa muḍāmā mūdāmapuru vuṭātā.

sanskrit: sarveṣāmeva lokānāmaikapadyena sarvaśaḥ | harṣo mahānabhūttatra lakṣmīnārāyaṇāgame || 74 || lakṣmyā vṛto mahāviṣṇurlakṣmīstenaiva saṃvṛtā | evaṃ parasparaṃ prītyā hyavalokanatatparau || 75 ||
reference: 74. At that union of Lakṣmī and Nārāyaṇa, the delight of everyone was very great. All the worlds, all the people everywhere were simultaneously happy and joyous. 75. Mahāviṣṇu was sought and wooed by Lakṣmī. Lakṣmī was wooed by him alone. Thus through mutual love they became absorbed in looking at each other.
baseline: One should worship all the people with the same spirit. One should be pleased with the presence of lord lakshminarayanā in the form of the great goddess lakshmī one should be blessed with the manifestation of vṛṣṇu the great god lakshmana and thus one should love one another.
morphology: One should worship all the people with one accord. One should rejoice at the coming of Lakshminarayan in the form of the great goddess. One would be blessed with the manifestation of Lakshmi Vrta Maha Viṣṇu Lakshmi and others. Thus one would be pleased with another.

sanskrit: śaṃkhāśca paṭahāścaiva mṛdaṃgānakagomukhāḥ | bheryaśca jharjharīṇāṃ ca sa śabdastumulo'bhavat || 76 ||
reference: 76. The sound of the various musical instruments and drums sucḥ as Paṭahas, conchs, Mṛdaṅgas, Ānakas, Gomukhas, Bherīs and Jharjharīs was very tumultuous.
baseline: The sound of the conch and the bolt should be heard by the people living in the marshy areas and the faces of cows.
morphology: The sound of the conch and the bolt should be heard by the people living in the marshy areas and the cows.

Tata, Vitata, Ghana and Suṣira, the groups of Gandharvas and celestial damsels propitiated the all-pervading Lord Hari in every way. Gandharvas, being proficient in the art of music delighted the lord. Nārada, Tumburu and other Gandharvas and Yakṣas then sang sweetly. The groups of Suras and Siddhas served thus lord Nārāyaṇa who is in the form of the Supreme Ātman and whose enlightenment was boundless, deep and profound.
baseline: The singing of the singers should be done in the same manner as that of the sages the ghaṇas the suṣis the svaras and the hymns of the gods. The instruments should be sung in the similar manner. The gāndharvasas should be worshipped in the form of the gāṇḍharvasāsāma and the jagurna the dumburāda the Gandharva the rakshasasas and the sāgāraksha and the suṇghāsīs are worshipped as the
morphology: The singing of the singers should be done in a manner that is pleasant. These should be sung in the form of the instruments of the ghana and the sūhira. In the same way Viṣṇu should be worshipped in the spirit of the whole world with the accompaniment of the musical instruments. The gāndharvāsārasāma should be heard while singing the songs of the jagurna dumburāda gānderva vaikṣa sāṇḍharva sūkhā and sūrṣa are sung in a

sanskrit: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ prathame māheśvarakhaṇḍe kedārakhaṇḍe samudramanthanākhyāne lakṣmīprādurbhāvavarṇanaṃnāmaikādaśo'dhyāyaḥ || 11 ||
reference: Due to their negligence in worshipping Gaṇeśa, Asuras did not get the fruit (Ratnas—jewels) of their labour of churning the ocean.
baseline: One hundred and eight great gods are mentioned in the Sriskaṇḍa scripture. The first one in the Saṃhita scripture is named as Mahesvara scripture the Kedar scriptures are named as Samudra scriptures the Nākhya scriptures and the manifestations of Lakshmi.
morphology: The great goddess Lakshmi should be mentioned as one of the great goddesses in the sriskaṇḍa and the sāhāśrī scriptures in the first month of the month of Mahesvara.

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca | praṇamya paramātmānaṃ ramāyuktaṃ janārddanam | amṛtārthaṃ mamaṃthuste surāsuragaṇāḥ punaḥ || 1 ||
reference: Notes: This chapter describes how Asuras were cheated by Viṣṇu by assuming the form of an enchantress and were deprived of their share of Amṛta. Lomaśa said: 1. After bowing down to Janārdana, the Supreme Being, along with Ramā, the groups of Suras and Asuras once again churned the ocean for the sake of Nectar.
baseline: Having worshipped the Supreme Self one should be blessed with joy and happiness. One should again worship the suns form for the sake of the elixir.
morphology: Having worshipped the Supreme Self one should worship the people with joy and happiness. One should again worship the sun and the sun for the sake of the elixir.

sanskrit: udadhermathyamānācca nirgataḥ sumahāyaśāḥ | dhanvaṃtaririti khyāto yuvā mṛtyuñjayaḥ paraḥ || 2 ||
reference: 2. From the ocean that was being churned, came out a youthful person of very great fame, well-known as Dhanvantari.[1] He was the great conqueror of Mṛtyu (Death).
baseline: One who is born out of the desire for wealth should be blessed with wealth. One who becomes rich should be known as a young man who gives death.
morphology: One who is born out of the desire to be good and who is known to be rich should pay tribute to a young man who has attained death.

sanskrit: pāṇibhyāṃ pūrṇakalaśaṃ sudhāyāḥ parigṛhya vai | yāvatsarve surāḥ sarve nirīkṣaṃte manoharam || 3 ||
reference: 3-4. He held in his hands a pot filled with nectar. While all Suras were (gladly) looking at the fascinating Lord Dhanvantari, Daityas wanted to attack him in a body and snatch away the pot (of nectar) that had been held in the hands of Dhanvantari.
baseline: The full lotus of water should be taken with the purification of the sun. Every time the melody is seen by all the people it is beautiful.
morphology: Having taken the full lotus of water and the purified water it is beautiful to see the notes of the sun every year.

sanskrit: yāvattaraṃgamālābhirāvṛto'bhūdbhiṣaktamaḥ | śanaiḥ śanaiḥ samāyāto dṛṣṭo'sau vṛṣaparvaṇā || 5 ||
reference: 5. The excellent physician surrounded by a series of waves was advancing slowly when he was seen by Vṛṣaparvan.
baseline: One should observe that the ground is covered with a lotus flower and gradually become smooth. One should see the bull and the mountain. 5.
morphology: Then we see the mountain of bulls in the form of a lotus. Then gradually we see that the mountain is full of flowers.

sanskrit: karasthaḥ kalaśastasya hṛtastena balādiva | asurāśca tataḥ sarve jagarjuratibhīṣaṇam || 6 ||
reference: 6. The pot that was in his hand was forcibly taken by him (Vṛṣaparvā). Thereupon, Asuras roared in a terrific manner.
baseline: One should make the urn strong with his heart. Then all the demons should be threatened.
morphology: The urn should be made strong by the heart of the bearer. Then all the demons should be threatened.

sanskrit: kalaśaṃ sudhayā pūrṇaṃ gṛhītvā te samutsukāḥ | daityāḥ pātālamājagmustadā devā bhramānvitāḥ || 7 ||
reference: 7. Seizing and taking the pot filled with nectar, the impatient Daityas came down to Pātāla. Then Devas became confused and embarrassed.
baseline: Having taken the jar full of goodness they are full of all things. The demons and the gods are illusioned in the abyss of the earth.
morphology: Having taken the jar full of goodness they are full of all things. The demons and the gods have gone astray in the abyss of darkness.

sanskrit: anujagmuḥ susaṃnaddhā yoddhukāmāśca taiḥ saha | tadā devānsamālokya balirevamabhāṣata || 8 ||
reference: 8. They (Devas) who were well-prepared and ready for a battle, pursued them with a desire to fight. Turning towards Devas, Bali spoke thus:
baseline: Then he should worship the gods and make sacrifices with them.
morphology: Having worshipped the gods he said to them O Lord of the worlds good conduct good deeds and valiant warriors one should offer sacrifices.

sanskrit: baliruvāca | vayaṃ tu kevalaṃ devāḥ sudhayā paritoṣitāḥ | śīghrameva pragaṃtavyaṃ bhavadbhiśca surottamaiḥ || 9 ||
reference: 9. O Devas, we are contented and gratified with the nectar only. You excellent Suras do go back quickly.
baseline: We are only pleased with the goodness of the gods. You should also make your progress soon.
morphology: We are only pleased with the goodness of the gods. You should also make your progress soon.

sanskrit: triviṣṭapaṃ mudā yuktaiḥ kimasmābhiḥ prayojanam | purāsmābhiḥ kṛtaṃ maitraṃ bhavadbhiḥ svārthatatparaiḥ | adhunā viditaṃ tattu nātra kāryā vicāraṇā || 10 ||
reference: 10. Please go back to Triviṣṭapa (Heaven) joyously. Of what avail are we to you? Formerly we entered into a friendly alliance with you only because we wanted to realize our common objectives. Now it has been known to you. Do not have any doubt in it hereafter.
baseline: What good is it for us to have the three parts of the body with the māda. The māitrā made with the prāsmas is for your own benefit. Now it is known to be the work of the king.
morphology: What good is it for us to have the three parts of the body with the māda. The māitrā made with the prāsmas is for your own benefit. Now it is known to us.

sanskrit: evaṃ nirbhārtsitāstena balinā surasattamāḥ | yathāgatena mārgeṇa jagmurnārāyaṇaṃ prabhum || 11 ||
reference: 11. Thus rebuked and repulsed by Bali, those excellent Suras went back to Lord Nārāyaṇa along the path by which they had come.
baseline: Having thus been made free one should offer sacrifices to the lord as soon as possible. One should offer the jagmurnarāyāna to him by the way as may be attained.
morphology: Having thus been made free from the evil one one should offer sacrifices to the Lord as soon as possible.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā viṣṇunā sarve surā bhagnamanorathā | āśvāsitā vacobhiśca nānānunayako vidaiḥ || 12 ||
reference: 12. On meeting him, all the Suras whose desires were frustrated, were consoled by Viṣṇu with various kinds of words capable of pacifying them:
baseline: Having seen him all the spirits of Viṣṇu are broken. One who is comforted by him is called Vāccha and one who is not afraid of many things.
morphology: Having seen him all the spirits of Viṣṇu are broken. One who is comforted by him one who is blessed by him and others.

sanskrit: mā trāsaṃ kurutātrārtha ānayiṣyāmi tāṃ sudhām | evamābhāṣya bhagavānmukundo'nāthasaṃśrayaḥ || 13 || sthāpayitvā surānsarvāṃstatraiva madhusūdanaḥ | mohanīrūpamāsthāya daityanāmagrato'bhavat || 14 ||
reference: 13-14. “In this matter, do not be afraid unnecessarily. I shall bring back the nectar”, said Lord Viṣṇu, the refuge of those who are helpless. The slayer of Madhu (Viṣṇu) having asked all the Suras to stay there itself, assumed the form of a charming lady, Mohinī, and appeared before Daityas.
baseline: One should not be afraid of him and bring him back to the place of worship. Having placed him in the temple of Lord Mukundu one should seek refuge in the sun. Having said this Madhusudana became the name of the demon in the form of a goddess. One should be worshipped in the same manner.
morphology: Having said this one should not be afraid of him and bring him back to the place of worship. Having placed him in the temple of Lord Mukundo one would get the name of the demon Madhusudana. Having said that He should be worshipped as the manifestation of the form of the goddess.

sanskrit: tāvaddaityāḥ susaṃrabdhāḥ parasparamathābruvan | vivādaḥ sarvadaityānāmamṛtārthe tadā'bhavat || 15 ||
reference: 15. By that time Daityas had become highly excited and agitated. They spoke to one another (about this). For the sake of nectar, all the Daityas began arguing with one another.
baseline: Then the two men standing in front of each other got into an argument and the matter was settled for the sake of the same.
morphology: Then the discordant men of the king's house and his servants stood in peace among themselves. Then the dispute arose between them for the sake of all the gods.

sanskrit: evaṃ pravartamāne tu mohinīrūpamāśritām | dṛṣṭvā yoṣāṃ tadā daivātsarvabhūtamanoramām || 16 || vismayena samāviṣṭā babhūvustṛṣitekṣaṇāḥ | tāṃ saṃmānya tadā daityarājo baliruvāca ha || 17 ||
reference: 16-17. While this was going on, fortunately they saw a woman fascinating the minds of all living beings (who had assumed the form of Mohinī). They were struck with wonder and with covetous eyes (they staled at her). Honouring her, Bali, the king of Daityas, said:
baseline: The king of the gods should be worshipped in the form of the goddess of the earth. Seeing the goddess in this way the king should worship the goddess. The goddess should be worshiped in the presence of all the gods. The king should be adored by the king.
morphology: The king of the gods should be worshipped in this manner. Seeing the image of the goddess as enamoured the king should worship the goddess with all his glory. The king should be worshiped with great wonder.

sanskrit: baliruvāca | sudhā tvayā vibhaktavyā sarveṣāṃ gatihetave | śīghratvena mahābhāge kuruṣva vacanaṃ mama || 18 ||
reference: Bali said: 18. O highly fortunate lady, this nectar should be (properly) distributed by you, so that it can reach all. Be quick about it. Do as I request.
baseline: The sacrifice should be done with the help of the Lord. You should divide all the ways in a hurry. The great part should be divided as soon as possible.
morphology: The sacrifice should be made in the best way. You should divide all the paths. You will make a great division soon.

sanskrit: evamuktā hyuvācedaṃ smayamānā baliṃ prati | strīṇāṃ naiva ca viśvāsaḥ kartavyo hi vipaścitā || 19 ||
reference: 19. On being requested thus, she smilingly said to Bali: “Women should never be trusted by a wise man.[2]
baseline: The same is the case with the sacrifice made by a man who is free from affliction. The women should not be trusted by him.
morphology: The same is true for the sacrifice of a woman who has been made free. The women should not be confided in.

sanskrit: anṛtaṃ sāhasaṃ māyā mūrkhatvamati lobhatā | aśaucaṃ nirghṛṇatvaṃ ca strīṇāṃ doṣāḥ svabhāvajāḥ || 20 ||
reference: 20. The following are the inherent natural defects of women: Falsehood, daring, deception, foolishness, excessive greed, uncleanliness and ruthlessness.
baseline: A woman who is not brave enough to bear the burden of foolishness greed immodesty cruelty and the fault of women are inherently evil.
morphology: The evilness of women is the fault of nature. The evil conduct of men is the misfortune of foolishness the greed of men the evil of women the sin of unrighteousness and the sinfulness of men.

sanskrit: niḥsnehatvaṃ ca vijñeyaṃ dhūrtatvaṃ caiva tattvataḥ | svastrīṇāṃ caiva vijñeyā doṣā nāstyatra saṃśayaḥ || 21 ||
reference: 21. Lack of genuine affection as well as mischievous cunningness should also be known as existing in them, in fact. These defects should undoubtedly be known as existing (even) in one’s own wives.
baseline: One should know the principle of non-compliance and sly conduct. One should be able to know his wives without any doubt.
morphology: One should know the wisdom of the unkindness and the slyness of the wise in principle. One should not doubt his wives in knowledge.

sanskrit: yathaiva śvāpadānāṃ ca vṛkā hiṃsāparāyaṇāḥ | kākā yatāṃḍajānāṃ ca śvāpadānāṃ ca jaṃbukāḥ | dhūrtā tathā manuṣyāṇāṃ strījñeyā satataṃ budhaiḥ || 22 ||
reference: 22. Just as wolves among beasts of prey, crows among birds and foxes among wild animals are given to killing, so also women among human beings should always be understood by the wise as exceedingly mischievous and cunning.
baseline: In the same way the cow should be persecuted. The cow cow elephant cow and buffalo should be killed. The bull should be beaten and the women should be punished with the sword.
morphology: In the same way the cow should be persecuted by the cowherds. The cowherd should be beaten by the bullherds the coward the bullock the jumbuka the dumb and the women should be punished by the wise men.

sanskrit: mayā saha bhavadbhiśca kathaṃ sakhyaṃ pravartate | sarvathātra na vijñeyāḥ ke yūyaṃ caiva ka hyaham || 23 ||
reference: 23. How can there be friendship and alliance between me and you all. Should this not be considered? Who are you and who am I?
baseline: How can the union of you with me proceed? One does not know who you are.
morphology: How can the alliance between you and me continue? One does not know who you are.

sanskrit: tasmādbhavadbhiḥ saṃciṃtyakāryākāryavicakṣaṇaiḥ | kartavyaṃ parayā buddhyā prayātāsurasattamāḥ || 24 ||
reference: 24. Hence everything should be done by you after careful consideration with your keen intellect. Of course, you are very efficient in knowing what should be done and what should not be done, O excellent Asuras.”
baseline: One should think about the actions of the gods with the knowledge of the other. One should do these things with the wisdom of others.
morphology: One should think about the actions done by those who have experienced it. One should do these things with the wisdom of others.

sanskrit: baliruvāca | adyāmṛtaṃ ca sarveṣāṃ vibhajasva yathātatham | tvayā dattaṃ ca gṛhṇīmaḥ satyaṃsatyaṃ vadāmi te || 28 ||
reference: 27-29. “O lord, I shall follow your instructions whether they are good or bad.” Bali said: Today distribute the nectar among all in a befitting manner. We shall take what is given by you. It is true. I am speaking the truth.
baseline: The sacrifice should be divided among all those who have been killed today. As it is said I will take what you have given and tell them the truth.
morphology: The sacrifice should be divided among you as it is today. I shall tell you the truth by taking what you have given.

sanskrit: evamuktā tadā devī mohinī sarvamaṃgalā | uvācāthāsurānsarvānrocayaṃllaukikīṃ sthitim || 29 ||
reference: On being told thus, goddess Mohinī who was auspicious in every respect, spoke to all the Asuras desirous of following the conventional propriety: The Lord (i.e. Mohinī) said:
baseline: Then the goddess Mohini is liberated from all the illusions. She is said to have worshipped all the gods and goddesses and to be in the position of the world.
morphology: Then the goddess Mohini would be liberated from all the shadows and the king would be able to see all the gods and goddesses.

sanskrit: bhagavānuvāca | yūyaṃ sarve kṛtārthāśca jātā daivena kenacit | adyopāvāsasaṃyuktā amṛtasyādhivāsanam || 30 || kriyatāmasurāḥ śreṣṭhāḥ śubhecchā kiṃcidasti vaḥ | śvebhūte pāraṇaṃ kuryādvratārcanaratiśca vaḥ || 31 || nyāyopārjitavittena daśamāṃśena dhīmatā | kartavyo viniyogaśca īśaprītyarthahetave || 32 ||
reference: 30-32. By a stroke of good luck, all of you have become blessed and achieved your desired objective, O excellent Asuras. Do observe fast today and let the preliminary consecratory rite of the nectar be performed. Something is yet (to be observed) with a desire for your welfare. Tomorrow you can have the Pāraṇā (ceremonial breakfast). Your desire for observances and worships (is commendable). For the sake of propitiating Īśa, the Viniyoga (ceremonious disposal) rite should be performed by an intelligent (devotee) with a tenth part of the amount legally and justifiably earned by him.
baseline: The Lord has said All that you have done is for the sake of the gods. The abode of the immortals should be placed in the temple of Amruta with the abode for the day. The best of the deities should be worshipped in the form of a son of the god Kūrī. The king should pay tribute to the goddess Śvēbhutā the king of the cow the lord of the earth the goddess of wealth obtained by the ten parts of the land. The duties of the lord should be done in the presence of the goddess.
morphology: The Lord said All that you have done is for the sake of the gods. The abode of the immortals should be placed in the abode for the present day. The best of the virtues should be worshipped in the form of a son of a cow. The king should be blessed with ten times the amount of money obtained by the god of gold the sum of the wealth acquired by the king of kuri and the ten times that obtained by him. The duty of the lord should be done in the presence of God.

sanskrit: tatheti matvā te sarve yathoktaṃ devamāyayā | cakrustathaiva daiteyā mohitā nātikovidāḥ || 33 ||
reference: 33. Saying “So be it”, they all honoured whatever was said by Devamāyā. Deluded and not being very proficient and experienced, they did everything advised by Devamāyā.
baseline: All those who do not worship the gods should be worshipped with the same chakra as the gods. The goddess should be fond of the gods and the son of the great grandson.
morphology: All those who do not worship the gods should be worshipped with the same chakra as the gods.

sanskrit: mayāsureṇa ca tadā bhavanāni kṛtāni vai | manojñāni mahārhāṇi suprabhāṇi mahāṃti ca || 34 ||
reference: 34. Very big, fascinating, lustrous and rich mansions were built by the Asura, Maya.
baseline: Then the buildings were built by the gods of the gods. The wise men were great and the good men were excellent and great.
morphology: Then the buildings were built by the gods. The wise men were great and the noble and the mighty.

sanskrit: teṣupaviṣṭāste sarve susnātāḥ samalaṃkṛtāḥ | sthāpayitvā susaṃrabdhāḥ pūrṇaṃ kalaśamagrataḥ || 35 ||
reference: 35. They sat in those abodes after taking bath and adorning themselves befittingly. Excited much, they placed the full pot (of nectar) in front of themselves.
baseline: All the bathing bodies should be placed in the same place and the full lotus should be kept in the right place.
morphology: All the bathing vessels are placed in the same place and the pots should be made full of water.

sanskrit: rātrau jāgaraṇaṃ sarvaiḥ kṛtaṃ paramayā mudā | athoṣasi pravṛtte ca prātaḥsnānayutā bhavan || 36 ||
reference: 36. With very great joy, all of them kept vigil during the night. At dawn, they engaged themselves in taking early morning ablutions.
baseline: O king of the world you should be awake in the night by all the elements. You should bathe in the morning after having experienced the abyssus.
morphology: The night should be kept awake by all. You should bathe in the morning in the presence of the Supreme Being.

sanskrit: asurā balimukhyāśca paṃktibhūtā yatākramam | sarvamāvaśyakaṃ kṛtvā tadā pānaratā bhavan || 37 ||
reference: 37. After finishing all necessary daily routine duties, Asuras, the chief of whom was Bali, sat in rows in due order. They were eager to drink (the nectar).
baseline: One should drink water after having done all the necessary steps in the order in which the demons and sacrificial figures are lined up.
morphology: Then you should drink water after having done all the necessary steps in the order in which the demons and sacrificial figures are lined up.

sanskrit: baliśca vṛṣaparvā ca namuciḥ śaṃkha eva ca | sudaṃṣṭraścaiva saṃhlādī kālanemirvibhīṣaṇaḥ || 38 || vātāpirilvalaḥ kumbho nikumbhaḥ pracchadastathā | tathā sundopasundau ca niśumbhaḥ śumbha eva ca || 39 || mahiṣo mahiṣākṣaśca biḍālākṣaḥ pratāpavān | cikṣurākhyo mahābāhurjṛbhaṇo'tha vṛṣāsuraḥ || 40 ||
reference: 38-41. The following were the important ones among Daityas etc.: Bali, Vṛṣaparvan, Narauci, Śaṅkha, Sudaṃṣṭra, Saṃhlādī, Kālanemi, Vibhīṣaṇa, Vātāpi, Ilvala, Kuṃbha, Nikuṃbha, Pracchada, Sunda, Upasunda, Niśuṃbha, Śuṃbha, Mahiṣa, Mahiṣākṣa, the valorous Biḍālākṣa, the mighty-armed Cikṣura, Jṛṃbhaṇa, Vṛṣāsura, Vibāhu, Bāhuka, Ghora, Ghoradarśana, Rāhu and Ketu. These and many other Daityas, Dānavas and Rākṣasas sat there in due order.
baseline: The bulls bulls and conch are the same as those found in the city of Sunda the king of Sāṇhalāśtra the god of war the goddess of war and the king the kālaṇe of the sea the great king of the vaṭapirilva kingdom the potter of fire the pitcher the mace the sage of the sun the lion of the bull the elephant of the cow the tiger of the great mountain the demon of Vṛṣuśura the lord of the sky the mighty
morphology: The bull bull cow and conch are the same as in the case of a cow. One who lives in the country of the sun one who is living in the region of the sea one living in a forest one having the vaata pīrīlva kālaṇe kumbha nikumbha etc. One should be covered with the beautiful flowers one with the moustache the moss the bull the lion the king of the bulls the great king the lord of the cow the god of the sky the demon

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tu koṭisaṃkhyānāṃ daityānāṃ paṃktirāsthitā || 42 || tatastayā tadā devyā amṛtārthaṃ hi vai dvijāḥ | yajjātaṃ tacchṛṇaudhvaṃ hi tayā devyā kṛtaṃ mahat || 43 ||
reference: 42-43. There were rows and rows of those Daityas numbering crores and crores. Now, O Brāhmaṇas, listen to what happened thereafter and what great things were done by that goddess in the matter regarding (the distribution of) the nectar.
baseline: Then the goddess should worship the elves in the same way for the sake of the elixir. The sacrifice made by the goddess is great.
morphology: Then the goddess should offer the same amount of elixir for the sake of immortality. The sacrifice made by the goddess would be great.

sanskrit: sarve vijñāpitāḥ sadyo gṛhītakalaśā tadā | śobhayā parayā yuktā sākṣātsā viṣṇumohinī || 44 || karasthena tadā devī kalaśena virājitā | śuśubhe parayā kāṃtyā jaganmaṃgalamaṃgalā || 45 ||
reference: 44-45. All were informed by her immediately (to be ready). She took up the pot. That Viśvumohinī was endowed with the greatest splendour. The goddess appeared splendid with the pot resting in her hands. The (goddess) conducive to the auspiciousness of all auspicious things in the universe shone with the greatest lustre.
baseline: All are declared to have taken the kālāśa. Then the goddess Viṣṇu should be worshipped directly with the kálāṣa and the goddess should be enlivened with a kālaṣa. The goddess should also be worshipping with the Kālasa. Then she should be mercilessly worshipped in the temple of the lord jāgānmangala.
morphology: All the objects are declared to be the objects of worship. Then the image of Viṣṇu should be placed directly on the other side of the temple with the ornamental garland. Then with the garland of garlands the goddess should be enshrined with the kalasa. The image of jagānāmangala should be made with the fragrance of the kanta.

sanskrit: pariveṣadharāḥ sarve surāste hyasurāṃtikam | āgatāstatkṣaṇādeva yatra te hyasurottamāḥ || 46 ||
reference: 46. At the very same instant, all the Suras who had halos around them, came to the place where those excellent Asuras were present.
baseline: The circumambulation of the circumambulants is said to be the sound of the sun. Then immediately they come where they are known to be.
morphology: The circumambulation of the circumambulants is said to be the sound of the sun. The moment they arrive they are said to have become sound.

sanskrit: tāndṛṣṭvā mohinī sadya uvāca pramadottamā || 47 ||
reference: 47. On seeing them, Mohinī, the most excellent one among young women, said immediately: Mohinī said:
baseline: Having seen him one should immediately say that the goddess is the supreme god.
morphology: Having seen that the goddess is now said to be the supreme goddess.

sanskrit: mohinyuvāca | ete hyatithayo jñeyā dharmmasarvasvasādhanāḥ | ebhyo deyaṃ yatāśaktyā yadi satyaṃ vaco mama | pramāṇaṃ bhavatāṃ cādya kurudhvaṃ mā vilaṃbatha || 48 ||
reference: 48. These (people) should be known as guests. They are conducive to the accomplishment of every thing virtuous. If you keep the promise given to me, something should be given to these in accordance with your capacity. You are the authority in this regard. Do everything now. Do not delay.
baseline: O king if you know these things you will get rid of them. If you give these things to me with your strength you should tell me the truth. You should prove them to me. Do not delay.
morphology: O king of the world if you know these things you will destroy them. If you tell me the truth with the same strength and knowledge do not delay.

sanskrit: pareṣāmupakāraṃ ca ye kurvaṃti svaśaktitaḥ | dhanyāste caiva vijñeyāḥ pavitrāḥ lokapālakāḥ || 49 ||
reference: 49. Those who render help to others in accordance with their capacity are blessed ones. They should be known to be very pure and protectors of the worlds.
baseline: Those who do good to others and those who are of their own strength are blessed. Those who are wise and holy are the lokpalakas.
morphology: Those who do good to others and those who are of their own strength are blessed. Those who are wise and holy are the lokpalakas.

sanskrit: tasmādvibhajanaṃ kāryaṃ mayaitasya śubhavratāḥ | devebhyaśca prayacchadhvaṃ yaddhi cātmapriyāpriyam || 51 ||
reference: 50-51. Those who endeavour only for (filling in) their belly should be known as destined to suffer. There is no doubt about this. Hence, O (friends) of auspicious rites, this should be divided by me. You give Devas whatever you like or dislike.
baseline: Then the division should be done by the gods and the good deeds should be worshipped by them. The war should be waged by the lord and the love of the soul should be desired by him.
morphology: Then the division should be done. Then the good things should be worshipped by the gods. The meritorious one should seek the victory of the soul and the beloved one.

sanskrit: ityukte vacane devyā tathā cakrurataṃ dritāḥ | āhvayāmāsurasurāḥ sarvāndevānsavāsavān || 52 ||
reference: 52. When these words were spoken by the goddess, the energetic and alert Asuras did so. The Asuras invited all Devas including Vāsava.
baseline: The goddess should say the same thing to the chakrūrta. The king of the gods asura should be called the abode of all gods.
morphology: The goddess should say the same thing to the chakrāruta. The king of the gods asura and sūrā are called to be the abode of all gods.

sanskrit: upaviṣṭāśca te sarve amṛtārthaṃ ca bho dvijāḥ | teṣūpaviśyamāneṣu hyuvāca paramaṃ vacaḥ | mohinī sarvadharmmajñā asurāṇāṃ smayanniva || 53 ||
reference: 53. All of them sat, O Brāhmaṇas, for the sake of receiving the nectar. While they were occupying their seats, Mohinī who was conversant with all holy rites and virtuous acts, smilingly said to the Asuras these great words:
baseline: All those sitting on the ground are worshipped for the sake of immortality. Those who are seen in the form of three forms are said to be supreme. The goddess of all dharmic knowledge is known as the goddess of the gods.
morphology: All those sitting on the ground are worshipped for the sake of immortality. Those who are seen as manifesting themselves are said to be supreme. The goddess Mohini is the knowledge of all dharmas and the goddess of the demons.

sanskrit: mohinyuvāca | ādau hyabhyāgatāḥ pūjyā iti vai vaidikī śrutiḥ || 54 ||
reference: Mohinī said:
baseline: One who is a devotee of the goddess is said to have worshipped the goddess.
morphology: It is said to be a devotee of the goddess Mohi who is worshipped in the past.

sanskrit: tasmādyūyaṃ vedaparāḥ sarve devaparāyaṇāḥ | bruvaṃtu tvaritenaiva ādau keṣāṃ dadāmyaham | amṛtaṃ hi mahābhāgā balimukhyā vadaṃtu bhoḥ || 55 ||
reference: 54-55. The Vedic Text prescribes that the guests should be honoured at the very outset. Hence, you who axe all devoted to the gods and the Vedas speak out immediately. So whom shall I give the nectar at the very outset? Indeed, let those whose leader is Bali, let those persons of exalted fortune say.
baseline: Then all the devotees of the Vedas should be worshipped with the same devotion. Then the Lord will give the elixir to some of them. He will say that the great god is the supreme sacrifice.
morphology: Then all the devotees of the Vedas should be worshipped with the same devotion. Then I should give the elixir to some people as soon as possible. The sacrifice of the great devotee should be said by the devotee.

sanskrit: balinoktā tadā devī yatte manasi rocate | svāminī tvaṃ na saṃdeho hyasmākaṃ suṃdarānane || 56 ||
reference: 56. Then the goddess was told by Bali. “(Do) what appeals to your mind. O lady of beautiful face, you are our mistress. There is no doubt about it.”
baseline: Then the goddess will be pleased with the sacrifice. You are the master. There is no doubt in our beautiful worship.
morphology: Then the goddess should be pleased with the sacrifice. You are the master. There is no doubt that you are beautiful.

sanskrit: evaṃ saṃmānitā tena balinā bhāvitātmanā | pariveṣaṇakāryārthaṃ kalaśaṃ gṛhya satvarā || 57 ||
reference: 57-58. On being honoured thus by that Bali of pure soul, the goddess hurriedly took up the pot for the purpose of serving.
baseline: Having thus esteemed him as a sacrificial spirit one should take the urn for the purpose of serving him.
morphology: Having thus been honored by him one should take the urn for the purpose of serving him with the spirit of sacrifice.

sanskrit: tasmānnarendrakarabhorulasaddṛkūlā śroṇītaṭālasagatirmavihvalāṃgī | sā kūjatī kanakanūpurasiṃjitena kuṃbhastanī kalaśapāṇirathāviveśa || 58 ||
reference: A silk cloth shone over her thighs resembling the trunk of a royal elephant. She walked rather slowly on account of the (huge) buttocks. Her limbs were agitated and excited due to inebriation. With the tinkling of the golden anklets, she appeared to be cooing (like a cuckoo). Her breasts resembled pitchers. With the pot (of nectar) in her hand, she entered (the place where they were seated).
baseline: Then there should be a bow made of water containing the kāṇakaṇupura water and the water of the pot with water.
morphology: Then there should be a bow made of water containing the kumbhas water and water.

sanskrit: tadā tu devī pariveṣayaṃtī sā mohinī devagaṇāya sākṣāt | vavarṣa deveṣu sudhārasaṃ punaḥ punaḥ sudhāhārarasāmṛtaṃ yathā || 59 || punaśca te devagaṇāḥ sudhārasaṃ dattaṃ tayā parayā viśvamūrtyā | balimukhyāḥ saha lokapālā gaṃdharvayakṣāpsarasāṃ gaṇāśca || 60 ||
reference: 59-60. Then the goddess Mohinī proceeded serving the group of Devas directly. She showered on Devas the juice of the nectar again and again as though their sole diet consisted of this nectar. The groups of Devas, the chief among whom was Devendra, and the groups of Gandharvas, Yakṣas and celestial damsels along with Guardians of the Quarters swallowed again and again the juice of nectar served by that great (goddess) of cosmic form.
baseline: Then the goddess should be worshipped in front of the goddess Mohini and the gods should be reawakened again and again. Then the deities should be purified. Then they should be given purification by the other gods. The gods should also be purged by the cosmic image. The people should be sacrificed with the garlands of gandhar gaṇḍa kāśāra and gāna.
morphology: Then the goddess should be worshipped by the goddess Mohini in the presence of the gods. Then the gods should be purified again and again. Then they should be given the purification of the deities. Then again the gods were purified by the image of the universe. The people should be offered the garland of the god Gandharva and the arrow of the king along with the sacrificial lotus.

sanskrit: sarve daityā āsanasthā punaśca te devagaṇāḥ sudhārasaṃ dattaṃ pīḍitāśca | tūṣṇīṃbhūtā balimukhyā dvijeṃdrā manasvino dhyānaparā babhūvuḥ || 61 ||
reference: 61. All Daityas, the chief among whom was Bali, O leading Brāhmaṇas, continued to be seated there. They were anxious and afflicted with hunger. The resolute Daityas kept quiet and were engaged in meditation.
baseline: All the demigods should be seated in the seat. Then the gods should be restored and the victim should be given the grace. Having become oblivious the mind should be meditated upon by the sacrificial lord Dwijendra.
morphology: All the demigods should be seated in the seat. Then they should be given to the gods for the purpose of improving the condition of the people and the victims. Having become weak and facing the enemy the mind should be meditated upon by Dwijendra.

sanskrit: tatastathāvidhāndṛṣṭvā daityāṃstānmohamāśritān | tadā rāhuśca ketuśca dvāvetau daityapuṃgavau || 62 || devānāṃ rūpamāsthāya amṛtārthaṃ tvarānvitau | upaviṣṭau tadā paṅktyāṃ devānāmamṛtārthinau || 63 ||
reference: 62 -63. On seeing those Daityas in such a plight after resorting to a delusion, the two leading Daityas Rāhu and Ketu assumed the forms of Devas and hurriedly sat in the row of Devas for receiving the nectar.
baseline: Having seen the image of the demigods in the same way Rahu and Ketu are worshipped in the two directions. The demigod Pungavu is said to be in a hurry for the elixir in the form of the gods. Then the gods are seated in a row and their devotees are worshipping him.
morphology: Then the gods should be seen standing in front of him. Then Rahu and Ketu should be worshipped in the two directions. Then the deities should be seated in a row in the form of the gods and the goddess should be fasted for the elixir.

sanskrit: yadāmṛtaṃ pātukāmo rāhuḥ paramadurjayaḥ | candrārkābhyāṃ prakathito viṣṇoramitatejasaḥ || 64 || tadā tasya śiraśchinnaṃ rāhordurvigrahasya ca | śivaro gaganamāpede kabaṃdhaṃ ca mahītale | bhramamāṇaṃ tadā hyadrīṃścūrṇayāmāsa vai tadā || 65 ||
reference: 64-65. The exceedingly invincible Rāhu was desirous of drinking the nectar. When this was reported to Viṣṇu of unmeasured splendour by the Sun and the Moon, the head of Rāhu of deformed body was cut off. The head went up into the sky. The headless body dropped down on the earth. Rolling down, it crushed many mountains into small particles.
baseline: When the image of Rahu is made of stone the highest form of darkness. The image of Viṣṇu is formed by the rays of the moon. Then the head of the image is cut off from the image. Then it is placed on the ground of the sky and the arms of the god Śiva. Then there is a movement of the heart.
morphology: When the image of Rahu is raised to the ground and the image is made to be of Vishnu the image that is made of the moon and the objects of the sky and the images of the gods of the universe. Then the image should be cut off from the head and the figure of Rahor the idol of the god the circle of the celestial body and the circle should be placed on the ground. The image should then be made to rotate.

sanskrit: sādriśca sarvabhūlokaścūrṇitaśca tadā'bhavat | tayā tena ca dehena cūrṇitaṃ sacarācaram || 66 || dṛṣṭvā tadā mahādevastasyopari tu saṃsthitaḥ | nivāsaḥ sarvadevānāṃ tasyāḥ pādatale'bhavat || 67 || pīḍanaṃ tatsamīpetha nivāsa iti nāma vai || 68 ||
reference: 66-68. The entire world including the mountains was reduced to fine dust. On seeing that the entire universe consisting of mobile and immobile beings was smashed to fragments by her (i.e. Mohinī) through that body (of Rāhu), Mahādeva stood above it. The abode of all Devas was at the soles of her feet. The affliction (?) was near her, hence the name Nivāsa[3] (abode) (obscure).
baseline: Then the lord of the world became full of all beings and the body was crushed by him. Seeing that the king was standing on top of him the lord became the seat of all the gods at his feet. He said that the place of torment should be situated near him.
morphology: Then the lord of the world became full of all the gods and the body was crushed by him. Seeing that the king was standing on top of him the lord became the abode of all gods at his feet. The torment is called abode near him.

sanskrit: mahatāmālayaṃ yasmādyasyāstaccaraṇāṃbujam | mahālayeti vikhyātā jagattrayavimohinī || 69 ||
reference: 69. Since her lotus-like feet had been the abode (ālaya) of great ones (mahatām), the enchantress of the three worlds became reputed as Mahālayā.
baseline: The great temple is said to be that of the king. The king of the kingdom is described as the worldly bewitch.
morphology: A great temple is said to be the most beautiful place in the world. It should be described as a great temple.

sanskrit: ketuśca dhūmarūpo'sāvākāśe vilayaṃ gataḥ | sudhāṃ samarpya caṃdrāya tirodhānagato'bhavat || 70 ||
reference: 70. Ketu vanished into the sky in the form of smoke. It was after handing over the nectar to the Moon that he vanished thus.
baseline: The image of Ketu the form of smoke has gone to the sky. Having offered the sun it has come to the moon.
morphology: The image of Ketu the form of smoke has gone to the sky. Having offered the goodness it has come to the moon.

sanskrit: vāsudevo jagadyonirjagatāṃ kāraṇaṃ param | viṣṇoḥ prasādāttajjātaṃ surāṇāṃ kāryasiddhidam || 71 ||
reference: 71. Vāsudeva is the origin of the universe. He is the supreme cause of all the worlds. It was due to Viṣṇu’s grace that everything took place favouring the realization of Devas’ objectives.
baseline: The Lord Vasudeva is the cause of the creation of the world. The offerings made by Viṣṇu and the performance of the hymns are said to be accomplished.
morphology: The Lord Vasudeva is the cause of the creation of the world. Lord Viṣṇu's offerings to the gods and the performance of the hymns is said to be the accomplishment of the task.

sanskrit: asurāṇāṃ vināśāya jātaṃ daivaviparyayāt | vinā daivena jānīdhvamudyamo hi nirarthakaḥ || 72 ||
reference: 72. Since the fate was adverse, the enterprise of Mohinī was conducive to the destruction of Asuras. Understand that all exertions without (favourable) fate are useless.
baseline: One who destroys the demons without knowing the gods would become a god. He would become meaningless without knowing God.
morphology: One who destroys the demons would become a god without knowing the gods. He would be meaningless without knowing them.

sanskrit: yaugapadyena taiḥ sarvaiḥ kṣīrābdhermaṃthanaṃ kṛtam | siddhirjātā hi devānāmasiddhirasurānprati || 73 ||
reference: 73. The churning of the ocean was conducted by all of them simultaneously. But, it ended in the success of Devas, while Asuras failed (in their objective).
baseline: The merriment of the kshetra should be done with the combination of the two elements. One who acquires perfection would be the god of happiness and prosperity.
morphology: They should be worshipped with the combination of kshetra and bhārma. The god of perfection is the one who gives to the gods amasiddhirāsura.

sanskrit: tataśca te devavarānprakopitā daityāśca māyāpravi mohitāḥ punaḥ | anekaśastrāstrayutāstadā'bhavanviṣṇau gate garjamānāstadānīm || 74 ||
reference: 74. Therefore, they were furious at the excellent Devas. Daityas who were deluded took up many weapons and missiles. When Viṣṇu went away they began to roar. FOOTNOTES AND REFERENCES: Dhanvantari: Mbh, Ādi 18.38 also states that Dhanvantari came out of ocean along with a pot of Amṛta. He is regarded as an incarnation of Viṣṇu. This divine physician Dhanvantari is different from Dhanvantari, the physician-king of Vārāṇasī. He learnt Āyurveda from sage Bharadvāja and composed a systematic work of eight parts on Āyurveda and taught it to different disciples (BdP II.3, 67.1-24).
baseline: Then the gods gods and gods were again enamoured by the divine power. The king of the kingdom of Vāṣṇu with many weapons went and roared with it.
morphology: Then again they became enamoured by the gods gods spirits gods and gods. They were again enamored by the power of Maya with many weapons and the goddess Viṣṇu went and roared at them.

sanskrit: iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ prathame māheśvarakhaṇḍe kedārakhaṃḍe samudramaṃthanākhyāne devānāmamṛtaprāśanavarṇanaṃnāma dvādaśo'dhyāyaḥ || 12 ||
reference: These traditional verses are meant for creating disaffection about Saṃsāra. Mohinī (Viṣṇu) cleverly uses them to create confidence about her in the gullible Asuras. The whole chapter shows how Mohinī cunningly appeals to the noble qualities of Asuras and cheats them.
baseline: In the same way in the scriptures of the great srīskaṇḍa a sāhāśāra is said to be one hundred and eighty thousand. In the preceptor's account the name of the god should be mentioned as twelve hundred and twelve.
morphology: In the same way in the srīskaṇḍa treatise the great men should be made to stand on one side of the sea. In the sāhita treatise on the first side of Mahesvara the name of the god should be mentioned as twelve hundred and twelve.

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca | tataste garjjamānāśca ākṣipaṃtaḥ surānraṇe | śatakratupramukhyāṃstanmahābalaparākramān || 1 || vimānamāruhya tadā mahātmā vairocaniḥ sarvabalena sārddham | daityaiḥ sameto vividhairmahābalaiḥ surānpradudrāva mahābhayāvaham || 2 ||
reference: 1-2. Then (those Asuras) roared at the Suras, the chief among whom was Indra, and whose strength and valour was great. They challenged them for a fight. The noble-souled son of Virocana got into his aerial chariot. He was accompanied by Daityas who were very powerful and who came in various (groups). With his entire army he rushed at Suras in a terrible way.
baseline: Then the sun should be raised in the sun and the roar should be heard in the sky. Then the king should be defeated by the enemy with all his might. Then he should be killed by the air force. He should be accompanied by the demons the king of the sun the mighty king and the king.
morphology: Then the sun should rise in the sky with the roar of the sun and the sunrise with the sound of the sky. The chief king should beat the enemy with all his might and the enemy should be defeated by the enemy. The king should be accompanied by the demons and the king of the mountains with all their strength.

sanskrit: svāni rūpāṇi bibhraṃtaḥ samāpetuḥ sa hasraśaḥ | kecidvyāghrānsamārūḍhā mahiṣāṃśca tathā pare || 3 ||
reference: 3. They had assumed their (original real) forms. They attacked (the enemies) in thousands. Some of them rode on tigers and others on buffaloes.
baseline: Having lost his form he would end up having to face the two tigers and the buffaloes.
morphology: Having lost his form he would end up having two horses and a buffalo.

sanskrit: mayūrānrājahaṃsāṃśca kukkuṭāṃśca tathā pare | keciddhayānsamārūḍhā uṣṭrānaśvatarānapi || 5 || gajānkharānpare caiva śakaṭāṃśca tathā pare | pādātā bahavo daityāḥ khaṅgaśaktyṛṣṭipāṇayaḥ || 6 ||
reference: 4-6. Some of them rode on horses, others on elephants; while some others rode on lions, panthers and śarabhas (eight-footed mythical animal), peacocks, royal swans, cocks, horses, elephants, camels, mules and asses. Some drove in carts. Many Daityas came on foot with swords, javelins and daggers in their hands.
baseline: The peacocks elephants dogs buffaloes monkeys etc. are placed on the other side of the mountain. Some of the horses are also placed on top of the elephant. Five of them are on the left side of them and one of them is on the right side of it. One of them has to walk on the feet of a great beast.
morphology: Both the peacocks jaguars dogs horses horses and horses are placed on the other side. Some of the horses are also placed on top of the elephant. Five of them are on the left side of the bull. Many of them have feet and arms.

sanskrit: parighāyudhinaḥ pāśaśūlamudgarapāṇayaḥ | asilomānvitāḥ kecidbhuśuṃḍīparighāyudhāḥ || 7 || hayanāgarathāścānye samārūḍhāḥ prahāriṇaḥ | vimānāni samārūḍhā balimukhyāḥ sahasraśaḥ || 8 ||
reference: 7-8. There were demons with iron bars as weapons. Others had nooses, javelins and iron clubs in their hands. Some had thin-bladed swords. Others had bhuṣuṇḍī (a sort of missile) and iron bolts as their weapons. Others came on horses, chariots and elephants and began to strike. Thousands of Asuras, the chief among whom was Bali, rode in aerial chariots.
baseline: One who is armed with a spear a spear and a sword should be armed with the axe and a muzzle. Some of the weapons should be mounted on a pole and the arms should be placed on the ground. One who carries a spear should carry a thousand pieces of fire and a bullock should be thrown into the air.
morphology: One who is armed with a spear a spear and a sword should be armed with the axe a sword a mace a bow a dart a piece of cloth a pair of horses a horse a cow a bull and a horse should be killed. One who carries a sword and a spear should be defeated by the enemy. One should be able to destroy the enemy with the weapons of war.

sanskrit: sparddhamānāstatānyonyaṃ garjaṃtaśca muhurmuhuḥ | vṛṣaparvā hyuvā cedaṃ balinaṃ daityapuṃgavam || 9 ||
reference: 9. They vied with one another roaring frequently. Vṛṣaparvan then said to Bali, the leading Daitya:
baseline: One who strikes him with the sword one who roars with it and one who is afraid of the bull a cow a bull and a cow and a bull are the sacrifices made by him.
morphology: One who strikes him with the sword one who roars with it and one who shines with the horse one with the bull and one with a bull and another with the sacrifice of a demon.

sanskrit: tvayā kṛtaṃ mahābāho iṃdreṇa saha saṃgamam | viśvāso naiva kartavyo durhṛdā ca kathaṃcana || 10 ||
reference: 10. “O mighty one, an alliance was entered into with Indra by you. One should not place too much of faith in an evil-minded person.
baseline: You have done the great thing together with Indra. You have not done the belief and the evil heart.
morphology: You have done the great thing with Indra. You have not done the belief. You do not do the evil thing with your heart.

sanskrit: ūnenāpi hi tucchena vairiṇāpi kathaṃcana | maitrī buddhimatā kāryā āpadyapi nivartate || 11 ||
reference: 11-12. By no means should one trust and enter into an alliance with a base person, even if one happens to be weak and inferior. Friendship must be formed with an intelligent person. In case of emergency (he will help one) to make the mishap ineffective.
baseline: One who does not speak to an enemy even if he does not do so would be called a friend. One would get rid of the matter even if they do not do it wisely.
morphology: One who does not speak to the enemy even if he does not do so will get rid of friendship even if the matter is of wisdom.

sanskrit: na viśvasetpūrvavirodhinā kvacitparājitāḥ smo'tha bale tvayādhunā | purāṇaduṣṭāḥ kathamadya vai punarmaṃtraṃ vikartuṃ na ca te yateran || 12 ||
reference: One must not believe in a person who has been an enemy previously. It is because of you, O Bali, that we have been defeated now! Why should those chronic rogues not try to undo what has been agreed upon?”
baseline: O king you are the one who has not believed in the past and has never been defeated by the adversary. You are now the enemy of the ancient world. They are not able to destroy the mantras again.
morphology: O king you have never been victorious by the strength of your adversaries. You have not been able to destroy the ancient enemies. They have never done so.

sanskrit: ityūcuste durādharṣā yoddhukāmā vyavasthitāḥ | dhvajaiśchatraiḥ patākaiśca raṇabhūmimamaṃḍayan || 13 ||
reference: 13. Those (sturdy Asuras) who could not be thwarted and were desirous of fighting said thus and arrayed themselves suitably. They adorned the battlefield with banners, umbrellas and flags.
