baseline: Then there should be armed men armed with the sword armed with a flag and a flag. The battle ground should be raised with eight flags.
morphology: The battle lines should be raised with the following lines armed with the flag the chariots the flag and the battlefield.

sanskrit: cāmaraiśca diśaḥ sarvā lopitaṃ ca raṇasthalam | tathā sarve surāstatra daityānprati samutsukāḥ || 14 ||
reference: 14-15. They covered all the quarters with chowries. The battlefield was completely covered up.
baseline: The direction of the chasm is all lost and the place of battle is all there. And the sun is all here for the demons.
morphology: The direction of the chasm and the place of battle are all lost. All the tunes are given to the demons therein.

sanskrit: pītvāmṛtaṃ mahābhāgā vāhānyāruhya daṃśitāḥ | gajārūḍho maheṃdropi vajrapāṇiḥ pratāpavān | sūryaścoccaiḥ śravārūḍho mṛgā rūḍhaśca candramāḥ || 15 ||
reference: Similarly all Suras were also eager to (fight with) Daityas. Those persons of exalted fortune drank the nactar, put on the coats of mail and got on their respective vehicles. Mahendra, the valorous one with vajra (thunderbolt) in his hand, rode on his elephant. The Sun was seated on Uccaiḥśravas and the Moon rode on a deer.
baseline: The king of the mighty rivers is said to have made a great sacrifice by having a great vessel and to have been beaten with a spear. He also made the king of Vajrapani proud by raising the sun sound beast deer and moon.
morphology: The king of the great rivers of the world is said to have made a great sacrifice by making a great ship of gold the king of horses the lord of the gods of the earth the prince of diamonds the sun the voice of the king the son of a man the god of the moon and the great king of kings are known to be mighty.

sanskrit: chatracāmarasaṃvītāḥ śobhitā vijayaśriyā | praṇamya viṣṇuṃ te sarva iṃdrādyā jayakāṃkṣiṇaḥ || 16 ||
reference: 16. They were equipped with umbrellas and chowries. They were rendered splendid by the martial glory born of victory. Desirous of victory, all those persons beginning with Indra bowed down to Viṣṇu.
baseline: Having worshipped Lord Viṣṇu with the chariot the chasm and the garland of victory all of them should be worshipped with the mantra of Indra and victory.
morphology: Having worshipped Viṣṇu with the chariots and the garlands adorned with flowers one should worship him with the garland of Indra and wish him victory.

sanskrit: te viṣṇunā hyanujñātā asurānprati vai ruṣā | asurāśca mahākāyā bhīmākṣā bhīmavikramāḥ || 17 || teṣāṃ boramabhūdyuddhaṃ devānāṃ dānavaiḥ saha | tumulaṃ ca mahāghoraṃ sarvabhūtabhayāvaham || 18 ||
reference: 17-18. Permitted by Viṣṇu, they angrily (rushed at) Asuras. Asuras of huge body, terrible eyes and dreadful exploits (withstood them). The fight of Devas with Dānavas was very terrible, tumultuous and exceedingly dreadful, instilling fear into all living beings.
baseline: Those are the rūsas who have been given to the demons by Viṣṇu. The demons the great ones the mighty ones and the mighty men the men of war the gods and the gods. The war between them and the demigods the war and the war of the gods the battle of the great gods and all the great things are given to them by me.
morphology: Those are the rūsas who know the nature of the gods. The great asuras are known to be known by Viṣṇu. The mighty asuras and the mighty vimāksha are known as bhiṇavikras. The war between them and the gods and the demons is known as the battle. The battle between the two gods is great. I am a great warrior and the fear of all beings.

sanskrit: śaradhārānvitaṃ sarvaṃ babhūva paramādbhutam | tataśca ṭacaṭāśabdā babhūvuśca diśodaśa || 19 ||
reference: 19-20. Arrows were continuously showered. Everything became excessively wonderful. The rough and harsh noise like Caṭacaṭā reverberated in all the ten directions.
baseline: All things that are made of water are excellent. Then the words tācāta tākā and vaṇu are said to be tenfold.
morphology: All things that are made of water are excellent. Then the words tākuta and vaṇu are said to be tenfold.

sanskrit: tato nimiṣamātreṇa śaraghātayutā bhavan | śaratomaranārācairāhatāścāpatanbhuvi || 20 || vidhyamānāstathā kecidvividhuścāparānraṇe | bhallairbhagnāśca patitā nārācaiḥ śakalīkṛtāḥ || 21 ||
reference: Within a moment, they were wounded by arrows. Struck and hurt by arrows, iron clubs, javelins and iron-tipped missiles, they fell on the ground.
baseline: Then you shall be struck with a sword with the same length as the chariot. The chariots of the king are made of gold and gold. The twenty feet are made to be worn in the same way as in the case of a cow and a cow. The four feet of a bull falling from the ground are made out of gold.
morphology: Then you shall be struck with a sword with the same length as the chariot with the sword and with the spear with a bow and a sword with twenty steps. Then there should be a lot of women falling on the ground and the slayer of the bull and the bearer of the sword should be cast into the fire.

sanskrit: kṣuraprahāritāḥ keciddaityā dānavarākṣasāḥ | śilīmukhairmāritāśca bhagnāḥ kecicca dānavāḥ || 22 ||
reference: 21-22. Even as they were being split and pierced, they split and tore others in the battle. They were shattered with Bhalla,1 arrows and smashed to pieces by Nārācas (iron-tipped arrows). Some of the Daityas, Dānavas and Rākṣasas were hit with many Kṣurapras (arrows with horseshoe-shaped tips) and they appeared to be torn with them. Some Dānavas were shattered and killed by Śilīmukhas (sharp-pointed arrows).
baseline: Some of them are killed by the razor and others by the arrow. Some of the arrows are destroyed by the stone and other objects.
morphology: Some of them were killed by the razor and others by the arrow. Some of the arrows were destroyed by the stone and other objects.

sanskrit: evaṃ bhagnaṃ dānavānāṃ ca sainyaṃ dṛṣṭvā devā garjamānāḥ samaṃtāt | hṛṣṭāḥ sarve saṃmilitvā tadānīṃ labdhvā yuddhe te jayaṃ ślāghayante || 23 ||
reference: 23. On seeing the army of Dānavas broken up thus, Devas roared and moved all round. Delighted, they assembled together and celebrated the victory they had gained.
baseline: Having thus seen the army of the demons and the gods roaring in the same way the gods gather all the enemies together and after that they get victory in the war.
morphology: Having thus seen the army of the demons broken and the gods roaring in the same way. Having gathered all the warriors together they get victory in the battle.

sanskrit: śaṃkhavāditraghoṣeṇa pūritaṃ ca jagattrayam | devānprati kṛtāmarṣā dānavāste mahābalāḥ || 24 || baliprabhṛtayaḥ sarve saṃbhrameṇotthitāḥ punaḥ | vimānaiḥ sūryasaṃkāsairanekaiśca samanvitāḥ || 25 || dvaṃdvayuddhaṃ sutumulaṃ devānāṃ dānavaiḥ saha | saṃpravṛttaṃ punaścaiva parasparajigīṣayā || 26 ||
reference: 24-26. The three worlds were filled with the sounds of conchs and musical instruments. Dānavas of great strength became furious with Devas. Bali and all the others rose up once again with great excitement. They were equipped with many aerial chariots resembling the sun. With a desire to conquer each other Devas and Dānavas engaged themselves in tumultuous duels.
baseline: The world is filled with the sound of the conch the sounding of the trumpet the voice of the gods the spirit of the demons the great gods all the sacrificial spirits the mighty ones the brahmins the celestials the suns rays the war of the two planes the battle of the sun and the enemy the fight of the universe and the war between the demigods the gods and the gods.
morphology: The world is filled with the sound of conch and the sounding of the trumpet. The demon is the great demon. All the sacrificial spirits are again stirred up by the forces of the sun and the enemy. The war between the two forces is waged by the vimana and the sun. The enemies of the gods are once again living in the circle of the universe. They are living among themselves.

sanskrit: balinā dānaveṃdreṇa maheṃdro yuyudhe tadā | tathā yamo mahābāhurnamucyā saha saṃgataḥ || 27 ||
reference: 27. Mahendra fought with Bali, the lord of Dānavas. Similarly, Yama of great and powerful arms met Namuci in combat.[1]
baseline: Then the king of the kingdom of Mahāṇḍra would fight with the demon of the sacrifice. Then he would join the great king of muṣa.
morphology: Then the king of Yama would fight with the demon king with the sacrifice. Then he would be joined with the great demon king.

sanskrit: nairṛtaḥ praghasenaiva pāśī kuṃbhena saṃgataḥ | nikuṃbhenaiva sumahadyuddhaṃ cakre sadārayaḥ || 28 ||
reference: 28. Nairṛta fought with Praghasa. Varuṇa clashed with Kuṃbha. Sadāraya (Wind-god) fought with Nikuṃbha.
baseline: One who enters the circle with the pāśi kumbha in the opposite direction would be able to fight a battle with the sādāra in the same way.
morphology: One who enters a battle with the side of the pit of the kumbha after having drawn it straight away would be able to fight the battle in the same way.

sanskrit: somena saha rāhuśca yuddhaṃ cakre sudāruṇam | rāhuṇā candradehotthamamṛtaṃ bhakṣitaṃ tadā | saṃparkādamṛsyaiva yathā rāhustathā'bhavat || 29 ||
reference: 29. Rāhu fought a very terrible combat with Soma (the Moon). The Amṛta (nectar) arising from the body of the Moon was imbibed by Rāhu. Due to the contact with nectar (another figure) like Rāhu rose up.
baseline: One who eats the food of the moon and the body together with Soma and Rahu in the cycle of war is good. Then the king should be given the gift of contact as if he had become Rahu.
morphology: Then Rahu would eat the moon and the body of the king in the cycle of war with Sōma and Rahu in the same manner as the king.

sanskrit: tāni sarvāṇi dṛṣṭāni śaṃbhunā parameṣṭhinā | āśrayo'haṃ ca sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ | asurāṇāṃ surāṇāṃ ca sarveṣāmapi vallabhaḥ || 30 || evamuktastadā rāhuḥ praṇamya śirasā śivam | maulau sthitastadā caṃdro amṛtaṃ vyasṛjadbhayāt || 31 || tena tasya hi jātāni śirāṃsi subahūnyapi | ekapadyena teṣāṃ ca srajaṃ kṛtvā manoharām | babaṃdha śaṃbhuḥ śirasi śirobhūṣaṇavatkṛtam || 32 ||
reference: 30-32. All these things were seen by Śaṃbhu, the great lord. “There is no doubt about this that I am the base and support of all living beings. I am affectionate and dear to all, Asuras as well as Suras.” On being told thus Rāhu bowed down to Śiva. The Moon stationed on his crest discharged nectar out of fear. On account of it, many such heads were produced simultaneously. Śaṃbhu made them into a beautiful garland and tied it to his head like a (decorative) head-ornament.
baseline: Having seen all these things one would find that Shambhu is the supreme god. One would doubt the existence of all beings. One should worship all the gods gods sages spirits gods and other beings. Having worshipped Rahu at the same time and worshipping him at the head of the maulu one should worship the moon the nectar the sun the sky and the sun. Having created them with the same thread one man would make them beautiful. Having tied the head with the shambhu the head would be made to bear the crown.
morphology: Having seen all these things one would find that they are made of the same material and the supreme form. One would doubt the existence of all the elements the gods the demons the spirits the sages the senses all things and all things. Having worshipped Rahu in the form of a maul one should bow down to him and worship him with the head the moon the nectar the sun and the sun. Having created them with the same thread one of them would be made beautiful. One should bind the head of Shambhu the head and the head

sanskrit: aśanātkālakūṭasya nīlakaṃṭho'bhavattadā | devānāṃ kāryasiddhyarthaṃ muṃḍamālā tathā kṛtā || 33 ||
reference: 33. By swallowing Kālakūṭa for the purpose of accomplishing the objective of Devas, he became blue-throated with a garland of skulls (thus) made.
baseline: The sapphire of the kutas of Asanatakāla should be offered. The same is done for the performance of the duties of the gods.
morphology: The garland of the sapphire tree of the kutas of Asanataka is made of blue stone. The same is done for the performance of the duties of the gods.

sanskrit: dadhāra śirasā tāṃ ca muṇḍamālāṃ maheśvaraḥ || 34 ||
reference: 34. Maheśvara wore the garland of skulls.
baseline: The head should be covered with the head and the head with the garland of the head the head of the lord Śiva.
morphology: The head should be covered with a mound and the head with a garland.

sanskrit: tayā srajā'sau śuśubhe mahātmā devādidevastripurāṃtako haraḥ | gajāsuro yena nipātito mahānathāṃdhako yena kṛtaśca cūrṇaḥ || 35 ||
reference: 35. By means of that garland shone the noble-souled Hara, the primordial lord of Devas, the destroyer of Tripura. He is the lord by whom the great demon Gaja (Elephant) was struck down and the huge (demon) Andhaka was reduced to dust.
baseline: The king who created the elephant should be worshipped as the lord of gods gods goddesses and goddesses. He who destroyed the elephant the king of the great elephant and the king who destroyed it should be punished with powder.
morphology: The king who created them the great gods goddesses gods and goddesses of the world the king who destroyed the elephant the ruler of the great elephant and the king of the king who destroyed them should be punished with powder.

sanskrit: gaṃgā dhṛtā yena śirassumadhye caṃdraṃ ca cūḍe kṛtavānbhayāpahaḥ | vedāḥ purāṇāni tathāgamāśca tathaiva nānāśrutayo'tha śāstram || 36 || jalpaṃti nānāgamabhedairmīmāṃsamānāśca bhavaṃti mūkāḥ | nānāgamārcāyamataprabhedairnirūpyamāṇo jagadekabaṃdhuḥ || 37 ||
reference: 36-37. It was Śiva by whom Gaṅgā was held in the middle of his head. He, the dispeller of fear, kept the Moon on his crest. Vedas, Purāṇas, Āgamas, different kinds of Śrutis and scriptures argue and discuss variously in accordance with difference in their respective texts. In the course of their discussion they become dumb. Śiva, the sole friend of the universe, is being investigated and described differently according to the opinion of the preceptors of different Āgamas.
baseline: One who has taken the Ganges and made the moon in the middle of the head and made it into a fire should be feared. The Vedas the Puranas and the Agamas should be mentioned in various scriptures. The jalapantis are the four different types of animals and the muṇas are the dumb ones. The brothers of the world are known to be those who carry the earth and the earth.
morphology: One who holds the Ganges in the middle of the head and the moon in the form of a fire should be afraid. The Vedas the Puranas and the Agamas should be told in different ways. The scriptures are as follows. The jalapantis the gods of the world the demons the muṇas and the gods are different.

sanskrit: śivaṃ hi nityaṃ paramātmadaivaṃ vedaikavedyaṃ paramātmadivyam | vihāya taṃ mūḍhajanāḥ pramattāḥ śivaṃ na jānaṃti parātmarūpam || 38 ||
reference: 38. Abandoning the eternal lord Śiva, the supreme spirit that could be comprehended only through the Vedas, deluded people commit blunders. They do not realize Śiva of the form of the Great Spirit.
baseline: One should always worship the supreme god Śiva in the form of a devotee in the Vedas. One should give him to the Supreme Lord without leaving him as a fool one who is superior and not as the manifestation of another.
morphology: One should always worship the supreme god Śiva in the same way as the Vedas. One should worship the Supreme Lord without leaving him as the preceptor of the world. One who does not know the nature of the universe should worship him.

sanskrit: yenaiva sṛṣṭaṃ vidhṛtaṃ ca yena yena śritaṃ yena kṛtaṃ samagram | yasyāṃśabhūtaṃ hi jagatkadācidvedāṃtavedyaḥ paramātmā śivaśca || 39 ||
reference: 39. Śiva is the Paramātmā (Supreme Soul) by whom everything is created and sustained. He pervades everything and evolves everything. The entire universe is a part of this Lord. He may, perhaps, be comprehended through the Vedānta.
baseline: Whosoever creates and destroys the universe and who hears it and who makes it complete the world and the gods of the world are the objects of the universe. Lord Śiva.
morphology: One who has heard of the creation and the destruction of the universe and who has made it whole is the creator of the world and the supreme god Śiva.

sanskrit: āḍhyo vāpi daridro vā uttamo hyadhamo'pi vā | śivabhaktirato nityaṃ śiva eva na saṃśayaḥ || 40 ||
reference: 40. A person always engaged in devotion to Śiva is undoubtedly Śiva, whether he is rich or poor, noble or base.
baseline: One should never doubt that one would always be a devotee of Lord Śiva if one is poor or good or has a heart.
morphology: One should never doubt that one would always be a devotee of Lord Śiva if one is poor or good and has a heart.

sanskrit: yo vā parakṛtāṃ pūjāṃ śivasyopari śobhitām | dṛṣṭvā saṃtoṣamāyāti dāyaṃ prāpnoti tatsamam || 41 ||
reference: 41. If a person becomes delighted on seeing the splendid worship of Śiva performed by others, he gets a gift (i.e. merit) equal to his (i.e. that of the worshipper).
baseline: One who worships another person who is worshipped by the lord Śiva and who is pleased by seeing him gets the same amount of money.
morphology: One who worships another person who is blessed with the glory of Śiva and who sees and is satisfied with that person gets the same.

sanskrit: ye dīpamālāṃ kurvaṃti kārtikyāṃ śraddhayānvitāḥ | yāvatkālaṃ prajvalaṃti dīpāste liṃgamagrataḥ | tāvadyugasahasrāṇi dātā svarge mahīyate || 42 ||
reference: 42. People should offer rows of lamps in the month of Kārttika with great faith. A devotee who offers lamps thus is honoured in heaven for as many thousands of Yugas as the number (of hours) during which those lamps burn in front of the Liṅga.[2]
baseline: Those who make a garland of lamps and worship the goddess Kartikeya light the lamp for a long time. The lamp is the linga and the gift of thousands of yugas is given to heaven.
morphology: Those who make garlands of lamps and worship the goddess Kartikeya light the lamp for a long time the linga the goddess of the universe and the giver of thousands of yugas would be blessed in heaven.

sanskrit: kausuṃbhatailasaṃyuktā dīpā dattāḥ śivālaye | dātāraste'pi kailāse modante śivasaṃnidhau || 43 ||
reference: 43. If the lamps with safflower oil are offered in the temple of Śiva, those who offer them rejoice in Kailāsa in the presence of Śiva.
baseline: A lamp made of cow dung and oil should be offered to Lord Śiva. One who gives it should also offer it to śiva in the evening.
morphology: A lamp made of cowhide and oil is offered to the lord. The donors are also offered to him in the form of a lotus.

sanskrit: atasītailasaṃyuktā dīpā dattāḥ śivālaye | te śivaṃ yāṃti saṃyuktāḥ kulānāṃ ca śatena vai || 44 ||
reference: 44. If the lamps with linseed oil are offered in the temple of Śiva, those who offer them rejoice in Kailāsa in the presence of Śiva.
baseline: A lamp made of a lotus oil is given to the lord Śiva. It is said to be the sumptuous sum of the kulas and the kula.
morphology: A lamp made of a lotus oil is given to the lord. They are said to be the joint sons of the king and his clan.

sanskrit: jñānino'pi hi jāyaṃte dīpadānaphalena hi || 45 ||
reference: 45-46. As a result of the offering of lamps, people become Jñānins (endowed with perfect knowledge).
baseline: He should be blessed with the gift of lamps and fruits.
morphology: He should also be blessed with the gift of lamps and fruits.

sanskrit: tilatailena saṃyuktā dīpā dattāḥ śivālaye | te śivaṃ yāṃti saṃyuktāḥ kulānāṃ ca śatena vai || 46 ||
reference: If the lamps with gingelly oil are offered in the temple of Śiva, they (the offerers) go to Śiva in the company of a hundred members of their family.
baseline: The lamp given to the lord Śiva is said to be the combination of the sesamum and oil. He would be the union of the two clans.
morphology: The lamp given to the lord Śiva with sesamum oil is said to be the same as that given to a hundred clans of people.

sanskrit: ghṛtāktā yaiḥ kṛtā dīpā dīpitāśca śivālaye | te yāṃti paramaṃ sthānaṃ kulalakṣasamanvitāḥ || 47 ||
reference: 47. Those by whom lamps are filled with ghee and lit in the temple of Śiva, go to the highest abode in the company of a hundred thousand members of own family.
baseline: Those with whom the ghee is made and the lamp is lit in the temple of Shiva are said to be the supreme place equal to one hundred thousand.
morphology: Those with whom the garhta is made and the lamp is lit in the temple of Shiva are said to be the supreme place.

sanskrit: karpūrāgurudhūpaiśca ye yajaṃti sadā śivam | ārārtikāṃ sakarppūrāṃ ye kurvaṃti dinedine | te prāpnuvaṃti sāyujyaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā || 48 ||
reference: 48. Those who worship Śiva always with camphor, aloe and incense and those who perform the rite of waving lights everyday along with camphor, attain Sāyujya (identity with the Divinity). There is no doubt about it.
baseline: Those who do the ritual of offering garlands garlands and garlands to Lord Śiva always and those who do it day after day are called saujya.
morphology: Those who do the ritual of offering garlands garlands and garlands to Lord Śiva always and those who make offerings to the lord of the earth day after day are called saujya.

sanskrit: ekakālaṃ dvikālaṃ vā trikālaṃ ye hyataṃdritāḥ | liṃgārcanaṃ prakurvaṃti te rudrā nātra saṃśayaḥ || 49 ||
reference: 49. Those who worship the Liṅga once, twice or thrice a day with care are Rudras (themselves). There is no doubt about it.
baseline: Those who have lost their linga for one or two or three periods are said to be in doubt. Those who do not worship the linga are called Rudra.
morphology: Those who do not worship the linga once twice or thrice are in doubt.

sanskrit: rudrākṣadhāraṇaṃ ye ca kurvaṃti śivapūjane | dāne tapasi tīrthe ca parvakāle hyataṃdritāḥ | teṣāṃ yatsukṛtaṃ sarvamanaṃtaṃ bhavati dvijāḥ || 50 ||
reference: 50. If the devotees wear Rudrākṣa beads[3] at the time of the worship of Śiva, when charitable gifts are offered, when penance is performed, in the holy spots and during festive occasions with care, their merit is infinite, O Brāhmaṇas.
baseline: Those who worship Lord Śiva by worshipping the Rudraksha are worshipped in the month of Dhanā penance pilgrimage and during the festive season. The meritorious deeds of those who have lost their hearts are done by two men.
morphology: Those who worship Lord Śiva by worshipping the Rudraksha are worshipped in the month of Dhanā penance pilgrimage and during the festive season. They are killed by the evil spirits. Their sacrifice is done by the two gods.

sanskrit: rudrākṣā ye śivenoktāstācchṛṇudhvaṃ dvijottamāḥ | ārambhaikamukhaṃ tāvadyābadvaktrāṇi ṣoḍaśa | eteṣāṃ dvau ca vijñeyau śreṣṭhau tārayituṃ dvijāḥ || 51 ||
reference: 51. Listen, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, to what Śiva has said about Rudrākṣa beads. There are Rudrākṣas with one face, two faces etc. up to sixteen faces- Among these, two should be known as the most excellent ones. O Brāhmaṇas, which redeem (devotees).
baseline: The rudraksha which are said to be the chariots of Lord Śiva should be twofold. The first one should be facing one direction and the second one would be sixteen directions. These two are known to be superior.
morphology: The rudraksha which are said to be for the protection of Shiva should be two cubits long. The first one should have one face and the second one should be sixteen cubits. These two should be known to be superior.

sanskrit: rudrākṣāṇāṃ paṃcamukhakhastathā caikamukhaḥ smṛtaḥ | ye dhārayaṃtyekamukhaṃ rudrākṣamaniśaṃ narāḥ | rudralokaṃ ca gacchaṃti modante rudrasaṃnidhau || 52 ||
reference: 52. They are the five-faced Rudrākṣa and the single-faced Rudrākṣa. Those men who always wear the single-faced Rudrākṣa, go to the world of Rudra and rejoice in the presence of Rudra.
baseline: The five faces of the Rudraksha are known as the chikmukha. Those who bear one face of the rudraksham are known to be the nāra. The rudra loka is known to go to the rudras and to be worshipped in the sun.
morphology: The five faces of the rudraksha are the five faces. The four faces of a chakra are the faces. Those who are facing one face are the heads of the rudra. Those men who are going to Rudra the world of the Rudra and those who are in the midst of Rudra are known to be the faces of Rudras.

sanskrit: japastapaḥ kriyā yogaḥ snānaṃ dānārcanādikam | kriyate yacchṛbhaṃ karmma hyanaṃtaṃ cākṣadhāraṇāt || 53 ||
reference: 53. Japa, penance, holy rites, yogic practice, holy bath, charitable gift, worship etc.—if these splendid rites are performed while wearing Rudrākṣa beads, these rites yield infinite results.
baseline: The practice of chanting the steps bathing offering prayers offering gifts etc. should be done with the help of the charioteer.
morphology: The practice of chanting the steps bathing offering food and making offerings is done by the priest. The practice is performed by the knower of the chakras.

sanskrit: śunaḥ kaṃṭhanibaddho'pi rudrākṣo yadi vartate | so'pi saṃtāritastena nātra kāryā vicāraṇā || 54 ||
reference: 54. If a Rudrākṣa bead is tied round the neck of even a dog, it will be redeemed thereby. There is no doubt about it.
baseline: If a cow is tied to the neck and the rudraksha is there it should also be placed on the head and the work should be done.
morphology: If the dog is tied to the neck and the rudraksha is there it should be removed and the work should be done by him.

sanskrit: tathā rudrākṣasaṃbaṃdhātpāpamapikṣayaṃ vrajet | evaṃ jñātvā śubhaṃ karma kāryaṃ rudrākṣabaṃdhanāt || 55 ||
reference: 55. Due to the association of the Rudrākṣa bead one’s sin will be destroyed. Knowing this one should perform auspicious rites after wearing a Rudrākṣa bead.
baseline: In the same way one would get the benefits and harm of having a rudraksha. Knowing this one would do auspicious deeds by having a Rudrakshana bandha.
morphology: In the same way one would get the benefits of having a rudraksha. Knowing this one would do auspicious work by having a Rudrakshaka bandha.

sanskrit: tripuṇḍradhāraṇaṃ yeṣāṃ vibhūtvā mantrapūtayā | te rudraloke rudrāśca bhaviṣyaṃti na saṃśayaḥ || 56 ||
reference: 56. If the devotees have Tripuṇḍra (three horizontal parallel lines on the forehead) (marked) with Vibhūti (sacred ash) sanctified by Mantras, they will undoubtedly become Rudras and (rejoice) in the world of Rudra.
baseline: Those who have been worshipped by the goddess Rudra and the goddess of the three arms should be worshipped. There is no doubt that Rudra would also be born in the world of Rudra.
morphology: Those who are worshipped after having worshipped the triptych should be worshipped in Rudrala. There is no doubt that Rudra would be worshipping in the world.

sanskrit: kapilāyāśca saṃgṛhya gomayaṃ cāṃtarikṣagam | śuṣkaṃ kṛtvātha saṃdāhyaṃ vibhūtyarthaṃ śivapriyaiḥ || 57 ||
reference: 57. The dung of a tawny-coloured cow should be gathered before it touches the ground. It must be dried and burned by the devotees of Śiva for preparing Vibhūti.
baseline: Having collected the kāpilāya and the cow one should go into space and dry it. One should worship Śiva in order to make the sandhāhya sound.
morphology: Having collected the kāpilāya and the cow one should go to the outer space and dry it up. One should worship Śiva in order to make the sandhāhya sound.

sanskrit: vibhūtīti samākhyātā sarvapāpapraṇāśinī | lalāṭeṃ'guṣṭharekhā ca ādau bhāvyā prayatnataḥ || 58 || madhyamāṃ varjayitvā tu aṃgulīkdvayena ca | evaṃ trirekhāsaṃyukto lalāṭe yasya dṛśyate | sa śaivaḥ śivavajjñeyo darśanātpāpanāśanaḥ || 59 ||
reference: 58-59. It is called Vibhūti. It destroys all sins. At the outset, a single line should be drawn carefully with the thumb on the forehead. Then, two lines should be drawn, one above and one below the previous line by means of two fingers avoiding the middle finger. If the three lines are clearly visible on the forehead, that person is a devotee of Śiva. He should be known as the destroyer of sins by (his) mere sight, like Śiva.
baseline: Having covered the face with the garland one who has committed all the sins and the stripes of the neck and the middle part of the body with the same effort with the help of two fingers one would see the garlands with the three lines of the forefinger and the saiva and the sage Śiva in the vision.
morphology: Having covered the ground with the garland the sins of all the sinners and the stripes of the knees should be removed from the centre with the help of two fingers. The one who has three fingers should be seen on the lintel. He should be worshipped by the sages of the kingdom of Śiva.

sanskrit: jaṭādharāśca ye śaivāḥ sapta paṃca tathā nava | jaṭā ye sthāpiyiṣyaṃti śaivena vidhinā yutāḥ || 60 || te śivaṃ prāpnuvaṃ tīha nātra kāryā vicāraṇā | rudrākṣadhāraṇaṃ kāryaṃ śivabhaktairviśeṣataḥ || 61 ||
reference: 60-61. Those devotees of Śiva who keep matted hair, keep five, seven or nine such clusters. Those who do so in accordance with the injunctions in Śaiva treatises, do attain Śiva. There is no doubt about this. Rudrākṣa beads should be worn particularly by Śiva’s devotees.
baseline: Those who are worshipped by the sages of jatādhara seven five nine and nine. those who are placed by a sage in the mound should be worshipped with the ritualistic yuddha. Those who get the siva would be asked to perform the duties. The worship of Rudraksha should be done by the devotees of siva.
morphology: Those who have set up the jatadharas the seven five jatas and the nine jats in the form of jaiva the mace should be kept in the same manner. They should be asked to do the work. The duties of the rudraksha are done by the devotees of the god.

sanskrit: alpena vā mahattvena pūjito vā sadāśivaḥ | kulakoṭiṃ samuddhṛtya śivena saha modate || 62 ||
reference: 62. Sadāśiva can be worshipped with a very little quantity (of materials) or with profusely rich material. The devotee redeems thereby ten million members of his family and rejoices with Śiva.
baseline: One who is worshipped with little or with great importance by the god Śāsiva would be bound with the kulakoti and would marry Śiva.
morphology: One who is worshipped with little or with great importance would be bound with the kulakoti and would marry Lord Śiva.

sanskrit: tasmācchivātparataraṃ nāsti kiṃciddvijottamāḥ | yadaivamucyate śāstre tatsarvaṃ śivakāraṇam || 63 ||
reference: 63. Hence, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, there is nothing greater than Śiva. When this is told in the scripture (it must be known that), everything has Śiva for its cause.
baseline: There is nothing better than that which has been given to you. If the scripture requires it it should be given to the cause of Śiva.
morphology: There is nothing better than that which is given to you by the Lord. If the scriptures are of the same nature it should be given to him.

sanskrit: śivo dātā hi lokānāṃ kartā caivānumoditā | śivaśaktyātmakaṃ viśvaṃ jānīdhvaṃ hi dvijottamāḥ || 64 ||
reference: 64. Indeed Śiva is the bestower of the worlds. He is the maker of the worlds. He rejoices along with (his devotees). Know, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, that the whole universe consists of both Śiva and Śakti.
baseline: The Lord Śiva is the giver of wealth. He is the doer of all beings. He should know the universe and the power of Śivā.
morphology: The Lord Śiva is the giver of wealth. He is the doer of all beings. He knows the universe. He has the power of śiva.

sanskrit: śiveti dvyakṣaraṃ nāma trāyate mahato bhayāt | tasmācchivaściṃtyatāṃ vai smaryatāṃ ca dvijottamāḥ || 65 ||
reference: 65. The two-syllabled name Śi-va saves one from very great danger. Hence, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, let Śiva be contemplated upon and remembered. The sages said:
baseline: One who writes the name with two syllables in the form of the syllable Śiva is given to him out of fear. One who does not want to do so would be given two letters.
morphology: One who invents the name with two syllables would be afraid of the great king. He would like to do so and would remember it with two letters.

sanskrit: ṛṣaya ūcuḥ | somanāthasya māhātmyaṃ jñātaṃ tasya prasādataḥ | rāhoḥ śirobhayātsarve rakṣitāḥ parameṣṭhinā || 66 || surāśceṃdrādayaścānye tasminyuddhe sudāruṇe | ata ūrdhvaṃ surāḥ sarve kimakurvata ucyatām || 67 || śivasya mahimā sarvaḥ śrutastava mukhodgataḥ | atha yuddhasya vṛttāntaḥ kathyatāṃ paramārthataḥ || 68 ||
reference: 66-68. The greatness of Somanātha has been understood. It was due to his grace that all were saved from the fear of the heads of Rāhu by Parameṣṭhin. Suras beginning with Indra and others (were saved by the lord) in that dreadful battle. Thereafter, what did all those Suras do? Let it be narrated. Everything about the greatness of Śiva as narrated by you was heard directly (while) uttered by you orally. Let the narration of the battle be made exactly as it happened.
baseline: The sage should rise up and know the greatness of Somnath by the prasadam of it. The king should be protected from the head and the head of the king by the supreme god. The suras should be kept at the same time in the battle. Then all the hymns should be uttered. The glory of Lord Śiva should be heard by everyone. The story of the battle should be told by the Supreme Lord.
morphology: The sage should rise up and make known the greatness of Somnath by offering it to him. The king should be protected from the head and the gods of the universe by the supreme gods. The chief gods should be worshipped by the lord of the sun and the king of the centre. Then all those who fight in the battle should be raised up. The glory of Lord Śiva should be revealed to all who hear him. He should narrate the story of the battle to the supreme god.

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca | yadā hi daityaiśca parājitāḥ surāḥ śambhuṃ ca sarve śaraṇaṃ prapannāḥ | śivaṃ praṇemuḥ sahasā surottamā yuddhāya sarve ca mano dadhustadā || 69 ||
reference: Lomaśa said: 69. When Suras were defeated by Daityas, all of them sought refuge in Śaṃbhu. The excellent Suras bowed down to Śiva. All of them immediately decided to fight.
baseline: When the goddess Hī is defeated all the sārāma and sāmbhu are given refuge. Suddenly the lord Śiva and the king of the sūrātas will give their heart to fight.
morphology: When the goddess Hī is defeated all the sārāma and sāmbhu are given refuge. Suddenly the lord Śiva and all the other sāṇeṇas get ready to fight the battle.

sanskrit: tathaiva daityā api yudhyamānā utsāhayuktātibalāśca sarve | devaiḥ sametāśca punaḥ punaśca yuddhaṃ pracakruḥ paramāstrayuktāḥ || 70 ||
reference: 70. Similarly, all Daityas who were very powerful and enthusiastic began to fight. Equipped with great missiles, they came into contact with Devas and fought again and again.
baseline: In the same way the demigods all those who fight with zeal and strength and those who engage in war with the gods again and again are armed with supreme weapons.
morphology: In the same way the demigods all those who fight with zeal and strength those who engage in war with the gods and those who wage war again and again and are armed with the supreme weapon.

sanskrit: evaṃ ca sarve hyasurāḥ surāśca śaktyṛṣṭiśūlaiḥ parighaiḥ paraśvadhaiḥ | jayārthinomarṣayutāḥ parasparaṃ siṃhā yathā haimavatīṃ durātyayāḥ | nihanyamānā hyasurāḥ suraistadā nānāstrayogaiḥ paramairnipetuḥ || 71 ||
reference: 71. Thus, all Suras and Asuras who were desirous of victory and who were exceedingly furious, fought with one another with javelins, swords, spears, iron bars and axes. Being struck down and hit by Suras with many great arrows and missiles combined with one another Asuras (though) indomitable fell down in the same manner as lions falling into Gaṅgā.
baseline: In the same way all the hymns suras shawls arms circles arms and arms are made of the elements of the sun. One should have a lion with the embers of victory and the emissaries together as if they were in the distance. The hymnes are made to be destroyed by the yogic forces.
morphology: In the same way all the hymns the suras the shawls the arms the circumferences the sides the horns the chariots the stripes the antlers the two horns one another as if they were a lion and the other were far away. The hymms which are destroyed are made of the yogas of the sun and other weapons.

sanskrit: cakruste sakalāmurvī māṃsaśoṇitakardamām | mahīṃ vṛkṣādrisaṃyuktāṃ sasāgaravanākarām || 72 ||
reference: 72. They made the entire earth muddy with flesh and blood. They made the entire earth including oceans, forests, mines, trees and mountains (full of blood and flesh).
baseline: The chakrūsthī is said to be the best of all animals. The kārdamā is the one who consumes all the flesh. The māhiṇa tree is the same as the sāgaravāṇakaara.
morphology: The chakrūṣta should be made of all the elements of the body and the kārdāma should be composed of the elements such as plants and water.

sanskrit: śirāṃsi ca kabandhāni kavacāni mahāṃti ca | dhvajārathāḥ patākāśca gajavājiśirāṃsi ca || 73 ||
reference: 73. Deep rivers of blood lashed and swept heads, headless bodies, great armours, flags, chariots, banners and heads of elephants and horses.
baseline: The heads the shoulders the armour the great flag the flag and the elephant and the lion are the great emblems.
morphology: The heads the shoulders the armour the great flag the flag and the elephant are the mainstays.

sanskrit: bahantyaścāpagā hyāsannadyo bhīrubhayāvahāḥ | agādhāḥ śoṇitodāśca taraṃto brahmarākṣasāḥ | tayaṃti parānbhūtapratapramatharākṣasān || 74 ||
reference: 74. These rivers instilled fear into the minds of cowards. Brahmarākṣasas crossed these bloody rivers and made the other goblins, ghosts, Pramathas and Rākṣasas cross them.
baseline: The brahmins should be made to stand on the ground with their arms and arms. The brahas should be placed on the floor with their hands covered with a lotus and their feet covered with mud. They should be raised above the earth.
morphology: One who has not been able to reach the sky would be afraid of the fearful elements of the universe. One who is not afraid of Brahman would get a lot of things. One would get the illusion of the gods and goddesses.

sanskrit: śākinīḍākinīsaṃghā yakṣiṇyo'tha sahasraśaḥ | nānākeliṣu saṃyuktāḥ parasparamudānvitāḥ || 75 ||
reference: 75. There were groups of female devils such as Śākinīs, Ḍākinīs etc. and thousands of Yakṣiṇīs. Rejoicing in the company of each other, they were engaged in various sports.
baseline: The group of goddesses should be divided into thousands of pairs. The groups should be made up of different types of animals. They should be given to each other.
morphology: The group of goddesses should be divided into thousands of pairs. The groups should be made up of different types of animals.

sanskrit: evaṃ saṃkrīḍamānāste bhūtapramatharākṣasāḥ | raṇe tasminmahāraudre devāsurasamāgame || 76 ||
reference: 76. Thus, in that highly dreadful battle Devas and Asuras clashed directly with one another. There Bhūtas, Pramathas and Rākṣasas continued their sports.
baseline: In the same way the gods and goddesses are worshipped in the temple.
morphology: In the same way the gods and demons are worshipped in the temple.

sanskrit: balinā saha devendro yuyudhe'dbhutavikramaḥ | śaktyā jaghāna deveṃdraṃ vairocaniramarṣaṇaḥ || 77 ||
reference: 77. Devendra of wonderful exploits fought with Bali. The infuriated son of Virocana (Bali) struck Devendra with a javelin.
baseline: The battle between the two gods is said to be a great achievement. The battle of the war between the king and the enemy should be fought with the strength of the enemy.
morphology: The battle between the two gods is said to be a great victory for the king of the war. The king of vairu is known to be powerful.

sanskrit: tāṃ śaktiṃ vañcayāmāsa mahendro laghuvikramaḥ | jaghāna sa baliṃ yatnāddaityeṃdraṃ parameṇa hi || 78 || vajreṇa śitadhāreṇa bāhuṃ ciccheda vikramī | gātāsurapatadbhūmau vimānātsūryasaṃnnibhāt || 79 ||
reference: 78-79. Mahendra of quick and nimble steps dodged that javelin. He struck Bali, the lord of Daityas, with great effort and force with his great thunderbolt of sharp edges The valorous (lord of Devas) cut off his (Bali’s) arms. (Thereupon) he fell down dead on the ground from his aerial chariot resembling the sun.
baseline: Having deceived that power Mahendrā is said to have made a small sacrifice. Having made a sacrifice he should offer the sacrifice to the lord of the earth and the king of the world. Having broken the arm with the diamond the king should be made to climb the ground of the sky and the sun from the sky.
morphology: Having deceived him with his strength Mahendra made a small sacrifice of the same kind. Having made a sacrifice of that kind the king of the two greats should be killed with a diamond. Having pierced the arms with a piece of water the enemy should be destroyed by the sun from the plane of the earth.

sanskrit: patitaṃ ca baliṃ dṛṣṭvā vṛṣaparvā rūpānvitaḥ | vavarṣa śaradhārābhiḥ payoda iva parvatam || 80 || maheṃdraṃ sagajaṃ caiva sahamānaṃ śitāñcharān | tadā yuddhamabhūdvoraṃ mahendravṛṣaparvaṇoḥ || 81 || nipātya vṛṣaparvāṇamiṃdraḥ parabalārdanaḥ || 82 ||
reference: 80-81. On seeing Bali fallen, Vṛṣaparvan furiously showered Mahendra and his elephant with a volley of arrows like the cloud showering a mountain. Mahendra bore the sharp arrows. Then a terrible battle ensued between Mahendra and Vṛṣaparvan.
baseline: Having seen the fall of a bull and the sacrifice of a cow a mountain is transformed into a mountain by the streams of water. Then the king of the mountains would be defeated by the forces of the mighty king. Then he would fight with the mighty men of war the mighty gods of the earth and the mighty warriors of the king. Having destroyed the bull the king would be victorious.
morphology: Having seen the sacrifice falling down the bull pigeon and the mountain are transformed into a mountain with the streams of water flowing from the spring. Then the king of the mountains and the king who had been accompanied by the cow and the horses would fight and destroy the king king of cows and king of birds. Then he would be defeated by the king.

sanskrit: tato vajreṇa mahatā dānavānavadhīdraṇe | śirasi ccheditāḥ kecitkecitkaṃdharato hatāḥ || 83 || vihvalāśca kṛtāḥ kecidiṃdreṇa kupitena ca | tathā yamena nihatā vāyunā varuṇena ca || 84 || kubereṇa hatāścānye nairṛtena tathā pare | agninā nihatāḥ kecidīśenaiva vidāritāḥ || 85 ||
reference: 82-85. Indra, the tormentor of the enemy’s army, caused Vṛṣaparvan to fall down. Then he killed Dānavas in the battle with his great thunderbolt. Some were pierced through the head. Some were hit in the neck. Some were rendered bewildered and afflicted by the furious Indra. Similarly, Dānavas were killed by Yama, Vayu and Varuṇa. Others were killed by Kubera and Nairṭta. Some were killed by Agni and torn asunder by Īśa
baseline: Then the head of a great god is killed by a diamond the head by a small stone the body of a man killed by an angry man and the body by a stone killed by the wind by a fire by fire and by fire. The other two are killed by fire fire and fire.
morphology: Then the great beast of the earth should be killed with a diamond the head of a man killed by an enemy the chief of a group of men killed by a cow the king of a cow killed by the enemy by a sword killed by fire the enemy killed by wind and war and the king killed by barons killed by burning fire and others by fire.

sanskrit: evaṃ tadā tairnihatā balīyaso mahāsurā vikramaśāninaśca | suraistu sarvaiḥ saha lokapālaiḥ śivaprasādā bhihatāstadānīm || 86 ||
reference: 86. Thus the powerful Asuras of great exploit were killed by Suras and the guardians of the worlds. It was due to the favour of Śiva that they were killed then.
baseline: Then the king of the mighty king Viṣṇu and his son Viśrama should be made to stand in the same way. He should be worshipped by the lord Śiva along with all the lokpalas.
morphology: Then the king of the mighty king Viṣṇu and his son Viṣṭramāṇu should be seated in the same position. He should be worshipped by the lord Śiva along with all the lokpalas.

sanskrit: tato mahādaityavaro durātmā sa kalānemiḥ paramāstrayuktaḥ | yayau tadānīṃ surasattamāṃstānhaṃtuṃ sadā krūramatiḥ sa ekaḥ || 87 ||
reference: 87. Then the great and excellent Daitya who was equipped with excellent missiles and weapons came in to kill the excellent Suras. The evil-minded demon who was very cruel in his heart advanced alone.
baseline: He should always be considered as a cruel person. He should then be the supreme weapon of art. He would always be a cruel man.
morphology: He should always be considered as a cruel person. He should be the supreme weapon of art. He would always be a cruel man.

sanskrit: siṃhārūḍho daṃśitaśca triśulena hi saṃyutaḥ | daityānāmarbudenaiva siṃhārūḍhena saṃvṛtaḥ || 88 ||
reference: 88. Armoured and armed with a trident, he rode on a lion surrounded by one hundred millions of Daityas, all riding on lions.
baseline: A lion is said to be armed with a sword and a sword. One who is armed with the axe of a lion is called a daitya a mārbuda.
morphology: A lion is tied to the trunk of a lion and is pierced with the trisula. He is bound with the bow of the lion and the head of the demon.

sanskrit: te siṃhā daṃśitāḥ sarve mahābalaparākramāḥ | teṣu siṃheṣu cārūḍhā mahādaityāśca tatsamāḥ || 89 ||
reference: 89. All those lions of great strength and exploit were equipped with coats of mail. The great Daityas riding on those lions were also equal to them.
baseline: All those lions who have been attacked are mighty. Among those lions four are great. The same is true for the great king.
morphology: All those lions who have been bitten by them are mighty and powerful. Among them all the four lions are great.

sanskrit: āyāṃtīṃ daityasenāṃ tāṃ sarvāṃ siṃhavibhūṣitām | kālanemiyutāṃ dṛṣṭvā devā iṃdrapurogamāḥ | bhayamājagmuratulaṃ tadā dhyānaparā bhavan || 90 ||
reference: 90. On seeing the entire army of Daityas, that was adorned by lions and led by Kālanemi, advancing, the Devas with Indra, their leader, became exceedingly frightened. Then they began to ponder.
baseline: Having seen the celestial arms of the great gods adorned with lions the gods of the past and past are worshipped by Indra. Then you will be meditated upon as if you are afraid of God.
morphology: Having seen the celestial body of the demon Śiva adorned with a lion the gods of time and space are worshipped by Indra. You should then meditate on the fear and illusion.

sanskrit: kiṃ kurmo'dya vayaṃ sarve kathaṃ jeṣyāma cādbhutam | etādṛśamasaṃkhyākamanīkaṃ siṃhasaṃvṛtam || 91 ||
reference: 91. ‘What shall we all do now? How will we conquer this wonderful and countless army surrounded by lions?’
baseline: It is wonderful how all of us get victory after knowing what to do. The number of such lions has been multiplied by four.
morphology: It is wonderful how all of us get victory by doing what we do. One such lion has got the number of lions.

sanskrit: evaṃ viciṃtyamānāste hyāgatastatra nāradaḥ | nāradena ca tatsarvaṃ purāvṛttaṃ mahattaram || 92 || kathitaṃ ca maheṃdrāya kālanemestapobalam | ajeyatvaṃ ca saṃgrāme varadānabalena tu || 93 ||
reference: 92-93. When they were thinking thus, Nārada happened to come there. The old story of Kālanemi’s power of penance was told to Mahendra by Nārada. He told him about his invincibility in battle, by virtue of the power of boons granted to him.
baseline: The king Narada is said to have achieved great success in the battle by the same means as Narada. He said that he would be able to do so by the time of the death of Indra and by the force of the gift of victory and victory in the war.
morphology: One who is so determined by the king of the kingdom of Hāgata Narada and Narada should do the same with the king. He said that he would be able to overcome the great king of Indra by force and victory in the battle.

sanskrit: viṣṇuṃ vinā vayaṃ devā aśaktā raṇamaṃḍale | jetuṃ ca sa tato viṣṇuḥ smaryatāṃ parameśvaraḥ | tamālanīlo varadaḥ sarvairvijayakāṃkṣibhiḥ || 94 ||
reference: 94. “O Devas, we are not competent to conquer (this army) in the battle ground without Viṣṇu’s help. Hence, let the great lord Viṣṇu, the lord dark in complexion like the Tamāla leaves, the bestower of boons, be remembered by (all of you) desirous of conquest.”
baseline: Without Viṣṇu we are the gods. He should be worshipped in the kingdom of Rāna. Then Viśṇu should be remembered by the Supreme Lord. The golden vardā should be given to all those desirous of victory.
morphology: Without Viṣṇu we are the gods. He should be worshipped in the kingdom of Rāna. Then Viśṇu should be remembered by the Supreme Lord. The vardā should be made blue with tamala and varda with all the desires of victory.

sanskrit: nāradasya vacaḥ śrutvā tadā devāstvarānvitāḥ | dhyānena ca mahāviṣṇuṃ tataḥ parabalārddanam | smaraṃtaḥ paramātmānamidamūcuśca taṃ vibhum || 95 ||
reference: 95. On hearing the words of Nārada, Devas hurriedly meditated on Mahāviṣṇu, the tormentor of the enemy’s army, the Supreme Soul. Remembering the lord, they prayed to him thus: Devas said:
baseline: Then the gods heard the words of Narada and worshipped him. Then after meditating on him they worshipped Lord Viṣṇu. Then they worshiped him with great force. Then the supreme spirit and the mind should be worshipped.
morphology: Then the gods heard the voice of Narada and worshipped him. Then they worshipped Lord Viṣṇu with meditation and then worshipped the supreme god. The mind should be made aware of him and the mind of the supreme soul.

sanskrit: devā ūcuḥ | namastubhyaṃ bhagavate namaste viśvamaṃgalam | śrīnivāsa namastubhyaṃ śrīpate te namonamaḥ || 96 ||
reference: 96. Obeisance to you, the lord, the cause of the auspiciousness of the universe. O Śrīnivāsa (Abode of Śrī), obeisance to you. O Śrīpati (Consort of Goddess Lakṣmī), obeisance, obeisance to you.
baseline: O Lord you are worshipped. Namaste to you Lord. Namaskar to you lord of the universe. O Lord Śrīṇava you are saluted. You are salutations to me.
morphology: The gods are high. Namaste to you. Namaskar to you Lord of the universe. You are worshipped by Śrīñavas. They worship you.

sanskrit: adyāsmānbhayabhītāṃstvaṃ kālanemibhayārditān | trātumarhasi daityācca devānāmabhayaprada || 97 ||
reference: 97. Today we are exceedingly frightened. We are oppressed by the fear of Kālanemi. It behoves you, O lord, the bestower of freedom from fear to Devas, to save us from the Daitya.
baseline: One who fears the gods would be afraid of them. One who gives a gift would be fearful of God.
morphology: One who fears the gods of the world would be afraid of them even today.

sanskrit: evaṃ dhyātaḥ saṃsmṛtaśca prādurbhūto haristadā | nīlo garuḍamāruhya jagatāmabhayapradaḥ || 98 ||
reference: 98. On being meditated and remembered thus, the dark-complexioned Hari, the bestower of freedom from fear to all the worlds, appeared before them riding on Garuḍa.
baseline: One who worships and remembers in this way and who is present in the world becomes a Hari a blue cow and gives fear to the world.
morphology: One who is thus worshipped and remembered would be defeated by the rising of the blue bull and the fear of the world.

sanskrit: cakrapāṇistadāyāto devānāṃ vijayāya ca | gaganasthaṃ mahāviṣṇuṃ garuḍopari saṃsthitam | śrīvāsamenaṃ durddharṣaṃ yoddhukāmaṃ dadarśire || 99 ||
reference: 99. The lord with the discus in his hand came there for the victory of Devas. They all saw Mahāviṣṇu seated on Garuḍa and stationed in the firmament, the invincible lord Śrīvāsa (the resort of Śrī) who was desirous of fighting.
baseline: One who gives the wheel water and water to the gods for their victory one who is standing on the garuda in the sky and the great vishnu is worshipped as Śrīvāsa. One who is a strong warrior should be worshipped in the temple.
morphology: One who gives the wheel water and water to the gods for victory one who is standing on the Garuda in the sky and the great Vishnu is standing above. One who is a strong warrior should be worshipped as Śrīvāsa.

sanskrit: tathā dṛṣṭvā kālanemistadānīṃ prahasyamāno'tiruṣā balānvitaḥ | kastvaṃ mahābhāga vareṇyarūpaḥ śyāmo yuvā vāraṇamattavikramaḥ | kare gṛhītaṃ niśitaṃ mahāprabhaṃ cakraṃ ca kasmātkathayasva me prabho || 100 ||
reference: 100. On seeing the lord like that, Kālanemi who was very mighty and highly infuriated, said laughingly (loudly): “Who are you, O exalted one of great fortune? You are excellent in form and features. You are young and dark-complexioned and possess the valour of an elephant in rut. A sharp-edged brilliant discus is held by you in your hand. Why? Let me know, O Lord.”
baseline: Having seen the same thing the king said that he would be able to reach the time. The king would be powerful in the form of a great man a man of great stature a young man of good form a warrior a king of great size a great king and a man who had achieved great success by doing so.
morphology: Having seen the same thing the king said that he would be able to destroy the forces of the enemy. The king should say that he has got the great part of the army and the great form of the mighty army the young man the warrior the mighty king the great king and the wheel of the war.

sanskrit: śrībhagavānuvāca | yuddhārthamiha cāyāto devānāṃ kāryasiddhaye | tvaṃ sthiro bhava re maṃda dahāmyadya na saṃśayaḥ || 101 ||
reference: The Lord said: 101. I came here for the purpose of fighting, for the fulfilment of the cause of Devas. Be steady, O stupid one, I shall undoubtedly burn you now.
baseline: O lord of the gods you have said this tea for the purpose of war. You are stable. You should not doubt that you will be able to fight the enemy.
morphology: The Lord said to me This tea is for the purpose of war. You are stable. You should not doubt that you will be able to slow down the fire.

sanskrit: śrutvā bhagavato vākyaṃ kālanemiḥ pratāpavān | uvāca ruṣito bhūtvā bhagavaṃtamadhokṣajam || 102 ||
reference: 102. On hearing the words of the Lord, the valorous Kālanemi became angry and said to lord Adhokṣaja (Viṣṇu):
baseline: Having heard the words of the Lord he became proud of the name of the time. Having said this the Lord should be worshipped.
morphology: Having heard the words of the Lord he became the supreme ruler of the kingdom. Having become the king he becomes the master of the lord.

sanskrit: mūlabhūto hi devānāṃ bhagavānyuddhadurmadaḥ | yuddhaṃ kuru mayā sārddhaṃ yadi śūro'si saṃprati || 103 ||
reference: 103. “You are the lord and root-cause of Devas. You are highly proud of your ability to fight. If you are a brave warrior, fight with me now.”
baseline: O Lord of the gods fight with me and fight against evil. If you fight with Me you will be the enemy.
morphology: O Lord of the gods fight with me and fight against evil. If you fight with Me you will be victorious.

sanskrit: prahasya bhagavānviṣṇuruvācedaṃ mahāprabhaḥ | gaganastho bhava tvaṃ hi mahīstho'haṃ bhavāmi vai || 104 || apraśastaṃ ca viṣamaṃ yuddhaṃ caiva yathā bhavet | tathā kuru mahābāho gagano vā mahītale || 105 ||
reference: 104-107. Lord Mahāviṣṇu of great lustre laughed and said: “Either you be stationed in the sky, or I shall be stationed on the earth. O mighty one, fight either in the sky or on the ground, so that the battle will not be on uneven planes and blameworthy.”
baseline: O lord of the universe Viṣṇu the king of the great king you are standing in the sky. You are standing here in my sky I am standing here and you are sitting here. May the battle be fought between you and me. Do the same to me.
morphology: O lord of the universe Viṣṇu the king of the sky you are the great lord. You are the king. I am the king and you are me. May the battle be fought between the king the great king or the mighty king of heaven.

sanskrit: tatheti matvā hi mahānubhāvo daityaiḥ sameto'rbudasaṃkhyakaiśca | siṃhoparisthaiśca mahānubhāvairmahābalaiḥ krūrataraistadānīm || 106 || gaganamatha jagāhe maṃdamaṃdaṃ mahātmā hyasuragaṇasameto viśvarūpaṃ jighāṃsuḥ | triśikhamaparamugraṃ gṛhya saṃdeśaceṣṭādaśanavikṛtavaktro yoddhukāmo hariṃ saḥ || 107 ||
reference: Saying “So be it” the Daitya of great mangificence, surrounded by one hundred million Daityas who were dignified and glorious and seated on lions, who were powerful and ruthless, rose up in the sky slowly. He was accompanied by the groups of Asuras. He was desirous of killing (Viṣṇu) the lord of cosmic form. He took up another fierce trident with a desire to fight with Hari. His mouth and face had a hideous form due to his (curved ferocious) teeth as well as (his desire to send) an oral message (to his followers).
baseline: He should be worshipped as the king of the world. Having said this he should be accompanied by the great men and the mighty men of the army. Having been placed on the throne of the lion the great man should be made to stand on the ground of the sky. Having taken the worldly form of the king the lord of the universe the king should be placed in the sky and the king who is a warrior should be sent to the king.
morphology: Having said that one should take the figure of the world one who is a great warrior and a great man with a number of demons and a mighty man standing on a lion and a noble man standing in the sky and having a fierce heart and having taken the image of the universe and having said the words of the prophet Hari after having made an attempt and having made a speech on the three horns of the king.

sanskrit: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ prathame māheśvarakhaṇḍe samudramaṃthanākhyāne devāsurasaṃgrāmavarṇanaṃnāma trayodaśo'dhyāyaḥ || 13 ||
reference: Rudrākṣa is the ‘berry’ of Elaeocarpus ganitrus. It is of different kinds, ‘one-faced’, ‘five-faced’ etc. Genuine ‘one-faced’ Rudrākṣa is rare and is valued highly. VV 50-55 describe the spiritual importance of wearing Rudrākṣa.[Sanskrit text for this chapter is available]
baseline: In the same way in the Sriskaṇḍa treatise the great men should be one hundred and eighty thousand. In the Sāhita treatise the description of the battle of the gods should be thirteen hundred and ten thousand words.
morphology: One should first describe the battle of the gods in the Sriskaṇḍa region as one of the great sāhastras and the other in the Sanhita region. The war between the two gods should be described as thirteen hundred and eighty times.

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca | tato yuddhamatīvāsīdasurairviṣṇunā saha | tataḥ siṃhāḥ sapakṣāste daṃśitāḥ paramādbhutāḥ || 1 || asurairuhyamānāste rahutmaṃtaṃ vyadārayan | siṃhāste dāritāstena khaṃḍaśaśca vidāritāḥ || 2 ||
reference: 1-2. Then the fight between Asuras and Viṣṇu became exceedingly terrific. The exceedingly wonderful winged lions equipped with armours and ridden by Asuras tore up Garuḍa. The lions too were pierced and torn to pieces by him.
baseline: Then the lion should be made to fight with the king of the two worlds. Then the lions should be beaten with the support of the king. Then they should be thrown into the abyss of the enemy. They should be cast into the pit of the lion. The lion should also be cast out.
morphology: Then the lion should be taken away from the king. Then the king of war should be accompanied by the lionesses the king and the viṣṇu king. And the lions should be beaten with a spear and the king should be destroyed. The lion should not be allowed to enter the kingdom.

sanskrit: viṣṇunā ca tadā daityāścakreṇa śakalīkṛtāḥ | hatāṃstānasurāndṛṣṭvā kālanemiḥ pratāpavān || 3 || triśūlenāhanadviṣṇuṃ roṣaparyākulekṣaṇaḥ | tamāyāṃtaṃ ca jagṛhe mukuṃdo'nāthasaṃśrayaḥ || 4 ||
reference: 3-4. Then Daityas were cut into pieces by Viṣṇu with his discus. On seeing Asuras killed, the valorous Kālanemi, with his eyes full of wrath, struck Viṣṇu with his trident. Mukunda (Viṣṇu), the support of those who are helpless, caught hold of the trident as it rushed at him.
baseline: Then Viṣṇu and the demigods were made to be shakalī with the sword. Having seen the sound of the sun he became the supreme ruler of the kingdom. He should be worshipped with the trisula the sword the weapon of the enemy the fiery sword and the mukundo the king the lord of the earth and the king of the world.
morphology: Then Viṣṇu and the demigods were made to be shakālī by him. Having seen the sun he became the supreme ruler of Kaṇāma. He should be worshipped with the trisula Śuṇa Hāṇḍvīṇu and the fiery kulākhu. The king should be placed on the ground with the mukundo nātha srāśrī.

sanskrit: kareṇa vāmena jaghāna līlayā taṃ kālanemiṃ hyasuraṃ mahābalam | tenaiva śūlena samāhato'sau mūrcchānvito'sau sahasā papāta || 5 ||
reference: 5. Viṣṇu playfully caught hold of Kālanemi, the Asura of great power with his trident, by his left hand sportively. Being struck with the self-same trident, he suddenly fell down senseless.
baseline: The king should be made to sit on the left side of the temple with the penance of the king. He should be raised to the head with the same shulk. He would fall asleep suddenly.
morphology: He should be made to suffer with the left hand with the kāraṇa and the leela with the kaalāna māhāsura and the mābhāla. He would get the same with the shulā and would fall asleep suddenly.

sanskrit: patitaḥ punarutthāya śanairunmīlya locane | purataḥ sthitamālokya viṣṇuṃ sarvaguhāśayam || 6 ||
reference: 6-7. The fallen Daitya came to senses again and slowly opened his eyes. Regaining consciousness, he saw Yiṣṇu standing in front of him—Viṣṇu, the lord abiding in the cavity of the heart of everyone. Kālanemi of great strength then spoke these words:
baseline: Having fallen down one should return to the abode of Lord Viṣṇu standing in the east.
morphology: Having fallen down and resurrected him one should worship Lord Viṣṇu standing in the east.

sanskrit: labdhasaṃjño'bravīdvākyaṃ kālanemirmahābalaḥ | tava yuddhaṃ na dāsyāmi nāsti loke spṛhā mama || 7 ||
reference: “I will not offer to fight with you, I have no desire for worlds (and worldly pleasures).
baseline: I shall not give you war. I will not give your war. The people will touch me.
morphology: I shall not give you war. I will not give your war. The people will touch me.

sanskrit: ye ye'surā hatā yuddhe akṣayaṃ lokamāpnuyuḥ | brahmaṇo vacanātsadya iṃdreṇa saha saṃgatāḥ || 8 || bhuṃjato vividhānbhogāndevavadvicaraṃti te | iṃdreṇa sahitāḥ sarve saṃsāre ca pataṃtyatha || 9 ||
reference: 8-9. According to the words of Brahmā, those Asuras who are killed in the battle will attain the Akṣaya (Everlasting) world. Immediately they will come into contact with Indra. Enjoying various kinds of worldly pleasures, they will roam about like gods along with Indra. Then they will fall down to the earthly world.
baseline: Those who have killed the gods in the war should be destroyed by the Brahman who has spoken with the sense of the earth. Those who suffer the senses and fall down in the world should be worshipped with the word bhūnjata bhūṇjata and other gods.
morphology: Those who kill the enemy in a battle should be counted as having lost their lives. The brahmins should be associated with the senses by saying the following words. Those who suffer from the sensations of the gods and goddesses should be destroyed in the world.

sanskrit: tasmādyuddhena maraṇaṃ na kāṃkṣe kṣaṇabhaṃguram | anyajanmani me vīra vairabhāvānna saṃśayaḥ | dātumarhasi me nātha kaivalyaṃ kevalaṃ param || 10 ||
reference: 10. Hence, I do not desire death in battle. It is of a momentary nature. O heroic lord, it behoves you to grant me Kaivalya (salvation) alone, the great benefit, in the course of my next birth, of course, as a result of an inimical attitude.”
baseline: Then death by war should not be a matter of momentary loss in the desire. The other forms of life should be given to me without any doubt except for the bravado enmity and that which is not the cause of death.
morphology: Then death should not be caused by war. The other forms of life should be given to me without any doubt except by the spirit of valour enmity and misfortune. I should not give the king a cow.

sanskrit: tatheti daityapravaro nipātitaḥ pareṇa puṃsā paramārthadena | dattvā'bhayaṃ devatānāṃ tadānīṃ tathā sudhāṃ devatābhyaḥ pradattvā || 11 ||
reference: 11. Saying “So be it”, the Supreme Being, the bestower of the greatest benefit, caused the excellent Daitya to fall down. Having given Sudhā (nectar) to Devas (before) and having granted freedom from fear to Devas (now) (the lord saved them).
baseline: Then the king of the gods should be destroyed by the supreme force. Then the gods would be feared and the same would be given to the gods.
morphology: Then the king should be destroyed by the gods. Then he should be given to the gods with the gift of pārmāma. Then the same goodness should be bestowed on the deities.

sanskrit: kālanemirhato daityo devā jātā hyakaṭakāḥ | śalyarūpo mahānsadyo viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā || 12 ||
reference: 12. Kālanemi, the great Daitya who was like a dart, was killed by Viṣṇu, the powerful lord. Devas became rid of thorns (enemies). 13-14. The lotus-eyed Lord vanished immediately.
baseline: One who has become a demon after having died would become a god. One who becomes a demon would be worshipped by Lord Viṣṇu in the form of a great sālya.
morphology: One who becomes a god after having been killed by a demon would become a demon. One who takes the form of Sālya would become Lord Viṣṇu with the great form of Viśṇu.

sanskrit: tirodhānaṃ gataḥ sadyo bhagavānkamalekṣaṇaḥ | iṃdro'pi kadanaṃ kṛtvā daityānāṃ paramādbhutam || 13 || patitānāṃ klībarūpāṇāṃ bhagnānāṃ bhītacetasām | muktakacchaśikhānāṃ ca cakre sa kadanakriyām || 14 ||
reference: Having caused extremely wonderful (terrific) havoc among Daityas, Indra also continued the slaughter of Daityas who were fallen, cowardly like eunuchs, broken (in spirit) and frightened in mind, and had their garments and tufts of hair loosened.
baseline: Having already lost the image of the lord one should also cast light on Indra and the demons. One who has fallen down and broken the forms of the gods and the fearful heart should be cast into the circle. One should cast a sword in the form of a sword and a shield free from fear.
morphology: Having removed the image of the lord and having removed it from the earth one should also remove the shadow of the gods and the demons. One who has fallen down and broken the forms of the demigods and the fearful mind one who has broken the shields of the free will and the illusion of the enemy in the circle should be killed.

sanskrit: arthaśāstraparo bhūtvā maheṃdro durātikramaḥ | daityānāṃ kālarūpo'sau śacīpatirudāradhīḥ || 15 ||
reference: 15. The liberal-minded consort of Śacī (Indra), who was like the god of Death unto Daityas and who could never be conquered (did all these things), because, he was devotedly following the (instructions laid down in the) Arthaśāstra.[1]
baseline: Having become an economist he is known as the king of the kingdoms. He is known to be the time of the demons. The king is also known as sāchipati.
morphology: Having become an economist he becomes the king of the kingdoms. He is the time of the demons. He becomes the master of the enemy.

sanskrit: evaṃ nihanymānānāmasurāṇāṃ śacīpateḥ | nivāraṇārthaṃ bhagavānāgato nāradastadā || 16 ||
reference: 16. While Asuras were being killed like this, the holy lord Nārada came there in order to make Indra desist from it.
baseline: In this way the lord should destroy the names of the enemies and protect them. The Lord should come to Narada for the relief.
morphology: In this way the names of the gods should be destroyed. The Lord should come to Narada for the relief.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca | yuddhahatāśca ye vīrā hyasurā raṇamaṇḍale | teṣāmanu kathaṃ kartā bhītānāṃ ca vihiṃsanam || 17 ||
reference: Nārada said: 17. Many heroic Asuras have been killed fighting in the battlefield. Why do you kill the frightened ones after that?
baseline: Narada said that those who killed the warriors and those who were killed in the battle should be killed by the mighty men of the kingdom. How can they be punished by the fearful men and by violence.
morphology: Narada said that those who killed the warriors and those who were killed in the battle should be killed by the mighty men of the army. How can they be punished by the fearful men and by violence.

sanskrit: ye bhītāṃśca prapannāṃścaghātayaṃti madoddhatāḥ | brahmaghnāste'pi vijñeyā mahāpātakasaṃyutāḥ || 18 ||
reference: 18. The haughty and arrogant ones who cause the death of those who are afraid and those who seek refuge should be known as murderers of Brāhmaṇas. They are guilty of great sins.
baseline: Those who are afraid of the enemy and harm the enemy are bound to be drunken. Those who do not know the Brahman they are bound together by the knowledge of the great enemy.
morphology: Those who are afraid of the enemy and harm the enemy those who are not aware of the Brahman are bound to suffer great loss by knowledge.

sanskrit: tasmāttvayā na karttavyaṃ manasāpi vihiṃsanam | evamuktastadā śakro nāradena mahātmanā || 19 || surasenānvitaḥ sadya āgato hi triviṣṭapam | tadā sarve suragaṇāḥ suhṛdbhyaśca parasparam | babhūvurmuditāḥ sarve yakṣagaṃdharvakiṃnarāḥ || 20 ||
reference: 19-20. Hence, even mentally injury should not be caused by you. On being told thus by the noble-souled Nārada, Indra immediately came back to Triviṣṭapa (heaven) accompanied by the armies of Suras. Then all the groups of Suras, all the Yakṣas, Gandharvas and Kinnaras became joyous. Along with their friends, they enjoyed the company of one another.
baseline: The same should not be done with the mind the mind and the heart. In the same manner the great man should be liberated from the evil spirits. He should be made to sit in the sun and come to the three directions. Then all the sugāṇas friends and friends should be taken to one another. All the yakshagandravakinas should be released from the darkness.
morphology: The same should not be done with the mind the mind and the heart. The same is liberated by the great man with the arrow the sun the fire the surasana the three elements of the body and the friends. Then all the gods the gods of the sun and the king of the earth and all the yakshagandhārvakinas should be worshipped together.

sanskrit: tadā iṃdro'marāvatyāṃ hasa śacyā'bhiṣecitaḥ || 21 || devarṣipramukhaiścaiva brahmarṣipramukhaistathā | śakro'pi vijayaṃ prāptaḥ prasādācchaṃkarasya ca || 22 ||
reference: 21-26a. Then Indra was crowned in Amarāvatī along with Śacī by leading celestial sages and leading Brāhmaṇa sages. It was due to the favour of Śaṅkara that Śakra attained victory.
baseline: Then Indra should be worshipped with the garland of Amravati. The king should be blessed with the crown of Brahma and the king of Sākrā who live in the face of the gods. He should also be blessed by the king.
morphology: Then Indra laughed at Amravati and worshipped him. He worshipped Brahma who dwells in the face of the gods and sages. He also conquered the king of gods and the king.

sanskrit: tadā mahotsavo viprā devaloke mahānabhūt | śaṃkhāśca paṭahāścaiva mṛdaṃgā murajā api | tathānakāśca bheryaśca nedurduṃdubhayaḥ samam || 23 || gāyakāścaiva gaṃdharvāḥ kinnarāścāpsapogaṇāḥ | nanṛturjagustuṣṭuvuśca siddhacāraṇaguhyakāḥ || 24 ||
reference: Then, O Brāhmaṇas, there was a great celebration in the world of Devas. Then conchs and different kinds of drums like Paṭahas, Mṛdaṅgas, Murajas, Ānakas, Bherīs and Dundubhis were sounded simultaneously. Gandharvas and Kinnaras were the musicians. The groups of celestial damsels danced. Siddhas, Cāraṇas and Guhyakas sang praises.
baseline: Then the festival of the gods became great. The conch and the mace of the earth the mridanga and the murja of the river are equal in size. The singers the gandharvas the kinnaravas and the sambhagas are equal to that of the king. The kings sons sons daughters sons and daughters are equal.
morphology: Then the festival of the gods became great and the people living in the fields of conch and pigeon should be worshipped as well as those living in mridanga and other parts of the world. The same is true for the people who live in the country and are not afraid of the king. The people living here are the singers the king of the Gandharvas the kings of the Ganges the rulers of the state and the leaders of the kingdom.

sanskrit: evaṃ vijayamāpannaḥ śakro devesvarastadā | devairhatāstadā daityāḥ patitāste mahītale || 25 ||
reference: Thus Śakra, the lord of Devas, attained victory. 26b-27a. At that time, the noble-souled Daityas, the chief among whom was Bali and who had been killed by Devas, fell down lifeless on the surface of the earth.
baseline: In this way the victory is achieved by the victory of the gods the gods and the demigods. The demigod has fallen on me.
morphology: In this way the victory is achieved by the victory of the gods the gods and the demigods falling down on me.

sanskrit: gatāsavo mahātmāno balipramukhato hyamī | tapastaptuṃ purā vipro bhārgavo mānasottaram || 26 ||
reference: Formerly the Brāhmaṇa Bhārgava (accompanied by his disciples) had gone to mount Mānasottara for performing penance. Hence he was not aware of that battle.
baseline: The last month or so the great spirit should be offered to the sacrificial lord. The penance should be completed by the priest. The sacrifice should be done by the lord of the earth.
morphology: The last month or so the great spirit should be worshipped with the preceptor of sacrifice. The penance should be completed with the scriptures vipra bhārga manasotara.

sanskrit: gataḥ śiṣyaiḥ parivṛtastasmādyuddhaṃ na veda tat | avaśeṣāśca ye daityāste gatā bhārgavaṃ prati || 27 || kathitaṃ vai mahaddhṛttamasurāṇāṃ kṣayāvaham | niśamya manyumāviṣṭo hyāgato bhṛgunaṃdanaḥ || 28 || śiṣyaiḥ parivṛto bhūtvā mṛtāṃstānasurānapi | vidyayā mṛtajīvinyā patitānsamajīvayat || 29 ||
reference: 27b-29. Those Daityas who had survived approached Bhārgava. The news of the great destruction of Asuras was conveyed to him. On hearing it, the son of Bhṛgu became furious. He returned surrounded by his disciples. With the Vidyā (magic formula) called Mṛtajīvinī (‘Resuscitator of the dead’), he revived the Asuras who had fallen dead.
baseline: Having covered those who have gone with their disciples they should not fight with the Vedas. Those who are left behind those who are demons should go to Bhārgava. They should be said to have destroyed the great rivers rivers and rivers. Having said that they would be worshipped by the disciples. They would also live with the dead animals and the fallen animals.
morphology: Having covered the disciples who had gone and had fought with them in the past the veda is not the same as that of Bhārgava. Those who were left behind the demons went to Bhāragava. He said that he would destroy the great sages and the gods. He would worship Bhrīguna after having been destroyed by the disciple. He also brought the dead animals and the animals that had fallen down by the knowledge of the dead.

sanskrit: nidrāpāyagatā yadvadutthitāste tadā'surāḥ | utthitaḥ sa baliḥ prāha bhārgavaṃ hyamitadyutim || 30 ||
reference: 30. Then those Asuras got up as though they had awakened from sleep. Bali who rose up, said to Bhārgava of unmeasured splendour:
baseline: When the sun has risen from sleep it should be offered to the sacrificial animal. The sacrifice should be made to him.
morphology: When he has fallen asleep and has risen from the dead the sūrā is raised. He should offer the sacrifice of Bhārga to the goddess Hāmita.

sanskrit: jīvitena kimadyaiva mama nāsti prayojanam | pātitastridaśeṃdreṇa yathā kāpuruṣastathā || 31 ||
reference: 31. “Of what avail is it to me today to be revived back to life? There is no benefit to me. I have been struck down by the lord of Devas like a mean contemptible wretch.”
baseline: There is no use for me to live with anything. One who has fallen asleep would become a coward by the use of the temple.
morphology: There is no use for me to live in the same place as a coward.

sanskrit: balinoktaṃ vacaḥ śrutvā śukro vacanamabravīt | manasvino hi ye śūrāḥ pataṃti samare budhā || 32 || ye śastreṇa hatāḥ sadyo mriyamāṇā vrajaṃti vai | triviṣṭapaṃ na saṃdeha iti vedānuśāsanam || 33 ||
reference: 32-33. On hearing the words uttered by Bali, Śukra spoke these words: “Those heroic persons who are high-souled and intelligent, who are learned, and who fall down dead in battle on being struck by a weapon go to heaven. This is undoubtedly the statement of the Vedas.”
baseline: Having heard the words of the sacrificial lord Śukra he said the words should be uttered. Those who fall down and fall down in the battle should understand that those who are killed by the enemy should be killed immediately. One should not doubt the doctrine of the Vedas.
morphology: Having heard the words of the sacrificial lord Śukra he said the words. Those who fall down in the battle with the knives those who fall asleep with the sword those killed with the weapon and those who die in the war the veda is said to be a preceptor.

sanskrit: evamāśvāsayāmāsa balinaṃ bhṛgunaṃdanaḥ | tapastatāpa vividhaṃ daityānāṃ siddhidāyakam || 34 ||
reference: 34. Thus, the son of Bhṛgu consoled Bali. He then performed various kinds of penance conducive to the achievement of Siddhis by Daityas.
baseline: This is the bhaṇḍi sacrifice and the boon of Bhriguṇa. The penance and the renunciation of the various demons are the perfect gifts.
morphology: This is the bhaśāraṇa sacrifice and the bhriguṇa oblation. The penance is the perfect offering to the various demons.

sanskrit: tathā daitya gatāḥ sarve bhṛguṇā ca pracoditāḥ | pātālamavasansarve balimukhyāḥ sukhena vai || 35 ||
reference: 35. All the Daityas urged by Bhṛgu went to Pātāla. All the Daityas, the chief among whom was Bali, stayed in Pātāla in happiness. FOOTNOTES AND REFERENCES: Arthaśāstra—A treatise on political economy. It is the title of a famous work of Kauṭilya or Ārya Cāṇakya who masterminded the revolution in Pāṭalīputra (Magadha), uprooted the Nanda dynasty and installed Candragupta Maurya as the King. Kauṭilya refers to many predecessors. Hence the Arthaśāstra mentioned here may be a more ancient work than that of Kauṭilya.[Sanskrit text for this chapter is available]
baseline: In the same way all the demons and the gods are stimulated. One who is sacrificial in the battle of Paṭāla māvasa will get victory with happiness.
morphology: In the same way the demons and all the gods are stirred up. One who is free from sacrifice in the night of Paṭāla māvasa goes away with happiness.

sanskrit: | ṛṣaya ūcuḥ | rājyaṃ prāpto hi deveṃdraḥ kathitaste guruṃ vinā | guroravajñayā jāto rājyabhraṃśo hi tasya tu || 1 || kena praṇoditaśceṃdro babhūva ciramāsane | tatsarvaṃ kathayāśu tvaṃ paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi naḥ || 2 ||
reference: The sages enquired: 1-2. It has been mentioned by you that Devendra regained kingdom without his preceptor. It was on account of disrespect to his preceptor that he had been dethroned from his kingdom. Urged by whom did he retain his position for a long time? Do tell us all these things quickly. We are very eager to hear it.
baseline: The sage who has attained the kingdom said that without the knowledge of the master he would go into exile. One who has been driven into the kingdom would become a king. One should say that he would not be interested in you. One would say that the king would go out of the kingdom without knowing the master. One could say that one would be driven into oblivion by the propitiation of the sage.
