morphology: The sage who has attained the kingdom of Śiva is said to have ascended up. He who gains the kingdom without the knowledge of the master is called Śevaṇḍva. One who becomes a fugitive from the kingdom after knowing the master one who is driven away by the forces of the king and who has become the centre of the universe is called as Śirāṣa. He is not interested in you.

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca | guruṇāpi vinā rājyaṃ kṛtavānsa śacīpatiḥ | viśvarūpoktavidhinā iṃdro rājye sthito mahān || 3 ||
reference: Lomaśa replied: 3-4. The consort of Śacī (Indra) ruled over the kingdom (of heaven) without his preceptor (Bṛhaspati). The great Indra (could) continue (to rule) over the kingdom due to the (religious) performance in accordance with the injunctions of Viśvarūpa.
baseline: One who has ruled without a master one who is a sācipati one standing in the kingdom of Indra in the manner described by the cosmic form is great.
morphology: One who has ruled without a master one who is a sāchipati one standing in the kingdom of Indra in the manner described by the cosmic form is great.

sanskrit: viśvakarmasuto viprā viśvarūpo mahānṛpaḥ | purohito'tha śakrasya yājakaścābhavattadā || 4 ||
reference: 5-6. O Brāhmaṇas, Viśvarūpa,[1] a great king, was the son of Viśvakarmā. He became the preceptor and performer of sacrifices for Śakra.
baseline: The image of Vishvakarma is the manifestation of the universe and is a great form. The priest should be the priest of the king.
morphology: One who is a priest of the lord Viśvāmarāsūtu the manifestation of the universe and the great form of the world should be worshipped as the priest.

sanskrit: tasminyajñe'vadānaiśca yajane asurānsurān | manuṣyāṃścaiva triśirā aparokṣaṃ śacīpateḥ || 5 ||
reference: In that Yajña, Triśiras (one with three heads) performed the worship with partial oblations separately for Asuras, Suras and human beings.
baseline: One who does not know these things and who has spoken the words of the Lord should be called as a son of the king. One who dwells in a man should be known as Trisira.
morphology: In the same manner as in the case of the king the king of the Assyrians should be known to the king. The king of Trisira should be called a sācipati.

sanskrit: devāndadāti sākrośaṃ daityāṃstūṣṇīmathādadāt | manuṣyānmadhyapātena pratyahaṃ sa grahāndvijaḥ || 6 ||
reference: In the direct presence of Indra everyday he used to give ladles (full of Soma) to Devas with a loud shout, to Daityas silently, and to human being in a fallen middle tone.
baseline: One who gives to the gods and goddesses the goods of the demigods and the objects of the sun should be given to them. One who falls between men and the planets should be worshipped.
morphology: One who gives to the gods and goddesses and gives to demons and objects and objects would be called sunny. One who falls between humans and planets would become a king.

sanskrit: ekadā tu maheṃdreṇa sūcito gurulāghavāt | alakṣyamāṇena tadā jñātaṃ tasya cikīrṣitam || 7 ||
reference: 7-8. Once he was detected due to his partiality (regarding relative importance of oblations) by Indra who remained concealed and unobserved. Then the desired object (of Triśiras) was understood (by Indra).
baseline: Once the master has been instructed by me he should be removed from the seat. Then he should know that he has been removed from it.
morphology: Once the preceptor has been instructed by me he should be removed from the seat of the master. Then he should know that he has been attracted by him.

sanskrit: daityānāṃ kāryasiddhyarthamavadānaṃ prayacchati | asau purohito'smākaṃ pareṣāṃ ca phalapradaḥ || 8 ||
reference: (Deveṇdra thought) ‘He is making this piecemeal offering for the sake of accomplishing the task of Daityas. He is our preceptor, but gives the benefit to (our) enemies.’
baseline: Having accomplished the task of the demons one who gives gifts is a priest. He is also a fruitful man for others.
morphology: Having accomplished the task of the demons the priest would be able to give us good things. He would also be successful for others.

sanskrit: iti matvā tadā śakro vajreṇa śataparvaṇā | ciccheda tacchirāṃsyeva tatkṣaṇādabhavadvadhaḥ || 9 ||
reference: 9. After thinking thus, Śakra cut off his heads instantaneously by means of his Vajra (thunderbolt) of hundred spikes. The death was instantaneous.
baseline: Having said this one should then offer a hundred prāvāṇas with a diamond. One would get the same amount of water immediately.
morphology: Having said this one should then offer hundred prāparvaṇas with a diamond and the same amount of water should be offered immediately.

sanskrit: yenākarotsomapānamajāyaṃta kapiṃjalāḥ | tatonyena surāpānātkalaviṃkā bhavanmukhāt || 10 || anyānanādajāyaṃta tittirā viśvarūpiṇaḥ | evaṃ hato viśvarūpaḥ śakreṇa maṃdabhāginā || 11 ||
reference: 10-11. The Kapiñjala (a sort of partridge) birds were born from the face with which he drank Soma juice. Then from the other face with which-he drank liquor, the Kalaviṅka (sparrow) birds were born. From the other (third) face, the Tittira birds of various forms were born. Thus, Viśvarūpa was killed by Śakra, the ill-fated one.
baseline: One who drinks water with the same amount of water as that of a cow one should drink water with it. One who does not drink wine with it would be facing you. The other would be the form of the universe with the sound of a lotus. Thus the form would be divided into ten parts with the light of the sun.
morphology: One who drinks water with the same quantity as the other should drink water with that amount of water with a cup of water. One who does not drink wine with that quantity would be facing you. The other would be the form of the universe with the sound of the ten syllables titiara visvaruṇa viṣvaruṣuṇu vaśvaruśa sākrā and viśvara.

sanskrit: brahmahatyā tadodbhūtā durdharṣā ca bhayāvahā | durdharṣā durmukhā duṣṭā caṇḍālarajasānvitā || 12 ||
reference: 12-14. The female fiend (born of and called) Brahmahatyā (‘Brāhmaṇa-murder’) manifested there. She was terrific and unthwartable. She was evil-faced, wicked, full of Cāṇḍāla impurity and could not be blocked or defeated.
baseline: The brahmahit is the killing of the enemy. The enemy is fearful. The adversary is evil the enemy is evil and the king is evil.
morphology: The brahmahit is the killing of the enemy. The enemy is evil and fearful. The adversary is evil the enemy is bad and the enemy of the army is evil.

sanskrit: brahmahatyā surāpānaṃ steyaṃ gurvaṃganāgamaḥ | ityeṣāmapyaghavatāmidameva ca niṣkṛtiḥ || 13 ||
reference: The terrible sinners are those who slay Brāhmaṇas, those who drink liquor, those who steal (gold etc.) and those who defile and outrage the modesty of the preceptor’s wife. The means of expiation for these sinners is the utterance of the names of Viṣṇu, since the mind has him for its object.
baseline: One who kills Brahma by drinking wine eating cow eating meat and eating meat should be expelled from the body.
morphology: One who kills Brahma drinks wine drinks ghee and drinks water would get rid of these diseases.

sanskrit: nāmavyāharaṇaṃ viṣṇoryatastadviṣayā matiḥ | triśirā dhūmrahastā sā śakraṃ grastumupāyayau || 14 ||
reference: The three-headed fiend with smoke-coloured hands rushed forth to swallow Indra.
baseline: One should worship Viṣṇu in the name of vyāharā. One should observe that the three should be smoked and one should be drunk.
morphology: One should worship the goddess Viṣṇu in the form of the name of the goddess. One would get the illusion of the three horns of smoke. One of them would get poisoned.

sanskrit: tato bhayena mahatā palāyanaparo'bhavat | palāyamānaṃ taṃ dṛṣṭvā hyanuyātā bhayāvahā || 15 ||
reference: 15. Thereupon (Indra) fled from there out of great fear. On seeing him fleeing, the terrible (devil) chased him.
baseline: Then the great escapeer became afraid of him. Seeing him flee he feared him.
morphology: Then the great flight of fear came to him. Seeing him flee he became afraid.

sanskrit: yato dhāvati sā'dhāvattiṣṭhaṃtamanutiṣṭhati | aṃgakṛtā yathā chāyā śakrasyapariveṣṭitum | āyāti tāvatsahasā iṃdro'pyapsu nyamajjata || 16 || śīghratvena yathā viprāściraṃtanajalecaraḥ || 17 ||
reference: 16-17. Wherever he ran, she too ran after him. If he stood anywhere, she too stood beside him. She behaved in the manner of a shadow of one’s own body. When she came so close as to envelop him, Indra sank beneath the waters suddenly, O Brāhmaṇas, like an old aquatic being.
baseline: One who runs away from the king should be made to sit on the ground in the same way as one who is in the shadow of the king. One who does so should be brought to the king of Indra and the king in the opposite direction. The king who is not afraid of the enemy should be taken away as soon as possible.
morphology: One who runs away from the earth and hastens to reach the top of the body should be surrounded by the shadow of the enemy. One who does so should be led to the king of Indra by the sword and the king should be brought to the throne as soon as possible.

sanskrit: evaṃ divyaśataṃ pūrṇaṃ varṣāṇāṃ ca śacīpateḥ | vasatastasya duḥkhena tathā caiva śatadvayam | arājakaṃ tadā jātaṃ nākapṛṣṭhe bhayāvaham || 18 || tadā ciṃtānvitā devā ṛṣayo'pi tapasvinaḥ | trailokyaṃ cā'padā grastaṃ babhūva ca tadā dvijāḥ || 19 ||
reference: 18-19. Thus three hundred divine years passed since the consort of Śacī (Indra) began staying (beneath the waters) with great misery. A terrific state of anarchy spread throughout heaven. Thereupon Devas, sages and ascetics became anxious and worried. All the three worlds were overwhelmed by adversity, O Brāhmaṇas.
baseline: In this way the divine hundred is completed in the years and the king of the four hundred in the days of his death. Then the evil one becomes aghast at the nose and becomes a fearful one. Then he who is worried about the gods and the sages becomes a penitent and becomes afflicted with the three worlds and becomes an evil one.
morphology: In this way the divine hundred is completed and the sācipati of the years is destroyed by the misfortune of the king. Then the king becomes a coward and the king gets frightened on the side of the nose. Then he becomes the god of the sage who is worried and becomes a penitent. He becomes the king of the three worlds and then becomes a tyrant.

sanskrit: eko'pi brahmahā yatra rāṣṭre vasati nirbhayaḥ | akālamaraṇaṃ tatra sādhūnāmupajāyate || 20 ||
reference: 20. Even if there is a single Brāhmaṇa-slayer in a kingdom staying there with impunity, untimely death of good men will take place there.
baseline: A brahmin living in a country is fearless. One who dies prematurely becomes a sādhu.
morphology: A sage should be worshipped in a country where one Brahman has no fear in the absence of death. One who dies prematurely becomes a sage.

sanskrit: rājā pāpayuto yasminrāṣṭre vasati tatra vai | durbhikṣaṃ caiva maraṇaṃ tathaivopadravā dvijāḥ || 21 ||
reference: 21. The king of the state wherein he (the Brāhmaṇa-slayer) lives, becomes contaminated by the sin. There will be (prevalence of) famine, death and calamities.
baseline: The king is a sinner if he dwells in a country where there is famine and death.
morphology: The king is a sinner if he dwells in a country and dies of hunger.

sanskrit: bhavaṃti bahavo'narthāḥ prajānāṃ nāśahetave | tasmādrājñā tu kartavyo dharmmaḥ śraddhāpareṇa hi || 22 ||
reference: 22. There will be many misfortunes causing the destruction of the subjects. Hence, Dharma should be practised by a king with great faith.
baseline: One should destroy the people by saying many words. By doing so one should attain righteousness by following the orders of God.
morphology: You should destroy the people by saying many words. By doing so the commandment should be done. The righteousness is done by following the belief.

sanskrit: tathā prakṛtayo rājñaḥ śucajitvena pratiṣṭhitāḥ | indreṇa ca kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ tena pāpena vai dvijāḥ | nānāvidhairmahātāpaiḥ sopadravamabhūjjagat || 23 ||
reference: 23. Similarly, the ministers of the king too should be installed with purity. Sin was committeed by Indra and due to that sin, O Brāhmaṇas, the whole of the universe met with calamities along with great distress of diverse kinds.
baseline: In the same way the king of nature is established as pure. The sins committed by Indra are punished by the sins done by him. He is also punished with many other sins.
morphology: In the same way the king of nature is established as pure and living. The sins committed by Indra are punished with the same amount of sins. The king of the kingdom is also punished with many other sins and other evils.

sanskrit: śaunaka uvāca | aśvamedhaśatenaiva prāptaṃ rājyaṃ mahattaram | devānāmakhilaṃ sūta kasmādvighramajāyata | śakrasya ca mahābhāga yathāvatkathayasva na || 24 ||
reference: Śaunaka enquired: 24. It was by performing a hundred horse-sacrifices that the great realm of Devas was acquired by him, O Sūta. Why then did Śakra meet with obstacles, O highly fortunate one? Do tell us exactly as it happened.
baseline: The king should be said to have attained greatness by the sacrifice of the horse. The king who had attained great glory by the killing of the elephant should be called the king of the gods. He should not retain the great portion of the sword.
morphology: The king should be said to have attained great kingdom by the killing of horses. The king of gods should be told how much he had lost his kingdom. The great portion of the sword should not be retained.

sanskrit: sūta uvāca | devānāṃ dānavānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ viśeṣataḥ | karmmaiva sukhaduḥkhānāṃ hetubhūtaṃ na saṃśayaḥ || 25 ||
reference: Sūta replied: 25. In the case of Devas, Dānavas and particularly that of human beings, Karman alone is undoubtedly the cause of happiness and misery.
baseline: One would not doubt the reasons for the happiness and sorrow of the gods and the demigods and especially of the humans.
morphology: One should not doubt that the gods demigods and humans in particular are the cause of happiness and sorrow.

sanskrit: indreṇa ca kṛtaṃ viprā mahadbhūtaṃ jugupsitam | guroravajñā ca kṛtā viśvarūpavadhaḥ kṛtaḥ || 26 || gautamasya guroḥ patnī sevitā tasya tatphalam | prāptaṃ maheṃdreṇa ciraṃ yasya nāsti pratikriyā || 27 ||
reference: 26-27. An immensely reprehensible act has been committed by Indra, O Brāhmaṇas, He insulted his Guru (preceptor Bṛhaspati). Viśvarūpa was slain. The wife of Gautama, his Guru (preceptor, elderly one), was carnally approached. It was the fruit of all these sins that was reaped by Mahendra for a long time. There was no way of atonement for the same.
baseline: One who has made a great contribution by Indra has become a juguśa. One who knows the wisdom of the master has acquired the world has served the wife of the guru of Gautama and has received the same amount of money from the master and has not received any response from him.
morphology: One who has made a great contribution by Indra has become a great juga and has knowledge of the master has acquired the universal form and has served the wife of Gautama the master and has received the reward for that. One who does not get the contribution from the master has got no response from him.

sanskrit: ye hi dṛṣkaṭatakarmmāṇo na kurvaṃti ca niṣkṛtim | durdaśāṃ prapnuvantyete yathaivendraḥ śatakratuḥ || 28 ||
reference: 28. If persons committing wicked and sinful deeds, do not perform expiatory rites (for the same), they do incur miseries just like Indra, (though) he had performed a hundred sacrifices.
baseline: Those who do not perform the deeds of a blind person should be expelled. The misfortune of the poor should be brought to the fore as if they were the sons of a centurion.
morphology: Those who do not do the deeds of the eye eye and eye etc. should be removed. The misfortune should be brought to the fore by the god Śetākratu.

sanskrit: duṣkṛtopārjitasyā taḥ prāyāścittaṃ hi tatkṣaṇāt | kartavyaṃ vidhivadviprāḥ sarvapāpopaśāṃtaye || 29 ||
reference: 29. If sins are committed, atonement should be performed instantaneously in accordance with the injunctions, O Brāhmaṇas, for the sake of quelling all the sins.
baseline: One should do this immediately after having acquired the bad deeds. He should do it after having remission of all sins against the law.
morphology: One should do this immediately after having acquired the evil deed. One has to do it after having repented of all sins against the law.

sanskrit: tataḥ svadharmaniṣṭhāṃ ca ye kurvaṃti sadā narāḥ | prātarmadhyāhnasāyāhne teṣāṃ pāpaṃ vinaśyati || 31 || prāpnuvaṃtyuttamaṃ lokaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā | tasmādasau durācāraḥ prāpte vai karmaṇaḥ phalam || 32 ||
reference: 30-32. If minor sins are repeatedly performed, they turn into major sins. Those men who steadfastly cling to their duties of the morning, midday and dusk can get their sins destroyed. They attain the excellent world. There is no doubt about it. Hence, this person of evil conduct (i.e. Indra) reaped the fruit of his karman.
baseline: Then those men who are always doing their duty and obedience to their religion their sins would be destroyed in the morning midday and evening. They would get the best of the world and ask for their work. Then those who do evil deeds would get their reward.
morphology: Then those men who are always doing their duty and obedience to their religion their sins would be destroyed in the morning evening and evening. They would get the best of the world. Then those who do evil deeds would get their reward.

sanskrit: sa pradhārya tadā sarve lokapālāstvarānvitāḥ | bṛhaspatimupāgamya sarvamātmani dhiṣṭhitam | kathayāmāsuravyagrā iṃdrasya ca guruṃ prati || 33 ||
reference: 33. All the Guardians of the Quarters hurriedly deliberated together. They approached Bṛhaspati and reported to the preceptor about Indra everything they had in their mind.
baseline: Then all the ombudsmen should come and worship the goddess Brihaspati. All the spirits should be worshipped. One should say Śura Viyagra Indra and the master.
morphology: Then all the lokpalas would be worshipped by him. Having ascended to Brihaspati all the spirits would be worshiped. Saying this to Indra the master of the gods asura vyāgrā and a.

sanskrit: devairuktaṃ vaco viprā niśamya ca bṛhaspatiḥ | arājakaṃ ca saṃprāptaṃ ciṃtayāmāsa buddhimān || 34 ||
reference: 34. On hearing the words uttered by Devas, Bṛhaspati, the intelligent (preceptor), thought about the anarchy that had begun to spread.
baseline: The image of Brihaspati is described as having the colour of the goddess  the blood of the gods the nature of the earth and the presence of the unmanifested.
morphology: The image of Brihaspati should be described as the image of a god the blood of a goddess the darkness of the earth the presence of an anarchy and the mind.

sanskrit: kiṃ kāryaṃ cādya kartavyaṃ kathaṃ śreyo bhaviṣyati | devānāṃ cādya lokānāmṛṣīṇāṃ bhāvitātmanām || 35 || manasaiva ca tatsarvaṃ kāryākāryaṃ vicārya ca | jagāma śakraṃ tvarito devaiḥ saha mahāyaśāḥ || 36 ||
reference: 35-36. ‘What shall be done now? How will they secure welfare—Devas, the worlds and sages of sanctified souls?’ In his mind, he thought over the details of what should and what should not be done. Accompanied by Devas, the preceptor of great fame went to Indra.
baseline: One should discuss with the gods the things to be done and how it would be better. One should explain to the gods the people the animals the spirits the mind all the activities and the other things. One would make a jagāma with the deities in haste.
morphology: Having considered what should be done and how it would be better for the gods to do the same the people men animals spirits etc. and the mind should also consider all the other things. The great men should go forth with the gods in haste.

sanskrit: prāpto jalāśayaṃ taṃ ca yatrāste hi puraṃdaraḥ | yasya tīre sthitā hatyā caṃḍālīva bhayāvahā || 37 ||
reference: 37. They reached the lake where Purandara (Indra) was lying (hidden) and on the bank of which was staying the (devil of) Brāhmaṇa slaughter terrible like a Caṇḍālī.
baseline: One who finds a water body and places it on the banks of the river is known as Purāṇāra. One who kills the king is known to be a fearful cow.
morphology: One who finds a water body and places it on the banks of the river is known as Purāndara. One who kills the king is known to be a coward.

sanskrit: tatroviṣṭāste sarve devā ṛṣigaṇānvitāḥ | āhvānaṃ ca kṛtaṃ tasya śakrasya guruṇā svayam || 38 ||
reference: 38. All the Devas, accompanied by the groups of sages sat there. Then Śakra was called by the preceptor himself.
baseline: All the gods are seated there and the sages are worshipped. The master of that lord has called him.
morphology: All the gods are seated there and the sages are worshipped. The master of the enemy has called him.

sanskrit: samutthitastataḥ śakro dadarśa svaguruṃ tadā | bāṣpapūritavaktro hi bṛhaspatimabhāṣata || 39 ||
reference: 39. Thereupon, Indra got up and saw his preceptor. With tears flowing over his face, he spoke to Bṛhaspati.
baseline: Then the disciple should be raised up. Then he should see his master. The disciple who is filled with steam should speak to Brihaspati.
morphology: Then the disciple should be raised from the ground and then he should visit his master. The disciple who is filled with vapour should speak to Brihaspati.

sanskrit: praṇipatya ca tatratyānkṛtāñjalirabhāṣata | tadā dīnamukho bhūtvā manasā saṃvimṛśya ca || 40 || svayameva kṛtaṃ pūrvamajñānalakṣaṇaṃ mahat | adhunaiva mayā kāryaṃ kiṃ kartavyaṃ vada prabho || 41 ||
reference: 40-41. He bowed down to all the persons assembled there. He pondered over the great (blunders) committed by himself before, as a result of ignorance. He joined his palms in reverence and with a piteous face spoke: “O Lord, tell me what should be done by me just now?”
baseline: Having worshipped the lord one should speak to him with the merciless voice and then become poor and think of the mind. Having done it by oneself the preconceived notions are great. Then the Lord will tell me what I should do.
morphology: Having worshipped the lord one should speak the words of the angel made therein. Having become poor the mind should think about it. Having done it by oneself the manifestation of the knowledge of the past is great. Then the Lord will tell me what I should do.

sanskrit: prahasyovāca bhagavānbṛhaspati rudāradhīḥ | purā tvayā kṛtaṃ yacca tasyedaṃ karmaṇaḥ phalam || 42 || māṃ ca uddiśya bho iṃdra tadbhogādeva saṃkṣayaḥ | prāyaścitaṃ hi hatyāyā na dṛṣṭaṃ smṛtikāribhiḥ || 43 ||
reference: 42-43. The holy lord Bṛhaspati of liberal mind laughed and said: “O Indra, this is the result of that act of yours committed previously against me. Only by experiencing its result, can it be annihilated. But, no atonement for Brāhmaṇa-slaughter has been seen (i.e. laid down) by the authors of Smṛti texts.
baseline: O lord of the universe you have done all that is required of you. You have done the same for me. O Indra after having spoken to me and having experienced it you will be able to make sure that you do not commit the murder.
morphology: O lord of the universe you have done all that is required of you. The deeds done by you are the fruit of your actions. O Indra after having spoken to me and having consumed it you will be able to make sure that you do not commit the murder.

sanskrit: ajñānato hi yajjātaṃ pāpaṃ tasya pratikriyā | kathitā dharmmaśāstrajñaiḥ sakāmasya na vidyate || 44 ||
reference: 44. Expiation has been prescribed by those conversant with Dharma Śāstras (Code of Laws) for the sin committed unknowingly. There is no atonement for an offence wilfully committed.
baseline: The answer to that sin is that of ignorance that which is not known to be true. That which is said by theologians is not true.
morphology: The answer to that sin is that of ignorance that which is not justified by the learned religious scholars.

sanskrit: sakāmena kṛtaṃ pāpamakāmaṃ naiva jāyate | tābhyāṃ viṣayabhedena prāyaścittaṃ vidhīyate || 45 ||
reference: 45. A sin committed by a person intentionally does not become one committed unintentionally. Expiation is laid down for both based on the differences in the objects.
baseline: The sin committed by the same person would not be forgiven. It would be better if the matter is resolved by them.
morphology: The sin committed by the sakāma is not justified by the matter of the sins committed.

sanskrit: maraṇāṃto vidhiḥ kāryo kāmena hi kṛtena hi | ajñānajanite pāpe prāyaścittaṃ vidhīyate || 46 ||
reference: 46. If a sin is committed wilfully (deliberately), the expiation is to be performed up to death. Atonement is laid down in case of sins committed unknowingly.
baseline: One should do the ritual of death with the desire to do the work. One would get rid of the sin by doing it without knowledge.
morphology: One should perform the ritual of death by doing it with lust. One would get remission of sins in the generation of ignorance.

sanskrit: tasmāttvayā kṛtaṃ yacca svayameva hato dvijaḥ | purohitaśca vidvāṃśca tasmānnāsti pratikriyā || 47 ||
reference: 47. Since this has been intentionally done by you, since the twice-born, the learned priest has been killed, there is no atonement.
baseline: That which has been done by the same person would be done by another person. The priest scholar and others would respond to that.
morphology: The same thing is done by the priest and the learned man. The answer should be given by the two priests.

sanskrit: yāvanmaraṇamapyeti tāvadapsu sthiro bhava || 48 ||
reference: 48. Stay in the waters here and wait for your death.
baseline: The more the death is attained the more stable you become.
morphology: The death of the deceased should be fixed in the two hands.

sanskrit: śatāśvamedhasaṃjñaṃ ca yatphalaṃ tava durmate | tannaṣṭaṃ tatkṣaṇādeva ghātito hi dvijo yadā || 49 ||
reference: 49. The meritorious deed of yours termed ‘performance of one hundred horse-sacrifices’, O evil-minded one, has already been destroyed at the very moment when the twice-born was killed by you.
baseline: If you do not know the meaning of the death of a hundred and twenty years old man the reward for that would be your death would be immediately destroyed.
morphology: If you do not know the meaning of the death of a man who has committed a hundred and twenty years of war the result will be disastrous for you. If you kill him immediately then he should be punished.

sanskrit: sacchidre ca yathā toyaṃ na tiṣṭhati ghaṭe'ṇvapi | tathaiva sukṛtaṃ pāpe hīyate ca pradakṣiṇam || 50 ||
reference: 50. Just as not a drop of water remains in a pot with holes, similarly meritorious deeds of a sinner go on reducing every moment.
baseline: In the same way that water does not remain in the openings it also happens to those who do not get it. In the similar way the circumambulation is done in the case of sins.
morphology: In the same way that water does not remain in the hole it also happens in those places. Similarly in the case of sins one gets circumambulation.

sanskrit: tasmācca daivasaṃyogātprāptaṃ svargādikaṃ ca yaiḥ | yathoktaṃ tadbhavetteṣāṃ dharmiṣṭhānāṃ na saṃśayaḥ || 51 ||
reference: 51. Hence, by good luck, if heaven etc. are attained, those can be retained only by really righteous ones. There is no doubt about it.”
baseline: He should not doubt the righteousness of those who have been given the gift of the gods and the heavenly abode.
morphology: One should not doubt the righteousness of those who have been given the gift of the gods and the heavenly abode.

sanskrit: etacchrutvā vacastasya śakro vacanamabravīt | kukarmaṇā madīyena prāptametanna saṃśayaḥ || 52 ||
reference: 52. On hearing his statement, Indra spoke these words: “Undoubtedly this has fallen to my lot through my own misdeeds.
baseline: Having spoken these words he said the words of his disciple. He doubted that he would get the evil deeds from me.
morphology: Having raised such an alarm he said the following words. He doubted that he had achieved the evil deeds of Madya.

sanskrit: amarāvatī māśu tvaṃ gaccha devarṣibiḥ saha | lokānāṃ kāryasiddhyarthe devānāṃ ca bṛhaspate | iṃdraṃ kuru mahābhāga yaste manasi rocate || 53 ||
reference: 53. Hasten to Amarāvatī along with the celestial sages, O Bṛhaspati. For the purpose of accomplishing the tasks of the worlds as well as of Devas, O sage of great fortune, crown as Indra, anyone whom you approve in your mind.
baseline: You go with the gods and goddesses of the world the great part of the mind which is good for the people and the gods. O Indra do the great portion which is desirable for you.
morphology: You go with the gods and goddesses on the morning of Amravati the great part of the mind that you want to do is done by Indra.

sanskrit: yathā mṛtastathā haṃ vai brahmahatyāvṛto mahān | rāgadveṣasamutthena pāpenāsmi pariplutaḥ || 54 ||
reference: 54. Enveloped by the great devil of Brahmahatyā, I am just like one who is dead. I have been overwhelmed by the sin arising from Rāga (attachment) and Dveṣa (hatred).
baseline: The manner in which Brahman has been killed is great. By raising up ones anger hatred and sin one becomes full of it.
morphology: As if he had died he would have killed Brahman. He would have been great. By the resurrection of his anger and hatred he would be filled with sin.

sanskrit: tasmāttvarānvitā yūyaṃ devarājānamāśuḥ vai | kurvatu madanujñātāḥ satyaṃ prativadāmi vaḥ || 55 ||
reference: 55. Hence hasten all of you to make someone king of Devas. You have my permission for the same. I am speaking the truth to you.”
baseline: You are the king of gods and the master of all beings. You know the truth and I tell you the truth.
morphology: You are the king of gods and the master of all beings. Knowing the Lord you should tell the truth.

sanskrit: evamuktāstadā sarve bṛhaspatipurogamāḥ | etyāmarāvatīṃ tūrṇaṃ puraṃdaraviceṣṭitam | kathayāmāsuravyagrā śacīṃ prati yathā tathā || 56 ||
reference: 56. On being told thus, all those (Devas) with Bṛhaspati at their head came to Amarāvatī immediately and coolly told Śacī everything about Indra’s activities as they had taken place.
baseline: All the prophets of Brihaspati are liberated from this. The trumpet should be placed at the same time as the bow. Let us say the same to the arrow as to the bow and arrow.
morphology: All the prophets of Brihaspati should be liberated from this. The trumpet should be placed at the same time as the bow. Let us say the same thing to Asura Vyagrha and Sāccha.

sanskrit: rājyasya hetoḥ kiṃ kāryaṃ vimṛśaṃtaḥ parasparam || 57 ||
reference: 57. They consulted one another and began to deliberate thus: ‘What should be done for the sake of the kingdom?’
baseline: What is the work for the sake of the kingdom and what should be done for the benefit of each other.
morphology: What are the functions of the king for the sake of the kingdom?

sanskrit: evaṃ vimṛśyamānānāṃ devānāṃ tatra nāradaḥ | yadṛcchayāgatastatra devarṣiramitadyutiḥ || 58 ||
reference: 58. While Devas were thus deliberating, Nārada, the celestial sage of unmeasured splendour, came there by chance.
baseline: In this way the gods who are seen there are described as Narada. The king of the gods is described as sīrī.
morphology: In this way the gods who are seen there Narada should be seen. The king of the gods should be worshipped in that place as far as he is concerned.

sanskrit: uvāca pūjito devānkasmādyūyaṃ vicetasaḥ | tenoktāḥ kathayāmāsuḥ sarvaṃ śakrasya ceṣṭitam || 59 ||
reference: 59. On being honoured, he asked Devas: “Why are you all sad and perplexed?” On being enquired (thus) they spoke everything about Śakra’s activities:
baseline: One who worships a god should say that he would do everything for him.
morphology: One who worships a god should say that he wants to do everything.

sanskrit: gatamiṃdrasya ceṃdratvamenasā parameṇa tu | tataḥ provāca tāndevāndevarṣirnārado vacaḥ || 60 ||
reference: 60. “Indra’s status of being the lord (of Devas) has come to an end on account of a great sin.” Thereupon Nārada, the celestial sage, spoke these words to those Devas:
baseline: One who is the master of the past and the past should have the centrality of the mind. Then one should say to those gods the king of the gods and the king.
morphology: Then the king should say to them that they are the gods and the king of the gods.

sanskrit: yūyaṃ devāśca sarvajñāstapasā vikrameṇa ca | tasmādiṃdro hi kartavyo nahuṣaḥ somavaṃśajaḥ || 61 || so'sminrāṣṭre pratiṣṭhāpyastvaritenaiva nirjarāḥ | ekonamaśvamedhānāṃ śataṃ tena mahātmanā | kṛtamasti mahābhāgā nahuṣeṇa ca yajvanā || 62 ||
reference: 61-62. “You are omniscient Devas endowed with the power of penance and valour. Hence Nahuṣa,[2] born in the Lunar race, should be made Indra. He should be established in this realm, O Devas, immediately. Ninety-nine horse-sacrifices have been performed by that noble-souled Nahuṣa, O highly fortunate ones. Nahuṣa was a regular performer of Yajñas
baseline: You are the gods and know that by the form of the sun the sun and the earth. Then the king of the kingdom of Soma should do the same thing. He should be placed in the land of Smyrna. The king of Scyrrmia should do one hundred times the worship of God. The great gift of God is done by him. The Lord of the universe is also known by the name of Nāhuṣa.
morphology: You are the gods and you know that by the way of the form of the sun you have done the same thing. Then the king of the Somavamsa clan should do the same. He should be placed in the kingdom of Sāminā. The king should do one hundred times the worship of God. The great fortune of the king should be done by him.

sanskrit: śacyā śrutaṃ ca tadvākyaṃ nāradasya mukhodgatam | gatāṃtaḥpuramavyagrā bāṣpapūritalocanā || 63 ||
reference: 63-67. That statement coming out of the mouth of Nārada was heard by Sacī. With her eyes filled with tears and not engaged in anything (seriously), she went into the inner apartment.
baseline: The same thing should be said of Narada in his mouth. The previous one should be the vapour filled with water.
morphology: The same thing should be said of Narada who had heard the story of the vapour filled bathing at the end of the past.

sanskrit: nāradasya vacaḥ śrutvā sarve devānvamodayan || 64 || nahuṣaṃ rājyamāroḍhumaikapadyena te yadā | ānīto hi tadā rājā nahuṣo hyamarāvatīm || 65 || rājyaṃ dattaṃ maheṃdrasya suraiḥ sarvairmaharṣibhiḥ | tadāgastyādayaḥ sarve nahuṣaṃ paryupāsata || 66 ||
reference: On hearing the words of Nārada, all the Devas congratulated him. They approved of his suggestion to make Nahuṣa the ruler of the realm unanimously. Then, king Nahuṣa was brought to Amarāvatī and the kingdom of Mahendra was given to him by all the Suras and great sages.
baseline: All the gods heard the voice of Narada and worshipped him. When the king had brought him with one accord the king should worship him. The king should be worshipped with the melody of Mahendra and all the gods should be worshiped. It is said that all the deities who came to him should worship the king.
morphology: The king should be brought to the king with one accord. When he had heard the voice of Narada all the gods would be pleased. He should be pleased with the king. When the king should have brought him home with one vow he should have given him the kingdom with the notes of Mahendra and all the great sages. Then he should be satisfied with all the words of the lord.

sanskrit: gaṃdharvāpsaraso yakṣā vidyādharamahoragāḥ | yakṣāḥ suparṇāḥ patagā ye cānye svargavāsinaḥ || 67 ||
reference: Then all of them served Nahuṣa. Agastya and others (sages), Gandharvas, Apsarās, Yakṣas, Vidyādharas, the great serpents, Rākṣasas, the birds of bright wings (suparṇas like Garuḍa) and other heaven-dwellers (served him).
baseline: One who is born with the gandharva vapāsara yaksha vidya dhar mahorāga yakshā suparna kite and those who live in heaven.
morphology: One who has knowledge of Gandharva Vāpsarā Yaksha Mahāoraga Yaksha Suparnā Kite and others who are the inhabitants of heaven.

sanskrit: tadā mahotsavo jāto devapuryāṃ niraṃtaraḥ | śaṃkhatūryamṛdaṃgāni nedurduṃdubhayaḥ samam || 68 ||
reference: 68. Then in the city of Devas, there was a continuous grand celebration. Concḥs, musical instruments, Mṛdaṅgas and Dundubhis sounded simultaneously.
baseline: Then the festival is held in the temple of the gods continuously. The heart and limbs of the goddess are equal to that of the king.
morphology: Then the festival would be held in the temple of the gods continuously. One would get the conch and heart parts and the other two parts would be equal.

sanskrit: gāyakāśca jagustatra tathā vādyāni vādakāḥ | nartakā nanṛtustatra tathā rājyamahotsave || 69 ||
reference: 69. In that grand celebration of the kingdom of Devas, musicians sang songs, players of instruments played on them and dancers danced.
baseline: The singers should be heard in the jaguar and the instruments should be played. The dancers should be performed in the nārtu and the king should be worshipped in the festival.
morphology: The singers should be heard in the jaguar and the instruments should be played in the harp. The dancers should be seen in the nārtu and the king should be worshipped in the festival.

sanskrit: abhiṣiktastadā tatra bṛhaspatipurogamaiḥ || 70 ||
reference: 70. Then he was coronated there by the sages, of whom Bṛhaspati was the foremost.
baseline: There is the preceptor Brihaspati in the anointed body.
morphology: The priest Brihaspati should go to the place where he is anointed.

sanskrit: arcito devasūktaiśca yathā vadgrahapūjanam | kṛtavāṃścaiva ṛṣibhirvidvadbhirbhāvitātmabhiḥ || 71 ||
reference: 71. He was worshipped with Deva-Sūkta and was made to perform the worship of Planets in due procedure and with formalities.
baseline: One should worship the gods and goddesses as if he were a priest. One should do the worship of the gods gods and gods by the sages and other spirits.
morphology: One should worship the gods and goddesses as if one were a priest. One should do the worship of the gods gods and other gods by the sages and other spirits.

sanskrit: tathā ca sarvaiḥ paripūjito mahānrājā surāṇāṃ nahuṣastadānīm | iṃdrāsane ceṃd samānarūpaḥ saṃstūyamānaḥ parameṇa varcasā || 72 ||
reference: 72. The great king Nahuṣa was duly honoured and respected by the learned sages of sanctified souls and by all others also. As the king of Suras, he sat on the throne of Indra. He had the same features as those of Indra. Endowed with the greatest splendour, he was eulogized by all.
baseline: In the same way the great king should be endowed with all the qualities of the senses. In the form of Indra the same form should be worshipped by the Supreme Lord.
morphology: In the same way the great king should be endowed with all the qualities of the sun and the king should give the same form in the indrasana.

sanskrit: sugaṃdhadīpaiśca suvāsasā yuto'laṃkārabhogaiḥ suvirājitāṃgaḥ | babhau tadānīṃ nahuṣo munīdraiḥ saṃstūyamāno hi tathā'mareṃdraiḥ || 73 ||
reference: 73. Dressed in excellent sweet-scented bright garments and with his person adorned excellently with ornaments and articles of enjoyment, Nahuṣa appeared resplendent as he was being eulogized by prominent sages and leading Devas.
baseline: Then the body should be made of the fragrance of the sun and the fragrances of the fire and the enjoyment of the earth. Then the mind should be prepared with the fragrant leaves and the senses should be given to it.
morphology: Then the body should be made to feel the fragrance of light and fragrance. Then the limbs should be adorned with the fragrances of gold and copper. Then they should be washed with the perfumes of the sun and water.

sanskrit: iti paramakalānvito'sau suramunivaragaṇaiśca pūjyamānaḥ | nahuṣanṛpavaro'bhavattadānīṃ hṛdi mahatā hṛcchayenataptaḥ || 74 ||
reference: 74. Thus the great king Nahuṣa who was endowed with great ingenuity and worshipped by groups of great Devas and sages, became severely tormented at heart by intense passion (lust).
baseline: One who has attained the highest degree of art is worshipped by the sages and the people. One who does not fall into the form of the sun would get a great heart.
morphology: Having said this one should be worshipped as having the highest form of art. One should not be afraid of the great heart when he has not been born.

sanskrit: nahuṣa uvāca | iṃdrāṇī kathamadyaiva nāyāti mama sannidhau | tāṃ cāhvayata śīghraṃ bho mā vilaṃbitumarhatha || 75 ||
reference: Nahuṣa said: 75. How is it that Indrāṇī does not come near me? Call her quickly. It does not behove you to delay.
baseline: O Nāhuṣa the queen of Indrāṇī she should be brought before me in the same manner. She should be asked to leave her as soon as possible. Do not delay.
morphology: O Nāhuṣa the queen of Indrāṇī should be brought before me at the same time. If you wish to make her go soon do not delay.

sanskrit: nahupasya vacaḥ śrutvā bṛhaspatirudāradhīḥ | śacībhavanamāsādya uvāca ca savistaram || 76 ||
reference: 76. On hearing the words of Nahuṣa, the liberal-minded Bṛhaspati went to Śacī’s abode and spoke in detail:
baseline: Having heard the words of Nāhupta Brihaspati Tritarāda and others the king of the temple of Sācī is said to have spoken in detail.
morphology: Having heard the words of Nāhupta Brihaspati Tritarāda and others are described in detail.

sanskrit: śakrasya durnimittena hyanīto nahuṣo'tra vai | rājyārte bhāmini tvaṃ ca arddhāsanagatā bhava || 77 ||
reference: 77. “It was on account of the calamity fallen on Indra that Nahuṣa was brought here for the sake of the kingdom. O beautiful lady, occupy half of his seat.”
baseline: The king should be killed here for the misfortune of the enemy. You should be half-suffering in the matter of the kingdom.
morphology: The king should be killed for the misfortune of the enemy. You should be half-suffering in the matter of the kingdom.

sanskrit: śacī prahasya covāca bṛhaspatimakalmaṣam | asau na paripūrṇo hi yajñaiḥ śakrāsane sthitaḥ | ekonamaśvamedhānāṃ śataṃ kṛtamanena vai || 78 || tasmānna yogyo prahasya covāca bṛhaspatimakalpaṇaṣam | asau na paripūrṇo hi yajñaiḥ śakrāsane sthitaḥ | avāhyavāhanenaiva atrāgatya labheta mām || 79 ||
reference: 78-79. Śacī laughed and spoke to sinless Bṛhaspati: “He has occupied the seat of Indra without completing the quota of (hundred) Yajñas. Only ninety-nine horse-sacrifices have been performed by him. Hence, he is not qualified enough to obtain me. Let this be thought over truthfully. If this senseless fellow still continues to be desirous of me, wife of another person, let him obtain me by coming here by means of a vehicle that is carried by undeserving carriers.”
baseline: One who does not want to go to the abode of Brihaspati should come here and get me. One who is not satisfied with the sacrifices and is sitting in the seat of the devotee should do the same by doing a hundred times with the mind. The one who is able to do so should not be satisfied with that seat and the one who has not completed the sacrifice and is staying in the chair of Brihadaspati. He should not come here in a vehicle and get Me.
morphology: One who does not know the meaning of the word Brihaspati should lie down on the ground. One who is not satisfied with the sacrifices should sit in the seat of the lord of the sun one who has done a hundred times the meditation of the Lord of the earth and one who is satisfied with that should lie in the chair of the god of the moon and who is unable to do so should come here and get me.

sanskrit: tatheti gatvā tvarito bṛhaspatiruvāca tam | nahuṣaṃ kāmasaṃtaptaṃ śacyoktaṃ ca yathātatham || 80 ||
reference: 80. Saying “So be it”, Bṛhaspati returned hurriedly to Nahuṣa who had been distressed through intense lust. He reported to him what was spoken by Śacī in her own words.
baseline: Then he should go and return to Brihaspati in haste. He should say that he has no desire and that he would do so.
morphology: Then he should go and return to Brihaspati in haste. He should say that he is satisfied with his desire and that he should do so.

sanskrit: tatheti matvā rājāsau nahuṣaḥ kāmamohitaḥ | vimṛśya parayā buddhyā avāhyaṃ kiṃ praśasyate || 81 || sa buddhyā ca ciraṃ smṛtvā brāhmaṇāścatapasvinaḥ | avāhyāśca bhavaṃtyasmādātmānaṃ vāhayāmyaham || 82 || dvābhyāṃ ca tasyāḥ prāptyarthamiti me hṛdi vartate | śibikāṃ ca dadau tābhyāṃ dvijābhyāṃ kāmamohitaḥ || 83 ||
reference: 81-84. Saying “So be it”, Nahuṣa who was deluded by lust, thought over it. He deliberated on this intelligently: ‘Who can be the carrier not worthy of being so?’ After thinking about it intelligently and trying to remember for a long time (he decided thus): “The Brāhmaṇas and the ascetics are not usually thought of as carriers. I shall make two of them bear me in order to reach her. This is my decision.” So (the king) who was deluded by lust gave the palanquin to two Brāhmaṇas.
baseline: The king should not think of the king as having a desire for him. He should think about what he wants to do with his mind. Having thought of him he should think of him as a brahmin. Having said that I want to say that he has got both his heart and his father's heart. Having understood him the brahmins should be aware of him. Having known him and his mother he would be able to understand him.
morphology: The king should not think that he has a desire for others. He should think of the Brahmanas and the other Brahmins with his intellect. He would like to know that the two men who have been given the gift of the mother the king the daughter of the daughter the son of the king and the daughter who have the desire of others would be pleased with him. The Brahman should remember him with the knowledge that he had the desire for the mother and daughter. The king would get the gift from me.

sanskrit: upaviśya tadā tasyāṃ śivabikāyāṃ samāhitaḥ | sarpasarpeti vacanānnodayāmāsa tau tadā || 84 ||
reference: Seated in that palanquin with great concentration, he urged them on with the words “Sarpa, sarpa” (Move on, move on). (Sarpa means ‘serpent’ also.)
baseline: Having sat down he is then buried in the abode of Śiva. The serpent gives the serpent his words. Then he is said to be pleased.
morphology: Having sat down he is buried in the abode of Śiva. The serpent sapens the words of the serpents.

sanskrit: agastyaḥ śibikāvāhī tataḥ kruddho'śapannṛpam | viprāṇāmavamaṃtā tvamunmatto'jagaro bhava || 85 ||
reference: 85. Agastya who had been one of the palanquin-bearers became infuriated and cursed the king. “You are a lunatic and despiser of Brāhmaṇas; you be a python.”
baseline: Then Agastya Śivaṇa the king of the world became angry and worshipped him. He should be worshipped as the lord of the universe. You should be worshiped as the supreme god.
morphology: Then Agastya and Śivikāvāhi became angry and worshipped him. You are the king of all beings. You become the king. You get the world.

sanskrit: śāpoktimātrato rājā patito brāhmaṇasya hi | tatraivājagaro bhūtvā vipraśāpo duratyayaḥ || 86 ||
reference: 86. Immediately, after the utterance of the curse by the Brāhmaṇa, the king became a python and fell from there itself. Indeed the curse of a Brāhmaṇa is untransgressable.
baseline: A king who has fallen is only a curse for a brahmin. He should be removed from the kingdom by becoming a king.
morphology: A king who has fallen down on account of a curse should be called a brahmin. Having become a king the king should be removed from the city.

sanskrit: yathā hi nahuṣo jātastathā sarve'pi tādṛśāḥ | viprāṇāmavamānena patinti niraye'śucau || 87 ||
reference: 87. Just as Nahuṣa became (a python), so also all like him fell into dirty hell by disrespecting Brāhmaṇas.
baseline: The same is the case with all men who have been born without the knowledge of the gods. One who has fallen asleep with the sound of the wind should be blessed with the gift of water.
morphology: Just as the son of Nahus is born so are all sons. The son of Vīpranāma should be born free from evil thoughts.

sanskrit: tasmāsarvaprayatnena padaṃ prāpya vicakṣaṇaiḥ | apramattairnarairbhāvyamihāmutra ca labdhaye || 88 ||
reference: 88. Hence, in order to attain benefits here and hereafter, a wise, circumspect person who has achieved a position of importance, should refrain in all possible ways from committing blunders.
baseline: Having obtained the position with all the efforts and with the discerning one one should attain the position of the son of the unbeliever.
morphology: Having attained that position with all his efforts and with his discernment one would get the son of a man who has not attained infallibility.

sanskrit: tathaiva nahuṣaḥ sarppo jātoraṇye mahābhaye | evaṃ caivābhavattatra devaloke hyarājakam || 89 ||
reference: 89. Nahuṣa became a serpent in a very dreadful forest. Hence there prevailed anarchy in the world of Devas.
baseline: In the same way the serpent Nāhuṣa should be feared in the battle. Thus the king should be worshipped in the world of gods.
morphology: In the same way the serpent Nāhuṣa becomes a great fear in the battle of jatorāna. Thus the king is the king in the world of gods.

sanskrit: tathaiva te surāḥ sarve vismayāviṣṭacetasaḥ | aho bata mahatkaṣṭaṃ prāptaṃ rājñā hyanena vai || 90 ||
reference: 90. Similarly, all the Devas were struck with consternation. “Alas! What a wretched condition the king has fallen into!
baseline: In the same way all those notes are wonderful. O king who gets a great loss by killing him is said to be 90.
morphology: In the same way all those notes are wonderful. One who gets great loss by killing the king would get great loss.

sanskrit: na martya loko na svargo jāto hyasya durātmanaḥ | satāmavajñayā sadyaḥ sukṛtaṃ dagdhameva hi || 91 ||
reference: 91. This evil-minded fellow has obtained neither the mortal world nor the heavenly world. His (fund of) merits has been instantaneously burnt down,
baseline: One who does not die and goes to heaven will never be destroyed by the evil spirit. One who has been burnt alive by the knowledge of the truth would soon be destroyed.
morphology: One who does not die and goes to heaven would not get the ill will. One who has been cured by the knowledge of the truth would get burnt.

sanskrit: yājñiko hyaparo loke kathyatāṃ ca mahāmune | tadovāca mahātejā nārado munisattamaḥ || 92 ||
reference: 92. If there is any other person who has performed (many) Yajñas, let him be named, O great sage.” Then the excellent sage Nārada of great splendour said:
baseline: One should say that one who is a yāgyānyika or a hymns should be offered to the great lord. One who is said to be a great god should say the same to Narada as to Munis.
morphology: One should say the words yāgyako hapāra to the great man. The words mahateja narada is better for the sage.

sanskrit: yayātiṃ ca mahābhāgā ānayadhvaṃ tvarānvitāḥ | devadūtāstu vai tūrṇaṃ yayātiṃ drutamānayan || 93 ||
reference: 93. “O highly fortunate ones, hasten to bring Yayāti.[3]” Messengers of Devas went immediately and brought Yayāti quickly.
baseline: One should bring a great devotee with haste and the angels should be quicken the journey. The angels are quickeners.
morphology: One should bring a great devotee to the place of his journey. The angels should be quickened and the journey should be expedited.

sanskrit: bhrāmarī ganḍamālī ca śvitry atho piśunas tathā / unmatto 'ndhaś ca varjyāḥ syur vedanindaka eva ca //
reference: An epileptic man, who suffers from scrofulous swellings of the glands, one afflicted with white leprosy, an informer, a madman, a blind man, and he who cavils at the Veda must (all) be avoided.
baseline: Bhrāmāri gāndamālī Śvitrī Atho Pīṣuṇas and Śuṇḍa śūrjya Sūrtha Vruddhandaaka are forbidden.
morphology: Bhrāmāri Gāndamālī Śvitrī Atho Pīṣuna and Śuṇḍa the one who is in a state of rest and restless and the one suffering from pain are the same.

sanskrit: śvakrīḍī śyenajīvī ca kanyādūṣaka eva ca / hiṃsro vṛṣalavṛttiś ca gaṇānāṃ caiva yājakaḥ // ācārahīnaḥ klībaś ca nityaṃ yācanakas tathā / kṛṣijīvī ślīpadī ca sadbhir nindita eva ca // aurabhriko māhiṣikaḥ parapūrvāpatis tathā / pretaniryāpakaś caiva varjanīyāḥ prayatnataḥ //
reference: A breeder of sporting-dogs, a falconer, one who defiles maidens, he who delights in injuring living creatures, he who gains his subsistence from Sudras, and he who offers sacrifices to the Ganas, He who does not follow the rule of conduct, a (man destitute of energy like a) eunuch, one who constantly asks (for favours), he who lives by agriculture, a club-footed man, and he who is censured by virtuous men, A shepherd, a keeper of buffaloes, the husband of a remarried woman, and a carrier of dead bodies, (all these) must be carefully avoided.
baseline: The priest should be a cowherd a woman who is a virgin a mischief mongering a coward a priest who is not good at all a man without conduct a scapegoat a barbarian a farmer a sage a poor man with a penitentiary a nobleman with a good reputation a brahmin a preacher a tyrant a king who is evil and a man of evil conduct.
morphology: The priest should be a cowherd a woman who is a virgin a mischiefgiver a coward a priest who is not good at all a man who has no conduct is always a beginner a farmer a maid of honour a sage a nobleman a preacher a teacher an advocate of the spirit a barbarian a poor priest an obstructionist an evil person a corrupt person an evildoer a tyrant a defrauded person one who has never lived in the past.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇo tv anadhīyānas tṛṇāgnir iva śāmyati / tasmai havyaṃ na dātavyaṃ na hi bhasmani hūyate //
reference: As a fire of dry grass is (unable to consume the offerings and is quickly) extinguished, even so (is it with) an unlearned Brahmana; sacrificial food must not be given to him, since it (would be) offered in ashes.
baseline: A brahmin should not be given to a man who has not attained to the earth as if he were a fire nor should he be made to burn the ashes.
morphology: A brahmin should not be given the fire of grass and the fire should be burnt.

sanskrit: apāṅktadāne yo dātur bhavaty ūrdhvaṃ phalodayaḥ / daive haviṣi pitrye vā taṃ pravaksyāmy aśeṣataḥ //
reference: I will fully declare what result the giver obtains after death, if he gives food, destined for the gods or manes, to a man who is unworthy to sit in the company.
baseline: The one who gives a gift to the unbelievers should follow you above the gods the parents or the parents.
morphology: One who gives a gift to a relative should follow him above you. He should be worshipped by the gods his parents and his relatives.

sanskrit: avratair yad dvijair bhuktaṃ parivetrādibhis tathā / apāṅkteyair yad anyaiś ca tad vai rakṣāṃsi bhuñjate //
reference: The Rakshasas, indeed, consume (the food) eaten by Brahmanas who have not fulfilled the vow of studentship, by a Parivettri and so forth, and by other men not admissible into the company.
baseline: One who is not able to do the same would get the same protection as another.
morphology: One who is not able to protect another person would be punished by the same thing as one who has not been able to do so.

sanskrit: dārāgnihotrasaṃyogaṃ kurute yo 'graje sthite / parivettā sa vijñeyaḥ parivittis tu pūrvajaḥ //
reference: He must be considered as a Parivettri who marries or begins the performance of the Agnihotra before his elder brother, but the latter as a Parivitti.
baseline: The one who makes a connection with the fire of the fire who sits on the earth and who is the guardian is the knowledgeable one. The heir is the ancestor.
morphology: One who attaches a fire fire and other objects to the earth and who is present in the house is known as the knower the master and the master.

sanskrit: parivittiḥ parivettā yayā ca parividyate / sarve te narakaṃ yānti dātṛyājakapañcamāḥ //
reference: The elder brother who marries after the younger, the younger brother who marries before the elder, the female with whom such a marriage is contracted, he who gives her away, and the sacrificing priest, as the fifth, all fall into hell.
baseline: The priest who gives to the priest should be known by the words pāvītti pārivatī jāyā. All those who give to him are known to go to hell.
morphology: The priest who gives to the priest should be known by the words pāvītti pārvita jāya yā. All those who give to him are known to go to hell.

sanskrit: tau tu jātau parakṣetre prāṇinau pretya ceha ca / dattāni havyakavyāni nāśayanti pradāyinām //
reference: But those two creatures, who are born of wives of other men, cause to the giver the loss (of the rewards), both in this life and after death, for the food sacred to gods or manes which has been given (to them).
baseline: Those who give the animals to another country those who do not want to give them their lives and those who give them to other countries destroy those who want to do them.
morphology: They destroy the objects that are given to them and those that are offered to them. They destroy those things which are given by the creatures in other places and their faces.

sanskrit: apāṅktyo yāvataḥ paṅktyān bhuñjānān anupaśyati / tāvatāṃ na phalaṃ tatra dātā prāpnoti bāliśaḥ //
reference: The foolish giver (of a funeral repast) does not reap the reward for as many worthy guests as a man, inadmissible into company, can look on while they are feeding.
baseline: A child should not be allowed to eat food in the same way as a child. He should not eat food from the same place. He will not get fruit from that place.
morphology: A child should not be allowed to eat food in a row without having to eat it. He will not get the fruit from that place.

sanskrit: vīkṣyāndho navateḥ kāṇaḥ ṣaṣṭeḥ śvitrī śatasya tu / pāparogī sahasrasya dātur nāśayate phalam //
reference: A blind man by his presence causes to the giver (of the feast) the loss of the reward for ninety (guests), a one-eyed man for sixty, one who suffers from white leprosy for a hundred, and one punished by a (terrible) disease for a thousand.
baseline: One who has not seen the eye would get sixty ears and would get a hundred ears. One who gives a thousand things to a sinner would get destroyed.
morphology: One who has not seen the ear of a sinner would get sixty ears. One who gives to a sick person would lose the reward of a thousand diseases.

sanskrit: yāvataḥ saṃspṛśed aṅgair brāhmaṇāñ śūdrayājakaḥ / tāvatāṃ na bhaved dātuḥ phalaṃ dānasya paurtikam //
reference: The giver (of a Sraddha) loses the reward, due for such a non-sacrificial gift, for as many Brahmanas as a (guest) who sacrifices for Sudras may touch (during the meal) with his limbs.
baseline: The priest of the Shudras should not be so much as to touch the body of the brahmins as to give fruits to the priest.
morphology: The priest of the Shudras should not be so close as to touch the body of the brahmins. He should not give the gift of fruits to the priest.

sanskrit: vedavic cāpi vipro 'sya lobhāt kṛtvā pratigraham / vināśaṃ vrajati kṣipram āmapātram ivāmbhasi // somavikrayiṇe viṣṭhā bhiṣaje pūyaśoṇitam / naṣṭaṃ devalake dattam apratiṣṭhaṃ tu vārdhuṣau // yat tu vāṇijake dattaṃ neha nāmutra tad bhavet / bhasmanīva hutaṃ dravyaṃ tathā paunarbhave dvije //
reference: And if a Brahmana, though learned in the Veda, accepts through covetousness a gift from such (a man), he will quickly perish, like a vessel of unburnt clay in water.180 (Food) given to a seller of Soma becomes ordure, (that given) to a physician pus and blood, but (that presented) to a temple-priest is lost, and (that given) to a usurer finds no place (in the world of the gods). What has been given to a Brahmana who lives by trade that is not (useful) in this world and the next, and (a present) to a Brahmana born of a remarried woman (resembles) an oblation thrown into ashes.
baseline: Having conquered the Vedas having made a bid to destroy the viprās by making them greedy one should destroy them. One who destroys them by selling them having destroyed them would get a mango tree having sold them and having put them in the temple would lose them if they were given to the gods would not be able to do so. If they are given to a merchant they should be given to another person the property property and property.
morphology: Having conquered the Vedas one would destroy the viprās by making them greedy. One would destroy them by making a lotus like a mango tree. One who destroys them would be destroyed by the sale of a piece of water one who would be worshipped by the gods in the form of a vipaśa. One given to the devalu who would not be destroyed who should be given to a merchant one given to an old man who is not a son of a god who has not been given to him. One should be destroyed in the matter of the earth

sanskrit: itareṣu tv apāṅktyeṣu yathoddiṣṭeṣv asādhuṣu / medo'sṛṅmāṃsamajjāsthi vadanty annaṃ manīṣiṇaḥ //
reference: But the wise declare that the food which (is offered) to other unholy, inadmissible men, enumerated above, (is turned into) adipose secretions, blood, flesh, marrow, and bone.
baseline: If you say that you are not good enough for others then you should say that food should be given to those who are illiterate.
morphology: If you say that you are not good enough for others then you should say that the dishonest people should be better off with food and other things.

sanskrit: apāṅktyopahatā paṅktiḥ pāvyate yair dvijottamaiḥ / tān nibodhata kārtsnyena dvijāgryān paṅktipāvanān //
reference: Now hear by what chief of twice-born men a company defiled by (the presence of) unworthy (guests) is purified, and the full (description of) the Brahmanas who sanctify a company.
baseline: The two lines should be divided into two parts. They should be separated into two lines with the syllable kārtśnya.
morphology: The two lines should be divided into two parts. The two rows should be drawn with the syllable kārtasnya.

sanskrit: triṇāciketaḥ pañcāgnis trisuparṇaḥ ṣaḍaṅgavit / brahmadeyātmasantāno jyeṣṭhasāmaga eva ca //
reference: A Trinakiketa, one who keeps five sacred fires, a Trisuparna, one who is versed in the six Angas, the son of a woman married according to the Brahma rite, one who sings the Gyeshthasaman,
baseline: One who is born with the three limbs one who has five limbs three wings six limbs the sons of the spirit of Brahman and the elder one is the supreme body.
morphology: One who is born with the three limbs one who has five limbs three colours six limbs the son of the spirit of Brahman and the elder one is the same.

sanskrit: pūrvedyur aparedyur vā śrāddhakarmaṇy upasthite / nimantrayeta tryavarān samyag viprān yathoditān //
reference: On the day before the Sraddha-rite is performed, or on the day when it takes place, let him invite with due respect at least three Brahmanas, such as have been mentioned above.
baseline: One should present the three gods in the east the king of the east or the king who is worshipping. The three gods should be properly worshipped.
morphology: One who has worshipped in the east or in the west should be invited to worship the three gods.

sanskrit: ketitas tu yathānyāyaṃ havye kavye dvijottamaḥ / kathaṃ cid apy atikrāman pāpaḥ sūkaratāṃ vrajet // āmantritas tu yaḥ śrāddhe vṛśalyā saha modate / dātur yad duṣkṛtaṃ kiṃ cit tat sarvaṃ pratipadyate //
reference: But a Brahmana who, being duly invited to a rite in honour of the gods or of the manes, in any way breaks (the appointment), becomes guilty (of a crime), and (in his next birth) a hog. But he who, being invited to a Sraddha, dallies with a Sudra woman, takes upon himself all the sins which the giver (of the feast) committed.
baseline: One who invents a sin after having committed the offence of trespassing would be called a ketite. One who gives a penance with a bull would be declared as evil by the god.
morphology: One who invents a sin after having committed an offence should say that he has done the same thing as the king. The one who invokes the sins of the enemy would get away with the evil deed and would leave with the bull the one who gives the deed would get rid of everything.

sanskrit: somapās tu kaveḥ putrā haviṣmanto 'ṅgiraḥsutāḥ / pulastyasyājyapāḥ putrā vasiṣṭhasya sukālinaḥ //
reference: The Somapas are the sons of Kavi (Bhrigu), the Havishmats the children of Angiras, the Agyapas the offspring of Pulastya, but the Sukalins (the issue) of Vasishtha.
baseline: Somapāsa the son of Kāva Hāvīṣmanta the son and Āngir the son are the sons of Pūlāṣṭya Sājya Paṇa Vāśita Sukālī.
morphology: The sons of Somapāsa Kāvē Hāvīṣmanta Angirā Sūtā Pulasti Yājya Vāsīta Sukālī are the sons of Vāṣṭhī.

sanskrit: agnidagdhānagnidagdhān kāvyān barhiṣadas tathā / agniṣvāttāṃś ca saumyāṃś ca viprāṇām eva nirdiśet //
reference: One should know that (other classes), the Agnidagdhas, the Anagnidagdhas, the Kavyas, the Barhishads, the Agnishvattas, and the Saumyas, are (the manes) of the Brahmanas alone.
baseline: One should refer to the fiery fire fire agni fire and fire the poems the banishments the fire gold gold etc. and the miracles.
morphology: One should refer to the fiery fire fire fiery and fiery weapons the poems of the Bahrīṣadsa and the fire the fire and the spirit of the Sāmya and the viprasas.

sanskrit: ya ete tu gaṇā mukhyāḥ pitṝṇāṃ parikīrtitāḥ / teṣām apīha vijñeyaṃ putrapautram anantakam //
reference: But know also that there exist in this (world) countless sons and grandsons of those chief classes of manes which have been enumerated.
baseline: The chief of the fathers should be known to be of such a number. The son and son should be regarded as infinite.
morphology: Those who are the chief of the clan should be known to their fathers. They should be called the sons and grandsons of eternal knowledge.

sanskrit: rājatair bhājanair eṣām atho vā rajatānvitaiḥ / vāry api śraddhayā dattam akṣayāyopakalpate //
reference: Even water offered with faith (to the manes) in vessels made of silver or adorned with silver, produces endless (bliss).
baseline: One who gives a king a cow a buffalo a horse or a woman with a crown a man given with faith is considered to be inexhaustible.
morphology: One who gives the king a piece of rice or a piece made of rice with the help of the king or one who has got the gift of rice from the king or one given it with the belief of the lord is considered to be inexhaustible.

sanskrit: daivakāryād dvijātīnāṃ pitṛkāryaṃ viśiṣyate / daivaṃ hi pitṛkāryasya pūrvam āpyāyanaṃ smṛtam //
reference: For twice-born men the rite in honour of the manes is more important than the rite in honour of the gods; for the offering to the gods which precedes (the Sraddhas), has been declared to be a means of fortifying (the latter).
baseline: By doing the work of the gods the father's work of two nations would be divided. The god should remember to do the service of the father before the work.
morphology: By doing the work of the gods the father of the two nations would be separated. The god should be remembered as having done the work before the father.

sanskrit: teṣām ārakṣabhūtaṃ tu pūrvaṃ daivaṃ niyojayet / raksāṃsi vipralumpanti śrāddham ārakṣavarjitam //
reference: Let him first invite a (Brahmana) in honour of the gods as a protection for the (offering to the manes); for the Rakshasas destroy a funeral sacrifice which is left without such a protection.
baseline: They should be placed in the reserve by the god first. The worship should be done by the rakshasas and the viprālumpas.
morphology: They should be placed in the reserve by the god first. The worship of the rakshasas should be done by the king.

sanskrit: daivādyantaṃ tad īheta pitrādyantaṃ na tad bhavet / pitrādyantaṃ tv īhamānaḥ kṣipraṃ naśyati sānvayaḥ //
reference: Let him make (the Sraddha) begin and end with (a rite) in honour of the gods; it shall not begin and end with a (rite) to the manes; for he who makes it begin and end with a (rite) in honour of the manes, soon perishes together with his progeny.
baseline: It should not be till the god has given it to the parents. You will lose the strength of the god to the father.
morphology: It should not be till the god is worshipped. It should never be until the father is killed. You lose the strength of the god.

sanskrit: śuciṃ deśaṃ viviktaṃ ca gomayenopalepayet / dakṣināpravaṇaṃ caiva prayatnenopapādayet //
reference: Let him smear a pure and secluded place with cowdung, and carefully make it sloping towards the south.
baseline: The land should be clean and separated and the cow should be covered with cow dung. The man should be prepared with the right hand. One should get profit by making efforts.
morphology: The land should be cleaned and the ground should be separated and the cow should be covered with cow dung.

sanskrit: āsaneṣūpakḷpteṣu barhiṣmatsu pṛthakpṛthak / upaspṛṣṭodakān samyag viprāṃs tān upaveśayet // upaveśya tu tān viprān āsaneṣv ajugupsitān / gandhamālyaiḥ surabhibhir arcayed daivapūrvakam // teṣām udakam ānīya sapavitrāṃs tilān api / agnau kuryād anujñāto brāhmaṇo brāhmaṇaiḥ saha //
reference: The (sacrificer) shall make the (invited) Brahmanas, who have duly performed their ablutions, sit down on separate, prepared seats, on which blades of Kusa grass have been placed. Having placed those blameless Brahmanas on their seats, he shall honour them with fragrant garlands and perfumes, beginning with (those who are invited in honour of) the gods. Having presented to them water, sesamum grains, and blades of Kusa grass, the Brahmana (sacrificer) shall offer (oblations) in the sacred fire, after having received permission (to do so) from (all) the Brahmana (guests) conjointly.
baseline: One should sit on the seats in the form of a spire separate from the outer parts of the ground with the spire of the upper part of the seat sitting on the seat and sitting in the seat with the scissors of the sun worshipped by the goddess Surabhi with garlands of fragrance bringing the spears sesamum and sesame seeds and with the permission of the Brahman in the fire.
morphology: One should place the outer parts of the body on the seats and the outer part of the seats on the other side of the ground. The upper parts of a seat should be placed on the right side and the upper parts should be kept on the left side. Having sat on the seat one should place them on the ground and the other parts on the front side. One should bring their utensils the sacred ones the sesamum and the leaves together with the brahmins and bring them to the Lord.

sanskrit: akrodhanān suprasādān vadanty etān purātanān / lokasyāpyāyane yuktān śrāddhadevān dvijottamān //
reference: They (also) call those first of twice-born men the ancient deities of the funeral sacrifice, free from anger, easily pleased, employed in making men prosper.
baseline: Having said these the gods of worship should be worshipped twice. These are the old ones. They should be said to be good things for the people.
morphology: Having said that these are the old things the gods of worship should be worshipped in the presence of the people.

sanskrit: apasavyam agnau kṛtvā sarvam āvṛtya vikramam / apasavyena hastena nirvaped udakaṃ bhuvi //
reference: After he has performed (the oblations) in the fire, (and) the whole series of ceremonies in such a manner that they end in the south, let him sprinkle water with his right hand on the spot (where the cakes are to be placed).
baseline: Having covered the whole body with a fire one should wash the body with the hands of the abuser.
morphology: Having covered all the things one should make the abyss in the fire. One should wash the body with the abhyasvāṇī hand and make it clear.

sanskrit: nyupya piṇḍāṃs tatas tāṃs tu prayato vidhipūrvakam / teṣu darbheṣu taṃ hastaṃ nirmṛjyāl lepabhāginām //
reference: Having offered those cakes according to the (prescribed) rule, being pure, let him wipe the same hand with (the roots of) those blades of Kusa grass for the sake of the (three ancestors) who partake of the wipings (lepa).
baseline: The hands should be removed from the sides of the head and the body should be covered with a piece of cloth.
morphology: Having laid down the loincloths one should then use them as per the ritual. One should remove the hands from those walls with a piece of cloth.

sanskrit: ācamyodakparāvṛtya trir āyamya śanair asūn / ṣaḍ ṛtūṃś ca namaskuryāt pitṝn eva ca mantravat //
reference: Having (next) sipped water, turned round (towards the north), and thrice slowly suppressed his breath, (the sacrificer) who knows the sacred texts shall worship (the guardian deities of) the six seasons and the manes.
baseline: Having recited the three hymns acha myodakāra one should offer salutations to the six seasons of the month of śāna asana and the same to the fathers.
morphology: Having recited the hymn acha mya dākārava one should worship the six seasons of the month of śāna asana and the three seasons. One should chant the same mantra for the fathers.

sanskrit: piṇḍebhyas tv alpikāṃ mātrāṃ samādāyānupūrvaśaḥ / tān eva viprān āsīnān vidhivat pūrvam āśayet //
reference: But taking successively very small portions from the cakes, he shall make those seated Brahmana eat them, in accordance with the rule, before (their dinner).
baseline: You should respect the amount of small things in the foreground. The same should be done for the seats and the seats in the past.
morphology: You should respect the quantity of small things in the foreground. The same should be done for the seats and the seats in the past.

sanskrit: dhriyamāṇe tu pitari pūrveṣām eva nirvapet / vipravad vāpi taṃ śrāddhe svakaṃ pitaram āśayet //
reference: But if the (sacrificer's) father is living, he must offer (the cakes) to three remoter (ancestors); or he may also feed his father at the funeral sacrifice as (one of the) Brahmana (guests).
baseline: If the father is to be worshipped in the east he should be purified by the priest. If he is to worship him in the west he has to worship his father.
morphology: If the father is to be worshipped in the east he should be purified. If he is to worship the father in the west then he should worship him and wish his father.

sanskrit: pitā yasya nivṛttaḥ syāj jīvec cāpi pitāmahaḥ / pituḥ sa nāma saṅkīrtya kīrtayet prapitāmaham //
reference: But he whose father is dead, while his grandfather lives, shall, after pronouncing his father's name, mention (that of) his great-grandfather.
baseline: One whose father has retired and who lives in the house of his grandfather should chant the name of his father. He should praise him by chanting the words pāpita.
morphology: The name of the father should be mentioned as pāṭipātā. He should praise his father by chanting the hymn pātmā.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ dattvā tu hasteṣu sapavitraṃ tilodakam / tatpiṇḍāgraṃ prayaccheta svadhaiṣām astv iti bruvan // pāṇibhyāṃ tūpasaṃgṛhya svayam annasya vardhitam / viprāntike pitṝn dhyāyan śanakair upanikṣipet //
reference: Having poured water mixed with sesamum, in which a blade of Kusa grass has been placed, into the hands of the (guests), he shall give (to each) that (above-mentioned) portion of the cake, saying, 'To those, Svadha!' But carrying (the vessel) filled with food with both hands, the (sacrificer) himself shall gently place it before the Brahmanas, meditating on the manes.
baseline: Having given them the sacred sap the tiladaka the sprigs of the sun the leaves of the mouth and the head of the body should be used. Having collected the incense from the water the cow should be made to eat food by itself. Having meditated on the ancestors in the vipranthika the cowherd should be worshipped by the Upanishads.
morphology: Having given them the sacred sāpavitā tilodaka the pitchers the hands the arms the head the limbs the legs the feet the body the heart the mind the stomach the breuva one should collect the ghee and increase the food by himself. One should meditate on the ancestors in the morning and then the cow should be worshipped by the Upanikyas.

sanskrit: ubhayor hastayor muktaṃ yad annam upanīyate / tad vipralumpanty asurāḥ sahasā duṣṭacetasaḥ //
reference: The malevolent Asuras forcibly snatch away that food which is brought without being held with both hands.
baseline: The food should be offered freely to both the hands. The same should be given to the demon suddenly to the evil mind.
morphology: One who is free from both the hands would get food by the same means. Then the evil spirit would suddenly become evil.

sanskrit: upanīya tu tat sarvaṃ śanakaiḥ susamāhitaḥ / pariveṣayeta prayato guṇān sarvān pracodayan //
reference: All this he shall present (to his guests), being pure and attentive, successively invite them to partake of each (dish), proclaiming its qualities.
baseline: All that is offered should be served with the cow and the cow should be well-adjusted. The merits of the service should be encouraged.
morphology: All the qualities should be worshipped by the cow and all the animals should be treated well.

sanskrit: yad yad roceta viprebhyas tat tad dadyād amatsaraḥ / brahmodyāś ca kathāḥ kuryāt pitṝṇām etad īpsitam //
reference: Whatever may please the Brahmanas, let him give without grudging it; let him give riddles from the Veda, for that is agreeable to the manes.
baseline: O Amatsara one who gives to the Brahman should speak to his fathers as he wishes.
morphology: It is said that Amatsara should tell the story of Brahma and his ancestors if he gives what he wants in his anger.

sanskrit: harṣayed brāhmaṇāṃs tuṣṭo bhojayec ca śanaiḥśanaiḥ / annādyenāsakṛc caitān guṇaiś ca paricodayet //
reference: Himself being delighted, let him give delight to the Brahmanas, cause them to partake gradually and slowly (of each dish), and repeatedly invite (them to eat) by (offering) the food and (praising) its qualities.
baseline: The merits of the brahmins should be expressed by the meritorious eating of food and slowly eating food. The virtues of those who eat food and drink food should be described by the priest.
morphology: The merits of the brahmins should be described as joyful enjoyable enjoyment food and enjoyment.

sanskrit: vratastham api dauhitraṃ śrāddhe yatnena bhojayet / kutapaṃ cāsanaṃ dadyāt tilaiś ca vikiren mahīm //
reference: Let him eagerly entertain at a funeral sacrifice a daughter's son, though he be a student, and let him place a Nepal blanket on the on the seat (of each guest), scattering sesamum grains on the ground.
baseline: One should also observe a fast and eat food with diligence. One should give a cup a cup and a piece of rice and sell the rice.
morphology: One should also observe a fast and eat food with diligence. One should give a cup a cup and a piece of rice and sell the rice.

sanskrit: ghrāṇena sūkaro hanti pakṣavātena kukkuṭaḥ / śvā tu dṛṣṭinipātena sparśeṇāvaravarṇajaḥ //
reference: A boar makes (the rite) useless by inhaling the smell (of the offerings), a cock by the air of his wings, a dog by throwing his eye (on them), a low-caste man by touching (them).
baseline: A cow is killed by the smell of a bird a dog by the attack of a parrot a cow by the loss of sight a pigment of colour and a bird by touching it.
morphology: A dog is killed by the smell of a bird a dog by the occurrence of a paralysis and a cow by the loss of sight and touch.

sanskrit: khañjo vā yadi vā kāṇo dātuḥ preṣyo 'pi vā bhavet / hīnātiriktagātro vā tam apy apanayet punaḥ //
reference: If a lame man, a one-eyed man, one deficient in a limb, or one with a redundant limb, be even the servant of the performer (of the Sraddha), he must be removed from that place (where the Sraddha is held).
baseline: A lame man or a poor man should be sent to a donor. He should be stopped from doing so again.
