morphology: A lame man or a poor man should be sent to a charity. He should be stopped again if he is not good enough.

sanskrit: asaṃskṛtapramītānāṃ tyāgināṃ kulayoṣitām / ucchiṣṭaṃ bhāgadheyaṃ syād darbheṣu vikiraś ca yaḥ // uccheṣaṇāṃ bhūmigatam ajihmasyāśaṭhasya ca / dāsavargasya tat pitrye bhāgadheyaṃ pracakṣate //
reference: The remnant (in the dishes), and the portion scattered on Kusa grass, shall be the share of deceased (children) who received not the sacrament (of cremation) and of those who (unjustly) forsook noble wives. They declare the fragments which have fallen on the ground at a (Sraddha) to the manes, to be the share of honest, dutiful servants.
baseline: One who renounces the immaterial property of the poor and those who are in bondage to the poor should be given a share in the property. One who has left behind a share of property in the court would get the share of the property of a slave in the possession of his parents. The share of land and property would be given to a slave.
morphology: One who renounces the immaterial property and shares the property of the poor one who has left the property in the dervices and another who has been left out of the property and the land of the slave class would get the share in the property.

sanskrit: āsapiṇḍakriyākarma dvijāteḥ saṃsthitasya tu / adaivaṃ bhojayec chrāddhaṃ piṇḍam ekaṃ ca nirvapet //
reference: But before the performance of the Sapindikarana, one must feed at the funeral sacrifice in honour of a (recently-) deceased Aryan (one Brahmana) without (making an offering) to the gods, and give one cake only.
baseline: One of the objects should be placed in the same place as the two parts of the body. One piece should be removed from the body after having been thrown into the ground.
morphology: One of the objects should be placed in the same position as the two objects of the body. One of them should be removed from the body after having been thrown into the ground.

sanskrit: sahapiṇḍakriyāyāṃ tu kṛtāyām asya dharmataḥ / anayaivāvṛtā kāryaṃ piṇḍanirvapanaṃ sutaiḥ //
reference: But after the Sapindikarana of the (deceased father) has been performed according to the sacred law, the sons must offer the cakes with those ceremonies, (described above.)
baseline: One should do the same thing in the case of the action of the co-parent. The other action should be done by the sūta.
morphology: One should do the same thing in the case of the joint action of the two parts. The other part of the action should be done by the priest.

sanskrit: śrāddhabhug vṛṣalītalpaṃ tad ahar yo 'dhigacchati / tasyāḥ purīṣe taṃ māsaṃ pitaras tasya śerate //
reference: If the partaker of a Sraddha (-dinner) enters on the same day the bed of a Sudra female, the manes of his (ancestors) will lie during that month in her ordure.
baseline: The one who gives the oblation of the sacred tree of Śrādhbhuga the lotus that which has fallen on his forehead and that which is placed on his head should be worshipped by his father.
morphology: One who has worshipped a cow a bull a small animal or a man who has gone to the place of worship should offer the same to his father.

sanskrit: pṛṣṭvā svaditam ity evaṃ tṛptān ācāmayet tataḥ / ācāntāṃś cānujānīyād abhito ramyatām iti //
reference: Having addressed the question, 'Have you dined well?' (to his guests), let him give water for sipping to them who are satisfied, and dismiss them, after they have sipped water, (with the words) 'Rest either (here or at home)!'
baseline: After having asked for it one should thus offer the contented ones. Then one should say that one would get pleasure from the choice of the person at the end.
morphology: After having asked for it one should make the satisfied persons happy by saying that they would be happy by having the chanjunjani at the end.

sanskrit: svadhāstv ity eva taṃ brūyur brāhmaṇās tadanantaram / svadhākāraḥ parā hy āṣīḥ sarveṣu pitṛkarmasu //
reference: The Brahmana (guests) shall then answer him, 'Let there be Svadha;' for at all rites in honour of the manes the word Svadha is the highest benison.
baseline: The brahmins should be made to bear the same burden as their own. Then the brahmin should bear the burden of his own responsibility.
morphology: The brahmins should be made to bear the same burden as their own. Then the brāhmaṇas should bear the burden of their own duties.

sanskrit: tato bhuktavatāṃ teṣām annaśeṣaṃ nivedayet / yathā brūyus tathā kuryād anujñātas tato dvijaiḥ //
reference: Next let him inform (his guests) who have finished their meal, of the food which remains; with the permission of the Brahmanas let him dispose (of that), as they may direct.
baseline: Then one should offer the leftovers of those grains as per the breuces. As permissible the same should be done by the two brothers.
morphology: Then one should offer the leftovers of those grains as per the breuces. As per the permission of Kuri the same should be offered by the two.

sanskrit: pitrye svaditam ity eva vācyaṃ goṣṭhe tu suśṛtam / saṃpannam ity abhyudaye daive rucitam ity api // aparāhṇas tathā darbhā vāstusaṃpādanaṃ tilāḥ / sṛṣṭir mṛṣṭir dvijāś cāgryāḥ śrāddhakarmasu saṃpadaḥ //
reference: At a (Sraddha) in honour of the manes one must use (in asking of the guests if they are satisfied, the word) svaditam; at a Goshthi-sraddha, (the word) susrutam; at a Vriddhi-sraddha, (the word) sampannam; and at (a rite) in honour of the gods, (the word) rukitam. The afternoon, Kusa grass, the due preparation of the dwelling, sesamum grains, liberality, the careful preparation of the food, and (the company of) distinguished Brahmanas are true riches at all funeral sacrifices.
baseline: One who has given to his parents who is well-off in the church who has prospered in the past and who is pleased with the gods who does not want to get away with the wealth of his wife who earns wealth by the evening who acquires wealth by doing good deeds who creates wealth who gives wealth and earns good fortune.
morphology: One who has given to his parents who has been blessed with wealth in the assembly who is blessed by the gods who enjoys prosperity in the evening who acquires wealth by doing the ritualistic rites of worship who earns wealth by creating wealth and who has acquired wealth by worshipping the gods.

sanskrit: munyannāni payaḥ somo māṃsaṃ yac cānupaskṛtam / aksāralavaṇaṃ caiva prakṛtyā havir ucyate //
reference: The food eaten by hermits in the forest, milk, Soma-juice, meat which is not prepared (with spices), and salt unprepared by art, are called, on account of their nature, sacrificial food.
baseline: One who has not had any meat or drink should eat the meat and drink it. One who does not eat meat and drinks it should be called a hāvir by nature.
morphology: One who consumes the meat of a sage a cow and a cow should be called a havi by nature.

sanskrit: visṛjya brāhmaṇāṃs tāṃs tu niyato vāgyataḥ śuciḥ / dakṣiṇāṃ diśam ākāṅkṣan yācetemān varān pitṝn //
reference: Having dismissed the (invited) Brahmanas, let him, with a concentrated mind, silent and pure, look towards the south and ask these blessings of the manes:
baseline: Having thrown away the brahmins he should be assigned to them. He should be purified. The right direction should be sought by the parents of the bridegroom.
morphology: Having thrown away the brahmins one should make them clean and seek the right direction. One should wish the boons to the fathers.

sanskrit: dātāro no 'bhivardhantāṃ vedāḥ saṃtatir eva ca / śraddhā ca no mā vyagamad bahudeyaṃ ca no 'stv iti //
reference: 'May liberal men abound with us! May (our knowledge of) the Vedas and (our) progeny increase! May faith not forsake us! May we have much to give (to the needy)!'
baseline: There is no belief in the Vedas and the saints nor in the donors nor the gods nor many gods.
morphology: There is no devotion to the Vedas the saints nor to the givers nor much to be given.

sanskrit: piṇḍanirvapaṇaṃ ke cit parastād eva kurvate / vayobhiḥ khādayanty anye prakṣipanty anale 'psu vā //
reference: Some make the offering of the cakes after (the dinner); some cause (them) to be eaten by birds or throw them into fire or into water.
baseline: One who makes the filth of the body from the other side of the earth should eat it with the help of the elders. The other should be thrown into the canal.
morphology: One who makes a painting of a piece of water from the same place and eats it with the help of the old man should throw the other part of the water into the canal.

sanskrit: pativratā dharmapatnī pitṛpūjanatatparā / madhyamaṃ tu tataḥ piṇḍam adyāt samyak sutārthinī // āyuṣmantaṃ sutaṃ sūte yaśomedhāsamanvitam / dhanavantaṃ prajāvantaṃ sāttvikaṃ dhārmikaṃ tathā //
reference: The (sacrificer's) first wife, who is faithful and intent on the worship of the manes, may eat the middle-most cake, (if she be) desirous of bearing a son. (Thus) she will bring forth a son who will be long-lived, famous, intelligent, rich, the father of numerous offspring, endowed with (the quality of) goodness, and righteous.
baseline: One who worships the godly wife the god of righteousness the father the mother the middle then the pinda the sutarīna the sundial the thread the sun the yāsudha the virtuous the noble the righteous the rich the people the wealth and the wealth of the people should be made to be worshipped.
morphology: One should worship the wife of the godly husband the father the wife the mother the middle one the pindā the daughter of the nobleman the son of the sutras and the wife who has been given the yāsodha in a suit for the rest of her life the husband of the rich man the king of the people the god of righteousness the lord of wealth and the king.

sanskrit: praksālya hastāv ācāmya jñātiprāyaṃ prakalpayet / jñātibhyaḥ satkṛtaṃ dattvā bāndhavān api bhojayet //
reference: Having washed his hands and sipped water, let him prepare (food) for his paternal relations and, after giving it to them with due respect, let him feed his maternal relatives also.
baseline: Having opened the hands of the knower one should make a plan for the acquaintance. One should also eat food after giving good deeds to the acquaintances.
morphology: Having opened the hands one should make a request to the acquaintance. One should also eat food after giving good deeds to those who know him.

sanskrit: uccheṣaṇaṃ tu tat tiṣṭhed yāvad viprā visarjitāḥ / tato gṛhabaliṃ kuryād iti dharmo vyavasthitaḥ //
reference: But the remnants shall be left (where they lie) until the Brahmanas have been dismissed; afterwards he shall perform the (daily) domestic Bali-offering; that is a settled (rule of the) sacred law.
baseline: The ritual of offering a house should be arranged in such a way that the parting of the house is removed.
morphology: The ritual of offering a house should be arranged in such a way that if it is removed it remains as if it were thrown away.

sanskrit: havir yac cirarātrāya yac cānantyāya kalpate / pitṛbhyo vidhivad dattaṃ tat pravakṣyāmy aśeṣataḥ //
reference: I will now fully declare what kind of sacrificial food, given to the manes according to the rule, will serve for a long time or for eternity.
baseline: One who has given to the fathers in the prescribed manner the yajna for the night should do it for the whole night.
morphology: One who has given to the fathers in the manner prescribed for the night should do so with the knowledge of the Lord.

sanskrit: tilair vrīhiyavair māṣair adbhir mūlaphalena vā / dattena māsaṃ tṛpyanti vidhivat pitaro nṛnām //
reference: The ancestors of men are satisfied for one month with sesamum grains, rice, barley, masha beans, water, roots, and fruits, which have been given according to the prescribed rule,
baseline: One should worship the mother with the prasadam or the fruit of the root of the animal. The father should offer the mother and the sons with the māsadam.
morphology: One should worship the mother of the sons of the king by offering a piece of meat or a piece with the fruit of the mother the father the wife the mother and the children.

sanskrit: ṣaṇmāsāṃś chāgamāṃsena pārṣatena ca sapta vai / aṣṭāv enasya māṃsena rauraveṇa navaiva tu //
reference: Six months with the flesh of kids, seven with that of spotted deer, eight with that of the black antelope, but nine with that of the (deer called) Ruru,
baseline: The six months should be divided into seven parts with the meat of goats and the eight parts with its meat.
morphology: The six months should be divided into seven parts with the meat of a goat and the eight parts with its meat.

sanskrit: daśamāsāṃs tu tṛpyanti varāhamahiṣāmiṣaiḥ / śaśakūrmayos tu māṃsena māsān ekādaśaiva tu // saṃvatsaraṃ tu gavyena payasā pāyasena ca / vārdhrīṇasasya māṃsena tṛptir dvādaśavārṣikī //
reference: Ten months they are satisfied with the meat of boars and buffaloes, but eleven months indeed with that of hares and tortoises, One year with cow-milk and milk-rice; from the flesh of a long-eared white he-goat their satisfaction endures twelve years.
baseline: The ten months are given to the bridegroom the eight months to the wife the eleven months to be spent on meat the year to be paid with cow money and money the twelve years of the marriage with the meat of the bride the twelfth year of the life of the wife and the rest of the body.
morphology: The ten months are given to the bridegroom mother wife mother and children. The eleven months are provided with meat. The year is provided with cow money and money. The twelve years are provided by the bride and the meat.

sanskrit: kālaśākaṃ mahāśalkāḥ khaṅgalohāmiṣaṃ madhu / ānantyāyaiva kalpyante munyannāni ca sarvaśaḥ //
reference: The (vegetable called) Kalasaka, (the fish called) Mahasalka, the flesh of a rhinoceros and that of a red goat, and all kinds of food eaten by hermits in the forest serve for an endless time.
baseline: The kālāśaka mahāśalaka khāngālohāmiṣa honey ananta and the munyāṇas are worshipped everywhere.
morphology: The kālāśaka mahāśalaka khāngala lohāmi honey ananta and munyāna are worshipped everywhere.

sanskrit: yat kiṃ cin madhunā miśraṃ pradadyāt tu trayodaśīm / tad apy akṣayam eva syād varṣāsu ca maghāsu ca //
reference: Whatever (food), mixed with honey, one gives on the thirteenth lunar day in the rainy season under the asterism of Maghah, that also procures endless (satisfaction).
baseline: If the mixture is given with honey the same should be done in the thirty-fourth year in the month of May and in the months of May.
morphology: If the mixture is given with honey the amount should be thirty three times equal to the amount of the same in ten years and in eight years.

sanskrit: api naḥ sa kule bhūyād yo no dadyāt trayodaśīm / pāyasaṃ madhusarpirbhyāṃ prāk chāye kuñjarasya ca //
reference: 'May such a man (the manes say) be born in our family who will give us milk-rice, with honey and clarified butter, on the thirteenth lunar day (of the month of Bhadrapada) and (in the afternoon) when the shadow of an elephant falls towards the east.'
baseline: And if one does not eat in the garden one should give thirty three ounces of water to the cow before the offering of honey and the offering made of cow dung.
morphology: And if one does not eat in the well one should give thirty-three ounces of water honey and a spoonful of honey before the sunrise.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇapakṣe daśamyādau varjayitvā caturdaśīm / śrāddhe praśastās tithayo yathaitā na tathetarāḥ //
reference: The days of the dark half of the month, beginning with the tenth, but excepting the fourteenth, are recommended for a funeral sacrifice; (it is) not thus (with) the others.
baseline: The fourteenth day should be avoided on the tenth day after having been placed on the Krishna side. The date of the worship should not be fixed as it is.
morphology: The fourteenth day should be set aside for the tenth day on the Krishna side and the date should be fixed at the widest in the month of Śrādha.

sanskrit: vasūn vadanti tu pitṝn rudrāṃś caiva pitāmahān / prapitāmahāṃs tathādityān śrutir eṣā sanātanī //
reference: They call (the manes of) fathers Vasus, (those of) grandfathers Rudras, and (those of) great-grandfathers Adityas; thus (speaks) the eternal Veda.
baseline: The sage Vāsuṇa says that the sons of Rudra Rudra and Paṭamāṇa should be worshipped. The sons of Sūratī are worshipped by the sages.
morphology: The sons of Vasu are said to be the sons of Rudrāma Rudra Paṭamāṇu Pratipita Mahāṇa Dāyātī Sūrtī.

sanskrit: caturtham āyuṣo bhāgam uṣitvādyaṃ gurau dvijāḥ / dvitīyam āyuṣo bhāgaṃ kṛtadāro gṛhe vaset //
reference: Having dwelt with a teacher during the fourth part of (a man's) life, a Brahmana shall live during the second quarter (of his existence) in his house, after he has wedded a wife.
baseline: One who has completed the fourth ayūsha part should be worshipped by the preceptor the teacher the second ayuṣa part and the one who has done the fourth abhyas part should reside at home.
morphology: One who has completed the fourth ayūsha part the preceptor the teacher the second ayuṣa part and the master should live in the house.

sanskrit: ṛtāmṛtābhyāṃ jīvet tu mṛtena pramṛtena vā / satyānṛtābhyām api vā na śvavṛttyā kadā cana //
reference: He may subsist by Rita (truth), and Amrita (ambrosia), or by Mrita (death) and by Pramrita (what causes many deaths); or even by (the mode) called Satyanrita (a mixture of truth and falsehood), but never by Svavritti (a dog's mode of life).
baseline: One should never live by the death of the deceased or by the immortality of the dead or by any of the virtuous deeds.
morphology: One should never live by the death of the deceased or by the immortality of the dead or by any of the truthful deeds.

sanskrit: satyānṛtaṃ tu vāṇijyaṃ tena caivāpi jīvyate / sevā śvavṛttir ākhyātā tasmāt tāṃ parivarjayet //
reference: But trade and (money-lending) are Satyanrita, even by that one may subsist. Service is called Svavritti; therefore one should avoid it.
baseline: A person who does not know the truth and who does business should be called a servant. He should be converted into a servant by that.
morphology: A man who does good work should be called a servant of the king. He should be converted into a merchant.

sanskrit: ṣaṭkarmaiko bhavaty eṣāṃ tribhir anyaḥ pravartate / dvābhyām ekaś caturthas tu brahmasattreṇa jīvati //
reference: One of these follows six occupations, another subsists by three, one by two, but the fourth lives by the Brahmasattra.
baseline: One of the four living beings is known to be living by the Brahman. One of these three forms is known as the Brahma.
morphology: One of the three karmākas should follow the same path as you. One of these two should live with the four elements of Brahman.

sanskrit: vartayaṃś ca śiloñchābhyām agnihotraparāyaṇaḥ / iṣṭīḥ pārvāyaṇāntīyāḥ kevalā nirvapet sadā //
reference: He who maintains himself by picking up grains and ears of corn, must be always intent on (the performance of) the Agnihotra, and constantly offer those Ishtis only, which are prescribed for the days of the conjunction and opposition (of the moon), and for the solstices.
baseline: The fire should always be lit with the rods stones and stones and the fire should be made of water.
morphology: One should always keep the fire the fire and the fire in the form of a stone. One should keep the bricks the water and the water in the ground.

sanskrit: na lokavṛttaṃ varteta vṛttihetoḥ kathaṃ cana / ajihmām aśathāṃ śuddhāṃ jīved brāhmaṇajīvikām //
reference: Let him never, for the sake of subsistence, follow the ways of the world; let him live the pure, straightforward, honest life of a Brahmana.
baseline: One who does not walk in the circle of the world and does not practice the practice of the abode of the unbelievers should live a life of a brahmin.
morphology: One who does not walk in the circle of the people and does not practice the practice of the abode of the unbelievers should live a life of a brahmin.

sanskrit: saṃtoṣaṃ param āsthāya sukhārthī saṃyato bhavet / saṃtoṣamūlaṃ hi sukhaṃ duḥkhamūlaṃ viparyayaḥ //
reference: He who desires happiness must strive after a perfectly contented disposition and control himself; for happiness has contentment for its root, the root of unhappiness is the contrary (disposition).
baseline: One who is satisfied with happiness and trust in others should be restrained. The source of happiness is the source of sorrow.
morphology: One who is satisfied with happiness and trust in others one who is content with the source of happiness one should be contented with the cause of sorrow and vice versa.

sanskrit: ato 'nyatamayā vṛttyā jīvaṃs tu snātako dvijaḥ / svargāyuṣyayaśasyāni vratāṇīmāni dhārayet //
reference: A Brahmana, who is a Snataka and subsists by one of the (above-mentioned) modes of life, must discharge the (following) duties which secure heavenly bliss, long life, and fame.
baseline: The two masters of the living beings should thus be endowed with the vratāṇis of heavenly life and life.
morphology: The master of the living entity should thus possess the vratāṇis of heavenly life and life.

sanskrit: vedoditaṃ svakaṃ karma nityaṃ kuryād atandritaḥ / tad dhi kurvan yathāśakti prāpnoti paramāṃ gatim //
reference: Let him, untired, perform daily the rites prescribed for him in the Veda; for he who performs those according to his ability, attains to the highest state.
baseline: The veda should be performed with its own kārma always and with the mind. The power obtained by doing that is the ultimate movement.
morphology: Having performed the Vedas one should always perform his own deeds in the innermost sense. One attains the ultimate speed as soon as one acquires the power.

sanskrit: nehetārthān prasaṅgena na viruddhena karmaṇā / na vidyamāneṣv artheṣu nārtyām api yatas tataḥ //
reference: Whether he be rich or even in distress, let him not seek wealth through pursuits to which men cleave, nor by forbidden occupations, nor (let him accept presents) from any (giver whosoever he may be).
baseline: One should not act contrary to the meaning of the word or the meaning which is not there. Then one should not do evil deeds.
morphology: One should not act against others in the context of the meaning of the word or the meaning or the other.

sanskrit: indriyārtheṣu sarveṣu na prasajyeta kāmataḥ / atiprasaktiṃ caiteṣāṃ manasā saṃnivartayet //
reference: Let him not, out of desire (for enjoyments), attach himself to any sensual pleasures, and let him carefully obviate an excessive attachment to them, by (reflecting on their worthlessness in) his heart.
baseline: All the sensory objects should not be given away by desire. The mind should be transformed into a state of overexertion.
morphology: All the senses should not be spread by the desire. The mind of those who are overly interested should be changed.

sanskrit: sarvān parityajed arthān svādhyāyasya virodhinaḥ / yathā tathādhyāpayaṃs tu sā hy asya kṛtakṛtyatā //
reference: Let him avoid all (means of acquiring) wealth which impede the study of the Veda; (let him maintain himself) anyhow, but study, because that (devotion to the Veda-study secures) the realisation of his aims.
baseline: He should do the same thing as those who are against his own practice by abandoning everything.
morphology: He should do the same thing as those who oppose his studies by abandoning everything.

sanskrit: buddhivṛddhikarāṇy āśu dhanyāni ca hitāni ca / nityaṃ śāstrāṇy avekṣeta nigamāṃś caiva vaidikān //
reference: Let him daily pore over those Institutes of science which soon give increase of wisdom, those which teach the acquisition of wealth, those which are beneficial (for other worldly concerns), and likewise over the Nigamas which explain the Veda.
baseline: One should always observe the scriptures in the fields and observe the conduct of the Vedic disciples.
morphology: One should always observe the scriptures in the field and observe the Vedic practices for the benefit of the people.

sanskrit: jñānenaivāpare viprā yajanty etair makhaiḥ sadā / jñānamūlāṃ kriyām eṣāṃ paśyanto jñānacakṣuṣā //
reference: Other Brahmanas, seeing with the eye of knowledge that the performance of those rites has knowledge for its root, always perform them through knowledge alone.
baseline: The eyes of the wise man always look at these things with the forehead the root of knowledge and the actions of the learned man.
morphology: The eyes of the wise man always look at these things with the eyeballs of knowledge.

sanskrit: agnihotraṃ ca juhuyād ādyante dyuniśoḥ sadā / darśena cārdhamāsānte paurṇāmāsena caiva hi //
reference: A Brahmana shall always offer the Agnihotra at the beginning or at the end of the day and of the night, and the Darsa and Paurnamasa (Ishtis) at the end of each half-month,
baseline: One should always worship the fire god and the goddess of fire at the end of the fourteenth month in the month of Purnima.
morphology: One should always worship the fire god in the fourteenth month of the lunar month with the diṣṇīśa at the end of the full moon.

sanskrit: āsanāśanaśayyābhir adbhir mūlaphalena vā / nāsya kaś cid vased gehe śaktito 'narcito 'tithiḥ // pāṣāṇḍino vikarmasthān baiḍālavratikāñ śaṭhān / haitukān bakavṛttīṃś ca vāṅgātreṇāpi nārcayet //
reference: No guest must stay in his house without being honoured, according to his ability, with a seat, food, a couch, water, or roots and fruits. Let him not honour, even by a greeting, heretics, men who follow forbidden occupations, men who live like cats, rogues, logicians, (arguing against the Veda,) and those who live like herons.
baseline: One who has destroyed the seat or the ground with the fruit of the ground and has destroyed it would have destroyed it. One who is sitting on the ground would have to destroy the power of the enemy. The enemy would have killed those who are in the position of the vikrāma the enemy the king of the war the demon of the cow the god of war and the king who is in the place of war should be killed with the sword.
morphology: One should not destroy the seat or the ground with the fruit of the ground. One should destroy it with the power of the enemy. The enemy should destroy the enemy with the weapons of war. The enemies should be killed with the weapon of war the enemy of war and the enemy the king of war should be destroyed with the sword.

sanskrit: vedavidyāvratasnātāñ śrotriyān gṛhamedhinaḥ / pūjayed dhavyakavyena viparītāṃś ca varjayet //
reference: Those who have become Snatakas after studying the Veda, or after completing their vows, (and) householders, who are Srotriyas, one must worship by (gifts of food) sacred to gods and manes, but one must avoid those who are different.
baseline: One should worship the disciples of the house the hearers the teachers of the Vedas the masters of the houses the priest the king of the earth and the opposites should be forbidden.
morphology: Those who study the Vedas teach the scriptures baptize the hearers worshipers of houses worship and worship the gods.

sanskrit: rājato dhanam anvicchet saṃsīdan snātakaḥ kṣudhā / yājyāntevāsinor vāpi na tv anyata iti sthitiḥ //
reference: A Snataka who pines with hunger, may beg wealth of a king, of one for whom he sacrifices, and of a pupil, but not of others; that is a settled rule.
baseline: The king should seek wealth and the graduates should be hungry. The king who lives in the inner kingdom should not go abroad.
morphology: A graduate who seeks wealth from a king would be starved. If he does not get it from the king he would not be able to get it.

sanskrit: na sīdet snātako vipraḥ kṣudhā śaktaḥ kathaṃ cana / na jīrṇamalavadvāsā bhavec ca vibhave sati //
reference: A Snataka who is able (to procure food) shall never waste himself with hunger, nor shall he wear old or dirty clothes, if he possesses property.
baseline: The master should not suffer from hunger and power. He should not be illiterate. One should not get ill.
morphology: The master should not be hungry hungry strong weak and illiterate.

sanskrit: kḷptakeśanakhaśmaśrur dāntaḥ śuklāmbaraḥ śuciḥ / svādhyāye caiva yuktaḥ syān nityam ātmahiteṣu ca // vaiṇavīṃ dhārayed yaṣṭiṃ sodakaṃ ca kamaṇḍalum / yajñopavītaṃ vedaṃ ca śubhaṃ raukme ca kuṇḍale //
reference: Keeping his hair, nails, and beard clipped, subduing his passions by austerities, wearing white garments and (keeping himself) pure, he shall be always engaged in studying the Veda and (such acts as are) conducive to his welfare. He shall carry a staff of bamboo, a pot full of water, a sacred string, a bundle of Kusa grass, and (wear) two bright golden ear-rings.
baseline: One who gives a piece of stone with the garland of kārptakāṣa a shloka with the shlokāmbara in his hands a saṇa with the savaṇa in his studies one with the ātma in his body one who carries the vaṇavīna string a yasti a soda a lotus a veda an auspicious scripture and a kundala should be offered to him.
morphology: One who gives a piece of stone with the garland of kārptakāṣa a shlokāmbara with the saviour in his studies one who is always armed with the spirit a string of vainva a stick a bow a lotus a veda a sacred vessel and a kundala should be placed in the temple.

sanskrit: nekṣetodyantam ādityaṃ nāstaṃ yāntaṃ kadā cana / nopasṛṣṭaṃ na vāristhaṃ na madhyaṃ nabhaso gatam //
reference: Let him never look at the sun, when he sets or rises, is eclipsed or reflected in water, or stands in the middle of the sky.
baseline: One should not eat food till the time of the fire. One should never eat food without eating food. One does not eat meat or eat food in the middle of the night.
morphology: One should never eat food till the time of the fire nor eat food nor drink water nor go to the middle.

sanskrit: nāñjayantīṃ svake netre na cābhyaktām anāvṛtām / na paśyet prasavantīṃ ca tejaskāmo dvijottamaḥ //
reference: A Brahmana who desires energy must not look at (a woman) who applies collyrium to her eyes, has anointed or uncovered herself or brings forth (a child).
baseline: One who does not have the right to get a baby and does not want to get an infant should not open his eyes. One who has not had childbirth should not get a child born with a penis.
morphology: One who does not get the eye eye nose mouth eye etc. and does not open them does not give birth to children and is blessed with two sons.

sanskrit: na phālakṛṣṭe na jale na cityāṃ na ca parvate / na jīrṇadevāyatane na valmīke kadā cana //
reference: Nor on ploughed land, in water, on an altar of bricks, on a mountain, on the ruins of a temple, nor ever on an ant-hill,
baseline: There is neither water nor choice in the form of a stone nor mountain nor a place for the worship of a dead god.
morphology: There is neither water nor choice in the temple of the goddess Phalakrṣta nor mountain. Neither the goddess of the dead nor the goddess Valmiki should ever be worshipped.

morphology: One who dwells in a village without religion would not suffer from disease. One who lives in a mountain would not get any disease.

morphology: One should not dwell in the kingdom of the Shudras nor in the kingdoms of the pāśandīs and the king of the nādharmikas.

morphology: One should always recite the chants of Brahma the chords of Brahman the two syllables of the scriptures the couplets of the two hymns the disciples should be taught the kurvaṇa scriptures in the night in the ear in the ears and in the hands of the students in the evening and in a group of the pāṇas in the morning.

sanskrit: etāṃs tv abhyuditān vidyād yadā prāduṣkṛtāgniṣu / tadā vidyād anadhyāyam anṛtau cābhradarśane // nirghāte bhūmicalane jyotiṣāṃ copasarjane / etān ākālikān vidyād anadhyāyān ṛtāv api // prāduṣkṛteṣv agniṣu tu vidyutstanitaniḥsvane / sajyotiḥ syād anadhyāyaḥ śeṣe rātrau yathā divā //
reference: When one perceives these (phenomena) all together (in the twilight), after the sacred fires have been made to blaze (for the performance of the Agnihotra), then one must know the recitation of the Veda to be forbidden, and also when clouds appear out of season. On (the occasion of) a preternatural sound from the sky, (of) an earthquake, and when the lights of heaven are surrounded by a halo, let him know that (the Veda-study must be) stopped until the same hour (on the next day), even if (these phenomena happen) in the (rainy) season.
baseline: When you have learned these things in the fire that has been lit then you should teach them in the morning in the evening in evening when you have seen the light of the sky when walking on the ground when moving the lights in night when doing the chowkidarshana when making the light move when having done the study of the sun when the light is not lighted in the night after having made the light spread in the open you should learn these things and when you do the study you get the knowledge of the light.
morphology: When you have learned these things in the fire which has been lit up then the knowledge should be given to the disciple to the charioteer and to the astrologer to conduct the earth in the night to light the lights to make the discard of the fire to teach the disciples in the morning to spread the light in the evening to give electricity and light to the children of the sun.

sanskrit: nityānadhyāya eva syād grāmeṣu nagareṣu ca / dharmanaipuṇyakāmānāṃ pūtigandhe ca sarvadā //
reference: For those who wish to acquire exceedingiy great merit, a continual interruption of the Veda-study (is prescribed) in villages and in towns, and (the Veda-study must) always (cease) when any kind of foul smell (is perceptible).
baseline: One should always observe the preceptor Nityāṇa in the villages and cities. One should do good deeds of righteousness skill and devotion.
morphology: One should always worship the god Nityāṇa in the villages and cities. One should worship the virtues virtues and virtues.

sanskrit: antargataśave grāme vṛṣalasya ca sannidhau / anadhyāyo rudyamāne samavāye janasya ca //
reference: In a village where a corpse lies, in the presence of a (man who lives as unrighteously as a) Sudra, while (the sound of) weeping (is heard), and in a crowd of men the (recitation of the Veda must be) stopped.
baseline: One who is in the village and the bull in the area should be present in the presence of the bull and one who is sitting in the company should not be heard.
morphology: One who is in the village and in the presence of a bull one who is sitting in the company of the people in the city and the other in the middle of the country should be worshipped.

sanskrit: pratigṛhya dvijo vidvān ekoddiṣṭasya ketanam / tryahaṃ na kīrtayed brahma rājño rāhoś ca sūtake //
reference: A learned Brahmana shall not recite the Veda during three days, when he has accepted an invitation to a (funeral rite) in honour of one ancestor (ekoddishta), or when the king has become impure through a birth or death in his family (sutaka), or when Rahu by an eclipse makes the moon impure.
baseline: The king of Brahma Rahos and Sutaka should be worshipped twice. The king should not be praised.
morphology: The king of Brahma and Rahośa are not known to be wise.

sanskrit: śayānaḥ prauḍhapādaś ca kṛtvā caivāvasakthikām / nādhīyītāmiṣaṃ jagdhvā sūtakānnādyam eva ca // nīhāre bāṇaśabde ca saṃdhyayor eva cobhayoḥ / amāvāsyācaturdaśyoḥ paurṇamāsyaṣṭakāsu ca //
reference: While lying on a bed, while his feet are raised (on a bench), while he sits on his hams with a cloth tied round his knees, let him not study, nor when he has eaten meat or food given by a person impure on account of a birth or a death, Nor during a fog, nor while the sound of arrows is audible, nor during both the twilights, nor on the new-moon day, nor on the fourteenth and the eighth (days of each half-month), nor on the full-moon day.
baseline: Having laid down the feet and having matured the feet one should offer the saiva saktika nādhīya māsī śutaka kāna nīrā nihara arrow sādhyā pāṇimāvāśa pūrṇimasvatrā and sāktaka on the full moon.
morphology: Having laid down the feet and having matured the feet one should offer the saiva saktika nādhi mīsā jākhā sutaka kāna nīrā arrow sambhā pūrṇimāśa māsvā mūrṣṇī and śvāda.

sanskrit: amāvāsyā guruṃ hanti śiṣyaṃ hanti caturdaśī / brahmāṣṭakapaurṇamāsyau tasmāt tāḥ parivarjayet //
reference: The new-moon day destroys the teacher, the fourteenth (day) the pupil, the eighth and the full-moon days (destroy all remembrance of) the Veda; let him therefore avoid (reading on) those (days).
baseline: One who kills a disciple on the fourteenth day of the new moon and then kills the master should convert them to the month of brahmāṣṭaka pūrna.
morphology: One who kills the master with the new moon and kills the disciple with the fourteenth month of the month of Brahma Astakāpūrna should convert them.

sanskrit: pāṃsuvarṣe diśāṃ dāhe gomāyuvirute tathā / śvakharoṣṭre ca ruvati paṅktau ca na paṭhed dvijaḥ // nādhīyīta śmaśānānte grāmānte govraje 'pi vā / vasitvā maithunaṃ vāsaḥ śrāddhikaṃ pratigṛhya ca //
reference: A Brahmana shall not recite (the Veda) during a dust-storm, nor while the sky is preternaturally red, nor while jackals howl, nor while the barking of dogs, the braying of donkeys, or the grunting of camels (is heard), nor while (he is seated) in a company. Let him not study near a burial-ground, nor near a village, nor in a cow-pen, nor dressed in a garment which he wore during conjugal intercourse, nor after receiving a present at a funeral sacrifice.
baseline: One who does not go into a row should do so in the morning and evening. One who has not gone into the middle of the night should do it in the evening and then go to the other side of the house. One should not do it at the end of the funeral or in the village or in a cow shed. One would live in a place where there is no intercourse and would have it after having worshipped.
morphology: One should not go into a row in the direction of the cow in the year of the pawn and one should go to the cow on the day of the attack. One who does not go out in the line of the sword should not do so. One should go into the village and live in a cow shed at the end of the cremation. One would live in the village or have sex with a cow and live with it and worship it.

sanskrit: prāṇi vā yadi vāprāṇi yat kiṃ cic chrāddhikaṃ bhavet / tad ālabhyāpy anadhyāyaḥ pāṇyāsyo hi dvijaḥ smṛtaḥ //
reference: Be it an animal or a thing inanimate, whatever be the (gift) at a Sraddha, let him not, having just accepted it, recite the Veda; for the hand of a Brahmana is his mouth.
baseline: If any animal is found to be more than three times the amount of water should be given to it.
morphology: If any animal is found to be more than four times the number of its members should be calculated. Then it should be remembered by the priest.

sanskrit: corair upadrute grāme saṃbhrame cāgnikārite / ākālikam anadhyāyaṃ vidyāt sarvādbhuteṣu ca //
reference: When the village has been beset by robbers, and when an alarm has been raised by fire, let him know that (the Veda-study must be) interrupted until the same hour (on the next day), and on (the occurrence of) all portents.
baseline: One who has committed a theft or mischief in a village one who has made a fire in the village and one who is not aware of the incident should be punished with the same punishment.
morphology: One who has committed a theft or mischief in a village one who has made a fire in the village and one who does not have knowledge of the time and all the enemies should be punished.

sanskrit: nādhīyītāśvam ārūḍho na vṛkṣaṃ na ca hastinam / na nāvaṃ na kharaṃ noṣṭraṃ neriṇastho na yānagaḥ //
reference: Let him not recite the Veda on horseback, nor on a tree, nor on an elephant, nor in a boat (or ship), nor on a donkey, nor on camel, nor standing on barren ground, nor riding in a carriage,
baseline: Neither a tree nor an elephant nor a fort nor an ox or a ship nor any other vehicle should be placed in the front.
morphology: One should not climb a tree or a elephant or a boat or a ship or a caravan or a horse or a bull or a cow or a dog or a man with a neck and a neck.

sanskrit: na vivāde na kalahe na senāyāṃ na saṃgare / na bhuktamātre nājīrṇe na vamitvā na śuktake //
reference: Nor during a verbal altercation, nor during a mutual assault, nor in a camp, nor during a battle, nor when he has just eaten, nor during an indigestion, nor after vomiting, nor with sour eructations,
baseline: There is neither strife nor strife in the army nor in the company of the enemy. Neither the mother of the victim nor the mother is destroyed nor the son of a sūkta.
morphology: There is no dispute in the army there is no strife in the war in the battle there are no quarrels in the company there will be no loss in the mother and there will not be any misfortune in the fight.

sanskrit: atithiṃ cānanujñāpya mārute vāti vā bhṛśam / rudhire ca srute gātrāc chastreṇa ca parikṣate // sāmadhvanāv ṛgyajuṣī nādhīyīta kadā cana / vedasyādhītya vāpy antam āraṇyakam adhītya ca //
reference: Nor without receiving permission from a guest (who stays in his house), nor while the wind blows vehemently, nor while blood flows from his body, nor when he is wounded by a weapon. Let him never recite the Rig-veda or the Yagur-veda while the Saman (melodies) are heard; (let him stop all Veda-study for a day and a night) after finishing a Veda or after reciting an Aranyaka.
baseline: Having accepted the offer made by the host one would get a sword or a sword. One would get the sword from the ground and would get it from the roof of the pitchers. The sound of the same sound would be heard from the king. When the sound of Śāmā should be heard by the lord of the Vedas one should enter the end of the temple and take it.
morphology: After having accepted the offer made by the host one should enter the gate or the fire. One would see the ghat with a piece of cloth on the ground. One should make the sound of the sāmādvāna sound like the voice of the ragyajuṣi. One will never be able to reach the end of the veda. One has to enter the arranyaka.

sanskrit: etad vidvanto vidvāṃsas trayīniṣkarṣam anvaham / kramataḥ pūrvam abhyasya paścād vedam adhīyate //
reference: Knowing this, the learned daily repeat first in due order the essence of the three (Vedas) and afterwards the (text of the) Veda.
baseline: The veda should be recited after having been recited three times by the learned scholars in the previous series.
morphology: The veda should be recited in the following order after having been studied three times in the past.

sanskrit: paśumaṇḍūkamārjāra- śvasarpanakulākhubhiḥ / antarāgamane vidyād anadhyāyam aharniśam //
reference: Know that (the Veda-study must be) interrupted for a day and a night, when cattle, a frog, a cat, a dog, a snake, an ichneumon, or a rat pass between (the teacher and his pupil).
baseline: One should learn the lesson on the penetration of animals snakes and spiders.
morphology: One should learn the lessons of the animal the cow the snake the spiders the axe the bow the arrow and the bow.

sanskrit: dvāv eva varjayen nityam anadhyāyau prayatnataḥ / svādhyāyabhūmiṃ cāśuddham ātmānaṃ cāśuciṃ dvijaḥ //
reference: Let a twice-born man always carefully interrupt the Veda-study on two (occasions, viz.) when the place where he recites is impure, and when he himself is unpurified.
baseline: One should avoid the same two things with constant effort in the next two chapters. One should teach the land to be pure one should purify the soul and one should be clean.
morphology: One should avoid the two things by constantly trying to study the land and purify the soul.

sanskrit: madhyaṃdine 'rdharātre ca śrāddhaṃ bhuktvā ca sāmiṣam / saṃdhyayor ubhayoś caiva na seveta catuṣpatham //
reference: At midday and at midnight, after partaking of meat at a funeral dinner, and in the two twilights let him not stay long on a cross-road.
baseline: One should worship at midnight in the middle of the day and pay obeisance at night. One should not serve the four paths in the evening and evening.
morphology: Having performed the ritual at midnight midday evening evening and evening one should not serve the four paths.

sanskrit: udvartanam apasnānaṃ viṇmūtre raktam eva ca / śleśmaniṣṭhyūtavāntāni nādhitiṣṭhet tu kāmataḥ //
reference: Let him not step intentionally on things used for cleansing the body, on water used for a bath, on urine or ordure, on blood, on mucus, and on anything spat out or vomited.
baseline: Oudvārtana ablution bathing blood in the white thread goodness piety and the end of the body should be worshipped with lust.
morphology: Oudvārtana ablution bathing blood in the outer part of the body good conduct piety and other things should be done with the desire.

sanskrit: vairiṇaṃ nopaseveta sahāyaṃ caiva vairiṇaḥ / adhārmikaṃ taskaraṃ ca parasyaiva ca yoṣitaṃ //
reference: Let him not show particular attention to an enemy, to the friend of an enemy, to a wicked man, to a thief, or to the wife of another man.
baseline: The enemy should seek help in the absence of the enemy. The enemy would be a traitor a thief and a woman in public.
morphology: The enemy should not be served by the enemy. The enemy would be helped by the king. The evildoer would be caught by the thieves in public.

sanskrit: na hīdṛśam anāyuṣyaṃ loke kiṃ cana vidyate / yādṛśaṃ puruṣasyeha paradāropasevanam //
reference: For in this world there is nothing so detrimental to long life as criminal conversation with another man's wife.
baseline: There is no such thing as a man who does not live a lifetime. He should serve others as a husband.
morphology: There is no such thing as a man who does not live a lifetime.

sanskrit: kṣatriyaṃ caiva sarpaṃ ca brāhmaṇaṃ ca bahuśrutam / nāvamanyeta vai bhūṣṇuḥ kṛśān api kadā cana //
reference: Let him who desires prosperity, indeed, never despise a Kshatriya, a snake, and a learned Brahmana, be they ever so feeble.
baseline: The kshatriyas serpents brahmins and Brahmins are considered to be the most virtuous. In the same way Lord Śuṇu is considered to have been the king of the krsna.
morphology: The Kshatriyas the cowherds serpents Brahmins and many others are considered to be noble. In the same way Lord Śrīna and Kṛṣa are not known to be evil.

sanskrit: nātmānam avamanyeta purvābhir asamṛddhibhiḥ / ā mṛtyoḥ śriyam anvicchen naināṃ manyeta durlabhām //
reference: Let him not despise himself on account of former failures; until death let him seek fortune, nor despair of gaining it.
baseline: O son of a man who has sought death and has sought it should be considered as rare.
morphology: Having sought the death of a srīya one should consider the nāṇa as rare. One would not be able to do so.

sanskrit: satyaṃ brūyāt priyaṃ brūyān na brūyāt satyam apriyam / priyaṃ ca nānṛtaṃ brūyād eṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ //
reference: Let him say what is true, let him say what is pleasing, let him utter no disagreeable truth, and let him utter no agreeable falsehood; that is the eternal law.
baseline: One who does not know the truth and does not love the breuyas does not hate the truth. One who is not fond of the brauyas would not be able to do so.
morphology: One who does not know the truth and does not love the breuyas does not hate the truth does no love and does no evil. This is the eternal dharma.

sanskrit: bhadraṃ bhadram iti brūyād bhadram ity eva vā vadet / śuṣkavairaṃ vivādaṃ ca na kuryāt kena cit saha //
reference: (What is) well, let him call well, or let him say 'well' only; let him not engage in a useless enmity or dispute with anybody.
baseline: One should say that one who is good or brave should not engage in a dry fight or dispute with the enemy.
morphology: One should say that one who is good or noble should not engage in a dispute with the enemy. One should not argue with the king.

sanskrit: hīnāṅgān atiriktāṅgān vidyāhīnān vayo'dhikān / rūpadraviṇahīnāṃś ca jātihīnāṃś ca nākṣipet //
reference: Let him not insult those who have redundant limbs or are deficient in limbs, nor those destitute of knowledge, nor very aged men, nor those who have no beauty or wealth, nor those who are of low birth.
baseline: Those who have weak limbs those who have no knowledge those without knowledge and those who are of advanced age should be destroyed. Those who do not have the form the fluid the caste and the poor should be killed.
morphology: Those who have weak limbs those who have no knowledge those without knowledge and those who are of advanced age should be destroyed. Those who do not have the form the form and the caste should be killed.

sanskrit: na spṛśet pāṇinocchiṣṭo vipro gobrāhmaṇānalāṇ / na cāpi paśyed aśuciḥ sustho jyotirgaṇān divā //
reference: A Brahmana who is impure must not touch with his hand a cow, a Brahmana, or fire; nor, being in good health, let him look at the luminaries in the sky, while he is impure.
baseline: One who does not touch the water does not want to drink water is a cow a cow and a cow. One who is not defiled and is not fit should give light.
morphology: One who does not touch the water and does not want to drink it one who does nothing for the protection of the cow and the cow should not touch it and one who is not clean should not give it.

sanskrit: anāturaḥ svāni khāni na spṛśed animittataḥ / romāṇi ca rahasyāni sarvāṇy eva vivarjayet // maṅgalācārayuktaḥ syāt prayatātmā jitendriyaḥ / japec ca juhuyāc caiva nityam agnim atandritaḥ //
reference: Except when sick he must not touch the cavities (of the body) without a reason, and he must avoid (to touch) the hair on the secret (parts). Let him eagerly follow the (customs which are) auspicious and the rule of good conduct, be careful of purity, and control all his organs, let him mutter (prayers) and, untired, daily offer oblations in the fire.
baseline: Anāṭura should not touch his own body without touching it. The mysteries of the Romans should be revealed to everyone. One who practices good conduct should always chant the hymn jīnitrāya jāpēchā and jūhu. One should always keep the fire in his heart.
morphology: Anatura should not touch his own body or body and avoid all the mysteries of the Romans. One should try to be virtuous. The spirit should always chant jyotīrāya jāpēchā and jūhu fire and fire.

sanskrit: vedam evābhyasen nityaṃ yathākālam atandritaḥ / taṃ hy asyāhuḥ paraṃ dharmam upadharmo 'nya ucyate //
reference: Let him, without tiring, daily mutter the Veda at the proper time; for they declare that to be one's highest duty; (all) other (observances) are called secondary duties.
baseline: The Vedas should always be mentioned in the scriptures. It should be said to be a dharma or a sub dharma.
morphology: One should always observe the Vedas and observe them in the same manner. He should be called the dharma and the subdharma after this.

sanskrit: paurvikīṃ saṃsmaran jātiṃ brahmaivābhyasyate punaḥ / brahmābhyāsena cājasram anantaṃ sukham aśnute //
reference: He who, recollecting his former existences, again recites the Veda, gains endless bliss by the continual study of the Veda.
baseline: Having recited the pūrvīkaṇī scriptures one should again observe the practice of Brahman and attain eternal bliss.
morphology: Having recited the pūrvīkaṇī scriptures one would get happiness from the practice of Brahman once again. One would get eternal happiness by practicing Brahman.

sanskrit: sāvitrāñ śāntihomāṃś ca kuryāt parvasu nityaśaḥ / pitṝṃś caivāṣṭakāsv arcen nityam anvaṣṭakāsu ca //
reference: Let him always offer on the Parva-days oblations to Savitri and such as avert evil omens, and on the Ashtakas and Anvashtakas let him constantly worship the manes.
baseline: One should always worship the gods of the earth and the gods at the time of the festival. One should worship the deities of the fathers at the same time and at different times.
morphology: One should always worship the gods of the earth and the gods the gods and goddesses of the universe the deities of the four gods and the goddesses.

sanskrit: sarvalakṣaṇahīno 'pi yaḥ sadācāravān naraḥ / śraddadhāno 'nasūyaś ca śataṃ varṣāṇi jīvati //
reference: A man who follows the conduct of the virtuous, has faith and is free from envy, lives a hundred years, though he be entirely destitute of auspicious marks.
baseline: A man who is virtuous and devoid of all qualities would live for hundred of years without having to pay attention.
morphology: A man who is virtuous and devoid of all qualities would live for hundred of years without any fear.

sanskrit: nāstikyaṃ vedanindāṃ ca devatānāṃ ca kutsanam / dveṣaṃ dambhaṃ ca mānaṃ ca krodhaṃ taikṣṇyaṃ ca varjayet //
reference: Let him avoid atheism, cavilling at the Vedas, contempt of the gods, hatred, want of modesty, pride, anger, and harshness.
baseline: An atheist should avoid suffering and harm the gods enmity arrogance honour anger and jealousy.
morphology: One should avoid unbelief pain misery enmity arrogance honour anger greed hatred hatred and hatred of gods.

sanskrit: parasya daṇḍaṃ nodyacchet kruddho nainaṃ nipātayet / anyatra putrāc chiṣyād vā śiṣṭyarthaṃ tāḍayet tu tau //
reference: Let him, when angry, not raise a stick against another man, nor strike (anybody) except a son or a pupil; those two he may beat in order to correct them.
baseline: If they do not pay the fine in public they should be removed from the house of an angry person. If they are caught by the son or beaten for the sake of good.
morphology: If they do not pay the fine in public they should be removed from the body of the angry person and the son should be beaten for good.

sanskrit: tāḍayitvā tṛṇenāpi saṃrambhān matipūrvakam / ekaviṃśatīm ājātīḥ pāpayoniṣu jāyate //
reference: Having intentionally struck him in anger, even with a blade of grass, he will be born during twenty-one existences in the wombs (of such beings where men are born in punishment of their) sins.
baseline: One who has not been beaten or beaten with a stick or with the help of a sword would be born twenty one times in the absence of sin.
morphology: One who has not been beaten and has not had the strength of his feet on the grass with his heart would become a sinner by the twenty-one days of his death.

sanskrit: śoṇitaṃ yāvataḥ pāṃsūn saṃgṛhṇāti mahītalāt / tāvato 'bdān amutrānyaiḥ śoṇitotpādako 'dyate //
reference: As many particles of dust as the blood takes up from the ground, during so many years the spiller of the blood will be devoured by other (animals) in the next world.
baseline: One who collects the pāṣuna from the ground would get the product of blood from the sons of the king.
morphology: One who collects the pāṇus from the ground would then get the products of blood from the sons of unborn sons.

sanskrit: na kadā cid dvije tasmād vidvān avagured api / na tāḍayet tṛṇenāpi na gātrāt srāvayed asṛk //
reference: A wise man should therefore never threaten a Brahmana, nor strike him even with a blade of grass, nor cause his blood to flow.
baseline: If one does not repeat the vow once the learned man should not be beaten even if he does not do it. He should not attack the grass and the water should not flow from the ground.
morphology: If one does not know the meaning of the word one should not be beaten even by the wise man. One who does not get rid of the words of the sage should never be hit by the grass.

sanskrit: adhārmiko naro yo hi yasya cāpy anṛtaṃ dhanam / hiṃsārataś ca yo nityaṃ nehāsau sukham edhate //
reference: Neither a man who (lives) unrighteously, nor he who (acquires) wealth (by telling) falsehoods, nor he who always delights in doing injury, ever attain happiness in this world.
baseline: One who does not do evil and does not commit any crime and who is not subject to the curse of the enemy and who indulges in violence and mischief would enjoy eternal happiness.
morphology: One who does not do evil and does not commit any crime and who is not subject to the curse of the enemy one who does violence who is always happy and merry.

sanskrit: na sīdann api dharmeṇa mano 'dharme niveśayet / adhārmikānāṃ pāpānām āśu paśyan viparyayam //
reference: Let him, though suffering in consequence of his righteousness, never turn his heart to unrighteousness; for he will see the speedy overthrow of unrighteous, wicked men.
baseline: The mind should not be placed in the righteousness even if it is not straight. The sins of the unrighteous should be seen as evil.
morphology: The mind should not be put into the righteousness even if it is not straight. The sins of the unrighteous should be reversed by observing them.

sanskrit: nādharmaś carito loke sadyaḥ phalati gaur iva / śanair āvartyamānas tu kartur mūlāni kṛntati //
reference: Unrighteousness, practised in this world, does not at once produce its fruit, like a cow; but, advancing slowly, it cuts off the roots of him who committed it.
baseline: A man who has not been worshipped by the gods would soon become like a cow. He who does not want to be worshipped would then make the roots.
morphology: A person who has not been worshipped by the gods would soon become a cow and would be reaping the fruits of the gods. If he does not do so he would become the king.

sanskrit: ṛtvikpurohitācāryair mātulātithisaṃśritaiḥ / bālavṛddhāturair vaidyair jñātisaṃbandhibāndhavaiḥ //
reference: With an officiating or a domestic priest, with a teacher, with a maternal uncle, a guest and a dependant, with infants, aged and sick men, with learned men, with his paternal relatives, connexions by marriage and maternal relatives,
baseline: The priest should be known to the priest priest uncle associate child elder doctor acquaintance and friends.
morphology: The priest should be associated with the priest the elder with the child the priest with the mother the teacher with the relatives the doctor with the acquaintance and the blind.

sanskrit: mātāpitṛbhyāṃ jāmībhir bhrātrā putreṇa bhāryayā / duhitrā dāsavargeṇa vivādaṃ na samācaret //
reference: With his father and his mother, with female relatives, with a brother, with his son and his wife, with his daughter and with his slaves, let him not have quarrels.
baseline: The dispute between the parents and the brother should be resolved by the son and the wife. The dispute should not be settled by the husband and servants.
morphology: A dispute between the parents and the brother should not be resolved by the wife the son the daughter the servants and the wife.

sanskrit: ācāryo brahmalokeśaḥ prājāpatye pitā prabhuḥ / atithis tv indralokeśo devalokasya ca rtvijaḥ //
reference: The teacher is the lord of the world of Brahman, the father has power over the world of the Lord of created beings (Pragapati), a guest rules over the world of Indra, and the priests over the world of the gods.
baseline: O preceptor Brahma Lokā Prajapati Pita Prabhu the guest you are the master of Indra the king of the worlds of gods.
morphology: The preceptor should be of the form of Brahma Praja the lord of the earth the master of the universe the guest of the world of Indra the king of the worlds of gods.

sanskrit: jāmayo 'psarasāṃ loke vaiśvadevasya bāndhavāḥ / saṃbandhino hy apāṃ loke pṛthivyāṃ mātṛmātulau //
reference: The female relatives (have power) over the world of the Apsarases, the maternal relatives over that of the Visve Devas, the connexions by marriage over that of the waters, the mother and the maternal uncle over the earth.
baseline: The sons of the gods of the universe the friends of the lord the relatives the sons of mothers the mothers of the earth the children of the world the brothers the daughters of the king the wives of the sons the mother of the daughters the parents of the children and the children who belong to the family.
morphology: People who are friends of the universal god jāmayo pāsaraśa and related to the world are the members of the earth and mother.

sanskrit: ākāśeśās tu vijñeyā bālavṛddhakṛśāturāḥ / bhrātā jyeṣṭhaḥ samaḥ pitrā bhāryā putraḥ svakā tanuḥ // chāyā svo dāsavargaś ca duhitā kṛpaṇaṃ param / tasmād etair adhikṣiptaḥ sahetāsaṃjvaraḥ sadā //
reference: Infants, aged, poor and sick men must be considered as rulers of the middle sphere, the eldest brother as equal to one's father, one's wife and one's son as one's own body, One's slaves as one's shadow, one's daughter as the highest object of tenderness; hence if one is offended by (any one of) these, one must bear it without resentment.
baseline: Having known the heavens the boy the elder the younger the older the father the husband the son the wife the sons the mother the servants the shadow the self the servant the lord and the king are always in possession of the sky.
morphology: Having known the heavens the old man the elder man brother elder brother equal father husband son son and his own son the shadow should be placed on him and his servants and the grace should be bestowed on him.

sanskrit: hiraṇyam āyur annaṃ ca bhūr gauś cāpy oṣatas tanum / aśvaś cakṣus tvacaṃ vāso ghṛtaṃ tejas tilāh prajāḥ //
reference: Gold and food destroy his longevity, land and a cow his body, a horse his eye (sight), a garment his skin, clarified butter his energy, sesamum-grains his offspring.
baseline: Hiranya Ayur Ananda Bhura Gausha Tapi Ośāṭa Tanum Horses Eyes Skin Vāsava Tejā Tilā Praja etc. should be worshipped.
morphology: Hiranya Ayur Ananda Bhūra Gāśa Tapi Ośāṭa Tāṇumu Śvāṣa Eksha Tīvā Vāśu Tejā Tilā Praja etc.

sanskrit: tasmād avidvān bibhiyād yasmāt tasmāt pratigrahāt / svalpakenāpy avidvān hi paṅke gaur iva sīdati //
reference: Hence an ignorant (man) should be afraid of accepting any presents; for by reason of a very small (gift) even a fool sinks (into hell) as a cow into a morass.
baseline: If they do so they should be expelled from it. If they are not released from it they would be expelled by the governor.
morphology: If they do so they will be divided into two parts. If they are separated from one another they would be divided in a small way. They would be made to sit like cow.

sanskrit: yathā plavenāupalena nimajjaty udake taran / tathā nimajjato 'dhastād ajñau dātṛpratīcchakau //
reference: As he who (attempts to) cross water in a boat of stone sinks (to the bottom), even so an ignorant donor and an ignorant donee sink low.
baseline: One who is not aware of this should offer water to the priest.
morphology: One who is not aware of this should offer the gift of water.

sanskrit: dharmadhvajī sadā lubdhaś chādmiko lokadambhakaḥ / baiḍālavratiko jñeyo hiṃsraḥ sarvābhisaṃdhakaḥ //
reference: (A man) who, ever covetous, displays the flag of virtue, (who is) a hypocrite, a deceiver of the people, intent on doing injury, (and) a detractor (from the merits) of all men, one must know to be one who acts like a cat.
baseline: One who always humbles the dharmadhvajī one who humbly embraces the world one known to be a tyrant and one who knows all things is bound by the enemy.
morphology: One who is always attracted by the dharmadhvajī one who is known to be a brahmin a man of the world and a man who is violent and has all the enemies is known as Baidalavrta.

sanskrit: parakīyanipāneṣu na snāyād dhi kadā cana / nipānakartuḥ snātvā tu duṣkṛtāṃśena lipyate //
reference: Let him never bathe in tanks belonging to other men; if he bathes (in such a one), he is tainted by a portion of the guilt of him who made the tank.
baseline: One who does not wash the body of a foreigner with a piece of cloth should never wash it with the blood of a man who has never had a sinus. One who has bathed eight times should be covered with the part of the body which is not fit for him.
morphology: One who does not wash the body of a foreigner with a piece of water should never wash it with the blood of a nervous person. After having washed the body with eight pieces of water one should not wash with the part of the body that is not evil.

sanskrit: yānaśayyāsanāny asya kūpodyānagṛhāṇi ca / adattāny upayuñjāna enasaḥ syāt turīyabhāk //
reference: He who uses without permission a carriage, a bed, a seat, a well, a garden or a house belonging to an (other man), takes upon himself one fourth of (the owner's) guilt.
baseline: One would get the gift of these wells gardens and houses by the use of the yāna bed.
morphology: One would get the gift of these wells gardens and houses by the use of the yāna bed.

sanskrit: yamān seveta satataṃ na nityaṃ niyamān budhaḥ / yamān pataty akurvāṇo niyamān kevalān bhajan //
reference: A wise man should constantly discharge the paramount duties (called yama), but not always the minor ones (called niyama); for he who does not discharge the former, while he obeys the latter alone, becomes an outcast.
baseline: One should not worship the rules of the Buddha in the fall of the yāmaṇa. One should worship the laws of the ākravāṇa only in the falling of the Yāmañas.
morphology: One should not worship the rules of the Buddha in the fall of the yāmāna. One should worship only those rules which are fixed in the service of the Yāmaṇa.

sanskrit: nāśrotriyatate yajñe grāmayājikṛte tathā / striyā klībena ca hute bhuñjīta brāhmaṇaḥ kva cit //
reference: A Brahmana must never eat (a dinner given) at a sacrifice that is offered by one who is not a Srotriya, by one who sacrifices for a multitude of men, by a woman, or by a eunuch.
baseline: A brahmin should be worshipped in the form of a priest in the village and a woman in the temple in the month of nāśrūtri.
morphology: A brahmin should be worshipped with the garland of a village a woman a priest a man and a woman on the ground.

sanskrit: aślīkam etat sādhūnāṃ yatra juhvaty amī haviḥ / pratīpam etad devānāṃ tasmāt tat parivarjayet //
reference: When those persons offer sacrificial viands in the fire, it is unlucky for holy (men) it displeases the gods; let him therefore avoid it.
baseline: One should convert it to the form of the gods by making it as āśalika where the sages are worshipped.
morphology: One should convert it to the abode of the gods by making it as āślīka where it belongs to the saints and āmi havi Pratipa etc.

sanskrit: mattakruddhāturāṇāṃ ca na bhuñjīta kadā cana / keśakīṭāvapannaṃ ca padā spṛṣṭaṃ ca kāmataḥ // bhrūṇaghnāvekṣitaṃ caiva saṃspṛṣṭaṃ cāpy udakyayā / patatriṇāvalīḍhaṃ ca śunā saṃspṛṣṭam eva ca //
reference: Let him never eat (food given) by intoxicated, angry, or sick (men), nor that in which hair or insects are found, nor what has been touched intentionally with the foot, Nor that at which the slayer of a learned Brahmana has looked, nor that which has been touched by a menstruating woman, nor that which has been pecked at by birds or touched by a dog,
baseline: One should never eat intoxicating and angry things and eat them. One should not eat the products of insects hair feet and feet and touch them with lust one should eat the fruits of the foetus and the hair of the mother one who is in contact with the body and the body with the leaves of the cow and one who has heard from the mother and the mother should eat them with the help of a cloth.
morphology: One should never eat drunken and angry people those who do not eat food those with hair and worms those touching the feet those looking at the foetus those in contact with the eye those sleeping on the ground and those who sleep on the floor those lying on the bed and those sitting on the mattress.

sanskrit: gavā cānnam upaghrātaṃ ghuṣṭānnaṃ ca viśeṣataḥ / gaṇānnaṃ gaṇikānnaṃ ca viduṣā ca jugupsitam //
reference: Nor food at which a cow has smelt, nor particularly that which has been offered by an invitation to all comers, nor that (given) by a multitude or by harlots, nor that which is declared to be had by a learned (man),
baseline: One who has not been able to find a cow or a cow one who has been given a gift or a gift one with a gun a maid a juguśa a man with a pen and a jugaśa is known to be a great man.
morphology: One who has not been able to find a cow or a cow one who has been given a gift or a gift one with a gun a maid a juguśa and others would get the money.

sanskrit: abhiśastasya ṣaṇḍhasya puṃścalyā dāmbhikasya ca / śuktaṃ paryuṣitaṃ caiva śūdrasyocchiṣṭam eva ca // cikitsakasya mṛgayoḥ krūrasyocchiṣṭabhojinaḥ / ugrānnaṃ sūtikānnaṃ ca paryācāntam anirdaśam // anarcitaṃ vṛthāmāṃsam avīrāyāś ca yoṣitaḥ / dviṣadannaṃ nagaryannaṃ patitānnam avakṣutam //
reference: Nor (the food given) by a physician, a hunter, a cruel man, one who eats the fragments (of another's meal), nor the food of an Ugra, nor that prepared for a woman in childbed, nor that (given at a dinner) where (a guest rises) prematurely (and) sips water, nor that (given by a woman) whose ten days of impurity have not elapsed, Nor (food) given without due respect, nor (that which contains) meat eaten for no sacred purpose, nor (that given) by a female who has no male (relatives), nor the food of an enemy, nor that (given) by the lord of a town, nor that (given) by outcasts, nor that on which anybody has sneezed;
baseline: One who has been accused of killing a bull a cow a man with a brahmin a sage a shrew a Shudra a priest a doctor a hunter a tyrant a thief a drunken man a woman a poor woman an unruly man an unclean man and a woman are accused of committing adultery.
morphology: One who is accused of having killed a bull a cow a boar a brahmin a sage a priest a doctor a shudra a man who is not fit for a fight a hunter a tyrant a thief a woman who is illiterate a virgin a poor woman a city and a city should be destroyed.

sanskrit: piśunānṛtinoś cānnaṃ kratuvikrayiṇas tathā / śailūṣatunnavāyānnaṃ kṛtaghnasyānnam eva ca // karmārasya niṣādasya raṅgāvatārakasya ca / suvarṇakartur veṇasya śastravikrayiṇas tathā //
reference: Nor the food (given) by an informer, by one who habitually tells falsehoods, or by one who sells (the rewards for) sacrifices, nor the food (given) by an actor, a tailor, or an ungrateful (man), By a blacksmith, a Nishada, a stage-player, a goldsmith, a basket-maker, or a dealer in weapons,
baseline: One who sells gold gold silver silver and gold iron iron and iron gold and silver iron etc. is the same as one who does not do wrong. One who does wrongful deeds one who is a knight one with a knower and one who sells weapons is a gold maker one selling weapons one having a flute and one having an incarnation of colours.
morphology: One who sells gold gold silver silver and gold iron iron and iron gold and copper iron etc. and iron and steel iron or iron copper copper and iron are the best of the enemies.

sanskrit: śvavatāṃ śauṇḍikānāṃ ca cailanirṇejakasya ca / rañjakasya nṛśaṃsasya yasya copapatir gṛhe //
reference: By trainers of hunting dogs, publicans, a washerman, a dyer, a pitiless (man), and a man in whose house (lives) a paramour (of his wife),
baseline: The king of the king who has a cow and a cow a cow or a cow that has a colour a dye and a daring cow and a king whose head is placed in the house.
morphology: The king of the king who has a cow and a cow a cow or a cow that has a colour a dye and a daring man and a king whose wife is a maid of honour in the house.

sanskrit: pūyaṃ cikitsakasyānnaṃ puṃścalyās tv annam indriyam / viṣṭhā vārdhuṣikasyānnaṃ śastravikrayiṇo malam //
reference: The food of a physician (is as vile as) pus, that of an unchaste woman (equal to) semen, that of a usurer (as vile as) ordure, and that of a dealer in weapons (as bad as) dirt.
baseline: If you put the flowers of the healer the food the senses the waste of the old man the sale of weapons the excrement.
morphology: If you put the flowers of the healer the food the senses the waste of the old man the weapons and the excreta.

sanskrit: ya ete 'nye tv abhojyānnāḥ kramaśaḥ parikīrtitāḥ / teṣāṃ tvagasthiromāṇi vadanty annaṃ manīṣiṇaḥ //
reference: The food of those other persons who have been successively enumerated as such whose food must not be eaten, the wise declare (to be as impure as) skin, bones, and hair.
baseline: Those who eat these things are known to be good for their health. The wise men should say that they should eat food and drink water in their own way.
morphology: Those who eat these things are known to be good for their health. Those who do not eat food should be known to the wise.

sanskrit: bhuktvāto 'nyatam asyānnam amatyā kṣapaṇaṃ tryaham / matyā bhuktvācaret kṛcchraṃ retoviṇmūtram eva ca //
reference: If he has unwittingly eaten the food of one of those, (he must) fast for three days; if he has eaten it intentionally, or (has swallowed) semen, ordure, or urine, he must perform a Krikkhra penance.
baseline: One who has made a sacrifice for the sake of others should pay three times the amount of money for the purpose of the sacrifice. One who does not want to be sacrificed should pay the same amount as that for the cause of the loss.
morphology: One who has not been given the gift would get the gift of three things. The gift of the gift should be given to him in the form of sand and water.

sanskrit: nādyāc chūdrasya pakvānnaṃ vidvān aśrāddhino dvijaḥ / ādadītāmam evāsmād avṛttāv ekarātrikam //
reference: A Brahmana who knows (the law) must not eat cooked food (given) by a Sudra who performs no Sraddhas; but, on failure of (other) means of subsistence, he may accept raw (grain), sufficient for one night (and day).
baseline: One who does not know the nature of the fire should be given two days and one night. One who is not aware of it should be allowed to escape from it.
morphology: One who consumes a piece of rice after having been washed should be given to the wise man and the unbeliever and the other two. One night should be taken away from him.

sanskrit: tān prajāpatir āhaitya mā kṛdhvaṃ viṣamaṃ samam / śraddhāpūtaṃ vadānyasya hatam aśraddhayetarat //
reference: The Lord of created beings (Pragapati) came and spake to them, 'Do not make that equal, which is unequal. The food of that liberal (usurer) is purified by faith; (that of the) of the) other (man) is defiled by a want of faith.'
baseline: Having said that do not treat them as equal to the evil. One should not ignore the death of the worshipper.
morphology: Having said that do not treat them as evil. The death of a priest should not be considered as unheard of.

sanskrit: śraddhayeṣṭaṃ ca pūrtaṃ ca nityaṃ kuryād atandritaḥ / śraddhākṛte hy akṣaye te bhavataḥ svāgatair dhanaiḥ // dānadharmaṃ niṣeveta nityam aiṣṭikapaurtikam / parituṣṭena bhāvena pātram āsādya śaktitaḥ //
reference: Let him, without tiring, always offer sacrifices and perform works of charity with faith; for offerings and charitable works made with faith and with lawfully-earned money, (procure) endless rewards. Let him always practise, according to his ability, with a cheerful heart, the duty of liberality, both by sacrifices and by charitable works, if he finds a worthy recipient (for his gifts.)
baseline: Having believed and having fulfilled the desire and desire for the eternal abode of the mind having believed one should welcome you with riches having forbidden charity having always worshipped the goddess Aśṭhika having filled the vessel with the grace of the Lord having been strengthened.
morphology: Having always believed and fulfilled the desire one should always welcome you with wealth with devotion with respect with trust with a gift with the gift of charity and with a vessel filled with joy and with joy.

sanskrit: yat kiṃ cid api dātavyaṃ yācitenānasūyayā / utpatsyate hi tat pātraṃ yat tārayati sarvataḥ //
reference: If he is asked, let him always give something, be it ever so little, without grudging; for a worthy recipient will (perhaps) be found who saves him from all (guilt).
baseline: Any thing that is offered should be given even if it has been asked for. The vessel that is sold is the one that is destroyed.
morphology: Any thing that is offered should be given even if it has been asked for. The vessel that is sold should be destroyed.

sanskrit: vāridas tṛptim āpnoti sukham akṣayyam annadaḥ / tilapradaḥ prajām iṣṭāṃ dīpadaś cakṣur uttamam //
reference: A giver of water obtains the satisfaction (of his hunger and thirst), a giver of food imperishable happiness, a giver of sesamum desirable offspring, a giver of a lamp a most excellent eyesight.
baseline: O Varidasa one who acquires happiness and bliss by having food sesamum tilaprada prāpaṇa śiva dīpāda and eye are good.
morphology: One who acquires happiness happiness food sesamum salutations and good eyes would be better for the people.

sanskrit: vāsodaś candrasālokyam aśvisālokyam aśvadaḥ / anaḍuhaḥ śriyaṃ puṣṭāṃ godo bradhnasya viṣṭapam // yānaśayyāprado bhāryām aiśvaryam abhayapradaḥ / dhānyadaḥ śāśvataṃ saukhyaṃ brahmado brahmasārṣṭitām // sarveṣām eva dānānāṃ brahmadānaṃ viśiṣyate / vāryannagomahīvāsas- tilakāñcanasarpiṣām //
reference: A giver of a garment a place in the world of the moon, a giver of a horse (asva) a place in the world of the Asvins, a giver of a draught-ox great good fortune, a giver of a cow the world of the sun; A giver of a carriage or of a bed a wife, a giver of protection supreme dominion, a giver of grain eternal bliss, a giver of the Veda (brahman) union with Brahman; The gift of the Veda surpasses all other gifts, water, food, cows, land, clothes, sesamum, gold, and clarified butter.
baseline: The vāsodāśa the moon the celestial body the horse the bull the elephant the cow the goddess of prosperity the wife the bride and the bridegroom of the bride the daughter of the husband the mother of the maid of honour and the wife of the groom the god of wealth the lord of food the king of wealth and prosperity Brahma the Lord of all gifts the gift of Brahman the God of all beings the bestowing of the gods the gods of many worlds the sarsara and the sard
morphology: The vāsodāśa the moon the chariot the horse the bull the elephant the cow the śrīya the goddess of prosperity the wife of the brahmin the daughter of the warrior the bridegroom the queen of wealth the mother of the bride the maid of honour the gift of food the eternal happiness of Brahman the bestowing of all gifts on the celestial body the offering of Brahma and the bestowance of all beings would be given to her.

sanskrit: na vismayeta tapasā vaded iṣṭvā ca nānṛtam / nārto 'py apavaded viprān na dattvā parikīrtayet //
reference: Let him not be proud of his austerities; let him not utter a falsehood after he has offered a sacrifice; let him not speak ill of Brahmanas, though he be tormented (by them); when he has bestowed (a gift), let him not boast of it.
baseline: One should not forget the penance of the priest one who has not done any evil deed and one who does not want to do it. One should never do evil deeds and give false statements.
morphology: One should not forget the penance of the priest one who has done it with the will and one who had done it would not be able to do it. One would not do it by offering the vipras after having been accused by the priest.

sanskrit: mṛtaṃ śarīram utsṛjya kāṣṭhaloṣṭasamaṃ kṣitau / vimukhā bāndhavā yānti dharmas tam anugacchati //
reference: Leaving the dead body on the ground like a log of wood, or a clod of earth, the relatives depart with averted faces; but spiritual merit follows the (soul).
baseline: The body of the deceased should be thrown away and the body should be removed from the wood. One who binds a man with a limb should follow the path of righteousness.
morphology: The body of the deceased should be thrown away and the body should be removed from the wood. The man who binds the enemy should follow the dharma.

sanskrit: uttamān uttamān eva gacchan hīnāṃs tu varjayan / brāhmaṇaḥ śreṣṭhatām eti pratyavāyena śūdratām //
reference: A Brahmana who always connects himself with the most excellent (ones), and shuns all inferior ones, (himself) becomes most distinguished; by an opposite conduct he becomes a Sudra.
