baseline: The brahmins should go only to the best and the weak should be avoided. The sudras should be trusted to be superior.
morphology: The brahmins should go only to the best and the weak should be avoided. The Brahmanas should be superior and the Shudras should be established with this belief.

sanskrit: edhodakaṃ mūlaphalam annam abhyudyataṃ ca yat / sarvataḥ pratigṛhṇīyān madhv athābhayadakṣiṇām //
reference: He may accept from any (man), fuel, water, roots, fruit, food offered without asking, and honey, likewise a gift (which consists in) a promise of protection.
baseline: One who takes away the basic fruits food and other things from all places should be given to him or her.
morphology: One who takes away everything from others would get food and other things. One who does not want to suffer would get fear from others.

sanskrit: śayyāṃ gṛhān kuśān gandhān apaḥ puṣpaṃ maṇīn dadhi / dhānā matsyān payo māṃsaṃ śākaṃ caiva na nirṇudet //
reference: A couch, a house, Kusa grass, perfumes, water, flowers, jewels, sour milk, grain, fish, sweet milk, meat, and vegetables let him not reject, (if they are voluntarily offered.)
baseline: One should not eat meat vegetables rice fish fish etc.
morphology: One should not eat meat vegetables fish rice cow and goat in the room.

sanskrit: gurūn bhṛtyāṃś cojjihīrṣann arciṣyan devatātithīn / sarvataḥ pratigṛhṇīyān na tu tṛpyet svayaṃ tataḥ // guruṣu tv abhyatīteṣu vinā vā tair gṛhe vasan / ātmano vṛttim anvicchan gṛhṇīyāt sādhutaḥ sadā //
reference: He who desires to relieve his Gurus and those whom he is bound to maintain, or wishes to honour the gods and guests, may accept (gifts) from anybody; but he must not satisfy his (own hunger) with such (presents). But if his Gurus are dead, or if he lives separate from them in (another) house, let him, when he seeks a subsistence, accept (presents) from good men alone.
baseline: One should not accept the master his servants the priest the god the devotee the worshipper the adversary those who have taken back everything from him. One should always accept the spirit of the master without having been present in the house. One who has sought the profession of the self should always remain at home.
morphology: One should choose the teachers servants priests gods and other deities. One should not take back everything by himself. He should stay in the house without having been admitted by the teachers. One who has sought the profession of the self should always accept it. He would always be good.

sanskrit: ārdhikaḥ kulamitraṃ ca gopālo dāsanāpitau / ete śūdreṣu bhojyānnā yāś cātmānaṃ nivedayet //
reference: His labourer in tillage, a friend of his family, his cow-herd, his slave, and his barber are, among Sudras, those whose food he may eat, likewise (a poor man) who offers himself (to be his slave).
baseline: One should present the wealth family and friends of ones father servant servant etc. and one who eats food and drinks food in these places.
morphology: One should present the wealth family and friends of the lord servants servants and parents. One should offer food and other gifts to the sages.

sanskrit: yo 'nyathā santam ātmānam anyathā satsu bhāṣate / sa pāpakṛttamo loke stena ātmāpahārakaḥ //
reference: He who describes himself to virtuous (men), in a manner contrary to truth, is the most sinful (wretch) in this world; he is a thief who makes away with his own self.
baseline: One who does not know the nature of the soul and who does nothing about it would be said to be a sinner. He would be called a spirit destroyer by the people.
morphology: One who does not know the nature of the soul would speak otherwise. One who commits a sin would become a spirit destroyer.

sanskrit: vācy arthā niyatāḥ sarve vāṅgūlā vāgviniḥsṛtāḥ / tāṃs tu yaḥ stenayed vācaṃ sa sarvasteyakṛn naraḥ //
reference: All things (have their nature) determined by speech; speech is their root, and from speech they proceed; but he who is dishonest with respect to speech, is dishonest in everything.
baseline: All the words that are said to have been spoken should be said to be the meaning of the words. Those who say that they have been heard should say that all the words written in the scriptures are not true.
morphology: All the words that are said to be meaningful are made with the fingers the words of the mouth the one who is said to have sucked them the man who does not do all the deeds is a man.

sanskrit: maharṣipitṛdevānāṃ gatvānṛṇyaṃ yathāvidhi / putre sarvaṃ samāsajya vasen mādhyasthyam āśritaḥ //
reference: When he has paid, according to the law, his debts to the great sages, to the manes, and to the gods, let him make over everything to his son and dwell (in his house), not caring for any worldly concerns.
baseline: Having settled everything in the son the king should go to the gods of the great sages and the gods. He should be placed in the middle.
morphology: Having settled everything in the son one should go to the great sage and the gods in the same manner. One should depend on the mediator.

sanskrit: ekākī cintayen nityaṃ vivikte hitam ātmanaḥ / ekākī cintayāno hi paraṃ śreyo 'dhigacchati //
reference: Alone let him constantly meditate in solitude on that which is salutary for his soul; for he who meditates in solitude attains supreme bliss.
baseline: One who thinks alone would always get the benefit of the self. One who does so alone would get benefit from it.
morphology: One who thinks alone always becomes better for the self. One who does so alone gets better for himself.

sanskrit: sa tān uvāca dharmātmā maharṣīn mānavo bhṛguḥ / śrūyatāṃ yena doṣeṇa mṛtyur viprān jighāṃsati //
reference: Righteous Bhrigu, the son of Manu, (thus) answered the great sages: 'Hear, (in punishment) of what faults Death seeks to shorten the lives of Brahmanas!'
baseline: He said to them that the god of righteousness should be shown to the sages men and women. One who dies on account of sin would be able to destroy them.
morphology: He said to them that the god the great man the man and the goddess should be seen. One who dies on account of the fault of the sage would destroy the sages.

sanskrit: anabhyāsena vedānām ācārasya ca varjanāt / ālasyād annadoṣāc ca mṛtyur viprāñ jighāṃsati //
reference: 'Through neglect of the Veda-study, through deviation from the rule of conduct, through remissness (in the fulfilment of duties), and through faults (committed by eating forbidden) food, Death becomes eager to shorten the lives of Brahmanas.'
baseline: One who does not practice the Vedas or practices should be forbidden. One who dies by laziness and eating food and doing evil deeds should be punished by the king.
morphology: One who does not practice the Vedas or practices should be banned. One who dies from laziness and food defect should be punished with death.

sanskrit: lohitān vṛkṣaniryāsān vṛścanaprabhavāṃs tathā / śeluṃ gavyaṃ ca peyūṣaṃ prayatnena vivarjayet //
reference: One should carefully avoid red exudations from trees and (juices) flowing from incisions, the Selu (fruit), and the thickened milk of a cow (which she gives after calving).
baseline: The reds trees flowers scorpions horses cows goats cows and other animals should be removed with the effort.
morphology: The reds trees flowers scorpions birds horses cows goats and other animals should be removed with the effort.

sanskrit: vṛthā kṛsarasaṃyāvaṃ pāyasāpūpam eva ca / anupākṛtamāṃsāni devānnāni havīṃṣi ca // anirdaśāyā goḥ kṣīram auṣṭram aikaśaphaṃ tathā / āvikaṃ saṃdhinīkṣīraṃ vivatsāyāś ca goḥ payaḥ //
reference: Rice boiled with sesamum, wheat mixed with butter, milk and sugar, milk-rice and flour-cakes which are not prepared for a sacrifice, meat which has not been sprinkled with water while sacred texts were recited, food offered to the gods and sacrificial viands, The milk of a cow (or other female animal) within ten days after her calving, that of camels, of one-hoofed animals, of sheep, of a cow in heat, or of one that has no calf with her,
baseline: The cow should be given the same amount of water as the cow in the form of a cow the cow cow milk camel ox cow and cow and the cow should not be wasted.
morphology: One should eat the same thing as a cow cow goat cow and camel cow or cow buffalo sheep cow etc. The unformed meat gods cows cows and cows milk oysters one and a half cow and cow sheep and goat are wasted in the absence of water water and water.

sanskrit: kravyādāñ śakunān sarvāṃs tathā grāmanivāsinaḥ / anirdiṣṭāṃś caikaśaphāṃṣ ṭiṭṭibhaṃ ca vivarjayet //
reference: Let him avoid all carnivorous birds and those living in villages, and one-hoofed animals which are not specially permitted (to be eaten), and the Tittibha (Parra Jacana),
baseline: The omens should be worshipped in the same manner as those of the inhabitants of the villages. The unspecified parts of the chakasabhas and the tittibhams should be avoided.
morphology: The omens should be removed from all parts of the city and the inhabitants of the villages. The unspecified parts of a tree should be kept away from the eyes.

sanskrit: kalaviṅkaṃ plavaṃ haṃsaṃ cakrāhvaṃ grāmakukkuṭam / sārasaṃ rajjuvālaṃ ca dātyūhaṃ śukasārike //
reference: The sparrow, the Plava, the Hamsa, the Brahmani duck, the village-cock, the Sarasa crane, the Raggudala, the woodpecker, the parrot, and the starling,
baseline: One should give the kalavinka the swan the chakra the village the kukkuda the stork the rope and the sandal of the goat.
morphology: One should give the kalavinka the flood the swan the chakra the village and the kukkuda the stork the rope and the water of the river.

sanskrit: pratudāñ jālapādāṃś ca koyaṣṭinakhaviṣkirān / nimajjataś ca matsyādān saunaṃ vallūram eva ca //
reference: Those which feed striking with their beaks, web-footed birds, the Koyashti, those which scratch with their toes, those which dive and live on fish, meat from a slaughter-house and dried meat,
baseline: The feet of the fish should be placed on the ground with the same length as the mace. The feet should be kept on the sides of the mound. The fish should also be kept in the same position.
morphology: The feet of the king should be placed on each side with a mace a bow a sword a spear a fish a snake a bull and a bull.

sanskrit: bakaṃ caiva balākāṃ ca kākolaṃ khañjarīṭakam / matsyādān viḍvarāhāṃś ca matsyān eva ca sarvaśaḥ //
reference: The Baka and the Balaka crane, the raven, the Khangaritaka, (animals) that eat fish, village-pigs, and all kinds of fishes.
baseline: One should have a cow cow mule kangaritaka fish buffalo wild buffalo and fish in all places.
morphology: One should have a cow cow calf kancharitaka fish buffalo and fish in all places.

sanskrit: pāṭhīnarohitāv ādyau niyuktau havyakavyayoḥ / rājīvān siṃhatuṇḍāś ca saśalkāś caiva sarvaśaḥ //
reference: (But the fish called) Pathina and (that called) Rohita may be eaten, if used for offerings to the gods or to the manes; (one may eat) likewise Ragivas, Simhatundas, and Sasalkas on all (occasions).
baseline: The king should be appointed as the chief among the preceptors with the penance of the king the king of the lion the lord of the sword and the king in all cases.
morphology: The king should be appointed as the chief among the preceptors and the king should have the lion elephant and mace in all places.

sanskrit: na bhakṣayed ekacarān ajñātāṃś ca mṛgadvijān / bhakṣyeṣv api samuddiṣṭān sarvān pañcanakhāṃs tathā // śvāvidhaṃ śalyakaṃ godhāṃ khaḍgakūrmaśaśāṃs tathā / bhakṣyān pañcanakheṣv āhur anuṣṭrāṃś caikatodatah //
reference: Let him not eat solitary or unknown beasts and birds, though they may fall under (the categories of) eatable (creatures), nor any five-toed (animals). The porcupine, the hedgehog, the iguana, the rhinoceros, the tortoise, and the hare they declare to be eatable; likewise those (domestic animals) that have teeth in one jaw only, excepting camels.
baseline: One should not eat the same animal unknown animal antelope animal animal etc. All the animals mentioned in the book should be given five parts cow cow and cow sword mustard and five parts of food.
morphology: One who does not eat a cow an unknown animal a deer a bird a dog an animal and a cow should be given five pieces of food.

sanskrit: amatyaitāni ṣaḍ jagdhvā kṛcchraṃ sāntapanaṃ caret / yaticāndrāyāṇaṃ vāpi śeṣeṣūpavased ahaḥ //
reference: He who unwittingly partakes of (any of) these six, shall perform a Samtapana (Krikkhra) or the lunar penance (Kandrayana) of ascetics; in case (he who has eaten) any other (kind of forbidden food) he shall fast for one day (and a night ).
baseline: Having made six offerings of the same kind one should offer the chandrayaṇa and the rest of the form to the king.
morphology: Having made six offerings of unbleached rice one should offer the kruchra as a consolation and the chandraya as a gift and the remaining offerings should be made by him.

sanskrit: saṃvatsarasyaikam api caret kṛcchraṃ dvijottamaḥ / ajñātabhuktaśuddhyarthaṃ jñātasya tu viṣeśataḥ //
reference: Once a year a Brahmana must perform a Krikkhra penance, in order to atone for unintentionally eating (forbidden food) but for intentionally (eating forbidden food he must perform the penances prescribed) specially.
baseline: One of the chariots of the year should be made to be known for the purpose of purifying the unknowable.
morphology: One of the chariots for the year should be made with the same amount of water as the other. One should be known for the purification of the unknowable.

sanskrit: yajñārthaṃ brāhmaṇair vadhyāḥ praśastā mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ / bhṛtyānāṃ caiva vṛttyartham agastyo hy ācarat purā // babhūvur hi puroḍāśā bhakṣyāṇāṃ mṛgapakṣiṇām / purāṇeṣv api yajñeṣu brahmakṣatrasaveṣu ca //
reference: Beasts and birds recommended (for consumption) may be slain by Brahmanas for sacrifices, and in order to feed those whom they are bound to maintain; for Agastya did this of old. For in ancient (times) the sacrificial cakes were (made of the flesh) of eatable beasts and birds at the sacrifices offered by Brahmanas and Kshatriyas.
baseline: One who kills a brahmin for the sake of a sacrifice should worship the king of birds of prey. One who worships the servants of the king should worship him in the circle of fire. The king of the gods should worship a priest a king who eats food a bird of prey a priest who is worshipped in the Puranas and the gods of the universe and stars.
morphology: One who kills a brahmin for the sake of sacrifice should worship the birds of prey. One who worships the servants should worship Agastya in the circle of the cow. The priest should worship those who eat food and eat food the king of birds the gods of the universe the goddess of fire the celestial figures and the gods and goddesses of Brahma and the stars.

sanskrit: yat kiṃ cit snehasaṃyuktaṃ bhakṣyaṃ bhojyam agarhitam / tat paryuṣitam apy ādyaṃ haviḥśeṣaṃ ca yad bhavet //
reference: All lawful hard or soft food may be eaten, though stale, (after having been) mixed with fatty (substances), and so may the remains of sacrificial viands.
baseline: What is said to be food containing affection and not being eaten should be prepared first and the rest.
morphology: What is said to be food containing affection and not being eaten should be the first and the last of the things that are said to have been eaten.

sanskrit: etad uktaṃ dvijātīnāṃ bhakṣyābhakṣyam aśeṣataḥ / māṃsasyātaḥ pravakṣyāmi vidhiṃ bhakṣaṇavarjane // prokṣitaṃ bhakṣayen māṃsaṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ ca kāmyayā / yathāvidhi niyuktas tu prāṇānām eva cātyaye //
reference: Thus has the food, allowed and forbidden to twice-born men, been fully described; I will now propound the rules for eating and avoiding meat. One may eat meat when it has been sprinkled with water, while Mantras were recited, when Brahmanas desire (one's doing it), when one is engaged (in the performance of a rite) according to the law, and when one's life is in danger.
baseline: Having said this one should eat food of two kinds of people without ceasing to eat meat. One should eat meat which has been preserved in the preceptor's order. One who eats meat as desired by the brahmins should eat the meat as prescribed by him.
morphology: Having said this the food of the two castes should be made available to them without any limit. The meat should be taken out of the house as per the rules of the law. The food should be provided to the brahmins and the animals should be fed as prescribed.

sanskrit: carāṇām annam acarā daṃṣṭriṇām apy adaṃṣṭriṇaḥ / ahastāś ca sahastānāṃ śūrāṇāṃ caiva bhīravaḥ //
reference: What is destitute of motion is the food of those endowed with locomotion; (animals) without fangs (are the food) of those with fangs, those without hands of those who possess hands, and the timid of the bold.
baseline: The cowherds should eat food from the cows cows buffaloes cows and other animals.
morphology: The cowherds should be fed with rice and the cowherd should be given to the cows and other animals.

sanskrit: nāttā duṣyaty adann ādyān prāṇino 'hanyahany api / dhātraiva sṛṣṭā hy ādyāś ca prāṇino 'ttāra eva ca //
reference: The eater who daily even devours those destined to be his food, commits no sin; for the creator himself created both the eaters and those who are to be eaten (for those special purposes).
baseline: One who does not want to suffer the loss of ones life one who kills another and one who creates another is born as a mother one living in the beginning as a wife one born as an aunt one created as a daughter one made as a husband one with a mother and one with an uncle.
morphology: One who kills the living beings in the first place one who kills those living in the second place is created by the mother the mother of the living entity and one who gives birth to that living entity.

sanskrit: yajñāya jagdhir māṃsasyety eṣa daivo vidhiḥ smṛtaḥ / ato 'nyathā pravṛttis tu rākṣaso vidhir ucyate //
reference: 'The consumption of meat (is befitting) for sacrifices,' that is declared to be a rule made by the gods; but to persist (in using it) on other (occasions) is said to be a proceeding worthy of Rakshasas.
baseline: One who performs a ritual for the sacrifice of a devotee one who does not eat meat one should remember the ritual of the deity. One who practices the practice of the demon is called a ritualist.
morphology: One who performs a ritual for the sacrifice of the animal one who does not eat meat one should remember the ritual of the god. One who does so would be called a demon.

sanskrit: krītvā svayaṃ vāpy utpādya paropakṛtam eva vā / devān pitṝṃś cārcayitvā khādan māṃsaṃ na duṣyati //
reference: He who eats meat, when he honours the gods and manes, commits no sin, whether he has bought it, or himself has killed (the animal), or has received it as a present from others.
baseline: Having bought and produced the vapi by himself one who has done charity would not eat meat after having worshipped the gods and the fathers.
morphology: One who has bought and produced the meat himself and has done charity would not eat meat after having worshipped the gods and the fathers.

sanskrit: nādyād avidhinā māṃsaṃ vidhijño 'nāpadi dvijaḥ / jagdhvā hy avidhinā māṃsaṃ pretas tair adyate 'vaśaḥ //
reference: A twice-born man who knows the law, must not eat meat except in conformity with the law; for if he has eaten it unlawfully, he will, unable to save himself, be eaten after death by his (victims).
baseline: One who does not eat meat without having to eat it should be called a sage. One who has not eaten meat without being aware of the law should eat meat after having eaten it.
morphology: One who does not eat meat without having to eat it should be called a sage. One who has not eaten meat without being aware of the law should eat it twice.

sanskrit: asaṃskṛtān paśūn mantrair nādyād vipraḥ kadā cana / mantrais tu saṃskṛtān adyāc chāśvataṃ vidhim āsthitaḥ //
reference: A Brahmana must never eat (the flesh of animals unhallowed by Mantras; but, obedient to the primeval law, he may eat it, consecrated with Vedic texts.
baseline: When the rite should be performed for the worship of uncultured animals and animals. When should one perform the ritual for the protection of animals and for the welfare of the samskrits.
morphology: When the rite of worship should be performed for the unruly animals and animals. When it should be done for the samskrits it should not be repeated for the same.

sanskrit: kuryād ghṛtapaśuṃ saṅge kuryāt piṣṭapaśuṃ tathā / na tv eva tu vṛthā hantuṃ paśum icchet kadā cana //
reference: If he has a strong desire (for meat) he may make an animal of clarified butter or one of flour, (and eat that); but let him never seek to destroy an animal without a (lawful) reason.
baseline: The kuriād should be made with ghee ghee and starch. You do not want to kill the animal in vain. You never want to do that.
morphology: The kuriād should be made with ghee ghee and starch. You do not want the animal to be killed in vain. You never want to kill it.

sanskrit: yāvanti paśuromāṇi tāvatkṛtvo ha māraṇam / vṛthāpaśughnaḥ prāpnoti pretya janmani janmani //
reference: As many hairs as the slain beast has, so often indeed will he who killed it without a (lawful) reason suffer a violent death in future births.
baseline: One who gives birth to animals and other animals would get death. One who does not give birth would get annihilation.
morphology: One gets death by the killing of any animal or animal. One gets birth by giving birth to animals after having lost his life.

sanskrit: oṣadhyaḥ paśavo vṛkṣās tiryañcaḥ pakṣiṇas tathā / yajñārthaṃ nidhanaṃ prāptāḥ prāpnuvanty utsṛtīḥ punaḥ //
reference: Herbs, trees, cattle, birds, and (other) animals that have been destroyed for sacrifices, receive (being reborn) higher existences.
baseline: The animals birds trees and creepers found dead for the sake of sacrifice are again to be worshipped.
morphology: The animals birds trees and other animals found dead for the purpose of sacrifice should be re-sentenced.

sanskrit: eṣv artheṣu paśūn hiṃsan vedatattvārthavid dvijaḥ / ātmānaṃ ca paśuṃ caiva gamayaty uttamaṃ gatim //
reference: A twice-born man who, knowing the true meaning of the Veda, slays an animal for these purposes, causes both himself and the animal to enter a most blessed state.
baseline: One who knows the meaning of animals violence Vedic principles material things spirit animal animal etc. would get better speed.
morphology: One who knows the meaning of animals violence Vedic principles meaning spirit animal and other things should move in a good way.

sanskrit: gṛhe gurāv araṇye vā nivasann ātmavān dvijaḥ / nāvedavihitāṃ hiṃsām āpady api samācaret //
reference: A twice-born man of virtuous disposition, whether he dwells in (his own) house, with a teacher, or in the forest, must never, even in times of distress, cause an injury (to any creature) which is not sanctioned by the Veda.
baseline: A priest should not live in a house or a forest and should not commit the offence of committing violence against others.
morphology: A priest should not live in a house or a forest. He should not commit violence even if he has not been punished by the king.

sanskrit: yā vedavihitā hiṃsā niyatāsmiṃś carācare / ahiṃsām eva tāṃ vidyād vedād dharmo hi nirbabhau //
reference: Know that the injury to moving creatures and to those destitute of motion, which the Veda has prescribed for certain occasions, is no injury at all; for the sacred law shone forth from the Veda.
baseline: One who does not know the Vedas and does not commit violence does not practice nonviolence and is free from the Veda.
morphology: One who does not know the meaning of the Vedas and does not commit violence does not believe in nonviolence and is free from the vedas.

sanskrit: yo 'hiṃsakāni bhūtāni hinasty ātmasukhecchayā / sa jīvāṃś ca mṛtaś caiva na kva cit sukham edhate //
reference: He who injures innoxious beings from a wish to (give) himself pleasure, never finds happiness, neither living nor dead.
baseline: One who has committed an act of violence and the killing of a spirit being by the desire of the self that living being should be killed and the other living being would not be happy.
morphology: One who has committed an act of violence and has a desire to enjoy the soul would not get happiness if he dies.

sanskrit: yad dhyāyati yat kurute ratiṃ badhnāti yatra ca / tad avāpnoty ayatnena yo hinasti na kiṃ cana //
reference: He who does not injure any (creature), attains without an effort what he thinks of, what he undertakes, and what he fixes his mind on.
baseline: One who meditates on the matter and kills the enemy should do so without having to think about whether he would become a king or not.
morphology: One who meditates on that which he has done and where it has been done and who has not done so would be killed by him.

sanskrit: nākṛtvā prāṇināṃ hiṃsāṃ māṃsam utpadyate kva cit / na ca prāṇivadhaḥ svargyas tasmān māṃsaṃ vivarjayet //
reference: Meat can never be obtained without injury to living creatures, and injury to sentient beings is detrimental to (the attainment of) heavenly bliss; let him therefore shun (the use of) meat.
baseline: The flesh is produced by the violence of the creatures by being naked. The heavenly beings should not be able to destroy the flesh by the killing of the animals.
morphology: The flesh is produced by the violence of the creatures by being naked. The heavenly beings should not destroy the flesh.

sanskrit: na bhakṣayati yo māṃsaṃ vidhiṃ hitvā piśācavat / na loke priyatāṃ yāti vyādhibhiś ca na pīḍyate //
reference: He who, disregarding the rule (given above), does not eat meat like a Pisaka, becomes dear to men, and will not be tormented by diseases.
baseline: One who does not eat meat after having done the ritual should be treated as a devil. One who is not fond of people and afflicted by disease should not suffer.
morphology: One who does not eat meat after having done the ritual should be treated as a devil. One who has not loved the people and is not afflicted by disease should not suffer.

sanskrit: svamāṃsaṃ paramāṃsena yo vardhayitum icchati / anabhyarcya pitṝn devāṃs tato 'nyo nāsty apuṇyakṛt //
reference: There is no greater sinner than that (man) who, though not worshipping the gods or the manes, seeks to increase (the bulk of) his own flesh by the flesh of other (beings).
baseline: One who wants to increase his own meat with other meat should ask his father gods and other gods.
morphology: One who wants to increase his own body with other body parts should ask the gods and the fathers without having to do so.

sanskrit: phalamūlāśanair medhyair munyannānāṃ ca bhojanaiḥ / na tat phalam avāpnoti yan māṃsaparivarjanāt //
reference: By subsisting on pure fruit and roots, and by eating food fit for ascetics (in the forest), one does not gain (so great) a reward as by entirely avoiding (the use of) flesh.
baseline: The fruit should be taken with the help of the leaves and the food of the sages. The fruit is not obtained if the meat is left out.
morphology: The fruit should be taken with the help of the leaves and the food of the sages. The fruits should not be eaten with the meat.

sanskrit: na māṃsabhakṣaṇe doṣo na madye na ca maithune / pravṛttir eṣā bhūtānāṃ nivṛttis tu mahāphalā //
reference: There is no sin in eating meat, in (drinking) spirituous liquor, and in carnal intercourse, for that is the natural way of created beings, but abstention brings great rewards.
baseline: There is no sin in eating meat drinking and having intercourse. This practice is a great reward for the purification of demons.
morphology: There is no sin in eating meat drinking and having intercourse. This practice is great benefit for the demons.

sanskrit: yathedaṃ śāvam āśaucaṃ sapiṇḍeṣu vidhīyate / janane 'py evam eva syān nipuṇaṃ śuddhim icchatām //
reference: As this impurity on account of a death is prescribed for (all) Sapindas, even so it shall be (held) on a birth by those who desire to be absolutely pure.
baseline: In the same way in the case of the birth of a child the body should be placed in the lump of blood. In the similar way one should wish for the cleansing of the child.
morphology: In the same way in the case of the birth of a child the body should be placed in a lotus. In the similar way one should wish for the cleansing of the child.

sanskrit: sarveṣāṃ śāvam āśaucaṃ mātāpitros tu sūtakam / sūtakaṃ mātur eva syād upaspṛśya pitā śuciḥ //
reference: (Or while) the impurity on account of a death is common to all (Sapindas), that caused by a birth (falls) on the parents alone; (or) it shall fall on the mother alone, and the father shall become pure by bathing;
baseline: All the bodies should be washed with soap by the parents. The mother should be clean by touching all the hands of the father.
morphology: All the bodies should be washed with soap by the parents. The mother should be clean by touching the mother. The father should be cleansed by touching all the animals.

sanskrit: nirasya tu pumāñ śukram upaspṛsyaiva śudhyati / baijikād abhisaṃbandhād anurundhyād aghaṃ tryaham //
reference: But a man, having spent his strength, is purified merely by bathing; after begetting a child (on a remarried female), he shall retain the impurity during three days.
baseline: One should purify the body of the sage by offering the sukrāma and the upasprā in the form of a purification. One should offer the three prāṇudhyas with the anurundhā from the abhimsa.
morphology: One should purify the body by offering thanks to the lord of the pituitary gland. One should offer three things to the king of the vaijikas by offering prayers to him with the fragrance of anura.

sanskrit: guroḥ pretasya śiṣyas tu pitṛmedhaṃ samācaran / pretahāraiḥ samaṃ tatra daśarātreṇa śudhyati //
reference: A pupil who performs the Pitrimedha for his deceased teacher, becomes also pure after ten days, just like those who carry the corpse out (to the burial-ground).
baseline: The disciples of the preceptor are said to have worshipped their father. They are purified there by ten nights.
morphology: The disciples of the preceptor and the spirit are purified by the ten nights therein with the same manner as those of the prophets.

sanskrit: nṛṇām akṛtacūḍānāṃ viśuddhir naiśikī smṛtā / nirvṛttacūḍakānāṃ tu trirātrāc chuddhir iṣyate //
reference: (On the death) of children whose tonsure (Kudakarman) has not been performed, the (Sapindas) are declared to become pure in one (day and) night; (on the death) of those who have received the tonsure (but not the initiation, the law) ordains (that) the purification (takes place) after three days.
baseline: One who does not have the knives the knots the purified knives etc. and those who do not have any knives should be punished with three rounds.
morphology: The three nights of the chutneys of the niras should be remembered as the pure night. The chutchukas of nirās should be worshipped as the three nights.

sanskrit: nāsya kāryo 'gnisaṃskāro na ca kāryodakakriyā / araṇye kāṣṭhavat tyaktvā kṣapeyus tryaham eva tu // nātrivarṣasya kartavyā bāndhavair udakakriyā / jātadantasya vā kuryur nāmni vāpi kṛte sati //
reference: Such (a child) shall not be burnt with fire, and no libations of water shall be offered to it; leaving it like a (log of) wood in the forest, (the relatives) shall remain impure during three days only. The relatives shall not offer libations to (a child) that has not reached the third year; but if it had teeth, or the ceremony of naming it (Namakarman) had been performed, (the offering of water is) optional.
baseline: One who does not perform the ritual or the ritual of doing the ritual should leave the wood in the forest and forgive him for the same. One should do the ritual for the night and year. One who has done the conduct of a friend a friend or a friend should do it for three years. When he has done this action or the act of killing a cow he should pay tribute to him.
morphology: One who does not perform the ritual or conduct of the ritual should leave the wood in the forest and forgive him for the same. One who has done the ritual for the month of a month or three years should do the abode of a friend water and other activities for the sake of the family or the death of a son or the name of a servant should be mentioned as vapi.

sanskrit: strīṇām asaṃskṛtānāṃ tu tryahāc chudhyanti bāndhavāḥ / yathoktenaiva kalpena śudhyanti tu sanābhayaḥ //
reference: (On the death) of females (betrothed but) not married (the bridegroom and his) relatives are purified after three days, and the paternal relatives become pure according to the same rule.
baseline: If a woman is not allowed to go out of her way her friends will be able to penetrate her three hands. If she is not able to do so she will be purified.
morphology: If a woman is not able to bear the unruly things of a man her friends will be able to touch her three times. If she does not do so then she will be purified by the grace of her husband.

sanskrit: saṃnidhāv eṣa vai kalpaḥ śāvāśaucasya kīrtitaḥ / asaṃnidhāv ayaṃ jñeyo vidhiḥ saṃbandhibāndhavaiḥ //
reference: The above rule regarding impurity on account of a death has been prescribed (for cases where the kinsmen live) near (the deceased); (Sapinda) kinsmen and (Samanodaka) relatives must know the following rule (to refer to cases where deceased lived) at a distance (from them).
baseline: The same kalpa is said to be the same as that of a corpse. This is known as the method of the blind.
morphology: The same kalpa is said to be the same as that of a corpse. The method known as asānamnidhava is known to the blind.

sanskrit: atikrānte daśāhe ca trirātram aśucir bhavet / saṃvatsare vyatīte tu spṛṣṭvaivāpo viśudhyati //
reference: If the ten days have passed, he shall be impure during three (days and) nights; but if a year has elapsed (since the occurrence of the death), he becomes pure merely by bathing.
baseline: The three nights in the ten months after the attack are considered unclean. If it happens in a year then the contact with the animal is purified.
morphology: One should be unclean for three nights at the end of the ten days and at the same time in the month of the tenth month. If it happens in the year of the seventh year then the touch and water are purified.

sanskrit: antardaśāhe syātāṃ cet punar maraṇajanmanī / tāvat syād aśucir vipro yāvat tat syād anirdaśam //
reference: If within the ten days (of impurity) another birth or death happens, a Brahmana shall remain impure only until the (first) period of ten days has expired.
baseline: If it is found in the inner part of the body it should be reincarnated. It should be so long as it is not unclean. It is so long if it is undefiled.
morphology: If it is found in the inner part of the body it should be called death and birth again. It should be considered unclean till the time it is not known.

sanskrit: trirātram āhur āśaucam ācārye saṃsthite sati / tasya putre ca patnyāṃ ca divārātram iti sthitiḥ // śrotriye tūpasaṃpanne trirātram aśucir bhavet / mātule pakṣiṇīṃ rātriṃ śiṣyartvigbāndhaveṣu ca //
reference: They declare that, when the teacher (akarya) has died, the impurity (lasts) three days; if the (teacher's) son or wife (is dead, it lasts) a day and a night; that is a settled (rule). For a Srotriya who resides with (him out of affection), a man shall be impure for three days; for a maternal uncle, a pupil, an officiating priest, or a maternal relative, for one night together with the preceding and following days.
baseline: One should observe the three nights in the morning and evening in the preceptor his son wives day and night in the hearer three nights with the incense in the ear the mother the bird the night the disciple the blind and the uncle should be unclean.
morphology: One should observe the three nights in the morning and evening in the preceptor his sons and wives in the evening and night in the hearers the three days in the ear the birds in the mother and the disciples in the house and the children in the two houses.

sanskrit: prete rājani sajyotir yasya syād viṣaye sthitaḥ / aśrotriye tv ahaḥ kṛtsnam anūcāne tathā gurau //
reference: If the king in whose realm he resides is dead, (he shall be impure) as long as the light (of the sun or stars shines), but for (an intimate friend) who is not a Srotriya (the impurity lasts) for a whole day, likewise for a Guru who knows the Veda and the Angas.
baseline: The king should be pleased with that which is good for him and the master should be aware of that which has been done by him in the month of Ashrotra.
morphology: The king should be pleased with the matter of which he is pleased. The master should explain to him the things mentioned in the scriptures.

sanskrit: na vardhayed aghāhāni pratyūhen nāgniṣu kriyāḥ / na ca tatkarma kurvāṇaḥ sanābhyo 'py aśucir bhavet //
reference: Let him not (unnecessarily) lengthen the period of impurity, nor interrupt the rites to be performed with the sacred fires; for he who performs that (Agnihotra) rite will not be impure, though (he be) a (Sapinda) relative.
baseline: One who does not increase the number of āghāhās in the form of serpents does not do any work in the name of serpentines. He should not be defiled by the offerings made by him.
morphology: If one does not increase the number of āgha one should not do any work on the nāgas. One should not defile the kurva and the saṇas.

sanskrit: ācamya prayato nityaṃ japed aśucidarśane / saurān mantrān yathotsāhaṃ pāvamānīś ca śaktitaḥ //
reference: He who has purified himself by sipping water shall, on seeing any impure (thing or person), always mutter the sacred texts, addressed to Surya, and the Pavamani (verses).
baseline: One should always chant the hymns of the sun and the pāvāmanīśa with fervour and vigour.
morphology: One should always chant the hymns of the sun and the pāvāmanīśa with enthusiasm and vigour.

sanskrit: nāraṃ spṛṣṭvāsthi sasnehaṃ snātvā vipro viśudhyati / ācamyaiva tu niḥsnehaṃ gām ālabhyārkam īkṣya vā //
reference: A Brahmana who has touched a human bone to which fat adheres, becomes pure by bathing; if it be free from fat, by sipping water and by touching (afterwards) a cow or looking at the sun.
baseline: Having washed with the water of the river Nārā the water that touches and cleanses the earth is called nyāma nyūma gaṇa albhāraka and vaṇḍa.
morphology: Having washed with the water of the river Nārā the water that touches and cleanses the earth is called nārma nāmā gāma albhāra gaṇa vaṇḍa.

sanskrit: vṛthāsaṃkarajātānāṃ pravrajyāsu ca tiṣṭhatām / ātmanas tyāgināṃ caiva nivartetodakakriyā // pāṣaṇḍam āśritānāṃ ca carantīnāṃ ca kāmataḥ / garbhabhartṛdruhāṃ caiva surāpīnāṃ ca yoṣitām //
reference: Libations of water shall not be offered to those who (neglect the prescribed rites and may be said to) have been born in vain, to those born in consequence of an illegal mixture of the castes, to those who are ascetics (of heretical sects), and to those who have committed suicide, To women who have joined a heretical sect, who through lust live (with many men), who have caused an abortion, have killed their husbands, or drink spirituous liquor.
baseline: One who has left the self should remain in the vanity of the sons sons and daughters and those who have gone abroad one who has renounced the self one whose actions have been done in the past one with a penitentiary a dependent a charioteer a woman with a desire a husband a wife a son a daughter a man with a daughter and a wife who have taken a drink of wine.
morphology: One who has left the self one who has abandoned it one should remain in the house of the wife one with the wife and children one having left the body one living in the womb one in the caravan one wanting to have children those who are dependent on it and those who do not want to do it.

sanskrit: na rājñām aghadoṣo 'sti vratināṃ na ca sattriṇām / aindraṃ sthānam upāsīnā brahmabhūtā hi te sadā //
reference: The taint of impurity does not fall on kings, and those engaged in the performance of a vow, or of a Sattra; for the (first are) seated on the throne of Indra, and the (last two are) ever pure like Brahman.
baseline: The king is not the fault of the king nor of the devotees and not of the seventy. He always becomes Brahman by worshipping the place of Indra.
morphology: The king should never be blamed for the sins of the king. He should always be worshipped at the place of the seven gods. He would always be Brahman.

sanskrit: rājño mahātmike sthāne sadyaḥśaucaṃ vidhīyate / prajānāṃ parirakṣārtham āsanaṃ cātra kāraṇam //
reference: For a king, on the throne of magnanimity, immediate purification is prescribed, and the reason for that is that he is seated (there) for the protection of (his) subjects.
baseline: The king should sit in a place of great importance for the protection of his subjects. The seat should be placed in the seat.
morphology: The king should be placed in a place of great importance. The seat for the protection of the subjects should be kept in the same place.

sanskrit: ḍimbhāhavahatānāṃ ca vidyutā pārthivena ca / gobrāhmaṇasya caivārthe yasya cecchati pārthivaḥ //
reference: (The same rule applies to the kinsmen) of those who have fallen in a riot or a battle, (of those who have been killed) by lightning or by the king, and (of those who perished fighting) for cows and Brahmanas, and to those whom the king wishes (to be pure).
baseline: The earth should be electrified by the omens and the earth and the god of the cow should be worshipped by the earth.
morphology: The earth should be electrified by the omens the earth and the earth. The earthly body should be worshipped by the cowherd.

sanskrit: udyatair āhave śastraiḥ kṣatradharmahatasya ca / sadyaḥ saṃtiṣṭhate yajñas tathāśaucam iti sthitiḥ //
reference: By him who is slain in battle with brandished weapons according to the law of the Kshatriyas, a (Srauta) sacrifice is instantly completed, and so is the period of impurity (caused by his death); that is a settled rule.
baseline: One who invokes the gods of Kshatrādharma with weapons and destroys the religion of Kṣṭrātrā is now established as the state of oblation and purification.
morphology: One who invokes the gods of the kingdom of Kshatrādharma with weapons and kills the enemy would get the sacrifice and the position of the abode.

sanskrit: etad vo 'bhihitaṃ śaucaṃ sapiṇḍeṣu dvijottamāḥ / asapiṇḍeṣu sarveṣu pretaśuddhiṃ nibodhata //
reference: Thus the purification (required) on (the death of) Sapindas has been explained to you, O best of twice-born men; hear now the manner in which men are purified on the death of any (relative who is) not a Sapinda.
baseline: This is said to be the cleansing of the body in the two parts of the sacrament. The purification of the soul should be done in all the parts.
morphology: The same is said to be true for the purification of the body in the two parts of a body.

sanskrit: yady annam atti teṣāṃ tu daśāhenaiva śudhyati / anadann annam ahnaiva na cet tasmin gṛhe vaset //
reference: But if he eats the food of the (Sapindas of the deceased), he is purified in ten days, (but) in one day, if he does not eat their food nor dwells in their house.
baseline: If food is brought to them after ten days they would be purified. If food does not reach them after one day they should stay in that house.
morphology: If food is brought to them after ten days they would be purified. If food does not reach them after one day they should stay in that house.

sanskrit: anugamyecchayā pretaṃ jñātim ajñātim eva ca / snātvā sacailaḥ spṛṣṭvāgniṃ ghṛtaṃ prāśya viśudhyati //
reference: Having voluntarily followed a corpse, whether (that of) a paternal kinsman or (of) a stranger, he becomes pure by bathing, dressed in his clothes, by touching fire and eating clarified butter.
baseline: One who knows the spirit by the desire to follow it and does not know it after having bathed one who touches the fire having covered it with water and purifying it.
morphology: One who knows the spirit by the desire to follow it and does not know it after having bathed one who touches the fire having covered it with water cleanses it.

sanskrit: na vipraṃ sveṣu tiṣṭhatsu mṛtaṃ śūdreṇa nāyayet / asvargyā hy āhutiḥ sā syāc chūdrasaṃsparśadūṣitā //
reference: Let him not allow a dead Brahmana to be carried out by a Sudra, while men of the same caste are at hand; for that burnt-offering which is defiled by a Sudra's touch is detrimental to (the deceased's passage to) heaven.
baseline: The dead should not be carried away with the sword by the enemy. The body should be left untouched by the evil spirit. It should be destroyed by the sword.
morphology: The dead should not be carried away with the sword if the weapon is not standing on its own. It should be killed by the enemy. It is a sin. It has been defiled by the touch of the sword.

sanskrit: jñānaṃ tapo 'gnir āhāro mṛn mano vāry upāñjanam / vāyuḥ karmārkakālau ca śuddheḥ kartṝṇi dehinām //
reference: The knowledge (of Brahman) austerities, fire, (holy) food, earth, (restraint of) the internal organ, water, smearing (with cowdung), the wind, sacred rites, the sun, and time are the purifiers of corporeal (beings).
baseline: The food should be offered to the mind with the mantra of jnāṇa tāpu. The air should be given to the body with the penance of the mind and the food should also be offered with the utopāna. The body should be cleansed with the karma kaala.
morphology: One should eat food with knowledge penance mind heart food food etc. One should drink water and purify the body with the help of the wind.

sanskrit: sarveṣām eva śaucānām arthaśaucaṃ paraṃ smṛtaṃ / yo 'rthe śucir hi sa śucir na mṛdvāriśuciḥ śuciḥ //
reference: Among all modes of purification, purity in (the acquisition of) wealth is declared to be the best; for he is pure who gains wealth with clean hands, not he who purifies himself with earth and water.
baseline: One who is clean should remember that the same thing means that he is clean for all. He who is pure for all should be clean and not the one who is unclean for all others.
morphology: One who is clean should remember the meaning of the same thing as that of the unclean man. He who is not clean should be clean and not dirty.

sanskrit: kṣāntyā śudhyanti vidvāṃso dānenākāryakāriṇaḥ / pracchannapāpā japyena tapasā vedavittamāḥ //
reference: The learned are purified by a forgiving disposition, those who have committed forbidden actions by liberality, secret sinners by muttering (sacred texts), and those who best know the Veda by austerities.
baseline: The disciples are purified by the offering of gifts and the workers are made to do penance with the recitation of hymns.
morphology: The disciples are purified by the end of the month. Those who do the work by giving gifts by chanting the hymns of the hidden papa by doing penance by reciting the scriptures by offering the sacred scriptures.

sanskrit: adbhir gātrāṇi śudhyanti manaḥ satyena śudhyati / vidyātapobhyāṃ bhūtātmā buddhir jñānena śudhyati //
reference: The body is cleansed by water, the internal organ is purified by truthfulness, the individual soul by sacred learning and austerities, the intellect by (true) knowledge.
baseline: The mind is purified by the truth. The spirit the intellect and the spirit are purified with knowledge.
morphology: The mind is purified by the truth. The spirit intellect intellect and knowledge are purified with knowledge.

sanskrit: eṣa śaucasya vaḥ proktaḥ śarīrasya vinirṇayaḥ / nānāvidhānāṃ dravyāṇāṃ śuddheḥ śṛṇuta nirṇayam //
reference: Thus the precise rules for the purification of the body have been declared to you; hear now the decision (of the law) regarding the purification of the various (inanimate) things.
baseline: The same is said for defecation. The decision of the body should be made by hearing the purification of various substances.
morphology: It is said to be the cleansing of the body. It is the purification of various substances.

sanskrit: nirlepaṃ kāñcanaṃ bhāṇḍam adbhir eva viśudhyati / abjam aśmamayaṃ caiva rājataṃ cānupaskṛtam //
reference: A golden vessel which shows no stains, becomes pure with water alone, likewise what is produced in water (as shells and coral), what is made of stone, and a silver (vessel) not enchased.
baseline: One who cleanses the temple of Kanchana with a piece of pure water and a thousand cubits of ash is blessed with the kingdom of Chaṇu.
morphology: One who cleanses the temple of Kanchana with pure water would get a billion pieces of ash and the kingdom would be destroyed by the sea.

sanskrit: apām agneś ca saṃyogād dhaimaṃ raupyaṃ ca nirbabhau / tasmāt tayoḥ svayonyaiva nirṇeko guṇavattaraḥ //
reference: From the union of water and fire arose the glittering gold and silver; those two, therefore, are best purified by (the elements) from which they sprang.
baseline: One who acquires the qualities of a person by the combination of fire and fire courage silver nirbhābhū etc. would be able to determine their own merit.
morphology: The combination of fire fire courage silver and immortality would determine the quality of those who are self sufficient.

sanskrit: tāmrāyaḥkāṃsyaraityānāṃ trapuṇaḥ sīsakasya ca / śaucaṃ yathārhaṃ kartavyaṃ kṣārāmlodakavāribhiḥ // dravāṇāṃ caiva sarveṣāṃ śuddhir utpavanaṃ smṛtam / prokṣaṇaṃ saṃhatānāṃ ca dāravāṇāṃ ca takṣaṇam //
reference: Copper, iron, brass, pewter, tin, and lead must be cleansed, as may be suitable (for each particular case), by alkaline (substances), acids or water. The purification prescribed for all (sorts of) liquids is by passing two blades of Kusa grass through them, for solid things by sprinkling (them with water), for (objects) made of wood by planing them.
baseline: One should wash the copper and copper vessels the cupcakes the bottle the bottles the lid the water the saliva the liquid and all the purified products. One should immediately recall the purification of the vessels and the arches.
morphology: The purification of the copper and copper vessels the burning of the kāṇas the washing of the bottles the cleaning of the water with the salts salts and other liquid should be done in such a way. The purifying products should be prepared immediately.

sanskrit: carūṇāṃ sruksruvāṇāṃ ca śuddhir uṣṇena vāriṇā / sphyaśūrpaśakaṭānāṃ ca musalolūkhalasya ca //
reference: The Karu and (the spoons called) Sruk and Sruva must be cleaned with hot water, likewise (the wooden sword, called) Sphya, the winnowing-basket (Surpa), the cart (for bringing the grain), the pestle and the mortar.
baseline: The chariots the chariot the sword the purifier the warren with heat the king of the muslims the ruler of the pagans the chieftain the governor of the kingdom of the Musalulukkhas and the chief minister of the princely state.
morphology: The chariots the chariot the sword the purifier the warring with heat the king of the muslilokkhas the ruler of the king and those of the sons of the sage should be purified.

sanskrit: cailavac carmaṇāṃ śuddhir vaidalānāṃ tathaiva ca / śākamūlaphalānāṃ ca dhānyavac chuddhir iṣyate // kauśeyāvikayor ūṣaiḥ kutapānām ariṣṭakaiḥ / śrīphalair aṃśupaṭṭānāṃ kṣaumāṇāṃ gaurasarṣapaiḥ //
reference: Skins and (objects) made of split cane must be cleaned like clothes; vegetables, roots, and fruit like grain; Silk and woollen stuffs with alkaline earth; blankets with pounded Arishta (fruit); Amsupattas with Bel fruit; linen cloth with (a paste of) yellow mustard.
baseline: One would get rid of the grains fruits vegetables fruits etc. with the help of the cow cow goat buffalo buffaloes goats cow and goat etc.
morphology: One would get rid of the cow cow goat sheep cow and cow buffalo sheep and goat etc.

sanskrit: kṣaumavac chaṅkhaśṛṅgāṇām asthidantamayasya ca / śuddhir vijānatā kāryā gomūtreṇodakena vā // prokṣaṇāt tṛṇakāṣṭhaṃ ca palālaṃ caiva śudhyati / mārjanopāñjanair veśma punaḥpākena mṛnmayam //
reference: A man who knows (the law) must purify conch-shells, horn, bone and ivory, like linen cloth, or with a mixture of cow's urine and water. Grass, wood, and straw become pure by being sprinkled (with water), a house by sweeping and smearing (it with cowdung or whitewash), an earthen (vessel) by a second burning.
baseline: One who cleanses the ground with a cow cow buffalo cow or cow is purified by the use of cow and cow dung. One who purifies the grass and grass from the ground and leaves should be re-cooked with the mixture of ghee and rice.
morphology: One who cleanses the body of a cow with the help of cow cow and other animals should be washed with ghee and ghee. One who purifies the ground with the use of cow and cow dung should be purified with the aid of a trowel and a piece of grass. One would get rid of the mud by cooking the garland and food again.

sanskrit: madyair mūtraiḥ purīṣair vā ṣṭhīvanaih pūyaśoṇitaiḥ / saṃspṛṣṭaṃ naiva śuddhyeta punaḥpākena mṛnmayam //
reference: An earthen vessel which has been defiled by spirituous liquor, urine, ordure, saliva, pus or blood cannot be purified by another burning.
baseline: The ground should not be purified by the use of wine urine puris water flowers perfumes etc.
morphology: The ground should not be purified by the use of wine urine purse water flowers flowers etc. and the ground should be cooked again.

sanskrit: saṃmārjanopāñjanena sekenollekhanena ca / gavāṃ ca parivāsena bhūmiḥ śudhyati pañcabhiḥ //
reference: Land is purified by (the following) five (modes, viz.) by sweeping, by smearing (it with cowdung), by sprinkling (it with cows' urine or milk), by scraping, and by cows staying (on it during a day and night).
baseline: The land is cleansed by the combination of the five elements of sāmarjana pājāṇa sikonuṇa and gavāna. The earth is purified by the arrangement of five elements.
morphology: The land is cleansed by the combination of the five elements of sāmarjana pājāṇa sikonuṇa and gavāva.

sanskrit: yāvan nāpaity amedhyāktād gandho lepaś ca tatkṛtaḥ / tāvan mṛdvāri cādeyaṃ sarvāsu dravyaśuddhiṣu //
reference: As long as the (foul) smell does not leave an (object) defiled by impure substances, and the stain caused by them (does not disappear), so long must earth and water be applied in cleansing (inanimate) things.
baseline: One should wash all the things that are impure with the fragrance and ointment from the impure water.
morphology: One who has not had a bad day would get the smell and the perfume from the unclean place. He would get all the things and purification from the earth.

sanskrit: ūrdhvaṃ nābher yāni khāni tāni medhyāni sarvaśaḥ / yāny adhas tāny amedhyāni dehāc caiva malāś cyutāḥ //
reference: All those cavities (of the body) which lie above the navel are pure, (but) those which are below the navel are impure, as well as excretions that fall from the body.
baseline: The upper part of the body should be covered with a mālāśa. The outer part should cover all the parts of the face. The lower part should be washed with a malāṣa.
morphology: The upper part of the body should be covered with the leaves the upper part with the hair and the lower part with hair.

sanskrit: vasā śukram asṛṅ majjā mūtraviṭ ghrāṇakarṇaviṭ / śleśma aśru dūṣikā svedo dvādaśaite nṛṇāṃ malāḥ //
reference: Oily exudations, semen, blood, (the fatty substance of the) brain, urine, faeces, the mucus of the nose, ear-wax, phlegm, tears, the rheum of the eyes, and sweat are the twelve impurities of human (bodies).
baseline: The vāsa sūkrā asrāṇga mājā urine fragrance ear hair tears defilement blood blood and blood should be offered to the twelve nirās.
morphology: The vāsa sūkrā asrāṇga mājā urine fragrance ear hair tears defilement blood and blood should be offered to the twelve niras.

sanskrit: ekā liṅge gude tisras tathaikatra kare daśa / ubhayoḥ sapta dātavyā mṛdaḥ śuddhim abhīpsatā //
reference: He who desires to be pure, must clean the organ by one (application of) earth, the anus by (applying earth) three (times), the (left) hand alone by (applying it) ten (times), and both (hands) by (applying it) seven (times).
baseline: One should make three pieces of the anus in one penis and ten pieces in another. Seven pieces of mud should be given to both of them.
morphology: One should make three pieces of the rectum in one piece and ten pieces in another. Seven pieces of mud should be given in both the parts.

sanskrit: etac chaucaṃ gṛhasthānāṃ dviguṇaṃ brahmacāriṇām / triguṇaṃ syād vanasthānāṃ yatīnāṃ tu caturguṇam //
reference: Such is the purification ordained for householders; (it shall be) double for students, treble for hermits, but quadruple for ascetics.
baseline: This square is twice the area of the house for brahmins three times the area for foresters and four times for those who do not.
morphology: This square is twice the area of the house for celibates three times the area for foresters and four times for those who do not.

sanskrit: trir ācāmed apaḥ pūrvaṃ dviḥ pramṛjyāt tato mukham / śarīraṃ śaucam icchan hi strī śūdras tu sakṛt sakṛt //
reference: Let him who desires bodily purity first sip water three times, and then twice wipe his mouth; but a woman and a Sudra (shall perform each act) once (only).
baseline: O Śudras women who wish to defecate the body should be circumcised with the three achaṇas and the two prāmījas should be removed first.
morphology: O Śudras women who wish to defecate on the face the body and the body should be circumcised by the three aṣāma.

sanskrit: nocchiṣṭaṃ kurvate mukhyā vipruṣo 'ṅgaṃ na yānti yāḥ / na śmaśrūṇi gatāny āsyaṃ na dantāntaradhiṣṭhitam //
reference: Drops (of water) from the mouth which do not fall on a limb, do not make (a man) impure, nor the hair of the moustache entering the mouth, nor what adheres to the teeth.
baseline: One who does not go to the head of the chief priest and does not destroy the body one who has not gone to the grave and one who is not dependent on the teeth.
morphology: One who does not go to the head of the chief priest should not be ashamed. Those who do not leave the grave should not go. One who is not ashamed of the fact that the body is not placed inside the teeth.

sanskrit: spṛśanti bindavaḥ pādau ya ācāmayataḥ parān / bhaumikais te samā jñeyā na tair āprayato bhavet //
reference: Drops which trickle on the feet of him who offers water for sipping to others, must be considered as equal to (water collected on the ground; they render him not impure.
baseline: The points of the feet that are touched on the other side of the earth are known to be equal to the ground.
morphology: The points that touch the feet and the other parts of the earth are known to be the same.

sanskrit: ucchiṣṭena tu saṃspṛṣṭo dravyahastaḥ kathaṃ cana / anidhāyaiva tad dravyam ācāntaḥ śucitām iyāt //
reference: He who, while carrying anything in any manner, is touched by an impure (person or thing), shall become pure, if he performs an ablution, without putting down that object.
baseline: How can one not touch the object of contact with the object after having removed it. The object should be purified from the body after having been washed.
morphology: How can one not touch the object of contact with the object that has been removed. The object should be kept clean in the absence of the object.

sanskrit: vānto viriktaḥ snātvā tu ghṛtaprāśanam ācaret / ācāmed eva bhuktvānnaṃ snānaṃ maithuninaḥ smṛtam // suptvā kṣutvā ca bhuktvā ca niṣṭhīvyoktvānṛtāni ca / pītvāpo 'dhyeṣyamāṇaś ca ācāmet prayato 'pi san //
reference: He who has vomited or purged shall bathe, and afterwards eat clarified butter; but if (the attack comes on) after he has eaten, let him only sip water; bathing is prescribed for him who has had intercourse with a woman. Though he may be (already) pure, let him sip water after sleeping, sneezing, eating, spitting, telling untruths, and drinking water, likewise when he is going to study the Veda.
baseline: One should wash the water with ghee after bathing with vantu vīrīktā bath with water with the same quantity of water as before. One should also wash the body with water after lying down and wash it with water. One would eat the water after having washed it with the water of the same amount.
morphology: One should wash the water with ghee after having washed the leaves bath with water after having bathed the victim bathing with gau bath and bathing in the same way. Having washed the victim after having slept the accused should be killed and those who have been beaten should be made to drink water and drink water.

sanskrit: eṣāṃ śaucavidhiḥ kṛtsno dravyaśuddhis tathaiva ca / ukto vaḥ sarvavarṇānāṃ strīṇāṃ dharmān nibodhata //
reference: Thus the rules of personal purification for men of all castes, and those for cleaning (inanimate) things, have been fully declared to you: hear now the duties of women.
baseline: These methods of defecation are said to purify things. Similarly the said method should be used to teach women of all hues and religions.
morphology: These methods of defecation are said to purify things. Similarly the said method should be used to teach women of all hues and religions.

sanskrit: bālayā vā yuvatyā vā vṛddhayā vāpi yoṣitā / na svātantryeṇa kartavyaṃ kiṃ cid kāryaṃ gṛheṣv api //
reference: By a girl, by a young woman, or even by an aged one, nothing must be done independently, even in her own house.
baseline: A young woman or a boy should not do any work in the house.
morphology: A woman should not do any work at home with the help of a boy or a young man or an old woman.

sanskrit: bālye pitur vaśe tiṣṭhet pāṇigrāhasya yauvane / putrāṇāṃ bhartari prete na bhajet strī svatantratām // pitrā bhartrā sutair vāpi necched viraham ātmanaḥ / eṣāṃ hi viraheṇa strī garhye kuryād ubhe kule //
reference: In childhood a female must be subject to her father, in youth to her husband, when her lord is dead to her sons; a woman must never be independent. She must not seek to separate herself from her father, husband, or sons; by leaving them she would make both (her own and her husband's) families contemptible.
baseline: The father should remain in the womb of the father in his childhood. The husband of the sons should not worship the wife for freedom. The wife should not be worshipped by the husband the wife should be separated from the husband and the husband should not do so. The mother should be kept in the house of the bridegroom.
morphology: The father should remain in the womb of the child in the form of a calf in the youth in the absence of the husband of the sons in the marriage. The wife should not be free if the husband does not love the wife. The husband should not marry the wife in the house of the mother. The mother should be separated from the husband in the presence of the son. The woman should be left alone in the pit.

sanskrit: nāsti strīṇāṃ pṛthag yajño na vrataṃ nāpy upoṣaṇam / patiṃ śuśrūṣate yena tena svarge mahīyate //
reference: No sacrifice, no vow, no fast must be performed by women apart (from their husbands); if a wife obeys her husband, she will for that (reason alone) be exalted in heaven.
baseline: There is no separate sacrifice for women no fasting fasting serving the husband and making him merry in heaven.
morphology: There is no separate sacrifice for women there is no fasting for the husband the husband should be served with it and he should be blessed with heaven.

sanskrit: pāṇigrāhasya sādhvī strī jīvato vā mṛtasya vā / patilokam abhīpsantī nācaret kiṃ cid apriyam //
reference: A faithful wife, who desires to dwell (after death) with her husband, must never do anything that might displease him who took her hand, whether he be alive or dead.
baseline: A virtuous woman of the pāṇigraha is said to be alive or dead. The recitation of the hymn abhīpāsātī should not be considered as undesirable.
morphology: A woman who is a devotee of Panigraha living or dead should not be worshipped in return. What is wrong with her?

sanskrit: kāmaṃ tu ksapayed dehaṃ puṣpamūlaphalaiḥ śubhaiḥ / na tu nāmāpi gṛhṇīyāt patyau prete parasya tu //
reference: At her pleasure let her emaciate her body by (living on) pure flowers, roots, and fruit; but she must never even mention the name of another man after her husband has died.
baseline: The body should be offered with flowers and fruits and not with the name of the bridegroom.
morphology: The body should be offered with flowers fruits and good things. The name should also be taken from the husband and the love should be revealed to him.

sanskrit: āsītā maraṇāt ksāntā niyatā brahmacāriṇī / yo dharma ekapatnīnāṃ kāṅkṣantī tam anuttamam //
reference: Until death let her be patient (of hardships), self-controlled, and chaste, and strive (to fulfil) that most excellent duty which (is prescribed) for wives who have one husband only.
baseline: One who desires the righteousness of a single wife would be better off.
morphology: One who desires to marry a woman of the same religion would be better off.

sanskrit: mṛte bhartari sāḍhvī strī brahmacarye vyavasthitā / svargaṃ gacchaty aputrāpi yathā te brahmacāriṇaḥ // apatyalobhād yā tu strī bhartāram ativartate / seha nindām avāpnoti paralokāc ca hīyate //
reference: A virtuous wife who after the death of her husband constantly remains chaste, reaches heaven, though she have no son, just like those chaste men. But a woman who from a desire to have offspring violates her duty towards her (deceased) husband, brings on herself disgrace in this world, and loses her place with her husband (in heaven).
baseline: A woman who has committed an act of celibacy after having killed her husband and has made arrangements for her to go to heaven as if she were a son of a brahmin would be condemned by the husband and her children. That woman who commits adultery would be punished by the king.
morphology: A woman who has married a man after having died should be made a brahmacharya by the husband. A woman going to heaven should be given a son as if she had been a celibate. If a woman overreaches her husband by having children she would be condemned and the other world would be destroyed.

sanskrit: nānyotpannā prajāstīha na cāpy anyaparigrahe / na dvitīyaś ca sādhvīnāṃ kva cid bhartopadiśyate //
reference: Offspring begotten by another man is here not (considered lawful), nor (does offspring begotten) on another man's wife (belong to the begetter), nor is a second husband anywhere prescribed for virtuous women.
baseline: A priest should not be charged with the offence of committing a crime against another person. He should not charge any other person for committing an offence.
morphology: One should not accuse the sages of any evil deeds and the other sadhvis of doing evil.

sanskrit: patiṃ hitvāpakṛṣṭaṃ svam utkṛṣṭaṃ yā niṣevate / nindyaiva sā bhavel loke parapūrveti cocyate //
reference: She who cohabits with a man of higher caste, forsaking her own husband who belongs to a lower one, will become contemptible in this world, and is called a remarried woman (parapurva).
baseline: One who denies the superiority of the self by having a husband killed is said to be a superior. One who denigrates the superior would be declared a superior by the people.
morphology: One who destroys the master the master and the master of the enemy and forbids the best of oneself and denigrates others would be considered as superior.

sanskrit: vyabhicārāt tu bhartuḥ strī loke prāpnoti nindyatām / śṛgālayoniṃ prāpnoti pāparogaiś ca pīḍyate //
reference: By violating her duty towards her husband, a wife is disgraced in this world, (after death) she enters the womb of a jackal, and is tormented by diseases (the punishment of) her sin.
baseline: A woman who has a husband fornicating with a man would get a man to be defrauded. A man who gets a fox would suffer from sin and disease.
morphology: A husband gets a wife from a man for committing adultery and a woman gets a cowardice. He also gets a disease and suffers from sin.

sanskrit: uddāmakallolaravā dehādrau vahatīha me / taraṅgataralākārā tarattṛṣṇātaraṅgiṇī //
reference: The stream of worldly avarice flows like a rapid current within the rock of my body, with precipitate force (in my actions), and loud resounding waves.
baseline: May the fiery rock bearers carry the body and the earth. The stripes bearers of the wave bearers are the three colours of the sun.
morphology: May one who carries the head shoulders arms body arms and legs the bearer of the waves the host of water the king of the earth the lord of all beings the god of the universe the goddess of all things the mother of all forms.

sanskrit: vegaṃ saroddhumudito vātyayeva jarattṛṇam / nītaḥ kaluṣayā kvāpi tṛṣṇayā cittacātakaḥ //
reference: Our minds are driven by foul avarice from one place to another, as the dusty dry hays are borne away by the winds, and as the Chatakas are impelled by thirst to fly about.
baseline: One who has a desire for a child should take the jārāttrāna with the bow and bow with speed the sārudha the mouth and the wind.
morphology: One who has a thirst for water should take the jārāttrāna with speed sārudha muḍī vaṭya nītā kuluṣa kāvā and chātaka with thirst.

sanskrit: yāṃ yāmahamatīvāsthāṃ saṃśrayāmi guṇaśriyām / tāṃ tāṃ kṛntati me tṛṣṇā tantrīmiva kumūṣikā //
reference: It is avarice which destroys all the good qualities and grace which we adopted to ourselves in good faith, just as the mischievous mouse severs the wires.
baseline: The meritorious woman who has been blessed with the yama māhmī vāsāya that is the one who gives her the kumushika and the string of desire.
morphology: The meritorious woman who has been blessed with the yama māhmī vāsā is called kumushika.

sanskrit: payasīva jaratparṇaṃ vāyāviva jarattṛṇam / nabhasīva śaranmeghaścintācakre bhramāmyaham //
reference: We turn about upon the wheel of our cares, like withered leaves (floating) upon the water, and like dry grass uplifted by the wind, and as autumnal clouds (moving) in the sky.
baseline: One who has gone to the abode of the sun one who has not gone into the abyss and one who does not want to go into the illusion and wanders in the chakra should be worshipped.
morphology: One should walk in the circle of the mind with the pāyāsiva jāratpāṇa vāya yāvā zāratrāṇā nāśiva sārmanma ghaṇṭa.

sanskrit: gantumāspadamātmīyamasamarthadhiyo vayam / cintājāle vimuhyāmo jāle śakunayo yathā //
reference: Being over powered by avarice, we are disable to reach the goal (of perfection), as a bird entangled in the snare, is kept from its flight.
baseline: We should be able to reach the place of the soul to reach it to the water of the mind to go into the net and to cast a spell as if it were an omen.
morphology: We should go to the place where we want to go and worship the spirit. We should worship the waters of the mind and the waters in the net.

sanskrit: tṛṣṇābhidhānayā tāta dagdho'smi jvālayā tathā / yathā dāhopaśamanamāśaṃke nāmṛtairapi //
reference: I am so greatly burnt by the flame of avarice, that I doubt whether this inflammation may be assuaged even by administration of nectar itself.
baseline: The fire should be lit by the invocation of Trīnṣṇa. Just as the flame should be burnt by the oblation of the fire the fire should also be burnt with the invoking of the flame.
morphology: The fire should be lit by the invocation of Trīṣṇa. Just as the flame should be burned by the oblation of the fire the fire should also be burnt by the offering of namritti.

sanskrit: dūraṃ dūramito gatvā sametya ca punaḥpunaḥ / bhramatyāśu diganteṣu tṛṣṇonmattā turaṅgamī //
reference: Avarice like a heated-mare takes me far and farther still from my place, and brings me back to it again and again. Thus it hurries me up and down and to and fro in all directions for ever.
baseline: Having gone far away and having completed it again one should again go back to the distant places of the gods. One would get a threesome in the sky.
morphology: Having gone far away and having completed it again one should return to the sky with the illusion. One should go to the abode of thirst and happiness.

sanskrit: jaḍasaṃsargiṇī tṛṣṇā kṛtordhvādhogamāgamā / kṣubdhā granthimatī nityamāraghaṭṭāgrarajjuvat //
reference: We are pulled up and cast down again like a bucket in the well, by the string of avarice.
baseline: One who has made a wish by the combination of jāda sāṅgrāga śvādhvā dhoga māgmā gland gṇṭimātī gnāṭi maraghatā garuja rājvātā.
morphology: One who desires to have the union with the flesh should go to the highest place of worship. One who is hungry should always get rid of the pitchers of the earth.

sanskrit: antargrathitayā dehe sarvaduśchedayā'nayā / rajjvevāśu balīvardastṛṣṇayā vāhyate janaḥ //
reference: Man is led about like a bullock of burthen by his avarice, which bends his heart as fast as the string does the beast, and which it is hard for him to break.
baseline: One who is born out of the blood of a cow and who has been cast into the body with all the malefications should be washed away with the raga and the bālivardha.
morphology: One who is born out of the blood of a cow and who has been cast into the body with all the malefications should be carried away by the sacrifice of the king.

sanskrit: putramitrakalatrāditṛṣṇayā nityakṛṣṭayā / khageṣviva kirātyedaṃ jālaṃ lokeṣu racyate //
reference: As the huntress spreads her net to catch birds in it, so does our affection for our friends, wives and children stretch these snares to entrap us every day.
baseline: The net is said to be built among the people by the son of Śiva.
morphology: A net is made among the people by the son Śutramī Śiva Kālātratrādīṣṇu with the eternal kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit: bhīṣayatyapi dhīraṃ māmandhayatyapi sekṣaṇam / khedayatyapi sānandaṃ tṛṣṇākṛṣṇeva śarvarī //
reference: Avarice like a dark night terrifies even the wise, blindfolds the keen-sighted, and depresses the spirit of the happiest of men.
baseline: Having feared him having feared him and having sought him he should be persecuted having suffered him enjoying himself and having longed for him should be worshipped.
morphology: Having feared him having feared him and having worshipped him one should seek protection. Having persecuted him he should enjoy happiness and desire.

sanskrit: kuṭilā komalasparśā viṣavaiṣamyaśaṃsinī / daśatyapi manākspṛṣṭā tṛṣṇā kṛṣṇeva bhoginī //
reference: Our appetite is as heinous as a serpent, soft to feel, but full of deadly poison, and bites us as soon as it is felt.
baseline: O Kṛṣṇa the savior the one who is possessed by the desire of the mind and the other by the evil one is a thief a person who is poisonous and blessed.
morphology: A woman who is a thief a soft touch a poison and a blasphemous person a woman who enjoys the desire of the mind and a person who is fond of Krishna should be worshipped.

sanskrit: bhindatī hṛdayaṃ puṃsāṃ māyāmayavidhāyinī / daurbhāgyadāyinī dīnā tṛṣṇā kṛṣṇeva rākṣasī //
reference: It is also like a black sorceress that deludes men by her magic, but pierces him in his heart, and exposes him to danger afterwards.
baseline: The heart of Bhinda the heart of Pūṇa the goddess of ill fortune the divine goddess of misfortune the celestial goddess Trināna the demoness of Krishna and others.
morphology: The heart of Bhinda the heart of Pūṇasa the goddess of ill fortune the divine goddess of misfortune Trīnṣṇava the demoness and the goddess Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit: tandrītantrīgaṇaiḥ kośaṃ dadhānā pariveṣṭitam / nānande rājate brahmaṃstṛṣṇā jarjaravallakī //
reference: This body of ours shattered by our avarice is like a worn out lute, fastened by arteries resembling the wires, but emitting no pleasing sound.
baseline: The body of the king is surrounded by three groups of devotees. Brahman is the one who reigns in the nine days.
morphology: The body is surrounded by the three parts of the body. Brahman reigns in the nine parts. He is the one who is in a bad condition.

sanskrit: nityamevātimalinā kaṭukonmādadāyinī / dīrghatantrī ghanasnehā tṛṣṇā gahvaravallarī //
reference: Our avarice is like the long fibered, dark and juicy poisonous creeper called Kaduka, that grows in the caverns of mountains, and maddens men by its flavour.
baseline: O goddess of the earth one who gives to the earth with the wind and water with the katukonma mādaṇī thread longs deeps love desire heart heart etc.
morphology: O goddess of the air water fire fire and water the goddess of wealth the mother of wealth and wealth longsuffering deep love desire deep and vaṇvālārī.

sanskrit: anānandakarī śūnyā niṣphalā vyarthamunnatā / amaṅgalakarī krūrā tṛṣṇā kṣīṇeva mañjarī //
reference: Avarice is as vain and inane, fruitless and aspiring, unpleasant and perilous, as the dry twig of a tree, which (bears no fruit or flower) but is hurtful with its prickly point.
baseline: Anāṇandakārī is void and unfruitful. A person who is not able to bear the brunt of the temptation is called a manjari.
morphology: Anāṇandakārī is void and unfruitful. A person who is evil and has a penance for the wrath of the enemy is free from the desire for pleasure.

sanskrit: anāvarjitacittāpi sarvamevānudhāvati / na cāpnoti phalaṃ kiṃcittṛṣṇā jīrṇeva kāminī //
reference: Venality is like a churlish old woman, who from the incontinence of her heart, courts the company of every man, without gaining the object of her desire.
baseline: Even if the mind is unformed it will not bear any fruit and will not be destroyed.
morphology: Even if the mind is unformed one would not get all the weapons. The fruit would not bear any fruit and the body would get destroyed.

sanskrit: saṃsāravṛnde mahati nānārasasamākule / bhuvanābhogaraṅgeṣu tṛṣṇā jaraṭhanartakī //
reference: Greediness as an old actress plays her various parts in the vast theatre of world, in order to please the different tastes of her audience.
baseline: One who has great desire in the circle of the world in the collection of all the elements in those parts of the earth and in those areas of the enjoyment one who has a desire for food and water should do great work.
morphology: One who has great desire in the world in the universe in all the parts of the universe and in the cosmic world is blessed with the fragrance of the earth.

sanskrit: jarākusumitārūḍhā pātotpātaphalāvaliḥ / saṃsārajaṃgale dīrghe tṛṣṇā viṣalatā tatā //
reference: Parsimony is as a poisonous plant growing in the wide wilderness of the world, bearing old age and infirmity as its flowers, and producing our troubles as its fruits.
baseline: The fruit of the leaves should be made with the garākusumita and the leaves are made of water. The long thirst in the forest of the world should be filled with poison.
morphology: The fruit is made of leaves and the leaves are made of jarākusumita. The long thirst in the forest of the world is poisonous.

sanskrit: yanna śakroti tatrāpi dhatte tāṇḍavitāṃ gatim / nṛtyatyānandarahitaṃ tṛṣṇā jīrṇeva nartakī //
reference: Our churlishnesss resembles an aged actress, attempting a manly feat she has not the strength to perform, yet keeping up the dance without pleasing.
baseline: The dance should be performed with the accompaniment of yāna shakrātī tāndavita gait nārāṇatya anandaṇa and without the desire.
morphology: The dance should be performed in the same manner as the yāna shakrāti dhātā tāndavītā and gāti.

sanskrit: bhṛśaṃ sphurati nīhāre śāmyatyāloka āgate / durlaṅghayeṣu padaṃ dhatte cintā capalabarhiṇī //
reference: Our fleeting thoughts are as fickle as pea-hens, soaring over inaccessible heights under the clouds (of ignorance); but ceasing to fly in the day light.
baseline: The bhiṣma is the flutter in the nee the shadow of the earth and the earth. The chariot of the charioteer is the worry in the case of a person who has lost his position in a difficult position.
