morphology: One who touches the ground with the bhiṣma flicks in the nee one who has to face the earth with the sand one should be worried about the feet of the charioteer.

sanskrit: jaḍakallolabahulā ciraṃ śūnyāntarāntarā / kṣaṇamullāsamāyāti tṛṣṇā prāvṛṭtaraṅgiṇī //
reference: Avarice is like a river in the rains, rising for a time with its rolling waves, and afterwards lying low in its empty bed.
baseline: The thirst for water is manifested in the form of a lotus and a lot of water in the middle of the sky.
morphology: One who has a desire for water in the form of a lotus and a lot of water should be made to sit in the middle of the sky for a while.

sanskrit: naṣṭamutsṛjya tiṣṭhantaṃ tṛṣṇā vṛkṣamivāparam / puruṣātpuruṣaṃ yāti tṛṣṇā loleva pakṣiṇī //
reference: Avarice is as inconstant as a female bird, which changes her mates at times, and quits the arbor that no longer bears any fruit.
baseline: Having created the destruction of the earth one should stand on the tree of thirst. One who has got the desire of the man should go to the garden of birds.
morphology: Having created the fragrance the bird should stand above the tree of thirst. The man should be worshipped as the prasadam. The bird should be kept as the lloka of desire.

sanskrit: padaṃ karotyalaṅghye'pi tṛptāpi phalamīhate / ciraṃ tiṣṭhati naikatra tṛṣṇā capalamarkaṭī //
reference: The greedy are as unsteady as the flouncing monkey, which is never restive at any place, but moves to places impassable by others, and craving for fruits even when satiate.
baseline: Even if one is satisfied with the position of the kārūtīla one will get the fruit. One would get the thirst at some place.
morphology: Even if one is satisfied with the position of the kārūtīla one will get the fruit. One would get the thirst at some place.

sanskrit: idaṃ kṛtvedamāyāti sarvamevāsamañjasam / anārataṃ ca yatate tṛṣṇā ceṣṭeva daivikī //
reference: The acts of avarice are as inconstant as those of chance, both of which are ever on the alert, but never attended with their sequence.
baseline: Having done this one would get all the things that belong to ones self. One would get the immortality of the gods by having a desire.
morphology: Having done this one would get all the things that are present in the temple. One would get the immortality of the gods by having a thirst.

sanskrit: kṣaṇamāyāti pātālaṃ kṣaṇaṃ yāti nabhasthalam / kṣaṇaṃ bhramati dikkuñje tṛṣṇā hṛtpadmaṣaṭpadī //
reference: Our venality is like a black-bee sitting upon the lotus of our hearts, and thence making its rambles above, below and all about us in a moment.
baseline: One who has gone to a place that is not far away for a while one who has wandered for a moment and who has made a wish for the heart and the body of a person in the direction of the heart.
morphology: One who has gone to a place that is not far away for a while one who has wandered in the direction of the heart and the heart for a long time and one who is in the right direction for a short while should go to the abode.

sanskrit: sarvasaṃsāradoṣāṇāṃ tṛṣṇaikā dīrghaduḥkhadā / antaḥpurasthamapi yā yojayatyatisaṃkaṭe //
reference: Of all worldly evils, avarice is the source of the longest woe. She exposes to peril even the most secluded man.
baseline: One who has longed for all the evils and misdeeds and has longsuffering should also add to the trouble in the inner court.
morphology: One who has longsuffering for all samsara and bad things should also add to the misery in the inner world.

sanskrit: prayacchati paraṃ jāḍyaṃ paramālokarodhinī / mohanīhāragahanā tṛṣṇā jaladamālikā //
reference: Avarice like a group of clouds, is fraught with a thick mist of error, obstructing the light of heaven, and causing a dull insensibility.
baseline: One who has sought the protection of the world beyond the realm of the universe one who is enamoured by the elements of the earth and one who has a penance for water should seek it.
morphology: One who has sought the protection of the world beyond the realm of the celestial body one who has been enthralled by the fire of the water one with the goddess of the heart and one with water is worshipped.

sanskrit: sarveṣāṃ jantujātānāṃ saṃsāravyavahāriṇām / pariprotamanomālā tṛṣṇā bandhanarajjuvat //
reference: Penury which seems to gird the breasts of worldly people with chains of gems and jewels, binds them as beasts with halters about the necks.
baseline: All beings beings and the world should be worshipped with the pratyotmāla garland.
morphology: All beings beings creatures and the world should be worshipped with the pratyotmāla garland.

sanskrit: vicitravarṇā viguṇā dīrghā malinasaṃsthitiḥ / śūnyā śūnyapadā tṛṣṇā śakrakārmukadharmiṇī //
reference: Covetousness stretches itself long and wide and presents to us a variety of hues as the rainbow. It is equally unsubstantial and without any property as the iris, resting in vapour and vacuum and being but a shadow itself.
baseline: A woman who is of a strange colour and has a long and dirty condition should be made to crave for nothing.
morphology: O woman of good deeds who has a long and dirty condition who is of a strange colour who desires nothing and who has an empty position becomes a goddess of good conduct.

sanskrit: aśanirguṇasasyānāṃ phalitā śaradāpadām / himaṃ saṃvitsarojānāṃ tamasāṃ dīrghayāminī //
reference: It burns away our good qualities as electric fire does the hay; it numbs our good sense as the frost freezes the lotus; it grows our evils as autumn does the grass; and it increases our ignorance as the winter prolongs the night.
baseline: The fruit of the buds of Asaṇirguna should be offered to the king of Sāradapada. The sum of the fruits of the rosaries should be given to him as long as possible.
morphology: The fruit of the buds of Asaṇirguna is said to be the fruit of Śarada. The fruits of hīma sambhitsara rojas tāmasa and dirhāmī are described.

sanskrit: saṃsāranāṭakanaṭī kāryālayavihaṃgamī / mānasāraṇyahariṇī smarasaṃgītavallakī //
reference: Greediness is as an actress in the stage of the world; she is as a bird flying out of the nest of our houses; as a deer running about in the desert of our hearts; and as a lute making us sing and dance at its tune.
baseline: The samsara drama is performed in the form of a devotional song. The hymns are sung by the lord of the universe.
morphology: One who performs the samsara nataka and the kāṇatakāṇī of the office should perform the hymns. One who sings the hymn sāmarāṇya hārīṇī sāmrāgī vallaki etc.

sanskrit: vyavahārābdhilaharī mohamātaṅgaśrṛṅkhalā / sarganyagrodhasulatā duḥkhakairavacandrikā //
reference: Our desires like billows toss us about in the ocean of our earthly cares; they bind us fast to delusion as fetters do the elephant. Like the ficus indicus they produce the roots of our regeneration, and like moon beams they put our budding woes to bloom.
baseline: One who has done the ritual should be guided by the illusion of the body and the chain of the limbs. One who does not suffer from the anger of the heaven one who does the chandrīkāra of sorrow and others.
morphology: One who is behaving in a manner that is similar to that of a celestial body one who is having an illusion one with a limb and a chain of limbs and one who does not suffer from the evil of anger and sorrow and one with the moon.

sanskrit: jarāmaraṇaduḥkhānāmekā ratnasamudgikā / ādhivyādhivilāsānāṃ nityaṃ mattā vilāsinī //
reference: Avarice like (Pandora's) box is filled with miseries, decrepitude and death, and is full of disorder and disasters like a mad bacchanal.
baseline: The gems ornaments ornaments and other objects are the eternal means of enjoyment and pleasure.
morphology: The gems and ornaments of the kingdom of Jārāma Marāna Dākhana etc. are always rich in wealth and wealth.

sanskrit: kṣaṇamālokavimalā sāndhakāralavā kṣaṇam / vyomavīthyupamā tṛṣṇā nīhāragahanā kṣaṇam //
reference: Our wishes are sometimes as pure as light and at others as foul as darkness; now they are as clear as the milky way, and again as obscure as thickest mists.
baseline: One who is in the world for a while one who is dark and has no hair one with the air one having the heart and one who has a desire for a new body one should be in the space for a moment.
morphology: One who is in the world for a while one who is dark and has no hair one with the heart one in the air one having the desire for water and one who has the heart for a long time.

sanskrit: gacchatyupaśamaṃ tṛṣṇā kāyavyāyāmaśāntaye / tamī ghanatamaḥkṛṣṇā yathā rakṣonivṛttaye //
reference: All our bodily troubles are avoided by our abstaining from avarice, as we are freed from fear of night goblins at the dispersion of darkness.
baseline: The thirst should be attained by going to the abode of Śuṣma in the Kaavyāma abode in peace. Then the highest form of Kṛṣṇa should be maintained in the form of the rakshavas.
morphology: One should go to the abode of Śuśma and seek tranquillity in the practice of Kaavyāma. One should be as dense as Kṛṣṇa in the process of protection.

sanskrit: tāvanmuhyatyayaṃ mūko loko vilulitāśayaḥ / yāvadevānusaṃdhatte tṛṣṇā viṣaviṣūcikā //
reference: So long do men remain in their state of (dead like) dumbness and mental delirium, as they are subject to the poisonous cholic of avarice.
baseline: The thirst of the gods is poisonous and poisonous.
morphology: One who has a desire for the gods would be poisonous and poisonous.

sanskrit: loko'yamakhilaṃ duḥkhaṃ cintayojjhitayojjhati / tṛṣṇāviṣūcikāmantraścintātyāgo hi kathyate //
reference: Men may get rid of their misery by their being freed from anxieties. It is the abandonment of cares which is said to be the best remedy of avarice.
baseline: One who has a desire for a thing is said to be a man of good fortune. One who does not want to suffer or suffer is called a man with a thirst a mind and a mind.
morphology: It is said to be the mantra for the desire desire worry sorrow anxiety anxiety etc.

sanskrit: tṛṇapāṣāṇakāṣṭhādisarvamāmiṣaśaṅkayā / ādadānā sphuratyante tṛṣṇā matsyī hrade yathā //
reference: As the fishes in a pond fondly grasp the bait in expectation of a sop, so do the avaricious lay hold on any thing, be it wood or stone or even a straw.
baseline: The fish should be made to swallow the water of the lake with the help of the grass and the leaves of the fish.
morphology: The fish should be made to swallow the water of the lake with the help of the oyster. The fish of thirst should be thrown into the lake.

sanskrit: rogārtiraṅganātṛṣṇā gambhīramapi mānavam / uttānatāṃ nayantyāśu sūryāṃśava ivāmbujam //
reference: Avarice like an acute pain excites even the gravest of men to motion, just as the rays of the sun raise the lotus blossoms.
baseline: One who is seriously ill should also be treated as a man. One who does not suffer from disease should be treated with the sun water and water.
morphology: A person who is seriously ill should also be treated with the sun sun and water.

sanskrit: antaḥśūnyā granthimatyo dīrghasvāṅkurakaṇṭakāḥ / muktāmaṇipriyā nityaṃ tṛṣṇā veṇulatā iva //
reference: It is compared with the bamboo in its length, hollowness, hard knots, and thorny prickles, and yet it is entertained in expectation of its yielding the manna and a pearly substance.
baseline: One who has a long and arched gland in the inner space one who is free from temptation and desires for eternal happiness one with a bowel etc.
morphology: One who is always thirsting for happiness like the flint one who has a long and curved spindle in the inner pituitary gland and one who is free from temptation is like the bowel.

sanskrit: aho bata mahaccitraṃ tṛṣṇāmapi mahādhiyaḥ / ducchedāmapi kṛntanti vivekenāmalāsinā //
reference: Yet it is a wonder that high-minded men, have been able to cut off this almost unseverable knot of avarice, by the glittering sword of reason:
baseline: O Vata the great image the thirst and the great desire are done by the disciple.
morphology: The great image of aha vata and the great desire of a great man should be done by the disciple of the mind.

sanskrit: nāsidhārā na vajrārcirna taptāyaḥkaṇārciṣaḥ / tathā tīkṣṇā yathā brahmaṃstṛṣṇeyaṃ hṛdi saṃsthitā //
reference: As neither the edge of the sword, nor the fire of lightning, nor the sparks of the red-hot iron, are sharp enough to sever the keen avarice seated in our hearts.
baseline: The heart should not be heated by the burning of a diamond in the form of a fountain as if it had been placed by the same sharpness as the Brahman the Śrīṣna and the Kāṇa.
morphology: The heart should not be set on the river Nasidhara. It should be heated with the incense stick of the eye. The same should be done with the fiery thread of Brahman and the Śrīṣna.

sanskrit: ujjvalā'sitatīkṣṇāgrā snehadīrghadaśā parā / prakāśā dāhaduḥsparśā tṛṣṇā dīpaśikhā iva //
reference: It is like the flame of a lamp which is bright but blackening and acutely burning at its end. It is fed by the oily wicks (of years), is vivid in all, but never handled by any body.
baseline: One who has a light a sharp eye a long heart a deep heart an open heart one who touches the fire a thirst is like a flame of light.
morphology: One who is so bright so bright and affectionate so long and full of love light hunger touch desire desire etc. is like the flame of light.

sanskrit: api merusamaṃ prājñamapi śūramapi sthiram / tṛṇīkaroti tṛṣṇaikā nimeṣeṇa narottamam //
reference: Penury has the power of bemeaning the best of men to (the baseness of) straws in a moment, notwithstanding their wisdom, heroism and gravity in other respects.
baseline: One who is merciless wise brave stable and has a thirst for the best of all things is made a thirsty man with a minute of rest.
morphology: One who is merciless wise brave stable and has a thirst for a minute would make him the best.

sanskrit: saṃstīrṇagahanā bhīmā ghanajālarajomayī / sāndhakārogranīhārā tṛṣṇā vindhyamahātaṭī //
reference: Avarice is like the great valley of the Vindhya hills, that is beset with deserts and impenetrable forests, is terrible and full of snares laid by the hunters, and filled with the dust and mist.
baseline: One who has made a sound with the horns of the sāmsthīrngaṇa gāṇa one who has built a wall of water with the sound of a mace one with the water of sandha kāra gorṇī and one who is in the midst of a great wind.
morphology: One who has got a lotus a mace a water of water a solid and water one who has had the desire to get a cow one with a penis one having a heart and a heart one should get a great victory.

sanskrit: ekaiva sarvabhuvanāntaralabdhalakṣyā durlakṣyatāmupagataiva vapuḥsthitaiva / tṛṣṇā sthitā jagati cañcalavīcimāle kṣīrodakāmbutarale madhureva śaktiḥ //
reference: One single avarice has every thing in the world for its object, and though seated in the breast, it is imperceptible to all. It is as the undulating Milky ocean in this fluctuating world, sweeping all things yet regaling mankind with its odorous waves.
baseline: One who has lost sight of all the objects in the world and has lost his senses and who has not lost his mind has already established his thirst for the world. He has got the power of honey in the form of water and water in the chanchalvichima.
morphology: One who has lost sight of all the objects in the earth and has lost his senses who has already established his thirst for the world who is in the midst of the earth and who has got the power of honey in the form of water and water.

sanskrit: śrīrāma uvāca / ārdrāntratantrīgahano vikārī paripātavān / dehaḥ sphurati saṃsāre so'pi duḥkhāya kevalam //
reference: This body of ours that struts about on earth, is but a mass of humid entrails and tendons, tending to decay and disease, and to our torment alone.
baseline: O Śrīma one who has made the earth wet and the earth barren and the body rotten and the world suffering only for the sake of suffering should be worshipped.
morphology: O Śrīma one who has said that the body should be kept in a state of deformity and that which is not fit for the purpose of living. One who is not suffering in the world would be destroyed.

sanskrit: ajño'pi tajjñasadṛśo valitātmacamatkṛtiḥ / yuktyā bhavyo'pyabhavyo'pi na jaḍo nāpi cetanaḥ //
reference: It is neither quiescent nor wholly sentient, neither ignorant nor quite intelligent. Its inherent soul is a wonder, and it is reason (and its absence) that makes it graceful or otherwise.
baseline: One who is ignorant and has knowledge one who is selfish and has the ability to do good deeds one should be able to control the mind even if he is not conscious.
morphology: One who is ignorant knowledgeable wise selfish and selfish should be able to do good deeds. One who has mastery over the mind should not be born blind or conscious.

sanskrit: jaḍājaḍadṛśormadhye dolāyitadurāśayaḥ / avivekī vimūḍhātmā mohameva prayacchati //
reference: The sceptic is doubtful of its inertness and intellection: and the unreasonable and ignorant people are ever subject to error and illusion.
baseline: A dura that is swaying in the middle of the earth like a jadājada a dura a foolish spirit that is unintelligent and does not want to be attracted.
morphology: A foolish spirit in the middle of the earth like a jadājādā and a dura that is swaying in the midst of the sun would be attracted by the illusion.

sanskrit: stokenānandamāyāti stokenāyāti kheditām / nāsti dehasamaḥ śocyo nīco guṇabahiṣkṛtaḥ //
reference: The body is as easily gratified with a little, as it is exhausted in an instant, hence there is nothing so pitiable, abject and worthless as our bodies.
baseline: One who enjoys the enjoyment of the praise does not regret it. One who has not enjoyed the body has not suffered from it has lost the quality.
morphology: One who is pleased with the praise one who is sorry for the praise and one who does not suffer the loss of the body and one whose qualities are inferior and undefiled.

sanskrit: āgamāpāyinā nityaṃ dantakesaraśālinā / vikāsasmitapuṣpeṇa pratikṣaṇamalaṃkṛtaḥ //
reference: The face is as frail as a fading flower: now it shoots forth its teeth like filaments, and now it dresses itself with blooming and blushing smiles as blossoms.
baseline: One should always make a garland of flowers with the help of incense sticks teeth and hair.
morphology: One should always make a garland of flowers with the fragrance of teeth hair flowers and flowers of development.

sanskrit: bhujaśākho ghanaskandho dvijastambhaśubhasthitiḥ / locanālivilākrāntaḥ śiraḥpīṭhabṛhatphalaḥ //
reference: The body is as a tree, having its arms resembling the branches, the shoulder-blades like stems, the teeth as rows of birds, the eye-holes like its hollows, and the head as a big fruit.
baseline: The bhuṣa branch the cube the double pillar the auspicious position the head the seat the great fruit the lotus the lokālīvilaka and the head.
morphology: The bhujṣa branch the cube the sambhāṇḍha pillar the two pillars the superior position the head and the seat are the great fruits.

sanskrit: śravadantarasagrasto hastapādasupallavaḥ / gulmavānkāryasaṃghāto vihaṅgamakṛtāspadaḥ //
reference: The ears are as two wood-peckers, the fingers of both hands and feet as so many leaves of the branches, the diseases as (parasite) plants, and the acts of the body are as axes felling this tree, which is the seat of the two birds the soul and intelligence.
baseline: One who has heard the sound of the Śravadantara and the hands feet feet and feet should be made to swallow the flower and the body should be covered with a panoramic thread.
morphology: One who has heard the sound of the Śravāṇta rāsa the hands legs feet feet and feet should be covered with the gulmavāṇākāraṇa and the sāmhāganda are said to be a panorama.

sanskrit: sacchāyo dehavṛkṣo'yaṃ jīvapānthagaṇāspadaḥ / kasyātmīyaḥ kasya para āsthānāsthe kilātra ke //
reference: This shady arbor of the body, is but the temporary resort of the passing soul, what then whether it be akin to or apart from anybody, or whether one would rely in it or not.
baseline: A tree of the body that is clean is said to be a tree of life. One who has a soul should be placed next to another in the court and at the fort.
morphology: A tree of the body should be clean. It should be considered as a group of living beings. One should have the spirit in the palace and another in the fort.

sanskrit: tāta saṃtaraṇārthena gṛhītāyāṃ punaḥpunaḥ / nāvi dehalatāyāṃ ca kasya syādātmabhāvanā //
reference: What man is there, O venerable fathers! that would stoop to reflect within himself, that this body is repeatedly assumed only to serve him as a boat to pass over the sea of the world.
baseline: Then one would be taken back again by the means of the transfiguration. One would get the spirit of the ship and the body.
morphology: Then one would be re-acquired for the purpose of the transfiguration. One would get self-consciousness in the ship and the body.

sanskrit: dehanāmni vane śūnye bahugartasamākule / tanūruhāsaṃkhyatarau viśvāsaṃ ko'dhigacchati //
reference: Who can rely any confidence in his body, which is as a forest full of holes, and abounds in hairs resembling its trees?
baseline: One who does not believe in the names of the bodies the forest the sky the mountains the hills the sun the fire the air the earth the world the universe the heavens and the sky would be destroyed.
morphology: One would lose faith in the names of the bodies in the forest in the wilderness in many places in a group of people and in the case of a person who has not had a good time.

sanskrit: māṃsasnāyvasthivalite śarīrapaṭahe'dṛḍhe / mārjāravadahaṃ tāta tiṣṭhāmyatra gatadhvanau //
reference: The body composed of flesh, nerves and bones, resembles a drum without any musical sound, and yet I sit watching it as a cat.
baseline: The body should be placed on the side of the body with the flesh and the body on the sides. The body of the deceased should be kept on the ground in the same manner.
morphology: The body should be placed on the side of the body with the flesh and the body on the sides. The body of the deceased should be kept on the ground in the same way.

sanskrit: saṃsārāraṇyasaṃrūḍho vilasaccittamarkaṭaḥ / cintāmañjaritākāro dīrghaduḥkhaghuṇakṣataḥ //
reference: Our bodies are as trees growing in the forest of the world, bearing the flowers of anxiety, and perforated by the worms of woe and misery, and mounted upon by the apish mind.
baseline: One who has made a wish for the welfare of the world one who has not suffered a loss of longsuffering and compassion and one who does not want to suffer a loss.
morphology: One who has made a wish for the welfare of the world one who has left a desire for a place one whose heart is long and suffering from the illusion of anger sorrow sorrow and sorrow.

sanskrit: tṛṣṇābhujaṅgamīgehaṃ kopa kāka kṛtālayaḥ / smitapuṇyodgamaḥ śrīmāñchubhāśubhamahāphalaḥ //
reference: The body with its smiling face appears a goodly plant, bearing the fruits both of good and evil; but it has become the abode of the dragon of avarice, and a rookery of the ravens of anger.
baseline: One who has made a crow and a cow of his own accord who has done a great work of art who is the son of a sage who begets a son who gives a good gift to him is the fruit.
morphology: One who has made a crow and a cow with the limbs of a trisinhabhuṇa one who is born with the skill of smitma one with the gift of shrimā one that is able to speak and one who has the power of the mind and the fruit of the body.

sanskrit: suskandhoghalatājālo hastastabakasundaraḥ / pavanaspanditāśeṣasvāṅgāvayavapallavaḥ //
reference: Our arms are as the boughs of trees, and our open palms like beautiful clusters of flowers, the other limbs are as twigs and leaves, and are continually shaken by the breath of life.
baseline: One who has the hands hands arms arms and hands is beautiful. One who does not want to be left behind would get the wind the wind and the wind.
morphology: One who has the hands hands arms arms and hands is beautiful one who has got the wind the breath the body the limbs and the palms.

sanskrit: sarvendriyakhagādhāraḥ sujānustambha unnataḥ / sarasacchāyayā yuktaḥ kāmapānthaniṣevitaḥ //
reference: The two legs are the erect stems (of the arbor of the body), and the organs are the seats of the birds of sense. Its youthful bloom is a shade for the passing traveller of love.
baseline: The pillar should be of all senses and the base should be raised. It should be covered with a lustre.
morphology: One who has all the senses and the heart the right pillar the upper one one who has the best of eyes one with the lustre and the back of the body is made to stand on the ground.

sanskrit: mūrdhasaṃjanitā''dīrghaśiroruhatṛṇāvaliḥ / ahaṃkāragṛdhrakṛtakulāyaḥ suṣirodaraḥ //
reference: The hanging hairs of the head resemble the long grass growing on the tree (of the body); and egoism like a vulture (in hollow), cracks the ear with its hideous shrieks.
baseline: The head should be long and straight and the neck should be covered with a thread. The neck of the ego should be closed and the body should be shrewd.
morphology: One who is foolish has a long head and has a thick hair has an ego and has an arrow. One who has a bow made of holes has to be merciless.

sanskrit: vicchinnavāsanājālamūlatvāddurlavākṛtiḥ / vyāyāmavirasaḥ kāyaplakṣo'yaṃ na sukhāya me //
reference: Our various desires like the pendant roots and fibres of the fig tree, seem to support its trunk of the body, though it is worn out by labour to unpleasantness.
baseline: The root of the net is broken the root of which is weak the base of the thread is weak and the root is weak. It does not make me happy.
morphology: The root of the net is broken the root of which is weak the base of the thread is weak and the root is not good.

sanskrit: kalevaramahaṃkāragṛhasthasya mahāgṛham / luṭhatvabhyetu vā sthairyaṃ kimanena mune mama //
reference: The body is the big abode of its owner's egoism, and therefore it is of no interest to me whether it lasts or falls.
baseline: One who has a great house in the house of pride or who has been robbed or who is afraid of me should be fixed in my mind.
morphology: One who has a great house with a lotus a house of pride or a house which is a place of robbery should be kept in my mind for some time.

sanskrit: paṅktibaddhendriyapaśuṃ valattṛṣṇāgṛhāṅganam / rāgarañjitasarvāṅgaṃ neṣṭaṃ dehagṛhaṃ mama //
reference: This body which is linked with its limbs like beasts of burthen labour, and is the abode of its mistress Avarice—painted over by her taints of passions, affords me no delight whatever.
baseline: The right side of the body should be placed in a row with the senses and the right side in the front. The upper part should be set aside for the body.
morphology: The right side of the body should be placed in a row with the senses and the right side in the front. The body should not be made to be burnt by the raga. The house should be my body.

sanskrit: pṛṣṭhāsthikāṣṭhasaṃghaṭṭaparisaṃkaṭakoṭaram / āntrarajjubhirābaddhaṃ neṣṭaṃ dehagṛhaṃ mama //
reference: This abode of the body which is built by the frame-work of the back-bone and ribs, and composed of cellular vessels, tied together by ropes of the entrails, is no way desirable to me.
baseline: The body should be placed in the back the trunk the neck the buttocks the inner thighs and the chest. The house should be built in front of the body.
morphology: The body should be placed in the back and the chest in the middle of the neck. The inner part of the body should not be tied together with the inner threads.

sanskrit: prasṛtasnāyutantrīkaṃ raktāmbukṛtakardamam / jarāmaṅkoladhavalaṃ neṣṭaṃ dehagṛhaṃ mama //
reference: This mansion of the body, which is tied with strings of the tendons, and built with the clay of blood and moisture, and plastered white with old age, is no way suited to my liking.
baseline: One who has made a penance for the worship of God one who has given blood and blood and one who had made a sacrifice for the sake of the body would lose his body house and body.
morphology: One who has made a penance of blood blood and blood should offer the mantras to the preceptor. One who consumes the body should offer jārāmaṇkola and dāva.

sanskrit: cittabhṛtyakṛtānantaceṣṭāvaṣṭabdhasaṃsthiti / mithyāmohamahāsthūṇaṃ neṣṭaṃ dehagṛhaṃ mama //
reference: The mind is the architect and master of this bodily dwelling, and our activities are its supports and servants; it is filled with errors and delusions which I do not like.
baseline: The illusion of the great body is the destruction of the house of the body.
morphology: The state of the mind made with the mind the mind and the mind should be kept in a state of rest. My body should be destroyed by the illusion of the body.

sanskrit: duḥkhārbhakakṛtākrandaṃ sukhaśayyāmanoramam / durīhādagdhadāsīkaṃ neṣṭaṃ dehagṛhaṃ mama //
reference: I do not like this dwelling of the body with its bed of pleasure on one side, and the cries of pain as those of its children on the other, and where our evil desires are at work like its bawling hand-maids.
baseline: One who has made a bed of happiness and sorrow one who is a servant of a cow or one who has taken away a cow or a maid of blood would destroy the house of the body.
morphology: One who has made a bed of happiness and sorrow one who has not had a long life or one who is a servant of a cow would destroy the house of the body.

sanskrit: malāḍhyaviṣayavyūhabhāṇḍopaskarasaṃkaṭam / ajñānakṣāravalitaṃ neṣṭaṃ dehagṛhaṃ mama //
reference: I cannot like this body, which like a pot of filth, is full of the foulness of worldly affairs, and mouldering under the rust of our ignorance.
baseline: The illusion of the body and the misfortune of the world the lack of knowledge and the absence of resources the ignorance of the illusion and the destruction of the house of the flesh is my desire.
morphology: The illusion of the body should be made to be a matter of wealth. The illusory and illiterate person should be destroyed.

sanskrit: gulphagugguluviśrāntajānūrdhvastambhamastakam / dīghadordārusudṛḍhaṃ neṣṭaṃ dehagṛhaṃ mama //
reference: It is a hovel standing on the two props of our heels, and supported by the two posts of our legs.
baseline: The pillar should be placed in the form of a pillar with the reclining gulphaguguggulu and the rest of the body. The body should be kept in a deep place like this.
morphology: One who is resting on a pillar a pillar and a mound or a house of the body should be placed in a deep place.

sanskrit: prakaṭākṣagavākṣāntaḥ krīḍatprajñāgṛhāṅganam / cintāduhitṛkaṃ brahmanneṣṭaṃ dehagṛhaṃ mama //
reference: It is no lovely house where the external organs are playing their parts, while its mistress the understanding sits inside with her brood of anxieties.
baseline: One who is aware of the game in the open and open room one who is conscious of the mind and the mind one with the mind should seek the abode of Brahman.
morphology: One who is aware of the game in the open and open room one who is conscious of the mind and the mind and one who desires to enjoy the Brahman and the body is my home.

sanskrit: mūrdhajācchādanacchannakarṇaśrīcandraśālikam / ādīrghāṅgulinirvyūhaṃ neṣṭaṃ dehagṛhaṃ mama //
reference: It is a hut which is thatched over with the hairs on the head, decorated with the turrets of the ears, and adorned with jewels on the crest, which I do not like.
baseline: O lord of the earth the shadow of the moon the dark ear the head the forefinger the body the house of the body etc. should be worshipped by me.
morphology: O lord of the moon the king of the earls who is covered with the cover of the head the lord of arms the master of the fingers the house of the body and the house are my objects.

sanskrit: sarvāṅgakuḍyasaṃghātaghanaromayavāṅkuram / saṃśūnyapeṭavivaraṃ neṣṭaṃ dehagṛhaṃ mama //
reference: This house of the body is walled about by all its members, and beset by hairs growing like ears of corn on it. It has an empty space of the belly within (which is never full), and which I do not like.
baseline: All the parts of the body should be covered with water and the outer part should be washed with water.
morphology: One who has lost all the organs the body the house and the body should be destroyed.

sanskrit: nakhorṇanābhinilayaṃ saramāraṇitāntaram / bhāṅkārakāripavanaṃ neṣṭaṃ dehagṛhaṃ mama //
reference: This body with its nails as those of spiders, and its entrails growling within like barking dogs, and the internal winds emitting fearful sounds, is never delightsome to me.
baseline: After having destroyed the temple the temple of the gods should be destroyed. The forest of the god of war the house of the body should be removed.
morphology: One who does not want to destroy the body should destroy it. One who has not destroyed it should destroy the house of the body.

sanskrit: praveśanirgamavyagravātavegamanāratam / vitatākṣagavākṣaṃ tanneṣṭaṃ dehagṛhaṃ mama //
reference: What is this body but a passage for the ceaseless inhaling and breathing out of the vital air? Its eyes are as two windows which are continually oped and closed by the eyelids. I do not like such a mansion as this.
baseline: The entrance exit passage and passage of the wind should be made clear. It should be the house of the body.
morphology: The entrance exit exit and passage of the wind should be made clear. It should be placed in the outer chamber of the body.

sanskrit: jihvāmarkaṭikākrāntavadanadvārabhīṣaṇam / dṛṣṭadantāsthiśakalaṃ neṣṭaṃ dehagṛha mama //
reference: This mansion of the body with its formidable (wide-open) door of the mouth, and (ever-moving) bolt of the tongue and bars of the teeth, is not pleasant to me.
baseline: Having touched the tongue the ear the mouth and the door of the body are threatened. Having seen the stone of the eye the house of my body would be destroyed.
morphology: Having touched the tongue forehead mouth mouth and mouth having seen the body of a man the body should be destroyed.

sanskrit: tvaksudhālepamasṛṇaṃ yantrasaṃcāracañcalam / manaḥ sadākhunotkhātaṃ neṣṭaṃ dehagṛhaṃ mama //
reference: This house of the body, having the white-wash of ointments on the outer skin, and the machinery of the limbs in continued motion, and the restless mind burrowing its base like the mischievous mouse, is not liked by me.
baseline: The body should always be kept in the place of the body. The mind should always remain in the area of the movement of the machine.
morphology: The body should always be kept in the place of the mind and the body.

sanskrit: smitadīpaprabhodbhāsi kṣaṇamānandasundaram / kṣaṇaṃ vyāptaṃ tamaḥpūrairneṣṭaṃ dehagṛhaṃ mama //
reference: Sweet smiles like shining lamps, serve to lighten this house of the body for a moment, but it is soon darkened by a cloud of melancholy, wherefore I cannot be pleased with it.
baseline: The image of the sun the light of the sky the beauty of the moment the blissful beauty of that moment and the presence of the body in the whole house are my desires.
morphology: O Smitā Deepa Prabhudeva Sāmmananda Suṇḍāṇḍa Sammanā Tamā Tāmā and the house of the body should be fully adorned.

sanskrit: samastarogāyatanaṃ valīpalitapattanam / sarvādhisāragahanaṃ neṣṭaṃ dehagṛhaṃ mama //
reference: This body which is the abode of diseases, and subject to wrinkles and decay, and all kinds of pain, is a mansion wherewith I am not pleased.
baseline: All the diseases should be treated with a lotus flower. All the ailments should be taken care of. The house of the body should be destroyed.
morphology: All the diseases should be treated with the vālipāla leaves. All the ailments should be taken care of. The house of the body should be destroyed.

sanskrit: akṣarkṣakṣobhaviṣamā śūnyā niḥsārakoṭarā / tamogahanadikkuñjā neṣṭā dehāṭavī mama //
reference: I do not like this wilderness of the body, which is infested by the bears of the senses. It is empty and hollow within, with dark groves (of entrails) in the inside.
baseline: The body should be washed with the poison of the āksharaksha and the śārakotras of the abyss. It should not be washed away.
morphology: The body should be washed away with the poison of the āksharaksha and the śārakotras of the abode of the demon Tamogahana.

sanskrit: dehālayaṃ dhārayituṃ na śaknomi munīśvara / paṅkamagnaṃ samuddhartuṃ gajamalpabalo yathā //
reference: I am unable, O chief of sages! to drag my domicile of the body, just as a weak elephant is incapable to draw out another immerged in a muddy pit.
baseline: I cannot hold the temple of the body of the lord. I should not be able to hold the fire of the god.
morphology: One cannot possess the temple of the body. One who is a sage one who has a penance one that is a little strong enough to be able to fight the sea.

sanskrit: kiṃ śriyā kiṃ ca rājyena kiṃ kāyena kimīhitaiḥ / dinaiḥ katipayaireva kālaḥ sarvaṃ nikṛntati //
reference: Of what good is affluence or royalty, this body and all its efforts to one, when the hand of time must destroy them all in a few days.
baseline: One gets rid of everything by the practice of Śrīya Kāya Kaṇī Kīmīhita a few times in a day.
morphology: One gets rid of everything by the practice of śrīya kāya kaṇa kīmīṭha and a few times.

sanskrit: raktamāṃsamayasyāsya sabāhyābhyantaraṃ mune / nāśaikadharmiṇo brūhi kaiva kāyasya ramyatā //
reference: Tell me, O sage! what is charming in this body, that is only a composition of flesh and blood both within and without it and frail in its nature.
baseline: One should not hold a piece of rice in his hand after having done all the rituals for the sake of blood and blood.
morphology: One should hold a piece of fruit in the hands of a person who has not attained the righteousness after having had the blood and blood at the same time.

sanskrit: maraṇāvasare kāyā jīvaṃ nānusaranti ye / teṣu tāta kṛtaghneṣu kaivāsthā vada dhīmatām //
reference: The body does not follow the soul upon death; tell me Sir, what regard should the learned have for such an ungrateful thing as this.
baseline: Those who deny life on the occasion of death should say that they should be slow.
morphology: Those who do not give life in the event of death should say that they should be restrained by the words of the kāyavas.

sanskrit: mattebhakarṇāgracalaḥ kāyo lambāmbubhaṅguraḥ / na saṃtyajati māṃ yāvattāvadenaṃ tyajāmyaham //
reference: It is as unsteady as the ears of an infuriate elephant, and as fickle as drops of water that trickle on their tips. I should like therefore to abandon it, before it comes to abandon me.
baseline: One who does not give me the gift of a cow or a long hair should not be spared by me.
morphology: One who does not worship me should give me a piece of cloth with the colour karna grachala or a long thread. He should not give me anything.

sanskrit: pavanaspandataralaḥ pelavaḥ kāyapallavaḥ / jarjarastanuvṛttaśca neṣṭo me kaṭunīrasaḥ //
reference: It is as tremulous as the leaves of a tree shaken by the breeze, and oppressed by diseases and fluctuations of pleasure and pain. I have no relish in its pungency and bitterness.
baseline: The wind wind water peacock mace grass mud earth earth and water are the mainstay of the river.
morphology: The wind wind water sand etc. are weak and weak. They do not grow well. They get the poisonous water.

sanskrit: bhuktvā pītvā ciraṃ kālaṃ bālapallavapelavām / tanutāmetya yatnena vināśamanudhāvati //
reference: With all its food and drink for evermore, it is as tender as a leaflet and is reduced to leanness in spite of all our cares, and runs fast towards its dissolution.
baseline: After having eaten and drunk the rice one should drink the water with the help of a cow a cow and other animals. One should destroy it with care.
morphology: After having eaten and drunk for a long time one should take the children children and children and destroy them with care.

sanskrit: tānyeva sukhaduḥkhāni bhāvābhāvamayānyasau / bhūyo'pyanubhavankāyaḥ prākṛto hi na lajjate //
reference: It is repeatedly subjected to pleasure and pain, and to the succession of affluence and destitution, without being ashamed of itself as the shameless vulgar herd.
baseline: He should not be ashamed of the fact that he has already experienced the superiority of the earth. He should also enjoy happiness sorrow feeling feeling etc.
morphology: He should not be ashamed of the fact that he has already experienced the superiority of the earth.

sanskrit: suciraṃ prabhutāṃ kṛtvā saṃsevya vibhavaśriyam / nocchrāyameti na sthairyaṃ kāyaḥ kimiti pālyate //
reference: Why nourish this body any longer, when it acquires no excellence nor durability of its state, after its enjoyment of prosperity and exercise of authority for a length of time.
baseline: Having made the well of the lord and having served him one should not think of the abode of the potential. One should not say that what is the cause of stability and what is maintained.
morphology: Having made the well of the lord and having served him one should not think of the abode of the potential. One should not be adamant about what is to be maintained.

sanskrit: jarākāle jarāmeti mṛtyukāle tathā mṛtim / sama evāviśeṣajñaḥ kāyo bhogidaridrayoḥ //
reference: The bodies of the rich as well as those of the poor, are alike subject to decay and death at their appointed times.
baseline: One who is aware of the importance of the same should do so in the case of death in the event of death. One who knows the same is known to be a devotee of the poor.
morphology: One who knows the meaning of death in the case of death is known as jārakāla and one who does not eat food is known to be equal to that of the other.

sanskrit: saṃsārāmbhodhijaṭhare tṛṣṇākuharakāntare / suptastiṣṭhati mukteho mūko'yaṃ kāyakacchapaḥ //
reference: The body lies as a tortoise in the cave of avarice amidst the ocean of the world. It remains there in the mud in a mute and torpid state, without an effort for its liberation.
baseline: One who is free from the evil will remain asleep in the seat of the world in the room of the senses at the place of the thirst in that of the mouth of the kāṇtas in a room of water.
morphology: One who is free from the evil will remain asleep in the seat of the world in the room of the sun on the floor of the temple in a place of thirst in that of the kanta and in that place of the muṣṇu.

sanskrit: dahanaikārthayogyāni kāyakāṣṭhāni bhūriśaḥ / saṃsārābdhāvihohyante kaṃcitteṣu naraṃ viduḥ //
reference: Our bodies floating as heaps of wood on the waves of the world, serve at last for the fuel of funeral fire (on the pile); except a few of these which pass for human bodies in the sight of the wise.
baseline: One who is able to do the burning should offer a lot of kākāṣas. One who has not done any work in the world would get a man.
morphology: One who is able to burn a fire or to do any work would be better off. One who does not want to burn the fire would be destroyed.

sanskrit: dīrghadaurātmyavalayā nipātaphalapātayā / na dehalatayā kāryaṃ kiṃcidasti vivekinaḥ //
reference: The wise have little to do with this tree of the body, which is beset by evils like noxious orchids about it, and produces the fruit of perdition.
baseline: A wise man does not do any work with the power of the body and does not suffer loss with the force of the heart.
morphology: One who is wise will not do any work with the absence of the body and will not suffer loss with the loss of the fruits due to the longness fortitude wealth etc.

sanskrit: majjankardamakośeṣu jhaṭityeva jarāṃ gataḥ / na jñāyate yātyacirātkaḥ kathaṃ dehadarduraḥ //
reference: The body like a frog, lies merged in the mire of mortality, where it perishes no sooner it is known to have lived and gone.
baseline: One would not know how the jāra went into the cells of the mermaids soon after. One would never know how it got into the body.
morphology: One would not know how the jārā went into the body of the mermaids and the cells of the virgins.

sanskrit: niḥsārasakalārambhāḥ kāyāścapalavāyavaḥ / rajomārgeṇa gacchanto dṛśyante neha kenacit //
reference: Our bodies are as empty and fleeting as gusts of wind, passing over a dusty ground, where nobody knows whence they come, and whither they go.
baseline: One can see the sun sky sky and air passing through the path of the river.
morphology: One can see the sun sky sky and air passing through the path of the king.

sanskrit: vāyordīpasya manaso gacchato jñāyate gatiḥ / āgacchataśca bhagavañcharīrasya kadācana //
reference: We know not the course of our bodies (their transmigrations), as we do not know those of the winds, light and our thoughts; they all come and go, but from where and whither, we know nothing of.
baseline: The mind of the lamp of Vayordīpa is known to be moving and the body of the lord should never be moved.
morphology: The mind of the lamp of Vayor is known to be moving and the body of the god is sometimes not moving.

sanskrit: baddhāsthā ye śarīreṣu baddhāsthā ye jagatsthitau / tānmohamadironmattāndhigdhigastu punaḥpunaḥ //
reference: Fie and shame to them, that are so giddy with the ebriety of their error, as to rely on any state or durability of their bodies.
baseline: Those who are bound in the body those who are in the world those which are bound again the mind should be made to fall into the darkness.
morphology: Those who are bound in the body those who are in the world are bound again.

sanskrit: nāhaṃ dehasya no deho mama nāyamahaṃ tathā / iti viśrāntacittā ye te mune puruṣottamāḥ //
reference: They are the best of men, O sage! whose minds are at rest with the thought, that their ego does not subsist in their bodies, nor are the bodies theirs at the end.
baseline: Those men who are at rest in the mind who are not of the body and who are of the mind.
morphology: Those men who are at rest in the mind should say that I am not the body nor the body.

sanskrit: mānāvamānabahulā bahulābhamanoramāḥ / śarīramātrabaddhāsthaṃ ghnanti doṣadṛśo naram //
reference: Those mistaken men that have a high sense of honor and fear dishonor, and take a pleasure in the excess of their gains, are verily the killers both of their bodies and souls.
baseline: A man should be a man of many qualities. He should be bound only by the body. He would be a male.
morphology: The human beings are many many and many. They are bound only to the body. The evil ones are the men.

sanskrit: śarīraśvabhraśāyinyā piśācyā peśalāṅgayā / ahaṃkāracamatkṛtyā chalena chalitā vayam //
reference: We are deceived by the delusion of egoism, which like a female fiend (sorceress) lies hid within the cavity of the body with all her sorcery.
baseline: We are deceived by the mischief of the body the misfortune of the mind the ego the act of defrauding the body and the limbs of the muscles.
morphology: We are deceived by the mischief of the body the body and the body of the enemy the loins of the muscles the ego and the act of deceit.

sanskrit: prajñā varākā sarvaiva kāyabaddhāsthayānayā / mithyājñānakurākṣasyā chalitā kaṣṭamekikā //
reference: Our reason unaided (by religion) is kept in bondage like a female slave within the prison of our bodies, by the malicious fiend of false knowledge.
baseline: All the wise men should be bound with a string of weapons. The misguided man should be deceived by the false knowledge of the enemy.
morphology: All the wise men should be bound with the threads of the right hand and deceived by the false knowledge and illusion.

sanskrit: na kiṃcidapi dṛśye'sminsatyaṃ tena hatātmanā / citraṃ dagdhaśarīreṇa janatā vipralabhyate //
reference: It is certain that whatever we see here is unreal, and yet it is a wonder, that the mass of men are led to deception by the vile body, which has injured the cause of the soul.
baseline: The image of the body burnt by him would not be visible to the public.
morphology: The image of the body burnt by him would not be visible to the people.

sanskrit: dinaiḥ katipayaireva nirjharāmbukaṇo yathā / patatyayamayatnena jaraṭhaḥ kāyapallavaḥ //
reference: Our bodies are as fleeting as the drops of a water-fall, and they fall off in a few days like the withered leaves of trees.
baseline: One should make a waterfall with a small amount of water. One should fall down with the help of water jaratha kaya and pallavas.
morphology: One should make a waterfall with a small amount of water in the morning and then fall down with the water of jaratha kayapallava.

sanskrit: kāyo'yamacirāpāyo budbudo'mbunidhāviva / vyarthaṃ kāryaparāvarte parisphurati niṣphalaḥ //
reference: They are as quickly dissolved as bubbles in the ocean; it is in vain therefore that it should hurl about in the whirlpool of business.
baseline: One who does not do any work without the help of a cow cow sheep or buffalo should not do so.
morphology: One who does not do any work without the help of a cow cow or cow or other animal would be rendered worthless.

sanskrit: mithyājñānavikāre'sminsvapnasaṃbhramapattane / kāye sphuṭatarāpāye kṣaṇamāsthā na me dvija //
reference: I have not a moment's reliance in this body, which is ever hastening to decay;and I regard its changeful delusions as a state of dreaming.
baseline: In the event of the destruction of false knowledge the illusion of the dream is not repeated. In the case of a dream it is not possible for me to remain for a while.
morphology: The illusion of knowledge is not the same as that of a dream. It is not a matter of time for me.

sanskrit: taḍitsu śaradabhreṣu gandharvanagareṣu ca / sthairyaṃ yena vinirṇītaṃ sa viśvasitu vigrahe //
reference: Let those who have any faith in the stability of the lightning, of the autumn clouds, and in glacial castles, place their reliance in this body.
baseline: One who is determined to be stable in the cities of Sharad Bharata and Gandharva should be trusted by the divine.
morphology: One who is determined to be stable in the cities of Śarādbhrāda Gandharva etc. in the months of tādītśu and vīgrā is believed to be a virgins.

sanskrit: satatabhaṅgurakāryaparamparā vijayijātajayaṃ haṭhavṛttiṣu / prabaladoṣamidaṃ tu kalevaraṃ tṛṇamivāhamapohya sukhaṃ sthitaḥ //
reference: It has outdone all other things that are doomed to destruction in its instability and perishableness. It is moreover subject to very many evils; wherefore I have set it at naught as a straw, and thereby obtained my repose.
baseline: Having conquered the tradition of continuous division and work the victory of the people would be achieved in the tenacity of actions. The great error would be the victory for the enemy. The victory would be attained by the conquest of the earth.
morphology: One who is constantly divided by the practice of doing the work and conquers the victory of the people one who is in a state of obstruction and one who has a strong defect in the conduct of the work should be able to attain happiness after having attained the mastery of the art.

sanskrit: śrīrāma uvāca / labdhvāpi taralākāre kāryabhārataraṃgiṇi / saṃsārasāgare janma bālyaṃ duḥkhāya kevalam //
reference: One receiving his birth in the unstable ocean of the world, which is disturbed by the billows of the bustle of business, has to pass his boyhood in sufferings only.
baseline: O Śrīma one who is born in the sea of samsara and who has acquired the wealth and wealth of the world would be born only for the misery.
morphology: O Śrīma one who is born in the sea of samsara and who has acquired wealth and wealth in the form of a liquid form should be given the charge of the waves.

sanskrit: aśaktirāpadastṛṣṇā mūkatā mūḍhabuddhitā / gṛdhnutā lolatā dainyaṃ sarvaṃ bālye pravartate //
reference: Want of strength and sense, and subjection to diseases and dangers, muteness and appetence, joined with longings and helplessness, are the concomitants of infancy.
baseline: Having said the words weak foolish having thought blind having taken the word lol all the things that happen in childhood go on.
morphology: Having said that one who is weak and has no sense of mind one should not be foolish. One who has not grasped all things would become weak in his childhood.

sanskrit: roṣarodanaraudrāsu dainyajarjaritāsu ca / daśāsu bandhanaṃ bālyamālānaṃ kariṇāmiva //
reference: Childhood is chained to fretting and crying, to fits of anger, craving and every kind of incapacity, as an elephant when tied to the post by its shackles.
baseline: One should bind a child in ten days in the form of a bond in the case of anger strife indignation anger anger etc.
morphology: One should bind a child in ten days in the form of an offering of blood and blood in the case of a person suffering from indigestion childbirth property etc.

sanskrit: na mṛtau na jarāroge na cāpadi na yauvane / tāścintāḥ parikṛntanti hṛdayaṃ śaiśaveṣu yāḥ //
reference: The vexations which tease the infant breast, are far greater than those which trouble us in youth and old age, or disturb one in disease, danger or at the approach of death.
baseline: Neither the dead nor the sick nor the oppressed nor the young. The thoughts of the heart in the infancy period go round and round.
morphology: Neither the dead nor the sick nor the oppressed nor the young. These thoughts go around the heart in infancy.

sanskrit: tiryagjātisamārambhaḥ sarvairevāvadhīritaḥ / lolo bālasamācāro maraṇādapi duḥkhadaḥ //
reference: The acts of a boy are as those of young animals, that are always restless and snubbed by every body. Hence boyhood is more intolerable than death itself.
baseline: The beginning of the month of Triyāragājatī is said to be above all. The death of a child is also sad.
morphology: The beginning of the month of Triyāragājatī is above all. The death of a child is also sorrowful.

sanskrit: pratibimbaghanājñānaṃ nānāsaṃkalpapelavam / bālyamālūnasaṃśīrṇamanaḥ kasya sukhāvaham //
reference: How can boyhood be pleasing to any body, when it is but a semblance of gross ignorance, and full of whims and hobbies, and ever subject to miscarriages.
baseline: The knowledge of the image the image of the mind the knowledge of all things the wisdom of many things and the knowledge that is good for ones happiness and prosperity.
morphology: The knowledge of the reflections and the illusions of many things is good. One should enjoy the pleasure of having children and children.

sanskrit: jalavahnayanilājasrajātabhītyā pade pade / yadbhayaṃ śaiśave'buddhyā kasyāpadi hi tadbhavet //
reference: It is this silly boyhood which is in constant dread of dangers arising at every step from fire, water and air, and which rarely betide us in other states of life.
baseline: The fear of the waters flowing in the form of water should be repeated in the following stages. The fear should be expressed in the child in the manner of wisdom.
morphology: The fear of the king should be expressed in the following manner in the form of fear in the manner of water and water. The fear should be said to be a matter of wisdom in infancy.

sanskrit: līlāsu durvilāseṣu durīhāsu durāśaye / paramaṃ mohamādhatte bālo balavadāpatan //
reference: Boys are liable to very many errors in their plays and wicked frolics, and in all their wishes and attempts beyond their capacities:hence boyhood is the most perilous state.
baseline: The child should be strong in the form of greed misfortune longing misery illusion love and affection.
morphology: The child should be strong in the form of greed misfortune longing misery illusion love and great enmity.

sanskrit: vikalpakalpitārambhaṃ durvilārasaṃ durāspadam / śaiśavaṃ śāsanāyaiva puruṣasya na śāntaye //
reference: Boys are engaged in false pursuits and wicked sports, and are subject to all foolish puerilities. Hence boyhood is fit for the rod and not for rest.
baseline: The beginning of the choice is not good for the man. The beginning is bad for the king. The child is not for the rule of the man in peace.
morphology: The beginning of the choice is not good for the man. The beginning is bad for the king. The child is not safe for him to rule.

sanskrit: ye doṣā ye durācārā duṣkramā ye durādhayaḥ / te sarve saṃsthitā bālye durgarta iva kauśikāḥ //
reference: All faults, misconduct, transgressions and heart-aches, lie hidden in boyhood like owls in hollow caves.
baseline: All those who have committed evil deeds misdeeds evil deeds etc. are established in their childhood.
morphology: All those who do evil evil and evil and those who suffer evil in their childhood are wise as if they were in a difficult situation.

sanskrit: bālyaṃ ramyamiti vyarthabuddhayaḥ kalpayanti ye / tānmūrkhapuruṣānbrahmandhigastu hṛtacetasaḥ //
reference: Fie to those ignorant and foolish people, who are falsely led to imagine boyhood as the most pleasant period of life.
baseline: Childhood is said to be pleasant. Those who imagine themselves as foolish men brahmins heart heart and heart.
morphology: The senses of the child are thought to be pleasant in vain. Those who are foolish men brahmins heart heart and heart are considered to be good.

sanskrit: yatra dolākṛti manaḥ parisphurati vṛttiṣu / trailokyā'bhavyamapi tatkathaṃ bhavati tuṣṭaye //
reference: How can boyhood appear pleasing to any one, when the mind swings like a cradle towards every object of desire, however wrong it is deemed to be in both worlds.
baseline: Where the heart is made to move in the form of a bow the same is done in the three worlds.
morphology: Where the mind is made to move in the shape of a bow it becomes satisfied with the three worlds.

sanskrit: sarveṣāmeva sattvānāṃ sarvāvasthābhya eva hi / manaścañcalatāmeti bālye daśaguṇaṃ mune //
reference: The minds of all living beings are ever restless, but those of young people are ten times more at unrest.
baseline: All the qualities are equal to that of the sattvas. The mind becomes ten times more active in childhood.
morphology: The mind should be stimulated ten times in the childhood.

sanskrit: manaḥ prakṛtyaiva calaṃ bālyaṃ ca calatāṃ varam / tayoḥ saṃśliṣyatostrātā ka ivāntaḥ kucāpale //
reference: The mind is naturally unsteady, and so is boyhood also. Say what can save us from that state of life, when both these vagrant things combine to our destruction.
baseline: One who moves the mind and the child in the same way would be blessed. One who does not move the arms would be able to do so.
morphology: The gift of moving the child should be made by the nature of the mind itself. One who is able to move the child would be given the gift of the combination of these.

sanskrit: strīlocanaistaḍitpuñjairjvalājālaistaraṅgakaiḥ / cāpalaṃ śikṣitaṃ brahmañchaiśavākrāntacetasaḥ //
reference: The glances of women, the flashes of lightning, the flame of fire, and the ever-rolling waves, have all imitated the fickleness of boyhood.
baseline: One who has been taught to worship Brahman would be like a woman who has thought of him. He would be worshipped by the celestials with the rosewood of water water and stones.
morphology: One who has been taught the Brahmana is a man with eight words and a heart.

sanskrit: śaiśavaṃ ca manaścaiva sarvāsveva hi vṛttiṣu / bhrātarāviva lakṣyete satataṃ bhaṅgurasthitī //
reference: Minority seems to be a twin brother to the mind, and resembles it in the unsteadiness and frailty of all its purposes.
baseline: One who lives in the mind in his infancy and in all the professions should be a brother. He should be always in a state of fragility.
morphology: One who lives in the mind in his infancy and in all his professions as a brother and in the goal is in a state of constant fragility.

sanskrit: sarvāṇi duḥkhabhūtāni sarve doṣā durādhayaḥ / bālamevopajīvanti śrīmantamiva mānavāḥ //
reference: All kinds of miseries, misdeeds and miscarriages await on boyhood, as all sorts of men hang upon the rich.
baseline: All the misfortune all the faults all misery all evil deeds children men living like Srimanta.
morphology: All the misfortune all the faults all misery all evil deeds children men living like Srimanta etc.

sanskrit: navaṃ navaṃ prītikaraṃ na śiśuḥ pratyahaṃ yadi / prāpnoti tadasau yāti viṣavaiṣamyamūrcchanām //
reference: Boys are fond of fresh things at all times, and on their failing to get the same, they fall to a fainting fit, as if from the effect of poison.
baseline: If a child does not get the nine things that he loves he will get the same.
morphology: If a child does not get the nine things that are good for him he will get poison.

sanskrit: stokena vaśamāyāti stokenaiti vikāritām / amedhya eva ramate bālaḥ kauleyako yathā //
reference: A boy like a dog, is as easily tamed as he is irritated at a little, and he is as glad to lie in the dust, as to play with dirt.
baseline: The child is pleased with the performance of the hymns. The disciple is pleased by the performance. The boy is happy by the execution of the Hymns as if he were a cowherd.
morphology: One who is pleased with the distortions of the body is blessed with praise. One who enjoys the illusion is blessed by the child as the cowherd.

sanskrit: ajasravāṣpavadanaḥ kardamākto jaḍāśayaḥ / varṣokṣitasya taptasya sthalasya sadṛśaḥ śiśuḥ //
reference: A foolish fretful boy with his body daubed in mire with the tears in his eyes, appears as a heap of dry clay soiled by a shower of rain.
baseline: A child should be made to drink water with the help of a lotus a clay pot and a jadāṣa. A child who has been kept for a year should be placed on a hot place.
morphology: A child should be made to drink water of the same quantity as the place where the fire is kept for a year.

sanskrit: bhayāhāraparaṃ dīnaṃ dṛṣṭādṛṣṭābhilāṣi ca / lolabuddhi vapurdhatte bālyaṃ duḥkhāya kevalam //
reference: Boys are subject to fear and voracity; they are helpless but fond of every thing they have seen or heard, and equally fickle in their bodies and mind. Hence boyhood is a source of troubles only.
baseline: One who is afraid of food and greed who looks blind and has lusts who has a lame mind and who has grown old would spend his childhood only for the sake of sorrow.
morphology: One who is afraid of food and greedy for sight and sight one who has good intellect and a child who is suffering only for the sake of suffering one should be able to see and see.

sanskrit: svasaṃkalpābhilaṣitānbhāvānaprāpya taptadhīḥ / duḥkhametyabalo bālo viniṣkṛtta ivāśaye //
reference: The foolish and helpless child, becomes as sad and sour when he fails to get the object of his fancy, as when he is thwarted from the thing desired.
baseline: Having obtained his own determination with the desire and feelings he should be made to suffer a strong child. He should be destroyed.
morphology: Having obtained his determination with the desire and feelings he should be punished with the same amount of pain and the child should be destroyed.

sanskrit: durīhālabdhalakṣāṇi bahuvakrolbaṇāni ca / bālasya yāni duḥkhāni mune tāni na kasyacit //
reference: Children have much difficulty to get at the things they want, and which they can ask only by indistinct words. Hence no one suffers so much as boys.
baseline: The miseries of a boy should not be felt by anyone.
morphology: The miseries of a boy should not be felt by anyone.

sanskrit: bālo balavatā svena manorathavilāsinā / manasā tapyate nityaṃ grīṣmeṇeva vanasthalī //
reference: A boy is as much irritated by the eagerness of his whimsical desires, as a patch of ground in the desert is parched by the summer heat.
baseline: The boy becomes strong with his own mind and the mind becomes tormented by the desire of the people in the summer season.
morphology: The mind is always tormented by the force of the child by the desire of the mind by his own strength by a place of forest in the summer.

sanskrit: vidyāgṛhagato bālo parāmeti kadarthanām / ālāna iva nāgendro viṣavaiṣamyabhīṣaṇām //
reference: A boy on entering his school, is subjected to corrections, which are as painful to him as the goading and fetters to the elephant.
baseline: The boy who goes to the house of knowledge and worships the gods of the earth like the king of alas is known to be a poisonous demon.
morphology: One who goes to the house of knowledge one who is a boy who invades the king of the king who is like a demon and who is poisonous and a threat is called a boy.

sanskrit: nānāmanorathamayī mithyākalpitakalpanā / duḥkhāyātyantadīrghāya bālatā pelavāśayā //
reference: A great many whims and hobbies, and a variety of false fancies, tend continually to afflict boyhood, which is ever fond of toys and trifles.
baseline: The child should be made to suffer for a long time by the illusion of the preceptor.
morphology: One who has not been born with a child should be born with the illusion of having a son. One who is suffering for a long time should be blessed with a son with a long heart.

sanskrit: saṃhṛṣṭo bhuvanaṃ bhoktamindumādātumambarāt / vāñchate yena maurkhyeṇa tatsukhāya kathaṃ bhavet //
reference: How can senseless childhood be said to be a happy state of life, when the child is led by its ignorance to swallow everything in the world, and to wish to lay hold on the moon in the sky.
baseline: One would like to get the fragrance of the sun from the mother of the beast. One would want to get it from the goddess. How can that be obtained from the mouth.
morphology: One would like to get the fragrance of the sun from the mother and the mother of the child. How can that be obtained by the mouth of the mother.

sanskrit: antaścitteraśaktasya śītātapanivāraṇe / ko viśeṣo mahābuddhe bālasyorvīruhastathā //
reference: Say great sage! what difference is there between a child and a tree, both of which have sensitiveness, but unable to defend themselves from heat and cold.
baseline: One who has the power to endure a great war should be given a special gift in the winter season.
morphology: One who has the power to endure a great war should be given a special gift in the winter season.

sanskrit: uḍḍītumabhivāñchanti pakṣābhyāṃ kṣutparāyaṇāḥ / bhayāhāraparā nityaṃ bālā vihagadharmiṇaḥ //
reference: Boys are of the nature of birds, being both subject to fear and hunger, and ready to fly about when impelled by them.
baseline: The children should be always fearful and fearful.
morphology: One who is always afraid of children those who are illiterate and those who want to escape from the enemy one who is not afraid of the enemy should do the same.

sanskrit: śaiśave guruto bhītirmātṛtaḥ pitṛtastathā / janato jyeṣṭhabālācca śaiśavaṃ bhayamandiram //
reference: Again boyhood is the abode of fear from all sides; such as from the tutor, father, mother, elder brother and elderly boys, and from every body besides.
baseline: In infancy the master should be afraid of his father. The elder son should be fearful of the father.
morphology: In infancy the master becomes fearful and the father becomes afraid. The elder son becomes the father. The younger son becomes fear.

sanskrit: sakaladoṣadaśāvihatāśayaṃ śaraṇamapyavivekavilāsinaḥ / iha na kasyacideva mahāmune bhavati bālyamalaṃ parituṣṭaye //
reference: Hence the hopeless state of childhood, which is full of faults and errors, and addicted to sports and thoughtlessness, cannot be satisfactory to any body.
baseline: One who takes refuge in the ten things that are evil and those who are illiterate would not be able to do so.
morphology: One who takes refuge in all the sins and misdeeds of ten thousand thousand thousand people would not be able to attain great heights.

sanskrit: śrīrāma uvāca / bālyānarthamatha tyaktvā pumānabhihatāśayaḥ / ārohati nipātāya yauvanaṃ saṃbhrameṇa tu //
reference: Rama continued:—The boy having passed his state of blemishes, gladly steps to his youth with hopes of gaining his objects that tend only to his ruin.
baseline: O Śrīma one who has left behind a child a mother a son a daughter a wife an aunt a priest a young man a noble person a man who has ascended a mountain and who has destroyed it is said to be proud.
morphology: O Śrīma one who has left behind a child one should climb the mountain and destroy the youth with pride.

sanskrit: tatrānantavilāsasya lolasya svasya cetasaḥ / vṛttīranubhavanyāti duḥkhādduḥkhāntaraṃ jaḍaḥ //
reference: The insensible youth feels at this time the wanton inclinations of his loose mind, and goes on falling from one tribulation to another.
baseline: One who experiences his own senses with the lloka of the inner abode there and the root after suffering and suffering would get pleasure.
morphology: One who experiences his own senses and desires for the enjoyment of the past and the desire for the comfort of the future would be born out of sorrow and sorrow.

sanskrit: svacittabilasaṃsthena nānāsaṃbhramakāriṇā / balātkāmapiśācena vivaśaḥ paribhūyate //
reference: He is overcome as one subdued by the power of delusive cupid, lying hidden in the cavity of the heart.
baseline: One who makes a vow with his own mind and the firmament of the bow would be able to do many things. He would get the gift with the same amount of money.
morphology: One who does not commit a crime would be destroyed by the commission of a crime. One who is willing to commit an offence would be punished.

sanskrit: cintānāṃ lolavṛttīnāṃ lalanānāmivā'vṛtīḥ / arpayatyavaśaṃ ceto bālānāmañjanaṃ yathā //
reference: His ungoverned mind gives rise to loose thoughts like those of voluptuous women, and these serve to beguile him like the magic collyrium (in the hand) of boys.
baseline: One should worship the children by offering them with the words ālaṇa kyāla lāva kālaśa and other things.
morphology: One should worship the children by offering them with the words ālaṇa kyāla lāva kṣṇu and āna as if they were the children.

sanskrit: te te doṣā durārambhāstatra taṃ tādṛśāśayam / tadrūpaṃ pratilumpanti duṣṭāstenaiva ye mune //
reference: Vices of the most heinous kind betake persons of such (perverse) minds in their youth, and lead them to their ruin.
baseline: Those who commit the same offence should begin to be punished. Those who do not do so should be punished with the same punishment.
morphology: Those who commit such a crime should be punished with the same punishment. Those who do not do so should be called evil.

sanskrit: mahānarakabījena saṃtatabhramadāyinā / yauvanena na ye naṣṭā naṣṭā nānyena te janāḥ //
reference: The paths of youth lead them to the gate of hell through a maze of errors. Those that have been left uncorrupt by their youth, are not to be corrupted by anything else.
baseline: Those people who do not get destroyed by the young man by the seeds of the great rakā by the children of the wanderers those people who are not harmed by the evil one.
morphology: Those people who do not get destroyed by the seeds of the great rakā those who get lost by the destruction of the youth those people who get ruined by the loss of the nāna those are those who are not destroyed by them.

sanskrit: nānārasamayī citravṛttāntanicayombhitā / bhīmā yauvanabhūryena tīrṇā dhīraḥ sa ucyate //
reference: Whoso has passed the dreadfully enchanted coast of youth, fraught with various flavours and wonders, are said to be truly wise.
baseline: One who is determined by the spirit of a young man should be said to be courageous.
morphology: One who is determined by the spirit of a young man should say that he is courageous.

sanskrit: nimeṣabhāsurākāramālolaghanagarjitam / vidyutprakāśamaśivaṃ yauvanaṃ me na rocate //
reference: I take no delight in our unwelcome youth, which appears to us in the form of a momentary flash of lightning, and soon succeeded by the loud roaring of the clouds.
baseline: I do not like the sound of light and light and youth.
morphology: One does not like to see the light of electricity and light of youth in the form of a garland and roar for a minute.

sanskrit: madhuraṃ svādu tiktaṃ ca dūṣaṇaṃ doṣabhūṣaṇam / surākallolasadṛśaṃ yauvanaṃ me na rocate //
reference: Youth like rich wine is sweet and delicious (at first), but becomes bitter, insipid and noxious in a short time. Hence it is not delectable to me.
baseline: Sweet tasty bitter dirty evil poisonous like the sound of a trumpet I do not like youth.
morphology: The sweetness taste bitterness defilement blasphemy etc.

sanskrit: asatyaṃ satyasaṃkāśamacirādvipralambhadam / svapnāṅganāsaṅgasamaṃ yauvanaṃ me na rocate //
reference: Youth appearing (at first) as a reality, is found to be a false, transient thing, as deceptive as a fairy dream by night. Hence I like it not.
baseline: I do not like the falsehood falsehood and falsehood. The dream and the body of the child are not good for me.
morphology: I do not like the falsehood falsehood and falsehood. The dreaming body and the body of the child are not good for me.

sanskrit: sarvasyāgre sarvapuṃsaḥ kṣaṇamātramanoharam / gandharvanagaraprakhyaṃ yauvanaṃ me na rocate //
reference: It is the most charming of all things to men, but its charm is soon lost and fled. Therefore the phantasmagoria of youth is not pleasing to me.
baseline: I do not like the youth in front of the Gandharva city the beauty of everything and everything for a moment.
morphology: I don 't like the youth in front of the Gandharva city the beauty of everything and everything for a moment.

sanskrit: iṣuprapātamātraṃ hi sukhadaṃ duḥkhabhāsuram / dāhapoṣapradaṃ nityaṃ yauvanaṃ me na rocate //
reference: Youth as an arrow shot is pleasant to see, but painful to feel its smart. Hence I do not like youth that produces blood heat.
baseline: I do not enjoy the happiness sorrow pleasure pleasure and happiness of the fall of the river of the elephant the burning and the nourishing of the eternal youth.
morphology: One who experiences happiness sorrow hunger nourishment and eternal youth is not liked by me.

sanskrit: āpātamātraramaṇaṃ sadbhāvarahitāntaram / veśyāstrīsaṃgamaprakhyaṃ yauvanaṃ me na rocate //
reference: Youth as a harlot is charming at first sight, but turning heartless soon after. Hence it is not to my liking.
baseline: I do not like the youthful attitude towards a prostitute a woman without good qualities a man without good feelings a wife with a wife a friend a courtesan and others.
morphology: I do not like the youthful attitude towards a prostitute woman and her company.

sanskrit: ye kecana samārambhāste sarve sarvaduḥkhadāḥ / tāruṇye saṃnidhiṃ yānti mahotpātā iva kṣaye //
reference: As the efforts of a dying man are all for his torment, so the exertions of the young are portentous of his destruction.
baseline: All those who have begun the ceremony all those who are afflicted with sorrow those who lose their wealth in their youth and those who do not get the great output.
morphology: All those who have begun the ceremony all those who are afflicted with sorrow those who lose their wealth in the youth become great products.

sanskrit: hārdāndhakārakāriṇyā bhairavākāravānapi / yauvanājñānayāminyā bibheti bhagavānapi //
reference: Puberty advances as a dark night spreading the shadow of destruction. It darkens the heart and mind by its hedious appearance, and intimidates even the god.
baseline: One who forms a Bhārāva who is the one who causes darkness in the heart also becomes the Lord by the knowledge of the youth.
morphology: One who becomes a Bhairava by the act of darkening the heart one who becomes the Lord by the practice of knowledge and knowledge of the youth.

sanskrit: suvismṛtaśubhācāraṃ buddhivaidhuryadāyinam / dadātyatitarāmeṣa bhramaṃ yauvanasaṃbhramaḥ //
reference: Errors growing in youth, cause copious mistakes in life, by upsetting good sense and setting at naught the approved good manners.
baseline: One who has forgotten the wisdom the wisdom and the wisdom of the mind the gift of knowledge the illusion of youth the journey of life etc.
morphology: One who has forgotten the virtues of good speech one who has acquired wisdom has given to others illusions has gone through the journey of youth.

sanskrit: kāntāviyogajātena hṛdi duḥsparśavahninā / yauvane dahyate jantustarurdāvāgninā yathā //
reference: The raging fire in the hearts of the young, caused by separation of their mates, burns them down like trees by a wild fire.
baseline: The heart should be touched with the kanta yogājata and burnt with the fire of fire. The animal should be burned with the flame of fire in its youth.
morphology: The heart should be touched with the kanta yogājata and burnt with the fire of fire.

sanskrit: sunirmalāpi vistīrṇā pāvanyapi hi yauvane / matiḥ kaluṣatāmeti prāvṛṣīva taraṅgiṇī //
reference: As a clear, sacred and wide stream, becomes muddy in the rains, so doth the mind of man however clear, pure and expanded it may be, gets polluted in his youth.
baseline: One who has not been able to attain the height of the mountain even if he has not attained the height would have become corrupt. One who does not want to suffer would have to go through the waves.
morphology: One who has not been able to attain the height of the mountain would be a young man. One who does not want to suffer would become a poor man. He would become an evil man.

sanskrit: śakyate ghanakallolā bhīmā laṅghayituṃ nadī / na tu tāruṇyataralā tṛṣṇātaralitāntarā //
reference: It is possible for one to cross over a river made terrible by its waves, but no way possible to him to get over the boisterous expanse of his youthful desires.
baseline: It is possible to cross the river with a solid stone and not with a thirsting bow.
morphology: It is possible to cross the river with a solid rock and not with a thirst for youth.

sanskrit: sā kāntā tau stanau pīnau te vilāsāstadānanam / tāruṇya iti cintābhiryāti jarjaratāṃ janaḥ //
reference: O how (lamentably) is one's youth worn out with the thoughts of his mistress, her swollen breasts, her beautiful face and her sweet caresses.
baseline: One who has become ill after having thought that he would be a young man would get the gift of those luxuries in the form of a kanta two breasts and a penis.
morphology: One who has become ill after having thought that he would be a young man would get the gift of those luxuries in the form of a kanta two breasts and a penis.

sanskrit: naraṃ taralatṛṣṇārti yuvānamiha sādhavaḥ / pūjayanti na tu cchinnaṃ jarattṛṇalavaṃ yathā //
reference: The young man afflicted with the pain of soft desire, is regarded by the wise in no better light than a fragment of (useless) straw.
baseline: O Narāṇa the one who worships water water and water the young and the virtuous. One should not worship the pitchers.
morphology: O Narā Yūna Yāna and Yūṇa the virtuous are worshipped as the sons of water water and water.

sanskrit: nāśāyaiva madārtasya doṣamauktikadhāriṇaḥ / abhimānamahebhasya nityālānaṃ hi yauvanam //
reference: Youth is the stake of haughty self-esteem, as the rack is for the immolation of the elephant giddy with its frontal pearl.
baseline: One who has made a mistake for the destruction of the body and the loss of the self one who has taken pride and the eternal glory of the great man one should be a youth.
morphology: One who has made a mistake for the destruction of the body and the loss of the self one who has taken pride and the perpetual loss of life one should be a youth.

sanskrit: manovipulamūlānāṃ doṣāśīviṣadhāriṇām / śoṣarodanavṛkṣāṇāṃ yauvanaṃ bata kānanam //
reference: Youth is a lamentable forest, where the mind as the root of all, gives growth to jungles of (love sick) groans and sighs, and tears of sorrow. The vices of this time, are as venomous snakes of the forest.
baseline: One who is guilty of the root cause of the mind the poisonous one the young one of the trees of the sun the old man the son of the elephant the one who is the enemy of the evil one and the other.
morphology: One who has the qualities of the mind the roots the faults the poisonous ones the plants of the sun the trees of the fire the youth the bātaka the kanaṇa.
