sanskrit: rasakesarasaṃbādhaṃ kuvikalpadalākulam / duścintācañcarīkāṇāṃ puṣkaraṃ viddhi yauvanam //
reference: Know youthful bloom of the person to resemble the blooming lotus of the lake said:—the one is full of affections, bad desires and evil intents, as the other is fraught with bees, filaments, petals and leaves.
baseline: The association of the rasakaṣa with the kuṇi kālākāla dāla kula the purification of the chakranikas the desire to be worried the knowledge of the youth.
morphology: The association of the rasaka kesara kuṇi kupa dāla kula kulā kūṇḍa chakra chankra kāṇikara pūrṣa vidya yuṇu and yuva.

sanskrit: kṛtākṛtakupakṣāṇāṃ hṛtsarastīracāriṇām / ādhivyādhivihaṃgānāmālayo navayauvanam //
reference: The new bloom of youth is the resort of anxiety and disease, which like two birds with their (black and white) plumage of vice and virtue, frequent the fountain of the young man's heart.
baseline: A person who is born with a penis made out of a piece of wood and a heart made of a stone should be blessed with a new form of life.
morphology: One who has made a carving of the wings the heart the feet the charioteers the head and the head should be given a new form of life.

sanskrit: jaḍānāṃ gatasaṃkhyānāṃ kallolānāṃ vilāsinām / anapekṣitamaryādo vāridhirnavayauvanam //
reference: Early youth resembles a deep sea, disturbed by the waves of numberless amusements, transgressing all bounds, and regardless of death and disease.
baseline: One would get the number of roots past and past and stones luxuries unexpected wealth and many other things.
morphology: One would get the past number of roots stones luxuries unannounced wealth and other things.

sanskrit: sarveṣāṃ guṇasargāṇāṃ parirūḍharajastamāḥ / apanetuṃ sthitiṃ dakṣo viṣamo yauvanānilaḥ //
reference: Youth is like a furious gust of wind, over-loaded with the dust of pride and vanity, and sweeps away every trace of the good qualities.
baseline: One should maintain all the virtues and qualities. One should be able to attain the position of the righteousness and the mind of the youth.
morphology: One should maintain all the qualities of the body. One should be able to maintain the position of the head and the mind of the youth.

sanskrit: nayanti pāṇḍutāṃ vakramākulāvakarotkaṭāḥ / ārohanti parāṃ koṭiṃ rūkṣā yauvanapāṃsavaḥ //
reference: The rude dust of the passions of youths, disfigures their face, and the hurricane of their sensualities cover their good qualities.
baseline: The Pandu leaves the mountain with a lot of hair and the young pāśas climb the mountain.
morphology: The Pandutas who carry the bulls who climb the hill who carry a lot of stones and who are young and have no fear of the enemy are called vakrama kula vakrā and kāktaka.

sanskrit: udvodhayati doṣāliṃ nikṛntati guṇāvalim / narāṇāṃ yauvanollāso vilāso duṣkṛtaśriyām //
reference: Youthful vigour awakens a series of faults, and destroys a group of good qualities, by increasing the vice of pleasures.
baseline: One who invents the evil one will get rid of the good one. One who does not want to give pleasure or pleasure to the young one would get happiness and misfortune.
morphology: One who invents the evil one will get rid of the good one. One who does not want to give pleasure or pleasure to the young one would get ill.

sanskrit: śarīrapaṅkajarajaścañcalāṃ matiṣaṭpadīm / nibadhnanmohayatyeṣa navayauvanacandramāḥ //
reference: Youthful bloom confines the fickle mind to some beauteous person, as the bright moon-beams serve to shut the flitting bee in the dust of the closing lotus.
baseline: The body and the parts of the body should be placed in the eighty-somethings. The new moon should be made to be enchanted by the nibbādhana.
morphology: The four parts of the body the bākājārajjā and the mātisātpādī should be placed in the middle. The new moon should be enchanted by the nine elements.

sanskrit: śarīrakhaṇḍakodbhūtā ramyā yauvanavallarī / lagnameva manobhṛṅgaṃ madayatyunnatiṃ gatā //
reference: Youth like a delightsome cluster of flowers, growing in the arbour of human body, attracts the mind as the bee to it, and makes it giddy.
baseline: Having divided the body one who has become a young man one becomes a virgin. One who has made the mind and body of a man go to the highest point.
morphology: Having destroyed the body part one would attain great height by making the mind and body part of the body as well as the mind.

sanskrit: śarīramarutāpotthāṃ yuvatāmṛgatṛṣṇikām / manomṛgāḥ pradhāvantaḥ patanti viṣayāvaṭe //
reference: The human mind anxious to derive pleasure from the youthfulness of the body, falls into the cave of sensuality, as a deer running after the mirage of desert heat, falls down into a pit.
baseline: The body death death and death of a young man the mind and the animals falling down on the ground are the mainstay of the mind.
morphology: After having destroyed the body the young animals fall into the pit of the earth. The animals of the mind fall down on the ground.

sanskrit: śarīraśarvarījyotsnā cittakesariṇaḥ saṭā / laharī jīvitāmbhodheryuvatā me na tuṣṭaye //
reference: I take no delight in moony youth, which guilds the dark body with its beams, and resembles the stern mane of the leonine mind. It is a surge in the ocean of our lives.
baseline: The body should be worshipped with the sun and the heart should be worshiped with the kesara of the mind. The illusion of the living beings should not be pleased with me.
morphology: The body should be worshipped with the sun and the heart should be worshiped with the kesara of the mind. The illusion of the living should not be pleased with me.

sanskrit: dināni katicidyeyaṃ phalitā dehajaṅgale / yuvatā śaradasyāṃ hi na samāśvāsamarhatha //
reference: There is no reliance in youth, which fades away as soon as summer flowers in this desert of the body.
baseline: One who has spent so many days in the forest of the body would not get peace in the winter.
morphology: The days are so long that the fruits are not found in the forest. The young man would not be able to breathe in the autumn.

sanskrit: jhaṭityeva prayātyeva śarīrādyuvatākhagaḥ / kṣaṇenaivālpabhāgyasya hastāccintāmaṇiryathā //
reference: Youth is as a bird, and as soon flies away from our bodily cage as the philosopher's stone, which quickly disappears from the hands of the unfortunate.
baseline: One should immediately try to get rid of the body the body and the body. One should not make a mistake for a while. One would get a wish for good fortune.
morphology: One should immediately try to get rid of the body the body and the body. One should think of the fate of the hands and the mind.

sanskrit: yadā yadā parāṃ koṭimadhyārohati yauvanam / valganti sajvarāḥ kāmāstadā nāśāya kevalam //
reference: As youth advances to its highest pitch, so the feverish passions wax stronger for our destruction only.
baseline: When the outer corner of the body is raised in the middle the youth is removed. The elves are only destroyed by the desire.
morphology: When one has ascended into the middle of the other corner one would get the youth. The elves would destroy the desire.

sanskrit: tāvadeva vivalganti rāgadveṣapiśācakāḥ / nāstameti samastaiṣā yāvadyauvanayāminī //
reference: As long as the night (delusion) of youth does not come to its end, so long the fiends of our passion do not cease to rage in the desert of the body.
baseline: Those who do evil deeds should be worshipped with the same words. These are said to be evil.
morphology: Those who do evil deeds should be worshipped with the same words.

sanskrit: nānāvikārabahule varāke kṣaṇanāśini / kāruṇyaṃ kuru tāruṇye mriyamāṇe sutai yathā //
reference: Pity me, O sage! in this state of youth, which is so full of perturbations, as to have deprived me of the sight (light) of reason. O pity me as thou wouldst for thy dying son.
baseline: One should do mercilessly in the death of a young man by sleeping on the floor of a well with a lotus.
morphology: One should destroy the enemy for a while in the form of a lotus. One should do mercilessly in the death of a young man by sleeping.

sanskrit: harṣamāyāti yo mohātpuruṣaḥ kṣaṇabhaṅginā / yauvanena mahāmugdhaḥ sa vai naramṛgaḥ smṛtaḥ //
reference: The foolish man who ignorantly rejoices at his transient youth, is considered as a human beast.
baseline: One who is pleased with the love of the man with a momentary fragrance one who is very happy with the youth and one who has great affection with the mind is remembered as a man of good nature.
morphology: One who is pleased with the love of the man one who is happy with the pleasure of the person and one who has great pleasure with the youth one should remember the nature of the mind.

sanskrit: mānamohānmadonmattaṃ yauvanaṃ yo'bhilaṣyati / acireṇa sa durbuddhiḥ paścāttāpena yujyate //
reference: The foolish fellow who is fond of his youth which is flushed with pride and fraught with errors, comes to repent (of his folly) in a short time.
baseline: One who is ill-informed will soon be united with repentance.
morphology: One who is ill-informed will soon be joined with repentance.

sanskrit: te pūjyāste mahātmānasta eva puruṣā bhuvi / ye sukhena samuttīrṇāḥ sādho yauvanasaṃkaṭāt //
reference: Those great minded men are honoured on earth, who have safely passed over the perils of youth.
baseline: Those worshipped are the great souls. Those men who are satisfied with happiness those who are happy and those who get rid of the problems of youth those are the virtuous.
morphology: Those worshipped are the great souls. Those men who are satisfied with happiness those who are happy and those who get rid of the problem of youth those are the good men.

sanskrit: sukhena tīryate'mbhodhirutkṛṣṭamakarākaraḥ / na kallolabalollāsi sadoṣaṃ hatayauvanam //
reference: One crosses over with ease the wide ocean which is the horrible habitation of huge whales; but it is hard to pass over our youth, that is so full of vices and the billows.
baseline: One who does not commit a crime should not commit the crime of killing a young man.
morphology: One who does not commit a crime should not commit the crime of killing a young man. One who is not guilty of any offence should be punished.

sanskrit: vinayabhūṣitamāryajanāspadaṃ karuṇayojjvalamāvalitaṃ guṇaiḥ / iha hi durlabhamaṅga suyauvanaṃ jagati kānanamambaragaṃ yathā //
reference: It is very rare to have that happy youth which is fraught with humility, and spent in the company of respectable men; which is distinguished by feelings of sympathy, and is joined with good qualities and virtues.
baseline: O lord of the earth one who is blessed with modesty mercilessness grace light grace and virtues one with a weak limb and a young man should worship the world.
morphology: O lord of the earth one who is adorned with modesty mercilessness kindness light and goodness has the qualities of a poor person a young man a man with a weak limb a world with a heart and a heart.

sanskrit: śrīrāma uvāca / māṃsapāñcālikāyāstu yantralole'ṅgapañjare / snāyvasthigranthiśālinyāḥ striyāḥ kimiva śobhanaṃ //
reference: Rama added:—What beauty is there in the person of a woman, composed of nerves, bones and joints? She is a mere statue of flesh, and a frame of moving machinery with her ribs and limbs.
baseline: O Śrīma one who has five parts of the body one that has five organs one in the body and one who is a member of the limbs one with nerves and glands and another with a woman is beautiful.
morphology: O Śrīma one who has five parts of the body and five parts one with the limbs one having nerves and glands and another with the body one should worship the goddess.

sanskrit: tvaṅmāṃsaraktabāṣpāmbu pṛthakkṛtvā vilocanam / samālokaya ramyaṃ cetkiṃ mudhā parimuhyasi //
reference: Can you find any thing beautiful in the female form, separated from its (component parts of the) flesh, skin, blood and water, that is worth beholding? Why then dote upon it?
baseline: Having separated the spears from the flesh of the body one should worship the goddess after having worshipped her in the same manner. Having worshipped the goddess Rāmya the goddess of love and love should be worshipped.
morphology: Having separated the spears from the flesh of thee one should worship the goddess after having worshipped her in the form of a serpent.

sanskrit: itaḥ keśā ito raktamitīyaṃ pramadātanuḥ / kimetayā ninditayā karoti vipulāśayaḥ //
reference: This fairy frame consisting of hairs in one part and blood in the other, cannot engage the attention of a high-minded man to its blemishes.
baseline: One who does this with the hair blood and other things is doing this with contempt.
morphology: One who has so many hairs so many bloods such as those of the king of the kingdom who has done such a thing with such blasphemousness.

sanskrit: vāsovilepanairyāni lālitāni punaḥ punaḥ / tānyaṅgānyaṅga luṇṭhanti kravyādāḥ sarvadehinām //
reference: The bodies of females, that are so covered with clothing and repeatedly besmeared with paints and perfumes, are (at last) devoured by carnivorous.
baseline: They would again and again plunder all the parts of the body by plundering all the organs.
morphology: They would again and again plunder all the parts of the body by plundering the objects of the vasovilipaṇirya.

sanskrit: meruśrṛṃgataṭollāsigaṃgājalarayopamā / dṛṣṭā yasminstane muktāhārasyollāsaśālitā //
reference: The breasts of women decorated with strings of pearl, appear as charming as the pinnacles of Sumeru, washed by the waters of Ganges falling upon them.
baseline: One who has seen the water of the river Gāṅga the river of water and water in the form of a pole is blessed with free food.
morphology: One who has seen the waters of the river meruśrīngta tollāsīganga jalā yopāma in which he is blessed with free food is blessed.

sanskrit: śmaśāneṣu diganteṣu sa eva lalanāstanaḥ / śvabhirāsvādyate kāle laghupiṇḍa ivāndhasaḥ //
reference: The breasts of women decorated with strings of pearl, appear as charming as the pinnacles of Sumeru, washed by the waters of Ganges falling upon them.
baseline: The same lantern should be placed in the dead bodies and the same should be used in the night. In the same time a small penis should be kept in the dark.
morphology: The same lantern should be placed on the sides of the body in the cremation grounds. It should be worn in the evening and the body should be covered with a small piece.

sanskrit: raktamāṃsāsthidigdhāni karabhasya yathā vane / tathaivāṅgāni kāminyāstāṃ pratyapi hi ko grahaḥ //
reference: There is no difference between a woman and a young elephant that lives in the jungle, both of them being made of blood, flesh and bones. Then why hunt after her.
baseline: One who has left the body of a cow or animal in the forest would like to have that part of the body.
morphology: One who has left the body of a cow or animal in the forest would not want to have those parts.

sanskrit: āpātaramaṇīyatvaṃ kalpate kevalaṃ striyāḥ / manye tadapi nāstyatra mune mohaikakāraṇam //
reference: A woman is charming only for a short time, and does not long last to be so. I look upon her merely as a cause of delusion.
baseline: Only women are allowed to perform the ritual of abhātārāma. One of the reasons for this is that they are not allowed to do so.
morphology: One should not think of the illusion of women as the only cause of illusion.

sanskrit: vipulollāsadāyinyā madamanmathapūrvakam / ko viśeṣo vikāriṇyā madirāyāḥ striyāstathā //
reference: There is no difference between wine and a woman, both of them tending equally to produce high-flown mirth and jollity, and creating revelry and lust.
baseline: A woman should be made to drink wine with vipulola alaādaṇīya manma and matha. One should drink wine without any distortion.
morphology: A woman who drinks wine with the help of a vipulo alla and other spirits should be made to drink with the mother.

sanskrit: lalanālānasaṃlīnā mune mānavadantinaḥ / prabodhaṃ nādhigacchanti dṛḍhairapi śamāṅkuśaiḥ //
reference: Uxorious men are like chained elephants among mankind, that will never come to sense however goaded by the hooks of reason.
baseline: The senses of man are destroyed by the combination of saliva water and water. The consciousness of man is destroyed even if it is strong.
morphology: The senses of man are destroyed by the combination of saliva water and water in the forehead. The consciousness of man is destroyed even if he is strong.

sanskrit: keśakajjaladhāriṇyo duḥsparśā locanapriyāḥ / duṣkṛtāgniśikhā nāryo dahanti tṛṇavannaram //
reference: Women are the flames of vice, their black-dyed eye and hairs are as their smoke and soot. They are as intangible as fire, though pleasing to the sight. They burn the man as fire consumes the straw.
baseline: Women with hair light touch greed love evil fire fire and fire are burnt in the forest.
morphology: Those who are fond of having a hair light touch greed evil fire fire and fire etc. are burning the forest of grass.

sanskrit: jvalatāmatidūre'pi sarasā api nīrasāḥ / striyo hi narakāgnīnāmindhanaṃ cāru dāruṇam //
reference: They burn from afar (more than fire), and are as dry as bones (in their hearts), though appearing as soft and juicy to sight. They serve as fuel to the fire of hell, and are dangerous with their charmingness.
baseline: A woman who is angry with the fire and the fire of hell is four times worse.
morphology: A woman who is angry with the fire and the fire of hell is four times worse.

sanskrit: vikīrṇākārakabarī tarattārakalocanā / purṇendubimbavadanā kusumotkarahāsinī //
reference: The woman resembles a moon-light night, veiled over by her loosened locks, and looking through her starry eyes. She shows her moon-like face amidst her flowery smiles.
baseline: O Kusumotaka the king of the earth who is a man of many forms who has been born with the fragrance of the sun and who is the son of a demon.
morphology: The image of Kusumotaka is described as having the shape of a bead with the form of a scatter the colour of the bead the color of the water and the colour śūmotaka.

sanskrit: līlāvilolapuruṣā kāryasaṃhārakāriṇī / paraṃ vimohanaṃ buddheḥ kāminī dīrghayāminī //
reference: Her soft dalliance destroys all manly energy, and her caresses overpower the good sense of men, as the shade of night does the sleeping.
baseline: The lilā vilola purūsā the destroyer of all evil deeds and the kāmīna of the intellect the long and long form are the other forms of illusion.
morphology: The lilāvilola man is the destroyer of all evil deeds. Then vimohana is the master of the mind.

sanskrit: puṣpābhirāmamadhurā karapallavaśālinī / bhramarākṣivilāsāḍhyā stanastabakadhāriṇī //
reference: The woman is as lovely as a creeper in its flowering time. Her palm are the leaves and her eyes as the black-bees (on the flower). Her breasts are as the uplifted tops of the plant.
baseline: A woman with a breast and a chest should be adorned with flowers flowers and flowers honey garlands and garlands.
morphology: A woman with a lotus a pearl a mermaid a bearer of hair a man with a breast a mother with a bow a woman with an armour a bridegroom a maid of arms and a woman holding a breast and a piece of cloth should be offered.

sanskrit: puṣpakesaragaurāṅgī naramāraṇatatparā / dadātyunmattavaivaśyaṃ kāntā viṣalatā yathā //
reference: The lovely damsel is like a poisonous creeper, fair as the filament of a flower but destructive of life, by causing inebriation and insensibility.
baseline: One who gives flowers hair hair and hair should be worshipped with the garland. One who does not give gifts should be called a kanta or a virgin.
morphology: One who gives flowers hair hair and hair should be worshipped with the mantra nāmarāṇatapara. One who does not give birth to a child should be called kanta and vīsilāta.

sanskrit: satkāryocchvāsamātreṇa bhujaṅgadalanotkayā / kāntayoddhriyate jantuḥ karabhyevorago bilāt //
reference: As the snake-catcher entices the snake by his breath and brings it out of its hole, so does the woman allure the man by her officious civilities, and gets him under her control.
baseline: The animal should be made to fight with the arms and legs with the help of the meritorious hands. The beast should be raised from the ground with the hands and arms.
morphology: One should fight the enemy with the arms legs and legs. The enemy should fight against the enemy.

sanskrit: kāmanāmnā kirātena vikīrṇā mugdhacetasām / nāryo naravihaṃgānāmaṅgabandhanavāgurāḥ //
reference: Concupiscence as a huntsman, has spread his nets in the forms of women, for the purpose of ensnaring the persons of deluded men like silly birds.
baseline: One who is attracted by the desire the desire and the desire of the heart the body the mind and the body should be bound together.
morphology: One who is attracted by the desire desire sacrifice and wriggling in the heart should bind the body of a woman a man a woman and a man.

sanskrit: lalanāvipulālāne manomattamataṃgajaḥ / ratiśṛṅkhalayā brahmanbaddhastiṣṭhati mūkavat //
reference: The mind of man though as fierce as that of a furious elephant, is tied fast by the chain of love to the fulcrum of women, just as an elephant is fastened (by his leg) to the post, where he remains dull and dumb for ever.
baseline: One who is bound by the chain of the rati the Brahman as if he is silent in the lāna and the pūlula of the mind the body of the soul the mind and the body.
morphology: One who is bound by the chain of the rati the mind the body and the body of the Brahman in the lāna the muṇḍu and the pūlāla forms a mute body.

sanskrit: janmapalvalamatsyānāṃ cittakardamacāriṇām / puṃsāṃ durvāsanārajjurnārī baḍiśapiṇḍikā //
reference: Human life is as a pool in which the mind moves about in its mud and mire (as a fish). Here it is caught by the bait of woman, and dragged along by the thread of its impure desires.
baseline: The bāṇma the fruit the fishes the heart the chariot the bull the garland the pitchers the dervasana the arrow the body the head the penis and the body.
morphology: One who is born with fruits fishes spirits servants and servants one who is not afraid of evil will become the king.

sanskrit: manduraṃ ca turaṅgāṇāmālānamiva dantinām / puṃsāṃ mantra ivāhīnāṃ bandhanaṃ vāmalocanā //
reference: The beauteous-eyed damsel is a bondage to man, as the stable is to the horse, the fastening post to the elephant, and as spells are to the snakes.
baseline: The temple should be placed in the form of a tower and the garland. The mantras should be held in the left hand.
morphology: The mantras should be placed on the left side of the temple. The garlands should be made to be placed in the same way as the garlands of the tower. The mantrals should be tied together.

sanskrit: nānārasavatī citrā bhogabhūmiriyaṃ mune / striyamāśritya saṃyātā parāmiha hi saṃsthitim //
reference: This wondrous world, with all its delights and enjoyments, began with woman and depends on women for its continuance.
baseline: The image of Nanārāśvati is placed on the ground of enjoyment in the forehead. It is placed in the upper body after having been meditated upon by a woman.
morphology: The image of Nanārsavati should be placed in the ground of enjoyment in the forehead. It should be set on the earth after having been meditated upon by a woman.

sanskrit: sarveṣāṃ doṣaratnānāṃ susamudgikayā'nayā / duḥkhaśṛṅkhalayā nityamalamastu mama striyā //
reference: A woman is the casket of all gems of vice (Pandora's box), she is the cause of the chain of our everlasting misery, and is of no use to me.
baseline: O my lady the eternal wealth of all misfortune gems and other things should be bestowed with the chain of sorrows.
morphology: O my lady the eternal wealth is made of all the bad jewels with the chain of sorrows and good and bad.

sanskrit: kiṃ stanena kimakṣṇā vā kiṃ nitambena kiṃ bhuvā / māṃsamātraikasāreṇa karomyahamavastunā //
reference: What shall I do with her breast, her eyes, her loins, her eyebrows, the substance of which is but flesh, and which therefore is altogether unsubstantial.
baseline: One should eat the meat with one of the two parts with the mother whether with the breasts the forehead the buttocks the chest the mouth and the mouth with the mouth.
morphology: One should eat meat with one of the two ingredients. One should do it with the breasts one with the buttocks one without the mouth and one with all the other ingredients.

sanskrit: ito māṃsamito raktamito'sthīnīti vāsaraiḥ / brahmankatipayaireva yāti strī viśarārutām //
reference: Here and there, O Brahman! her flesh and blood and bones undergo a change for the worse in course of a few days.
baseline: It should be made of flesh and blood. It should also be made from the blood of the abode of Brahman the goddess of the universe.
morphology: This is the blood of the flesh and the righteousness of the living beings. A woman should be made to stand on the path of Brahman.

sanskrit: yāstāta puruṣaiḥ sthūlairlalitā manujaiḥ priyāḥ / tā mune pravibhaktāṅgyaḥ svapanti pitṛbhūmiṣu //
reference: You see sir, those dearly beloved mistresses, who are so much fondled by foolish men, lying at last in the cemetery, and the members of their bodies all mangled and falling off from their places.
baseline: The members of the family who enter the forefathers'lands should be worshipped by the men who are in the same position as the men.
morphology: Those who are worshipped by men in their houses and those who are loved by men should enter the forefathers'lands.

sanskrit: yasminghanatarasnehaṃ mukhe patrāṅkurāḥ striyaḥ / kāntena racitā brahmanpīyate tena jaṅgale //
reference: O Brahman! those dear objects of love—the faces of damsels, so fondly decorated by their lovers with paints and pastes, are at last to be singed on the piles.
baseline: A woman who has a penis made of copper and leaves in her mouth and has a deep love in the forest is blessed with Brahman.
morphology: A woman who has a penis made of copper and leaves in her mouth and has a deep love in the forest should worship Brahman.

sanskrit: keśāḥ śmaśānavṛkṣeṣu yānti cāmaralekhikām / asthīnyuḍuvadābhānti dinairavanimaṇḍale //
reference: Their braided hairs now hang as flappers of chowry on the arbors of the cemetery, and their whitened bones are strewn about as shining stars after a few days.
baseline: The hair should be placed in the trees for burial and the scribe should be kept in the temple.
morphology: The hair should be placed in the trees of the burial. The scribe should be kept in the temple.

sanskrit: pibanti pāṃsavo raktaṃ kravyādāścāpyanekaśaḥ / carmāṇi ca śivā bhuṅkte khaṃ yānti prāṇavāyavaḥ //
reference: Behold their blood sucked in by the dust of the earth, voracious beasts and worms feeding upon their flesh, jackals tearing their skin, and their vital air wafted in the vacuum.
baseline: One who drinks pans drinks blood and receives many things and who consumes food and drinks water from Lord Śiva one who is alive and well.
morphology: One who drinks pāṇsa blood and other things should be offered to him. One who consumes sāmarāṇas and others should be given food and water.

sanskrit: ityeṣā lalanāṅgānāmacireṇaiva bhāvinī / sthitirmayā vaḥ kathitā kiṃ bhrāntimanudhāvatha //
reference: This is the state to which the members of the female body must shortly come to pass, you say all existence to be delusion, tell me therefore why do you allow yourselves to fall into error?
baseline: What illusion would you find by saying these things to a woman who is going to be born with the same limb as her mother.
morphology: What illusion would you find by saying these things with the forehead forehead and head.

sanskrit: bhūtapañcakasaṃghaṭṭasaṃsthānaṃ lalanābhidham / rasādabhipatatvetatkathaṃ nāma dhiyānvitaḥ //
reference: A woman is no other than a form composed of the five elements, then why should intelligent men be fondly attached to her (at the risk of their ruin)?
baseline: One should meditate on the names of the elements the elements of the universe the objects of the union the place of the lāṇavidhā rāasa abhīpatā etc.
morphology: One should meditate on the names of the elements the elements and the objects of the union of the gods the lāṇavidhā rāsa dābhipātā.

sanskrit: śākhāpratānagahanā kaṭvamlaphalamālinī / sutālottālatāmeti cintā kāntānusāriṇī //
reference: Men's longing for women is likened to the creeper called Suta, which stretches its sprigs to a great length, but bears plenty of bitter and sour fruits.
baseline: One who has made a cut with the branches and the stones one who has got the fruit of the lotus one should think of the kanta and other things.
morphology: One should not think of the kanta. One would get the fruit of the lotus with the branches and the ornaments.

sanskrit: kāndigbhūtatayā ceto ghanagardhāndhamākulam / paraṃ mohamupādatte yūthabhraṣṭamṛgo yathā //
reference: A man blinded by avarice (for the supportance of his mate) is as a stray deer from its herd; and not knowing which way to go, is lost in the maze of illusion.
baseline: One who has become a cow a cow and a cow should be made to eat with the sound of the rosary. One who is attracted to the cow should eat the cow and go astray.
morphology: One who has become a cow a cow and a cow should be covered with a thick cloth. One who is attracted by the illusion should be attracted by a young stray beast.

sanskrit: śocyatāṃ paramāṃ yāti taruṇastaruṇīparaḥ / nibaddhaḥ kariṇīlolo vindhyakhāte yathā gajaḥ //
reference: A young man under the control of a young woman, is as much lamentable as an elephant fallen into a pit of the Vindhya mountain in pursuit of his mate.
baseline: One who is bound by a sword should be made to lie down on the other side of the mountain. The elephant should be kept in the same position as the elephant in the Vindhyakha.
morphology: One who is bound by a sword should be made to lie down on the ground with the sword the elephant the vindhyaka and the elephant.

sanskrit: yasya strī tasya bhogecchā niḥstrīkasya kva bhogabhūḥ / striyaṃ tyaktvā jagattyaktaṃ jagattyaktvā sukhī bhavet //
reference: He that has a wife, has an appetite for enjoyment on earth; but one without her has no object of desire. Abandonment of the wife amounts to the abandoning of the world, and forsaking the world is the path to true happiness.
baseline: A woman who desires to enjoy the enjoyment of a woman should leave her husband and go to the world and express happiness.
morphology: A woman who desires to enjoy the pleasure of a woman should leave the enjoyment of her husband and express herself to the world and become happy.

sanskrit: āpātamātraramaṇeṣu sudustareṣu bhogeṣu nāhamalipakṣaticañcaleṣu / brahmanrame maraṇarogajarādibhītyā śāmyāmyahaṃ paramupaimi padaṃ prayatnāt //
reference: I am not content, O Brahman! with these unmanageable enjoyments which are as flickering as the wings of bees, and are as soon at an end as they are born (like the ephemerids of a day). I long only for the state of supreme bliss, from my fear of repeated births transmigration), decay and death.
baseline: O Brahman one who is afraid of death disease disease and disease should seek the supreme position in the areas of the earth.
morphology: O Brahman one who is afraid of death disease disease etc. and who is seeking the highest position in the world should not do this in the areas of oblations and enjoyments.

sanskrit: śrīrāma uvāca / aparyāptaṃ hi bālatvaṃ balātpibati yauvanam / yauvanaṃ ca jarā paścātpaśya karkaśatāṃ mithaḥ //
reference: Boyhood has scarcely lost its boyishness when it is overtaken by youth, which is soon followed by a ruthless old age, devouring the other two.
baseline: O Śrīma one who has not had enough of his childhood attains strength gains youth and after having attained the height of his youth falls into the darkness.
morphology: O Śrīma one who has not attained the age of puberty has attained the strength of youth has achieved youth and after having attained the height of youth is said to be a false falsehood.

sanskrit: himāśanirivāmbhojaṃ vātyeva śaradambukam / dehaṃ jarā nāśayati nadī tīrataruṃ yathā //
reference: Old age withers the body like a frost freezing the lake of lilies. It drives away the beauty of the person as a storm does the autumnal clouds; and it pulls down the body, as a current carries away a tree on the bank.
baseline: The Śarāmbukha leaves the body as the wind and the Śaṃbuktas eat food in the form of the himāśaṇirīva. It destroys the roots of the body and the river.
morphology: The Śarāmbukha tree destroys the roots of the body and the river.

sanskrit: jarjarīkṛtasarvāṅgī jarā jaraṭharūpiṇī / virūpatāṃ nayatyāśu dehaṃ viṣalavo yathā //
reference: The old man with his limbs slackened and worn out by age, and his body weakened by infirmity, is treated by women as a useless beast.
baseline: The garland made of jārjāri the garland of water the form of jarātha the body should not be distorted. It should be poisonous.
morphology: The garland made of jārjāri the garland of jarātha the body is poisonous and does not get deformed.

sanskrit: śithilādīrṇasarvāṅgaṃ jarājīrṇakalevaram / samaṃ paśyanti kāminyaḥ puruṣaṃ karabhaṃ yathā //
reference: ?missing text?
baseline: One would see a man with a loose neck and a necklace and a body of a dead body as if he were a cow as if it were a mace.
morphology: A man who is a lame man would see a garland with a loose thread and a piece of cloth that is worn down. He would look like a black man with a carob.

sanskrit: anāyāsakadarthinyā gṛhīte jarasā jane / palāyya gacchati prajñā sapatnyevāhatāṅganā //
reference: Old age drives a man's good sense, as a good wife is driven away by her step dame.
baseline: One who is caught by the enemy with an effortless weapon would escape and go to his wife and wife.
morphology: One who is caught by the enemy with an effortless act of force would go into hiding. One who flees would go to his wife and wife.

sanskrit: dāsāḥ putrāḥ striyaścaiva bāndhavāḥ suhṛdastathā / hasantyunmattakamiva naraṃ vārdhakakampitam //
reference: A man in his state of tottering old age, is scoffed at as a dotard by his own sons and servants, and even by his wife, and all his friends and relations.
baseline: The servants sons wives friends friends and friends should be pleased. The male should be mercilessly married and aged.
morphology: The servants sons wives friends relatives friends and friends should be pleased. The male should be mercilessly married and aged.

sanskrit: duṣprekṣyaṃ jaraṭhaṃ dīnaṃ hīnaṃ guṇaparākramaiḥ / gṛdhro vṛkṣamivādīrghaṃ gardho hyabhyeti vṛddhakam //
reference: Insatiable avarice like a greedy vulture alights on the heads of the aged, when their appearance grows uncouth, and their bodies become helpless, and devoid of all manly qualities and powers.
baseline: One who is poor weak good powerful poor poor and weak has the strength of a tree a cow a horse a bull a man with the neck a woman with the heart a great growth is a great strength.
morphology: One who is poor weak weak and has good power one who is a cow a cow and a cow should be raised.

sanskrit: dainyadoṣamayī dīrghā hṛdi dāhapradāyinī / sarvāpadāmekasakhī vārdhake vardhate spṛhā //
reference: Appetite the constant companion of my youth, is thriving along with my age, accompanied with her evils of indigence, and heart-burning cares and restlessness.
baseline: The heart is long and evil in the day the heart is burning and the body is growing in the same old age.
morphology: The heart is long and evil in the day the heart is burning and the body grows in the same old age with all the steps.

sanskrit: kartavyaṃ kiṃ mayā kaṣṭaṃ paratretyatidāruṇam / apratīkārayogyaṃ hi vardhate vārdhake bhayam //
reference: Ah me! what must I do to remove my present and future pains? It is this fear which increases with old age, and finds no remedy.
baseline: What should I do after having suffered a lot. The fear in old age increases if I have not been able to do so.
morphology: What should I do if I have to suffer again. The fear increases in old age.

sanskrit: ko'haṃ varākaḥ kimiva karomi kathameva ca / tiṣṭhāmi maunameveti dīnatodeti vārdhake //
reference: What am I that am brought to this extremity of senselessness, what can I do in this state. I must remain dumb and silent. Under these reflections there is an increased sense of helplessness in old age.
baseline: Who is the bridegroom and what is the maidservant and what should I do. One who is silent and who gives charity to the old man should remain silent.
morphology: One who does not know who he is would say what he would do. He would remain silent and would give the poor man the gift of old age.

sanskrit: kathaṃ kadā me kimiva svādu syādbhojanaṃ janāt / ityajasraṃ jarā caiṣā ceto dahati vārdhake //
reference: How and when and what shall I eat, and what is sweet to taste? These are the thoughts which trouble the mind of one when old age comes upon him.
baseline: How many times should I know the taste taste food etc. One should burn these two jāra chaisas in the old age.
morphology: How many times should I know the taste taste food etc. One should burn the hair of the old man with the help of a cow.

sanskrit: gardho'bhyudeti sollāsamupabhoktuṃ na śakyate / hṛdayaṃ dahyate nūnaṃ śaktidausthyena vārdhake //
reference: There is an insatiable desire for enjoyments, but the powers to enjoy them are lacking. It is the want of strength which afflicts the heart in old age.
baseline: The heart is not able to be consumed by the garhdhu. The heart gets burnt by the saliva of the potency.
morphology: The heart is not able to be consumed by the garhdhu bhūyudhu sollas and sambhava. The heart gets burnt by the saliva and the potency.

sanskrit: jarājīrṇabakī yāvatkāyakleśāpakāriṇī / rauti rogoragākīrṇā kāyadrumaśiraḥsthitā //
reference: Hoary old age sits and shrieks as a heron on the top of the tree of this body, which is infested within it by the serpents of sickness.
baseline: The head of the kāyādrūma should be placed in the form of a dead body and the head of a sick person should be kept in the position of the head.
morphology: One who has fallen into the abyss one who has suffered from disease one whose head is fixed in the ground and another who has become ill one with a disease and one who is suffering from diseases is in the position of the head.

sanskrit: tāvadāgata evāśu kuto'pi paridṛśyate / ghanāndhyatimirākāṅkṣī mune maraṇakauśikaḥ //
reference: As the grave owl—the bird of night, appears unexpectedly to our sight soon as the evening shades cover the landscape, so does the solemn appearance of death overtake us in the eve of our life.
baseline: One who comes to that place and who is present in that place is seen as having the desire to die in the face of the darkness.
morphology: One who comes to that place would see a cow. One who has the desire to die in the middle of a thick cloud would get death.

sanskrit: sāyaṃsaṃdhyāṃ prajātāṃ vai tamaḥ samanudhāvati / jarāṃ vapuṣi dṛṣṭvaiva mṛtiḥ samanudhāvati //
reference: As darkness prevails over the world at the eve of the day, so doth death overtake the body at the eve of the life.
baseline: One should pay tribute to the king in the evening evening and evening. One should give tribute to death by seeing the jāra vāpuṣi.
morphology: One should pay tribute to the king in the evening evening and evening. One should give tribute to death by observing the jārāma and vapu.

sanskrit: jarākusumitaṃ dehadrumaṃ dṛṣṭvaiva dūrataḥ / adhyāpatati vegena mune maraṇamarkaṭaḥ //
reference: Death overtakes a man in his hoary old age, just as an ape alights on a tree covered with pearly flowers.
baseline: Having seen the image of the dead body in the distance one would be taught that death should be done in the forehead with speed.
morphology: Having seen the image of the body in the distance one would be taught that death should be done in the forehead with speed.

sanskrit: śūnyaṃ nagaramābhāti bhāti cchinnalato drumaḥ / bhātyanāvṛṣṭimāndeśo na jarājarjaraṃ vapuḥ //
reference: Even a deserted city, a leafless tree and parched up land may present a fair aspect, but never does the body look well that is pulled down by hoary age.
baseline: The city is said to be empty and the river to be chiseled. The river should not rain or rain and the land should not fall.
morphology: The city is said to be empty and the river to be chiselled out. The river should not rain on the land of the sister nor the river of the king.

sanskrit: kṣaṇānnigaraṇāyaiva kāsakvaṇitakāriṇī / gṛdhrīvāmiṣamādatte tarasaiva naraṃ jarā //
reference: Old age with its hooping cough lays hold on a man, just as a vulture seizes its prey with loud shrieks in order to devour it.
baseline: One who has made a sacrifice for the sake of the cause of the death of a man should offer a piece of water to the mother of the child.
morphology: One who does not want to be a cow one who has not been killed for a while and who has been killed by the enemy should be made to suffer from the disease of śākvaṇita.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvaiva sotsukevāśu pragṛhya śirasi kṣaṇam / pralunāti jarā dehaṃ kumārī kairavaṃ yathā //
reference: As a girl eagerly lays hold on a lotus flower whenever she meets with one, and then plucks it from its stalk and tears it to pieces, so does old age overtake the body of a person and break it down at last.
baseline: Having seen it one who has experienced the wrath of the Lord the head and the body of the virgins should be enlivened for a while.
morphology: Having seen it one would get the head for a while and the body would become a virgin.

sanskrit: sītkārakāriṇī pāṃsuparuṣā parijarjaram / śarīraṃ śātayatyeṣā vātyeva tarupallavam //
reference: As the chill blast of winter shakes a tree and covers its leaves with dust, so does old age seize the body with a tremor and fill all its limbs with the rust of diseases.
baseline: One who has done the practice of sitting should offer the pāśupārūśa garland puris pārījārjājara garland and vātī.
morphology: One who has done the act of sitting having the hands legs hands hands and feet and the body should be made to sit on the earth.

sanskrit: jarasopahato deho dhatte jarjaratāṃ gataḥ / tuṣāranikarākīrṇaparimlānāmbujaśriyam //
reference: The body overtaken by old age becomes as pale and battered, as a lotus flower beaten by frost becomes withered and shattered.
baseline: Having destroyed the body with the incense the body is destroyed by the destruction of the body. The temple of Parimlana and Amambu is made of snow and water.
morphology: Having destroyed the body with the incense the body is destroyed by the fire. The Śuśṇaka carcass is made of water and the temple of the goddess Amla is destroyed.

sanskrit: jarā jyotsnoditaiveyaṃ śiraḥśikharipṛṣṭhataḥ / vikāsayati saṃrabdhaṃ vātakāsakumudvatī //
reference: As moon-beams contribute to the growth of Kumuda flowers on the top of mountains, so does old age produce grey hairs resembling casla flowers on the heads of men.
baseline: The head should be raised from the base of the spire with the jāra jyotasnodita. The wind should be protected and the kumudvati should be placed on the top.
morphology: The head should be raised from the base of the spire with the jāra jyotasnodita.

sanskrit: paripakvaṃ samālokya jarākṣāravidhūsaram / śiraḥkūṣmāṇḍakaṃ bhuṅkte puṃsāṃ kālaḥ kileśvaraḥ //
reference: Death the lord of all beings, views the grey head of a man as a ripe pumpkin seasoned with the salt of old age, and devours it with zest.
baseline: Having attained maturity one should worship the sun the sun and the moon. One who has eaten the head and the trunk of the cow should worship Lord Kaṇla.
morphology: Having attained maturity one should worship the king of the king the king and the king.

sanskrit: jarājahnusutodyuktā mūlānyasya nikṛntati / śarīratīravṛkṣasya calatyāyuṣi satvaram //
reference: As the Ganges upsets a neighbouring tree by its rapid course, so does old age destroy the body, as the current of our life runs fast to decay.
baseline: The root of the tree is removed by the use of the jārājāna. The tree of the body is removed after having been moved for a long time.
morphology: The root of the tree is removed by the use of the jārājāna tree. The life of the plant is completed by the movement of the trees along the body.

sanskrit: jarāmārjārikā bhuṅkte yauvanākhuṃ tathoddhatā / paramullāsamāyāti śarīrāmiṣagardhinī //
reference: Old age which preys on the flesh of the human body, takes as much delight in devouring its youthful bloom as a cat does in feeding upon a mouse.
baseline: One who consumes the fire the fire and the fire of the young man one who has not lost his life one whose body is full of all goodness and one who is strong in the body becomes a man of great strength.
morphology: One who is hungry for food who is young and who is full of joy and who has not lost his body becomes weak and weak.

sanskrit: kācidasti jagatyasminnāmaṅgalakarī tathā / yathā jarākrośakarī dehajaṅgalajambukī //
reference: Decrepitude raises its ominous hoarse sound of hiccough in the body, as the jackal sends forth her hideous cry amidst the forest.
baseline: One who has made a jambukhi of the body should be called jāṅgala kārī.
morphology: One who has made a jaṅgala is called jāgatya. One who makes a jāṇgala jambukī is known as jārākrāśka jāmbukī jaṇgāla jāmbukī.

sanskrit: kāsaśvāsasasītkārā duḥkhadhūmatamomayī / jarājvālā jvalatyeṣā yasyāsau dagdha eva hi //
reference: Dotage as an inward flame consumes the living body as a wet log of wood, which thereupon emits its hissing sounds of hiccough and hard breathing, and sends up the gloomy fumes of woe and sighs.
baseline: One who is burnt by the fire who is suffering from sorrow who has suffered the loss of breath and who has been burned by the burning of the fire.
morphology: One who is burning with the fire who is suffering from the burning sensation of the fire and who has been burnt by the fire should be worshipped.

sanskrit: jarasā vakratāmeti śuklāvayavapallavā / tāta tanvī tanurnṛṇāṃ latā puṣpānatā yathā //
reference: The body like a flowering creeper, bends down under the pressure of age, turns to grey like the fading leaves of a plant, and becomes as lean and thin as a plant after its flowering time is over.
baseline: The jars are said to be curved. The leaves of the plants are called sukla vaipallava tanvi tāṇu nirna linga and flowers.
morphology: The jars are said to be curved. The leaves of the flowers are called sukla viva and pallava. Then they are called tāṇvī. The flowers of the creepers are called vaṇtā.

sanskrit: jarākarpūradhavalaṃ dehakarpūrapādapam / mune maraṇamātaṅgo nūnamuddharati kṣaṇāt //
reference: As the infuriate elephant upsets the white plantain tree in a moment, so does old age destroy the body that becomes as white as camphor all over.
baseline: The salutations of the sun water water and water should be offered to the body and the body. The salutation of the mother of death should be done in the morning.
morphology: One who has made a sacrifice for the sake of the body one who has left the body and the mother of death would get peace from the moment of death.

sanskrit: maraṇasya mune rājño jarādhavalacāmarā / āgacchato'gre niryāti svādhivyādhipatākinī //
reference: Senility, O sage! is as the standard bearer of the king of death, flapping his chowry of grey hairs before him, and bringing in his train an army of diseases and troubles.
baseline: The king should be killed by the chariot of the king the king of the jāradhavala clan the queen of the ruler of the kingdom should be sent to the king.
morphology: The king should be killed in the morning by the king the king of jāradhavala and the chāmara of the king.

sanskrit: na jitāḥ śatrubhiḥ saṃkhye praviṣṭā ye'drikoṭare / te jarājīrṇarākṣasyā paśyāśu vijitā mune //
reference: The monster of old age, will even overcome those that were never defeated in wars by their enemies, and those that hide themselves in the inaccessible caverns of mountains.
baseline: Those who enter the fort in numbers with their enemies and do not get victory. Those who are defeated by a rakshasa and their cattle are victorious.
morphology: Those who enter the city in numbers with their enemies and do not get victory. Those who are defeated by the animals of the rakshasas who are in danger of getting destroyed.

sanskrit: jarātuṣāravalite śarīrasadanāntare / śaknuvantyakṣaśiśavaḥ spandituṃ na manāgapi //
reference: As infants cannot play in a room that has become cold with snow, so the senses can have no play in the body that is stricken with age.
baseline: One who does not want to beat the children would be able to do so even if they do not wish to.
morphology: One who has not been able to beat the children would not be able to do so.

sanskrit: daṇḍatṛtīyapādena praskhalantī muhurmuhuḥ / kāsādhovāyumurajā jarā yoṣitpranṛtyati //
reference: Old age like a juggling girl, struts on three legs at the sound of coughing and whiffing, beating as a tymbal on both sides.
baseline: The king of Kaśādhu Vāyūmūrja and the king of Jāra are worshipped with the third leg of the rosary.
morphology: The king of Kaśādhu the wind the king of jāra and the queen of the womb are worshipped by the muhurmuhū who is the third leg of the punishment.

sanskrit: saṃsārasaṃsṛterasyā gandhakuṭyāṃ śirogatā / dehayaṣṭyāṃ jarānāmnī cāmaraśrīrvirājate //
reference: The tuft of grey hairs on the head of the aged body, represents a white flapper (chowry) fastened to the top of a handle of white sandal wood, to welcome the despot of death.
baseline: One who is born with the samsara srītā gāndhaka kuta sirogata jārāmana jarā and sāmarā srijā is the king.
morphology: One who has made a gift of samsara srītā gāndhaka sirogata jārāma sriṣrī rājā is the king of the chāmaras.

sanskrit: jarācandrodayasite śarīranagare sthite / kṣaṇādvikāsamāyāti mune maraṇakairavam //
reference: As hoary age makes his advance like moon-light on the site of the body, he calls forth the hidden death to come out of it, as the moon-light makes the nilumbium to unfold its buds.
baseline: One who is born with the zara chandrūda and who is in the city of the body for a while and who dies in the forehead.
morphology: One who is in the city of the body on the day of the rising of the zara chandrūda becomes the king of death in two periods.

sanskrit: jarāsudhālepasite śarīrāntaḥpurāntare / aśaktirārtirāpacca tiṣṭhanti sukhamaṅganāḥ //
reference: Again as the white wash of old age whitens the outer body, so debility, diseases and dangers become its inmates in the inner typo apartment.
baseline: One who has not been able to bear the loss of his body would be left in the heart and the other side of the body.
morphology: If the body is broken and the heart is broken then the body should be kept in a state of bliss.

sanskrit: abhāvo'gresarī yatra jarā jayati jantuṣu / kastatreha samāśvāso mama mandamatermune //
reference: It is the extinction of being that is preceded by old age; therefore I as a man of little understanding, can have no reliance in old age (though extolled by some){GL_NOTE:73106:}
baseline: Where there is a lack of water the king of the earth conquers the animals the goddess of the musk the mother of all beings and the goddess samshvāśa in front of me is slow.
morphology: Where there is a lack of water there is victory in the battle of the animals. One who has the strength of the musk one who has peace in front of me and my mother is weak.

sanskrit: kiṃ tena durjīvitadurgraheṇa jarāgatenāpi hi jīvyate yat / jarājagatyāmajitā janānāṃ sarvaiṣaṇāstāta tiraskaroti //
reference: What then is the good of this miserable life, which lives under the subjection of old age? Senility is irresistable in this world, and defies all efforts to avoid or overcome it.
baseline: One who does not live with the fortification of a city that is not alive by it would live without it. He would reject all the people who have been conquered by the king.
morphology: One who does not live by it would get destroyed by the destruction of the fort. He would not get rid of all the people living by it.

sanskrit: śrīrāma uvāca / vikalpakalpanānalpajalpitairalpabuddhibhiḥ / bhedairuddhuratāṃ nītaḥ saṃsārakuhare bhramaḥ //
reference: Men of little understandings are found to fall into grave errors in this pit of the world, by their much idle talk, ever doubting scepticism, and schisms.
baseline: O Śrīma one who invents a choice a choice and a choice should be made by the wise. One who does not want to be divided should take the illusion into the world.
morphology: O Śrīma one who invents a choice a choice and a choice should be made with less knowledge. One who does not want to be divided should go into the world.

sanskrit: satāṃ kathamivāstheha jāyate jālapañjare / bālā evāttumicchanti phalaṃ mukurabimbitam //
reference: Good people can have no more confidence in the net work of their ribs, than little children may have a liking for fruits reflected in a mirror.
baseline: The children want the fruit of the tree to be placed in the net.
morphology: The children want the fruit of the tree to be placed in the net.

sanskrit: ihāpi vidyate yeṣāṃ pelavā sukhabhāvanā / ākhustantumivāśeṣaṃ kālastāmapi kṛntati //
reference: Time is a rat that cuts off the threads of all thoughts (prospects), which men may entertain here about the contemptible pleasures of this world.
baseline: These are also those who enjoy the feeling of happiness. The cane that is left behind in the past also consumes it.
morphology: These are the things which give pleasure and enjoyment. They also give pleasure to the rest of time.

sanskrit: na tadastīha yadayaṃ kālaḥ sakalaghasmaraḥ / grasate tajjagajjātaṃ protthābdhimiva vāḍavaḥ //
reference: There is nothing in this world which the all-devouring time will spare. He devours all things as the submarine fire consumes the over-flowing sea.
baseline: If one does not do so then one would get all the things that are required for him. If he does not get the same amount of water then he would get more water.
morphology: If one does not do so then one would get all the diseases. One would get more diseases.

sanskrit: samastasāmānyatayā bhīmaḥ kālo maheśvaraḥ / dṛśyasattāmimāṃ sarvāṃ kavalīkartumudyataḥ //
reference: Time is the sovran lord of all, and equally terrible to all things. He is ever ready to devour all visible beings.
baseline: One who has done all the things that are seen in the form of Bhima Mahesvara Kaṇu Kaalaka Maśvara and others should do the same.
morphology: One who has done all the usual things one who is black and has seen all the things and one who has made all the kavālikas should be worshipped.

sanskrit: mahatāmapi no devaḥ pratipālayati kṣaṇam / kālaḥ kavalitānantaviśvo viśvātmatāṃ gataḥ //
reference: Time as master of all, spares not even the greatest of us for a moment. He swallows the universe within himself, whence he is known as the universal soul.
baseline: The great god does not maintain the moment. The time of the twisted universe is gone.
morphology: The great god does not maintain the time for a while. The time of the twisted and the eternal universe has gone to the world.

sanskrit: yugavatsarakalpākhyaiḥ kiṃcitprakaṭatāṃ gataḥ / rūpairalakṣyarūpātmā sarvamākramya tiṣṭhati //
reference: Time pervades all things, but has no perceptible feature of his own, except that he is imperfectly known by the names of years, ages and kalpas.
baseline: A little manifestation has been made by the preceptors of the ages years and years. The form form and spirit remain in all forms.
morphology: The form of the soul should be kept in all its forms. The manifestation of the form should be a little more than the description of the years and years.

sanskrit: ye ramyā ye śubhārambhāḥ sumeruguravo'pi ye / kālena vinigīrṇāste garuḍeneva pannagāḥ //
reference: All that was fair and good, and as great as the mount of Meru, have gone down in the womb of eternity, as the snakes are gorged by the greedy Garuda.
baseline: Those rāmya the beginning of the sun those who are born in the summer and those who have been destroyed by the seasons the garudena and the pāṇagāga are the two things.
morphology: Those rāmya the beginning the end and those of Sumerugura who have been destroyed by time the garudena and the pāṇagas.

sanskrit: nirdayaḥ kaṭhinaḥ krūraḥ karkaśaḥ kṛpaṇo'dhamaḥ / na tadasti yadadyāpi na kālo nigiratyayam //
reference: There was no one ever so unkind, hard-hearted, cruel, harsh or miserly, whom time has not devoured.
baseline: One who does not have the strength and the strength of the body one who is harsh one with the heart and one who has the grace is not a black person.
morphology: One who does not have the strength and hardness one who is harsh and has the heart and the heart of a man does not get the grace. One who is not black will not get it.

sanskrit: kālaḥ kavalanaikāntamatiratti girannapi / anantairapi lokaughairnāyaṃ tṛpto mahāśanaḥ //
reference: Time is ever greedy although he should devour the mountains. This great gourmand is not satiated with gorging every thing in all the worlds.
baseline: One who is satisfied with the creation of the world even at the end of the clock and at the height of the mountain is also a great man.
morphology: One who is satisfied with the creation of the world even at the end of the sky and at the same time at the time of the wind should be made to climb the mountain of eternity.

sanskrit: haratyayaṃ nāśayati karotyatti nihanti ca / kālaḥ saṃsāranṛttaṃ hi nānārūpaṃ yathā naṭaḥ //
reference: Time like an actor plays many parts on the stage of the world. He abstracts and kills, produces and devours and at last destroys every thing.
baseline: One who destroys the harātya one who kills the kāratya and one who does not destroy the samsara one is a knower of all forms.
morphology: One who destroys or destroys the harātya one who kills the kāla samsara nrita etc. is a player in many forms.

sanskrit: bhinatti pravibhāgasthabhūtabījānyanāratam / jagatyasattayā bandhāddāḍimāni yathā śukaḥ //
reference: Time is incessantly picking up the seeds of all the four kinds of living beings from this unreal world, as a parrot picks up the seeds from under the cracked shell of a pomegranate.
baseline: One who has been born with the seeds of the earth and is living in the inner part of the world should be bound with the elements of the universe such as boar.
morphology: One who has been born with the seeds of the earth and is living in the inner part of the world should be bound with the elements of the universe.

sanskrit: śubhāśubhaviṣāṇāgravilūnajanapallavaḥ / sphūrjati sphītajanatājīvarājīvanīgajaḥ //
reference: Time like a wild elephant uproots all proud living beings in this world, as the other pulls up the trees of the forest with their tusks.
baseline: O lord of good good poisonous evil evil and evil one who is born alive and who is living and living should be blessed by the sun.
morphology: O lord of the earth the sun of the world the sky of the living beings the waters of the universe the air of life the water of life and the earth.

sanskrit: viriñcimūlabrahmāṇḍabṛhaddevaphaladrumam / brahmakānanamābhogi paramāvṛtya tiṣṭhati //
reference: This creation of God is like a forest, having Brahma for its foundation and its trees full of the great fruits of gods. Time commands it throughout its length and breadth.
baseline: One who consumes the fruits of the gods by the Brahmana kāṇa is supreme.
morphology: One who consumes the fruits of the gods with the brahmakaṇas would be supreme.

sanskrit: yāminī bhramarāpūrṇā racayandinamañjarīḥ / varṣakalpakalāvallīrna kadācana khidyate //
reference: Time glides along incessantly as a creeping plant, composed of years and ages as its parts, and the sable nights as black bees chasing after them.
baseline: One would sometimes draw a garland of water with the garlands of the rainbow and the kalavallis.
morphology: One would sometimes draw the garlands of yāmīna bhavrāra purṇa garland garlands rainbow kalavallis etc.

sanskrit: bhidyate nāvabhagno'pi dagdho'pi hi na dahyate / dṛśyate nāpi dṛśyo'pi dhūrtacūḍāmaṇirmune //
reference: Time, O sage, is the subtlest of all things. It is divided though indivisible, it is consumed though incombustible, it is perceived though imperceptible in its nature.
baseline: If it is destroyed it is not burnt in the fire. It is not seen in the sight and in the face of the rascal.
morphology: If it is broken then it is not burnt even in the case of a shipwreck or a firearm. It is neither seen nor seen in the sight of a rascal.

sanskrit: ekenaiva nimeṣeṇa kiṃcidutthāpayatyalam / kiṃcidvināśayatyuccairmanorājyavadātataḥ //
reference: Time like the mind is strong enough to create and demolish any thing in a trice, and its province is equally extensive with it.
baseline: One should rise a few times in a minute. One should not fall into the darkness. One who gives the kingdom to the king should be destroyed a few days later.
morphology: One should rise a few times in a minute and give the king a king a king and a king.

sanskrit: durvilāsavilāsinyā ceṣṭayā kaṣṭaṣuṣṭayā / dravyaikarūpakṛdrūpaṃ janamāvartayansthitaḥ //
reference: Time is a whirlpool to men; and being accompanied with desire his insatiable and ungovernable mistress and delighting in illicit enjoyments, he makes them do and undo the same thing over and over again.
baseline: One who has made a return to the form of wealth wealth grace wealth and prosperity with the efforts of others would be able to do so.
morphology: One who has made a return to the form of wealth wealth krudra wealth and wealth would get success by making efforts for the sake of the welfare of the poor.

sanskrit: tṛṇaṃ pāṃsuṃ mahendraṃ ca sumeruṃ parṇamarṇavam / ātmaṃbharitayā sarvamātmasātkartumudyataḥ //
reference: Time is prompted by his rapacity to appropriate every thing to himself, from the meanest straw, dust, leaves and worms, to the greatest Indra and the mount Meru itself.
baseline: One should make all the objects of the soul sound with the leaves leaves flowers leaves and colours of grass pāṇa mahendra sumeru atmanbhrītā.
morphology: One should make all the objects of the soul sound with the leaves leaves flowers leaves and colours.

sanskrit: krauryamatraiva paryāptaṃ lubdhatātraiva saṃsthitā / sarvadaurbhāgyamatraiva cāpalaṃ vāpi duḥsaham //
reference: Time is the source of all malice and greediness, and the spring of all misfortunes, and intolerable fluctuations of our states.
baseline: One who has plundered enough for the purpose of committing a crime would get away with all misfortune. One would get a flatterment and suffer misery.
morphology: One who has plundered enough for the purpose of committing a crime would get away with all misfortune.

sanskrit: preraya~llīlayārkendū krīḍatīva nabhastale / nikṣiptalīlāyugalo nije bāla ivāṅgaṇe //
reference: As boys with their balls play about their play-ground, so does time in his arena of the sky, play with his two balls of the sun and moon.
baseline: One who plays with the lily in the open ground one who is not attracted by the lilies and the other who is thrown into the open field one should play with the ball in the court.
morphology: One who plays with the lily of the propitiation in the open ground one who is cast into the field of the child one should play with it.

sanskrit: sarvabhūtāsthimālābhirāpādavalitākṛtiḥ / vilasatyeva kalpānte kālaḥ kalitakalpanaḥ //
reference: Time at the expiration of the kalpa age, will dance about with a long chain of the bones of the dead hanging from his neck to the feet.
baseline: One who has made a plan for the construction of a temple should have all the elements of the body the elements the objects of the earth the things of the world the time of the Kalpāṇta and the art of art.
morphology: One who has got all the elements the bones the hair and the hair of the body the elixir of the mind the time of the illusion the Kalātā kalpaṇa.

sanskrit: asyoḍḍāmaravṛttasya kalpānte'ṅgavinirgataiḥ / prasphuratyambare merurbhūrjatvagiva vāyubhiḥ //
reference: The gale of desolation rising from the body of this desolator of the world at the end of a kalpa age, causes the fragments of mount Meru to fly about in the air like the rinds of the bhoja-petera tree.
baseline: One would get a circle of water with the elements of the forehead and the forearms and the air with the spire and the earth at the end.
morphology: One would get a circle of water with the elements of the forehead and the forearms and the air with the spire and the earth at the end of the movement.

sanskrit: rudro bhūtvā bhavatyeṣa mahendro'tha pitāmahaḥ / śakro vaiśravaṇaścāpi punareva na kiṃcana //
reference: Time then assumes his terrific form of fire ([Sanskrit: pralayagni]), to dissolve the world in empty space, when the gods Brahma and Indra and all others cease to exist.
baseline: Having become Rudra one should not repeat the words of Mahendra the great grandfather śakra Vaisarvana etc..
morphology: Having become Rudra one should not repeat the words of Mahendra the great grandfather śakra Vaisarvana etc..

sanskrit: dhatte'jasrotthitoddhvastānsargānamitabhāsvarān / anyāndadhaddivānaktaṃ vīcīrabdhirivātmani //
reference: As the sea shows himself in a continued series of waves rising and falling one after another, so it is time that creates and dissolves the world, and appears to rise and fall in the rotation of days and nights.
baseline: One should worship the gods of the earth and the other gods the gods gods and spirits.
morphology: One should worship the gods of the earth and the other gods the gods gods spirits and spirits.

sanskrit: mahākalpābhidhānebhyo vṛkṣebhyaḥ pariśātayan / devāsuragaṇānpakvānphalabhārāniva sthitaḥ //
reference: Time plucks the gods and demigods as ripe fruits, from their great arbor of existence, at the end of the world,
baseline: Having worshipped the gods gods and other beings in the form of a tree one would get good fruits and other things.
morphology: Having worshipped the gods gods tribes gods and goddesses in the form of a tree one would get the fruits and other things.

sanskrit: kālo'yaṃ bhūtamaśakaghuṃghumānāṃ prapātinām / brahmāṇḍodumbaraughānāṃ bṛhatpādapatāṃ gataḥ //
reference: Time resembles a large fig tree (Ficus religiosa), studded with all the worlds as its fruits, and resonant with the noise of living beings like the hissing of gnats about them.
baseline: The time has now passed for the creation of the universe the great gods the gods and the mountains the earth the clouds the mountains and the rivers.
morphology: The time has now passed for the creation of the universe the great gods the gods and the mountains the earth the clouds the mountains and the mountain.

sanskrit: sattāmātrakumudvatyā cijjyotsnāpariphullayā / vapurvinodayatyekaṃ kriyāpriyatamānvitaḥ //
reference: Time accompanied by Action as his mate, regales himself in the garden of the world, blossoming with the moon-beams of the Divine Spirit.
baseline: One should worship the goddess with the prasadamāla kumudvatya in the form of a lotus. One should perform a particular act of worship.
morphology: One should worship the goddess with the prasadamāla kumudvatya in the form of a lotus. One should perform a particular act of worship and enjoyment.

sanskrit: anantāpāraparyantabaddhapīṭhaṃ nijaṃ vapuḥ / mahāśailavaduttuṅgamavalambya vyavasthitaḥ //
reference: As the high and huge rock supports its body upon the basis of the earth, so does time rest itself in endless and interminable eternity.
baseline: The seat should be fixed up to the point of infinity. One should be seated on the seat of the great celestial body with two limbs.
morphology: The seat should be fixed till the point of infinity. The seat is fixed on the great rock and the other parts of the body.

sanskrit: kvacicchayāmatamaḥśyāmaṃ kvacitkāntiyutaṃ tatam / dvayenāpi kvacidriktaṃ svabhāvaṃ bhāvayan sthitaḥ //
reference: Time assumes to himself various hues of black, white and red (at night, day and midday) which serve for his vestures.
baseline: One who wishes to do so would be in a position to be alone. One who does not want to do it would be left alone. The other would be sitting in a place with a nature that does not differ.
morphology: One who wishes to do so would be in a state of extreme darkness. One would be left with the nature of nothingness in the two states.

sanskrit: saṃlīnāsaṃkhyasaṃsārasārayā svātmasattayā / urvyeva bhāraghanayā nibaddhapadatāṃ gataḥ //
reference: As the earth is the great support of hills which are fixed upon it, so is time the support of all the innumerable ponderous worlds that constitute the universe.
baseline: One would get the status of a bound by the collection of the number of things and the sum total of all things and by the possession of ones own self.
morphology: One would attain the status of a knower by the sumptuous number of the members of the body and by the sublimation of the self.

sanskrit: na khidyate nādriyate nāyāti na ca gacchati / nāstameti na codeti mahākalpaśatairapi //
reference: Hundreds of great kalpa ages (of the creation and dissolution of the world) may pass away, yet there is nothing that can move eternity to pity or concern, or stop or expedite his course. It neither sets nor rises.
baseline: One who does not eat does not drink and does not sleep does Nāyaṇa go away and never frowns even after having had a hundred days.
morphology: One who does not eat does not drink and does not sleep does neither eat nor frowns even if he has a great penis.

sanskrit: kevalaṃ jagadārambhalīlayā ghanahelayā / pālayatyātmanātmānamanahaṃkāramātatam //
reference: Time is never proud to think, that it is he who without the least sense of pain and labor, brings this world into play and makes it to exist.
baseline: One should worship the Lord with the garland of jagadar and garland with a lotus. One should observe the mind with the spirit.
morphology: One should worship the Lord of the earth with the lilies of the jagadarambhāla and with the garlands of the ghee. One should be proud of the spirit.

sanskrit: yāminīpaṅkakalitāṃ dinakokanadāvalīm / meghabhramarikāmātmasarasyāropayansthitaḥ //
reference: Time is like a reservoir in which the nights are as mud, the days as lotuses, and the clouds as bees.
baseline: One who has made a journey of clouds and the incarnations of the spirit is placed in the temple of the sun.
morphology: One who has made a journey of the clouds and the sun is placed in the temple of the goddess Yāmīṇī Pāṇaka and Kaṇaka in the day.

sanskrit: gṛhītvā kṛpaṇaḥ kṛṣṇāṃ rajanīṃ jīrṇamārjanīm / ālokakanakakṣodānāharatyabhito girim //
reference: As a covetous man, with worn out broom sticks in hand, sweeps over a mountain to gather the particles of gold strewn over it, so does time with his sweeping course of days and nights, collect in one mass of the dead all living beings in the world.
baseline: Having taken the king of Kṛṣṇa the king should be made to suffer the loss of the king. Having taken away the image of the goddess of light the mountain should be taken away.
morphology: The king should be taken away and the king should pay tribute to the departed lord krsna. He should be given the gift of the goddess of light and the goddess Giri.

sanskrit: saṃcārayankriyāṅgulyā koṇakeṣvarkadīpikām / jagatsadmani kārpaṇyātkva kimastīti vīkṣate //
reference: As a miserly man trims and lights a lamp with his own fingers, to look into his stores at each corner of the room; so does time light the lamps of the sun and moon to look into the living beings in every nook and corner of the world.
baseline: One sees what happens when the celestial objects are placed in the corners of the earth by moving the fingers of action.
morphology: One can see what happens by moving the spheres of action in the corners of the earth.

sanskrit: prekṣyāharvinimeṣeṇa sūryākṣṇā pākavantyalam / lokapālaphalānyatti jagajjīrṇavanādayam //
reference: As one ripens the raw fruits in sun and fire in order to devour them, so does time ripen men by their sun and fire worship, to bring them under his jaws at last.
baseline: Having worshipped the sun the sun and the sky should be worshipped. The ombudsman should be blessed with fruits and the world should be made alive.
morphology: One should worship the sun with the sun the sun and the sun in the morning and make the lokpal fruitful. One should offer the jagjirnava.

sanskrit: jagajjīrṇakuṭīkīrṇānarpayatyugrakoṭare / krameṇa guṇavallokamaṇīnmṛtyusamudgake //
reference: The world is a dilapidated cottage and men of parts are rare gems in it. Time hides them in the casket of his belly, as a miser keeps his treasure in a coffer.
baseline: One should offer the jagajīrāna kutikīrna in the temple of the god Gārga gradually and the meritorious one should be killed by the death of the lord.
morphology: One should offer the jagajīrāna kutikīrna in the temple of the god Gārga. One should gradually get the qualities of the world. One would get the death of the king.

sanskrit: guṇairāpūryate yaiva lokaratnāvalī bhṛśam / bhūṣārthamiva tāmaṅge kṛtvā bhūyo nikṛntati //
reference: Good men are like a chaplet of gems, which time puts on his head for a time with fondness, and then tears and tramples it down.
baseline: The image of the earth is made like the image of a jewel and the image is made of the same colour as that of a cow. The image is said to be of the nature of the world.
morphology: One who consumes a lotus a pearl or a piece of water and makes it like a jewel and brings it to the ground would get rid of it.

sanskrit: dinahaṃsānusṛtayā niśendīvaramālayā / tārakesarayājasraṃ capalo valayatyalam //
reference: Strings of days, nights and stars, resembling beads and bracelets of white and black lotuses, are continually turning round the arm of time.
baseline: One should worship the king of the stars with the garland of the goddess Nishendivārā with the rosary of the elephant dīnhāṇa the chariot and the ring.
morphology: One should worship the king of the stars with the garland of Śeṣendivar with the rosary of the elephant of the day the chariot of the king and the ring of the earth.

sanskrit: śailārṇadyudharāśṛṅgajagadūrṇāyusaunikaḥ / pratyahaṃ pibate prekṣya tārāraktakaṇānapi //
reference: Time (as a vulture) looks upon the world as (the carcase of) a ram, with its mountains, seas, sky and earth as its four horns, and the stars as its drops of blood which it drinks day by day.
baseline: One who drinks water containing the elements of the form of stone iron water gold jagga gurna yuśaṇik star blood etc. should also drink water after having seen them.
morphology: One who drinks water containing the elements of the form of the star red and red should drink water with the syllable śila nārna yudhra śrīṅga jāgudvara yuśaṇikā.

sanskrit: tāruṇyanalinīsoma āyurmātaṅgakesarī / na tadasti na yasyāyaṃ tucchātucchasya taskaraḥ //
reference: Time destroys youth as the moon shuts the petals of the lotus. It destroys life as the lion kills the elephant: there is nothing however insignificant that time steals not away.
baseline: The thief of a thief is not the one who has not had a good life.
morphology: One who does not have the right to enjoy the life of a young man or the body of a man or his mother would not be a thief.

sanskrit: kalpakelivilāsena piṣṭapātitajantunā / abhāvo bhāvabhāsena ramate svātmanātmani //
reference: Time after sporting for a Kalpa period in the act of killing and crushing of all living beings, comes to lose its own existence and becomes extinct in the eternity of the Spirit of spirits.
baseline: One who has not experienced the absence of animals and animals falling on the ground with the illusion of kalpa keli vilasa is pleased with the feeling of self.
morphology: One who has not experienced the absence of animals and animals falling on the ground with the illusion of kalpa keli vilasa is pleased with the feeling of self.

sanskrit: kartā bhoktātha saṃhartā smartā sarvapadaṃ gataḥ //
reference: Time after a short rest and respite reappears as the creator, preserver, destroyer and remembrancer of all. He shows the shapes of all things whether good or bad, keeping his own nature beyond the knowledge of all. Thus doth time expand and preserve and finally dissolve all things by way of sport.
baseline: The doer who consumes food and then kills the doer should be remembered.
morphology: One who kills a doer a person who consumes food and then remembers all the deeds has passed away.

sanskrit: sakalamapyakalākalitāntaraṃ subhagadurbhagarūpadharaṃ vapuḥ / prakaṭayansahasaiva ca gopayan vilasatīha hi kālabalaṃ nṛṣu //
reference: ?missing text?
baseline: O Vāpu one who has made the manifestations of the manifest form of good evil evil and evil in the form of all the elements of the universe and who has hidden the illusion of the power of blackness and blackness in the eyes of the people.
morphology: Having covered the earth with all the elements of art one should worship the gods of good and evil manifest and manifest in the form of the gods and keep the forces of blackness and blackness in his hands.

sanskrit: śrīrāma uvāca / asyoḍḍāmaralīlasya dūrāstasakalāpadaḥ / saṃsāre rājaputrasya kālasyākalitaujasaḥ //
reference: Rama rejoined:—Time is a self-willed sportsman as a prince, who is inaccessible to dangers and whose powers are unlimited.
baseline: O Śrīma the king of the king the son of a king should be removed from his position.
morphology: O Śrīma the king of the king the son of a king should be given the position of a prince in the world.

sanskrit: asyaivācarato dīnairmugdhairbhūtamṛgabrajaiḥ / ākheṭakaṃ jarjarite jagajjaṅgalajālake //
reference: This world is as it were a forest and sporting ground of time, wherein the poor deluded worldlings are caught in his snare like bodies of wounded stags.
baseline: One who has not been worshipped by the gods of the earth and the wild animals should be worshipped in the same manner. One who is a hunter should be destroyed in the world.
morphology: One who has not been worshipped by the gods of the earth and the wild animals would be destroyed by the evil forces of the king.

sanskrit: ekadeśollasaccāruvaḍavānalapaṅkajā / krīḍāpuṣkariṇī ramyā kalpakālamahārṇavaḥ //
reference: The ocean of universal deluge is a pleasure-pond of time, and the submarine fires bursting therein as lotus flowers.
baseline: The king of Kalpakaala is known to be the ones own country ones son cow wilderness water water and water.
morphology: Oka ḍesvāla Śaṇuva Vādaṇa Nāla and Pākāja Rāmya Puskarīna Kalpakaala Mahārna etc.

sanskrit: kaṭutiktāmlabhūtādyaiḥ sadadhikṣīrasāgaraiḥ / taireva taiḥ paryuṣitairjagadbhiḥ kalvavartanam //
reference: Time makes his breakfast of this vapid and stale earth, flavoured with the milk and curd of the seas of those names.
baseline: One should worship the gods of the earth by making them abound with the fruits of the sea water water and salt.
morphology: One should worship the gods of Kalvārttara by making offerings made with the spices of katuti malabhuta sāgarā sardhikhira sagarā tāirā and other sacred things.

sanskrit: caṇḍī caturasaṃcārā sarvamātṛgaṇānvitā / saṃsāravanavinyastā vyāghrī bhūtaughaghātinī //
reference: His wife Chandi (Hecate) with her train of Matris (furies), ranges all about this wide world as a ferocious tigress.
baseline: The king of the world should be worshipped with the chariot square mātri gāna sambara vāṇavana vighrī bhūtu and ghāgha.
morphology: The king of the world is known to be a coward a cowherd a ghost and a murderer.

sanskrit: jñadhvī karatale jñathvī pānapātrī rasānvitā / kamalotpalakahlāralolajālakamālitā //
