reference: The earth with her waters is like a bowl of wine in the hand of time, dressed and flavoured with all sorts of lilies and lotuses.
baseline: One who knows the kāṇḍhī should know the palm of the pot of water and drink the juice of the lotus. One who has knowledge of the water should know that it is a lotus a lotuses ants aphrodisiacs a nettle a linga a malika.
morphology: One who knows the kāṇḍhī should know the palms of water one who drinks water and drinks water. One who has knowledge of the lotus leaves and the waters of water should be known as jalakāla.

sanskrit: virāvī vikaṭāsphoṭo nṛsiṃho bhujapañjare / saṭāvikaṭapīnāṃsaḥ kṛtaḥ krīḍāśakuntakaḥ //
reference: The lion with his huge body and startling mane, his loud roaring and tremendous groans, seems as a caged bird of sport in the hand of time.
baseline: One who has made a sacrifice of a viravi vikātasphotu nrīsimha bhujapanjara sattavikatapina krida sakuntaka is made to be able to play.
morphology: One who is a viravi a virgin a mighty lion a lion an elephant a horse a bull a krida akuntaka a king made of seven pieces of water is said to be the best.

sanskrit: alābuvīṇāmadhuraḥ śaradvyomalasacchaviḥ / devaḥ kila mahākālo līlākokilabālakaḥ //
reference: The Mahakala like a playful young Kokila (cuckoo), appears in the figure of the blue autumnal sky, and warbling as sweet as the notes of a lute of gourd.
baseline: One who is blessed with alavuṇī amudhra sardvya malasa chāvī deva kila mahākala lila kokila boy etc.
morphology: One who is blessed with alaubuvi amudhra sardvya malasa chāvī deva kila mahākala lila kokila boy etc.

sanskrit: ajasrasphūrjitākāro vāntaduḥkhaśarāvaliḥ / abhāvanāmakodaṇḍaḥ parisphurati sarvataḥ //
reference: The restless bow of death is found flinging its woeful arrows (darts of death) with ceaseless thunder claps on all sides.
baseline: One who has made a lot of stones one who has not had the strength of the earth and one who does not have the power of the enemy is bound to be destroyed everywhere.
morphology: One who has created a lotus one who has made a lot of excrement and one who is suffering from the disease of āvirāṇam one whose stick is not in danger of being destroyed is always in danger.

sanskrit: anuttamastvadhikavilāsapaṇḍito bhramaccalanparivilasanvidārayan / jarajjagajjanitavilolamarkaṭaḥ parisphuradvapuriha kāla īhate //
reference: This world is like a forest, wherein sorrows are ranging about as playful apes, and time like a sportive prince in this forest, is now roving, now walking, now playing and now killing his game.
baseline: One who wanders around in the midst of a great multitude of delights would get a lot of pleasure. One who has not been able to do so would get rid of the illusion of the enemy. One would get time.
morphology: Having wandered about in the midst of the great multitude of delights of you one would find that the time of wanderings would be better for you.

sanskrit: śrīrāma uvāca atraiva durvilāsānāṃ cūḍamaṇirihāparaḥ / karotyattīti loke'smindaivaṃ kālaśca kathyate //
reference: Time stands the foremost of all deceitful players in this world. He acts the double parts of creation and destruction, and of action and fate.
baseline: It is said that Lord Śrīma would make the illusions here and would make a lotus flower here. It would be called the end of time.
morphology: It is said that Lord Śrīma would make a sacrifice here and the people would make it. It is also called the time.

sanskrit: kriyāmātrādṛte yasya svaparispandarūpiṇaḥ / nānyadālakṣyate rūpaṃ na karma na samīhitam //
reference: Time has no other character but those of action and motion by which his existence is known to us, and which bind all beings.
baseline: One who has not been given the form of his own self should be treated as if he has not done any work.
morphology: One who has the form of his own self and has the appearance of the other forms should not do any work.

sanskrit: teneyamakhilā bhūtasaṃtatiḥ paripelavā / tāpena himamāleva nītā vidhuratāṃ bhṛśam //
reference: Fate is that which frustrates (the necessary consequences of) the acts of all created beings, as the solar heat serves to dissolve the conglomeration of snows.
baseline: Then one should worship the spirits of the devils. One should treat the widows with heat and bring them to the mountain of snow.
morphology: Then one should worship the children of the spirits of the gods. One should take away the widow who has been taken away by the heat from the mountains of snow.

sanskrit: yadidaṃ dṛśyate kiṃcijjagadābhogi maṇḍalam / tattasya nartanāgāramihāsāvatinṛtyati //
reference: This wide world is the stage wherein the giddy mob dance about.
baseline: If one sees the temple of the god of water one will get to dance in the palace of the king.
morphology: If one sees the temple of the god of the gods one would dance to the dance of the king.

sanskrit: tṛtīyaṃ ca kṛtānteti nāma bibhratsudāruṇam / kāpālikavapurmattaṃ daivaṃ jagati nṛtyati //
reference: Time has a third name of a terrifying nature known as Kritantah (Fate), who in the form of a Kapalika (one holding human skulls in his hand), dances about in the world.
baseline: The third one is called the final one. The name is confused the name is bad the god is the one who performs the dance of the world.
morphology: The third one is called the final one. The name is confused the name is bad the god of the world is dancing in the form of the kāpālikā.

sanskrit: nṛtyato hi kṛtāntasya nitāntamiva rāgiṇaḥ / nityaṃ niyatikāntāyāṃ mune paramakāmitā //
reference: This dancing and loving Kritantah (Fate), is accompanied by his consort called Destiny to whom he is greatly attached.
baseline: One who performs a dance should always be in the final position of the raga. One who does this is always in the perpetual position at the end of the cycle.
morphology: One who performs a dance should always be in the final position of the ragins. One who is always in the eternal position should always perform the mune.

sanskrit: śeṣaḥ śaśikalāśubhro gaṅgāvāhaśca tau tridhā / upavīte avīte ca ubhau saṃsāravakṣasi //
reference: Time (as Siva), wears on his bosom of the world, the triplicate white and holy thread composed of the serpent named Ananta and the stream of Ganges, and the digit of the moon on his forehead.
baseline: The remaining three are the Śaśikalāśuśva and the Gāṅgavāha rivers. Both are seated on the ground and are the manifestations of the universe.
morphology: The remaining three are the Śaśikalāśuśva and the Gaṇgava vahas. Both are seated on the ground and are the manifestation of the universe.

sanskrit: candrārkamaṇḍale hemakaṭakau karamūlayoḥ / līlāsarasijaṃ haste brahmanbrahmāṇḍakarṇikā //
reference: The sun and the moon are the golden armlets of time, who holds in his palm the mundane world as the paltry plaything of a nosegay.
baseline: The celestial objects in the circle of the crescent are the hemakataka and the kārmula. In the hands of the lord lila sījama Brahman Brahma Brahmā Brahmas Karnika Karnikāna etc.
morphology: The celestial objects in the circle of the moon the crescent and the karmula should be placed in the hands of the lord lila the celestials the brahmins the gods the karnikas.

sanskrit: tārābinducitaṃ lolapuṣkarāvartapallavam / ekārṇavapayodhau tamekamambaramambaram //
reference: The firmament with its stars appears like a garment with coloured spots in it; the clouds called Pushkara and Avarta are as the skirts of that garment, which are washed by Time in the waters of the universal deluge.
baseline: The garland should be made of the leaves of a star a flower of a lotus a pearl a piece of water and a string of leaves.
morphology: The garland should be made of a string a piece of cloth and a piece made of water. The garlands should be placed in a single row.

sanskrit: evaṃrūpasya tasyāgre niyatirnityakāminī / anastamitasaṃrambhamārambhaiḥ parinṛtyati //
reference: Before him, dances his beloved Destiny with all her arts for ever, to beguile the living that are fond of worldly enjoyments.
baseline: A woman who has been appointed as a priest in such a form should perform the ritual with the preceptors and the initiators.
morphology: A woman who has been appointed as such should perform a dance with the preceptor and the initiator.

sanskrit: tasyā nartanalolāyā jaganmaṇḍapakoṭare / aruddhaspandarūpāyā āgamāpāyacañcure //
reference: People hurry up and down to witness the dance of Destiny, whose unrestrained motion keeps them at work, and causes their repeated births and deaths.
baseline: The same dance should be performed in the temple of the lord in the sanctum sanctorum of the temple and in the arch of the arch.
morphology: The same dance should be performed in the precincts of the mandapācātra. The arch should be placed in the form of an arruddhaśpaṇḍa.

sanskrit: cārubhūṣaṇamaṅgeṣu devalokāntarāvalī / āpātālaṃ nabholambaṃ kabarīmaṇḍalaṃ bṛhat //
reference: The people of all the worlds are studded about her person as her ornaments, and the sky stretching from the heaven of gods to the infernal regions, serves for the veil on her head.
baseline: The four parts of the body the outer part of the temple the inner part of it the upper part the navel the chamber of the grave and the larger part.
morphology: The four parts of the body the outer part of the temple the inner part of it the upper part the navel the grave and the great part of its body are worshipped.

sanskrit: narakālī ca mañjīramālā kalakalojjvalā / protā duṣkṛtasūtreṇa pātālacaraṇe sthitā //
reference: Her feet are planted in the infernal regions, and the hell-pits ring at her feet like trinkets, tied by the string of evil deeds or sins.
baseline: O Narakālī the goddess of fire and water of fire standing in the path of the abyss with the thread of evil threads.
morphology: O Narakālī the goddess of fire and water of fire standing in the path of the abyss with the thread of the evil thread.

sanskrit: kastūrikātilakakaṃ kriyāsaṃkhyopakalpitam / citritaṃ citraguptena yame vadanapaṭṭake //
reference: She is painted all over from head to foot by the god Chitra Gupta with ornamental marks prepared by her attendants (the deeds of men), and perfumed with the essence of those deeds.
baseline: The figure of a musk should be drawn with the image of the cardamom. The figure should be placed on the plate of the pot.
morphology: The number of kriyas should be drawn with the cardamom. The figure should be painted with the scripture.

sanskrit: kālāsyaṃ samupādāya kalpānteṣu kilākulā / nṛtyatyeṣā punardevī sphuṭacchailaghanāravam //
reference: She dances and reels at the nod of her husband at the end of the Kalpas, and makes the mountains crack and crash at her foot-falls.
baseline: One should worship the goddess Kaalāsya at the end of the Kalpāṇas. The goddess should be worshipped in the form of a kila kula nātiya and again.
morphology: One should worship the goddess Kaālaśya at the end of the Kalpāṇas. The goddess should be worshipped again in the form of a kila kula nātirāya kāla kulā kūla ghana kala kalpa kīla and kālākula.

sanskrit: paścātprālambavibhrāntakaumārabhṛtabarhibhiḥ / netratrayavṛhadrandhrabhūribhāṅkārabhīṣaṇaiḥ //
reference: Behind her dance the peacocks of the god Kumara; and Kala the god of death staring with his three wide open eyes, utters his hideous cries.
baseline: Then the three eyes should be covered with a lotus and the three holes should be filled with the illusion of the earth.
morphology: Then the three eyes the three holes of the eye the ground and the other parts of the body are covered with the illusions of the illusion of delusion.

sanskrit: lambalolajaṭācandravikīrṇaharamūrdhabhiḥ / uccaraccārumandāragaurīkabaracāmaraiḥ //
reference: Death dances about in the form of the five headed Hara, with the loosened braids of hair upon him; while Destiny in the form of Gauri, and her locks adorned with Mandara flowers keeps her pace with him.
baseline: The chandravīra is made up of the four parts of the earth. The upper part of the body is made of white cloth and the lower part of it is made out of red cloth.
morphology: The chandravikāra is made up of the four elements of the lumbar form the mārudha the chariot the garland the cow and the cow.

sanskrit: uttāṇḍavācalākārabhairavodaratumbakaiḥ / raṇatsaśatarandhrendradehabhikṣākapālakaiḥ //
reference: This Destiny in her war-dance, bears a capacious gourd representing her big belly, and her body is adorned with hundreds of hollow human skulls jingling like the alms-pots of the Kapali mendicants.
baseline: One who is walking on the north one who is moving on the south one with the arms one having the arms of the king one holding the body and the other having the hands of the lord of the earth and one who has the heart of the body.
morphology: One should be guided by Bhairava who is a man walking on the north side of the earth and the king of the rivers and the lord of the body and the guardians of the fire.

sanskrit: śuṣkaśārīrakhaṭvāṅgabharairāpūritāmbaram / bhīṣayatyātmanātmānaṃ sarvasaṃhārakāriṇī //
reference: She has filled (reached) the sky with the emaciated skeleton of her body, and gets terrified at her all destructive figure.
baseline: One who consumes everything from the soul should offer the fragrant leaves of the body the fragrance of the limbs the perfume of the gods the goddess of death.
morphology: One who consumes everything from the body to the soul should offer the fragrant leaves of the body the fragrance of the limbs the perfume of the spirit the goddess of death the destroyer of all things.

sanskrit: viśvarūpaśiraścakracārupuṣkaramālayā / tāṇḍaveṣu vivalgantyā mahākalpeṣu rājate //
reference: The skulls of the dead of various shapes adorn her body like a beautiful garland of lotuses, which keep hanging to and fro during her dance at the end of a Kalpa age.
baseline: One who has the form of the universe the head the face the hair and the hair of the body the king of the great kalapas in the vivālgantya and the tantavas is the king.
morphology: One who has the form of the universe the head and the head of the body the four parts of the earth the palms of the gods the vivalgantas the king of the great kalapas and the kings king is the one who reigns in the torments.

sanskrit: pramattapuṣkarāvartaḍamaroḍḍāmarāravaiḥ / tasyāḥ kila palāyante kalpānte tumburādayaḥ //
reference: The horrible roaring of the giddy clouds Pushkara and Avarta at the end of the Kalpa, serves to represent the beating of her Damaru drum, and put to flight the heavenly choir of Tumburu.
baseline: One who has made a sacrifice by the way of offering a piece of cloth a piece a string of cloth and a sword should be thrown at the end of the kalpa.
morphology: One who has made a sacrifice by the arrow should not be afraid of it. His axe should be thrown away at the end of the Kalpa.

sanskrit: nṛtyato'ntaḥ kṛtāntasya candramaṇḍalabhāsinaḥ / tārakācandrikācāruvyomapicchāvacūlinaḥ //
reference: As death dances along, the moon appears like his ear-ring, and the moon-beams and stars appear like his crest made of peacocks' feathers.
baseline: The king of the moon and the king of his kingdom should perform the dance. The king should be worshipped by the charioteers of the star moon and other celestial bodies.
morphology: Those who dance with the moon and the celestial body at the end those who worship the star the moon the charioteer and those who do not want to dance.

sanskrit: ekasmiñchravaṇe dīptā himavānasthimudrikā / apare ca mahāmeruḥ kāntā kāñcanakarṇikā //
reference: The snow-capt Himalaya, appears like a circlet of bones in the upper loop of his right ear, and the mount Meru as a golden areola in that of the left.
baseline: The Śimāna mudrīka is illuminated with the sound of a spring the śimāvaṇa mudrāka is placed on the top and the great meru is the kanta and the kāṇcāna karnika.
morphology: The śimvana mudrīka is lit in the morning with a mace. On the other side is the great mermaid and the kanta kāṇa kāñaka karnika.

sanskrit: atraiva kuṇḍale lole candrārkau gaṇḍamaṇḍale / lokālokācalaśreṇī sarvataḥ kaṭimekhalā //
reference: Under their lobes are suspended the moon and the sun, as pendant ear-rings glittering over his cheeks. The mountain ranges called the lokaloka are fastened like chains around his waist.
baseline: Here in the circle the moon the earth the rhino the gondola the loins the waist the neck and all around the lokalokācāla range.
morphology: Here in the temple of the moon the kundalāla the lola the chandrakāla and the gondhāla are placed in the circle of the people. The lokalokācāla range is everywhere at the waist.

sanskrit: itaścetaśca gacchantī vidyudvalayakarṇikā / anilāndolitā bhāti nīradāṃśukapaṭṭikā //
reference: The lightnings are the bracelets and armlets of Destiny, which move to and fro as she dances along. The clouds are her wrappers that fly about her in the air.
baseline: It is also known to be the karnika of electricity. It is said to be made of ghee and water.
morphology: It goes to such a place as the karnika of electricity ghee water and other elements.

sanskrit: musalaiḥ paṭṭiśaiḥ prāsaiḥ śūlaistomaramudgaraiḥ / tīkṣṇaiḥ kṣīṇajagadvāntakṛtāntairiva saṃbhṛtaiḥ //
reference: Death is furnished with many weapons, as clubs, axes, missiles, spears, shovels, mallets and sharp swords, all of which are sure weapons of destruction.
baseline: One who has made the world weak and has been imprisoned by the muṣāla pātisā prāśa śula stoma muḍgārā sharpened and the āṇtāra is bound by the mantras.
morphology: One who has made the world weak with the stripes of the muslims the striped ones the muḍgārās and the sharpened ones and those who have built the world in the past and the rest of the world.

sanskrit: saṃsārabandhanādīrghe pāśe kālakaracyute / śeṣabhogamahāsūtraprote mālāsya śobhate //
reference: Mundane enjoyments are no other than long ropes dropped down by the hand of death, and keeping all mankind fast bound to the world; while the great thread of infinity (ananta) is worn by him as his wreath of flowers.
baseline: The garland is adorned with the fragrance of the sun and the rest of the enjoyment.
morphology: The garland is adorned with the fragrance of the samsara and the garland of the sun for the rest of the enjoyment.

sanskrit: jīvollasanmakarikāratnatejobhirujjvalā / saptābdhikaṅkaṇaśreṇī bhujayorasya bhūṣaṇam //
reference: The belts of the seven oceans are worn about the arms of Death as his bracelets resplendent with the living sea-animals, and the bright gems contained in their depths.
baseline: The jewel of jivevallas merriment the jewel of the sun the diamond of the fire the ornament of the bhujayor is of the order of seven years.
morphology: The jewel of jivevallas the meritorious one the jewel of the earth the fiery one and the ornament of the bow and arrow are of the order of seven years.

sanskrit: vyavahāramahāvartā sukhaduḥkhaparamparā / rajaḥpūrṇatamaḥśyāmā romālī tasya rājate //
reference: The great vortices of customs, the successions of joy and grief, the excess of pride and the darkness of passions, form the streaks of hair on his body.
baseline: The king should be the most perfect ruler. The king is the king of all beings.
morphology: The king should have the highest degree of happiness and compassion in his conduct. His kingdom should be ruled by the king.

sanskrit: evaṃprāyaḥ sa kalpānte kṛtāntastāṇḍavodbhavām / upasaṃhṛtya nṛtyehāṃ sṛṣṭvā saha maheśvaram //
reference: After the end of the world, he ceases to dance, and creates anew all things from the lowest animal that lives in the earth, to the highest Brahma and Siva.
baseline: In this way he has done the sublimation of the temple. Having completed the dance he has created the temple of lord Mahesvara.
morphology: In this way he would have done at the end of the Kalpāṇa. Having completed the worship he would dance with Mahesvara.

sanskrit: punarlāsyamayīṃ nṛtyalīlāṃ sargasvarūpiṇīm / tanotīmāṃ jarāśokaduḥkhābhibhavabhūṣitām //
reference: Destiny as an actress, acts by turns her parts of creation and destruction, diversified by scenes of old age, sorrow and misery.
baseline: Then the dance of the goddess lilies the form of heaven the goddess of the sun the mermaids and the goddess jārāshoka should be adorned with the grace of sorrow.
morphology: Then the dance of the goddess lilies the form of heaven the goddess of the sun the mermaids and the goddess jarāshoka are adorned with the grace of sorrow.

sanskrit: bhūyaḥ karoti bhuvanāni vanāntarāṇi lokāntarāṇi janajālakakalpanāṃ ca / ācāracārukalanāmacalāṃ calāṃ ca paṅkādyathārbhakajano racanāmakhinnaḥ //
reference: Time repeatedly creates the worlds and their woods, with the different abodes and localities teeming with population. He forms the moveable and immovable substances, establishes customs and again dissolves them, as boys make their dolls of clay and break them soon afterwards.
baseline: One who performs the bhūvāyaṇa rites the forest the inner world the network of the people the kalpaṇas the chālaṇas and the pākādaṇas should be prepared.
morphology: One who performs the bhūvāyaṇa rites the forest the inner world the network of the people the kalpaṇas the chalas chāla pākāda nāhārvakās and the artefacts should be prepared.

sanskrit: śrīrāma uvāca / vṛtte'sminnevameteṣāṃ kālādīnāṃ mahāmune / saṃsāranāmni kaivāsthā mādṛśānāṃ vadatviha //
reference: Rama said:—Such being the all destructive conduct of time and others (as already described), what confidence, O great sage, can men like me, have upon them?
baseline: O Śrīma one should say these things in the morning and in the evening. One should say the words of the samsara sāṃrāma kāvaśa mādusha etc.
morphology: O Śrīma one should say these things to the great lord Śirāma. One should say the words of the samsara Kaiva Maśu and others.

sanskrit: vikrītā iva tiṣṭhāma etairdaivādibhirvayam / mune prapañcaracanairmugdhā vanamṛgā iva //
reference: We all remain here, O sage! as slaves sold to Fate and Destiny, and are deceived by their allurements as beasts of the forest.
baseline: One should stand like a seller in the form of a beast. One should build the universe in the forehead and be like a wild animal.
morphology: One should stand like a seller in the form of a wild animal. One should build the universe in the foreground. One would be like a wild beast.

sanskrit: eṣo'nāryasamāmnāyaḥ kālaḥ kavalanonmukhaḥ / jagatyavirataṃ lokaṃ pātayatyāpadarṇave //
reference: This Fate whose conduct is so very inhuman, is always up to devour all beings, and is incessantly throwing men into the sea of troubles.
baseline: One who has not been able to do so would be facing the world from the other side. One who is facing the sky from the left side of the earth would fall down from the right side.
morphology: This is the same as the āṇirāya and the time. The world should be divided into two parts.

sanskrit: dahatyantardurāśābhirdevo dāruṇaceṣṭayā / lokamuṣṇaprakāśābhijvālābhirdahano yathā //
reference: He is led by his malicious attempts to inflame the mind with inordinary desires, as the fire raises its flames to burn down a habitation.
baseline: One who has made a great effort to burn the fire the fire and the gods of the world the light and the fire should be destroyed.
morphology: One who has made a great effort to burn the fire the fire and the fire should be worshipped with great fervour.

sanskrit: dhṛtiṃ vidhurayatyeṣā maryādārūpavallabhā / strītvātsvabhāvacapalā niyatirniyatonmukhī //
reference: Destiny the faithful and obedient wife of Fate, is naturally fickle on account of her being a female, and is always bent on mischief and disturbing the patience.
baseline: A woman should be a widower a person of high status a woman a man of good character and a woman of good fortune.
morphology: One who is a widower should not make a vow to a woman as a matter of honour. One who does not want to be a woman should be bound by the rules of the nature.

sanskrit: grasate'virataṃ bhūtajālaṃ sarpa ivānilam / kṛtāntaḥ karkaśācāro jarāṃ nītvā'jaraṃ vapuḥ //
reference: As the heinous serpent feeds upon the air, so does cruel Death ever swallow the living. He ripens the body with old age to create his zest, and then devours all animals warm with life.
baseline: The snake should be made to eat with the help of a string of water and the snake should not be eaten with the aid of a stick.
morphology: Having taken away the garland of the ghosts the snake and the water of the forest should be removed.

sanskrit: yamo nirghṛṇarājendro nārtaṃ nāmānukampate / sarvabhūtadayodāro jano durlabhatāṃ gataḥ //
reference: Death is called a relentless tyrant, having no pity even for the sick and weak; nor any regard for any one in any state of life.
baseline: One who has not been able to bear the loss of his life would become a king. One who does not want to suffer the loss would become poor.
morphology: One who has not been able to bear the loss of his life would become a king. One who does not want to suffer the loss would become poor.

sanskrit: sarvā eva mune phalguvibhavā bhūtajātayaḥ / duḥkhāyaiva durantāya dāruṇā bhogabhūmayaḥ //
reference: Every one in this world is fond of affluence and pleasures, not knowing that these are only calculated to lead him to his ruin.
baseline: All beings should be made to feel the ill effects of evil spirits. One should suffer misfortune misfortunities evil enjoyment and misery.
morphology: All beings should be made to feel the ill effects of evil spirits. One should suffer misfortune misfortunities misery evil enjoyment etc.

sanskrit: āyuratyantacapalaṃ mṛtyurekāntaniṣṭhuraḥ / tāruṇyaṃ cātitaralaṃ bālyaṃ jaḍatayā hṛtam //
reference: Life is very unsteady. Death is very cruel. Youth is very frail and fickle, and boyhood is full of dullness and insensibility.
baseline: One who has attained the end of his life one who is determined to die and one who has completed four years of life has lost his childhood in the form of a child.
morphology: One who has attained the end of his life one who is committed to death one with the end and another with the child has lost his father son daughter son and mother.

sanskrit: kalākalaṅkito loko bandhavo bhavabandhanam / bhogā bhavamahārogāstṛṣṇāśca mṛgatṛṣṇikāḥ //
reference: Man is defiled by his worldliness, his friends are ties to the world, his enjoyments are the greatest of his diseases in life, and his avarice and ambition are the mirage that always allures him.
baseline: The people who are associated with the art and the bondage should be bound by you. You should suffer from diseases and diseases.
morphology: You are bound by the bondage of the people who are associated with the art and blasphemy. You suffer from diseases and diseases. You are the enemy of the world.

sanskrit: śatravaścendriyāṇyeva satyaṃ yātamasatyatām / praharatyātmanaivātmā manasaiva mano ripuḥ //
reference: Our very senses are our enemies, before which even truth appears as falsehood; the mind is the enemy of the mind and self is the enemy of self.
baseline: The enemy the senses the spirit the mind and the mind should be defeated.
morphology: The enemy the senses the spirit the mind and the mind should be defeated.

sanskrit: ahaṃkāraḥ kalaṅkāya buddhayaḥ paripelavāḥ / kriyā duṣphaladāyinyo līlāḥ strīniṣṭhatāṃ gatāḥ //
reference: Self-esteem is stained (with the name of selfishness), intelligence is blamed for its fallaciousness, our actions are attended with bad results, and our pleasures tend only to effeminacy.
baseline: The ego the intellect the mind the actions the ill-fruitful deeds the lilies the womanhood the piety of the woman are gone.
morphology: The ego the intellect the mind the actions the misfortune the lilies the womanhood the virtues the ill-fruits of the deeds etc. are the reasons for the blasphemy.

sanskrit: vāñchāviṣayaśālinyaḥ saccamatkṛtayaḥ kṣatāḥ / nāryo doṣapatākinyo rasā nīrasatāṃ gatāḥ //
reference: All our desires are directed to enjoyments; our love of truth is lost; our women are the ensigns of vice, and all that were once so sweet, have become tasteless and vapid.
baseline: Those who do good deeds and do evil deeds should be punished. Those who are not good at the time of their desire should be blamed for the loss.
morphology: Those who do good deeds on the grounds of want good deeds evil deeds wrong deeds bad deeds misfortune bad habits evil conduct evil behavior etc. become dull.

sanskrit: vastvavastutayā jñātaṃ dattaṃ cittamahaṃkṛtau / abhāvavedhitā bhāvā bhāvānto nādhigamyate //
reference: Things that are not real, are believed as real, and have become the cause of our pride, by hardening us in untruth, and keeping us from the light of truth.
baseline: Having given knowledge of things and facts the mind becomes proud. Having felt the lack of feeling the feeling disappears.
morphology: One who gives knowledge of things and facts one who is given to the mind becomes proud one whose feelings are not affected by the lack of feeling and one who does not want to go away.

sanskrit: tapyate kevalaṃ sādho matirākulitāntarā / rāgarogo vilasati virāgo nopagacchati //
reference: My mind is at a loss to think what to do; it regrets at its increased appetite for pleasure, and for want of that self-denial.
baseline: One who does penance only with the mind balanced in the inner part of the body one who is not afraid of anger and evil will get victory.
morphology: One who does penance only with the mind balanced in the heart one who is not afraid of anger and evil will get victory.

sanskrit: rajoguṇahatā dṛṣṭistamaḥ saṃparivardhate / na cādhigamyate sattvaṃ tattvamatyantadūrataḥ //
reference: My sight is dimmed by the dust of sensuality: the darkness of self-esteem prevails upon me: the purity of mind is never reached to, and truth is far off from me.
baseline: One who has seen the manifestation of the king one who has not been able to attain the ultimate state of sātva one would not get it.
morphology: One who sees the king the chiefly ones wealth increases. One does not get the power and the principle from far away.

sanskrit: sthitirasthiratāṃ yātā mṛtirāgamanonmukhī / dhṛtirvaidhuryamāyātā ratirnityamavastuni //
reference: Life is become uncertain and death is always advancing nigh; my patience is disturbed, and there is an increased appetite for whatever is false.
baseline: One who is standing still or standing in the direction of death one who is facing death and one who has been sitting on the path of the earth should be made to stand on the ground.
morphology: One who is standing still in the direction of death one who is facing death and one who has been sitting on the ground in the form of a river one should stand on the path leading to death.

sanskrit: matirmāndyena malinā pātaikaparamaṃ vapuḥ / jvalatīva jarā dehe pratisphurati duṣkṛtam //
reference: The mind is soiled by dullness, and the body is cloyed with surfeit and ready to fall; old age exults over the body, and sins are conspicuous at every step.
baseline: O Pāpu one of the leaves should be washed with the oil of the mother the burning water of the jāra and the fire of the body should be flushed out.
morphology: One should wear a piece of cloth with the garland of the mother a string of fire a thread of fire and water. It is made difficult.

sanskrit: yatnena yāti yuvatā dūre sajjanasaṃgatiḥ / gatirna vidyate kācitkvacinnodeti satyatā //
reference: Youth flies fast away with all our care to preserve it; the company of the good is at a distance; the light of truth shines from no where;and I can have recourse to nothing in this world.
baseline: One who goes far away with diligence and attains good company one who is on the move and gives some good advice gives truth.
morphology: One who is far away from good company with diligence one who is in a state of motion and one who knows the truth gives the truth.

sanskrit: mano vimuhyatīvāntarmuditā dūratāṃ gatā / nojjvalā karuṇodeti dūrādāyāti nīcatā //
reference: The mind is stupified within itself, and its contentment has fled from it: there is no rise of enlightened sentiments in it, and meanness makes its advance to it from a distance.
baseline: One who gives the mind away with the mind and the mind with the heart one who goes far away from the heart and one who does not want to go away with compassion and gives away the inferiority.
morphology: One who gives the mind away with the mind and the mind with the heart and the heart should go far away. One who does not give mercy would get away with inferiority.

sanskrit: dhīratā'dhīratāmeti pātotpātaparo janaḥ / sulabho durjanāśleṣo durlabhaḥ satsamāgamaḥ //
reference: Patience is converted into impatience; man is liable to the states of birth and death; good company is rare, but bad company is ever within the reach of every body.
baseline: One who produces leaves with patience and has good fortune one who does not have the ability to fight evil people is poor and has a good fortune.
morphology: One who produces leaves with courage and selflessness would get good things. One who does not have the ability to fight evil people would get bad things. He would get better things.

sanskrit: āgamāpāyino bhāvā bhāvanā bhavabandhanī / nīyate kevalaṃ kvāpi nityaṃ bhūtaparamparā //
reference: All individual existences are liable to appear and disappear; all desires are chains to the world, and all worldly beings are ever seen to be led away per force where no body can tell.
baseline: The feeling of the spirit in the form of the incarnation of the past is bound to you. One would only carry on the tradition of the ghost forever.
morphology: The feeling of the spirit is bound to you by the preceptors of the past. One would only take away the tradition of the ghost forever.

sanskrit: diśo'pi hi na dṛśyante deśo'pyanyāpadeśabhāk / śailā api viśīryante kaivāsthā mādṛśe jane //
reference: What reliance can there be on human life, when the points of the compass become indistinct and undiscernible; when the countries and places change their positions and names, and when mountains even are liable to be dilapidated?
baseline: One would not see the land even in the third day. One would find the stone also spread in the middle of the sky.
morphology: One would not see the land even in the second half. One would find the stone spread out in the middle of the cave.

sanskrit: adyate sattayāpi dyaurbhu'vana cāpi ūyate / dharāpi yāti vaidhuryaṃ kevāsthā mādṛśe jane //
reference: What reliance can there be on man, when the heavens are swallowed in infinity, when this world is absorbed in nothingness, and the very earth loses her stability?
baseline: One would get the gift of gold even after having been given to the mother. One would also get the property of the mother by having a cow.
morphology: Even if one does not have the right to live today one would get the property of the king. One would get a valid property from the mother.

sanskrit: śuṣyantyapi samudrāśca śīryante tārakā api / siddhā api vinaśyanti kaivāsthā mādṛśe jane //
reference: What reliance can there be on men like ourselves, when the very seas are liable to be dried up, when the stars are doomed to fade away and disappear, and when the most perfect of beings are liable to dissolution?
baseline: The sun the sea the stars the siddhas and the goddess are destroyed by the Kaivas.
morphology: The stars and the siddhas are destroyed by the sea and the sea. The siddhas are destroyed with the Kaiva.

sanskrit: dānavā api dīryante dhruvo'pyadhruvajīvitaḥ / amarā api māryante kaivāsthā mādṛśe jane //
reference: What reliance can there be on men like us, when even the demigods are liable to destruction, when the polar star is known to change its place, and when the immortal gods are doomed to mortality?
baseline: The demons are also killed by the gods. The immortals are killed by a cow.
morphology: The demons are also killed by the cow and the elves are killed by them.

sanskrit: śakro'pyākramyate vakrairyamo'pi hi niyamyate / vāyurapyetyavāyutvaṃ kaivāsthā mādṛśe jane //
reference: What reliance can there be on men like us, when Indra is doomed to be defeated by demons; when even death is hindered from his aim, and when the current air ceases to breathe?
baseline: One who has not been able to bear the wind should be made to drink the water with the help of the cow. The same is done with the advice of the mother.
morphology: The same is prescribed for the defiance of the wind by the use of cow dung cowdung and cowdough.

sanskrit: somo'pi vyomatāṃ yāti mārtaṇḍo'pyeti khaṇḍatām / magnatāmagnirapyeti kaivāsthā mādṛśe jane //
reference: What reliance can there be on men like us, when the very moon is to vanish with the sky, when the very sun is to be split into pieces, and when fire itself is to become frigid and cold?
baseline: One who has made a fire should also make a piece of the ground with the help of the mādrīsa.
morphology: One should also make a piece of the ground with the help of a māgna and fire. One should make a fragment of the same piece with the aid of the mādrṣa.

sanskrit: parameṣṭhyapi niṣṭhāvānhriyate hīrarapyajaḥ / bhavo'pyabhāvamāyāti kaivāsthā mādṛśe jane //
reference: What reliance can there be on men like us, when the very Hari and Brahma are to be absorbed into the Great One, and when Siva himself is to be no more.
baseline: One who is faithful even after having attained the supreme position would lose the pride of the diamond. One who has attained the superior position would get the glory of the mother.
morphology: One who is faithful even after having attained the supreme position would lose the pride of the diamond. One who has attained the superior position would get the glory of the mother.

sanskrit: kālaḥ saṃkālyate yena niyatiścāpi nīyate / khamapyālīyate'nantaṃ kaivāsthā mādṛśe jane //
reference: What reliance can there be on men like us, when the duration of time comes to be counted, when Destiny is destined to her final destiny, and when all vacuity loses itself in infinity?
baseline: The time is shortened so that even the appointed one is taken away. One who does so would get a lot of money from the mother.
morphology: The time is fixed by which even the appointed one is taken away. One who has not gone to the cave should go to the mother.

sanskrit: aśrāvyāvācyadurdarśatattvenājñātamūrtinā / bhuvanāni viḍambyante kenacidbhramadāyinā //
reference: That which is inaudible, unspeakable, invisible, and unknowable in his real form, displays to us these wondrous worlds by some fallacy.
baseline: The images of the earth are made to be visible by the sound of sound and sound. The objects of the sky are made of the elements known by the words kāṇa śvāṇu bhaṇḍvā bhavṇu and bhavā.
morphology: The images of the earth are distorted by the illusion of hearing the illusions of sight and the unknowable.

sanskrit: ahaṃkārakalāmetya sarvatrāntaravāsinā / na so'sti triṣu lokeṣu yasteneha na bādhyate //
reference: No one conscious of himself (his egoism), can disown his subjection to that Being, that dwells in the hearts of every one.
baseline: One who is not bound by any of the three things would not be bound by the ego.
morphology: One should not be bound by the three things that are everywhere in the world.

sanskrit: śilāśailakavapreṣu sāśvabhūto divākaraḥ / vanapāṣāṇavannityamavaśaḥ paricodyate //
reference: This sun said:—the lord of worlds, is impelled (by that power) to run over hills, rocks and fields, like an inert piece of stone, hurled down from a mountain and borne away by a current stream.
baseline: The Divākarā is known to be the one who has placed the earth on the rocks and rocks. One who has left behind the forest mountains and other things is known as the Divāgarā.
morphology: The Divākarā is known to be the divine one who worships the gods on the faces of the rocks and rocks. He is known as Vāṇapāśa.

sanskrit: dharāgolakamantasthasurāsuragaṇāspadam / veṣṭyate dhiṣṇyacakreṇa pakvākṣoṭamiva tvacā //
reference: This globe of earth, the seat of all the Suras and Asuras, and surrounded by the luminous sphere in the manner of a walnut covered by its hard crust, subsists under His command.
baseline: One who is seated on a pole with the garlands of the gods of the sun the king of the king is surrounded by a chakra with the same skin as a pakva.
morphology: The sun should be placed in the center of the temple and the skin should be covered with a stick of water.

sanskrit: divi devā bhuvi narāḥ pātāleṣu ca bhoginaḥ / kalpitāḥ kalpamātreṇa nīyante jarjarāṃ daśām //
reference: The Gods in the heavens, the men on earth and the serpents in the nether world, are brought into existence and led to decay by His will only.
baseline: The goddess of the earth the gods of the sky the men who enjoy themselves in the abyss and the pitchers the illusion of the mind is taken to the tenth place.
morphology: The gods of the earth the goddess of divinity the gods of earth and those who enjoy themselves in the abyss are taken away from the illusion.

sanskrit: kāmaśca jagadīśānaraṇalabdhaparākramaḥ / akrameṇaiva vikrānto lokamākramya valgati //
reference: Kama (Cupid) that is arbitrarily powerful, and has forcibly overpowered on all the living world, has derived his unconquerable might from the Lord of worlds.
baseline: One who has attained the attainment of vikrāṇta vālgati kāmā jagīṣṇa śāraṇa and vāla should go to the world in the same sequence.
morphology: One who has attained the attainment of vikrāṇta vālgati kāma jāgīṣṇara and vaṇgati should go to the world in the same sequence.

sanskrit: vasanto mattamātaṅgo madaiḥ kusumavarṣaṇaiḥ / āmoditakakupcakraśceto nayati cāpalam //
reference: As the heated elephant regales the air with his spirituous exudation, so does the spring perfume the air with his profusion of flowers, unsettling the minds of men.
baseline: One who brings water from the spring water and wine with the kusuma rain should take the chariot to the āmā kupcha and krṣa.
morphology: One who brings water from the spring and the wine of the month with kusuma and rain one who takes water from a mango tree to a tree is called chapalā.

sanskrit: anuraktāṅganālolalocanālokitākṛti / svasthīkartuṃ manaḥ śakto na viveko mahānapi //
reference: So are the loose glances of loving damsels directed to inflict deep wounds in the heart of man, which his best reason is unable to heal.
baseline: One who does not have the strength of the mind to heal one who is not wise or great should not think of the matter of the body.
morphology: One who does not have the strength of the mind to heal one who is not wise or great should not think of the matter of the body and the body.

sanskrit: paropakārakāriṇyā parārtiparitaptayā / buddha eva sukhī manye svātmaśītalayā dhiyā //
reference: One whose best endeavour is always to do good to others, and who feels for others' woes, is really intelligent and happy under the influence of his cool judgement.
baseline: The Buddha should be pleased with the meritorious conduct of others by the preceptor of charity. He should be blessed with the coolness of the self.
morphology: The Buddha should be pleased with the meritorious conduct of others. He should be blessed with the coolness of the self.

sanskrit: utpannadhvaṃsinaḥ kālavaḍavānalapātinaḥ / saṃkhyātuṃ kena śakyante kallolā jīvitāmbudhau //
reference: Who can count the number of beings resembling the waves of the ocean, and on whom death has been darting the submarine fire of destruction.
baseline: One can find out the number of kallu living and dead animals.
morphology: One can find out the number of black and white flowers produced by the sun and the number living flowers flowers fruits etc.

sanskrit: sarva eva narā mohāddurāśāpāśapāśinaḥ / doṣagulmakasāraṅgā viśīrṇā janmajaṅgale / saṃkṣīyate jagati janmaparamparāsu lokasya tairiha kukarmabhirāyuretat //
reference: All mankind are deluded to entrap themselves in the snare of avarice, and to be afflicted with all evils in life, as the deer entangled in the thickets of a jungle.
baseline: All men should be worshipped with the garlands of gods animals animals and animals. The garland of cows animals etc. should be kept in the wilderness. The world should be built with the folk traditions.
morphology: All men should be worshipped with the garlands of gods gods animals animals and animals. The garland of the pitchers should be spread in the forest. The world should be destroyed by the creation of the people and the birth traditions should be preserved by the king.

sanskrit: ākāśapādapalatākṛtapāśakalpaṃ yeṣāṃ phalaṃ nahi vicāravido'pi vidmaḥ //
reference: The term of human life in this world, is decreased in each generation in proportion to (the increase of their wicked acts). The desire of fruition is as vain as the expectation of reaping fruits from a creeper growing in the sky: yet I know not why men of reason would not understand this truth.
baseline: One who does not get the fruits of the sky feet and other objects of the form of the side would also be wrong.
morphology: One who does not get the fruits of the sky the sky and the earth and those who do not get their fruits should also be aware of it.

sanskrit: adyotsavo'yamṛtureṣa tatheha yātrā te bandhavaḥ sukhamidaṃ saviśeṣabhogam / itthaṃ mudhaiva kalayansuvikalpajālamālolapelavamatirgalatīha lokaḥ //
reference: This is a day of festivity, a season of joy and a time of procession. Here are our friends, here the pleasures and here the variety of our entertainments. Thus do men of vacant minds amuse themselves with weaving the web of their desires, until they become extinct.
baseline: One who has made a journey after the death of a relative and enjoys a special enjoyment by doing so would get the good fortune of the people. One who does so would be able to make a choice of goods and goods.
morphology: One should observe this day the festival of the month of May the journey of the deceased those relatives happiness enjoyment and enjoyment. One should do so. The people should worship the gods and goddesses of the world.

sanskrit: śrīrāma uvāca / anyacca tātā'titarāmaramye manorame ceha jagatsvarūpe / na kiṃcidāyāti tadarthajātaṃ yenātiviśrāntimupaiti cetaḥ //
reference: Rama said:—O sage! this seemingly pleasing but actually unpleasant world, has nothing in it that is productive of such a thing as can afford tranquility to the soul.
baseline: One who has not been born with the form of Śrīma one who has been born without having attained rest would not be able to see the face of the world in the manner described in the scriptures.
morphology: One who gives the form of the world to another person would not be able to get rest. One who does not give the appearance of the universe to another would not get peace.

sanskrit: bālye gate kalpitakelilole manomṛge dāradarīṣu jīrṇe / śarīrake jarjaratāṃ prayāte vidūyate kevalameva lokaḥ //
reference: After the playful boyhood is over, the mind wastes itself in the society of women like the deer fallen in a cavern, then the body bends down under old age, and the man has only to grieve.
baseline: After having passed through childhood one would get the illusion of the mind in the form of an animal the body in the shape of a deer the dead body and the poor man in the way of life.
morphology: After having passed through the childhood one who has lost his mind in the wilderness has lost the spirit in the desert has become a poor person in the body and has tried to destroy it.

sanskrit: jarātuṣārābhihatāṃ śarīrasarojinīṃ dūratare vimucya / kṣaṇādgate jīvitacañcarīke janasya saṃsārasaro'vaśuṣkam //
reference: As the body is stricken with the frost of old age, its beauty flies afar from it like the bloom of the fading lotus, and then the fountain of man's worldliness is at once dried up.
baseline: One should worship the goddess of the earth the goddess āsura the body the universe and the world in a distant place. One who is living in the world of the four worlds should be clean.
morphology: One should worship the goddess of the earth the goddess jāratūsara the body the universe and the world of the living beings in a distant place.

sanskrit: yadā yadā pākamupaiti nūnaṃ tadā tadeyaṃ ratimātanoti / jarābharā'nalpanavaprasūnā vijarjarā kāyalatā narāṇām //
reference: As the body gets towards its decline, so much doth death rejoice in it. The body grows lean with grey hairs upon the head, just as a creeper fades away with the flowers upon it.
baseline: When the saliva has been cooked it should be poured into the water with the same quantity as the jārābhāra. The water should be sprinkled with water and water.
morphology: When the saliva has been cooked it should be poured into the water with the salt and the water should be sprinkled with water and water.

sanskrit: tṛṣṇānadī sāratarapravāhagrastākhilānantapadārthajātā / taṭasthasaṃtoṣasuvṛkṣamūlanikāṣadakṣā vahatīha loke //
reference: All living creatures are borne away by the stream of avarice, which upsets the tree of contentment growing on the bank and flows on for ever in this world.
baseline: The waters of the river Trisna are flowing in the form of water. The waters flowing from the river to the river are flowing and the waters flowing out of the lake are flowing. The people should be free from the evil spirits.
morphology: The river of thirst should flow in the form of water. The waters of the river should be filled with water and other things. The people should be free from the evil spirits. They should be pure and happy.

sanskrit: śārīranauścarmanibandhabaddhā bhavāmbudhāvālulitā bhramantī / praloḍyate pañcabhirindriyākhyairadhobhavantī makarairadhīrā //
reference: Human body is like a vessel covered with skin; and glides over the ocean of the world (without its helmsman of reason). It is tossed about by sensual pleasures, and goes down under the water by the pressure of its whale-like passions.
baseline: The five senses of the mind and the body are bound together by the two arms.
morphology: The five senses of the mind and the body are bound together.

sanskrit: tṛṣṇālatākānanacāriṇo'mī śākhāśataṃ kāmamahīruheṣu / paribhramantaḥ kṣapayanti kālaṃ manomṛgā no phalamāpnuvanti //
reference: The world is a wilderness abounding in creepers of avarice and trees of sensuality, with hundreds of desires as their branches. Our minds like monkeys pass their time in roving about this forest without getting the fruits.
baseline: One who does not walk on the path of greed and greed would lose one hundred branches of desire in the king. One who wanders around would lose his mind for a long time and would not get any fruit.
morphology: Those who walk on the path of thirst and greed one hundred branches of lust and greedy people would be destroyed. Those who are wandering around would not bear fruit.

sanskrit: kṛcchreṣu dūrāstaviṣādamohāḥ svāsthyeṣu notsiktamanobhirāmāḥ / sudurlabhāḥ saṃprati sundarībhiḥ ranāhatāntaḥkaraṇā mahāntaḥ //
reference: Those that do not yield to grief in troubles, that are not elated with prosperity, nor smitten at heart by women, are rare in this world.
baseline: Those who are far away from the pitchers those who are ill and those who do not get well those men who are not good those with good qualities those having good qualities and those having a heart that is great should be killed by the mighty king.
morphology: Those who are far away from the pitchers those who are ill and those who do not get well those men who are not good those people who are good and those whose heart is not great those those who fight the enemy should be made great.

sanskrit: taranti mātaṅgaghaṭātaraṅgaṃ raṇāmbudhiṃ ye mayi te na śūrāḥ / śūrāsta eveha manastaraṅgaṃ dehendriyāmbhodhimimaṃ taranti //
reference: Those who fight boldly in the battle fields and withstand the war-elephants, are not so very brave in my opinion, as those who withstand the surges of the mind amidst the streams of carnal appetites.
baseline: The swords that float on the mother the body the heart the mind the senses and the mind should be made to float on me.
morphology: Those who swim on the mother body arm arm and arm and those who fight against the enemy should not swim on me. Those who are brave should swim on my body and mind.

sanskrit: akliṣṭaparyantaphalābhirāmā na dṛśyate kasyacideva kācit / kriyādurāśāhatacittavṛttiryāmetya viśrāntimupaiti lokaḥ //
reference: I see no such deeds in the world which endure to the last (or final emancipation) of men. Actions proceeding from a desire of fruition in fools, serve only for their restlessness on earth.
baseline: One who does not get any benefit from any of his actions and does not want to do any work till the end of the aqlīsta period would get rest.
morphology: One who does not get any benefit from any action or activity after having attained the state of mind would get rest.

sanskrit: kīrtyā jagaddikkuharaṃ pratāpaiḥ śriyā gṛhaṃ sattvabalena lakṣmīm / ye pūrayantyakṣatadhairyabandhā na te jagatyāṃ sulabhā mahāntaḥ //
reference: Such men are rare in the world, that have filled the corners of the world with their fame and valour, who have filled their houses with true riches acquired by honest means and an unwavering patience.
baseline: Those who do not have the fortitude the greatness of the world the glory of the king the house of lord Śrīya the power of the mighty and the strength of the goddess lakshmī those who are not bound by the impenetrable bond are the greatest of all.
morphology: Those who do not have the fortitude and fortitude to fill the house of lord Śrī with glory and glory and those who are not bound by the world will get the world easily.

sanskrit: apyantarasthaṃ giriśailabhittervajrālayābhyantarasaṃsthitaṃ vā / sarvaṃ samāyānti sasiddhivegāḥ sarvāḥ śriyaḥ santatamāpadaśca //
reference: Good and bad fortune always overtake a man, even if he were living in an aperture of the rock or within the walls of mountains, or even if he were enclosed within an iron built closet.
baseline: All the sādhi vegas and all the srīas and santāpadas should be placed in the middle of the hill and the walls of the river.
morphology: All the sādhi vegas and all the srīas and santāpadas are situated in the innermost part of the hill the walls and the walls of the river.

sanskrit: putrāśca dārāśca dhanaṃ ca buddhyā prakalpyate tāta rasāyanābham / sarvaṃ tu tannopakarotyathānte yatrātiramyā viṣamūrcchanaiva //
reference: Our sons and riches are mere objects of delight to us. It is as erroneous to suppose them to be of any good to us at the end, as to expect any benefit from the decoction of poison.
baseline: The sons servants servants and wealth should be thought of wisely. Then all things should be done without any difficulty.
morphology: The sons daughters wealth and other things should be thought out with the wisdom. Then all the things that are made of alchemy should be done in the same way.

sanskrit: viṣādayukto viṣamāmavasthā mupāgataḥ kāyavayovasāne / bhāvānsmaransvāniha dharmariktān janturjarāvāniha dahyate'ntaḥ //
reference: Old people being reduced to calamitous circumstances at the pitiable state of the decay of their bodies and decline of life, have greatly to be tormented at the thoughts of the impious deeds.
baseline: One who is in a state of distress and misfortune would get burnt by the fire. One would get the illusion of feeling and death by the burning of animals animals and animals.
morphology: One who is in a state of distress and misfortune would get burnt in the night. One who has not been able to bear the loss would get the loss of his life.

sanskrit: kāmārthadharmāptikṛtāntarābhiḥ kriyābhirādau divasāni nītvā / cetaścaladbarhiṇapicchalolaṃ viśrāntimāgacchatu kena puṃsaḥ //
reference: Men having passed their early days in the gratification of their desires and other worldly pursuits at the expense of the acts of virtue and piety, are as much troubled with anxieties at the end, that their minds are seized with a tremor like that of the plumage of a peacock shaken by the breeze. How then can a man attain to tranquility at any time?
baseline: Having taken the days in the course of the activity with the preceptors of the mind and having attained the righteousness of the heart one should come to rest with the penance of the disciple the penitentiary the charioteer the priest and the priest.
morphology: Having taken the days in the course of the activity with the spirit of the mind and having attained the righteousness of the heart one should come to rest with the mind mind heart and heart.

sanskrit: purogatairapyanavāptarūpaistaraṅgiṇītuṅgataraṅgakalpaiḥ / kriyāphalairdaivavaśādupetairviḍambyate bhinnarucirhi lokaḥ //
reference: Wealth whether forthcoming or unattainable, whether got by labour or given by fortune, is all as deceitful to the worldly minded, as the high waters of rivers.
baseline: One who has different interests in the form of the wind the movement of the earth the movements of the body the actions of the gods the manifestations of the elements the elements of the universe the objects of the world the nature of the stars the forms of the objects the images of the planets the world of the worlds is divided into two parts.
morphology: One who has not been able to attain the goal of the enemy would be divided into two parts.

sanskrit: imānyamūnīhi vibhāvitāni kāryāṇyaparyantamanoramāṇi / janasya jāyājanarañjanena javājjarāntaṃ jarayanti cetaḥ //
reference: That such and such desirable acts are to be done, are the constant thoughts of men, who desire to please their sons and wives, until they are worn out with age and become crazy in their minds.
baseline: One who does not believe in the existence of the king one who is not affected by the evil deeds and who is doing the deeds of the lord should be worshipped with the mantra jāyājāna nārājana jāvāja javāja.
morphology: One who does not believe in others one who does evil deeds and does not want to do evil deeds one would end his life with the victory of the people and the victory over the enemy.

sanskrit: parṇāni jīrṇāni yathā tarūṇāṃ sametya janmāśu layaṃ prayānti / tathaiva lokāḥ svavivekahīnāḥ sametya gacchanti kuto'pyahobhiḥ //
reference: Like leaves on trees that grow to fall, and falling make room for others to shoot forth, are those men who devoid of reason, die away daily to be born again.
baseline: Just as the leaves are worn out and the young ones are taken along and the children go along with them. In the same way the people go along without their senses.
morphology: Just as the leaves are worn out and the children are taken along with the children the children go along with them without their knowledge.

sanskrit: itastato dūrataraṃ vihṛtya praviśya gehaṃ divasāvasāne / vivekilokāśrayasādhukarma rikte'hni rātrau ka upaiti nidrām //
reference: Men having travelled here and there and far and near, return to their homes at the end of the day; but none of them can have rest by day or night, except the virtuous few that live by honest dealings.
baseline: Having so far wandered around one would enter the palace by day and make a conscious celestial body. One would find it empty by night and sleep.
morphology: Having so far wandered away from him one would enter the house by day by night by sleeping in the sky and by doing the ritual of the discreet celestial body.

sanskrit: vidrāvite śatrujane samaste samāgatāyāmabhitaśca lakṣmyām / sevyanta etāni sukhāni yāvattāvatsamāyāti kuto'pi mṛtyuḥ //
reference: After quelling his enemies and getting enough of riches in his clutches, the rich man just sits down to enjoy his gains; when death comes upon him, and interrupts his joy.
baseline: Having gathered all the enemies in the temple and having worshipped Lakshmi one should enjoy these pleasures till the death of any one.
morphology: Having gathered all the enemies in the midst of a riot one should serve Lakshmi in the temple. One who consumes these pleasures would never die.

sanskrit: kuto'pi saṃvardhitatuccharūpairbhāvairamībhiḥ kṣaṇanaṣṭadṛṣṭaiḥ / viloḍyamānā janatā jagatyāṃ navetyupāyātamaho na pātam //
reference: Seeing the vile trash of worldly gains earned and accumulated by the basest means to be but transitory, the infatuated mob do not perceive their approaching dissolution.
baseline: One who has not seen the world at all would not be able to see the people who have been vanquished from the world.
morphology: A person who has not seen the world at all should not enter the world of a new age.

sanskrit: priyāsubhiḥ kālamukhaṃ kriyante janaiḍakāste hatakarmabaddhāḥ / yaiḥ pīnatāmeva balādupetya śarīrabādhena na te bhavanti //
reference: Men loving their own lives, and making mouths at the demise of others, are like a herd of sheep bound to the stake, and staring at the slaughter of their fellows, yet feeding themselves to fall as fattened victims to death.
baseline: Those who are bound by the forces of the dead are not bound by their bodies. Those who have been killed by the enemies of the enemy are bound to death.
morphology: Those who are bound by the forces of the dead and those who drink from the dead are not bound by their bodies.

sanskrit: ajasramāgacchati satvaraivamanārataṃ gacchati satvaraiva / kuto'pi lolā janatā jagatyāṃ taraṅgamālā kṣaṇabhaṅgureva //
reference: The multitude of people on earth, is ever seen to appear in and disappear from it as fast as the passing waves of the sea, but who can tell whence they come and whither they return.
baseline: One who comes to the earth with a lotus goes to the temple of Lord Avāiva with a little bit of time. One who goes to Lola the people the world the waves and the waves of the world would be destroyed for a while.
morphology: One who comes to Ajāśra soon one who goes to Avāyavamana soon and who goes back to Nārta one should also go to Lola and the people of the world.

sanskrit: prāṇāpahāraikaparā narāṇāṃ mano manohāritayā haranti / raktacchadāścañcalaṣaṭpadākṣyo viṣadrumālolalatāḥ striyaśca //
reference: Women are as delicate as poisonous creepers, that with their red petaled lips and garments, and their eyes as busy as fluttering bees, are killers of mankind and stealers of their ravished hearts.
baseline: One who consumes the life of a man would destroy the heart of the men with charm blood and blood cover sixty parts of the body poison and malice and women.
morphology: One who consumes the life of a man would destroy the heart of the men with charm. One who destroys the blood and blood cover would be destroyed by the destruction of the region and the poisonous elements.

sanskrit: ito'nyataścopagatā mudhaiva samānasaṃketanibaddhabhāvā / yātrāsamāsaṃgasamā narāṇāṃ kalatramitravyavahāramāyā //
reference: Men are as passengers in a procession, repairing from this side and that to join at the place of their meeting. Such is the delusive union of our wives and friends here.
baseline: It is more than that. The same signs are bound together in the same manner in the month of the journey. The conduct of the men should be done in the months of the march.
morphology: These are more than these. The same signs should be fixed in the same manner in the case of a man in the course of his journey.

sanskrit: pradīpaśāntiṣviva bhuktabhūridaśāsvatisnehanibandhanīṣu / saṃsāramālāsu calācalāsu na jñāyate tattvamatāttvikīṣu //
reference: As the burning and extinguishing of the lamp depend on the wick and its moistening oil; so does our course in this transitory world (depend on our acts and affections only). Nobody knows the true cause of this mysterious existence.
baseline: One who is blessed with the lamp the serpent the goddess of peace the four hundred and thirty-somethings of the earth the conduct of the world the objects of the universe the principles of religion etc. is not known.
morphology: One who is blessed with the lamp the serpent the goddess of peace the four hundred and thirty-somethings of the earth the conduct of the world and the world is not known in the principles and other things.

sanskrit: saṃsārasaṃrambhakucakrikeyaṃ prāvṛṭpayobudbudabhaṅgurapi / asāvadhānasya janasya buddhau cirasthirapratyayamātanoti //
reference: The revolution of the world is comparable with that of the potter's wheel and the floating bubbles of rain water; that appear to be lasting to the ignorant observer only.
baseline: One who does not know the nature of the universe the mind of a person who is oblivious to it and who is not aware of it should be given the preceptor of eternal life.
morphology: One who does not know the mind of a person should be able to understand the world. One who is conscious of the mind should be aware of the existence of the universe.

sanskrit: śobhojjvalā daivavaśādvinaṣṭā guṇāḥ sthitāḥ saṃprati jarjaratve / āśvāsanādūrataraṃ prayātā janasya hemanta ivāmbujasya //
reference: The blooming beauty and graces (of youth), are destined to be snatched away at the approach of old age. The youthful hopes also of men fly at a distance like the bloom of lotus buds in winter.
baseline: Eightfold the glory of the fire of the divine abode is placed in the present day in the form of a dilapidated body. The relief of the man who has gone far away is that of Hemanta the son of the god of fire and that of the king of Bambuja.
morphology: One who has sought solace from a far away person Hemanta Ewambuja and others should be blessed with the glory of light and the two qualities of the divine abode.

sanskrit: punaḥpunardaivavaśādupetya svadehabhāreṇa kṛtopakāraḥ / vilūyate yatra taruḥ kuṭhārairāśvāsane tatra hi kaḥ prasaṅgaḥ //
reference: The tree which is ordained to be useful to mankind by the loads of fruits and flowers that it bears upon its body, is fated also to be hewn down by the cruel axe at last. How then can beneficent men expect to avoid the cruel hand of death.
baseline: One who has again returned to the abode of the gods and made a sacrifice with his own body is said to be doing good. Wherever he is going to make an axe what is the matter there?
morphology: One who has again returned to the abode of the gods and made a sacrifice with his own body is said to be doing good. Wherever one takes refuge in the axe what is the matter here?

sanskrit: manoramasyāpyatidoṣavṛtterantarviṃghātāya samutthitasya / viṣadrumasyeva janasya saṅgādāsādyate saṃprati mūrcchanaiva //
reference: Society with relatives is (of all others) as perilous as that of a poisonous plant; it is pleasant for its domestic affections, which are in reality but delusions of the soul.
baseline: One who has been raised to the point where he has made a mistake should be made to get rid of the mind. One who is in the company of a person with poison should be put to death.
morphology: One who has been raised to the point where he has made a mistake should be made to go to the temple. One who is in the company of a man with poison should be put to death.

sanskrit: kāstā dṛśo yāsu na santi doṣāḥ kāstā diśo yāsu na duḥkhadāhaḥ / kāstāḥ prajā yāsu na bhaṅguratvaṃ kāstāḥ kriyā yāsu na nāma māyā //
reference: What is that thing in the world, which has no fault in it; and what is that which does not afflict or grieve us; what being is born that is not subjected to death, and what are those acts that are free from deceit?
baseline: One who does not see a thing one who has no faults those who do not suffer from sorrow those people who are weak and those who have no deeds those whose name is not Maya are the subjects of suffering.
morphology: One who does not see a thing one who has no faults those who do not suffer and those who suffer from diseases and diseases those people who are castrated those whose actions are not worthy of attention those whom are not capable of doing any work.

sanskrit: kalpābhidhānakṣaṇajīvino hi kalpaughasaṃkhyākalane viriñcayāḥ / ataḥ kalāśālini kālajāle laghutvadīrghatvadhiyo'pyasatyāḥ //
reference: Those living a Kalpa age are reckoned as short-lived, compared with those living for many Kalpas, and they again are so in respect to Brahma. Hence the parts of time being all finite, the ideas of their length or shortness are altogether false.
baseline: One who has been given the title of Kalpa the protector the guardian the master the teacher of art and the master of the army should be given the distinction of small and tall in the course of his college.
morphology: One who has not been able to learn the art of drawing should be able to understand the meaning of the word kālpa that which is the protection of the living beings. One who does not know the art and the number of things should be taught the art form in the college.

sanskrit: sarvatra pāṣāṇamayā mahīdhrā mṛdā mahī dārubhireva vṛkṣāḥ / māṃsairjanāḥ pauruṣabaddhabhāvā nāpūrvamastīha vikārahīnam //
reference: Things that are called mountains are made of rocks, those that are called trees are made of wood, and those that are made of flesh are called animals, and man is the best of them. But they are all made of matter, and doomed to death and decay.
baseline: Everywhere a tree should be made of stone mud ghee wood meat and other things. It should not be made in the form of a man and should be without any disorder.
morphology: Everywhere a tree should be made of stone mud ghee cow dung meat and other things. It should not be made in the form of a man and should be without disorder.

sanskrit: ālokyate cetanayā'nuviddhā payonubaddho'stanayo nabhaḥ sthāḥ / pṛthagvibhāgena padārthalakṣmyā etajjagannetaradasti kiṃcit //
reference: Many things appear to be endued with intelligence, and the heavenly bodies seem to be full of water; but physicists have found out by analysis that, there is no other thing any where except (minutiae of) matter.
baseline: One who is not connected with the earth by means of consciousness is illuminated. One who does not want to be associated with the world one who is connected with it and one who has not got any object from the earth is given a gift.
morphology: One who is not connected with the earth by the consciousness of the light one who is connected to the sky and one who does not want to be connected with other things is given a gift.

sanskrit: camatkṛtiśceha manasvilokacetaścamatkārakarī narāṇām / svapne'pi sādho viṣayaṃ kadācitkeṣāṃcidabhyeti na citrarūpā //
reference: It is no wonder that this (unreal world) should appear a miraculous (reality) to the wise, and seem marvelously striking in the minds of mankind; since the visions in our dreams also appear so very fascinating to every one in their state of dreaming.
baseline: A woman who does not think of the mind the heart the spirit the mind and the mind of the world even in a dream would not be able to understand the subject matter.
morphology: A woman who has a mind and a heart that is made of miraculous objects and does not want to be seen in the form of images would never be able to conceive even in a dream.

sanskrit: adyāpi yāte'pi ca kalpanāyā ākāśavallīphalavanmahattve / udeti no lobhalavāhatānāmudāravṛttāntamayī kathaiva //
reference: Those that are corrupted in their greediness (after worldly enjoyments), will not even in their old age, receive the sermons on their eternal concerns, which they think to be false chimeras as those of a flower or a creeper growing in the sky.
baseline: If one does not imagine the sky the sky and the fruits of the earth would be destroyed. One would not get greedy and greedy.
morphology: The story of the king of the sky and the kingdom of the earth is not known to date.

sanskrit: ādātumicchanpadamuttamānāṃ svacetasaivāpahato'dya lokaḥ / patatyaśaṅkaṃ paśuradrikūṭādānīlavallīphalavāñchayaiva //
reference: People are still deluded in their minds in wishing to attain the state of their superiors; but they fall down still lower like beasts (goats) from the top of a hill, in wishing to lay hold on the fruits of a verdant creeper out of their reach.
baseline: One who does not want to get the good things done by his own mind should fall down and make a wish for the welfare of the animals animals and animals.
morphology: One who does not want to get the good things from his own heart would fall down and would get the fruits of the evil beast cow cow and bull.

sanskrit: avāntaranyastanirarthakāṃśacchāyālatāpatraphalaprasūnāḥ / śarīra eva kṣatasaṃpadaśca śvabhradrumā adyatanā narāśca //
reference: Young men spending their wealth in personal gratifications, are as useless as plants growing in the bowels of a deep and inaccessible cavern, which spread their fruits and flowers, leaves and branches and their shades to the use of nobody.
baseline: The body is the fruit of the fruits of the fruit and the body is its own property. It is the body of the brother the brother and the son of a man.
morphology: One who has left the body with the illusion of having left behind a part of his body and leaves has left behind the fruits has lost his body his brother brother and brother and is now dead.

sanskrit: kvacijjanā mārdavasundareṣu kvacitkaṭhoreṣu ca saṃcaranti / deśāntarāleṣu nirantareṣu vanāntakhaṇḍeṣviva kṛṣṇasārāḥ //
reference: Men are found to resemble the black antelopes (in their wanderings):some of them roving about the sweet, soft and beautiful sceneries of the country, and others roaming in sterile tracts and parts of boundless forests.
baseline: The kvācījjana wanders in the wilderness and in the open fields and in rare places. The kṛṣṇa sāra wanders across the country and continuously in the forest and in parts.
morphology: The kvācījñas walk in the wilderness and in the open fields and in rare places in the country. The kṛṣṇa sāra is constantly wandering in the forest.

sanskrit: dhāturnavāni divasaṃ prati bhīṣaṇāni ramyāṇi vā vilulitāntatamākulāni / kāryāṇi kaṣṭaphalapākahatodayāni vismāpayanti na śavasya manāṃsi keṣām //
reference: The daily and diversified acts of nature are all pernicious in their nature; they appear pleasant and ravishing to the heart for a time, but are attended with pain in the end, and fill the mind of the wise with dismay.
baseline: One who does not destroy the mind of the body or the heart of the dead would not be able to do these things.
morphology: Those things which are not good for the body those which are bad for the day those that are good for it those things which do not bear the fruits of suffering and those which destroy the mind of the body.

sanskrit: janaḥ kāmāsakto vividhakukalāceṣṭanaparaḥ sa tu svapne'pyasmiñjagati sulabho nādya sujanaḥ / kriyā duḥkhāsaṅgā'vidhuravidhurā nūnamakhilā na jāne netavyā kathamiva daśā jīvitamayī //
reference: Man is addicted to greediness, and is prone to a variety of wicked shifts and plots; a good man is not now to be seen even in a dream, and there is no act which is free from difficulty. I know not how to pass this state of human life.
baseline: One who is lustful and does not know how to live should be taken away by the efforts of the various arts. One who does not get success in the dream does not suffer from the misfortune sorrow and misery and does nothing wrong.
morphology: One who is lustful and does not know how to live should be taken away by the desire of the people by the effort of various arts by doing the same thing in a dream by making the movement of the body smooth by not doing the action of sorrow without knowing how to do the actions of the poor and poor.

sanskrit: śrīrāma uvāca / yaccedaṃ dṛśyate kiṃcijjagatsthāvarajaṃgamam / tatsarvamasthiraṃ brahmansvapnasaṃgamasaṃnibham //
reference: Rama said:—Whatever we see of all moveable or immovable things in this world, they are all as evanescent as things viewed in a dream.
baseline: One would see that Śrīrama is said to be the seat of the universe. One would find that which is standing on the earth standing on it sitting on the ground and meeting the dream of Brahman.
morphology: One would get to see the image of Śrīrama. One would see that which is standing on the earth which is sitting on the sky and which has the same position as that of Brahman and which is associated with the dream.

sanskrit: śuṣkasāgarasaṃkāśo nikhāto yo'dya dṛśyate / sa prātarabhrasaṃvīto nagaḥ saṃpadyate mune //
reference: The hollow desert that appears as the dried bed of a sea to-day, will be found to-morrow to be a running flood by the accumulation of rain-water in it.
baseline: One who has seen the dry sea the sea and the sea and the waters of the sea in a clear sky would get wealth.
morphology: One who has seen the sea dried up and the sky clean is seen in the sky. He who has not been able to escape from the earth becomes rich in the moon.

sanskrit: yo vanavyūhavistīrṇo vilīḍhagagano mahān / dinaireva sa yātyurvīsamatāṃ kūpatāṃ ca vā //
reference: What is to-day a mountain reaching the sky and with extensive forests on it, is in course of time levelled to the ground, and is afterwards dug into pit.
baseline: One who is a forest forest wilderness forest and wilderness or a great city should go to the king. One who does not want to go into the wilderness should be called a wizard.
morphology: One who is a forest man and has a large forest a big tiger a man who is not a traveller a poor man or an evil person should be killed.

sanskrit: yadaṅgamadya saṃvītaṃ kauśeyasragvilepanaiḥ / digambaraṃ tadeva śvo dūre viśaritā'vaṭe //
reference: The body that is clothed to-day with garments of silk, and decorated with garlands and fragrance, is to be cast away naked into a ditch to-morrow.
baseline: One should worship the Digambara at the same distance on the same day.
morphology: One should worship the Digambara at a distance of one ounce.

sanskrit: yatrādya nagaraṃ dṛṣṭaṃ vicitrācāracañcalam / tatraivodeti divasaiḥ saṃśūnyāraṇyadharmatā //
reference: What is seen to be a city to-day, and busy with the bustle of various occupations, passes in course of a few days into the condition of an uninhabited wilderness.
baseline: Wherever the city is seen in a different way it is said to be a place of worship for many days.
morphology: Wherever the city has been seen the area of practice is different. It is said to be a place of peace and righteousness for days.

sanskrit: yaḥ pumānadya tejasvī maṇḍalānyadhitiṣṭhati / sa bhasmakūṭatāṃ rājandivasairadhigacchati //
reference: The man who is very powerful to-day and presides over principalities, is reduced in a few days to a heap of ashes.
baseline: The one who gives the pumāna the light the ground and the earth the incinerator and the king should be worshipped.
morphology: One who gives the pumana to a bright circle and dominates it would be reduced to ashes. He would be destroyed by the king.

sanskrit: araṇyānī mahābhīmā yā nabhomaṇḍalopamā / patākācchāditākāśā saiva saṃpadyate purī //
reference: The very forest which is so formidable to-day and appears as blue as the azure skies, turns to be a city in the course of time, with its banners hoisted in the air.
baseline: One who is the great pride of the wilderness who is not a part of the sky and who is covered with a flag becomes rich.
morphology: One who is rich in the sky covered with a flag who is the great pride of the wilderness who has a heaven and earth who gets wealth from the sky.

sanskrit: yā latāvalitā bhīmā bhātyadya vipināvalī / divasaireva sā yāti punarmarumahīpadam //
reference: What is (to-day) a formidable jungle of thick forests, turns in time to be a table-land as on the mount Meru.
baseline: The one who is born with a lotus the one who has been given to the sister by Bhima the other one who goes to the temple of Viṇavali after a day would again attain the position of the lord.
morphology: The one who is born with a lotus and the sister of Bhima and the one who has become a virgin would go back to his mother's place after one day.

sanskrit: salilaṃ sthalatāṃ yāti sthalībhavati vāribhūḥ / viparyasyati sarvaṃ hi sakāṣṭhāmbutṛṇaṃ jagat //
