reference: Water becomes land and land becomes water. Thus the world composed of wood, grass and water becomes otherwise with all its contents in course of time.
baseline: The place of salilām becomes sālīm where the land of varībhūr is situated. The earth is divided into three parts.
morphology: The place of salilām becomes sālikām where the land of varībhūr happens to be. The earth is divided into three parts.

sanskrit: anityaṃ yauvanaṃ bālyaṃ śarīraṃ dravyasaṃcayāḥ / bhāvādbhāvāntaraṃ yānti taraṅgavadanāratam //
reference: Our boyhood and youth, bodies and possessions are all but transient things, and they change from one state to another, as the ever fluctuating waves of the ocean.
baseline: The body should be kept in the form of a mass of material things. After the manifestation of the feeling the wave should be sent to it.
morphology: The body should be preserved in the form of a little youth child and the body in the way of the feeling of the mind.

sanskrit: vātāntardīpakaśikhālolaṃ jagati jīvitam / taḍitsphuraṇasaṃkāśā padārthaśrīrjagatrtraye //
reference: Our lives in this (mortal) world, are as unsteady as the flame of a lamp placed at the window, and the splendour of all the objects in the three worlds, is as flickering as the flashing of the lightning.
baseline: One who is alive who is living and who is not living who has the energy of water and the resources of water in the air and the light of fire and who has got the energy from the earth.
morphology: One who is alive who is living who has the energy of water which has the power of the wind who sheds light and light on the earth and who has got the energy from the sun one who has created the earth.

sanskrit: viparyāsamiyaṃ yāti bhūribhūtaparamparā / bījarāśirivājasraṃ pūryamāṇaḥ punaḥpunaḥ //
reference: As a granary stored with heaps of grains is exhausted by its continued waste, so is the stock of life spent away by its repeated respirations.
baseline: One should repeat the tradition of varikāyāsāmya which has been perfected by the sowing of seeds sesamum and other grains.
morphology: One should repeat the tradition of varikāyāsāmya where the seeds are made from a lotus and the seeds of the king are made full.

sanskrit: manaḥpavanaparyastabhūribhūtarajaḥpaṭā / pātotpātaparāvartaparābhinayabhūṣitā //
reference: The mind of man is as fluctuating as a flag waving in the air and filled with the dust of sin, to indicate its wavering between the paths of heaven and hell.
baseline: The leaves are made of the same ground and the leaves of the plant are made out of the leaves and the flowers are made from the leaves.
morphology: After having made the leaves of the plant of the mind one should worship the ground ground and water.

sanskrit: ālakṣyate sthitiriyaṃ jāgatī janitabhramā / nṛttāveśavivṛtteva saṃsārārabhaṭīnaṭī //
reference: The existence of this delusive world, is as the appearance of an actress on the stage, shuffling her vests as she trudges along in her dancing.
baseline: One who is in the position of the world one who is born alive and who is living in the state of ignorance and one who has been in the world of dance and worship is the master of the universe.
morphology: One who is in the position of the world one who is born into the illusion of the universe and who is not in the world of dance is a devotee of this world.

sanskrit: gandharvanagarākāraviparyāsavidhāyinī / apāṅgabhaṅgurodāravyavahāramanoramā //
reference: It's scenes are as changeful and fascinating as those of a magic city; and its dealings as bewitching and momentary as the glances of a giggling girl.
baseline: The conduct of the Gandharvas should be different from that of the cities. It should be described as the conduct of a person who is not able to bear a limb.
morphology: The conduct of a person with a limb and limb should be described as similar to that of a Gandharva a city and a city.

sanskrit: taḍittaralamālokamātanvānā punaḥpunaḥ / saṃsāraracanā rājannṛttasakteva rājate //
reference: The stage of the world presents us a scene of continued dancing (of the sorceress of deception), and the deceptive glances of her eyes resembling the fleeting flashes of lightning.
baseline: The king should be re-constructed by the mother of the people of the land of Tadittarla. He should rule the kingdom of Nritya.
morphology: The king should be re-constructed by the mother of the people of the land of Tadittarla. The king of the kingdom of Nritta would rule the kingdom.

sanskrit: divasāste mahāntaste saṃpadastāḥ kriyāśca tāḥ / sarvaṃ smṛtipathaṃ yātaṃ yāmo vayamapi kṣaṇāt //
reference: The days, the great men, their hey-days and deeds (that are past and gone), are now retained in our memory only, and such must be our cases also in a short time.
baseline: The day is the great end. The wealth and actions are the same. The path of memory should be followed for all of us from time to time.
morphology: The great wealth and deeds should be made available in the same day. All these should be taken to the path of memory. We should also go from moment to moment.

sanskrit: pratyahaṃ kṣayamāyāti pratyahaṃ jāyate punaḥ / adyāpi hatarūpāyā nānto'syā dagdhasaṃsṛteḥ //
reference: Many things are going to decay and many coming anew day by day; and there is yet no end of this accursed course of events in this ever-changeful world.
baseline: Every time I get lost every time it happens again. Even now it is not in the form of a dead body.
morphology: Every time I get lost it happens again. Even now the body is not burnt in the form of a stone.

sanskrit: tiryaktvaṃ puruṣā yānti tiryañco naratāmapi / devāścādevatāṃ yānti kimiveha vibho sthiram //
reference: Men degenerate into lower animals, and those again rise to humanity (by metempsychosis), gods become no-gods, and there is nothing that remains the same.
baseline: One who is not afraid of men one who is afraid of gods and goddesses and one who does not want to be afraid of them is stable.
morphology: One who is obedient to men one who is not afraid of men and one who does not want to be afraid of gods and goddesses one should be able to do this.

sanskrit: racayanraśmijālena rātryahāni punaḥpunaḥ / ativāhya raviḥ kālo vināśāvadhimīkṣate //
reference: The sun displays every thing to light by his rays, and watches over the rotations of days and nights, to witness like time the dissolution of all things.
baseline: The night is again destroyed by the burning of the fire of the raṣma. The night of the river is again washed away by the overflow of water. The black river ends the period of destruction.
morphology: The night is again destroyed by the burning of the fire of the raṣma of the creation. The night of the sun is destroyed by overflow of water. The black river ends the period of destruction.

sanskrit: brahmā viṣṇuśca rudraśca sarvā vā bhūtajātayaḥ / nāśamevānudhāvanti salilānīva vāḍavam //
reference: The gods Brahma, Vishnu and Siva and all material productions, are reduced to nothingness, like the submarine fire subsiding under the waters of the deep.
baseline: Brahma Viṣṇu Rudra and all the other beings of the earth are destroyed.
morphology: Brahma Viṣṇu Rudra and all the other beings are destroyed.

sanskrit: dyauḥ kṣamā vāyurākāśaṃ parvatāḥ sarito diśaḥ / vināśavāḍavasyaitatsarvaṃ saṃśuṣkamindhanam //
reference: The heaven, the earth, the air, the sky, the mountains, the rivers, and all the quarters of the globe, are subject to destruction like the dry fuel by the all-destroying fire of the last day.
baseline: The wind sky mountains the direction of destruction the sun water and fire should be given to all.
morphology: The wind sky mountains the direction of destruction and destruction should be given to all.

sanskrit: dhanāni bāndhavā bhṛtyā mitrāṇi vibhavāśca ye / vināśabhayabhītasya sarvaṃ nīrasatāṃ gatam //
reference: Riches and relatives, friends, servants and affluence, are of no pleasure to him who is in constant dread of death.
baseline: Those who are afraid of destruction and fear of destruction those who are friends with wealth and friends and those who have a bond with a fiancee all these things become dull.
morphology: Those who are afraid of destruction and fear of destruction those who are friends friends allies servants friends etc. who are bound by wealth have gone into silence.

sanskrit: svadante tāvadevaite bhāvā jagati dhīmate / yāvatsmṛtipathaṃ yāti na vināśakurākṣasaḥ //
reference: All these are so long delightful to a sensible man, as the monster of death does not appear before the eye of his mind.
baseline: One who gives his own self one who gives it to the gods and the world is slow. One who does not go down the path of oblivion and destruction would not be able to do so.
morphology: One who gives his own self one who worships the gods the world the earth the path leading to destruction and the path of destruction is not slow.

sanskrit: kṣaṇamaiśvaryamāyāti kṣaṇameti daridratām / kṣaṇaṃ vigatarogatvaṃ kṣaṇamāgatarogatām //
reference: We have prosperity at one moment, succeeded by adversity at another; so we have health at one time, followed by sickness soon after.
baseline: One who is poor for a while becomes ill. One who has ill health for a moment becomes ill for a second.
morphology: One who is poor for a while one who is illiterate for a long time and one who becomes ill for an extended period of time.

sanskrit: pratikṣaṇaviparyāsadāyinā nihatātmanā / jagadbhrameṇa ke nāma dhīmanto hi na mohitāḥ //
reference: What intelligent being is there, that is not misled by these delusions of the world, which represent things otherwise than what they are, and serve to bewilder the mind?
baseline: One should not be seduced by the immortal spirit by the provocation of the world by the illusion of the universe by any illusion.
morphology: One should not be seduced by the immortal spirit by the illusion of the world and by the delusion of life.

sanskrit: tamaḥpaṅkasamālabdhaṃ kṣaṇamākāśamaṇḍalam / kṣaṇa kanakaniṣyandakomalālokasundaram //
reference: (The world is as varying) as the face of the skies; it is now as black as dark clay, and in the next moment bright with the golden hues of fair light.
baseline: One who has got the sum of three parts of the sky for a while one who has not been able to do any work in the past and one who is beautiful in the world of the earth.
morphology: One who has got the sum of three parts of the sky for a while one who has not got the space for awhile one with the lotus and the world is beautiful.

sanskrit: kṣaṇaṃ jaladanīlābjamālāvalitakoṭaram / kṣraṇamuḍḍāmararavaṃ kṣaṇaṃ mūkamiva sthitam //
reference: It is now over-cast by azure clouds resembling the blue lotuses of the lake, and roaring loudly for a time and then being dumb and silent on a sudden:
baseline: A castle with a garland of blue and blue flowers should be placed in the middle of the hill. A temple of pearls and pearls should be kept in the mouth for a while.
morphology: A castle with a garland of blue and blue flowers should be placed for a while. A palace with a muzzle should be kept for a few seconds.

sanskrit: kṣaṇaṃ tārāviracitaṃ kṣaṇamarkeṇa bhūṣitam / kṣaṇamindukṛtāhlādaṃ kṣaṇaṃ sarvabahiṣkṛtam //
reference: Now studded with stars, and now glowing with the glory of the sun;then graced by the pleasant moonbeams, and at last without any light at all.
baseline: One who has chosen the star for a while one who has been blessed with the kāṇma of time and one who is blessed with a moment of happiness is free from all evils.
morphology: One who has chosen the star for a while one who has been blessed with the kāṇma kārna for a moment one whose heart is not broken one with the jaṇma for a minute one in which everything is destroyed.

sanskrit: āgamāpāyaparayā kṣaṇasaṃsthitināśayā / na bibheti hi saṃsāre dhīro'pi ka ivānayā //
reference: Who is there so sedate and firm, that is not terrified at these sudden appearances and their disappearance, and the momentary durations and final dissolution of worldly things?
baseline: One who is patient in the world would not be harmed by the destruction of the situation for a while by the coming and passing.
morphology: One who is patient in the world would not be harmed by the destruction of the situation for a while by the coming and passing.

sanskrit: āpadaḥ kṣaṇamāyānti kṣaṇamāyānti saṃpadaḥ / kṣaṇaṃ janma kṣaṇaṃ mṛtyurmune kimiva na kṣaṇam //
reference: What is the nature of this world, where we are overtaken by adversity at one moment, and elated by prosperity at another, where one is born at a time, and dies away at another?
baseline: One would get wealth by the time of danger by the moment of birth by death by no means.
morphology: One who is born a moment before death would not get wealth. One who dies a moment after birth would get wealth in that moment.

sanskrit: prāgāsīdanya eveha jātastvanyo naro dinaiḥ / sadaikarūpaṃ bhagavankiṃcidasti na susthiram //
reference: One that was something else before, is born as a man in this life, and is changed to another state in course of a few days; thus there is no being that remains steadily in the same state.
baseline: One who is born after having attained the preceptor position would not be able to attain the eternal form of God.
morphology: One who is born without having attained the preceptor status would not be able to attain the eternal form of God.

sanskrit: ghaṭasya paṭatā dṛṣṭā paṭasyāpi ghaṭasthitiḥ / na tadasti na yaddṛṣṭaṃ viparyasyati saṃsṛtau //
reference: A pot is made of clay, and cloth is made of cotton, and they are still the same dull materials of which they are composed: thus there is nothing new in this world that was not seen or known before, and that changes not its form.
baseline: The position of the pit is not the same as that of any other pit. If the pit has been placed on a pit it will not be reversed.
morphology: The position of the pit is not the same as that of any other pit. If the pit has been set on a pit on the other side it will not be reversed.

sanskrit: tanotyutpādayatyatti nihatyāsṛjati kramāt / satataṃ rātryahānīva nivartante naraṃ prati //
reference: The acts of creation and destruction, of diffusion, production, and sustentation follow one another, as the revolution of day and night to man.
baseline: One who creates a man by making the creation of a tree and then ceases to exist in the course of the night. One who destroys a man would get rid of him.
morphology: One who makes a sacrifice by making a sacrifice for the sake of the cause of death would get rid of the loss of life and death. One who does not lose the night would get remission.

sanskrit: aśūreṇa hataḥ śūra ekenāpi hataṃ śatam / prākṛtāḥ prabhutāṃ yātāḥ sarvamāvartyate jagat //
reference: It happens sometimes, that an impotent man slays a hero, and that hundreds are killed by one individual; so also a commoner becomes a noble man, and thus every thing is changeful in this varying world.
baseline: One who is killed by an Assyrian would be killed by a mighty warrior. One who kills a nobleman would be destroyed by the world.
morphology: One who is killed by the king of the Assyrians would be killed by a mighty warrior. One hundred men would be slain by the lord of the gods. All those who are killed by him would be destroyed by the world.

sanskrit: janateyaṃ viparyāsamajasramanugacchati / jaḍaspandaparāmarśāttaraṅgāṇāmivāvalī //
reference: These bodies of men that are always changing their states, are as bodies of waters rising and falling in waves by motion of the winds.
baseline: The people are divided into different parts. The king of the king is pleased with the sound of the roots and the advice of the gods.
morphology: One would get the sermon of the people in a different way. One gets the advice of the roots the voice and the words of the king.

sanskrit: bālyamalpadinaireva yauvanaśrīstato jarā / dehe'pi naikarūpatvaṃ kāsthā bāhyeṣu vastuṣu //
reference: Boyhood lasts but a few days, and then it is succeeded by youth which is as quickly followed by old age: thus there being no identity of the same person, how can one rely on the uniformity of external objects?
baseline: One who has attained the age of puberty after less than one day would become a virgin. One who becomes a virgins in the body would also become a maleficent in the external world.
morphology: One who has attained the age of puberty after a year or less would become a virgin. One who becomes a virgins in the body would also become an infernal in the external world.

sanskrit: kṣaṇamānanditāmeti kṣaṇameti viṣāditām / kṣaṇaṃ saumyatvamāyāti sarvasminnaṭavanmanaḥ //
reference: The mind that gets delighted in a moment and becomes dejected in the next, and assumes likewise its equanimity at another, is indeed as changeful as an actor.
baseline: One who is distressed by the fact that the moment is pleasant the moment being pleasant and the moment becoming gentle one who is not pleased with everything is called a man.
morphology: The moment of happiness is called the moment. Then the moment of sadness is called benevolence. The moment becomes benign. All that happens is called vanavana.

sanskrit: itaścānyaditaścānyaditaścānyadayaṃ vidhiḥ / racayanvastunāyāti khedaṃ līlāsvivārbhakaḥ //
reference: The creator who is ever turning one thing into another in his work of creation, is like a child who makes and breaks his doll without concern.
baseline: One who does so and does not do so would be sorry.
morphology: One who does so would be sorry if he has to make such a gift. One who has not done so would not be sorry.

sanskrit: cinotyutpādayatyatti nihatyāsṛjati kramāt / satataṃ rātryahānīva nivartante naraṃ prati //
reference: The actions of producing and collecting (of grains), of feeding (one's self) and destroying (others), come by turns to mankind like the rotation of day and night.
baseline: One who does not choose to make a sacrifice and then destroys it in the course of the night would get rid of the loss.
morphology: One who makes a sacrifice by making a sacrifice after having prepared a sacrifice for the sake of the cause of death would get rid of the loss of the enemy by making repeated sacrifices.

sanskrit: āvirbhāvatirobhāvabhāgino bhavabhāginaḥ / janasya sthiratāṃ yānti nāpado na ca saṃpadaḥ //
reference: Neither adversity nor prosperity is of long continuance in the case of worldly people, but they are ever subject to appearance and disappearance by turns.
baseline: One who has not experienced the manifestation or the manifestations of the spirit one who has had a share in the affairs of the people and one who does not enjoy the stability and wealth of his people.
morphology: You are the partaker of the manifestations and the manifestation of the emotions. You are not the partakers of the people. You do not want the stability of the world. You get wealth.

sanskrit: kālaḥ krīḍatyayaṃ prāyaḥ sarvamāpadi pātayan / helāvicalitāśeṣacaturācāracañcuraḥ //
reference: Time is a skilful player and plays many parts with ease; but he is chiefly skilled in tragedy, and often plays his tragic part in the affairs of men.
baseline: One should play with the time and spread all the elements in the ground. The rest of the four rituals should be performed with the help of the chakra.
morphology: One should play with the time. One should perform the chakra and the other four chakras after removing all the elements from the ground.

sanskrit: samaviṣamavipākato vibhinnāstribhuvanabhūtaparamparāphalaughāḥ / samayapavanapātitāḥ patanti pratidinamātatasaṃsṛtidrumebhyaḥ //
reference: All beings are produced as fruits in the great forest of the universe, by virtue of their good and bad acts (of past lives): and time like a gust of wind blasts them day by day before their maturity.
baseline: The fruits of the various forms of the earth and the earth are divided into two parts. They fall every day after the rains. The fruits fall from the rivers.
morphology: The fruits of the various forms of the earth and the earth are equal in size and different in size. They fall every day after the fall of the rain or rain.

sanskrit: śrīrāma uvāca / iti me doṣadāvāgnidagdhe mahati cetasi / prasphuranti na bhogāśā mṛgatṛṣṇāḥ saraḥsviva //
reference: Thus is my heart consumed by the wild-fire of those great worldly evils, and there rises in me no desire of enjoying them, as there rises no mirage from a lake.
baseline: O Śrīma one who has not experienced the death of Shri Krishna one that has not suffered the loss of his life and who has suffered the fire has become conscious of me.
morphology: O Śrīma one who has said that he would be guilty of the fire would be great. He would not be pleased by the death of Shri Krishna.

sanskrit: pratyahaṃ yāti kaṭutāmeṣā saṃsārasaṃsthitiḥ / kālapākavaśāllolā rasā nimbalatā yathā //
reference: My existence upon earth gets bitter day by day, and though I have got some experience in it, yet its associations have made me as sour as the Nimba plant by its immersion in water.
baseline: One who has not been able to get rid of the disease would get the condition of the world. One who does not want to suffer from the disease of kalapaka vaśala lola rasa nimbalata etc.
morphology: One who has not been able to get rid of the disease would get the condition of the world. One who does not want to suffer from the disease should get the juice of water from the pot of fire water and water.

sanskrit: vṛddhimāyāti daurjanyaṃ saujanyaṃ yāti tānavam / karañjakarkaśe rājanpratyahaṃ janacetasi //
reference: I see wickedness on the increase, and righteousness on the decline in the mind of man, which like the sour Karanja (crab) fruit, becomes sourer every day.
baseline: The king should make every man aware of the kāranjaka.
morphology: The king should make every man aware of the increase in the amount of money.

sanskrit: bhajyate bhuvi maryādā jhaṭityeva dinaṃ prati / śuṣkeva māṣaśimbīkā ṭaṅkārakaravaṃ vinā //
reference: I see honour is eaten up every day by mutual altercations of men, using harsh words to each other as they crack the nuts under their teeth.
baseline: One who worships the earth should be treated with dignity immediately. One who is dry should eat meat without having to pay taxes.
morphology: One who worships the earth and gains its glory soon one who does not have to pay a penny without having to do so every day.

sanskrit: rājyebhyo bhogapūgebhyaścintāvadbhyo munīśvara / nirastacintākalitā varamekāntaśīlatā //
reference: Too much eagerness for royalty and worldly enjoyments, is equally prejudicial to our welfare; as we loose our future prospects by the former, and our present happiness by the latter.
baseline: The king should worship the gods of the kingdoms and the king of the kingdom.
morphology: The king should worship the gods of the kingdoms and the king of the kingdom the king the lord of the sages and those who do not care.

sanskrit: nānandāya mamodyānaṃ na sukhāya mama striyaḥ / na harṣāya mamārthāśā śāmyāmi manasā saha //
reference: I take no delight in my gardens nor have any pleasure in women; I feel no joy at the prospect of riches, but enjoy my solace in my own heart and mind.
baseline: My wife should not enjoy the garden of my mind for the sake of my happiness. I should not rejoice with my heart for my pleasure.
morphology: My wife should not enjoy the garden with me for the sake of my happiness. I should not rejoice with my mind for the purpose of my pleasure.

sanskrit: anityaścāsukho lokastṛṣṇā tāta durudvahā / cāpalopahataṃ cetaḥ kathaṃ yāsyāmi nirvṛtim //
reference: Frail are the pleasures of the world, and avarice is altogether intolerable; the bustle of business has broken down my heart, and (I know not) where to have my tranquility.
baseline: One who has not been able to see the world would then be in a bad mood. One who does not know how to escape would become a defilement.
morphology: Then the people should be afraid of the enemy. How can I get rid of such a person?

sanskrit: nābhinandāmi maraṇaṃ nābhinandāmi jīvitam / yathā tiṣṭhāmi tiṣṭhāmi tathaiva vigatajvaram //
reference: Neither do I hail death nor am I in love with my life; but remain as I do, devoid of all anxiety and care.
baseline: I do not enjoy death I enjoy living I live as if I were standing.
morphology: I enjoy death happiness joy living as I am standing the flame of the past.

sanskrit: kiṃ me rājyena kiṃ bhogaiḥ kimarthena kimīhitaiḥ / ahaṃkāravaśādetatsa eva galito mama //
reference: What have I to do with a kingdom and with all its enjoyments? Of what avail are riches to me, and what is the end of all our exertions? All these are but requirements of self-love, from which I am entirely free.
baseline: What is my kingdom what is my enjoyment what are my enjoyments and what are those benefits. That is my pride.
morphology: What if I have done with the kingdom what with the enjoyment what for the sake of the ego what is wrong with me.

sanskrit: janmāvalivaratrāyāmindriyagranthayo dṛḍhāḥ / ye baddhāstadvimokṣārthaṃ yatante ye ta uttamāḥ //
reference: The chain of (repeated) births is a bond that binds fast all men by its strong knots of the senses; those striving to break loose from this bondage for their liberation, are (said to be) the best of men.
baseline: Those who are bound by the scriptures of the three senses of the birth and the death are said to be better for the remission.
morphology: Those who are bound by the scriptures of the senses those who are firm in their birth and the three senses are better for the remission of the two diseases.

sanskrit: mathitaṃ māninīlokairmano makaraketunā / komalaṃ khuraniṣpeṣaiḥ kamalaṃ kariṇā yathā //
reference: These haughty damsels whom the god of love employs to ravage the hearts of men, resemble a group of elephants subverting a lotus bed under their feet.
baseline: One should make a lotus with the garland of māṇīla kārna komala khuṇīṣpa kamala lotus karaṇa with the leaves of kāraṇī.
morphology: One should make a lotus with the nectar leaves of manīla kārna komla khūrna and kālama with the flowers of kāraṇī.

sanskrit: adya cetsvacchayā buddhyā munīndra na cikitsyate / bhūyaścittacikitsāyāstatkilāvasaraḥ kutaḥ //
reference: The treatment of the mind with pure reason being neglected now (in youth), it is hard to heal it afterwards (in age), when it admits of no cure.
baseline: If today the sage does not treat with cleansing and wisdom then there is no chance for that to be cured.
morphology: If one does not treat the sage with a clean mind today then there is no chance for that to be cured.

sanskrit: viṣaṃ viṣayavaiṣamyaṃ na viṣaṃ viṣamucyate / janmāntaraghnā viṣayā ekadehaharaṃ viṣam //
reference: It is the worldliness of man that is his true poison, while real poison is no poison to him. It is the poison of worldliness which destroys his future life, while real poison is only locally injurious to him.
baseline: A poison is not a poison except for the matter of the poison. A body is poisoned by the poison of the birth death and death.
morphology: A poison is not a matter of matter. It is a matter for the purpose of the birth and the death of a person.

sanskrit: na sukhāni na duḥkhāni na mitrāṇi na bāndhavāḥ / na jīvitaṃ na maraṇaṃ bandhāya jñasya cetasaḥ //
reference: Neither pleasure nor pain, nor friends nor relatives, nor even life and death, can enchain (affect) the mind that has received the light of truth.
baseline: There are neither pleasures nor sorrows nor friends nor friends neither living nor bound by death.
morphology: There are neither pleasures nor sorrows nor friends nor friends neither living nor bound by death.

sanskrit: tadbhavāmi yathā brahmanpūrvāparavidāṃ vara / vītaśokabhayāyāso jñastathopadiśāśu me //
reference: Teach me, Oh Brahman! that art the best of the learned in the mysteries of the past and future, teach me so that I may soon become like one devoid of grief and fear and worldly troubles, and may have the light of truth beaming upon me.
baseline: The same feeling as that of the Brahman the preceptor the booner the protector of the enemy the enemy should be known to me.
morphology: The same feeling as that of the Brahman the preceptor the booner the enemy of the enemy and the enemy should be known to him.

sanskrit: vāsanājālavalitā duḥkhakaṇṭakasaṃkulā / nipātotpātabahulā bhīmarūpā'jñatāṭavī //
reference: The forest of ignorance is laid over with the snare of desire, it is full of the thorns of misery, and is the dreadful seat of destruction and the danger.
baseline: One who has a desire a network of desires sorrow misfortune misery a combination of afflictions destruction destruction and destruction would be the result of the destruction of many gods.
morphology: One who has a desire a network of passions sorrow consternation misfortune destruction destruction and destruction would become a lot of fear.

sanskrit: krakacāgraviniṣpeṣaṃ soḍhuṃ śaknomyahaṃ mune / saṃsāravyavahārotthaṃ nāśāviṣayavaiśasam //
reference: I can rather suffer myself to be put under the jaws of death with his rows of teeth like saws, but cannot bear the dreadly pains of worldly cares and anxieties.
baseline: I can wash away the waste water from the earth. I can raise the world and destroy it.
morphology: I can destroy the evil spirits of the world. I wish to raise the world and destroy it.

sanskrit: idaṃ nāstīdamastīti vyavahārāñjanabhramaḥ / dhunotīdaṃ calaṃ ceto rajorāśimivānilaḥ //
reference: It is a gloomy error in this world to think that I have this and have not the other; it serves to toss about our minds as a gust of wind disperses the dust of the earth.
baseline: This is the nastīdā of the vyāgarā enjoyment the ambivalence the rhythm of the dhunotī the movement of the chariot and the chaita of the king.
morphology: It is said to be the abode of vyāharā enjoyment. It should be the seat of dhunotī. The seat of king rājorāshimīvani.

sanskrit: tṛṣṇātantulavaprotaṃ jīvasaṃcayamauktikam / cidacchāṅgatayā nityaṃ vikasaccittanāyakam //
reference: It is the thread of avarice that links together all living beings like a chaplet of pearls; the mind serves to twirl about this chain, but pure consciousness sits quiet to observe its rotation.
baseline: One who is born with a thirst a desire for life and a desire to grow and develop is always a member of the body.
morphology: One who is born with a thirst a desire for life a spirit a body a mind and a body should develop in the form of a small body and develop constantly.

sanskrit: saṃsārahāramaratiḥ kālavyālavibhūṣaṇam / troṭayāmyahamakrūraṃ vāgurāmiva kesarī //
reference: I who am devoid of desires, would like to break this ornamental chain of worldliness, hanging about me as a deadly serpent, in the same manner, as a lion breaks asunder the net.
baseline: The garland of water water earth earth and earth the garland the sword the arrow the horse the elephant the king of war the goddess of war and the goddess kesari are to be worshipped.
morphology: The garland of water water and flowers should be made with the garlands of samsara garland water sandal and water.

sanskrit: nīhāraṃ hṛdayāṭavyāṃ manastimiramāśu me / kena vijñānadīpena bhindhi tattvavidāṃvara //
reference: Do you now, O most learned sage, scatter the mist which has overspread the forest of my heart, and the darkness which has overcast my mind, by the light of true knowledge.
baseline: The neehara should be placed in the heart the heart and the heart. Then one should worship the gods with the lamp of knowledge.
morphology: The neehara should be placed in the heart the heart and the heart. One should worship the gods with the lamp of knowledge.

sanskrit: vidyanta eveha na te mahātman durādhayo na kṣayamāpnuvanti / ye saṅgamenottamamānasānāṃ niśātamāṃsīva niśākareṇa //
reference: There are no anxieties, O sage! which cannot be put to an end by the society of good minded men; the darkness of night can be well removed by moon-beams.
baseline: Those great men who do not suffer evil and do not want to be destroyed by the illusion of the present. Those who associate with the best of the mind with the evil spirit and the evil spirits are not able to be harmed.
morphology: Those great men who do not suffer from misfortune and do not want to suffer loss are those who associate themselves with the best of men those who are not willing to suffer death.

sanskrit: āyurvāyuvighaṭṭitābhrapaṭalīlambāmbuvadbhaṅguraṃ bhogā meghavitānamadhyavilasatsaudāminīcañcalāḥ / lolāyauvanalālanājalarayaścetyākalayya drutaṃ mudraivādya dṛḍhārpitā nanu mayā citte ciraṃ śāntaye //
reference: Life is as fickle as a drop of water pending on a mass of clouds blown away by the winds. Our enjoyments are as unsteady as the lightning that flickers in the midst of clouds. The pleasures of youth are as slippery as water. With these reflections in my mind, I have subdued them all under the province of peace and tranquility.
baseline: Having said this before having made a fast vow having said that I am ready to go back and forth in peace in my heart.
morphology: Having said this before having made a fast vow having said the words ayurveda vyūvī bhra pāṭa lilā limbu ḍhungu bhā bha bhavītā vilāsā sādāminī kāla avana lālā nājala and nāla. Having made a firm vow I am not at peace in my heart.

sanskrit: śrīrāma uvāca / evamabhyutthitānarthaśatasaṃkaṭakoṭare / jagadālokya nirmagnaṃ mano mananakardame //
reference: Seeing the world thus ingulphed amidst the abyss of hundreds of rising dangers and difficulties, my mind is immerged in the mire of anxieties.
baseline: O Śrīma one who has been raised from the ground in the midst of a hundred cramped corners and who has gone into the world and destroyed the mind in the act of mind.
morphology: O Śrīma one who has been raised from the ground in the midst of a hundred cramped corners and who has gone to the world and destroyed the mind and mind.

sanskrit: mano me bhramatīvedaṃ saṃbhramaścopajāyate / gātrāṇi parikampante patrāṇīva jarattaroḥ //
reference: My mind is wandering everywhere and I am struck with fear at every thing; my limbs are shaking with fear like the leaves of a withered tree.
baseline: The mind becomes illusion and confusion. The letters are spread around in the dimensions.
morphology: The mind becomes illusion and confusion. The dimensions of the leaves and leaves are circumscribed.

sanskrit: anāptottamasaṃtoṣadhairyotsaṅgākulā matiḥ / śūnyāspadā bibhetīha bālevālpabaleśvarā //
reference: My mind is bewildered by impatience for its want of true contentment, just as a young woman is afraid in a desert for want of the company of her strong handed husband.
baseline: O Balāva the supreme god of happiness happiness longevity good fortune good conduct good sense good will good faith goodness good and bad will and blissful nature are to be worshipped.
morphology: O Balāva the supreme one one who is satisfied with the best of things and one who does not want to suffer the loss of the body one should be blessed with the blissful child.

sanskrit: vikalpebhyo luṭhantyetāścāntaḥkaraṇavṛttayaḥ / śvabhrebhya iva sāraṅgāstucchālambaviḍambitāḥ //
reference: The thoughts of my mind are entangled in my desire for worldly enjoyments, as stags are caught in the pit strewn with grass over it.
baseline: One who has been robbed by the choice of the enemy and who has made a mistake in the heart should be made to wear a robe with a string and a piece of cloth.
morphology: Those who steal from the options and those who do not want to do so should be made to wear the garlands of the heart. The garlands should be kept as long as possible.

sanskrit: avivekāspadā bhraṣṭāḥ kaṣṭe rūḍhā na satpade / andhakūpamivāpannā varākāścakṣurādayaḥ //
reference: The senses of an unreasonable man, ever run astray to the wrong and never turn to the right way; so the eyes of a blind man lead him but to fall into the pit.
baseline: One who is illiterate and corrupt should not suffer in the absence of good. One who does not suffer from darkness should not be afraid of evil spirits evil spirits and evil spirits.
morphology: One who is illiterate and corrupt should not suffer in the absence of good. One who does not suffer from darkness and evil should not do evil.

sanskrit: nāvasthitimupāyāti na ca yāti yathepsitam / cintā jīveśvarāyattā kānteva priyasadmani //
reference: Human thoughts are linked to the animal soul as consorts to their lords. They can neither sit idle nor ramble at liberty, but must remain as wives under the control of their husbands.
baseline: The position of the boat is not good. The thought that is desired in the world is good and good.
morphology: One who does not get the position of the ship and who wants to stay in it is said to be dear to him.

sanskrit: śagdhi pūrdhi pra yaṁsi ca śiśīhi prāsi udaram pūṣan iha kratum vidaḥ
reference: Be gracious to us, fill us full, give, feed us, and invigorate: O Pûshan, find thou power for this.
baseline: One should worship the sāgdhi purdhi and the vīṣīsī as the disciple the abdominal part of the body and the flowers.
morphology: The disciple should be worshipped with the shagdhi purdhi and the disciple with the prāsīsī abdominal mantras.

sanskrit: eṣo iti uṣāḥ apūrvyā vi ucchati priyā divaḥ stuṣe vām aśvinā br̥hat
reference: Now Morning with her earliest light shines forth, dear Daughter of the Sky: High, Aṣvins, I extol your praise,
baseline: O Esho one who is blessed with the divine form of the goddess Uṣa is blessed by the goddess Vī. One who is worshipped by the equines is great.
morphology: O Esau the great goddess of the sun the goddess of love and the goddess Śiva the supreme goddess of wealth and the great god of the sky.

sanskrit: yā dasrā sindhu mātarā manotarā rayīṇām dhiyā devā vasu vidā
reference: Sons of the Sea, mighty to save discoverers of riches, ye Gods with deep thought who find out wealth.
baseline: O lord Vasu the god of the mind the king of the heart and the goddess of the body are known to have measured the amount of sindhu on the day of dusra.
morphology: O lord Vasu the god of the mind the king of the heart and the goddess of the body are known to have measured the amount of sindhu on the day of dusra.

sanskrit: vacyante vām kakuhāsaḥ jūrṇāyām adhi viṣṭapi yat vām rathaḥ vi bhiḥ patāt
reference: Your giant coursers hasten on over the region all in flames, – When your car flies with winged steeds.
baseline: It is said that the chariot should be placed on the ground and the horse should be thrown down.
morphology: It is said that a horse should be thrown into the lake and the chariot should be pulled down.

sanskrit: haviṣā jāraḥ apām piparti papuriḥ narā pitā kuṭasya carṣaṇiḥ
reference: He, liberal, lover of the flood, Lord of the House, the vigilant, Chiefs! with oblations feeds you full.
baseline: One should offer a jar of water to his father. One should not drink water from the pit.
morphology: One should offer a jar of water to his father. One should not offer water to the father.

sanskrit: ādāraḥ vām matīnām nāsatyā mata vacasā pātam somasya dhr̥ṣṇu yā
reference: Ye have regard unto our hymns, Nâsatyas, thinking of our words: Drink boldly of the Soma juice.
baseline: One who does not believe in the belief of the gods should offer the leaves of the soma to the god Dhruśṇu.
morphology: One who does not believe in the existence of gods should eat the leaves of the sāma and the druṣṇu leaves.

sanskrit: yā naḥ pīparat aśvinā jyotiṣmatī tamaḥ tiraḥ tām asme iti rāsāthām iṣam
reference: Vouchsafe to us, O Aṣvin Pair, such strength as, with attendant light, May through the darkness carry us.
baseline: If one does not drink the water one would get the flame from the omens. The water would be called amma.
morphology: One who does not drink the water should say that he would get light from the equines and that he should get the water from the arrow.

sanskrit: ā naḥ nāvā matīnām yātam pārāya gantave yuñjāthām aśvinā ratham
reference: Come in the ship of these our hymns to bear you to the hither shore O Aṣvins, harness ye the car.
baseline: The chariot should be made of two horses.
morphology: The chariot should be made with the horses of the same name after having crossed the path of the devotees by a boat.

sanskrit: aritram vām divaḥ pr̥thu tīrthe sindhūnām rathaḥ dhiyā yuyujre indavaḥ
reference: The heaven's wide vessel is your own on the flood's shore your chariot waits Drops, with the hymn, have been prepared.
baseline: The chariot of the sindhus should be placed on the earth and the goddess Aritra on the other side of the earth.
morphology: The chariots of the sindhus are worshipped in the temple of āritra vam and diva.

sanskrit: divaḥ kaṇvāsaḥ indavaḥ vasu sindhūnām pade svam vavrim kuha dhitsathaḥ
reference: Kaṇvas, the drops are in the heaven; the wealth is at the waters' place: Where will ye manifest your form?
baseline: One who worships the god Vāsudeva Kanavasa Indava Vasu Sīndhu and others should worship the goddess Vāvira.
morphology: One who worships the goddess Kanavasa the goddess of water and the goddess Vasu should worship Vāvrī in the position of the goddess Sīndhu.

sanskrit: abhūt oṁ iti bhāḥ oṁ iti aṁśave hiraṇyam prati sūryaḥ vi akhyat jihvayā asitaḥ
reference: Light came to lighten up the branch, the Sun appeared as it were gold: And with its-tongue shone forth the dark.
baseline: The sun should be said to be the abhuta obhaya ohbhaya and to Hiranya.
morphology: The sun should be said to be the abhuta obhaya ohbhava and to Hiranyā.

sanskrit: abhūt oṁ iti pāram etave panthā r̥tasya sādhu yā adarśi vi srutiḥ divaḥ
reference: The path of sacrifice was made to travel to the farther goal: The road of heaven was manifest.
baseline: The path beyond that is called abhutu oma the path of the sādhu of the seasons. The sādhudhu who is the manifestation of the sun and the sun should be worshipped in this manner.
morphology: The path beyond that is called abhutu oma the path of the sādhu of the seasons. The path of a sage should be seen by the goddess Śruti.

sanskrit: tat tat it aśvinoḥ avaḥ jaritā prati bhūṣati made somasya pipratoḥ
reference: The singer of their praise awaits whatever grace the Aṣvins give, who save when Soma gladdens them.
baseline: That is the same as that of the god Avāśvīṇu. He worships the goddess Sarita in the form of the son of Sūma.
morphology: That is the same as that of the equines. They worship the goddess Zārita in the form of the son of Sāma.

sanskrit: vāvasānā vivasvati somasya pītyā girā manuṣvat śambhūitiśam bhū ā gatam
reference: Ye dwellers with Vivasvan come, auspicious, as to Manu erst; come to the Soma and our praise.
baseline: One who has fallen down after having drunk the cup of soma would get eighty feet of earth.
morphology: One should worship the goddess Vāvasana and the goddess Sūma. One should drink the drink of the goddess Śambhu the eighty-fourth part of the earth.

sanskrit: yuvoḥ uṣāḥ anu śriyam pari jmanoḥ upa ācarat r̥tā vanathaḥ aktu bhiḥ
reference: O circumambient Aṣvins, Dawn follows the brightness of your way: Approve with beams our solemn rites.
baseline: One who worships Yūva Usha Anū Śrīma and others would be worshipped by Rīta and Vāṇatha.
morphology: One who worships the goddess Yūva Usha Anū Śrīma and others should worship the goddess Rita and the forest.

sanskrit: ubhā pibatam aśvinā ubhā naḥ śarma yacchatam avidriyābhiḥ ūtibhiḥ
reference: Drink ye of our libations, grant protection, O ye Aṣvins Twain, With aids which none may interrupt.
baseline: One who drinks water from the ground should not drink from the feet of the horses. One who does not drink water from a horse should drink from those who do not know the nature of the body.
morphology: One who drinks from the ground one who does not drink from the sky and one who is not afraid of the sky should drink from it.

sanskrit: ayam vām madhumat tamaḥ sutaḥ somaḥ r̥ta vr̥dhā tam aśvinā pibatam tiraḥ ahnyam dhattam ratnāni dāśuṣe
reference: ASVINS, for you who strengthen Law this sweetest Soma hath been shed. Drink this expressed ere yesterday and give riches to him who offers it.
baseline: This is the vāma the honey the sūma and the soma. The sāmā should be drunk by the horsemen. The arrow should be washed with the gems.
morphology: This is the vāma the honey the sūma and the soma. The sāmā should be drunk with the āśvīra and the arrow should be washed with the gems and the dāśu.

sanskrit: tri vandhureṇa tri vr̥tā su peśasā rathena ā yātam aśvinā kaṇvāsaḥ vām brahma kr̥ṇvanti adhvare teṣām su śr̥ṇutam havam
reference: Come, O ye Aṣvins, mounted on your triple car three-seated, beautiful of form To you at sacrifice the Kaṇvas send the prayer: graciously listen to their call.
baseline: The three vandhuras are followed by the three vortices the pāśis the chariots the horses the kanvasas the brahmins.
morphology: The three vandhura three virtha the pāśis the chariots the horses the kanvasas the brahmins and the horses are heard in the following lines.

sanskrit: aśvinā madhumat tamam pātam somam r̥ta vr̥dhā atha adya dasrā vasu bibhratā rathe dāsvāṁsam upa gacchatam
reference: O Aṣvins, ye who strengthen Law, drink ye this sweetest Soma juice. Borne on your wealth-fraught car come ye this day to him who offers, ye of wondrous deeds.
baseline: Having wasted the month of Soma the leaves should be washed with honey with the leaves of the horses. Today the king of Dāsara would be misguided and would go to his wife in the chariot.
morphology: One who has lost his feet in the month of Soma by riding a horse has lost it. One who becomes a servant in the chariot and goes to the king on the day of Dāśrā is misguided.

sanskrit: triṣ sadhasthe barhiṣi viśva vedasā madhvā yajñam mimikṣatam kaṇvāsaḥ vām suta somāḥ abhi dyavaḥ yuvām havante aśvinā
reference: Omniscient Aṣvins, on the thrice-heaped grass bedew with the sweet juice the sacrifice. The sons of Kaṇva, striving heavenward, call on you with draughts of Soma juice out-poured.
baseline: O Visva the one who has left the temple after having meditated on the Vedas and performed the sacrifice one who is sitting on the ground should offer oblations. One who is sleeping on the right side of the temple should worship the gods. The gods are worshipped by the equines.
morphology: The sacrifice should be performed by the disciple of the god Viṣṇu on the third day of the month of Sādhya. The disciple should be worshipped with the scripture vīśvīva vedaśa. The priest should be seated on the seat of the horse.

sanskrit: yābhiḥ kaṇvam abhiṣṭi bhiḥ pra āvatam yuvam aśvinā tābhiḥ su asmān avatam śubhaḥ patī iti pātam somam r̥ta vr̥dhā
reference: O Aṣvins, with those aids wherewith ye guarded Kaṇva carefully, Keep us, O hords of Splendour: drink the Soma juice, ye strengtheners of holy law.
baseline: The kanva should be worshipped by the priest the young man should be offered to the priest and the wife should be given the auspicious leaves of the husband.
morphology: Having worshipped the kāṇva of the king and having worshipped him the young man should come to us with the arms of the goddess as soon as possible. He should offer us the auspicious leaves of the husband.

sanskrit: su dāse dasrā vasu bibhratā rathe pr̥kṣaḥ vahatam aśvinā rayim samudrāt uta vā divaḥ pari asme iti dhattam puru spr̥ham
reference: O Mighty Ones, ye gave Sudâs abundant food, brought on your treasure-laden car; So now vouchsafe to us the wealth which many crave, either from heaven or from the sea.
baseline: One who is a servant or a servant one who is misguided by the chariot one that is driven by the horse or by the sea or by a divinity is said to be a cow.
morphology: One who is a servant of a dāśra one who is misguided by the chariot one that is driven by the horse one with the sea or the other or one who carries the sun or the sun is said to be in us.

sanskrit: yat nāsatyā parāvati yat vā sthaḥ adhi turvaśe ataḥ rathena su vr̥tā naḥ ā gatam sākam sūryasya raśmi bhiḥ
reference: Nâsatyas, whether ye be far away or close to Turvaṣa, Borne on your lightly-rolling chariot come to us, together with the sunbeams come.
baseline: One who does not do any work on the earth or on the other side of the earth should not be carried away by the chariot. One who has not gone past the rays of the sun should be sent to the sky.
morphology: One who does not want to go into the abode of the demon should not go out with the chariot or the sun the rays of the sun.

sanskrit: arvāñcā vām saptayaḥ adhvara śriyaḥ vahantu savanā it upa iṣam pr̥ñcantā su kr̥te su dānave ā barhiḥ sidatam narā
reference: So let your coursers, ornaments of sacrifice, bring you to our libations here. Bestowing food on him who acts and gives aright, sit, Chiefs, upon the sacred grass.
baseline: O Śrīva one should carry seven cubits of water with him. One should ask this subaśma for the same. One would get a cow for the sake of the god.
morphology: The king should carry seven cubits of water with him. He should ask for the same amount of water. The king would offer a cow to the god.

sanskrit: tena nāsatyā ā gatam rathena sūrya tvacā yena śaśvat ūhathuḥ dāśuṣe vasu madhvaḥ somasya pītaye
reference: Come, O Nâsatyas, on your car decked with a sunbright canopy, Whereon ye ever bring wealth to the worshipper, to drink the Soma's pleasant juice.
baseline: Then the sun should be cast into the chariot and the skin should be washed away with it. The sun should not be cast in the form of a cow and the mother should drink the drink of the sun.
morphology: Then the sun should be cast into the sea with the chariot and the skin should be washed away with the sun. Then the king should be seated on the seat of the elephant.

sanskrit: ukthebhiḥ arvāk avase puruvasūitipuru vasū arkaiḥ ca ni hvayāmahe śaśvat kaṇvānām sadasi priye hi kam somam papathuḥ aśvinā
reference: With lauds and songs of praise we call them down to us, that they, most rich, may succour us; For ye have ever in the Kaṇvas' well-loved house, O Aṣvins, drunk the Soma juice.
baseline: One should worship the goddess Arvaka with the uttheya leaves puruśuṭipu kasu arkās and svāśvatī kāṇvas and sādāśī pārīya kāma soma pāpātu.
morphology: One should worship the goddess Arvaka with the uttheya leaves puru sūtipu kasu arka sāśvatā kāṇva sudasī pāpātu hī kām soma asvīṇa as well as others.

sanskrit: saha vāmena naḥ uṣaḥ vi uccha duhitaḥ divaḥ saha dyumnena br̥hatā vibhāvari rāyā devi dāsvatī
reference: DAWN on us with prosperity, O Ushas, Daughter of the Sky, Dawn with great glory, Goddess, Lady of the Light, dawn thou with riches, Bounteous One.
baseline: O lord Uṣa the highest among the gods is worshipped with the vamāṇas and the great goddess Dvīmā is worshipping with the diyumṇas.
morphology: O lord Uṣa should be worshipped with the left hand and the upper arm with the right hand and with the forehead with the diṣṇa.

sanskrit: aśva vatīḥ go matīḥ viśva suvidaḥ bhūri cyavanta vastave ut īraya prati mā sūnr̥tāḥ uṣaḥ coda rādhaḥ maghonām
reference: They, bringing steeds and kine, boon-givers of all wealth, have oft sped forth to lighten us. O Ushas, waken up for me the sounds of joy: send us the riches of the great.
baseline: One who does not behave like a horse or a cow or a bull or a man who is good in the world or a person or a thing should not be attracted by the fire. One who is not afraid of the fire should be beaten by the god Radha.
morphology: The behavior of horses cows gods gods and goddesses should be worshipped in the world. One should not be afraid of the evil spirits. One who does not want to be harmed by the evil one should be beaten by the god Uṣa.

sanskrit: uvāsa uṣāḥ ucchāt ca nu devī jīrā rathānām ye asyāḥ ācaraṇeṣu dadhrire samudre na śravasyavaḥ
reference: Ushas hath dawned, and now shall dawn, the Goddess, driver forth of cars Which, as she cometh nigh, have fixed their thought on her, like glory-seekers on the flood.
baseline: Ovaśa Uṣa and Uṣṭha are the nine goddesses of the chariots. Those who do not hear the sound of the sea at the time of this ritual should not do so.
morphology: Ovaśa Uṣa and Uṣṭha are the nine goddesses of the chariots. Those who do not hear the sound of the sea at the time of this ritual should be worshipped.

sanskrit: uṣaḥ ye te pra yāmeṣu yuñjate manaḥ dānāya sūrayaḥ atra aha tat kaṇvaḥ eṣām kaṇva tamaḥ nāma gr̥ṇāti nr̥ṇām
reference: Here Kaṇva, chief of Kaṇva's race, sings forth aloud the glories of the heroes' names,– The. princes who, O Ushas, as thou comest near, direct their thoughts to liberal gifts.
baseline: The sun should be placed here. Those who worship the sun should pay tribute to the gods. These should be worshipped by the sun. These are the names of the gods and goddesses.
morphology: The sun should be placed here in the form of the heart and the kanva should be named after the kanaṇa.

sanskrit: ā gha yoṣāiva sūnarī uṣāḥ yāti pra bhuñjatī jarayantī vr̥janam pat vat īyate ut pātayati pakṣiṇaḥ
reference: Like a good matron Ushas comes carefully tending everything: Rousing all life she stirs all creatures that have feet, and makes the birds of air fly up.
baseline: O yosha the daughter of the sun Uṣa the goddess of the earth is worshipped by the king. Vrījana is worshipping the wife of the king and the birds are worshipping her.
morphology: O yosha the daughter of the goddess Usha when she has gone to the ground with her husband she will destroy the birds.

sanskrit: vi yā sr̥jati samanam vi arthinaḥ padam na veti odatī vayaḥ naki ḥ te paptivāṁsaḥ āsatevi uṣṭau vājinī vati
reference: She sends the busy forth, each man to his pursuit: delay she knows not as she springs. O rich in opulence, after thy dawning birds that have flown forth no longer rest.
baseline: One who creates the vīsāmanā vīrthaṇī sāmāṇā and does not read the verses should say that the vāṇas should be worshipped. One who does not do so would be called a vājini.
morphology: One who creates the vī one who equals others and who does not get the position of the arhtiyas should read the scriptures. He should not repeat the words of the prophets. The vājini should come and worship the goddess.

sanskrit: eṣā ayukta parāvataḥ sūryasya ut ayanāt adhi śatam rathebhiḥ su bhagā uṣāḥ iyam vi yāti abhi mānuṣān
reference: This Dawn hath yoked her steeds afar, beyond the rising of the Sun: Borne on a hundred chariots she, auspicious Dawn, advances on her way to Men.
baseline: This is said to be the best way to escape the sun from the sky and one hundred chariots should be driven away by usha.
morphology: This is said to be the same as that of the sun. One who has gone from the sun to the sky with the chariots of hundred and fifty yatras one who has left the earth and has gone to the people.

sanskrit: viśvam asyāḥ nanāma cakṣase jagat jyotiḥ kr̥ṇoti sūnarī apa dveṣaḥ maghonī divaḥ uṣāḥ ucchat apa sridhaḥ
reference: To meet her glance all living creatures bend them down: Excellent One, she makes the light. Ushas, the Daughter of the Sky, the opulent, shines foes and enmities away.
baseline: The light of the world is called Visva this name the eye the sun the hatred the night the day of Mahogany Usha the high god.
morphology: The light of the world is called Visva the name of the universe is Nāna the eye the sun the abode of malice the sky the moon the day of the sun and the sun of usha are the highest.

sanskrit: uṣaḥ ā bhāhi bhānunā candreṇa duhitaḥ divaḥ āvahantī bhūri asmabhyam saubhagam vi ucchantī diviṣṭiṣu
reference: Shine on us with thy radiant light, O Ushas, Daughter of the Sky, Bringing to us great store of high felicity, and bearning on our solemn rites.
baseline: Ośa a bhahi bhaṇu the moon milk water the sun the sky water and the sun are worshipped.
morphology: Ośa the sister of Bhanu the goddess of the moon the sun the moon and the sun are worshipped.

sanskrit: viśvasya hi prāṇanam jīvanam tve iti vi yat ucchasi sūnari sā naḥ rathena br̥hatā vibhāvari śrudhi citra maghe havam
reference: For in thee is each living creature's breath and life, when, Excellent! thou dawnest forth. Borne on thy lofty car, O Lady of the Light, hear, thou of wondrous wealth, our call.
baseline: One who has attained the height of life by the chariot should not think big. He should be heard in the form of a figure.
morphology: One who has attained the height of life by the chariot should not think of the greatness of the image.

sanskrit: uṣaḥ vājam hi vaṁsva yaḥ citraḥ mānuṣe jane tena ā vaha su kr̥taḥ adhvarān upa ye tvā gr̥ṇanti vahnayaḥ
reference: O Ushas, win thyself the strength which among men is wonderful. Bring thou thereby the pious unto holy rites, those who as priests sing praise to thee.
baseline: The image made by a man should be made to look like a vājā. The images made by him should be considered as the subjunctive of the gods.
morphology: The image made by a man should be used as a vājā and the images made by him should be taken by those who worship him.

sanskrit: viśvān devān ā vaha soma pītaye antarikṣāt uṣaḥ tvam sā asmāsu ghāḥ go mat aśva vat ukthyam uṣaḥ vājam su vīryam
reference: Bring from the firmament, O Ushas, all the Gods, that they may drink our Soma juice, And, being what thou art, vouchsafe us kine and steeds, strength meet for praist and hero might.
baseline: O Visva the gods O Sūma the one who drinks water from space Ośa he who pierces the earth the cow the horse the elephant the Śuṇa and the semen.
morphology: O Visva the gods the sun the water the sky the cow the horse the fire the vajma the semen the Śiva the blood and the blood.

sanskrit: yasyāḥ ruśantaḥ arcayaḥ prati bhadrāḥ adr̥kṣata sā naḥ rayim v iśva vāram su peśasam uṣāḥ dadātu sugmyam
reference: May Ushas whose auspicious rays are seen resplendent round about, Grant us great riches, fair in form, of all good things, wealth which light labour may attain.
baseline: One who has not been blessed by the priest with the rosary should not be given to the priest. One who does not want to be worshipped by the lord should be given the penis of Usha every week.
morphology: The one who has not been blessed by the priest with a piece of cloth should not be given to the priest. He should not give it to usha the wife of the god.

sanskrit: ye cit hi tvām r̥ṣayaḥ pūrve ūtaye juhūre avase mahi sā naḥ stomān abhi gr̥ṇīhi rādhasā uṣaḥ śukreṇa śociṣā
reference: Mighty One, whom the R̥ishis of old time invoked for their protection and their help, O Ushas, graciously answer our songs of praise with bounty and with brilliant light.
baseline: The sage should be worshipped in the east in the morning and in the evening. He should not be praised and should be taken away. Radha Uṣa Sukra and others should be worshiped.
morphology: The sage who has worshipped you in the east should be worshipped in the morning. He should not praise you and take you away. The goddess Radhasana Uṣa and Sūkara should be worshiped in the evening.

sanskrit: uṣaḥ yat adya bhānunā vi dvārau r̥ṇavaḥ divaḥ pra naḥ yacchatāt avr̥kam pr̥thu chardiḥ pra devi go matīḥ iṣaḥ
reference: Ushas, as thou with light to day hast opened the twin doors of heaven, So grant thou us a dwelling wide and free from foes. O Goddess, give us food with kine.
baseline: Ośa the goddess of the cow and the god of religion should be worshipped in the morning. If one does not pay the debtors in the doorway and day then one should not give the debtor the money.
morphology: Ośa the goddess of the cow and the god of religion is said to be the one who would not pay the debtors in the gates and the earth.

sanskrit: sam naḥ rāyā br̥hatā viśva peśasā mimikṣva sam il̥ābhiḥ ā sam dyumnena viśva turā uṣaḥ mahi sam vājaiḥ vājinī vati
reference: Bring us to wealth abundant, sent in every shape, to plentiful refreshing food, To all-subduing splendour, Ushas, Mighty One, to strength, thou rich in spoil and wealth.
baseline: The vājini should be sung with the syllable sāma nā raya bṛhata vīśva pāśisā mīmīksvī sāmī lāla aa sā mām diumna vīṣva tura māhī samā vajā.
morphology: The viṣva the great one the vivaśa the pāśis the mīmīksvā the sāmī the āsam and the vājini the Vivaśva Tura Uṣa Mahi Sām Vājā are the instruments.

sanskrit: uṣaḥ bhadrebhiḥ ā gahi divaḥ cit rocanāt adhi vahantu aruṇa psavaḥ upa tvā sominaḥ gr̥ham
reference: E'EN from above the sky's bright realm come, Ushas, by auspicious ways: Let red steeds bear thee to the house of him who pours the Soma, juice.
baseline: O Śuṣa the lord of the earth who is worshipped by the devotees the king of the sun the goddess of the sky the god of fire the son of arauna and the lord who is the master of the house should be worshipped.
morphology: O Śuṣa the lord of the earth the king of the sun the god of the sky the goddess of the moon the son of Āruna the mother of Sūmī the wife of the king the husband of the goddess Uṣa.

sanskrit: su peśasam sukham ratham yam adhi asthāḥ uṣaḥ tvam tena su śravasam janam pra ava adya duhitaḥ divaḥ
reference: The chariot which thou mountest, fair of shape, O Ushas light to move,– Therewith, O Daughter of the Sky, aid men of noble fame today.
baseline: O Śuṣa pesasama sukhā chariot the highest form of the body the sun sound sound and sound are given to the people.
morphology: O Śuṣa the superior of the chariot you are the one who gives the sound of the voice to the people. He should be blessed with milk today.

sanskrit: vayaḥ cit te patatriṇaḥ dvipat catuḥ pat arjuni uṣaḥ pra āran r̥tūn anu divaḥ antebhyaḥ pari
reference: Bright Ushas, when thy times return, all quadrupeds and bipeds stir, And round about flock winged birds from all theboundaries of heaven.
baseline: The three pitchers are divided into two parts. The four pitchers of the chariot are named after Arjuna Uṣa and the two chariots are given for the end of the seasons.
morphology: Ośāṇu the fourth son of Arjuna who is the wife of three sons named Vāya the third son of Pratipāta and the fourth daughter named Uṣa the last son of Avārtha the eighth son of Uṣṇu and the last of the two sons named Anū.

sanskrit: vyi ucchantī hi raśmi bhiḥ viśvam ābhāsi rocanam tām tvām uṣaḥ vasu yavaḥ gīḥ bhiḥ kaṇvāḥ ahūṣata
reference: Thou dawning with thy beams of light illumest all the radiant realm. Thee, as thou art, the Kaṇvas, fain for wealth, have called with sacred songs.
baseline: O rāśmi bhi the manifestation of the universe one who exalts the vyā yavā gī bī kānvā and makes the rocana sound.
morphology: O rāśmi the manifestation of the universe the vyāṣmī and the vīṣma are the manifestations. The vāṣuṣa vāśuśu yava gī bhi kāṇva abhūśa nāśvā are the incarnations.

sanskrit: yena pāvaka cakṣasā bhuraṇyantam janān anu tvam varuṇa paśyasi
reference: With that same eye of thine wherewith thou lookest brilliant Varuṇa, Upon the busy race of men,
baseline: You see Varuṇa looking at the people with the eyes of a poor man and the eye of a fool.
morphology: O Varuna you see the people who have been killed by the evil eye. You see them as far as Bhruṇa.

sanskrit: ut yan adya mitra mahaḥ ārohan ut tarām divam hr̥t rogam mama sūrya harimāṇam ca nāśaya
reference: Rising this day, O rich in friends, ascending to the loftier heaven, Sûrya remove my heart's disease, take from me this my yellow hue.
baseline: O friend of mine who has ascended the mountain today may you destroy my heart disease my sun my sky and my earth.
morphology: O friend of mine who has climbed the mountain today destroy the disease of my heart and my sun the sun and the sky.

sanskrit: śukeṣu me harimāṇam ropaṇākāsu dadhmasi atho iti hāridraveṣu me harimāṇam ni dadhmasi
reference: To parrots and to starlings let us give away my yellowness, Or this my yellowness let us transfer to Haritâla trees.
baseline: In the fields of flowers one should eat green vegetables in the fields one has to eat wheat and in the rivers one should drink green vegetables.
morphology: One who is born in the fields of crops one who is a farmer and who is not a farmer should be given the title of a farmer.

sanskrit: ut agāt ayam ādityaḥ viśvena sahasā saha dviṣantam mahyam randhayan mo iti aham dviṣate radham
reference: With all his conquering vigour this Âditya hath gone up on high, Giving my foe into mine hand: let me not be my foeman's prey.
baseline: Then after having come here with the help of the universe suddenly after having cooked me for two hours I will return to the chariot.
morphology: Then after having come here with the help of the universe suddenly after having cooked me for two hours I will say that I am ready.

sanskrit: abhi tyam meṣam puru hūtam r̥gmiyam indram gīḥ bhiḥ madata vasvaḥ arṇavam yasya dyāvaḥ na vi caranti mānuṣā bhuje maṁhiṣṭham abhi vipram arcata
reference: MAKE glad with songs that Ram whom many men invoke, worthy of songs of praise, Indra, the sea of wealth; Whose gracious deeds for men spread like the heavens abroad: sing praise to him the Sage, most liberal for our good.
baseline: O Indra one who is a sheep a cow a priest a devotee of the god Indra a servant of the king of the army one whose arms are not moving and who is not moving should be worshipped by the king.
morphology: O Indra the god of the rygms the lord of the horses the king of the steeds the goddess of the sheep the mother of the cow the wife of the elephant the husband of the lion and the king who is not a member of the army should be worshipped.

sanskrit: abhi īm avanvan su abhiṣṭim ūtayaḥ antarikṣa prām taviṣībhiḥ āvr̥tam indram dakṣāsaḥ r̥bhavaḥ mada cyutam śata kratum javanī sūnr̥tā ā aruhat
reference: As aids the skilful R̥ibhus yearned to Indra strong to save, who fills mid-air, encompassed round with might, Rushing in rapture; and -o'er Ṣatakratu came the gladdening shout that urged him on to victory.
baseline: O Indra the Saviour of the south the lord of the east the king of the west the queen of the north the son of the sun the daughter of the king the wife of the queen the mother of the nine sons of the four great sages and the king.
morphology: O Indra the lord of the south the king of the east the queen of the west the son of the sun the goddess of gold and gold should be worshipped in the morning.

sanskrit: tvam gotram aṅgiraḥ bhyaḥ avr̥ṇoḥ apa uta atraye śata dureṣu gātu vit sasena cit vi madāya avahaḥ vasu ājau adrim vavasānasya nataryan
reference: Thou hast disclosed the kine's stall for the Angirases, and made a way for Atri by a hundred doors. On Vimada thou hast bestowed both food and wealth, making thy bolt dance in the sacrificer's fight.
baseline: You should worship the tribe of the angira and the cow the cow and go to a hundred places in the distance. You should pray to Vasu and Adrī to the king of Vavasana.
morphology: You should worship the tribe of the angira and the king of the vavasasana. You should visit a hundred places here and go to a far away place. Then you should worship Vasu Adri Vavasana and others.

sanskrit: tvam apām api dhānā avr̥ṇoḥ apa adhāraya parvate dānu mat vasu vr̥tram yat indra śavasā avadhīḥ ahim āt it sūryam divi ā arohayaḥ dr̥śe
reference: Thou hast unclosed the prisons of the waters; thou hast in the mountain seized the treasure rich in gifts. When thou hadst slain with might the dragon Vr̥itra, thou, Indra, didst raise the Sun in heaven for all to see.
baseline: O Śuṇa the sun the goddess of the earth the king of the mountains the god Vritra the son of Indra the corpse the body of the king and the goddess Aśrāhāya are worshipped in the sky.
morphology: O Vritrā one who gives to the dead of Indra and the body of a demon the sun the goddess of the earth and the king of the mountains should be worshipped in the form of a vīrtra.

sanskrit: tvam māyābhiḥ apa māyinaḥ adhamaḥ svadhābhiḥ ye adhi śuptau ajuhvata tvam piproḥ nr̥ manaḥ pra arujaḥ puraḥ pra r̥jiścānam dasyu hatyeṣu āvitha
reference: With wondrous might thou blewest enchanter fiends away, with powers celestial those who called on thee in jest. Thou, hero-hearted, hast broken down Pipru's forts, and helped R̥ijiṣvan when the Dasyus were struck dead.
baseline: O king of the kingdom of Bihar thou who hast conquered the king of Bihar by means of the illusion of the gods who have been subjugated by the illusions of the king who has destroyed the kingdom who had conquered the kingdom and who had destroyed the king. Thou hast destroyed the kings of the cities and cities.
morphology: O king of Bihar you are the king of the poor and those who are under the control of your own hands. You are the ruler of the people. You have destroyed the hearts of those who have been killed by you. You will destroy those who were killed by us.

sanskrit: tvam kutsam śuṣṇa hatyeṣu āvitha arandhayaḥ atithi gvāya śambaram mahāntam cit arbudam ni kramīḥ padā sanāt eva dasyu hatyāya jajñiṣe
reference: Thou savedst Kutsa when Ṣushṇa was smitten down; to Âtithigva gavest Ṣambara for a prey. E'en mighty Arbuda thou troddest under foot: thou from of old wast born to strike the Dasyus dead.
baseline: Having said this the king should not commit the murder of a thief. Having said that he should pay tribute to the king. He should be punished with a fine of Rs.100.
morphology: The king should give half of the hostages to the assassins and then make them pay tribute to the great sambar and the king of the arboretum. The robbers should be punished with the same amount of money.

sanskrit: tve iti viśvā taviṣī sadhryak hitā tava rādhaḥ soma pīthāya harṣate tava vajraḥ cikite bāhvoḥ hitaḥ vr̥śca śatroḥ ava viśvāni vr̥ṣṇyā
reference: All power and might is closely gathered up in thee; thy bounteous spirit joys in drinking Soma juice. Known is the thunderbolt that lies within thine arms: rend off therewith all manly prowess of our foe.
baseline: Having believed that you are a god the king of the universe should be pleased with you. The king of your kingdom would be happy with the diamond the enemy of the enemy the lord of the world the goddess of the earth and the goddess Vṛṣṇa.
morphology: Having believed that you are a god the king of the earth should rejoice with the sound of the diamond. The king of yours should be pleased with the diamond the good of the arms the evil of the enemy and the world the god of the universe.

sanskrit: vi jānīhi āryān ye ca dasyavaḥ barhiṣmate randhaya śāsat avratān śākī bhava yajamānasya coditā viśvā it tā te sadha mādeṣu cākana
reference: Discern thou well Aryas and Dasyus; punishing the lawless give them up to him whose grass is strewn. Be thou the sacrificer's strong encourager all these thy deeds are my delight at festivals.
baseline: O Janīhihi the king of the kings servants the robbers and the king who rule over the king after cooking the food should be ashamed of your master. He should have faith in them.
morphology: O Janīhi the king of Aryans and robbers who rule by cooking food for you and those who rule over you. O Avrat you are the master of the enemy. You have faith in him. These are the servants of the king.

sanskrit: anu vratāya randhayan apa vratān ābhūbhiḥ indraḥ śnathayan anābhuvaḥ vr̥ddhasya cit vardhataḥ dyām inakṣataḥ stavānaḥ vamraḥ vi jaghāna sam dihaḥ
reference: Indra gives up the lawless to the pious man, destroying by the Strong Ones those who have no strength. Vamra when glorified destroyed the gathered piles of the still waxing great one who would reach the heaven.
baseline: After having cooked for the vow of annu one should observe the vow with the forehead and the image of the old man should be increased. The image of an anubhava should be given to the old person. The figure should be worshipped with the words vamara vi jagāṇa.
morphology: After having cooked for the vow of annu Indra worshipped with the words of abhu and said that the image of the old man should be increased. He should be worshipped by the goddess Vāmarā and the goddess Jāgha.

sanskrit: takṣat yat te uśanā sahasā sahaḥ vi rodasī iti majmanā bādhate śavaḥ ā tvā vātasya nr̥ manaḥ manaḥ yujaḥ ā pūryamāṇam avahan abhi śravaḥ
reference: The might which Uṣanâ hath formed for thee with might rends in its greatness and with strength both worlds apart. O Hero-souled, the steeds of Vâta, yoked by thought, have carried thee to fame while thou art filled with power.
baseline: Then the body should be immediately washed with water and the sun should be placed in the middle of the fire. The body should not be made to be covered by the wind. The mind should be covered with water. The heart should be filled with water and the heart with water should be removed.
morphology: Then the body should be placed in a place where the sun is suddenly rising with the sun and the heart should be filled with the wind. The body should not be left in the air. The mind should be kept in the place where you are filled with water.

sanskrit: mandiṣṭa yat uśane kāvye sacā indraḥ vaṅkūiti vaṅku tarā adhi tiṣṭhat i ugraḥ yayim niḥ apaḥ srotasā asr̥jat vi śuṣṇasya dr̥ṁhitāḥ airayat puraḥ
reference: When Indra hath rejoiced with Kâvya Uṣanâ, he mounts his steeds who swerve wider and wider yet. The Strong hath loosed his bolt with the swift rush of rain, and he hath rent in pieces Ṣushṇa's firmbuilt forts.
baseline: The temple that is built in the form of the sun the temple that has been built in a poem the idol of Indra the bow the arrow and the bow should be placed on the ground. It should not be made of water.
morphology: The temple that is built in the form of the sun the temple that has been built in a poem and the temple where Indra is standing on the right side of the bank the one that is not made from the source of evil and which has been destroyed by the forces of evil.

sanskrit: ā sma ratham vr̥ṣa pāneṣu tiṣṭhasi śāryātasya pra bhr̥tāḥ yeṣu mandase indra yathā suta someṣu cākanaḥ anarvāṇam ślokam ā rohase divi
reference: Thou mountest on thy car amid strong Soma draughts: Ṣâryâta brought thee those in which thou hast delight. Indra, when thou art pleased with men whose Soma flows thou risest to unchallenged glory in the sky.
baseline: The chariot bull and elephant standing on the leaves of the river are the objects of worship for which Indra is seated in the middle of the earth. The chakas anvaravana shlokas are worshipped in the sun.
morphology: The chariot should be placed on the leaves of a bull and the feet of a sārāyata should be fixed on the sides of the chariots. In the case of the sāmya there should be Indra sitting on the right side of the river. In case of sūma the chakas should be recited on the left side.

sanskrit: adadāḥ arbhām mahate vacasyave kakṣīvate vr̥cayām indra sunvate menā abhavaḥ vr̥ṣaṇaśvasya sukrato itisu krato viśvā it tā te savaneṣu pra vācyā
reference: To old Kaksivin, Soma-presser, skilled in song, O Indra, thou didst give the youthful Vr̥ichayâ. Thou, very wise, wast Menâ, Vrishaṇaṣva's child: those deeds of thine must all be told at Soma feasts.
baseline: O Indra one who has heard the words of the goddess Arbha the great goddess of the earth the cow the wilderness the forest the scorpion the fragrant land the sun the sacred water of the world the belief of the god is said to be good.
morphology: O Indra who has heard the story of the goddess Arbha the great goddess of the earth the king of the celestial body the goddess of fire the god of the sky the mother of the scorpion the lord of the sun the Lord of the universe and the goddess Śukrātu are said to have believed in her.

sanskrit: indraḥ aśrāyi su dhyaḥ nireke pajreṣu stomaḥ duryaḥ na yūpaḥ aśva yuḥ gavyuḥ ratha yuḥ vasu yuḥ indraḥ it rāyaḥ kṣayati pra yantā
reference: The good man's refuge in his need is Indra, firm as a doorpost, praised among the Pajras. Indra alone is Lord of wealth, the Giver, lover of riches, chariots, kine, and horses.
baseline: O Indra you are the one who destroys the king. One who is not a cow horse cow chariot vaśu you Indra it is the king of the world.
morphology: O Indra you are the king. You do not destroy the horses cows chariots horses horses etc.

sanskrit: idam namaḥ vr̥ṣabhāya sva rāje satya śuṣmāya tavase avāci asmin indra vr̥jane sarva vīrāḥ smat sūri bhiḥ tava śarman syāma
reference: To him the Mighty One, the self-resplendent, verily strong and great, this praise is uttered. May we and all the heroes, with the princes, be, in this fray, O Indra, in thy keeping.
baseline: O Lord of the gods of the universe O lord of the sun O king of the earth O Lord of the goddess Vāśva the goddess of truth of happiness of good fortune of your lord Indra and of all the mighty men of the tribe of Indra.
morphology: O Lord of the gods of the universe and the mighty one of Indra you should worship the goddess Vāśvara in this manner.

sanskrit: tyam su meṣam mahaya svaḥ vidam śatam yasya su bhvaḥ sākam īrate atyam na vājam havana syadam ratham ā indram vavr̥tyām avase suvr̥kti bhiḥ
reference: I GLORIFY that Ram who finds the light of heaven, whose hundred nobly-natured ones go forth with him. With hymns may I turn hither Indra to mine aid,– the Car which like a strong steed hasteth to the call.
baseline: Then the sheep should be worshipped in the form of a cow. The cow should be offered to a man who has not been given a havan. The chariot should be given to a woman who has been worshipped by Indra.
morphology: Then the sheep should be worshipped in the form of a cow and the bull should be offered to a man who has not been given a havan. The chariot should be given to Indra.

sanskrit: saḥ parvataḥ na dharuṇeṣu acyutaḥ sahasram ūtiḥ taviṣīṣu vavr̥dhe indraḥ yat vr̥tram avadhīt nadī vr̥tam ubjan arṇāṁsi jarhr̥ṣāṇaḥ andhasā
reference: Like as a mountain on firm basis, unremoved, he, thousandfold protector, waxed in mighty strength, When Indra, joying in the draughts of Soma juice, forced the clouds, slaying Vr̥itra stayer of their flow.
baseline: He would not rise from the mountains and fall into the mountains. He would be blinded by the incarnation of Indra who would destroy Vritra the river and raise Arna.
morphology: He would not rise from the mountains and fall into the mountains. He would fall into a thousand holes in the mountains the river Vritra and the river would rise and make the earth blind.

sanskrit: saḥ hi dvaraḥ dvariṣu vavraḥ ūdhani candra budhnaḥ mada vr̥ddhaḥ manīṣi bhiḥ indram tam ahve su apasyayā dhiyā maṁhiṣṭha rātim saḥ hi papriḥ andhasaḥ
reference: For he stays e'en the stayers, spread o'er laden cloud, rooted in light, strengthened in rapture by the wise. Indra with thought, with skilled activity, I call, most liberal giver, for he sates him with the juice.
baseline: He should be made to sit in the doorway of the temple. He should not be seen sitting in the doors of the house with the moon the sun the moon and the moon. He is old and obedient. One should be worshipped by Indra. One who is blind and has no night should be killed by him.
morphology: He should be made to sit in the doorway of the temple with the moon the sun the moon and the moon. The old man and Indra should be worshipped by the goddess. The night should be spent in the house of the god Indra. He should not be blinded by the night.

sanskrit: ā yam pr̥ṇanti divi sadma barhiṣaḥ samudram na su bhvaḥ svāḥ abhiṣṭayaḥ tam vr̥tra hatye anu tasthuḥ ūtayaḥ śuṣmāḥ indram avātāḥ ahruta psavaḥ
reference: Whom those that flow in heaven on sacred grass, his own assistants, nobly-natured, fill full like the sea,– Beside that Indra when he smote down Vr̥itra stood his helpers, straight in form, mighty, invincible.
baseline: The goddess should be worshipped with the words aa yama dīvī sādham bārhīṣa sudra saṃu bhuṣṇu vritra vrāṣṭra anus tāṣtu sūṣma and Indra.
morphology: The goddess should be worshipped with the words aa yama dīvī suddham bārhiṣa sudra bhuṣṇu vritra vīrṣṭra kārūtā sūṣma and īndra.

sanskrit: abhi sva vr̥ṣtim made asya yudhyataḥ raghvīḥ iva pravaṇe sasruḥ ūtayaḥ indraḥ yat vajrī dhr̥ṣamāṇaḥ andhasā bhinat valasya paridhīn iva tritaḥ
