reference: To him, as in wild joy he fought with him who stayed the rain, his helpers sped like swift streams down a slope, When Indra, thunder-armed, made bold by Soma draughts, as Trita cleaveth Vala's fences, cleft him through.
baseline: Having conquered his own body and having fought this battle with me Indra who is as prone as Raghvi has the strength of his body and is blinded by the vajra and the dhruṣa of the vāla.
morphology: Having conquered his own body and having fought with it Indra who is as prone as the lord of the earth who is blind as the king of the sky who has a vajra a dhuṣa and is like the circumference of a vala is threefolded.

sanskrit: pari īm ghr̥ṇā carati titviṣe śavaḥ apaḥ vr̥tvī rajasaḥ budhnam ā aśayat vr̥trasya yat pravaṇe duḥ gr̥bhiśvanaḥ ni jaghantha hanvoḥ indra tanyatum
reference: Splendour encompassed thee, forth shone thy warrior might: the rain-obstructer lay in mid-air's lowest deep, What time, O Indra, thou didst cast thy thunder down upon the jaws of Vritra hard to be restrained.
baseline: The body of the king is said to have been destroyed by the evil spirit of Vritrāśa. The evil spirit should be destroyed by Indra.
morphology: The body of the king should be covered with a piece of cloth and the body should be washed with water. The king should not be afraid of the evil spirit of Vritrāṣa. He should be punished by Indra.

sanskrit: hradam na hi tvā ni r̥ṣanti ūrmayaḥ brahmāṇi indra tava yāni vardhanā tvaṣṭā cit te yujyam vavr̥dhe śavaḥ tatakṣa vajram abhibhūti ojasam
reference: The hymns which magnify thee, Indra, reach to thee even as water-brooks flow down and fill the lake. Tvashṭar gave yet more force to thine appropriate strength, and forged thy thunderbolt of overpowering might.
baseline: O Brahman the lord of Urmā the king of Urāma the god of growth the gods of Udaṇa the kingdom of Yūda the body of Vārvruddha the diamond of the body and the goddess of light are worshipped.
morphology: O Śiva O Brahman O Indra those who increase you the body should be worshipped with a diamond and the body with the same amount of diamond should be offered to you.

sanskrit: jaghanvān oṁ iti hari bhiḥ sambhr̥takrato itisambhr̥ta krato indra vr̥tram manuṣe gātu yan apaḥ ayacchathāḥ bāhvoḥ vajram āyasam adhārayaḥ divi ā sūryam dr̥śe
reference: When, Indra, thou whose power is linked with thy Bay Steeds hadst smitten Vr̥itra, causing floods to flow for man, Thou heldst in thine arms the metal thunderbolt, and settest in the heaven the Sun for all to see.
baseline: Having said this Hari bhi should worship Vritrā Indra Vrītra the king of the earth. Having worshipped the goddess as the goddess of the sun the goddess should be worshipped with the words abhava vajra ayaśa abhāśā and diṣṇa.
morphology: Having said this that Hari should be able to reach the ground and the sun should be made to reach a man. Having said that O Hari Vritra Indra Vrītra Vratrṣa Vīṣṇu Avya Vajra Ayasa Adhyāma Diṣṇa Sun and others should be worshipped.

sanskrit: br̥hat sva candram ama vat yat ukthyam akr̥ṇvata bhiyasā rohaṇam di vaḥ yat mānuṣa pradhanāḥ indram ūtayaḥ svaḥ nr̥ ṣācaḥ marutaḥ amadan anu
reference: In fear they raised the lofty self-resplendent hymn, praise giving and effectual, leading up to heaven, When Indra's helpers fighting for the good of men, the Maruts, faithful to mankind, joyed in the light.
baseline: The great man should be worshipped with his own moon and the king should be killed with the help of his own body. The man should worship Indra with his arms and arms.
morphology: The great man should offer the moon of his own kind and the king should offer a rohan of his choice. The man should worship Indra the sun the fire the sea and the earth.

sanskrit: dyauḥ cit asya ama vān aheḥ svanāt ayoyavīt bhiyasā vajraḥ indra te vr̥trasya yat badbadhānasya rodasī iti made sutasya śavasā abhinat śiraḥ
reference: Then Heaven himself, the mighty, at that Dragon's roar reeled back in terror when, Indra, thy thunderbolt In the wild joy of Soma had struck off with might the head of Vr̥itra, tyrant of the earth and heaven.
baseline: The image of Śuṭa is said to have been made by the king of Vritra. The figure of Viṣṇu should be made to look like a diamond. The head of Indra should be cast as the corpse of Vṛtras son of Rudāśī.
morphology: The image of Śuṭa is said to be the image of the god Viṣṇu. He should be worshipped by the king of Vīrtras. The figure of Viṣṭra is described as having the form of the head. The body of Sūtā is described to be that of Rudasī.

sanskrit: yat it nu indra pr̥thivī daśa bhujiḥ ahāni viśvā tatananta kr̥ṣṭayaḥ atra aha te magha van vi śrutam sahaḥ dyām anu śavasā barhaṇā bhuvat
reference: O Indra, were this earth extended forth tenfold, and men who dwell therein multiplied day by day, Still here thy conquering might, Maghavan, would be famed: it hath waxed vast as heaven in majesty and power.
baseline: One who has heard the words of Indra the earth the ten elements the belief the krṣtīya here and the māgha vāṇavī along with the sound one who gives the body and others.
morphology: The ten elements of the earth earth and earth are said to be like this. The ten things of the universe are called krṣtīs. They are said that they should be accompanied by the sound of the āgha vana. They should be given to the body of the king.

sanskrit: tvam asya pāre rajasaḥ vi omanaḥ svabhūti ojāḥ avase dhr̥ṣat manaḥ cakr̥ṣe bhūmim prati mānam ojasaḥ apaḥ [svar iti] svaḥ pari bhūḥ eṣi ā divam
reference: Thou, bold of heart, in thine own native might, for help, upon the limit of this mid-air and of heaven, Hast made the earth to be the pattern of thy strength: embracing flood and light thou reachest to the sky.
baseline: Oṇa the king of the earth the lord of the self the master of the mind the land the power the energy the earth and the earth are the objects of the worship.
morphology: Oṇa the lord of the earth the king of the world the master of the self the mind and the land should be worshipped in the abode.

sanskrit: tvam bhuvaḥ prati mānam pr̥thivyāḥ r̥ṣva vīrasya br̥hataḥ patiḥ bhūḥ viśvam ā aprāḥ antarikṣam mahi tvā satyam addhā nakiḥ anyaḥ tvāvān
reference: Thou art the counterpart of earth, the Master of lofty heaven with all its mighty Heroes: Thou hast filled all the region with thy greatness: yea, of a truth there is none other like thee.
baseline: You are the lord of the earth the great husband of the mighty one the king of the world the master of the universe the chief of space the real one and half of you.
morphology: You are the lord of the earth the great husband of the mighty king the king of the world the lord the master of space the god of the universe the one who is true the other who is not true and you are the king.

sanskrit: na yasya dyāvāpr̥thivī iti anu vyacaḥ na sindhavaḥ rajasaḥ antam ānaśuḥ na uta sva vr̥ṣṭim made asya yudhyataḥ ekaḥ anyat cakr̥ṣe viśvam ānuṣak
reference: Whose amplitude the heaven and earth have not attained, whose bounds the waters of mid-air have never reached,– Not, when in joy he fights the stayer of the rain: thou, and none else, hast made all things in order due.
baseline: One who does not give the earth sindhva rajas ananta anshu or his own rain and his war against me and others would not be able to make the world happy.
morphology: One who does not give the earth sindhu rajas ananta anshu and his own rain and his war against me and others should not be considered as the world.

sanskrit: ārcan atra marutaḥ sasmin ājau viśve devāsaḥ amadan anu tvā vr̥trasya yat bhr̥ṣṭi matā vadhena ni tvam indra prati ānam jaghantha
reference: The Maruts sang thy praise in this encounter, and in thee all the Deities delighted, What time thou, Indra, with thy spiky weapon, thy deadly bolt, smotest the face of Vr̥itra.
baseline: The archons would die here and the gods of the universe would be worshipped there. The king would not be able to do so by the execution of Vritrā.
morphology: The archons would die here and the gods of the universe would be worshipped there. The king would not be able to do so by the killing of Vritra.

sanskrit: ni oṁ iti su vācam pra mahe bharāmahe giraḥ indrāya sadane vivasvataḥ nu cit hi ratnam sasatām iva avidat na duḥ stutiḥ draviṇaḥ deṣu śasyate
reference: WE will present fair praise unto the Mighty One, our hymns to Indra in Vivasvdn's dwelling-place; For he hath ne'er found wealth in those who seem to sleep: those who give wealth to men accept no paltry praise.
baseline: The words nī obhārī are said to be the same as that of māhā bhārā īndra vivasvatā nūitāhi gāṇa sāsatām nī pradavīṇā dhū praise praise.
morphology: The words nī obhārī  and māh bārā girā īndra in the court of the lord Viṣvatva the words nūitā hī gāṇa sāsātā are said to be the same. Neither the praise nor misfortune are found in the lands of the dravins.

sanskrit: duraḥ aśvasya duraḥ indra goḥ asi duraḥ yavasya vasunaḥ inaḥ patiḥ śikṣānaraḥ pra divaḥ akāma karśanaḥ sakhā sakhi bhyaḥ tam idam gr̥ṇīmasi
reference: Giver of horses, Indra, giver, thou, of kine, giver of barley, thou art Lord and guard of wealth: Man's helper from of old, not disappointing hope, Friend of our friends, to thee ,as such we sing this praise.
baseline: One who is far away from the horse one who is distant from the cow and one who lives in the wilderness of the barley should take this gift from his wife. One who has been educated would get the gift of akāma and kārṣana. One would get it from his mother.
morphology: One who is far away from the horse one who is distant from the cow and one who lives in the wilderness of the barley should be given this gift by his wife. One who has been taught by him would get this gift from him.

sanskrit: śacī vaḥ indra puru kr̥t dyumat tama tava it idam abhitaḥ cekite vasu ataḥ sam gr̥bhya abhi bhūte ā bhara mā tvāyataḥ jarituḥ kāmam ūnayīḥ
reference: Indra, most splendid, powerful, rich in mighty deeds, this treasure spread around is known to be thine own. Gather therefrom, O Conqueror, and bring to us: fail not the hope of him who loves and sings to thee.
baseline: O Indra the Supreme Lord of the universe one should give to thee that which has been given to him by thee and that which is given to you by him.
morphology: O Indra the lord of the earth and the king of the universe one should pay tribute to him by saying that he would get this from you. He should therefore accept the gift and become a devotee. One should not give up the desire for you.

sanskrit: ebhiḥ dyubhiḥ su manāḥ ebhiḥ indu bhiḥ niḥ undhānaḥ amatim gobhiḥ aśvinā indreṇa dasyum darayantaḥ indu bhiḥ yuta dveṣasaḥ sam iṣā rabhemahi
reference: Well pleased with these bright flames and with these Soma drops, take thou away our poverty with seeds and kine. With Indra scattering the Dasyu through these drops, freed from their hate may we obtain abundant food.
baseline: The mind should be divided into two parts. These two should be called Indu Bhī Uḍṇa Uṇḍa Amatī Aśvī Indra Indū Viṣṇu Yūtu Rābhā and others.
morphology: The heart should be made to feel the indu bhi udhana cow āśvī īndhu bhee and the dāśya.

sanskrit: sam indra rāyā sam iṣā rabhemahi sam vājebhiḥ puru candraiḥ abhidyu bhiḥ sam devyā pra matyā vīra śuṣmayā go agrayā aśva vatyā rabhemahi
reference: Let us obtain, O Indra, plenteous wealth and food, with strength exceeding glorious, shining to the sky: May we obtain the Goddess Providence, the strength of heroes, special source of cattle, rich in steeds.
baseline: O Indra the king of the cow the lord of the horse and the goddess of the moon should be worshipped with the words sām Indra rāya sāma iṣa rava māhī sāmpu mā māpu moṇḍra sābhī mābhā vīhā māvī sāvira sūṣma pāmā gāvā sūhṣmā and śvāhmā.
morphology: O Indra Rāya Esha Ravimha Vājya Puru Chandra Bhī Sam Devī Pratyayā Vira Shūṣma Gū Agrā and the horses should be worshipped.

sanskrit: te tvā madāḥ amadan tāni vr̥ṣṇyā te somāsaḥ vr̥tra hatyeṣu sat pate yat kārave daśa vr̥trāṇi aprati barhiṣmate ni sahasrāṇi barhayaḥ
reference: These our libations strength-inspiring, Soma draughts, gladdened thee in the fight with Vr̥itra, Hero Lord, What time thou slewest for the singer with trimmed grass ten thousand Vr̥itras, thou resistless in thy might.
baseline: Those who have killed Vritrāśa with the vrṣṇī tree should be punished with ten vritrṣas in the caravas. They should be expelled from the carvings. Thousands of them should be released.
morphology: They said that they would kill Vritrās with the vrṣṇas. They would find that ten Vṛtras would be expelled from the caravans without any resistance. Thousands of Vrśṇas would be released.

sanskrit: yudhā yudham upa gha it eṣi dhr̥śṇu yā purā puram sam idam haṁsi ojasā namyā yat indra sakhyā parāvati ni barhayaḥ namucm nāma māyinam
reference: Thou goest on from fight to fight intrepidly, destroying castle after castle here with strength. Thou, Indra, with thy friend who makes the foe bow down, slewest from far away the guileful Namuci.
baseline: One who submits to a war a battle a fight and a battle should be done by the same dhruśṇu who is the purification of the universe. He should be worshipped by Indra and the goddess Parvati. The name may be mentioned as mayīna.
morphology: One should worship Indra the king of war the lord of war and the king who is worshipped in the form of a priest the god of war.

sanskrit: tvam karañjam uta parṇayam vadhīḥ tejiṣṭhayā atithi gvasya vartanī tvam śatā varṅgedasya abhinat puraḥ ananu daḥ pari sūtāḥ r̥jiśvanā
reference: Thou hast struck down in death Karanja, Parṇaya, in Âtithigva's very glorious going forth. Unyielding, when R̥ijiṣvan compassed them with siege, thou hast destroyed the hundred forts of Vangr̥ida.
baseline: The king should offer the kārāṇja or the foliage of the garland to the guests with a sharp note. He should offer a hundred varangas. The king would offer the purā anānu dā and the sutras.
morphology: You should make a garland or a foliage with a bright flower. You should give a hundred varangades of flowers and the sun should be placed on the walls of the temple.

sanskrit: tvam etān jana rājñaḥ dviḥ daśa abandhunā su śravasā upa jagmuṣaḥ ṣaṣṭim sahasrā navatim nava śrutaḥ ni cakreṇa rathyā duḥ padā avr̥ṇak
reference: With all-outstripping chariot-wheel, O Indra, thou far-famed, hast overthrown the twice ten Kings of men, With sixty thousand nine-and-ninety followers, who came in arms to fight with friendless Suṣravâs.
baseline: The king should give these to the king twice ten times with the sound of sound and sixty thousand nine times with sound and nine times the sound should be heard with the chariot and the sounding of sound.
morphology: The king should have two of these men and ten of them in the form of a mace. He should have sixty thousand nine thousand of them as his deputy. He would have nine of them on the side of the chariot.

sanskrit: tvam āvitha su śravasam tava ūti bhiḥ tava trāma bhiḥ indra tūrvayāṇam tvam asmai kutsam atithi gvam āyum mahe rājñe yūne arandhanāyaḥ
reference: Thou hast protected Suṣravâs with succour, and Tûrvayâṇa with thine aid, O Indra. Thou madest Kutsa, Âtithigva, Âyu, subject unto this King, the young, the mighty.
baseline: You are the hearer your hearer and your mother. You are Indra the bearer and you are the host of us all. O king you are a guest and you have to offer food to me.
morphology: You should hear the sound of the sun you should hear it your mother Indra the goddess of fire and you should worship us. You should worship the king of the world.

sanskrit: ye ut r̥ci indra deva gopāḥ sakhāyaḥ te śiva tamāḥ asāma tvām stoṣāma tvayā su vīrāḥ drāghīyaḥ āyuḥ pra taram dadhānāḥ
reference: May we protected by the Gods hereafter remain thy very prosperous friends, O Indra. Thee we extol, enjoying through thy favour life long and joyful and with store of heroes.
baseline: The gods of Indra Gopa Sākhya those who have attained the height of glory Śiva the same you are the hero. You are the one who has attained the age of glory.
morphology: The gods of Indra Gopa and Sākhya those who have been raised up by you Śiva you are the hero. You are the endowed with life.

sanskrit: mā naḥ asmin maghavan pr̥t su aṁhasi nahi te antaḥ śavasaḥ pari naśe akrandayaḥ nadyaḥ roruvat vanā kathā na kṣoṇīḥ bhiyasā sam ārata
reference: URGE us not, Maghavan, to this distressful fight, for none may comprehend the limit of thy strength. Thou with fierce shout hast made the woods and rivers roar: did not men run in crowds together in their fear?
baseline: O Maghavans who do not want to be killed in this war. They should not get drunk and drink water from the rivers. The story of the forest should not be told by the king.
morphology: O king do not ask me. O king of the mighty king you will not be able to find the dead bodies inside. You will not get drunk and you will get the rivers and rivers. You should not talk about the forest. You do not get the fear of the enemy.

sanskrit: arca akrāya śākine śacī vate śr̥ṇvantam indram mahayan abhi stuhi yaḥ dhr̥ṣṇunā śavasā rodasī iti ubhe iti vr̥ṣā vr̥ṣa tvā vr̥ṣabhaḥ ni r̥ñjate
reference: Sing hymns of praise to Ṣakra, Lord of power and might; laud thou and magnify Indra who hearcth thee, Who with his daring might, a Bull exceeding strong in strength, maketh him master of the heaven and earth.
baseline: Having worshipped Indra in the form of a bull the priest should worship the goddess Śācī in the morning. The goddess who is worshipped by the lord Śrūṣṇu as the corpse the sun the bull and the bull should be worshipped as standing.
morphology: Having worshipped Indra in the form of a bull the priest should be shaken by the shakin the sācī and the Śrīṇvatas. The lord who is standing in the body of a cow the bull bull and bull should be worshipped.

sanskrit: arca dive br̥hate śūṣyam vacaḥ sva kṣatram yasya dhr̥ṣataḥ dhr̥ṣat manaḥ br̥hat śravāḥ asuraḥ barhaṇā kr̥taḥ puraḥ hari bhyām vr̥ṣabhaḥ rathaḥ hi saḥ
reference: Sing forth to lofty Dyaus a strength-bestowing song, the Bold, whose resolute mind hath independent sway. High glory hath the Asura, compact of strength, drawn on by two Bay Steeds: a Bull, a Car is he.
baseline: The priest should spread the light in a big way and the chariot should be placed in his seat. The king should be made to stand on the right hand of the king. He should be worshipped by the king of the great sārava asura. The lord of the city should be called Hari. Bhārva Varaśa and the car should be built.
morphology: One who has a large heart and a large voice in the form of a bull and a chariot is said to be the king of the gods. He who has got his seat from the seat of the king should be worshipped as the king.

sanskrit: tvam divaḥ br̥hataḥ sānu kopayaḥ ava tmanā dhr̥ṣatā śambaram bhinat yat māyinaḥ vrandinaḥ mandinā dhr̥ṣat śitām gabhastim aśanim pr̥tanyasi
reference: The ridges of the lofty heaven thou madest shake; thou, daring, of thyself smotest through Ṣambara, When bold with gladdening juice, thou warredst with thy bolt, sharp and twoedged, against the banded sorcerers.
baseline: The sun should be large and angry and the sun should not be shaken by it. One should say sambara that is shītam svrndi sambar svarāṇa vrndī sātmā sīta gāvātā asana and sāhāna.
morphology: O lord of the earth you are the great one. You are the one who is angry with me. Then you will be angry at me. You will be pleased with me you will get angry with my brother and you will become angry with the mother. You shall be happy with me and I will get you.

sanskrit: ni yat vr̥ṇakṣi śvasanasya mūrdhani śuṣṇasya cit vrandinaḥ roruvat vanā prācīnena manasā barhaṇāvatā yat adya cit kr̥ṇavaḥ kaḥ tvā pari
reference: When with a roar that fills the woods, thou forcest down on wind's head the stores which 8usga kept confined, Who shall have power to stay thee firm and eager-souled from doing still this day what thou of old hast done?
baseline: The image of Vrṇuṣa the head of the breath the image of Śuṣṇa that of Vṛndī the roar of the forest the old man would explain to you who is the king of Kṛṇa today.
morphology: The image of the vrṇuṣi breath the murk of the sun the image of Vrndīs the images of the roar of the forest the ancient man would explain to you who is the one who has done the painting today.

sanskrit: tvam āvitha naryam turvaśam yadum tvam turvītim vayyam śatakrato itiśata krato tvam ratham etaśam kr̥tvye dhane tvam puraḥ navatim dambhayaḥ nava
reference: Thou helpest Narya, Turvaṣa, and Yadu, and Vayya's son Turvîti, Ṣatakratu! Thou helpest horse and car in final battle thou breakest down the nine-and-ninety castles.
baseline: You are the king of the city. You are not the king. You should be the king you are the lord of the sea. You have to be the lord. You want to be a king. If you want to build a chariot you should buy money. You do not get arrogance.
morphology: You are the king the king of the city the chief minister the governor of the state the ruler of the kingdom of the king and the governor.

sanskrit: saḥ gha rājā sat patiḥ śūśuvat janaḥ rāta havyaḥ prati yaḥ śāsam invati ukthā vā yaḥ abhi gr̥ṇāti rādhasā dānuḥ asmai uparā pinvate d ivaḥ
reference: A hero-lord is he, King of a mighty folk, who offers free oblations and promotes the Law, Who with a bounteous guerdon welcomes hymns of praise: for him flows down the abundant stream below the sky.
baseline: The king should be the king the husband should be made to sleep and the ruler should be sent to the king at night. The king who takes the crown or the king who accepts the crown should be taken back by the king.
morphology: The king should be the king the husband should be shushuva. One who takes the rule of the king by night and the king should say that the king who takes it is rādhasa. The king who gives it to us is called rādhas.

sanskrit: asamam kṣatram asamā manīṣā pra soma pāḥ apasā santu neme ye te indra daduṣaḥ vardhayanti mahi kṣatram sthaviram vr̥ṣṇyam ca
reference: His power is matchless, matchless is his wisdom; chief, through their work, be some who drink the Soma, Those, Indra, who increase the lordly power, the firm heroic strength of thee the Giver.
baseline: Those who increase the number of Indra and Dāduśa in the form of a kṣatra sāma pā soma pá sūpa santu asaṇa maniṣa sama pīa pēa aśa vrṣṇya svrīṣṇā māhi kṣāstra sattravira sthivira vṛṣṇīya etc. are the great sattras.
morphology: Those who increase the number of Indra and Dāduśa in the form of a ksatra maneśa pāsa soma paṣa sāmā sūma sambhā and sūmā are the same.

sanskrit: tubhya it ete bahulāḥ adri dugdhāḥ camū sadaḥ camasāḥ indra pānāḥ vi aśnuhi tarpaya kāmam eṣām atha manaḥ vasu deyāya kr̥ṣva
reference: Therefore for thee are these abundant beakers Indra's drink, stone-pressed juices held in ladles. Quaff them and satisfy therewith thy longing; then fix thy mind upon bestowing treasure.
baseline: These are the two different kinds of milk and milk. The samsara leaves are made by Indra the pāṇa leaves. The kāmā is made of water and the kāma is made by him. He should be worshipped with his mind.
morphology: These are the many things that should be offered to you. These two are the milk and the cow the chasm the leaves of Indra the water of Ashu the desire for love.

sanskrit: apām atiṣṭhat dharuṇa hvaram tamaḥ antaḥ vr̥trasya jaṭhareṣu parvataḥ abhi īm indraḥ nadyaḥ vavriṇā hitāḥ viśvāḥ anu sthāḥ pravaṇeṣu jighnate
reference: There darkness stood, the vault that stayed the waters' flow: in Vr̥itra's hollow side the rain-cloud lay concealed. But Indra smote the rivers which the obstructer stayed, flood following after flood, down steep declivitics.
baseline: O Indra the king of Vritrās womb the goddess of the earth and the goddess Hvarā the mother of the gods of the world the wife of Vrṣṭra the queen of the mountains the daughter of Indra who is killed by the rivers and rivers the lord of the universe and the king who is prone to evil.
morphology: O Indra who has been killed by rivers rivers and rivulets who is sitting on the ground with the sword and the sword in the middle of Vritra and the mountains and who has fallen on the earth.

sanskrit: saḥ śe vr̥dham adhi dhāḥ dyumnam asme iti mahi kṣatram janāṣāṭ indra tavyam rakṣa ca naḥ maghonaḥ pāh i sūrīn rāye ca naḥ su apatyai iṣe dhāḥ
reference: So give us, Indra, bliss-increasing glory give us great sway and strength that conquers people. Preserve our wealthy patrons, save our princes; vouchsafe us wealth and food with noble offspring.
baseline: He should not wear the head of a man and wear the hair of a woman. He should wear the clothes of a cow and wear clothes of the same size. He would not protect the people of the kingdom of Indra. The head of the king would not be covered by the head and the head would be washed by the hands of the mother.
morphology: He should be said to be the greatest of men. He should not be called the king of the kingdom of the king nor protect the king. He would not be known to be a king. The king of king Indra would not protect him.

sanskrit: divaḥ cit asya varimā vi papratha indram na mahnā pr̥thivī cana prati bhīmaḥ tuviṣmān carṣaṇi bhyaḥ ātapaḥ śiśīte vajram tejase na vaṁsagaḥ
reference: THOUGH e'en this heaven's wide space and earth have spread them out, nor heaven nor earth may be in greatness Indra's match. Awful and very mighty, causing woe to men, he whets his thunderbolt for sharpness, as a bull.
baseline: One who does not worship Indra or the earth should not worship him. One who worships him should not be afraid of the fire. One should not drink the vajra or the fiery water.
morphology: One who does not worship Indra or the earth should not worship him. One who is afraid of you should worship Bhima and the fire one who is not afraid of the fire and one who has not worshipped him should not be afraid to worship him or the king of the earth.

sanskrit: saḥ arṇavaḥ na nadyaḥ samudriyaḥ prati gr̥bhṇāti vi śritāḥ varīma bhiḥ indraḥ somasya pītaye vr̥ṣa yate sanāt saḥ yudhmaḥ ojasā panasyate
reference: Like as the watery ocean, so doth he receive the rivers spread on all sides in their ample width. He bears him like a bull to drink of Soma juice, and will, as Warrior from of old, be praised for might.
baseline: He who does not worship the rivers rivers and the sea would be worshipped by Indra. He who worships the bulls would be mercilessly defeated by the king. He would be victorious in the battle.
morphology: He who does not worship the rivers rivers and the sea should be worshipped. He who worships Indra should be killed by a bull in the battle of Soma. He should be mercilessly worshipped by the king.

sanskrit: tvam tam indra parvatam na bhojase mahaḥ nr̥mṇasya dharmaṇām irajyasi pra vīryeṇa devatāti cekite viśvasmai ugraḥ karmaṇe puraḥ h itaḥ
reference: Thou swayest, Indra, all kinds of great manly power, so as to bend, as't were, even that famed mountain down. Foremost among the Gods is he through hero might, set in the van, the Strong One, for each arduous deed.
baseline: He should not eat the mountain of Indra. He should worship the gods with valour and vigour. If he does not worship Indra he should be angry with the world.
morphology: He should not eat the mountain of Indra. He should worship the gods with great valour and devotion. He would be a fierce lord of the universe. He will be the king of the world.

sanskrit: saḥ it vane namasyu bhiḥ vacasyate cāru janeṣu pra bruvāṇaḥ indri yam vr̥ṣā chanduḥ bhavati haryataḥ vr̥ṣā kṣemeṇa dhenām maghavā yat invati
reference: He only in the wood is praised by worshippers, when he shows forth to men his own fair Indrapower. A friendly Bull is he, a Bull to be desired when Maghavan auspiciously sends forth his voice.
baseline: He should worship in the forest and worship the four gods of the world. The goddess Indrā is known to be a vrṣa and the goddess of the earth is known as Hariya. The vrśa is known by the name of the goddess with the name Vrṣha.
morphology: He worshipped the goddess in the forest and worshipped her. Among the four persons the goddess Brūvana the goddess Indrī and the goddess Vṛṣu are worshipped. The goddess Vrṣu is worshipped in the wilderness.

sanskrit: saḥ it mahāni sam ithāni majmanā kr̥ṇoti yudhmaḥ ojasā janebhyaḥ adha cana śrat dadhati tviṣi mate indrāya vajram ni ghanighnate vadham
reference: Yet verily the Warrior in his vigorous strength stirreth up with his might great battles for mankind; And men have faith in Indra, the respIendent One, what time he hurleth down his bolt, his dart of death.
baseline: He should do these things with great force. He should fight with a mighty force. One should give a sound sound sound to the people. He would kill Indra with a diamond and a cube.
morphology: He should say that he is great. He should do these things with mejmana. He would not be able to fight against the mighty men. If he believes that Indra should be killed with a diamond and a cube.

sanskrit: saḥ hi śravasyuḥ sadanāni kr̥trimā kṣmayā vr̥dhānaḥ ojasā vi nāśayan jyotīṁṣi kr̥ṇvan avr̥kāṇi yajyave ava su kratuḥ sartavai apaḥ sr̥jat
reference: Though, fain for glory, and with strength increased on earth, he with great might destroys the dwellings made with art, He makes the lights of heaven shine forth secure, he bids, exceeding wise, the floods flow for his worshipper.
baseline: He should make the houses of the hearers and the houses made of wood. He should destroy the fire and destroy it. He would make the walls of the houses worthless and create evil.
morphology: He would destroy the houses of the hearers the houses and houses of those who destroy the energy and the light. He would create misfortune by making them fall into darkness.

sanskrit: dānāya manaḥ soma pāvan astu te arvāñcā harī iti vandana śrut ā kr̥dhi yamiṣṭhāsaḥ sārathayaḥ ye indrca te na tvā ketāḥ ā dabhnuvanti bhūrṇayaḥ
reference: Drinker of Soma, let thy heart incline to give; bring thy Bays hitherward, O thou who hearest praise. Those charioteers of' thine, best skilled to draw the rein, the rapid sunbeams, Indra, lead thee not astray.
baseline: Having said that the heart of the cow should be made to fall on the ground. The king should be worshipped as āravaṇcha hāri. Having worshipped yāmīṣṭha the king of the kingdoms of Indra. Those who do not worship the gods should be killed.
morphology: Having said this those who have the heart of a cow who have not been killed by the king of the king should be worshipped as āravaṇcha hāri. Those who are the servants of Yāmīṣṭha and who do not have the mind of Indra should not be killed.

sanskrit: apra kṣitam vasu bibharṣi hastayoḥ aṣāl̥ham sahaḥ tanvi sr̥utaḥ dadhe āvr̥tāsaḥ avatāsaḥ na kartr̥ bhiḥ tanūṣu te kratavaḥ indra bhūrayaḥ
reference: Thou bearest in both hands treasure that never fails; the famed One in his body holds unvanquished might. O Indra, in thy members many powers abide, like wells surrounded by the ministering priests.
baseline: O Vāsu the one who has not been harmed and who has left the body in the hands of Viṣṇu one who is born with me and who is not covered by the incarnation in the form of a cow and who does not have the incarnations in the forms of the two sons.
morphology: The incarnations of Vasu Viṣṇu Bhūrī and others are unbroken. The incarnation should not be covered with the mantle of Indra and Bhūra.

sanskrit: eṣaḥ pra pūrvīḥ ava tasya camriṣaḥ atyaḥ na yoṣām ut ayaṁsta bhurvaṇiḥ dakṣam mahe pāyayate hiraṇyayam ratham āvr̥tya hari yogam r̥bhvasam
reference: FOR this man's full libations held in ladles, he hath roused him, eager, as a horse to meet the mare. He stays his golden car, yoked with Bay Horses, swift, and drinks the Soma juice which strengthens for great deeds.
baseline: The chariot of Hiranyā is said to have been placed in the east and the chariots of Hari in the south.
morphology: The chariot of Hiranyā is placed in the east and the chariots of Hari Yoga and Śrī are placed on the right side of the earth.

sanskrit: tam gūrtayaḥ neman iṣaḥ parīṇasaḥ samudram na sam caraṇe san iṣyavaḥ patim dakṣasya vidathasya nu sahāḥ girim na venāḥ adhi roha tejasā
reference: To him the guidance-following songs of praise flow full, as those who seek gain go in company to the flood. To him the Lord of power, the holy synod's might, as to a hill, with speed, ascend the loving ones.
baseline: He should not be called the master of the sea. He should never be made to walk on the sea or the sea nor the husband of the king of the south or the son of the enemy nor should he go to the hill.
morphology: He should not be called the master of the sea. He should never touch the sea with the feet of the king nor the husband of the lord of the south nor his wife the king of the mountains nor should he touch the mountains.

sanskrit: saḥ turvaṇiḥ mahān areṇu paiṁsye gireḥ bhr̥ṣṭiḥ na bhrājate tujā śavaḥ yena śuṣṇam māyinam āyasaḥ made dudhraḥ ābhūṣu rāmayat ni dāman i
reference: Victorious, great is he; in manly battle shines, unstained with dust, his might, as shines a mountain peak; Wherewith the iron one, fierce e'en against the strong, in rapture, fettered wily Sushna fast in bonds.
baseline: He would not be able to reach the great mountain of the mountains. He should not be afraid of the body of a cow. The body should be washed away by the sun and the mother should be fed with milk. The mother should also be given milk.
morphology: He should be placed in a large hall with a mound of water. The body should not be washed away by the fire of the mountain. The dead body should be kept in a well that has been dried up. The mother should be given milk and milk. The brethren should be buried in the ground.

sanskrit: devī yadi taviṣī tvāvr̥dhā ūtaye indram siṣakti uṣasam na sūryaḥ yaḥ dhr̥ṣṇunā śavasā bādhate tamaḥ iyarti reṇum br̥hat arhari svani ḥ
reference: When Strength the Goddess, made more strong for help by thee, waits upon Indra as the Sun attends the Dawn, Then. he who with his might unflinching kills the gloom stirs up the dust aloft, with joy and triumphing.
baseline: If the goddess is standing on the ground and having worshipped Indra in the morning the sun should not rise. The sun should be placed on the corpse of the demon Śuṣṇu.
morphology: If the goddess is standing on the ground and the sun is not standing in the sky and the body of Indra is being shaken by the sun. The sun which is facing the earth should be placed on the corpse. It should be worshipped by the great king.

sanskrit: vi yat tiraḥ dharuṇam acyutam rajaḥ atisthipaḥ divaḥ ātāsu barhaṇā svaḥ mīl̥he yat made indra harṣyā ahan vr̥tram niḥ apām aubjaḥ arṇavam
reference: When thou with might, upon the framework of the heaven, didst fix, across, air's region firmly, unremoved, In the light-winning war, Indra, in rapturous joy, thou smotest Vr̥itra dead and broughtest floods of rain.
baseline: O king of the earth one who has not been able to reach the earth would get the gift of water from the sky. One who does not want to go to the sky would get a gift from Indra Harsi Ahana Vritra Apa Avābāj and others.
morphology: O king of the earth one who has got the arrow the king the great king and the king who has the power of the sky the gods of the air the god of the sun the goddess of the sea Indra Hārṣya Ahana Vritra Apa Avābā Arnā and others.

sanskrit: tvam divaḥ dharuṇam dhiṣe ojasā pr̥thivyāḥ indra sadaneṣu māhinaḥ tvam sutasya made ariṇāḥ apaḥ vi vr̥trasya samayā pāṣyā arujaḥ
reference: Thou with thy might didst grasp,the holder-up of heaven, thou who art mighty also in the seats of earth. Thou, gladdened by the juice, hast set the waters free, and broken Vr̥itra's stony fences through and through.
baseline: O Indra the great among the houses of the earth you are the god of the day the king of the land the lord of the sky and the king who is the master of the world you should worship the sun the sun and the earth. You should worship Vritra and the gods of the time.
morphology: O Indra you are the supreme god of the earth. You are the king of the world. You should be the king in the form of the sun. You become the king. You get the power of Vritra. You have the power to destroy the enemy.

sanskrit: pra maṁhiṣṭhāya br̥hate br̥hat raye satya śuṣmāya tavase matim bhare apām iva pravaṇe yasya duḥ dharam rādhaḥ viśva āyu śavase apa vr̥tam
reference: To him most liberal, lofty Lord of lofty wealth, verily powerful and strong, I bring my hymn,– Whose checkless bounty, as of waters down a slope, is spread abroad for all that live, to give them strength.
baseline: O Lord of the universe and the body of Radha one who is prone to misfortune and misery should be made to fall into the abyss of the body with great devotion. One who is full of faith in you should be blessed with great happiness.
morphology: O Lord of the universe and the body of Radha who is prone to misfortune who has a great heart who is full of joy and who has great heart and who is capable of suffering.

sanskrit: agha te viśvam anu ha asat iṣṭaye āpaḥ nimnāiva savanā haviṣmataḥ yat parvate na sam aśīta haryataḥ indrasya vajraḥ śnathitā hiraṇyayaḥ
reference: Now all this world, for worship, shall come after thee-the offerer's libations like floods to the depth, When the well-loved one seems to rest upon the hill, the thunderbolt of Indra, shatterer wrought of gold.
baseline: The king should not be placed on a mountain. He should be made to sit on a hill. The king of Hiranyā should be seated on a diamond of Indra.
morphology: The king of Hiranyā should not be placed on a mountain. The king should not sit on a hill. He should be made to sit on the hill. The diamond of Indra should be placed in the form of a diamond.

sanskrit: asmai bhīmāya namasā sam adhvare uṣaḥ na śubhre ā bhara panīyase yasya dhāma śravase nāma indriyam jyotiḥ akāri haritaḥ na ayase
reference: To him the terrible, most meet for lofty praise, like bright Dawn, now bring gifts with reverence in this rite, Whose being, for renown, yea, Indra-power and light, have been created, like bay steeds, to move with speed.
baseline: Ośma Bhima Namasa Uṣa Śubhre Aa Bharā Panīya the abode of which is called Śrāvāsa Indrāya Jūtī Akārī and Hari.
morphology: Ośma Bhīma Namasa Uṣa Uśa Śubhre Aā Bharā Panīya the abode of which is called Śrāvaṣe Indrā Jūtī Akāri Hari Hari and others.

sanskrit: ime te indra te vayam puru stuta ye tvā ārabhya carāmasi prabhuvaso itiprabhu vaso nahi tvat anyaḥ girvaṇaḥ giraḥ saghat kṣoṇīḥ iva prati naḥ harya tat vacaḥ
reference: Thine, Indra, praised by many, excellently rich! are we who trusting in thy help draw near to thee. Lover of praise, none else but thou receives our laud: as earth loves all her creatures, love thou this our hymn.
baseline: O Indra we are the sons of the king. The Lord should not say that you are the master from the beginning. You should not give another cow cow horse cow and cow. One should not lose it.
morphology: O Indra we praise you for having begun you are the master and you are not the lord. You are not another god. You do not harm others like Girā and Kṣonī.

sanskrit: bhūri te indra vīryam tava smasi asya stotuḥ magha van kāmam ā pr̥ṇa anu te dyauḥ br̥hatī vīryam mame iyam ca te pr̥thivī neme ojase
reference: Great is thy power, O Indra, we are thine. Fulfil, O Maghavan, the wish of this thy worshipper. After thee lofty heaven hath measured out its strength: to thee and to thy power this earth hath bowed itself.
baseline: O Indra you have got the semen. You have got this fragrance. You give me the vana kaṇam. You get the great semen and you get the earth.
morphology: O Indra you are the one who smells the fragrance of the earth. One who gives you the fragrant fragrance the great virginity of the world and the greatness of the universe should be worshipped.

sanskrit: tvam tam indra parvatam mahām urum vajreṇa vajrin parva śaḥ cakartitha ava asr̥jaḥ ni vr̥tāḥ sartavai apaḥ satrā viśvam dadhiṣe kevalam sahaḥ
reference: Thou, who hast thunder for thy weapon, with thy bolt hast shattered into pieces this broad massive cloud. Thou hast sent down the obstructed floods that they may flow: thou hast, thine own for ever, all victorious might.
baseline: The king of the mountains of Indra the king of Urum the prince of Vajrījṇa and the king who circled the mountains with the diamond the god of the earth the gods of the universe the seven gods and the world are the only companions.
morphology: O Indra you are the mountain. You are the great mountain the mountain of iron the mountains of diamond and the mountains. You make a circle. You do not want to be destroyed. You want to destroy the world. You have only one companion.

sanskrit: ā svam adma yuvamānaḥ ajaraḥ tr̥ṣu aviṣyan ataseṣu tiṣṭhati atyaḥ na pr̥ṣṭham pruṣitasya rocate divaḥ na sānu stanayan acikradat
reference: Never decaying, seizing his appropriate food, rapidly, eagerly through the dry wood he spreads. His back, as he is sprinkled, glistens like a horse: loud hath he roared and shouted like the heights of heaven?
baseline: One who has not had the pleasure of having the back of his body would not be pleased. One who does not have the breasts would not do so.
morphology: One who has not had the pleasure of having the back of his body would not be pleased. One who does not have the heart would not like to have the body of a young man sitting on the grass and sitting on it.

sanskrit: asmai it oṁ iti pra tavase turāya prayaḥ na harmi stomam māhināya r̥cīṣamāya adhri gave oham indrāya brahmāṇi rāta tamā
reference: EVEN to him, swift, strong and high. exalted, I bring my song of praise as dainty viands, My thought to him resistless, praise-deserving, prayers offered most especially to Indra.
baseline: O Brahma the night of Indra one should not worship the goddess Śrūmī. One should not pray to the lord Hirāma for the sake of greatness.
morphology: O Brahma the night of Indra one should not worship the goddess Śrūmī.

sanskrit: asmai it oṁ iti prayaḥ iva pra yaṁsi bharāmi āṅgūṣam bādhe su vr̥kti indrāya hr̥dā manasā manīṣā pratnāya patye dhiyaḥ marjayanta
reference: Praise, like oblation, I present, and utter aloud my song, my fair hymn to the Victor. For Indra, who is Lord of old, the singers have decked their lauds with heart and mind and spirit.
baseline: Having said this one should do the same thing as before. One who touches the fingers of the body with the finger one who has broken the heart mind mind and heart of Indra and has committed suicide should be killed.
morphology: O Sāmya one who touches the fingers of the body with the same kind of effort as us and then becomes a member of the heart mind mind and heart of Indra. One who does not suffer from the disease should be killed.

sanskrit: asmai it oṁ iti tyam upa mam svaḥ sām bharāmi āṅgūṣam āsyena maṁhiṣṭham acchokti bhiḥ matīnām suvr̥kti bhiḥ sūrim vavr̥dhadhyai
reference: To him then with my lips mine adoration, winning heaven's light, most excellent, I offer, To magnify with songs of invocation and with fair hymns the Lord, most bounteous Giver.
baseline: The subahman is said to be able to do this by us and the finger is done by me. By doing this by me the good word is known as bhī. By making the sun rise and rising.
morphology: O Sūrī one who has attained the attainment of this position should say that he should be able to bear the weight of his own body with his fingers. One who has achieved good fortune by doing this would be the master of the people of the faith.

sanskrit: asmai it oṁ iti stomam sam hinomi ratham na taṣṭāiva tat sināya giraḥ ca girvāhase su vr̥kti indrāya viśvam invam medhirāya
reference: Even for him I frame a laud, as fashions the wright a chariot for the man who needs it,– Praises to him who gladly hears our praises, a hymn well-formed, all-moving, to wise Indra.
baseline: The chariot should not be thrown into the sea. The charcer should be made to sit in the same position. The horse should be placed in the seat of the horse. The cow should be kept in the front seat. The king should be seated in the chair. He should be called Indra the world and the wise man.
morphology: The chariot should not be thrown into the river. The chords should be placed in the middle of the hill. The girder should be made to stand on the mountain. The king should be seated on the hill and should be worshipped as the god of the universe.

sanskrit: asmai it oṁ iti saptim iva śravasyā indrāya arkam juhvā sam añje vīram dāna okasam vandadhyai purām gūrta śravasam darmāṇam
reference: So with my tongue I deck, to please that Indra, my hymn, as 'twere a horse, through love of glory, To reverence the Hero, bounteous Giver, famed far and wide, destroyer of the castles.
baseline: Having heard the seven words āśmaī it obhārī one should pay tribute to Indra by offering the ark and offering the boar at the same time. One should worship the goddess Oksam and the goddess of the heart.
morphology: Having heard that it should be done in the same manner as seven others one should pay tribute to Indra by offering the ark and offering the boon of ooksam and garland.

sanskrit: iti tvaṣṭā takṣat vajram svapaḥ tamam svaryam raṇāya vr̥trasya cit vidat yena marma tujan īśānaḥ tujatā kiyedhāḥ
reference: Even for him hath Tvashṭar forged the thunder, most deftly wrought, celestial, for the battle, Wherewith he reached the vital parts of Vr̥itra, striking-the vast, the mighty with the striker.

morphology: The image of Vritra should be described as having the meaning of Śiva. It should be mentioned as having a diamond a gold a silver a diamond and a golden crown. The figure of Vṛtras should be known as the name of the king.

sanskrit: asya it oṁ iti mātuḥ savaneṣu sadyaḥ mahaḥ pitum papivān cāru annā muṣāyat viṣṇuḥ pacatam sahīyān vidhyat varāham tiraḥ adrim astā
reference: As soon as, at libations of his mother, great Vishṇu had drunk up the draught, he plundered. The dainty cates, the cooked mess; but One stronger transfixed the wild boar, shooting through the mountain.

sanskrit: asmai it oṁ iti gnāḥ cit deva patnīḥ indrāya arkam ahi hatye ūvur ity ūvuḥ pari dyāvāpr̥thivī iti jabhre urvī iti na asya te iti mahimānam pari staitistaḥ
reference: To him, to Indra, when he slew the Dragon, the Dames, too, Consorts of the Goda, wove praises. The mighty heaven and earth hath he encompassed: thy greatness heaven and earth, combined, exceed not.

sanskrit: asya it eva pra ririce mahitvam divaḥ pr̥thivyāḥ pari antarikṣāt sva rāṭ indraḥ dame ā viśva gūrtaḥ su ariḥ amatraḥ vavakṣe raṇāya
reference: Yea, of a truth, his magnitude surpasseth the magnitude of earth, mid-air, and heaven. Indra, approved by all men, self-resplendent, waxed in his home, loud-voiced and strong for battle.

sanskrit: asya it eva śavasā śuṣantam vi vr̥ścat vajreṇa vr̥tram indraḥ gāḥ na vrāṇāḥ avanīḥ amuñcat abhi śravaḥ dāvane sa cetāḥ

baseline: The first cow should be sent to the cow. Indra should go to the body of the deceased. Vāṣuṇa should worship it. Vasu should worship the goddess of the earth. Vīṣṇu should be worshipped in the form of a lion.
morphology: The first cow should be sent to the cow. The mother of the cow should go to Indra and the body should be given to you. The wife should be worshipped by Vasu Bhavya Sīndhu and the mother should be offered to him as the mother of a cow.

sanskrit: āpaḥ na devīḥ upa yanti hotriyam avaḥ paśyanti vi tatam yathā rajaḥ prācaiḥ devāsaḥ pra nayanti deva yum brahma priyam joṣayante varāḥ iva
reference: The heavenly Waters come not nigh the priestly bowl: they but look down and see how far mid-air is spread: The Deities conduct the pious man to them: like suitors they delight in him who loveth prayer.
baseline: One who does not worship the gods would see the king as the king the king and the gods of the east. One who worships the gods yum brahm and joshyā would be like a cow.
morphology: One who does not worship the gods would see that the king and the king would lead the devas to the east. One who loves the gods yum brahm and josha would be pleased by them.

sanskrit: adhi dvayoḥ adadhāḥ ukthyam vacaḥ yata srucā mithunā yā saparyataḥ asam yattaḥ vrate te kṣeti puṣyati bhadrā śaktiḥ yajamānāya sunvate
reference: Praiseworthy blessing hast thou laid upon the pair who with uplifted ladle serve thee, man and wife. Unchecked he dwells and prospers in thy law: thy power brings blessing to the sacrificer pouring gifts.
baseline: One who makes a vow to the lord of the two abode should say that he should worship the goddess Mithuna. He should offer the same to the master.
morphology: One should say that if one has offered a vow to the lord with the mithuna of srūccha and the other two mithu one should offer the same to the master.

sanskrit: āt aṅgirāḥ prathamam dadhire vayaḥ iddha agnayaḥ śamyā ye su kr̥tyayā sarvam paṇeḥ sam avindanta bhojanam aśva vantam go mantam ā paśum naraḥ
reference: First the Angirases won themselves vital power, whose fires were kindled through good deeds and sacrifice. The men together found the Paṇi's hoarded wealth, the cattle, and the wealth in horses and in kine.
baseline: The first animal should be made to be burnt in the fire. The first one should be the āṭṭa anṅgira āta and the first one that is burnt in a fire. By doing this the whole thing should be eaten without any hindrance. The horse should be fed. The cow should be offered to the man.
morphology: The first animal should be made to be covered with fire by the fire of the ātma the anggira the cow the man the animal the horse the goat the buffalo and the cow.

sanskrit: yajñaiḥ atharvā prathamaḥ pathaḥ tate tataḥ sūryaḥ vrata pāḥ venaḥ ā ajani ā gāḥ ājat uśanā kavyaḥ sacā yamasya jātam amr̥tam yajāmahe
reference: Atharvan first by sacrifices laid the paths then, guardian of the Law, sprang up the loving Sun. Uṣanâ Kâvya straightway hither drove the kine. Let us with offerings honour Yama's deathless birth.
baseline: The first path should be followed by the offering of oblations. Then the sun should be fasted and the vrat should be offered to the bridegroom. Then one should offer the sacred yama's birth and nectar.
morphology: The first path should be made by offering sacrifices. Then the sun should be worshipped and the vrat should be offered to the goddess aajaṇī aa gaājā. Then after having worshipped yama the birth of yama and the immortality should be performed.

sanskrit: barhiḥ vā yat su apatyāya vr̥jyate arkaḥ vā ślokam āghoṣate divi grāvā yatra vadati kāruḥ ukthyaḥ tasya it indraḥ abhi pitveṣu raṇyati
reference: When sacred grass is trimmed to aid the auspicious work, or the hymn makes its voice of praise sound to the sky. Where the stone rings as'twere a singer skilled in laud, --Indra in truth delights when these come near to him.
baseline: One who has left a son or a daughter or a son or an arka or a shloka is said to be worshipped by the god Indra. One who does so would be blessed by his father.
morphology: One who is born with a son or a daughter or a son and who has left a son or who is living in a village or a village or one who is a devotee of a goddess or a cow or a priest or a man who has raised a calf or other animal or a person who has been killed by a demon or a demon would be worshipped by Indra.

sanskrit: asāvi somaḥ indra te śaviṣṭha dhr̥ṣṇo iti ā gahi ā tvā pr̥ṇaktu indriyam rajaḥ sūryaḥ na raśmi bhiḥ
reference: The Soma hath been pressed for thee, O Indra; mightiest, bold One, come. May Indra-vigour fill thee full, as the Sun fills mid-air with rays.
baseline: O Asāvī Somā Indrā Teśvīṣta Dhrūshno Aa Ghaṇḍī Uṇṭhā Indra Sun Rāśmī Brahman Brahma Yūṇu Sūrṣṇā Tūṇḍu Indirā Rajā Ráśmā Bhī.
morphology: O Śoṇa Indra the son of Asāvi the king of the senses the sun the goddess of light and the goddess Rāśmi should be worshipped.

sanskrit: indram it harī vahataḥ apratidhr̥ṣṭa śavasam r̥ṣīṇām ca stutīḥ upa yajñam ca mānuṣāṇām
reference: His pair of Tawny Coursers bring Indra of unresisted might Hither to R̥ishis' songs of praise and sacrifice performed by men.
baseline: O Indra one who carries the body of a sage without any fear should praise the sages and offer sacrifices to the people.
morphology: O Indra one who carries the body of Hari with him is boundless. One should praise the sages and the people and offer sacrifices.

sanskrit: iti arvācīnam su te manaḥ grāvā kr̥ṇotu vagnunā
reference: Slayer of Vr̥itra, mount thy car; thy Bay Steeds have been yoked by prayer. May, with its voice, the pressing-stone draw thine attention hitherward.
baseline: One should observe that the heart should be warmed with the words aravācāṇu.
morphology: One should observe that the heart should be warmed by the vāgna.

sanskrit: imam indra sutam piba jyeṣṭham amartyam madam śukrasya tvā abhi akṣaran dhārāḥ r̥tasya sādane
reference: This poured libation, Indra, drink, immortal, gladdening, excellent. Streams of the bright have flowed to thee here at the seat of holy Law.
baseline: O Indra one should drink the sutam and the elder one the wine of immortality the letters of Śukra tava śrāha and Śrāda in the month of Sādana.
morphology: O Indra one who drinks the sutam the elder one the immortal one and one who consumes the letters of Śukra Śraṇu and Śrāda should be offered in the morning and evening of the month.

sanskrit: indrāya nūnam arcata ukthāni ca bravītana sutāḥ amatsuḥ indavaḥ jyeṣṭham namasyata sahaḥ
reference: Sing glory now to Indra, say to him your solemn eulogies. The drops poured forth have made him glad: pay reverence to his might supreme.
baseline: Having worshipped Indra with salt the sun should be sprinkled with a thread of bāvitā. The elder son of Indra should be worshipped with namas.
morphology: Having worshipped Indra with salt the thread should be broken and the threads should be offered. The elder one should be worshipped with the bow of Amatsu.

sanskrit: nakiḥ tvat rathītaraḥ harī yat indra yacchase nakiḥ tvā anu majmanā nakiḥ su aśvaḥ ānaśe
reference: When, Indra, thou dost yoke thy Steeds, there is no better charioteer: None hath surpassed thee in thy might, none with good steeds o'ertaken thee.
baseline: The chariot should be given to you by Hari. The charcer should be offered to Indra. The horse should be made to bear the same weight as mejmana.
morphology: O Hari who gives the chariot to you and the other side of it. O Indra you should not give it to me. You should not take it.

sanskrit: yaḥ ekaḥ it vi dayate vasu martāya dāśuṣe īśānaḥ aprati skutaḥ indraḥ aṅga
reference: He who alone bestoweth on mortal man who offereth gifts, The ruler of resistless power, is Indra, sure.
baseline: The one who gives it should be killed by Śuśu and the one who has left behind the body of Indra.
morphology: The one who gives the same as the other should be killed by the god Vasu the king of the dāśuśa and the king īṣṇa.

sanskrit: kadā martam arādhasam padā kṣumpam iva sphurat kadā naḥ śuśravat giraḥ indraḥ aṅga
reference: When will he trample, like a weed, the man who hath no gift for him? When, verily, will Indra hear our songs of praise?
baseline: Sometimes the body of a person who has not been killed or killed should be shaken like the feet of a cow. Sometimes the head of a man who has never served a cow should not be shaven.
morphology: Sometimes the body should be placed on the ground and the feet should be raised like a stone. Then the body of Indra should not be placed in the ground.

sanskrit: yaḥ cit hi tvā bahu bhyaḥ ā suta vān āvivāsati ugram tat patyate śavaḥ indraḥ aṅga
reference: He who with Soma juice prepared amid the many honours thee,– Verily Indra gains thereby tremendous might.
baseline: The body of Indra should be placed in the form of a lotus and the body should be kept in the same place.
morphology: The body of Indra who is living in a place of great fear and rest on the earth would be destroyed by the fiery spirit.

sanskrit: svādoḥ itthā viṣu vataḥ madhvaḥ pibanti gauryaḥ yāḥ indreṇa sa yāvarīḥ vr̥ṣṇā madanti śobhase vasvīḥ anu sva rājyam
reference: The juice of Soma thus diffused, sweet to the taste, the bright cows drink, Who for the sake of splendour close to mighty Indra's side rejoice, good in their own supremacy.
baseline: One who drinks honey with the help of the āndravas and the vrṣṇas would enjoy his kingdom.
morphology: One who drinks honey from the waters of the sky with the same taste as that of the vipu one who drinks water from the sun and the other who drink from the water of the Śvṛṣṇa river would be blessed with the glory of the kingdom.

sanskrit: tāḥ asya pr̥śana yuvaḥ somam śrīṇanti pr̥śnayaḥ priyāḥ indrasya dhenavaḥ vajram hinvanti sāyakam vasvīḥ anu sva rājyam
reference: Craving his touch the dappled kine mingle the Soma with their milk. The milch-kine dear to Indra send forth his death-dealing thunderbolt, good in their own supremacy.
baseline: Those who worship the sun should be worshipped by the young men. The cows of Indra should be worshiped by the devotees. The buffaloes of Indra would be worshipping the diamond.
morphology: The young men who ask for this would be called Soma and the cows of Indra would be taken away by the king. They would be known as Syaka and Vāsiva.

sanskrit: tāḥ asya namasā sahaḥ saparyanti pra cetasaḥ vratāni asya saścire purūṇi pūrva cittaye vasvīḥ anu sva rājyam
reference: With veneration, passing wise, honouring his victorious might, They follow close his many laws to win them due preeminence, good in their own supremacy.
baseline: Those who worship this place together with the vow of devotion should observe the vow in the morning. One who has settled his kingdom in the previous mind should perform the vow.
morphology: Those who worship this place together with the vow of devotion should be worshipped by the mind. One who has fulfilled the vow in the presence of the mind should return to his kingdom.

sanskrit: indraḥ dadhīcaḥ astha bhiḥ vr̥trāṇi aprati skutaḥ jaghāna navatīḥ nava
reference: With bones of Dadhyac for his arms, Indra, resistless in attack, Struck nine-and-ninety Vr̥itras dead.
baseline: O Indra one who is born in the middle of the earth and who is the son of Vritra is not a man.
morphology: O Indra the king of Dādhīccha Vritra Vrātras and the nine great gods are the nine gods.

sanskrit: icchan aśvasya yat śiraḥ parvateṣu apa śritam tat vidat śaryaṇāvati
reference: He, searching for the horse's head, removed among the mountains, found At Ṣaryaṇâvân what he sought.
baseline: The head of the horse should be heard in the mountains as desired by the king.
morphology: The head of the horse should be heard in the mountains as desired.

sanskrit: atra aha goḥ amanvata nāma tvaṣṭuḥ apīcyam itthā candramasaḥ gr̥he
reference: Then verily they recognized the essential form of Tvashṭar's Bull, Here in the mansion of the Moon.
baseline: Here the name of the cow is haaṇvata and the moon should be worshipped in the house.
morphology: The name of the cow should be mentioned here. The moon should be placed in the house.

sanskrit: kaḥ adya yuṅkte dhuri gāḥ r̥tasya śimī vataḥ bhāminaḥ duḥ hr̥ṇāyūn āsan iṣūn hatsu asaḥ maya bhūn yaḥ eṣām bhr̥tyām r̥ṇadhat saḥ jīvāt
reference: Who yokes to-day unto the pole of Order the strong and passionate steers of checkless spirit, With shaft-armed mouths, heart-piercing, health-bestowing? Long shall he live who richly pays their service.
baseline: One who has made a debt to his servant by offering a piece of gold a cow a horse and a cow in the month of the month and a man who had made a loss to his wife would get the money.
morphology: One who has made a debt to the servant of a cow a cow and a cow in the month of yuṇḍa and hastu hātu and bhuṇa should pay the debt.

sanskrit: kaḥ īṣate tujyate kaḥ bibhāya kaḥ maṁsate santam indram kaḥ anti kaḥ tokāya kaḥ ibhāya uta rāye adhi bravat tanve kaḥ janāya
reference: Who fleeth forth? who suffereth? who feareth? Who knoweth Indra present, Indra near us? Who sendeth benediction on his offspring, his household, wealth and person, and the People?
baseline: One who is pleased with the gift of God one who is happy with the loss of life another who is satisfied with the achievement of goodness one with goodness and one with whom one gets pleasure from the gift or one who has to suffer from the evil of evil will get victory.
morphology: One who is pleased by the illusion of God one who is happy with God and one who becomes happy with the goodness of God. One who gives peace to God another who gives power to God and one person who has power over others.

sanskrit: kaḥ agnim īṭe haviṣā ghr̥tena srucā yajātai r̥tu bhiḥ dhruvebhiḥ kasmai devāḥ ā vahān āśu homa kaḥ maṁsate vīti hotraḥ su devaḥ
reference: Who with poured oil and offering honours Agni, with ladle worships at appointed seasons? To whom to the Gods bring oblation quickly? What offerer, God-favoured, knows him thoroughly?
baseline: One who makes fire and bricks and hates the gods one who makes the gods of yājāta rūta bhi and dhruva fall in the sky and who makes them fall into the abyss.
morphology: One who makes a fire and a brick one who hates the earth and the gods of the earth and who brings the gods to the earth with the elements of the sun and the pole and gives me the haṇam.

sanskrit: tvam aṅga pra śaṁsiṣaḥ devaḥ śaviṣṭha martyam na tvat anyaḥ magha van asti marḍitā indra bravīmi te vacaḥ
reference: Thou as a God, O Mightiest, verily blessest mortal man. O Maghavan, there is no comforter but thou: Indra, I speak my words to thee.
baseline: O lord of the body and the body of the deceased. You are not the other one. O king of the forest. O Indra you are the one who killed the body.
morphology: O lord of the body and the body of the deceased. You are not the other one. O king you are the king of the dead. O lord Indra you are a king.

sanskrit: mā te rādhāṁsi mā te ūtayaḥ vaso iti asmān kadā cana dabhan viśvā ca naḥ upa mimīhi mānuṣa vasūn i carṣaṇi bhyaḥ ā
reference: Let not thy bounteous gifts, let not thy saving help fail us, good Lord, at any time; And measure out to us, thou lover of mankind, all riches hitherward from men.
baseline: We should never think that they are not equal to the form of Radha. They are not capable of supporting us. They do not have faith. These people are afraid of us.
morphology: They should not be worshipped by the goddess Radha. They should never be feared by us. We should never fear the gods. They do not believe in us. These people are afraid of us.

sanskrit: ā vidyunmat bhiḥ marutaḥ su arkaiḥ rathebhiḥ yāta r̥ṣṭimat bhiḥ aśva parṇaiḥ ā varṣiṣṭhayā naḥ iṣā vayaḥ na paptata su māyāḥ
reference: COME hither, Maruts, on your lightning laden cars, sounding with sweet songs, armed with lances, winged with steeds. Fly unto us with noblest food, like birds, O ye of mighty power.
baseline: O Śiva one who has gone to the desert with the ark the chariot the horse the leaves the elephant the bear the cow the animal and the elephant should be taken away from me.
morphology: O Śiva one who has gone to the desert with the ark the chariot the horse and leaves and has not been blessed with the vaśa.

sanskrit: te aruṇebhiḥ varam ā piśaṅgaiḥ śubhe kam yānti rathatūḥ bhiḥ aśvaiḥ rukmaḥ na citraḥ svadhiti vān pavyā rathasya jaṅghananta bhūma
reference: With their red-hued or, haply, tawny coursers which speed their chariots on, they come for glory. Brilliant like gold is he who holds the thunder. Earth have they smitten with the chariot's felly.
baseline: They should be offered in the form of a boon with the arms arms and arms. The chariot should be made into a good one. The horse should not be made to bear the image. The pigeon should be placed on the trunk of the charioteer.
morphology: They should be offered in the form of a boon with the arms and arms. The chariot should be made of two parts and the horse should not be drawn. The king should be placed on the ground at the junction of the chariots.

sanskrit: śriye kam vaḥ adhi tanūṣu vāśīḥ medhā vanā na kr̥ṇavante ūrdhvā yuṣmabhyam kam marutaḥ su jātāḥ tuvi dyumnāsaḥ dhanayante adrim
reference: For beauty ye have swords upon your bodies. As they stir woods so may they stir our spirits. For your sake, O ye Maruts very mighty and well-born, have they set the stone, in motion.
baseline: One who does not know the merits of the gods would be blessed by the goddess Śrī. One who is born out of you would get wealth from the goddess Dūmnā.
morphology: One who does not know the wisdom of the gods and who is superior to him would be blessed by you. One who dies from you would be rich by you and the other would be endowed with wealth.

sanskrit: ahāni gr̥dhrāḥ pari ā vaḥ ā aguḥ imām dhiyam vārkāryām ca devīm brahma kr̥ṇvantaḥ gotamāsaḥ arkaiḥ ūrdhvam nunudre utsa dhim pibadhyai
reference: The days went round you and came back O yearners, back, to this prayer and to this solemn worship. The Gotamas making their prayer with singing have pushed the well's lid up to drink the water.
baseline: The goddess Brahma should be worshipped with the words ahaṇī grādhrā pārī aa āga dhīmā vārākārya gotāma arqā and the water of the upper salt river.
morphology: The goddess Brahma should be worshipped with the words ahaṇī grādhrā pārī aa āga vārakārya and the goddess should be offered with the ark of the cow and the water of the river salutations.

sanskrit: etat tyat na yojanam aceti sasvaḥ ha yat marutaḥ gotamaḥ vaḥ paśyan hiraṇya cakrān ayaḥ daṁṣṭrān vi dhāvataḥ varāhūn
reference: No hymn way ever known like this aforetime which Gotama sang forth for you, O Maruts, What time upon your golden wheels he saw you, wild boars rushing about with tusks of iron.
baseline: Having not left this plan the mother-in-law knows that the king of the kingdom of Hiranyā should see the wheels of Hiranya. He should give them to the king. He would run away from them.
morphology: One who does not know the plan should leave it alone. One who sees Hiranyas wheel and the horses of the king should run away from the king.

sanskrit: eṣā syā vaḥ marutaḥ anu bhartrī prati stobhati vāghataḥ na vāṇī astobhayat vr̥thā āsām anu svadhām gabhastyoḥ
reference: To you this freshening draught of Soma rusheth, O Maruts, like the voice of one who prayeth. It rusheth freely from our hands as these. libations wont to flow.
baseline: This is the same as that of a woman who is dying and who is worshipping her husband. One who does not speak from the tiger would be destroyed by the enemy.
morphology: This is the same as that of a woman who dies and who worships her husband without having uttered a word from a tiger.

sanskrit: ā naḥ bhadrāḥ kratavaḥ yantu viśvataḥ adabdhāsaḥ apari itāsaḥ ut bhidaḥ devāḥ naḥ yathā sadam it vr̥dhe asan apra āyuvaḥ rakṣitāraḥ dive dive
reference: MAY powers auspicious come to us from every side, never deceived, unhindered, and victorious, That the Gods ever may be with us for our gain, our guardians day by day unceasing in their care.
baseline: O Bhadra one who has not been saved from the illusion of the universe and who has never been destroyed by the gods should not do good deeds. One who has been saved for a long time would not be able to do good.
morphology: O... one who has not been blessed with the gift of goodness has not lived long enough and has not had any trouble with the gods.

sanskrit: devānām bhadrā su matiḥ r̥ju yatām devānām rātiḥ abhi naḥ ni vartatām devānām sakhyam upa sedima vayam devāḥ naḥ āyuḥ pra tirantu jīvase
reference: May the auspicious favour of the Gods be ours, on us descend the bounty of the righteous Gods. The friendship of the Gods have we devoutly sought: so may the Gods extend our life that we may live.
baseline: One who does not worship the gods the gods and the goddess of the night the life of the living beings should be fixed in the same manner as the one who worships the gods.
morphology: The image of the god Bhadra should be straight and the image should be fixed. If the god is not worshipped in the night the image of God should be placed in the middle of the night. We should not worship the gods. Let the life of the gods pass away.

sanskrit: tān pūrvayā ni vidā hūmahe vayam bhagam mitram aditim dakṣam asridham aryamaṇam varuṇam somam aśvinā sarasvatī naḥ su bhagā mayaḥ karat
reference: We call them hither with a hymn of olden time, Bhaga, the friendly Daksha, Mitra, Aditi, Aryaman, Varuṇa, Soma, the Aṣvins. May Sarasvatî, auspicious, grant felicity.
baseline: They should be sent away from the east. We are the gods friends allies friends and friends. Aditi Daksha Asridha Aryamana Varuṇa Soma Asvīna Sarasvatī.
morphology: They should be sent away from the east. We should leave the earth the friend the enemy Aditi Daksha Asridha Aryamana Varuṇa Soma Asvīna Sarasvati and others.

sanskrit: tat naḥ vātaḥ mayaḥ bhu vātu bheṣajam tat mātā pr̥thivī tat pitā dyauḥ tat grāvāṇaḥ soma sutaḥ mayaḥ bhuvaḥ tat aśvinā śr̥ṇutam dhiṣṇyā yuvam
reference: May the Wind waft to us that pleasant medicine, may Earth our Mother give it, and our Father Heaven, And the joy-giving stones that press the Soma's juice. Aṣvins, may ye, for whom our spirits long, hear this.
baseline: That which is not the wind that which is the ground that is the earth that that is given by the father that that   that should be heard by the horse that.
morphology: Then the wind should be made to fall on the earth. Then the earth should fall on its mother. Then it should be given to the father. The earth should rise on its feet. The sky should fall off on its knees. The sun should rise and fall on it. The king should be heard by the horses.

sanskrit: tam īśānam jagataḥ tasthuṣaḥ patim dhiyam jinvam avase hūmahe vayam pūṣā naḥ yathā vedasam asat vr̥dhe rakṣitā pāyuḥ adabdhaḥ svastaye
reference: Him we invoke for aid who reigns supreme, the Lord of all that stands or moves, inspirer of the soul, That Pûshan may promote the increase of our wealth, our keeper and our guard infallible for our good.
baseline: Then the earth should be placed in the east and the earth in the west. The body should be made of the same size as that of the jinn. We should not put flowers in the ground as in the case of the Vedas. The feet should be kept on the ground and the feet should not be left on the earth.
morphology: Then the earth should be placed on the east side of the earth. Then the body should be made to stand on the left side. Then we should not wear clothes like the veda and the feet should be kept on the right side.

sanskrit: svasti naḥ indraḥ vr̥ddha śravāḥ svasti naḥ pūṣā viśva vedāḥ svasti naḥ tārkṣyaḥ ariṣṭa nemiḥ svasti naḥ br̥haspatiḥ dadhātu
reference: Illustrious far and wide, may Indra prosper us: may Pûshan prosper us, the Master of all wealth. May Târkshya with uninjured fellies prosper us: Br̥ihaspati vouchsafe to us prosperity.
baseline: One who is not selfish one who is old and has no sense of hearing is not good for the world one whose mind is not in the Vedas one with the mind is poor and one who does not have the power of the universe one without the power to do so one not having the power.
morphology: One who does not know the nature of the universe does not understand the meaning of the word Śvāṇa does NOT understand the nature. One who is old and has heard the universe and the Vedas is not aware of the existence of the world one who is illiterate and does not believe in the nature and nature of Brihaspati.

sanskrit: pr̥ṣat aśvāḥ marutaḥ pr̥śni mātaraḥ śubham yāvānaḥ vidatheṣu jagmayaḥ agni jihvāḥ manavaḥ sūra cakṣasaḥ viśve naḥ devāḥ avasā ā gaman iha
reference: The Maruts, Sons of Prani, borne by spotted steeds, moving in glory, oft visiting holy rites, Sages whose tongue is Agni, brilliant as the Sun,– hither let all the Gods for our protection come.
baseline: The horses should be asked to die and the mother should be told to do good. The disciples should be aware of the fire tongue mind eye voice and the world. The gods should not be heard.
morphology: The horses should be asked to die and the mother should be told to do good. Those who know the world the fire the tongue the mind the voice the eyes the world and the gods should not go away.
