baseline: One who stands on the horses standing on the sides of the lords standing in front of the centre and standing in the direction of the celestial body should be worshipped by the lord of that place. Having worshipped all the gods and worshipped them one should offer sacrifices to the gods. One who offers a sacrifice to a son of a brahmacharin should offer a sacrifice of the same name.
morphology: One who stands on the horses standing on the sides of the river and standing in front of the centre standing in the direction of the celestial body and standing on that side of the earth and having taken all the offerings made by him should offer sacrifices to the gods worshipping the gods and worshipping them.

sanskrit: sa vā ebhyastatpuro 'dāśayat / ya ebhyo yajñam prārocayattasmātpurodāśaḥ purodāśo ha vai nāmaitadyatpuroḍāśa iti sa eṣa ubhayatrācyuta āgneyo 'ṣṭākapālaḥ puroḍāśo bhavati //
reference: Now that (cake), which caused the sacrifice to attract (or, appear to) them, first (puras) bestowed (dâs) it upon them: hence it is (called) purodâsa, for purodâsa, doubtless, is the same as purodâsa . This same cake on eight potsherds for Agni is indispensable on both occasions (at the new- and full-moon ceremonies).
baseline: One who offers a sacrifice to these men would be called a prudāśo. One who does not offer a sacrifice would become a pūrudāṣo. He would become the prudáśo of fire and fire.
morphology: He who offers a sacrifice to these men would be called a priest a priest and a priest. He who does not offer a sacrifice would be declared a fireman or a guard of fire.

sanskrit: nāmāvāsyamagnīṣomīya eva paurṇamāsaṃ haviḥ sāṃnāyyamāmāvāsyaṃ yajña evaiṣa ubhayatrāvakLpto nedyajñādayānīti nveva purastātpaurṇamāsasya kriyata evamvāmāvāsyasyaitannu tadyasmādatra kriyate //
reference: That one (for Agni) constitutes rather the regular (or, corresponding) sacrifice on both occasions, and because of its fearing lest it should become detached from the sacrifice, it is offered up at the beginning of both the full-moon and the new-moon sacrifice: this is the reason why it is offered at this particular time.
baseline: The same month as the full moon in the month of Navāsīma Ganīśoṃ the same month should be worshipped in the same manner as the month in which the worship of the goddess is done in the previous month. It should not be performed in this manner.
morphology: The same month as the full moon in the month of Navāsīma Agniśoṃ the same month in which the goddess should be worshipped in the same manner as the goddess of the moon one should not perform the same sacrifice with the intention of offering two things. One should do the same thing in the previous month of the month ending with Vāmasīma.

sanskrit: iṣṭyā mā yājayetyetayaiva yājayedyatkāmā vā etamṛṣayo 'juhavuḥ sa ebhyaḥ kāmaḥ samardhyata yatkāmo ha vā etena yajñena yajate so 'smai kāmaḥ samṛdhyate yasyai vai kasyai ca devatāyai havirgṛhyate 'gnau vai tasyai yuhvatyagnā u ceddhoṣyantsyātkimanyasyai devatāyā ādiśettasmādagnaya eva //
reference: Whatever desire the Rishis entertained when they performed that sacrifice, that desire of theirs was accomplished; and accordingly whatever desire he (the sacrificer) entertains in having this sacrifice performed, that desire of his is accomplished. For whatever deity sacrificial food is taken, to that deity they offer it up in the fire (Agni);--and if he is about to offer it up in the fire, why should he announce it to another deity? To Agni alone therefore (it is announced).
baseline: The priest should not offer any kind of sacrifice to any deity. He should offer the same amount of money to these devotees. He who gives the same kind of love to any of the deities would be blessed with that kind of affection. He would also offer a gift to any other deity. The same would be offered to the gods of the world.
morphology: The priest should not offer any sacrifice to any deity. He should offer any offering made to them by offering a sacrifice to the goddess. He who offers a sacrifice made to a particular deity would be enriched by the offering of the sacrifice. He would also offer the oblation made to the deity made to be worshipped by the goddess Yuhvatyagna the incarnation of the goddess Chedodhyanta and the incantation made by him.

sanskrit: agnirvai sarvā devatāḥ / agnau hi sarvābhyo devatābhyo juhvati tadyathā sarvā devatā upadhāvedevaṃ tattasmādagnaya eva // agnirvai devānāmaddhātamām /
reference: Agni (the fire), assuredly, represents all the deities, since it is in the fire that they make offering to all deities: to Agni alone therefore (he should announce it), since he thereby has recourse to all the deities.
baseline: The fire should be worshipped by all the gods the fire fire and fire should also be offered to all the deities.
morphology: All the gods should be worshipped with fire fire and fire. In the same way all gods should worship the gods with fire.

sanskrit: agnirvai devānāṃ mṛduhṛdayatamaḥ / yaṃ vai mṛduhṛdayatamam manyeta tamupadhāvettasmādagnaya eva //
reference: Agni, assuredly, is the most tender-hearted of gods: let him then have recourse to him whom he considers the most tender-hearted of gods, and therefore (announce the sacrifice) to Agni.
baseline: One who is the softest heart of the gods by the fire one who is considered to be the mildest heart should worship him.
morphology: One who is considered to be the softest heart of the gods and the one who is the lightest of the fire should worship him.

sanskrit: agnirvai devānāṃ nediṣṭham / yaṃ vai nediṣṭhamupasartavyānām manyeta tamupadhāvettasmādagnaya eva //
reference: Agni, assuredly, is the nearest of the gods: let him then have recourse to him whom he considers as the nearest of those to be approached, and therefore (let him announce the sacrifice) to Agni.
baseline: One should worship the gods with fire and not with fire. He should worship those worshipped with fire not with water.
morphology: One who does not believe in the fire the gods and the gods should be destroyed by the fire. One who believes in those who do not want to do so should be punished by him.

sanskrit: sa yadīṣṭiṃ kurvīta / saptadaśa sāmidhenīranubrūyādupāṃśu devatāṃ yajati taddhīṣṭirūpam mūrdhanvatyau yājyānuvākye syātāṃ vārtraghnāvājyabhāgau virājau saṃyājye //
reference: If (beside the full-moon sacrifice) he perform an ishti (with a view to the accomplishment of somespecial desire) , let him recite seventeen kindling verses; (and in that case) he utters the offering-prayer (yâgyâ) in a low voice, for this is the characteristic form of an ishti; the yâgyâ and the anuvâkyâ should contain the word 'head ;' the two butter-portions should be offered to the Vritra-slayer (Indra); and the two samyâgyâs should be in the virâg metre.
baseline: He should perform the oblation of the seven hundred and twenty-somethings. He should offer the oblations of the form of the goddess to the gods of the sun man woman man and man. The priest should give the obeisance of the priest the chief minister king king and king in the union of the king.
morphology: He should perform the ritual of yadisti. He should offer the form of the goddess as nūbrūya ādupāṇu and the form as mūrdhāvatya. The priest should speak these words to the king the king and the king.

sanskrit: tvaṣṭurha vai putraḥ /
reference: Tvashtri had a three-headed, six-eyed son.
baseline: He is the son of Tūṣṭrū.
morphology: He is the son of Tūṣṭrū.

sanskrit: triśīrṣā ṣaḍakṣa āsa tasya trīṇyeva mukhānyāsustadyadevaṃrūpa āsa tasmādviśvarūpo nāma //
reference: He had three mouths; and because he was thus shaped, his name was Visvarûpa ('All-shape').
baseline: He should have three heads and six arms. He should be worshipped as a god with his three faces.
morphology: He should have three heads and six sides. He should be worshipped as the third face. He would be worshipping the form of God.

sanskrit: tasya somapānamevaikam mukhamāsa / surāpāṇamekamanyasmā a /śanāyaikaṃ tamindro didveṣa tasya tāni śīrṣāṇi praciceda //
reference: One of his mouths was Soma-drinking, one spirit-drinking, and one for other kinds of food. Indra hated him and cut off those heads of his.
baseline: One should drink the soma of the same mouth one should drink wine another one should offer the tāmīndra and the heads.
morphology: One should drink the same lotus in the mouth and one should drink wine in the face. Then we should give one tāmīndra in the morning and spread the heads of the same.

sanskrit: sa yatsomapānamāsa / tataḥ kapiñjalaḥ samabhavattasmātsababhruka iva babhruriva hi somo rājā //
reference: Now from the one which was Soma-drinking, a hazel-cock (francoline partridge) sprang forth; whence the latter is of brownish colour, for king Soma is brown.
baseline: He should drink the same amount of water in the month of yāsoma. Then he should be made to eat and drink with the same quantity of water as the king.
morphology: He should drink water in the month of Yāsoma. Then he should be equal to Kapinjala. He should be like a rabbit and a king.

sanskrit: tataḥ kalaviṅkaḥ samabhavattasmātso 'bhimādyatka iva vadatyabhimādyanniva hi surām pītvā vadati //
reference: From the one which was spirit-drinking, further, a sparrow sprang; whence the latter talks as if stammering, for he who has drunk spirits, talks as if he stammered.
baseline: Then the kalavinka is said to be equal to that which is equal to the amount of his desire. Having said that he drinks the sura after having said that.
morphology: Then the kalavinka should be equated with that which is said to be the same as that of the abode of desire. He drinks the surma after having said that the abodes of desire are equal to that of a god.

sanskrit: atha yadanyasmā aśanāyāsa / tatastittiriḥ samabhavattasmātsa viśvarūpatama iva santyeva ghṛstokā iva tvanmadhustokā iva tvatparṇeṣvāścutitā evaṃ rūpaṃ hi sa tenāśanamāvayat //
reference: Then from the one which served for other kinds of food, a partridge sprang; whence the latteris much variegated in colour: on its wings, namely, butter-drops, as it were, have dropped in one place and honey- (or mead-) drops in another, for suchlike, as it were, was the food which he consumed with that (mouth).
baseline: Then when we have made an offering he should offer the same to us. He should make the offering of the same kind of gift as the worldly form. He would also make the offer of the gift of honey as a gift.
morphology: Then if we are to be worshipped in the same manner as others he will be worshipping you in the form of the world as if you were worshipped with the same kind of fire as in the case of the abomination of the universe as when you are worshipped by him.

sanskrit: sa tvaṣṭā cukrodha /
reference: Tvashtri was furious: 'Has he indeed slain my son?' he exclaimed.
baseline: He is the one who has destroyed you.
morphology: He should be worshipped with the chukkrodh.

sanskrit: kuvinme putramavadhīditi so 'pendrameva somamājahre sa yathāyaṃ somaḥ prasuta evamapendra evāsa //
reference: He brought Soma-juice from which Indra was excluded; and just as the Soma-juice on being produced had Indra excluded from it (apendra), so it remained (when it was offered up).
baseline: The son should be worshipped in the form of a kuṇimā. He should be offered to the son of Somāma in the same manner as the son given to him.
morphology: The son should be given to the priest in the same manner as to the son of the lord. He should be blessed with the son in equal measure.

sanskrit: idaṃ vai mā somādantaryantīti sa yathā balīyānabalīyasa evamanupahūta eva yo droṇakalaśe śukra āsa tam bhakṣayāṃ cakāra sa hainaṃ jihiṃsa so 'sya viṣvaṅṅeva prāṇebhyo dudrāva mukhāddhaivāsya na dudrāvātha sarvebhyo 'nyebhyaḥ prāṇebhyo 'dravattadadaḥ sautrāmaṇītīṣṭistasyāṃ tadvyākhyāyate yathainaṃ devā abhiṣajyan //
reference: Indra thought with himself, 'They are now excluding me from Soma!' and though uninvited, he consumed what pure (Soma) there was in the tub, even as the stronger (consumes) that of a weaker. That (Soma) however, injured him; it flowed in all directions from (the openings of) his vital airs; from his mouth alone it did not flow, but from all the other (openings of the) vital airs it flowed; hence (was instituted) at that time the ishti, called Sautrâmanî: on the occasion of that (ceremony) it is explained how the gods healed him .
baseline: He who eats a piece of meat after having been blessed with a cow should not eat it. He should not drink water from the mouth of a cow and should not consume milk from a cow. He would not drink milk from any animal and would not eat milk from another animal.
morphology: He who eats a cow and eats it after having been blessed with a sacrifice a sacrifice and a sacrifice made by the same man should not do so. He should not eat the cow and eat it. He would not drink milk from the mouth and drink from the water of the cow the water from the cow or from the blood of the animals. He is said to have done the same thing as the one who was killed by God.

sanskrit: sa tvaṣṭā cukrodha kuvinme 'nupahūtaḥ somamababhakṣaditi sasvayameva yajñaveśasa cakre sa yo droṇakalaśe śukraḥ pariśiṣṭa āsa ta pravartayāṃ cakārendraśatrurvardhasveti so'gnimeva prāpya sambabhūvāntaraiva sambabhūvetyu haika āhuḥ so 'gnīṣomāvevābhisambabhūva sarvā vidyāḥ sarvaṃ yaśaḥ sarvamannādyaṃ sarvāṃ śrīṃ //
reference: Tvashtri was furious, and exclaimed, 'Has he indeed consumed my Soma uninvited?' However, he himself desecrated the sacrifice, for what pure (Soma) there was left in the tub he let flow (into the fire), saying, 'Grow thou, having Indra for thy foe !' The moment it reached the fire, itdeveloped (into human shape), or, as some say, it so developed whilst on its way (to the fire). It became possessed of Agni and Soma, of all sciences, all glory, all nourishment, all prosperity.
baseline: He who has made the oblation of a drona should be worshipped in the same way as that of a cow and eat the summa bhavābā in the morning. He who is attached to the pot of the goddess dronā then he should worship the lord of the enemy Śvardhāśvatī. Having attained the fire he should be offered to the god Sambhubhu the god of fire the king of all knowledge all knowledge and all happiness all happiness and all joy.
morphology: He who offers the oblation in the same way as the one who is attached to the vessel of Drona and who eats the summa and bhaṭuva food in the cave then he becomes the chief enemy of the enemy. Having attained the fire he acquires the knowledge of all things and becomes the master of all knowledge. He becomes the lord of all beings.

sanskrit: tasmādvṛtro 'tha yadapātsamabhavattasmādahistaṃ danuśca danāyūśca māteva ca piteva ca parijagṛhatustasmāddānava ityāhuḥ //
reference: And since it so developed whilst rolling onwards (vrit), it became Vritra; and since he sprang forth footless, therefore he was a serpent. Danu and Danâyû received him like mother and father , whence they call him Dânava.
baseline: If he has made a gift to his mother and mother he should take the gift of his wife mother brother wife wife and children.
morphology: If you have two sons you will get the same amount of money as your father. You will get a son daughter mother daughter and son. You also get the gift from me.

sanskrit: atha yadabravīdindraśatrurvardhasveti / tasmādu hainamindra eva jaghānātha yaddha śaśvadavakṣyadindrasya śatrurvardhasveti śaśvadu ha sa evendramahaniṣyat //
reference: And because he (Tvashtri) said, 'Grow thou, having Indra for thy foe!' therefore Indra slew him (Vritra). Had he said, 'Grow thou, the foe (slayer) of Indra!' he (Vritra) would certainly have forthwith slain Indra.
baseline: If the enemy of the enemy is the same as that of the king he should be killed by the king. If the king of the kingdom is killed by him he would be killed.
morphology: If the enemy of the centre of the earth is vardhśvatī then the king of the world is the same as that of Hāyāṇimāndra. If the king is the enemy and the enemy is Vardhṣvatṛṣvā then he will be destroyed.

sanskrit: tasmādu ha smeṣumātrameva tiryaṅvardhata iśumātram prāṅkṣo vaivāvaraṃ samudraṃ dadhāvava pūrvaṃ sa yāvatsa āsa sahaiva tāvadannāda āsa //
reference: And because he (Tvashtri) said, 'Grow thou!' therefore he (Vritra) grew an arrow's range sideways and an arrow's range forward: he forced back both the western ocean and the eastern one; and in proportion as he extended did he devour the food.
baseline: Then he should rise only three times. He should raise the sea as far as possible. He would have been with him as long as he had been before.
morphology: Then he would rise only three times. He would raise the sea as far as he could. He should rise only one time. He had been there with him as long as he had been before.

sanskrit: tasmai ha sma pūrvāhṇe devāḥ / aśanamabhiharanti madhyandine manuṣyā aparāhṇe pitaraḥ //
reference: In the fore-noon the gods offered him food, at mid-day the men, and in the after-noon the Fathers.
baseline: Then the gods should be worshipped in the morning in the middle of the day and men should be worshiped in the evening.
morphology: Then the gods should be worshipped in the morning in the middle of the day and the men should be worshiped in the evening.

sanskrit: sa vā indrastathaiva nuttaścaran / agnīṣomā upamantrayāṃ cakre 'gnīṣomau yuvaṃ vai mama stho yuvayorahamasmi na yuvayoreṣa kiṃ cana kam ma imaṃ dasyuṃ vardhayatha upa māvartethāmiti //
reference: Now while Indra was thus moving on (in pursuit of Vritra), he addressed Agni and Soma, 'Ye belong to me and I belong to you! That one is nothing to you: why then do ye support that Dasyu against me? Come over to me!'
baseline: He should also repeat the words of Indra the fire the sub-mantra the circle the flame the yuva the young the jūva yorhamā what should I do with the young man the thief the robber and the robbers.
morphology: He should also chant the same words as Indra fire vice mantra circle flame fire and fire the young man should be my son and the king should not be my brother. What should I do with this son of a thief?

sanskrit: kimāvayostataḥ syāditi tābhyāmetamagnīṣom īyamekādaśakapālam puroḍāśaṃ niravapattasmādagnīṣomīya ekādaśakapālaḥ puroḍāśo bhavati //
reference: They replied, 'What is to be our reward in that case?' He offered them that Agni-Soma cake on eleven potsherds: this is the reason why there is a cake on eleven potsherds for Agni and Soma.
baseline: One should know whether the fire should be destroyed or not. The fire should not be destroyed in one month. One would get destroyed by fire in another month.
morphology: One should know whether the fire should be destroyed or not. The fire should not be destroyed in one month. The flame should be removed from the ground after eleven days.

sanskrit: tāvenamupāvavṛtatuḥ / tāvanu sarve devāḥ preyuḥ sarvā vidyāḥ sarvaṃ yaśaḥ sarvamannādyaṃ sarvā śrīsteneṣṭvendra etadabhavadyadidamindra eṣa u paurṇamāsasya bandhuḥ sa yo haivaṃ vidvānpaurṇamāsena yajata etāṃ haiva śriyaṃ gacatyevaṃ yaśo bhavatyevamannādo bhavati //
reference: They went over to him, and after them went forth all the gods, all the sciences, all glory, all nourishment, all prosperity: thus by offering that (cake to Agni and Soma) Indra became what Indra now is. Such then is the significance of the full-moon offering; and he who, knowing this, performs the full-moon offering in this wise, attains to the same state of prosperity, becomes thus endowed with glory, becomes such a consumer of food (as Vritra).
baseline: One who gives all knowledge all success all happiness all joy all prosperity all wealth and all happiness to all gods one who is a friend in the month of the full moon and a wise man who gives the gift of the holy month of Pournima becomes a friend of the king. One who gets the gift from the lord of knowledge and the king of the moon becomes a king.
morphology: One who gives all knowledge to the gods all success to them all happiness all joy all pleasure all prosperity all goodness all wealth and all happiness in the month of the full moon one who is a friend of the king who is known to be a wise man who has been a member of the kingdom of the moon and who has given the gift of the holy month of Pournima becomes a king.

sanskrit: tadveva khalu hato vṛtraḥ / sa yathā dṛtirniṣpīta evaṃ saṃlīnaḥ śiśye yathā nirdhūtasakturbhastraivaṃ saṃlīnaḥ śiśye tamindro 'bhyādudrāva haniṣyan //
reference: Now Vritra, on being struck, lay contracted like a leather bottle drained of its contents, like a skin bag with the barley-meal shaken out.
baseline: In the same way Vritra would be defeated. He would be destroyed as soon as possible. The disciple would be killed as if he had been defeated by the disciple. He should be destroyed in the same manner as in the case of a disciple who had not been defeated.
morphology: In the same way Vritra should be killed in the same manner as in the case of a disciple who has been caught by the enemy. The disciple should be beaten with the same clothes as the disciple with whom he had not been beaten.

sanskrit: mā nu me prahārṣīstvaṃ vai tadetarhyasi yadahaṃ vyeva mā kuru māmuyā bhūvamiti sa vai me 'nnamedhīti tatheti taṃ dvedhānvabhinattasya yatsaumyaṃ nyaktamāsa taṃ candramasaṃ cakārātha yadasyāsuryamāsa tenemāḥ prajā udareṇāvidhyattasmādāhurvṛtra eva tarhyannāda āsīdvṛtra etarhītīdaṃ hi yadasāvāpūryate 'smādevaitallokādāpyāyate 'tha yadimāḥ prajā aśanamicante 'smā evaitadvṛtrāyodarāya baliṃ haranti sa yo haivametaṃ vṛtramannādaṃ vedānādo haiva bhavati //
reference: He said, 'Do not hurl (thy thunderbolt) at me! thou art now what I (was before) Only cut me in twain; but do not let me be annihilated!' He (Indra) said, 'Thou shalt be my food!' He replied, 'So be it!' He accordingly cut him in twain; and from that (part) of his which was of the Soma nature , he made the moon, and that which was demoniacal (asurya) he made enter these creatures as their belly; hence people say : 'Vritra was then a consumer of food, and Vritra is so now.' For even now, whenever that one (the moon) waxes fuller, it fills itself out of this world ; and wheneverthese creatures crave for food, they pay tribute to this Vritra, the belly. Whosoever knows that Vritra as a consumer of food, becomes himself a consumer of food.
baseline: If he does not do the same thing as the king he should not do it. If he has not done the same to me if he has done it in the month of May he would have done it to me. If the king of the two kingdoms of the kingdom of Bihar and the king had not done it then the king would have destroyed the king. If his sons were to be worshipped in the same month the king should have worshipped him in the morning if they had worshipped the king in the evening if the king was worshipped by us if we had offered a sacrifice to him
morphology: If he has said that he would not make a sacrifice as if he had made a sacrifice to the mother of a man who had been sent to the earth by me he would have made it to the moon in the month of May and if he has sent a gift of the moon the same would have been done to the people of the month as before. If he had offered a gift to the goddess after having been carried away by the king he should have offered it to her. If the gift is made to him by the lord of the earth the gift made by him would be made to the king of the world

sanskrit: tā u haitā devatā ūcuḥ / yā imā agnīṣomāvanvājagmuragnīṣomau yuvaṃ vai no bhūyiṣṭhabhājau stho yayorvāmidaṃ yuvayorasmānanvābhajatamiti //
reference: Those deities then said, 'Ye, Agni and Soma, whom we have followed hither, take the best part (of the sacrificial food): do let us share along with you in what ye have!'
baseline: That which is a god of fire fire war fire and fire is not a part of the earth. It is called yauva yaorva jayorvāmī yuva and yūrva.
morphology: That is the high deity that is the fire the fire and the fire. That is not the earth the earth and the earth.

sanskrit: kimāvayostataḥ syāditi yasyai kasyai ca devatāyai havirnirvapāṃstadvām purastādājyasya yajāniti tasmādyasyai kasyai ca devatāyai havirnirvapanti tatpurastādājyabhāgāvagnīṣomābhyāṃ yajanti tanna saumye 'dhvare na paśau yasyai kasyai ca devatāyai nirvapāniti hyabruvan //
reference: They both said, 'What (share) shall then be ours?' They replied, 'For whatever deity they shall take out sacrificial food, they shall in the first place offer to you some clarified butter!' Whenever, therefore, they take out sacrificial food for any deity, they in the first place offer two butter-portions to Agni and Soma. This does not take place at the Soma-sacrifice, nor at the animal offering; for they said, 'for whatever deity they take out .
baseline: One who has made a sacrifice for any deity should pay tribute to that particular deity. One who does not make a sacrifice to any other deity would be given his share of the property. One should not give his property to any animal. He would not give any animal to any deity.
morphology: One who has not given to any other deity the gift of water from that place would get the gift. One who does not give to any animal or any other goddess the gift would get to another deity. He would not get his share of the gift from those two gods.

sanskrit: sa hāgniruvāca /
baseline: He should be seated on the throne.
morphology: He should be seated on the throne.

sanskrit: mayyeva vaḥ sarvebhyo juhvatu tadvo 'haṃ mayyābhajāmīti tasmādagnau sarvebhyo devebhyo juhvati tasmādāhuragniḥ sarvā devatā iti //
reference: Agni then said, 'In me they shall sacrifice for all of you, and thus I give you a share in me!' For this reason they sacrifice in Agni (the fire) to all the gods; and for this reason they say that Agni is all the deities.
baseline: The fire of the fire is said to be the fire of all gods.
morphology: The fire of the fire should be offered to all the gods. In the same way the fire of fire is offered to the gods by all the deities.

morphology: O Sāma one who worships all the gods should worship me in the same way. He should worship all the deities.

But (it may be objected) if this is twofold only, why then this manifold performance:--the two butter-portions for Agni and Soma, the low-voiced offering to Agni and Soma, and the rice-cake for Agni and Soma,--when by means of any one of these he obtains all, why then this manifold performance? [The answer to this objection is that] so manifold is the power, the generative force of Agni and Soma.

sanskrit: kimidaṃ jāmi kriyate 'gnīṣomayorevājyasyāgnīṣomayoḥ puroḍāśasya yadanantarhitaṃ tena jāmītyanena ha tvevājāmyājyasyetaram puroḍāśasyetaraṃ tadanyadivetaramanyadivetaram bhavatyṛcamanūcya juṣāṇena yajatyṛcamanūcyarcā yajati tadanyadivetaramanyadivetaram bhavatyanena ha tvevājāmyupāṃśvājyasya yajatyuccaiḥ puroḍāśasya sa yadupāṃśu tatprājāpatyaṃ rūpaṃ tasmāttasyānuṣṭubhamanuvākyāmanvāha vāgghyanuṣṭubvāgghi prajāpatiḥ //
reference: Moreover, after reciting a Rik-verse as anuvâkyâ, he pronounces the yâgyâ with the word 'pleased' (in the case of the butter-portions to Agni and Soma); and after reciting a Rik-verse as anuvâkyâ, he pronounces the yâgyâ in the form of a Rik-verse (in the case of the low-voiced offering to Agni and Soma), hence the one is (again) different from the other . Sameness of performance is also avoided in this way: in a low voice (he utters the formulas when) he offers of the butter, and with a loud voice of the cake; and what is (uttered) in a low voice, that is the manner of Pragâpati: hence he recites for that (low-voicedoffering) an anushtubh-verse as the invitatory formula (anuvâkyâ), for the anushtubh represents speech, and Pragâpati also is speech.
baseline: The king of the two kingdoms of the fire the kingdom of the sun the king of fire and the king the chief minister of the kingdoms the governor of the kingdom the lord of the gods of the east the prince of the west the ruler of the north the son of a man who is born out of the absence of fire and who is living out of it the god of the earth the goddess of the sky the other gods the gods gods and goddesses of the south the sons of the moon the kings of the East and those who are born

reference: Those two (qualities), truly, are related to the natures of Agni and Soma: that which is white is related to Agni, and that which is black is related to Soma. If, however (it were asserted), on the contrary, that what is black is related to Agni, and what is white is related to Soma,--[the answer would be:--] what sees is of the nature of Agni, for dry, as it were, are the eyes of one who looks, and that which is dry relates to Agni;--and what sleeps is of the nature of Soma, for moist, as it were, are the eyes of one who is asleep, and moist also is Soma. morphology: The wind that touches the branches of the river should be kept in place. The wind which touches the ground should be placed in place in the same way. If it rains or if it rains then it should be spread. Then the wind should remain in place and the other branches should be removed. It should not be spread in the form of water.

sanskrit: atha mātṛṇāmekāṃ śākhayopaspṛśati /
reference: After separating one of the mothers from her calf, he touches her, with the text (Vâg. S.
baseline: One of the branches of the mother is thus touched.
morphology: In this way one of the branches of the mother is touched.

sanskrit: vatsena vyākṛtya devo vaḥ savitā prārpayatviti savitā vai devānām prasavitā savitṛprasūtā yajñaṃ sambharāniti tasmādāha devo vaḥ savitā prārpayatviti //
reference: I, I d), 'May the divine Savitri animate you--' for Savitri, indeed, is the impeller (prasavitri) of the gods:[paragraph continues] 'may they, impelled by Savitri, prepare the sacrifice!' so he thinks, and for this reason he says, 'May the divine Savitri animate you!'
baseline: Having worshipped the goddess with the vātsa one should offer the goddess Savita. One who gives birth to the goddess would be blessed with the gift of the mother the sacrifice of the child and the offering made by the goddess of the womb would be given to her.
morphology: Having worshipped the gods with the vātsa Savita should be offered to the gods. Having given birth to the goddess the goddess should offer the sacrifice of the mother and child. Having offered the sacrifice to the god of the womb she should offer it to the lord.

sanskrit: yajño vai śreṣṭhatamaṃ karma yajñāya hi tasmādāha śreṣṭhatamāya karmaṇa iti //
reference: '--To the most glorious work!' for assuredly the sacrifice is the most glorious work: hence, when he says 'to the most glorious work!' he means to say 'to the sacrifice.'
baseline: The highest form of sacrifice is called the supreme form of action.
morphology: The highest form of action for the sacrifice is the sacrifice for the supreme form.

sanskrit: āpyāyadhvamaghnyā indrāya bhāgamiti / tadyathaivādo devatāyai havirgṛhṇannādiśatyevamevaitaddevatāyā ādiśati yadāhāpyāyadhvamaghnyā indrāya bhāgamiti //
reference: 'Make swell, ye invincible (or inviolable) ones, the share for Indra!' In like manner as then , taking the sacrificial food (rice), he announces it to the deity, so now also he announces that (libation of milk) to the deity when he says 'make swell, ye invincible ones, the share for Indra!
baseline: One who takes a part in the worship of Indra by taking a part of the offerings made to him would be called a partaker of Indra. In the same way one who takes the gift from the deity would be ordered to give the same direction to the deity. If one gets it by taking part in that parting one would be known as Indra.
morphology: One who takes a part in the worship of Indra by offering a dvāhmāgha is called a partaker. In the same way one who gives a gift to a deity would get a share in the service of the deity by offering the same direction. If one gets it one would get the partaker of Indra.

sanskrit: prajāvatīranamīvā ayakṣmā iti / nātra tirohitamivāsti mā va stena īśata māghaśaṃsa iti mā vo nāṣṭrā rakṣāṃsīśatetyevaitadāha dhruvā asmingopatau syāta bahvīrityanapakramiṇyo 'sminyajamāne bahvyaḥ syātetyevaitadāha //
reference: 'Over you that are rich in offspring, over you that are free from suffering and disease--;' in this there is nothing that is obscure; '--no thief, no ill-wisher may lord it!'--he thereby means to say, 'may the evil spirits, the Rakshas, not lord it over you!'--'May ye be numerous and constant to this lord of cattle!'--thereby he means to say 'may ye be numerous with this sacrificer, and not abandon him.'
baseline: O king of the earth one who is not a priest should not be worshipped by the gods. One who does not worship the gods of the world should not worship them. One should worship the goddess of the universe and the goddesses of the gods the goddessesses goddesses and goddesses.
morphology: O Lord of the earth O lord of the gods O Lord O king of the universe O God of the world O son of the king of gods do not worship the goddess of heaven O mother of the goddesses O goddess of fire O daughter of the god of the sky O god of salvation One who is worshipped by the gods in this temple and who has been worshipped in the form of many gods and goddesses.

sanskrit: athāhavanīyāgārasya vā purastāt / gārhapatyāgārasya vā śākhāmupagūhati yajamānasya paśūnpāhīti tadbrahmaṇaivaitadyajamānasya paśūnparidadāti guptyai //
reference: He then hides the branch on the front (eastern) side either of the Âhavanîya or the Gârhapatya house, with the formula , 'Protect the sacrificer's cattle!' he thus makes over the sacrificer's cattle to it for protection by means of the Brahman (sacred writ).
baseline: The branch of the house of the lord which is in the east or in the north and which has been left behind by the lord of the land should be opened and the animals of the master should be taken away.
morphology: The branch of a house that is not built or that which has been built in the past or that has been left behind by the lord should be opened and the animals of the master should be taken away.

sanskrit: tasyām pavitraṃ karoti / vasoḥ pavitramasīti yajño vai vasustasmādāha vasoḥ pavitramasīti //
reference: On it he fastens a strainer (pavitram) , withthe formula , 'Vasu's means of purification (ventilator, strainer, pavitram) art thou!' Vasu, indeed, is the sacrifice: for this reason he says, 'Vasu's means of purification art thou!'
baseline: One who sanctifies that place one who worships the holy place and one who offers sacrifices to the Lord becomes a holy place.
morphology: One who purifies that is called vasū vāsū the sacred one and one who offers sacrifices is vāśu sāma mā vaśu and vaṣu.

sanskrit: atha yavāgvaitāṃ rātrimagnihotraṃ juhoti /
reference: That night he performs the Agnihotra with rice-gruel (yavâgû).
baseline: Then yavāgvaita should be worshipped in the night.
morphology: Then the fire should be lit in the night.

sanskrit: ādiṣṭaṃ vā etaddevatāyai havirbhavati yatpayaḥ sa yatpayasā juhuyādyathānyasyai devatāyai havirgṛhītaṃ tadanyasyai juhuyādevaṃ tattasmādyavāgvaitāṃ rātrimagnihotraṃ juhoti juhvatyagnihotramupakLptokhā bhavatyathāhopasṛṣṭām prabrūtādeti yadā prāhopasṛṣṭeti //
reference: That milk, namely, (which he milks that night) has already been announced as sacrificial food to a (special) deity; hence, if he were to make the offering with milk, he would offer to one deity that which has been set apart as sacrificial food for another deity: this is the reason why on that night he performs the Agnihotra with rice-gruel. As soon as they have performed the Agnihotra, the pot is made ready.
baseline: One who has made a sacrifice for the goddess of fire by the order of this deity should offer the same to the deity of the city of Juhu. One who does not want to lose the fire of the night would get the gift of fire fire iron and other elements. One would get that gift when he creates a fire.
morphology: One who has made a sacrifice for the goddess of fire by the order of this deity should be offered to her. One who makes a sacrifice to that deity by the same name should be given the gift of fire fire and other gifts. The one who makes an offering to the goddess by night fire water and other things would be given to you. When he has made the sacrifice of fire and fire he would get the gift.

sanskrit: athokhāmādatte dyaurasi pṛthivyasītyupastautyevaināmetanyahayatyeva yadāha dyaurasi pṛthivyasīti mātariśvano gharmo 'sīti yajñamevaitatkaroti yathā gharmam pravṛñjyādevam pravṛṇakti viśvadhā asi parameṇa dhāmnā dṛṃhasva mā hvāriti dṛṃhatyevaināmetadaśithilāṃ karoti mā te yajñapatirhvārṣīditi yajamāno vai yajñapatistadyajamānāyaivaitadahvalāmāśāste //
reference: He puts the pot on (the Gârhapatya hearth), with the text : 'Thou art the sky! thou art the earth!'--he praises and eulogises her by thus saying, 'thou art the sky! thou art the earth!'--'Mâtarisvan's cauldron (gharma) art thou !' he thereby makes it (a means of) sacrifice, and puts it on just as if he were putting on the[paragraph continues] (pravargya-) cauldron (gharma) .--'All-holding art thou! stand firm by the highest law! do not waver!'--thereby he steadies it, renders it firm.--'May thy Lord of Sacrifice not waver!'--the Lord of Sacrifice, doubtless, is the sacrificer, hence it is for the sacrificer that he thereby prays for steadiness.
baseline: If a devotee who has made a sacrifice to the earth sage priest priest or other person is doing it on the ground then the devotee should offer the sacrifice to his mother lord lord of the earth and the goddess of the universe. He should not make the sacrifice of the supreme god to the Lord of the world.
morphology: If a devotee who has made a sacrifice to the god of the earth and the mother of the goddess of the land and the wife of the mother and the bridegroom of the house of the wife and the daughter of the husband of the daughter the priest should not make the sacrifice of the lord of the world as if he had made a vow to the lord and the goddess.

sanskrit: atha pavitraṃ nidadhati /
reference: He then puts the strainer (on the pot).
baseline: The sacred thing is thus worshipped.
morphology: The sacred one is thus worshipped.

sanskrit: tadvai prāṅnidadhyātprācī hi devānāṃ digatho udagudīcī hi manuṣyāṇāṃ digayaṃ vai pavitraṃ yo 'yam pavate so 'yamimāṃllokāṃstiryaṅṅanupavate tasmādudaṅnidadhyāt //
reference: He puts it down with the top turned eastwards, for the east is the region of the gods; or with the top turned northwards, for the north is the region of the men; means of purification (pavitram) assuredly is that (wind) which here blows, it sweeps across these worlds: let him therefore put it down with the front northwards .
baseline: In the same way one who has made a holy offering to the gods the direction of the gods and the directions of the people should be raised up. One who has received the gift of the sacred food should make the whole world fall into a state of darkness.
morphology: In the same way one who has seen the directions of gods and the directions that lead to the sun and the direction of men and who has found the holy place in the world would get it.

sanskrit: tadyathaivādaḥ /
reference: Just as then (i.e.
baseline: Thus the argument is made.
morphology: The same is true for the same thing.

sanskrit: somaṃ rājānam pavitreṇa sampāvayantyevamevaitatsampāvayatyudīcīnadaśaṃ vai tatpavitram bhavati yena tatsomaṃ rājānaṃ sampāvayanti tasmādudaṅnidadhyāt //
reference: at the Soma-sacrifice) they clarify king Soma with a strainer, in like manner he now clarifies (the milk); and since the strainer wherewith on that occasion they clarify king Soma has its fringe directed towards the north, therefore let him now also put it down with the top northward.
baseline: The king is blessed with the same wealth as the king. The king should be given the same amount of wealth as that of the king and the king should get that amount.
morphology: One who acquires the wealth of a king with the same amount of wealth as the king with respect to his wealth would get that wealth.

sanskrit: tannidadhāti / vasoḥ pavitramasīti yajño vai vasustasmādāha vasoḥ pavitramasīti śatadhāraṃ sahasradhāramityupastautyevainadetanmahayatyeva yadāha śatadhāraṃ sahasradhāramiti //
reference: He puts it down, with the text , 'Vasu's means of purification (pavitram) art thou!'--Vasu, indeed, is the sacrifice: for this reason he says, 'Vasu's means of purification art thou! flowing in a hundred streams, flowing in a thousand streams!'--he praises and eulogises it when he says, 'flowing in a hundred streams, flowing in a thousand streams.'
baseline: One who worships the sacred stream one who worshipeth the sacred river one that worships Vasu Sāma Maa Vasa and others should worship the holy river. One who offers a hundred streams a thousand streams three hundred streams and a thousand rivers should worship it.
morphology: One should offer the sacred water to him. One should worship the holy water one should offer water and one should worship it. One would offer a hundred streams one hundred streams and one thousand streams. One who offers water would get a thousand streams and the other would get water.

sanskrit: atha vācaṃyamo bhavati ā tisṛṇāṃ dogdhorvāgvai yajño 'vikṣubdho yajñaṃ tanavā iti // tadānīyamānamabhimantrayate /
reference: He now maintains silence as long as the milking of the three (cows) lasts, for the sacrifice, doubtless, is speech: 'May I perform the sacrifice undisturbed!' so he thinks.
baseline: Then the sacrifice of the three men is said to have been made by the priest. The sacrifice of a man who is in a state of confusion is said as the sacrifice made by him.
morphology: Then the sacrifice should be performed with the same manner as before. It should be said that the sacrifice made with the two sides of the three sides should be offered with the vow of tāṇava.

sanskrit: devastvā savitā punātu vasoḥ pavitreṇa śatadhāreṇa supveti tadyathaivādaḥ somaṃ rājānam pavitreṇa sampāvayantyevamevaitatsampāvayati //
reference: When it (the milk of each of the three cows) is poured (by the milker from the wooden pail through the strainer into the pot), he (the Adhvaryu) consecrates it by (whispering each time) the formula , 'May the divine Savitri purify thee with Vasu's means of purification, well cleansing and flowing in a hundred streams!' for just as then (at the Soma-sacrifice) they clarify king Soma with a strainer, so he thereby clarifies (the milk).
baseline: One who gives a gift to a deva a savita a purified animal a sacred animal and a king would get the same amount of wealth from a holy person.
morphology: One who worships the gods the Savita the Punātu the Vāsū and the Sūma should be worshipped with a hundred threads. In the same way one who invents the Soma the king the sūm the sacred one should be blessed with all that he has.

sanskrit: athāha kāmadhukṣa iti amūmiti sā viśvāyurityatha dvitīyām pṛcati kāmadhukṣa ityamūmiti sā viśvakarmetyatha tṛtīyām pṛcati kāmadhukṣa ityamūmiti sā viśvadhāyā iti tadyatpṛcati vīryāṇyevāsvetaddadhāti tisro dogdhi trayo vā ime lokā ebhya evainadetallokebhyaḥ sambharatyatha kāmaṃ vadati //
reference: He then says , 'Which didst thou milk?' 'Such and such a one,' (the milker replies.) 'This one is Visvâyu (containing all life),' he (the Adhvaryu) says. He then asks regarding the second one, 'Which didst thou milk?' 'Such and such a one,' is the reply. 'This one is Visvakarman (all-doing),' he says. He then asks regarding the third, 'Which didst thou milk?' 'Such and such a one,' is the reply. 'This one is Visvadhâyas (all-sustaining),' he says.
baseline: Having said that one who has not been able to attain the goal of the world would ask for the second goal. One who has attained the goal would ask the third goal which would be the goal for the world. He would say that he would attain the target of the universe. He should say that the goal is three goals and three goals for the people who have achieved the goal. The goal would be to achieve this goal.
morphology: One who has made a vow of abhāhā kāmādhuksha after having attained the age of vyśva would ask for the second one who would have attained the height of kāma dhukshā who has attained the world would have asked for the third one which would be called kaamdhukshaka who should have attained vyṣvādha who will have three or more sons.

sanskrit: athottamāṃ dohayitvā /
reference: He is now at liberty to speak.
baseline: Having enlivened the body with a lotus.
morphology: Having blessed the eight.

sanskrit: yena dohayati pātreṇa tasminnudastokamānīya palyaṅya pratyānayati yadatra payaso 'hāyi tadihāpyasaditi rasasyo caiva sarvatvāyedaṃ hi yadā varṣatyathauṣadhayo jāyanta oṣadhīrjagdhvāpaḥ pītvā tata eṣa rasaḥ sambhavati tasmādu rasasyo caiva sarvatvāya tadudvāsyātanakti tīvrīkarotyevainadetattasmādudvāsyātanakti //
reference: After having the last (cow) milked, and having poured a drop of water into the pail which he has made the milker use, and stirred it, he pours it to (the milk) , thinking 'what milk was left there, let that also be here!'--(he does so) for the completeness of the sap; for when it rains here, then plants spring up, and on the plants being eaten and the water drunk, thence is this juice produced: and therefore (the water is poured to the milk) for the completeness of the sap. Having then taken it off (the fire), he coagulates it : he thereby makes it sharp (pungent); for this reason he coagulates it, after taking it off (the fire).
baseline: When one drinks the juice of all the elements of the body after having taken it one should drink it with the same quantity of water. One who drinks it after having had taken the same amount of water with the pot the water with which he drinks it the juice with the mixture of water water milk water etc.
morphology: When one drinks water containing all the elements of the universe one should drink water containing water and water with the same quantity of water. One who drinks the same amount of water after having taken it should drink the juice of the sun water milk water and other substances. One should drink this juice after having consumed all the substances containing the elements containing the element of water water etc..

sanskrit: indrasya tvā bhāgaṃ somenātanacmīti tadyathaivādo devatāyai havirgṛhṇannādiśatyevamevaitaddevatāyā ādiśati yadāhendrasya tvā bhāgamiti somenātanacmīti svadayatyevainadetaddevebhyaḥ //
reference: He coagulates it, with the formula , 'With Soma I coagulate thee, the portion of Indra!' Just as on a former occasion , when taking sacrificial food for a deity, he announces it (to that deity), in like manner he now announces it to the deity, saying, 'Thee, the portion of Indra!' By saying 'with Soma I coagulate thee,' he makes it palatable to the gods.
baseline: One who takes the part of Indra to the goddess Sōmanatana in the same way as the one who gives it to the gods should give the same direction to the deities. If one takes the portion of Indra one should give it to those who give it.
morphology: One who takes the part of Indra to the goddess Sōmanata would thus give the same direction to the gods. One who gives the same part to the deities would get the same. If one takes the portion of Indra one would get it from the gods of his own heart.

sanskrit: athodakavatottānena pātreṇāpidadhāti / nedenadupariṣṭānnāṣṭrā rakṣāṃsyavamṛśāniti vajro vā āpastadvajreṇaivaitannāṣṭrā rakṣāṃsyato 'pahanti tasmādudakavatottānena pātreṇāpidadhāti // so 'pidadhāti /
reference: He then covers it over by a vessel , with the hollow part upwards and containing water, 'lest the evil spirits, the Rakshas, should touch it from above;' for water, indeed, is a thunderbolt; hencehe thus drives away from it the evil spirits, the Rakshas, with a thunderbolt: this is the reason why he covers it over by a vessel with the hollow part upwards and containing water.
baseline: One who takes away the body of a man with a piece of cloth and leaves it with a pot or with a pair of clothes or a piece made of cloth or two pieces of cloth with a cloth would get rid of it.
morphology: One who takes away the body of a man with a piece of cloth and leaves it with a pot or with two pieces of cloth and with a pair of cloths or a diamond or with a bag of cloth or with the same piece of paper and takes away that part of the body with the cloth would get rid of it.

sanskrit: viṣṇo havyaṃ rakṣeti yajño vai viṣṇustadyajñāyaivaitaddhaviḥ paridadāti guptyai tasmādāha viṣṇo havyaṃ rakṣeti // ṛṇaṃ ha vai jāyate yo 'sti /
reference: He covers it over, with the formula , 'O Vishnu, protect the oblation!' for Vishnu, indeed, is the sacrifice; hence he thereby makes over this sacrificial food to the sacrifice for protection: for this reason he says, 'O Vishnu, protect the oblation!'
baseline: One who gives a sacrifice to a devotee of Viṣṇu would protect the desire of Viśṇu. One who acquires knowledge would get a secret from him. He would protect Viṣñu's desire. He will get debt.
morphology: One who protects the desire of Viṣṇu by offering a sacrifice one who gives a gift to a wise person and one who is in debt by giving it to a secret person would protect the interest of Viśṇu.

sanskrit: sa jāyamāna eva devebhya ṛṣibhyaḥ pitṛbhyo manuṣyebhyaḥ //
reference: Verily, whoever exists, he, in being born, is born as (owing) a debt to the gods, to the Rishis, to the fathers, and to men .
baseline: He should go to the gods sages fathers and men.
morphology: He should go to the gods sages fathers and men.

sanskrit: sa yadeva yajeta / tena devebhya ṛṇaṃ jāyate taddhyebhya etatkaroti yadenānyajate yadebhyo juhoti // atha yadevānubruvīta /
reference: For, inasmuch as he is bound to sacrifice, for that reason he is born as (owing) a debt to the gods: hence when he sacrifices to them, when he makesofferings to them, he does this (in discharge of his debt) to them.
baseline: The debt is owed to the god by him. He would get it from the king by the debtor. He gets it from him by the same account.
morphology: He would get a debt from the god by the time he returns it. He would obtain it from the same person by the day he returns the debt.

sanskrit: tena 'rṣibhya ṛṇaṃ jāyate taddhyebhya etatkarotyṛṣīṇāṃ nidhigopa iti hyanūcānamāhuḥ //
reference: And further, inasmuch as he is bound to study (the Veda), for that reason he is born as (owing) a debt to the Rishis: hence it is to them that he does this; for one who has studied (the Veda) they call 'the Rishis' treasure-warden.'
baseline: Then the debt is made from the sage. Then the treasure of the sages should be taken from him.
morphology: Then the debt is made from the sage. Then the treasure of the sages should be taken from him.

sanskrit: atha yadeva prajāmiceta / tena pitṛbhya ṛṇaṃ jāyate taddhyebhya etatkaroti yadeṣāṃ saṃtatāvyavacinnā prajā bhavati //
reference: And further, inasmuch as he is bound to wish for offspring, for that reason he is born as (owing) a debt to the fathers: hence when there is (provided by him) a continued, uninterrupted lineage, it is for them that he does this.
baseline: If a son is born to a nobleman he owes a debt to his father. He would then acquire the property of his offspring.
morphology: If a son of a nobleman has a debt from his father he would be the heir of that nobleman.

sanskrit: tena manuṣyebhya ṛṇaṃ jāyate taddhyebhya etatkaroti yadenānvāsayate yadebhyo 'śanaṃ dadāti sa ya etāni sarvāṇi karoti sa kṛtakarmā tasya sarvamāptaṃ sarvaṃ jitaṃ //
reference: And further, inasmuch as he is bound to practise hospitality, for that reason he is born as (owing) a debt to men: hence when he harbours them, when he offers food to them, it is (in discharge of his debt) to them that he does so. Whoever does all these things, has discharged his duties: by him all is obtained, all is conquered.
baseline: One who has made a debt to a man by doing so would get it from him. The one who gives it to those who are living with it would get all the gains by doing all these things.
morphology: He who gives these things to a man who has already made a debt to him would get all his gains by doing so.

sanskrit: sa yena devebhya ṛṇaṃ jāyate / tadenāṃstadavadayate yadyajate 'tha yadagnau juhoti tadenāṃstadavadayate tasmādyatkiṃ cāgnau juhvati tadavadānaṃ nāma //
reference: And, accordingly, in that he is born as (owing) a debt to the gods, in regard to that he satisfies (ava-day) them by sacrificing; and when he makes offerings in the fire, he thereby satisfies them in regard to that (debt): hence whatever they offer up in the fire, is called avadânam (sacrificial portion) .
baseline: He who owes a debt to the gods would get it. If he acquires it he would get the same amount as the fire. If the fire is given to him then he would be given that amount.
morphology: He who owes a debt to a god would get it. If he gives it to you if he earns it from you then he would get the same amount of money from you. That would be given to him.

sanskrit: tadvai caturavattam bhavati / idaṃ vā anuvākyātha yājyātha vaṣaṭkāro 'tha sā devatā caturthī yasyai devatāyai havirbhavatyevaṃ hi devatā avadānānyanvāyattā avadānāni vā devatā anvāyattānyatiriktaṃ ha tadavadānaṃ yatpañcamaṃ kasmā u hi tadavadyettasmāccaturavattam bhavati //
reference: Now this (oblation) consists of four cuttings; (the reason for this is, that) there is here first, the invitatory prayer (anuvâkyâ), then the offering-prayer (yâgyâ), then the vashat-call, and as the fourth, the deity for which the sacrificial food is[paragraph continues] (destined): for in this way the deities are dependent on the sacrificial portions, or the portions are dependent on the deities: hence what fifth cutting there is (made by some), that is redundant, for--for whom is he to cut it? For this reason it consists of four cuttings.
baseline: In the same way a priest should be called a chaturvata or a vāṣṭaka or a devata a person who is the fourth of the four gods. He should offer gifts to a deva a devatya an aviharaṭya a divinity an invincible one a deity a man who is not known to be a devātā and a person given gifts to others.
morphology: In the same way a chaturvattha is said to be the fourth deity. The one who is worshipped by the priest the one who gives gifts to the four gods the other who gives them to the other gods and the other one who seeks them and gives them away and that one who does not want to give them is called kāṣma and so on.

baseline: The sacrifice made by the priest is the same as that made by a priest. reference: They said to the Adhvaryu priest, 'Sprinkle the sacrificial dishes (with butter) in proper succession; and replenish them for the sake of one (additional) portion, and again render them fit for use; and then cut off one portion for each!'
baseline: As before one should make a gift and the other should be made again. That is the only gift that should be given.
morphology: As we have done in the past let us make one offering and make another offering. That is the only offering that should be offered.

sanskrit: yathāpūrvaṃ havīṃṣyabhyaghārayadekasmā avadānāya punarāpyāyayadayātayāmānyakarottata ekaikamavadānamavādyattasmādvāstavya ityāhurvāstu hi tadyajñasya yaddhuteṣu haviḥṣu tasmādyasyai kasyai ca devatāyai havirgṛhyate sarvatraiva sviṣṭakṛdanvābhaktaḥ sarvatra hyevainaṃ devā anvābhajan //
reference: The Adhvaryu accordingly sprinkled the sacrificial dishes in proper succession, and replenished them for the sake of one (additional) portion, and again rendered them fit for use, and cut off one portion for each. This then is the reason why he (Rudra) is called Vâstavya , for a remainder (vâstu) is that part of the sacrifice which (is left) after the oblations have been made: hence, if sacrificial food is offered to any deity, the Svishtakrit (Agni, 'the maker of good offering') is afterwards invariably offered a share of it; because the gods invariably gave him a share after themselves.
baseline: One who has made such a sacrifice should return to the gods of the east the king of the west the chief minister the governor of the north the minister of the south the ruler of the eastern states and the governor.
morphology: One should say that one should offer the same amount of money as before to a devotee of a particular god. One should make such offerings to a person who is a warrior one who has knowledge of the same and who is worshipped everywhere. One who worships a particular deity should offer it to another god.

sanskrit: tadvā agnaya iti kriyate / agnirvai sa devastasyaitāni nāmāni śarva iti yathā prācyā ācakṣate bhava iti yathā bāhīkāḥ paśūnām patī rudro 'gniriti tānyasyāśāntānyevetarāṇi nāmānyagnirityeva śāntatamaṃ tasmādagnaya iti kriyate sviṣṭakṛta iti //

The name Agni, doubtless, is the most auspicious[paragraph continues] (sânta), and the other names of his are inauspicious: hence it is offered to (him under the name of) 'Agni,' and to (him as) the Svishtakrit.
baseline: Then the fire should be made in the form of fire the gods should be called the names of the fire as in the case of the king the husband of the other animals should be worshipped by Rudra.
morphology: Then the fire should be made in the form of fire. The gods should be called the names of the gods the gods of the fire the goddess of the earth the king of the animals the husband of the other animals Rudra the lord of the wild animals and the god of the forest.

sanskrit: te hocuḥ / yattvayyamutra satyayakṣmahi tannaḥ sviṣṭaṃ kurviti tadebhyaḥ sviṣṭamakarottasmātsviṣṭakṛta iti //
reference: They (the gods) said, 'What we have offered unto thee who art in yonder place , do thou render that well-offered (svishta) for us!' He made it well-offered for them; and this is the reason why (it is offered) to (Agni as) the Svishtakrit.
baseline: They are the sons of the same god. They are said to be the son of a different god. He who cleanses the body from the same thing is said to have cleansed it from that.
morphology: They are the sons of the god Yātha. They are said to be pure. Then they are purified. They should be purified by the same.

sanskrit: so 'nuvākyāmanūcya sampaśyati / ye tathāgniṃ sviṣṭakṛtamayāḍagniragneḥ priyā dhāmānīti tadāgneyamājyabhāgamāhāyāṭsomasya priyā dhāmānīti tatsaumyamājyabhāgamāhāyāḍagneḥ priyā dhāmānīti tadya eṣa ubhayatrācyuta āgneyaḥ puroḍāśo bhavati tamāha //
reference: Having recited the invitatory formula , he (the Hotri) enumerates (those deities) which (have received oblations at the fore-offerings, butter-portions, &c.), as well as Agni Svishtakrit:--'May Agni offer Agni's favourite dainties!' thereby he refers to Agni's butter-portion . 'May he offer Soma's favourite dainties!' thereby he refers to Soma's butter-portion.--'May he offer Agni's favourite dainties!' thereby he refers to that indispensable cake for Agni which is (offered) on both occasions (at the new- and full-moon sacrifices).
baseline: The one who consumes the fire after having been washed with the fire of the fire and who has made it clear and has made the fire a favorite abode should be divided into the kingdom of fire kingdom kingdom of water kingdom and kingdom of the gods and the one who is divided into two kingdoms the king of fire and fire should be given the abode of fire.

Then the kingdom of fire should be divided into two parts. The kingdom of the mother mother daughter mother and daughter should be taken up as the abodes of fire.

sanskrit: ayāḍdevānāmājyapānām priyā dhāmānīti tatprayājānuyājānāha prayājānuyājā vai devā ājyapā yakṣadagnerhotuḥ priyā dhāmānīti tadagniṃ hotāramāha tadasmā etāṃ devā āhutiṃ kalpayitvāthainenaitadbhūyaḥ samaśāmyanpriya enaṃ dhāmannupāhvayanta tasmādevaṃ saṃpaśyati //
reference: 'May he offer the favourite dainties of butter-drinking gods!' thereby he refers to the fore-offerings (prayâga) and after-offerings (anuyâga), for, assuredly, the butter-drinking gods (represent) the fore-offerings and after-offerings.--'May he offer Agni the Hotri'sfavourite dainties!' thereby he refers to Agni as Hotri; for after the gods had set apart this oblation for him, they still further propitiated him by this (formula), and invited him to his favourite dainty : this is the reason why he thus enumerates.
baseline: The king should worship the goddess Ayādda the king drink beloved abode worshipped the goddess of the earth the lord of the fire the god of the gods the gods of the world the goddess who worships the fire and the god who worshiped the abode of fire. baseline: One who performs the ritual of worshipping the gods in the east should do the ritual ablution of the fire fire and fire. One who does not perform the ritual sacrifice of the deities in the past would do it in the first instance.

reference: [The Hotri continues to recite]: 'May he sacrifice to his own greatness!' baseline: Wherever a deity invokes him he also exalts himself. What is done by that person to make him proud of him. He pleases him there. Then he becomes happy and becomes proud. That person is called a great person.
morphology: Wherever a deity invokes him he also invents himself and makes himself glorious. What is done by that person to make him proud he pleases him. Then the person who has a smile on his face becomes glorious.

baseline: O Yājatā the Lord of all beings.
morphology: O Yājatā one who is the mother of all beings is called Esha.

'Gladden thou the longing gods, O youngest!' this much in the invitatory formula refers to the Visve Devâh . 'O Agni, Hotri of the cult! when this day (thou comest) to the men ;' this much in the offering-formula refers to the Visve Devâh. And because such is the form of these two (formulas), therefore they are ofthe form of the evening libation; and this is why the invitatory and offering-formulas on this occasion are made closely to correspond to each other.

morphology: The same sacrifice should be offered in the same manner as the one called upon by the Lord for the day morning and evening. He who gives this gift would get his land and his property.

morphology: One who is born with the letters ekāśaṇa śākshara and śūtupta Śrītva and the other three letters would be born as a son.

baseline: One who has made a sacrifice to a brahmin in the form of a bridegroom should not be afraid of the nakedness. morphology: In the same way we should worship the gods.
