reference: 'He who acts thus towards his own daughter, our sister, [commits a sin],' they thought.
baseline: If so done one should make his own blood.
morphology: If so done one should make his own milk and drink it.

sanskrit: te ha devā ūcuḥ / yo 'yaṃ devaḥ paśūnāmīṣṭe 'tisaṃdhaṃ vā ayaṃ carati ya itthaṃ svāṃ duhitaramasmākaṃ svasāraṃ karoti vidhyemamiti taṃ rudro 'bhyāyatya vivyādha tasya sāmi retaḥ pracaskanda tathennūnaṃ tadāsa //
reference: The gods then said to this god who rules over the beasts (Rudra) , 'This one, surely, commits a sin who acts thus towards his own daughter, our sister. Pierce him!' Rudra, taking aim, pierced him. Half of his seed fell to the ground.
baseline: One who grazes a cow or animal with his own hair and makes it his own is said to be the same as that of Rudra. Having married him he should be made to lie down with his wife.
morphology: He who grazes a cow or animal with his own hair and makes it his own is said to be the same as that of a cow. He should be married to a man who is not a god.

sanskrit: tasmādetadṛṣiṇābhyanūktam /
reference: And thus it came to pass.
baseline: It should be made available in such a manner.
morphology: It should be made available to such persons.

sanskrit: pitā yatsvāṃ duhitaramadhiṣkan kṣmayā retaḥ saṃjagmāno niṣiñcaditi tadāgnimārutamityukthaṃ tasmiṃstadvyākhyāyate yathā taddevā retaḥ prājanayaṃsteṣāṃ yadā devānāṃ krodho vyaidatha prajāpatimabhiṣajyaṃstasya taṃ śalpaṃ nirakṛntantsa vai yajña eva prajāpatiḥ //
reference: Accordingly it has been said by the Rishi with reference to that (incident), 'When the father embraced his daughter, uniting with her, he dropped his seed on the earth.' This (became) the chant (uktha) called âgnimâruta ; in (connection with)this it is set forth how the gods caused that seed to spring . When the anger of the gods subsided, they cured Pragâpati and cut out that dart of this. (Rudra); for Pragâpati, doubtless, is this sacrifice.
baseline: The same is said to be the case when the sons of the gods are angry with their fathers who have made the sacrifice of their children by the sun by the sand by which they are not allowed to join together. When the sons are born by the fire by that sun when the wrath of their gods is dissipated the sacrifice made by the king is the same as that made by a priest.
morphology: The same is said to be the case when the son of a priest who has given a gift to a priest who has not been blessed by his father and who has been denied access by the king is given the gift of fire fire and fire. When the son is born by the lord of the king of the gods the gift is given to the king.

sanskrit: te hocuḥ / upajānīta yathedaṃ nāmuyāsatkanīyo hāhuteryathedaṃ syāditi //
reference: They said (to one another), 'Think of some means by which that (part of the sacrifice torn out with the dart) may not be lost, and how it may be but a small portion of the offering itself!'
baseline: They should be called the hochu the subjunctive. They should not be called as āmuṣatkāṇī.
morphology: They should be called hochu upāṇī namu atkāna hahutereyā.

sanskrit: te hocuḥ / bhagāyainaddakṣiṇata āsīnāya pariharata tadbhagaḥ prāśiṣyati tadyathāhutamevam bhaviṣyatīti tadbhagāya dakṣiṇata āsīnāya paryājahrustadbhago 'vekṣāṃ cakre tasyākṣiṇī nirdadāha tathennūnaṃ tadāsa tasmādāhurandho bhaga iti //
reference: They said, 'Take it round to Bhaga (Savitri, the Patron), who sits on the south side (of the sacrificial ground): Bhaga will eat it by way of fore-portion , so that it may be as though it were offered. They accordingly took it round to Bhaga, who sat on the south side. Bhaga (Savitri) looked at it: it burnt out his eyes .
baseline: He would avoid sitting on the right side of the body of the enemy. The enemy would then enter that house as if he were sitting on that side of that army. He would have to sit on the left side of it. He should have the right hand of that enemy.
morphology: He would avoid sitting on the right side of the body of the enemy. The enemy would then ask the enemy to sit on the left side of that enemy. He would have enough of that to be sitting on that enemy and the enemy would have no fear in the circle. He should have the enemy sitting on his enemy.

sanskrit: no nvevātrāśamatpūṣṇa enatpariharateti tatpūṣṇe paryājahrustatpūṣā prāśa tasya dato nirjaghāna tathennūnaṃ tadāsa tasmādāhuradantakaḥ pūṣeti tasmādyam pūṣṇe caruṃ kurvanti prapiṣṭānāmeva kurvanti yathādantakāyaivam //
reference: They said, 'It has not yet become appeased here: take it round to Pûshan!' They accordinglytook it round to Pûshan. Pûshan tasted it: it knocked out his teeth. And thus it came to pass. Hence they say, 'Pûshan is toothless;' and therefore, when they prepare a mess of boiled rice (karu) for Pûshan, they prepare it from ground rice, as is done for one toothless.
baseline: One who has not given any gift to the king should offer the same amount of food to the priest. One who does not want to give the gift of food and drink to the poor should give it to him. The king should make the gift to him by offering the same quantity of food. The same should be done by the priest who has made the gift.
morphology: One who has not given the gift of a cow one who has given it to a man should not eat the food and drink the food of the cow and eat it. One who does not eat it should eat it and then eat it with the help of the priest. The same should be done by those who eat it as well.

sanskrit: no nvevātrāśamadbṛhaspataya enatpariharateti tadbṛhaspataye paryājahruḥ sa bṛhaspatiḥ savitārameva prasavāyopādhāvatsavitā vai devānām prasavitedam me prasuveti tadasmai savitā prasavitā prāsuvattadenaṃ savitṛprasūtaṃ nāhinattato 'rvācīnaṃ śāntaṃ tadetannidānena yatprāśitram //
reference: They said, 'It has not yet become appeased here: take it round to Brihaspati !' They accordingly took it round to Brihaspati. Brihaspati hasted to Savitri for his impulsion (influence, prasava ), for assuredly Savitri is the impeller (prasavitri) of the gods. 'Impel (influence) this for me!' he said. Savitri, as the impeller, accordingly impelled it for him, and being thus impelled by Savitri, it did not injure him: and thus it was henceforth appeased.
baseline: One who gives birth to a goddess who is born as a son of Brihaspati and who has given birth as a daughter who has already given birth to another child who would give birth to the same god. One who delivers a daughter as a mother and gives birth as an infant who does not want to give birth as well as to others would be blessed with peace.
morphology: One who gives birth to a goddess who is born of the same name as Brihaspati and who has given birth to another who has not been born to him. One who does not want to give birth to any child who gives it to the same god who delivers it to him who brings it to me who takes it away and gives it away.

sanskrit: sa yatprāśitramavadyati /
reference: This, then, is essentially the same as the fore-portion.
baseline: One should be blessed with seven prāṣīs.
morphology: One should be blessed with seven prāśītras.

sanskrit: yadevātrāviddhaṃ yajñasya yadrudriyaṃ tadevaitannirmimīte 'thāpa upaspṛśati śāntirāpastadadbhiḥ śamayatyatheḍām paśūntsamavadyati //
reference: Now when he cuts off the fore-portion, he cuts out what is injured in the sacrifice,--what belongs to Rudra. Thereupon he touches water: water is (a means) of lustration, hence he lustrates by means of water .
baseline: One who makes a sacrifice to a god without having to go to the same place would get peace. One who gives the animals to the other would get relief by offering them in the same way.
morphology: If the sacrifice is made without the presence of the gods the sacrifice should be made in the same manner. Then the animal should be put to rest in peace. The animals should be brought to rest by the devotees.

sanskrit: sa vai yāvanmātramivaivāvadyet /
reference: He now cuts off piece by piece the idâ , (which represents) cattle.
baseline: He should be equal to all.
morphology: He should be equal to all others.

sanskrit: tathā śalpaḥ pracyavate tasmādyāvanmātramivaivāvadyedanyatarata ājyaṃ kuryādadhastādvopariṣṭādvā tathā khadanniḥsaraṇavadbhavati tathā nisravati tasmādanyatarata ājyaṃ kuryādadhastādvopariṣṭādvā //
reference: Let him cut off (for the fore-portion) ever so small a piece : thus the dart comes out; let him therefore cut off ever so small a piece. He should (according to some) put clarified butter on one side only, either below or above: thus that which is hard becomes soft and flows forth; and for this reason he should put butter on one side only, either below or above.
baseline: Then the slap should be placed in the same way as that of the other two parts. Having placed the slab on top of the two parts of the body the sloop should be removed and the slit should be left on the other side.
morphology: Then the slap should be placed in the same way as that of the other two parts. The slab should be raised above the two parts of the body and the slit should be removed from the other parts of it.

sanskrit: dvirhaviṣo 'vadāyāthopariṣṭādājyasyābhighārayati tadyathaiva yajñasyāvadānamevametat //
reference: Having (nevertheless ) made an underlayer of butter and a double cutting from the oblation (havis), he pours butter on the upper side of it; for it is only in this way that this becomes part of the sacrifice.
baseline: It is said to be the offering of sacrifices.
morphology: It is said to be the offering of sacrifices.

sanskrit: tanna pūrveṇa pariharet /
reference: Let him not carry it (to the Brahman) along the front (east) side of the Âhavanîya fire); (though) some, it is true, do carry it along the front side.
baseline: It should be placed in the east.
morphology: It should be placed in the east.

sanskrit: pūrveṇa haike pariharanti purastādvai pratyañco yajamānam paśava upatiṣṭhante rudriyeṇa ha paśūnprasajedyatpūrveṇa pariharette 'sya gṛhāḥ paśava upamūryamāṇā īyustasmādityeva tiryakprajihīta tathā ha rudriyeṇa paśūnna prasajati tiryagevainaṃ nirmimīte //
reference: For on the front side stand the cattle facing the sacrificer: hence he would impose the power of Rudra on the cattle, if he were to carry it along the front side, and his (the sacrificer's) household and cattle would be overwhelmed. Let him therefore cross over in this way (behind the paridhis); for thus he does not impose Rudra's power on the cattle and he removes that (dart) sideways .
baseline: The lord of the animals standing on the east side of the hill is said to be the master of the animal standing on each of the two sides. He should worship the animals in the east. The animals should be worshipped by Rudrāyāya the lord of his house the chief priest the king of the forest the ruler of the land the governor of the kingdom of the king the minister of the country and the governor should worship him.
morphology: The lord of the animals standing on the east side of the hill is said to be the master of the animal standing on each side. The king of the cattle standing on both sides of the mountain is saidto have raised the animals from the east and the king of his house is supposed to have raised them from the west. He is known as the lord of animals living in the east the king who has raised the cattle from the north the lord who has built the temple from the south and the god of the earth is known to have created the mountain.

sanskrit: devasya tvā savituḥ prasave 'śvinorbāhubhyām pūṣṇo hastābhyām pratigṛhṇāmīti //
reference: He (the Brahman) receives it, with the text , 'At the impulse (prasava) of the divine Savitri I receive thee with the arms of the Asvins, with the hands of Pûshan!'
baseline: One should worship the gods in the form of the hands hands and hands in childbirth.
morphology: One should worship the gods in the form of flowers and hands in the birth.

sanskrit: tadyathaivādo bṛhaspatiḥ savitāram / prasavāyopādhāvatsavitā vai devānām prasavitedam me prasuveti tadasmai savitā prasavitā prāsuvattadenaṃ savitṛprasūtaṃ nāhinadevamevaiṣa etatsavitārameva prasavāyopadhāvati savitā vai devānām prasavitedam me prasuveti tadasmai savitā prasavitā prasauti tadenaṃ savitṛprasūtaṃ na hinasti //
reference: And in like manner as Brihaspati then hasted to Savitri for his impulsion,--for, assuredly, Savitri is the impeller of the gods,--and said, 'Impel this for me!' and Savitri, the impeller, impelled it for him; and, impelled by Savitri, it did not injure him; so now also this one (the Brahman) hastes to Savitri for his impulsion,--for, assuredly, Savitri is the impeller of the gods,--and says 'impel this for me!' and Savitri, the impeller, impels it for him; and, impelled by Savitri, it does not injure him.
baseline: In the same way Śivitā Brihaspati Savitara śvitrā Avatā Dāvā Devā Pārāda Dīvā are given to the goddess of childbirth. To that person Savita is given birth. To the one who gives birth to a daughter to the one having not given birth to the god to that person also on this auspicious day Saviti the mother of the childbearing mother the daughter of the god is given to him.
morphology: In the same way Brihaspati should give birth to the goddess Savita the goddess of birth who gives birth to a child who is born to a god and who is not born to the gods. Having given birth to her who has not given birth even to a goddess who gave birth to an infant who would not give birth.

sanskrit: agneṣṭvāsyena prāśnāmīti na vā agniṃ kiṃ cana hinasti tatho hainametanna hinasti //
reference: He eats the fore-portion, with the text , 'With Agni's mouth I eat thee!' for Agni, assuredly, it does not injure in any way; and so neither does it injure him (the Brahman).
baseline: One would not question whether the fire should be burnt or whether it should be burned.
morphology: One would not question whether fire should be made into a fire or whether it should be called a fire.

sanskrit: tanna dadbhiḥ khādet / nenma idaṃ rudriyaṃ dato hinasaditi tasmānna dadbhiḥ khādet //
reference: He must not chew it with his teeth: 'lest this power of Rudra should injure my teeth!' so (he thinks), and therefore he must not chew it with his teeth.
baseline: One should eat with his own hands. One would eat with the same hands with the help of his wife.
morphology: One should eat with his own hands. One would eat with the same hands if he had given the rudriya.

sanskrit: athāpa ācāmati / śāntirāpastadadbhiḥ śāntyā śamayate 'tha parikṣālya pātraṃ //
reference: He then rinses his mouth with water;--water is (a means of) purification: hence he purifies himself with water, (that is, a means of) purification. After he has rinsed the vessel ,--
baseline: The vessel should be made to rest in peace with the words āthāpa achaṭamī pāshantirāpāda.
morphology: The vessel should be placed in a place of calmness with the syllable āthāpa achaṭamī. It should be offered in peace.

sanskrit: athāsmai brahmabhāgam paryāharanti /
reference: They bring him the Brahman's portion .
baseline: The Brahmana part is worshipped in the same way.
morphology: The Brahmana part is worshipped in the same way.

sanskrit: brahmā vai yajñasya dakṣiṇata āste 'bhigoptā sa etam bhāgam pratividāna āste yatprāśitraṃ tadasmai paryāhārṣustatprāśīdatha yamasmai brahmabhāgam paryāharanti tena bhāgī sa yadata ūrdhvamasaṃsthitaṃ yajñasya tadabhigopāyati tasmādvā asmai brahmabhāgam paryāharanti //
reference: The Brahman, in truth, sits south of the sacrifice, as its guardian. He sits facing that portion. As regards the fore-portion, that they have already brought to him and he has eaten it. In the Brahman's portion which they now bring to him, he obtains his own share; and henceforth he watches what remains incomplete of the sacrifice: for this reason they bring him the Brahman's portion.
baseline: He who is rightfully worshipped by Brahma and who is left behind in the offering of the sacrifice and who has been given this portion of the offering for the purpose of offering the sacrifice for the sake of others should offer it to Yama who has already offered the portion of Brahman to him. He should then offer the portion for the sacrifice which is placed above and after that would be offered to us.
morphology: He who is rightfully worshipped by Brahma and who has been given this portion of the sacrifice would be blessed with this portion. He would then offer to Yama the portion of Brahman in the offerings made to him. He should then offer that portion to Yāma. If he shares that portion of sacrifice which is situated above the ground he would then take away the portion from us.

sanskrit: sa vai vācaṃyama eva syāt / brahmanprasthāsyāmītyaitasmādvacaso vivṛhanti vā ete yajṇaṃ kṣaṇvanti ye madhye yajñasya pākayajñiyayeḍayā caranti brahmā vā ṛtvijām bhiṣaktamastadbrahmā saṃdadhāti na ha saṃdadhyādyadvāvadyamāna āsīta tasmādvācaṃyama eva syāt //
reference: He (the Brahman) must maintain silence (from the time he takes his seat on being elected) up to that speech (of the Adhvaryu), 'Brahman, shall I step forward?' Those (priests) who, in the midst of the sacrifice, perform the idâ, which represents the domestic offerings (pâkayagña) , tear the sacrifice to pieces, injure it. Now the Brahman, assuredly, is the best physician: hence the Brahman thereby restores the sacrifice; but, if he were to sit there talking, he would not restore it: he must therefore maintain silence.
baseline: One who worships Brahman or the two deities in the middle of the sacrifice and the sacrifice of the priest should be worshipped in the same manner. One who does not worship the god Brahma or the goddess of renunciation should be offered to Brahma and the other one should not be offered.
morphology: One who worships Brahman or the two deities in the middle of the sacrifice and the sacrifice should be worshipped in the same manner. One who worshipped Brahma or the devotee of Rītvījā or the god Brahma should not worship him.

sanskrit: sa yadi purā mānuṣīṃ vācaṃ vyāharet / tatro vaiṣṇavīmṛcaṃvā yajurvā japedyajño vai viṣṇustadyajñam punarārabhate tasyo haiṣā prāyaścittiḥ //
reference: If he should utter any human sound before that time, let him there and then mutter some Rik or Yagus-text addressed to Vishnu; for Vishnu isthe sacrifice, so that he thereby again obtains a hold on the sacrifice: and this is the expiation of that (breach of silence).
baseline: If he consumes the whole of man he should be worshipped there as the vaśṇava animal as yajurva as well as the yajurvedic animal. He would be known as Viṣṇu.
morphology: If he consumes the whole man he will be blessed with the vaśṇava animal the yajurva yajurveda jyāpādhyāgyāna the knowledge of Viṣṇu and his disciples will be restored.

sanskrit: sa yatrāha brahmanprasthāsyāmīti tadbrahmā japatyetaṃ te devā savitaryajñam prāhuriti tatsavitāram prasavāyopadhāvati sa hi devānām prasavitā bṛhaspataye brahmaṇa iti bṛhaspatirvai devānām brahmā tadya eva devānām brahmā tasmā evaitatprāha tasmādāha bṛhaspataye brahmaṇa iti tena yajñamava tena yajñapatiṃ tena māmaveti nātra tirohitamivāsti //
reference: When he (the Adhvaryu) says, 'Brahman, shall I step forward?' the Brahman mutters thus , 'This thy sacrifice, O divine Savitri, they have announced . . .,'--thereby he has recourse to Savitri for his impulsion (prasava), for he is the impeller (prasavitri) of the gods;--'to Brihaspati, the Brahman,'--for Brihaspati, assuredly, is the Brahman of the gods: hence he announces that (sacrifice) to him who is the Brahman of the gods; and accordingly he says, 'to Brihaspati, the Brahman.'--'Therefore prosper the sacrifice, prosper the lord of sacrifice, prosper me!' In this there is nothing that requires explanation.
baseline: He who worships Brahman Praśātra that is the place where Brahman is worshipped. He who gives birth to a goddess who is known to be a devotee of the gods who gives him birth and gives birth and who is born to the gods of the universe. He gives Brahman to the god Brihaspati the same as Brahma the god of the cosmos. He offers Brahma to the goddess Brihapratya the sacrificial lord of the celestial body the priest of the goddess Brahman and the priest to the king of the earth.
morphology: He who worships Brahman Praśātha that place where Brahman is worshipped that god should be worshipped. He who gives birth to a goddess that goddess should be known as Sāvitrāya that person who is born to the goddess Brihaspati that who is called Brahma that is called Brihaprāṣa and that is named as Brahma. That person who offers a sacrifice to the god Brahma should be called Brahman.

sanskrit: mano jūtirjuṣatāmājyasyeti /
reference: [He continues, Vâg. S.
baseline: The king should be of the mind shoes and the body of the king.
morphology: The king should be of the mind shoes and the king of the world.

sanskrit: manasā vā idaṃ sarvamāptaṃ tanmanasaivaitatsarvāmāpnoti bṛhaspatiryajñamimaṃ tanotvariṣṭaṃ yajñaṃ samimaṃ dadhātviti yadvivṛḍhaṃ tatsaṃdadhāti viśve devāsa iha mādayantāmiti sarvaṃ vai viśve devāḥ sarveṇaivaitatsaṃdadhāti sa yadi kāmayeta brūyātpratiṣṭheti yadyu kāmayetāpi nādriyeta // manave ha vai prātaḥ /
reference: II, ]: 'May his mind delight in the gushing (of the) butter !' By the mind, assuredly, all this (universe) is obtained (or pervaded, âptam): hence he thereby obtains this All by the mind.--'May Brihaspati spread (carry through) this sacrifice! May he restore the sacrifice uninjured!'--he thereby restores what was torn asunder.--'May all the gods rejoice here!'--'all the gods,' doubtless, means the All: hence he thereby restores (the sacrifice) by means of the All. He may add, 'Step forward!' if he choose; or, if he choose, he may omit it.
baseline: The mind should be filled with all these things and the mind should also be made to sit in the morning. If the mind is not satisfied with the sacrifice made by him it should be given to the gods of the world. If it is satisfied with all the things done by the gods in the world then it should remain in the night.
morphology: The mind should be filled with all these things and the mind should also be made to sit in the morning. The heart should be made ready for the worship of Brihaspati the body should be prepared for the sacrifice of the Lord the world should be ready for it. The Lord should be satisfied with all the things that are offered to him. If he wants to do so he should leave him alone. If the mind is ready for anything that is not going to be done by the gods of the world then he should be happy.

sanskrit: avanegyamudakamājahruryathedam pāṇibhyāmavanejanāyāharantyevaṃ tasyāvanenijānasya matsyaḥ pāṇī āpede //
reference: In the morning they brought to Manu water for washing, just as now also they (are wont to) bring (water) for washing the hands. When he was washing himself, a fish came into his hands.
baseline: The fish of the king should be given to him as a gift. The king should offer water to the king.
morphology: The fish of the king should be offered to him as a gift for the worship of the goddess Avanegyamudka and the king of the world.

sanskrit: sa hāsmai vācamuvāda / bibhṛhi mā pārayiṣyāmi tveti kasmānmā pārayiṣyasītyaugha imāḥ sarvāḥ prajā nirvoḍhā tatastvā pārayitāsmīti kathaṃ te bhṛtiriti //
reference: It spake to him the word, 'Rear me, I will save thee!' 'Wherefrom wilt thou save me?' 'A flood will carry away all these creatures : from that I will save thee!' 'How am I to rear thee?' It said, 'As long as we are small, there is great destruction for us: fish devours fish.
baseline: He should say that he will not cross the river. He should not cross it. I will cross it and all these people will be defeated. How can they be conquered by him.
morphology: He should say that he would not cross the border with the enemy. He would say that all these people would be defeated by him. How could they be conquered by him?

sanskrit: yāvadvai kṣullakā bhavāmo bahvī vai nastāvannāṣṭrā bhavatyuta matsya eva matsyaṃ gilati kumbhyām māgre bibharāsi sa yadā tāmativardhā atha karṣūṃ khātvā tasyām mā bibharāsi sa yadā tāmativardhā atha mā samudramabhyavaharāsi tarhi vā atināṣṭro bhavitāsmīti //
reference: Thou wilt first keep me in a jar. When I outgrow that, thou wilt dig a pit and keep me in it. When I outgrow that, thou wilt take me down to the sea, for then I shall be beyond destruction.' It soon became a ghasha (a large fish); for that grows largest (of all fish) .
baseline: When a fish is swallowed up by the sea after having been washed with the same quantity of water as the other fish it will become a lotus. When it is washed with water and eaten with the help of the potter it should not be thrown into the sea. If it has not been washed away with the aid of the sea it would become so.
morphology: When a fish is swallowed by you by the sea it will become a lotus. When it is washed by a potter it is not allowed to eat it. If it does not get washed away by the river it would become a bittersweet. If the fish is not washed away from the sea.

sanskrit: sa hi jyeṣṭhaṃ vardhate 'thetithīṃ samāṃ tadaugha āgantā tanmā nāvamupakalpyopāsāsai sa augha utthite nāvamāpadyāsai tatastvā pārayitāsmīti //
reference: Thereupon it said, 'In such and such a year that flood will come. Thoushalt then attend to me (i.e. to my advice) by preparing a ship ; and when the flood has risen thou shalt enter into the ship, and I will save thee from it.'
baseline: He should rise and rise above the height of the ship. He should come to the same place and then go to the other side of the boat.
morphology: He should rise and rise above the height of the ship. He should come to the sea with the same amount of water as the old man. He would rise up and go across the river with the size of the boat.

sanskrit: tamevam bhṛtvā samudramabhyavajahāra /
reference: After he had reared it in this way, he took it down to the sea.
baseline: Having worshipped him he should be worshipped from the sea.
morphology: Having worshipped him he should be offered to the sea.

sanskrit: sa yatithīṃ tatsamām paridideṣa tatithīṃ samāṃ nāvamupakalpyopāsāṃ cakre sa augha utthite nāvamāpede taṃ sa matsya upanyāpupluve tasya śṛṅge nāvaḥ pāśam pratimumoca tenaitamuttaraṃ girimatidudrāva //
reference: And in the same year which the fish had indicated to him, he attended to (the advice of the fish) by preparing a ship; and when the flood had risen, he entered into the ship. The fish then swam up to him, and to its horn he tied the rope of the ship, and by that means he passed swiftly up to yonder northern mountain.
baseline: He should then circumvent the waters of the sea and then go to the sea. He should rise up in the circle of the river. Then he should be caught by the sea of fish water and water. Then the sea should be raised to the top of the lake.
morphology: He should then set forth the same thing in the circle of the ship and then raise the boat in the same way. He should raise the ship in a circle. Then the fish should be thrown into the sea and the boat should be set on the top of the mountain. Then he should bow down to the mountain and make a bow.

sanskrit: apīparaṃ vai tvā vṛkṣe nāvam pratibaghnīṣva taṃ tu tvā mā girau santamudakamantaścaitsīdyāvadudakaṃ samavāyāttāvattāvadanvavasarpāsīti sa ha tāvattāvadevānvavasasarpa tadapyetaduttarasya girermanoravasarpaṇamityaugho ha tāḥ sarvāḥ prajā niruvāhātheha manurevaikaḥ pariśiśiṣe //
reference: Fasten the ship to a tree; but let not the water cut thee off , whilst thou art on the mountain. As the watersubsides, thou mayest gradually descend!' Accordingly he gradually descended, and hence that (slope) of the northern mountain is called 'Alarm's descent .' The flood then swept away all these creatures, and Manu alone remained here.
baseline: O king of the king one of the men should not enter into a boat on the same tree as that of a king. He should not go into the sea with the sandal mud mantras water and drink together. The king should not leave the river with the snake. He would go to the sea of the gods. The lord should return the water to the king. All those people should go into a safe place. One man should be placed in a bag.
morphology: O king of the world you should not set a boat on a tree and you should make it fall into the sea. You should not make it reach the sea and make it pass through the river. He should not leave the sea the river the sea of the gods the serpent and the river of the sea together. The king should leave all the people in the sea in the morning. One man should be taken into the ark.

sanskrit: sorcaṃcrāmyaṃścacāra prajākāmaḥ /
reference: Being desirous of offspring, he engaged in worshipping and austerities.
baseline: We are the subjects.
morphology: We are the subjects.

sanskrit: tatrāpi pākayajñeneje sa ghṛtaṃ dadhi mastvāmikṣāmityapsu juhavāṃ cakāra tataḥ saṃvatsare yoṣitsambabhūva sā ha pibdamānevodeyāya tasyai ha sma ghṛtam pade saṃtiṣṭhate tayā mitrāvaruṇau saṃjagmāte //
reference: During this time he also performed a pâka-sacrifice: he offered up in the waters clarified butter, sour milk, whey, and curds. Thence a woman was produced in a year: becoming quite solid she rose; clarified butter gathered in her footprint. Mitra and Varuna met her. They said to her, 'Who art thou?' 'Manu's daughter,' she replied.
baseline: In the same year after having worshipped the priest he should worship the priest in the morning and then the wife should worship him in the evening. He should worship a woman who has been worshipped by the priest. He would worship her in the same manner. He will worship her and make her sit in the seat.
morphology: Then after having worshipped him in the month of May after having made a vow he should worship the goddess of peace and prosperity. Then in the year ending he would worship the wife of a man who had offered a drink and would worship her in the same manner. He would be worshipped in the posture of a friend wife and mother.

sanskrit: tāṃ hocatuḥ kāsīti /
reference: 'Say (thou art) ours,' they said.
baseline: One who does that would get a lotus.
morphology: It is said to be the same as that of a cow.

sanskrit: manorduhitetyāvayorbrūṣveti neti hovāca ya eva māmajījanata tasyaivāhamasmīti tasyāmapitvamīṣāte tadvā jajñau tadvā na jajñāvati tveveyāya sā manumājagāma //
reference: 'No,' she said, 'I am (the daughter) of him who begat me.' They desired to have a share in her. She either agreed or did not agree , but passed by them. She came to Manu. Manu said to her, 'Who art thou?' 'Thy daughter,' she replied.
baseline: One who is born of the mother and the wife of the son of a man who has suffered a heart attack and has become the mother of a woman would be destroyed by the enemy. One who does not suffer the loss of the mind would become the enemy of the king.
morphology: One who is born of the mother and the mother of the son of a man who is suffering from mental illness and who is not aware of the death of the husband should be made aware of it.

sanskrit: tava duhiteti katham bhagavati mama duhiteti yā amūrapsvāhutīrahauṣīrghṛtaṃ dadhi mastvāmikṣāṃ tato māmajījanathāḥ sāśīrasmi tām mā yajñe 'vakalpaya yajñe cedvai māvakalpayiṣyasi bahuḥ prajayā paśubhirbhaviṣyasi yāmamuyā kāṃ cāśiṣamāśāsiṣyase sā te sarvā samardhiṣyata iti tāmetanmadhye yajñasyāvākalpayanmadhyaṃ hyetadyajñasya yadantarā prayājānuyājān //
reference: 'How, illustrious one, (art thou) my daughter?' he asked. She replied,[paragraph continues] 'Those offerings (of) clarified butter, sour milk, whey, and curds, which thou madest in the waters, with them thou hast begotten me. I am the blessing (benediction): make use of me at the sacrifice! If thou wilt make use of me at the sacrifice, thou wilt become rich in offspring and cattle. Whatever blessing thou shalt invoke through me, all that shall be granted to thee!' He accordingly made use of her (as the benediction) in the middle of the sacrifice; for what is intermediate between the fore-offerings and the after-offerings, is the middle of the sacrifice.
baseline: The Lord will give you the gift of a cow a buffalo a cow and a cow. The king of the kingdom of Bihar would not offer the sacrifice of cows. He would offer many animals and other animals to the devotees. He should offer them the offering of cows cows and cows. If he has the knowledge of the matter then he would offer them all the offerings.
morphology: One who has made a sacrifice to you should not say that he would make a sacrifice of many animals and other animals. He should say that if he has made an offer to you he would be able to offer the sacrifice to me. If he has knowledge of the matter then he should say to the devotees that he will not offer the oblation of the mother son mother brother mother and mother. If the sacrifice is made by him he should offer all the animals and animals.

sanskrit: tayārcaṃcrāmyaṃścacāra prajākāmaḥ /
reference: With her he went on worshipping and performing austerities, wishing for offspring.
baseline: We are the subjects.
morphology: We shall discuss the things prepared for us.

sanskrit: tayemām prajātim prajajñe yeyam manoḥ prajātiryāmvenayā kāṃ cāśiṣamāśāsta sāsmai sarvā samārdhyata //
reference: Through her he generated this race, which is this race of Manu; and whatever blessing he invoked through her, all that was granted to him.
baseline: One should know the kind of people who belong to that particular tribe. One should worship the same class of people with the help of the same kind of tribe.
morphology: One should know the kind of people who belong to such a tribe. One should offer all the things to the king with the help of that tribe.

sanskrit: sa yo haivaṃ vidvāniḍayā caratyetāṃ haiva prajātim prajāyate yām manuḥ prājāyata yāmvenayā kāṃ cāśiṣamāśāste sāsmai sarvā samṛdhyate //
reference: Now this (daughter of Manu) is essentially the same as the Idâ; and whosoever, knowing this, performs with (the) Idâ , he propagates this race which Manu generated; and whatever blessing he invokes through it (or her), all that is granted to him.
baseline: One who grazes a cow with the help of a learned man would become a member of the cow breed. One who is born with the yama would become rich by the sacrifice of a cow.
morphology: One who grazes a cow with the help of a learned man would become a member of the tribe of cows. One who is born with the knowledge of manu would become rich by the sacrifice of a cow.

sanskrit: sā vai pañcāvattā bhavati / paśavo vā iḍā pāṅtā vai paśavastasmātpañcāvattā bhavati //
reference: It (the idâ) consists of a fivefold cutting; for the idâ, doubtless, means cattle, and cattle consist of five parts : for this reason it (the idâ) consists of a fivefold cutting.
baseline: That is the fifth element. The animal is the same as that of a pangata. The object of the animal is equal to that of the other five elements.
morphology: That is the fifth element. The animal is also called a pangta. The animals are also called the objects.

sanskrit: sa samavadāyeḍām / pūrvārdham puroḍāśasya praśīrya purastāddhruvāyai nidadhāti tāṃ hotre pradāya dakṣiṇātyeti // sa hoturiha nilimpati /
reference: When he (the Adhvaryu) has cut off the idâ piece by piece , and broken off the fore-part of thecake (for the sacrificer's portion), he puts it (the latter) down (on the barhis) before the dhruvâ-spoon. Having then handed over the former (the idâ) to the Hotri , he passes by him towards the south.
baseline: He should offer the equal amount of water. He should spread the forehead half of the time in front of the pole and give it to the horse. He would then set it on the right side.
morphology: He should place the head of the bull on the right side of the ground and the forehead on the left side of it. He should offer the head to the pole and the head should be placed on the south side.

sanskrit: taddhotauṣṭhayornilimpate manasaspatinā te hutasyāśnāmīṣe prāṇāyeti //
reference: He anoints the Hotri here (with clarified butter taken from the idâ); and with it the Hotri anoints his lips, with the text, 'Of thee, offered by the lord of the mind, I eat for sap, for out-breathing!'
baseline: One who is born with the spirit of the mind would get life by the sacrifice of the soul.
morphology: One who is born with the spirit of the mind would get life by the same means.

sanskrit: atha hoturiha nilimpati / taddhotauṣṭhayornilimpate vācaspatinā te hutasyāśnāmyūrja udānāyeti //
reference: He then anoints the Hotri here ; and with it the Hotri anoints his lips, with the text, 'Of thee, offered by the lord of speech, I eat for strength, for in-breathing!'
baseline: Then the sun should be set on the earth. Then it should be raised on the eight sides of the earth with the words hutāsāṇā and mūrjā.
morphology: Then one who is a hotturī should be made to stand on the ground. Then one should be given the sacred water of the sun with the uttā yorṇīmpa leaves.

sanskrit: etaddha vai manurbibhayāṃ cakāra / idaṃ vai me taniṣṭhaṃ yajñasya yadiyamiḍā pākayajñiyā yadvai ma iha rakṣāṃsi yajñaṃ na hiṃsyuriti tāmetatpurā rakṣobhyaḥ purā rakṣobhya ityeva prāpayata tatho evaināmeṣa etatpurā rakṣobhyaḥ purā rakṣobhya ityeva prāpayate 'tha yatpratyakṣaṃ na prāśnāti nedanupahūtām prāśnāmītyetadevaināṃ prāpayate yadoṣṭhayornilimpate //
reference: At that time, namely, Manu became apprehensive (thinking), 'This (part) of my sacrifice--that is, this idâ representing the domestic offering--is certainly the weakest: the Rakshas must notinjure my sacrifice at this place.' Accordingly by that (butter, taken from the idâ, and smeared on his lips) he promoted it (the idâ to a safe place, thinking), 'Before the Rakshas (come)! before the Rakshas (come)!' And in like manner this one also thereby promotes (the idâ to a safe place, thinking), 'Before the Rakshas (come)! before the Rakshas (come)!' And though he does not (at present) eat (the idâ) visibly, lest he should eat it before it is invoked, he nevertheless promotes it (to a safe place), when he smears the (butter) on his lips.
baseline: Having done so one would get the same amount of money for the sacrifice. If one does not perform the sacrifice of the sacred sacrifice he would get it. If he does not do the sacrifice and does not commit any violence he should get the protection from the protectors. If the protector does not question the face he will get the gift of the goddess. He would get that amount from those who protect him.
morphology: Having done so one would get the same thing by offering a sacrifice of the same kind as that of a man and the same would be done by offering the same amount of food. If one does not offer the sacrifice of these things he would get full protection from those who protect him. If he does not question the guardians he will get the protection of the gods. If you do not question him directly you will get that amount.

sanskrit: atha hotuḥ pāṇau samavadyati /
reference: He now cuts off piece by piece (the avântaredâ) in (or, into) the Hotri's hand.
baseline: Then the water is equal to the water.
morphology: Then the water should be equal to the water.

sanskrit: samavattameva satīṃ tadenāṃ pratyakṣaṃ hotari śrayati tayātmaṃcūtayā hotā yajamānāyāśiṣamāśāste tasmāddhotuḥ pāṇau samavadyati //
reference: That which is cut up piece by piece he thus makes visibly enter the Hotri; and through that which has entered (or is cooked in) his own self, the Hotri invokes a blessing on the sacrificer: for this reason he cuts it off piece by piece in the Hotri's hand .
baseline: The same sati should be offered to those who are in a position to be worshipped by the lord. One would hear the same thing directly from the master.
morphology: The same sati should be offered to those who have heard the same thing directly and the same should be given to the master in the same manner.

sanskrit: athopāṃśūpahvayate /
reference: He now calls (the idâ) in a low voice.
baseline: It is said to be a part of the body.
morphology: It is said to be a part of the body.

sanskrit: etaddha vai manurbibhayāṃ cakāredaṃ vai me taniṣṭhaṃ yajñasya yadiyamiḍā pākayajñiyā yadvai ma iha rakṣāṃsi yajñaṃ na hanyuriti tāmetatpurā rakṣobhyaḥ purā rakṣobhya ityevopāṃśūpāhvayata tatho evaināmeṣa etatpurā rakṣobhyaḥ purā rakṣobhya ityevopāṃśūpahvayate //
reference: At that time, namely, Manu became apprehensive (thinking), 'This (part) of my sacrifice--that is, this idârepresenting the domestic offerings--is certainly the weakest: the Rakshas must not injure my sacrifice at this place.' He accordingly called it to him in a low voice (thinking), 'Before the Rakshas (come)! before the Rakshas (come)!' And in like manner this one (the Hotri) thereby calls it (thinking), 'Before the Rakshas (come)! before the Rakshas (come)!'
baseline: In the same way if I have made a sacrifice of ten thousand rupees for the sake of the protection of the people the sacrifice should not be taken away. If I have not made the sacrifice of one hundred rupees for that protection the part of the whole protection for those who are protected should be taken out.
morphology: In the same way as in the case of the sacrifice of a man one should not make a sacrifice of the same kind as that of a sacrifice. If one does not make the sacrifice for the protection of the people one would not be able to do so. If he does not perform the sacrifice he should not give the same amount of money to the protectors.

sanskrit: upahūtaṃ rathantaraṃ saha pṛthivyopa māṃ rathantaraṃ saha pṛthivyā hvayatāmupahūtaṃ vāmadevyaṃ sahāntarikṣeṇopa māṃ vāmadevyaṃ sahāntarikṣeṇa hvayatāmupahūtam bṛhatsaha divopa mām bṛhatsaha divā hvayatāmiti tadetāmevaitadupahvayamāna imāṃśca lokānupahvayata etāni ca sāmāni //
reference: He calls thus (in a low voice) , 'Hither is called the Rathantara (chant), together with the earth: may the Rathantara, together with the earth, call me ! Hither is called the Vâmadevya (chant), together with the atmosphere: may the Vâmadevya, together with the atmosphere, call me! Hither is called the Brihat (chant), together with the sky: may the Brihat, together with the sky, call me!' In thus calling her (the Idâ) to him, he calls to him both these (three) worlds and those chants .
baseline: The chariot should be placed with the earth and the chariots should be laid with the left hand the goddess of the earth the mother of the left armour the wife of the right armoury the daughter of the mother the husband of the wife the bridegroom of the daughter the sister of the husband the widow of the son of the father the son or mother of a daughter and the son daughter of a son the father of the bride the brother of the groom the elder son of a mother who is the mother and the mother.
morphology: The chariot should be placed with the earth and the chariots should be made with the left hand the goddess of the earth the mother of the left armour the wife of the right armoury the daughter of the great armour and the daughter-in-law of the king.

sanskrit: upahūtā gāvaḥ saharṣabhā iti / paśavo vā iḍā tadenām paro 'kṣamupahvayate saharṣabhā iti samithunāmevaināmetadupahvayate //
reference: 'Hither are called the cows , together with thebull!'--the idâ, assuredly, means cattle: hence it is her he thereby calls in an indirect (mystic) way; (and in saying), 'together with the bull,' he calls her together with her mate.
baseline: A cow that has been offered as a gift is called saharsabha. A cow or animal should be offered to a cow or a cow to a man who has been given the title of saharasabha.
morphology: It is said that a cow should be worshipped as the saharsabha a cow as the cow a beast a man as the head of a cow and a man named as saharsabha.

sanskrit: upahūtā saptahotreti / tadenāṃ saptahotrā saumyenādhvareṇopahvayate //
reference: 'Hither is called (Idâ) by that (sacrifice) which is performed by the seven Hotris!'--he thereby calls her by the Soma-sacrifice performed by the seven Hotris .
baseline: The seven elements of the sun are worshipped with the subhutas. The seven ornaments of the tādeṇas are worshipping with the saṃmyaṇa sound.
morphology: The seven elements of the sun are worshipped with the subhutas. The seven ornaments of the tādeṇas are worshiped with the saumya sāmya and dhvara.

sanskrit: tadenām pratyakṣamupahvayate tatuririti sarvaṃ hyeṣā pāpmānaṃ tarati tasmādāha tatuririti //
reference: 'Hither is called Idâ, the conquering!'--he thereby calls her directly. 'Conquering' he says, because she overcomes evil, and for that reason he calls her 'the conquering.'
baseline: Then all the sins should be washed away.
morphology: Then the manifest manifestation of the same is revealed to us. Then all sins should be washed away.

sanskrit: upahūtaḥ sakhā bhakṣa iti / prāṇau vai sakhā bhakṣastatprāṇamupahvayata upahūtaṃ hegiti tacarīramupahvayate tatsarvāmupahvayate //
reference: 'Hither is called the friend, the food !'--the friend, the food, doubtless, means breath: hence he thereby calls hither the breath. 'Hither is called the Hek !'--he thereby calls hither the (body of idâ), he thereby calls hither the entire (idâ).
baseline: One should eat the food of the living entity one should eat food from the body one would eat from the air and one would drink the food from that body.
morphology: One who consumes food with the same amount of food as the living organism would become a member of the body. One who eats food with that amount of water would become the member of that body.

sanskrit: iḍopahūtopahūteḍopo asmāṃ iḍā hvayatāmiḍopahūteti tadupahūtāmevaināmetatsatīm pratyakṣamupahvayate yā vai sāsīdgorvai sāsīccatuṣpadī vai gaustasmāccaturupahvayate // sa vai caturupahvayamānaḥ /
reference: He now intones (in a loud voice): 'Idâ is called hither! Hither (thither) is called Idâ! May Idâ also call us to her!' In saying, 'Idâ is calledhither,' he, in a direct way, calls her, who is thereby called hither, as being what she really was: a cow, assuredly, she was, and a cow is four-footed; and therefore he calls her four times .
baseline: The same thing which is made to be made to appear in the form of a cow the same thing that is made of cow that is also made to look like a cow and that which has been made to sound like a horse is made into a cow.
morphology: One who is born of the son of a man who has been born with a cow who has become a cow or a cow and who has not been given a horse or a horse should be made to eat.

sanskrit: atha nānevopahvayate 'jāmitāyai jāmi ha kuryādyadiḍopahūteḍopahūtetyevopahvayetopahūteḍeti veḍopahūteti tadarvācīmupahvayata upahūteḍeti tatparācīmupo asmāṃ iḍā hvayatāmiti tadātmānaṃ caivaitannāntaretyanyatheva ca bhavatīḍopahūteti tatpunararvācīmupahvayate tadarvācīṃ caivaināmetatparācīṃ copahvayate //
reference: By saying, 'Idâ is called hither!' he calls her hitherwards; and by 'Hither (or thither, lit. called to somebody) is called Idâ!' he calls her thitherwards. By saying, 'May Idâ also call us to her,' he does not omit himself, and, besides, it (the formula) is changed. By (the second), 'Idâ is called hither!' he again calls her hitherwards; so that he thereby (and by the second, 'Hither is called Idâ,' again) calls her hitherwards and thitherwards.
baseline: Then the king should be made to sit on the ground. Then he should be given to the king. Then the governor should be placed on the floor of the temple. Then after having made the order of the king of the kingdom of Bihar the governor of the state of Bihar should be raised to the floor. The governor should not be allowed to enter the house of the chief minister.
morphology: Then the king should be made to sit on the ground with his own hands. Then he should be called to the seat of the king. Then the priest should be raised to the floor with his wife. He should be placed on the floor of the house with his mother his wife his father his brother his daughter his mother and his brother. He would be raised from the ground to the ground.

sanskrit: mānavī ghṛtapadīti / manurhyetāmagre 'janayata tasmādāha mānavīti ghṛtapadīti yadevāsyai gṛtam pade samatiṣṭhata tasmādāha ghṛtapadīti //
reference: 'Manu's daughter, the butter-pathed (ghritapadî);'--Manu, indeed, begat her of old: for this reason he says, 'Manu's daughter.' 'The butter-pathed' he says, because butter gathered in her footprint: therefore he calls her 'butter-pathed.'
baseline: A man should offer ghee to a woman who is sitting in a position where it has been placed.
morphology: A man should offer ghee to a woman who is sitting on the ground. He should offer it to her.

sanskrit: uta maitrāvaruṇīti / yadeva mitrāvaruṇābhyāṃ samagacata sa eva maitrāvaruṇo nyaṅgo brahmā devakṛtopahūteti brahmā hyeṣāṃ devakṛtopahūtopahūtā daivyā adhvaryava upahūtā manuṣyā iti taddaivāṃścaivādhvaryūnupahvayate ye ca mānuṣā vatsā vai daivyā adhvaryavo 'tha ya itare te mānuṣāḥ //
reference: And further, 'She who belongs to Mitra and Varuna;'--this 'Maitrâvaruna nature' (is hers), because she met Mitra and Varuna .--'She, the god-fashioned one, is called hither as the Brahman ;for she, the god-fashioned one, is indeed called hither as their Brahman.--'Hither are called the divine Adhvaryus, called hither the human!'--he thereby calls both the divine Adhvaryus and those that are human: the divine Adhvaryus indeed are the calves (vatsâh), and what others there are, are the human ones.
baseline: O Maitravaṇī one who has joined the two friends that is the same as the friend one is called Brahma the creator of the gods the protector of the universe the one who subjugates the gods and the other beings and the person who submits to the gods is called subhutā man man and woman. Those who submit to others are called vatsa god man.
morphology: O Maitravaṇī one who is united with the friends of the enemies that is called Maitravāṇī. One who is uniting with the enemies of the allies that one is called Brahma the protector of the gods that has been subjugated to the gods and that who is subjutant to the demigods that man who is subject to the subjuntations of gods and those who are subject to them that person who is subjected to the devutations of the demi-souls and others is called as maitravara

sanskrit: ya imaṃ yajñamavānye ca yajñapatiṃ vardhāniti / ete vai yajñamavanti ye brāhmaṇāḥ śuśruvāṃso 'nūcānā ete hyenaṃ tanvata eta enaṃ janayanti tadu tebhyo nihnute vatsā u vai yajñapatiṃ vardhanti yasya hyete bhūyiṣṭhā bhavanti sa hi yajñapatirvardhate tasmādāha ye ca yajñapatiṃ vardhāniti //
reference: '--They who are to prosper this sacrifice, they who are to prosper the lord of sacrifice.' Those Brâhmanas, who have studied and teach the Veda, assuredly prosper the sacrifice, since they spread (perform) and produce it: these he thereby propitiates. And the calves also assuredly make the lord of sacrifice prosper; for the lord of sacrifice who possesses abundance of them, does indeed prosper; for this reason he says, 'They who are to prosper the lord of sacrifice.'
baseline: The brahmins who perform these sacrifices and the chief priest of the sacrificial house are called to increase the amount of the sacrifice. Those who do so are called brahmin servants servants and servants. The king of the oblation is called Vatsa and the king of sacrifices is named Vatsā. He who increases the quantity of the sacrifices is called as Vardhana.
morphology: If the chief of the sacrificial body is increased in the same way as the brahmins who are serving the devotees the servants of the priest the sons of the king the king of the bridegroom should be raised in such a way that the head of the sacrifice should be increased.

sanskrit: upahūte dyāvāpṛthivī pūrvaje ṛtāvarī devī devaputre iti tadime dyāvāpṛthivī upahvayate yayoridaṃ sarvamadhyupahūto 'yaṃ yajamāna iti tadyajamānamupahvayate tadyadatra nāma na gṛhṇāti pro 'kṣṃ hyatrāśīryadiḍāyām mānuṣaṃ ha kuryādyannāma gṛhṇīyādvyṛddhaṃ vai tadyajñasya yanmānuṣaṃ nedvyṛddhaṃ yajñe karavāṇīti tasmānna nāma gṛhṇāti //
reference: 'Hither are called the primeval, law-abiding, divine (fem.) heaven and earth, whose sons are gods.' He thereby calls to him those two, heaven and earth, within which all this (universe) is embraced.--'Hither is called this sacrificer:' thereby he calls the sacrificer to him. Why he does not mention his name on this occasion, is that this is a mysterious benediction on the idâ. Were he, on the contrary, to mention the name, he would do what is human, and the human certainly is inauspicious at the sacrifice: hence he does not mentionthe name, lest he should do what is inauspicious at the sacrifice .
baseline: One who gives to the earthly ancestors the gods goddesses gods sons of gods in the morning in that case the earth would sit on the earth all the middle children would be called the master. One who does not take the name of a man in the evening would get the title of a priest a man named Hā kuriḍīna a woman named after a nobleman or a woman called Vruddhāya.
morphology: One who gives to the earthly ancestors the gods of the earth the goddess of the seasons the sons of the gods and the earth is sitting on the earth. One who does not take the name of a man in the middle of all the gods and the king of the land would get the title of the king. One would get a man named Hā Kūrīdīna the lord of the country the king named Yāṇṇu the son of the lord the ruler of the kingdom the chief minister the governor of the state the master of the nation the

sanskrit: uttarasyāṃ devayajyāyāmupahūta iti / tadasmā etajjīvātumeva paro 'kṣamāśāste jīvanhi pūrvamiṣṭvāthāparaṃ yajate //
reference: 'Hither (he is) called for future worship of the gods;' he thereby in a mysterious manner invokes the blessing of life on this (sacrificer); for as he sacrificed heretofore, so, while living, he will sacrifice hereafter.
baseline: The answer should be said to be Oupāhata in the abode of the gods that is to say O Lord of all beings that which is the preceptor of the life of the universe and that which has been worshipped on the day before.
morphology: The answer should be said to be that of the deity jyāma. We shall then repeat the same thing in the morning evening evening and evening.

sanskrit: tadasmā etatprajāmeva paro 'kṣamāśāste / yasya hi prajā bhavatyamuṃ lokamātmanaityathāsmiṃloke prajā yajate tasmātprajottarā devayajyā //
reference: Moreover, he thereby in a mysterious manner invokes the blessing of offspring for him; for whosoever has offspring,--while he, on his part, goes to yonder world, his offspring sacrifice in this world: hence future worship of the gods means offspring.
baseline: Then we should worship the Lord of the earth in the same manner as the king of the world. Then the king should worship his subjects the people and the spirit of the universe.
morphology: Then we shall say that the king of the world should be worshipped in the same manner as the king. The king of gods should be worshiped in the world. He should be known as the lord of the universe.

sanskrit: tadasmā etatpaśūneva paro 'kṣamāśāste yasya hi paśavo bhavanti sa pūrvamiṣṭvāthāparaṃ yajate //
reference: Moreover, he thereby in a mysterious manner invokes the blessing of cattle for him; for whosoever has cattle, will sacrifice hereafter, as he has sacrificed heretofore.
baseline: The one who has the same animal in the parakṣmāśa scriptures after having said these things would get the same amount of money as before.
morphology: The one who has the same animals in the law of the kingdom of Brahma and the king of the king should pay tribute to the previous king.

sanskrit: bhūyasi haviṣkaraṇa upahūta iti / tadasmā etajjīvātumeva paro 'kṣamāśāste jīvanhi pūrvamiṣṭvātha bhūyobhūya eva haviṣkaroti //
reference: 'Hither (he is) called for more abundant havis-offering;' he thereby in a mysterious manner invokes the blessing of life on him; for as he has sacrificed heretofore, so while living will he hereafter again and again make offerings.
baseline: One who has made a vow should do so after having made the vow of abhivāṇa. He would do so on the day before and on the night before.
morphology: One who has been blessed with the gift of the earth would be blessed with it. He would also be blessed by the earth on the day before in the month of jiva after having been blessed by us.

sanskrit: tadasmā etatprajāmeva paro 'kṣamāśāste yasya hi prajā bhavatyeka ātmanā bhavatyathota daśadhā prajayā haviṣkriyate tasmātprajā bhūyo haviṣkaraṇam //
reference: Moreover, he thereby in a mysterious manner invokes the blessing of offspring for this (sacrificer); for whosoever possesses offspring,--though he, of his own self, be one only, yet that offering is made tenfold by his offspring: hence offspring means more abundant offering.
baseline: Then shall we say that in the same manner as in the case of the king the king of the kingdom of the east his subjects would be ten subjects.
morphology: Then we shall say that the king of this kingdom should be destroyed by the ten kings of the kingdom of Kāṣma.

sanskrit: tadasmā etatpaśūneva paro 'kṣamāśāste / yasya hi paśavo bhavanti sa pūrvamiṣṭvātha bhūyobhūya eva haviṣkaroti //

morphology: The one who has the same animals in the temple should be blessed with the same amount of water as before. He should be worshipped on the ground.

sanskrit: eṣā vā āśīḥ jīveyam prajā me syācriyaṃ gaceyamiti tadyatpaśūnāśāste tacriyamāśāste śrīrhi paśavastadetābhyāmevaitadāśīrbhyāṃ sarvamāptaṃ tasmādvā ete atra dve āśiṣau kriyate //
reference: This then is the benediction (implied in these formulas), 'May I live, may I have offspring, may[paragraph continues] I obtain prosperity!' baseline: One should say that he would be the one who would live or live in the kingdom of Satya. One should worship the goddess Sāṣṇu in the Tāśrīma scriptures the goddess of animals animals and objects. One would be blessed with all these two blessings.
morphology: One should say that he would be the only one alive. He should be blessed with two things after having been blessed with the gift of animals and animals in the Tāśṇā scriptures.

sanskrit: devā ma idaṃ havirjuṣantāmiti / tasminnupahūta iti tadyajñasyaivaitatsamṛddhimāśāste yaddhi devā havirjuṣante tena hi mahajjayati tasmādāha juṣantāmiti // tāṃ vai prāśnantyeva /
reference: "[He continues to call], 'Hither (he is) called to this (sacrifice, for the prayer ), ""May the gods graciously accept this my offering (havis)!''' he thereby invokes complete success on the sacrifice; for what offering the gods graciously accept, by that one gains great things: for this reason he says, 'may they graciously accept .'"
baseline: The lord should know that he is the son of a cow that he should be blessed with prosperity and that the god should be pleased with that. He should be worshipped by him.
morphology: The lord should know that he is the son of a cow that he should be blessed with prosperity and that the god should be worshipped by him in the same manner.

morphology: A cow or animal should be killed by a snake or by a naked man without a neck. It should be destroyed by the enemy.

morphology: One who is born with the spirit of life would be born with it.

sanskrit: hotari tvadyajamāne tvadadhvaryau tvadatha yatpūrvārdham puroḍāśasya praśīrya purastāddhruvāyai nidadhāti yajamāno vai dhruvā tadyajamānasya prāśitam bhavatyatha yatpratyakṣaṃ na prāśnāti nedasaṃsthite yajñe prāśnānītyetadevāsya prāśitam bhavati sarve prāśnanti sarveṣu me hutāsaditi pañca prāśnanti paśavo vā iḍā pāṅktā vai paśavastasmātpañca prāśnanti //

baseline: If you do not question the priest the priest should be asked if he is not willing to offer a sacrifice. He should ask all the five questions of the lord whether he is willing to give five questions or whether he wants to give a gift or not.

sanskrit: atha yatra pratipadyate / taccaturdhā puroḍāśaṃ kṛtvā barhiṣadaṃ karoti tadatra pitṛṇāṃ bhājanena catasro vā avāntaradiśo 'vāntaradiśo vai pitarastasmāccaturdhā puroḍāśaṃ kṛtvā barhiṣadaṃ karoti //

baseline: Then the fire should be made to burn and the earth should be burned and the mother should be burnt. baseline: One who drinks this water and drinks it with the help of fire water water and other things would be thirsty. One who does not believe in the performance of the Vedas would be able to do so even if he does not agree with it.

sanskrit: agne vājajidvājaṃ tvā sasṛvāṃsaṃ vājajitaṃ sammārjmīti sariṣyantamiti vā agra āha sariṣyanniva hi tarhi bhavatyathātra sasṛvāṃsamiti sasṛveva hyatra bhavati tasmādāha sasṛvāṃsamiti //
reference: He sweeps (each time), with the formula , 'O Agni, food-gainer, I cleanse thee, the food-gainer, who hast hastened to the food!' baseline: If the fire is made to be lit by the priest the fire should be lit with the same sound as the fire and if the fire has been lit with a similar sounding sound and it is not made to sound. Then the four parts of the body should be burnt in the same place.
morphology: If the fire is made to be worshipped in the form of a fire the fire should be offered to the king the king should be worshipping the king and the king of the kingdom of Sārava and the chief minister should offer the same to you.

sanskrit: athānuyājānyajati /

morphology: One who worships ata should worship ata.

sanskrit: atha yadanuyājānyajati /
reference: Now this is why he makes the after-offerings.
baseline: Then the priest should be worshipped.
morphology: Then the priest should be worshipped.

sanskrit: candāṃsi vā anuyājāḥ paśavo vai devānāṃ candāṃsi tadyathedaṃ paśavo yuktā manuṣyebhyo vahantyevaṃ candāṃsi yuktāni devebhyo yajñaṃ vahanti tadyatra candāṃsi devāntsamatarpayannatha candāṃsi devāḥ samatarpayaṃstadatastatprāgabhūdyaccandāṃsi yuktāni devebhyo yajñamavākṣuryadenāntsamatītṛpan //
reference: The after-offerings assuredly are the metres , and the metres are the cattle of the gods: hence as cattle, when harnessed, here convey (burdens) for men, so in like manner the metres, being harnessed,convey the sacrifice to the gods. baseline: One should offer a sacrifice to the gods by offering a piece of sandal or a piece containing the same amount of sandals as that of animals animals and other animals men women animals horses horses etc. One would offer a gift to the deities gods goddesses equals gods and goddesses.
morphology: Those who follow the sandals the animals the gods the offerings made to the gods and those who carry the animals and carry them to humans and those carrying them carry them and offer them to the deities. The offerings made by the gods would be equal to those made by them.

sanskrit: atha yadanuyājānyajati /
reference: And this again is why he makes the after-offerings.
baseline: Then the priest should be worshipped.
morphology: Then the priest should be worshipped.

sanskrit: candāṃsi vā anuyājāścandāṃsyevaitatsaṃtarpayati tasmādanuyājānyajati tasmādyena vāhanena dhāvayettadvimucya brūyātpāyayatainatsuhitaṃ kurutetyeṣa u vāhanasyāpahnavaḥ //
reference: The after-offerings are the metres: hence he thereby gratifies the metres, and for this reason also he makes the after-offerings. morphology: It is said to be like the unmanly one. If the earth is established in the same way as it was when it was conquered it will be restored to its original state. Then it will become man again.

sanskrit: te vai patnīḥ saṃyājayiṣyantaḥ pratiparāyanti /
reference: Being about to perform the patnîsamyâgas , they betake themselves back to the Gârhapatya fire.
baseline: Those wives would be consoled. They would be returned.
morphology: Those wives would be consoled. They would be punished.

sanskrit: juhūṃ ca sruvaṃ cādhvaryurādatte vedaṃ hotājyavilāpanīmagnīt //
reference: The Adhvaryu takes the guhû and sruva, the Hotri the veda, and the Âgnîdhra the butter-(melting) pot.
baseline: One should recite the scriptures of the king after having worshipped the jhu śruva and Śrūvā.
morphology: The veda should be recited in the form of a rosary with the syllable jūhu sruva chādhvārūda hota and rajya.

sanskrit: taddhaikeṣāmadhvaryuḥ / pūrveṇāhavanīyam paryeti tadu tathā na kuryādbahirdhā ha yajñātsyādyatteneyāt //
reference: Here now the Adhvaryu, according to some, passes the Âhavanîya on the east side. Let him not, however, do this; for were he to walk on that side, he would be outside the sacrifice.
baseline: One should not offer the sacrifice of a cow or other animal in the form of an animal.
morphology: One should not offer the sacrifice of the priest in the form of a cow or other animal in the east.

sanskrit: jaghaneno haiva patnīṃ /
reference: According to others, the Adhvaryu walks (so as to pass) behind the (sacrificer's) wife .
baseline: The wife should be the wife of a cow.
morphology: The wife should be the wife of a cow.

sanskrit: ekeṣāmadhvaryureti no eva tathā kuryātpūrvārdho vai yajñasyādhvaryurjaghanārdhaḥ patnī yathā bhasattaḥ śiraḥ pratidadhyādevaṃ tadbahirdhā haiva yajñātsyādyatteneyāt //
reference: Let him not, however, do this either; for verily the Adhvaryu is the fore-part, and the wife is the hind-part of the sacrifice: hence, if he were to pass so, it would be as if one were to put his head behind; and he (the Adhvaryu) would be outside the sacrifice.
baseline: The wife should offer half the amount of the sacrifice as before. The head should be placed on each of the two sides of the head and the head on the other side of the deity.
morphology: The wife should offer half the amount of the sacrifice as before. The head of the devotee should be placed on the head and the head on each side of the deity.

sanskrit: antareṇo haiva patnīṃ /
reference: According to others, the Adhvaryu passes between the wife (and the Gârhapatya fire).
baseline: The wife should be of the same nature as the wife.
morphology: One who has a wife is called Antaraṇo.

sanskrit: ekeṣāmadhvaryureti no eva tathā kuryādantariyāddha yajñātpatnīṃ yatteneyāttasmādu pūrveṇaiva gārhapatyamantareṇāhavanīyaṃ caiti tathā ha na bahirdhā yajñādbhavati yatho evādaḥ pracarannantareṇa saṃcarati sa u evāsyaiṣa saṃcaro bhavati //
reference: Let him not, however, do this either; for were he to pass that way, he would cut off the wife from the sacrifice. Along the east side of the Gârhapatya and the inner side of the Âhavanîya (he passes); for thus he is not outside the sacrifice; and as before, in walking forward (to the Âhavanîya), he passed along the inner side, so he now also takes that path.
baseline: One who does not make a sacrifice to the wife of the husband by the same means as that of the wife would not be able to do so. One who makes a sacrifice by the other means would not go beyond the service of the mother and the wife would be made to do it by the preceptor.
morphology: One who does not make a sacrifice to the wife of the husband of a woman by the means of the āvādaṇa mantra should be offered to her. One who makes a sacrifice by the way of the mother of the bridegroom by the method of the mantras of the house of the wife and does not go out of the place of the sacrifice should be worshipped by the priest of the daughter of the son of the king.

sanskrit: atha patnīḥ saṃyājayanti /
reference: They now perform the patnîsamyâgas.
baseline: Thus the wives are restrained.
morphology: Thus the wives are restrained.

sanskrit: yajñādvai prajāḥ prajāyante yajñātprajāyamānā mithunātprajāyante mithunātprajāyamānā antato yajñasya prajāyante tadenā etadantato yajñasya mithunātprajananātprajanayati tasmānmithunātprajananādantato yajñasyemāḥ prajāḥ prajāyante tasmātpatnīḥ saṃyājayanti //
reference: From the sacrifice offspring is assuredly produced; and (that offspring) produced from the sacrifice is produced from union; and (the offspring) produced from union is produced after (in consequence of) the completion of the sacrifice: hence one thereby (i.e. by the patnîsamyâgas) causes that (offspring) to be produced by means of a productive union after the completion of the sacrifice. And so now also offspring is produced by means of a productive union after the completion of the sacrifice. This is why they now perform the patnîsamyâgas.
baseline: The two subjects of the sacrifice are the subjects. Those who perform the sacrifice and those who perform it are the subject of the final sacrifice. Then those who do not perform the oblation are called the subjects of that oblation. Then the subjects who perform this oblation would be called Mithuna. Then their subjects would be known as Mithuna and the subjects would become subjects of those oblations.
morphology: The people of the two sacrificial houses are the subjects of the sacrifice. Those who perform the sacrifice are the subject of the oblation of the mithuna those who do not perform the oblations of the mermaids are the members of the sacrificial house. Then those who perform this oblation are the offspring of the servitorious house of the deceased. Those people who perform these oblations are called subjects of that oblation.

sanskrit: catasro devatā yajati /
reference: He makes offering to four deities.
baseline: The four gods are worshipped.
morphology: Four gods are worshipped.

sanskrit: catasro vai mithunaṃ dvandvaṃ vai mithunaṃ dve dve hi khalu bhavato mithunamevaitatprajanane kriyate tasmāccatasro devatā yajati //
reference: Four doubtless means a couple; for a couple means a pair (dvandva, lit. two and two), and two and two indeed they are: thus a productive union is thereby effected; and accordingly he makes offering to four deities.
baseline: The four mithuna two mithu two hīla mithun and the three mithūs are given to the gods for the purpose of procreation.
morphology: A mithuna is said to be the fourth among the four mithunas. A midduna is known to be double the middinas. The middins are given to you in the birth of the mithune. The gods are known to give the three mithinas to you.

sanskrit: reto vā ājyaṃ reta evaitatsiñcati tasmādājyahaviṣo bhavanti //
reference: Butter indeed means seed: hence he thereby scatters seed, and therefore makes them of butter for sacrificial food.
baseline: The sand or the sand that is present in the earth is water. It becomes poisonous.
morphology: The sand or the sand that is present in the earth is water. It becomes poisonous.

sanskrit: tira iva vai mithunena caryate tira ivaitadyadupāṃśu tasmādupāṃśu caranti //
reference: Secretly, doubtless, union takes place; and secretly also (takes place) what (is spoken) in a low voice: this is why they perform in a low voice.
baseline: One who grabs a piece of water with the mithuna is called a tira. He grabs it with the tira a pūpanshu and then he grazes with it.
morphology: One who grazes with a mithuna like a spade would be grazed with the spade. One would graze with the same spade as with a pigeon.

sanskrit: atha somaṃ yajati /
reference: He first makes offering to Soma.
baseline: It gives the summa.
morphology: It gives the son of Soma.

sanskrit: reto vai somo reta evaitatsiñcati tasmātsomaṃ yajati //
reference: Soma indeed means seed; hence he thereby scatters seed: this is why he makes offering to Soma.
baseline: The sand is equal to the amount of sand. The water is obtained from it.
morphology: One gets the sum of sesamum from the same amount of sand and water from it.

sanskrit: atha tvaṣṭāraṃ yajati /
reference: He then makes offering to Tvashtri.
baseline: Then he will get you.
morphology: This will make you feel good.

sanskrit: na rājñāṃ yatra pīḍā syānāśramāṇāṃ vināśanam| sa deśo dṛśyatāṃ saumya nāparādhyāmahe yathā||
reference: And where if a kingdom is established it might:not disturb the peace of hermitage and happiness of other kings.
baseline: The king should not suffer in the absence of the king. He should be destroyed in the presence of the kingdom. He would not be able to see the land. He is not able to be gentle.
morphology: The king should not be destroyed by the destruction of the king's house by suffering. He should be seen in the country. We should not allow the king to be benevolent.

sanskrit: tathoktavati rāme tu bharataḥ pratyuvāca ha| ayaṃ kārupatho deśo ramaṇīyo nirāmayaḥ||
reference: Răma, having finished his speech Bharata replied:-The country of Kårupatha is highly picturesque and freed from all thorns.
baseline: Then the king should say to the king of India that he would heal the country and the country from the path of the car.
morphology: Then the king of India should say that he would heal the country and the country by the car path.

sanskrit: niveśyatāṃ tatra puramaṅgadasya mahātmanaḥ| candraketoḥ suruciraṃ candrakāntaṃ nirāmayam||
reference: Let the city for high souled Angada be established there. And let the beautiful and healthy country of Candradkānta be the kingdom of Candraketu.
baseline: One should place the idol of the great man at the top of the temple. One should offer the suruṣirācira and the chandrakanta in the form of the crescent of the moon.
morphology: One should place the idol of the great man at the base of the temple. One should make the crescent of the moon with the incense stick and the incantation of the lilies of the chandrakanta as a cure.

sanskrit: tadvākyaṃ bharatenoktaṃ pratijagrāha rāghavaḥ| taṃ ca kṛtvā vaśe deśamaṅgadasya nyaveśayat||
reference: Rāma approved of the words of Bharata and having brought the country of Kārupatha under his subjection gave it to Angada.
baseline: In the same way the king of India said that the king should be taken into custody. Having done that he should place the king on the throne.
morphology: In the same way Bharata said to Raghava that he should be taken into custody. Having done so he placed the king of the country on the throne.

sanskrit: aṅgadīyā purī ramyāpyaṅgadasya niveśitā| ramaṇīyā suguptā ca rāmeṇākliṣṭakarmaṇā|||
reference: He reared a beautiful and well-protected city for Angada.
baseline: The body of the king should be placed in the temple with the prasadam of the limbs. The body should be adorned with the fragrant fragrance of the goddess Rama.
morphology: The body of the king should be placed in the temple with the fragrance of the limbs. The fragrance should be made of the fragrant leaves of the goddess Rama.

sanskrit: candraketośca mallasya mallabhūmyāṃ niveśitā| candrakānteti vikhyātā divyā svargapurī yathā||
reference: And in the country of Malaya he reared a city for Candraketu, named Candrakāntā highly picturesque and like to the city of celestials.
baseline: The image of Chandra is placed on the ground of Malla. The image described as Chandrakanta is said to be like that of the divine heaven.
morphology: The image of Chandra is placed on the ground of Malla and the image of Chandrakanta is described as the divine heaven.

sanskrit: tato rāmaḥ parāṃ prītiṃ lakṣmaṇo bharatastathā| yayuyuddhe durādharṣā abhiṣekaṃ ca cakrire|| abhiṣicya kumārau dvau prasthāpya susamāhitau| aṅgadaṃ paścimāṃ bhūmiṃ candraketumudaṅmukham|| aṅgadaṃ cāpi saumitrirlakṣmaṇo'nujagāma ha| candraketostu bharataḥ pārkhāigrāho babhūva ha||
reference: There upon greatly delighted Rāma, irrepressible in battle, Laksmana and Bharata, having performed the ceremony of installation ordered them to go their respective cities. Angada started towards the West and Candraketu towards the North. Sumitra's son Lakşmana went with Angada and Bharata accompanied Candraketu.
baseline: Then Rama should be worshipped by the other side by Lakshmana by Bharata in the war by the king of the enemy by having worshipped him in the chakra by offering him two kumaras by leaving the western part of the body by holding the forehead of the crescent by sitting on the head of the moon by touching the left side of the head by worshipping him by making him obeisance by worshiping him and by having said that he would worship him.
morphology: Then Rama should be worshipped in front of others lakshmana bharata in the war of yuva riddled with evil and abhisheka the kumars should be placed on the chakra. Having set out two sons should be bound with the same body. The body should be made to face the west the body of the moon the face of the body the head of the head and the body and the limbs should be tied together.

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇastvaṅgadīyāyāṃ saṃvatsaramathoṣitaḥ| putra sthite durādharṣe ayodhyāṃ punarāgamat||
reference: Having spent a year in Angada's city and finding his son well established in the kingdom Lakşmana returned to Ayodhyā.
baseline: One should return to Ayodhya in the year of Lakshmana and his wife in which he was born in the month of Samvat. If his son is present then he should return in the season of Durrādhāśa.
morphology: One should return to Ayodhya in the year of Lakshmana and his wife in which he was born. If his son is present then he should return in the month of Rudraśa.

sanskrit: bharato'pi tathaivoṣya saṃvatsaramato'dhikam| ayodhyāṃ punarāgamya rāmapādāvupāsta saḥ||
reference: And Bharata, according to his desire, having spent more than a year in the city of Candrakāntă, came back to Ayodhyā and saluted Rama's feet.
baseline: Having said so to Bharata he should return to Ayodhya with his feet.
morphology: He should also repeat the same thing to Bharata and the year before. He should return to Ayodhya and worship Lord Rama.

sanskrit: ubhau saumitribharatau rāmapādāvanuvratau| kālaṃ gatamapi snehānna jajñāte'tidhārmikau||
reference: The pious Laksmana and Bharata— both the brothers, were greatly attached to Råma; and though the spent their days in another place they did not experience any pain in consequence of separation from their sons.
baseline: Both are the manifestations of Śaumitrī Bharata Rāmapada and Vātra. One who knows the past without affection or affection is a virtuous person.
morphology: Both are the manifestations of the greatness of Rama. The past is also known as the time without affection. The present is known as dharmic.

sanskrit: evaṃ varṣasahasrāṇi daśa teṣāṃ yayustadā| dharme prayatamānānāṃ paurakāryeṣu nityadā||
reference: Observing all virtues in this way, Rāma, the foremost of the pious, Bharata and Lakşmaņa governed the subjects for ten thousand years.
baseline: In the same way ten thousand years should be given to those who practice religion in the course of their duties in the city.
morphology: In the same way ten thousand years should be given to them. The priest should always be present in the duties of the priesthood.

sanskrit: vihṛtya kālaṃ paripūrṇamānasāḥ śriyā vṛtā dharmapure ca saṃsthitāḥ| trayaḥ samiddhāhutidīptatejaso hutāgnayaḥ sādhumahādhvare trayaḥ||
reference: Having spent their days in the city of Ayodhyā, the very city of virtue, the three brothers, appearing graceful like the burning fire receiving oblations in a great sacrifice, attained to joy in the fullness of time.
baseline: Having spent time in the sanctum sanctorum of the temple the srīya should be placed in the temple with the mind full of the sun. The fire should be lit three times in the morning and three times at the altar of the saint.
morphology: Having spent time in the sanctum sanctorum of the temple the devotees should be placed in the temple with their whole mind. The fire should be lit three times in the morning and the fire should not be lit in the evening.

sanskrit: etadākhyāya rāmāya maharṣiḥ kumbhasaṃbhavaḥ| asyāmevāparaṃ vākyaṃ kathāyāmupacakrame||
reference: Having related this story to Rāma the great saint Agastya again said in this context.
baseline: This is said to be the best thing for Rama. The great sage Kumbhasambhava is the bestower of this good. The story is told in the cycle of the Upa.
morphology: This is said to be the best bet for Lord Rama. The king of the potter is known to be able to do this. The story is told in the scripture.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa daṇḍaḥ kākutstha bahuvarṣagaṇāyutam| akarottatra dāntātmā rājyaṃ nihatakaṇṭakam||
reference: O Kākutstha, having subdued his passions, the king Danda, reigned undisturbed in this wise for many long years.
