baseline: Then the punishment should be repeated for a number of years. Then the king should be punished with the sword of the spirit and the sword should be destroyed.
morphology: Then the punishment should be repeated for a number of years. The kingdom of the spirit should be destroyed by the king.

sanskrit: atha kāle tu kasmiṃścidrājā bhārgavamāśramam| ramaṇīyamupākrāmaccaitre māsi manorame||
reference: Thereupon during spring, in the month of Caitra the king arrived at the picturesque hermitage of the preceptor Sukra.
baseline: In such a time the king of the land should be destroyed by the enemy. The king should be made to sit in the palace of the king. The queen should be worshipped in the temple of the lord.
morphology: In such a time the king of the poor should worship Bhārga the lord of the earth. The king should worship the goddess in the form of the mother of the illusion.

sanskrit: tatra bhārgavakanyāṃ sa rūpeṇāpratimāṃ bhuvi| vicarantīṃ vanoddeśe daṇḍo'paśyadanuttamām|| sa dṛṣṭvā tāṃ sudurmedhā anaṅgaśarapīḍitaḥ| abhigamya susaṃvignaḥ kanyāṃ vacanamabravīt||
reference: At that time, Sukra's daughter, matchless in beauty and grace, was walking in the forest. The king saw that jewel of a girl, and being stricken with lust and growing restless he approached her and said.
baseline: There he should worship the image of Bhārgavakāṇya in the form of a virgin. He should see the wandering forest as a punishment for the purpose. Seeing that he is ill and suffering from his own body he should say the following words. The virgin who is ill acquainted with the good should be taken to the king.
morphology: He should be worshipped there in the form of a virgin and the image of a woman. Seeing that he has been punished for wandering in the wilderness he should say that he is suffering from the disease of the body and other organs. He should say to the virgin who is ill and ill.

sanskrit: kutastvamasi suśroṇi kasya vāsi sutā śubhe| pīḍito'hamanaṅgena pṛcchāmi tvāṃ śubhānane||
reference: O you having a beautiful waist, O fair lady, whose daughter are you? O you having a moonlike countenance, I have been assailed by the arrows of Cupid and hence I do accost you thus.
baseline: One who has been afflicted with the disease should ask thee in the form of a benediction.
morphology: One who has been afflicted with the disease should ask thee in good words.

sanskrit: tasya tvevaṃ bruvāṇasya mohonmattasya kāminaḥ| bhārgavī pratyuvācedaṃ vacaḥ sānunayaṃ tvidam||
reference: Hearing the words of the vicious-souled Danda, maddened with lust, Sukra's daughter humbly said.
baseline: One who has the desire to worship the goddess Brūvaṇa the goddess of beauty and the goddess Bhārgavī one who has a desire to be worshipped should say the words sañuṇa.
morphology: One who has the desire to be blessed with the gift of Brahman one who is a devotee of the goddess of the universe one should say the words of Bhārga Pratyuva and Sāna.

sanskrit: bhārgavasya sutāṃ viddhidevasyākliṣṭakarmaṇaḥ| arajāṃ nāma rājendra jyeṣṭhāmāśramavāsinīm|| mā māṃ spṛśa balādrājankanyā pitṛvaśā hyaham| guruḥ pitā me rājendra tvaṃ ca śiṣyo mahātmanaḥ||
reference: """O king of kings I am the daughter of the humbly Sukra of unwearied actions and my name is Araja. I am living in this hermitage, O king, do not touch me forcibly for I am a maid and hence under the guardianship forcibly for my father. Besides my father is my preceptor, and you are also his disciple."
baseline: One should not touch me the son of Bhārgava the disciple of Vidyadeva the master of the labourer the servant of the worker the lord of the firmament the elder brother of the servant the king of the mighty king the daughter of the father the teacher the father of the king you are the student of the great man.
morphology: One should not touch me the king of the mighty king the son of Bhārgava the disciple of Viddhidevā the master of the poor and the worker of the labourer. One should say that the name of the king is rājendra. One who is a resident of the upper house should not be touched by me one who is the father of a king one with the strength and one who has a father.

sanskrit: vyasanaṃ sumahatkruddhaḥ sa te dadyānmahātapāḥ| yadi vānyanmayā kārya dharmadṛṣṭena satpathā|| varayasva naraśreṣṭha pitaraṃ me mahādyutim| anyathā tu phalaṃ tubhyaṃ bhaveddhorābhisaṃhitam||
reference: Being enraged he shall imprecate you with a curse. O foremost of men, if you do cherish any desire for me, do you honestly and piously pray for it to my sire. Or else you shall suffer dreadful consequences in the long run.
baseline: He who is fond of the addictions and mercilessly angry should give them to the enemies. If he has done the deeds of the enemy with the spirit of righteousness then he should give the noble man the great father as a gift. Otherwise he would get the reward.
morphology: He who is fond of those things and has a good heart should give them. If he does these things out of righteousness then he should offer the best of men and his father in a noble manner. Otherwise he would get the reward.

sanskrit: krodhena hi pitā me'sau trailokyamapi nirdahet| dāsyate cānavadyāṅga tava mā yācitaḥ pitā ||
reference: When worked up with ire, my father can reduce even the three worlds to ashes. O you of a blameless person, if you do pray, my father may make me over to your hands.
baseline: O father if you are angry with me you will be punished even by the three worlds. If you want to give your body do not ask your father.
morphology: O father if you are angry with me you will be punished even by the three worlds. If you wish to be given a part of your body do not ask your father.

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvāṇāmarajāṃ daṇḍaḥ kāmavaśaṃ gataḥ| pratyuvāca madonmattaḥ śirasyādhāya cāñjalim||13
reference: Arajas having said this, the king Danda, maddened with lust, placing folded palms on his head, said.
baseline: In this way the punishment of the king of Brūvanāmarājā went to Kāmāśa. He should pay tribute to Maṇṇa with the head and head.
morphology: In this way the punishment of the king of Brūvanāmarājā went to lust. Every man should be punished with the sacrifice of the head.

sanskrit: prasādaṃ kuru suśroṇi na kālaṃ kṣeptumarhasi| tvatkṛte hi mama prāṇā vidīryante varānane|| tvāṃ prāpya tu vadho vāpi pāpaṃ vāpi sudāruṇam| bhaktaṃ bhajasva māṃ bhīru bhajamānaṃ suvihvalam||
reference: Be you propitiated with me, O you having a graceful person; do not tarry even for a moment. My heart bursts out for you, O you having a moon-like countenance. For acquiring you I can even take upon myself my own destruction or dreadful iniquity. Do you seek me, O fair ladyI am beside myself for you.
baseline: O king of the world you will not be able to save me for a long time. You will destroy my life by making offerings. You get rid of me from the bridegroom. You become a victim of sin. You worship the devotee. You make me fearful and worship you. You give me good fortune.
morphology: O king of the world you will not be able to save me for a long time. You will destroy my life by your provocation. You get rid of me from the bridegroom you kill me you commit sin you suffer from evil you worship me and make me fearful and worship you.

sanskrit: evamuktvā tu tāṃ kanyāṃ dobhyāṃ prāpya balādalī| visphurantīṃ yathākāmaṃ maithunāyopacakrame|| tamanartha mahāghoraṃ daṇḍaḥ kṛtvā sudāruṇam| nagaraṃ prayayāvāśu madhumantamanuttamam||
reference: Having said this the king forcibly ravished her. Having perpetrated such a mighty iniquity he speedily returned to his own city Madhumanta.
baseline: Having thus liberated the bride the bridegroom should be taken away and given to a strong force. The woman should be thrown into the cycle of sexual intercourse as if she had been punished with a great punishment. The city should be given the best of honey and honey.
morphology: Having thus liberated the virgin from the evil one the force of the enemy should be taken to the other side. Then as far as possible after having punished her with a great punishment in the cycle of sexual intercourse she should be punished with a fine. The city should be given the best of honey and honey.

sanskrit: arajāpi rudantī sā āśramasyāvidūrataḥ| pratīkṣate susaṃtrastā pitaraṃ devasaṃnibham||
reference: Arajă cried aloud in forest at no distance from the hermitage and waited for here sire who had been away on visiting the celestials. a blameless person, if you do pray, my father may make me over to your hands.
baseline: She cries in the distance from the hermitage even as she prays and waits for her father.
morphology: She cries even when she prays. She waits for her father from far away in the hermitage.

sanskrit: arajāpi rudantī sā āśramasyāvidūrataḥ| pratīkṣate susaṃtrastā pitaraṃ devasaṃnibham||
reference: Arajă cried aloud in forest at no distance from the hermitage and waited for here sire who had been away on visiting the celestials.
baseline: She cries in the distance from the hermitage even as she prays and waits for her father.
morphology: She cries even when she prays. She waits for her father from far away in the hermitage.

sanskrit: sa tu rākṣasaśārdūlo nidrāmadasamākulaḥ| rājamārga śriyā juṣṭaṃ yayau vipulavikramaḥ||
reference: That tiger-like Rakşasa possessed of prowess, (still) under the influence of slumber, strode along the picturesque highway.
baseline: He is the demon Śardulo who is full of sleep and rest. He is a great record when he is on the path of the lord Śrīya.
morphology: He is the demon Śardulo who is full of sleep and rest. He is a great record when he is on the path of the lord Śrīya.

sanskrit: rākṣasānāṃ sahasraiśca vṛtaḥ paramadurjayaḥ| gṛhebhyaḥ puṣpavarṣeṇa kīryamāṇastadā yayau||
reference: That exceedingly unconquerable one, surrounded by thousands of Raksasas, went on, showered with blossoms from the houses (standing by).
baseline: One who casts thousands of demons into the houses with the rain of flowers is said to be the greatest evil.
morphology: One who casts thousands of demons into the houses with the rain of flowers would be blessed with the highest glory.

sanskrit: sa hemajālavitataṃ bhānubhāsvaradarśanam| dadarśa vipulaṃ ramyaṃ rākṣasendraniveśanam||
reference: Then he saw the grand and graceful residence of the lord of the Räkşasas, having golden networks and sun-bright to behold.
baseline: He is the manifestation of Hemājala. The manifestation is the sight of Bhanubhāśu. The appearance is immense and the apparition of the demon Sendra.
morphology: He is the manifestation of the celestial body of Bhanubhāsa. He is said to be the manifestations of the great demon Sendra.

sanskrit: sa tattadā sūrya ivābhrajālaṃ praviśya rakṣodhipaterniveśanam| dadarśa dūre'grajamāsanasthaṃ svayaṃbhuvaṃ śakra ivāsanastham|4||
reference: Entering the mansion of the Raksasa sovereign, like the sun entering into a mass of clouds, he saw his elder brother seated at a distance; even as Sakra sees the Self-sprung seated.
baseline: Then the sun should enter the net and protect the earth. Then the earth should be placed at a distance from the earth and placed in the abode of God.
morphology: Then the sun should enter the netherworld and raise the guardianship. Then the earth should be placed in the abode of the gods at a distance of three miles.

sanskrit: bhrātuḥ sa bhavanaṃ gatvā rakṣogaṇasamanvitaḥ| kumbhakarṇa: padanyāsairakampayata medinīm||
reference: Kumbhakarņa surrounded by numbers of Rākşasas, entered his brother's abode, making the very earth tremble with his tread.
baseline: The brother goes to the palace and confers protection on the bridegroom. The maidens should be given the position of kumbhācārna.
morphology: The brother goes to the palace and confers protection on the bridegroom. The maidens should be worshipped after having attained the position of kumbhakarana.

sanskrit: so'bhigamya gṛhaṃ bhrātuḥ kakṣyāmabhivigāhya ca| dada dvignamāsīnaṃ vimāne puṣpake gurum ||
reference: Arriving at the abode and passing the entrance, he saw his superior anxiously seated on the car, Pusphaka.
baseline: Having entered the house of the master the brother should enter the room and leave the room. The master should give the two-legged man a flower in the plane.
morphology: Having entered the house of ones brother and having entered into the room of another one should give the double oblation to the master in the plane of flowers.

sanskrit: atha dṛṣṭvā daśagrīvaḥ kumbhakarṇamupasthitam| tūrṇamutthāya saṃhṛṣṭāḥ saṃnikarṣamupānayat||
reference: Seeing Kumbhakarņa come, the Ten necked one, exceedingly rejoiced, raised him up and drew him near himself.
baseline: Having seen these ten giraffes standing on a potter one should raise the horn and raise the samsara.
morphology: Having seen these ten giraffes standing on the top of the potter's neck the arrow should be raised to the height of ten cubits. The arrows should be made to reach the right side of the earth.

sanskrit: athāsīnasya paryaṅke kumbhakarṇo mahābalaḥ| bhrāturvavande caraṇau kiṃ kṛtyamiti cābravīt||
reference: "Then the exceedingly mighty Kumbhakarņa saluted the feet of his brother and said, ""What did you say ?"""
baseline: The king of Mahabalā the king of the potter who is sitting on the mountain of Athasinā and who is the great king. What should be done at the feet of the brother Varvaṇḍa.
morphology: The king of Mahabalāla is said to be the kumbhakaṇa at the seat of the king. What should be done at the feet of the brothers and the king of the kingdom of Vāṇḍa.

sanskrit: punaḥ sa muditotpatya rāvaṇaḥ pariṣasvaje| sa bhrātrā saṃpariṣvakko yathāvaccābhinanditaḥ||
reference: Thereat, delighted, Ravana, springing up, again embraced (his brother). And embraced (by his brother), and duly greeted by him, that brother (of Ravana).
baseline: Then again he should be killed and the king should be sent to the council. He should be blessed as if he were a brother or a nobleman.
morphology: Then again he should be mercilessly worshipped. He should be pleased as if he were a brother and a nobleman.

sanskrit: kumbhakarṇaḥ śubhaṃ divyaṃ pratipede varāsamam| sa tadāsanamāśritya kumbhakarṇo mahābalaḥ|| saṃraktanayanaḥ krodhādrāvaṇaṃ vākyamabravīt|
reference: Kumbhakarņa seated himself on a shining and superb seat. And seating himself on that seat, the wondrous powerful Kumbhakarna, with his eyes reddened in wrath, addressed Ravana, saying.
baseline: Having worshipped the kumbhākarna as the auspicious god of wealth and the divine god of prosperity the king should worship the potter after having worshipped him in the same posture. Having protected him from wrath he should pray to the king of wrath.
morphology: Having worshipped the kumbhākarna as the auspicious god of wealth the divine god of prosperity the lord of wealth and wealth should be worshipped in the same posture. He should worship the kambhākaṇa king and the great king.

sanskrit: kimarthamahamādṛtya tvayā rājaprabodhitaḥ|| śaṃsa kasmādbhayaṃ te'tra ko vā preto bhaviṣyati| bhrātaraṃ rāvaṇaḥ kruddhaṃ kumbhakarṇamavasthitam|| roṣeṇa parivṛttābhyāṃ netrābhyāṃ vākyamabravīt||
reference: O king, why honouring me, has you awaked me? Tell me whence springs your fear? And who shall be a ghost?* Thereat Ravana, waxing wroth, and with his eyes rolling in rage, said to Kumbhakarma, seated. *Having been slain by me.
baseline: The king should explain to the king why he has spoken to you. Who would be pleased if he does so. The king would be angry with his brother Ravana who is angry with him who would be afraid of him. He would be enraged by him.
morphology: The king should explain to me why he has spoken to you and what he fears. If he does so who would love him? He should say to his brother Ravana angry and angry at the kumbhakaṇa king. He should be angry with him and the king should be afraid of him.

sanskrit: ayaṃ te sumahānkālaḥ śayānasya mahābala| suṣuptastvaṃ na jānīye mama rāmakṛtaṃ bhayam||
reference: O highly powerful one, you have slept away a long space of time. And having been asleep, you did not know the great fear of mine springing from Rama.
baseline: This is the great time for sleeping. One who does not know the fear of my Rama should sleep.
morphology: This is the great time for sleeping. One who does not know the fear of Rama should sleep.

sanskrit: eṣa dāśarathiḥ śrīmānsugrīvasahito balī| samudraṃ lavayitvā tu kulaṃ naḥ parikṛntati||
reference: This graceful son to Daśaratha possessed of strength, along with Sugriva, having crossed the ocean, is destroying our race.
baseline: This dāśarāthi is the sacrifice of the lord along with the goddess sūgriva. One would not be able to circumvent the clan if the sea were to be plucked.
morphology: This is the king of the dāśarāthīs. He is a sacrifice with good qualities. He would not be able to destroy the clan by having the sea covered.

sanskrit: hanta paśyasva laṅkāyāṃ vanānyupavanāni ca| setunā sukhamāgatya vānaraikārṇavaṃ kṛtam||
reference: Alack! see in own Lanka, woods and forests have been flooded with an ocean of monkeys never even coming without any ado by the bridge (which they have constructed).
baseline: One should see the forests and forests in Lanka. Having returned happily with the bridge one should worship the monkeys.
morphology: Then you see the forests and forests in Lanka. Having returned happily with the bridge the monkeys have been made to live in the forest.

sanskrit: ye rākṣasā mukhyatamā hatāste vānarairyudhi vānarāṇāṃ kṣayaṃ yuddhe na paśyāmi kathaṃcana|| na cāpi vānarā yuddhe jitapūrvāḥ kadācana||
reference: Those Rākşasas that were prime have been slain in battle by the monkeys; but I find no destruction of the monkeys in fight. Nay, the monkeys have been before vanquished (by the Raksasas) in battle.
baseline: One who kills a demon chiefly would never see the monkeys in the war. One who destroys monkeys would never get victory in the battle.
morphology: One who kills a demon chiefly one who kills monkeys war monkeys etc. in a war should not be seen. One who does not fight the monkeys should never be caught by the king.

sanskrit: tadetadbhayamutpannaṃ trāyasveha mahābala| nāśaya tvamimānadya tadarthaṃ bodhito bhavān||
reference: Therefore has this fear sprung up in my heart). Save me from this, O exceedingly powerful one. Do you now destroy these. It is for this that I have roused you.
baseline: Then you will be able to destroy the great king. You should destroy him and make him aware of it.
morphology: Then you will be able to destroy the great king. You should destroy him and make him aware of it.

sanskrit: sarvakṣapitakośaṃ ca sa tvamabhyupapadya mām| trāyasvemāṃ purīṃ laṅkāṃ bālavṛddhāvaśeṣitām||
reference: Do you, favouring me, whose exchequer is empty, save this city of Lanka, having only young folks and the aged left.
baseline: He should give me the body of the father of all the children. He should also give me that which is left of the children and elders.
morphology: He should give me the body of the father and all the children. He should offer me three things a lanka a boy an old man and the rest of you.

sanskrit: bhrāturarthe mahābāho kuru karma suduṣkaram| mayaivaṃ noktapūrvo hi bhrātā kaścitparaṃtapa ||
reference: O long-armed one, do you perform your dearest acts in behalf of your brother. O subduer of enemies, I had never before said so to my brother.
baseline: O Great Lord for the sake of the brethren do good deeds and evil deeds. Saying this to me The elder brother is a great servant.
morphology: O Great Lord for the sake of the brethren do good deeds and evil deeds. Saying this before you This brother is a great servant.

sanskrit: tvayyasti mama ca snehaḥ parā saṃbhāvanā ca me| devāsureṣu yuddheṣu bahuśo rākṣasarṣabha|| tvayā devāḥ prativyūhya nirjitāścāmarā yudhi ||
reference: In you is my affection and great is the probability of your succeeding. In the wars of the celestials and Asuras, O foremost of Rāks asas, countless were the celestials that you as an antagonist had beaten.
baseline: You are my love and the possibility beyond me. In the wars of gods and other beings many demons should fight against the gods. You should fight the king without being defeated by the demons.
morphology: You are my love and my potential. You have raised many demons in the wars of the gods. You stand before the gods and have conquered the war.

sanskrit: tadetatsarvamātiṣṭha vīrya bhīmaparākrama| nahi te sarvabhūteṣu dṛśyate sadṛśo balī||
reference: Therefore, o you of dreadful strength! summon your entire energy. Him find I not among all beings, who is your peer in prowess.
baseline: The same kind of sacrifice is found in all the gods.
morphology: The same kind of sacrifice should be offered to the god Bhima without having to bear the same amount of semen.

sanskrit: kuruṣva me priyahitametaduttama yathāpriyaṃ priyaraṇa bāndhavapriya| svatejasā vyathaya sapatnavāhinīṃ śaraddhanaṃ pavana ivodyato mahān||
reference: O lover of battle! O dear to friends, as you like, do this beloved good office, this prime benefit, to me. By your own energy, smite the hostile hosts, even as a mighty and strong wind (scattered away) autumnal clouds.
baseline: O king of the earth the best of all things are those things which are dear to me. The best of things to be dear to you are those which are bound by your own glory. The wind that blows the seven vessels of gold is great.
morphology: O Kurusva the best of all things are those things which are dear to me those which are beloved those that are dear those who are bound together and those which have their own glory the vessels of gold the wind and the wind.

sanskrit: maṇiṃ dattvā tataḥ sītā hanūmantamathābravīt| abhijñānamabhijñātametad rāmasya tattvataḥ||
reference: Having made over the gem, Sītā said to Hanumān, This sign is very well known to Rāma.
baseline: Then Sita should offer the garland to Lord Hanumanta. This is said to be the principle of Rama.
morphology: Then Sita gave the bead and worshipped Lord Hanumanta. This is said to be the principle of Rama.

sanskrit: maṇiṃ dṛṣṭvā tu rāmo vai trayāṇāṃ saṃsmariṣyati| vīro jananyā mama ca rājño daśarathasya ca||
reference: Seeing this gem, that hero, Rāma, shall recollect three persons, his mother, myself, and king Dasaratha, You, O foremost of monkeys, will again be commissioned on this business.
baseline: Having seen the bead Rama will remember the three men. The king and Dasaratha will be remembered as the sons of the brave.
morphology: Having seen the bead he will remember the three men like Rama the hero the mother the king and Dasharatha.

sanskrit: sa bhūyastvaṃ samutsāhacodito harisattama| asmin kāryasamutsāhe pracintaya yaduttaram||
reference: Do you bethink you as to what you will do afterwards, when you had been entrusted with this task.
baseline: It is better to say that he is good in the same way as in the case of a zealous person. If he does not do this thing with enthusiasm then he should think of the answer.
morphology: It is better for him to be happy with the spirit of the earth. He should think about this task with enthusiasm. If he is not happy with it.

sanskrit: tvamasminkāryaniryoge pramāṇaṃ harisattama| tasta cintaya yo yatno duḥkhakṣayakaro bhavet||
reference: O foremost of monkeys, you are capable of compassing this work. Therefore, think as to what course of his (Rāma's) shall remove (my) misery.
baseline: It is better for you to give evidence in this matter. Then consider that whosoever would suffer would be the worse.
morphology: It would be better for you to set up a work in this area. Then consider the one who has lost his misery.

sanskrit: hanūmanyatnamāsthāya duḥkhakṣayakaro bhava| sa tatheti pratijñāya mārutirbhīmavikramaḥ|| śirasā''vandya vaidehīṃ gamanāyopacakrame|
reference: "O Hanumān, undergoing toils, be you instrumental in removing my misery. Saying, ""So be it,” the Wind-god's offspring of terrible prowess, bowing down the head, prepared to depart."
baseline: O Hanumāna you are the destroyer of sorrows in the presence of other gods. He is the one who promises to be the master of Maruthi. He should offer the head of Viṣṇu and go to the Vedic temple in the cycle of the wheel.
morphology: O Hanumāna you are the destroyer of sorrows in the presence of other gods. He is the one who promises to be the master of Maruthi Virākrama the king of the gods. Having offered him the head he should go to the temple of the god.

sanskrit: jñātvā samprasthitaṃ devī vānaraṃ pavanātmajam|| bāṣpagadgadayā vācā maithilī vākyamabravīt|
reference: Seeing that (Hanumān) was about to set out, that exalted one, Mithila's daughter, addressed that monkey, son to the Wind-god, in words choked by the vapour of grief.
baseline: Knowing the nature of the goddess vanara and the spirit of the wind one should recite the word Maithili with the words vapāga gāgadga.
morphology: Having known that the goddess of the universe is a monkey one should worship the spirit of the wind with the vow of Maithili with the vapi gāgadga.

sanskrit: hanūmankuśalaṃ brūyāḥ sahitau rāmalakṣmaṇau|7|| sugrīvaṃ ca sahāmātyaṃ sarvānvṛddhāṃśca vānarān| brūyāstvaṃ vānaraśreṣṭha kuśalaṃ dharmasaṃhitam||
reference: O Hanumān, do you communicate good news to both Rāma and Lakşmaņa, to Sugrīva with his counsellors, and to all the aged monkeys. And, O best of monkeys, in consonance with righteousness, communicate good tidings (to Rāma).
baseline: One who has the ability to learn the art of a monkey one who has got the skill of a cow and one who is good at it and another who is rich at home and two monkeys is said to be the best skill of the monkey.
morphology: One who has the ability to learn hāṇumāṇa kusalā brūya rāma lakshmana sugriva sambhātī all the great monkeys and monkeys should be taught the best skill and the code of righteousness.

sanskrit: yathā ca sa mahābāhurle tārayati rāghavaḥ| asmādduḥkhāmbusaṃrodhāttvaṃ samādhātumarhasi||
reference: And it behove you to strive so that the mighty-armed Rāghava may rescues me from this sea of sorrow.
baseline: As he makes a star in the great temple the raghav should be restrained from us. He should be removed from us by the arrow.
morphology: As he makes a star in the great temple of the raghavas he will get rid of all those who obstruct him from the path of the snake.

sanskrit: jīvantī māṃ yathā rāmaḥ sambhāvayati kīrtimān| tattvayā hanumanvācyaṃ vācā dharmamavāpnuhi||
reference: O Hanumān, do you speak so that the illustrious Rāma may deliver me while I am still alive; and thereby do you reap righteousness.
baseline: One who invents the preceptor Śiva the living mother as mentioned by Śrīma will attain glory. One who submits to Śuṇu would get the promise of righteousness.
morphology: One who invents the preceptor Śiva the mother of life as well as that of Rama would bring glory. One should make a promise to Hanumana by the principle of righteousness.

sanskrit: nityamutsāhayuktasya vācaḥ śrutvā mayeritāḥ| vardhiṣyate dāśaratheḥ pauruṣaṃ madavāptaye||
reference: Ever breathing high spirits, Dasarathi, (Dasaratha's son) hearing my words, shall attain an access of manliness for my deliverance.
baseline: Having heard the words of one who is always cheerful one would be blessed with the boon of wine. One would get more wealth by the tenth day.
morphology: Having heard the words of one who is always cheerful one should be merry. One who is a noble man will increase his wealth by ten days.

sanskrit: matsaṃdeśayutā vācastvattaḥ śrutvaiva rāghavaḥ| parākrame matiṃ vīro vidhivatsaṃvidhāsyati||
reference: Soon as Rāghava shall hear words couching tidings of me, that hero shall duly resolve on displaying his prowess.
baseline: O Raghava one who has heard the message of the fish and has spoken it to you will be able to do the duty of a brave man in the future.
morphology: The king should be heard by the disciples of the fish. The king of the swords should be made to hear the sound of the voice of the serpent. He should not be afraid of the spirit of the enemy.

sanskrit: sītāyāstad vacaḥ śrutvā hanūmān mārutātmajaḥ| śirasyañjalimādhāya vākyamuttaramabravīt||
reference: Hearing this speech of Sītā, Hanumān, son to the Wind-good, with his joined hands raised to his head, said.
baseline: Having heard the words of Sita Lord Hāṇu killed the spirits. He prayed the words to the head and the head.
morphology: Having heard the words of Sita Lord Hāṇumā Lord of the souls of the sons of Śiva and Marutas should pray to him. He should pay tribute to the head.

sanskrit: kṣiprameṣyati kākutstho hapṛkṣapravarairvṛtaḥ| yaste yudhi vijityārīśokaṃ vyapanayiṣyati||
reference: Soon shall Käkutstha come, surrounded by the foremost monkeys and bears; and, vanquishing the foe in fight, shall remove your grief.
baseline: One who has conquered a war would be destroyed by the enemy.
morphology: One who has conquered a war would be destroyed by the enemy.

sanskrit: nahi paśyāmi matryeṣu nāsureṣu sureṣu vā| yastasya vamato bāṇān sthātumutsahate'grataḥ||
reference: Find I none either among men, or Asuras, or celestials, that dares remain before him as he discharges his shafts.
baseline: I do not see in the eyes or in the ears or in all the senses. If the arrows are placed in the mouth of the enemy they will be destroyed.
morphology: I do not see the arrows in the mātris or in the nostrils or the sūrās. The arrows are placed in the mouth of the god.

sanskrit: apyarkamapi parjanyamapi vaivasvataṃ yamam| sa hi soḍhuṃ raṇe śaktastava hetorviśeṣataḥ||
reference: For you, in especial, he can stand in conflict even the Sun, Indra, nay-Yama himself, that offspring of the Sun.
baseline: O Vaivasvattha one who has the power to destroy the enemy in the form of fire and rain is called Yama. One who is strong in the battle should be called Hātor.
morphology: O Vaivasvattha Yama one who has the power to destroy the enemy in the form of fire and rain should be worshipped in particular.

sanskrit: sa hi sāgaraparyantāṃ mahīṃ sādhitumarhati| tvanimitto hi rāmasya jayo janakanandini||
reference: For you, he prepare himself to conquer the Earth bounded by the main; and victory, you daughter of Janaka, shall be Rāma's.
baseline: He will attain me up to the sea. For you he will achieve the victory of Rama.
morphology: He will make me reach the sea. He will give you the victory of Rama and the joy of Janaka.

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā samyak satyaṃ subhāṣitam| jānakī bahu mene taṃ vacanaṃ cedamabravīt||
reference: Hearing his words excellently spoken and thoroughly true, Jānaki honoured them highly, and spoke (as follows).
baseline: Having heard his words it is true. O Janaki I have heard him say many things. Then he should pray to me.
morphology: Having heard of his words he said that it was true. Janaki listened to him very carefully. He said that he would be pleased.

sanskrit: tatastaṃ prasthitaṃ sītā vīkṣamāṇā punaḥpunaḥ| bhartṛsnehānvitaṃ vākyaṃ sauhārdādanumānayat||
reference: And gazing at him once and again as he prepared to go away, Sītā froin affection honoured the speech which had been uttered (by Hanuman) out of attachment to his master.
baseline: Then Sita stood there and watched him again. The words of the husband and his wife are said to be of good fortune.
morphology: Then Sita should be seen standing therein again. Then the words of the husband and his wife are said to be amicable.

sanskrit: yadi vā manyase vīra vasaikāhamariṃdama| kasmiṃścit saṃvṛte deśe viśrāntaḥ śvo gamiṣyasi||
reference: If you wish it, O hero, do you, O subduer of enemies, stay here for one day. Having rested in some hidden nook, you will depart tomorrow.
baseline: If you wish to be a brave man you should go to the country tomorrow after resting in the holy place.
morphology: If one believes that he is a mighty man he should go to the country after having made a vow. He would go home tomorrow.

sanskrit: mama caivālpabhāgyāyāḥ sāṃnidhyāt tava vānara | asya śokasya mahato muhūrta mokṣaṇaṃ bhavet||
reference: O monkey, (if you do remain), your vicinity shall for a moment remove the huge grief of me of slender luck.
baseline: Having recited the hymn mi chaivalpa bhavagyāda your monkey should be released from this great sorrow.
morphology: Having recited the hymn māhātmūhūrtha one should get rid of this great sorrow.

sanskrit: tato hi hariśārdūla punarāgamanāya tu| prāṇānāmapi saṃdeho mama syānnātra saṃśayaḥ||
reference: But even if you go (passing today here), I have, O tiger-like monkey, doubts as to your return; and, accordingly, doubt, certainly, as to my life.
baseline: O Hariśardula there is no doubt about my life.
morphology: Then you should return to Hariśardula. There is doubt about my life.

sanskrit: tavādarśanajaḥ śoko bhūyo māṃ paritāpayet| duḥkhādduḥkhaparāmṛṣṭāṃ dīpayanniva vānara ||
reference: And the grief incident to my not seeing you shall burn me greatly, even, O monkey, as grief burn one that is already consumed by sorrow over and over again.
baseline: One who has seen the rainbow should be sad. One who is a monkey should make me suffer from sorrow and empathic sorrow. He should give me light.
morphology: One who has seen the sun should feel sadness and sorrow in the earth. One who gives light to the illusion of sorrow and sorrow should be called a monkey.

sanskrit: ayaṃ ca vīra saṃdehastiṣṭhatīva mamāgrataḥ| sumahāṃstvatsahāyeṣu haryukṣeṣu harīśvaraḥ|| kathaṃ nu khalu duṣpāraṃ tariṣyati mahodadhim| tāni hapṛkṣasainyāni tau vā naravarātmajau||
reference: And, O hero, O lord of monkeys, this doubt is also before me. How, alas! shall the mighty lord of monkeys, albeit backed by the monkeys and bears, cross over the mighty main hard to cross, and (how shall) those forces consisting of bears and monkeys or those sons of the best of men (cross over the same)?
baseline: This is the brahmin the doubtful one. The lord Hari will bring you good things and evil things in the sky. The king of the earth will bring back evil things. These are the forces of the enemy. These two are the spirits of men.
morphology: This is the mighty doubt that has come to me. The lord Hari will bring good things to you and evil things in the kingdom of Hariuksha. May the lord Hari bring good and bad things. These are the forces of the enemy. These two are the spirits of man.

sanskrit: trayāṇāmeva bhūtānāṃ sāgarasyeha laṅghane| śaktiḥ syād vainateyasya tava vā mārutasya vā||
reference: In all the three worlds, Vinata's offspring, your self, and the Wind-god, have talone the power of crossing over the deep.
baseline: The three elements are the same in the case of the sea and the sea. The power is said to be yours or that of Marutas.
morphology: These three are the elements of the sea. The power of the ocean should be divided into three parts. The strength should be given to you or to Marut.

sanskrit: tadasminkāryaniryoge vīraivaṃ duratikrame| kiṃ paśyase samādhānaṃ tvaṃ hi kāryavidāṃ varaḥ||
reference: Then, for the accomplishment of this work, difficult to compass, what, O hero, O you best of those conversant with business, what way do you see as to its success?
baseline: In that case one should be brave enough to perform the task. See what is the peace. You are the master of the task and the boon.
morphology: In that case the hero should be removed from the distance. See if you find peace. You are the master of the work.

sanskrit: kāmamasya tvamevaikaḥ kāryasya parisādhane| paryāptaḥ paravīraghna yaśasyaste phalodayaḥ||
reference: Or you alone, O destroyer of hostile heroes, are quite enough for the fulfilment of this purpose; and you shall reap, in the shape of fame, the fruit of your achievement.
baseline: You are the only one who has the desire to do the work. One who is not brave enough to do it should follow the success.
morphology: You are the only one who has the desire to do the work. One who is not brave enough and who has achieved success should follow him.

sanskrit: balaiḥ samagrairyudhi māṃ rāvaṇaṃ jitya saṃyuge| vijayī svapuraṃ yāyāt tattasya sadṛśaṃ bhavet||
reference: But if (Rāma) himself together with all his forces, conquering Ravana and (recovering me) in battle, returned victorious to his own city, this would be worthy of himself.
baseline: Having conquered the battle of the whole kingdom of Śiva one should go to his own city and become like him.
morphology: Having conquered the king of the kingdom of Rāvana and having conquered the battle of Balā one should go to his own city and become like him.

sanskrit: balaistu saṃkulāṃ kṛtvā laṅkāṃ parabalārdanaḥ| māṃ nayed yadi kākutsthastat tasya sadṛśaṃ bhavet||
reference: If blocking up Lankā with his army, that afflictor of hostile hosts, Kākutstha took me (hence), that would be worthy of him.
baseline: Having collected the ball the ball should be made strong and the ball is made strong. If it does not hold me then it should be like that.
morphology: Having collected the ballast the lanka should be strengthened. If it does not hold me then it should be similar to that.

sanskrit: tadyathā tasya vikrāntamanurūpaṃ mahātmanaḥ| bhavedāhavaśūrasya tathā tvamupapādaya||
reference: Do you, therefore, adopt such means that the high-souled heroic warrior may have an opportunity of putting forth prowess.
baseline: As for him he should be a great man in the form of vikrātmana. He should be like the king of the fire. You should also be the master.
morphology: The figure of the great man should be like the figure of vikrātmana. You should also be like that of the king of the fire.

sanskrit: tadarthopahitaṃ vākyaṃ praśritaṃ hetusaṃhitam| niśamya hanumāśeṣaṃ vākyamuttaramabravīt||
reference: Hearing those words fraught with sense and reason and informed with affection, Hanumān, by way of reply said mildly.
baseline: Then the words that are not appropriate for the purpose of the prayer should be asked. Having said this one should pray to Lord Hanumantha after having said the following words.
morphology: Then the question should be asked about the reason for the statement. Having said this one should pray to Lord Hanumantha.

sanskrit: devi hayṛkṣasainyānāmīśvaraḥ plavatāṃ varaḥ| sugrīvaḥ satyasampannastavārthe kṛtaniścayaḥ||
reference: O revered lady, that foremost of monkeysthe lord of bears and monkeys-Sugrīva, possessed of truth, has made up his mind on your behalf.
baseline: The goddess should be the superior of the army the lord of the flood the boon the good and the rich in truth.
morphology: May the goddess of the higher order of the army and the lord of the flood be blessed. May the virtuous be blessed with the truth.

sanskrit: sa vānarasahasrāṇāṃ koṭībhirabhisaṃvṛtaḥ| kṣiprameṣyati vaidehi rākṣasānāṃ nibarhaṇaḥ||
reference: That destroyer of Rākşasas, O daughter of Vaidehi, environed by thousands of millions of monkeys, will come hither without delay.
baseline: He would destroy the monsters and other monsters. He would make a great effort to destroy the demons.
morphology: He is the one who has destroyed the monsters and other monsters. He will destroy the demons of the vaidī.

sanskrit: tasya vikramasampanna sattvavanto mahābalāḥ| manaḥ saṃkalpasampātā nideśe harayaḥ sthitāḥ|| yeṣāṃ nopari nādhastānna tiryak sajjate gatiḥ| na ca karmasu sīdanti mahatsvamitatejasaḥ||
reference: And exceedingly powerful and mighty monkeys possessed of prowess, and speeding far with the rapidity of thought, are in his command. Nothing can impede their courses, either upward, or downward, or tending in both directions, and those ones of measureless energy never experience depression in the most arduous undertakings.
baseline: One who has the power and the determination of the mind and the desire of the heart should be placed in the house of Hari. One who does not do the work of the knower should be prepared for the movement of the body. One not doing the work should be called a great master.
morphology: One who has the power and the determination of his mind and is standing on the ground should not be afraid of those who do not want to do it. One who does not do good deeds should be prepared to go ahead with the movement. He should not do evil deeds. He would not be able to do great good.

sanskrit: asakṛt tairmahotsāhai: sasāgaradharādharā | pradakṣiṇīkṛtā bhūmirvāyumārgānusāribhiḥ||
reference: Braced by their exalted spirits, these, resorting to the aerial way have many a time and oft circumambulated the Earth containing mountains and meads.
baseline: The waters of the sea the ocean the river the earth and the air should be circumambulated by a series of paths.
morphology: The waters of the sea the ocean and the ocean are made of unbleached water. The earth and air are made round and round.

sanskrit: madviśiṣṭāśca tulyāśca santi tatra vanaukasaḥ| mattaḥ pratyavaraḥ kaścinnāsti sugrīvasaṃnidhau||
reference: There are (in that army) rangers of woods, some equal and some superior to me. And near Sugrīva there are none who are inferior to me.
baseline: There are two kinds of wine and the same kind of wine in the forest. Every man who is drunk is a man in the midst of the peace.
morphology: There is a forest in the forest and the equals of the rivers. Every man who is drunk should be mercilessly restrained.

sanskrit: ahaṃ tāvadiha prāptaḥ kiṃ punaste mahābalāḥ| nahi prakṛṣṭāḥ preṣyante preṣyante hītare janāḥ||
reference: And since even I have reached this place, what shall I say of those ones endowed with immense might? Nor are superior (monkeys) sent on errands; it is only the inferior ones that are sent.
baseline: What if I get it again and the mighty ones are sent back. If not sent back people will be sent back to them.
morphology: What if I get the same thing again and the great ones are not sent. People will be sent to him.

sanskrit: tadalaṃ paritāpena devi śoko vyapaitu te| ekotpātena te laṅkāmeṣyanti hariyūthapāḥ|| mama pṛṣṭhagatau tau ca candrasūryāvivoditau| tvatsakāśaṃ mahāsaṅghau nṛsiṃhāvāgamiṣyataḥ||
reference: Then, O exalted one. you need not grieve: let your sorrow depart. Those leaders of monkey herds will come to Lankā by one bound; and, like to the risen Sun and Moon, those leonine men, having large numbers to back them, will come to your side, riding my back.
baseline: Then the goddess should suffer with the sorrows of suffering. With the one product they would become lankas. Then the green leaves would become my back and the sun would rise. You would become the sky and the king would become a lion.
morphology: Then the goddess should suffer with the sorrows of that land. With the one product they would be called lanka. Then the green leaves would be followed by the moon and sun. You would be the sky and the king the lion and the lion.

sanskrit: tau hi vīrau naravarau sahitau rāmalakṣmaṇau| āgamya nagarī laṅkāṃ sāyakairvidhamiṣyataḥ||
reference: Those heroes and foremost of men, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa both, coming to the city of Lankā, shall destroy her by means of their shafts.
baseline: These are the heroes men men and men. Having come to the city of Lanka together with Rama Lakshmana and others.
morphology: These two are the heroes men men and men. Then they should come and take the city of Lanka in a different way.

sanskrit: sagaṇaṃ rāvaṇaṃ hatvā rāghavo raghunandanaḥ| tvāmādāya varārohe svapurīṃ prati yāsyati||
reference: And slaying Rāvaņa together with his adherents, Raghu's son, taking you, O paragon among women, shall return to his own city.
baseline: Having killed Ravana Raghuṇanda the king of the ragas would go to his wife in the form of a bridegroom.
morphology: Having killed the son of Ravana Raghunandana the king of Raghavas will go to his wife in the form of a bridegroom.

sanskrit: tadāśvasihi bhadraṃ te bhava tvaṃ kālakākṣiṇī| nacirād drakṣyase rāmaṃ prajvalantamivānalam||
reference: Therefore, do you take heart, good betide you! Do you remain, eagerly wishing for the time. It will not be long before you shall behold Rāma resembling flaming fire.
baseline: Then you should worship the god Brahma. You are the goddess of time. You should see Rama from the side of the nose. He should be worshipped in the form of fire.
morphology: Then you should worship God. You are the goddess of time. You should see Lord Rama from the seat of fire.

sanskrit: nihate rākṣasendre ca saputrāmātyabāndhave| tvaṃ sameṣyasi rāmeṇa śaśāṅkeneva rohiṇī||
reference: On the lord of Rākṣasas being slain along with his counsellors and friends, you shall meet with Rāma, even as Rohinī meet with the Moon.
baseline: O Brahman you will be destroyed in the center of the demons and you will get peace. You will be absorbed by Rama in the centre of the earth.
morphology: The king should be killed in the center of the demon and the king of the enemy should be destroyed in the middle of the battle. You will be destroyed by Rama. You should be defeated in the battle of Rohini.

sanskrit: kṣipraṃ tvaṃ devi śokasya pāraṃ drakṣyasi maithili| rāvaṇaṃ caiva rāmeṇa drakṣyase nihataṃ balāt||
reference: O worshipful one, speedily shall you behold the other shore of your misery, O Maithili; and you shall see Rāvana slain by Rāma by might of arm.
baseline: The goddess Tūpā is the one who sees the other side of the sorrow. The goddess Maithili is the king of Ravana. The king who sees him is killed by force.
morphology: The goddess is quick to see beyond the sorrows. O Maithili one who sees Rāvana and Rama with the force of force should be killed.

sanskrit: evamāśvāsya vaidehīṃ hanūmān mārutātmajaḥ| gamanāya matiṃ kṛtvā vaidehī punarabravīt||
reference: Having thus solaced Vaidehi's daughter, Hanumān, son to the Wind-god again spoke to Vaidehi, saying.
baseline: Having believed in the same Lord Hanumāṇu should be killed by the spirit. Having made a vow to go away Lord Vaidehi should pray again.
morphology: Having thus exhaled Hanumāṇu the spirit of Marutāja after having made a vow to go away the god Vaidehi again prayed to him.

sanskrit: tamarighnaṃ kṛtātmānaṃ kṣipraṃ drakṣyasi rāghavam| lakṣmaṇaṃ ca dhanuṣpāṇiṃ laṅkādvāramupāgatam||
reference: Soon shall you behold that destroyer of foes, Rāghava of subdued soul, and the bow-bearing Laksmana also, come to the gate of Lanka.
baseline: Having made a mistake with the sword one would see a raghava with a sharp heart. One would get a bow and a bow from the gate of Lanka.
morphology: Having made a mistake with the sword one would see a raghava with a sharp heart. One would get a bow a bow and a bow from the gate of Lanka.

sanskrit: nakhadaṃṣṭrāyudhān vīrān siṃhaśārdūlavikramān| vānarān vāraṇendrābhān kṣipraṃ drakṣyasi saṃgatān||
reference: And soon shall you behold the assembled heroic monkeys, endowed with the prowess of lions and tigers, and the splendour of the monarch of monkeys, and having nails and teeth for their arms.
baseline: Having seen the knives arms weapons valour lions horses monkeys deer elves eloquent monkeys etc. one would be able to find their companions.
morphology: Having seen the knives arms weapons valiant men lions horses monkeys elves eloquent monkeys etc. the king of the earth and the mighty king of war should be sent to his company.

sanskrit: śailāmbudanikāśānāṃ laṅkāmalayasānuṣu| nardatāṃ kapimukhyānāmārye yūthānyanekaśaḥ||
reference: And you shall, O noble one, behold innumerable companies of choice monkeys, resembling hills and clouds, roaring on the plateaus of Malaya in Lankā.
baseline: One should offer a lot of things to the people in the form of sand mud and sand. One should not make a lotus flower on the ground of the mountain.
morphology: One should not be afraid of many things in the form of stones stones rocks mountains etc.

sanskrit: sa tu marmaṇi ghoreṇa tāḍito manmatheṣuṇā| na śarma labhate rāmaḥ siṃhārdita iva dvipaḥ||
reference: Like an elephant tormented by a lion, Rāma afflicted in the vitals by the dreadful shafts of Manmatha, dose not attain ease.
baseline: He should be beaten with the sword of Marmāṇī. He should not be ashamed of the fact that he is a lion.
morphology: He should be beaten with the sword of Marmāṇī. He should not be ashamed of the fact that Rama is a lion.

sanskrit: ruda mā devi śokena mā bhūtte manasobhayam| śacīva bha; śakreṇa saṅgameṣyasi śobhane||
reference: Do not weep, exalted one, in sorrow. Let not fear take possession of your heart! Even as Sacī meet with Sakra, shall you, O auspicious one, meet with your lord.
baseline: The goddess Rudma should not be grieved by the ghosts. One should be pleased with the spirit. One would be merry with the shakr and one would get merry.
morphology: The goddess Rudma should not be grieved by the ghost. The spirit should be pleased with the spirit. One should be merry with the grace. One would get merry by the grace of the goddess.

sanskrit: rāmād viśiṣṭaḥ ko'nyo'sti kaścit saumitriṇā samaḥ| agnimārutakalpau tau bhrātarau tava saṃśrayau|53 ||
reference: Who is greater than Rāma? And who is equal to Saumitri? (i.e. Sumitra's son, Laksmana) And these brothers resembling Fire and the Wind, are your help.
baseline: One who is more than that of Rama is equal to that of Sāumitrīna. The two brothers are your protector.
morphology: One who is more than that of Rama is equal to that of Sūmitrī. The two brothers are your protector.

sanskrit: nāsmiṃściraṃ vatsyasi devi deśe rakṣogaṇairadhyuṣite'tiraudre| na te cirādāgamanaṃ priyasya kṣamasva matsaṃgamakālamātram||
reference: O revered one, you will not have to dwell long in this extremely dreadful place inhabited by the Rākşasas. The arrival of your beloved one is not distant. Just remain expecting (as best you may), during the time that elapses between this and my meeting with Rāma.
baseline: The goddess Naśmī and Vātsya should be protected in the country. They should not come to the king. The king should be forgiven only for the time of joining the fish.
morphology: The goddess of the night should be worshipped in the country and protect the people from the evil spirits. They should not come to the king of the sea and forgive the beloved for the association of the fish.

sanskrit: bharadvājāśramaṃ gatvā krośādeva nararṣabhaḥ| janaṃ sarvamavasthāpya jagāma saha mantribhiḥ|| padbhyāmeva tu dharmajño nyastaśastraparicchadaḥ| vasāno vāsasī kṣaume purodhāya purohitam||
reference: Having arrived at (the neighbourhood of) Bharadvāja's asylum, that foremost of men while it was a krosa (to the destination), left his forces behind and went thither, accompanied by his counsellors alone. And leaving his attire and arms, and clad in a silk cloth, that pious one placing the priest in front, went on foot.
baseline: Having gone to the abode of Bharādvaja one should worship the king of Narāśabha with the sword. Having placed all the people together with the jāga the ministers should worship him and give him the righteous man. He should be made to wear the armour. The priest should be worshipped in the absence of the king.
morphology: Having gone to the abode of Bharadwaja one should worship the god Narasabha in the form of a cow. Having placed all the people together with the jagāma the ministers should be made to worship the gods. The priest should be given the mantle of arms. The lord should be the seat of the priest in the place of the enemy.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃdarśane tasya bharadvājasya rāghavaḥ| mantriṇastānavasthāpya jagāmānupurohitam||
reference: Then with the view of seeing Bharadvāja, that descendent of Raghu leaving behind the counsellors also, went in the wake of the priest.
baseline: Then after having visited him the king of Bharadvāja should be worshipped by the chief priest. Having made his presence known to the people he should worship the gods.
morphology: Then the king of Bharadwaja should be visited by the chief priest. Having made his presence known to the people he should be worshipped.

sanskrit: vasiṣṭhamatha dṛṣṭvaiva bharadvājo mahātapāḥ| saṃcacālāsanāt tūrṇaṃ śiṣyānarghyamiti bruvan||
reference: "As soon as Bharadvāja of rigid austerities saw Vasiştha, he at once rose from his seat, saying to him disciples ""Arghya!"""
baseline: Having seen Vāṣṣṭimatha Bharādvaja the great god of fire should be worshipped. The disciples should be made to draw a trumpet from the chakalasana.
morphology: Having seen Vāsisthimatha Bharādvaja the great god of fire should be worshipped. The disciples should be guided by the chariot.

sanskrit: samāgamya vasiṣṭhena bharatenābhivāditaḥ| abudhyata mahātejāḥ sutaṃ daśarathasya tam||
reference: On being called upon by Vasiştha, that highly energetic one understood that it was Daſaratha's son.
baseline: Having assembled with Vāsisthā one should greet Bharata with the garland. Having said this the great gods should worship him as the son of Dasharatha.
morphology: Having assembled with Vāsisthā one should greet Bharata with the garland of the great goddess Dārāṣṭra.

sanskrit: tābhyāmarthya ca pādyaṃ ca dattvā paścāt phalāni ca| ānupūrvyācca dharmajñaḥ papraccha kuśalaṃ kule|| ayodhyāyāṃ bale kośe mitreṣvapi ca mantriṣu| jānan daśarathaṃ vṛttaṃ na rājānamudāharat||
reference: Having offered them (the guests) water to wash their feet and Arghya, as well as fruits subsequently, that virtuous one (Bharadvāja) successively enquired after the welfare of their (respective) homes; and after that, of the forces, exchequer, friends and counsellors in Ayodhyā. And knowing that Dasaratha had departed this life, he did not ask anything relating to the monarch.
baseline: Having said that one should give the feet and then the fruits. One who has knowledge of the scriptures should ask the wise man in the past and the wise one in the temple one who has the strength and the friends in Ayodhya and the ministers should also ask him. He should not give the king a circle of ten cubits.
morphology: Having said that one should give the feet and fruits. One who has knowledge of the preceptor should ask the wise man in the temple and his friends in the palace and the king in Ayodhya. He should not give the tenfold circle to the king.

sanskrit: vasiṣṭho bharataścainaṃ papracchaturanāmayam| śarīre'gniṣu śiṣyeṣu vṛkṣeṣu mṛgapakṣiṣu||
reference: Then Vasiştha and Bharata questioned him as to his welfare, in relation to the body, the (sacrificial) fire, the trees, the beasts and the birds (of the hermitage).
baseline: One should worship Vāṣṭīṣṭha Bharata and others in the form of the mantras. One should also worship the disciples in the body trees and birds of prey.
morphology: One should worship Vāṣṭīṣtha Bharata and others. One should also worship the disciples in the body trees and birds of prey.

sanskrit: tatheti tu pratijñāya bharadvājo mahāyaśāḥ| bharataṃ pratyuvācedaṃ rāghavasnehabandhanāt||
reference: "To all this returning ""So it is,” the illustrious Bharadvāja from affection for Rāghava said to Bharata."
baseline: Then Bharādvāja should be made the supreme ruler with the promise. Bharātha should be worshipped with the bond of love and affection from Raghava.
morphology: Then Bharādvājū is said to be the supreme god. Bharātha should be worshipped with the vow of love and affection.

sanskrit: kimihāgamane kāryaṃ tava rājyaṃ praśāsataḥ| etadācakṣva sarvaṃ me na hi me śudhyate manaḥ||
reference: What is the use of your visit here, seeing that you are engaged in the task of governing the kingdom? Do you relate all this to me; my mind is ill at ease.
baseline: The work done in the coming of Kīmihāmā is the administration of your kingdom. Having seen this I do not think that I will get everything clean.
morphology: The work done in the coming of Kīmihām is the administration of your kingdom. Having said this I do not think that everything will be cleansed.

sanskrit: suṣuve yamamitraghnaṃ kausalyā''nandavardhanam| bhrātrā saha sabhāryo yaściraṃ pravājito vanam|| niyuktaḥ strīnimittena pitrā yo'sau mahāyaśāḥ| vanavāsī bhavetīha samāḥ kila caturdaśa|| kaccinna tasyāpāpasya pāpaṃ kartumihecchasi| akaṇṭakaṃ bhoktumanā rājyaṃ tasyānujasya ca||
reference: That slayer of foes and perpetuator of his race who has been born by Kausalyā, and who along with his wife and brother has been banished to the woods for a long term, that illustrious one who enjoined by his sire in the interests of a woman, has become an inhabitant of the woods for fourteen years, do you, desirous of securely enjoying the kingdon belonging to him as well to his younger brother, intend to do any harm to that sinless one?
baseline: One who has gone into the forest with his brother and his attendants should be appointed as the chief minister for the sake of his wife. One who is a resident of the forest should be made to live in the forest for fourteen days. He who consumes the land of the king and his son should be punished for committing the sin of committing the crime. One should eat food and eat food.
morphology: One who has been appointed as the chief minister of a forest for the sake of a woman who has crossed the river with his brother who has gone into the forest with him who is a member of the council and who is not a friend of the king who wants to make him a sinner of the sin of a man living in a forest. One who lives in the forest should be the king of a country that consumes a lot of food.

sanskrit: evamukto bharadvājaṃ bharataḥ pratyuvāca ha| paryaśrunayano duḥkhād vācā saṃsajjamānayā||
reference: Thus accosted, Bharata replied to Bharadvāja with tears filling his eyes and his words choked with grief.
baseline: O Bharādvāja one who is free from this and who has returned from the kingdom of Bharāṭa one should return to the earth with the promise of peace. One who has heard the sound of the wind should return with sorrow.
morphology: O Bharādvāja one who is liberated from this and who is worshipped by Bharātā one should return to the earth after having heard the word of peace from the sorrowful.

sanskrit: hato'smi yadi māmevaṃ bhagavānapi manyate| matto na doṣamāśaṅke maivaṃ māmanuśādhi hi||
reference: Undone am I if the reverend one also deems me so. Do not apprehend any wrong from me; and do you not reproach me thus.
baseline: If one considers me to be a god one should not get drunk. One should not think of me as a man.
morphology: If I am the enemy even if I am considered to be a god then I should not be drunken. If I do not feel guilty I should be called a man.

sanskrit: na caitadiṣṭaṃ mātā me yadavocanmadantare| nāhametena tuṣṭaśca na tadvacanamādade||
reference: Whatever my mother has said in relation to me, does not express my wish, I am not satisfied with that, nor do I endorse her speech.
baseline: If the mother is not mentioned in the scriptures she should say that she is not pleased with me. Then she should not say the same thing.
morphology: If I say that the mother is not pleased with me then I am not happy with it.

sanskrit: ahaṃ tu taṃ naravyāghramupayātaḥ prasādakaḥ| pratinetumayodhyāyāṃ pādau cāsyābhivanditum||
reference: I, intending to pacify him, and going to that chief of men, with the view of taking him to Ayodhyā and of paying homage to his feet.
baseline: I am the one who gives pleasure to those men who have lost their houses. One should take them to the warrior and make them rejoice with their feet and hands.
morphology: I am the one who gives pleasure to him by losing the neck of the man. One should worship him with the feet and feet in the fight against the enemy.

sanskrit: taṃ māmevaṃgataṃ matvā prasādaṃ kartumarhasi| śaṃsa me bhagavan rāmaḥ kva samprati mahīpatiḥ||
reference: Thinking me as already gone, you should show your favour to me. O reverend Sir, tell me where stay at present Rāma, lord of the earth.
baseline: Having worshipped him with the mantras of Ma ̄ ma one should offer him the prasa ̄ dam. Lord Rama should be worshipped as the supreme lord.
morphology: Having worshipped him with the mantras of the lord Śamśa Lord Rama one should offer him prasadam.

sanskrit: vasiṣṭhādibhitvigbhiryācito bhagavāṃstataḥ| uvāca taṃ bharadvājaḥ prasādād bharataṃ vacaḥ||
reference: Besought by Vasiştha and the other Rtvijas, the venerable Bharadvāja well pleased, spoke to Bharata.
baseline: The lord should be worshipped with the words vāśṣṭīṣḍī bhīvīrīṣṭhī bīrāṭhā bārādvājā. He should be blessed with the word bharāṭa.
morphology: He should be worshipped by the lord Vāṣṣṭhīdī Bhīvīrīya and thus the god Bharādvāja should be blessed with the prāśa.

sanskrit: tvayyetat puruṣavyāghra yuktaṃ rāghavavaṃśaje| guruvṛttirdamaścaiva sādhūnāṃ cānuyāyitā||
reference: foremost of men, even this is worthy of you. Serving superiors, restraint of the senses, and following the pious, are ever found in one sprung in the Rāghava line.
baseline: One who has been given the gift of a man a tiger and a member of the clan of Raghava should be given the title of the master. One who is living on the path of viṣṇu should be made the son of a saint.
morphology: One who has been given the gift of a man a tiger and a member of the clan of Raghava should do the same. One who lives in the preceptor's house should be given the honour of the saints.

sanskrit: jāne caitanmanaḥsthaṃ te dṛḍhīkaraṇamastviti| apṛcchaṃ tvāṃ tavātyarthaṃ kīrtiṃ samabhivardhayan||
reference: I know that even this is your intention, but for the purpose of making your mind all the firmer, I had asked you in this wise; so that your fame might greatly increase.
baseline: Having said this one should be able to confirm that he is aware of the manifestations of Caitmana. He should be made to know the manifestation of the same.
morphology: Having said this you should be sure of the fact that you are aware of the manifestations of Caitanya. You should be able to express yourself evenly by raising the glory for the sake of the same.

sanskrit: jāne ca rāmaṃ dharmajñaṃ sasītaṃ sahalakṣmaṇam| ayaṃ vasati te bhrātā citrakūṭe mahāgirau||
reference: I also know the righteous Rāma with Sītā and Lakşmaņa. This brother of yours at present stays at the mighty mountain Citrakuta.
baseline: One who knows Rama one who knows the righteousness one known as Sātimā one with Lakshmana one living in the same place as his brother one of the great gods in the image.
morphology: One who knows Rama one who knows the righteousness one known as Sātimā and one who is a co-lakshman would find this place in the house of his brother in the temple of Chitrakuta.

sanskrit: śvastu gantāsi taṃ deśaṃ vasādya saha mantribhiḥ| etaṃ me kuru suprājña kāmaṃ kāmārthakovida||
reference: On the morrow you will set out for that region. Do you to-day sojourn here along with your counsellors. O wise one, do this at your pleasure, O you understanding interest and desire.
baseline: Having settled the land tomorrow with the ministers I shall do this with good advice. I will do this for the welfare of the people.
morphology: Having settled the land on the same day he should be accompanied by his ministers. I shall do this with good commandment.

sanskrit: tatastathetyevamudāradarśanaḥ pratītarūpo bharato'bravīd vacaḥ| cakāra buddhiṃ ca tadāśrame tadā niśānivāsāya narādhipātmajaḥ||
reference: "Thereat the gently-looking and highly famous one said, “Be it so;"" and the king's son made up his mind to spend the night in the great hermitage (of the saint)."
baseline: Then the image should be seen in the same manner as the image. Then it should be said that the mind should be made aware of it. Then the figure should be placed in the seat of the male ruler.
morphology: Then the image of a man should be shown to him in the same manner as that of another man. He should be told to do so in the morning and then the wisdom should be revealed to him. Then the king should make a mark on him.

sanskrit: tataste rākṣasendreṇa coditā mantriṇaḥ sutāḥ| niryayurbhavanāt tasmāt sapta saptārcivarcasaḥ||
reference: Then ordered by the lord of Rākşasas, the sons of his counsellors, seven (in number) in splendour reseinbling fire, issued forth that mansion.
baseline: Then the ministers should be pierced by the rakshasasandra. The seven arches should be made from it after the war has begun.
morphology: Then the ministers who were cast into the sea by the demon Sendra should be made to sleep seven or four times with it.

sanskrit: mahadbalaparīvārā dhanuṣmanto mahābalāḥ| kṛtāstrāstravidāṃ śreṣṭhāḥ parasparajayaiṣiṇaḥ|| hemajālaparikṣiptairdhvajavadbhiḥ patākibhiḥ| toyadasvananirghoṣairvājiyuktairmahārathaiḥ|| taptakāñcanacitrāṇi cāpānyamitavikramāḥ| visphārayantaḥ saṃhṛṣṭāstaḍidvanta ivāmbudāḥ|| jananyastāstatasteṣāṃ viditvā kiṃkarān hatān| babhūvuḥ śokasambhrāntāḥ sabāndhavasuhṛjjanāḥ||
reference: And surrounded by a mighty army, furnished with bows, endowed with wondrous strength, and accomplished in arms— the foremost of those acquainted with weapons-each burning for victory, with mighty cars yoked with steeds, covered with golden net-works, bearing pennons and standards, and having sounds like those proceeding from clouds, exultingly stretching with immeasurable prowess bows decked with gold, resembling clouds surcharged with lightning, those warriors sallied out. Learning that the servants had been slain, their (i.e. the mothers of the sons of the councillors) mothers, along with their friends and kindred, were overpowered with grief.
baseline: One who has made a great weapon with a strong armour and a bow and a mighty warrior one who has mastered the weapon and has conquered each other by throwing a net of fire a flag a sword a spear a mace a string of water a carrot a horse a cow a deer a tiger a bearer of a sword and a cow should be thrown into the sea. One who knows that they have been killed by the mighty king would be killed by those who have spread the fire and spread it.
morphology: One who has made a great force a great man with a bow a mighty man with an excellent weapon one who has won over another with a string of horns a flag with a long neck and a straight neck a man who has not been able to fight a war a woman who has been killed by a man with the sword a horse a cow a deer a tiger a lion a monkey a bear a bull a king a warrior a knight a sage a merry man a person who knows that they have been killed.

sanskrit: te parasparasaṃgharṣāstaptakāñcanabhūṣaṇāḥ| abhipeturhanūmantaṃ toraṇasthamavasthitam||
reference: And vieing with each other in eagerness, those (warriors) decked in ornaments of polished gold, confronted Hanumān staying at the gate.
baseline: They are in conflict with each other and are adorned with a piece of cloth. The arch is placed at the base of the arch.
morphology: They are in conflict with each other. They are adorned with a piece of cloth. They should be placed on the arches of the king.

sanskrit: sṛjanto bāṇavṛṣṭiṃ te rathagarjitani:svanāḥ| prāvṛṭkāla ivāmbhodā vicerunairṛtāmbudāḥ||
reference: And with their cars sending roars, the Rākşasas, pouring showers of shafts, ranged (the field), resembling clouds during the rainy season.
baseline: They create arrows and rain water. They make the chariot sounding. They give the sound of water to the earth. They spread the sound like the wind.
morphology: They create arrows and rain water. They make the chariots sound. They give the sound of the sun. They spread the sound like the sun and the sound from the sky.

sanskrit: avakīrṇastatastābhirhanūmāñśaravṛṣṭibhiḥ| abhavatsaṃvṛtākāraḥ śailarāḍiva vṛṣṭibhiḥ||
reference: Covered with those arrowy showers, Hanuman had his person concealed, like the monarch of mountains hidden by a downpour.
baseline: It is made of water and water. It is formed by the rain of the sun. It becomes white with the rain from the rocks and rocks.
morphology: It is said to have been destroyed by the rain of the sun. It has become a circle of rocks and rain.

sanskrit: sa śarānvañcayāmāsa teṣāmāśucaraḥ kapiḥ| rathavegāṃśca vīrāṇāṃ vicaranvimale'mbare||
reference: That swift-speeding monkey, coursing the cloudless sky, evaded those shafts of those heroes, as well as the impetuosity of their cars.
baseline: He should worship the goddess Śāraṇva. He should be worshipped by the goddess Kaupi. The charioteer should be guided by the mighty men.
morphology: He should worship the goddess Sarāṇva. He should treat the chariots and the mighty men with grace.

sanskrit: sa taiḥ krīḍandhanuṣmadbhiomni vīraḥ prakāśate| dhanuṣmadbhiryathā medhairmārutaḥ prabhurambare||
reference: That hero, playing pranks with those bowmen, appeared like the masterful Wind playing tricks with the bow-bearing clouds. (i.e. having the iris.)
baseline: He is known to be a man of great strength. He is said to be the bravest among men. He should be known as the brahmin the wise the brave and the mighty.
morphology: He is known to be a man of great strength. He is said to be brave and brave. He should bear the bow the sword and the meritorious mārta in the form of the lord.

sanskrit: sa kṛtvā ninadaṃ ghoraṃ trāsayaṃstāṃ mahācamūm| cakāra hanūmānvegaṃ teṣu rakṣaḥsu vīryavān||
reference: Sending up a dreadful shout, and thereby filling that vast host with fright, the energetic Hanumān rushed on that Rākşasa army.
baseline: Having done that one should make a vow and make a great effort. Having done this one one would get rid of the evil spirits of those men.
morphology: Having done that one should make a vow of great distress and great misery. Having done so, one should say that Lord hanumana should protect them and give them semen.

sanskrit: talenābhihanat kāṃścitpādaiḥ kāṃścitparaṃtapaḥ| muṣṭibhiścāhanatkāṃścinnakhaiḥ kāṃścid vyadārayat|| pramamāthorasā kāṃścidūrubhyāmaparānapi| kecittasyaiva nādena tatraiva patitā bhuvi||
reference: That subduer of enemies slew some with slaps, and some he rived with nails, and some he killed by blows, and others with (the pressure of) his chest. And some dropped down on the ground at the very same spot at the sounds that he emitted.
baseline: One who has made a fall on the ground with a piece of cloth and a piece or two of cloth should be made to sit on the floor with his fists and two fingers and another with his hands and arms. One who makes a fall from the ground should be called a ketcha.
morphology: He should be made to sit on the floor with his hands and feet on the ground on the left side of the hill on the right side. He should also be made able to stand with his fists on both the sides of his eyes on the other side.

sanskrit: tatasteṣvavapanneṣu bhūmau nipatiteṣu ca| tatsainyamagamatsarvaṃ diśo daśa bhayāditam||
reference: And on their being slain or falling on the earth, that army, afflicted with affright, began to fly in all directions.
baseline: Then the land should be divided into ten parts. The same is said to be ten parts of the earth.
morphology: Then the land should be divided into ten parts. The same is said to be ten parts of the earth.

sanskrit: vinedurvisvaraṃ nāgā nipeturbhuvi vājinaḥ| bhagnanīḍadhvajacchatrairbhūśca kīrṇābhavad rathaiḥ ||
reference: The elephants roared in frightful tones, and the steeds fell down on the earth. And the Earth was covered with broken boxes, flag-staffs, and umbrellas, (belonging to the cars), as also with the cars themselves.
baseline: The vinaṇe is the sound of the wind and the vājīna is the voice of the nāga and the nipeturbhui. The vāja is broken and the dhvagājha is covered by the chariots and the kīrna is made of water.
morphology: The sound of the wind the sound of water the voice of the king the wind of the earth the waves of the sea the flag the chariots the kirana the earth and the earth are broken.

sanskrit: stravatā rudhireṇātha sravantyo darśitāḥ pathi| vividhaiśca svanairlaṅkā nanāda vikṛtaṃ tadā||
reference: And rivers running gore were seen on the way, and Lankā uttered various frightful cries.
baseline: The path shown by the lines of the rivers is different. Then the lines should be drawn in different directions. Then they should be broken.
morphology: The path shown by the lines of the rivers flowing in the direction of the river is different. Then the lines should be drawn with the same colour.

sanskrit: sa tānpravṛddhān vinihatya rākṣasān mahābalaścaṇḍaparākramaḥ kapiḥ| stadeva vīro'bhijagāma toraṇam||
reference: Having slain those overgrown Rākşasas, that exceedingly powerful and heroic monkey of terrific power, desirous of again coping with other Rākşasas, retraced his steps to the selfsame entrance.
baseline: He who destroys the great men and the demons and the mighty men and makes a series of attacks is a coward. He should be worshipped as a warrior and as a king.
morphology: He who destroys the mighty men and the demons the mighty ones and those who do evil deeds should be punished with a sword.

sanskrit: tathāgatāṃ tāṃ vyathitāmaninditāṃ vyatītaharṣāṃ paridīnamānasām| śubhāṃ nimittāni śubhāni bhejire naraṃ śriyā juṣṭamivopasevinaḥ||
reference: Like to servants waiting upon a wealthy person various auspicious omens waited upon Sītā of a blameless and comely person, racked with grief and divested of joy.
baseline: Then one should come and enjoy the merriment of the distressed man the pleasure of spending time in the heart the happiness of the mind the good things for the sake of the good man that of the poor man and that of a cow.
morphology: Then one should come and enjoy the merriment of a man suffering from affliction the loss of his heart the pleasure of the mind the good things for the sake of good the evil man should be worshipped in the house of a sage the king of a cow the lord of the cow and the king.

sanskrit: rājyāvṛtaṃ kṛṣṇaviśālaśuklam| prāspandataikaṃ nayanaṃ sukeśyā mīnāhataṃ padmamivābhitāmram||
reference: And the large left eye of that dame having graceful hairs, having dark pupils, white ends and thick eye-lashes, began to dance like a lotus shaken by a fish.
baseline: The king should have a broad white hair with black hair. One should look at the eyes with a broad nose. The eye should be beautiful with a lotus lotus and white hair.
morphology: The king should have a large body of black hair. One should see a serpent with a broad nose and one should be blessed with a lotus lotus etc..

sanskrit: bhujaśca cārvañcitavṛttapīnaḥ parāyaṃkālāgurucandanāhaḥ| anuttamenādhyuṣitaḥ priyeṇa cireṇa vāmaḥ samavepatāśu||
reference: And her beautiful, round, plump left hand, which, ere this, sprinkled with costly aguru and sandal, used to serve for a pillow to Rāma, began to dance now again and again after a long time.
baseline: The left arm should be divided into four parts. The left shoulder should be made of the same length as the left arm. The right arm should not be made to be drawn.
morphology: One who has four arms four circles one who has not been able to walk on the ground and one who is not afraid of the enemy should go to the temple. One who does not want to be afraid of him should leave the left side of the temple with a piece of cloth.

sanskrit: stayordvayoḥ saṃhatayostu jātaḥ| praspandamānaḥ punarūrurasyā rāmaṃ purastāt sthitamācacakṣe||
reference: And her well built plump left thigh, resembling the trunk of an elephant, dancing, announced that she would soon behold Rāma.
baseline: The two hymns are said to be the same. The sound of the trumpet sounding again should be heard from the forehead and the eye of Rama.
morphology: The two hymns are said to be the same. The rāma should be placed in front of the forehead and the eyes of the king again on the trumpet.

sanskrit: mīṣadrajodhvastamivātulākṣyāḥ| vāsaḥ sthitāyāḥ śikharāgradantyāḥkiṃcit paristraṃsatacārugātryāḥ||
reference: And the gold-hued cloth, now covered with dust, of that damsel of a comely person, having teeth like pomegranate seeds, slipped a little off its place.
baseline: One who is in the position of the seat the seat and the seat of the head should be placed on the ground and the other on the hill should be kept on the four sides.
morphology: One who is in the position of the seat the seat of the head and the head of the body should be placed on the ground. One who has a seat on the hill should sit on a hill and walk on the mountain.

sanskrit: etairnimittairaparaiśca subhrūḥ saṃcoditā prāgapi sādhusiddhaiḥ| vātātapaklāntamiva praṇaṣṭaṃ varṣeṇa bījaṃ pratisaṃjaharṣa||
reference: And being enlivened by those and various other auspicious omens, she attained joy like to a seed, spoiled by the wind and the sun, growing afresh in the rainy season.
baseline: O Subrahmanya one who has been blessed by the sages for this and other reasons should offer the seeds in the same manner as the wind wind and wind. One should give the seeds five times a year.
morphology: O Subhru one who has made a sacrifice for the sake of this and other things should be worshipped by the sages. One should offer the seed in the form of wind and water as if it were a desert. One would get the seed by the rain.

sanskrit: tasyāḥ punarbimbaphalopamoṣṭhaṃ svakṣibhukeśāntamarālapakṣma| vaktraṃ babhāse sitaśukladaṃṣṭra rāhormukhāccandra iva pramuktaḥ||
reference: And her countenance, having lips red as Bimba fruits, beautiful eyes, eye-brows extending to ears, curling eye-lashes and white teeth, again appeared graceful like to the Moon released from the full grasp of Rahu. (Like the Moon when full eclipse is just over-In mythology Rāhu is the son of Sinika, a Daitya, with the tail of a dragon whose head was severed from-his body by Vişnu, but being immortal this head and tail retained their separate existence and being transferred to the stellar sphere, became the authors of eclipses.)
baseline: The mouth of the king should be made to be like that of a rahmukha and the mouth of a stone. The speaker should be like the forehead of a river.
morphology: The mouth should be repeated with the syllable rāhāmūkṣa. The forehead should be placed at the end of the rectangle. The mouth of the speaker should be set on the right side of the arrow and the head should be opened like the head of a rahmukha.

sanskrit: sā vītaśokā vyapanītatandrā śāntajvarā harṣavibuddhasattvā| aśobhatāryā vadanena śukle śītāṃśunā rātririvoditena ||
reference: Her grief and exhaustion were removed. sorrow was pacified and her heart was filled with joy. And she with her countenance appeared beautiful like a lunar night beautified by the rays of the Moon.
baseline: He should be blessed with the sound of the wind calm and bright. The sun should be warmed with the words of the goddess of evil dry and cool and the night should be bright.
morphology: He should be blessed with the gift of the sun and the sound of the calm flame and the joy of the night. He would be blessed by the word of the goddess of evil.

sanskrit: tataḥ śūrpaṇakhā ghorā rāghavāśramamāgatā| rākṣasānācacakṣe tau bhrātarau saha sītayā||
reference: Then the grim Śūrpanakhā, coming to Rāghava's asylum pointed out to the Rākşasas those brother in company with Sītā.
baseline: Then Sarpanakha the cowherd returns to the abode of Raghava. The two go forth with their brethren in the eyes of the demons and Sita.
morphology: Then Surpanakha the knower of the cow and Raghava the hermitage would return. The two would be seen with their brothers in the eyes of demons and Sita.

sanskrit: te rāmaṃ parṇaśālāyāmupaviṣṭaṃ mahābalam| dadṛśuḥ sītayā sārdhaṃ lakṣmaṇenāpi sevitam||
reference: And they saw the mighty Rāma seated in the cottage in company with Sītā, and ministered to by Laksmana.
baseline: He should worship Rama in the palace of the foliage of the great king. He should be worshipped with Sita and with Lakshmana.
morphology: He should be placed in the room of the foliage of Lord Rama. He should not be seen sitting with Sita or with Lakshmana.

sanskrit: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā rāghavaḥ śrīmānāgatāṃstāṃśca rākṣasān| abravīd bhrātaraṃ rāmo lakṣmaṇaṃ dīptatejasam||
reference: And seeing her, as well as the Rākşasas who had come, Rāma remarked to his brother, Lakşınaņa of flaming energy.
baseline: Having seen him the king of the raghas the lord of the harem and the demons should be worshipped. Abravi Rama Lakshmana and the light of life should be worshiped.
