morphology: Having seen him the gods of the earth and the demons should be worshipped. Lord Rama should be worshiped as the brother of Avravida lord of the sky and lord of light.

sanskrit: muhūrte bhava saumitre sītāyāḥ pratyanantaraḥ| imānasyā vadhiṣyāmi padavīmāgatāniha||
reference: O Sumitrā's son, do you for a while guard Sītā. I shall slay these that have come to this asylum here.
baseline: You are in the right place in the moment and Sita is in the opposite direction. I will kill you on account of my belief.
morphology: In the instant you become the protector of Sita. I will kill you with my belief.

sanskrit: vākyametat tataḥ śrutvā rāmasya viditātmanaḥ| tatheti lakṣmaṇo vākyaṃ rāghavasya prapūjayan||5
reference: Hearing these words of Rāma versed in the knowledge of self, Lakşmaņa honoured his speech by saying, So be it.
baseline: Having heard the words one should know the wisdom of Rama. The words of Lakshmana should be worshipped in the worship of Raghava.
morphology: Having heard the statement made by him one should know the wisdom of Rama. The words of Lakshmana should be worshipped by Raghava.

sanskrit: rāghavo'pi mahaccāpaṃ cāmīkaravibhūṣitam| cakāra sajyaṃ dharmātmā tāni rakṣāṃsi cābravīt||
reference: And the righteous Rāghava strung his mighty bow decked with gold; and addressed the Raksasas.
baseline: The king should also pay tribute to the great sins of the gods. Then the godly spirit should protect them.
morphology: The great sins of Raghava and others should be worshipped by the righteous spirit. Then they should be protected.

sanskrit: putrau daśarathasyāvāṃ bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau| praviṣṭau sītayā sārdhaṃ duścaraṃ daṇḍakāvanam|| phalamūlāśanau dāntau tāpasau brahmacāriṇau| vasantau daṇḍakāraṇye kimarthamupahiṃsatha||
reference: We that have entered into this untraceable forest of Dandaka in company with Sītā are the sons of Dasaratha, the brothers, Rama and Lakşmana. Why do you intend to do injury to us. Subsisting on fruits and roots, having our senses under control, carrying on asceticism and leading a Brahmacarya life, we are passing our days in the forest of Dandaka.
baseline: The sons of Dasharatha the brothers of Rama Lakshmana Sita the king who entered the forest with the evil spirit and the king of the forest the bearer of fruits the owner of teeth the brahmins the lord of the spring the ruler of the river etc. should be punished.
morphology: The sons of Dasharatha the brothers of Rama Lakshmana Sita the king who entered the forest with the evil one the ruler of the forest the bearer of fruits the driver of fire the brahmins and the king of the river Vasanta should be punished.

sanskrit: yuṣmān pāpātmakān hantuṃ viprakārān mahāhave| ṛṣīṇāṃ tu niyogena samprāptaḥ saśarāsanaḥ||
reference: It is do destroy you, wicked, and troublesome that I equipped with the bow have come here at the desire of the saints.
baseline: The great king should kill those who commit sins against you in different ways. The sages should be given the seat of Sāsara.
morphology: The sages should be given the seat of Sāsara to kill those who commit sins against you.

sanskrit: tiṣṭhataivātra saṃtuṣṭā nopavartitumarhatha| yadi prāṇairihārtho vo nivartaghnāḥ||
reference: Stay there content you should not move further. If you have a care for your lives, desist, you rangers of the night.
baseline: If one is satisfied with the position of the body one would be able to move the body. If one does not get the life one should move the head.
morphology: If one is satisfied with the position of the body one would be able to move without losing his life.

sanskrit: tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā rākṣasāste caturdaśa| ūcurvācaṃ susaṃkruddhā brahmaghnāḥ śūlapāṇayaḥ|| saṃraktanayanā ghorā rāmaṃ saṃraktalocanam| paruṣā madhurābhāṣaṃ hṛṣṭā dṛṣṭaparākramam||
reference: Hearing those words of his, those fourteen grim Rākşasas bearing darts in their hands, exceedingly enraged, with their eyes reddened, breathing high spirits, harshly said to the sweetspeeched Rāma, having his eyes reddened whose prowess they had not seen before.
baseline: Having heard the opposite of him the demon is fourteen. Having worshipped Brahma with the rosary the bull the water and the water of the bull are protected by him. Having protected him from the roar the king is protected. Having seen the parusha the sweet tongue and the sound of the sun he should follow the order.
morphology: Having heard the opposite of him the demon is fourteen. Having fought with the bull Brahma the bull and water should be taken away from him and the king should be protected by the sword. Having seen the parrot and the tongue of the king hārṣta should be seen in the following order.

sanskrit: krodhamutpādya no bhartuḥ kharasya sumahātmanaḥ| tvameva hāsyase prāṇān sadyo'smābhirhato yudhi ||
reference: Having excited there our lord. the high-souled Khara, it is you that shal: lose your life no later than this day, being slain by us in battle.
baseline: Having produced anger one would not be able to bear the pleasure of the enemy. You are the one who gives life to the enemy in a jovial manner. Now we are in war.
morphology: One who does not get angry by the husband one who has good intentions for the wife one should fight the war of the souls in the present day. You are the one who gives laughter.

sanskrit: kā hi te śaktirekasya bahūnāṃ raṇamūrdhani | asmākamagrataḥ sthātuṃ kiṃ punaryo māhave||
reference: What power hast you, being one to stay before us many in the field, what shall I say of your coping with us in conflict?
baseline: One who has the strength of many things should be made to stand on the ground. What is the greatness of our standing on the earth?
morphology: One who has the strength of many things should be called the king. What is the greatness of our country?

sanskrit: ebhirbāhuprayuktaiśca parighaiḥ śūlapaṭṭiśaiḥ| prāṇāṃstyakṣyasi vīryaṃ ca dhanuśca karapīḍitam||
reference: In consequence of the parighas (iron-clubs), darts, and pattisas (a kind of sharp-edged sword) discharged by our arms, you will surely lose your life, along with your prowess, and this bow which you press with your hand.
baseline: One who uses the arrow and the axe with the periphery and the stripes of the bow and the bow should be made to see the soul. One who makes a bow and a bow would get the blood.
morphology: One who uses the arrow and the axe with the periphery and the stripes of the bow and the bow should be made to see the soul. One who makes a bow and a bow would be called a sage.

sanskrit: ityevamuktvā saṃrabdhā rākṣasāste caturdaśa| udyatāyudhanistriṃśā rāmamevābhidudruvuḥ||
reference: Having said this in wrath, those fourteen Rākşasas, uplifting their weapons and daggers rushed towards Rāma.
baseline: Having thus liberated ones body the fourteenth one is a demon. One who is armed with the weapon of the enemy is called rāma mēvā dudruva.
morphology: Having thus liberated ones body the fourteenth demon is the king. The fourteenth one is the lord of the arms and the king of the two arms.

sanskrit: cikṣipustāni śūlāni rāghavaṃ prati durjayam| tāni śūlāni kākutsthaḥ samastāni caturdaśa||
reference: And discharged darts at the invincible Rāghava. Thereupon Kākutstha by means of shafts decked with gold, cut off those fourteen darts of theirs.
baseline: The four axes of the cow are said to be four hundred and ten. The axe of the raghavas is said to have been a victory for them.
morphology: The four axes are said to be the fourteenth of the four horns.

sanskrit: tāvadbhireva ciccheda śaraiḥ kāñcanabhūṣitaiḥ| tataḥ paśyānmahātejā nārācān sūryasaṃnibhān|| jagrāha paramakuddhaścaturdaśa śilāśitān| gṛhītvā dhanurāyamya lakṣyānuddiśya rākṣasān|| mumoca rāghavo bāṇān vajrāniva śatakratuḥ|
reference: Seeing this, that exceedingly cnergetic one, waxing highly enraged, look out fourteen darts with many golden arrows, whetted on stone, resembling the sun. And even as Satakratu hurls the thunder bolt, Rāghava drawing his bow and taking his aim at the Rākşasas, let go those shafts.
baseline: Then the king should be made to eat the cow cow buffalo elephant bull bullock bullocks bulls bull and bullock and the king of the sun should be given to him. Having taken the cow and the bull he should be offered to the target. Having said this to the king the raga arrow diamond and other stones should be worshipped.
morphology: Then the king should be shaven with a mace and adorned with stones. Then the cow cow elephant bull bull and bull should be set on the sun. Then he should be taken away by the king and made to sit on a stone. Having made a bow and facing the target he should bow down to the gods. The ragha arrow and diamond should be placed on the ground.

sanskrit: te bhitvā rakṣasāṃ vegād vakṣāṃsi rudhiraplutāḥ|| viniṣpetustadā bhūmau valmīkādiva pannagāḥ|
reference: And those Rākşasas, their breasts pierced with vehemence, and themselves bathed in blood, fell down to the carth, like snakes dropping down from an ant hill.
baseline: They should be made to stand fast and the chests should be covered with blood and water and the ground should be washed with water on the day of vālmika.
morphology: The ground should be covered with water and the chest should be washed with water with the same speed. On the day of vālmikā the ground should become clear.

sanskrit: tairbhagnahadayā bhūmau chinnamūlā iva drumāḥ|| nipetuḥ śoṇitasnātā vikṛtā vigatāsavaḥ|
reference: And with their breasts pierced, they, dripping with blood, deformed and deprived of their lives, lay on the ground like trees whose roots have been severed.
baseline: One who has left the earth with the water of the sun and the water should be washed with the same water as with the chinna mula. The previous ones have been sold.
morphology: The earth should be covered with a piece of cloth made of white cloth and the water should be washed with water.

sanskrit: tān bhūmau patitān dṛṣṭvā rākṣasī krodhamūchitāḥ|| upagamya kharaṃ sā tu kiṃcitsaṃśuṣkaśoṇitā| papāta punarevārtā saniryāseva vallarī||
reference: Seeing them fallen-on the ground, the Rākşasī, beyond herself in wrath, approaching Khara, with her blood a little dried up, again in distressful guise threw herself on the earth, like a plant exuding gum.
baseline: Having seen those fallen on the ground the demons are removed from their anger and they are able to reach him. He is a little bit dry and tired. He should be returned to his father.
morphology: Having seen those fallen on the ground the demons are removed from the anger. He is able to reach that place. He has become a little defiled. He should repeat the words of Sāṇirāyāya and Vālārya.

sanskrit: bhrātuḥ samīpe śokārtā sasarja ninadaṃ mahat| sasvaraṃ mumuce vāṣpaṃ vivarṇavadanā tadā||
reference: And in presence of her brother, she set up a mighty roar; and then her face grown pallid, she dropped tears, emitting cries.
baseline: One who grieves near his brother brother sister brother and mother is great. One who gives the sound of vapour on the muṣuṇa should then be described as a great one.
morphology: One who grieves with his brother brother sister brother and sister is great. One who gives the sound of vapour on the muṣuṇa should be described as the same.

sanskrit: nipātitān prekṣya raṇe tu rākṣasān pradhāvitā śūrpaṇakhā punastataḥ| vadhaṃ ca teṣāṃ nikhilena rakṣasāṃ śaśaṃsa sarvaṃ bhaginī kharasya sā||
reference: Seeing those Rākşasas slain in battle, Śūrpanakhā again hastened (to his brother); and the sister of Khara, related in detail the slaughter of those Rākşasas.
baseline: Having sent away those who had been killed the king again sent the demon king back to his kingdom. The king should be punished with death and protection from their destruction. All the sisters of the king are to be punished by him.
morphology: Having sent away those who had been killed the king again sent forth the rakshasas the svarapankha who had driven them into the wilderness and had saved them from their destruction. The king should be blessed with all the weapons of his sister.

sanskrit: ṛṣyamūkāt tu hanumān gatvā taṃ malayaṃ girim| ācacakṣe tadā vīrau kapirājāya rāghavau||
reference: Having departed from Rşyamuka, and arrived at the Malaya hill, Hanumān informed the king of monkeys of (the arrival of) the descendants of Raghu.
baseline: Then the king should go to Hanumana with the advice of the sage. Then the mountain should be made into a mountain. Then he should be seen by the king of the mighty Kapīs.
morphology: Then the king should go to Hanumu from the seat of the sage and make him climb the mountain of Malaya. Then the mighty king should be called Raghava.

sanskrit: ayaṃ rāmo mahāprājña samprāpto dṛḍhavikramaḥ| lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā rāmo'yaṃ satyavikramaḥ||
reference: O exceedingly wise one, this one that has come here is Rāma having truth for his prowess.
baseline: This Rama is the supreme authority. He is the firm record holder. Lord Rama is also the true record holder along with Lakshmana.
morphology: This Rama is the supreme authority. He is the firm record of victory. Lord Rama the brother of Lakshmana is the true record.

sanskrit: ikvākūṇāṃ kule jāto rāmo daśarathātmajaḥ| dharme nigaditaścaiva piturnideśakārakaḥ||
reference: This is Rāma having truth for his prowess, in company with his brother, Lakşmaņa. Rāma the son of Dasaratha, is born in the race of the Ikş wākus. Ever doing the will of his sire, he has been sent hither, in order that his father's verity may stand in tact.
baseline: The king of Śrīma is said to have descended from the tribe of the equines and to be the son of the god Dasharatha. He is the ruler of his father's kingdom and the one who lives in the prescribed religion.
morphology: One who lives in a village of the same kind of people as the king of the kingdom of Śarāma and the spirit of Dārāsātra should go to the clan of the sons of śarāṣṭra. One who is determined by the religion should follow his father.

sanskrit: rājasūyāśvamedhaiśca vahniryenābhitarpitaḥ| dakṣiṇāśca tathotsṛṣṭā gāvaḥ śatasahasraśaḥ|| tapasā satyavākyena vasudhā yena pālitā| strīhetostasya putro'yaṃ rāmo'raṇyaṃ samāgataḥ||
reference: Raima, who has come to the forest, is the son of him who has propitiated Fire with Rājasuyas and horse sacrifices,-dispensing Dakshinas and kine by hundreds and thousands-and who has governed the earth by asceticism and truthful speech. His son Rāma has come to the forest through a woman.
baseline: The king should be worshipped with the words of the lord Sūyāśvā and Vāṇirya. The south should be offered with the sacred cow and the south with a hundred thousand cows. The woman should be reared with the word Vāsudha with the truth. The son should be given to the king with the vow of Rama.
morphology: The king is said to have killed the king the god of war the king of the south the cow that was raised by him in the south and the hundred thousand cows that were reared by him with the word of truth. The woman who raised him by the word vāsudha should be worshipped by the king and his son by the god Rama.

sanskrit: tasyāsya vasato'raṇye niyatasya mahātmanaḥ| rāvaṇena hṛtā bhāryā sa tvāṃ śaraṇamāgataḥ||
reference: While that high-souled one having his senses under control was dwelling in the woods, his wife was carried off by Rāvana; and he (Rāma) has (in consequence) sought your protection.
baseline: He should be the master of that place. He would be the wife of Ravana. He should take refuge in you.
morphology: He should be the master of that place. He should take refuge in you by the heart of Ravana. He would return to you.

sanskrit: bhavatā satyakāmo tau bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau| pragṛhya cārcayasvaitau pūjanīyatamābubhau||
reference: Do you, granting an interview to the brothers Rāma and Lakşmaņa-both of them worthy of homage-who pe eager for your friendship, receive them respectfully.
baseline: You are the true kāma the two brothers the lord Rama and the lord Laksmana. You should worship the Lord by worshipping him.
morphology: You are the true kāma the two brothers and Rama and Lakshmana. One should worship the Lord by worshipping him in the morning and worshipping Himself.

sanskrit: śrutvā hanūmato vākyaṃ sugrīvo vānarādhipaḥ| darśanīyatamo bhūtvā prītyovāca ca rāghavam|| bhavān dharmavinītaśca sutapāḥ sarvavatsalaḥ| ākhyātā vāyuputreṇa tattvato me bhavadguṇāḥ||
reference: Hearing Hanuman's words, Sugrīva-lord of monkeys, becoming visible (at his will), gladly spoke to Rāghava, sir, you are versed in morality, and bear love towards all. The son of the wind-god has faithfully described your virtues to me.
baseline: Having heard the words of Hanumata the king of monkeys the lord of the forest the chieftain having been shown to be beloved and having said that you are the king. You are the god of righteousness the son of the sun and all things. The son of Vayu is said to be the master of all virtues.
morphology: Having heard the words of Hanumata the king of monkeys the lord of the forest and the king should be seen. Having said that you are the king who is endowed with righteousness who is the son of the wind and who has said that you are all good.

sanskrit: tanmamaivaiṣa satkāro lābhaścaivottamaḥ prabho| yattvamicchasi sauhārda vānareṇa mayā saha ||
reference: That you, O lord, are anxious to contract friendship with me who am a monkey does me honour and is my gain.
baseline: O lord of good things and good gain by doing so. You wish to have peace with me by the monkey.
morphology: O lord of good things good things and good things are to be obtained by the merry monkeys. You wish to have peace with me.

sanskrit: rocate yadi me sakhyaṃ bāhureṣa prasāritaḥ| gṛhyatāṃ pāṇinā pāṇirmaryādā badhyatāṃ dhruvā||
reference: If you relish friendship with me, do you take this stretched arm and my hand with yours, and bind yourself fast with a vow.
baseline: If it pleases me to have the alliance spread out across the arms it should be taken by Panīna. The king of Panīmarā should be bound with water.
morphology: If it pleases me the alliance should be spread with the arms. It should be taken with the pāṇīna. The king of the waters should be bound with the dhruva.

sanskrit: etat tu vacanaṃ śrutvā sugrīvasya subhāṣitam| samprahṛṣṭamanā hastaṃ pīḍayāmāsa pāṇinā|| hṛṣṭaḥ sauhṛdamālambya paryaṣvajata pīḍitam|
reference: Hearing these sweet words of Sugrīva, (Rāma) exceedingly delighted, pressed Sugrīva's hand with his. And contracting friendship with Surgrīva, Rāma experiencing great joy embraced him warmly.
baseline: Having heard these words one would be pleased with the goodness of the lord. One would be afflicted by the hands of the sambhāraṣṭhmana who would suffer from the water. One should be happy with the sound of the water and suffer the affliction.
morphology: Having heard these words one would be pleased with the grace of the lord. One would be afflicted by the pain of the hands of the sambhāraṣruta. One should be happy with the sound of the water.

sanskrit: tato hanūmān saṃtyajya bhikṣurūpamariṃdamaḥ|| kāṣṭhayoḥ svena rūpeṇa janayāmāsa pāvakam|
reference: Then that subduer of foes, Hanumān, leaving off the guise of a beggar, in his native shape produced a fire with two pieces of wood.
baseline: Then after having worshipped Hanumans one would get the form of a bhiksha and the shape of a mace. One would get that form of the pāvakā in his own form from the wood.
morphology: Then after having worshipped Hanumu one should worship him in the form of a beggar. He should worship the king in the forms of a cow and a cow in his form.

sanskrit: dīpyamānaṃ tato vahni puṣpairabhyarcya satkṛtam|| tayormadhye tu suprīto nidadhau susamāhitaḥ| tato'gniṃ dīpyamānaṃ tau cakratuśca pradakṣiṇam|| sugrīvo rāghavaścaiva vayasyatvamupāgatau|
reference: Then worshipping that flaming fire with flowers, he, well pleased, carefully placed it between them (Rāma and Sugrīva). Then Sugrīva and Rāghava went round the fire; and (thus) were fastened in friendship.
baseline: Having worshipped the flowers of the goddess after having worshipped them with a lamp one should worship them in the middle of the temple. One should observe the circumambulation of the two lamps of the chakrākrātu and the circle of the gods. One who worships the goddess should be worshipped by the lord of the earth.
morphology: Having worshipped the goddess after having worshipped her with a flower in the middle of the morning she should worship her husband in the evening. Then the priest should worship the goddess and the two goddesses of light and circumambulate the circle. The king should worship Raghava and the people living in the old age.

sanskrit: tataḥ suprītamanasau tābubhau harirāghavau|| anyonyamabhivīkṣantau na tṛptimabhijagmatuḥ|
reference: And with delighted hearts, both of them-the monkey and Rāghava began to gaze at each other, yet they did not feel satiated.
baseline: Then the superior mind should be said to be a tabernacle a house of deer a place which is not satisfied with the world.
morphology: Then the lord of the tabernacle and the king of Hari should be pleased with each other. He should not be satisfied.

sanskrit: tvaṃ vayasyo'si hṛdyo me hyekaṃ duḥkhaṃ sukhaṃ ca nau||17| sugrīvo rāghavaṃ vākyamityuvāca prahṛṣṭavat|
reference: You are the friend of my heart. Our happiness and misery are common,-Sugriva, rejoicing greatly, said these words to Rāghava.
baseline: You are of age you are of heart you have got sorrow happiness happiness and nine other things. The words of Raghava Sugriva and others are described in the preface.
morphology: You are of age you are of heart you have sorrow you get happiness and you get pleasure. The words of Sugriva Raghava and others are said to be good.

sanskrit: tataḥ suparṇabahulā bhaṅktvā śākhāṃ supuṣpitām|| sālasyāstīrya sugrīvo niṣasāda sarāghavaḥ|
reference: Then spreading a beautifully blossoming spray of Sala, full of foliage, Sugriva made an awning and sat down with Rāghava.
baseline: Then after having broken the branches of the great flower of the sun the branches should be sprinkled with flowers and the saal should be washed with sugar and nisada.
morphology: Then the branches should be divided into four parts. Then the leaves should be washed with the saal and dried with the sagir nisāda and sāragha.

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇāyātha saṃhṛṣṭo hanumān mārutātmajaḥ|| śākhāṃ candanavṛkṣasya dadau paramapuṣpitām|
reference: Hanumăn, the son of the wind-god with great joy gave to Lakşmaņa a bough of a sandal tree, plentifully blossoming.
baseline: One should worship Hanumāṇa with the garland of lakshmana and the branches of the sandalwood tree.
morphology: One should worship Hanumāṇa with the garland of Lakshmana and the branches of the sandalwood tree.

sanskrit: tataḥ prahṛṣṭaḥ sugrīvaḥ ślakṣṇaṃ madhurayā girā|| pratyuvāca tadā rāmaṃ harṣavyākulalocanaḥ|
reference: Next Sugriva, feeling high rapture, with his eyes expanded with joy, answered Rāma blandly in sweet words.
baseline: Then one who has been worshipped by the sages would get the fragrance sweetly. Then one would hear the voice of Rama with joy and happiness.
morphology: Then the lord should be worshipped with the fragrance of sweet ghee. Then the king should be heard with joy and happiness.

sanskrit: ahaṃ vinikṛto rāma carāmīha bhayāditaḥ|| hṛtabhāryo vane trasto durgametadupāśritaḥ|
reference: Oppressed have I been, O Rama; and here am always afflicted with fear. Deprived of my wife, I have, agitated with apprehension, sought refuge in this dense wilderness.
baseline: I have said that Rama is the charioteer. He is afraid of you. He has said three things in the forest and has taken refuge in the fort.
morphology: O Rama who is the charioteer and the fearful one he should go to the forest and the fort of Trastha.

sanskrit: so'haṃ trasto vane bhīto vasāmyubhrāntacetanaḥ|| vālinā nikṛto bhrātrā kṛtavairaśca rāghava|
reference: I am afflicted with fright, and worried by fear, with my senses bewildered in this wood. Wronged have I been by Vāli, my brother; and I have incurred his hostility, O Raghava.
baseline: One who is afraid of the forest living in the forest and conscious of the illusion of the enemy and who has been taken away by his brother and the enemy made by him is Raghava.
morphology: O Raghava I am the fearful one living in the forest living in a state of illusion conscious and having been driven out by the enemy by my brother.

sanskrit: vālino me mahābhāga bhayārtasyābhayaṃ kuru|| kartumarhasi kākutstha bhayaṃ me na bhaved yathā|
reference: And, O exalted one, do you dispel the fear of me, who am tormented with fear on account of Vali. And, O Kakutstha, it behoves you so to act that I may not become subject to fear.
baseline: One should fear the great part of the fear of the enemy. One should do this without fear as if he were a coward.
morphology: One should fear the great part of the fear of the enemy. He should do this. One should not be afraid of him as if he were a cow.

sanskrit: evamuktastu tejasvī dharmajño dharmavatsalaḥ|| pratyabhāṣata kākutsthaḥ sugrīvaṃ prahasanniva|
reference: Thus addressed, the powerful Kākutstha, knowing righteousness, and devoted to virtue, answered Sugriva, smiling,
baseline: One who is free from evil and knows the righteousness of the world one who is righteous and has knowledge of the truth should speak to him in the same manner.
morphology: One who is free from evil and knows the righteousness of the world one who is righteous and has knowledge of the truth and one who speaks of the goodness of God in the form of a cow is a man of great pride.

sanskrit: upakāraphalaṃ mitraṃ viditaṃ me mahākape|| vālinaṃ taṃ vadhiṣyāmi tava bhāryāpahāriṇam|
reference: O mighty monkey, that the outcome of amity is good offices I am well aware of. I will slay that captor of your wife Vāli.
baseline: I shall kill the king of the great city who has been known to be a friend of the beneficent. I will kill him as your wife and husband.
morphology: Having known the benefits of a friend I shall kill him as if he were a great servant.

sanskrit: amoghāḥ sūryasaṃkāśā mameme nicitāḥ śarāḥ|| tasmin vālini durvṛtte nipatiṣyanti vegitāḥ| kaṅkapatrapraticchannā mahendrāśanisaṃnibhāḥ|| tīkṣṇāgrā ṛjuparvāṇaḥ saroṣā bhujagā iva|
reference: These infallible sharpened shafts of inine, resembling the sun, feathered with the plumes of the Kanka, like to the thunderbolt of the great Indra, having sharp heads and even knots, like in infuriated serpents,-being let go with vehermence, shall alight upon the impious Vali.
baseline: O Amogha the sun sambhā śāmya māhmī sārā sara vāli svāla svarāṇa vaṇḍu vilā kāṇpāra mahāndra sānīsana sībhava rījuparvana saruṣa bhujuga are the two vilas which are drawn in the same way.
morphology: O Amogha the sun the sākṣaṇa and the śārva are drawn into the earth. The vālikas are drawn to the earth and the vālias are cast into the river. The kankapatra is drawn from the face of the king. The sharpened garland of the sun and the water of the sea are drawn like the bhujaga.

sanskrit: tamadya vālinaṃ paśya tīkṣṇairāśīviṣopamaiḥ|| śarairvinihataṃ bhūmau prakīrṇamiva parvatam|
reference: Do you today behold Vāli slain with sharpened shafts, resembling snakes,—like to a torn hill lying on the ground.
baseline: Then one would see a mountain with a sharp edge and a poisonous ground. The earth would be like a mountain spread out over a wide area.
morphology: Then one would see a mountain like a mountain spread over the earth and the earth with its sharpness and sharpness.

sanskrit: sa tu tad vacanaṃ śrutvā rāghavasyātmano hitam| sugrīvaḥ paramaprītaḥ paramaṃ vākyamabravīt||
reference: Hearing those words of Răghava fraught with his welfare, Sugrīva supremely rejoiced, said these words, informed with rapture, You hero!
baseline: He should hear the words of Raghava. The spirit of the lord should be good. He should pray the supreme word to the Supreme Lord.
morphology: He should hear the words of Raghava. The spirit of the lord should be good. The virtuous one should pray the supreme word with utmost affection.

sanskrit: tava prasādena nṛsiṃha vīra priyāṃ ca rājyaṃ ca samāpnuyāmaham| tathā kuru tvaṃ naradeva vairiṇaṃ yathā na hiṃsyāt sa punarmamāgrajam ||
reference: You lion among men! by your grace shall I obtain both my beloved and my monarchy. O God among men, do you so deal with that foe, my elder brother, that he may not again wrong venomous me.
baseline: With your grace I shall end the kingdom of Nrīsimha Viraṇa Priyāna the enemy of the enemy. He should return to me without any violence.
morphology: With your grace I shall end the kingdom of Nrīsimha Viraṇa Priyāna and the enemy of the gods. You should do the same. He should return to me without any violence.

sanskrit: sītākapīndrakṣaṇadācarāṇāṃ rājīvahemajvalanopamāni| sugrīvarāmapraṇayaprasaṅge vāmāni netrāṇi samaṃ sphuranti||
reference: The left eyes of Sītā, the lord of apes, and night rangers-respectively like the lotus, gold, and flaming fire, throbbed when the friendship between Rāma and Sugrīva was contracted.
baseline: The eyes of the charioteer should be made to look like the left eye with the preceptor Śugrivarāma.
morphology: The eyes of the charioteer should be made to look like the left eye with the preceptor Śugrivarāma.

sanskrit: atha rātryāṃ vyatītāyāṃ viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ| āpṛṣṭvā tau ca rājānau jagāmottaraparvatam||
reference: Then when the right had passed away, the mighty Muni Viśvāmitra, having greeted the monarchs, yet out for the Northern mountains.
baseline: Then the king Viṣṭimāṭra would be great in the night and the king would be the king of the two kingdoms. The king would then ascend the mountain beyond the earth.
morphology: Then the king Viṣṭimāṭra would be great in the night and the king would be the king of the world.

sanskrit: viśvāmitre gate rājā vaidehaṃ mithilādhipam| āpṛṣdaiva jagāmāśu rājā daśarathaḥ purīm||
reference: When Viśvāmitra had gone away, king Dasaratha, greeting Mithila's lord, Vaideha, actively prepared for setting out for his own capital.
baseline: Having gone to the temple of Visva-mitra the king should be worshipped as Vāideha Mithila Adhipada and the king of jagāmasu Dasaratha as the lord of the temple.
morphology: The king of Mithila is the chief among the gods of the universe. On the other hand the king of jagāmasu king of dāśaratha is known to be the lord of Puri.

sanskrit: atha rājā videhānāṃ dadau kanyādhanaṃ bahu| gavāṃ śatasahasrāṇi bahūni mithileśvaraḥ|| kambalānāṃ ca mukhyānāṃ kṣaumān koṭyambarāṇi ca| hastyaśvarathapādātaṃ divyarūpaṃ svalaṃkṛtam|| dadau kanyāśataṃ tāsāṃ dāsīdāsamanuttamam| hiraṇyasya suvarṇasya muktānāṃ vidrumasya ca ||
reference: Then the king of the Videhas gave a dower consisting of various things. And Mithilā's lord gave many hundred thousands of kine, and excellent woollen stuffs, and Koțis of common cloths; and elephants, and horses, and cars, and footmen, as well as an hundred damsels adorned, endowed with elegance to form goodly waitingmaids. And well-pleased the king gave as a noble dower gold and silver and pearls and coral.
baseline: Thus the king should give the bridegroom a lot of money and the bride a hundred thousand pieces of gold the chief among the mattresses the head the chest the arms the feet the divine form the bride the maidservant the daughter of Hiranya the gold and the free of the bondage.
morphology: Thus the king should give the bridegroom a lot of money. The king should buy a hundred thousand pieces of gold and many pieces of brass and the chiefly blankets the chief articles of gold the main articles of silver the head of gold in the hands the feet of the gods the divine form of gold made of gold. The bride should be given to the maidservant in the form of a hundred pieces of silver and gold.

sanskrit: dadau rājā susaṃhṛṣṭaḥ kanyādhanamanuttamam| dattvā bahuvidhaṃ rājā samanujñāpya pārthivam|| praviveśa svanilayaṃ mithilāṃ mithileśvaraḥ| rājāpyayodhyādhipatiḥ saha putrairmahātmabhiḥ|| ṛṣīn sarvān puraskṛtya jagāma sabalānugaḥ|
reference: Having given divers kinds of articles, that king, the lord of Mithila, bidding adieu to the monarch (Dasaratha), re-entered his own capital. And the master of Ayodhyā accompanied with his high-souled sons, and headed by the saints in a body, started on the journey, followed by his own army.
baseline: The king of the king should give the bridegroom a good gift and the bride a good fortune. Having given the king a lot of gifts he should enter the earth with his wife Mithila the king with the chieftain of the warrior the sages with sons and other noble persons and the king would be blessed with all the virtues.
morphology: The king of the king should be blessed with a daughter and the best of wealth. Having given her many gifts the king would accept her and enter the earth. Having obtained the kingdom of Mithila the lord Mithila and the king and the chieftain of the war the sages should be rewarded with sons and great souls and the world would be energized.

sanskrit: gacchantaṃ tu naravyāghra sarṣisaṅgha sarāghavam|| ghorāstu pakṣiṇo vāco vyāharanti samantataḥ| bhaumāścaiva mṛgāḥ sarve gacchanti sma pradakṣiṇam||
reference: As that tiger-like one was on his way, in company with Rāghava and the saints, the fowls began to utter frightful cries all around, and the beasts on earth to stream in a Southern direction.
baseline: As one goes along the path one would see a lion tiger bear lion lion and a lion. One would see birds and birds in the sky. All the deer living in the land would go round and round the earth.
morphology: As we go along the path of the tiger tiger bear lion lion and other animals the birds and birds are seen in the sky. All those living in the earth and those living on the earth are going round and round.

sanskrit: tān dṛṣṭvā rājaśārdūlo vasiṣṭhaṃ paryapṛcchata| asaumyāḥ pakṣiṇo ghorā mṛgāścāpi pradakṣiṇāḥ|| kimidaṃ hṛdayotkampi mano mama viṣīdati|
reference: Beholding them, that tiger-like monarch asked Vasistha, saying, Those birds of fierce aspects emit frightful cries and beasts stream in a Southerly direction. What is this? My heart tremble and my mind is not at ease.
baseline: Having seen them the king should worship Vasisthā. Having seen the birds of the sea the horses the deer etc. one would find that the heart and the mind would be disturbed.
morphology: Having seen them the king should worship Vasistha. Having seen the birds of Asaumya horses deer etc. one would be shocked by the heart heart and mind.

sanskrit: rājño daśarathasyaitacchrutvā vākyaṃ mahānṛṣiḥ|| uvāca madhurāṃ vāṇī śrūyatāmasya yat phalam| upasthitaṃ bhayaṃ ghoraṃ divyaṃ pakṣimukhāccyutam|| mṛgāḥ praśamayantyete saṃtāpastyajyatāmayam|
reference: Hearing the speech of king Dasaratha, that mighty saint spoke sweetly, saying, 'These fowls of the air by their cries presage some dreadful impending evil; but these beasts betoken peace restored. Therefore do you renounce anxiety'
baseline: Having heard the words of king Dārṣṭara after having rebuked him the great sage said to him that he should listen to the sweet speech. The fear present is terrible and the fear of the divine bird has gone away. He should be angry with the antics in the end.
morphology: The great sage Dāśrātha the king of the kingdom of the king after having raised his voice and having heard the sweet words said to him the fruit of our speech. The fear present is terrible the fear of the divine and the face of the birds is removed. The evil one should be angry in peace and peace.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ: saṃvadatāṃ tatra vāyuḥ prādurbabhūva ha|| kampayan medinī sarvāṃ pātayaṃśca mahādumān| tamasā saṃvṛtaḥ sūryaḥ sarve nāvediṣurdiśaḥ|| bhasmanā cāvṛtaṃ sarvaṃ sammūḍhamiva tadbalam|
reference: As they were thus conversing, there blew a strong wind; and all the earth began to speak; and the trees to topple down. And a deep gloom enveloped the sun; and no quarter could be discovered. And enveloped in ashes, that host became stupefied.
baseline: The wind that blows there and the earth trembles and all the leaves are covered with water and the sun is covered with a lotus and the fire is burnt in the sky.
morphology: The wind that blows there and the earth trembles and all the leaves are covered with water and the sun is covered with a lotus and the fire is covered by the fire. It is the strength of everything.

sanskrit: vasiṣṭha ṛṣayaścānye rājā ca sasutastadā|| sasaṃjñā iva tatrāsan sarvamanyadvicetanam| tasmiṃstamasi ghore tu bhasmacchanneva sā camūḥ||
reference: At that dreadful hour, Vasiştha and the other saints and the king alone retained their senses, all else were deprived of their senses, and the army was enveloped with ashes.
baseline: The king should sit there as if he had knowledge of all things. He should be the son of Vāṣṣṭīṣṭha the sage the king and the king of Sāsutā. That man should be aware of everything. He would be destroyed by the fire.
morphology: The king of Vasistha the sage and the king of Sāsutta should sit there as if they were conscious of all things. He should be aware of these things. Then he should go round and wash his body with water.

sanskrit: dadarśa bhīmasaṃkāśaṃ jaṭāmaṇḍaladhāriṇam| bhārgavaṃ jāmadagnyeyaṃ rājā rājavimardanam|| kailāsamiva durdharṣaṃ kālāgnimiva duḥsaham| jvalantamiva tejobhirdurnirīkṣyaṃ pṛthagjanaiḥ|| skandhe cāsajjya paraśuṃ dhanurvidyudgaṇopamam| pragṛhya śaramugraṃ ca tripuraghnaṃ yathā śivam ||
reference: The king saw that repressor of kings, the descendant of Bhrgu, Jamadagni's son, dreadful to behold, wearing a head of matted locks, like to the Kailāsa, had to baffle, resembling the fire at the universal dissolution, difficult to bear, flaming in energy, incapable of being looked at by the unrighteous, with his axe on his shoulder, equipped with a bow like to the lighting, and fierce arrows, looking like Śiva the slayer of Tripura.
baseline: The king should be worshipped with the garlands of bheemas and jata the garland of fire the king with the arrow and fire with the bow with his arms covered with a mace with a kālaṣmī strong armour with black fire and with the sword of mischief with fiery arms with bright lights and light and with a chasmara on his shoulders and with his armour and fire. The king who is a tripuragana is worshipped as Śiva.
morphology: The king should wear a garland of garlands with the garlands of bheem and jatā. Bhārga jāmādāgnya rajā vimrādaṇa kāyāla dūrdhāśa kaalāgarṇī duṣaṇīma jajavīrṇīṣa vījavīdūrnirīśa and the king should be adorned with the arrow and the fire of the sword and the sword of Śiva.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā bhīmasaṃkāśaṃ jvalantamiva pāvakam| vasiṣṭhapramukhā viprā japahomaparāyaṇāḥ|| saṃgatā munayaḥ sarve saṃjajalpuratho mithaḥ|
reference: Beholding him of dreadful appearance like to flaming fire, the Vipras headed by Viśvāmitra, engaged in reciting mantras and and offering oblations to the fire, those saints assembled together, began to converse with each other.
baseline: Having seen him Bhima Sankāśa Pāvaka Vāsisthā Pramukha Viṣṭipraha Homa Parāyāna Sage and all the sages who are associated with him are illusionful.
morphology: Having seen him Bhima Sankāśa Pāvaka Vāsisthā Pramukha Viṣṭipraha Homa Parayana all the sages who are associated with him are illusionful.

sanskrit: kaccit pitṛvadhāmarṣī kṣatraṃ notsādayiṣyati|| pūrvaṃ kṣatravadhaṃ kṛtvā gatamanyurgatajvaraḥ| kṣatrasyotsādanaṃ bhūyo na khalvasya cikīrṣitam||
reference: Is this one, enraged because of the slaughter of this sire, intent upon exterminating the Kș atriyas? Formerly, having slaughtered the Kșatriyas, he pacified his ire and mental ferment, 'therefore, the annihilate the Ksatriya once again can never be his endeavour.
baseline: The king of Kāccha Pitrāvādhamāśī will destroy the Kṣṭra. Having destroyed the Kāṣtravāśa earlier he would destroy the king of the Kshatrāśas. The king would not destroy the kingdom of Kṣtrāṣa.
morphology: The king of Kāccha Pitrāvādhamāśī the king of the Kṣatraśa kingdom will destroy the Kshatra kingdom. Having destroyed the Kśatra kingdom earlier he should not destroy the king. He should destroy the kingdom of Kṣatriyas.

sanskrit: evamuktvāya̭mādāya bhārgavaṃ bhīmadarśanam| ṛṣayo rāmarāmeti madhuraṃ vākyamabruvan||
reference: Having said this, the saints offered Arghya to Bhrgu's son of dreadful appearance; and addressed him in soothing words, saying, 'Q Rāma! O Rāma.
baseline: One should see Bhārgavam Bhīmādarshana who has been liberated by the same. The sage Śrīṣī is said to have worshipped Rama. The sweet words are said to be described.
morphology: One who worships Bhāmā Bhārga Bhīmā and others for the liberation of the world should say the sweet words of the sage Rama.

sanskrit: pratigṛhya tu tāṃ pūjāmṛṣidattāṃ pratāpavān| rāmaṃ dāśarathiṃ rāmo jāmadagnyo'bhyabhāṣata||
reference: Accepting that homage rendered to him by the saints, that puissant one, Jamadagni's son, Rāma, addressed Rāma, the son of Dasaratha.
baseline: Having worshipped him after having taken him home he would give him the glory of agriculture. He would say to him that Rama should be worshipped as the son of Dasharatha and Rama as his son.
morphology: Having worshipped him every day he said that he would be blessed with the wealth of the farmers. He would also be blessed by Rama Dasharatha Rama Jamadagni and others.

sanskrit: niviṣṭāyāṃ tu senāyāmutsuko bharatastataḥ| jagāma bhrātaraṃ draṣṭuṃ śatrughnamanudarśayan||
reference: Having quartered his forces, Bharata eager (to go to Rāma's place), went to see his brother, showing to Satrughna the signs of Rāma's abode being in the vicinity.
baseline: One who is sitting in the army and willing to fight the enemy should see Jagāma the brother of Satrughṇa.
morphology: One who is standing in the midst of the army and who is willing to fight with the enemy should see the king of Satrughnas and his brother.

sanskrit: ṛṣi vasiṣṭhaṃ saṃdiśya mātṛmeṃ śīghramānaya| iti tvaritamagre sa jagāma guruvatsalaḥ||
reference: "And having desired Vasistha, saying, “Bring my mothers without delay,"" that one attached to his superiors went before."
baseline: The sage Vāṣṭhī should be asked to return to his mother as soon as possible. He should be called forthwith.
morphology: The sage Vasistha should be suspected and the mother should be taken care of quickly. He should be immediately called to the seat of the master.

sanskrit: sumantrastvapi śatrughnamadūrādanvapadyata| rāmadarśanajastoṃ bharatasyeva tasya ca||
reference: And eager to see Rāma even like Bharata himself, Sumantra followed Bharata at a short distance.
baseline: One should also worship the sun god Satrughṇa and the goddess Mādurāda. One should worship Lord Rama and Bharata.
morphology: He should also be worshipped as the son of Satrughṇa the king of mādurāda the god of Rama the lord of Bharata and others.

sanskrit: gacchannevātha bharatastāpasālayasaṃsthitām| bhrātuḥ parṇakuṭī śrīmānuṭajaṃ ca dadarśa ha||
reference: As Bharata passed on, he observed a neat cottage of leaves stationed among the asylums of anchorets, furnished with a portion having a wall with a door.
baseline: One should go to the temple of Bharata. One should see the brother the foliage of the leaves the king of the muṭjana and the king.
morphology: One should go to the temple of Bharata. One should visit the temple. One would see the leaves of the brother one of the sons of Srimāṇa and one of Dāsara.

sanskrit: śālāyāstvagratastasyā dadarśa bharatastadā| kāṣṭhāni cāvabhagnāni puṣpāṇyapacitāni ca|| sa lakṣmaṇasya rāmasya dadarśāśramamīyuṣaḥ| kṛtaṃ vṛkṣeṣvabhijñānaṃ kuśacīraiḥ kvacit kvacit||
reference: Before the cottage, Bharata saw fuel broken up, and flowers gathered. And he saw at places signs of Kuśa and bark set up on trees when Rāma and Lakşmaņa (first) arrived at their asylum.
baseline: One who has seen the shalas and the garlands of the gods in the form of a tree should be worshipped with the words of Bharata. One who worships the gods lakshmana rāma and rāmas should be worshiped with flowers. He should know the wisdom of the trees and the knowledge of these gods is known only by the wise men.
morphology: He should be worshipped in the form of a shāla. He should worship the gods of India. The gods of the world the wood the fire the flowers the fruits and the flowers of the kingdom of Lakshmana the king of the king the lord of the army of Rama the servants of the lord yuṣṇa. The knowledge of these trees is known to the wise men in a very short time.

sanskrit: dadarśa bhavane tasmin mahataḥ saṃcayān kṛtān| mṛgāṇāṃ mahiṣāṇāṃ ca karīṣaiḥ śītakāraṇāt||7
reference: And in that habitation, Bharata saw great heaps of dry dung of deer and buffaloes, gathered for preventing cold.
baseline: Great treasures have been made therein in the palace of Dāśarās. They have been destroyed because of the cold by the carriages of deer buffaloes etc..
morphology: Great treasures have been made therein in the palace of Dāśarā. They are said to be cold because of the deer buffaloes and kārīs.

sanskrit: gacchanneva mahābāhuryutimān bharatastadā| śatrughnaṃ cābravīddhṛṣṭastānamātyāṃśca sarvaśaḥ||
reference: As he proceeded, the intelligent and mightyarmed Bharata with a cheerful heart remarked to Śatrughna and all the courtiers.
baseline: The king of Bharata should go to the same place as the king of the great powers. Satrughṇa should be worshipped everywhere in the kingdom of Sthiti.
morphology: One who goes to that place would get great blessings from Bharata. One who is a Shatrughna would get victory from the enemy and one who has got victory from his mother would get everything.

sanskrit: manye prāptāḥ sma taṃ deśaṃ bharadvājo yamabravīt| nātidūre hi manye'haṃ nadī mandākinīmitaḥ||
reference: I conceive, we have reached the tract that was mentioned by Bharadvāja. Hard by this spot, I fancy, is the river Mandākini.
baseline: O Bharadwaja you have asked for the land which you have got from your mother. You have asked me to go to your grandson's house. I am going to make the river slow.
morphology: O Bharadwaja you have got the land by the way of the river. You have asked me to go to your great grandson. I am going to make the river slow.

sanskrit: uccairbaddhāni cīrāṇi lakṣmaṇena bhavedayam| abhijñānakṛtaḥ panthā vikāle gantumicchatā||
reference: On high are barks set up by Lakşmaņa. Having to pass by the way at unusual hours, (Laksmana) has marked it with signs.
baseline: The holes should be made with lakshmana tied high. The path made by the knower should go to the sick man in case of ill health.
morphology: The incisions should be made with lakshmana tied high up. The path made by the knower should be known in the case of a defect.

sanskrit: itaścodāttadantānāṃ kuñjarāṇāṃ tarasvinām| śailapārśve parikrāntamanyonyamabhigarjatām||
reference: On the side of the hill is the way by which long-tusked elephants pass to and fro with vehemence, roaring at each other.
baseline: These are the four kunjars of the kundas. One should make a circumambulation on the side of the hill and the other two should be made to break it.
morphology: These are the four kunjars of the kundas. One should go round and round on the mountain side.

sanskrit: yamevādhātumicchanti tāpasāḥ satataṃ vane| tasyāsau dṛśyate dhūmaḥ saṃkulaḥ kṛṣṇavartmanaḥ||
reference: Here is seen the dense and dark smoke of that which the anchorets are ever anxious to preserve in the forest, fire.
baseline: One who wishes to have the metal in the forest would get the heat. One would get to see the smoke in the sky and the mixture of black and white.
morphology: One who wishes to have the metal in the sky and the heat in the forest would get it. He would get the smoke and the mixture of black and white.

sanskrit: atrāhaṃ puruṣavyāghraṃ gurusatkārakāriṇam| ārya drakṣyāmi saṃhṛṣṭaṃ maharṣimiva rāghavam||
reference: Even here shall I with a delighted heart see that foremost of men, the noble Rāghava resembling a Maharși, ever engaged in serving his superiors.
baseline: Here the male tiger the master the doer of good deeds the king of the kingdom of Aryās and the king Raghav are worshipped.
morphology: Here is the male tiger the master the doer of good deeds the king of the kingdom of Arya the lord of sages and the king Raghava.

sanskrit: atha gatvā muhūrta tu citrakūṭaṃ sa rāghavaḥ| mandākinīmanu prāptastaṃ janaṃ cedamabravīt||
reference: Then going to Citrakuta, that descendant of Raghu, coming to the Mandakini, said to the men.
baseline: Having gone there he should offer the muhurta of Chitrakātra to Raghava. He should say to the people that he has got a man who is weak.
morphology: Having gone there he should offer the muhurta of Chitrakrūta to Raghava. He should ask the people who have found him in a poor condition.

sanskrit: jagatyāṃ puruṣavyāghra āste vīrāsane rataḥ| janendro nirjanaṃ prāpya dhiṅme janma sajīvitam||
reference: That foremost of men in all the world, the lord of all, coming into seclusion, is in his yoga posture. O fie upon my birth and my life!
baseline: One who is born alive in the abode of jagatya a male tiger a man who is in the seat of vairasana and who has attained vanity is called janendro.
morphology: One who is born alive in the world after having attained vanity would be born in the abode of jāṇendrā.

sanskrit: matkṛte vyasanaṃ prāpto lokanātho mahādyutiḥ| sarvān kāmān parityajya vane vasati rāghavaḥ||
reference: For me, having come by misfortune, and renounced every comfort, the effulgent lord of men, Rāghava, is dwelling in the woods.
baseline: Having got the attachment in the matter of religion Lord Lokanatha is a great warrior. Having renounced all desires Raghava dwells in the forest.
morphology: Having attained the greatness of the world and having acquired the attachment of religion having renounced all desires he should go to the forest and live in the forest.

sanskrit: iti lokasamānuṣṭaḥ pādeṣvadya prasādayan| rāmaṃ tasya patiṣyāmi sītāyā lakṣmaṇasya ca ||
reference: I shall be taxed of men on the score. To-day (first) pacifying him, I will fall at the feet of Rāma as well as of Sitã and Lakşmaņa.
baseline: One should offer the same to the lord of the world and his wife. I am Rama and Sita and Lakshmana.
morphology: One should offer the same to the people and their husbands. I am Rama Sita Lakshmana and others.

sanskrit: evaṃ sa vilapaṃstasmin vane daśarathātmajaḥ| dadarśa mahatīṃ puṇyāṃ parṇaśālāṃ manoramām||
reference: Having thus bewailed, Dasaratha's son saw a splendid, charming, and holy dwelling in that forest, composed of leaves.
baseline: In this way he wails in the forest. The spirit of Dasharatha is great. The image of the king is said to be beautiful in the form of leaves.
morphology: Thus he laments in the forest. Then the spirit of Dasharatha should be worshipped in the wilderness. Then he should worship the great goddess of goodness and the garden of leaves.

sanskrit: sālatālāśvakarṇānāṃ parṇairbahubhirāvṛtām| viśālāṃ mṛdubhistīrṇāṃ kuśairvedimivādhvare|| śakrāyudhanikāśaiśca kārmukai rasādhanaiḥ| rukmapṛṣṭhairmahāsāraiḥ śobhitāṃ śatrubādhakaiḥ|| arkaraśmipratīkāśaioraistūṇagataiḥ śaraiḥ| śobhitāṃ dīptavadanaiḥ sarbhogavatīmiva|| mahārajatavāsobhyāmasibhyāṃ ca virājitām| rukmabinduvicitrābhyāṃ carmabhyāṃ cāpi śobhitām|| godhāṅgaliaurāsaktaiścitrakāñcanabhūṣitaiḥ| arisaṃdhairanādhṛṣyāṃ mṛgaiḥ siṃhaguhāmiva || prāgudakapravaṇāṃ vediṃ viśālāṃ dīptapāvakām| dadarśa bharatastatra puṇyāṃ rāmaniveśane||
reference: And Bharata beheld in Rāma's habitation a sacred structure made of leaves, covered with a profusion of Sāla, palm, and Aśvakarņa leaves; spread with soft Kuśa, like a dais in a sacrifice; adorned with bows resembling the iris, plaited on the back with gold, of mighty force, and capable of achieving arduous feets and destroying foes; and garnished with arrows in quivers, seeming like the rays of the sun, with flaming mouths, like to the Bhogavatī with serpents; and exceedingly beautified with golden sheaths and scimitars and shields spangled with gold and nice guana finger-fences decked with gold; inaccessible to foes like a lion's den to deer; and furnished with a spacious dais inclined on the north-east, with a fire flaming on it.
baseline: One should make a large wall of leaves leaves flowers flowers and flowers of the sun a mound with a soft base a wall of arms and arms a stone of arms an ornamental piece of cloth a piece of stone with the arms of the enemy an image of the king of the city a statue of the lord of the earth an idol of the great king a goddess of the world a king of gods a woman adorned with a lotus a lion a cave a temple of the god of the sea a place of worship an altar and a huge
morphology: One should make a large cave with the leaves leaves flowers flowers and flowers of the sun a small place with a soft base a mound an altar of arms a stone of arms and arms and a piece of wood with the ornamentation of the temple. One should decorate the city with the images of the enemy with the elements of the sky one with the objects of the earth the goddess of life the gods of the world the king of the universe the queen of the king the lord of the gods and the goddesses of the kingdom the great goddess of heaven and the king

sanskrit: nirīkṣya sa muhūrtaṃ tu dadarśa bharato gurum| uṭaje rāmamāsīnaṃ jaṭāmaṇḍaladhāriṇam|| kṛṣṇājinadharaṃ taṃ tu cīravalkalavāsasam| dadarśa rāmamāsīnamabhitaḥ pāvakopamam|| siṃhaskandhaṃ mahābāhuṃ puṇḍarīkanibhekṣaṇam| pṛthivyāḥ sāgarāntāyā bhartāraṃ dharmacāriṇam|| upaviṣṭaṃ mahābāhuṃ brahmāṇamiva śāśvatam| sthaṇḍile darbhasaṃstīrṇe sītayā lakṣmaṇena ca||
reference: And looking around, anon Bharata saw his superior Rāma seated in the cottage bearing a head of matted locks, clad in a black deer-skin, and having tattered cloth and bark for his garment. reference: And seeing him, overwhelmed with grief and affliction, the righteous and graceful son of Kaikeyi, Bharata, rushed (towards him).
baseline: Having seen him Bharata said that the lord should be full of sorrow and envy. Having worshipped him the god of righteousness should be worshipped by Bharata.
morphology: Having seen him Bharata said that the lord should be full of sorrow and envy. The supreme god should be worshipped by Bharata.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvaiva vilalāpā” bāṣpasaṃdigdhayā girā| aśaknuvan vārayituṃ dhairyād vacanamabruvan ||

baseline: Having seen it he fell down with a vapour and milk. He said the words with courage to destroy the invaders.
morphology: Having seen the vilāpā the water fell with the steam and milk. The words were spoken with courage to destroy the invaders.

sanskrit: yaḥ saṃsadi prakṛtibhirbhaved yukta upāsitum| vanyairmṛgairupāsīnaḥ so'yamāste mamāgrajaḥ||
reference: That elder brother of mine, who (seated) in court should be surrounded by the subjects intent upon paying him homage, is now surrounded by wild deer.
baseline: One who worships the earth and the world of nature one who is a wild animal and one who lives in the wilderness and one with the silver body is my son.
morphology: One who worships the earth and the earth in the midst of the nature and the wild animals should be worshipped. One who is not a wild animal should worship the earth.

sanskrit: vāsobhirbahusāhauryo mahātmā purocitaḥ| mṛgājine so'yamiha pravaste dharmamācaran||
reference: He that used to adorn his person with attire worth many thousands (of things), engaged in observing morality, is clad in deer-skin.
baseline: The great man should be worshipped with the garland of water the bhuṣāra and sahūrī. He should be worshiped in the kingdom of the beasts. If he enters the kingdom he should worship him.
morphology: The great man should be worshipped with the garlands of the gods the mighty men the brave men and the mighty warriors. He should be worshiped in the kingdom of the beasts of war.

sanskrit: adhārayad yo vividhāścitrāḥ sumanasaḥ sadā| so'yaṃ jaṭābhāramimaṃ sahate rāghapaḥ katham||
reference: Why does he that always wore variegated blossoms, Rāghava, bears this burthen of matted locks?
baseline: One who supports a different person always has to bear the burden of jata. One who carries the weight of jatabharām should be asked to explain how Raghāpā.
morphology: One who supports a different person always has to bear the burden of jata. One who carries the weight of jatabharā is called raghāpa.

sanskrit: yasya yajñairyathādiṣṭairyukto dharmasya saṃcayaḥ| śarīrakleśasambhūtaṃ sa dharma parimārgate||
reference: He who is worthy of acquiring religious merit by celebrating sacrifices according to the ordinance, is now following morality by afflicting his person.
baseline: One whose sacrifice is of the nature of patience who is free from suffering who accumulates the wealth of righteousness who has built up the body and afflictions leads to the attainment of goodness.
morphology: One whose sacrifice is made with patience who has got patience is the storehouse of righteousness. One who has built up the body and afflictions would go to the path of rightism.

sanskrit: candanena mahārheṇa yasyāṅgamupasevitam| malena tasyāṅgamidaṃ kathamāryasya sevyate||
reference: How is the person of that one whose body used to be daubed with costly sandal, covered with dust.
baseline: One who consumes a part of the body with sandal and a large amount of water should be served with a malai.
morphology: One who consumes a part of the body with sandal and a large amount of water would be served with the māla.

sanskrit: manimittamidaṃ duḥkhaṃ prāpto rāmaḥ sukhocitaḥ| dhigjīvitaṃ nṛśaṃsasya mama lokavigarhitam||
reference: It is for me that Rama, although deserving of comfort, has come by this misfortune. Wicked that I am, fie upon my life despised of men!
baseline: Having received this sorrow in the mind Rama is blessed with happiness. He who is alive living living and suffering is my world.
morphology: Having received this sorrow for the sake of the mind Rama is blessed with happiness. He who is alive and suffering from the tyranny of the world is known to me as the king.

sanskrit: ityevaṃ vilapana dīnaḥ prasvinamukhapaṅkajaḥ| pādāvaprāpya rāmasya papāta bharato rudan||
reference: Thus lamenting in woeful guise, with the lotus of his countenance covered with sweat, Bharata coming at Rāma's feet, fell at them bewailing.
baseline: One who so wails should say that he has heard the words of the priest the mouth mouth and feet. Having heard the sound of the voice of Rama one should cry to Bharata.
morphology: One who so wails should say that he has heard the words of the priest the mouth mouth feet feet and feet of Lord Rama. One who cries with the voice of Lord Bharata should do so.

baseline: Having said this the king of Bharata the great king who is afflicted with sorrow should be rebuked by the king.
morphology: The king of India is said to be great. Having said this the king should be rebuked.

sanskrit: bāṣpaiḥ pihitakaṇṭhaśca prekṣya rāmaṃ yaśasvinam| āryetyevābhisaṃkruśya vyāhatu nāśakat tataḥ||
reference: And beholding the illustrious Rāma, Bharata with his utterance choked with emotion, exclaimed, O noble one, and was unable to say anything further.
baseline: Having sent forth the kāṇḍas covered with vapours Śrīma should be successful. He should be destroyed by the invading aryatya.
morphology: Having sent forth the elbows covered with vapours Rama is successful. He should be destroyed by the invading aryatya.

reference: Then Śatrughna also weeping paid homage unto the feet of Rāma. And shedding tears, Rāma embraced them both. Then as in the sky, the Sun and the Moon meet with śukra and Brhaspati, those two princes (Rāma and Laks mana) met with Sumantra and Guha in the forest.
baseline: Then the king should be made to sit in the cave with the sun the king the sage and the king of the two gods. The king should offer thanks to the king and the sages of the king. The sage should also offer prayers at the feet of Rama in the forest.
morphology: Then the king should be seated in the cave with the sword of Sumantra. The king should also be seated on the throne of the king the king of the two gods the sage Nīshākar and the king who is living in the city of Divākārā. He should be worshipped with the rosary.

sanskrit: tān pārthivān vāraṇayūthapārhān samāgatāṃstatra mahatyaraṇye| vanaukasaste'bhisamīkṣya sarve tvaśrūṇyamuñcan pravihāya harṣam||
reference: And beholding those kings resembling leaders of elephant-herds met together in that mighty forest, the dwellers in the woods, resigning their cheerfulness, began to shed tears. forest, the dwellers in the woods, resigning their cheerfulness, began to shed tears.
baseline: Having said this one should rejoice when he enters the forest. Having seen the forest he should welcome all those who have heard of him.
morphology: Having gathered the people of the earth together with them one should rejoice when they enter the forest. Having seen the forest together they should be glad to hear you.

sanskrit: sa jitvā dhanadaṃ rāma bhrātaraṃ rākṣasādhipaḥ| mahāsenaprasūtiṃ tadyayau śaravaṇaṃ mahat||

baseline: He who gains wealth by having a brother named Rama as the protector of the demons and gives birth to a great child is said to be great.
morphology: He who gains wealth by having a brother named Rama as the protector of the demons would be blessed with great wealth.

sanskrit: athāpaśyaddaśagrīvo raukmaṃ śaravaṇaṃ mahat| gabhastijālasaṃvītaṃ dvitīyamiva bhāskaram|| sa parvataṃ samāruhya kaṃcidramyavanāntaram| prekṣate puṣpakaṃ tatra rāmaviṣṭambhitaṃ tadā||
reference: The Ten-necked Rāvana saw the great golden wood of reeds. Furnished with networks of solar rays, and appearing like a second Sun, and ascending the mountain, he was surveying the heart of the forest, when, O Rama, Puspaka was (suddenly) deprived of its motion.
baseline: One who has made a garland of gold and silver is great. One who makes a garbha neta and other forms of fire should climb the mountain and see the flower of Rama standing there after the battle.
morphology: One who has made a great sacrifice of a cow a cow and a cow should be offered to the king. He should offer a garland of water and another garland to the lord. He would climb a mountain and see the flower of the god Rama standing there in the midst of the forest.

sanskrit: viṣṭabdhaṃ kimidaṃ kasmānāgamatkāmagaṃ kṛtam| acintayadrākṣasendraḥ sacivaistaiḥ samāvṛtaḥ|| kinimittamicchayā me nedaṃ gacchati puṣpakam| parvatasyopariṣṭhasya karmedaṃ kasyacidbhavet|| tato'bravīttadā rāma mārīco buddhikovidaḥ| nedaṃ niṣkāraṇaṃ rājanpuṣpakaṃ yanna gacchati|| atha vā puṣpakamidaṃ dhanadānānyavāhanam| ato nispandamabhavaddhanādhyakṣavinākṛtam||
reference: The lord of Räkşasas, could not comprehend how the car which had been so made as to course in accordance with the wish of the rider, could have its course impeded; and thereat he in company with his. councillors thought, 'Wherefore does not his Puşpaka course at my desire over this mountain? Whose act is this?' Thereat Mārīca foremost of intelligent ones said, 'That Puspaka does not course cannot, sire, be without cause; or it may be that in consequence of Puşpaka not having borne any other than the bestower of riches, it has ceased its course not having the lord of wealth for its rider.'
baseline: One who has made a gift of a flower or a vehicle for the gift of money should not be allowed to go to the king. One who does not want to go up the mountain should go to a flower house. The king should not leave the flower house or a vessel to give money to a person who has not been given the gift. The chief minister should not make a gift to the lord. One whose wish is to get a flower from the top of the mountain would be given to a priest. The lord would not give it to a king.
morphology: One who has made a gift of a flower or a vehicle to give money to a person who has not been given a gift or a gift to a king or a man who has been given the gift of flowers by the chief minister should say that he would go to the temple with the wish of the king. One who would get the gift from the king would say that the king should remove the gift or the gift should be given to the king or the governor of the temple.

He should be called as Śankara the one who has reached the base of the rock and is standing there from the distance of the goddess. The light is placed in the form of Śula and the second one is named as śankara.

morphology: Having seen him one should know that he is a demon. He should be made to laugh and make his presence felt as if he were sitting there.

morphology: Then the king of the gods should be angry with him. Then he should be ashamed of his position.

The glory of the great goddess is known to be that of the son of a king who is capable of the power of such a thing as madrūpa and the glory of a great king. The monkeys of this clan are said to be destroyed by you.

morphology: Have I the power to kill you. O night watchman have I not killed you. You have not killed him as before by your deeds.

morphology: In the words thus uttered the gods are the sons of the gods the spirits of the sons. The gods and the sons are not to be blamed for the rain of flowers.

morphology: Having thought about it he then said the words Nandīvāla mābhāla. The mountain should be said to be a matter of ten months.

baseline: The stone should be placed on the ground in the direction of the flower and the stone should go to me. That is the source of the stone.
morphology: The stone should be placed in the place where I am going after the movement of the flower. Then I shall make it the source of the stone.

reference: It must be known by what influence Bhavasvara sport here king-like. He does not know that an occasion of fear has presented itself?'
baseline: One who is always playing with the lord and the king should know why. One should not know the place of fear.
morphology: One who is always playing with the lord one who is like a king should not know the place of fear.

baseline: Having liberated him Rama threw him into the mountains by throwing him in his arms. He lifted him up and soon he reached the rock.
morphology: Having liberated him from the clutches of Rama he threw him into the mountains and soon he fell down on the rock.

morphology: Then Rama the great and the master of the gods is worshipped by the goddess Hārā. With the toes of the feet he is attacked by the lilies.

morphology: Then the stone pillar should be placed on the side of the victim. The secretary should protect him from the illusion.

morphology: One should protect the arms with this rosary and then torment them. One should be liberated suddenly by the three worlds. One who trembles should be shaken.

reference: "His councillors considered it the concussion of the thunder at the universal disruption. And then the celestials with Indra at their head shook on their way; and the sea was wild and the mountains shook. And Yakşas and Vidyadharas and Siddhas asked, ""What is this.'"
baseline: Then the gods Indra and Viraśṇu should be worshipped in the morning with the diamond of the mother. Then the goddess Indra should walk around the world the sea the mountains the hills the rivers the fields the knowledge of the yakshas and the sambhāda.
morphology: Then the gods Indra and others walking on the earth and the sea and the mountains in the midst of the darkness would be destroyed by the combination of the elements of the diamond and the diamond in the upper part of the sky. The gods Yaksha and Vidyadhara would be able to do this.
