reference: 'Do you propitiate Uma's lord the bluethroated Mahādeva; for, O Daśānana, save him your refuge see we none in this matter.
baseline: May the lord of the sky be pleased with you. May you see the king of the sea and the king who has taken refuge here.
morphology: May the lord of the sky be pleased with you. May the king of the blue mountains take refuge in you. Let me see you here.

sanskrit: stutibhiḥ praṇato bhūtvā tameva śaraṇaṃ vraja| kṛpāluḥ śaṃkarastuṣṭaḥ prasādaṃ te vidhāsyati ||
reference: Bowing yourself down, do you seek him as your shelter. Then the kind Sankara, on being gratified, will confer on you his favour.
baseline: Having worshipped him with praise one should seek refuge in him. He would be blessed with the gift of the god Shankara.
morphology: Having worshipped him with praise one should seek refuge in him. He would be blessed with the grace of the lord Shankara.

sanskrit: evamuktastadāmātyaistuṣṭāva vṛṣabhadhvajam | samābhirvividhaiḥ stotraiḥ praṇabhya sa daśānanaḥ| saṃvatsarasahasraṃ tu rudato rakṣaso gatam||
reference: Thus accosted by his councillors, the Tenfaced one, bowing down to him having the bull for his standard, began to hymn him with various soma hymns; and the Rākşasa passed away a good thousand years in lamentations.
baseline: Having worshipped him with various hymns he should say that he is free from the evil spirit and should worship the flag of a bull. He should pray ten times a year and cry a thousand times and protect him.
morphology: Having worshipped the bull the flag of the bull and the goddess in the same manner and having worshipped it with various hymns he is said to have wept a thousand times a year and to have saved it.

sanskrit: tataḥ prīto mahādevaḥ śailāne viṣṭhitaṃ prabhuḥ| muktvā cāsya bhujārāma prāha vākyaṃ daśānanam||
reference: Thereat that Lord Mahādeva, pleased, set free the hands of Daśānana stationed at the top of the mount, and O Rāma, addressed him, saying.
baseline: Then the lord standing on the rock should say the following words. Having liberated him he should offer food.
morphology: Then the lord standing on the rock should say the following words. Having liberated him he should offer the bhujara.

sanskrit: prīto'smi tava vīrasya śauṭīryācca daśānana| śailākrāntena yo muktastvayārāvaḥ sudāruṇaḥ|| yasmāllokatrayaṃ caitadrāvitaṃ bhayamāgatam| tasmāttvaṃ rāvaṇo nāma nāmnā rājanbhaviṣyasi ||
reference: O Daśānana, pleased am I with you on account of your hymns. And as in consequence of your arms having been hurt by the mountain, you have uttered a terrific yell, which struck horror into the worlds and put them shaking, therefore, o King, your name shall be Ravana.
baseline: One who is liberated by the battlements of the mountains who is afraid of you and who is fearful of the world will become king in the name of Rāvaṇa.
morphology: I love you for having shown your valour and your strength and for having liberated you from the clutches of the rock. You are the king in the name of Rāvaṇu who is the king of the world and the king who is afraid of you.

sanskrit: devatā mānuṣā yakṣā ye cānye jagatītale| evaṃ tvāmabhidhāsyanti rāvaṇaṃ lokarāvaṇam||
reference: And deities and men, Yakşas and others living on earth shall call you Rāvana terror to creatures,
baseline: The gods men men and women who are in the world will be worshipped by you.
morphology: The gods men men and women who are present in the world would be worshipped by you. Thus you would become the king of the people.

sanskrit: gaccha paulastya visrabdhaṃ pathā yena tvamicchasi| mayā caivābhyanujñāto rākṣasādhipa gamyatām||
reference: Go, O Paulastya, which way you wish with confidence, and permitted by me, O Lord of Raksasas, go you.
baseline: Having gone to Paula he should be thrown down. You may find that which you desire. If you want to go down from me let me go to the king of demons.
morphology: Having gone to Paul he should be thrown down by him. If you wish to go down with me let me go to the demon king.

sanskrit: evamuktastu laṅkeśaḥ : śaṃbhunā svayamabravīt| prīto yadi mahādeva varaṃ me dehi yācataḥ||
reference: Thus accosted by Sambhu, Larkā's lord said of himself. 'If you are pleased with me, grant me a boon, who ask you for it.
baseline: O Sri Lanka one who is liberated from this would have to pray to Sāmbhu himself. One would get the boon of Lord Śiva if he desires it.
morphology: O Sri Lanka one who is liberated from this would pray to Sāmbhu himself. If you wish to give me a boon from the lord of love you should pray to me.

sanskrit: avadhyatvaṃ mayā prāptaṃ devagandharvadānavaiḥ| rākṣasairguhyakai gairye cānye balavattarāḥ||
reference: I have already obtained a boon, bestowing on me immunity from death at the hands of gods, Gandharvas and Dānavas; and Rākşasas and Guyhakas and Nāgas; and others also that are of more than ordinary strength.
baseline: I get the power of the gods and goddesses by offering gifts. The demons should be worshipped in the garbha. The mighty men should be worshiped in the ghuṇa.
morphology: I get the power by offering offerings to gods gods goddesses demons serpents and other powerful beings.

sanskrit: mānuṣāna gaṇe deva svalpāste mama saṃmatāḥ| dīrghamāyuśca meṃ prāptaṃ brahmaṇastripurāntaka| vāñchitaṃ cāyuṣaḥ śeṣaṃ śastraṃ tvaṃ ca prayaccha me||
reference: Man count I not ogod: They, I deem, are insignificant. I have also, O destroyer of Tripura, received a long lease of life from Brahmä. Now I wish to pass the remainder of my days in peace: and do you grant me a weapon.
baseline: I agree that there is little god in the number of men. I have got Brahman Astrī and Purantaka for a long time. The desired desire and the remaining weapon should be given to you.
morphology: The gods in the number of men are small. My consent is long and the one who has got Brahman Astrī Purantaka the one with the desired desire and the weapon should be used by you.

sanskrit: evamuktastatastena rāvaṇena sa śaṃkaraḥ| dadau khaṅgaṃ mahādīptaṃ candrahāsamiti śrutam| āyuṣaścāvaśaṣaṃ ca dadau bhūtapatistadā||
reference: Thus addressed by him, (Ravana,) Sankara gave him an exceedingly effulgent sword, famed as Candrahāsa; and the master of spectres then also granted him peace for the rest of his life.
baseline: Having liberated him he is said to be the god of the gods. Having liberating him from the wrath of Ravana he should be called Shankara. He should be heard as having given the great sword of Dāda the great moon Hāsa Ayūṣa Vāśa and the king as the king of the ghosts.
morphology: He should be liberated from this by Rāvana and should be called Śankara. One should hear that the king should be given the great sword of the moon. One would hear that of the king of the gods Aśuṣa Vāśa and Dāḍa and the king would be destroyed by the ghost.

sanskrit: dattvovāca tataḥ śaṃbhu vajñeyamidaṃ tvayā| avajñātaṃ yadi hi te māmevaiṣyatyasaṃśayaḥ||
reference: And making (the sword) over to him, Sambhu said, “You must not disregard this. If disregarded, it will for certain come (back) to me?'
baseline: Then you should give it to me. If they do not accept it they should leave me.
morphology: Then the Lord should give it to you. If they disobey you they will leave you.

sanskrit: evaṃ maheśveṇaiva kṛtanāmā sa rāvaṇaḥ| abhivādya mahādevamārurohātha puṣpakam||
reference: Having thus received his his name from Mahesvara, Rāvana, saluting Mahadeva, ascended Puspaka.
baseline: The same is said to have been done by Lord Śiva. Having saluted Śivāṇu the king of the gods should offer flowers.
morphology: The same is said to have been done by Lord Śiva. He should be worshipped with the garland of the lord mārūhā.

sanskrit: tato mahītalaṃ rāma paryakrāmata rāvaṇaḥ| kṣatriyānsumahāvīryānbādhamānastatastataḥ|| kecittejasvinaḥ śūrāḥ kṣatriyā yuddhadurmadāḥ| tacchāsanamakurvanto vineśuḥ saparicchadāḥ||
reference: Then, O Rāma, Rāvaņa, began to go round the earth. And opposed at places, by the heroic Kșatriyas endowed with energy and irrepressible in fight, fight, who refused submission, he exterminated them along with their retainers.
baseline: Then the king of the great kingdom of Rāma the king in the course of his journey the kshatriyas the mighty men and the warriors should be bound. Then there should be a group of sages the sages and the warlike men. The king of Vinaśu should be made to sit on the throne with his wife.
morphology: Then the king of the great king Rāma should be circumambulated by Ravana. The kshatriyas should be restrained by the mighty warriors. Then the sages the sage and the warlord should be made to sit in the seat.

sanskrit: apare durjayaṃ rakṣo jānantaḥ prājñasaṃmatāḥ| jitāḥ sma ityabhāṣanta rākṣasaṃ baladarpitam||
reference: "While other men of wisdom, knowing the Räkşasa to be invincible, said to the Rākṣasas elated with strength, ""We have been conquered?”"
baseline: The demon is said to have conquered the enemy and to have saved the enemy. He should be known to be wise. He would have conquered.
morphology: The demon is said to have conquered the enemy and to have saved the enemy by saying that he had won.

sanskrit: te dūtā rāmavākyena coditā laghuvikramāḥ| prajagmurmadhurāṃ śīghraṃ cakrurvāsaṃ na cādhvani||
reference: Having been despatched by Rama, quickmoving emissaries speedily arrived at Mathurā.
baseline: Those angels are the small vikrās who are worshipped by the word of Rama. One should not hear the sound of the chakrūrvasa as soon as possible.
morphology: Those angels are small figures who are attracted by the words of Rama. They do not hear the sound of the chakrūrvasa soon.

sanskrit: tatastribhirahorātraiḥ saṃprāpya mathurāmatha| śatrughnāya yathātattvamācakhyuḥ sarva eva tat||
reference: Continually travelling for three nights and days, they arrived there and communicated to Šatrughna the intelligence.
baseline: Then the enemy should be defeated by the forces of the enemy. The enemy should then be destroyed by the enemy by the enemies. All that happens to him is destroyed by them.
morphology: Then the enemy should be defeated by the forces of the enemy. Then the king should be destroyed by the enemies. The enemy should destroy the enemy with all his might.

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇasya parityāgaṃ pratijñāṃ rāghavasya ca| putrayorabhiṣekaṃ ca paurānugamanaṃ tathā|| kuśasya nagarī ramyā vindhyaparvatarodhasi| kuśāvatīti nāmnā sā kṛtā rāmeṇa dhīmatā||
reference: Having informed him of the renouncing of Lakşmaņa, Rāma's promise and the following of the citizens they said:-The intelligent Rāma has reared for Kuśī the spacious city of Kuśavati at the foot of the Vindhya range.
baseline: The renunciation of Lakshmana the promise of the kingdom of Raghava the consecration of the son of Yārvā the visit to the city of Kṣuśa and the siege of the Vindhya mountains is done by Rama in the name of Kśavaṭī.
morphology: The promise of abandoning Lakshmana and Raghava the ablution of the son the visit of the priest the city of Kusha Ramya and the siege of the Vindhya mountains is done by Rama in the name of Kusa.

sanskrit: śrāvastīti purī ramyā śrāvitā ca lavasya ha| ayodhyā vijanāṃ kṛtvā rāghavo bharatastathā|| svargasya samanodyogaṃ kṛtavantau mahārathau|
reference: The city of Śrāvasti has been reared for Lava, and the mighty car-warriors Rama and Bharata, making Ayodhyā void of men, have addressed themselves for repairing to heaven. Having speedily communicated to him this intelligence the emissaries took rest.
baseline: O Lord of the heavenly abode of the gods Śravasti Puri Ramya Shravita Lava after having vanished from Ayodhya the king of the earth Śrāvata became the king.
morphology: The king of the kingdom of Sravasti the king of Puri the lord of Lava and the king who conquered Ayodhya and made the king Bharata equal to heaven.

sanskrit: evaṃ sarvaṃ nivedyāśu śatrughnāya mahātmane|| viremuste tato dūtāstvara rājeti cābruvan| tacchrutvā ghorasaṃkāśaṃ kulakṣayamupasthitam|| prakṛtīstu samānīya kāñcanaṃ ca purodhasam| teṣāṃ sarvaṃ yathāvṛttamabravīdraghunandanaḥ|||||
reference: There upon they asked Satrughna to proceed soon. Observing the dreadful destruction of his race, Satrughna sent for his subjects and priests and informed them of everything.
baseline: Having thus submitted everything to the enemy the king would be pleased with the meritorious king. The king would then be pleased by the messenger. He would then raise up a garland of cows and make them fall into the pit. He should bring them back to their natural state and offer them the garland. The garland should be offered to him as well as to the king.
morphology: Having thus submitted everything to the enemy the king would be pleased with him. The messenger would then return to the king. Having raised up the sword he would be able to fight the enemy and the enemy would be defeated. He would then bring forth his nature and offer him a bow and bow. He should greet him with all the things that are good for him.

sanskrit: ātmanaśca viparyāsaṃ bhaviṣyaṃ bhrātṛbhiḥ saha| tataḥ putradvayaṃ vīraḥ so'bhyaṣiñcannarādhipaḥ||
reference: He also communicated to them his own destruction with his brothers. There upon the king Satrughna determined upon installing his two sons in the kingdom.
baseline: Then there will be a difference between the self and the brethren. Then the king will have two sons who are mighty.
morphology: Then there will be a contradiction between the self and the brethren. Then the king will have two sons who will be mighty.

sanskrit: subāhurmathurāṃ lebhe śatrughātī ca vai diśam| dvidhā kṛtvā tu tāṃ senāṃ mādhurī putrayordvayoḥ| dhanaṃ ca yuktaṃ kṛtvā sthāpayāmāsa pārthivaḥ|| subāhuṃ madhurāyāṃ ca vaidiśe śatrughātinam| yayau sthāpya tadāyodhyāṃ rathenaikena rāghavaḥ||
reference: Subāhu was placed on the throne of Mathurā and Satrughāti became the king of Vidiśā. Having thus established Subāhu in Mathură, and Śatrughātī in Vidiśā, the great hero Satrughna ascended his car and went to Ayodhyā.
baseline: Having placed the subahurmāthura in the same direction as that of the enemy and the enemy in the opposite direction. Having divided it into two parts one should place it in the army and the sons of the goddess and the other in the middle of the battle. Having placed it in a place containing wealth the earthly king should place the subaha the king of the kingdom and the king who had killed the enemy on the opposite side in the war. The raghavas should be placed in the midst of the fight with the charioteer.
morphology: Having divided the army into two parts the subahurma and the enemy and the assassin in the same direction. Having divided it the king should place it in the middle of the chariot and the king of the enemy in the opposite direction. The king of earth should put it in subahū and māudira and the two sons should have the wealth. Having placed it in a place where the enemy is killed.

sanskrit: vai sa dadarśa mahātmānaṃ jvalantamiva pāvakam| sūkṣmakṣaumāmbaradharaṃ munibhiḥ sārdhamakṣayaiḥ|| so'bhivādya tato rāmaṃ prāñjaliḥ prayatendriyaḥ| uvāca vākyaṃ dharmajñaṃ dharmamevānucintayan||
reference: And there he saw the great Rāma, clothed in silk raiment burning like fire in the midst of the ascetics. There upon remembering his duty he saluted Rāma, conversant with piety and with folded hands said.
baseline: He should be described as having a great spirit fiery spirit and pure nature. Having said this he should be worshipped by the sages as having four eyes. He should say that Rama Pranjali Prāyateśṇī and others are worshipped. Having thought of the righteousness of the people.
morphology: He should be described as having a great spirit fiery spirit and pure nature. He should also be worshipped by the sages as having four eyes. The words rāma pranjali prāyateṇī rāmā dhārmā and rāhmā are mentioned in the scriptures.

sanskrit: kṛtvāviṣekaṃ sutayordvayo rāghavanandana| tavānugamane rājanviddhimāṃ kṛtaniścayam|| na cānyadadya vaktavyamato vīra na śāsanam| vihanyamānamicchāmi madvidhena viśeṣataḥ|| tasya tāṃ buddhimaklībāṃ vijñāya raghunandanaḥ| bāḍhamityeva śatrughnaṃ rāmo vākyamuvāca ha||
reference: I have placed my two sons on the throne of my kingdom. I have now resolved upon following you, O King. O hero, do not command me otherwise. I pray only that I may not neglect your command. There upon understanding the firm resolution of Satrughna, the descendant of Raghu agreed.
baseline: Having said that the king should not be called a warrior. Having said this he should not rule the kingdom. Having known that the king is wise. Having done this and having said this to the king he would not be able to do so. I would like to make him obeisance with the words of Raghunandana. Having explained the words to him and the wise man the son of Satrughṇa would be destroyed.
morphology: Having said that the king should not be judged to be a hero or a ruler. Having said this to me I would like to say that Raghunandana should be defeated by me. Having known that the king is wise and wise and having said that to me. The king should be destroyed by me the sage Raghunandan.

sanskrit: tasya vākyasya vākyānte vānarāḥ kāmarūpiṇaḥ| ṛkṣarākṣasasaṅghāśca samāpeturanekaśaḥ||
reference: Immediately after Råma had said this, monkeys assuming shapes at will bears and Rākşasas, began to assemble there.
baseline: At the end of his speech the monkeys and the kāmārupas are said to be the group of rakshasas.
morphology: At the end of his speech the monkeys and Kamarupas are said to be the group of rakshasas.

sanskrit: sugrīvaṃ te puraskṛtya sarva eva samāgatāḥ| taṃ rāmaṃ draṣṭumanasaḥ svargāyābhimukhaṃ sthitam|| devaputrā ṛṣisutā gandharvāṇāṃ sutāstathā|
reference: Apprised of Rama's determination of going to heaven, monkeys, born of the celestials, Rșis and Gandharvas taking Sugriva before them, came there to see Rama.
baseline: Having worshipped the goddess Sugriva they all come together. Having seen him one should observe him standing facing the sky. The son of God the sage Sūṣu the son of Gandharva and the king of the Gandharvas should be worshipped.
morphology: Having worshipped the goddess Sugriva they all come together. Having seen him standing facing the sky with the face of the mind the son of God the sage Sūsuta and the god Gandharva are worshipped.

sanskrit: rāmakṣayaṃ viditvā te sarva eva samāgatāḥ|| tavānugamane rājansaṃprāptāḥ sma samāgatāḥ| yadi rāma vināsmābhirgacchestvaṃ puruṣocama|| yamadaṇḍamivodyamya tvayā sma vinipātitāḥ| etasminnantare rāmaṃ sugrīvo'pi mahābalaḥ| praṇamya vidhivadvīraṃ vijñāpayitumudyataḥ|21|| abhiṣicyāṅgadaṃ vīramāgato'smi nareśvara| tavānugamane rājanviddhimāṃ kṛtaniścayam||
reference: "All they came there knowing the departure of Rāma to heaven and said: ""O Răma, O foremost of men, if you do repair to heaven forsaking us all, it will be hurling Yama's rod upon us.” The highly powerful Sugrīva too saluting Rāma said:— lord of men, having placed Angada on the throne I have come hither. I have determined upon following you, O King."
baseline: Having known the loss of Rama they all come together. If the king is found to be in the midst of the fall of the river they will come together and if the king goes without us the king will go away as if he were a man. Having said that you have fallen down. In the meantime after having worshipped him the great king the lord the god of good and evil you will come back home. Having worshipped the king I will return the body of the king. The king has made a determination to go down.
morphology: Having known the loss of Rama they all come together. If the king is found to be on the way to him he would join them. If he leaves without us the king would go away as if he were a man and you would be destroyed. Then after having worshipped him the great king the lord of good and evil would come back home. Having worshipped the king he should return home with his body. The king would have made a decision to go back to him.

sanskrit: tairevamuktaḥ kākutstho bāḍhamityabravītsmayan| bibhīṣaṇamathovāca rākṣasendraṃ mahāyaśāḥ|| yāvatprajā dhariṣyanti tāvattvaṃ vai bibhīṣaṇa| rākṣasendra mahāvīrya laṅkāsthaḥ svaṃ dhariṣyasi|| yāvaccandraśca sūryaśca yāvattiṣṭhati medinī| yāvacca matkathā loke tāvadrājyaṃ tavāstviha||25
reference: Hearing the words of monkeys, Rāma said that their desire would be fulfilled. He then said to Vibhīşaņa the king of Räkşasas:-As long as people shall breathe, O Vibhisana, O highly powerful lord of Rakşasas, you shall preserve your body in Lankä. As long as the moon, the sun and the earth shall exist and as long as my story shall remain current, your kingdom shall be in existence.
baseline: The king of Lanka will be caught by the king of Yavatmal. The king who is the kings son the king and the sun will be captured by the lord of Yavata. He will be taken by the great king of the kingdom of Vībhīṣṇa. He who is free from evil will be conquered by the mighty king. He would be taken away by the queen of the kingdoms of the two great kingdoms. He should be given the king's kingdom.
morphology: One who is free from evil will be blessed with a cow a cow and a cow. One who has said that the king of the world would be a demon a king of great powers one who would be possessed by the king would be held by the mighty king of Lanka. One holding himself by the great king of demons by the lord of the earth by him who is a king and by the sun would become a king. One should say that he would possess the kingdom of the king.

sanskrit: śāsitaśca sakhitvena kārya te mama śāsanam| prajāḥ saṃrakṣa dharmeṇa nottaraṃ vaktumarhasi|| kiṃcānyadvaktumicchāmi rākṣasendra mahābala| ārādhaya jagatrāthamikṣvākukuladaivatam|| ārādhanīyamaniśaṃ deverapi savāsavaiḥ| tatheti pratijagrāha rāmavākyaṃ bibhīṣaṇaḥ| rājā rākṣasamukhyānāṃ rāghavājñāmanusmaran|28||
reference: You did, out of friendship, carry out my behests and perform my works. Do you piously govern your subjects. I should not speak any thing else. What shall I say more to you, O highly powerful lord of Rakşasas. Worshhip Jagannath (the lord of the world), the presiding deity of the Ikşvāku race.
baseline: The ruler should act with sincerity. He should speak to the people with the principle of protection. Having said this he should say something to the king. Having worshipped the king of the world Sagendra and Mahabala the king should worship the gods of the earth the gods the goddess of the universe the lord of the gods and the gods. Having spoken the words of Rama and the king the chief of the kings and the chieftains of the demons and the commandments of Raghava.
morphology: The king should worship the king of the world the king the chieftain the lord of the gods the god of the universe the great king and the king who is the chief of the kingdoms the ruler of the kingdom of the country the supreme ruler king of king king lord of kings chief of kings and lord of gods.

sanskrit: tamevamuktvā kākutstho hanūmantamathābravīt| jīvite kṛtabuddhistvaṃ mā pratijñāṃ vṛthā kṛthāḥ||29 matkathāḥ parcariṣyanti yāvalloke harīśvara| tāvadramasva suprīto madvākyamanupālayan|30|| evamuktastu hanumānarāghaveṇa mahātmanā| vākyaṃ vijñāpayāmāsa paraṃ harṣamavāpa ca|31|| yāvattava kathā loke vicariṣyati pāvanī| tāvatsthāsyāmi medinyāṃ tavājñāmanupālayan||
reference: Having thus addressed the king of Rakşasas always obeying Rāghava's command, Käkutstha said to Hanumān:— It is settled that you shall live forever, do you, now observe your promise. As long as my history shall run current in this world do you at my command live happily. Being thus addressed by the high-souled Rāghava Hanumān attained to great delight and said. As long as the sacred theme shall pass current in this world I shall live here carrying out your commands.
baseline: Having redeemed him the king of the cow the son of Hanumanta the chief minister of the kingdom of Bihar the governor of the princely state of Bihar and the governor should not make a promise to the king. He would not let go of the promise made to him by the time of his death. The king would say to the people that he would be free from the wrath of Lord Hārīśvara the lord of the universe the supreme god of the world the god of war the great lord of gods hāṇu raghavana and the king would
morphology: Having redeemed him he should say the words of Hanumanta the son of the great king. Having said these words to the people that he had promised him not to do so in vain he would not be able to understand the promise made to him in his lifetime. He would have said to the Lord Hari the lord of the world the king of the king the supreme lord the god of the gods and the great man who had spoken the word hāṇu raghavana the word of joy and wapas. The people would have heard the words that the king would have spoken

sanskrit: yāvatkaliśca saṃprāptastāvajjīvata sarvadā|| jāmbavantaṃ tathoktvā tu vṛddhaṃ brahmasutaṃ tadā| maindaṃ ca dvividaṃ caiva pañca jāmbavatā saha|
reference: There upon he said to the Jämbavān, Brahma's son, Mainda, Dvivida and five others in his company: “As long as the Kali age exists do you all live.”
baseline: Having obtained the jambavatakālī and having attained the yavātakāli and having said so the old man would always be able to get a jambava. Then he would get the brahmāsutā with five jambavatas.
morphology: The old man would always be a jambava with five jambavatas. Having said that the old man should be a brahmasutā with two cubits and five cubits.

sanskrit: tadevamuktvā kākutsthaḥ sarvāṃstānṛkṣavānarān| uvāca bāḍhaṃ gacchadhvaṃ mayā sādhaṃ yathoditam||
reference: Having thus addressed them all Kākuthstha said to bears and monkeys. Do you come all with me.
baseline: Having liberated him he should leave all the trees in the forest. He should say to them go to Baradha. I have said this to you.
morphology: Having liberated the same from the hands of the enemy he should leave all the trees. He should go to Baradha and say that he would be able to do so.

sanskrit: kṛtabuddhiṃ nivāsāya tatraiva sa munistadā| bharataṃ kekayīputramātithyena nyamantrayat||
reference: Then the ascetic asked Bharata, the son of Kaikeyi, when he had decided for staying there, to receive his hospitality.
baseline: The sage should be placed in the place where he has made his mind to reside. He should be worshipped with the son of Bharata as the chief guest.
morphology: The sage should be placed in the place where the wisdom is made to reside. The son of Bharata should be worshipped by the priest.

sanskrit: abravīd bharatastvenaṃ nanvidaṃ bhavatā kṛtam| pādyamaya̭mathātithyaṃ vane yadupapadyate||
reference: Thereat Bharata said, “You have for certain done this, (have offered me) water for washing my feet, Arghya, and hospitality with what can be procured in the forest.
baseline: O Abravi O Bharata thou hast made a promise to me. You have done it. You will find it in the forest.
morphology: O Abravi you have done unto me a great work. You have done to me. If you go into the forest you will get it.

sanskrit: athovāca bharadvājo bharataṃ prahasanniva| jāne tvāṃ prītisaṃyuktaṃ tuṣyestvaṃ yena kenacit||
reference: "Then Bharadvāja as if in jest, said to Bharata, ""I know you to be of a complacent disposition; and that you are pleased with anything and everything."""
baseline: O Bharādvāja the one who invents the word Bharāṭha one who knows that you are endowed with the qualities of love would see you as if he were a man.
morphology: O Bharādvāja the one who invents Bharātha one who knows that you are endowed with love would see you.

sanskrit: senāyāstu tavaivāsyāḥ kartumicchāmi bhojanam| mama prītiyathārūpā tvamarho manujarṣabha||
reference: But I wish to feast your forces. And, O best of men, it behoves you to act in harmony with my desire.
baseline: I shall serve food for you in the army. You are my beloved son. You have made me the son of a man.
morphology: I shall give food to those who live in the army. My beloved son of thee O Lord of men you are the best of men.

sanskrit: kimarthaṃ cāpi nikṣipya dūre balamihāgataḥ| kasmānnehopayāto'si sabalaḥ puruṣarṣabha||
reference: Why did you coming higher, leave your army at a distance:? And, you man of men, why did you not come accompanied with your forces?
baseline: Why should a strong man who has the ability to fight a man go far away after having been thrown away by a thief.
morphology: Why should one who is a strong man be thrown away and come away strong? One who is strong enough to fight against the enemy should be called strong.

sanskrit: bharataḥ pratyuvācedaṃ prāñjalistaṃ tapodhanam| na sainyenopayāto'smi bhagavan bhagavadbhayāt||
reference: Bharata replied to him, saying, “I had not come accompanied with my forces, from fear of you, O reverend Sir.”
baseline: One should not fear the Lord of the universe. One would not suffer in the army. He would not be afraid of the Lord.
morphology: One should not fear the Lord God. One would not suffer in the army.

sanskrit: rājñā hi bhagavan nityaṃ rājaputreṇa vā tathā| yatnataḥ parihartavyā viṣayeṣu tapasvinaḥ||
reference: O worshipful one, kings and their sons should always carefully avoid the regions of ascetics.
baseline: The king should always be the lord of the king or the king of the prince. One should try to avoid these things by doing penance.
morphology: The king should always be the lord of the king or the king of the prince. One should try to avoid such things by doing asceticism.

sanskrit: vājimukhyā manuṣyāśca mattāśca varavāraṇāḥ| pracchādya bhagavan bhūmiṃ mahatīmanuyānti mām||
reference: Choice steeds, men, and mad elephants of the best kind, covering a spacious tract of country, come in my train, respected Sir.
baseline: The forefathers men men and women are the manifestations of good deeds. By covering the earth the lord gives me great glory.
morphology: The forefathers men men and men should be worshipped. The lord of the earth is great by covering the earth.

sanskrit: te vṛkṣānudakaṃ bhūmimāśrameṣūṭajāṃstathā| na hiṃsyuriti tenāhameka evāgatastataḥ||
reference: That these might not injure trees or water or the grounds of the cottages pertaining to the asylums, have I come hither alone.
baseline: They should be made of the same kind of wood as the ground and the same form of grass. They should not be made to suffer. They must not be brought into the same place.
morphology: They should be made of the same kind of wood as the ground and the same form of grass. They should not be made to suffer violence. Then they should be brought to us.

sanskrit: ānīyatāmitaḥ senetyājñaptaḥ paramarṣiṇā| tathānucakre bharataḥ senāyāḥ samupāgamam||
reference: """Bring the forces here,"", thus desired by the mighty ascetic, Bharata accordingly caused the troops to be brought in."
baseline: One who is brought to the army should be known as Paramāśiṇa. One who comes from India should be called to the side of the army.
morphology: One who brings the army with him is known to be the supreme sage. Then the army should be called from India in the same manner.

sanskrit: agniśālāṃ praviśyātha pītvāpaḥ parimṛjya ca| ātithyasya kriyāhetorviśvakarmāṇamāhvayat||
reference: Then entering the chamber of the sacrificial fire, (Bharadvāja) having sipped water and rubbed his lips therewith, invoked Viśvakarmā for the purpose of entertaining his guest.
baseline: Having entered into the fire house and having purified it from the indignities of the brethren he should offer the worldly goods for the purpose of hospitality.
morphology: Having entered into the fire house one should purify himself from the evil spirits. One should offer the gifts of the world for the sake of the acts of hospitality.

sanskrit: āhvaye viśvakarmāṇamahaṃ tvaṣṭārameva ca| ātithyaṃ kartumicchāmi tatra me saṃvidhīyatām||
reference: I invoke Visvakarmā; even Tvasta himself. I wish to entertain guests. Let him accomplish this for me.
baseline: I am the master of the universe by calling you. I shall perform the ceremony of hospitality there.
morphology: I am the master of the universe by calling you. I shall perform the ceremony therein.

sanskrit: āhvayelokapālāṃstrīn devāśakrapurogamān| ātithyaṃ kartumicchāmi tatra me saṃvidhīyatām||
reference: I invoke the three guardians of the worlds, gods headed by Sakra. I wish to entertain guests. Let them accomplish this for me,
baseline: I shall call the men and women of the household of the gods and the people of the world. I shall make a feast therein.
morphology: The women of the temple should be called to worship the gods and goddesses. I shall make a ceremony there to welcome you.

sanskrit: prāksrotasaśca yā nadyastiryaksrotasa eva ca| pṛthivyāmantarikṣe ca samāyāntvadya sarvaśaḥ||
reference: Let those rivers that flow westwards, and those that move tortuously on the earth and in the sky, come hither in a body.
baseline: One who is the source of the earth and the other parts of the world should be placed at the same place in all directions.
morphology: One who is the source of the earth and the other parts of the world should be blessed with the prāksrāsūtra.

sanskrit: anyāḥ sravantu maireyaṃ surāmanyāḥ suniṣṭhitām| aparāścodakaṃ śītamikṣukāṇḍarasopamam||
reference: And let others run Maireya, and others refined wine, and others again cool waters resembling the juice of the sugarcane.
baseline: The other one should be made to flow in the form of a mairai and the other one is made to sit in the shape of a suramani. The other two are made to be made of water.
morphology: The other one should be made to flow from the sun and the other one is made to sit on the sun. The other two are made of water and water.

sanskrit: āhvaye devagandharvān viśvāvasuhahāhuhūn| tathaivāpsaraso devagandharvaiścāpi sarvaśaḥ||
reference: I invoke the celestials and the Gandharvas and Viśvāvasu and Hahā and Huhu and also the divine Apsaras and Gandharvis all.
baseline: O Lord of the gods and goddesses of the world oh Gods and goddess of the universe you should believe in the invocation.
morphology: O Lord of the gods and goddesses of the world oh Gods and goddess of the universe are called to you.

sanskrit: ghṛtācīmatha viśvācī miśrakeśīmalambuṣām| nāgadattāṃ ca hemāṃ ca somāmadrikṛtasthalīm||
reference: And Ghịtâcī, Viśvācī, Misrakesi and Alambuşā; and Nāgadattā and Hemā and Somā residing in the mountain.
baseline: One who has made a place of worship with the garhrita chīmtha viśva kesi malambu nāga dattā haemā soma and mādrīktā is known to be a great place.
morphology: The image of the earth is of the form of a lotus and the image of a serpent and the place of the heart of the serpent is known to be the place where the cow is worshipped.

sanskrit: śakraṃ yāścopatiṣṭhanti brahmāṇaṃ yāśca bhāminīḥ| sarvāstumburuṇā sārdhamāhvaye saparicchadāḥ||
reference: And those ladies that attend Sakra, and those that attend Brahmā. I invoke all these females well attired, in company with Tumuru.
baseline: The king of Brahman and the queen of Bhāmīs are said to be having four sons and one daughter. All these sons and daughters should be worshipped in the temple.
morphology: The king of Brahman and the king of Bhāmī are the sons of śakra who are the heirs of the king. All the sons and daughters of āmburuṇa and others are the members of the family.

sanskrit: vanaṃ kuruṣu yad divyaṃ vāsobhūṣaṇapatravat| divyanārīphalaṃ śaśvat tatkauberamihaiva tu||
reference: And let that beautiful forest of Kubera in the north Kuru, having its foliage resembling attires and ornaments, and its fruits debonair damsels, exist even at this very spot.
baseline: One should make the forest as a gift of the divine. One should give the fruit of the celestial gift as a fragrance. That is the same as that of the king.
morphology: One who makes the forest as a gift of the divine as if he were a flower would get the fruit of the god and that would be the same.

sanskrit: iha bhagavān somo vidhattāmannamuttamam| bhakṣyaṃ bhojyaṃ ca coṣyaṃ ca lehyaṃ ca vividhaṃ bahu|| vicitrāṇi ca mālyāni pādapapracyutāni ca| surādīni ca peyāni māṃsāni vividhāni ca|||
reference: And here let the worshipful Soma yield me excellent viands of diverse kinds in plenty; things; that may be eaten or enjoyed, sucked or licked; and variegated blossoms growing in the trees, and wines and (other) drinks, and meats of various kinds.
baseline: O lord of the universe you have to eat food suckle drink drink and meat. You have to be careful of many things. You get a lot of strange things fruits and plants. Drinks and meat etc.
morphology: O lord of the universe you have to eat food suckle drink drink and meat. Many things are found to be strange and many things are removed from plants and plants. You have to drink wine and meat etc.

sanskrit: evaṃ samādhinā yuktastejasāpratimena ca| śikṣāsvarasamāyuktaṃ suvrataścābravīnmuniḥ||
reference: Thus, furnished with unrivalled ascetic energy, did that anchorite observing excellent vows, express himself orthoepically in consonance with Śikṣā.
baseline: In this way the image of the goddess is associated with the samadhi and the image with the sāmya and the golden form with the time of learning is described by the lord Brahma.
morphology: In this way the image of the goddess is associated with the samadhi and the image with the sāmya and the golden form with the time of learning is described as sublime.

sanskrit: manasā dhyāyatastasya prāmukhasya kṛtāñjaleḥ| ājagmustāni sarvāṇi daivatāni pṛthak pṛthak || me
reference: And as he sat with joined hands facing the west with a rapt mind, there came separately all those deities.
baseline: The mind should meditate on the face of the earth. All these gods are different.
morphology: The mind should meditate on the face of the earth. All these gods should be separated from each other.

sanskrit: malayaṃ darduraṃ caiva tataḥ svedanudo'nilaḥ| upaspṛśya vavau yuktyā supriyātmā sukhaṃ śivaḥ||
reference: And then touching Malaya and Dardura, and laden (with perfumes), a delicious and welcome wind began to blow delightfully, removing sweat.
baseline: Then after having worshipped the goddess malaya dardura one would be able to enjoy the soul of lord Śiva by the subjunctive touch and by the tactile gesture.
morphology: Then one who has eaten malai dardura and then had a sweet bath would be able to reach the upper part of the body and enjoy the spirit of the lord Śiva.

sanskrit: tato'bhyavarṣanta ghanā divyāḥ kusumavṛṣṭayaḥ| devadundubhighoṣaśca dikṣu sarvāsu śuśruve||
reference: And the clouds poured down a pleasant shower of blossoms; and from all sides were heard sounds of celestial kettle-drums.
baseline: Then the rain should be thick and the rain of water should be lustrous. The sound of the gods and the sound of thunder should be seen in all places.
morphology: Then the rain should be thick and the rain of water should be light. The sound of the gods should be heard in all places.

sanskrit: pravavuścottamā vātā nanṛtuścāpsarogaṇāḥ| prajagurdevagandharvā vīṇāḥ pramumucuḥ svarān ||
reference: And a rare breeze set in, and the multitudes of Apsaras danced; and the celestials and the Gandharvas sang, and the Vinas let out their notes.
baseline: The swords are of the highest order flowing flowing and flowing. The swarams are of four kinds. The hymns are of guṇas gods goddesses harps and harps.
morphology: The sound of the rivers rivers streams rivers and rivers are the most important. The sound is heard by the people gods goddesses and goddesses.

sanskrit: sa śabdo dyāṃ ca bhūmī ca prāṇināṃ śravaṇāni ca| viveśoccāvacaḥ ślakṣṇaḥ samo layaguṇānvitaḥ||
reference: And the dulcet sounds high and low furnished with Sama and measure, entered the Earth and the firmament and the ears of all creatures.
baseline: He should give words land animals hearing sound sound and sound. He should be able to hear the voice of the living beings.
morphology: He should give words the earth the hearing of the creatures the voice of the world the sound of the sky the rhythm of the voice and the sound.

sanskrit: tasminnevaṃgate śabde divye śrotrasukhe nṛṇām| dadarśa bhārataṃ sainyaṃ vidhānaṃ viśvakarmaṇaḥ||
reference: When that celestial symphony delightful to the ears of men, had thus developed itself, Bharata's forces saw the workmanship of Visvakarman.
baseline: In the same way the divine should be heard in the words of the Sātrakshaṇa and the king should be seen in the form of Bharatāṇa. The army should be declared by Vīśvakrāma.
morphology: In the same way the gods should be heard in the same manner. The king should be pleased with the hearers. The army of India should be described as the army of the king.

sanskrit: babhūva hi samā bhūmiḥ samantāt pañcayojanam| śādvalairbahubhiśchannā nīlavaidūryasaṃnibhaiḥ||
reference: That spot widening into a level plain measuring five Yojanas was covered with thick grass resembling blue lapises.
baseline: This is the five measures of the ground in the equator. It should be divided into two parts. The distance between the two sides should be blue.
morphology: This is the five measures of the ground. The five measures are equal to the distance of the earth. The four lines are blue white and blue.

sanskrit: tasmin bilvāḥ kapitthāśca panasā bījapūrakāḥ| āmalakyo babhūvuśca cūtāśca phalabhūṣitāḥ||
reference: And on it stood Bilvas, and Kapitthas, Panasas, citrons, and Amalakas, and mangoes, embellished with fruits.
baseline: In that the bilva kapita pancha sesamum amla ghee pigeon pea and fruits are found.
morphology: The bilva kapita pancha sesamum amla pigeon pea and fruit are found in it.

sanskrit: uttarebhyaḥ kurubhyaśca vanaṃ divyopabhogavat| ājagāma nadī saumyā tīrajairbahubhirvṛtā||
reference: From the north Kuru had spread a wood capable of conferring every enjoyment; and a beautiful river coursed through bordered by many a tree.
baseline: The forest is like the enjoyment of the goddess from the north and the forest from the south. The river Ajgama is like a river and the river Sūmya is like that of the sea.
morphology: The forest should be spread from the north and from the east as if it were a divine enjoyment. The river Ajgama the river Saumya the rivers flowing from the shore and the sky should be covered with water.

sanskrit: catuḥśālāni śubhrāṇi śālāśca gajavājinām| harmyaprāsādasaṃyuktatoraṇāni śubhāni ca|| sitameghanibhaṃ cāpi rājaveśma sutoraṇam| śuklamālyakṛtākāraṃ divyagandhasamukṣitam|| caturasramasambādhaṃ śayanāsanayānavat| divyaiḥ sarvarasairyuktaṃ divyabhojanavastravat|| upakalpitasarvānnaṃ dhautanirmalabhājanam| klṛptasarvāsanaṃ śrīmatsvāstīrṇaśayanottamam||
reference: And there had arisen white edifices having four divisions; and stables for horses and elephants; and grand gateways belonging to places and mansions; and royal residences with graceful gates, resembling white clouds, bearing white garlands and washed with fragrant waters, having four corners, and spacious, fitted up with beds, seats, and vehicles, having every kind of excellent sapid food, stocked with excellent edibles and apparels, having every variety of food, possessing washed and bright vessels, with every description of seats, graceful, and accommodated with choice beds with coverlets.
baseline: The four palaces the white ones the palaces and the elephant garlands the walls of the palace and the palace are good and the king's garlands are covered with white sandals and the garlands with gold and gold. The garlands made of sukla malya the fragrance of the divine fragrance are made of sandals. The chaturasrama garland is made of the garland of the celestial elements and is made like a bed and the mantle of the goddess is made up of cow cow and pearls. The best seat is made from the garb
morphology: The four shalas are white the chariot the elephant the mace the palace and the walls of the palace. The king's garlands are made of white cloth and the garlands of gold and gold. The garlands made of silver and gold are made up of gold made of sandal and gold and made of fragrance. The carvings made of gold are like the bedding of a square ram made with the garland of the divine ghee made from the garb of the celestial god Sarva and made from cloth made of the elements of the gods

sanskrit: praviveśa mahābāhuranujñāto maharṣiṇā| veśma tad ratnasampūrṇa bharataḥ kaikayīsutaḥ|| anujagmuśca te sarve mantriṇaḥ sapurohitāḥ| babhūvuśca mudā yuktāstaṃ dṛṣṭvā veśmasaṃvidhim||
reference: Permitted by the Maharsi, Kaikeyi's son, Bharata, entered that mansion abounding in gems. And he was followed by the counsellors and the priests; and the latter beholding the arrangements of the palace, were filled with delight.
baseline: Having seen that the great sage had entered and had accepted the offer made by him he would have to pay tribute to him. Having seen the gift made by the king all the ministers would have been taken away from him. Seeing that he had not been given the gift he should have done the same.
morphology: Having seen that the great sage had entered the temple and had accepted it he said that he would get it from India with all the jewels. He would get all the ministers of the world. Seeing that he had got it and had done it, he said to him that he should do the same.

sanskrit: tatra rājāsanaṃ divyaṃ vyajanaṃ chatrameva ca| bharato mantribhiḥ sārdhamabhyavartata rājavat||
reference: And Bharata in company with the counsellors there went round the august royal seat, the chowri, and the umbrella, worthy of a king. And having bowed down to Rāma, he worshipped that seat.
baseline: There the seat of the king is the divine seat and the mantras are the same. The king should be made to walk around with the ministers of the kingdom.
morphology: The seat of the king should be placed there in the form of a divine mantra. The king should move around with the ministers of Bharata.

sanskrit: āsanaṃ pūjayāmāsa rāmāyābhipraṇamya ca| vālavyajanamādāya nyaṣīdat sacivāsane||
reference: And then holding the chowri of hair, he sat down on the seat of a minister.
baseline: The seat should be worshipped in the month of Ramāya and should be placed in the seat of the secretary.
morphology: The seat should be worshipped in the month of Ramāya. The priest should be placed in the seat of the secretary.

sanskrit: ānupūrvyāniṣeduśca sarve mantripurohitāḥ| tataḥ senāpatiḥ paścāt praśāstā ca nyaṣīdata||
reference: Then the counsellors and priests seated themselves according to rank. And thereafter the general and the protector of the encampment (got themselves seated).
baseline: Then the chief minister should be placed in charge of all the ministers. Then the governor should be put in charge.
morphology: Then the chief minister should be placed in charge of all the ministers. Then the governor should be put in charge.

sanskrit: tatastatra muhūrtena nadyaḥ pāyasakardamāḥ| upātiṣṭhanta bharataṃ bharadvājasya śāsanāt||
reference: Then at Bharadvāja's command, came into being near Bharata streams having Pāyasa for their slime.
baseline: Then the rivers are made to flow with the muhurta. The king of Bharādvāja is said to have established the kingdom of Bharat.
morphology: Then the rivers are made to flow with the muhurta. The king of Bharata should be worshipped with the prāṣaka of Bharadwaja.

sanskrit: āsāmubhayataḥ kūlaṃ pāṇḍumṛttikalepanāḥ| ramyāścāvasathā divyā brāhmaṇasya prasādajāḥ||
reference: And at the pleasure of the Brāhmaṇa, on both their banks arose charming dwellings, covered with pale clay.
baseline: One should worship the gods of the Brahmanas with the sand and sand of Pandu. The goddess Ramya should be worshipped with the prasadam of Brahmana.
morphology: The temple should be made of sand and sand. The temple of Rama should be placed in the form of offerings to the Brahmana.

sanskrit: tenaiva ca muhūrtena divyābharaṇabhūṣitāḥ| āgurviṃśatisāhasrā brāhmaṇā prahitāḥ striyaḥ|||
reference: And at that very moment there came twenty thousand women commissioned by Brahma, adorned with divine ornaments.
baseline: Those women who were killed by the brahmins would be adorned with divine ornaments with the same muhurta.
morphology: Those women who were killed by the brahmins in the previous hundred years were adorned with divine ornaments with the muhurta.

sanskrit: suvarṇamaṇimuktena pravālena ca śobhitāḥ| āgurviṃśatisāhasrāḥ kuberaprahitāḥ striyaḥ|| yābhirgṛhītaḥ puruṣaḥ sonmāda iva lakṣyate|
reference: And there came also twenty thousand females sent by Kuvera, decked out in gold and gems, pearls and corals. The sight of these was capable of filling men's mind with enchanting ravishment.
baseline: The golden beads are adorned with the free flowing water and the women are worshipped by the lord Kubera. The men are seen as having gold in the form of gold.
morphology: Having been adorned with gold and gold ornaments and flowing water the women who had been attacked by Kubera would be seen as having lost their husband.

sanskrit: āgurviṃśatisāhasrā nandanādapsarogaṇāḥ|| nāradastumbururgopaḥ prabhayā sūryavarcasaḥ| ete gandharvarājāno bharatasyāgrato jaguḥ||
reference: And there came from Nandana twenty thousand damsels; and Nārada and Tumburů and Gopa, resembling the sun in splendour. The Gandharba kings began to sing before Bharata.
baseline: The king of Gandharvas should be worshipped with the garlands of Nandā Nāda Naṇḍa Uśāśa Sāhasa Sūrya Garuśa and Prabhava. These are the kings of Gandhārva Bharata and Jagu.
morphology: The king of Gandharvas should be worshipped with the garlands of Nandā Nāda Naṇḍa and Sāśara. These are the kings of Gandhārā Bharata and Surya.

sanskrit: alambuṣā miśrakeśī puṇḍarīkātha vāmanā| upānṛtyanta bharataṃ bharadvājasya śāsanāt||
reference: And Alambusa, and Misrakesi, and Puņdarīka, and Vāmana danced before Bharata, at the command of Bharadvāja.
baseline: O alambuṣa misra keshi pundarikātha vamana the king of Bharādvājā is worshipped by the king.
morphology: O alambuṣa the one who is in the middle of the mountain and who is on the left side of the pundra the king of Bharadwaja should be worshipped.
