sanskrit: ko'sau parvatasaṃkāśo dhanuṣmānharilocanaḥ| yukte hayasahasreṇa viśāle syandane sthitaḥ|| ya eṣa niśitaiḥ śūlaiḥ sutīkṣṇaiḥ prāsatomaraiḥ| arciṣmadbhirvṛto bhāti bhūtairiva maheśvaraḥ|| kālajihvāprakāśābhirya eṣo'bhivirājate| āvṛto rathaśaktībhirvidyudbhiriva toyadaḥ||
reference: Who is this one resembling a mountain, furnished with a bow and having leonine eyes, that is stationed on a large car hoked with a thousand steeds, he that with effulgent sharpened darts and keen práśas and tomaras, shine like Maheśvara environed by spectres-he that displaying his fatal tongue appear splendid surrounded with darts in his car; like a mass of clouds graced with lightning.
baseline: One who sits on a mountain with a lotus a bow a spear a mace a large sardine with a high armour and a broad armour in the middle of the mountain is said to be a great king. One who stands on a sandal with a mound of sandals a sword a sage a priest a demon a man of good fortune a lord of gods a king who is known to have illuminated the sky with the light of a kālajiva a charioteer a warrior a mighty warrior and a king
morphology: One who sits on a mountain with a lotus a bow a spear a mace a large sandal and a large mace with a high armour a man standing on a sandal a priest standing on the hill with a sword a demon a king of gods a lord of gods and goddesses and a king who is known to have created the world by the light of the sky and the power of the chariot a god of wisdom and a great king is said to be the king.

sanskrit: dhanūṃṣi cāsya sajjāni hemapṛṣṭhāni sarvaśaḥ| śobhayanti rathaśreṣṭhaṃ śakracāpamivāmbaram||
reference: And his bows adorned and backed with gold all over, beautify his car even as Indra's bow beautify the firmament.
baseline: One who has the best of the chariots the king of the bulls and the kings wife and the sons of the king should be adorned with the garlands of gold and gold.
morphology: One who has got wealth and has prepared a lotus has got the hair on all the sides of the elephant. The chariot and the king of the bull are adorned.

sanskrit: ya eṣa rakṣaḥśārdūlo raṇabhūmiṃ virājayat| abhyeti rathināṃ śreṣṭho rathenādityavarcasā|| dhvajaśṛṅgapratiṣṭhena rāhuṇābhivirājate| sūryaraśmiprabhairbāṇardiśo daśa virājayan|| trinataṃ meghanidiṃ hemapṛṣṭhamalaṃkṛtam| śatakratudhanuḥprakhyaṃ dhanuścāsya virājate||
reference: Who is this foremost of Räkşasas and best of bowmen that embellishing the field of battle, approach on a car glorious as the sun; who, . displaying the ten cardinal points with his shafts resembling the rays of the sun, appear handsome with his peak of a banner bearing the figure of Rāhu, whose bow bent in three places, emitting roars resembling the rumbling of clouds, and plated with gold, look like the bow itself of Satakratu?
baseline: One who protects the chariot and the king of the war has conquered the battlefield. One who invades the chadiot the kings charioteer king of rahus kingdom with the flag and the horns standing on the throne one who invents the sun the sun and the sky the lord of the forest ten king one with the golden face and the elephant on the face of the moon and the arrow facing the hundred rivers is victorious.
morphology: One who protects the chariot and the king of the war has conquered the battlegrounds. One who invents the great chariots the king who invades the kingdom of Rahu with the flag and the horns standing on it one who invokes the sun the sky the moon the elephant the lion the arrow the bow and the elephant on the ground is invincible.

sanskrit: sadhvajaḥ sapatākaśca sānukarṣoṃ mahārathaḥ| catuḥsādisamāyukto meghastanitaniḥsvanaḥ||
reference: His mighty car furnished with a banner and ensign and bottom, and having clatter resembling the roaring of clouds, has four horsemen (attached to it).
baseline: The king should have seven cubits of sun and four cubits. He should have four cubit of sun. The king must have three cubits and one cubit.
morphology: The king should have seven cubits and four cubits. He should have four cubit and four hundred cubits of the sun. He would have eight cubits in the sky.

sanskrit: viṃśatirdaśa cāṣṭau ca tūṇāsya rathamāsthitāḥ| kārmukāṇi ca bhīmāni jyāśca kāñcanapiṅgalāḥ||
reference: There are on the car eight and thirty quivers and dreadful bows and yellow-golden bowstrings.
baseline: The chariots should be twenty thirty and four cubits long and the chariot should be made of two cubits. The workers should be of the size of a cow.
morphology: The chariots should be made of twenty and thirty cubits. The workers should be men men women men and men.

sanskrit: dvau ca khaṅgau ca pārśvasthau pradīpau pārśvaśobhitau| caturhastatsarucitau vyaktahastadaśāyatau||
reference: There are (in that car) two effulgent swords at iis side, illumining it, their hafts measuring four lands and their blades ten each.
baseline: The two horns are placed on the side and the lamp on the other side is placed on each side. The four arms are made of ten hands.
morphology: The two horns are placed on the sides and the lamps on the other side are lit. The four hands are drawn and the ten hands are made clear.

sanskrit: raktakaṇṭhaguṇo dhīro mahāparvatasaṃnibhaḥ| kālaḥ kālamahāvakro meghastha iva bhāskaraḥ||
reference: That calm (warrior) wears red garlands about is neck, and resembles-a mighty mountain. And very destroyer, he has a mighty mouth, appearing like that of the destroyer himself; and he look like the sun stationed on clouds.
baseline: One who has the qualities of blood hair guts courage great mountains and the presence of time is known as the great cloud.
morphology: One who has the qualities of blood blood hair and guts and has the strength of a great mountain is said to be the master of time. One who is like a cloud is known as Kaalāma Kaala Kaalama Kaāmā Vaakrā.

sanskrit: kāñcanāṅgadanadvābhyāṃ bhujābhyāmeṣa śobhane| śṛṅgābhyāmiva tuṅgābhyāṃ himavānparvatottamaḥ||
reference: With his arms adorned with golden angadas, he appear splendid like that best of mountains the Himavān with its towering summits.
baseline: One should be able to see the mountain of snow from the side of the head and from the sides of the arms. One should see the horns of the lion and the mountain from the two sides.
morphology: One should be able to see the mountain of snow from the side of the head and from the sides of the arms. One should see the horns and the mountains of snow and mountains.

sanskrit: kuṇḍalābhyāmubhābhyāṃ ca bhāti vakraṃ subhīṣaṇam| punarvasvantaragataḥ paripūrṇo niśākaraḥ||
reference: With his pair of ear-rings, his charming yet terrific countenance shine like the full Moon entering into Punarvasu.* *The seventh lunar asterism.
baseline: The circle should be between the sides of the kundalā and the forehead and the circumference should be good and dangerous. Then one should go back to the innermost point and make a complete escape.
morphology: One who has reached the innermost part of the body is said to be full of evil.

sanskrit: ācakṣva me mahābāho tvamenaṃ rākṣasottamam| yaṃ dṛṣṭvā vānarāḥ sarve bhayārtā vidrutā diśaḥ||
reference: O mighty-armed one, tell me all about this foremost of Rākşasas, seeing whom the monkeys, overwhelmed with fear, fly away in all directions.
baseline: One who sees a demon in the form of a demon who is a great figure and who is afraid of all the monkeys is afraid. One who knows the direction of evil is called a great king.
morphology: The great king is the best of demons. Seeing him all the monkeys are afraid and fearful.

sanskrit: sa pṛṣṭo rājaputreṇa rāmeṇāmitatejasā| ācacakṣe mahātejā rāghavāya vibhīṣaṇaḥ||
reference: Asked by the king's son Rāma of immeasurable prowess, the exceedingly energetic Vibhīşaņa spoke to Rāma, informing him.
baseline: He should be worshipped by the king of the kingdom of Śiva with the image of Rama in his eyes. The great demon Raghava is worshipped as Vibhishana.
morphology: He should be worshipped by the king of the kingdom of Śrīma. The king should be seen as a great demon with the eyes of the great king Raghava.

sanskrit: daśagrīvo mahātejā rājā vaiśravaṇānujaḥ| bhīmakarmā mahātmā hi rāvaṇo rākṣaseśvaraḥ|| tasyāsīdvīryavānputro rāvaṇapratimo bale| vṛddhasevī śrutidharaḥ sarvastraviduṣāṃ varaḥ||
reference: The highly powerful .king, Vaisravana's younger brother of dreadful deeds, the highsouled Rävaņa, is the sovereign of the Rāks asas. This one is his mighty son, like to Rāvaņa himself in strength. He serve the aged, is of wide celebrity and is the prime of those versed in all branches of knowledge.
baseline: The king of ten gods the great one the king the man of sound the god of the universe the lord of the rakshasas the son of Ravana and the king of the two gods should be worshipped. The lord of all the weapons should be called old and sounding.
morphology: The king of ten gods the great king the man of sound the king of the mighty men the god of fear the lord of the rakshasasas the son of the king and the king who is the son and son of Ravana the old man and the lord who is in charge of all the weapons and men of sound and sound should be worshipped as a boon.

sanskrit: aśvapṛṣṭhe nāgapṛṣṭhe khaḍne dhanuṣi karṣaṇe| bhede sāntve ca dāne ca naye mantre ca saṃmataḥ|| yasya bāhuṃ samāśritya laṅkā bhavati nirbhayā| tanayaṃ dhānyamālinyā atikāyamimaṃ viduḥ||
reference: He is competent to ride horses and elephants, to wield the sword or draw the bcw, or in sowing dissensions, or giving away, or in counsel, he reposing in whose arm Lanka has cast off fear. Know him to be Atikāya, son to Dhānyamāli.
baseline: One should draw a bow on the horse a serpent a pit a mace a bull a cow a buffalo an elephant a snake a deer a lion and a bull on the other side of a mountain. One whose arms are covered with lilacs should be fearless. One who has not had much to suffer from the evil evil of the grain should be blessed with the gift of a new mantra.
morphology: One should draw a bow on the horse a serpent a pit a bow a gift of peace a new mantra and the arms of a person who has been given a linga should be made free from fear. One who has got the lotus is given the gift of grain and has got a lotus.

sanskrit: etenārādhito brahmā tapasā bhāvitātmanā| astrāṇi cāpyavāptāni ripavaśca parājitāḥ||
reference: Having adored the pure-souled Brahma with austerities, he has obtained weapons, and has defeated his foes (in fight).
baseline: Having worshipped Brahma with the spirit of penance one would be defeated by the archers and other warriors.
morphology: Having worshipped Brahma with the spirit of penance and having worshipped him the weapons and weapons were destroyed.

sanskrit: surāsurairavadhyatvaṃ dattamasmai svayaṃbhuvā| etacca kavacaṃ divyaṃ rathaśca ravibhāsvaraḥ||
reference: You shall be incapable of being slain by celestials and Asura's was the boon conferred on him by the self-sprung; and he also gave him this celestial mail and this car resembling the effulgent Sun himself.
baseline: The lord of the self has given to him the power of surasura and the king of the chariots. The shield is the divine armour. The king of Ravibhāśvara has given it.
morphology: The lord of the self has given to me the authority of the king of the suns the lord of horses the divine armour the chariot and the king Ravibhāśvar.

sanskrit: etena śataśo devā dānavāśca parājitāḥ| rakṣitāni ca rakṣāṃsi yakṣāścāpi niṣūditāḥ||
reference: He has vanquished (in battle) hundreds of deities and Dänavas; and he has always) protected the Rakşasas, and destroyed Yakşas.
baseline: With this the hundred gods and the donors were defeated. The protectors and the soldiers were also destroyed.
morphology: With this the hundred gods and the donors were defeated. The protectors and the soldiers were also destroyed.

sanskrit: vajaṃ viṣṭambhitaṃ yena bāṇairindrasya dhīmatā| pāśaḥ salilarājasya yuddhe pratihatastathā ||
reference: This intelligent one resisted the thunder-bolt itself of Indra; and in encounter baffled the very noonse of the king of waters.
baseline: The vājam is said to be the strength of the arrow. The bow of Indra is the strength. The king of Salila is defeated in the battle.
morphology: The vājam is said to be the strength of the arrow. The king of Salila is defeated in the battle by the enemy.

sanskrit: eṣo'tikāyo balavānrākṣasānāmatharṣabhaḥ| sa rāvaṇasuto dhīmāndevadānavadarpahā||
reference: This one is Atikāya-foremost of Raksasas; and that son of Rāvana is the humbler of the hauteur of deities and Dänavas.
baseline: This is the king of the mighty rakshasasasana and the son of the demon Rāvanā. He is the god of the gods and the king.
morphology: This is the king of the mighty rakshasasana. He is the son of Ravana the god of wealth and wealth.

sanskrit: tadasminkriyatāṃ yatnaḥ kṣipraṃ puruṣapuṅgava| purā vānarasainyāni kṣayaṃ nayati sāyakaiḥ||
reference: Therefore, O best of persons, do you endeavour your best. This one with his shafts slaughter the monkey-hosts before (us).
baseline: One should try to do so with the help of a man who is quick to get rid of the old monkeys. The whole body of the monkeys leads to decay.
morphology: One who tries to do so would get rid of the old monkeys and their body.

sanskrit: tato'tikāyo balavānpraviśya harivāhinīm| visphārayāmāsa dhanurnanāda ca punaḥ punaḥ||
reference: Then the powerful Atikāya entering that monkey-force, stretched his bow and shouted again and again.
baseline: Then the mighty one would come down and spread the Hari vahini. Then the bow would be raised again and again.
morphology: Then the mighty one would enter the Hari vahini and again sound the bow and sound the trumpet.

sanskrit: taṃ bhīmavapuṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā rathasthaṃ rathināṃ varam| abhipeturmahātmānaḥ pradhānā ye vanaukasaḥ|| kumudo dvivido maindo nīlaḥ śarabha eva ca| pādapairgiriśṛṅgaiśca yugapatsamabhidravan||
reference: The high-souled principal monkeys, seeing that (hero) possessed of a dreadful person, that best of car-warriors-stationed on his car, rushed forward. And Kumuda and Dvivida and Mainda and Nila and Sarabha dashed on at one time with trees and mountain-peaks.
baseline: Having seen the image of Bhima the king of the chariot the chief among the spirits of the gods the lord of the forest the god of fire who is known to be a boon to the king and the king to the gods of the earth the kumudas the bivalves the maidens the nilgai and the svarabhas are known. The king is known as the king.
morphology: Having seen him one would get a boon of a chariot from the chariots. One who is the chief among the spirits would get the kumudva the bividdu the nilva and the sārbha. He would get both the legs and the horns together.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ vṛkṣāṃśca śailāṃśca śaraiḥ kanakabhūṣaṇaiḥ| atikāyo mahātejāścicchedāstravidāṃ varaḥ|4||
reference: Thereupon that foremost of those skilled in weapons, the exceedingly energetic Atikāya, severed those trees and rocks by means of shafts dight with gold.
baseline: Their trees rocks cities houses houses etc. are of great value. The gift of the weapon is to be destroyed.
morphology: Their trees and rocks are adorned with stones and ornaments. They are said to be the greatest gift of the gods.

sanskrit: tāṃścaiva sarvānsa harīśaraiḥ sarvāyasaibalī| vivyādhābhimukhānsaṃkhye bhīmakāyo viśāradaḥ||
reference: In that encounter that powerful one possessed of a gigantic person, skilled in arms, pierced all those monkeys staying before him with arrows entirely made of iron.
baseline: All those who live in that place should be worshipped by Hariṣa and all those who are married. One should worship the great god Viṣārāda in the numbers facing the enemy.
morphology: All those who dwell in it should be worshipped with the garlands of greenery. One should worship the god Bhāmaka in the numbers facing the bridegroom.

sanskrit: te'rditā bāṇavarṣeṇa bhinnagātrāḥ parājitāḥ| na śekuratikāyasya pratikatuṃ mahāhave|||
reference: And agonised, having their persons pierced in that mighty conflict by that arrowy shower, they were incapable of resisting the same.
baseline: Those who have been given to them are defeated by the arrows of different cities. One would not be able to make a symbol of the goddess Śhekuratika.
morphology: Those who had been given to them were defeated by the arrows of different cities. They should not be made to represent the image of the goddess of the universe.

sanskrit: tatsainyaṃ harivīrāṇāṃ trāsayāmāsa rākṣasaḥ| mṛgayūthamiva kruddho hariyauvanadarpitaḥ|||
reference: The Rakşasas terrified that host of monkeyheroes, even as an enraged lion priding in his youth terrify a society of deer.
baseline: The same army should be of the nature of a demon who is afraid of the mighty Hari. The king who is angry with the Hari should be punished by the king.
morphology: The same army should be used to terrorize the mighty Hari and the demons. The king should be angry with the Hari and be afraid of them.

sanskrit: sa rākṣasendro hariyūthamadhye nāyudhyamānaṃ nijaghāna kaṃcit| utpatya rāmaṃ ca dhanu:kalāpī sagarvitaṃ vākyamidaṃ babhāṣe||
reference: In the midst of those bands of monkeys, that lord of Raksasas did not slay anyone without battle. And then springing up before Rāma, that one furnished with his bow and quiver, addressed him in haughty words, saying.
baseline: He is the demon Sendra in the middle of Hariyuttha and the king of Kanchita in his own body. Having created him Rama should be worshipped as a bow and as a cow.
morphology: He is the demon Sendra in the middle of Hariyuttha and the king of Kanchita with his own body. Having created him and Rama with the bow and arrow and the word of pride is said to be mentioned in the speech.

sanskrit: naprākṛtaṃ kaṃcana yodhayāmi| yasyāsti śaktirvyavasāyayukto dadātu me śīghramihādya yuddham||
reference: Stationed in this car holding the bow and arrows in my hands, I will not fight any that is ignoble. Him that has strength, and that also understand this business, let him today speedily give me battle.
baseline: I shall fight with the bronze that has not been made. Whosoever has the strength and the strength of the army should be given it. I will fight the battle with him soon.
morphology: I shall fight with the bronze that has not been formed. Whosoever has the strength and the strength of the army should be given. Let me fight the battle with me soon.

sanskrit: tattasya vākyaṃ bruvato niśamya cukopa saumitriramitrahantā| amṛṣyamāṇaśca samutpapāta jagrāha cāpaṃ ca tataḥ smayitvā ||
reference: Hearing his speech, that slayer of foesSumitrā's son, was fired with wrath. And not bearing him, he sprang forward disregarding his antagonist's words, and took up his bow.
baseline: Having heard the words of that same Brahma one would be able to destroy the enemies of the kingdom of Sūmītra. One would get a lotus flower and the arrow would fall on him.
morphology: Having heard the words of that same Brahman one should make a note of the merits of the sacrifice. One should then make the oblation of the arrow and the bow and the sword.

sanskrit: kruddhaḥ saumitrirutpatya tūṇādākṣipya sāyakam| purastādatikāyasya vicakarṣa mahaddhanuḥ||
reference: And flying to fury, Sumitra's son, darting up, took out arrows from his quiver, and stretched his mighty bow in front of Atikāya.
baseline: One who is angry should get rid of the cow and throw the cow. One who throws the cow should give the cow a large amount of water.
morphology: One who is angry should get rid of the enemy and throw a pole and make a great sacrifice. One who does not get angry should be called a great man.

sanskrit: pūrayansa mahīṃ sarvāmākāśaṃ sāgaraṃ diśaḥ| jyāśabdo lakṣmaṇasyograstrāsayanrajanīcarān||
reference: Filling the entire earth and the sky and the ocean and all the cardinal quarters, the terrific twang of Lakşmaņa's bow struck terror into the (hearts of the) night-rangers.
baseline: The Purāyāṇas are the directions for the sea and the sky. The words lākṣṇa garuśa raṣaṇī and jājñī are described in the scriptures.
morphology: O Lord of the heavens the sea and the direction of all beings one should worship the gods of the sky the gods lakshmana garuśa sāyāna and jājani.

sanskrit: saumitreścāpanirghoṣaṃ śrutvā pratibhayaṃ tadā| visiṣmiye mahātejā rākṣasendrātmajo balī||
reference: Hearing the dreadful twang of the bow of Sumitrā's son , the exceedingly energetic and powerful son of the lord of Rākşasas was struck with surprise.
baseline: Then one who has heard the words saumitrīrā and pānaṇirighosha would become brilliant. Then one would be sacrificed to the great demon Sāndra.
morphology: Then one would hear the sound of the sun and sound of fire. One would then be blessed with the great spirit of the demons and the spirit of Indra.

sanskrit: tadātikāyaḥ kupito dṛṣṭvā lakṣmaṇamutthitam| ādāya niśitaṃ bāṇamidaṃ vacanamabravīt||
reference: Then Atikāya, enraged, seeing Lakşmaņa advance, taking sharpened shafts, spoke to him.
baseline: Having seen that the sword was pierced by him Lakshmana got up. The arrow should be drawn and the word should be uttered.
morphology: Having seen that the arrow was pierced by the fire Lakshmana arose from it. The arrow should be drawn and the word should be uttered.

sanskrit: bālastvamasi saumitre vikrameṣvavicakṣaṇaḥ| gaccha kiṃ kālasaṃkāśaṃ māṃ yodhayitumicchasi||
reference: You are a bc/, O Sumitra's sons and as such know not how to display prowess. Go you. Why wish you to fight with me resembling death itself.
baseline: O Balāṣṭva this is the son of Viṣṇu who is the disciple of Vīkramaśvu. What time and place would you wish to fight me?
morphology: O child you are the son of Viṣṇu. You want to fight me for a long time.

sanskrit: nahi madbāhusṛṣṭānāṃ bāṇānāṃ himavānapi| soḍhumutsahate vegamantarikṣamatho mahī||
reference: Not Himālaya itself or the firmament or the earth is capable of bearing the impetuosity of shafts shot by my arms.
baseline: Not the arrows made by the middle of the earth even the snowman but the propitiatory spirit.
morphology: Not only that but the arrows made by the mādbhās the snowman the sādhu muṣa mūṣmu vaigā mantrīkṣma and māhī are also said to be great.

sanskrit: sukhaprasuptaṃ kālāgni vibodhayitumicchasi| nyasya cāpaṃ nivartasva prāṇānna jahimadgataḥ||
reference: You wish to rouse a fire slumbering sweetly. Leaving alone your bow, do you return. Do not lose your life by coming in contact with me.
baseline: Having explained the darkness of happiness happiness and bliss one would get rid of the curse of life and death.
morphology: Having explained the illusion of happiness happiness and darkness one would get rid of the temptation of death and death.

sanskrit: athavā tvaṃ pratistabdho na nivartitumicchasi| tiṣṭha prāṇānparityajya gamiṣyasi yamakṣayam||
reference: Or it may be that you are proud; and therefore, have no mind to return. Stay then. Renouncing your life, you shall go to Yama's mansion.
baseline: Or else you would not be able to escape. You would leave the soul and go away.
morphology: Or else you would not be able to escape. You would leave your life and go away.

sanskrit: paśya me niśitānbāṇānirapudarpaniṣūdanān| īśvarāyudhasaṃkāśāṃstaptakāñcanabhūṣaṇān| 55 ||
reference: Behold my whetted arrows-crushers of the insolence of foes resembling the weapon itself of the Lord,* adorned with burnished gold. *Isvara, Siva, His weapon is the trident.
baseline: Behold now that I have prepared the vessels for the fire the water and the water of the sea the weapons of God the space and the ornaments of the Lord.
morphology: Behold now that I have set forth the weapons the waters the water the fire the earth the arms the space the weapons and the ornaments.

sanskrit: eṣa te sarpasaṃkāśo bāṇaḥ pāsyati śoṇitam| mṛgarāja iva kruddho nāgarājasya śoṇitam| ityevamuktvā saṃkruddhaḥ śaraṃ dhanuṣi saṃdadhe||
reference: Even as a lion enraged shedded the blood of a mighty elephant, this arrow of mine resembling a serpent shall shed your blood. Having delivered himself thus, he fired with wrath set his shaft on his bow.
baseline: He would then pass the serpent and the arrow. The king would become angry like the king of the king. Having liberated him from the wrath of Nagarāja he would be able to fight with the arrows.
morphology: He would then pass the serpent and the arrow. He would be like a king who is angry and the king of the king would be defeated. He should be liberated from this and the sword and bow would be destroyed.

sanskrit: śrutvātikāyasya vacaḥ saroṣaṃ sagarvitaṃ saṃyati rājaputraḥ| sa saṃcukopātibalo manasvī uvāca vākyaṃ ca tato bṛhacchrīḥ||
reference: Hearing in that encounter Atikāya's wrathful speech fraught with hauteur, the highly powerful and intelligent son of the king possessed of exceeding grace, was transported with passion; and he said.
baseline: The king of the kingdom is said to be the son of a sriva. The son of the king is to be proud of the saucer. He is to say that he is willing to sacrifice his property. He should say that the king should be a great servant.
morphology: The son of a king who has taken a sārūtvatīka Śrūṭva the mouth of a cow and is proud of it would say that he would be able to bear the burden of the sword. He would say the words of the mind.

sanskrit: na vākyamātreṇa bhavānpradhāno na katthanātsatpuruṣā bhavanti| mayi sthite dhanvini bāṇapāṇau nidarśayasvātmabalaṃ durātman||
reference: You can not attain pre-eminence solely by virtue of your speech. One cannot be a worthy person simply by say. O wicked-minded one, do you display your strength on me equipped with the bow and holding arrows in my hands.
baseline: One who does not speak the words of the lord or the chief of the king would not be able to say the words. One who is standing on me would not get the strength of the self. One would get the power of the evil spirits by pointing the arrows at the lord.
morphology: Neither the chief of the gods nor the chief among them are those who are not able to speak. The arrows of the rich man standing in me and those of the poor man are the strength of the self.

sanskrit: karmaṇā sūcayātmānaṃ na vikasthitumarhasi | pauruṣeṇa tu yo yuktaḥ sa tu śūra iti smṛtaḥ| 59||
reference: Manifest yourself by your valour, you ought not to blow your own trumpet. He, who is actually powerful identified as a real gallant.
baseline: One who has done good deeds should not be corrupted. One who is able to do good deeds is known to be a brave man.
morphology: One who is able to do the work of a noble man should remember that he is brave.

sanskrit: sarvāyudhasamāyukto dhanvī tvaṃ rathamāsthitaḥ| śarairvā yadi vāpyastrairdarśayasva parākramam||
reference: Seated on a chariot and skilled in archery you are equipped with all weapons, therefore, you display your own prowess either with your arrows or with arms.
baseline: You are a noble man with all the weapons at your disposal. If you are standing in the chariot you will be able to see the strength of the enemy.
morphology: You are a noble man with all the weapons at your disposal. If you are a sāraiva you will be able to bear the brunt of the attack.

sanskrit: tataḥ śiraste niśitaiḥ pātayiṣyāmyahaṃ śaraiḥ| mārutaḥ kālasaṃyuktaṃ vṛntāttālaphalaṃ yathā||
reference: Then, I shall cut off your head with my sharpened arrows like wind falls down a palm fruit from its stalk, ripened in the process of time.
baseline: Then shall I make the head of the city to be cast into the sea with the arrows fixed on it. Marutas would be as if he were the fruit of the four leaves of the earth having the same length.
morphology: Then shall I make the dead of the cities with the heads fixed on them. Marutas would be the best of the four fruits of the earth with the time.

sanskrit: adya te māmakā bāṇāstaptakāñcanabhūṣaṇāḥ| pāsyanti rudhiraṃ gātrābāṇaśalyāntarotthitam||
reference: To-day shall my shafts decked in gold, drink your blood flowing from your person and issuing of wounds inflicted by my resembling darts.
baseline: Today they are the arrows of the mother. They are the ornaments of the father. They have to be placed in the form of a large arrow and the arms of the king.
morphology: Today they are the arrows of the mother. They are the ornaments of the father. They have to be placed in the form of sandals and the arms of the son of a great man.

sanskrit: bālo'yamiti vijñāya na cāvajñātumarhasi| bālo vā yadi vā vṛddho mṛtyu jānīhi saṃyuge||
reference: "'This one is a boy', thinking this, you ought not to slight me. Whether I am a boy or an old* man' death shall you know in the conflict. *The commentator says the passage means-""You know (me) for death itself.” I prefer the sense given."
baseline: One who knows whether he is a boy or an old man would not know whether he has died or not.
morphology: One who knows whether he is a boy or an old man would not know whether he has died or not.

sanskrit: bālena viṣṇunā lokāstrayaḥ krāntāstrivikramaiḥ| lakṣmaṇasya vacaḥ śrutvā hetumatparamārthavat|| atikāyaḥ pracukrodha bāṇaṃ cottamamādade|| tato vidyādharā bhūtā devadaityā maharṣayaḥ| guhyakāśca mahātmānastadyuddhaṃ dadṛśustadā||
reference: It was as a boy that Vişņu had overpowered the triune world with his prowess.” Hearing Laksmana's words, fraught with reason and high sense, Vidyadharas and ghosts, deities, Daityas out arrows and Maharşis, and the high-souled Guhyakas then beheld that marvel.* *The encounter that ensued between Lakşmaņa and Atikāya.
baseline: Having heard the words of Lakshmana the king of the world the great warrior king of gods the mighty warrior and the great knight of the gods should be given the gift of the arrow.
morphology: Having heard the words of Lakshmana the king of the world Viṣṇu the son of the king the great warrior the master of the gods and the great knight of the war should be given to him.

sanskrit: tato'tikāyaḥ kupitaścāpamāropya sāyakam| lakṣmaṇāya pracikṣepa saṃkṣipanniva cāmbaram||
reference: Then Atikāya, enraged, setting his arrow on his bow, shot it at Lakşmaņa, as if devouring up the welkin.
baseline: Then one who is angry with others should say sākāmara. The preceptor should be sent to Lakshmana and the chamber should be made small.
morphology: Then one who is angry with others should say sākā one who does not get angry and one who gets angry should say a word to Lakshmana and the chamber should be shortened.

sanskrit: tamāpatantaṃ niśitaṃ śaramāśīviṣopamam| ardhacandreṇa ciccheda lakṣmaṇaḥ paravīrahā||
reference: Thereat, Lakşmaņa-slayer of hostile heroes-with a crescent severed that sharpened shaft resembling a venomous serpent, as it was descending.
baseline: The sword is said to be a poison. Lakshmana should be chiseled with half a crescent. He should be merciless.
morphology: One who is determined to beat the sword with the sword one who is ashamed of the poison and one who does not want to fight with the moon should be beaten with half a crescent.

sanskrit: taṃ nikṛttaṃ śaraṃ dṛṣṭvā kṛttabhogamivoragam| atikāyo bhṛśaṃ kruddhaḥ pañca bāṇānsamādadhe|| tāśarānsaṃpracikṣepa lakṣmaṇāya niśācaraḥ| tānaprāptāśitairbāṇaiściccheda bharatānujaḥ||
reference: Seeing the shaft severed, like a serpent having its person cut off, Atikāya waxing exceedingly enraged, took up five arrow; and the nightranger discharged them at Lakşmaņa. Thereat Bharata's younger brother cut off the approaching arrows with whetted shafts.
baseline: Having seen the sword drawn out of it one would become angry with the five arrows in the middle of the battle. Having seen it he would be able to get the sword. Having said that The king of Bharata would destroy it. He would have to offer the five bows and arrows to Lakshmana at night. Having received the sword the king would get it.
morphology: Having seen the image of the body that has been drawn one should go to the other side as if he had made an offering. One who is angry with the five arrows should offer the five cards to Lakshmana at night. One that has got the sword should be removed from the sky by Bharata.

sanskrit: sa tāñchittvā śitairbāṇairlakṣmaṇaḥ paravīrahā| ādade niśitaṃ bāṇaṃ jvalantamiva tejasā ||
reference: Having severed them with sharpened shafts, Lakşmaņa— slayer of hostile heroes-took up a sharpened arrow, as if flaming in energy.
baseline: Having drawn the sword he would be able to destroy the enemy. Then the arrow should be set on fire as if it were a fiery fire.
morphology: He would be the king of the sky and the lord of the earth. Then the arrow that was drawn on him would be as bright as the flame.

sanskrit: tamādāya dhanuḥśreṣṭhe yojayāmāsa lakṣmaṇaḥ| vicakarṣa ca vegena visasarja ca sāyakam||
reference: And taking it, Lakşmaņa set it on his excellent bow; and drawing the latter, vigorously discharged the shaft.
baseline: One who gains a bow with the help of a lotus should be called lakshmana. One who acquires a great bow with a great speed and a great figure should be worshipped as sāyaka.
morphology: One who gains a bow with the help of a lotus should be called lakshmana. One who acquires the strength of the bow with speed and the force of vissarā should be worshipped as Śyaka.

sanskrit: pūrṇāyatavisṛṣṭena śareṇa nataparvaṇā| lalāṭe rākṣasaśreṣṭhamājaghāna sa vīryavān|72||
reference: That hero endowed with prowess hit that foremost of Rākşasas in the forehead with that i shaft having bent knots, discharged from his bow drawn to its full bent.
baseline: The king should be made to sit on the ground with the sun full of water and without water. He should be given semen with the rakshasasas the best of the great horses.
morphology: The king should be made to sit on the ground with the sun full of water and without water. He should be given semen with the rakshasasas the greatest of the great horses.

sanskrit: sa lalāṭe śaro magnatasya bhīmasya rakṣasaḥ| dadṛśe śoṇitenāktaḥ pannagendra ivācale|73||
reference: That arrow piercing the forehead of that dreadful Raksasas, and smeared with blood, appeared like the lord of serpents in a mountain.
baseline: He is the protector of Bhima in the garland of fire. He is known to have heard the sound of gold in the form of gold. He should be known as Pāṇagendra.
morphology: He is the protector of Bhima in the garland of fire. He is known to have heard the sound of gold in the form of gold.

sanskrit: rākṣasaḥ pracakampe'tha lakṣmaṇeṣuprapīḍitaḥ| rudrabāṇahataṃ ghoraṃ yathā tripuragopuram|| cintayāmāsa cāśvasya vimṛśya ca mahābalaḥ|74|| sādhu bāṇanipātena ślāghanīyo'si me ripuḥ|
reference: The Raksasas, smarting under Laksmana's shaft, showered, like the dreadful gateway of Tripura battered by Rudra. Then recovering himself and reflecting, he said.* *Cintayāmasa-thought, I apprehend, means said in this connection.
baseline: The demon is said to be the fiercest and the demon to be killed by Lakshmana. Rudra the demon of fire the god of fire and the king of fire should be worshipped in the form of the tower of the Tripurā the great king who is worshipped by the sages.
morphology: The demon is said to be the fiercest and the demon to be destroyed by Lakshmana. Rudra the destroyer of fire the enemy of fire and the mighty king is thought to have destroyed the tower of Tripurā the king of the four gods. He should be praised by the sages with the shooting of the arrow.

sanskrit: vidhāyaivaṃ vidāryāsyaṃ vinamya ca mahābhujau| sa rathopasthamāsthāya rathena pracacāra ha!75 ||
reference: Excellent well! By this discharge of your shaft, you approve yourself as a foe in whom I can well glory. Having spoken thus candidly, he, folding his hands at ease, and seated on the platform of his car, began to range in it.
baseline: Having worshipped the great priest he should be humbled by the manner of the king and spread the word with the chariot.
morphology: Having made a vow and having humbled him he should spread the word of the great priest with his chariot and his chadiot.

sanskrit: ekaṃ trīpañca saptati sāyakānrākṣasarṣabhaḥ| ādade saṃdadhe cāpi vicakarṣotsasarja ca|76 ||
reference: Then that foremost of Raksasas began to take up, set and shoot one, three, five, or seven shafts.
baseline: One should be three five seven and the other one should be a saṃkāraksha sārbha. One should sit in the same position and make a vikākaraśa saṃraja.
morphology: One should have three five seven and one saikā raksha sarsabha and one should have a sāndhā on the same day.

sanskrit: te bāṇāḥ kālasaṃkāśā rākṣasendradhanuścyutāḥ| hemapuṅkhā raviprakhyāścardīptamivāmbaram||
reference: Those shafts resembling Fate itself, plated with gold at the feathered parts, and looking like the Sun himself (in splendour), discharged from the bow of the lord of Rakşasas, lighted up the heavens.
baseline: They are the arrows of the time the rakshasasas the sandals the rainbows the haemapunkha the bows of the lord of the sky the arrow of the sun and the arches of the moon.
morphology: They are the arrows of the time and the rakshasas the sandals and the rainbows. The haempunkha is the symbol of the divine manifestation of the god Ravī.

sanskrit: tatastārākṣasotsṛṣṭāśaraughānarāghavānujaḥ| asaṃbhrāntaḥ praciccheda niśitairbahubhiḥ śaraiḥ||
reference: Thereat Raghava's younger brother by means of many a sharpened shaft calmly cut off all those vollies of arrows shot by the Rakşasas.
baseline: Then there should be a rakshasa of the same size and a ragha of the other half of the body. The king of the two sides should be divided into two parts.
morphology: Then there should be a rakshasa of the same size and a raghavana of different sizes. He should be divided into two parts.

sanskrit: tāśarānyudhi saṃprekṣya nikṛttānrāvaṇātmajaḥ| cukopa tridaśendrārirjagrāha niśitaṃ śaram||
reference: And finding all those arrows riven in the encounter, that enemy of the lord of the immortals, Ravana's son, was fired with wrath, and took up a whetted shaft.
baseline: Having recited the tāśāraṇyūdhyūdhi one should say that the sun should be made clear and the spirit should be drawn. One should make a note of the three senses of the earth.
morphology: Having said this one should not be afraid to fight with the enemy. One should be aware of the nature of the fire. One would get three things and one would get victory. One will get victory from the enemy of war.

sanskrit: sa saṃdhāya mahātejāstaṃ bāṇaṃ sahasotsṛjat| tena saumitrimāyāntamājaghāna stanāntare||
reference: Then aiming that arrow, that highly powerful one suddenly shot it; and with that, rushing on, hit Sumitra's son in the chest.
baseline: He would have made a great arrow at the meeting with the king. He would then have made the arrow with his own hands. Then he would have the arms of the king at the end of the battle.
morphology: He would make a great arrow with his arms at the time of meeting with him. He would then make the arrow at the end of the breast with the arms of the goddess Sāmuti.

sanskrit: atikāyena saumitristāḍito yudhi vakṣasi| susrāva rudhiraṃ tīvra madaṃ matta iva dvipaḥ||
reference: Struck in the encounter by Atikaya, the son of Sumitra began to bleed copiously, like a mad elephant discharging the temporal jouice.
baseline: One should fight the battle with the spirit of the enemy with a lotus and a merciless heart. One should be able to fight with the sword of the king with a sharp blade of wine and drunkenness.
morphology: One should fight with the spirit of the enemy with a lotus and a merry spirit. One would be divided into two parts by the forceful wine and drunkenness.

sanskrit: sa cakāra tadātmānaṃ viśalyaṃ sahasā vibhuḥ| jagrāha ca śaraṃ tīkṣṇamastreṇāpi samādade|8||
reference: Then that lord at once extricated the arrow; and then took up a keen shaft and fixed the same on his weapon.* *i.e. the bow.
baseline: He would then describe the spirit as suddenly manifesting itself. He would also be pleased with the serpents and the fiery spirits.
morphology: He who has done that would soon become energized by the spirit. He would also be pleased by the fiery spirit of the lord.

sanskrit: āgneyena tadātreṇa yojayāmāsa sāyakam| sa jajvāla tadā bāṇo dhanuścāsya tadātmanaḥ||
reference: Then he set a shaft (on his bow-string) reciting a formula for the Agneya* (Belonging to the god of Fire.) weapon; and thereat his arrow as well as bow flamed up.
baseline: Then the fire should be joined with the fire and then the bow and arrow should be drawn.
morphology: Then the fire should be raised with the fire and the saikām should be drawn with the flame. Then the arrow and bow should be placed.

sanskrit: atikāyo'titejasvī raudramalaṃ samādade| tena bāṇaṃ bhujaṃgābhaṃ hemapukhamayojayat||
reference: Then the highly powerful Atikaya took up a Ruadra* weapon; and thereon fixed a shaft plated with gold at the feathered part, and resembling a serpent in sheen. *Relative to Rudra.
baseline: One should worship the raudra malam with a lotus flower. He should then offer the arrow the bow the hempukha and other things.
morphology: One should worship the raudra malam with a lotus flower the arrow the bhujhungabhu the hemapukha and the mace.

sanskrit: tadalaṃ jvalitaṃ ghoraṃ lakṣmaṇaḥ śaramāhitam| atikāyāya cikṣepa kāladaṇḍamivāntakaḥ||
reference: And even as the reaper hurled his rod, did Lakşmaņa hurl that weapon inspired with divine energy, dreadful and aflame, at Atikaya.
baseline: The fiery lotus is said to be fiery and the fiery lakshmana to be ashamed of. One who scratches the ground for more than one hour would be punished with the same punishment.
morphology: The fiery lotus of Lakshmana the fierce lotus the brahminous lotus and the chirping of a lotus should be punished with the same punishment.

sanskrit: āgneyāstrābhisaṃyuktaṃ dṛṣṭvā bāṇaṃ niśācaraḥ| utsasarja tadā bāṇaṃ raudraṃ sūryāstrayojitam||
reference: Seeing that shaft set upon an Āgneya weapon, that night-ranger discharged a Raudra arrow set upon a Solar weapon.
baseline: Having seen the arrow with the arrows of fire and fire the night bearer is said to be the sun bearer. The arrow should be placed in the sun when the sun is the source.
morphology: Having seen the arrow with the fiery scriptures and the arrows of the night one who creates a source should say that the sun is made with the arrays of fire and fire.

sanskrit: tāvubhāvambare bāṇāvanyonyamabhijannatuḥ| tejasā saṃpradīptāgro kuddhāviva bhuṃjagamau|| tāvanyonya vinirdahya petatuḥ pṛthivītale|| nirarciṣau bhasmakṛtau na bhrājete śarottamau| tāvubhau dīpyamānau sma na bhrājete mahītale||
reference: There like a pair of infuriated serpents, those arrows with their heads flaming in energy, baffled each other in the sky. And burning each other, the shafts fell on the earth; and those best of arrows, shorn of brilliance and reduced to ashes, were deprived of their splendour. And having blazed in the welkin, those two fell down to the earth reft of their lustre.
baseline: Having said this one should not burn in the earth. One should not light a fire in the sky. One who is not burning in the ground should be thrown into the earth after having said that The fire should be lit with a fiery flame and the fire should not be thrown out. One would not burn the fire. He would not be burnt by the sun.
morphology: Having said this one should not make a brahminous incense stick or fire in the form of a fire. One should make a fiery fire bright hot bitter fiery burning burning and burning in the ground. One would not be able to make a fire a fire or fire. He would not make an incineration in the earth. He should not be made to burn in the sky. One who does not burn the fire would not become a fire in my body.

sanskrit: tato'tikāyaḥ saṃkruddhastvāṣṭramaiṣīkamutsṛjat| tataściccheda saumitrirastramaindreṇa vīryavān|||
reference: Then Atikāya wrought up with wrath discharged an arrow called Aişīka dedicated to Tvaştā. Thereat the powerful son of Sumitrā severed that shaft by an Aindra* weapon. *Belonging to Indra.
baseline: Then he should be circumcised with the same thread. Then he would be made to drink with the fragrance of the thread. He would then be destroyed with the thread of the string of arms.
morphology: Then he should be circumcised with the same thread. He should be made to drink with the thread of the threads of the earth. Then the thread should be cut with the string of the string the thread and the thread with which the thread is made.

sanskrit: aiṣīkaṃ nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā kumāro rāvaṇātmajaḥ| yāmyenāstreṇa saṃkuddho yojayāmāsa sāyakam|| tatastadatraṃ cikṣepa lakṣmaṇāya niśācaraḥ| vāyavyena tadatreṇa nijaghāna sa lakṣmaṇaḥ||
reference: Seeing Aisika baffled, that Prince-son to Rāvana-fired with rage, fixed an arrow on a Yămya' weapon; and then the night-ranger shot that weapon at Lakşmaņa. And Lakşmaņa resisted it by a Vāyavya' weapon. 1. What could this be like? The commentator is silent over this important point. 2. Belonging to the wind-god.
baseline: Having seen that the demon was killed the son of Ravana the spirit of Raven the demon of Yāmyāna and the constriction of the constellation together with the saṃkāṇa thread should be offered to Lakshmana at night. He should be given the sword by Lakshman in the north east and his own body by him.
morphology: Having seen that the demon was killed the son of Ravana the spirit of Raven and the constriction of the constellation yāyyāna got the saikas. Then the king of Lakshmana got the sword. The king of night fell on him. He got his sword from the north east and the sword from his side got rid of it.

sanskrit: athainaṃ śaradhārābhirdhārābhiriva toyadaḥ| abhyavarṣata saṃkruddho lakṣmaṇo rāvaṇātmajam|12||
reference: Then as a mass of clouds poured down showers, Laksmana, enraged, poured volleys of shafts on Rāvana's son.
baseline: One who has made a gift of water with the help of water water and water should be offered to him. One who is afflicted with the disease of Śāṇvana should be given the gift of the spirit of Rāvana.
morphology: One who has made a gift of water with the help of water water and water should be offered to him. One who is afflicted with the disease of Śāṇvāṇa should offer water to the spirit of Rāvana.

sanskrit: te'tikāyaṃ samāsādya kavace vajrabhūṣite| bhagnāgraśalyāḥ sahasā peturbāṇā mahītale|13||
reference: Thereupon, hitting Atikāya, those arrows coming in contact with his mail, had their barbs broken, and fell down to the earth.
baseline: Having said that the diamond should be placed on the shield and the stone should be broken suddenly. Then the stone of the pit is placed on me.
morphology: Then the diamond is adorned with the same amount of gold and the shield is broken and the stone is suddenly thrown into the ground by Peter.

sanskrit: tānmoghānabhisaṃprekṣya lakṣmaṇaḥ paravīrahā| abhyavarṣata bāṇānāṃ sahasreṇa mahāyaśāḥ|14||
reference: Seeing them baffled, that slayer of hostile heroes-the renowned Laksmana-began to shower shafts by thousands.
baseline: Having recited the hymn tāmnomoghāṇa vīśaśa lakshmana is the supreme hero. Avyavarsa is said to be a thousand arrows. Mahāyāsā is described as eight hundred.
morphology: Having recited the hymn tāmnomoghāṇa vīśmā lakshmana is the supreme hero. He should be worshipped with a thousand arrows.

sanskrit: sa vṛṣyamāṇo bāṇaudhairatikāyo mahābalaḥ| avadhyakavacaḥ saṃkhye rākṣaso naiva vivyathe|| na śaśāka rujaṃ kartuṃ yudhi tasya narottamaḥ|
reference: And albeit showered with those arrows, that Raksasas, the mighty Atikāya-in that encounter was not pierced by them on account of his impenetrable mail; and that best of men failed to hurt him in the contest.
baseline: He is the greatest of men. He should not fight a demon in the number of his arms. He is better not to fight a king than a demon.
morphology: He is the greatest of men who fight against evil spirits. One who does not fight a demon in number should not fight against the evil one. He is better not to fight a war against evil.

sanskrit: athainamabhyupāgamya vāyurvākyamuvāca ha|| brahmadattavaro hyeṣa avadhyakavacāvṛtaḥ| brāhmaṇāstreṇa bhindhyenameṣa vadhyo hi nānyathā|| avadhya eṣa hyanyeṣāmastrāṇāṃ kavacī balī||
reference: "Then approaching him, the wind-god spoke to him, saying, ""This one has received a boon from Brahmā, and is covered with an impenetrable mail. Pierce him with a Brahma* weapon. He cannot otherwise be slain. This one clad in mail and endowed with prowess is forsooth incapable of being slain by others."" *Belonging to Brahma."
baseline: Having come to the same place as the god of fire one should say that he has been given to Brahman by the Lord of the air. Having said this the brahmin should be divided by the scripture. Having recited the words of Nāṇya he should sacrifice the armour of these weapons.
morphology: Having said this O Brahmana after having come to the temple of the same name and having said the words of the air he said that he had given Brahman he should be made to recite the words. Having said that O brahmin he who has made a difference with the scripture should be called a nāṇī. He should sacrifice the shields of these weapons.

sanskrit: tatastu vāyorvacanaṃ niśamya saumitririndrapratimānavīryaḥ| samādadhe bāṇamathogravegaṃ tadbrāhmamastraṃ sahasā niyujya|18||
reference: Hearing the words of the wind-god, Sumitrā's son like to Indra in prowess took an arrow endowed with fierce impetuosity, and at once set it on a Brahma weapon.
baseline: Then the image of Saumitra and Indra should be removed from the sky and the image should be destroyed. The arrow should be raised with the speed of the bow and the armour should be placed immediately.
morphology: Then the image of Saumitra Indra the supreme hero of the universe should be removed from the sky and the arrow should be raised to the speed of the bow and the weapon of the god Brahma should be placed at once.

sanskrit: tasminvarāstre tu niyujyamāne saumitriṇā bāṇavare śitāo| diśaśca candrārkamahāgrahāśca nabhaśca tatrāsa rarāsa corvī||
reference: On that sharp-headed best of arrows being fixed on that foremost of weapons, the cardinal quarters and the Moon and the sun and the mighty planets and the sky were saized with affright; and the earth shook.
baseline: Then the sun should be placed on the arrow and the moon should be set on the bow. The direction should be fixed on the forehead. The moon the sky the great object should be kept on the ground.
morphology: Then the sun should be placed on the arrow and the moon should be set on the bow and the sky should be fixed on it. Then the moon the sky the great object should be thrown into the ark and there should be a fire.

sanskrit: taṃ brahmaṇo'streṇa niyujya cāpe śaraṃ sapuvaṃ yamadūtakalpam| saumitririndrārisutasya tasya sasarja bāṇaṃ yudhi vajrakalpam||
reference: And inspiring that arrow furnished with a feathered part and resembling an emissary of Yama himself, and fixing the same on his bow, Sumitrā's son in that encounter discharged that shaft like to the thunder-bolt at the son of the enemy of Indra.
baseline: Having placed him with the arrow of Brahman one should draw the sword of Sārma Sāpuva Yāmādutā Kālāpa. Having drawn the arrows of Sūmaitrīndra Rīsuta the king should fight the battle of Vajra.
morphology: Having placed him in the arms of Brahman one should draw a sword snake sword yama tukalpa arrow war and diamond.

sanskrit: taṃ lakṣmaṇotsṛṣṭavivṛddhavegaṃ samāpatantaṃ śvasanogravegam| suparṇavajrottamacitrapuṅkha tadātikāyaḥ samare dadarśa||
reference: And in that conflict Atikāya beheld that shaft fair-feathered and having its feathered part dight with splendid diamonds, acquiring enhanced vehemence arising from its having been discharged by Lakşmaņa, and hissing and rushing on with tremendous impetuosity.
baseline: The speed of the breath should be equal to that of Lakshmana the highest and the highest in the world. The best of the images should be shown to him in the battle.
morphology: The speed of the breath should be equal to that of Lakshmana the highest form of the body and the speed of growth. The best form of life should be shown in the battle.

sanskrit: taṃ prekṣamāṇaḥ sahasātikāyo jaghāna bāṇainiśitairanekaiḥ| stathātivegena jagāma pārśvam||
reference: Seeing it, Atikäya swiftly resisted it with countless sharpened shafts. But endowed with the energy of Suparna himself, that shaft vehemently went to him.
baseline: One who has seen it should be accompanied by a pair of arrows and two men standing on the other side of the ground with the same speed.
morphology: One who sees it with the help of the arrows and other warriors should follow the path of jagā with speed.

sanskrit: tamāgataṃ prekṣya tadātikāyo bāṇaṃ pradīptāntakakālakalpam| jaghāna śaktyaṣṭigadākuṭhāraiḥ śūlaiḥ śaraścāpyavipanaceṣṭaḥ||
reference: Seeing that shaft flaming and resembling the Fatal destroyer himself, coming, he, exerting himself to the utmost resisted it with darts and Rştis and maces and adzes and javelins and arrows.
baseline: Having sent forth the arrow that had come to him he would then make an attempt to destroy him by having the arrows illuminated with the light of the hour. Having obtained the powers of the enemy and the sword with the axes and the axe of the king one would get a great effort.
morphology: Having sent forth the arrow that had come to him he should make an attempt to destroy him by making a fire with the arrows shining brightly and by making him fall down with the axe and the sword.

sanskrit: tānyāyudhānyadbhutavigrāhaṇi moghāni kṛtvā sa śaro'gnidīpaḥ| pragṛhya tasyaiva kirīṭajuṣṭaṃ tadātikāyasya śiro jahāra||
reference: But beating down all those weapons of wonderful forms, that arrow alive with flames, coming to the diadem-decked head of Atikāya, severed the same (in twain).
baseline: Having made the miracles of that weapon and the miraculous images of that god he should be worshipped as the sun the lamp of fire the crown and the head of that king should be destroyed.
morphology: Having made the miracles of his arms and arms and the illusions of his enemies and the fire of the fire he should be crowned with the crown. He should be made to burn the head of the king.

sanskrit: tacchiraḥ saśirastrāṇāṃ lakṣmaṇeṣupramarditam| papāta sahasā bhūmau śṛṅga himavato yathā||
reference: That head furnished with a corsalet, cut off by Laksmana's arrow, suddenly dropped to the earth, like a summit of Himavān toppling (to the ground).
baseline: Then the pāpātā should be placed on the top of the body and the arms of the goddess lakshmana. Suddenly the ground and the peak would become snow.
morphology: One should offer the same to the lord of the body arms lakshmana papa and suddenly the top of the ground becomes snow as mentioned above.

sanskrit: taṃ bhūmau patitaṃ dṛṣṭvā vikṣiptāmbarabhūṣaṇam| babhūvurvyathitāḥ sarve hataśeṣā niśācarāḥ||
reference: Seeing him rolling on the earth, with his attire and ornaments scattered about, those nightrangers that survived were overwhelmed with grief.
baseline: When he saw that the earth had fallen down he was thrown into the abyss of darkness. All those who had perished were destroyed.
morphology: When he saw that he had fallen on the ground he was thrown into the abyss. All those who had perished were killed.

sanskrit: te viṣaṇṇamukhā dīnāḥ prahārajanitaśramāḥ| vineduruccairbahavaḥ sahasā visvaraiḥ svaraiḥ||
reference: And with pale forces and distressed, they, fatigued in consequence of the thrashing they had undergone, suddenly began to cry in frightful accents.
baseline: Those who are ill-feeling and prone to the blows are the workers. The men who are suddenly in the air are called vivisāra and sounding.
morphology: Those who are ill-fated ill-tempered and prone to attack are the workers. The men who are afraid of the enemy should be suddenly heard by the disciples.

sanskrit: tatastatparito yātā nirapekṣā niśācarāḥ| purīmabhimukhā bhītā dravanto nāyake hate||
reference: On their leader having been slain, those nightrangers that were about (Atikāya), without waiting any longer, overwhelmed with panic, rushed towards the city.
baseline: Then they should be returned to the king without waiting for the night. They should be fearful and afraid of the face of the sea.
morphology: Then they should be made to go to the king without waiting for the night. They should be afraid of the king and should be sent to the chief minister.

sanskrit: praharṣayuktā bahavastu vānarāḥ praphullapadmapratimānanāstadā| apūjayallakṣmaṇamiṣṭabhāginaṃ hate ripau bhīmabale durāsade||
reference: On their foe endowed with terrific prowess and incapable of being conformed, having been slain, innumerable monkeys filled with excess of joy, and displaying countenances resembling blown lotuses, paid homage to Lakşmaņa working out their welfare.
baseline: The image of Prafulla is said to be of many things containing the prāśa and the image of the monkeys to be worshipped. One who is a partaker of the lotus should worship Bhimbala in the palace of the king.
morphology: The monkeys should be blessed with many things containing the prāśa and the image of Prafulla. The king should be lucky to be blessed by the goddess Bhimbala.

sanskrit: vīkṣamāṇastato laṅkāṃ kapiḥ kṛtamanorathaḥ| vardhamānasamutsāhaḥ kāryaśeṣamacintayat||
reference: Casting his eyes on Lankā, the monkey, his wish attained, increasing his person and bursting with spirits, considered as to how to give the coup de grace to his exertions.
baseline: Having seen the lanka made by him one should think of the remaining part of the task.
morphology: Having seen the lanka made by him one should think of the end of the task.

sanskrit: kiṃ nu khalvaśiṣṭaṃ me kartavyamiha sāmpratam| yadeṣāṃ rakṣasāṃ bhūyaḥ saṃtāpajananaṃ bhavet||
reference: What recently is to done by me here to finish this business, that may afflict them the more?
baseline: What should be done with the remains of the skull. This is the last thing that will protect them and cause them to get angry.
morphology: What should be done with the remains of the skull. This is the last thing. These things should be protected and the earth should be angry.

sanskrit: vanaṃ tāvatpramathitaṃ prakṛṣṭā rākṣasā hatāḥ| balaikadeśaḥ kṣapitaḥ śeṣaṃ durgavināśanam||
reference: I have ravaged the wood, and slain the choice Rākşasas, and destroyed by main force a portion of the army. Now it remains to demolish the fortifications.
baseline: The forest is said to have been destroyed by a demon named Prakrṣṭha. The black country is destroyed and the remaining fortifications are destroyed.
morphology: One who destroys a forest or a fort is killed by a demon named Prakrṣṭha. The remaining part of the kingdom is destroyed by the demon named Bālaka.

sanskrit: durge vināśite karma bhavet sukhapariśramam| alpayatnena kārye'smin mama syāt saphalaḥ śramaḥ||
reference: On the fortifications being destroyed, my work shall nave its toils crowned with joy. By undergoing slight labour in this business, I shall have my pains furnished with fruit.
baseline: The work done in the fort should be of good effort if it is destroyed. With a little effort in this work my work should be successful.
morphology: The work done in the fort should be of good quality. With less effort in the work it should be my successful work.

sanskrit: yo hyayaṃ mama lāṅgule dīpyate havyavāhanaḥ| asya saṃtarpaṇaṃ nyāyyaṃ kartumebhirgṛhottamaiḥ||
reference: That bearer of sacrificial offerings (Vide ante) who flame on my tail, it is my duty to propitiate him with these excellent edifices.
baseline: The light is lit in my lapel the air carriage. The offering of this incarnation should be done justly.
morphology: One who lights a lamp in my lapel should worship the air carrier. One who worships it should do justice to it.

sanskrit: tataḥ pradīptalāṅgulaḥ savidyudiva toyadaḥ| bhavanāgreṣu laṅkāyā vicacāra mahākapiḥ||
reference: Thereat that mighty monkey, with his tail aglow, and resembling a cloud (luminous) with lightning, began to range before the dwellings in Lankā.
baseline: Then there is a bright green finger and the water is given to the goddess of light. The great goddess is said to have spoken of Lanka in the houses and houses.
morphology: Then there is a bright green finger and the water is given to the goddess of power. The great goddess is said to have spoken of Lanka in the houses of gods.

sanskrit: gṛhād gṛhaṃ rākṣasānāmudyānāni ca vānaraḥ| vīkṣamāṇo hyasaṃtrastaḥ prāsādāṃśca cacāra saḥ||
reference: And that monkey with a calm mind, eyeing (all round), ranged one house from another, and gardens, and stately piles.
baseline: A monkey is known to have seen the houses of demons gardens and monkeys. He has to see the houses and the palaces.
morphology: A monkey is a man who has seen the houses of demons gardens houses and houses. He is the king of the palaces.

sanskrit: avaplutya mahāvegaḥ prahastasya niveśanam| agni tatra vinikṣipya śvasanena samo valī|| tato'nyat pupluve veśma mahāpārśvasya vīryavān| mumoca hanumānagni kālānalaśikhopamam||
reference: And that one gifted with exceeding vehemence, and in strength resembling the Wind, bounding up set fire to the dwelling of Prahasta. Then Hanuman endowed with prowess, leaping up, set to Mahaparsva's mansion fire resembling that at the universal dissolution.
baseline: Having poured out the fire the great fire should be placed on the arm. Having thrown the fire there and having inhaled it the sāmo vālī should say more than that. The sesamum of the great brim should be cast into the pool of water. The fire of Hanuman should be burnt with the fire of fire.
morphology: Having poured out the great fire the fire should be thrown there and the spirit should be placed in the hands of the great king. Having exhaled the fire he should give more than that. He should be made to drink the great water of the Lord in the pool of water. The fire of Hanuman should be burnt with the fire of fire and fire.

sanskrit: vajradaṃṣṭrasya ca tathā pupluve sa mahākapiḥ| śukasya ca mahātejāḥ sāraṇasya ca dhīmataḥ||
reference: And (then) the mighty monkey darting up, set fire to Vajradanştra's; and (then) that highly energetic one set fire to Suka's and to the intelligent Sārana's.
baseline: He is also said to be great in the form of a diamond a mace a puffer a boar a sage a cow an elephant and a cow.
morphology: He is also great in the form of a diamond and a mace a boar a cow a deer and a deer.

sanskrit: tathā cendrajito veśma dadāha hariyūthapaḥ| jambumāleḥ sumāleśca dadāha bhavanaṃ tataḥ|| raśmiketośca bhavanaṃ sūryaśatrostathaiva ca| hrasvakarṇasya daṃṣṭrasya romaśasya ca rakṣasaḥ|| yuddhonmattasya mattasya dhvajagrīvasya rakṣasaḥ| vidyujjihvasya ghorasya tathā hastimukhasya ca|| karālasya viśālasya śoṇitākṣasya caiva hi| kumbhakarṇasya bhavanaṃ makarākṣasya caiva hi|| narāntakasya kumbhasya nikumbhasya durātmanaḥ| yajñaśatrośca bhavanaṃ brahmaśatrostathaiva ca||
reference: And the leader of monkey bands in the same way burnt down Indrajit's mansion; and then he burnt the abodes of Sumāli and Jambumălī; and Rasmiketu's mansion and Suryasatru's, and Hrasvakarma's, and the Raksasa Romasa's; and the houses of Yuddhonmatta, and Matta, and the Rākṣasa Dhvajagrīva, and the calm Vidyujjihva, and Hastimukha; and of Karāla, and of Viśāla, and of Sonitāksa; and Kumbhakarma's mansion, and Nikumbha's, and the residence of Yajnasatru, and of Brahmasatru.
baseline: The same is the case with the chandrajita vesmā dāda hāriyutāpa jambu māla sūmaal dada dadha haṇa rāśmīketa building sun śrutrāṣṭra protection the protection of the enemy the defence of the battle the defense of the war the fight the guard the enemy of the army the protector of the flag the defender of the sword the guardian of the mighty king the chieftain
morphology: The same is the case with the chandrajita the vesum the dādha the riyutapada the jambu māla the sūmala the building of the śūrṣmīkata the palace of the sun the house of the enemy the protection of the flag the defence of the war the battle the fight and the battle of the king the guard of the sword the defense of the mighty king of the army and the defence against the enemy of the enemies of the world the construction of the

sanskrit: varjayitvā mahātejā vibhīṣaṇagṛhaṃ prati| kramamāṇaḥ krameṇaiva dadāha haripuṅgavaḥ||
reference: And leaving alone the dwelling of Vibhişaņa, that exceedingly energetic one-foremost of monkeys-by and by burnt (all the houses there).
baseline: Having been prevented the great king would go to the house of Vibhishana. Then the king would be destroyed gradually.
morphology: Having conquered the great king of the kingdom of Vibhishana the king of Hari the gods of the kingdoms of Hari and the kings of the kings of the states would be destroyed in succession.

sanskrit: teṣu teṣu mahārheṣu bhavaneṣu mahāyaśāḥ| gṛheṣvṛddhimatāmṛddhiṃ dadāha kapikuñjaraḥ||
reference: In those costly mansions and dwellings, that famous one, that foremost of monkeys, burnt all the wealth of those affluent persons.
baseline: Among them there are great men in the houses great men of great stature. In the house prosperity prosperity and prosperity should be worshipped.
morphology: Among them there are great men in the houses great men of the houses and great men. In the houses one should worship prosperity and prosperity. One should worship Kapikunjara.

sanskrit: sarveṣāṃ samatikramya rākṣasendrasya vīryavān| āsasādātha lakṣmīvān rāvaṇasya niveśanam||
reference: Having passed the dwellings of all, that powerful and auspicious one approached the residence of the lord of Rākşasas, Rāvaņa.
baseline: Having equated all the demons one should get the semen of Indra. Having worshipped him Lord Lakshmi should place him in the place of Ravana.
morphology: Having equated all the demons one should get the semen of Indra. One should place the seat of Rāvana on the throne of Lakshmana.

sanskrit: tatastasmin gṛhe mukhye nānāratnavibhūṣite| merumandarasaṃkāśe nānāmaṅgalaśobhite || pradīptamagnimutsṛjya lāṅgulāgre pratiṣṭhitam| nanāda hanumān vīro yugāntajalado yathā||
reference: And in that foremost of mansions, adorned or with various gems, resembling Meru Mandara, graced with diverse auspicious things, he set to the same, fire flaming at the end of his tail. And the heroic Hanumān roars, resembling a cloud (appearing) at the end of a Yuga.
baseline: Then in that house in the main place there are many jewels adorned with different kinds of ornaments. In the temple of meru māndarāśaṇṣṇaka there are nine kinds of flowers. Having illuminated the fire and having lit the fire they are placed in the langugārga. The hero Hanumāṇa should be worshipped as if he were the king of the yuga.
morphology: Then in that house the chief among the many jewels is adorned with the meru mandraks the suns rays and the fire which is illuminated by the sun and is placed in the langugura. The hero of the war Hanumana is worshipped as the king of jugaṇa.

sanskrit: śvasanena ca saṃyogādativego mahābalāḥ| kālāgniriva jajvāla prāvardhata hutāśanaḥ||
reference: And assisted by the wind, that highly powerful and vehement one (Fire) flaimed up, like fire at the wreck of all, and the fire attained energy.
baseline: O great one who gives the union with the breath the fire of time and the flame of fire and the light of fire should be increased.
morphology: O great one who gives union with the breath the fire of time and the flame of fire should be increased.

sanskrit: pradīptamagniṃ pavanasteṣu veśmasu cārayan| tāni kāñcanajālāni muktāmaṇimayāni ca|| bhavanāni vyaśīryanta ratnavanti mahānti ca| tāni bhagnavimānāni nipeturvasudhātale||
reference: The wind spreading the flaming fire all round those dwellings, those mansions furnished with golden networks; and containing pearls and gems; enjewelled and magnificent, were shorn of their splendour.
baseline: The light should be spread in the air and the wind should be fed in the vesmas. These are the Kanchanjala jaṇas and the Muktāmanī gems. These buildings should be divided into two parts. The stones should be placed in the form of stones. These planes should be broken and thrown into the earth.
morphology: The light of the sky should be spread in the air and the wind should be seen in the sky. These should be covered with a net of water and made free. The buildings should be made of gold and gems. The planes should be broken and placed in a well.

sanskrit: bhavanānīva siddhānāmambarāt puṇyasaṃkṣaye| saṃjajñe tumulaḥ śabdo rākṣasānāṃ pradhāvatām|| sve sve gṛhaparitrāṇe bhagnotsāhojjhitaśriyām| nūnameṣo'gnirāyātaḥ kapirūpeṇa hā iti|| krandantyaḥ sahasā petuḥ stanaṃdhayadharāḥ striyaḥ|
reference: "And cracked edifices began to topple down to the ground, like the mansions of Siddhās falling from the firmament of the exhaustion of their righteousness. And there arose a mighty uproar of those Rākşasas, as, bereft of their good fortune, despairing of preserving their abodes, they rushed in all directions, ""Forsooth it is Fire himself that has come hither in the form of a monkey.” And females crying with babes on their breasts, suddenly plunged (into the fire)."
baseline: Having heard the words of Tūmula one who has lost the righteousness of a noble person by the name of the building one would get rid of the demons. One would find that the house would be destroyed by the spirit of the enemy. One who has not lost the spirit would get the blood of a woman by the sound of the fire. One should say to him suddenly after having wept that the fire should be turned into a fire.
morphology: One who has not built a house should be blessed with the name of a man who has attained perfection. Having heard the word tūmula one should worship the demons. One who is self-sacrificing should be encouraged to destroy the house and save the house. Having said the words namāṇa iñgaṇī iṇeñirāyātā haa suddenly one who has fallen asleep and has become a woman should be breastfed.

sanskrit: kāścidagniparītāṅgayo haryebhyo muktamūrdhajāḥ|| patantyo rejire'bhrebhyaḥ saudāmanya ivāmbarāt|
reference: And some fair ones with hair dishevelled, and surrounded on all sides with fire, as they fell down from dwellings, looked lovely like lightning from the welkin.
baseline: One who is free from the forces of fire and other elements would fall into the river.
morphology: One who has not been given any fire or other part of the body would fall free from the enemies of the Hariyas.

sanskrit: vajravidrumavaidūryamuktārajatasaṃhatān|| vicitrān bhavanāddhātūnsyandamānān dadarśa saḥ|
reference: And he (Hanuman) saw various kinds of metals, mixed with diamonds, and coral, and lapises and pearls and silver, running down in streams from the mansions.
baseline: He would show the strange buildings of the gods and their merriment by making them free from the clutches of the diamond the wind and the distance.
morphology: He would show the strange buildings of the gods and their merriment.

sanskrit: nāgnistṛpyati kāṣṭhānāṃ tṛṇānāṃ ca yathā tathā|| hanūmān rākṣasendrāṇāṃ vadhe kiṃcinna tṛpyati| na hanūmadviśastānāṃ rākṣasānāṃ vasundharā ||
reference: And as Fire is not cloyed with wood and straw, Hanumān never at all felt satiety on slaying those foremost of Räkşasas. And the Earth could not contain the Rākşasas slain by Hanumăn.
baseline: Just as the serpents are worshipped by the gods of the earth the gods animals and birds of the sky the demons of the world are worshipping the gods. The demons are not worshipped in the form of gods.
morphology: Just as the serpents are worshipped by the gods the gods of the earth the animals of the forest and the grass the demons of the world are worshipping the gods.

sanskrit: hanūmatā vegavatā vānareṇa mahātmanā| laṅkāpuraṃ pradagdhaṃ tad rudreṇa tripuraṃ yathā||
reference: And as Rudra had burnt down Tripura, the vehement and high-souled monkey, Hanumān, burnt down Lankā.
baseline: The great man hanumata is said to be the speed with which the monkeys move. The king of Lanka is described as having illuminated Tripura with Rudra.
morphology: The great man hanumata is said to be the speed with which the monkeys move. The lankapura is saidto be the wind with the roda and the tripurā.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa laṅkāpuraparvatāgre samutthito bhīmaparākramo'gniḥ| prasārya cūḍāvalayaṃ pradīpto hanūmatā vegavatopasṛṣṭaḥ||
reference: And rising to the brow of Lanka's mount, (Trikūţa on which Lankā rested) the fire of terrific energy kindled by the impetuous Hanumān, spread wide his tongues.
baseline: Then he rises in the mountains of Lanka Pārvātā Bhima Parakrama Kāmkam spreads the chudāla and illumines the sky. Then he becomes the manifestation of Hanumata Vega and Sātra.
morphology: Then he would rise in the mountains of Lanka Pārvāda Bhima Parākrama Kāmkam spread his arms and illuminate the sky. He would rise up with the fire of Hanumata.

sanskrit: yugāntakālānalatulyarūpaḥ samāruto'gnirvavṛdhe divaspṛk | vidhūmaraśmirbhavaneṣu sakto rakṣaḥśarīrājyasamarpitārciḥ||
reference: With the Wind assisting him, the smokeless Fire in the dwellings, with his flames feeding on the bodies of the Rākşasas representing sacrificial offerings, spread his magnitude, touching the horizen-resembling the conflagration kindled the universal dissolution.
baseline: One who has the form of a sambarū an arrow and a tree of the day in the year ending with the end of the age would be able to protect the body and the kingdom in the event of the occurrence of a widow son daughter and son.
morphology: One who has the form of a sambarū a lotus and a tree of the same size for the duration of the epoch should be worshipped daily. One who is able to protect the widows and widows in the event of their death should be offered to the king.

sanskrit: ādityakoṭīsadṛśaḥ sutejā laṅkāṃ samastāṃ parivārya tiṣṭhan| bhindannivāṇḍaṃ prababhau mahāgniḥ||
reference: And possessing the fierce energy of a koti suns, the nighty Fire completely encompassing the entire Lanka, increased (in volume), riving at the mundane Egg with various sounds resembling thunder-claps.
baseline: The king of the kingdom of Vindāṇiva and the lord of the great fire are said to be like Aditya koti and to be the son of Sūtjā. He should have all the members of the family.
morphology: The king of Lanka should be seated on the throne with his whole family like Aditya koti. He should be worshipped as Bhinda Ninnivanda Prabhava Maha and Agni.

sanskrit: tatrāmbarādagniratipravṛddho rūkṣaprabhaḥ kiṃśukapuṣpacūḍaḥ| nirvāṇadhūmākularājayaśca nīlotpalābhāḥ pracakāśire'bhrāḥ||
reference: And the Fire of terrific might, having his flames resembling Kinsuka blossoms, rising up to the sky, clouds caused by volumes of smoke arising from extinguished fire, in hue resembling blue lotuses, looked exceedingly beautiful.
