reference: Being reincarnated as if being liberated, he has the power and ability to teach the Dharma that liberates living beings from their bondage.
baseline: He is free and the products are free he is free and he is bound the strength of the sattvas the reflector of bondage and the protector of righteousness.
morphology: He is free and the products are liberated and the forces of the sattvas are bound the forces are bound and the bondage is liberated.

sanskrit: yathoktaṃ bhagavatā sa tāvad ātmanā baddhaḥ paraṃ bandhanān mocayiṣyatīti nādaṃ sthānaṃ vidyate /
reference: As the Lord declares ‘It is not possible for one who is himself bound to deliver others from their bondage.
baseline: He who is bound by the self and then clears the bonds is said to be the place where the bondage is to be made.
morphology: He who is bound by the spirit and then breaks the bonds should be called a place of worship.

sanskrit: yas tv ātmanā muktaḥ paraṃ bandhanān mocayiṣyatīti sthānam etad vidyate tasmān muktena bodhisatvena bhavitavyam, na baddhena /
reference: But one who is himself liberated is able to liberate others from their bondage.’ Therefore, the bodhisattva should participate in liberation and should not participate in bondage.
baseline: If you are liberated by the self the bonds will be released. These should be liberated and not bound.
morphology: If you are liberated by the self the bonds will be released. These should be free and not bound.

sanskrit: tatra katamo bandhaḥ,
reference: “What is bondage?
baseline: How many bonds are there?
morphology: How many bonds are there.

sanskrit: katamo mokṣaḥ /
reference: And what is liberation?
baseline: What is salvation?
morphology: What is Moksha?

sanskrit: anupāyād bhavagatiparigraho bodhisatvasya bandhaḥ,
reference: To indulge in liberation from the world without employing liberative art is bondage for the bodhisattva.
baseline: By doing this you are bound to the bodhisattvas.
morphology: By doing this you are bound by the bodhisattvas.

sanskrit: upāyād bhavagatigamanaṃ mokṣaḥ /
reference: To engage in life in the world with full employment of liberative art is liberation for the bodhisattva.
baseline: By means of the remedy you get rid of the motion.
morphology: The path leading to you is called moksha.

sanskrit: anupāyād dhyānasamādhyāsvādanatā bodhisatvasya bandhaḥ,
reference: To experience the taste of contemplation, meditation, and concentration without skill in liberative art is bondage.
baseline: The bond of the bodhisattvas should be meditated on by the unbroken mind and enjoyment of the medium.
morphology: The bond of the Bodhisattvas should be meditated on by the unmanifested and the enjoyment of the medium.

sanskrit: upāyena dhyānasamādhyāsvādanatā mokṣaḥ /
reference: To experience the taste of contemplation and meditation with skill in liberative art is liberation.
baseline: One who meditates on the medium with the help of the medium would get salvation.
morphology: One gets salvation by meditating on the medium with the help of the medium.

sanskrit: anupāyasaṃgṛhītā prajñā bandhaḥ, upāyasaṃgṛhītā prajñā mokṣaḥ /
reference: Wisdom not integrated with liberative art is bondage, but wisdom integrated with liberative art is liberation.
baseline: One who has collected knowledge without fail and has collected the means one who has acquired knowledge and has attained salvation.
morphology: One who collects knowledge by the means of the unprocessing one who gathers wisdom by the method of the bondage and one who accumulates knowledge is called moksha.

sanskrit: prajñayāsaṃgṛhīta upāyo bandhanam, prajñāsaṃgṛhīta upāyo mokṣaḥ /
reference: Liberative art not integrated with wisdom is bondage, but liberative art integrated with wisdom is liberation.
baseline: One who acquires knowledge and association would be bound by the means obtained. One who obtains knowledge would get salvation.
morphology: One should be bound by the means of knowledge and association. One would get salvation by means of the means acquired by knowledge.

sanskrit: tatra katamo 'nupāyasaṃgṛhītā prajñā bandhaḥ,
reference: “How is wisdom not integrated with liberative art a bondage?
baseline: How many things should be collected there. The bond of wisdom should be fixed.
morphology: How many things should be collected there. The bond of wisdom should be fixed.

sanskrit: yad idaṃ śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitanidhyaptiḥ, na ca lakṣaṇānuvyañjanabuddhakṣetrālaṃkārasatvaparipācananidhyaptiḥ / iyam anupāyasaṃgṛhītā prajñā bandhaḥ /
reference: Wisdom not integrated with liberative art consists of concentration on voidness, signlessness, and wishlessness, and yet it fails to concentrate on cultivation of the auspicious signs and marks, on the adornment of the buddhafield, and on the work of development of living beingsand it is bondage.
baseline: If it is not for the sake of emptiness it should not be considered as a sign of ignorance. It should be known to be a matter of knowledge.
morphology: One who does not know the meaning of the word should not be made to suffer for the absence of it. One who is not aware of the signs does not possess the knowledge of the area and the ornament of the mind and does not get the knowledge.

sanskrit: tatra katamopāyasaṃgṛhītā prajñā mokṣaḥ,
reference: “How is wisdom integrated with liberative art a liberation?
baseline: One who has collected knowledge and salvation would get the benefits of the same.
morphology: One who gathers wisdom and salvation would get wealth.

sanskrit: yad idaṃ lakṣanānuvyañjanabuddhakṣetrālaṃkārasatvaparipācananidhyapticittaṃ ca śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitaparijayaś ca / iyam upāyasaṃgṛhītā prajñā mokṣaḥ /
reference: Wisdom integrated with liberative art consists of concentration on cultivation of the auspicious signs and marks, on the adornment of the buddhafield, and on the work of development of living beings, all the while concentrating on deep investigation of voidness, signlessness, and wishlessnessand it is liberation.
baseline: One who acquires such a measure of knowledge and salvation by having the knowledge of the objects of the mind the ornament of the area the decoration of the house the digestion the desire to be possessed the purification of the body and the purified things for the sake of the absence of the enemy is thus known.
morphology: One who acquires knowledge and salvation by having the knowledge of the objects of the mind the ornament of the area the purification of the digestive system the desire to get rid of it and one who has made a gift for the sake of the absence of it should do so.

sanskrit: tatra katamaḥ prajñayāsaṃgṛhīta upāyo bandhaḥ,
reference: “What is the bondage of liberative art not integrated with wisdom?
baseline: There is no limit to the amount of knowledge obtained from the body.
morphology: There is no limit to the amount of knowledge obtained from the body.

sanskrit: yad idaṃ sarvadṛṣṭikleśaparyutthānānuśayānunayapratighapratiṣṭhitasya sarvakuśalamūlārambho bodhau cāpariṇāmanā / ayaṃ prajñayāsaṃgṛhīta upāyo bandhaḥ /
reference: The bondage of liberative art not integrated with wisdom consists of the bodhisattva’s planting of the roots of virtue without dedicating them for the sake of enlightenment, while living in the grip of dogmatic convictions, passions, attachments, resentments, and their subconscious instincts.
baseline: That which has been established by raising the head above all the visible difficulties and having raised the head the mind should begin with the root of all the senses. This knowledge should be bound by the effect of the slap. It should be obtained by the body.
morphology: One who raises all the eyes the head and the head to the point of suffering and starts all the senses of the mind by the effect of the slap one who acquires knowledge and the body is bound.

sanskrit: tatra katamaḥ prajñāsaṃgṛhīta upāyo mokṣaḥ,
reference: “What is the liberation of liberative art integrated with wisdom?
baseline: There is no remedy for salvation.
morphology: One who has collected knowledge from there would get salvation.

sanskrit: yad idaṃ sarvadṛṣṭikleśaparyutthānānuśayānunayapratighaprahīṇasya sarvakuśalamūlārambho bodhau pariṇāmitas tasya cāparāmarśaḥ / ayaṃ bodhisatvasya prajñāsaṃgṛhīta upāyo mokṣaḥ /
reference: The liberation of liberative art integrated with wisdom consists of the bodhisattva’s dedication of his roots of virtue for the sake of enlightenment, without taking any pride therein, while forgoing all convictions, passions, attachments, resentments, and their subconscious instincts.
baseline: If one does not see all the problems and rise up from the abyss one would get rid of all misfortune and the mind would be affected by the beginning of all the miseries. This would be the remedy for the bodhisattvas.
morphology: If one does not see all the problems and rise up from the darkness one would get rid of all misfortune and the mind would be destroyed by the beginning of all the miseries. This would be the remedy for the bodhisattvas.

sanskrit: tatra mañjuśrīḥ glānena bodhisatvenaivam ime dharmā nidhyapayitavyāḥ /
reference: “Mañjuśrī, thus should the sick bodhisattva consider things.
baseline: There manjusri should be worshipped as a bodhisattva with the hymn gālaṇa.
morphology: There manjusri should be worshipped as a bodhisattva with the hymn glāna.

sanskrit: kāyasya cittasya ca vyādheś cānityaduḥkhaśūnyānātmapratyavekṣaṇā, iyam asya prajñā /
reference: His wisdom is the consideration of body, mind, and sickness as impermanent, miserable, empty, and selfless.
baseline: This is the wisdom of the mind.
morphology: This is the wisdom of the mind. One who does not want to suffer from the disease of the body and the mind one who does nothing without the feeling of the soul and one who observes the spirit.

sanskrit: yat punaḥ kāyavyādhipariharaṇatayā na khidyate, na pratibadhnāti saṃsāram, satvārthayogam anuyuktaḥ, ayam asyopāyaḥ /
reference: His liberative art consists of not exhausting himself by trying to avoid all physical sickness, and of applying himself to accomplish the benefit of living beings, without interrupting the cycle of reincarnations.
baseline: One who does not treat the disease again and does not fight back would not be able to save the world. This is a good practice.
morphology: One who does not treat the disease again and again and does not fight back the world would not be able to make good use of it.

sanskrit: punar aparaṃ yat kāyasya vyādheś cittasya cānyonyaparāparatāṃ na nirnavatāniḥpurāṇatāṃ pratyavekṣate, iyam asya prajñā /
reference: Furthermore, his wisdom lies in understanding that body, mind, and sickness are neither new nor old, whether considered simultaneously or sequentially.
baseline: Then the wisdom of the same is seen in the ancient scriptures. It does not determine the evil deeds of the mind in the case of the disease of the body.
morphology: The wisdom of the same is to see the ancient wisdom that does not determine the wrongness of the mind in the matter of the disease of the body and the evil deeds of others.

sanskrit: yat punaḥ kāyasya vyādheś cittasya ca nātyantopaśamaṃ nirodham atyayati,
reference: And his liberative art lies in not seeking pacification or cessation of body, mind, or sicknesses.
baseline: That which is again a disease of the body and not of the mind would be prevented.
morphology: That which is again a disease of the body and not of the mind would prevent the disease.

sanskrit: evaṃ hi mañjuśriḥ glānena bodhisatvena cittaṃ nidhyapayitavyam / na ca tena nidhyaptau vānidhyaptau vā sthātavyam /
reference: “That, Mañjuśrī, is the way a sick bodhisattva should concentrate his mind he should live neither in control of his mind, nor in indulgence of his mind.
baseline: In this way the mind should be made to rest as a bodhisattva with the chant of hī manjūśrī. One should not rest on the seat of the king or on the ground of the enemy.
morphology: In this way the mind should be made to rest as a bodhisattva with the hymn hī manjūśrī. One should not rest with it. One has to rest with the word vāṇidhyāpta.

sanskrit: yadi hy anidhyaptau tiṣṭhed bāladharma eṣaḥ / atha nidhyaptau tiṣṭhec chrāvakadharma eṣaḥ /
reference: To live by indulging the mind is proper for fools and to live in control of the mind is proper for the disciples.
baseline: If one has remained undefiled the child should be subject to this. Then one should remain confined to this religion.
morphology: If one has remained undefiled then the Bal dharma should be retained.

sanskrit: tasmād bodhisatvena na nidhyaptau sthātavyam /
reference: Therefore, the bodhisattva should live neither in control nor in indulgence of his mind.
baseline: If so done one should not remain in the position of a bodhisattva.
morphology: If so done one should not remain in the abode as a bodhisattva.

sanskrit: yad atrāsthānam ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
reference: Not living in either of the two extremes is the domain of the bodhisattva.
baseline: That place here is the place for the bodhisattvas to visit.
morphology: That place here is the pasture for the bodhisattvas.

sanskrit: yan na pṛthagjanagocaro nāryagocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ / yat saṃsāragocaraś ca na ca kleśagocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
reference: “Not the domain of the ordinary individual and not the domain of the arhat, such is the domain of the bodhisattva. The domain of the world yet not the domain of the afflictions, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.
baseline: One who does not know the world and does not suffer is known to be a Bodhisattva. One who is not aware of the world is known as Bodhidhasa.
morphology: One who does not know the world and does not suffer is known to be a bodhisattva. One who is not aware of the world is known as bodhidhasa.

sanskrit: yan nirvāṇapratyavekṣaṇagocaraś ca na cātyantaparinirvāṇagocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
reference: Where one understands liberation, yet does not enter final and complete liberation, there is the domain of the bodhisattva.
baseline: If the nirvana is not visible to all. It is the manifestation of the bodhisattvas.
morphology: If the nirvana is not visible to all. It is the manifestation of the bodhisattvas.

sanskrit: yac caturmārasaṃdarśanagocaraś ca sarvamāraviṣayātikrāntagocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
reference: Where the four māras manifest, yet where all the works of māras are transcended, there is the domain of the bodhisattva.
baseline: One who has seen the four elements of the universe and has seen all the aspects of the world is known to be a bodhisattva.
morphology: This is the manifestation of the bodhisattva.

sanskrit: yat sarvajñajñānaparyeṣṭigocaraś ca na cākāle jñānaprāptigocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
reference: Where one seeks the gnosis of omniscience, yet does not attain this gnosis at the wrong time, there is the domain of the bodhisattva.
baseline: One who does not know the knowledge of the omniscient is known to be aware of it. This is the manifestation of the bodhisattvas.
morphology: One who does not know the knowledge of the omniscient and acquires knowledge in the chakalā is known to be a bodhisattva.

sanskrit: yac catuḥsatyajñānagocaraś ca na cākāle satyaprativedhagocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
reference: Where one knows the four noble truths, yet does not realize those truths at the wrong time, there is the domain of the bodhisattva.
baseline: One who does not know the truth of the four things and does not perceive the truth in the chakalā is known to be a bodhisattva.
morphology: The four things which are known to be true are not known to the disciple. This is the secret of the bodhisattvas.

sanskrit: yad adhyātmapratyavekṣaṇagocaraś ca saṃcintyabhavopapattiparigrahagocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
reference: A domain of introspective insight, wherein one does not arrest voluntary reincarnation in the world, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.
baseline: One who observes the spirituality and perceives the illusion of the mind should consider that it is a manifestation of the bodhisattvas.
morphology: This is the manifestation of the Bodhisattva.

sanskrit: yad ajātipratyavekṣaṇagocaraś ca na ca niyāmāvakrāntigocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
reference: A domain where one realizes birthlessness, yet does not become destined for the ultimate, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.
baseline: If it is not visible to the unborn it should not be seen to be fixed. This is the manifestation of the bodhisattvas.
morphology: This is the manifestation of the bodhisattvas.

sanskrit: yat pratītyasamutpādagocaraś ca sarvadṛṣṭivigatagocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
reference: Where one sees relativity without entertaining any convictions, there is the domain of the bodhisattva.
baseline: One who has seen the manifestation of all things and has seen all things is known to be the master of the bodhisattvas.
morphology: This is the manifestation of the bodhisattvas.

sanskrit: yat sarvasatvasaṃgaṇikāgocaraś ca na ca kleśānuśayagocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
reference: Where one associates with all beings, yet keeps free of all afflictive instincts, there is the domain of the bodhisattva.
baseline: One who does not suffer from all the things that are associated with him and who is not suffering is the manifestation of the bodhisattvas.
morphology: One who does not suffer from all the things that are associated with him and who is not suffering from him is a manifestation of the bodhisattvas.

sanskrit: yad vivekagocaraś ca na ca kāyacittakṣayaniśrayagocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
reference: A domain of solitude with no place for the exhaustion of body and mind, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.
baseline: One who does not perceive the wisdom and does not trust the will of the body is known to be a bodhisattva.
morphology: One who does not know the wisdom of the mind and who is dependent on the mind is known to be a bodhisattva.

sanskrit: yat traidhātukagocaraś ca na ca dharmadhātusaṃbhedagocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
reference: The domain of the triple world, yet indivisible from the ultimate realm, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.
baseline: One who does not distinguish between the three forms of dharma and dharma is known to be a bodhisattva.
morphology: One who does not distinguish between the three forms of dharma and dharma is known to be a bodhisattva.

sanskrit: yac chūnyatāgocaraś ca sarvākāraguṇaparyeṣṭigocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ / yad ānimittagocaraś ca satvapramocanārambaṇavitarkagocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
reference: The domain of voidness, yet where one cultivates all types of virtues, such is the domain of the bodhisattva. The domain of signlessness, where one keeps in sight the deliverance of all living beings, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.
baseline: One who has seen the manifestation of the Bodhisattvas in all forms and manifestations of the qualities of the bodhisatvas one who has not seen the revelation of sattva and the remission of sātamāṇa one which has been described as manifest in the manifestations is known to be the manifestion of the past.
morphology: This is the manifestation of the Bodhisattvas the manifestations of the buddhis and the manifest manifestations in all forms and manifestations. The manifestations are manifest in the manifesting of the unspeakable and manifest in manifestations and manifestation.

sanskrit: yad apraṇihitagocaraś ca saṃcintyabhavagatisaṃdarśanagocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
reference: The domain of wishlessness, where one voluntarily manifests lives in the world, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.
baseline: One who has seen the manifestation of the bodhisattvas should consider that which is not known to him.
morphology: One who has seen the manifestation of the bodhisattvas should consider that which is not known to him.

sanskrit: yad anabhisaṃskāragocaraś ca sarvakuśalamūlābhisaṃskārāpratiprasrabdhigocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
reference: “A domain essentially without undertaking, yet where all the roots of virtue are undertaken without interruption, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.
baseline: One who has not been able to do so would be exposed to all kinds of mischief and gain. This is the manifestation of the bodhisattvas.
morphology: This is the manifestation of the bodhisattvas.

sanskrit: yat ṣaṭpāramitāgocaraś ca sarvasatvacittacaritapāragamanagocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
reference: The domain of the six transcendences, where one attains the transcendence of the thoughts and actions of all living beings, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.
baseline: One who has passed through the path of the bodhisattvas with the chariot of the six prāmās and the chācāra of the four prāmarās is known to have passed through all the manifestations of the mind.
morphology: This is the path of the bodhisattvas which has six sides and the chariots of the charyas and the passage of all the spirits.

sanskrit: yat ṣaḍanusmṛtigocaraś ca na ca sarvāsravakṣayagocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
reference: The domain of the six superknowledges, wherein defilements are not exhausted, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.
baseline: One who remembers six things and does not forget all things is known to be a bodhisattva.
morphology: One who remembers six things and does not forget all things is the master of the bodhisattvas.

sanskrit: yat saddharmapratiṣṭhānagocaraś ca na ca kumārgādhyālambanagocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
reference: The domain of living by the holy Dharma, without even perceiving any evil paths, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.
baseline: One who does not observe the principles of righteousness and does not obey the orders of the priest should not do so. This is the manifestation of the bodhisattvas.
morphology: One who does not observe the principles of righteousness and does not follow the rules of the priesthood should not do so. This is the path of the bodhisattvas.

sanskrit: yac caturapramāṇagocaraś ca na ca brahmalokopapattisparśanagocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
reference: The domain of the four immeasurables, where one does not accept rebirth in the heaven of Brahmā, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.
baseline: One who does not touch the image of Brahma the world of anger the fourfold manifestation of the manifestation is known to be the manifestations of the bodhisattvas.
morphology: If there is a square of evidence and one does not touch the image of Brahma one would not be able to reach the bodhisattvas.

sanskrit: yad dhyānasamādhisamāpattigocaraś ca na ca samādhisamāpattivaśenopapattigocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
reference: The domain of contemplation, concentration, and absorption, where one does not reincarnate in the formless realms by force of these concentrations and absorptions, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.
baseline: If the meditation is completed and the burial is not completed it is a manifestation of the bodhisattvas.
morphology: This is the manifestation of the bodhisattva.

sanskrit: yat smṛtyupasthānagocaraś ca na ca kāyavedanācittadharmātyarthagocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
reference: The domain of the four foci of mindfulness, where body, sensation, mind, and things are not ultimately of concern, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.
baseline: One who does not remember and finds a place is not known to be conscious. This is the manifestation of the bodhisattvas.
morphology: One who does not remember the place of his absence and does not understand the nature of the mind and the dharmā means that he is not aware of the bodhisattvas.

sanskrit: yat samyakprahāṇagocaraś ca na ca kuśalākuśaladvayopalambhagocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
reference: The domain of the four right efforts, where the duality of good and evil is not apprehended, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.
baseline: One who is not able to do well and is not good enough to be able to perform the task is known as a bodhisattva.
morphology: One who is not able to do well and who is illiterate should not do so. This is the path of the bodhisattvas.

sanskrit: yad ṛddhipādābhinirhāragocaraś cānābhogarddhipādavaśavartigocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
reference: The domain of the four bases of magical powers, where they are effortlessly mastered, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.
baseline: The one who is found to be in the position of a bodhisattva should be removed from the seat of the priest.
morphology: This is the manifestation of the bodhisattva.

sanskrit: yat pañcendriyagocaraś ca sarvasatvendriyaparāparajñānagocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
reference: The domain of the five spiritual faculties, where one knows the degrees of the spiritual faculties of living beings, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.
baseline: The five senses which are known to be known to all and the senses that are not known to others are known as the manifestations of the bodhisattvas.
morphology: The five senses which are known to be known to all and the senses that are not known to us are the manifestations of the bodhisattvas.

sanskrit: yat pañcabalapratiṣṭhānagocaraś ca daśatathāgatabalābhisaṃdarśanagocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
reference: The domain of living with the five powers, where one delights in the ten powers of the tathāgata, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.
baseline: One who has seen the manifestation of the five forces and has seen a tenfold manifestation is known to be a bodhisattva.
morphology: One who has attained the position of the five forces and who has visited a place with ten forces is known to be a bodhisattva.

sanskrit: yat saptabodhyaṅgapariniṣpattigocaraś ca buddhiprabhedajñānakauśalyagocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
reference: The domain of perfection of the seven factors of enlightenment, where one is skilled in the knowledge of fine intellectual distinctions, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.
baseline: The seven senses which are visible to the naked eye and the knowledge and skill of the intellect are visible. This is the manifestation of the bodhisattvas.
morphology: One who is able to discern the seven senses of the body and to know the differences between the intellect and the intellect is known to be the master of the bodhisattvas.

sanskrit: yan mārgapratiṣṭhānagocaraś ca kumārgānadhyālambanagocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ / yac chamathavidarśanāsaṃbhāraparyeṣṭigocaraś ca na cātyantaśāntipatanagocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
reference: The domain of living by the eightfold path, without even perceiving any evil paths, such is the domain of the bodhisattva. The domain of the cultivation of the aptitude for mental quiescence and transcendental analysis, where one does not fall into extreme quietism, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.
baseline: If the path has been established and the bodhisattvas are standing in the middle of the elephant it should be seen as the pasture for the buddhis. If it is not seen with the sixfold vision and the body is not visible with the sambhāra. It should be known as the place of peace.
morphology: If the path has been established and if it has been placed in the middle of a cow it should be seen as the pasture for the bodhisattvas. If it has not been seen with the sixfold vision and without the control of the mind it is not known as the future of the past.

sanskrit: yad anutpādalakṣaṇasarvadharmamīmāṃsanagocaraś ca rūpalakṣanānuvyañjanabuddhakāyālaṃkārapariniṣpattigocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /

sanskrit: ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ / yad dharmacakrapravartanamahāparinirvāṇasaṃdarśanagocaraś ca bodhisatvacaryātyajanagocaraś ca, ayam api bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
reference: The domain where one turns the wheel of the holy Dharma and manifests the magnificence of ultimate liberation, yet never forsakes the career of the bodhisattva, such is the domain of the bodhisattva!”

sanskrit: vimalakīrtir āha asti bhadantaśāriputra tathāgatānāṃ bodhisatvānāṃ cācintyo nāma vimokṣaḥ, yatrācintyavimokṣe pratiṣṭhito bodhisatvaḥ sumeruṃ parvatarājaṃ tāvad uccaṃ tāvat pragṛhītaṃ tāvad udviddhaṃ tāvad vistīrṇaṃ sarṣapaphalakośe praveśayet /

baseline: The bodhisattva placed in the open space after having thought of Vimalakīrti the son of Vāṇḍaśarī and the sons of Tātāgatā the buddhis of the four sages the name Vimokṣa. morphology: One should not expand the fruit cell of mustard and one should not put the sumeru.

sanskrit: na cāturmahārājakāyikā devās trayastriṃśato vā jānīran ḥ kasmin vayaṃ prakṣiptāḥ / anye ca satvā ṛddhivineyā jānīyuḥ paśyeyus taṃ sumeruṃ parvatarājaṃ sarśapaphalakośapraviṣṭam /

morphology: The king of the mountains king of sarsonās king goddess of gods or thirty others should not be thrown into it. The other seven should be known by the name of Vruddhīvina. He should be placed in the chest of fruits.

sanskrit: ayaṃ bhadantaśāriputra bodhisatvānām acintyasya vimokṣasya viṣayapraveśaḥ /

morphology: This is the entry into the matter of the emancipation of the bodhisattvas from the illusion of the sons of the god Bhādantāśarī.

sanskrit: punar aparaṃ bhadantaśāriputra acintyavimokṣapratiṣṭhito bodhisatvo yaś caturṣu mahāsamudreṣv apskandhas tam ekasmin romakūpe prakṣipet na ca matsyakacchapaśiśumāramaṇḍūkānām anyeṣāṃ vaudakānāṃ prāṇināṃ pīḍā bhavet / na ca nāgayakṣagandharvāsurāṇām evaṃ bhavet ḥ kasmin vayaṃ prakṣiptāḥ /
reference: “Furthermore, reverend Śāriputra, the bodhisattva who lives in the inconceivable liberation can pour into a single pore of his skin all the waters of the four great oceans, without injuring the wateranimals such as fish, tortoises, crocodiles, frogs, and other creatures, and without the nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, and asuras even being aware of where they are.
baseline: Then the son of a sage who is a bodhisattva standing on the other side of the sea and having been cast into a pit of the sun would not be able to bear the sufferings of fish buffalo monkeys buffaloes and other animals. The son of the sage should not be cast into the pit.

sanskrit: sā ca kriyā prajñāyeta / na ca kaścit satvo vihiṃsito viheṭhito vā bhavet /

sanskrit: imaṃ ca trisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātuṃ bhārgavacakram iva parigṛhya dakṣiṇe pāṇāv avabhrāmya gaṅgānadīvālikāsamān lokadhātūn kṣipet na ca satvā jānīran ḥ kasmin vayaṃ nītāḥ, kuto vāgatā iti / punar api cānāyya yathāsthānaṃ sthāpayet / na ca gamanāgamanaṃ saṃjānīran /
reference: “Such a bodhisattva can pick up with his right hand this billionworld galactic universe as if it were a potter’s wheel and, spinning it round, throw it beyond universes as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, without the living beings therein knowing their motion or its origin, and he can catch it and put it back in its place, without the living beings suspecting their coming and going and yet the whole operation is visible.

morphology: Having taken the three cubits of gold and the eight cubits the metal of the earth the iron of the world the water of the south the elements of the river Ganges rivers rivers and other elements of earth and the metal should not be taken away by us. sanskrit: tatrācintyavimokṣapratiṣṭhito bodhisatvo 'pramāṇasaṃsāravainayikānāṃ satvānāṃ vainayikavaśam upādāya saptarātraṃ kalpam atikrāntam ādarśayet saṃkṣiptasaṃsāravainayikānāṃ satvānāṃ vainayikavaśam upādāya kalpaṃ saptarātram atikrāntam ādarśayet /
reference: The bodhisattva who lives in the inconceivable liberation, for the sake of disciplining those living beings who are disciplined through immeasurable periods of evolution, can make the passing of a week seem like the passing of an eon, and he can make the passing of an eon seem like the passing of a week for those who are disciplined through a short period of evolution.

reference: Having crossed buddhafields as numerous as the sands of the Ganges downward, and having taken up a buddhafield, he can rise up through buddhafields as numerous as the sands of the Ganges and place it on high, just as a strong man may pick up a jujube leaf on the point of a needle.

sanskrit: evam eva āyuṣmañ śāriputra ihācintyavimokṣe nirdiśyamāne sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhā iha jātyandhā iva cakṣurvihīnā ekasminn apy acintyakāraṇe na pratyakṣāḥ /
reference: Likewise, venerable Śāriputra, when this door of the inconceivable liberation is taught, all the disciples and solitary sages are sightless, like the man blind from birth, and cannot comprehend even a single cause of the inconceivable liberation.

morphology: One who knows the name of the scholar should liberate him from the thought and give him good sense in the answer of the listener.

sanskrit: sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhair imaṃ dharmanirdeśaṃ śrutvā rudadbhis trisāhasramahāsāhasro lokadhātur vijñāpayitavyaḥ / sarvabodhisatvaiś ca pramuditair imam acintyavimokṣaṃ śrutvā mūrdhnā saṃpratyetavyaḥ, adhimuktibalaṃ ca saṃjanayitavyam /

sanskrit: kuṇḍalī iti matiḥ ca iyam jāta avasthā viśeṣayoḥ / caitra kuṇḍalayoḥ eva saṃyogaḥ iva jāyate //

sanskrit: saḥ avasthā atiśayaḥ tādṛś dṛṣṭaḥ anyatra niṣidhyate / caitre kuṇḍale ityādau na saṃyogaḥ tu adṛṣṭitaḥ //

sanskrit: na para abhimatāt yogāt jāyate yukta vastu dhīḥ / yukta buddhi tayā yadvat prāsāda ādiṣu yukta dhīḥ // aneka vastu sadbhāve jāyamāna tayā athavā / vibhakta aneka tantu ādi viṣayāḥ iva būddhayaḥ // vibhāge api yathāyogam vācyam etat pramā dvayam / ekasya aneka vṛttiḥ ca na yuktā iti prabādhakam //
reference: The notion of things being ‘conjunct’ cannot be due to the conjunction postulated by the other party,a) because it is the notion op ‘being conjunct’,—like the notion op ‘being conjunct’ in connection with the mansion and such things;—or (b) because it appears only when there is more than one thing,—like the cognitions op several differentiated yarns.—The same two arguments may be urged mutatis mutandis, against disjunction also.—And the reason annulling (both these conceptions op conjunction and disjunction) consists in the pact that it cannot be right for one thing to subsist in more things than one
baseline: One should not think that the objects which are made from the yogic practice are good. One should say that many things are good and one should go to the palace and other places. morphology: One should not think about the objects that are present in the temple. One should say that the objects which are found in the palace are not present in good spirits. Many objects are found to be present in a good mood. Many things are found inside the palace. Many fibres are found outside the temple and the other are not found in a particular department. One person should not have two professions. One man should not be present here.

sanskrit: para apara abhidhāna ādi nimittam yat ca kalpyate / para tvam apara tvam ca diś kālau adhikam na tat // yathā nīla ādi rūpāṇi krama bhāva vyavasthiteḥ / anya upādhi viveke api tathā u acyante tathā apare //
reference: The name (and idea) of ‘priority’ and ‘posteriority’ have been assumed as the basis of the notions of ‘fore’ and ‘aft’,—as these notions cannot be determined in reference to space and time.—But just as the blue and other colours, which come into existence in succession (one after the other), come to be spoken of ‘fore’ and ‘aft’, without reference to distinctions due to any other conditions,—so would the said notions be in regard to other things also
baseline: The other forms of the word are also mentioned in the preceptor's order. The other names are given in the foreword the other form the third form and the other forms are not so much in the past. Just as the blue forms are assigned in the order of the precessor the others are assigned to the other titles in the sense of wisdom.
morphology: Then the other syllables should be mentioned for the sake of the beginning. Then you should be described as the other and the other forms should not be mentioned in the same way in the order as the blue syllables the original forms the other titles should be given in the sense of order.

sanskrit: saṅkhyā yoga ādayaḥ sarve na dravya avyatirekiṇaḥ / tad vyavacchedaka tvena daṇḍa ādiḥ iva ced matam // teṣām saṃvṛti sattvena varṇana ādiṣṭa sādhanam / tattva anya tvena nirvācyam na eva saṃvṛti sadyataḥ //
reference: If it be held that—“number, conjunction and the rest cannot be non-different from substance, because they serve to characterise and differentiate this latter,—like the stick”,—then [our answer is that] there is proving of what is admitted by us, if what is meant is that they have an ‘illusory existence’; because what is ‘imaginary’ cannot be defined either as ‘this’ or ‘not this
baseline: One should say that one who destroys all things and does not acquire the elements would be punished as if they were acquired by the beginning. One would describe them by the prāmvritti sattva. One should not acquire any other means or principles by the end.
morphology: One who does not attain the number of yogas does not acquire all things and does not destroy them one should punish them as if they were born. One should describe them with the principle of samvritti one who has ordered the means and other elements. One who has not attained samvrutti should not do so.

sanskrit: atha anirvacanīya tvam samūha ādeḥ niṣidhyate / yasmāt niyata dharma tvam rūpa śabda rasa ādi vat //

baseline: Having said this unambiguously it is forbidden for you to enter into a group. You are the prescribed form sound taste and sound.
morphology: The group of people is forbidden to speak so. The prescribed religion should be described as the form the word the rasa and the words.

sanskrit: niḥsvabhāva tayā tasya tattvataḥ ambara padma vat / na siddhāḥ niyatāḥ dharmāḥ kalpanā āropitāḥ tu te // tathā eva uktau anekāntaḥ viyat padma ādibhiḥ yatas / abhedaḥ vyatirekaḥ ca vastuni eva vyavasthitaḥ //
reference: In reality, the ‘group’ is absolutely feature-less; hence, like the ‘sky-lotus’, it can have no specific properties; they are all figments of imagination.—Even when stated in this form, the reasoning adduced would be ‘fallible’, in view of things like the ‘sky-lotus in fact, ‘non-difference’ as well as ‘difference’ rests always in an object
baseline: Those who do not have the nature of the self those who do the work of the lotus those which are not established by the principles of the pāmā the dharmā and the concept of dharma those that are imposed by the lotuses etc. The objects which are undisturbed and opposites are the same.
morphology: Those who do not possess the nature of the self those who do so by the principle of the āmbar pāmas those which do not fulfil the principles of the dharmā and are not determined by the concept of dharma and those who are imposed by the lotus etc. The objects which are unbreakable and opposites are arranged in the same manner.

sanskrit: saṅkhyā ādeḥ dravyataḥ anya tvam evam ced pratipādyate / āśraya asiddha tā hetoḥ saṅkhyā ādīnām asiddhitaḥ //
reference: Thus then, if what is meant to be asserted is that number and the rest are other than (different from) substance,—then the reason becomes open to the fallacy of ‘having no substratum’,—because number and the rest are not admitted at all

morphology: The number of the adivasis is said to be the same as that of others. If the shelter is not available for them the number of Adivasis would be not available.

sanskrit: samuccaya ādi bhinnam tu dravyam eva tathā ucyate / svarūpāt eva bhedaḥ ca vyāhataḥ sādhitaḥ bhavet //
reference: If it is substance itself, as diversified through ‘group’, etc., that is spoken of as such,—then what the argument would prove would be the difference of substance from itself—thus involving self-contradiction
baseline: The difference between the set and the object is said to be the same as that of the form. The difference should be made by the same method.
morphology: The difference between the set and the object is said to be the same as the difference between forms.

sanskrit: vega ākhyaḥ bhāvanā saṃjñaḥ sthita sthāpaka lakṣaṇaḥ / saṃskāraḥ trividhaḥ proktaḥ na asau saṃgacchate akhilaḥ // kṣaṇika tvāt padārthānām na kācid vidyate kriyā / yad prabandhasya hetuḥ syāt saṃskāraḥ vega saṃjñakaḥ //
reference: Momentum has been described as being of three kinds—named ‘vega’, velocity,—‘bhāvanā’, impression,—and ‘sthitasthāpaka’, ‘elasticity’.—all this however is not compatible because things being momentary, there can be no action in them, of the continuity of which the momentum named ‘velocity’ could be the cause
baseline: One who does not know the speed the feeling the sense the position the establishing qualities the three kinds of samskars the whole world is not connected with you for a while. One who knows the nature of things and the reason for the arrangement of things is samskaras vaagas samsakars sanskaras etc.
morphology: One who does not associate with the three forms of samskara one who has the sense of speed one that has the senses and the three kinds of qualities that are established in the form of the three types of sāśkars one whose actions are temporary and does not involve the objects one is the cause of the management of sanskars and one who is aware of the speed.

sanskrit: bhāvanā ākhyaḥ tu saṃskāraḥ cetasaḥ vāsanā ātmakaḥ / yuktaḥ na ātma guṇaḥ ca idam yujyate tad nirākṛteḥ //
reference: The momentum called ‘impression’ is of the nature of an impress on the mind. it cannot be a quality of the soul; because this has been rejected
baseline: One who does not possess the qualities of the self would not be able to do so if he disbelieved.
morphology: One who does not possess the qualities of the self would not be able to attain these qualities.

sanskrit: sthita sthāpaka rūpaḥ tu na yuktaḥ kṣaṇabhaṅgataḥ / sthita artha asambhavāt bhāve tādrūpyāt eva saṃsthitiḥ //
reference: There can be no such quality as ‘elasticity’, because things are in a ‘perpetual flux’, and hence nothing can be lasting (sthita); if there were any such thing, it should continue to exist in that same form
baseline: The established form is not established by the moment of division. The meaning of standing is impossible. It is established by that form.
morphology: The established form is not established by the moment of division. The meaning of standing is impossible. It is established by that form.

reference: The momentary existence of a thing consists merely in its being produced from its cause; and the ‘continuity in the chain’ also (of every succeeding thing) is due to being produced from each preceding thing
baseline: A moment is a place created for its own sake. It should be continued with the previous effect and with the arrangement.
morphology: One should maintain one place for a while for his own sake. One should proceed from the previous influence with the arrangement.

sanskrit: na anyathā udayavān eṣa kasya asau sthāpakaḥ tatas / na ca asya dṛṣṭam hetu tvam saṃskāraḥ anyaḥ api vā bhavet // utpannasya eva ceṣṭaḥ ayam vastra ādeḥ sthāpakaḥ guṇaḥ / guṇa saṃskāra nāma evam sarvathā api na saṃbhavī //
reference: What is not-momentary] does not appear in any other form;—of what then could the momentum be the ‘establisher’?—Nor has this momentum been found to have causal character; the cause then may consist of this momentum or something else. Further, the momentum in question has been held to be a quality that re-establishes what has been already produced,—such for example, as the cloth.—What therefore has been called a ‘quality’ and ‘momentum’ is not possible
baseline: If it is not raised it should not be placed in the hands of any other person. It should be seen as the cause of the creation. It is not possible to place it in the clothes of another person. The qualities of the person should be retained in the same manner.
morphology: If it is not raised it should not be placed in the place of any other person. If it has not been placed in that place it would not be possible to place it in the same way as the one who created it. It should be placed on the same cloth and the same quality as that placed on it.

sanskrit: manaḥ yoga ātmanām pūrvam vistareṇa nibandhanāt / para ukta lakṣaṇa upetam na adṛṣṭam upapadyate //
reference: Mind, mind’s contact and the soul having been previously discarded,—there can be no ‘unseen force’ of the kinds postulated by the other party
baseline: The preliminaries to the mind the yoga the practice of the self the prelimination and the premeditation should be followed. The above attributes should not be considered as good.
morphology: The preceptor of the mind the yoga of the self should be described in detail. Then the above mentioned qualities should not be considered as good.

sanskrit: kṣaṇa kṣayiṣu bhāveṣu karma utkṣepa ādi asambhavi / jāta deśe cyuteḥ eva tad anya prāpti asambhavāt //
reference: In things that are in a ‘perpetual flux’, any action, in the shape of ‘throwing up’ and the like, is impossible; because it ceases at the very place where it is born, and hence it cannot get at any other place

morphology: It would be impossible to extract the work for a while in the absence of the desire. It would become impossible to obtain it in the country.

sanskrit: janma atirikta kālam hi kriyā kālam pare jaguḥ / iṣṭa āśutara nāśeṣu dīpa ādiṣu api vastuṣu //

baseline: One should create a column beyond the circle of action. One should destroy eight things lamps etc.
morphology: One should create a column beyond the kriya column. One should destroy the objects such as fire fire and other objects.

sanskrit: tathā hi kāraṇa āśleṣaḥ sāmānyasya abhivyañjanam / sva avayave tatas karma vibhāgaḥ tad anantaram // saṃyogasya vināśaḥ ca tatas dravyasya saṃkṣayaḥ / ṣaṣ kṣaṇa sthāyi tā eva iṣṭā dīpa ādau api vastuni //
reference: At the first moment) there is contact with the cause, (2) then the appearance of the generic character,—then (3) some commotion in the parts of the object,—then (4) the disruption of the parts,—then (5) the destruction of the contact,—then (6) the destruction of the object;—in this way, even in the case of the lamp-flame and such things, what has been held is that they last for six moments only

morphology: The same is the cause of the manifestation of the common illusion the division of the action in one's own body after that the destruction of the association the loss of that matter the absence of that thing the remaining of the lamp for sixty seconds the same thing.

sanskrit: paścima agrima deśābhyām viśleṣa a āśleṣa saṃbhave / gantā aparaḥ vā sarvaḥ ca karma ādhāraḥ prakalpitaḥ // yaḥ janmaḥ kṣaṇam adhyāste na eva jātu cala ātmakaḥ / tasya aṇu antara mātre api deśa saṃkrānti asambhavaḥ //
reference: It is only when there is separation from the posterior spot, and contact with the frontal spot, that the object may be assumed to be ‘going’ (‘in motion’), or to be the substratum of any other action. when the mobile person does not last even for a moment,—even though such a person be extremely small, there is no possibility of passing over to another spot removed by the minutest point
baseline: One who has not studied the birth of a person the moment of his birth the movement of the soul the distance between the two countries the country is impossible. One who does not study the birth and the base of all actions even if he does not understand the difference between the atoms of those two countries would not be able to reach the country.
morphology: One who does not study the moment of his birth who is not able to move even if he is born and who is unable to move the country even if his mind is separated from it should be analyzed in the west and the next country.

sanskrit: sthairye tu vastunaḥ sarve durghaṭāḥ gamana ādayaḥ / sutarām eva sarvāsu daśāsu asya aviśeṣataḥ //
reference: In case the object is something lasting, ‘going’ and the rest are all impossible; because such an object should remain the same under all conditions,
baseline: In the case of a fixed object all the misfortune of the object should be avoided. The sutras should be made available in all the ten parts of the body.
morphology: In the case of a fixed object all the misfortune of the object should be avoided. The sutras should be made to pass in all the ten days. It should be retained in its original form.

sanskrit: yadi gantṛ ādi rūpam tad prakṛtyāḥ gamana ādayaḥ / sadā syuḥ kṣaṇam api evam na avatiṣṭheta niścalam // yasmāt gati ādi asattve api prāpnuvanti asya ce dhruvam / atyakta pūrvarū tvāt gati ādi udaya kāla vat //
reference: If the action of going and the rest constituted the very essence of the ‘moving entity’,—then, this latter could not stay immobile for even a single moment; because even when the going, etc. are not there, they should certainly be there,—inasmuch as the object has not renounced its previous form, and is exactly as it was at the time of the appearance of the going, etc
baseline: If the form of nature is always present in the beginning the movement of nature should be continuous even for a moment and the motion of the body does not remain like this. One gets its pole even in the absence of the motion. One who moves from the east to the east would get the motion from the beginning and rise of time.
morphology: If the form of nature is always present in the beginning the movement of nature should be continuous and the moment is not so stable. Even if the movement starts from the beginning and does not happen then one gets the pole of this form. The movement from the east to the east is called the movement beginning beginning and beginning of the rise.

sanskrit: atha āgantra ādi rūpam tad prakṛtyā agamana ādayaḥ / sadā syuḥ kṣaṇam api ekam na eva praspanda vat bhavet // yasmāt gati ādi bhāve api niścala ātmakam eva tat / atyakta pūrvarūpa tvāt niścala ātmaka kāla vat //
reference: If, on the other hand, the objects were, by their nature, of the nature of the ‘immobile entity’,—then absence of going should be there always, and there would be no movement of any kind even for a moment. because, even when going might be there, the object would still be of the nature of the ‘immobile entity’,—because it will not have renounced its previous nature,—just as at the time when it was not moving
baseline: Then the original form should always be derived from the nature of the incarnation. Not a single moment should be repeated. The movement that leads to the beginning of the movement should be determined by the self. The earlier form should be fixed by you.
morphology: One should always begin with the original form of the incarnation that comes from the nature and does not get a single beat. One should never get a beat by the beginning of the movement and the beginning and the fixed self. One who becomes the past form and then ceases to be a fixed self would become the same.

sanskrit: yadi tu syāt agantā ayam ekadā ca anyathā punar / paraspara vibhinna ātma saṃgateḥ bhinna tā bhavet //
reference: If the object were mobile at one time and immobile at another then, inasmuch as two mutually different characters would be there, it would be two different objects
baseline: If it has not been done once it should be done again. It should be different for different parts of the self.
morphology: If it has not been done once it should be done again. It should be different for different parts of the self.

sanskrit: atyanta bhinnau ātmānau tau iti vyavasīyate / viruddha dharma vṛtti tvāt cala niścala vastu vat //
reference: It is clearly seen that the two are entirely different; because of the presence of contradictory properties:—like two things of which one is moving and another not moving
baseline: It is said to be very different from those of the spirits. The opposite is the practice of dharma. You move from a fixed object.
morphology: It is said to be very different from those of the spirits. The opposite is the practice of dharma. You move from a fixed object.

sanskrit: dṛśya tva abhimatam karma na vastu vyatireki ca / dṛśyate saḥ pi nā eva asya sattā yukti anupātinī //
reference: The action that is regarded as visible is nothing different from the object. even such existence of it as would be compatible with reason, is never actually perceived
baseline: One who does not want to see the object and does not do any work should not be seen. He should never be seen to be the master of this entity.
morphology: One who does not want to see the object and does not do any work should not be seen. One who is not aware of the existence of the object should be considered as equal to that.

sanskrit: asthire vā sthire vā evam gati ādīnām asambhavaḥ / prāktana apara deśābhyām vibhāga prāpti ayogataḥ //
reference: Thus ‘going’ and the rest are impossible either in permanent or impermanent things; because it is not possible for them either to be separated from their former place, or to get at another place
baseline: It is impossible for a person to move in such a way whether standing or standing on the bones. He would not be able to get division from the previous countries.
morphology: It is impossible for a person to move in such a way whether in the form of bones or in a stationary position. It is not possible to get division from other countries.

sanskrit: deśa antara upalabdheḥ tu nairantaryeṇa janmanaḥ / samāna apara vastūnām gati bhrāntiḥ pradīpa vat //
reference: The notion of ‘going’ is an illusion,—as in the lamp-flame,—due to the appearance of different but similar things being found consecutively in diverse places
baseline: One who is born from the opposite side of the earth and who has attained the distance of the country would be wrong in the movement of other things.
morphology: One who is born from the opposite side of the earth and who has acquired the country and the other side of it would be wrong in the way of other things.

sanskrit: dravya ādiṣu niṣiddheṣu jātayaḥ api nirākṛtāḥ / padārtha traya vṛttāḥ hi sarvāḥ tāḥ parikalpitāḥ //
reference: Substance’ and other categories having been rejected, the ‘universals’ also have become rejected; as they have all been assumed to subsist in the three categories

sanskrit: tatra iyam dvividhā jātiḥ paraiḥ abhyupagamyate / sāmānyam eva sattā ākhyam samasteṣu anuvṛttitaḥ // dravya tva ādi tu sāmānyam sat viśeṣaḥ abhidhīyate / sva āśrayeṣu anuvṛttasya cetasaḥ hetu bhāvataḥ // vijātibhyaḥ ca sarvebhyaḥ sva āśrayasya viśeṣaṇāt / vyāvṛtti buddhi hetu tvam teṣām eva tatas sthitam //
reference: The ‘universal’ is postulated by the other party in the following manner: “it is of two kinds—‘being’ is a ‘universal’ which is ‘universal’ only,—as it pervades over all things; ‘substance’ and the rest, while being ‘universals are also spoken of as ‘particulars’; because in regard to their own substrata, they become the cause of their comprehensive notion, and also serve to differentiate their substrata from all things belonging to other ‘universals’—and in this way they also become the cause of the exclusive notion of those substrata.”
baseline: There are two kinds of people who come from other countries who are said to be common to others who follow the same entity in all things and who are found to be ordinary in the beginning who have followed the same in their own houses who would be known to others by their own conscience who should be known as theirs who belong to different castes who live therein.
morphology: There are two kinds of people who are born out of others. The common one is called the entity. The original one is known to be common to all. The object is known as the special one. The disciple who is living in his or her own houses is known by the spirit to be the cause of his own consciousness. The enemy is known for his or their own self-sacrifice. He or she is said to be standing there because of the illusion of his mind.

sanskrit: viśeṣāḥ eva kecid tu vyāvṛtteḥ eva hetavaḥ / nitya dravya sthitāḥ ye antyāḥ viśeṣāḥ iti varṇitāḥ //
reference: There are some ‘particulars’ which serve as the basis of ‘exclusion’ only; these have been described as ‘ultimate individualities subsisting in eternal substances
baseline: Some of the special things are said to be for the sake of vyavrti. The things which are present in the past are described as special for the end.
morphology: Some things are described as special for the sake of their existence those things which are always present and those which are described to be special for their end.

sanskrit: yad balāt paramāṇu ādau jāyante yoginām dhiyaḥ / vilakṣaṇaḥ ayam etasmāt iti pratyekam āśritāḥ //
reference: Inasmuch as it is on the strength of these that mystics have the notions,—in connection with the atom and other eternal substances,—that ‘this is different from that’,—these are regarded as subsisting in each of these sub stances.”
baseline: One who is born of a yogin with the same strength as an atom would get. One who becomes independent from this would be called unique.

reference: In the case of things created by imagination, there can be no universal subsisting in them; because there is no possibility of the existence of the individuals (that would make up the universals). Hence the ‘fallibility’ of the opponent’s reasons remains as before.—Similarly with regard to past and future things,—if there is a cognition of an eternal universal, then no such pure ‘universal’ (without the constituent individuals) can ever be apprehended. Or, if such a pure universal by itself were apprehended, then it could not be the ‘universal’ of any particulars. Such a universal could not be manifestable by particulars; just as the himālaya is not manifestable by the vindhya.—Nor can the universal be tied down to the particulars through its birth being dependent upon these,—nor lastly can the universal be dependent upon the particulars for its cognition, because it is eternal and because it is apprehended purely by itself.—There is also no possibility of its being dependent upon any such thing as the contact of its own substratum with the sense-organ concerned. Consequently this universal could either be apprehended at all times, or not apprehended at any time at all.—As regards its capacity to bring about its own cognition by itself, it may or may not have this capacity; whichsoever way it is, it would always remain so. Its natural form,—with or without the said capacity,—would be unshakeable, because it is itself permanent. Who then, could ever shake what is unshakeable?

reference: Why do you say that the word brings about the ‘exclusion of others’? as a matter of fact mere negation is not apprehended in the idea brought about by the word; on the contrary, in the case of all such words as ‘cow’, ‘gavaya’, ‘elephant’, ‘tree’ and so forth,—the verbal cognition that results is always in the positive form.”
baseline: The word naṇu or other mischief is said by you. It is not only forbidden. It pervades the genius. But the word cow cow elephant tree etc. starts the belief.
morphology: How can you say the words nāṇu or other falsehood not only forbidden but it is also expressed in the words gāvā gāva gavā elephant tree etc.

sanskrit: yadi gauḥ iti ayam śabdaḥ kṛtārthaḥ ada nya nirākṛtau / janakaḥ gavi go buddheḥ dṛśyatām aparaḥ dhvaniḥ //
reference: If the whole purpose of the word ‘cow’ is served by the. ‘exclusion of others’,—then, please find some other word which brings about the notion of ‘cow’ in regard to the cow itself.”
baseline: If the word cow is mentioned in the form of a cow then it should be said that the cow is the mother of the cow. The other sound should be seen in the mind.
morphology: If a cow is said to be the same as the other cow it should be said that the cow is not known to be a cow. It should be called a cow and another sound should be heard.

sanskrit: nanu jñāna phalāḥ śabdāḥ na ca ekasya phala dvayam / apavāda vidhi jñāne phalam ekasya vā katham //
reference: In fact, cognition is the fruit of words; and no single word can have two fruits. how too could both affirmation and negation be the fruit of any one word?”
baseline: One who knows the knowledge and the words should not bear one fruit and two fruits. One who does not know the method or the method should bear one.
morphology: The fruit of knowledge is neither one nor two. But the fruit of wisdom is one or two.

sanskrit: prāk agauḥ iti vijñānam go śabda śrāviṇaḥ bhavet / yena agoḥ pratiṣedhāya pravṛttaḥ gauḥ iti dhvaniḥ //
reference: When one hears the word ‘cow’ uttered, he should, first of all have the idea of the non-cow,—as the word ‘cow’ would have been uttered for the purpose of negativing the ‘non-cow’.”
baseline: The sound of cow should be heard before the knowledge of cow is known. Thus the sound of cows is said to be opposed.
morphology: The sound of cow should be heard in the preceptor and the sound of cows should be spoken in order to prevent the occurrence of cow.

sanskrit: ago nivṛttiḥ sāmānyam vācyam yaiḥ rurarīkṛtam / go tvam vastu eva taiḥ uktam etayā hi girā sphuṭam //
reference: Those who have admitted the universal ‘negation of the non-cow’ as the import of the word have, by the expression, admitted the universal ‘cow’ as an entity.”—[Ślokavārtika-Apoha 1]
baseline: Those who have made the cow a thing should be told that it is a clear thing.
morphology: Those who have made the cow as a thing should be told that it is a clear thing.

sanskrit: bhāva antara ātmakaḥ abhāvaḥ yena sarvaḥ vyavasthitaḥ / tatra aśva ādi nivṛtta ātmā bhāvaḥ sakā eti kathyatām //
reference: Inasmuch as all ‘inexistence’ has been held to be of the nature of some other ‘existence’,—please say what that ‘inexistence’ is which is of the nature of the ‘negation of the horse (and otehr non-cows)’?—[Ślokavārtika-Apoha 2]
baseline: The absence of the spirit within the self is said to be the reason for all being arranged. The spirit should be made to feel therein.
morphology: One should say that the feeling of the self is lacking in the sense of feeling and hence everything is arranged. One should feel the spirit at the beginning of the horse.

sanskrit: na iṣṭaḥ asādhāraṇa ātmā vaḥ viśeṣaḥ nirvikalpanāt / tathā ca śābaleya ādiḥ asāmānya prasaṅgataḥ // tasmāt sarbeṣu yat rūpam pratyekam pariniṣṭhitam / go buddhiḥ tad nimittā syā asti tat //
reference: You do not admit of any individuality in the nature of something uncommon (unique), because it is devoid of conceptual content; so also (you do not admit) the ‘variegated animal’ and the like; as in that case the import would not be universal (common).—Hence the idea of the ‘cow’ must be based upon that form which subsists in common in every single individual (cow); [and in this there can be no dispute between us].”—[Ślokavārtika-Apoha 3 & 10]
baseline: One who does not wish to have an extraordinary soul and has not been specially designed and who has not done so should be made aware of the peculiar circumstances. One who has acquired that form in all things is thus endowed with the knowledge of the cow.
morphology: One who does not want to have an extraordinary soul and has not been specially designed and who has been born out of an unusual context has therefore become the form of every one of them. One who has the knowledge of the cow is that person because of that.

sanskrit: niṣedha mātra rūpaḥ ca śabda arthaḥ yadi kalpyate / abhāva śabda vācyā syāt śūnyatā anya prakārakā //
reference: If the import of words be assumed to be of the nature of mere negation, then it would only be another kind of ‘void’ spoken of by means of the negative word.”
baseline: If the word meaning is to be construed as prohibitive and only form then the word absence would be considered as void.
morphology: If the word meaning is only the form and the words are forbidden the meaning of the word absence is said to be empty.

sanskrit: tasyām ca aśva ādi buddhīnām ātma aṃśa grahaṇam bhavet / tatra anya apoha vācya tvam mudhā eva abhyupagamyate //
reference: In that ‘void’ there would be an apprehension of the character of the cognitions themselves of the horse and other things; and in that case it would be useless to posit the ‘Apoha (negation) of others’ as the import of words.”—[Ślokavārtika-Apoha 37]
baseline: The horse should be taken as part of the self of the first wise. One who has not heard another lie would reach the point of death.
morphology: The horse should be taken as part of the self of the original intellects. Having said that one would get there by saying another falsehood. One would get here only after having said that.

sanskrit: sāmānyam vastu rūpam hi buddhi ākāraḥ bhaviṣyati / śabda artha prakalpitaḥ //
reference: In that case, the ‘form of the Cognition which is posited as the ‘Import of Words’, would be the Universal.”—[Ślokavārtika-Apoha 38]
baseline: The general object form would become the form of intellect. The word meaning would be approximated.
morphology: The common object form would be the form of intellect. The word meaning would be derived from the word.

sanskrit: vastu rūpā ca sā buddhiḥ śabda artheṣu upajāyate / teṣu vastu eva kalpyeta vācyam buddhi anapohakam //
reference: As a matter of fact, whenever the said cognition appears in connection with the import of words, it is always in the form of a positive entity; hence in such cases, the import could be assumed to consist of the positive entity only,—a cognition not of the nature of ‘Apoha’.”—[Ślokavārtika-Apoha 39]
baseline: The objects the silver the intellect the words and the meanings are derived from those objects. The objects are thus conceived.
morphology: The objects the silver the intellect the words and the meanings are derived from those objects.

sanskrit: asati api ca bāhye arthe vākya arthaḥ pratibhā yathā / padārthaḥ api tathā eva syāt kim apohaḥ prakalpyate //
reference: even in the absence of the corresponding external object there is intuition expressed by the sentence; similar may be the case with what is expressed by the word also; why should the apoha be postulated at all?”—[Ślokavārtika-Apoha 43]
baseline: If the meaning of the sentence is external and the meaning is same as that of the subject what is the illusion?
morphology: If the meaning of the sentence is external and the meaning is same as that of the subject whether it is false or false.

sanskrit: buddhi antarāt vyavacchedaḥ na ca buddhau pratīyate / svarūpa utpāda mātrāt ca na anyam aṃśam bibhartti sā //
reference: In the case of a cognition, no ‘exclusion of another cognition’ is apprehended; in fact, apart from the coming about of its own form, the cognition carries with it no other factor.”—[Ślokavārtika-Apoha 41]
baseline: One who divides the mind from the inner part of the body does not appear to be a wise person. One who does not deviate from the nature and the product of the form is not a part of it.
morphology: The mind is not separated from the inner part of the body and is not seen to be separate from the outer part. It is not different from the form and the product.

sanskrit: bhinna sāmānya vacanāḥ viśeṣa vacanāḥ ca ye / sarve bhaveyuḥ paryāyāḥ yadi apohasya vācya tā //
reference: If Apoha formed the import of words, then all words would be synonymous,—those that denote diverse universals, as well as those that denote particulars.”—[Ślokavārtika-Apoha 42]
baseline: The different common words particular words etc. should be the same for all. If the misperception has been read it should be repeated.
morphology: The different common words and special words should be the same for all. If one has read the misguided words it would be false.

sanskrit: saṃsṛṣṭa ekatva nānātva vikalpa rahita ātmanām / avastu tvāt apohānām na eva bhedaḥ api vidyate //
reference: There can be no difference among Apohas, because they are non-entities, and devoid of all such conceptions as ‘related ‘one’ and’ many.”—[Ślokavārtika-Apoha 45]
baseline: There is no difference in the existence of the self without having many options.
morphology: There is no difference between the one and the other. There is nothing wrong with you.

sanskrit: yadi vā bhidyamāna tvā dvastva sādhāraṇa aṃśa vat / avastu tve tu anānā tvā t paryāya tvāt na mucyate //
reference: If the Apohas are different, then they must be entities, because of that difference,—just like the specific individuality of things. If they are non-entities, then they cannot be many, and hence they cannot escape from being synonymous.”—[Ślokavārtika-Apoha 46]
baseline: If you are divided into two parts the common part of the body is said to be the same. You are not to be removed from the body by any means.
morphology: If you are divided into two parts the common part of the body is said to be the same. You are not to be removed from the body by any means.

sanskrit: nanu ca aśva ādi bhedena bhedaḥ apohasya setsyati / na viśeṣaḥ svatas tasya paratas ca upajāyate //
reference: There would certainly be difference among Apohas, based upon the difference among the horse and other things.—[Ślokavārtika-Apoha 47]a) “In fact, there can be no distinction among Apohas—either by themselves, or through others.”—[ibid.]b)
baseline: The difference between a bull and a horse is not different from the original. It does not make any difference. It also does not create its own layers.
morphology: The difference between a horse and a bull is not different from the original. The difference is not unique. It is not inherently different.

sanskrit: saṃsargiṇaḥ api hi ādhārāḥ yam na bhindanti rūpataḥ / apohyaiḥ bahis aṅgaiḥ sa bhidyeta iti a ti kalpanā //
reference: When even the substrata to which they are related do not make any difference in the form of the Apohas,—that they would be differentiated by the excluded things, which are exterior to them, would be an assumption that is too far-fetched.”—[Ślokavārtika-Apoha 52]
baseline: The idea is that one who does not penetrate the outer parts of the body with the help of the other parts of his body should be separated from the other.
morphology: One would imagine that one would not be separated from the other by the elements of the body such as those who are connected with him. One would be divided by the external organs such as the form of the enemy.

sanskrit: tathā eva ādhāra bhedena api asya bhedaḥ na yujyate / na hi sambandhi bhedena bhedaḥ vastuni api iṣyate // kim uta avastu asaṃsṛṣṭam avyāvṛttam nivarttate / anavāpta viśeṣa aṃśam yat kim api anirūpitam //
reference: In the same manner, its diversity cannot be due to the diversity of its substratum;—diversity in the relative of a thing does not justify the assumption of diversity in the thing also. How much less there is exclusion possible for that which is a non-entity, unrelated, undifferentiated, unspecified, vague and undetermined?”—[Ślokavārtika-Apoha 48-49]
baseline: In the same way the difference is not made by the difference in the base. The difference is also made by any difference in relation to the material. What is left is left undefiled and what is left unformed. What has been left undeveloped is left out.
morphology: In the same way the difference is not made by the difference in the base. By the difference between the two the difference of the objects is also not made. What is left out what is left over what has been left out and what has not been left behind what was left out of the particular part.

sanskrit: na ca aprasiddha sārūpyam apoha viṣaya ātmanā / śaktaḥ kaścid api jñātum gavādīn ataḥ //
reference: As a matter of fact, no one can conceive of the cow and other things—any similarity of form among whom is not admitted,—to be the substratum of Apoha.”
baseline: One should not mislead the self by making a false statement which is not known to him. One should know anyone.
morphology: One should not mislead the self by saying that one is not known to be powerful.

sanskrit: apohyān api ca aśva ādīn eka dharma anvayāt ṛte / na nirūpayitum śaktiḥ tad apohaḥ na siddhyati //
reference: In the absence of a common property, it is not possible to determine the things excluded (by Apoha). For this reason also there can be no Apoha.”—[Ślokavārtika-Apoha 72]
baseline: The power to define the misguided and the horses etc. is not established by the application of the same dharma. That misguidance is not proved.
morphology: The power to define a religion for the misguided and the horses etc. is not established by the power of misguiding.

sanskrit: na ca anvaya vinirmuktā pravṛttiḥ śabda liṅgayoḥ / tābhyām ca na vinā apohaḥ na ca asādhāraṇe anvayaḥ //
reference: Of the word and the indicative, no operation is possible without concomitance;—and without these (word and the indicative), there can be no Apoha;—and there can be no concomitance for what is ‘uncommon’ (unique, specific).”—[Ślokavārtika-Apoha 73]
baseline: Neither the words nor the gender of the person are known to be false or false. Neither the word nor the other words are known as false or illusory.
morphology: Neither the words nor the senses of the sexes should be used without any illusion or illusion. Nor should they be used in a way that is not appropriate.

sanskrit: apohaḥ ca api aniṣpannaḥ sāhacaṃrya kva kathyatām / tasmin adṛśyamāne ca na tayoḥ syāt pramāṇa tā //

baseline: One should say that there is no evidence of them in the case of falsehood illusion and illusion. One should not say that they are not visible in that.
morphology: One should say that there is no evidence of any illusion or illusion. One should not say that they are not visible in the story.

sanskrit: na ca adarśana mātreṇa tābhyām pratyāyanam bhavet / sarvatra eva hi adṛṣṭa tvāt pratyayaḥ na viśiṣyate //
reference: They could not signify anything by mere non-perception; because non-perception being common in all cases, there could be no distinction.—[Ślokavārtika-Apoha 75]
baseline: One should not confide in you by the mother of the unvisible. One would not be able to confide trust in you if he is not present everywhere.
morphology: One should not confide in you by the mother of the unapparent. One would not be able to confide with you by this fate everywhere.

sanskrit: atha asati api sārūpye syāt apohasya kalpanā / gavāśvayoḥ ayam kasmāt ago apohaḥ na kalpyate //
reference: It might be argued that—Even in the absence of similarity of form, there could be assumption of Apoha;—then why is the Apoha of the ‘non-cow’ not assumed in the case of the cow and the horse?”—[Ślokavārtika-Apoha 76]
baseline: Even if it is so the illusion should be conceived in the same way. This illusion cannot be imagined in any other way.
morphology: Even if it is so the illusion should be conceived in the same way. This illusion cannot be conceived by any of the gavasva.

sanskrit: śābaleyāt ca bhinna tvam bāhuleya aśvayoḥ samam / sāmānyam na anyat iṣṭam ced kva ago apohaḥ pravarttatām //
reference: Difference from the spotted cow is the same in the black cow and in the horse. so that if no other ‘commonalty’ is admitted, whereto would, the Apoha of the non-cow apply?”—[Ślokavārtika-Apoha 77]
baseline: You should separate the two cubs from each other and make the horses equal. The common one should not be equal to the other. If you do not wish to do so then you should introduce falsehood.
morphology: If you want to separate the horses from the horses you should make them equal. If you do not want to do otherwise then you should introduce the illusion.

sanskrit: indriyaiḥ na api ago apohaḥ prathamam vyavasīyate / na anyatra śabda vṛttiḥ ca kim dṛṣṭvā sa prayujyatām //
reference: As a matter of fact, the Apoha of the non-cow has never been previously perceived by the sense-organs;—and the operation of words does not lie anywhere else. On the perception of what then would the word be used?”—[Ślokavārtika-Apoha 78]
baseline: One would not know the meaning of the word or the practice of the words in the first place. He would not use it if he saw the words and practices elsewhere.
morphology: One would not be able to understand the senses. One would be misinformed in the first place. He would not use the words or the practices of others by seeing what they are.

sanskrit: pūrva uktena prabandhena na anumā api atra vidyate / sambandha anubhavaḥ api asya tena nā eva upapadyate //
reference: by what has gone before, there can be no inference either, in this case; and for the same reason there can be no conception of any connection of this.”—[Ślokavārtika-Apoha 79]
baseline: There is no sense of attachment or experience in this regard. It is not the same as the previous arrangement.
morphology: There is no sense of attachment or experience in this regard.

sanskrit: a go śabda abhidheya tvam gamya tām ca katham punar / na dṛṣṭaḥ yatra go śabdaḥ sambandha anubhava kṣaṇe //
reference: How could one apprehend the fact of something not being denoted by the word ‘cow’—‘It could be learnt from the fact that the word cow was not found to be applied to it at the moment of the apprehension of the connection of that word’. [This is what the Bauddha may say.]”—[Ślokavārtika-Apoha 81]
baseline: The word go you have found and how it is found again. You do not see where the word cow is found in the moment of contact.
morphology: The word go you have found out and how it is found again. You do not see where the word cow is found in the moment of contact.

sanskrit: ekasmāt tarhi go piṇḍāt yat anyat sarvam eva tat / bhavet apohyam iti etat na sāmānyasya vācya tā //
reference: In that case, all things, with the sole exception of the single individual cow, would become excluded by the Apoha; and in that case it would not be proved that any commonalty constitutes the import of words.”—[Ślokavārtika-Apoha 82]
baseline: It is not said by the common man that everything other than a cow and a cow should be made into a piece.
morphology: It is not said by the common man that all things other than a cow and a calf are illusory.

sanskrit: siddhaḥ ca agauḥ apohyeta goniṣedha ātmakaḥ ca saḥ / tatra gauḥ eva vaktavyaḥ nañā yaḥ pratiṣidhyate // sa ced ago nivṛtti ātmā bhavet anyonya saṃśrayaḥ / siddhaḥ ced gauḥ apohāṃrtha vṛthak apoha prakalpanam //
reference: It is only a well-established entity in the shape of the non-cow that could be excluded by the Apoha (denoted by the word ‘cow’);—and the non-cow is of the nature of the negation of the cow;—hence it has to be explained what this cow is which is negatived (in the non-cow).—If this cow is of the nature of the negation of the non-cow, then there is mutual interdependence.—If the cow is admitted as an entity for the sake of the Apoha, then the postulating of the Apoha becomes futile.”—[Ślokavārtika-Apoha 83-84]
baseline: One who is not a cow should be said to be the one who has committed suicide by committing the act of committing theft. One should be made a cow that is not in danger by committing theft by committing misdeeds.
morphology: One who is not justified by the belief that a cow should be destroyed by the enemy should be saved by one another.
