sanskrit: gavya siddhe tu agauḥ na asti tad abhāve tu gauḥ kutas / na ādhāra ādheya vṛtti ādi sambandhaḥ ca api abhāvayoḥ //
reference: Unless the cow is established, there can be no non-cow; and if there is no non-cow, how can the cow be there? Between two negations, there can be no such relation as that of the container and the contained and the like.”—[Ślokavārtika-Apoha 85]
baseline: If a cow is found to be good it is not good. If there is no cow then the cow should be taken care of. If the cow is not supported then it should not be used for the purpose of maintaining the habit and relationship.
morphology: If a cow is found to be ready it is not good. In the absence of that cow it would not be good. It would not have the base. It should not be associated with the beginning of the profession.

sanskrit: na ca asādhāraṇam vastu gamyate apohavat tayā / katham vā parikalpyeta sambandhaḥ vastu avastunoḥ //
reference: As a matter of fact, any thing uncommon (unique, specific) is never cognised as qualified by the Apoha. how too could any relationship be assumed between an entity and a non-entity?—[Ślokavārtika-Apoha 86]
baseline: An object that is not exceptional should not be misinterpreted. It should be described as having no relation to the object.
morphology: There is no such thing as an extraordinary thing. It is not known how it should be related to the objects.

sanskrit: svarūpa sattva mātreṇa na syāt kiñcid viśeṣaṇam / sva buddhyā rajyate yena viśeṣyam tat viśeṣaṇam //
reference: In fact, nothing can serve as a qualification. by its mere existence; it is only when it colours the qualified with its own cognition that it becomes its qualification.”—[Ślokavārtika-Apoha 87]
baseline: One who does not possess the qualities of the self the mother or the intellect would acquire the qualities that are inherent in one.
morphology: If the character is not of the nature of the mother then the adjective is derived from one's own intellect.

sanskrit: na ca api aśva ādi śabdebhyaḥ jāyate apoha bodhanam / viśeṣya buddhiḥ iṣṭā iha na ca ajñāta viśeṣaṇā //
reference: The terms ‘horse’ and the rest do not bring about the cognition of the Apoha; and the idea of the qualified that is held in this connection cannot be one in which the qualification is not cognised.”—[Ślokavārtika-Apoha 88]
baseline: Nor does the word śvāda occur in the preceptor. It is said to be wise and not known.
morphology: Nor does the word śvāda occur in the beginning of the story. It is said to teach illusion. It does not want wisdom. It has no unknown characteristics.

sanskrit: na ca anya rūpam anyādṛś kuryāt jñānam viśeṣaṇam / katham ca anyādṛśe jñāne tat ucyeta viśeṣaṇam //
reference: The qualification cannot bring about a cognition which is like something totally different; for how can that be said to be the qualification in a cognition which is like something different?”—[Ślokavārtika-Apoha 89]
baseline: One should not make any other form or adjective. One should say the adjectives in another form or in other forms.
morphology: One should not make any other form or adjective. One should say the adjectives in the knowledge of others.

sanskrit: atha anyathā viśeṣye api syāt viśeṣaṇa kalpanā / tathā sati hi yat kiñcid prapadyeta viśeṣaṇam //
reference: If a qualification be regarded as such even in regard to the qualified thing which is totally different, then, everything can serve as the qualification (of everything).”—[Ślokavārtika-Apoha 90]
baseline: It is said that if the adjective is not there then whatever adjectives are there would be given to it.
morphology: Then the adjective should be said to be the same as the noun otherwise. Then whatever adjectives are mentioned should be given.

sanskrit: abhāva gamya rūpe ca na viśeṣye asti vastu tā / viśeṣitam apohena vastu vācyam na te asti atas //
reference: If the qualified thing is cognisable in the form of negation, then it cannot be an entity; consequently for you, there can be no entity that could be denoted by words as qualified by Apoha.”—[Ślokavārtika-Apoha 91]
baseline: A thing that is lacking in its form or form is not in the special category. It is not so in the case of a thing that has been misused.
morphology: There is nothing lacking in the form and form of the object. That thing is not there in the world.

sanskrit: yadi api apoha nirmukte na vṛttiḥ śabda liṅgayoḥ / yuktaḥ tathā api bodhaḥ tu jñātum vastu avalambate //
reference: Even though the word and the indicative may not operate upon anything devoid of Apoha,—yet the cognition rests upon the entity which is what it apprehends.”—[Ślokavārtika-Apoha 92]
baseline: Even if one does not get rid of the error one would not be able to understand the meaning of the word and the words of the two genders.
morphology: Even if one does not get rid of the error one would not be able to understand the meaning of the word and the gender.

sanskrit: na ca asādhāraṇam vastu buddhau viparivarttate / na ca api nirvikalpa tvāt tasya yuktā adhigamya tā //
reference: As a matter of fact, the uncommon thing never figures in the cognition; nor again can it be rightly regarded as cognisable, because it is ‘indeterminate’.”—[Ślokavārtika-Apoha 93]

sanskrit: sarva śabdasya kaḥ ca arthaḥ vyavacchedyaḥ prakalpyate / na asarva nāma kiñcid hi bhavet yasya nirākriyā // eka ādi asarvam iti ced artha apohaḥ prasajyate / aṅgānām pratiṣiddha tvāt aniṣṭeḥ ca aṅginaḥ pṛthak // evam samūha śabda arthe samudāyi vyapohataḥ / anya aniṣṭeḥ ca sarve api prāpnuvanti nirarthakāḥ // dvi ādi śabdāḥ iha iṣṭāḥ ca ye samuccaya gocarāḥ / eka ādi pratiṣedhena na bhaveyuḥ tathāvidhāḥ
reference: In the case of the word ‘all’ (‘sarva’) what is it that is assumed to be the ‘excluded’? There is no such thing as the non-all, which could be excluded.—If it be urged that ‘one and the rest’ are the non-all, then it comes to be the exclusion of the denotation itself; as the parts would be excluded, and no whole is admitted.—Similarly, in regard to the denotation of the word ‘group’ (‘samūha’), the constituents would be excluded; and nothing apart from this is admitted; hence all such words become deprived of their meaning.—As regards the words ‘two’ and the rest, which also are applied to groups, as the ‘one’ and other constituents would be excluded, they could no longer be so applicable.—Then again, the denotation of the word ‘cow’ is said to be the ‘non-non-cow’;—now is this positive or negative? If it is positive, is it the cow or the non-cow?—If it is the cow, then there is no dispute; as the denotation turns out to be of the positive character. On the other hand, if it is the non-cow that is denoted by the word ‘cow’,—that would exhibit a wonderful insight into the meanings of words indeed!—Nor can it be negative; as, in that case injunction and the rest would not be possible.—Nor does any one ever comprehend a negation from the word ‘cow’.”

sanskrit: na agauḥ gauḥ iti śabda arthaḥ kasmāt ca apohaḥ iṣyate / kena hi ago tvam āsaktam gauḥ yena etat apohyate // agoḥ apohaḥ yaḥ ca ayam gavi śabda arthaḥ ucyate / sa kim goḥ vyatiriktaḥ vā avyatiriktaḥ upeyate // vibhinnaḥ api āśritaḥ vā syāt athavā syāt anāśritaḥ / āśrita tve guṇaḥ prāptaḥ na dravya vacanam tatas // atas gauḥ iti śabdena guṇa mātra abhidhānataḥ / sāmānādhikaraṇyam syāt na gauḥ gacchati tiṣṭhati // atha anāśrit
reference: Why is the denotation of the word (‘cow’) held to be the Apoha—in the form ‘the cow is not non-cow’? Who has ever attributed the character of the non-cow to the cow—that it is denied here?—It is held that it is the ‘exclusion of the non-cow’ in the cow, which forms the denotation of the word;—is this held to be something different from the cow? Or non-different?—If it is different, does it abide—or not abide—anywhere? If it does abide, then it becomes a quality, and the word cannot be denotative of the substance;—and thus as the word ‘cow’ would denote only a quality, there would be no co-ordination in such expressions as ‘the cow moves’, ‘the cow stands—if it does not abide in any thing, then what would be the sense in which it could be mentioned, for the purpose of exclusion, by the term ‘agoḥ’, ‘of the non-cow’?—If, lastly, the ‘Apoha’, ‘exclusion of others’ is held by you to be non-different (from the cow),—then it comes to be the same as cow; what more would, in that case, be expressed (by the term ‘Apoha’)?”
baseline: The word gau means neither cow nor cow and is it a misguided cow or a cow which is misused by you. A cow is said to be misguised by you and is not a cow. It means a cow or other than that whether it is a different cow or is dependent on you or not. It is said that a cow is not dependent on a cow and does not possess the qualities of a thing or a word. sanskrit: pratibhāvam apohaḥ ayam ekaḥ anekaḥ api vā bhavet / yadi ekaḥ aneka go yuktaḥ go tvam eva bhavet asau // aneka tve api ca ānantyam piṇḍa vat saṃprayujyate / tena bheda vat eva asya vācya tā na upayujyate //
reference: Is this Apoha one and the same in connection with all things? or is it several?—If one, then, being related to several cows, it would be the same as the universal—‘cow’—if it is several, then it would be endless,—like so many individual objects. consequently, just like the diverse individuals, this also could not be ‘denoted’
baseline: One who has the talent or the illusion of having a cow is called a cow. If one has many cows and has only one cow then he would be called many and would not be able to bear the burden of a pinda. He would not use it by reciting the same discordant verse.

sanskrit: anya apohaḥ ca kim vācyaḥ kim vā avācyaḥ ayam iṣyate / vācyaḥ api vidhi rūpeṇa yadi vā anya niṣedhataḥ // vidhi ātmanā asya vācya tve tyājyam ekānta darśanam / sarvatra anya nirāsaḥ ayam śabda arthaḥ iti varṇitam // atha apoha vyudāsena yadi apohaḥ abhidhīyate / tatra tatra evam icchāyām anavasthā bhavet tatas // atha api avācyaḥ eva ayam yadi apohaḥ tvayā iṣyate / tena anya apoha kṛt śabdaḥ iti bādhyeta te vacaḥ
reference: This Apoha, ‘exclusion of other things’—is it itself denoted or not-denoted? Even if it is denoted, is it denoted as something positive? Or only as the ‘negation of other things’?—If it is denoted as something positive, then you should abandon your extremist view, whereby it has been asserted that ‘in every case it is the exclusion of other things that is denoted by words.’—If, on the other hand, the said ‘exclusion’ (Apoha) is denoted in the form of the ‘exclusion of other things’,—then such a view would involve an infinite regress.—If then it be held by you that the said Apoha (exclusion of other things) is not denoted, then your assertion, that ‘the word always brings about the exclusion of other things’, would become annulled.”
baseline: One who has not heard another falsehood or what is said to be said or said to have been said or spoken or said or written or spoken in the manner prohibited or otherwise one who has read it by the self one should see it alone one would become disenchanted everywhere and one would find the falsehood therein. baseline: Even if they do not follow the same religion they will be misled and misguided. They will get away with a different character.
morphology: Even if they do not follow the same religion they will be misled and misled. They will get away with a different character.

sanskrit: eka pratyavamarśe hi kecid eva upayoginaḥ / prakṛtyāḥ bhedavat tve api na anyaḥ iti upapāditam //
reference: It would be only a few things which, while being diverse by themselves, would bring about a single determinate judgment; as already explained by us
baseline: It has been said that one should use only a few things in the course of a lifetime. You are not different from others as you are different from nature.
morphology: It has been said that one should use only a few things in a year. You are not different from others as you are different from nature.

sanskrit: a tad rūpa parāvṛttam vastu mātram sva lakṣaṇam / yatnena kriyamāṇaḥ ayam anvayaḥ na virudhyate //
reference: The ‘specific individuality’ consists of the thing-by-itself, as ‘excluded from what is not itself’;—an assertion of concomitance carefully made in this form would not be incongruous
baseline: A thing that has not changed its form and has only its own characteristics and is done with care is not opposed.
morphology: A thing that has not changed its form has only its own characteristics and is not opposed to this application.

sanskrit: yasmin adhūmataḥ bhinnam vidyate hi svalakṣaṇam / tasmin anagnitaḥ api asti parāvṛttam svalakṣaṇam // yathā mahānase ca iha vidyate adhūma bhedi tat / tasmāt anagnitaḥ bhinnam vidyate atra svalakṣaṇam //
reference: That wherein subsists the specific individuality (smoke) differentiated from non-smoke,—in that same subsists also the specific individuality (fire) differentiated from non-fire; as in the kitchen; and herein (in the hill) there is the specific individuality differentiated from non-smoke;—hence the specific individuality differentiated from non-fire also must be there
baseline: One who is not aware of the difference between the two is different from the one who is unaware of it. One who has not been aware of it is also aware of his own identity. Just as one who has been surrounded by a great body is aware of its own identity one who does not know about it is different here from the other.
morphology: One who is not aware of the difference between the two is different from the one who is unaware of it. One who has not been aware of it is also aware of his own identity. One whose identity is different is different than that which is not known to be great.

sanskrit: asataḥ nara śṛṅga ādeḥ yat ca bhinnam sva lakṣaṇam / buddhi dīpa ādi vat sarvam vyāvṛttam tat sthirāt api // asat rūpam tathā ca idam na śabda ādi sva lakṣaṇam / ittham nirdiṣṭa bhedena bhavati eva anvayaḥ amunā //
reference: The specific individuality that is differentiated from ‘man’s horns’ and other non-existent things is also differentiated from permanent things,—just as the cognition, the lamp-flame, etc. are;—the specific individuality of sound, etc. is not a non-existent thing.—In this way there can be the assertion of concomitance through differences as indicated
baseline: The image of a man is different from that of a lion and the image of an elephant is different. The image is different than that of an animal. The shape is different and the sound is not different from the original. It is different if it is fixed. It does not differ from the sound. It becomes different with the difference specified.
morphology: The image of a man is different from that of a lion and the image of an elephant is different. The image is different than that of the mind. The form is different and the sound is not different from the original. It is different only if it is fixed. It does not differ from the words. It becomes different.

sanskrit: avivikṣata bhedam ca tat eva parikīrttitam / sāmānya lakṣaṇa tvena na aniṣṭeḥ aparam punar //
reference: The specific individuality itself, when its distinction is not meant to be emphasised, has been described as constituting the ‘universal’ (or commonalty);—nothing else; as nothing else is acceptable
baseline: The difference that has not been established is the same as that which has been established. The common feature should not be repeated by you.
morphology: The difference that has not been established is the same as that which has been established. The common feature is not undesirable.

sanskrit: śabala apatyataḥ bhede bāhuleya aśvayoḥ same / turaṅga parihāreṇa go tvam kim tatra varttate //
reference: The difference from the variegated cow being equally present in the black cow and the horse, why is it that the universal ‘cow’, as differentiated from the horse, subsists in that?
baseline: Having divided the bull into two cubs the cow should be taken to the other side of the horse. Having taken the bull from the tower should be placed there.
morphology: The cow should be kept in the same place as the horses in the different parts of the city. By having the horns covered with a thread the cow should go to the other side.

sanskrit: tasya vyaktau samartha ātmā saḥ eva iti yadi iṣyate / tulya pratyavamarśe api sa śaktaḥ na turaṃgamaḥ //
reference: If it be held that ‘that alone has the capacity to manifest it’—then, even though the subsequent determinate judgment is the same, that alone has the capacity to produce it, and not the horse
baseline: If he is said to be capable of the manifestation of that being he would be the soul. Even if he is able to do so in the same manner he should not be strong.
morphology: If he is said to be capable of manifesting himself he would be the soul. He would not be able to do so even if he is equally powerful.

sanskrit: tādṛś pratyavamarśaḥ ca vidyate yatra vastuni / tatra abhāve api go jāteḥ ago apohaḥ pravarttate //
reference: Thus then, in whatever thing the said determinate judgment is present,—to that the ‘exclusion of the non-cow’ becomes applicable,—even in the absence of the universal ‘cow’
baseline: In such a situation where there is a lack of material things even in the absence of that place the illusion of cow is introduced.
morphology: In such a situation where there is a lack of material things even if there is no cow.

sanskrit: a go bhinnam ca yat vastu tat akṣaiḥ vyavasīyate / pratibimbam tat adhyastam sva saṃvittyā avagamyate // idam dṛṣṭvā ca lekena śabdaḥ tatra prayujyate / saṃbandha anubhavaḥ api asya vyaktam tena upapadyate //
reference: That thing which is ‘different from the non-cow’ is certainly apprehended by the sense-organs; the reflection also which is superimposed upon it is apprehended by its own cognition. it is on noticing this that people use the word; the recognition of its relation also becomes clearly explained on the same basis
baseline: The object that is different from the cow and that is separated by the axes the image is absorbed by the subject by its own manifestation. Seeing it the word lekena is used there. The experience of the relationship is also expressed by it.
morphology: The object which is different from the cow and is separated by the axes the image is absorbed by the master by his own presence. Seeing this the word lake is used there. The experience of the relationship is expressed by him.

sanskrit: tādṛś pratyavamarśaḥ ca yatra na eva asti vastuni / a go śabda abhidheya tvam vispaṣṭam tatra gamyate //
reference: When, in regard to anything, there is no such determinate judgment, the fact of its being denoted by the word ‘non-cow’ becomes clearly perceived
baseline: In such a case the object should be placed in a place where there is no other object. Having caught the sound of a cow you go to the place where it is not visible.
morphology: In the same way if there is no object in each of the two places you will reach the place where the sound of a cow is found.

sanskrit: gāvaḥ agāvaḥ ca saṃsiddhāḥ bhinna pratyavamarśataḥ / śabdaḥ tu kevalaḥ asiddhaḥ yatheṣṭam saṃprayujyate // na hi anya grahaṇam vastu bhinnam vittau apekṣate / anyonya āśraya doṣaḥ ayam tasmāt asmin nirāspadaḥ //
reference: The cow and the non-cow are both well-established,—as there are distinct determinate judgments in regard to both; it is only the word that is not well-established; and hence it is applied according to the speaker’s whim.—As a matter of fact, a distinct thing does not need for its apprehension, the apprehension of another thing; hence there is no room here for the charge of ‘mutual interdependence’
baseline: A cow and a cow are said to be different from each other. The word is said to have been different from the other. One who is not good enough for the other should not take another thing and want a different money. One should not seek refuge from another. This is the fault.
morphology: A cow and a cow are said to be different from each other and the word is said to have been different. One who is not good enough for others one who does not want to take things and others and one who wants to buy things and money from others is wrong.

sanskrit: avedya bāhya tattvā api prakṛṣṭa upaplavāt iyam / sva ullekham bāhya rūpeṇa śabda dhīḥ adhyavasyati // etāvat kriyate śabdaiḥ na artham śabdāḥ spṛśanti api / na apohena viśiṣṭaḥ ca kaścid arthaḥ abhidhīyate //
reference: As a matter of fact, verbal cognition, not taking cognizance of any external object, apprehends its own mark as something external, on account of strong illusion.—This is all that is done by words; and words do not even, touch the object; nor is any object denoted as qualified by Apoha.
baseline: One who does this by making a statement on the external side and then by making an announcement on the other side of the flood would not be able to understand the meaning of the words. One who makes such a statement would not touch the words and would not identify any meaning.
morphology: One who does this by making a mention of oneself in the form of words and not touching the meaning of the words and does not identify any meaning by making an illusion.

sanskrit: artha antara nivṛttyā āhuḥ viśiṣṭān iti yat punar / proktam lakṣaṇakāreṇa tatra arthaḥ ayam vivakṣitaḥ //
reference: As for the statement made by the author of the lakṣaṇa—that ‘words express things qualified by the exclusion of other things’, what it means is as follows
baseline: The meaning of the words āhu ahu and ahu is distinct from the other. If the word is again mentioned as having a characteristic it means that it is distinct.
morphology: The meaning of the words āhu ahu and ahu is distinct from the other. If the word is again mentioned as having a characteristic it means that it is distinct.

sanskrit: anya anya tvena ye bhāvāḥ hetunā karaṇena vā / viśiṣṭāḥ bhinna jātīyaiḥ asaṅkīrṇāḥ viniścitāḥ // vṛkṣa ādīn āhatān dhvānaḥ tad bhāva adhyasāyinaḥ / jñānasya utpādanāt etat jāti ādeḥ pratiṣedhanam //
reference: Those things that are qualified by the exclusion of other things,—either as their cause or their instruments—are definitely cognised as not mixed up with things of other kinds. The word expresses these things. and, because it brings about the cognition apprehending those things, there is denial of the ‘universal’ and such other commonalities
baseline: One who has not been able to understand the feelings of others those who have been harmed by you or by doing it for a reason those belonging to a different caste those not having the strength of the voice those afflicted by trees etc. and those who do not know the meaning of the sound one who has been harming the sound of the same one should oppose this nation and its products.
morphology: One who has not been able to understand the feelings of others those who have been harmed by you or by doing it for the sake of others. Those who have not been judged by the different castes the people who have suffered from the trees the sound of the trees etc. should be punished by the government.

sanskrit: buddhau ye vā vivarttante tān āha ābhyantarān ayam / nivṛttyā ca viśiṣṭa tvam uktam eṣām anantaram //
reference: Those things however which appear in the cognition—these internal (subjective) things the word denotes directly; and the fact of these things being qualified by ‘exclusion’ has just been explained
baseline: Those who describe themselves as Buddhas should say aha to those who are internal. Then after this you said that they should be discharged.
morphology: Those who describe themselves as the Buddhas should say aha these are the internal things. Then after this you said that they should be separated.

sanskrit: artha antara parāvṛttyā gamyate tasya vastunaḥ / kaścid bhāgaḥ iti proktam tat eva pratibimbakam //
reference: When it is said that ‘a certain portion of the thing is apprehended by the exclusion of other things’,—it is the said reflection that is meant
baseline: The meaning of an object is derived from the difference between its parts. It is said to be a part of the same.
morphology: The meaning of the object is known to be a part of that object. It is said to be the reflection.

sanskrit: artha antara parāvṛtta vastu darśana saṃśrayāt / āgatyāḥ tatra ca āropāt tasya bhāgaḥ apadiśyate //
reference: It is spoken of as a portion of the object, because it proceeds on the basis of the perception of the object as ‘excluded from other things’, and because it is superimposed upon the object
baseline: The part of the object that has been placed in the distance should be shown to the eye. If it is placed there after it has come and gone then it would be destroyed.
morphology: If the object is placed in the distance between the objects and is placed on the ground after having been placed there the part of the object would be shown as evil.

sanskrit: hetvarthaḥ karaṇa arthaḥ ca pūrvavat tena vā ātmanā / yadi vastu vijātīyāt na syāt bhinnam na tat tathā //
reference: As before, the instrumental ending may signify either the cause or the instrument. or it may signify that it is ‘in that form’.—If the thing were not differentiated from unlike things, then it could not be so
baseline: The meaning of the word haṭvartha or kārṇa is as before. If the object is not of a different species it is not different.
morphology: The meaning of the word haṭvartha kārna as before is that of the self. If the object is not of a different kind it is not different.

sanskrit: ago nivṛttiḥ anya tvam tasya ca ātma gatā eva sā / bheda uktau api abhāvaḥ tu kevalaḥ na nivarttate // tad viśeṣaṇa bhāve api vastu dhīḥ na vihīyate / kalpanā nirmitam ca idam abhede api viśeṣaṇam // sā upakṛṣya tatas dharmaḥ sthāpitaḥ bhedavān iva / yena daṇḍa ādi vat tasya jāyate hi viśeṣaṇam //
reference: What is meant by (the cow) being ‘different’ is only the ‘exclusion of the non-cow’; and this exclusion is of the nature of that same difference.—Even when the difference has been asserted, the thing itself does not entirely disappear. Thus even when it has the nature of the qualification, the cognition of the thing does not cease. even when there is non-difference, the qualification is there as a creation of fancy. That character, having been withdrawn therefrom, has been placed there as if different; whereby it becomes its qualification, like the stick and other things
baseline: The difference between the self and the self is said to be different and the absence of the self does not go away. It is said that the object is not good and the object does not get destroyed. The idea is created even if it is not possible. It has been created by the subcultures and the religion has been established and it has been divided. The punishment for the same is as if it had been done by the preceptor.
morphology: The distinction between the self and the self is said to have been made and the lack of it is not removed. It is said that the object is not destroyed by the mind and the idea is created even if it is established and the adhāṇa is not established. It becomes the same as that which was established by the preceptor. It gets punished as if it had not been established.

sanskrit: pratibhāsaḥ ca śabda arthaḥ iti āhuḥ tattva cintakāḥ / dṛśya kalpa avibhāga jñaḥ lokaḥ bāhyam tu manyate // tasya atas adhyavasāyena vyaktīnām eva vācya tā / tattvataḥ ca na śabdānām vācyam asti iti sādhitam //
reference: Discriminators of truth declare that what is denoted by the word is mere ‘reflection’. People, not knowing the distinction between what is ‘perceived’ and what is ‘fancied’ regard it to be something ‘external—as that is what is apprehended (by words), individuals are denoted by words.—In reality however there is nothing that is denoted by words,—as has been proved already
baseline: Having said that the principle of the word meaning is the same as that of a person. Those who think that the words are not visible those who perceive that the world is external and those who do not perceive the world as such are not the same in principle as those who speak the word.
morphology: Having said that the principle of the person is the meaning of the words. Having known the visible and the invisible parts of the world one would think that the people are external. Having said this to the individual it is not possible to say that the words are in the sense of the word.

sanskrit: ittham ca śabda vācya tvāt vyaktīnām asti apohya tā / sāmānyasya tu na apohaḥ na ca apohe api vastu tā //
reference: Thus, individuals being denoted by words, they are also capable of being ‘excluded’. As regards the universal, there can be no ‘exclusion even if there were ‘exclusion’ of it, it could not have the character of the ‘entity’
baseline: Having said so one should not mislead the common man by saying such a word. One should not deceive the common person by saying that which is the property of the individual.
morphology: Having said so one should not mislead the common man by saying such a word.

sanskrit: na abhābaḥ apohyate hi evam na abhāvaḥ abhāvaḥ iti ayam / bhāvaḥ tu na tadā ātmā iti tasya iṣṭā evam apohyatā //
reference: Negation is not ‘excluded’ (denied) in the words ‘negation is not negation’; it is however clearly ‘excluded’ (denied) in such expressions as ‘the entity is not of the nature of negation’
baseline: The feeling of lack is not such that it is not misused. Then the desire of the soul is not so misused as if it were not.
morphology: The feeling of lack is not such that it is not misused. Then the desire of the soul is not so misused as if it were not.

sanskrit: yaḥ nāma na yadā ātmā hi sa tasya apohaḥ ucyate / na bhāvaḥ abhāva rūpaḥ ca tad apohe na vastu tā //
reference: When one thing is not of the nature of another, it is called its ‘Apoha’ (exclusion, negation), and the entity is not of the nature of negation. but even though there is ‘Apoha’ of negation, it does not acquire the character of the positive entity
baseline: One who does not know the name of the soul when he is not aware of it is said to be illusory. One who is lacking in feeling and form is not called illusionful.
morphology: One who does not know the name of the soul is said to be illusory. One who has not experienced the absence of feeling and form is not called illusionary.

sanskrit: prakṛti īśa ādi janya tvam vastūnām na iti codite / prakṛti īśa ādi janya tvam na hi vastu prasiddhyati //
reference: Even though it is urged that ‘things are not produced by primordial matter or god and so forth’,—the character of being produced by primordial matter, god and so forth does not become a positive entity
baseline: One would say that the nature is Śeṣa the beginning of things and not you. One would not say that you are Prakṛti Esha the starting of things and one would not know that.
morphology: One would say that the nature is Śeṣa the beginning of things and not you. The nature is Esha the starting of things not you are known.

sanskrit: na atas asataḥ api bhāva tvam iti kleśaḥ na kañcana / tasya siddhau ca sattā asti sā ca asattā prasidhyati //
reference: Thus then there is no such calamity as that of the non-existent becoming a positive entity. In fact, even on the establishment of the negation, the existence remains there (in the entity),—and the non-existence (of the negation) becomes established thereby
baseline: One who does not have the feeling of suffering and suffering even if he does not want to do so would not be known to be perfect.
morphology: One who does not have the feeling of suffering and having the perfection of his existence would not be known to be evil even if he does not do so.

sanskrit: agotaḥ vinivṛttiḥ ca gauḥ vilakṣaṇaḥ iṣyate / bhāvaḥ eva tatas na ayam gauḥ agoḥ me prasajyate //
reference: The cow, which is ‘the negation of the non-cow’ is held to be a positive entity, and of a character different from that of the non-cow; but by this the non-cow does not become the cow, for me
baseline: The cow is said to be unique if it is left unattended. Then the cow is not given to me.
morphology: The cow is said to be unique if it is not seen and the cow is not given to me.

sanskrit: avastu viṣaye api asti cetaḥ mātra vinirmitā / vicitra kalpanā bheda raciteṣu iva vāsanā // tatas ca vāsanā bhedāt bhedaḥ sat rūpa tā api ca / prakalpyate hi apohānām kalpanā raciteṣu iva //
reference: Even in regard to non-entities, there can be impressions, created only by the mind (cognitions),—just as in the case of things of various kinds created by imagination. This diversity among Apohas, as also their positive character, would be assumed on the basis of the diversity among impressions; just as in the case of creations of imagination
baseline: It is also said to be about the matter of matter. It is only made out of strange imaginations. The difference between those desires and those desires is different. The differences between the desires and the differences are the same as those created by the illusion.
morphology: It is also said to be related to the subject matter. It is said to have created only strange imaginations. The difference between those desires and those desires is known to be the difference between the two forms. It also happens to be known as illusory imaginings.

sanskrit: yādṛśaḥ artha antara apohaḥ vācyaḥ ayam pratipāditaḥ / śabda antara vyapohaḥ api tādṛś eva avagamyatām //
reference: Just as we have explained the fact of ‘the exclusion of other things’ being denoted by words,—exactly in the same manner should be understood the ‘exclusion of other words’ also
baseline: The words interphilosophy are thus said to mean the same. The word interphylosophy is likewise said to be similar.
morphology: In the same way the meaning of the word is different. The words are different.

sanskrit: vastu iti adhyavasāya tvāt na avastu tvam apohayoḥ / prasiddham sāṃvṛte mārge tāttvike tu iṣṭa sādhanam //
reference: Inasmuch as the Apohas are apprehended as ‘things’ they cannot be regarded as non-entities; this is well known and admitted as pertaining to the illusory aspect of things. as regards the real aspect, what the opponent seeks to prove is accepted by us already
baseline: You do not want to suffer from the illusion of the object. You want to get the best of the means on the way.
morphology: You do not want to suffer from the illusion of the object. You want to get the best means of living on the path which is famous.

sanskrit: na vācyam vācakam vā api parama arthena kiñcana / kṣaṇabhaṅgiṣu bhāveṣu vyāpaka tva viyogataḥ //
reference: In reality, there can be nothing that can be either denoter or denoted,—as all things being in perpetual flux, no concomitance is possible
baseline: One who does not speak the same way or the same with the ultimate meaning would also spread in the present forms and the senses.
morphology: Even if you are not a speaker you will be separated from others by the ultimate meaning and spread over the past few moments.

sanskrit: tad gamya gamaka tvam ced sāṃvṛtam pratiṣidhyate / tāttvikīm samupāśritya vinivṛttyoḥ avastu tām // tathā api vyabhicāri tvam durvāram anuṣajyate / vikalpa racitaiḥ arthaiḥ śabdaiḥ tad vācakaiḥ api //
reference: If it is the illusory relation of denoter and denoted that is denied; on the basis of the real fact of the two exclusions being non-entities,—even so, ‘falsity’ becomes unavoidable; in view of such words and things denoted by them as are the creation of imagination
baseline: The same is said to be true for the same thing. Then the harlot should be made to know the meaning of the words with which he has made his choice. That is also true for him. He should be given to the disciple with the words   and that is to be accepted by the reader.
morphology: The same is said to be true for the same thing as that of a barbarian. The same thing is true for those who do not know the meaning of the word gāmaka. That is true also for the transgressor. That word should be said to have the meanings of the choice made by the speaker.

sanskrit: na hi teṣu asti sāmānyam vācyam tasya ca vācakam / na vācaka tvam śabdasya kṣaṇabhaṅgi svalakṣaṇam //
reference: As a matter of fact, there is ho ‘universal’ (commonalty) in the case of the things in question, which could be denoted; nor is there any universal word denotative of that universal; nor does the denotative character belong to the word, as specific individualities are all in perpetual flux
baseline: Neither is it common among them nor is it a word. Nor is it the speaker of the word and its momentary appearance a mark of its own.
morphology: Neither the speaker nor the speaker of the word is common among them. You are not the manifestation of your own character.

sanskrit: tasmāt tat dvayam eṣṭavyam pratibimba ādi sāṃvṛtam / teṣu tad vyabhicāri tvam durnivāram avasthitam //
reference: Hence both of these should be held to consist in the illusory ‘reflection’ etc.—Thus in view of these, the ‘falsity’ remains unshaken
baseline: Then the image should be divided into two parts. In those two parts the adulterer is said to be evil.
morphology: Then the two images should be drawn. The first of them should be covered. The adulterer is the one who is evil.

sanskrit: vidhi rūpaḥ ca śabda arthaḥ yena na abhyupagamyate / tad ābham jāyate cetaḥ śabdāt artha avasāyi hi // svārtha abhidhāne śabdānām arthāt anya nivartanam / tad yogaḥ vyatirekaḥ api mama tad pūrvakaḥ hi asau //
reference: For the man by whom the denotation of words is not admitted to be anything positive, the mind (cognition) reflecting the thing is what is brought about by the word, and this cognition ultimately brings about the idea of the thing. When words express their meanings, there is, by implication, the exclusion of other things; and through the presence of this there is negation also, as preceded by the apprehension of the positive thing.—
baseline: The words vidhi rūpā meaning that which does not get absorbed that which becomes the manifestation of the body the meaning of the words falling out of the selfishness the word giving another direction that is the opposite of yoga and that which is the former of me.
morphology: The meaning of the words should not be derived from the manner form and form. That which is not attained is called abhāma. That meaning should be derived out of the word abhaya that which is given to the words in the sense of selfishness and that which denotes another retreat. That is the opposite of yogā and that is my predecessor.

sanskrit: asambhavaḥ vidheḥ uktaḥ sāmānya ādeḥ asambhavāt / śabdānām ca vikalpānām vastunaḥ viṣaya tvataḥ //
reference: The ‘impossibility of the positive’ has been averred oh the ground that such things as the ‘universal’ and the like cannot form the subject of words and determinate conceptions
baseline: The word impossibility is said to be impossible. The words imposible and impossible are given to you in the matter of the objects.
morphology: The word impossibility is said to be impossible. It is impossible to say a simple statement. It should be said to you that the matter of the choice and the object is impossible.

sanskrit: nīlotpala ādi śabdebhyaḥ ekaḥ eva avasīyate / anīla anutpala ādibhyaḥ vyāvṛttam pratibimbakam //
reference: From the term ‘blue-lotus’, only one thing is cognised,—and that is the reflection excluded (differentiated) from the ‘non-blue’ and the ‘non-lotus’
baseline: The same is said to be true for the words nilotupala and anutputpala. For the words anila and anuttupala etc. one should be a reflector.

morphology: If one says that he digests it then the indifference does not remain. If one is hungry one gives it to him then another retraction would occur. If another one does not digress the other action would fall into the gap. Pārudasa would decide what would happen to him.

sanskrit: pacati iti aniṣiddham tu svarūpeṇa eva tiṣṭhati / iti etat ca bhavat vākyam paraspara parāhatam // anya rūpa niṣedhaḥ ayam svarūpeṇa eva tiṣṭhati / iti anyathā nirartham syāt prayuktam avadhāraṇam //
reference: Your assertion that “the cooking remains un-negatived in its own form” involves self-contradiction; because the words ‘in its own form’ can only mean that ‘there is negativing of the form of other acts’; otherwise the emphasising would be meaningless
baseline: If it is forbidden to be digested it should be said that it remains in the form. It is said to be mutually exclusive. If it does not exist in the other form it would be meaningless to say otherwise.
morphology: If it is not accepted that it is good for you it should be said that it exists only in the form. If it does not exist in the other form it would be meaningless.

sanskrit: niṣpanna tvam apohasya nirupākhyasya kīdṛśam / gagana indīvara ādīnām niṣpattiḥ nahi kācana // vastu iti adhyavasāyāt ced sa upākhyā tvena bhāti asau / tatas kim tulya dharma tvam vastubhiḥ ca asya gamyate //
reference: Apoha being featureless, what sort of ‘accomplishment’ could there be of it? Certainly there is no ‘accomplishment’ of the ‘sky-lotus’ etc.—If it be urged that “inasmuch as it is apprehended as a thing, it appears as with features”,—then (we ask) what if it is so?—[It may be said that] “From this it would follow that it has the same properties as entities.”
baseline: What is the nature of the illusion and the undeniable illusion that you have accomplished that which is not the matter of the sky that of the earth that is not a matter for which you have settled. That which is said to be the matter should be considered as such. What is your righteousness and that which are equal to that of those things.
morphology: What is the nature of the falsehood and the unspeakable falsehood that you have accomplished that you are not able to dispose of the things that belong to you that person should not be judged by you. That person should be judged on the basis of the fact that he is equal to you. What is his righteousness on the ground of the facts?

sanskrit: sādhya tva pratyayaḥ tasmāt tathābhūta ādi rūpaṇam / vastubhiḥ tulya rūpa tvāt tad nimittam prasajyate //
reference: Thus then, the notion of ‘being accomplished’, as also the conception of the ‘past’ etc.,—being of the same form as positive entities—comes to be based upon that same
baseline: You get the belief that the original form is derived from it. The same form is obtained from you for that purpose.
morphology: You get the belief that the original shape of the object is similar to that obtained by you.

sanskrit: vidhi ādau artharāśau ca nāstitā ādi niṣidhyate / sāmarthyāt na tu śabdena yat eva na vivakṣitam //
reference: In the case of all such denotations as the injunction and the like,—what is ‘excluded’ (negatived) is ‘non-existence’, etc.,—exactly that which is not meant to be spoken of; but this is done by implication,—not directly by the word
baseline: It is forbidden to say anything with the words or with the power.
morphology: It is forbidden to say anything with the words or with the power of the preceptor.

sanskrit: nañaḥ ca api nañā yuktau apohaḥ tādṛśaḥ bhavet / tad catuṣṭaya sadbhāve yādṛśaḥ saṃpratīyate // nañā yoge nañaḥ hi arthaḥ gamyate kasyacid vidhiḥ / tṛtīyena nañā tasya virahaḥ pratipādyate // niṣedhāya aparaḥ tasya turīyaḥ yaḥ prayujyate / tasmin vivakṣite tena jñāpyate anya nivartanam
reference: Of similar kind would be the Apoha, when a negative is joined with another negative; just as it is apprehended when there are four negatives. in some cases, when a negative is associated with another negative, what is apprehended from it is something positive; the third negative expresses the negation (absence) of that positive thing; and when for the negativing of that again a fourth negative is used, if that is meant to be spoken of, what is denoted by it is the ‘exclusion of another’
baseline: The falsehood should be such as to be false false and false. It is said to be true in good faith. One who does not do so in the form of yoga would get the meaning of the falsehood. The third method would reveal the difference between the false and the false. The other method would be known to prevent it. The one who uses the false statement would be declared to be wrong. The next method would prove to be evil.
morphology: One who does not know the meaning of the word nāgā one who is not able to understand it another person who is known to be wrong another one who has not done it should be informed in the manner described in the description. One who has done the same would get the meaning by doing the same in the form of goodness. One would be told by the third method. The other would be known by the other method.

sanskrit: na asau na pacanīti ukte gamyate pacati iti hi / audāsīnya ādi yogaḥ ca tṛtīyena hi gamyate // turye tu tad viviktaḥ asau pacati iti avasīyate / tena atra vidhi vākyena samam anya nivartanam //
reference: When it is said ‘nāsau na pacati’ (‘it is not that he does not cook’) what is understood is that ‘he cooks’; if a third negative is added, what is understood is either that ‘he is doing nothing’ or that ‘he is doing something other than cooking’;—and when a fourth negative is added, what is understood is something differentiated from this last, that is, ‘he is cooking’. So that here the ‘exclusion of another’ is similar to that in the case of the affirmative sentence
baseline: It is said that one who does not eat or drink should not eat and the same should be taken away with the preceptor and the third one should eat it after having done ablutions. It is believed that one should drink the same food after having gone out of the way. One should return the same amount of food by following the rules.
morphology: One who does not eat or drink should say that he has not eaten or has eaten. The original yoga should be prepared by the third day after having done ablution. He should be told that he would eat the same thing after having left it alone. He would be prepared to eat it with the same method and other methods.

sanskrit: samuccaya ādiḥ yaḥ ca arthaḥ kaścid ca ādeḥ abhīpsitaḥ / tad anyasya vikalpa ādeḥ bhavet tena vyapohanam //
reference: Of particles like ‘ca’ the meaning intended is something like ‘combination’; and thus there would be ‘exclusion’ by that, of things other than that, in the shape of ‘option’ and the like
baseline: The meaning of the word Śamucha is that which is desired by any one. It should be given to another as an alternative.
morphology: The meaning of the preceptor should be that which is desired by any one. That which would be preferred by another should be substituted by another.

sanskrit: vākya arthe anya nivṛttiḥ ca su jñātā eva tathā hi asau / padārthāḥ eva sahitāḥ kecid vākya arthaḥ ucyate // teṣām ca ye vijātīyāḥ te apohyāḥ su parisphuṭāḥ / vākya arthasya api te ca eva tebhyaḥ anyaḥ na eva saḥ asti hi //
reference: The exclusion of others’ is clearly understood in the case of the meaning of a sentence. it is only the denotations of certain words construed together that is spoken of as ‘the meaning of the sentence’; what would be ‘excluded’ by these words would clearly be the things different from those denoted by these words; so that the same would be ‘excluded’ by the meaning of the sentence also. Because the meaning of the sentence is nothing apart from the meanings of the words (composing it)
baseline: One who knows the meaning of the words the other means of retirement and the objects the objects and the meanings of some of the sentences are said to be false those who are strangers to them those people who are ignorant of the meaning and those who do not know the meaning those are not others.
morphology: One who knows the meaning of the words and the other things and who knows what they are those who bear the same things and say some words and say that they are different. Those who do not understand the meaning and those who are not aware of the meaning those are not different from those.

sanskrit: yat tatra jaḍa cetobhiḥ āśaṅkā āspadam iṣyate / tat eva kṣipyate tena viphala uccāraṇā anyathā // kiñcid hi aśaṅkamānaḥ asau kimartham paripṛcchati / a tad saṃskārakam śabdam bruvan vā svastha dhīḥ katham //
reference: What is regarded by dull-witted persons as open to doubt is what is ‘excluded’ by the word in question; otherwise, the utterance of the word would be useless.—If he does not regard anything as open to doubt, then why does he ask (another person) about it?—If one utters a word that does not bring about embellishment (enlightenment),—how can he be regarded as a sane-minded person?
baseline: If there is a fear in the mind of the head it will be thrown away. If it is not uttered properly then what is the meaning of that sound of the mouth which is the reformer the sound of blood the health of the body.
morphology: If there is a fear in the mind it will be given to you. If it is not fulfilled then why should it be repeated? If it does not get fulfilled then it should be said that it is good for you. Then what should be done by the person who is doing the ritualistic practice. When it is said to be healthy how can it be done?

sanskrit: cakṣuḥ jñāna ādi vijñeyam rūpa ādi iti yat ucyate / tena āropitam etat hi kenacid pratiṣidhyate //
reference: When it is asserted that ‘colour is cognisable by visual perception’—this certainly serves to ‘exclude’ (deny) something supposed by some person
baseline: It is said that the eye is the knowledge of the beginning the knowledge is the form the beginning. This is said to be the imputation.
morphology: It is said that the eye is the knowledge of the beginning and the form of knowledge is the beginning. This is said to be the beginning of the end.

sanskrit: na cakṣuḥ āśritena eva rūpam nīla ādi vedyate / kintu śrotra āśritena api nityena ekena cetasā //
reference: The supposition is]—“It is not by the cognition through the eye alone that the blue and other colours are cognisable,—but also by the one eternal cognition, through the ear also.”
baseline: One becomes blue in form with the eyes and the eyes with the eye. But one becomes conscious with the ear and the ear with the same eye.
morphology: One becomes blue in form by the presence of the eye and the eye. But one becomes conscious by the appearance of the ear and the ear.

sanskrit: prameya jñeya śabda ādeḥ pratiyatti nimitta tām / ittham vākya sthitasya eva dṛṣṭvā kāla antareṣu api // kevalasya upalambhe yā pratītiḥ upajāyate / plavamāna artha bhedeṣu sā tad vākya anusārataḥ // ghaṭa ādibhyaḥ api śabdebhyaḥ sā asti eva ca tathāvidhā / tasmāt haṭa ādi dhvanayaḥ samāḥ //
reference: That words like ‘knowable’, ‘cognisable’ serve as the means of producing cognitions (ideas) having been perceived only when they appear in a sentence,—if, at some other time? They are found to be used alone by themselves, the idea that is produced by them, in regard to things that are nebulous, is in accordance with what has been found in the case of their use in a sentence.—In fact, in the case of words like ‘jar’ also, it is the same; so that the words ‘knowable’ and the like are just like the words ‘jar’ and the rest

Seeing that the word is there for the time being the word should be placed in the inner parts also the words that are flowing in the upper part of the body and the meaning of the word in the different parts should be expressed in the words according to the syllable. The words that sound like the vowel sound sound etc. should be removed from it.
morphology: Having seen that the word is there for the purpose of imbibing the principle the word for the sake of imitating it the words for the same duration of time the belief that is produced in the inner parts of the body is only found in the above. The meaning that is flowing in the different parts of a sentence is according to that word. The sound that is repeated in the beginning and the beginning of the speech is equal to that.

sanskrit: apohya kalpanāyām ca varam vastu eva kalpitam / iti etat vyāhatam proktam niyamena anya varjanāt // vastu eva kalpyate tatra yat eva hi vivakṣitam / kṣepaḥ vivakṣitasya atas na tu sarvam vivakṣitam //
reference: The statement that, “rather than assume the ‘excluded’ thing it is far better to assume the thing itself”, is self-contradictory; as in every case there is ‘exclusion of some other thing’, that thing alone is assumed which is meant to be spoken of; hence there is implication of that which is meant to be spoken of; but all things are not meant to be spoken of
baseline: It is said to be a thing that has been conceived as a boon by misguiding and conceiving. It is forbidden by law to make any other thing possible. It should be said that whatever is conceived as such it should be done with the same thing. The object should not be conceived with the help of that particular thing and everything should be made clear.
morphology: It is said to be a thing that has been conceived as a boon for the purpose of conceiving. It is forbidden to say that another thing has been created as a rule. It should be said that whatever is conceived as such it should be done with that particular thing. The idea should not be made with that or all that is specified.

sanskrit: jñāna ākāra niṣedhaḥ tu sva vedya tvāt na śakyate / vidyate hi nirālambam āropakam anekadhā // jñānasya ātma gataḥ kaścid niyataḥ pratigocaram / avaśya abhyupagantavyaḥ svabhāvaḥ ca saḥ eva ca // asmābhiḥ uktaḥ ākāraḥ pratibimbam tad ābha tā / ullekhaḥ pratibhāsaḥ ca saṃjñā bhedaḥ tu akāraṇam //
reference: As for the denial of the idealistic form of things,—such denial is impossible because the fact is self-evident; as actually there are several impositions without any basic reality.—It has to be admitted that there must be something in the idea (or cognition) itself which appertains specifically to each object envisaged by it; and that is precisely its ‘nature’;—and this same ‘nature’ of the idea has been spoken of by us as ‘form ‘reflected image’, ‘appearance’, ‘figuring’, ‘manifestation so that there is only a difference in the name, without any real difference
baseline: One who has passed on the spirit of knowledge and who has become visible by default must be able to understand the nature of the form and the image mentioned by us. The difference between the manifestations of the manifestation and the concept of manifestation is not possible with the exception of the words jñāṇa and śakrā.
morphology: One who has passed on the spirit of knowledge one who has gone back and manifested the nature of knowledge and that which is said by us to be the shape and the image of the form is not possible by you. One who does not know the form and shape of knowledge is not allowed to go from you. He who has left the self of knowledge has gone from many places. He should be able to understand the nature and manifest the same. He is said to be a manifestation of that shape. He has mentioned that. The difference between talent and knowledge is without any reason.

sanskrit: evam ityādi śabdānām na evam ityādi vidyate / apohyam iti vispaṣṭam prakāra antara lakṣaṇam //
reference: In the case of the word ‘evam’ (thus), there is ‘naivam’ (not thus) which is clearly ‘excluded’; in the sense of ‘in another manner’
baseline: There is no such thing as a word given in such a way. It is not so it is not known to be false. It has a distinct feature.
morphology: There is no such thing in the wording as such. It is not so. The difference is evident in the way it is said to be incomprehensible.

sanskrit: vyavahāra upanīte ca sarva śabde api vidyate / vyudāsyam tasya ca arthaḥ ayam anya apohaḥ abhidhitsitaḥ //

morphology: The meaning of the word vyudāsya is also found in all the words. It is another fallacy.

reference: 1186) There are such misconceptions as—‘only external things like, the jar are soulless’, ‘only some men can go’; and it is these that are ‘excluded’

sanskrit: sarva aṅga pratiṣedhaḥ ca na eva tasmin vivakṣitaḥ / sva artha apoha prasaṅgaḥ ayam tasmāt ajña tayā ucyate //

morphology: He would say that all the parts of the body should be removed without knowing the meaning of the matter.

sanskrit: na bhāvaḥ na api ca abhāvaḥ apṛthak eka tva lakṣaṇaḥ / na āśrita anāśritaḥ apohaḥ na eka anekaḥ ca vastutas //
reference: It is neither positive nor negative; it is neither diverse nor same; it is neither subsistent, nor non-subsistent; it is neither one nor many
baseline: There is neither feeling nor lack of feeling one of the qualities of the self one without being dependent on the self and one without trust. One of the illusions is not many.
morphology: There is neither feeling nor lack of feeling. One is the manifestation of the self. One does not depend on the self and there is no illusion. One has many qualities.

sanskrit: tathā asau na asti tattvena yathā asau vyavasīyate / tat na bhāvaḥ na ca abhāvaḥ vastu tvena avasāyataḥ //

sanskrit: bheda abheda ādayaḥ sarve vastu sat pariniṣṭhitāḥ / niḥsvabhāvaḥ ca śabda arthaḥ tasmāt ete nirāspadāḥ //
reference: Diversity’ (difference) and ‘sameness’ (non-difference), etc. are resident in entities; while the ‘denotation of words’ is entirely featureless; hence the said characters have no place here
baseline: All things that have been acquired without any distinction have been established with sincerity. The word nirbhava means unselfishness. These things are thus undefiled.
morphology: All things that have been acquired without any distinction have been established with sincerity. The word nirbhāma means unselfishness.

sanskrit: anya artha vinivṛttim ca sākṣāt śabdaḥ karoti naḥ / kṛte svārtha abhidhāne tu sāmarthyāt sā avagamyate // na tadā ātmā parātmā iti vistareṇa upapāditam / parapakṣa anabhijñena tasmāt etat iha ucyate // kena hi ago tvam āsaktam goḥ yena etat apohyate / iti na eva abhimukhyena śabdena etat apohyate //
reference: For us the word does the ‘negativing of other things’ directly; and after the negativing has been done by the word, it becomes apprehended through its own force,—in the form ‘its nature is not the nature of anything else’,—as has been explained in detail (under text 1013); hence what is urged on the present occasion—‘who has attributed the character of the non-cow to the cow, that it has to be negatived?—Is through ignorance of the view of the other party. As a matter of fact, this is not what is held to be ‘negatived’ by the word directly
baseline: One who does not make a sound directly and does not give any meaning to another would not be able to do so. One would not get it by the power of selfishness would get it. Then the soul would be made to reach the other side without knowing it. He would say that it is a cow which is attached to him. It would not become a sound by the direction of the voice.
morphology: One who does not make a sound directly with another meaning and dispensations would not be able to do so with selfishness. One who is not able to understand the spirit would not get it. One would not know the other side and would say that he is attached to the cow. He would not understand it with the sound of the face.

sanskrit: katamena ca śabdena vācya tvam paripṛcchyate / apohasya kim etena yadi vā kim ghaṭa ādinā // śabda arthaḥ kim apohaḥ vā vidhiḥ vā iti nirūpaṇe / apohaḥ iti bhāti etat yat tat evam pratīyate // pratibimbam hi śabda arthaḥ iti sākṣāt iyam matiḥ / jāti ādi vidhi hāniḥ tu sāmarthyāt avagamyate // ghaṭa vṛkṣa ādi śabdāḥ ca tat eva pratibimbakam / bruvanti jananāt sākṣāt arthāt anyat kṣipanti tu // tasmāt na vidhi doṣaḥ asti na aniṣṭā ca
reference: The ‘denotability’ that you ask about—is ‘denotability’ by which word? Is it ‘denotability’ by the word ‘Apoha’? Or by the wobd ‘jar’ and the best?—As regards the question—whether the Apoha that is denoted is itself of the nature of Apoha (negation, exclusion) or it is something positive,—when we come to think of it, what is cognised is the apoha that figures in the cognition.—Our view is that what is denoted by the word directly is the reflected image,—and as regards ‘the negation of other things’, like the universal etc.,—That is comprehended only indirectly, through implication.—What all such words as ‘jar’, ‘tree’ and the like denote is the said reflected image, as it is the cognition of this that they produce directly; and anything else, they imply only indirectly.—Thus then, there is no incongruity regarding the positive character; nor is there anything undesirable for us.—As regards the alternative of Apoha not being ‘denotable’,—that we do not accept; and hence that is not our view
baseline: Having recited the words katmane you will be covered by the illusion whether by it or by it the word ghatā by the beginning the meaning of the word is false the definition of what is false or the method of the method is wrong it would appear as if it were false. The word reflexive meaning the beginning of the race meaning of this word is directly related to it. The same illusion would be transmitted by the power of the words ghat tree and other words. By that there would be no error in the method and the unperceived
morphology: Having recited the words katmane you are covered by the illusion whether by this or by that what is the meaning of the word ghata by that which is the beginning of the beginning by the definition of what is meant by the word katāna by this it appears as if it is false it looks like that. It looks as if the word jātiyaṇa the beginning and the end of the patha is directly derived from the power of the words gata tree and the beginning. The same illusion is obtained by the manifestation

sanskrit: eka tva nitya tā ādiḥ ca kalpitaḥ na tu tāttvikaḥ / tat atra hāsa karaṇam mahāvidvat tva sūcakam //

sanskrit: avadhāraṇa sāmarthyāt anya apohaḥ api gamyate / sva ātmā eva gamyate yatra viphalaḥ niyamaḥ amyathā //
reference: Even in cases where the thing itself is apprehended, the ‘exclusion of other things’ is also apprehended,—as is indicated by the force of the emphasising term (used by you); if it were not, then, the emphasising would be useless

sanskrit: yasya tarhi na bāhyaḥ arthaḥ api anyathā vṛttaḥ iṣyate / vandhyā suta ādi śabdasya tena kva apohaḥ ucyate //

baseline: The word vāndhyā is said to be false if it has no external meaning and otherwise the circle is given.

sanskrit: rūpa abhāvāt abhāvānām śabdāḥ jāti ādi vācakāḥ / na āśaṅkyāḥ eva siddhāḥ te nirbhāsasya eva sūcakāḥ //
reference: As non-entities have no form, words appertaining to those cannot be even suspected of being denotative of the universal and such things. in fact, it has been fully established that they are only indicators of the reflection

morphology: Those who speak the words due to lack of form absence caste origin fear not perfect are the indicators of ignorance.

sanskrit: artha śūnya abhijalpa uttha vāsanā mātra nirmitam / pratibimbam yat ābhāti tat śabdaiḥ pratipādyate //
