morphology: One who does not understand the subject of the matter of the vision and does not destroy the subject one who is not aware of it that illusion of the circle starts from the image one does not see it and the other thing is revealed from the manifestation of the image. One who is unaware of the subject is not able to understand it.

sanskrit: yat iva yasya yadi ca api asya bhāvasya yat rūpa sthiti kāraṇam / na vidyate na tattvena sa vyavasthāpyate budhaiḥ // avidyamāna sāsnā ādiḥ yathā karkaḥ gavātmanā / viśeṣaṇa viśiṣṭa artha viśiṣṭa artham grahaṇam na ca vidyate // sa vikalpaka bhāvasya sthiteḥ ākṣe nibandhanam / vipakṣaḥ śābaleya ādiḥ anyathā atiprasajyate // na ca aprasiddha tā hetoḥ jāti ādeḥ pratiṣedhataḥ
reference: Or again, when there is no basis for the existence of a thing in a certain form,—that thing in that form is not admitted as real, by the wise. For instance, the white horse is not admitted to be the cow because the dewlap and the other features of the cow are not present in the horse. In the case of sense-perception there is no reason for the presence of the determinate character (the character of being associated with conceptual content), which could bring about the apprehension of the thing along with its properties.—Spotted and other cows are instances to the contrary. If it were not so, it would lead to absurd contingencies.—The reason adduced cannot be said to be ‘unproven’ (or not-admitted); as the universal and other qualifying factors have all been rejected. Nor are the properties cognised as apart from those factors. Nor are there any such properties
baseline: One who does not have the reason for the existence of the form and the nature of the manifestation of this feeling is not governed by the principles of the Buddha the preceptor of the pre-existing sense as in the case of the kārkāśṇa gāvatmā who says that there is no special meaning in the concept of a particular sense who is opposed to the pretence of the substitution of the sense and who is not against the principle of caste and vice is otherwise overprotected.
morphology: One who does not have the reason for the existence of the form and the nature of the manifestation of the feeling of the same would not be able to do so by the principles of the Buddha. One who is not able to understand the meaning of a particular thing would not get the special meaning of the word as mentioned by the sāsana chieftain one who is unable to understand it and one who has not been able to control the position of the other one would be overburdened by the pretence of the idea of caste and vice versa.

sanskrit: nām api vācakam na eva yat śabdasya sva lakṣaṇam / sva lakṣaṇasya vācya tva vācaka tve hi dūṣite // adhyāropitam eva atas vācya vācakam iṣyate / anāropitam artham ca pratyakṣam pratipadyate // sva lakṣaṇasya sadbhāve sadbhāvāt tad abhāvataḥ / vyavadhāna ādi bhāve ca tasya api vyatirekataḥ //
reference: The name also, which would be the ‘specific individuality’ of the word, can never be denotative; as the idea of the ‘specific individuality’ being the denotes or the denoted has been already rejected.—It is for this reason that the idea of the denoter and denoted has been regarded as something superimposed (upon things);—while what one apprehends by sense-perception is something which is not superimposed; because this perception is there only when the ‘specific individuality’ is there,—and it is not there when the specific individuality is not there—through the intervention of something else or some such reason
baseline: A speaker who does not know the meaning of a word or its own characteristics and who has not heard the words or who has spoken the words and who is not aware of the characteristics of the word and after having read the description would be wronged. Having said so he would be given the meaning which is not in the goodness of his character and would be manifestly wronged by the absence of the meaning.
morphology: A speaker who does not know the meaning of a word or its own characteristics or who has not heard it and who has spoken it after having read it or has spoken the words or the words themselves and having spoken the scriptures would be wronged. Having read the words that have been imposed the speaker would be given the meaning that has not been imposed. He would express it directly in the sense of goodness absence of it obstruction and obstruction etc.

sanskrit: aśakya samayaḥ hi ātmā nīla ādīnām ananya bhāj / teṣām atas ca saṃvittiḥ na abhijalpa anuṣaṅgiṇī //
reference: The nature of the blue and other things, being individually specific, is incapable of having any convention in regard to it; the perception of these things, therefore, cannot be associated with words
baseline: The soul should be the unique element of the blue elements in the impossible time. It should not be associated with those elements.
morphology: The spirit should be the unique form of the blue forms of the adivasis at the time when it is impossible. It should not be associated with them.

sanskrit: nanu nāma ādikam mā abhūt tasya grāhyam viśeṣaṇam / tathā api asiddha tā hetoḥ na eva vyāvartete yatas // artha antara vyavacchinna rūpeṇa agrahaṇam yadi / artha mātra grahaḥ vā syāt agrahaḥ vā ghaṭe yathā // ghaṭa antara vyavacchinna rūpeṇa agrahaṇam yadi / ghaṭa mātra grahaḥ vā syāt agrahaḥ vā ghaṭasya vai //
reference: Name (universal) and the rest may not be the distinguishing properties perceived, in the object (op sense-perception);—even so, the reason put forward does not cease to be inadmissible; because if there is no apprehension of the thing as distinguished from other things, then, there would either be an apprehension of the thing by itself only, or no apprehension at all; as in the case of the jar,—if there is no apprehension of the jar as distinguished from other jars, then there is either apprehension of the jar by itself alone, or no apprehension of the jar at all.”
baseline: The name of the object should not be derived from the original name. It should also not be considered as an adjective. It does not apply to the object. If the object is separated from the object it means only the planet and the object becomes a planet. If it is divided into objects it becomes a house a house or a house.
morphology: If the name of the object is not derived from the original one it should not be considered as an adjective. It is not known to be so. If it is derived in the form of a separate object then it is not considered as such. If the object has been acquired in the manner of a planet it would be acquired only in the sense of the planet and the object of the objects would become a planet. If there is only a planet and object of that object it becomes an object.

sanskrit: grāhya antara vyavacchinnam bhāvena grāhi ced matam / sa vikalpaka vijñānam bhavet vṛkṣa ādi bodha vat //
reference: If perception is regarded as apprehending the thing as distinguished from other apprehensible things,—then this cognition would be conceptual (determinate), just like the cognition of the tree and other things.”
baseline: One who perceives the difference between the two and perceives it with the spirit one should consider it as an alternative science. One should understand the tree.
morphology: One who perceives the difference between the two and perceives it with a sense of feeling one should consider it as alternative knowledge. One should understand the tree as the beginning.

sanskrit: viśeṣaḥ aspṛṣṭa sāmānyaḥ na ca kaścana vidyate / grahaṇe ced tat aspaṣṭam vibhāva tvāt na gṛhyate //
reference: There is no particular (or individual) without a touch of the universal. if this is not touched in the apprehension, then the particular, becoming devoid of being, cannot be apprehended.”
baseline: There is no ordinary person who has not been touched by you. If you do not accept it you will not be accepted.
morphology: There is no ordinary person who is not well known. If you accept that person it is not acceptable to you.

sanskrit: viśiṣṭa viṣayaḥ bodhaḥ kalpanā na iti sāhasam / na viśeṣaṇa samvandhāt ṛte vaiśiṣṭya sambhavaḥ //
reference: The assertion that the cognition apprehends a qualified thing, and yet it is not conceptual implies great temerity indeed! certainly, no ‘qualification’ is possible except through connection with qualifications.”
baseline: One does not know the meaning of a particular thing and does not imagine it. One would not know that a particular matter is possible in a relationship.
morphology: One who does not understand a particular subject and does not imagine that the courage is not known. One would not know the importance of the subject in relation.

sanskrit: sajātīya vijātīya vyāvṛtta artha grahāt mataḥ / viśiṣṭa viṣayaḥ bodhaḥ na viśeṣaṇa saṅgateḥ //
reference: When the cognition is held to apprehend the qualified thing,—it is by reason of its apprehending the thing as differentiated from other homogeneous and heterogeneous things,—and not of the connection of qualifications
baseline: The meaning of the word varājya vyārtha means one who does not know the meaning of a particular subject. One does not understand the meaning.
morphology: The meaning of the word varājya vyavritta is that one does not know the meaning of a particular subject.

sanskrit: bhedaḥ vaiśiṣṭyam uktam hi na viśeṣaṇa saṅgtiḥ / bhinnam iti api tat vācā na anuviddham pratīyate //
reference: What is meant by ‘being qualified’ (distinguished) is ‘difference”—not the connection of qualifications. but the idea also that ‘this is different’ is not cognised as associated with words
baseline: The difference is said to be special and the association is not said. Even if it is different the covenant does not appear to be binding.
morphology: The difference is said to be special. It is said not to be related. Even if it is different the agreement is not agreed upon.

sanskrit: svabhāva apara niḥśeṣa padārtha vyatirekiṇi / gṛhīte sati tasmin tu vikalpaḥ jāyate tathā //
reference: It is only after the thing has been apprehended as the ‘negation of all things other than itself’,—that there appears the conceptual cognition in the said form
baseline: When the nature is taken over by the other elements and the rest is taken away by others there is an alternative.
morphology: When the nature is taken over by the other elements and the rest is taken away by others there is a choice in that.

sanskrit: viśeṣaṇa anavacchinnam paraiḥ sāmānyam iṣyate / nirvikalpaka vijñāna grāhyam tatra api atas samam //
reference: Other people regard.the universal as not distinguished by qualifications,—which universal they regard as apprehended by non-conceptual perception. what has been urged is applicable to that also
baseline: It is said that the unbroken part is given to the common man by others. The undecided science is accepted even there.
morphology: It is said to be common to others and unbroken. It is also equal to that where it is considered to be undefined.

sanskrit: viśeṣāt hi viśiṣṭam tat sāmānyam avagamyate / tad grāhakam atas prāptam vijñānam sa vikalpakam //
reference: The universal is recognised as ‘distinguished’ from the particular; hence the perception of it would have to be regarded (under the opponent’s contention) as conceptual
baseline: That which is unique from the particular is generally accepted by the customer. That which has obtained knowledge from the same is called alternative.
morphology: That which is unique from the particulars is generally accepted by the customer. That obtained by him is known as knowledge. That acquired by him as knowledge is called alternative.

sanskrit: nirviśeṣam gṛhītaḥ ced bhedaḥ sāmānyam ucyate / tatas viśeṣāt sāmānya viśiṣṭa tvam na yujyate //
reference: A thing is called ‘universal’ when it is apprehended without distinction; hence it is not right to regard the universal as something distinguished from the particular.”
baseline: The difference is said to be normal if the particular person is taken into custody. Then the difference is called normal. Then it is not equal to normal.
morphology: The difference is said to be normal if the particular person is taken into custody. Then the difference is called normal. Then it is not equal to normal.

sanskrit: vaiṣamya sama bhāvena jñāyamānāḥ ime kila / prakalpayanti sāmānya viśeṣa sthitim ātmani //
reference: When these (particulars) are cognised as similar or dissimilar, they indicate the existence in themselves, of the character of the ‘universal’ or the ‘particular’.”
baseline: Having equivocally understood these things one should imagine the general and special condition of the self.
morphology: They are known to be equal in appearance and to be able to perceive the general and special position of the self.

sanskrit: vaiṣamya sama bhāvaḥ ayam pravibhaktaḥ yadi iṣyate / sāmānyasya viśiṣṭa tvam tad avastham viśeṣataḥ // atha avibhaktaḥ eva ayam asaṅkīrṇā sthitiḥ katham / anyonya aparihāreṇa sthiteḥ gati antaram na ca //
reference: If the said ‘similarity’ and ‘dissimilarity’ are held to be differentiated, then the fact of the universal being distinguished from the particulars remains as before.—If, on the other hand, they are not held to be differentiated, then, how can the clearly marked division be possible, without crossing each other? there is no other way in which they could be conceived
baseline: If one enters the same position as the other one would be divided into two parts. Then that position would be special for the common man. That position would become undivided. This position would not be equal to the number of others and there would be no difference in the speed.
morphology: If one enters a place with the same feeling as that of the other one would be divided into two parts. Then one would get that state in particular. One would get undivided. One should get this state without any difference in speed and distance from one another.

sanskrit: viśeṣa ātma atirekeṇa na aparam bheda lakṣaṇam / tad rūpa asparśane teṣu grahaṇam katham ucyate // tad rūpa sparśane ca api bheda antara vibhedinaḥ / gṛhītāḥ iti vijñānam prāptam eṣu vikalpakam //
reference: Of the particular things there is no other characteristic except that of being ‘particular’ (or ‘distinct’); how then can there be any apprehension of them which does not envisage the ‘distinct’ form? Even if their forms are envisaged, they are apprehended only as distinct from other particulars; so that their perception would be ‘conceptual’
baseline: One who touches that form and does not perceive the difference in the other is called the substitution of that form. One who does not know the difference between the two forms is called subtracted from that form by touching that form and the difference is known as subtraction.
morphology: One who does not perceive the difference in the form of the self and the other features by the extreme distance of the form is called a different person. One who perceives the difference between the forms and the differences is called an alternative person.

sanskrit: nirupākhyāt ca sāmānyam viśeṣam saṃpratīyate / atas vikalpaka jñāna grāhyam tat api te bhavet // na asataḥ tat viśiṣṭam ced kibhidānīm tad ātmakam / no ced tathā api vaiśiṣṭyam tasmāt asya na kim matam //
reference: The universal is cognised as ‘distinguished’ (distinct) from the featureless thing; hence for you, it should be cognisable by conceptual perception.—If it be urged that “the universal cannot be regarded as distinguished from a non-entity”,—then (we ask) is it of the same nature as the non-entity? if not, then why is it not admitted that it is ‘distinguished’ from it?
baseline: The common and the special are known by the unspeakable. Then the knowledge of the alternative should be taken into account. If it is not known to be so then it should be known to the individual. If not to the particular person it should not be said to be true to the self if not to that particular thing then to that which it is said to have not to be said.
morphology: One who does not know the meaning of the word should say that it is common and that which is not known to be known to him. One who has not known the meaning one who knows the meaning and the meaning should not say that which was not known by him one should not believe that it belongs to him and one who has no knowledge of it should also say that what he believes is true.

sanskrit: a tad ātmakam eva idam vaiśiṣṭyam vastunaḥ api hi / na asat rūpam ca sāmānyam tat viśiṣṭam na te katham // tasmāt sva lakṣaṇe jñānam yat kiṃcid saṃpravarttate / vāc patha atīta viṣayam sarvam tat nirvikalpakam //
reference: As a matter of fact, in the case of the entity also, being ‘distinguished’ consists in not being that same; and as the universal is not the same as the non-entity, why can you not regard it as being ‘distinguished’ from the non-entity? From all this it follows that whatever cognition appears in regard to the ‘specific individuality’ of things appertains to what is beyond the range of words and is hence non-conceptual
baseline: A self is the characteristic of a thing it is not the appearance of the object the general appearance the specific form the knowledge of its features and the things beyond the path that it has gone through. It is the undefined one.
morphology: One who does not know the nature of things the nature the appearance the general form the special form and the knowledge of the characteristics of oneself and the things beyond the path would be able to understand something. One who knows everything would be undefined.

sanskrit: asti hi ālocana ajñānam ādyam ced nirvikalpakam / bāla mūka ādi vijñāna sadṛśam śuddha vastu jam // na viśeṣaḥ na sāmānyam tadānīm anubhūyate / tayoḥ ādhāra bhūtā tu vyaktiḥ eva avasīyate // tatas param punar vastu dharmaiḥ jāti ādibhiḥ yayā / buddhyā avasīyate sā api pratyakṣa tvena saṃmatā //
reference: At first there is only a pre-cognition, which is non-conceptual, like the cognition of the infant and the dumb and the like;—it is born purely of the thing (cognised); at that moment, neither the universal nor the particular character is apprehended; all that is apprehended is only a certain individual which is the substratum of both those characters
baseline: One who does not know the meaning of the word does not understand the meaning. One who is a child a dumb person and does not think of the meaning or a pure thing like knowledge does nothing good and does nothing ordinary then one who is the base of these things and who is living in them and then again living in the mind and living in religion caste etc. would also agree with you directly.
morphology: One who does not know the meaning of the word does not think it is ignorance is not able to understand it is a fool is an illiterate person has no knowledge is aware of the pure thing is neither good nor ordinary then the person who is the foundation of it and then the objects are settled by the people by the religion caste etc. and then again by the mind he is settled directly by you.

sanskrit: punar punar vikalpe api yāvān adhigamaḥ bhavet / tad sambandha anusāreṇa sarvam pratyakṣam iṣyate //
reference: Again and again, as more and more conceptual contents come in, there follow further apprehensions, in connection with the same; and all this is regarded as ‘sense-perceptionślokavārtika—sense-perception, 125)
baseline: All that is learnt should be repeated in a different way and the same should be given directly according to the relationship.
morphology: All that is learnt should be repeated in a different way. All this will be revealed according to the relationship.

sanskrit: na hi praviṣṭa mātrāṇām uṣṇāt garbha gṛha ādiṣu / arthāḥ na pratibhānti iti gamyante na indriyaiḥ punar //
reference: When a man returns from bright light into an inner room, things do not manifest themselves to him immediately upon his entrance; but that does not mean that later on he does not perceive those things by his sense-organs.”Ślokavārtika—sense-perception, 126)
baseline: One would find that the objects are not visible in the womb. They would not be warm in the form of heat. The objects would not appear in the sense organs.
morphology: One would not get the meaning of the objects in the womb from the heat of those objects which have not been entered. One would never get the sense organs again.

sanskrit: yathā tu ābhāsa mātreṇa pūrvam jñātvā svarūpataḥ / paścāt tatra vibuddhyante tathā jāti ādi dharmataḥ //
reference: Just as, in the first instances, he perceives a mere semblance of the thing and subsequently he perceives them in their true form,—so also with the properties of ‘class-character’ and the rest.”Ślokavartika—sense-perception, 127)
baseline: Just as the manifestations are known by the mother in the past by the form and then by the origin of the caste and religion.
morphology: Just as the manifestations are known by the mother in the past they are understood by the nature in the future and by the original religion.

sanskrit: yadi tu ālocya saṃmīlya netre kaścid vikalpayet / na syāt pratyakṣa tā tasya sambandha ananusārataḥ //
reference: If after having pre-cognised the thing, the man closes his eyes and then imposes conceptual contents,—this latter would not be ‘sense-perception’;—because it is not in accordance with the connection (op the sense-organs).”Ślokavārtika—sense-perception, 128)
baseline: If a person has made a choice in the eye after having discussed it he should not make a choice. He should not be associated with it in any way.
morphology: If a person has made a choice in the eyes after having discussed the matter together he should not make such a choice.

sanskrit: tat ayuktam yadi jñānam tat pravṛttam sva lakṣaṇe / anāviṣṭa abhilāpam tad jāti ādi grahaṇe api hi // tathā ca avācyam eva idam sādhitam prāk sva lakṣaṇam / tasmin vṛttam ca vijñānam niyatam nirvikalpakam //
reference: What has been urged is not right. if the cognition in question appertains to the specific individuality of the thing,—then, even on the apprehension of the universal and other properties, it should remain free from verbal expression. because it has been proved before that the specific individuality of things cannot be denoted by words; hence the cognition that rests upon that must be free from conceptual content (and association with words)
baseline: It is said that if the knowledge has already been acquired it should be applied to its own characteristics the undesirables that are present in it the desires that are not present in the country the original possession of the same and it should also be obtained in the past. The knowledge should be fixed in that circle and the knowledge should not be determined by the designer.
morphology: If the knowledge has already been established it should be considered as having its own characteristics. If it has not been established as such then it should also be accepted as having acquired the original characteristics of the caste. It should be declared as having attained its characteristics before and the circle and knowledge should be determined as undefined.

sanskrit: jāti mātra grahe tu syāt ekāntena vibhinna tā / viśeṣaṇasya na etat ca paraiḥ iṣṭam yathā uditam //
reference: If the universal alone were apprehended, then the qualification (property) would be something- absolutely distinct; and this is not what is acceptable to the other party, as asserted (by himself)
baseline: A nation should be separate from the planet. It should not be known to others as it is.
morphology: A nation should be different from others in its own way. It should not be known to others as it is derived from others.

sanskrit: yadi hi ekāntataḥ bhinnam viśeṣyāt syāt viśeṣaṇam / sva anurūpām tadā buddhim viśeṣye janayet katham //
reference: If the qualification were absolutely distinct from the qualified, then how could it bring about in the qualified a cognition in keeping with itself?”—[Ślokavārtika—sense-perception, 142]
baseline: If it is different from the speciality of the individual then the adjective should be similar to that of the self. Then how can the intellect be created in the particulars.
morphology: If it is different from that of the other adjectives then the adjective should be derived from that which corresponds to itself.

sanskrit: sva sāmānya ātmanoḥ yuktam jñānam ca ekam na vedakam / sa vikalpa anyathā bhāve prāktana apara vid na hi //
reference: One and the same cognition cannot comprehend both the specific individuality and the universal; because, if such a cognition were ‘conceptual’, there could be no comprehension of the former,—on the other hand, if it were otherwise, there could be no comprehension of the latter
baseline: One who has knowledge of his own ordinary self is not the same as that of the Vedas. One who does not think otherwise would not be able to understand the past.
morphology: One who has the knowledge of his common self is not the same as that of the Vedas. One who does not have the choice would not be the former.

sanskrit: ekāntena anya tā bhāvāt jāti ādi ādyena ced gatam / vijñāta artha adhigantṛ tvāt smārta jñāna samam param //
reference: On account of there being no absolute distinction (between the universal and the specific individuality),—if the universal and other properties have become already apprehended by the initial cognition,—then the subsequent cognition would be apprehending only what has been already apprehended,—and it would thus be like remembrance
baseline: One should know the meaning of the same after having conquered it. One should understand the same thing after knowing that one has gone from the beginning of the race to the beginning.
morphology: One should know the meaning of the word as far as possible. One should understand the meaning and understand the same.

sanskrit: saṃmugdha aneka sāmānya rūpeṇa adhigame sati / na eva ced niścitam vastu niścayaḥ tu uttarottaraḥ // samāropa vyavaccheda viṣaya tvāt yathā anumā / samāropa vyavaccheda viṣayaḥ niścayaḥ tathā //
reference: At the initial stage), there is only a vague idea of several universals, and there is no definite idea of anything; the definite idea comes only later; as this apprehends the thing as differentiated from all impositions (doubts and misconceptions). Just as inference apprehends the object as differentiated from impositions, so also does the (later) definite cognition.”
baseline: The subject matter of the final division should be determined by you in the same way as the subject matter is determined by an annuṣa.
morphology: The subject matter of the end and the parting should be determined by you in the same way as the subject matter is determined by the anumā ending and parting.

sanskrit: na samāropa viccheda viṣaya tvena māna tā / anumāyāḥ pramāṇa tva prasaṅgena smṛteḥ api // pratyakṣa anantara udbhūta samāropaṇa vāraṇāt / iṣṭam tu laiṅgikam jñānam pramāṇam na tat asti te // gauḥ śuklaḥ calati ityādau pratyakṣa anantaram na hi / samāropaḥ atra vijñāne vedyate yat niṣidhyate //
reference: As a matter of pact, the validity of inferential cognition does not rest upon its apprehending a thing differentiated from impositions; if that were so, then remembrance also would have to be regarded as valid. What really happens is that after the sense-perception (of a certain thing) there appear certain impositions (doubts and misconceptions), and it is by reason of setting aside these impositions that inferential-cognition has been regarded as valid.—This is not possible for you; because in the case of such cognitions as ‘the white—cow—walking’—after the sense-perception, no imposition is found to appear, which could be negatived (by the subsequent valid cognition)
baseline: One should not think of the end of the division even if the proof of the knowledge is mentioned in the context of the dissolution. One should also remember that the proof for the dissolution is directly derived from the sowing of the sow. One would not know the gender and the evidence for the same. One who does not believe in the knowledge of the cow the sukla the chariot etc. would not be able to do so directly after that.
morphology: One should not think about the end of the division even if the evidence for the division is mentioned in the context. One should remember that the proof for the dissolution is directly derived from the sowing of the sow and the proof of the knowledge of the sex is not there. One who does not know the cow the sukla the chariot the cow and the goat are not there after the conclusion of the discussion. The proof of sārūpa is not mentioned here and it is forbidden.

sanskrit: tattva anya tva ubhaya ātmānaḥ santi jāti ādayaḥ na ca / yat vikalpaka vijñānam pratyakṣa tvam prayāsyati // anvaya asatvataḥ bhedāt bhedena apratibhāsanāt / anyonya parihāreṇa sthiteḥ ca anya tva tattvayoḥ //
reference: As a matter of fact, universal and the rest do not exist, either as non-different, or as different, from (individuals),—by virtue of which the conceptual cognition of those could have the character of ‘perception’
baseline: The principle is the same as that of the other two spirits. You are not the originator of the race. You try to find out the alternative knowledge directly. You do not want to be different from each other. You want to know the difference between the two elements.

baseline: Having considered the general shape the difference between the castes the forms of the rasa and the knowledge of the origin the knowledge should not be subtracted from it. In the pursuit of justice all things are described by us. It should be considered as another manifest matter.

sanskrit: sarva ātmanā hi sārūpye jñānam ajñāna tām vrajet / sāmyam kenacid aṃśane sarvam syāt sarva vedakam //

sanskrit: kintu bāhya artha sadbhāva vāde sārūpya sambhavaḥ / dhruvam abhyupagantavyaḥ iti artham sa prakāśitaḥ // nirbhāsi jñāna pakṣe hi grāhyāt bhede api cetasaḥ / pratibimbasya tādrūpyāt bhāktam syāt api vedanam // yena tu iṣṭam na vijñānam artha asārūpya bhājanam / tasya ayam api na eva asti prakāraḥ bāhya vedane //
reference: But under the doctrine of the reality of the external world,, the possibility of the sameness of form has to be accepted; that is why it has been mentioned.—Under the doctrine, however, of cognition being a mere reflected image,—even if the cognition differs from the cognised object, the sameness of form belongs to the reflection; and the cognition can be only figurative.—Lastly, for one who does not admit the cognition to be the receptacle of the semblance of the object,—there is not even the said method possible for the cognising of the external object
baseline: But the outer meaning is possible by equating it with the promise of goodness the pole should reach the ground. The fearless person should be aware of the difference in the knowledge. sanskrit: sva para artha vibhāgena tu anumānam dvidhā iṣyate / svārtham trirūpataḥ liṅgāt anumeya artha darśanam // trirūpa liṅga vacanam parārtham punar ucyate / ekaika dvi dvi rūpaḥ arthaḥ liṅga ābhāsaḥ tatas mataḥ //
reference: Inference is held to be of two kinds, as divided into for one’s own benefit, and (2) for the benefit of others. baseline: The definition of self meaning is said to be twofold by the division of its own meaning. Selfishness should be considered as threefold and the meaning should be seen by the gender. The word linga should be repeated as one two one and the other. The concept of gender should be said as one.

sanskrit: anyathā anupapanna tve nanu dṛṣṭā su hetu tā / na asati tri aṃśakasya api tasmāt klībāḥ tri lakṣaṇāḥ //

sanskrit: sa śyāmaḥ tasya putra tvāt dṛṣṭā śyāmā yathā itare / iti tri lakṣaṇaḥ hetuḥ na niścityai pravarttate //

sanskrit: atha idam lakṣaṇam hetoḥ dharmiṇi eva avagamyate / yatas pramāṇāt na asiddhiḥ sādhyasya api tatas na tu // sādhyasya apratipattau hi hetoḥ api na niścayaḥ / atas nirarthakaḥ hetuḥ anyatas sādhya siddhitaḥ // anyonya āśraya doṣaḥ ca hetoḥ sādhyasya niścaye / dvayoḥ anyarā siddhau anyasya api aviniścaye //
reference: If the proposed definition of the probans is meant to be one that is found in the minor term only,—then that same means of cognition which has made the probans known would make known the probandum also. Thus the probans would be useless, the probandum having become known by other means.—There would be the incongruity of ‘mutual interdependence’ also, if the definite cognition of the probandum followed from the probans; and between these two, the cognition of one would be dependent upon the cognition of the other
baseline: Thus the same characteristic is achieved only by means of righteousness not by the evidence of incompleteness not even by the attainment of attainment. One would achieve it by taking refuge in another and committing a mistake for the purpose of achieving that goal. Both would be accomplished by the other. The other would also be undecided.

baseline: The three qualities of the voice related to viprātis are expressed in the words of the father whatever the voice of the hearer is mentioned in the scriptures. The voice related with the vowel is found in the past. The sound related to the vowels is not known in its past.
morphology: One who listens to the words of the father whatever the voice of the wife is mentioned the cause of the mother should be expressed in three signs. One who has heard the voice related to viprāprātī one who has not experienced it in the past and who has never experienced it for the sake of evil.

sanskrit: yasmin prāk upalabdhaḥ ca na upalabdhaḥ ca yatra saḥ / anvayaḥ vyatirekaḥ vā vispaṣṭam tatra dṛśyate // śabdaḥ tu jñāpayati artham na eva bāhyam kathaṃcana / anyathā asambhava abhāvāt vilakṣa āgamakaḥ tu asau // tasyām ca pratipādyāyām vailakṣaṇyam ati sphuṭam / vivakṣā saṃmukhībhāve na hi śabdaḥ prayujyate // dīpaḥ tu jñāpakaḥ na eva nīla ādeḥ liṅga bhāvataḥ / jñāna utpādana yogyasya jananāt tu tathā ucyate
reference: In that house wherein the father had been found before,—and also in that wherein he had not been found before,—there is the concomitance, positive and negative, clearly perceived,—as regards the word, it does not make known any external object at all; because in this case, the character of ‘being otherwise impossible’ is not present; the word can only be the indicator of the ‘speaker’s wish’ (to speak of a certain thing). If this (speaker’s wish) were meant to be what is expressed by the word, then its difference is quite clear. Because when the ‘speaker’s wish’ is not there, the word cannot be used.—As regards the lamp, it does not make the blue and other things known by becoming the indicative (inferential); all that it does is to make things capable of being cognised; and it is only in this sense that it is called a ‘means of cognition only in case the word were an inferential indicative, would it be necessary to consider if it fulfils the conditions of being present in the subject (minor term.) and so forth. Otherwise, why cannot the same be urged in connection with the eye and other organs (as means of cognition)?—Even through the character of ‘being otherwise impossible’, visibility cannot prove anything, unless it is present in the subject (minor term).—Thus ‘one-featured’ probans are all impotent.—In those that have been cited as ‘one-featured’ probans, the presence of two features becomes clearly indicated; and in those that have been cited as ‘two-featured’, the presence of three features becomes clearly indicated; because every probans must reside in the subject (which therefore is an additional condition that must be fulfilled).—If it be argued that “this feature is implied by the character of being otherwise impossible”,—that cannot be so; because in the case of sound, though visibility may be otherwise desired, it is not present in sound (which is the subject)
baseline: One who is not available in the past and who is found in the opposite direction or in a different direction is said to be the manifestation of the meaning of the word. One who does not know the meaning does not say the words outwardly or in the absence of the impossibility of it. One should not say that which is not possible and which would not be possible in the future. One would say that the word would be very clear in the context of the matter and would never be used in the direction of the object of the speech. morphology: One who has not been able to find the object before one who is not available and one who does not want to get the object or who is against it and where it is found in a clear place the word denotes the meaning of the object. One who comes out of the absence of the impossibility of it would not be able to express it. One would not use the word in a way that is too clear and distinct in the context of the problem. One should not say that the object is blue the object of knowledge is blue and the person is not capable of producing knowledge.

sanskrit: tad putra tva ādi hetūnām sandigdha vyatirekataḥ / na trailakṣaṇya sadbhāvaḥ vijātīya avirodhataḥ //
reference: In the case of such probans as ‘because he is the son of so and so’, the contrary being open to doubt, the three conditions are not present; because what is cited is not incompatible with the contrary
baseline: That son should be in doubt of the original intentions and not against the three.
morphology: That son should be the one who doubts the original intentions and does not oppose the three.
